reviews.comment: Don't take him
Does not care about student proformance
terrible experience
He is literally an Evil person

This dude literally doesn't care about anyone but himself. Usually never responds to emails and acts like you are dumb for even emailing or asking a question to him. Virginia Tech should be embarrassed that they hired this professor. I'm only doing well because I took Calc in hs.

Does not teach, rather has you work off the slides. If you are coming in without any calc classes taken in hs or in general, goodluck learning. He reviews the things you barely need to know for tests but spends most time reviewing things that wont really be on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst math teacher I have had in my academic career. Teaches incredibly fast, and very rarely will he take the time out of his day to ensure people understand. If you have the option, select another teacher for this course.
Genuinely the worst math teacher I have ever had, not only does he not teach the class material properly, but he will berate students for asking any questions.
belittles students for asking questions and goes so fast you aren't learning but just copying notes. no partial credit on exams or quizzes. does not care for students and is so full of himself.

His teaching style is so bad I genuinely think he wants to see his students fail. He clearly makes students feel embarrassed or dumb when they ask questions. He "teaches" insanely fast making it so you are not learning you are just copying. I will never take a class with this professor again and I advise you to do the same.

Worst teacher you will have your freshman year. Lectures are really fast and really useless because of Hulko. Tests are 15% of your grade, there's 12 questions and NO PARTIAL credit. Avoid him at all costs.

Absolutely horrible, practically insults anyone who asks a genuine question in class, and refuses to explain concepts thoroughly. Grades late and is extremely nitpicky when it comes to homework and tests. I had to fight to get a mistake he made during grading fixed. He always seemed annoyed when I showed up to office hours.
Very open to answering questions, you have to pay attention to keep up with the lecture notes, don't expect to get everything correct on written homework
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take this class, find another professor. If you ask a question, he won't really answer it, and leave you with more questions. 80 percent of the class is tests, and if you don't use his notes, he considers it cheating. All of it is theorem based, and it's all based on his notes taken in class. Do not take, please find another professor.

His class was extremely hard, and significantly harder than the other linear classes, his homework's are complicated and long. For example on his MCQ on tests require us to show work for credit no lucky guesses. I have A's in all my classes this including an A multivar calculus, but I think I might fail his class. AVOID HIM PLZ for your own good

His lectures are fast paced but helpful. The written homeworks take a while but are very similar to the tests, so make sure you understand them. His tests have extra credit true/false questions at the end.
Very intelligent and good at teaching, and yet belittles students. Homeworks and tests are fairly rough. Not worth taking.
Extremely hostile, would call questions stupid if he didn't like them
Worst professor I ever had, Tests are much harder than other Linear Algebra teachers. You can only use notes provided in class or he considers it “cheating”.

If you want to actually learn the basics of linear algebra without pulling your hair out and feeling stupid, take ANYONE else. This guy makes an intro class feel like torture. Save yourself the headache and the unnecessary workload. You'll spend way more time on this class than it's worth, and honestly, it feels like he enjoys making it that way.

For anyone who looks at this rating and has a deep heavy sigh, I was in your shoes. Don't be afraid of Dr. Hulko, he is pretty strict about his policies and wants you to succeed but the way he comes across might be a bit tough at first. I promise for any STEM majors, you will be okay. Also, the business majors review bombed him with a massive cope
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you don't have prior calculus experience, this class will be extremely difficult. He moves so fast during lectures, you're honestly better off learning the material yourself. He also makes you feel bad for asking questions and won't post any of the notes.

If you value your sanity, run. He is smug, constantly laughing at students and dripping with sarcasm He avoids answering questions and makes you regret asking. 1524 is easy if you have calc experience, but he piles on endless busy work and homework. He treats students like they are beneath him and makes learning painful. Avoid at all costs.
Smug, will laugh at you and be sarcastic at any chance given. Arrogant and will not answer questions. 1524 is easy if you have any calc experience. Lots of busy-work lots of homework that is useless.

Not a hard class at all. Everything taught in this class should be review from high school, thus, sometimes I scorn at paying money to take this class. There is homework that is due every week, but relatively easy with the amount of resources you have.

I would only take this class if you already have a prior knowledge of calculus - if you do, this class should not be much of an issue to you, yet if you haven't taken any calculus, he is going to move very quickly. The tests are often easier than the homeworks - study the written homeworks and WebAssigns. Overall, a good teacher, yet not easy.

Honestly all these reviews saying he's horrible are just lazy. The class is pretty easy if you try and I had no experience in calculus at all. He goes quick but he stops frequently to ask if everyone understands and has questions. He was very easy to reach and helpful. Every single class has the same amount of homework regardless of the teacher.

Hulko is very fast-paced in class. He doesn't post any notes on Canvas, and his lectures weren't the greatest. His presence feels very intimidating so going to a TA, friend, or YouTube for questions/help is best. If you took Calc AB in high school you'll be fine but definitely find a different professor.

He is very fast paced, will skip part of the notes to be ahead and does not post them. You're better off learning the concepts on youtube/on your own or through the TA. I don't recommend him, try to get a different professor. He is very hard to reach, especially through email. Tests are hard.
If you took AP Calc AB in high school, this class will be extremely easy for you until the last two weeks. Also so much busy work homework that is useless and just annoying.
This professor just doesn't teach well, he knows what to do but just can't teach it and moves at a very fast pace.

He was horrible at teaching and his lectures made no sense at some points. He knew what to do but he is not good at explaining things. The notes he put on canvas were basically useless. They were unfilled and when he was speeding through his lectures, he doesn't give you any time to write down the equations. Don't take him if you want to be happy.

Horrible teacher. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Moves at the speed of lighting. Lectures don't teach you anything. Does not post notes, so you can't check your work. Puts more content on tests and makes it harder than other classes in the same course. No late work. I genuinely feel like he wants his students to fail. The content wasn't hard he made it hard.

Avoid Professor Hulko. He is super passive-aggressive and will make you feel stupid for asking questions. Although the content isn't super difficult in this course, a lot of material is covered, and he isn't the best at explaining things. He moves so quickly that he cancelled a class since we were so ahead of all other sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He won't explain when you ask questions during class. All he does is speed through the notes and scroll before you even have a chance to ask any questions. He does NOT post any of his notes on canvas. He penalizes every little thing and laughs at you if you don't understand the material. Started off with 23 students in class, and now we are at 8.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Will be smug at you if you bring up any difficulties with the course. Incredibly rigid when grading, no bonus points for doing anything interesting. Will penalize every mistake on your paper with half off the entire question.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Arguably one of the most arrogant people I've ever had to associate with. Don't show up to office hours unless you want laughed at for not understanding topics that are barley discussed in class. Moves faster than any other class for 1524. Overall, a horrible professor and it is a shame Virginia Tech allows such behavior.
Dude cant teach, gets mad at anything you say. I dont know how he is even a professor.

Goes through lecture problems really fast and is bad at explaining the steps. Homework is much harder than classwork problems. No credit for late homework. Guys an a hole ngl. Homework is long and graded by accuracy. Wouldn't recommend taking this class unless it was the last choice. Not very helpful if you email him either.

I'm just glad I passed the class. He's a smart dude but I tried to interact with him as little as possible. He makes everything difficult. Don't talk to him if you don't want a sarcastic/smart answer. If you have a question, make sure you know what you're talking about first. Would post answers to tests/homeworks, but delete after about a week.

Not a nice guy and he moves at the speed of light during lectures making it very easy to get lost. Course exams are a small amount of very hard questions, i only passed the class because of the weekly homework assignments.

If you don't attend class good luck finding the notes. He won't post the filled in notes nor will he post his lectures. If you go to his office hours he'll give you attitude and is useless. Good luck finding a tutor that knows what they are doing in calculus. He gives zero extra credit and refuses to curve grades. Pretty much your on your own.

Professor Hulko moves through problems very fast which would be difficult for a newcomer to calculus. I barely attended this class as it was a large lecture hall and it was a 9am. I tended to do about 90% of my learning on my own through reviewing the homeworks and examples and it was not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He goes very fast at the beginning of the course since we just reviewed high school pre-calculus materials. He is very accessible after class during his office hours. Although lectures and recitation are not mandatory, I highly recommend you go for the good habit and keep up with the material and understand it.

He is a tough teacher for those who aren't good at math. His homework takes me anywhere from 1-4 hours, but they prepare me well for the tests and force me to memorize theorems which is good all around. His grading is tough, but consistent so it's hard to blame anyone but yourself when you get the same problems wrong multiple times.

He is the worst teacher I have ever had. He does know how to actually teach the material, he just goes through problems really fast, with no explanation. Is not understanding at all. By far the worst teacher, save your time.

Hulko was a nice man but was not very forgiving towards late assignments. He gave so much homework (3-4 pages of written & 40+ online math questions a week). His lectures were extremely fast paced and spontaneous and if you missed just one class, it would set you back a lot. If you did not do well in Algebra 2 and Pre Calc, you may fail this class.

Lectures were very fast paced and didn't make a lot of sense. Webassign homeworks were manageable but written assignments were long and hard. The beginning of class has "iclickers" that won't count for a grade unless attendance is low or if participation is bad. Test were very hard and he wont curve bc someone gets a 105 but averages were ~60-70%

I genuinely have never second guessed my major or field until I stepped into this class. The material covered and assignments / lectures were painful and in great volume, and they did not really match up to the exams at all which were graded in a struct manner. Lectures are not really helpful at all either, they go extremely surface level.

Professor Hulko is an amazing professor. As long as you work hard and show that you are willing to do better, he will work with you. His lectures are intriguing, and his exams are tough although there are never any curve balls thrown. As long as you study and attend lecture you will do well in this class.

Not a bad professor, Hulko is strict because he wants students to learn. As a result, his sections are harder than other linear sections but you will learn more being in his class than other sections. The best way to succeed in his class is to memorize every theorem and definition he throws at you. Exams are curved which can pass 100 points.

One of the worst teachers I've ever had. The tests are extremely difficult with no curve and essentially making you provide work on multiple choice questions and true or false questions ripped off from the definitions in the notes. Equally the homework's are extremely difficult, don't be surprised if it takes you 4-5 hours to do each one. BEWARE!

This is by far the worst professor I've ever had the displeasure of being with at Virginia Tech. If you have any other option to take Linear Algebra with another professor, I would highly consider it. His tests are insanely difficult and it is almost impossible to fully prepare to be that you even have to show work for multiple choice questions.

I cont stress this enough but if you're bad at math just like me TAKE THIS COURSE ONLINE. The only reason I was able to pass this course was because I took the course online. USE the VT MATH TUTOR on youtube he is an ANGLE and has done practice problems for the entire semester. You will pass with these tips. 

Also, I took his 1026 course
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Doesnt teach anything in class, just does practice problems on things that were never taught.

My old professor left the school 3 days after the drop classes closed, and so we got him. We were already 2-3 weeks on material apparently, so watching the lecture videos would take 5-6 hours. He left no chance in class to go over the material. On test 2 I did not meet a single person who got over a 70, and he refuses to curve. Do not take him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: When asking questions either in class or office hours he was very condescending and I would often leave even less confident in my understanding of the material. His tests were very difficult and he was a very picky grader and gave almost no partial credit. Test averages were typically in the 60s but no curve was given. Worst option for linear.

Hulko was not very nice or forgiving to his students. He would snicker if a student answered his question wrong or asked what he deemed as a dumb question. The homework and tests were difficult and he was an unforgiving grader. He made multiple students upset in office hours and I always left class feeling degraded and confused about the material.

Very Strict. Extremely tough and picky grader. Even though you might understand all the materials and do everything correctly, you will still receive a very low grade for not doing it "his way". I would only recommend taking him if you want to fail other than that stay away from him.
Very intentional and passionate professor. Very kind and easy to understand, genuinely wants you to succeed.
He is a great teacher. He also is very lenient on grading as long as you can put in minimal effort.

Khan is the goat. He is really kind in lecture and explains the content really well during class. Spends a lot of time deriving formulas during lecture, not too many practice problems. Tests were heavily curved. Take him if you can!

Bro is genuinely the goat- he's a very good teacher and you can tell he cares about the material himself, making it easier to pay attention and want to learn. Absolute 10/10 one of the best profs I've ever had

Khan is definitely one of the better physic professors. Unfortunately, though, his teaching method does not work for me. He mostly spends class deriving formulas instead of teaching the content or going through practice problems. Fortunately, his prequizzes allow for the tests to be significantly curved. Very nice man, though. Just very hard class

Professor Khan is one of the best physics professors at VT. He is kind and will walk you through any problem. He makes funny jokes and makes learning easy and clear. If you need to take physics 2, take it with him. he also gives curves and extra credit. He truly wants to see his students succeed

Dr. Khan is very passsionate about physics, it's clear that he enjoys what he does, and he wants you to as well! Let yourself enjoy his lectures, they're genuinely amazing. He has the enthusiasm of a kid and the knowledge of a career physicist.
The class goes the same as 2305, easy HW, prequizzes, straightforward exams, etc. Professor Khan specifically is very sweet and it's clear he has a huge passion for physics- W professor

Dr Khan gave good lectures and explained the concepts in an easy-to-understand, energetic and passionate way. He was also invaluable when you asked questions in class or during office hours. He even went above and beyond by making the second and final exams easier. Wish I could've attended his lectures more though, but it was an 8am :(

Truly a great professor, my favorite at VT so far. Obviously knows what he is talking about and has amazing lectures. Tests can be difficult and make up 60% of the grade but the curve is super helpful.
Dr. Khan is the GOAT for Physics II. I would've definitely failed if it wasn't for him hahaha. Super fun guy with such a bright personality. Definately enroll in his section if you can.

I didn't even have Dr. Khan as my main professor - I started going to his office hours because my professor's lectures were confusing. He's easily one of the best professors I've ever met. The PHYS 2306 content is conceptually challenging, however he was always able to explain any questions I had, and clearly enjoys teaching and helping students.

Rude and not good at teaching I got a 50 on the first exam just using the info he gave us in class. After that, I decided to save myself some time and read the textbook on my own, got a 100 on the second test. Also, I had a tragic accident happen over the semester and I had to inform all of my professors, and he just never responded.
One of the best teachers ive had here

Excellent lectures from this professor. Explains concepts very effectively and is always willing to answer questions. He prepares us well for the midterms and is very reasonable, understanding, and compassionate. Definitely take Dr. Khan if possible.

goooood afternoooooon hooookiiiessss. Physics 2 makes absolutely no sense sometimes. Stuff just happens because it wants to. Mechanical waves was fine but once electricity gets involved you're cooked. Formulas spawn out of thin air, and he's difficult to understand. If you want an A, just do the pre exams and use the far moola :) also O chem tutor.
dudes class was actually the worst. Just cheat on all the pre-exam quizzes like everyone else does and you're practically guaranteed an A. it's unbelievable how he's just oblivious to this shit.

Good lectures, with good notes. Pre-lecture videos on canvas helped SO much. Class is difficult but with a teacher like Dr. Khan, I really enjoyed it as he made it very funny, whilst caring about students well being and understanding of the content. PHYS2306 IS HARD, but if you work hard, take advantage of given resources, you can do well.

Lectures don't always teach what is on the test, watch the videos/read pre lecture slides so you have a better understanding. Teaches on whiteboard so go to class, do clicker questions. Almas is funny and caring and is definitely the best 2306 professor. DO NOT start dozing in class, one second goes by and youll be cramming for weeks. overall good

Good lecturer, but boring if you don't like physics. 25% of what's on the test is always absent from the lectures so read the pre-lecture slides: they have every equation you need. PHYS2306 is a hard class, but Almas is generous with grades and funny too, so it's not nearly as much of a slog.
Lectures are a bit scattered, so do the pre-lecture readings + videos beforehand! Funny guy who is very knowledgeable on the subject matter.

I had him online. He made lectures into videos to watch on our own time, which was nice. I liked that he posted practice tests before exams, but they were almost useless bc I couldn't read his handwriting so I didn't know what was going on. His lectures were confusing, there were better methods to teach (ex.theochemtutor on youtube is great).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice professor who truly enjoys teaching. Tests are hard, but he doesn't write them, the physics department does. His lectures are straightforward and he explains things well. Uses iClicker most days so don't skip too many classes. Can be a little boring but he really knows his stuff.
Nice guy. He tries to help you out as best as he can. The physics department is trying to make you fail. I did not understand anything the entire semester, but the lab and pre-exams saved my grade.

Super smart and also personable guy. He also doesn't have much extra homework (like the textbook chapter quizzes from PHYS 1) and just leaves any extra work you might want to do out of class up to you. You can tell he's really interested in what he's teaching and in whether or not you actually understand it. Couldn't ask for a better PHYS 2 teacher
Super funny professor who cares about his students. Do the homework, go to lecture, do the pre-quizzes, and you will get a good grade.
Great lecturer and is very knowledgeable. Tests are difficult, but as long as you attend all of the lectures, labs, and do the homework, passing is basically guaranteed.

You can tell when someone really knows their stuff, and Khan knows his stuff. Utilized lots of clear diagrams and demonstrations to illustrate lecture topics. Very clear about formulas and how to derive them, but doesn't always get the chance to work out a full example problem, so it can be hard to understand *how* to use the formula. Great prof!!

Dr. Khan is the most caring, knowledgeable, and understanding professor. Everything he teaches just flows easily out of his mouth in such a way the you can understand and relate this new information. He received a standing ovation from his class when he finished his final lecture. I feel lucky and privileged to have been able to be in his class.

I absolutely love him as a teacher. He is enthusiastic about what he teaches and has a wonderful time doing it. One of the few professors that understands you are human. He talks about how he would rather you pay attention a little bit and zone in and out rather than give 100% focus and not understand what's going on. His jokes make it more fun.
Great guy who gives awesome lectures. Easy to get a hold of, and really cares about his students. Khan is one of the best professors I have ever had.
Great professor who will give awesome lectures.

Learn what equations to use for what problems. Make sure you have all the equations you need. Do the 2 quizzes before the test for the generous extra credit applied to the tests. Pay attention when he goes over the iclickers so you can get it right. Lectures were decent. He tries his best and wants his students to learn. Friendly and nice guy.
It is difficult to understand the lectures. I was able to pass the class but it wasn't because of him. I would never take the class again.
Great lectures and he kept them funny and engaging. He explains topics so that students can easily understand, if you have questions he will always answer them.

Khan gave amazing lectures and reviewed material from previous lectures at beginning of every class. Did experiments which was cool. Attend class, do iclickers and extra credit quizzes. These quizzes act like curves and help your average so much after exams. Impossible to fail if you complete all HW, labs, recitation and extra credit quizzes.

I found 2306 very difficult; Dr. Khan is very knowledgeable about the subject, but I felt that he didn't give us enough example problems applying the more difficult formulas. The tests and quizzes are also much more difficult than either the practice problems or the homeworks. That being said, the XC from the quizzes are very generous.

This is the guy you want if you take 2306. Lectures are kind of disorganized but look out for the equations. GO TO CLASS, iClicker is 12% of your grade, just go and get the points. Grading system is super favorable, I failed every single test and quiz by 15+ points and still passed the class.

Professor Khan makes it clear on day one that he cares for all his students. He will take time out of his day to answer questions and will leverage the rules on occasion to help his students. He jokes and does a lot of demonstrations during his lectures and is as enthusiastic as a kid on Christmas. He really knows and enjoys physics.
He was such a great physics professor. He made classes enjoyable and was overall a very nice funny guy.

He's such a nice guy, pretty funny too. His class format can be kind of disorganized but there's very generous extra credit and the tests were usually easier than the quizzes so it ends up alright. Lectures just felt like random information a lot of the time so some more context/organization would have been nice. Very kind if you have questions tho

He has a well-meaning, offbeat sense of humor. If you take the optional quizzes, study, do all your homework, go to labs & recitations, you'll do fine. Decent extra credit. From what I've gathered he's the best option for 2306, and I genuinely do enjoy his class & appreciate him for the way he tries to make his lectures as calming as possible.
Nice

This is an excellent professor! His lectures can be boring, but he takes time for students to understand the material. The tests weren't that hard and the optional quizzes really do help boost your test grade. If you struggled with PHYS 2305, then I wouldn't worry too much when taking PHYS 2306 with this professor.

TAKE FOR PHYSICS 2306!!! Super kind and helped me out a ton when I had personal issues, unlike a lot of professors. SHOW UP TO CLASSSSSSSSS the clicker questions add up so fast if you don't go ur grade could drop almost 12 percent. You'll be kicking yourself if you don't go.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Holy sh!t I loved this guy. I was so excited to go to my 9AM lectures every morning. He had an in-class demonstration almost every day and i was captivated every lecture despite my sleep deprivation. He's just one of those lecturers yk loves their job. Also, IClicker questions were worth 12% of the course grade, so make sure you attend every one.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Khan was great. I went to class every day for the clicker questions so be prepared for that. His lectures are great, he cares and makes class interesting every day. Quizzes can be hard, some easier than others but definitely study. Genuinely cares about his students' success. Would definitely recommend him for any physics class.
Dr. Khan is probably one of the best professors I've ever had, it's just a shame I suck with electronics and magnetism.

The rest of the reviews are pretty spot on. Khan knows exactly what he is doing and hes pretty funny too. His teaching style, writing on the board and doing examples, may not be the best for some people, but most students just read the textbook or PowerPoint anyway. I would say hes definitely the best Physics 2 teacher in the department.

He consistently has the highest test averages and the class is largely graded on dept curved tests. Goofy and fun guy that is usually clear. His notes can sometimes be jumbled or not make sense. Get textbook online. Mastering hw can be difficult. He is likely your best option if it fits your schedule. We were behind for recitation with an uncool TA
Very good lectures. He writes notes on the whiteboard that are easy to follow and he does practice problems during class. I would highly recommend Khan for 2306.
His lectures are great; he doesn't really go through the powerpoints, but rather explains the chapter using the whiteboards and provides great examples to what we're doing.

Almas is a great professor to have for lecture, despite the out of major Physics classes being pretty low quality. He does a good job at explaining some simple topics, but can skip over derivations and integrations that can leave you confused. He is funny, curves the class well, and makes lecture more engaging than most other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Almas Khan is the man. He makes studying Electromagnetism fun. I really enjoyed his class, and wish he taught higher level physics/engineering  classes.

Almas Khan is a very interesting and amazing professor! He will teach you not only physics but also knowledges from different areas because he has a  lot of stores. He may even influence your life if you try to talk with him often. I like him very much! By the way, Physics is always easy!

I think Khan is a fantastic Lecturer. Every lecture he is passionate about what he is talking about. He is also an all around good person. For example, he delayed our first homework assignment because he knew that everyone was too hungover from the first football game of the season. Amazing guy, would definitely recommend you take him.
He is a good teacher and curves fairly. If you don't do well, you need to steer clear of Facebook and Reddit OR you are terrible at physics

Dr. Khan is one of the better teachers teaching PHYS 2305. He explains the material well and he is very helpful when students ask him about a subject. His tests are only 12 multiple choice questions but are easy. He also curves if the average of a test is less than 75. I highly recommend taking him if Dr. Chang was not available.

Great Professor!  He was very nice and open to questions.  He made class enjoyable (or as enjoyable as physics can be).  Tests were very fair that the curves on the test were very nice.  Great experience and great teacher.  Will be requesting him for Phys 2306 as well.

Khan is extremely nice and always willing to help any of his students. He is also very fair and curves tests and adjusts the class based on how his students are doing. This semester was his first time teaching 2305 so he was not always the best at teaching the material. I think that when he gets more experience he will be a great teacher.

He is a great teacher. If you go to all the lectures/recitations and write down what he does you will do fine. He gives reviews before the test which are similar to the real thing and he curves. If you need any help, go to his office hours and he is glad to help you. I am taking him again next year for 2306.

Notes do not help on homework or tests given during lecture. He is a better 1 on 1 teacher than a lecture teacher but his office hours are scarce. It is better to teach yourself with the book and solution manual provided online for the homework problems.

Best part... Recitation is not mandatory. Worst part... He isn't really the best teacher. I found it easier to just teach myself the material from the book. He does curve tests and gives practice problems to help study
If you're not a systems thinker, good luck. For such a difficult class (first time learning ASM), she makes it a whole lot easier.
didn't do the greatest in 2505 (material was rough), but she genuinely is very caring and supportive. she responds quickly and makes you feel supported, not judged. id definitely take her again.

She's an alright professor; however, the lectures and practice tests don't strongly reflect on the tests. The classwork slides, lecture notes, and the practice test won't prepare you for the actual test. The final exam was designed for CS students to fail. Half of the exam was rarely covered or talked about much in depth.

idk why people think shes boring. She's nice and gets straight to the point in lecture and doesn't entertain "those" types of CS students mid-lecture. She is very willing to help her students and provide examples in and out of class about a subject. For exams, be sure you understand the concepts well. The practice test doesn't always sync up.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice and avaiable out of class if needed. Personally helped me a lot with material I struggled to understand. 2505 is just not organized well imo and notes are hard to comprehend if not in-class doing them. Be ready for difficult projects and exams. Lots of studying is needed and def recommend a study group.

The final is literally impossible to study for. Study all you want from the slides, practice quizzes or practice exams, it does not matter. She will manage to make a paper that will make you want to end your life. Walking back from the final I felt like being hit by a car would feel nicer.

This class emphasizes the importance of starting strong, but even then, her lectures only covered the basics. The tests reflected on the lectures, classwork, and projects so better aim for all A's and understand the material. Her practice material for finals didn't reflect on the actual final exam. I failed and have to retake it again for next sem.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I don't really understand all the hate, as Senger really does care and try to make sure her students understand the material. She's pretty young and did her undergrad at tech here too, so she knows what it's like. She takes the time to explain difficult concepts and if you pay attention, especially to examples, you will do well.
Her 8am classes were the worst and her lectures are long and didnt really learn anything from it i had to withdraw from the course
She is kind and does her best to be helpful, but the lectures can be pretty boring... partially due to the material though.

Prof. Senger is a very good lecturer, so make sure to take good notes. Homeworks help your understanding and determine a lot of the grade, but make sure you go to office hours! You won't understand the content without it. Take initiative (office hours) if you don't understand something--the course content is very weird and you can get lost easily.

Very kind professor. Her lectures are very boring, but if you lock in and take notes, they are very useful for the projects and exams at least in my experience. I will say that there were a lot of delays with assignment releases and grading. I don't think she is as bad as some of the reviews say, but definetly not the best.

Senger is one of the better 1114 professors. Considering 1114 is a weed-out class, it will be difficult, but Prof. Senger tries her best to make it as easy as possible. The work is a little difficult but the lectures and reading the course help a lot. I would consider her the best prof. for 1114 (def not Edwards)
Much better than the other CS 1114 professors especially Edwards. She is very caring and understanding to any life circumstances. Her lectures are also informative as far as lectures go.

REALLY GREAT PROFESSOR! Senger gives amazing advice and can answer EVERY question even the most poorly worded CS questions. CS 1114 is tough, but her office hours are a lifesaver! Her lectures are awesome, and she's so sweet. She's the perfect professor for this class and she's never condescending.

Professor herself was very nice. Lectures aren't required but may be helpful if you just started programming. The course itself is difficult because it's a weed-out class. The main content of the class is from the weekly readings, lectures are just a bonus if you need more help. Labs are okay but the later programs are what kill people.

She's a fine professor, she is passionate but the course was created by Dr. Edwards and it is not a good course. CS 1114 is not a good course that is supposed to be an introductory course but what a lot of your grade counts for is not helpful to your learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Time consuming projects, bad queues, weren't given project 1 for a month or 2 and after that it all snowballed, we only had a week for Project 4 binary bomb.

Midterm and final avg really low too along with final exam, barely any curve. Professor made too many excuses during lecture on why something wasn't uploaded yet, all around unfun experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was an amazing teacher for CS1114 when I took her but for CS2505 I will never ever suggest her. I dont think anything in the lectures that were taught to us was used in the projects or the tests that we were expected to get good grades on. Everything is super hard in the class when its Professor Senger!!!

She barely graded anything until the last two weeks of the semester, so you didn't know your actual grade until the last week of the semester. The final was impossibly hard, and tanked my grade a whole 10%. Material on the final was barely anything covered in the lectures. Barely gives usable feedback, and so boring in lecture.

First of all this class is extremely difficult for many people that have never coded before and the course is designed to mostly be self-taught.  However, Allyson tries her best to explain what is in the reading activities during 45 minutes of lecture time in a clear and understandable way.  She is also a very nice and friendly person.

I really enjoyed having her! Her lectures explained concepts clearly, and I could tell that she enjoyed teaching. She's really nice, which is a breath of fresh air in the CS department. Also, she wasn't condescending when I asked her questions and would thoroughly explain her answers, so it made her seem very approachable. Highly recommend!

For lectures she read the weekly readings we needed to do ourselves to the class, so I got by teaching myself the material. The quizzes were heavily weighted for this class, although I don't think they're an accurate measurement of one's ability to write code or understand this class's content.

She is definitely the best chem professor in the department. Her lectures are really easy to follow and she gives a lot of examples and example problems in class to clarify tough subjects. Shes super nice too, though she is a no BS professor. Get ready to do a lot of Aleks homeworks.
Great professor and really cared about students
Great chem teacher! She explained things very well and was always willing to help or explain something. Need to study for the tests and do practice problems
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved having her as my professor. I am usually pretty bad at chemistry, but Dr. Arachchige helped me a lot. She takes complex topics and makes them understandable.

Genuinely one of the sweetest professors I've had. Cares about your learning and is very firm in her expectations when it comes to her students. Available for office hours and shows no bias against students who don't come all the time. All questions are treated equally and despite her qualifications, she will never make you feel bad.

Great professor, her lectures were really helpful and easy to follow. Only annoying thing is the iclicker but she drops your 6 lowest days so that's nice. As long as you do your homework and pay attention to your lectures, and practice, you should do decent in her class.
she was amazing!! lectures are clear, uploads all notes, and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. take her class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Arachchige was very helpful and caring. I liked how she based her lectures completely off of her notes, which made it easy to follow along and understand things. She would also give good demos/visuals to better understand concepts.

Amazing professor and knows what she is taking about. Dr. A is very passionate about both teaching and helping you succeed, as long as you make the effort to reach out outside of class/office hours. iClickers make attendance mandatory, but video lectures are usually provided.

Professor Arachchige is pretty good at what she does. She understands what she is teaching and does a good job of explaining and conveying the lessons. Exams suck because they are all at night. Attendance is mandatory because she uses the iClicker to ask questions.

I liked this professor, she seemed to truly care about our performances and tried to help us throughout. Her lectures were good, and tests were hard. I was surprised with how much harder tests 3 and 4 were, so be ready for that. Overall good professor though!

Dr. Arachchige is an amazing chem professor! Her lectures are extremely helpful as she covers the topic itself and problems relating to each topic. She also includes demonstrations in some lectures, like combustions and reactions that produce light or fire, which keeps her lectures very entertaining. Overall, I would definitely recommend her!

Dr. Arachchige is a very good professor overall. She does an excellent job at explaining why we need to know certain concepts in lecture. I recommend going to class as often as you can, as reviewing notes is one of the best ways to study for this course. I also highly recommend taking CHEM 1034 for extra review and better understanding of material.

Dr. Arachchige is a very good professor who explains concepts very well.  In class, she goes through the topics in depth to not just tell the information, but to teach it.  I highly recommend her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Be prepared to study a lot, but Dr. Arachchige gave great tips on how to study for exams and do well in the class.

You have to buy a physical iclicker for this class which kinda sucks but the iclicker is an easy grade since she tells you the right answer and only really uses it for attendance. She's overall a great teacher but the course itself is pretty difficult with a lot of studying no matter the professor.

Absolutely amazing professor. Really makes class engaging by doing experiments and clearly explaining concepts, she was always there to help me if I was struggling or didn't understand a concept. If you are nervous about Chemistry at VT, take Dr. Arachchige as she also provides many study materials.
Tips: Study hard, GO TO CLASS, go to her TA hours

Her lectures were very detailed and explained everything you needed to know. The slides she used were also very helpful. Definitely attend lectures, as there's going to be graded questions pretty much every lecture, and generally she's much better at explaining topics than the textbook.
Great lecturer. Just make sure you go to ever class or you will fall behind.

She is willing to help her students and wants them too succeed in class. She did fun experiments in class that made the lectures entertaining and effective. There's a lot of opportunity to boost your grade in the class through iClicker questions and unlimited homework attempts.
Professor Arachchige makes it easy to do well on tests because she provides provides slides you can fill out along with the lectures in class, practice sheets, and explains the concepts well.
Pretty good prof but she doesn't update grades on canvas so you kinda need to rely on yourself. GO to every class if you arent good at chem.
probably the best gen chem teacher, super detailed lectures and all of her practices were exactly like the tests, she covers everything you will need to know.

She is a great professor. Ms. Arachchige was the highlight of my semester. She made my classes easy to take in and also gave us very useful tips for our midterms. I did not have a good attendance score in this class, but attendance in her classes is really important. So go to her classes.
She was great! probably the best gen chem professor at VT

Dr. Arachichge had amazing lecture slides and her exams were fair. Acids/bases (Test 3) was a really hard unit but her lecture slides were very clear with expectations and I thought it was easier than CHEM 1035. Overall very helpful during office hours and very sweet.
She is an incredible professor!! Take her if you can. VT in general has a good chemistry department.

I had Arachchige for both 1035 &1036 and she is great! I highly recommend her; She is a great lecturer, is very accessible for office hours, and has a great personality. Show up to class, do the worksheets and homework, and always ask her questions. I did not think 1036 was worse than 1035. Also, her finals are also much easier than the midterms.

She overcomplicates some of the topics and doesn't make her lectures very engaging. It can also be hard to follow her example problems when she uses multiple slides and just says "from the previous slide". She is condescending in office hours and mentions how we had "learned this in class" when you have a question on a topic. I wish I took Bowen.

I found that CHEM 1036 was a good bit harder than 1035. Personally, I don't find the lectures very helpful but the homework, problem solving studio, and practice tests are sufficient. My advice is to focus a good amount of your effort on the recitation problems, since those are what will be on tests and the TA will help you figure out how to do it.

Chem1036 material was so much worse than 1035 and the curriculum is all over the place and complicated. But Arachchige does a good job of explaining it well, very friendly. Had her for 1035 and 1036, wish I could have her for Organic Chemistry.

Dr. Arachchige teaches decently, but the class is not set up for success. While she covers the material, the exams will have questions you have not seen before, and exams are the majority of your grade. This is universal for CHEM 1036, so I would still take it with her since she can explain well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a good professor. The tests can be hard because they're only 30 questions with no partial credit. This can make it harder to get A's on tests, which make up a huge portion of your grade. However, her lectures are detailed and she's good at explaining the material. She uses visual representations a lot which help class engagement
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Overall, wasn't a bad teacher- she goes fast sometimes and really slow other times. If you have taken AP chem, this class isn't too bad. Tests are the same for all CHEM 1036.

She is super sassy and rude though. Treated the TA poorly and didn't care much about individual needs. Definitely has favorites, so, if possible, become one.

I loved Dr Arachchige she was very clear about course expectations and lectures. I would say she was the best chem professor and I would totally take this course with her again. There are iclicker questions in class that are graded but super easy and she gives you the answers basically. Tests were very related to her lectures and homework.

Chem 1036 is challenging, but Professor Arachchige makes it manageable. Attend lectures, use the recorded videos, and leverage tools like Unstuck ai to excel. She genuinely cares and will help you succeed.

The practice tests are significantly easier than the actual exams. Test averages in the 70-80 range. The final exam is much easier than the midterms. Attendance is a large portion of final grade, so do not miss class often

Arachchige was a great professor for this class. Explaining everything well. The examples that she did in class while explaining were very similar to the questions on the test, practice tests were identical. Got a 76 on first test, 90's on all other tests, got an A- in class. Chem1035 in general wasn't as bad as people said, just practice.

The great thing about chem 1035 with Dr. A is that you can learn the content in many ways. Her lectures are very engaging, but if you don't understand them then the homework and practice problems help as well. If you still don't understand, you can read the textbook. Do the practice tests and you should do fine on the tests. I reccomend1034 tooo.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Arachchige truly cares about all of her students & their success! She has a lot of office hours and her lectures make material clear. Just make sure to actually attend the lectures and do all of the homework because it truly does help in the end. Also, she provides practice tests that are usually somewhat similair to the exam.
Great class. Don't schedule it early as attendance is crucial and can make/break your grade.

Professor Arachchige will pay special attention to any student who asks her for help individually. While she is a very intense individual most of the time, I would still recommend going to her office hours and getting to know her.

The class is NOT EASY. Be prepared to struggle. I spent a lot of time outside of class reteaching myself material.

Best chemistry professor. Her office hours carried me. Go to class and get iClicker points (I didn't and regret it). The tests can be challenging and you have to go into it knowing more than you think (for conceptual questions especially). ALEKS can be annoying so go to her with any and all questions!
Amazing professor! She explains topics thoroughly and in a way that is easy to understand.

Dr. Arachchige is THE CHEM1035 professor. She is incredibly well-spoken, explains topics well, and you can tell how knowledgeable she is in the subject. I can't recommend her enough, and will be taking CHEM1036 with her next semester!

Even though I did poorly in her class and ended up withdrawing, she was an amazing teacher. My grade in the class was due to my own work ethic not her teaching. She always makes the best jokes in class that make everyone laugh. Chemistry is hard but if you are willing to put in the work her class will be a right fit for you.

She explains all the material very well, and I found it very easy to follow along with all the topics. It can be hard to focus when in such a large lecture hall but taking notes and sitting the front half helps a ton. Study hard for the test using multiple tools. She even does some cool experiments in class that help explain the concepts.

Dr. Arachchige is one of the best professors I've ever had! She's passionate about chemistry and explains things extremely well. She also provides students with numerous resources that can be utilized outside of class (a major one beings ALEKS). As long as you pay attention during her lectures and keep up with the homework, you'll do great.
Very poor teaching and extremely tough grader
Very unclear and hides final grades

Great professor and would definitely take her again. She cares about her students and is easy to understand. The tests can be a bit difficult but as long as you go to office hours, study and do the ALEKS assignments you would pass. Test are similar to the homework questions so it'll be advisable to do them again a couple of times before the test.
Chemistry can be hard but Dr.Arachige does a very good job at teaching the concepts, she also makes herself very available and provides many resources.

Dr. Arachchige is a phenomenal professor. She has office hours throughout the week to answer questions, go over questions you might've missed on the test, and more. It's very important to pay attention in class and to go to lectures to get iClicker points.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Does a really good job with in-class demonstrations

Dr. Arachchige's lectures are clear and extremely helpful. Chem 1036 is a difficult class but if you're willing to pay attention in class and study a lot outside of class you can achieve a good grade. Make use of her office hours! She is a very caring professor who is always willing to explain concepts and problems that you don't understand.

I took Dr.Arachchige for Chem 1035 and 1036. The tests/assignments are the same regardless of your professor so the rating really comes down to how well they teach. Dr.Arachchige overcomplicates the material SO badly and her lectures do not make sense. I had to teach myself the entire class.

Chem is hard. The chem department SUCKS. However Arachchige knows the content well, and her lectures are helpful. She cares and will try to help you do well. In my opinion out off all the gen chem professors she is the hardest. Go to lecture and rewatch lecture videos. Good luck

Dr. Arachige is really great at what she does. I had a different chemistry professor last semester and she really made the difference in my grade. She has taught me how to study in not only chemistry but all of my college classes. I cannot recommend her enough!!

Dr. A is an amazing teacher! The tests are hard and this is made to be a weed out class, but if you put the time and effort into studying you will to fine. I took 1035/36 with her and had loads of success. Listen to how she tells you to study because she makes the tests and knows what is best to succeed. You can tell she loves her job and cares!
Dr. Arachchige cares for her students and is easy to connect with. Her courses are test-heavy, but you will see that universally in the VT chemistry department.
Dr. Arachchge is a fine teacher. She provides multiple resources for her students and is accesible. Great lecture outlines. She records her lectures in case someone wanted to review later.

You have to buy an online access code and/or textbook to the HW (3-4/wk)
Captivating useful lectures
Attendance is taken using easy Do Now quizzes 
You can repeat the HW until you get 100%
All hw/tests are multiple choice due to class size
She prefers students write rather than type notes
Excellent at communicating complex topics
I 100% Recommend

Congratulations, If you're reading this you got the best Gen Chem 1 Professor, and I'm happy for you. Arachchige is a great lecturer and makes the tests the entire department uses so she basically prepares you for what you need, unlike others who give fluff. You have the best professor: get that A

Dr. Arachchige is a wonderful professor! She truly wants her students to succeed. Her lectures are very helpful, pay attention to them!! I also highly recommend attending her office hours often. You will have to put effort in to earn a good grade, but the resources are there if you choose to use them (take the practice tests!).

One of the best chem professors out there. I will say, I found chem itself hard and she really does her best to provide a lot of resources and information for help sessions so make sure to talk to her if you're struggling! I would say this class is difficult, but due to my schedule it was hard to manage but she makes it a tad easier though!
Professor Arachchige is the best of the gen chem professors. She does a lot of demonstrations in class to show what she is talking about and she clearly cares what she lectures on.

Dr. Arachchige was a great teacher overall. However, I put in so many hours studying for this class and still did not get the grade I wanted. I studied and did work for this class every single day, and even took the recitation class with it. I got A's on all of the practice tests. I did not do well on any of the tests and it makes no sense.

OMG the best professor in the Chem department! I came in scared from high school chem and honestly expected to drop the class but was able to pass both semesters with Dr. Arachchige! Chemistry in general requires a lot of work, but she lays out what you need to do to pass. She also records all her lectures and holds multiple office hours.

Great teacher who thoroughly understood the content that was presented. She definitely knew what she was doing. Tried to make class entertaining with experiments and would go through the problems on screen when concepts are initially introduced. Don't be intimidated by class size, she uses a microphone and smaller screens for those in the back.

while 1035 n 1036 definitely are not easy classes, she is great at explaining during lectures and quite engaging too.  But my favorite thing about her is that despite the hundreds of students she has, if she meets with you individually she will remember you and genuinely shows interest in how you're doing in the class.  You can really tell she care

Dr. Arachchige is very good at teaching this course and gives great lectures. I would definitely recommend her class to anyone taking Chem 1036. She makes this very challenging course enjoyable and is a lively presence to see throughout the week.

Coming into Chem 1035/45 as a CS major, I had no idea that I would grow to love them so much the past two semester. I credit this to Dr. Arachchige and her evident passion for the field and the quality of education of her students. She has been the most influential teacher for me since probably elementary school.

I struggled a lot in 1036, but I think that if I didn't have her as my prof I would have failed. She really does care about how her students perform on the exams. There are multiple opportunities to reach out for help in her class, whether it's her office hours or TAs, who were also very helpful. If you think chem will be hard for you, take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely ADORED Arachige. She is an inspiration and I wish I could take her again for Ochem. Granted I'm not done with the semester yet, but she is by far the best professor I've ever had because of the way she teaches and her availability. Some exams definitely tripped me up, but overall it wasn't a super hard class.

Although Chem 1036 is difficult, my grades between chem 1035 and 1036 increased, which I credit in part to Dr. Arachchige. She wants her students to succeed, and is very helpful. Her lectures are engaging.
Lectures were kinda boring, found myself doing other things. Easy to learn material on your own with the text book and connect assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's one of my fav professors by far. The class is going to be difficult for most, but she simplifies it down to what needs to be taught and is effective in reiterating the info you need to know. Take her advice on how to succeed in the class and you will. Aside from her teaching, I adore her-- you can tell she's intelligent and loves her job.
She is extremely sweet and makes the lectures very understandable. Idk about other profs in comparison but I would recommend Arachchige for sure.
Professor Arachchige is a great professor. She makes the difficult subject of chemistry seem simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best professor for chemistry. Our class had the highest class average because of her, and definitely recommend.

Dr.Arachchige made gen chem an easy A. Her lectures are so amazing t hat I didn't even have to read the textbook which goes more in depth. She also helps you sometimes with the iclicker questions. She also posts recordings of her lectures online. Make sure you give yourself time to do all the homeworks before the test so you can study more.

I feel lucky to have gotten her for Chem 1035. She tries her best to make her lectures interesting, and sometimes does a short, interesting chemistry experiment to keep the class engaged. There is a good amount of homework, but I haven't heard anyone complain about it because the homework she assigns is actually really good review for the tests.

Professor Shamindri is great. Her lectures were great and easy. Going over the class outlines is enough for the exams. Her class involves iclicker questions so attendance is mandatory. Make sure to go to her office hours as well as your TAs. There is a lot of homework but you get unlimited attempts for them so you can easily get a 100 on that.

Professor Arachchige is amazing. Her classes are engaging and they are never boring. She does an excellent job at digesting difficult material into something which is easily understood and doesn't move too fast. Do the connects and practice tests, and exams are easy. She is a great professor and I'm glad to be taking her for 1036 next semester!

As long as you do the homework and pay attention in class, chem 1035 is an easy A. Her lectures are very helpful and go over all of the needed content. From time to time I would read the textbook to clarify things I missed in class, but you could definitely get by with never reading it. Would take again for sure.

Professor Arachchige is great! Class consists of mostly lectures and I-clicker questions, so don't skip too much! She tells you what you need to memorize for tests. In addition, her and her TAs have a ton of office hours. I really enjoyed her class. It is not the easiest class, but if you study and do the review, it's not bad.
Great prof for chem 1035, super helpful, and always clarified what was necessary to know for tests.
Arachchige is probably the best Chem 1035 professor. If you pay attention in lectures and do all of the homework, you will be prepared for tests and can expect to finish with at least a B.

The course does have a textbook, but Dr. Arachchige does not require you to use it. You won't know your grade in the class until the very end of the semester, unless you calculate it yourself. There is a lot of homework, almost every night, but it is easy to do it quickly and get an 100.

Shows lots of care for students, lectures are clear and informative and lots of reinforcing homework and extra practice is made available. Show up to class, complete the mandatory homework and recommended assignments, and you will be just fine. Dr. Arachchige is an amazing professor, would definitely take her course again.

She's a really good professor! The fact that there's a lot of homework is just what comes with chem, it doesn't have anything to do with her. Reading the textbook helps clarify things, but she goes over almost all the material in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chem 1035 is a very difficult and it seems as if the whole the Chem Department wants you to fail. However Arachchige is a very good professor. The lectures are well organized with a lot of example problems. If you have to take chem 1035 I highly recommend Arachchige as you will actually learn.

She does a great job at explaining difficult chemistry concepts. It is a relatively hard class, but she walks you through how to do problems that are on the tests and she explains it well. She also does real chemical reactions in class sometimes, which are always fun to watch.
There is going to be lots of homework, but that is department wide. Going to lectures and paying attention sets you up to do well on the homework which in turn sets you up to do well on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had never taken Chem lab before this and Dr.Arachchige made the transition super easy. Her pre-lab videos were extremely helpful, she was straightforward with what she was looking for in the pre and post labs in her rubrics and she answered all questions and was patient with me during office hours. 10/10 !
good

If it wasn't for Dr. Arachichige , I probably would not have the level of understanding of chemistry that I do now. As someone who really hates chemistry, she made the class tolerable, and her demonstrations were interesting. She tells you exactly what you need to do to get an A. Overall great professor, you can't go wrong with her.
Dr. Arachchige was great. She broke down steps and conveyed the material clearly. Do all the practice that she suggests and the class is easy.

Dr. Arachchige is a very solid choice for a professor. She is very good at what she is teaching and she is easily accessible. She has an accent which makes her look intimidating but she isnt and the lectures actually help with the homework and if you can solve the homework then the tests are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Arachchige was an excellent instructor with concise lectures and very clear explanations. She covered the content thoroughly and was always available to help.

reviews.comment: I found her to be clear professor and through in her explanations for each unit. However, I honestly was a bit intimidated to go and talk to her outside of class for help on some of the problems that we went over in class. I do think that she gave adequate practice material to prepare for the tests though.

Dr. Arachchige is a very sweet lady. She teaches well, and she is a solid professor. I think I could have gotten a better grade if I would have gone to her office hours or talked to her outside of class. She is very accessible and clearly wants her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Arachchige is a solid teacher. Her lectures are very well put together and informative. The ultimate key is to simply go to class and take decent notes. Also, taking the practice tests before each unit test is super helpful.

Dr. Arachchige explained the material very well and articulated exactly how to do each type of problem. She is very clear about what to expect on the tests. Go to class, pay attention, take the practice tests, and you'll be just fine. The class is all lecture and can get dull sometimes, but that's more a function of the class than the professor.

Honestly, one of the best chemistry professors at tech. She explains the material very well, and has lecture pre-recorded lectures in case you missed a day. There's quite a lot of homework but its very helpful! Always wants to make sure you know the material and are ready for tests. Would love to have her again as a professor!!!

She was one of the best professors I've ever had. Very lecture heavy however if you prepare like she says to, it's easy. Lots of homework but mainly for participation. Reading the textbook is vital and it makes it so much easier. It's an easy class if you show up and pay attention. She was super helpful and I'd love to have her as a professor again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Arachchige is very helpful. She explains material in a simple manner and shows how to work problems step by step.

Dr. Arachchige truly wanted her students to succeed, but in my opinion, the lectures she provided didnt allow students to fully comprehend the material. The key to this class is doing problems over and over again. If you go to her office hours, she will help you with a process, but most of the time, there was a less complicated approach.

I loved Professor Arachchige! She knew exactly what she was talking about and was always extremely helpful. It is chemistry though so it is definitely not easy but if you have to take it then take it with her. One of the best chem professors at Tech by far!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do everything she tells you to do and it is an easy A. Watch the lecture videos.
Lays down exactly what you need to do. Attend class, do extra practice, do textbook problems and dont miss any homework.
Exams are hard. But she provides lots of resources to help you succeed. Really helpful lecture notes. Watch the lecture recordings before you come to class and do extra practice to get an easy B.
Do not take her. This is the worst class I have ever taken. For some reason tech and Shamindri insisted on making this class impossible to weed out students. Why? Who knows! Stay away!

Dr. Arachchige is a good professor. She posts lecture videos that must be viewed before class and does lots of extra practice problems in class. Goes fast, but that is normal for a college chem class. Have to put in a lot of work to do well.
Lots of homework. Lecture recordings available. synchronous class meetings.
Does not answer questions or allow to ask for help on things. Very difficult to communicate with.
