If you did well in Bus Calc you should be fine. This class is self paced and Clark organizes material really well. Her lectures were straightforward for the most part and doing CPs are fine if you have reliable teammates. Its nice to check answers! She offers office hours and quizzes are similar to the work done in CPs. Nice to have discipline.

Entirely asynchronous class. 2 assignments are due every week, with a longer quiz/test every other week. 6 quizzes total, one final, and 18 mini-assignments worth 2 points each. One quiz is dropped and 10 assignments are too. About 1-1.5 hours of videos to watch in order to do the lecture notes and quizzes each week. Available for office hours.

She is an amazing lecturer with a VERY organized class structure. There was more than adequate time to finish the "quizzes" (basically midterms). You just had to put in the time to study, which I don't think the negative reviewers here bothered to do. Stay on top of the deadlines and don't cram everything in one night, and this class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She makes this class very challenging due to the nature of the class being completely asynchronous. If you want to do well, you have to write notes from scratch, go to office hours, and be insanely organized. But even with that, I feel she gives us not enough time to complete the "quizzes," which are basically midterms, and you got 6 of them :)

You do learn a lot with her, but you do have to put in a lot of effort to do well. Her video lectures are long and boring, plus her speaking voice is kinda annoying. She is not bad per se, its just you're pretty much on your own with this course, its asynchronous after all.

This class requires you to study and be on top of deadlines. I hate how Clark gives us 75 minutes to do a quiz(exam) as that's not enough time to finish the test thoroughly. Its just annoying as I'm not a BIT major, and to know that the other professors allow you to do their tests with open internet and Excel frustrates me to this day.

Professor Clark is definitely the hardest 3414 professor at Tech. If you're bad at managing your time, whether it's getting the CPs done on time or completing an exam, don't take this class. Granted you do learn a lot with her, plus she does give extra credit in the form of completing a SPOT Survey.

If your at Tech, try not to choose Clark for 3414, because her class is a whole different ball game compared to the other professors. Her tests are under lockdown browser and include a lot of information. Plus you pretty much have to motivate yourself to watch the lectures and be on top of all the assignments, which there are a lot of them.

This class definitely requires you to study in order to understand the CP's and her exams. The CP's can sometimes vary from there exams and it is so hard to study for this class, especially the final, because there is at least 50+ things to know. Wouldn't take this class again.

This class is extremely difficult. The CP assignments do not prepare you for the quizzes that make up most of your grade. There is also not enough time to complete the quizzes. Try to avoid taking this class.

Clark's canvas is very organized and well structured. Her videos and CPs are also very helpful in both learning and studying the content. I just wish she gives us more time on the exams, as they're long and can be math heavy. Not a bad class at all, but you have to manage your time and stay diligent if you want to do well.

Great format and organization of Canvas, but there was NOT enough time to complete quizzes that are mostly equation/math heavy. Also knowing that last years class had not only more time but no lockdown browser is unfair in my opinion.

After switching to her asynchronous class after an issue with my previous professor, my grade in the class immediately skyrocketed.  The CP exercises are designed to help you actually learn the subject matter, and it is done almost flawlessly.  Her video lectures are to the point, but also very descriptive.  Consider yourself lucky if you have her.

Required us to buy a textbook but the textbook wasn't even needed. The majority of the notes are from her personal lecture videos that take a long time to complete. I'm just mad that she even had us buy a textbook. DO NOT BUY IT!

I wish I could redo a spot survey because her final exam was ridiculously difficult. Literally picked the longest hardest questions from the CPs that require 1000 steps to do. Absolutely criminal. Even with two hours it was just not enough time to do everything and do it correctly. She truly wants her students to fail and it shows.

Super easy class if do the work on time. Watch the videos. do the CPs, then do the quizzes. She drops like six of your lowest CPs and then drops your lowest Quiz as well. Very easy class, very easy professor.

Apparently unpopular opinion - I wasn't the biggest fan of Prof Clark. She makes an easy class a lot harder than it needs to be. It almost seems like she just makes up a lot of the charts and formulas although I hope that's not the case. They're just difficult to understand and the video lectures don't line up with the CPs as well as they could.
Really easy and straightforward class, watch the videos and do the CPs and you will do completely fine on the quizzes.
Quizzes are basically exams, the content isn't too bad but it does take some work to do well. She gives a lot of structure and notes so as long as you go over that, you can do well.

Professor Clark is an amazing professor. Had her for BIT 3414 last semester and everything is straight forward. The class is definitely lecture heavy, and you don't want to miss class. That being said, her grade system is also straight forward and allows for leeway. If you're willing to dedicate the time needed for this class, it is not hard at all

clark made class easy to learn, she drops so many hws and participation grades. if you go to class and focus youll be fine to pass, make sure you do the reading Qs & quiz review practices bc they are similar to the actual quizzes.

She is by far the best professor I have had at VT yet. She gives you everything you need to be prepared for each class, and takes every class at a good pace, giving time to practice material and ask questions. The homework genuinely prepares you for the 6 quizzes given (1 dropped). You have to go to class to do well, but class is interactive.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Quizzes every 2 weeks, which are basically exams. Lots of in-class participation but it helps you. You definitely have to study and practice the material a lot to get a good grade but she doesn't give surprises on the tests. Overall, she is a good professor but if you aren't going to put in the effort, your grade will reflect it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE CLARK. Yes, she does give outline notes and its not a difficult class if you go to class and follow along. My grandfather passed away in the middle of the semester and she was not understanding at all about helping me make up missed class from attending his funeral.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: To those giving her a bad grade, it's obvious who watched videos and actually did the practices. She's very clear in her videos if you go along and fill in the notes. Additionally, all her quizzes are literally the same questions as the practice, just different numbers. She's rough with the tight timing, but overall, one of the better Professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor. The assignments due twice a week can be a lot with quizzes due about every other week. Quizzes are straight forward but are tricky with the time limit. Not a fan of calculating my own grade due to the chance of error. Overall, the class wasn't hard but required a decent amount of work for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: avoid like the plague
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She really helps you out if you need it, it's a math heavy class so if you're not good at math, make sure you actually pay attention in class and ask for help. Lectures are super dry at times, especially if you don't care about the class content, but she's such a great help and good at teaching that it balances out
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Clark gives you notes to fill in and a class assignment each class. Use these materials and the assigned readings to study and you'll do just fine. There are no exams, just a final and 6 quizzes. The quizzes are basically exams, 20-40 questions each, but 2 get dropped. Really hard to not pass this class.

3414 with Clark was unlike any other class I've taken at Virginia Tech. She creates "outlines" as notes and asks that you print them out and fill them out in class. If you don't go to class, you will do HORRIBLE in this class. None of her notes that are given in class are posted online. If you go to class and make an effort, you will succeed!

Dr. Clark is the best teacher that I've ever had at Virginia Tech.  Extremely helpful, always willing to answer any questions, material is difficult but she makes everything crystal clear.  Go to Class with the notes printed out and write everything down that she writes down on the notes.  TAKE HER FOR BIT 3414!
dr. clark is a great teacher and gives you everything you need to do well. print out the powerpoint slides, go to class and write down everything that she puts on the board and you should do great.
She was a wonderul teacher and helped me out a lot. I went to her office hours and she spent time with me going over my test. She helped me get an A on my second test. I really recommend her!

Dr. Clark is the best professor I have ever had. She comes to class prepared and her notes are very organized. Your grade is only based on quizzes and tests. The quizzes are only 4 points so you have to do well on them. But if you review the notes thoroughly the quizzes and tests will be easy. I only used the book once to review a part.

I have to disagree with 2 people above me. If you actually attend her lectures, there is no way you think her quizzes and tests are hard. It's straightforward unless you skip classes all the time and never do readings. If you did attend every lecture, took notes, read pages assigned to read, but fail quizzes and tests... you must drop the class.
STRUCTURED WELL, MANY EXTRA CREDITS,
No Comments

I agree with the other post.Quizzes are fairly easy,but the exams are excessively difficult.  She is very vague about material that will be included on exams and the questions on the exams are more difficult than the quantitative review. She is organized and classes are structured well, but her notes (PP slides) are again vague.Attendance suggested
Class seemed easy; however, tests, quizes, and homework were way harder then notes.  The book was not used so there were no other materials to reference to.

I actively avoided talking to her the whole semester, and my mental health was much better for it. The few times I did talk to her, she was presumptuous, assumed I did no work for my group, and didn't answer my question. You will spend hours reading and doing one assignment to receive an okay grade. Don't take her if you have the option.

reviews.comment: She is good at her job but she will be stern with you just do your work she's not a 1.

Do leave huge amount of time for this course, there are tones of millions of homework after every lecture and takes at least an hour for most of the quiz. You have to be very detailed on the homework if you care your grade. She doesn't open the grade calculation on canvas.

reviews.comment: A very mean professor. There is lots of time consuming quizzes and HW. I have never seen any professor send out an email two weeks before the semester to let the students be prepared.

She replaces half the classes with group work case studies. So you get half the time to learn the same material as the other sections. There is an insane amount of HW so never expect to have free time on Fridays or Tuesdays. The HW builds on itself, so if you miss one assignment, you will fail the next. She sends out an insane amount of email spam.

The class is awesome, I enjoyed the projects so much in fact that I switched from EE to CPE. However, Dr. Cooper and the TAs have feedback issues. Questions are ignored, or you will be sent to arbitrary documents that will not help at all. The material covered in the class is easy, so feedback is not very necessary, but it must be improved.

She is god's worst punishment for the terrible things I've done in the past. One of the guys once corrected her for something she solved wrong, after she fixed it she told him “are you happy now?”. She's rude, she thinks she's better than you, will look down on you if you ever ask for help, if you wonder if she at least teaches well, she doesn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Halfway through the year she started introducing these ridiculous in class questions that were impossible if you so much as looked away to for moment, for them she would go over a slide and in the last 2 seconds before going to the next say something like "That was question 4 btw". Eventually I just had my iPad record what she said.

My favorite class so far at tech. Material can be challenging sometimes due to the pace but just ask questions on the discord office hours and you will be successful. Dr.Cooper can be rude but she is an excellent lecturer and tells you what to do. She literally designed the course. Don't take this class for granted!

The class is challenging, but she is a GREAT professor! The hate that comes is because of how hard the class is. (I could've scored higher if I didn't have family complications) She is pretty understanding if you talk to her. She has in-person, Discord office hours and Q&A Fridays, if I remember correctly. Overall, she wants to see u WIN!!

I think that cooper is over hated due to the difficulty of the course. Lectures are long, but very informative, and she posts them with notes to canvas.  Projects specs are very clear on what to do and what not to do. Many places where her and her team are accessible outside of class. Overall, I think she did a good job with a hard class.

reviews.comment: I didn't interact with her and course team a lot but when I did she answered all my questions pretty nicely.

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is a very tough teacher and digital systems is overall a tough class. However, electrical engineering is not supposed to be easy to achieve. Most people who complain about this class are not willing to work for their degree/grade. Dr. Cooper is understanding if you are willing to learn. This class is a lot of work, but it is doable.

If you want a quiz after every class, go ahead and take her. She is very condescending and not helpful during office hours. The discord ta's are by far the most helpful and will get you through the class.

This class is truly something you can't do passively, you need full attention and honestly strive for a complete understanding. This class will push you to your limits, and it all builds, but at the end if you can stick it out, you won't regret it.

Decent teacher, very condescending to students, I learned a lot from the class. Steep learning curve and the start of the semester can drag you DOWN. Be prepared to spend hours on projects. reviews.comment: Hands down the most difficult course I have taken at Tech. Utilize her online office hours (ran by the TAs), start on the Learning Experiences early, and be prepared to receive no sympathy / help from Cooper. If you mess up, she will blame you and refer you to her syllabus. Additionally, make sure to get a good partner, it helps a lot.

i think shes a good teacher however this class is a lot of work. people sometimes think that it is because of her however i just think the class material itself is hard. 

please study and start early and go to office hours - she will be helpful. 

good teacher, sometimes kind of funny!

I don't get the issue with Dr. Cooper, very effective lecturer and teacher and is very clear on what is expected of you. Again, she's not a bad professor by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very tough class in general don't go in looking for an easy A. She is an amazing lecturer and explains the material really well. In class case study are extremely helpful for the projects throughout the semester. Lastly, don't get behind and try to stay on top of projects.
Many people don't like the class, but she's awesome, and I will die on this hill.

Do not self-advocate in any of Kristie's classes. at the very best, you will receive no further credit than you were given. At the very worst, you will have points further reduced. This has happened to me. With respect to 2544, spend as much time as you can on assignments as soon as they drop, because they are filled with needless busywork.

The least helpful and most condescending teacher I've ever gone to for help outside of class. I've heard she tends to be more respectful towards women, but I don't know for sure. Lectures are fine. Workload will take up all your free time, but it is manageable if started early. The Discord office hours are infinitely more helpful than hers.

She is a mess. Gives you a lot of time-consuming work. Gives a quiz at the end of each class. Lashes out at people who ask questions. Is the definition of a 🤓👆um akshully. At least the TAs are good and helpful. She needs to retire!

Worst professor I've ever taken. She acts like any small question is a huge favor or gives a rude response. She demands high courtesy but offers none. Her syllabus and grading are overly complicated, yet you still lose points without clarity. Everything feels designed to be inconvenient. She refuses to help or clarify instructions, DO NOT TAKE HER.

Kristie Cooper needs to retire already. If you are interested in having a quiz virtually every class, want to stay up all night completing her multiple LE assignments, and are generally interested in losing your sanity, take her class! It is so clear that she has favorite students and make sure to worship the TA or else you are screwed.

I had to work HARD to get an A in this class. Cooper always rude and never answered questions properly, always giving vague answers. The TA's pretty much are the only people I would give any credit to, they are really helpful. Me and my partner both couldn't stand Cooper, but if you are ready to work hard then it doesn't really matter i guess.
Thweatt tops this professor in every way.

She gives ok-ish lectures in the class and pretty helpful INSIDE the class. But outside of class she is the most uncompassionate, cold and lack simple human empathy. She will make you solve everything with her TAs so don't even bother emailing her. The class work is already hard and the class's environment makes it worse.

PLEASE check out these reviews: all the five-star ratings sound identical, almost like they're AI-generated or written by Cooper. Notice their high dislike count compared to the one-star's like count. I switched to Thweatt's class, and it was a far better experience.

She was not a great lecturer and had very tough grading. She would sometimes change the rubric for projects after the due date (Happened twice with proof my semester). reviews.comment: Don't waste your time reading the fake positive reviews she writes about herself. This prof has a degree in Mickey Mouse engineering and does not know anything. One of the most inflated egos in the entire university. Avoid if at all possible.

Dr. Cooper is serious but teaches the material very well. This is a project-based class, so the projects take up a lot of time, which Dr. Cooper is up-front about. Need help? Read the spec. Don't know where to start? Read the spec. Go to office hours hoping for help, they say read the spec. 

Tough teacher, tough grader, project heavy. Dr. Cooper is a nice person outside of class, but when it comes to this course she is very difficult.

you can skip her, she's gonna waste your time. Does not help at alll

Best teacher I've ever had. There were many opportunities to get help outside of class since ECE 2544 is a very project heavy course, but her lectures were great and very engaging. I had her for ECE1004 as well and took her class again because she was always very helpful.

This class is tough and a lot of work no matter who you have.  Cooper is very good at giving feedback and the main difference between her and the other professors is she has group work case studies.  These turned out to be very helpful when doing the assignments.  I would recommend Cooper

She's very kind. Everyone says she's passive-aggressive, but that's only if you ask questions which can be answered by looking at the assignment specifications. She does "case studies" that other sections don't do, which are basically in-class assignments that will help you complete the very difficult homeworks (called Learning Experiences).

Dr Cooper is ON YOUR SIDE! Assignments can take you days even with help, but ASK FOR HELP! I learned this too late thinking I could knock out assignments in two days on my own... I could not lol... She is a very caring professor if you show her respect and that you want to do well. Love her

The material of this class was incredibly difficult for me, but Cooper's assignment structure and approach in the lectures made it digestible for someone with almost 0 background in the subject. Start assignments early! She's always willing to help as long as you're putting forth the effort. This class is a lot of work, but it's definitely manageable if you start on time. READ ALL OF THE SPECS, they're super detailed and answer a lot of questions. Lots of resources available, and Cooper really makes this class fun.

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is a great teacher and explains the materials well. However, she gives too much homework that takes at least 3 - 5 hours each. Also gives projects that are extremely hard and sometimes out of the context of the class and she wants you to search for the answer. She is very rude and disrespectful to the students.

Dr. Cooper, while organized and knowledgeable of the topics, lacks any professionalism required to be a professor. She frequently belittles students in class. She also gives about double the amount of the work that the other professors give so you will have to spend hours a week working on it.

One of the best professors I have ever had at Virginia Tech. She took a very difficult class and made it very understandable. The projects were very time consuming but she gave you the resources you needed to complete them and learn a lot at the same time. No other professor has taught me such a sheer amount of material as her.

Very hard, but a very interesting class, and a very good teacher.  The projects are a bit too time consuming, but also somewhat fun.  Probably my biggest complaint was the tests were a little too long to completely finish in the time given.

She definitely knows the material in and out, but sometimes she overlooks that the students don't. You definitely need to attend class and pay attention because there is no text for the second half of the semester, and you will get lost. If you do the homework and pay attention, you should have no problem getting a decent grade in the class
No doubt she runs a tough class, but if you do all the work assigned to you (which is a lot) you'll do decently on the exams.

She is a very tough teacher. She gives hard homeworks, tough quizzes and tests, no curves. Projects take a long time. She is very helpful outside of class, and will respond to emails quickly. She is tough, but by the end of the class, you will definitely know it all.

This is a weedout class in the hardest majors offered at VT. It will bust your balls. On the upside, Dr. Cooper is a reasonably nice woman outside of class and will thoroughly respond to emails you might have.
No curves, hard tests, long-hard homeworks, lots of hard deadlines, and difficult projects. Supposedly, Cooper's class is one of the hardest offered at 'Tech. Beware...

WORST professor i've ever had...so hard, so unfair. for circuits all of the other professors let u use a cheat sheet, and they curve. she doesnt do either, her homeworks take forever. she is a disgrace to my education. i legitimately want to go up to her and ask her.."why are you so hard and mean" i just really don't know what excuse she has...
Tough professor, but wants his students to succeed. Beware of pop quizzes, which are graded on an inconsistent basis.

reviews.comment: I didn't realize how much I struggled with Cline's teaching style until I retook the class and understood everything better with a different professor. I wish his lectures were more structured, because sitting in his class felt like an endless road leading to nothing. The content is fascinating, only if you learn it and apply it on your own time.

Probably the best professor I've ever had. He teaches this class at 8am but I still looked forward to class as the lectures are extremely engaging. He is strict, but if you go to office hours you will find he is very nice and cares for your success. Just understand that this class is content heavy and a lot of diagramming.

Cline is the hardest and stricted professor ive had in college so far, but that's not a bad thing. He cares for Neuroscience and he shows that from day one. He wants his students to have an understanding of what they're getting into, as neuroscience majors will be in school for a large portion of their lives. If you want to be prepped, take him

Dr.Cline is one of the best professors I've had. His teaching style is very different from most professors, as he relies heavily on diagraming. reviews.comment: Had him for both 2025-26, he's a great teacher, you are forced to learn a lot, but the class is very difficult. reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I didn't pass the class, but Dr. Cline improved my experience. He is a great lecturer and passionate about the subject. He is also very kind and wants every student to succeed in his class. Get to know him because he is a professor you want to connect with.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cline is an amazing professor and an amazing personality as well. His lectures are interesting and engaging, and his teaching style is very intuitive. His exams are primarily diagram based, meaning you must be able to not only memorize, but also understand the material well enough to synthesize your own answers. His side tangents are hilarious.

The class is difficult, so put in the work. The grade is weighted heavily on the exams, which come from the power points. He doesn't go over everything in class, so be prepared for A LOT of outside work. Exams diagram based, which doesn't work for some people's learning style, but put in the work. Took a bit to get used to it, a learning curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cline is the best! This is a STEM major, it is going to be hard. You have to be ready to put the work in to get the grade you want and that has nothing to do with Dr. Cline at all. He does give pop quizzes but it is fairly easy to scope out what they might be on.

Dr Cline seems scary at first but he's an amazing professor. I have never understood and retained so much hard information and enjoyed it this much. While the exams are mainly diagrams which seems difficult, he gives you everything you need to know and explains in a very clear way. I'm glad I have him again for future neuro courses!

My friends and I took NEUR2025 and NEUR2026 with Dr. Cline, and he's hands down the best professor we've had. Yes, the class was challenging and required effort, but a year later, I still remember everything. If you think he's a bad teacher, maybe the problem isn't him—it's your unwillingness to put in the work. :)

he does an incredible job helping you visualize and understand the material. he is tough and the material is hard but if youre a neuroscience major you should be mentally prepared for the difficult course load.

reviews.comment: It felt impossible to succeed in this class without throwing the rest of your responsibilities out of the window. He is a great person and teacher just the amount and complexity of the content was wayyyy too much. Studied for over 40 hours in one week for an upcoming test and still could not get a passing grade.

No idea what I was getting into. Gives pop quizzes about every other class worth 20% of your grade without knowing what they will be on. Recommends you are 10-15 slides ahead for class. Reads slides SO fast, I have trouble following. Makes very discouraging comments if you are behind or aren't understanding which doesn't make me want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is unbelievably passionate about graph theory and combinatorics, and he shows how it's closely tied to everything in the world. He's theory heavy during lectures, but it's common enough subject that you can look anything up. Incredibly easy grader.

Fantastic professor - his lectures make fairly difficult content straightforward, and Dr. Clemons has videos on YouTube which are nearly identical to his lectures if you need to rewatch. Exams are also straightforward, and one exam is dropped so the final is optional. Would definitely recommend also super knowledgeable about the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Clemons was great for combo. He explained all the topics well and provided a lot of examples in class, as well as reviewing any homework questions we had. He's definitely in my top 3 math professors of all time! Make sure you go to class, and if you have to miss, go to office hours.

Took his online course during summer 2025, he is by far the BEST math professor I have ever had. The class itself is difficult, but professor Clemons makes it feel as easy as simple addition. His lectures made it feel like I was discovering the topics naturally and making the connections myself. This class truly  made me a better mathematician.

Dr. Clemons was a great professor for the math (multivariable calc) portion of this course! He always gave great examples in lectures and was generous with things like partial credit on exams. Also lenient with homework due dates. Just a great guy in general too, you can clearly tell he enjoys teaching.

Clemons is one of the best math professors I've had. He clearly cares about the content he's teaching and grades based on understanding rather than correct answers. If you go to class (graded attendance) and study the videos he gives for each unit, you'll ace each exam and learn a lot more than the textbook will ever teach you.

Professor Clemons is an amazing professor! I had him for combinatorics. He is an amazing lecturer, provides clear notes and has an entire class where he allows students to ask about questions from the HW. His midterms are very straight forward if you go to class. If you have a choice, choose Clemons he is awesome.
Great prof, has graded attendance ( 5 percent). Assigns a lot of hw compared to other profs but his midterms are straight forward and he is a very generous grader.

Dr Clemons is an amazing diff eq professor. He explains the concepts very thoroughly -- so, if you have a question in class, don't be afraid to ask. There is a lot of homework, but it will help you, and he goes over some problems in class -- do the homework! Tests are pretty straightforward. Would 100% take a class of his again.

Clemons is Amazing at explaining DiffEq concepts. Saved my grade in other classes (ECE2054, ME2004) that use DiffEq. Homeworks on the heavier side, but they're not bad. He grades exams by concept and doesn't grade arithmetic errors. No lecture notes so going to class is important, but its easy to do well if you go. Lots of space to ask questions.
King!!!!!!

The best professor I have had at Tech so far. He is good at answering everyone's questions and helps you easily understand the information. If you put in a fair amount of effort it will be pretty easy for you to get an A.

Dr. Clemons was the best math teacher I've had at Tech. He writes notes by hand on the chalkboard and does practice problems for a good amount of class. His example problems and advice are directly related to his tests, and his tests are very straightforward. If he feels like he didn't fully teach a concept, he gives very generous extra points.

I was very nervous to take this class, but Professor Clemons made it very straightforward and easy. He assigns a lot of homework but the quizzes and tests are just like the homework. Additionally, he uploads videos on Canvas to help with some of the harder homework problems. He is very kind during office hours and is a lenient grader.

Okay, so this guys class is tough as it is differential equations, but he is by far one of the best teachers I have ever had. He will go over examples of exactly what is on the test and he will do reviews and answer any questions he is asked. He played guitar for the class at one point and went over exactly what was on the test, Definitely take!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Makes an easy class way harder than it needs to be

Hopkins was a great teacher! I cannot disagree with the ratings enough. He did everything he could to give us the materials we needed, and his class was not very difficult. Hopkins even dedicated a day to hear us out about any ways we thought he could improve his course. Very caring and wants to see you succeed. Could not recommend him enough!
All you need to know is the class is really easy just do the work its not that much youll pass For Sure! The low ratings dont make sense.

I took this professor two semesters ago and now I'm about to take his MGT 2114 class. Remembering my experience back then, it's clear that these reviews are just freshmen who have just learned how college works. Craig Hopkins is such a nice guy, very understanding and super helpful if you make time to meet with him. The class itself was very test heavy, a lot of homework but not enough to bring your grade up if you bomb a test.. the tests are open note but you have to understand every term and definition or you won't be able to finish in time. Not terrible

Taking this class as a sophomore, I think that a lot of the other reviews are just freshman who were unprepared for what a college class is actually like. He's actually really helpful outside of class; just read the instructions and syllabus, show up, and communicate, and you'll be fine. Lots of group work but that's life.
Bad Teacher, Great Person

Participation is key - ask lots of questions. Met outside of class & office hours to fit my schedule. Walked through exams & quizzes to help me understand what I missed.

Class wasn't mandatory until he noticed a bunch of ppl skipping, then made it mandatory. Doesn't let you see quizzes or exams unless you schedule a time, which is annoying. He's def a super nice person and very understanding and lenient, but the amount of work is crazy.

imo he not as bad as everyone makes it seem. I believe he is willing to hear you out, but he will probably not give you the grade back. Probably the worst instructor I have ever had. Highly unflexible, and not willing to help. Do NOT take this teacher if you do not have to. harsh grader that makes class harder than it should be and never fully explains assignments. impossible to reach him out of class.

this guy sucks

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

Dr. Thorp is my favorite VT professor! He is a great guy and wants everyone to do well, but you will only get out of this class what you put in. Overall, I found the course quite easy but enjoyed every single minute of Dr. Thorp's lectures. 

Ask questions, participate in class, go to his office, and be there on Fridays for extra credit quizzes.
Dr. Thorp was my advisor and instructor in the late-80's. One of the best.

Dr. Thorp is super passionate and knows so much about the subject, it's fun to just listen to him lecture. Professor Thorp is a great lecture. If you like history, his class is pretty engaging. Every week you have to do an online quiz that goes along with the textbook, but you have unlimited tries. Professor Thorp is a great lecturer. His class is a little difficult but if you read you'll be fine. Quizzes are every Monday and cover the reading assigned, he drops the lowest two. reviews.comment: This professor know the subject he is teaching. He has a tendency to make his students feel inferior.

he's a damn good speaker. He knows his stuff well, but his quizzes and tests are really hard...they are crazy. very vague questions. However, he does give a lot of extra credit..around up to 5-7 points on ur final grade.

If you want to study the wonderful world of spelling according to Thorp, he's you man. Get a dictionary!

I enjoyed professor Decks class, if you don't take notes the class will be hard, however if you listen and take good notes that exactly what the test/quizzes are on. Her lectures were fun and engaging, she has fun stories from her real experience too which are cool.
I enjoyed her class.

Her in-class quizzes are extremely niche and confusing, and even she seems unsure of the answers at times. Exams rely entirely on lectures and require far more preparation than they should. She doesn't give grades until the semester ends, so if you like knowing your standing, avoid this class.

means well, but the class is difficult because she doesn't post notes, we can't take notes during example quizzes, and there's no study guide for exams. At the end of every class, there is a quiz and she tells you what to study for the exam roughly. She then claims that the exams are meant to be easy. Her style of teaching is outdated.

She is a very nice person, and you can tell that she enjoys what she teaches and is very knowledgeable. Make sure you write down everything.

go to class, pay attention, take good notes. key to achieving a A in this class, memorization is important and writing down those examples she makes because she puts some on the tests. overall class isn't too bad and actually made me learn considering tests are in person.

Deck is a nice PERSON and generally enjoyable. HOWEVER, teaching is perhaps not her strong suit. As with most Professors of Practice, she is extremely educated in her subject. But, she is not good at teaching it in any means.

The best worker won't make the best manager. The most productive manager will not make the best professor.
I can't believe people actually rate her low. Just go to class and pay attention and you will probably get a good grade. She makes it very simple for students too.

I literally don't know why she gets such bad reviews. Her class wasn't even that bad if you go to class, listen, and take notes. terrible professor, I've had her for two years now at Virginia Tech and every course is terrible. She is a terrible teacher doesn't understand the dynamics of learning. One of the best professors I've had at VT. Do not listen to these BS reviews. If you make an attempt she will recognize and reward.

This was a brutal class, while I believe that Prof. Deck has good intentions and is a nice lady, the way she teaches her class is extremely flawed. Poor teaching style and does lecture is all over the place. She is very kind but that does not mean she is a good professor. Not a good class but not the end of the world.

Terrible teacher makes an easy class over complicated because she refuses to post her slides with information on them. If you don't take perfect notes on everything she says in class you are cooked. Get a different teacher she is terrible
