reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Professor Deck and did really well in the class. However, YOU HAVE to attend classes and pay attention because there is a quiz every class. The questions on the exams and the quizzes are very specific so you NEED to take thorough notes in order to do well.
Please dont take her horrid teacher way too hard for a into class.

prof deck means well but i really dreaded going to class bc class is very disorganized. but its mandatory for quiz points; quizzes were not easy and you really need to pay attention during class and write down everything she says, quiz grade hurt my grade. exams were 80% short answers BUT she has extra credit SO DO IT

I feel like people exaggerate when they say this teacher sucks. The class was pretty easy. The pop quizzes aren't even hard. They are literally based on the class lecture you just learned. Smartbook is tedious, but copy, paste, and search some questions for Quizlet to help. Finally, Exams are pretty hard, so defo do your best to study.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She does not post all the slides she uses for her lessons for offline studying. It is very hard to learn a module in her class you have fallen ill and missed the notes.

don't take this class there is a quiz every day and she teaches like an elementary school teacher. the tests have little to no content covered in her terms sheet, lecture or homework and make up 75% of the grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She teaches a Brutal class does not need to be as hard as it is.

Teaches like a kindergarten teacher. twists up exams statistics to make herself look better and brags when the average is a c. Short answers on exams so if you forget the exact word you get it wrong (knowing the concept doesn't matter to her). Lectures are boring, worse than most classes.

I can't begin to explain about how dissapointed I was with how this class unfolded. Quizzes every class so attendance is mandatory. Seems to have the qualification of a second grader in teaching a class. I learned nothing and thought this would be the easiest class but instead it was the exact opposite. Enough said, don't take the class.

She's really nice, but super slow to give feedback. Just show up to class and take notes(do NOT skip class). The main project can be kind of time consuming, but I spent less than an hour on this class each week outside of class. Quizzes and tests are directly off what she lectures on and super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Hands down the worst professor I have not only had at Virginia Tech but in my entire life. Margaret Deck is single-handly the most frustrating and inconsiderat professor I have ever had and I truly feel sorry for any student who has to suffer through her class. She literally forgot to give the SSD office my test and I had to take it another day.

Hands down the worst professor I've had at Virginia Tech after being here for two years. Her powerpoint presentations are a complete eye sore as they have no structure or format. Mandatory quizzes every class, also has know idea how to properly use Canvas. Concepts learned in class are just basic common sense too, no reason to pay for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Wish I could give a zero rating. This is the worst teacher not only that I have had at Virginia Tech but the worst I have ever had in my entire life. She is ridiculously strict but at the same time has no idea what she is doing. If you have to take this class do it with someone else.

I signed up for a class that was completely asynchronous but Professor Deck took It upon herself to pick a mandatory class time once a week. She held her tests on Fridays at 7pm. She set up her canvas grading page completely wrong, I was behaving like I had an A+ in the class from canvas only to find out I had a C once I got my final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: BEST PROFESSOR, yes her class is a lot of work but if you try hard and ask questions she will see that and know how hard you are working. She is also always available to help outside of class. Before the final exam she let me zoom with her for 2 HOURS while I showed her everything in my study guide and she went over every single thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The most frustrating professor I've ever had. Half of her tests don't line up wth what was learned in class. Quizzes every class. Don't take her
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Other teachers are so much easier and this teacher is so boring. Some see her as nice but her lectures are so boring and all of the homework is just busy work. AVOID

This professor was so frustrating. She made exam questions extremely specific and did not tell you half of what would be on the exam. Every class we would have a quiz about the stuff she had just taught so if you zoned off for just a sec, good luck. I personally did not like her teaching style at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are very specific and often require filling in on word of a sentence that she said one time during her awfully boring lectures. You won't learn anything and you won't wan't to either based on how boring and irrelevant the lectures are.

Makes this simple class unnecessarily hard. half of her tests are short answer and super specific to her lectures. Gives you nothing helpful to review for tests. If you miss important information in class you will miss questions on the test. Uses "examples from class" in the test but ends up skipping half of them when youre in class. Shes nice tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Must know EVERYTHING that happened in class + all ch vocab. Takes cheating so seriously to the point that it is annoying. Almost every class cheating is brought up. You will have to study a good amount to get an A. Loves to put fill in the blank on tests, take someone else if possible. Way more stressful than an intro/principles class needed to be.
Do not take expecting an easy A. Her tests are extremely hard. Quizzes every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This teacher is awful. Her lectures are fine but she gives an attendance quiz at the end of every class so if you don't pay close attention the whole time you will fail them because they're on little details she mentions. The exams are ridiculously hard considering management is supposed to be situational and an easy concept. Homeworks take 2 hrs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tests are rather difficult any only pertain to about half of what she says in class lectures. The rest is from textbook which she doesn't even talk about. The in class quizzes can be difficult because the questions are based off of little random anecdotes she says in the lecture. Pretty tough course all in all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great teacher.  Makes the subject interesting and understandable.

Professor Deck is a really nice and helpful lady. Her lectures are very clear and only focus on things you'll need to know for the test. She tries to make them interesting, and they usually are. Homework is really easy but takes a long time to do. As long as you do the homework and go to class, it's an easy A.
Deck is awesome is your stay on top of your work.

It's not a terribly hard class, but her exams are unusually hard.  Also, the homework does not portray how the tests will be, and she does NOT put slides up online.  Class is just her reading from the slides, which is really dull, but you HAVE to go to class or find someone who has notes.  Tests are tricky, even if you study.  Be warned

Do not take Deck. She relies on PowerPoint for her lecture and purposely makes the exams confusing. The material is very simple but she finds a way to make it frustrating. Her exams are not even on the Learnsmart homeworks but rather on her PowerPoint which she refuses to post on Scholar. Stay away if you don't plan on going to class.

What kind of teacher cuts a review session an HOUR short THE CLASS BEFORE her exams? Just because shes feeling a little sick? Most moody teacher I've ever had the displeasure of learning from at this university. Very unprofessional and offended when she realizes people aren't listening to her lectures.
Great class, great teacher.

This class was ridiculous. The Learnsmart could have been helpful if the tests were actually on what they quizzed you about. Her lectures were boring, relying on PPT and reading notes directly off of a paper is not what I want my professors to do. I never did well because of the tricky questions. Horrible IMHO.

Deck is a nice lady, but she is the worst professor at VT. However she is an awful teacher. She is always late to class. She relies on powerpoint. Her tests are the worst. 80 questions, all designed to trick you. The material is incredibly simple, but she finds a way. Even if you study, you will find them to be very difficult. Stay away.
Easy material.  HW is 25% and easy to complete.  If you attend class and pay attention when you do your hw you should get an A

Lectures are very dry and he kind of just rambles on at the front of the room. He gives lots of time for questions when you are working on iclickers, but it doesn't help a whole lot when they are few and far between.
A big portion of his lectures are iClickers. Curved the final which was nice.

Super sweet guy, good office hours. Common office hours are super helpful too. Boring lectures (powerpoints) but gives good practice tests/resources. Hard tests and class though. I had pre-exams, so great curves. He also curved everyone's final by like 15 points and rounded everyone's grades if they were close. Will give u iClicker answers if u ask
Lecture heavy, yet does not explain concepts well. Quiet and confusing. A background is any kind of physics is VERY helpful. Utilize office hours and tutoring centers.
Fair course policies, grading policies etc. Lectures aren't always the easiest to follow but there are plenty of resources offered to help you out otherwise.
Just sit in front and he gives you the iclicker answers, funny guy too

He's a nice guy but the lectures are pretty boring, and most of the time is just spent waiting on iClickers. I struggled to pay attention most of the time, and did most of my learning out of class. That being said, he gives you really good review materials, and the pre-exam quizzes definitely saved my grade. The class overall wasn't too hard.
He's an ok professor, you just need to go to class for the IClickers. I barely paid attention to the lectures and I did ok but had to lock in for the tests and pre-exams.

super chill with i-clicker questions (so you need to attend class) but exam heavy, exams were pretty chill tho and honestly you don't need to study TOO much for the class. Do good on the first two midterms so you can bomb the final though, and he gave a pretty good curve at the end.
Need to pay attention in class and take advantage of the pre-exam score.

Dr Osborne was a great teacher, he's great at answering questions during lectures and helping you understand the question or the concept. He's super accessible outside of class and responds to emails super quick. It's not difficult to do well in this class just take time to understand the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very nice Professor and will answer any question. Gives answers to clicker questions if you ask. Clutched up and gave lots of extra points on final. Exams are worth everything in this class and you need to do very well on the pre exams. Take advantage of the 2 midterms so you're in a good spot for the final.

Osborne is an amazing professor. He is so attentive to every student in a huge lecture hall which is really hard to do. He gives plenty of extra credit and makes sure everyone understands the I-clicker questions. He's hands down the best physics professor I've had and he's just a kind guy in general. Great choice for 2305.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Physics is already a difficult subject to begin with. To make things worse, Dr. Osborne's teaching is just hard to follow because of how fast speaks and that he rushes through important concepts. Most of the lectures are spent just doing iClicker questions rather than material. Overall it was not a great experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gave the whole 2305 a 10-point curve on the final. Goated.

Lectures can be boring, yes. But overall the class is chill. He speaks kind of fast. The Iclicker questions are easy(just ask him and he'll give you the answer). The exams can be annoying though, sometimes the questions are not even like the practice exams.

Lectures can feel dry, but the course is structured like that with 200+ students in a class, but Prof. Osborne is super responsive. He posts a lot of resources, runs iClickers (easy points), and the pre-exam quizzes let you earn back points on exams. Exams are conceptually tricky but if you do the practice sets, fair. Overall nice professor and guy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures were a bit boring and hard to pay attention to, but he's a really nice guy and tries to make the class as easy as possible. There's lots of extra credit opportunities, and he basically gives out the answers to iclickers, so that makes it easy to get a 100 on them.

Possibly the most boring lectures. Made physics less interesting. Exams and quizzes were hard. Iclickers were somehow harder and required for attendance. Threw a crazy curve in at end of year which helped my grade. Overall nap time.
This guys iclickers are actually vile, trick questions dropped in. He drops 5, plus for every physics class u get a cheat sheet for the tests. Don't pick this guy tho, lectures are sleep time

Such a nice person. I had a personal emergency the day before an exam and was very worried that I would have to miss the exam, but Dr. Osborne doesn't go by the whole "Absences must be excused by the Dean of Students" policy, so I was able to email him my situation and he allowed me to reschedule. I am very grateful for him.

Dr. Osborne is definitely one of the better physics professors at VT. His lectures are a little boring, but he does iClickers which are a grade booster. He curves exams so the average is about an 80. He definitely wants everyone to do well and offers a lot of office hours. He's just a genuinely sweet person.

Dr. Osborne spent a lot of time on the iClickers so sit in the front and he'll basically give the answer to you. Overall he's pretty monotone so I didn't get a lot from his lectures but his slides were excellent. The first two units were pretty straight forward but final exam unit was rough but it's not difficult to get a high grade.

Lectures aren't very good, and a lot of time is wasted on iClicker questions instead of material. To be honest, you'll be fine in this class if you show up to class and read the textbook, as you will be learning 90% of the material from it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy enough class, just lots of hw.

Osborne gave so many extra credits. My fault was I missed a few. However, his biggest flaw is that he spends 20 minutes for an iClicker question and like 10 minutes on slides. He doesn't spend less time on slides explaining, instead he talks so fast and moves so fast that you do not have time to take notes.

Lectures are pretty boring, but Osborne explains every iClicker question. Gives a lot of extra credit and grade drops. Exams are hard, so it's important to do well on the pre-exams. Osborne will make sure your grade is ok (I did not get above a 73 on any exam and ended with a 90 in the class).

Style wasn't for me. He is a nice guy, but felt like he couldn't break down the concepts enough for the average person to understand. Homework and iClickers help to keep your grade afloat. He sometimes curves by .2 points. He does go around to help during Iclickers, so you can count on getting the right answer.

He would be a great professor if you're good at physics. But I'm not, and falling a little bit behind felt like a death sentence in this class. His lectures are so fast, when he actually decides to teach. Sometimes he let the iClicker run for >10 minutes, and wastes valuable lecture time. 

He's a wonderful guy, but not my style.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Out of the selection of PHYS-2205 professors, Osborne is definitely the best one. The course is hard, but he shows an effort to make sure everyone understands the content. His lectures are extremely boring and his hand writing is awful, but if you keep up with the homework, practices, and lecture, you'll do just fine for the exams!

His handwriting if illegible. He primarily taught the class through iClicker questions which took up a majority of the class time. He tries to explain except you couldn't even understand his explanation because of his writing. Theres a couple drops so that's helpful but overall Osborne needs to learn how to not talk in circles.

Large lecture class, however, gives a lot of time to think about clicker questions and always gives people opportunities to ask questions. Office hours were also super helpful and would definitely recommend. Also responds really fast to emails. Overall solid professor given that the class was so big.

LOVE THIS MAN. People give him crap because he teaches a hard class, BUT he's as clear as possible. Yes, it's a lot of homework but the practice problems are required to understand the concepts. Read the textbook. About 6 hours of homework a week. Just do practice problems again and again and you'll be fine. Always eager to help explain.

You will learn better with him than the other Physics professors. Do the weekly homework and practices and you will do good on the tests. He is very nice and understanding. The class is hard because it is physics, just pay attention.

I personally think he was a pretty good lecturer who wanted to make sure everyone understood the material. However his handwriting is illegible, he can't keep the room, and he would skimp out on some in dept material. Tests and homework aren't too difficult, however I did not make use of extra credit for exams when I should've. USE THE EXTRA CREDIT

Warning: His handwriting if illegible. He also cannot control his lecture as it frequently got very loud and seemed as if he wasn't paying attention to the engagement. Class just consisted of was 3 iClickers which took him 20 minutes to close and explain except you couldn't even understand his explanation because of his writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take the 5:30-6:45 PM secession. Your attention span will be so gone by that point and the lectures are so fast! U get used to it. If you're a good student, j want the credit C/B, you'll be fine. However, it's not an enjoyable class perse. The physics department isn't strong, but what I've heard from others is Osborn is better than others.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dude talks at the speed of light and is sometimes hard to follow during problems. I mostly learned from the homework because it's just difficult to pay attention. His handwriting is also terrible, he once accidently drew a pp (he was trying to draw a car). The class is really forgiving lot's of extra credit. Pre quizzes to get back points on tests.

Prof. Osborne is great! Talks quite fast, but you get used to it. He is very knowledgeable and it's obvious he cares about your learning. The iClickers during class are great becuase it forces you to pay attention. He walks around the room for anyone who has questions during the iClickers. Questions aren't hard for the iClickers.

Dr. Osborne explains things thoroughly and has easily accessible slides on canvas for review. Lectures can be pretty boring but he does explain things well. Homework questions can be pretty rough but that's just because physics is inherently hard.

Dr. Osborne conveys information using slides and constantly invokes the use of clicker questions to keep students engaged and to help them understand the concepts. His method of describing things is helpful, but his handwriting is terrible and at times illegible when he is demonstrating something.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are almost pointless. It's hard to understand his methods for solving problems, especially later in the semester with harder concepts. He's got really poor handwriting when writing on paper, but decent handwriting when writing on the whiteboard. His lectures are boring above all else.

Physics and math really are not my thing but I appreciated Mr. Osborne's lectures and his patience with helping me understand the concepts. His office hours are incredibly helpful and a good oppurtunity to connect with other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Boring lectures but easy grader, lots of ways to boost grade. He was good at answering questions if you just reach out. Wants students to succeed. Kind of awkward but nice.

The guy is a great professor. He makes himself extremely accessible to his students and is always helpful whether it be through email or office hours. This is a tough class and if you miss even one class you are at risk of missing out on a lot. Overall though, great guy (He doesn't get much into his personal life).

He seemed like a good guy, but I did not like his teaching style. I constantly zoned out to the professor tripping over his words or just speaking with a very monotonous tone. He explained tough concepts with calculus (in a non-calc course) or other tough physics concepts, making it hard to grasp the information.
Great guy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is the best intro to phys professor at VT, he sets up his class in a way that sets you up to succeed, and genuinely cares about his students (which is rare). He does do iClicker which kind of requires you to come to class. However, he spends a lot of time on each one and they are easy points toward your grade. I 100% rec this prof to anyone.

Osborne is probably the best of the options out there for 2305. Lectures aren't the most interesting out there but he helps out a lot with the clicker questions. Going to his office hours saved my grade, there was never anyone there and he would walk through the homework problems step by step.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Handwriting comparable to a 3rd grader. His delta symbol looked like a circle, and this translated to how he wrote his numbers and variables making it near impossible to follow his work. The cherry ontop was how he spent 75 minutes (in a 90 minute section) on just iclicker questions.

There are a lot of Iclicker questions during the lectures, but he and his TA walk around and talk to the students to help them understand it. Test are made by the department and homework may take a long time.

The way he speaks in lectures makes simple concepts much more complicated making lectures go really slow. The videos in the online textbook were much more useful and simplified the material in a way that made it easier to grasp. The pre-quizzes help your grade a lot and make achieving a good grade in the class very realistic.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the way he speaks makes it difficult to understand what he is overall teaching. honestly, i only ever learned the concepts from his lectures but failed to learn how to compute any of the questions in either the homework, studio, or tests. the pre-quizzes are nice, but having lectures be just iclicker questions is frustrating.

It's somehow harder to pay attention to his lectures than watching paint dry for an hour straight. Talks with a monotone voice nd the lecture time is filled with clicker questions so attendance is required. If you want an A in this class, then you need a study group and you'll want to actually do the assigned homework and quizzes.

As someone who fell asleep ONCE in hs, I never expected to be as drowsy as I was during his class. He tends to speak monotonously, and as such it's very easy to fall asleep in class. His handwriting is also almost impossible to decipher. Spends lots of time on iclickers. He's not a bad guy, but I wouldn't take him again or recommend him to anyone.

His class was very easy due to the extreme amounts of extra credit he gives out. It is basically impossible to fail his class if you take the "Pre-Exam Quizzes". Going into the final exam, I only need to get a 25% in order to keep an A in the class.

As a person he seemed like he cared about his students, but it was extremely difficult to pay attention to his long lectures. He does clicker questions like every other slide too. Tests were super hard but quizzes help with that.

His lectures are a bit boring and his voice made me want to fall asleep, but he taught the material well enough. Tests weren't too hard & had extra credit. There are 2 homework assignments a week: an easy enough (but somewhat time consuming) reading quiz on the textbook, and a Mastering Physics assignment that ranges from easy to very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very straightforward and did not waste too much time. Ask questions and he will be happy to answer them. Make sure to do the Pre-exam-quiz. Pay attention in class and you should definitely pass the class at the very least.

The way that he teaches isn't really for me, but he covers what he needs to. He always tries to help during clicker questions and whenever someone has a question, but sometimes it's a bit convoluted. Make sure to take notes that you'll understand without relying on the powerpoint slides.

Attendance is mandatory with iClicker (only participation, the answer doesn't need to be right). He does use slides which can be difficult to not space out. Homework is straightforward and easy. The tests are average difficulty, but there was an insane curve (+17% flat on midterm2 and final) so don't street too much over them. Overall a nice person

The greatest person on campus, not the best professor though. A large majority of class was spent on iClickers which left little time to work out examples. I managed to fail every single test I took for the class but still passed with a B-. This is a difficult course but if you do well in Lab and on Homework you will have no problem passing.

Osborne is a nice enough guy, but not good at teaching. He overcomplicates everything and spends a lot of time on I-clickers (more than he should) instead of explaining the material. Most of the professors for this class aren't good so he is average.

I love this professor, he is the best professor I have ever had. Of course physics itself is a challenging course, but he makes it feel like it is nothing. He takes his time and makes sure everyone understands the lesson. Please give this man a raise.
He does lots of practice problems each class, which for some might be helpful, but for myself I was lost always. Every class is a lecture, but extremely hard to follow.

Osborne is a nice guy, and you can tell he cares about his students which is more than a lot of professors. But man he is bad at teaching. He overcomplicates literally everything, his notes are almost impossible to understand. Just in general an extremely hard class.

Extremely hard class. Lecture heavy but doesn't clarify much. Super test heavy and your grade basically depends on how you do on them. Office hours didn't really help me. Lots of work: homework, problem solving studio, lab, etc. Would not take again.

Osborne is an above-average physics professor, which is saying a lot compared to the other options at VT. He cares about his students and will help you if you need, but he doesn't always explain concepts very well. His practice exams are WAY harder than the actual exam, so you'll be well-prepared. He's the best prof for PHYS 2305

I took General Physics 1 Spring '21 sem, and it was synchronous and online with roughly 250 students. Class was hard for me, because physics is just something that I'm not really good at. The professor will curve an exam (each midterm and/or the final exam) if its class average was below a certain percentage. I struggled severely but still had a B.

Osbornes a chill person, but I would constantly fall asleep in class after the first midterm. There are multiple extra credit attempts, so make sure to take advantage of all of them. If you just read through the book and work on a good chunk of the practice problems, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His zoom lectures weren't helpful, I ended up just learning from the textbook and got much higher grades on tests than my friends who relied on lectures. The average on a (MC!) test was a 44 and he only curved it 16 points, making the average a 60 because it "wasn't his fault." He tries and I like him as a person but I would try to get a diff prof.

Osborne was good at explaining concepts, but his monotone voice could be difficult pay attention to on Zoom at 8am. The best way to get good grades in this class is to attend review sessions outside of class. All three tests were curved, but don't rely on it. I think his lectures would be more beneficial if they were in-person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was a really down to earth professor but I didnt really learn a whole lot from the lectures. This class is really test heavy and there is a lot of random work to do which really isnt worth that much of the grade. The class was the problem not the professor.

Professor Osborne does a good job of lecturing, but does not go far past this. The class is heavily test reliant and there aren't many supplemental assignments to back up your total grade. The textbook is your best friend and practice problems are a good way of getting a grasp on the subject besides the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes a great guy, very nice and polite, however he struggles to explain some things to the degree required for someone to fully comprehend. Having said that, hes willing to go over a problem or concept as many times as you need. Tests are really easy, a mix of conceptual and technical questions but nothing too challenging.

Dr. Osborne is a very relaxed and kind man. His lectures can definitely be boring but he makes sure to answer any and ALL questions people have. Very understanding too. Exams are not easy, best advice is to stay on top of the material and ask questions during class. Overall I'd recommend him.
Dudes a god. Straight to the point, grades fast, answers questions well, etc.

Didn't learn anything I didn't know from highschool until the last 3 weeks. The class will be easy or difficult depending on your grasp of physics and the work you put in. Homeworks aren't hard, recitation problems and lab are easy if you leave enough time for them. Offers some extra credit and sometimes curves tests but will not bump final grade.

I had Osborne my first semester at Tech, and he really made physics my favorite class. In lecture he goes slow and explains concepts down to detail, and if you go to his office hours, he will work with you one-on-one, which he prefers! Most of the issues with this class come from the department, not from Ozzy.

Dr. Osborne is a really nice person but a very ineffective professor. When you ask for help, he'll just refer you to his email and once you email him he'll say to come to his office hours and go see the student success center. During office hours, you will not be able to ask personalized questions, you will just follow along the problems he does

Professor Osborone is by far the most patient instructor that I have seen on campus. While taking his PHYS2305, he clearly explains every concept, even though it might be difficult for students to comprehend. However, if students have any concerns about a specific topic, please go to his office hours because he is willing to resolve questions.

Grade return time was abysmal, and our midterm exam grade came out weeks after other sections' grades were returned. He is a very nice guy, but clearly is not a MatLab professor by trade. He asked the TA for clarifications constantly, and really did not know what was going on.

Not sure why RMP says Dr. Maczka works at Virginia Tech; he currently works at UTK. Anyway, Dr. Maczka is pretty good. He is nice and open to all questions. The class is about half lecture, half lab. I struggled with understanding EF141 a lot, but that is not his fault: I am just not great at physics. Just finish the busy work, and you will pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good at explaining stuff and helping with problems but honestly not the most entertaining. Sometimes just couldn't pay attention to the lectures because there was a lot of endless talking. You should be ready to learn most of the material as homework through the learning pages, and the due dates are consistent.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He uses a flipped classroom style of teaching, which I have never been a fan of, but if you like that than he's the perfect professor for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is very smart and he explains every step that he does in great detail, so you have to really pay attention to follow what he is saying. Most of the work we did was on our own outside of class, but anytime I emailed Dr. Maczka he gave detailed feedback that usually helped me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most of the material for EF had to be learned before the lecture. The pre-class is for a grade and there's a handful of practice problems you have to do on paper. Most of the time they were due hours before lecture, making it difficult to get help. Was very helpful if you had a question during or after lecture, but I wish more was taught in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Easy class with a lot of outside help available if you need it. As well as a lot of extra credit if you take the time to do it. Make sure you do the work before class to actually understand it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Theres a lot of work to do, but he's almost always available to help when you have extra questions.

Absolutely amazing professor, he explains the material very well and provides such detailed explanations and feedback if you ask a question. I once emailed him about something from class that I didn't understand, and he gave me a 3 paragraph explanation. Would 100% take again.

Prof. Maczka is a very good professor, he makes it very clear what will be on exams and gives us practice exams that are almost exactly the same as the test. If you do the very little homework he assigns, you shouldn't find it very hard to get a good grade in this class.

Maczka cares more about the class than you ever will. There are some assignments where I wrote 3 sentences and his feedback was 3 paragraphs. He doesn't do a lot of genuine teaching, but he is always happy to review your work and help you out. Super friendly and takes the class very seriously.

Gives you feedback, then takes points off for listening and applying her feedback. Has a rubric but doesn't post until after submission date, and takes points off that don't even apply to her own rubric. Grading makes no sense.

She is easily one of the most frustrating professors to have. She doesn't provide clear criteria on assignments and nitpicks the littlest of things. If you miss one grammatical error that you don't correct, you get a 0 for the assignment. It's an all-or-nothing class. Be prepared to be ridiculously frustrated with her grading and expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Zahm is by far the worst instructor I have ever had. She is rude/condescending towards students, gives unprofessional feedback on assignments and plays favorites extremely hard. The subject is not hard but she prides herself in being a tough prof. Good luck if you have an SSD accommodation, she doesn't care to respect those very much.
Assignments very manageable and all due at end of course.  Many guest speakers. Previously had her in undergrad and this class is better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When I needed to sign up for this course, an advisor referred to her as a "drill sergeant." She knows her stuff and she's a great resource. I use skills I learned from her frequently. But this will not be fun or enjoyable. Almost switched my major.
This class made no sense. No canvas page, very few email reminders or announcements, high expectations and no clear or consistent explanation of student responsibilities. ?????

Not open to communicating and never answers emails, the one time she did it was passive aggressive and rude. She didn't come to the last day of class and didn't notify us that she wouldn't be there. Doesn't provide clear instructions on assignments, no textbook and homework is "submitted" through google drive which is confusing and disorganized.

There are 4 assignments for the entire semester and she is a really tough grader and all of them. She does not use canvas, so you do not know your grade until the day you come back from winter break. This class honestly stressed me out a lot. But at the end you do get to re-do an assignment which helps a lot.

Horrible teacher. Gets mad when you ask questions or ask her to do anything. We went the entire semester constantly asking for a list of when things were due and were punished for asking her to do so. She is the worst teacher I have ever had, do not take her class. The only thing I learned in the course is how to deal with a salty old teacher.

If you have her for any of the courses.... drop them. As a professor and an "advisor" she really doesnt seem to care about her students at all. She is not helpful in class when a student asks a question and just goes off on about her career 80% of the time.   Dont even think about approaching her about questions about your career. She is the worst

She would only take attendance occasionally, and she would do it through  in class assignments, which would only happen randomly. She's so confusing, doesn't explain things well, and rambles endlessly. If you have a question for her, it's best to google it because she's useless.

Zahm is a good professor with an awesome sense of humor. Her class was entertaining even when the material she taught wasn't. Go to class; sometimes she gives in-class E.C. projects! I did not appreciate how many books her class required, but at least they were only paperbacks. And the homework is really annoying, but she's a lenient grader.

had her online class. would not recommend it. she seems to not like it when you ask questions. The class focuses on the political part of urban planning, not any design aspect. The material she gives to study does not seem to mesh with the questions on quizzes. overall  it was a struggle. glad it's over.
horrible. hard to communicate with and is very snappy/rude if you ask questions. I would avoid her!

Professor Zahm was terrible. Urban Public Issues was honestly just a bunch of useless reading because each quiz and test had nothing to do with what was important in the books. I would not recommend this class unless it's for a major.

She is the worst teacher i have ever had at VT. I have tried to request meetings at her office hours (by appointment only) and she has made no effort to do so. She makes emailing and communicating with students extremely difficult. She has made a minimal effort to be flexible to other major classes. I don't recommend taking her class.
Easy intro to planning class. do the work- get an A pretty straight forward
As long as you keep up. it's easy. she gives all the questions prior to tests. just do the work. and you're golden

She really knew her stuff and I loved the in-class activities.  If you did the work, it was really hard to do badly on tests plus there was an opportunity to earn unlimited extra credit.  My only complaint:  she could really snap at people sometimes, which I think made people not want to ask questions.

Dr. Zahm probably knows more about Urban Planning than most. She has an internationa reputation and clearly is well thought of in her field. If you, however, are looking for a piece of cake class, her classes aren't for you. She has high expectations, but no higher than those expected in the outside world. If you want a planning job, take her class

I made the mistake of taking two courses in the Urban studies department. I took  courses from Zahm, and Randolph.  Zahm is boring and seems to know nothing about what she is suppose to teach. Randolph trys to brain wash you to his way of thinking, and does not know there is a world outside of Blacksburg. Don't take any courses in this department.

Oh my.  She was God awful.  She clearly adores public planning but has no means of communicating that adoration besides the droning and monotonous spewing of planning techniques that no one gives two hoots about.  Be sure to memorize EVERYTHING in the notes or you'll do sub average on the tests.  Enjoy.
She knows alot, and really cares about what she teaches.  If you know everything on the review sheet you are good, going to class helps alot too!

I thought Dr. Zahm did a great job teaching the class.  If you attended class and actually took notes on the powerpoints, what she was saying about the powerpoints, her exams came almost word for word from the classes.  I agree, she may not be the friendliest teacher, but she's not impossible to talk to.  If you really need help, she will help you.

I thought that this professor was very helpful and worked to help her students recieve good grades by providing many extra credit opportunities. Although her tests were tough they were not impossible whatsoever and she makes the course itself is pretty interesting.

Even if you study well for her exams, attend every class and do the readings you're not guaranteed a good grade.  Dr. Zahm makes the course harder than it should be and makes the material boring and monotonous. Don't take Urban Affairs and Public Planning to fullfil your Univerisy core requirements for it's repsective area.

Though I did well in this class, this professor has NO people skills. She will basically refuse to talk to you after/before class, even if you try to visit her office. Her tests are impossible, and you NEED to do extra credit. Urban Planning is a really awesome major, but having this class as an intro class is one of the reasons why it's so small.

HORRIBLE teacher. I haven't learned a thing, but I was able to catch up on a lot of lost sleep in her class. Her lectures are the most boring things in the world.  Also, her exams will****u up the @$$.

Ummm... Be sure and not take this class. This is the most boring professor in the world. I took this class no knowing what urban public issues is and I still dont know.. Be sure and bring a pillow she'll put you into a coma. I hope i never see her again...
Dr. Helm clearly cares about anatomy and she is very helpful in office hours if you need extra help.

Literally the best animal science professor. She's so informational and helpful with not only the courses themselves, but also finding career pathways and opportunities throughout college and the future.
I love her, she's straightforward and easy to approach. the tests aren't bad either, just study the slides!

Very nice and clearly very knowledgeable. Tends to read off slides so lecture can be boring (especially as a 9am class) but content itself is easy. Get to drop 1 out of 5 test grades which is nice. Don't slack off and pay attention and there is no reason you can't end with an A.
She is fair and organized. I appreciated her teaching style.
I would take this class again and again. I loved Dr. Helm and I really enjoyed my time in her class! Tests aren't difficult, just make sure you study.

Dr. Helm is one of the best animal science professors. She cares about her students, allowing dropped assignments and tests, and gives a study guide before every exam. Anatomy is a difficult class, but she tries to make it as easy as possible.
Exams are specifically based on what you learn on presentations. Not very difficult just do your work and you should be fine.

Dr. Helm is so sweet and caring professor, and Intro to APSC was incredibly easy with her. She definitely tends to read off of the PowerPoints and doesn't add much information to them, and TopHat is only worth 5%, so attendance isn't a must. She's still a fantastic prof and is super helpful if you ever have questions during lecture.
Dr. Helm is so sweet! She is obviously sooo knowledgable in the field of animal science. Make sure to go to class and do the study guides. She is amazing.

Dr. Helm is my favorite professor. She was amazing for intro to apsc and I loved her in animal anatomy and physiology. She grades very fairly and is willing to work with you. She has amazing lectures. As long as you take good notes and study hard, you'll do well.
She is really great! lectures are well structured and relevant and tests have relevant questions. Pay attention, attend lectures, and study your notes. You can get an A.

Dr. Helm is a great professor. Seems to really care about her students and gives good feedback. ALS 2304 is very lecture heavy. To succeed, you have to organize the information and time your studying, as there is a lot of information the digest. In-class TopHat participation is important. The exams are not hard if you study.

Professsor Helm has good powerpoints that she presents every class. She is very knowledgeable and cares about what she's teaching. There is only one homework per test, and one test grade is automatically dropped. She always posts study guides before the tests. Attendance matters, but you can miss a few classes with no penalty.

This is an anatomy class so expect to dedicate a decent amount of time each week to studying. Dr. Helm provides a study guide so make sure to complete that because it tells you what to expect on the exams. There is a take-home portion that takes two hours to complete because it is all diagrams. Dr. Helm is so nice and caring. I loved her.

Dr. Helm is a great professor. Her exams are material taken straight from the powerpoint and she provides extra credit questions. The exams overall are easy and pretty straightforward. She is always willing to respond to every question very kindly. As long as you study the PowerPoints you should do fine in this class. Overall, she's super nice!

She explains the subject so well and makes it easy to understand every time. Gives around 4-6 points for extra credit each test (plus final) but you have to attend because you won't know when it will given out and the slides have fill in the blanks. Easiest class I've ever taken

Dr. Helm is an amazing professor who really cares about her students! She's always open to answering questions during class and is quite accessible outside class too. This course isn't hard at all, but it is a lot of information at once sometimes. Make quizlets and study a few days prior, and you should be good! Her exams are very straightforward.

Dr. Helm was an awesome professor. If you really wanted to, you could skip every single class and just look at the slides for each lecture, but I don't recommend that. I only skipped class a few times, but the way she talks through her lectures makes it soooo easy to understand all the topics.

This was one of my favorite classes. The information was very interesting, and I never felt bored during the lectures. Dr. Helm really wants students to succeed and gives plenty of opportunities to do so. The exams are pretty much straight from the slides so study the slides and study guides and you should do fine.

You don't want to miss any of her classes. She gives extra credit in class after exams. Show up to all of the classes in order to pass the exams. The exams are directly in the powerpoint and I would recommend going over each one fore a few minutes everynight.

My favorite professor at Virginia Tech! She actually cares for her students and how they perform in her class. Very interesting material that is important for a career in APSC. Tests are fairly easy if you spend at least some time studying the PowerPoints and looking over the study guide.

Absolutely loved Dr. Helm! Attendance isn't mandatory but you will want to go in order to get the fill in's for the powerpoint's which is what you need for tests! Class was always interesting and I learned so many new things about the animal industry I didn't know before. Study guides help w/ exams & go/listen to the zoom reviews before exams! :)
Great teacher, and information was very straightforward!
Great professor. Tests are made from the presentations. If you go to class and look over the presentations the tests will be easy.

Dr. Helm is great! Attendance isn't mandatory but I would recommend showing up to each class because she explains everything so great in-person. We don't get much homework and you should do well on the exams if you use the study guide. Also if you talk with her you can tell she truly cares about her students and treats us with a lot of respect.

Dr. Helm is a fine professor, dedicated and excited to teach. The lecture class is not mandatory but necessary to gain missing information. Flashcards, Flashcards, Flashcards, make sure you take them as you go and review them frequently. This class is all about memorization; The content is baseline information for the APSC major and career.

Emma Helm made it very clear that she truly cared about her students. She helped as much as she could by giving study guides and making the exams very doable if you just studied the information from the powerpoint. I enjoyed going to her class and never felt worried about exams. They were always fair and all the work was manageable as well.

Dr. Helm's class was really a lot of fun. The subject material is interesting to begin with, but you can tell that she puts forth the extra effort to make the class more enjoyable. She is also very kind and an easy person to approach and talk to with questions or even just discussing further into the material. Highly recommend!

Dr. Helm is awesome! You can tell she really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. she has fill in the blank presentations which is what you should definitely show up for, but she won't dock your grade for skipping class, she knows things happen. Absolutely love her, very pleasant and welcoming class to be in.

Dr. Helm is a great professor! She goes over all of the material necessary in class and answers any and all questions during her lectures. It's not mandatory to go to class, but she posts her lectures with missing blanks so you should go. As long as your study your notes before tests this class is an easy grade and the material is genuinely fun

Dr. Helm is such a great professor, anyone who gets the chance to take her class should do it. Her class is not hard at all as long as young show up, and study before the tests you should easily get an A. She is very knowledgeable and I found the class to be very interesting.

Professor Helm WANTS us to succeed. She is the only professor I've seen from the department who does open response questions as part of the HW, and I absolutely enjoy it because she is open-minded with her grading and doesn't come off as judgemental at all. I emailed her, fast response, very kind email back. Highly recommend!!!!!!!!!!!! :)

all you have to do to get an a in this class is 1) go to class - literally everything on the test is based on what he says in class, there is no notes posted, no slides posted, so I recommend going to class. 2) ask questions! he's so lenient and super chill and will work with you to understand it. he's chill take his class

Mike is amazing and very chill. If you just show up to class, pay attention, ask questions and take notes you will find the tests SUPER easy. If you are planning on skipping, his class is not for you because none of his lectures are posted online. He gives you a breakdown of what is going to be on each test and helps you prepare for it.
One of my favorites.

Mike is a great teacher.  The first half of the semester was a struggle, but once I got the hang of it, it was a fun class. Interesting stuff for just being microeconomics.  Would recommend him, but take good notes and ask questions if you don't understand.  Lots of opportunities for extra credit.
He's the sweetest guy ever, just come to class and ask questions. If you don't your grade will suffer the consequences.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mike is great. I had him for 1005 and 1006. Personally, I enjoyed 1006 more and felt it was a bit easier. You'll do well if you attend class, pay attention, and take notes. There are lots of graphs so be prepared to draw. He breaks down what the test will be on. You can ask him questions during the tests and he'll help you a lot; I recommend.

The professor is very smart and passionate about his topic and his students, but he misses the mark when it comes to his lectures. He will tell you what he thinks you need for the exam, but his exams can be unreasonably hard.

Great class and great professor! Really helps students understand concepts and wants you to engage in his class - ASK QUESTIONS! Only 4 tests, no cumulative, so make sure you are familiar with your notes. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class. Take good notes, pay attention during the lectures, and do not be afraid to ask questions. He loves students who pay attention and engage with him during class. Being able to draw out graphs and color graphs is extremely helpful. There is no homework, just 4 tests, and no cumulative final test. Great class, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The sweetest and most caring professor ever. It is difficult cause there are only five exams that are the entirety of your grade, but he genuinely gives you the material you need to pass the class. It is a very lecture heavy course and he does not post slides, so you really need to attend class.
Dr Mike is super sweet. He really cares about all his students and is passionate about his teachings. But, just beware that the class is ALL tests. No quizzes, homework, assignments, etc
Very lecture heavy- if you skip class you will fail. There are no assignments, tests only. Lecturers can get confusing sometimes he jumps around- ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mike is probably one of my favorite professors I've ever had, Ive had him for three courses. Ive learned so much in his classes and I would take another class. With that being said, I never got higher than a B in any of his classes. You take 4 exams and those are the only grades. The entire course is lecture based which may be hard for some people.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not enjoy this professor, there will be no slide presentations, in the middle of explaining topics he will go on side tangents, only grades are exams, unclear with definitions and examples, when I asked him for advice or help, I was told to find students that know what's going on for help instead of receiving help from him.
Mike is the best!!!

Mike is awesome! The content is entirely lecture based so take good notes on what he's saying! He not only teaches us economics, but is a very inspirational and caring person in general and will give life advice. He will make jokes with us and always involve students. Go to all the lectures or you will not be prepared for tests.

Mike is a really nice person, but not the best professor. Your grade is based off of 4 tests, no homework or attendance grades, and the tests are hard. There are no powerpoints or notes, so you have to take notes exactly as he says them and hope that it is on the test. Since no notes or powerpoints are ever posted, you can't miss class.
Really clear with lectures and always encourages students to ask questions. Amazing professor would absolutley take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mike is an amazing professor as long as you show up to class and ask questions about the things that you don't understand. Your only grades are 4 tests throughout the semester, so if that isn't your thing, this might not be it for you. He's almost always available for questions though, so the class really isn't difficult at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is really easy if you actually go if you don't go you will fail but if you go and write down everything he repeats you will get an A
Attendance isn't mandatory but he won't post any lecture notes online. He's very nice and loves to get to know his students, but he will call on you in class without warning.
Super fun professor & easy to do well on tests as long as you go to class and participate

Mike is an amazing professor! Your grade for the semester is based just on 4 exams, there isnt much room for error. His lectures are clear but in order to pass this class you must attend the lectures and take notes. Great caring guy that cares about his students but in order to succeed you need to hold yourself accountable throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mike was a great professor to have as a freshman. Although attendance isn't taken, you definitely wont get an A or B if you skip because the only grades you get come from exams. The material on these exams is taken directly from class. Super easy grader though and always rounds up, especially if you are respectful and he sees that you care.

Really sweet person, not my favorite professor. Your only grades are tests, and the tests are fully based on things he says in lecture, but the lectures are hard to take notes on because they're like an hour-long conversation. There are no PowerPoints, lectures are not recorded, and the optional textbook is not really helpful for his tests.

Good professor but a class can be difficult because his lectures are mostly based on him talking. There are barely any notes visibly so you have to write everything based on what he is saying. If you are good at micro/macro then you should be good. The graphs are difficult to understand so pay attention.

There is no textbook or posted lectures. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you miss you will have to get notes from someone else. Class is not too hard if you pay attention and write notes. Ask questions him questions in class if you are confused and he will explain fully.
Lots of fun

Took this class over the summer and he was the best! If you actually go to class and take notes, this class is easy. He's funny, cares about his students, and always makes the lectures fun by incorporating stories. Easily one of the best teachers/profs I've ever had! Can't recommend him enough. There was a textbook, but I got away with using a PDF.
He is very good at communicating the topics he is teaching.

Mike is AMAZING and so involved outside of the classroom within economics. He really loves all of his students. Kind of old-school, lecture, exam style but this is not bad. I think it gets the main points across. Uses lockdown but you will be fine as long as you pay attention, take notes, and study. Go to class! Received extra credit points twice.

Dr. Mike Ellerbrock is possibly one of my favorite professors at Virginia Tech. MAKE SURE TO GO TO CLASS. All of his tests are purely based on his lectures. Everything he teaches makes sense and he works with students to help them understand the content. There are four tests.

Mike is super friendly and genuinely cares about his students. However, his teaching style is not for everyone, and when asked to paraphase, he just uses the same wording, granted he's probably done this for many many years. His class is SOLELY based on exams, so if you study and work hard, you will likely do well.

Going into this class, I felt confident after hearing all of the good reviews from past students. I quickly realized his teaching was not all that it was racked up to be. Everyone I talked to in class agreed that his lectures were hard to follow and he didn't provide good answers when you ask questions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor, 4 tests throughout semester which make up entire grade. Go to class and ask questions. Nice guy, great teacher, absolute comedian in lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mike is a very nice guy but his lecterns can be all over the place and sometimes confusing. The TA definitely helped a lot because she was able to explain in a simpler form. Both Mike and the TA were happy and open to help students and answer any questions. Attendance is not taken but coming to the lectures is very important.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mike is great!! Class is fun and enjoyable and he teaches extremely well and provides valuable life lessons as well. His grades are all the exams, but he prepares you well for them and they're multiple choice. Go to class! and take good notes and youll be more than prepared for the exams. also, somehow he remembers faces and names.. very impressive
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mike God forbid you call him Dr. Ellerbrock was one of the worst professors Ive ever had. He barely completes his sentences, gets confused by his own words, and is just a crappy professor all the way around. Economics has always been my favorite subject, now I hate it. If you must take this course please try to find another professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mike is one of the best professors I have ever had. He actually makes the class enjoyable. Class isn't mandatory, but if you don't go, you won't pass. Majority of the time his test questions will be word for word what he says in class, so if you take good notes you'll do really well. He really cares about his students and wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mike is really a gem! He will work with you if you need help, but you need to show up for class and ask questions when you are confused. Your grade comes from 4 exams. As long as you study, go to class, take good notes, and speak up you will have a great experience. Seriously he is the kindest professor and really wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is very personable. Although I dont understand economics he made it very easy. He uses a lot of examples and graphs so I recommend having a notebook to draw in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Mike was hands down one of the best professors I could have had for a freshman year during COVID. He took the time to get to know us (our majors, what year we were, what we were interested in) even with hundreds of us in the class. Your grade is solely based on exams but he did allow our class to be open note (won't happen in a normal year). 10/10

Im surprised with my experience with Ellerbrock after hearing these positive reviews. 1st, he only gives your grade from 4 exams. No extra credit. No HW. No boost. And I emailed him ONCE, wrote a very formal, kind email to ask if he will curve grades. And his reply was extremely rude, discouraging and immature. He replied with CAPS and !!!! ��
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mike's class was the kind where the grade you get is the one you earned. I wouldn't take his class again only because the material was not of my interest. 4 tests are your only grades so you need to fully understand the material. When covid hit, he made our entire grade of only 3 tests to "help us" but instead made it harder. But a nice dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have taken 3 of Mike's classes. He is very clear at the beginning of the semester that if you just come to class or rewatch lectures (while we are online) you will pass. I honestly don't understand how people can do poorly in his classes when if you just attend lectures and pay attention without taking notes you could still get a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professors who voice their political agenda in class, like Mike, display the lowest interest of educating their students. Also, if you enjoy being graded entirely on four exams that are filled with typos and cryptic non-subject-related questions, Mike Ellerbrock is the economics professor you're looking for. Exercise caution when enrolling.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have had Mike for 3 classes now and he is seriously the greatest professor ever! So sweet and encouraging. He takes time to know his students and ensures the best experience in all of his classes! I wish he could teach all of my classes!

Best professor I will ever have. I'm so greatfull to have had the chance to take the course with him. He cares about each student, and if you engage in class and answer or ask questions he will give you " an A for the day". His tests are a little tricky but not bad if you take detailed notes.

Mike was such a good professor. While the only grades for the class are the four tests, as long as you listen to his lectures you will be fine. Mike is really a great professor who takes the time to get to know his students. I will definetly try to take a course with him again!

Took online in 2020. All lectures. Mike is a laid-back, good-natured person. He is forgiving, but will only give so much leeway. The only grades are test grades, but honestly if you go to/watch the lectures you will be fine. He is always happy to answer questions. Don't forget about this class though. None of the tests are dropped.

Mike is the best! He'll teach you as much about life as about economics. He cares about his students and takes the time to learn people's names, even in huge lectures. No matter your major, take a class with Mike before you graduate.
