reviews.comment: Mike taught a very hard topic in a very understandable and realistic way. he gave a lot of real life examples and took the time to go through everything in great detail.  He made a giant lecture hall seem small by encouraging questions. Great life lessons built in. I would recommend everyone take him for their Econ alternate. Best professor yet.

One of the most passionate professors out there! The fact that he makes an attempt to learn everyone's names (in a lecture class) is really impressive. If you go to office hours, he will try to help you as best as he can (one on one) just so you can understand the material. Highly recommend taking his classes. Also, he cracks jokes often.
Really nice guy. One of my favorite professors. Really inspiring. I don't even like econ, but I loved his class.

Mike is a fantastic professor. He gets to know all of his students by name, even in a lecture class. He encourages learning and understanding the material, rather than memorizing. Make sure you to go class, as he will tell you exactly what is going to be on the exams. The final is not cumulative. The textbook is not necessary. Take his classes!

Mike is a great teacher, easy to understand and will never trick you on tests. Final isn't cumulative, no outside work, and he works hard to make sure you understand everything. He is funny and interesting. I loved having him!!

Mike Ellerbrock is an exceptional professor at Virginia Tech, and is probably one of the best ones that you could have. If you are ever considering taking an Economics course, please request Mike Ellerbrock. Every student needs to experience his teaching at least once in their Virginia Tech college career.

Mike tells you everything you need to know in class. Class isn't mandatory; he doesn't post online notes and tests are easy if you go but hard if you skip. No outside work except for reading every few weeks. He's welcoming and friendly and very much wants his students to do well. I would definitely recommend Mike!

Great teacher and a super nice person, overall. If you go to class and pay attention, he gives you most of the test questions word for word. Extremely helpful if you need it. I highly suggest taking his class.

Great teacher. He's very busy so he tries to help you get the most out of your classtime to minimize time spent at home other than for further clarification. He also truly cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. Very willing to help. I highly recommend taking his class, as well as taking a trip to talk to him during office hours.
Great teacher/guy. More then willing to help when asked. Will remember your name in a class of 70 people after hearing it once, amazing!

Mike is the best professor I have had yet at Virginia Tech.  He genuinely cares about his students and about his career.  He knows how to really grab your attention and can make just about anything sound interesting.

Mike has an amazing way to engage his audience and get people excited to learn the material. He is very practical, and tells us how he disagrees with most teaching styles. He is funny, too. He genuinely cares for each and every student, memorizes your name, and wants to help you or refer you to his TA when you need of assistance.

Mike is the best professor I've had yet at Tech! He is a terrific guy and a great teacher. Religion and Science is really easy and interesting the way he teaches it. He gives out his phone number to call ANYTIME. He's a sweet heart and kinda reminds me of santa clause :P

He is an amazing teacher that really wants to get to know his students on a personal level.He makes an effort to learn students names. He maps out the test for which makes studying easy. If you attend class and take notes you have everything you need for the test. He is an excellent speaker. He is also always available for help.

Mike is a GREAT guy. I recommend him to anyone. He truely cares about his students and wants you to learn the material.  He keeps a slow pace and keeps it interesting. Great speaker as well.  I would recommend him for Macro econ; however, he was fuzzy in Micro (AAEC 1005) because he hadnt taught the class in awhile.  TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Mike is a good guy. The class is pretty slow paced, he goes over each topic about four times to make sure everyone catches it, so sometimes it gets boring, but if all you have to do to get an A is actually go to class and stay awake, I say it is worth it. Has amazing review sessions where he essentially maps out the test. Awesome professor.

I had him for AAEC 1006 and 4344.  He is a great teacher and seems to remember EVERYONE, even in a huge lecture class.  He was always extremely helpful and makes sure everyone understands everything.  Interesting in class, so you stay awake even if you don't like the subject.  Always helpful.  Definitely recommend.

this cat rocks!!! he doesnt move on until hes sure u understand the material, he gives you his phone numbers and tells u to call him anytime, ANYTIME!!! and he is always availiable to help you in his office, but teacher ever
Economics isn't my thing, but he teaches in a way that makes you appreciate it. He's a great teacher and a really cool guy...I'd recommend him to anyone!
Great teacher!
He is so crazy! He is a great teacher, and always clarifies all the material before a test.
This is the best class.  Mike is really easy to understand, and clarifies the subject really well.  His tests aren't that hard, and he goes over everything on the test.

Dr. Hogan has the hardest tests of all 1106 professors. He consistently claims his questions are fair, but after the first test, even students who had him for 1105 agreed it was nothing like before. He's passive aggressive when you ask questions. Just take anyone else.

overall good professor, this class is def harder than BIOL 1105, even if you took AP Bio bc unit 2 and 3 were basically not covered by AP Bio at all. class is mostly just understanding and memorizing concepts

Trust me, I watched the videos before class. I took IB HL Bio in HS. All the Bio classes are lecture heavy but I HEAVILY dislike his approach to iClickers being based on accuracy, he blows by them so fast, and some of the questions weren't even in the provided videos prior to class. He's also rude and passive aggressive when asking a question.

Dr. Hogan is a great professor. The pros of taking his class is interesting lectures and clear objectives for what to learn and study. He's a very organized and reasonable professor. I always felt prepared for exams. The only con of this class I can think of is there are no curves on the exams. Reasonable amount of extra credit though.

Technically there is a textbook but honestly I didn't touch it all year. If you took AP bio in high school then you'll be fine. He does use an iclicker but you don't have to buy a physical remote for the class. Overall he's a great guy and very open to questions.

Hogan is a very straightforward teacher. Love his lectures. The homework is usually textbook readings and videos with fill in notes, but the only graded hw is a 10-ish question assignment. I got thru without the textbook and occasionally doing hw notes. He spends half the class lecturing and the half is group activity. Very helpful with questions.
Great professor and would definitely take again. The course material is difficult and the tests are weighted heavy, but he is great with his lectures, and the group activities are helpful.

Dr. Hogan is a very good teacher, he offers a lot of office hours and doesn't lecture for too long. Each class we have group assignment that has TA's that are very nice and helpful. 

Class is mandatory because there are iClicker questions that you can only answer in class that are for a grade. 

He also posts videos, so no textbook needed!

Dr. Hogan is pretty good professor, it's clear he is very passionate about what he does. His tests are very application based and sometimes the wording can be tricky. He does require a textbook for the course; however, I personally did not buy it, and I ended with a 92.54% (maybe could have gotten that A with taking notes).

Tough class, but Dr. Hogan does what he can to make it manageable. Do his class the way it's meant to be done (watch video lectures prior, pay attention & take more notes in class) and you'll be fine! He has many useful materials and resources to help you study. Lectures can get boring, but stay committed and build a routine as the semester goes on

The course itself is challenging, especially for those who haven't taken AP bio, but Dr. Hogan is kind and helpful. He gives good study tips and practice tests while some other professors do not. Make sure to watch the videos before his lectures and make note of what he goes over in class because the info in the mini lesson are on the tests.

I had him for a winter course and as an asynch professor he was one of the best I'd had. He was great at giving feedback on discussion posts and tests and helpful if you had any issues with the class. On the final test, I got locked out early but he was really helpful and did everything he could to try and get it back. Very understanding professor.

He says taking AP Bio doesn't matter- it 100% does. If you haven't taken AP Bio, I could see the clear struggles someone would have. He uses a watch the lectures beforehand, and then briefly goes over them in class. However, he doesn't seem to care about his students and always threatens the honor code if you ask for extra credit.

Professor Hogan was a great professor and a nice guy; the course is difficult, but his teaching style of learning the material beforehand and using the lecture/class time as a review was helpful for me and he also encouraged peer work on the activities at the end of classes.

This class has a lot of similar aspects to AP bio, and if you had already taken that class you should be fine. Even if he says that taking AP bio doesn't make a difference, it does. Without AP bio I can see how this class can become difficult.

Dr. Hogan passion in his teachings but goes on tangents. Gen bio is hard and he does not provide any extra credit like other professors. IClickers tests you on material that you are currently learning and are accuracy graded. Dr. Hogan is good for that as his office hours he's open to help. Grade-wise, I would go for a different professor.

Dr. Hogan is very personable and is always willing to help if you are confused or need assistance with understanding material. His tests cover the material he goes over in class, and he gives practice tests that are very helpful.

He as a teacher is fine. He answers questions thoroughly in office hours, but can sometimes go off on a tangent during class. The class itself can be difficult if you haven't taken AP Bio. It's important to learn the material prior to class!!! Gave 1 point of extra credit on the final. (Like atp just don't give extra credit)

Overall was a good guy. You need to watch the lecture videos or read the textbook (which is more in depth and helpful) before class to be prepared. Practice questions and activities in groups are graded each class so must be present for those grades. Tests are worth a lot, but are pretty similar to AP biology and textbook notes

His tests are worth 70% of your overall grade, meaning if you do bad on one singular test, your grade is done for. As well, his "lectures" are videos you watch before coming to class, along with just rereading off the same slides during lecture classes.

Professor Hogan was one of the kindest people I have ever met. He is such a sweet guy and truly wants students to succeed, thoroughly answers questions and makes sure you understand before moving on. Bio is just super content heavy in general so just try a bit and you'll be fine

Awesome professor! Go to office hours, he is extremely kind and will explain things to you if you are confused. Lectures convey material very well and he is honestly really funny. Tests were extremely fair. (study extra hard for test 3). Loved the course. Would definitely take for 1106.

While the videos cover all the material, Professor Hogan does a great job on his in class lectures. This class is exceedingly difficult for a freshman class, with that being said, Professor Hogan does a GREAT job providing support as long as you apply yourself. His office hours are the best!

Professor Hogan is great. He clearly knows what he is talking about and finds a way to make it accessible to everyone. I think he's the best of the introductory bio professors.  There's a manageable amount of homework but that is a course thing not a him thing.
i will join in

Overall, as a person I found Dr. Hogan a bit sexist. He was a really good professor and one of the best bio professors I had as a bio major. His exams were straightforward. I took the class in the summer so it was a small class. We had one major group project that was pretty easy and straightforward, so long as you follow his guidelines.

Dr. Hogan was a fine teacher. A classical college professor I feel, Hogan was helpful and understanding with his students, but was still stern as one would expect a college professor to be. Watching the video lectures and going over the study guides is enough to pass, I generally got Bs doing this.

he is a very good at teaching. you use iclicker to track attendance. you get 2/5 points for attendance and can get 5/5 for getting three of the iclicker questions correct. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS AND REVIEW SESSIONS. if you do the lecture videos and study the homework quizzes & attend office hours and review sessions you will be golden.

Nice guy, but at times it didn't feel like he did knew to what extent we were supposed to learn the material. That was frustrating and led to miscommunications in regard to what content was on the test. Online teaching has to be hard but the guy should at least review the lessons thoroughly before giving a lecture. Fine other that.

Dr. Hogan will make it work for you if you display a solid work ethic in his class. reviews.comment: He's okay. not the best professor you could have for bio 1105 or 1106 but certainly not the worst. His exams are harder than most bio classes and his lectures can be boring sometimes but he really wants us to succeed.

Dr. Hogan was very caring, and if you make an effort, he will take note of it. He likes students that make an effort to come to office hours, and will even remember your name. He is good at explaining things, and his lectures are interesting. He is also witty and funny. The workload for the class isnt bad, but it is study heavy.

The class discusses current issues relating to human biology, and he wants to have the class participate. As more issues come up though, he tends to express his viewpoint in a different way compared to the differing opinion.
Great teacher! Exams are difficult but he works with you. Honestly a great guy

Hogan really cares about the success of his students. He uses a flipped classroom format, which allows for a lot of review and questions in the actual lecture. He is always prepared to answer many questions and ensure that material is clear with the class. Additionally, he gives good feedback. best advice: study the activities and do practice Q's!!

Dr. Hogan is the bomb. He cares about his students and their grades, as long as they express interest in improving it. He is quick to reply to emails, and is very helpful during office hours. He tries to explain more difficult concepts easily and typically, does a good job. His tests are hard, but if you study smart, you should do just fine.

reviews.comment: Principles is a flipped classroom, and that's true for all profs. Hogan did a great job of explaining the material in class and the examples he gave in lecture helped a lot. He is great at answering questions, and is very accessible. Use the learning objectives to study for the exams, show up and pay attention, and the class isn't really that hard.
He taught the material well, but the class was set up so that the students were required to teach themselves at home beforehand.

The pre lecture and lecture give you everything you need to get a good grade on the four tests. The book is not helpful. Class is technically not mandatory, but there are clicker questions that are graded and you have to be there to answer. Also, every class has a group activity to incorporate the material and you need to be there to contribute.

All tests are based off of online lectures you watch before class. I took AP Bio in high school and got a 4 on the test so a good amount of the material I had seen before which made things easier. Class is review over the topic, clicker questions (for completion!), and an activity. Good prof!
Very Caring and engaging.

If you can take Dr. Hogan's class I highly recommend it. He is very friendly, helpful, and clear to his students. If the class is confused he will stop to address confusion. He also suggested anyone to take his 1106 class over the winter which was a breeze and saved me from 1106 in the spring which people struggled with.
If you go to office hours he's more than happy to help but you have to take the first step. He explains things really well one on one.

Dr. Hogan is really smart and can explain the concepts really well. However, he doesn't because of the "reverse classroom" bull. Tests are worth way too much of your grade, there is no extra credit, and the long, irrelevant activities take too much time to do and 50% of the time have no relevance to the tests.  There are no pluses or minuses either
Reverse classroom makes you apply the material to real-life which is helpful. He's a really nice guy and if you go to his office hours he'll help you out! I'd recommend him he's a good guy

Quizzes on 2 chapters a week, some with an unrealistic amount of information. Assigns quizzes due the same week as his exams. Good with extra credit and homework to raise the grade but a lot of workload.

I highly recommend Dr. Hogan's class. Hes funny and does demonstrations to help you understand concepts. His tests aren't easy and neither are his quizzes, but you can do the work. Read along in the textbook! Hes better than any other freshman bio professor I've heard of, and I plan to take one of his classes again int he future.

very easy if you pay attention and skim the book. Hes very funny and knows college students and treats them as equals. Hes like a kid really. theres advanced topics but his tests reduce them to basic concepts

Dr.Hogan is a great teacher! His lectures are sharp, and he understands the students. If you read the chapters and follow his powerpoints, its a pretty basic class! But a warning, Dr. Hogan tests emphasize charts and figures taken from the book, as well as class videos. Also should be good at memorizing vocab! His class is great for visual learners
Extremely difficult for a general class. I have heard of much better, more helpful professors.
1. Absurd amount of "classwork," homework, and Peer plus. 2. Class is completely meaningless, but mostly required attendance. 3. Very slow and inconsistent assignment grading.

An okay professor, but the amount of "classwork" and homework is a lot. The TAs are incredibly slow, so one week you would be at an 'A' and after four weeks, your grade drops to a 'B-/C+.' The exam is alright. Would help if we could resubmit the work and not accept the points deducted because the instructions are unclear half of a time.

reviews.comment: Professor Ellis is amazing. Her lectures are very interesting and to the point, which makes understanding concepts very easy. She genuinely cares a lot about her students and she's very sweet. Would definitely take her classes again.

all profs teach the class with identical format + content. so whoever your prof is shouldn't make a big diff in your grade. i personally loved her, not sure why her rating is so low. super sweet and caring. exams  pretty easy, projects kinda long/hard so start early. strict on project/lab deadlines, so don't expect TAs/profs to accommodate for you
Course is taught entirely through online recording and readings.

reviews.comment: Lectures were helpful, not too much work outside of the projects. However she messed up my grade on a project, when I talked to her about it in class she said to email her about it. She never responded to my email or changed my grade which caused me to get a B instead of B+.

reviews.comment: She does not taking extenuating circumstances into consideration. She unfairly listens to other people in terms of grade curves, but probably won't curve your grade. She did not teach anything in class. Going to class was a waste of time. She could barely answer questions too. She only assigned online content pages which were helpful if u can teach yourself well. Projects were hard and took a long time. She was not understanding to external circumstances either. I would not recommend her as a teacher.
easy class, you learn most of the material by yourself through the stuff in canvas.

reviews.comment: Margaret Ellis does NOT care about you, or your problems. I have reached out multiple times for assistance, only to be ignored or, on the rare instance of being acklowdged, have my problems be completely disregarded. This has been going on since the beginning of the semester.

The lectures are practically not useful for your time, but her online content pages are very helpful and teach you for most of the semester. The class is easy, and if you need further help, the TA's are helpful as well. Just don't procrastinate!

Her and a lot of the TAs (but definitely not all of them) are really rude. All content is taught through online videos and the lecture is treated like a study hall that no one attends. Fortunately, it is a really easy class content-wise, with test questions repeated from earlier quizzes and free hundreds from projects if you start them in time.

Professor Ellis is amazing! The class is very easy if you just start your projects early and study for the quizzes by reviewing past quizzes and questions on the content pages. The assesments are literally mostly just repeated questions from the previous quizzes. You don't really have to go to her class to do well, but I recommend still going.

Welcome to Yappsville! Prof. Ellis is the mayor. Lectures are completely useless, she isn't good at actually teaching, and can be rude/delusional. Content/class isn't hard, just prepare to learn most of it through youtube and other online tutorials. TAs are great and can absolutely help, so go to office hours. Dont waste your time going to class.
I really really dont like her.
bruh all she does is yap yap yap and there is nothing helpful. there's so much work ive never ever had so much homework its not even funny.

I've went to like 7 of her lectures total this entire semester, and 3 of them were for the in-class assessment/tests that are proctored. It took 4 lectures to realize that this professor really isn't that good or fun to be around. Everything you need for this class is posted on canvas. Not a bad class, but a bad professor.

Rude and uncaring. Shared a concern with her and she told me to stop complaining and just do my work. Also followed syllabus for a late policy, and when she didn't count my project I told her I can submit for 10 percent late. She changed the syllabus to 10 points and gave me a zero on the project. No feedback nor any compassion or understanding Bad

reviews.comment: she is worst possible professor I have ever seen. Too harsh and never cared about anything and judge pretty first. Its like being in the army camp in her class. And does not show any respect to any TA or students. Department should take strong steps and investigate against her.
Honestly not a very difficult class if you've taken ap csa, attendance not mandatory and just complete the labs on time and you'll be good

Margaret Ellis is very kind, and she cares about her students, but she doesn't know how to teach. During the lectures, she just answers people's questions from Piazza for 50 minutes. A lot of my projects (despite following all the guidelines perfectly) lost points for not commenting the way she wanted. The coursework itself is very easy.

Ellis was incredibly unprofessional and disrespectful as a professor. She did not seem to care for her students, and was very dismissive of issues. If possible, aim to take a different professor. This one will make your CS journey hell.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very rude professor, lots of homework and labs that are a very tiny part of the grade, 0 feedback on some assignments that are graded harshly. Class feels like a high school class calling attendance and taking points off if you don't show up this is college not high school.

awful and not caring for any of her students. Doesn't even matter if WW3 happens, you need to go to lab or you lose all your points. Not compassionate with students problems and does not really help when you have the need. Does not communicate well requirements either or listen to questions. If you take her u might as well just look up YouTube vids

Cons: Neglects student concerns; disinterested in teaching; Dull, unhelpful lectures; most learning is self-directed via modules; Punishes students for VT system issues(via point deductions); Inefficient time-wasting policies for labs, assignments; Heavy tests; Lots of busy work
Pros: Holds office hours; Available outside of class; Knows Java well.

She really cares about teaching and understands students' difficulties in learning Java and other CS topics (especially people who are new to coding). She is very approachable and truly cares about students' growth in the course topics. She answers our questions both in class and during office hours with passion.

Answers questions via a discussion portal so anyone can ask a question at any time of the day. She does her teaching through online modules and if you pay attention the exams are not bad at all and the labs use a lot of the same code as in the modules. Lectures aren't mandatory but if you are struggling on a project, she goes through useful info.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: While the class was technically in-person, all the lectures were recordings from previous online classes. So really, it was just an async class. Every week, there's a decent amount of video lectures to watch with a section quiz at the end, but you can always speed up or rewatch the videos if you want. Projects aren't difficult, but start early!

I do not understand why the midterms and the final test are weighted more than the huge amount of other work that we need to do (labs, projects, quizzes, codworkouts, opendsa, etc.). She simply does not teach, I tried emailing her several times in which I did not even receive a response. The interactions I had with her made me confirm she was rude.

Doesnt actually lecture, just had video recordings from past years posted (which are mediocre at best). An insane amount of work for a 3 credit hour class. In response to complaints about my groupmates not participating in the project I was told to just do their code for them. Professor was rude and condescending in interactions I had with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Likes to do group projects. Probably to make it easier to grade. Doesn't take into consideration poor group members. States that if group members don't do the work you should do it for them to meet deadlines. Still gives the other members the same grade even though they don't do the work.

Rude, unnecessary hostile, lazy and boring. She doesnt even teach, you just watch her lectures from past years. I had a situation in which 5 of my 6 professors gave me extensions, and guess who didnt even care? I dont know a single person in my class who likes her and her class. Coding is fun, but surprisingly enough she can make it boring.

I felt that prof. Ellis really cared about her students the entire semester. She was always looking for ways to improve/get feedback. 2114 is just a hard class, no matter who you get, and I think you'd be lucky to have her as a prof. rather than anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is somebody who understands programming and Java inside out. I feel like I will walk away from this class having a full understanding of data structures. The problem is that she isn't the best in terms of explaining things, but she's very knowledgeable and if you just put a little more effort in understanding her, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: After taking three years of CS classes in high school, I was greatly disappointed by Virginia Tech. While I have learned a lot in this class, the way Professor Ellis teaches is boring and uninspiring. There's way too much work and poorly written instruction to go through for each lab. This is not the way CS is meant to be taught.

The description for projects and labs are extremely awful, sometimes you can't even read what's her meaning of the steps. Can't even read what's the feedback of the project meaning. Huge amount of work with only a 3 credit class.
Rude teacher, extremely condescending.

The class as a whole is okay. I definately learned a lot from it, and Prof. Margaret Ellis gives a lot of lectures which are okay, however, she doesn't engage much with her class at all. She isn't at all a helpful professor to reach out too. Every question I've asked her wasn't helpful and you can tell she doesn't care about you or your concerns.

Understand some Java before taking this class. The whole class is assuming you know Java.  She's not a bad teacher, but she's a coder at heart, which makes her a more difficult teacher to deal with in terms of explaining. Still, Ellis is one of the best in the department. It's manageable.
Decent guy who has very bad handwriting. He doesn't even try to make it legible. Do not sit in the back, or else it'll look like you're copying down Chinese characters. You have been warned.

Professor Martin was a very knowledgeable professor; you will get a good grade in his class as long as you show up, do the homework (and extra credit if wanted), and practice/study the material (practice tests, etc.).
Possibly the worst professor I've ever had.
Cannot teach properly.
Bad teacher, just does practice questions and barely teaches.

ACIS 2116 is a class I'll never forget due to how complex, rigorous, and annoying it was. I'm not an ACIS major, and the class made me feel like I'm learning more than I'll ever need to know. The HW and class hours are as helpful in preparing you for the exam as Slusher's AC (Slusher doesn't have AC). Overall, a boring and overly strict class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Martin is very no-nonsense and blunt but is a good professor and cares about his students. You will pass if you do ALL of the assignments, complete your homework with care. He offers lots of options for extra credit. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS MULTIPLE TIMES BEFORE THE EXAMS. They are nearly identical to the questions you will get on the exam.

Great professor overall, you'll get a very good grade as long as you pay attention and take it seriously. He offers a LOT of extra credit (homeworks, once a certain threshold in points is reached, also count as extra credit). The test questions don't require much critical thinking and many are directly borrowed from the practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He brings his dog to class (doesn't get better). Only ranked a 4 difficulty because there's a lot of material to cover. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are a lot of extra credit opportunities if you go, and he gives you all the questions on the test beforehand

One of the best professors I've had so far. He really cares for the class and his students. Attendance definitely correlates with good grades, also make sure to do the practice exams and really understand the methodology. Only ranked as a 4 in difficulty because the material is so vast, otherwise would be a 1 or 2/5 in difficulty.

Professor Martin does a great job giving you all the tools you need, go to class, participate in lectures and you get out of class early and get a baseline understanding. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS, test questions are either 1:1 from the practice one or have slight changes. I used ChatGPT to reverse engineer answers and know what to do for test.

I took the class with one of his graduate students (K. Kinskie), and her class, homework, and overall attendance felt worthless when preparing for an exam. Professor Martin takes the class too seriously when, in reality, it's an intolerable, extra, and forgettable course for all business majors. The HW was a useless pain in the ass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: IF YOU DO NOT GET AN A IN THIS CLASS IT IS COMPLETELY YOUR FAULT. He literally gave us every single question that was going to be on the test before the test came around. Anyone who ranks him as hard for ACIS 2116 simply did not try. The guy is great. He is funny and he brings his dog to class. What's not to love?
not a very good professor
He's the goat

Really great guy, great professor. Class isn't too hard, just pay attention in class and you should be fine. He gives out reviews so using those to study for quizzes and exams are very helpful. One thing is that he cold calls on students, so beware. His adorable dog comes to class too and it's probably the best thing. Ends class early some days too
Tough exams, but such a good guy and teacher.
I like him a lot make sure you do the practice tests and you'll be fine

I had a TA/grad student for this class, it was pretty much just lectures but it was fine. The good thing about this class was all the resources they gave you. There were explanations for every HW assignment and super helpful practice exams + videos.
Not a good professor

Eric Martin is one of the best professors I have had at tech. He expects a lot from you but he truly wants everyone in the class to succeed. He also gives a lot of helpful test prep and has videos explaing how to do all of the problems. He is also the head of 2116 so he knows more than the ta's would.

Professor Martin is absolutely the best accounting teacher I've had and it has been a pleasure being in his class. Yes the class does require a lot of work and studying, but when you put the effort in you will get an amazing grade. DO THE PRACTICE exams  cannot stress this enough. He truly cares about his students. Going to miss Winnie his dog

Martin is one of the best professors I have had. People think he is tough but if you work hard, ask questions, and go to him if you need help, he will help you. I failed the first exam and went to him for help after, and succeeded on all of the other exams. Also brings his dog to class which rocks.

I had a TA (Cecilia Sun) instead of Eric Martin. The lecture took the entire class, take notes nothing special. Prof Martin's Canvas and study material for the exams are super helpful. The practice exams are one for one just like the actual exam. Connect assignments are extremely annoying, long, and wayyy more confusing than the actual exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Martin is very straightforward and is by far the best professor I have had. Would recommend him 10/10.

Did'nt actually have him but rather his TA/Grad Student. I love that gives out practice exams as it helps you study. However, the homeworks is just irrationally hard and takes forever to do. Plus they don't help you for the exams.

Super nice and great teacher, I sat in the front and got cold called a lot but if I got something wrong he would just laugh it off with me. All his tests are based on practice quizzes so its pretty easy to get a good grade in his class as long as you study early. He also brings his dog to class, great dude and great teacher
He is a good guy but cannot clarify things well. He goes through problems as if you know how to do them already. Nice and easy person, bad at teaching.

I had Eric this past spring instead of a TA for 2116 and it definitely helped. This class is very hard but if you show up, study for the exams, and ask questions you will be fine. He's really nice if you get to know him and just wants to help his students. Studying and doing the practice tests are CRITICAL or else you will fail the class!!!

I think that this is less of a professor problem and more of a class structure problem. The amount of time put toward homework and watching lectures needed to achieve a good grade is absolutely outrageous. If you are planning to juggle two summer classes along with this course, DO NOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you use the resources he provides you will do very well

Dr. Martin is not only highly intelligent in what he teaches, but he's also kind and does everything he can to help students. He has practice exams with EVERY SINGLE exam problem. He also has the sweetest dog that he brings to class nicknamed "chubby puppy" and she loves to walk around class getting pets from everyone and napping under your desk.

He is really a great professor and genuinely cares about his students. He wants his students to succeed and will take the time out of his day to answer any questions or go over exams with you. He also gives you the material that will be on the exams, literally hands you the exact questions. Super cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Accounting is one of my weakest subjects so i was very worried for this class. I had martin as my actual professor and it is the main reason i passed the class. He makes the exams and he creates a practice exam that you can do (do all the problems) and its almost exact to the exams. As well he actually wants his students to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took it with Martin. He writes the exams so go to class and he will tell you "this will be on the test". Do the practice exams to study. It's long (100+ questions) but some of them are literally copied and pasted onto the actual exam. He asks students questions, so do the sb (and hw if you can) before the class so that way you know how to answer.
I think he is a great teacher! You Just half to meet him half way and not be rude. AMAZING TEACHER just study

reviews.comment: He gets a bad rep but he really wants his students to succeed. Make sure to ask questions in class if you do not understand a concept, he is so helpful and willl make sure you get a concept right. I took his class during the fall semester and really enjoyed it.

My class was taught by Fernandez (a GTA). She did practice problems during class and held good office hours. reviews.comment: Got a perfect on the last 2 exams. Never went to class but I really put in the work outside of it. STUDY the practice tests until you know every single answer. Prof is a really great guy and does want you to do well, you just need to put in the work. This isn't an easy class it's.. accounting. A lot of these reviews are just people that didn't try.

This is my second time taking the class because I had to withdrawal the first time. He is very rude and loves to embarrass his students. He is the least understanding professor I've ever had and all my peers who have taken him have their own bad stories about him. Make sure you study the practice tests that is the only way to pass the exams.

Awful, claims grades are based on attendance but if you show up he just wastes time playing with his dog. He genuinely cares about students... getting honor coded and brags about how happy he gets. This class is very hard and the homeworks all take ages to complete.

reviews.comment: Simply a terrible professor, but theres not much you can do about it because everybody is underneath his supervision. Go Hokies!

reviews.comment: The entire class is based on the exams with averages being in the 60s and no curves were given. A week is required to get a b on an exam with the homework consistently taking 8 hours.

reviews.comment: Dude gives the worst review sessions of all time. Just seems like he can never do anything nice for his students, just feels like one of those professors who has to be the rude one.

didn't have eric martin but TA ; if you can take acis 2116 at your community college DO IT. rlly hard class but do able, do the practice exam bc they are the question pool for the actual exam. sbs & hws during the week and 3 exams including final , going to class is not rlly helpful except for review days

Eric Martin is a very nice man and his dog is cute. However, it is hard to ask questions bc most time he won't help you. His tests are extremely difficult and so is the homework. This was the hardest class I have ever taken. All classes are taught by TAs. If you don't come to class you will fail. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His recorded lectures wont teach you anything, he basically just reads off the powerpoint and doesnt elaborate or give further explanation. I had him 2115 before covid and 2116 during, he did the same thing for in person lectures. Class/ homework doesnt prepare you for the exams, the textbook will be your best friend.

*from an acis major* Had him for 1504 last year and for 2116. Definitely favors his female students. His lectures BARELY skimmed the material covered on the exam, and HW was way easier than the exams as well. Basically, the exams were impossible because we were not provided with the resources to learn the material. If you can take anyone else.

Lectures were prerecorded, but was just the prof reading directly off a powerpoint. I couldn't bear to get up at 8, so I didn't attend the in-person chapter reviews - they might have helped. Homework is easy, but the tests (80% of the grade) are much more difficult. Overall I'd consider it a pretty poor class, but I might just hate accounting.

reviews.comment: Professor Martins class is not easy and is a bit exam heavy. However, he is very reachable to students and is a great lecturer. If you do the homework and use his review pages, you will be just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Martin is the general professor for this class and teaches with his lectures, but the sections each have individual professors. Professor Martin is unsympathetic, and it's extremely hard to understand his tone of voice. Take with another professor if you can. Also, this class is much easier than ACIS 2115.

Coach is a great professor but taking his class online is extremely boring. All lectures are pre-recorded as well as all practice questions. The only time you can get extra help is during office hours. Tests are extremely hard but you are given a ton of resources to use for studying. This class is hard so keep that in mind.

*TAKEN FALL 2020 DURING COVID-19* Eric Martin is an amazing Professor. He wants you to do well, I promise. But you have to be willing to put in the work. Accounting 2116 is not an easy course. But he really gives you everything you need to pass. I went from a 42/F to a 84/B in his class. He helped me get on a good track and he will help you to!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: (Taken Fall 2020) Eric Martin is a good guy. He's definitely the most fair professor I've had. The only problem being that since this class is a ton of students, it's very lecture heavy and your exam grades are most of your entire grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Martin was a great professor for my first excel class at VT and in my accounting class now. Everyone thinks he's rude but it made class a little bit more interesting when he called someone out. Lectures are posted online & in person, says exam questions during them and bolds questions on exam. Very involved in VT and business school.

The class itself is easy and he does teach it effectively, but if you're looking for a professor who clearly cares about his job and respects his students, Eric Martin is NOT that man. He's sexist, makes comments in class that prove he doesn't like what he teaches, and is just plain rude in an attempt to be a "cool" professor. Cute dog though.

Prof. Martin is a fine professor who doesn't seem to care much about the material. I'm told that this is his last semester teaching it, and due to coronavirus and us being online, he clearly just wants the semester to be over. When we were at school, he was a funny guy who brought his dog in. He sometimes said things that upset some students.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A good professor who gives you the opportunities to get an A, you just have to study for the test and pay attention to his lectures. Also, do the HW. There isn't much and it's an easy grade booster. Honestly, for a mandatory class, Freshman are lucky to have him. Just put in the effort and stay up with the material throughout the course.

i didn't love his class but it's a fairly easy A. he posts his lectures online so really the only days you have to go to class are on exam days--would still recommend going though. he's a nice guy and his office hours are helpful if you feel confused. he's also the only prof for this class so you're kinda stuck with him.

Eric Martin was a mediocre professor. He had his moments when I appreciated him, but most of the time he seemed like an ass. If you're a business major though, you pretty much have to take his class. I did appreciate the lecture videos, they helped a lot with studying for tests and early class times.

I stopped going to this class because I couldn't get myself up at 8am, but when I did go to class, I enjoyed Coach (as he likes to be called). All the lectures are online, the homework is pretty easy, and he brings his dog to class sometimes :)
Hes great, class is optional.
Considering that most of his class is about learning how to use Microsoft Excel, he makes it a lot more interesting than you think it would be. Also, he brings his dog into class every now and then.

EAM (as he calls himself) was a fun teacher. He learned my name because I sat in the front and it made class more bearable because he kept me engaged. If you don't go, watch the online lectures and read the textbook. His study guides are an exact replica of what is on the exams and do the Simpath assignments to keep your grade floating.

Attendance is completely optional because everything is online so no one really shows up to class. There's 3 exams which he made harder this year that some people did really well on and some people did really bad on. The exams are 20 questions mcq but they can be a little tricky if you didn't study. The rest of the grades are easy. Fun professor.
You can watch lectures from you room instead of going to class. Easy if you just do the work. I could've gotten an A if I put work in.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The first day of class he tells you that you don't have to come to class and you can watch the lectures online which are a lot shorter. He's pretty funny the days I went to class. The class usually goes for the whole 75 minutes.
He's pretty chill and makes all the lectures online so you don't have to go to class (besides test days). Easy class if you put in the time to watch/ go to the lectures and/or read the book.

He is called Coach so classes are like practice and Exams are game days. He is so funny and makes learning the material so fun and easy. If you get him be sure to ask about how he rejected Taylor Swift when she bought him a drink. Beware, if he learns your name he will talk to you all semester, not ask you questions, he just says your name randomly

This class is very chill. He gives enough homework that if you do bad on a test you still have an A. He's nice and funny but I don't know him that well because it's such a big class. I get bored sometimes because it's basically just excel but it's important for business school and he tries to make it less boring.

I enjoyed him, he was funny in class though sometimes he mumbled and was hard to understand. The class lectures move pretty fast, but they're provided online if you have trouble keeping up. Easy homework, just time consuming.

This class is so boring but pretty easy. I would skip sometimes and be fine. The tests are kinda easy if you study. I always just read the textbook before the tests because I didn't take great notes. Martin is very monotone and some days I thought I was gonna die of boredom. There is extra credit and easy homework every week
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: teaches the basic Business class at VT in which every business student MUST take. You have to buy the textbook($) as well as the SIMNet code ($$$) to be in this class. He has the lectures online as well as practice quizzes to help you out. The exams are from the lecture slides. You can read the slides the day before and get an A.

Class is pretty straightforward. 3 tests and a final. Exams are short (30 mins) not too hard. Drops some questions on some tests so you can end up with a 120%. Showing up to class has its perks because he discusses the questions that are going to be on the exam.

ACIS 1504 is literally the easiest class you will ever take. Attendance isn't mandatory at all. You can either go to the 75 min class where he jokes around for 90% of class or watch the lecture videos online for about 12 minutes. Homework is 20% of your grade and is super easy and short. TAKE THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS!!! SUPER GPA booster.
Great professor, knew what he was doing. There to help. 10/10 would take his class again

One of the nicest and most informative teachers I've had here at VT. I read how difficult Calc 2 was here at VT, but in her class, it was a very low-pressure and fun environment. She is available a lot of the time and will take time out of her day to help students when needed. If you're taking 1226, definitely take it with her.

I don't know why everyone is hating on her. She is such a nice women who spends so much of her time making sure you understand her class. She post videos of her lectures every night and sends announcements out when test are and if they are moved. If you just participate and actually read announcements she will make Calc 2 the easiest class ever

I struggled to keep up with this class. Final grades were not clearly communicated, and changes to test dates were sometimes unclear. I also found that the lectures did not always explain the material.When I reached out for help, the support from TAs was limited and did not always clarify my confusion. I now have to retake the class.
Quite a bit of HW but very managable in regards to due dates and working with her during office hours.
Funny, informative, helpful.
Her lectures aren't the greatest but the fact that she is willing to sacrifice her personal time and help you outside of office hours says more about her character than anything. 5/5.
She's nice, maybe the old comments reflect her from years past but she's genuinely very kind and accomodating.
It's hard to stay on top of this class, final grades aren't shared, test date changes aren't communicated properly, and the lectures don't teach the material clearly. TAs weren't much help either.

If you like surprises, this class delivers! Final grades? Who knows. Important announcements? Good luck finding them. The material isn't well explained, and the TAs are about as helpful as a screen door on a submarine.

The instructor does not post final grades and communication can be inconsistent, particularly regarding important announcements such as test schedule changes. The material could be presented more clearly, and the TAs were not particularly helpful.

Final grades are never posted, and communication is extremely poor—both during lectures and for essential updates like changes to test dates. The course material is not effectively taught, and the TAs provide little to no support.

I had trouble keeping up in this class because final grades were never posted, and communication about things like test date changes was lacking. The lectures didn't explain the material well, and the TAs weren't very supportive.

Communication in this course is a challenge, especially regarding test dates and final grades. The lectures could better convey the material, and the TAs were not very helpful, but with extra effort, it's possible to get through the course.

She doesn't post final grades and communication is really bad, both in lectures and for important things like test date changes. The material isn't taught very well overall, and the TAs were not helpful at all.

Overall, the course suffered from limited communication. Grades were not posted clearly, and important updates, such as changes to exam dates, were often unclear or delayed. The teaching did not effectively cover the core material, and the TA support could have been stronger.

Genuinely am not sure what the other people are talking about. Insanely sweet person who seems like she actually cares about your education. Her tests are pretty easy and she is always willing to make time to help you. Definitely take her for Calc 2.
WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD. She does not care about her students.

Just to preface I did take calculus in high school. The tests overall were pretty easy and I thought were much easier than the homework/problems we did in the notes. Classes are skippable and notes are posed online. She's super kind and is always willing to help. People who post negative reviews clearly don't want it.

reviews.comment: She doesn't post overall grades, is very bad at communication (in lectures and general important announcements like test date changes), and is not good at teaching the overall material. She also had a really bad TA selection.

I'm not sure why she gets so much hate on here, I took her class and had a good experience, the grading policy is fair and well laid out, and she is friendly and easy to communicate with and ask for help from during class. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I literally don't think I could even pick what she looks like out of a crowd. I've seen her a total of one time, the rest of the class is online. I'm not sure what her job is since the tests and quizzes are graded online, and the labs are taught by someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class was at the math emporium so naturally a lot of the class is self discipline and getting through the material on your own. Professor England is a very nice lady and wants all of the students to succeed. She is available at her office hours for much of the week and always willing to help. Overall, if you're willing to work, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class, if you don't intend to take it with friends, is very difficult. She teaches by working through the steps to solve the problem. She doesn't really do any work outside of her very limited office hours: the notes, videos, and tests were pre-made many years ago, and all the grading is done through a computer. She does nothing but tutor.
Very straightforward online lessons. Short and sweet. The class itself is not super difficult.
Class is very easy. Her notes are very organized and she really tried to help whenever possible. It mainly depends on us and how much we are willing to do.

This class is terrible. It is impossible to learn the required material from the Math Emporium. The online text skips steps and almost always give examples that are useless when actually taking the quizzes. Mrs. England's lectures and lecture notes are out of date. They focus on information that is no longer required and leave out new key concepts.

I only spoke with her once. And I didn't find her helpful. She had extremely limited office hours (hours at the empo) and though there is staff to help, sometimes you want to hear it from the professor. This class for me was difficult, and I took both semesters of AP calc in high school... She is very good about answering emails though.

If you go to Tech pray you get Mrs. England she is a wonderful Linear Algebra teacher. I was bad at algebra but she took the time to explain everything.  She is also great even though she has over 1,000 students so give her a brake!

Linear Algebra was probably the easiest class I took this semester.  It is completely self-taught through short lecture videos and an online text book.  I spent maybe 2 hours a week total on this course.  The quizzes can be taken from anywhere on campus which makes it easier, so you don't have to travel to the empo except for tests.
Answers her e-mails!

this class was incredibly easy, but i never actually spoke with the professor. i dont know what exactly she does since she doesnt have a class to teach and the lectures are pre-recorded. watch the lectures online and do the practice quizzes and its a breeze.

This is an online teach it to yourself class, and Jerri England doesn't give you any help herself. She posts lectures online, and in the lectures she works example problems, but the example problems are so easy my 4th grade sister could do them. The actual problems require more info than whats given in examples and lectures.
Hard course, because I got extremely sick half way through the semester. She was very helpful!

Yes, the class is teach-it-yourself, but if u don't understand something GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS! She helped me SOOOO much. The class shouldn't be hard if u just ask her for help(email or office hours).

I haven't really dealth with her too much being that it's an online class, but her supplementary lectures are very usefull and she won't hesitate in returning your emails asking her for help.  This class seems pretty pointless, but it's an easy A.

She is a great professor.  Be sure to watch the supplementary lectures, they really help a lot!  The class is cool because you can get it over with before the end of the semester.  She is also extremely nice and always willing to help.  She is the kind of teacher that makes you want to do well!
WORTHLESS. What the hell is she gettin payed for? You never see her except the first week of class and you teach yourself the class.
So she heads the online class... had nothing to her... but she answered one of my red cup questions and was very nice!
Took her for an online class-was very helpful and very understanding when I was too ill to take a required quiz!
WORTHLESS.
Great teacher!

Dr. Evans is a nice guy but his lectures are around 10-15 minutes and barely give you any material to study. Attendance is mandatory for in class assignments. Tests are much harder than other bio professors and have a lot of extremely specific questions that are offhandedly mentioned during lecture so either pay attention really well or record them
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are most of your grade and the tests are very hard. The lectures are very short. Very nice guy, but I would not take again as a professor. You will need to study a lot more than other biology classes.

Format just like 1105. Not really under his control, it's a department thing. Watch the videos before the lecture, and you'll be fine. Activities were not that bad; any weirdly specific test question is usually something he says in class so just pay attention. I preferred Bill Wills, but I didn't mind him.

I was not a fan of his teaching style. His lectures make it so you have to be there in class to learn all of the material. He isn't very tech-savvy and did not put much effort into helping with the test review. The TAs carried this class for me, and Dr Evans didn't help teach the material.

Hes nice but i hated his lectures. Boring and long, activities were annoying and hes not good at using technology. He says the makes the tests easy but they are often very specific application questions so make sure you study. Make sure you go to office hours after your test to see what you got wrong bc the final is all the most missed questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funny, great guy. Terrible teacher. In fact he barely teaches at all. He lecture minimalistic slides for maybe 20 minutes and sends you off to do an activity. Isn't helpful in office hours, and says in his syllabus that he will round up your grade after the final has been taken but went completely MIA after the final unable to reach. Hard tests too

Compared to other intro to bio professors I think that Dr.Evans is harder. He does not not give you clear content to study because his lectures are just to short. The homeworks and in class activities are not very relevant to the exams because he does not make them. The final is easy. Study for all of the exams and you should be ok.

Dr. Evans isn't a terrible professor, he's actually the opposite. My one issue with him though would be how difficult his tests are. Average class scores range from 60-70% while all other BIOL 1106 classes lap us with 90-100%'s. It's unfortunate but just make sure to study more than your other bio friends.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Evans is a nice professor and all, but he's tough. His tests are extremely difficult and he doesn't provide any study guides—just mini lectures (like all bio professors). Other professors offer more resources and easier exams and some curve. Evans is known for making his exams hard, so be ready to put in more effort than your bio friends.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a very sweet and funny guy, his lectures are always engaging. I love the routine format of this class. He typically lectures for about 20 minutes, then the rest of the class is spent working on an activity with classmates. Tests are 70% of your grade, so be sure to study well.

Dr. Evans is a very average professor. He seems bored when giving lectures and gets angry at students who are even a little late to class, kicking them out in front of the entire class. His tests are pretty difficult, especially test 3, so be aware. I'm not sure how he hasn't realized that his bad test scores are his fault, not the students'.

Each class, he has a "mini-lesson." His lessons are around 20 minutes and very surface-level and don't add value.  After this mini-lesson, we have an in-class activity. Dr. Evans got angry halfway through the semester that people were only showing up for the in-class activity after the lesson. He has threatened to kick students out that were late.

He's really awesome and his mini lectures are super helpful. My only qualm would be his tests, as I believe that because he writes his own questions it can sometimes make getting the correct answer hard; he knows what he's talking about when he writes the question, but no one else does!

Evans was great about breaking down the material. He was funny, and kept me fully engaged during his lectures which only tend to last between 15-20 minutes. A majority of the class is spent working in a group. I wish he would've posted more study resources like practice tests or outlines. He seems to be very traditional when it comes to grades.

BEST bio professor I have had. I had him for BIO 1106 and wish I also took him for BIO 1105. He is super nice and breaks the information down in lecture to make it easier to understand. Make sure to take notes in class because some of the information presented in lecture is not on the homework or in the homework videos.

Best bio professor I have had. He does a really good job at making the material easier to understand. As usual for bio class, there are activities with a group at the end of every class, but they weren't super hard. Make sure to take notes during lecture since some of the materials in lecture are not found in the homework or videos.

I loved Dr. Evans. He is an amazing professor, and he has interesting lectures. While the exams were a bit difficult, it was a rare situation where despite the difficult exams he was so amazing that it was worth it and the extra work. He also is super accessible out of class, and it is a great opportunity to get to know him.

Dr. Evans was pretty good as far as bio profs go. You have the usual assignments: in class groupwork, 4 tests (+final), hw quizzes. Tests are very reasonable if you study. I made practice tests from the hw & activity questions and I went to review sessions and I did well. He has office hours and is more than willing to help students as needed.

Dr. Evans is a great help during office hours. He does not do iClickers, so you do not have that grade boost and it's difficult to assess yourself. He only lectures for like 10-20 min so it's really on you to know the info, and his tests are really hard. It's hard to go from quick lectures to knowing everything for the tests. The final is easy
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Reading the book is not necessary but recommended as he barely lectures. 10-15 minute lectures, flys through material. It's up to you to really understand it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Evans seems like a good professor. He has a pretty good sense of humor, but he also seems very set in his ways. This class is meant to give students new to Virginia Tech resources to help you succeed. However, it felt like a waste of time. Attendance is required and is checked with a sign-in sheet. This class is graded by very few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jack is by far my favorite professor at Virginia Tech. No professor has ever made a class so enjoyable and easy to understand. He is very funny while remaining on topic, and his office hours are so helpful as he allows you to go over your tests and review questions you missed. I never dreaded going to his class, and I feel like I learned a lot.

Respectable guy. No grading exceptions and there's only 4 assignments for the whole class, so do all of them. Easy 100 right there. Very knowledgeable about Biology careers and gives good, straightforward advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: By far one of the easiest classes offer by college of science. You have only 4 assignments all year and for the most part they are pretty easy.

This man is so funny, I would show up to class just to hear this man give us lectures. This is suppose to be an easy class, help to get freshman on their feet. Lots of guest speakers, but they are super helpful. I recommend you get the chance to meet this man, easy credit and fun.

He follows the textbook, so focus a lot more on the textbook content than the mini and online lectures. He doesn't really go over anything specific, but he might put something you thought would be irrelevant on the quizzes and tests. He doesn't seem to check over the questions he types for the test/quizzes, so beware incoherent grammar and spelling

Dr. Evans does not seem like respects students as we respect him. The work is very doable and a regular amount of studying could get you an A in this class. The group worksheets are doable but you are stuck with the same group for the semester.
DR. EVANS IS THE BEST! Very caring and nice person who will do anything to help you succeed in the class. He is very funny and makes class fun. Highly recommend him!!

He definitely made a potentially hard class a lot easier. He presents the material very clearly and doesn't add in a lot of extra detail, and plus he's super funny and caring. TA's are good and the activities are pretty straightforward. Would definitely recommend for bio!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really funny and cool guy. Definitely would recommend him, he makes the stupid way gen bio is set up a bit better. You have to attend class to do activities but they don't take long and you always get out early.
He is a great professor and hilarious! He cares about his students and his subject so much. His tests are pretty hard & with questions based on scenarios.

He's a funny guy but honestly not that great of a teacher. Whenever he holds review sessions and you ask a question he says "I'm not going to answer that. Look in your notes" and its discouraging. Exams count for 70% of our grade which is excessive to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Second semester freshman bio is hard in general. Jack makes it more tolerable than any other professor at Tech.

He's really helpful, especially for Bio majors because he is the head of Bio Advising. He's easily accessible outside of class, and he makes it easy to ask him questions in class too. His jokes may not agree with everyone, but he's genuinely a funny guy and super helpful and informative!

Jack Evans was my teacher for bio 1004 but he was also much more than that. He's so quick to help students and give them advice on their academic careers and more.  He's insightful, knowledgable, and reassuring, and not to mention hilarious.

I absolutely loved Dr. Evans for Biology 1004. It's very rare for him to give out hw but they're easy A's if you review his examples in the book. Dr. Evans praises those who come to class by giving free 100's to those who are there right as class starts or will hand out homework at the very beginning or end of class. Overall an amazing professor!
I got to know him very well, and I am happy that I got know him so well, almost like a dad.
GREATEST TEACHER EVER!!!
Well this was only a Biology Seminar, but Jack is the man. He is cool, chill, relaxed, fun. Stop by and talk to him about your Biology questions, he's a really helpful guy.

He let me turn something in late with no penalty. It's all very clear, the assignments are few and easy, and even though it's boring, going to class and doing the homework makes getting anything less than an A impossible.

Biol 1004 itself is quite easy.  Jack Evans makes class a little less boring with his enthusiasm and humor.  This course is an easy A because all you have to do is complete the very few (emphasize on few) assignments.  Pay close attention to your Four Year Plan which you will form in this class,which you have forever to complete.
Great professor, your TA will help a lot

I had her for first-semester biology, and her teaching style is similar to AP Bio. Exams are comprehension-based, and she kinda tells you what to focus on for the exams if you pay attention and go to class. There are clicker questions, and she simplifies the videos. IF YOU DID NOT TAKE AP BIO IN HIGH SCHOOL, BE PREPARED TO STUDY A LOT!!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: questions are unevenly distributed across the material and are poorly worded test questions meant to throw students off their game. Not very lenient - refused to work with me to reschedule the final exam (even though I came to her on day 1 of class about it)
Pretty decent professor, exams are not bad, you should pay attention in lectures for sure and watch the video notes before class.

Great professor, when you watch the vids before each lecture and pay attention, she explains things really simply and helpfully. Tests were not that bad and comparable to what we had to do as homework

Dr. Emori is a very sweet woman, but her lecture style didn't work for me personally. She tries to make the content more interesting, but the silly analogies she would use would take me out of the focus of the content. The class is very lecture heavy, so if you zone out a lot I would not recommend. Overall, very sweet but you have to pay attention.

She's fine. I will say the tests are not that hard, and it's pretty easy to get an 85+ if you actually study. If you don't study, you're screwed. My biggest advice is to go to her office hours before a test. Students have to ask her questions, but she tends to focus in on topics that are covered on the test, which saved me a couple of times.
She is nice, but talks too quickly and expects a lot from students. Very difficult to learn from her lectures be she goes through them so quickly so there is time for 45 minutes of group work.

She was a good teacher although some of her lectures went very into depth and became very confusing due to analogies she made. I found it hard to follow a lot of the time and the tests very very much in depth too.

she is very nice and class is somewhat enjoyable. Tests are hard tho and you really have to understand the material. the exams are a big part of your grade so if u do bad on one or two it takes a lot of work to bring it up. she does have a lot a times to meet outside of class and seems very eager to help people understand the material
Pretty good teacher tbh. She's really sweet but its just like any other bio class. Tests are a little difficult but as long as you understand everything you should be fine.
If you already know the material you will do fine but it's hard to learn as she doesn't teach and relies on pre recorded lectures.

She's super nice when you meet her outside of class. Be prepared to watch a lot of videos before class and take a lot of notes or else you'll not understand anything and you might not do very well. Her lectures are super short and afterwards she does group participation. If you rely on just her lectures, you will not do well on the test.

Definitely one of the best biology professors at VT. Her lectures were super helpful and not boring at all. I really appreciated how much she seemed to care about the material and that we understood it.

She is very nice BUT says the textbook is not necessary but it is very helpful and explains the material clearer and better. Her slides are really hard to get material from but her exams are mostly straightforward if you take the time to study. Her office hours are really helpful and she's super approachable.

Emori has great examples and analogies in her lectures that make complex topics easy to understand. The lecture is followed by a group activity graded by TAs, which can be inconsistent. Watch the video lectures to prepare for class. Her tests are fairly difficult because most questions ask you to apply the knowledge, rarely straightforward at all.

Great lectures, good explanations of concepts-a lot of material here is pretty high level. TA review sessions were helpful. Helps you learn how to read academic papers through active class days. Also get out of class early usually which is nice but some lectures can feel rushed.
Emori did a good job in class of breaking down topics, but her TA led group projects every class are annoying and graded on an inconsistent scale.
She was great! She cares and has engaging lectures.

Such a nice person but her slides are so confusing! I really appreciate her effort but it was so hard to learn from the way she taught. Her exams were  very difficult so be well prepared. She uses iClickers to grade attendance which is nice but it does not substitute working hard. Not the worst professor out there but certainly not the best either

Had a medical emergency and ended up stuck at Urgent Care so I missed one class. Despite having a doctor's note, this professor informed me that I would be unable to make-up any of the work missed in class (including a quiz grade) and this would count as an unexcused absence because I did not inform her I was going to get sick... before I got sick.

Definitely one of the harder test givers from the biol 1105 professors but if you try you will succeed and actually learn. Go to her office hours if you want to get her tests she tells you everything you need to learn and how to study!

She seemed to lecture too fast and not explain material well in class, so iClickers were pretty difficult to answer. I do appreciate her "active days" where we have an opportunity for active learning, but those weren't as effective as they could be since her lectures were confusing. Despite this she is very caring and posts lots of review material.

The course itself wasn't awful, however Dr. Emori definitely was not the most caring professor out there. Additionally, she does not provide study guides to prepare you for tests unlike other biology professors here at VT. Be prepared to move quickly and have a concrete understanding of biology prior to signing up for her course

Very strict on grading policy. Do the prelectures for this class, most topics lectured on in class go way deeper and thats the stuff on the exams. Good for premed, prepares for harder bio classes but it takes a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are not very long but are informative. After lectures, there's a group activity which are good to look over when study tests. Personally, I thought tests weren't difficult and always got above a 90%. Make sure to look over the homework and slides before the exam because they have a lot of information on them. Will never round grades.
The course was fine, and Emori was okay, though she was very unforgiving with her grading. She will NOT round your grade, or give you extensions. She taught well.

Very fun teacher with a very formulaic structure to her classes (Lecture -> group assignment -> hw quiz). Imo, you'll be teaching yourself the content in this class through lesson videos rather than her lectures. However, I would say she's the best Biol1105 teacher to get bc her exams are relatively easy + she posts good review material.

Dr. Emori is really good! Just watch the video lectures and take the homework quizzes before class to do well on the iclickers. While the video lectures can be material dense, her lectures in class make everything much clearer, so take notes in class. She points out things to look out for on her tests and makes helpful review videos for each unit.

Take IN DEPTH notes in class because what she talks about in class is always going to be directly correlated with the exam. Go to her office hours she's SUPER GOOD at explaining things and will tell you more specifically what you need to know for the exams. iClicker questions are good to review before exams, and study all the LO's she gives!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class
