reviews.comment: Tests are 70% of your grade. Tests are very are to complete. I have not gotten better than a C on any test and I am a very good student. There are no study guides just blank learning objectives. Topics are not explained well and things are moved over very quickly, you are expected to know information before you get to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a sweet prof! Incredibly passionate about the subject and gives great feedback, but class is still really difficult. All notes are taken outside of class-- lecture is just a review + practice. Her UTAs are great! Doesn't give study guides or practice tests, so be warned! Not impossible to get an A, but certainly nowhere close to easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are clear, she states all the needed information in a way that is in-depth, yet still easy to understand, and she provides course materials that assist in understanding complicated topics.
Dr. Emori is a very caring teacher who is passionate about what she teaches. Her lectures are interesting and everything for the test is on the slideshow/homeworks.

I took 1105 and Dr Emori been my favorite professor since then. Showing up to class is so important. Her tests are almost 100% what she goes over in class and on the class slides. Homework is a few lecture videos that I take notes on and then put into a quizlet. She posts review videos for every topic you need to know for the tests. Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had taken the 1105 class for the 2024 semester. She was very nice from my time spent with her, but I felt helpless as the semester went on. I would study, take the video notes, and watch the review lectures twice and still fail. This class feels like it is directed towards biology majors despite half of the class needing it as a pathway course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I agree with the comments about how she sends mean emails. She is extremely rude even when you try to communicate nicely. Other professors give resources such as study guides and practice tests but she gives nothing. Doesn't do much to prepare you for the tests. She will not budge your grades no matter what. Would not take the class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Other Bio 1105 classes got practice tests but you don't with Dr. Emori. She's not flexible nor understanding if extenuating circumstances come up. If you get really sick she will make you jump through piles of paperwork. Her emails are rude. She is not open to makeup exams. Had an awful experience with her and will not pick her for 1106.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Emori expects you to know the material before class and give graded iclickers on the material. She provides almost no study guides or resources before the test (while every other professor does so). She is extremely strict about grading homework/classwork and will not change your grade even if your mistake is her fault. She also sends mean emails.

Great professor, always included anecdotes/stories in her lectures to help you memorize the material (that she would then use as test questions, so be sure to go to lectures!). Be aware her attendance policy is strict, so be sure you understand it. If you pay attention and start studying a few days before her tests, you'll likely do well.
Professor Emori is quite challenging but also a talented, enjoyable teacher. She has tough tests but I learned lots!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: GO TO CLASS!! most of her exam questions come directly from her lectures. Def record what she says in class too, and ask AI to make a practice test based on what she says in class. I can guarantee u will get a good grade if u do this. Her tests are harder than other professors tho, very funny professor, love her

I had Emori for both first year biology classes (1105/1106) and she was great! She explains each topic very clearly in a quirky and easy way within her lecture slides. Compared to other professors, her exams are harder, and she does not provide study guides. But she gives amazing review videos and has great communication. She was very enjoyable!!

I wish the first-year biology classes allowed for a bit more room for error and wasn't as test-heavy. However, I understand that this isn't within the control of one particular professor, so I won't let that fact impact my rating. Professor Emori was always very energetic and gave helpful analogies for complicated topics!
Great professor, lectures are easy to follow, the tests are very easy. Loves to connect the material to actual science and research papers.

If you're taking biology, it is essential to take Dr. Emori. She explains concepts very simply and offers quirky stories you'll remember on tests. Come to class because iClickers (Participation grades) can help raise your grade. Doing well on Tests is where the bulk of your grade comes from, so study study study for those! 12/10 professor.

Bio 1106 is much better than 1105 and Emori did an okay job at teaching. I had a different prof for 1105 and what I liked better about Emori was she doesn't use a monotone voice and you can tell she is passionate about what she is teaching. That being said sometimes she gets a little too passionate and goes off on rants. She is a very caring prof.

Dr. Emori tries to be a good professor but her slides don't cover the material in her exams. She's nice, but isn't lenient at all in her grading. Her exams are the hardest out of all of the other professors. In the past she added curves, but in my section she didn't. Don't let her rating fool you. She doesn't give any extra help either.

She is interactive and does a great job at explaining and walking through the class notes and slides, even better than when I had her for 1105. She can be flexible for office hours sometimes, holds test review sessions, and makes review videos for tests that are helpful.
She's very interactive and explains well. I got the grade I did because I didn't study, but she is great. She loves to help if you need it.

Love love love her. Had her for cell diff and she is very easy to understand. She always gives analogies to help us remember concepts. No book required. She has one homework a week that usually has 2 attempts (grade booster). Tests are pretty straightforward. In class activities with iClicker questions also boost your grade.

Dr. Emori is very knowledgeable and kind. She is always willing to help her students and created post-class review videos and pre-test online review lessons which I found extremely helpful. I would definitely recommend using the videos and objectives to take notes, as this is what she uses to create test questions. Attendance taken through iClicker
Take it with Mike or Hogan. Not worth it. She doesn't give practice tests either.
Awesome teacher! She is very challenging and expects effort but you will understand biology very well by the end of the course

she's a great teacher, very knowledgable. however, her tests were ridiculously difficult. she offered some extra credit points throughout the semester which was nice. she's a very kind teacher and wants you to do well. if you don't test well, i wouldn't recommend taking her class. other than the hard tests, she's a good teacher.

If you are a perfect student she'll love you. If you're like everyone else, she'll show you contempt at best. She doesn't answer questions in detail, and moves at the pace of the fastest students only. I found it clear that she is there to teach, but not to make sure we learn. Avoid.

Dr. Emori is the best! BIOL 1105 can be a challenging class due to the sheer amount of information it covers, but she does a wonderful job at supporting students with office hours and review sessions. Her metaphors are mind blowing and she explains topics so well. Constructed my entire schedule for next semester for her section of BIOL 1106!

Professor Emori is a great person, I just think she is way too smart to teach a freshman-level class. She tends to overcomplicate things and make them sound much easier than they actually are and then I end up having to teach myself everything. She does seem really passionate about the subject but I do not understand her.

She is very interested in the material she teachers however she goes on about stories that make the concept harder to understand. Vocab heavy and must know the specific details to get a good grade. She is super nice and cares about her students!!

Dr. Emori is very nice and passionate about biological sciences. It's clear she wants to see everyone of her students success with her extra resources, interesting facts, and during her well-explained lectures. This class was the class that forced me to rethink my studying habits in the best way.

Professor Emori is a good and cheerful person. She is not the problem as much as Biology 1105 is.

Get ready to due work outside of class. Personally the pre-class lectures were extremely helpful, I took notes on those instead of the lecture and found that my grade and understanding improved. Her lectures were not helpful. Don't skip.

Bio can be a hard class but she makes it manageable to students through her various review sessions before tests and in-depth notes. Students watch videos before class then go over the lecture and participate in a group assignment during class. She is very accessible to help students and prepare them for exams. Also homework isn't bad.

I loved Emori's class, I think that as long as you do the Hw before hand you will be fine. Take good notes, she is really good at setting up her lectures to be only what you need for the exams, so make sure you pay attention. She is kind, and always tries to help you succeed!
Very clear in conveying the content and has the best analogies!
Really good professor; easy to stay attentive during class, she posts lots of review material and her exams aren't too hard.

I took this class over the summer and overall, Dr. Emori comes across as a very kind professor. She failed me by 0.04% after completing extra credit, going to her office hours, and spending loads of time outside of class studying. She is a mom and her main conversation topic is her son and her husband who is also a professor at Tech.

She wasn't bad but if you take her class online the lecture notes aren't even her voice which I find funny and annoying because I couldn't stand the other person's voice. If you need to email her she will respond quickly. Overall decent professor.

I'd recommend watching the pre-class homework videos in order to get the most out of the class lectures. Dr. Emori made her own slides that cover the topics she thinks are most important. Since she makes her own tests, this is the information that is most helpful to study. Her tests are somewhat tough but definitely doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a great teacher and has many helpful methods of helping students learn the material. She is accessible outside of class, but don't expect that to be much help. Her material goes in depth and she offers extensive review guides before every test. Tests aren't that bad, she literally tells you what to study for. Attendance is mandatory.

I do think she is very passionate about teaching, but if you do not watch the online lectures there is no way your doing well. I did not miss a class and the test were still very hard. Her test questions are very word heavy and convoluted. There is group work, iclickers, and homework quizzes after every class.

Dr. Emori's classes are fairly easy if you have taken AP Biology. I had her for both 1105 and 1106 and I really enjoyed my time with her. I would strongly advice watching the pre-lecture videos because not all the exam material is covered during lecture. She is passionate about biology and I think makes a great professor for 1st year material.

Super sweet professor, and very clearly loves what she is teaching. Tests can be sort of difficult, but if you put enough time into them, they're manageable. I didn't like the group work during each lecture, I would have rather just done it as individual homework as some people wouldn't show up or were difficult to work with.

I had Dr. Emori for cell functions and she was a great professor! The material was clearly presented and I found the tests straight forward. There are clicker questions during class so attendance is required.

One of the only classes that I enjoyed attending. She tried to make every lesson as interesting as possible which can be hard to do for some lectures. She also had many opportunities to have students ask her questions. She would even be willing to stay a bit after class to answer any questions you have, which shows she cares for her students.

She is so nice, one of the first professors who I felt comfortable going to her office hours. She is very willing to help students and isn't one of those professors who get annoyed at you for asking stupid questions. If you put in the effort, you will do good in her class.

Took her class over the summer. I'd only study for a couple days before. I didn't read the textbook at all, and found it didn't really matter for the exams-the exams were heavily based off her ppts and lectures. Lots of other grades to boost your exam grades, and there was one extra credit assignment. I believe we got one exam curved?

I took Dr. Emori's BIOL 1106 in the summer of 2021 as a Summer Academy student. She was absolutely incredible. She genuinely cares about her students and is always willing to find a time to help you understand a topic you may not understand. Her tests are hard but if you pay attention in class and supplement with your textbook, you will do great

Dr. Emori wants you to succeed and tried to make her lectures not so cut and dry by adding a lot of real-life scenarios to help you understand the concepts. BUT, the exams are brutal. You will not pass the class if you are only studying a day or two for the exams. Homework is easy but the exams are what is killer :(

If you read the book, listen and take notes on the videos, and read her notes, you should get an A-B in the class. She is really nice but also really strict on deadlines and test dates, don't waste your time asking for an extension, you're not going to get it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to take a course that requires all outside classroom learning, this is the one for you. The all over the place technique of material presentation makes for an almost impossible and effective study and preparation plan for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Emori for 1105 and 1106 and she's by far the best in my opinion. The class isn't super easy but its not impossible to get the A you just have to work for it. She has multiple opportunities for yo to see her and get help. She has review guides posted for each test. DO THEM they're so helpful in understanding  the things she may ask on a test.

Dr. Emori is one of the best professors i've had. bio isnt an easy class, but 1106 is much better than 1105. Dr. Emori explains the material so well, i can go to class and just pay attention, and understand it well. Tests are decent, kinda difficult but questions come from homework, iclickers, and in class powerpoints which she provides.

I felt as though she really made it incredibly hard to do well. The test questions themselves were super convoluted and didnt always seem to relate to what was went over in lecture. Study guides were vague and not super helpful. Dr. Emori was also incredibly inconsiderate at times. Just choose another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Emori is a very kind, caring individual. I straight up failed my first exam and went to her office hours and she was very encouraging about my prospects for the rest of the semester. You can tell that she cares about her students, although her tests are hard compared to other professors that teach this course.

Dr Emori is an absolutely amazing professor. She gives excellent detail about the topics present in 1105 and is evidently well versed in what she teaches. However; her tests are HARD. If you don't review, you will not pass them. Go to class, take notes on the videos, review iClickers, homewors and FRQ's, and STUDY VOCAB!!! Do all that and you pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Highly suggest looking at the class slides and taking notes either before or after class, she goes way too fast for you to possibly get them written down in time. Exams are so unnecessarily hard. Her exam questions are so intricate and complicated they're like word problems. Don't buy the textbook, she provides free online alternatives first day.

Class is very homework and lecture heavy. There are homework quizzes after every class and in class she spends about 30 minutes lecturing then the second half of class you work with teams to do an FRQ which is graded and you have to be in class for. There are also Iclicker questions every class so its very hard to miss classes and pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a very good and organized teacher. You can tell she is engaged and loves what she does. If you go over the homework, in class work, and study guide you will do well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I think Professor Emori is a great teacher, it's just a lot of material that has to be crammed into one semester which is really hard for first time college students. You have to watch video lectures outside of class, take notes, and then attend in person class for more lecture and a group activity. Exams are difficult too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took her for 1105- definitely a "weed out" class for higher biological sciences. Her exams were WAY more difficult than they needed to be, I often felt as though I was seeing the information for the very first time while I was testing. There's an in class activity that you need to be present for at every lesson. DOES NOT ROUND GRADES!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was the death of me. I dreaded going each day. The teacher is sweet but does not teach the material well. Get ready to study and teach yourself a lot!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Emori this summer for BIOL 1106. She was super sweet and always came around to answer any questions we had. Make sure you go to her office hours because its super helpful and she takes a lot of time explaining things you don't understand the concept. Very caring and values you as a person meaning if you are sick she is very understanding.
Pay attention to the lecture slides and videos. The in-person lecture itself really isn't that great but worth coming to. Tests are awfully hard so you really need to know your stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Extremely nice and offers review videos and office hours to help you succeed. However she goes over very broad subjects and expects you to go in the book to get more detailed information. Very upfront about whats on the test. Course material is difficult.

Homework at the end of almost (if not all) lessons. Tests were on lockdown browser, timed, and you can't go back to questions after you answer (she said it was to prevent cheating). Did not post lectures or exam reviews so if you don't go to class you will miss everything. Office hours were very helpful for me. She wants her to succeed. Hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thought she was a great professor with fun lectures and iclickers. You CANNOT skip class. Tests were hard, but manageable if you really studied for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took her for Bio 1105 and Bio 1106. She makes the tests way harder than they need to be. I often felt as if I wouldn't have done better no matter how much I studied. (lots of trick questions, tricky true false, etc.) You also couldn't go backward on the tests. I loved her as a person, but she isn't easy

(Had her during COVID) I really like Dr. Emori also had her for intro bio. She had iclicker questions during class. The only downside was the lockdown browser tests when COVID first hit since most professors were more lenient, but her tests were not bad at all. She is also very helpful if you have questions. Pretty typical biology class.
She is very inconsiderate sometimes and seems like she doesn't want you to succeed. Her tests are hard and the classes do not prepare you them.

Shes an amazing nice caring person and a great teacher. In class assignments are not bad at all and the iClickers werent either. Her tests on the other hand are in my opinion much harder than other professors(detailed and complex) Its difficult to do well on them even if you enjoy her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Emori was a very enthusiastic teacher and a wonderful person. She was always happy and in a good mood which made classes easier to follow along for. The only negative thing I will say is that tests were always difficult, more so than other classes. But it is passable and you learn a lot with Dr. Emori
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Took her for 1105 and made sure not to take her for 1106. Does not rounds grades, even 89.9%. She made exams much harder than they needed to be. She is a very nice lady, but I am not a fan of her questions or lectures. Take someone else and I promise you will do better.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 1106 is much easier than 1105. Just do the activities and the review guides she makes and you have the answers to the test.

I had Dr. Emori for Biol 1105 and 1106, despite her time and location for 1106 being less than ideal (Goodwin at 2pm :/). She's too amazing a teacher to pass up. She makes a noticeable effort to make class and learning entertaining and you can tell she loves what she does. She is easy to understand and even acts things out, making biology amazing.

Dr. Emori is one of the best teachers hands down. She genuinely cares about her students and presents the material in a non-confusing way! I strongly recommend going to her office hours if you are confused with a topic because she will take the time out and teach you- she even does individual office hour appointments!

Dr. Emori is one of the best teachers Ive ever had! Shes caring and loves her students. Shes excellent at explaining concepts, and will work with you till you understand. She also wants us all to pass and is a fair grader.

Your grade is first of all very much determined by your TA, as they grade most of your work. I personally found her lectures to be super bland and confusing especially if I wasn't hyper focused the entire out of class video. She was also a rude to a member of group on many occasions. I also thought her exam were much harder than they needed be
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Emori is an amazing human being. Her lectures are interesting and tries to help with the in class assignments. Her tests are straight forward and she curves them if the average is low. She is very helpful in office hours by relating confusing topics to real world examples. She is very sweet and deserves the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Would definitely recommend going to her office hours if you are confused on a topic, she explains material much simpler one-on-one. Biology is a hard class in general, but she is an excellent teacher as well as very intelligent.
She is a really good professor. Her lectures were pretty clear, and mostly short, and then do inclass activities. She makes learning easy and uses TAs to help grade and explain concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Emori is one of the best teachers Ive had in a while. She is kind and truly cares about what she is teaching and her students. Emori will take the time to explain what you are having difficulties with and always appears to be in a good mood. She is well spoken and an uniquely intricate person. I wish I knew her better.

This course, no matter which professor you have is flipped-classroom so you have to show up to all of the classes to get credit for the activities done in each class. Dr. Emori is I think one of the better professors to get for Biology 1105 and 1106. She explains things really well in class and she curves the tests if the average is low.

I absolutely LOVE her. Her class is very easy if you do the work, and there isn't a lot of it. If you need an easy A, this class is for you. I have taken both her Chem in context classes, and in the first semester I received a 110%, and this semester I am currently sitting at a 120%. Great class.

She is very hit or miss; for me, it was a miss. She is very talkative and says a lot of unnecessary things that don't relate to the lecture. She will often call you out and put you on the spot. If you want a funny teacher that engages with you, then she is for you, but if you want to learn and sit there unbothered, then she's not for you.

Despite the other reviews, she is VERY EASY for the virtual ChemContext class. I agree her videos are kind of random but entertaining. She seems kind of disorganized with the course, but it is extremely easy. Slightly inconsistent workload throughout but never too much

Aside from her engaging and fun personality, she really wastes a lot of time in lecture. She is careless and really just talks about irrelevant things. A lot of this class I had to learn on my own. I would recommend others if you want to pass.
Teaches more about her life and less about chemistry

While she is a nice and fun person, she is not very good at teaching. You will have to learn the material by yourself because she primarily goes over practice questions from her slides, and she can be very confusing when explaining concepts. Attendance is taken through iClickers, but she ends up giving out the answers before the polls close.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were completely unorganized and she would take more time talking about her life than the actual notes. Told us it was our job to learn the material, and then would take a whole class period to go through very few practice questions and was also very confusing when explaining. I learned more from the TAs than her. Very self-taught class.
lectures are bad

She is great, super energetic in class. The lectures are engaging with I-Clicker everyday, but she tells you the answers before closing it. The practice tests are made from old test questions. Her lectures are mainly practice, each lecture is solving the problems not a lot of actual lecturing but it works really well.
Just be consistent with your work and complete your HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
I just have a few things to say:


She's an ICON, she's a LEGEND, and she IS the MOMENT

"Chlorine, Fluorene, and a Rotisserie chicken!"

Her lectures were very good an informative. She gives many in class examples that help with the test questions. 5 tests including the final but old tests are provided. She wants you to succeed and offers a lot of office hours to facilitate struggling students. I would definitely take her class again.

I love Dr. Eddleton! This class is lecture heavy but it's chemistry... she makes lectures entertaining with colleagues Dr. Wall and Dr. Wagner. She does use iclicker BUT makes sure to tell you the correct answer so you can change your vote. Tests are very similar to practice tests. Homeworks can be a lot but you get drops. I recommend!

Dr. Eddleton was a phenomenal instructor. The biggest thing is that you have to make yourself known. As long as you talk to her and put a name to your face for her you'll have no issues whatsoever. Assignments are a breeze and the only way to not get an A in CHEM 1004 is to not try at all. She's funny, down to Earth, and easy to get along with.

Dr. Eddleton is so incredibly kind and you can tell she cares about students. Her lectures tended to be very unorganized which was quite frustrating and I learned a lot more by doing the homework individually. Chem itself is an incredibly difficult course and much of your grade comes from the exams.

Class lectures are honestly pretty unorganized/random which I found frustrating. That being said, you have to attend lectures to get iClicker points so it can be painful to sit through sometimes. Although, Dr. Eddleton does seem to care for her students and acknowledges how difficult the content is. She provides many resources to help with it.
Don't do what I did and not go to class; attendance makes up a good portion of the grade. Otherwise, Ms. Eddleton is super nice, and your FYE class will be fine.

Professor Eddleton is extremely caring and respects her students. She is a kind soul and is very lenient with students who are struggling. I would definitely take a course of hers again, she became a great figure to look up to my freshman year. I cannot express how kind this woman is! You will enjoy her class. Go out of your way to get to know her!

Amazing. Not only a great professor, but a great advisor. She was very encouraging and brought in great speakers to each class. Each activity had meaning and purpose and I learned a lot from her class.

Professor Eddleton was really fun as a professor but I felt I was missing some of the important content. I would take her again, but the class can be tough if you aren't very familiar with chemistry already.
I liked her as a person. The hard part of this class is the exams.
I like the professor so much. She is so caring at Class. She gave extra care to course re-takers.

Overall this is a classic weed-out class. Class is not something I would wish on someone I like and it kinda feels like squid games past the halfway mark, a lot of my non-engineering friends failed out, but other than that if you can lock in you'll be fine. Eddleton is a fine teacher, but you'll learn the material online. Study a lot for an A or B

I love Jeannine she really cares about everyone in the chem department and wants you to succeed. Go to class it'll make her like you. Incredibly hard to reach via email though do not expect answers in a timely manner or at all sometimes. Overall, she's a gem.

She spends most of the lectures goofing off or ranting and waits until the last 5-10 minutes to actually teach and go over things, but in a not very helpful way.She doesnt respond to emails,ever. Relies a lot on the TAs for help teaching content, and constantly tells students they will fail the course, but she is funny so there's that

Just do the practice tests, and you'll be fine. She's super super nice, and willing to help, but makes zero sense in her lectures (she'll rant on random topics), but just show up, ignore it, and do the homework. Not hard class if you understand the practice test.

Prof Eddleton gets off-topic a lot during lectures but she gives you the answers to iClickers. I didn't pay attention during the lectures and I think I could've done better in the course if I had, but not by a lot. Eddleton was the only prof that made all the smartbooks and connects for a unit due on the same day which is something I liked.

A very peppy professor who brags about low scores and tries to scare you but don't be worried. Only went over problems, so read textbook for conceptual info. This class is classic weed-out. Do iClickers in class, HWs, and practice exams. Exams weren't bad if you studied properly. Dropped one midterm, some HWs, and few iClickers when I had her.

When starting at VT I heard nightmare stories about CHEM 1035 and specifically Eddleton. The class was structured well, and the required iClickers helped me practice the material learned in the homework, and the review sessions ran by the TAs were amazing. Tests weren't too bad, practice tests were helpful. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Don't want to skew her ratings because I'm not a STEM student and chem in context isn't even a chem class, but she was entertaining and her class was ridiculously easy. Great pathways class. You don't need to show up to class or be even slightly scientifically inclined. Just turn in assignments.

A really fun and energetic professor that is perfect for the FYE course I took with her. It was 8 am and miss girl was ready to vibe and talk about chemistry. Pretty easy assignments and really nice overall.

Jeannine is a great person, and for the FYE class she is perfect at inspiring college students to keep pushing through and discover what they love about chemistry. If you approach her she will care a lot and she's always willing to help her students.

I really don't even know what to say about Prof Eddleton. A part of me is thankful for her class because it boosted my GPA but also the content of her course j doesn't even make sense. It made me mad b/c I took 2 chem courses with her and literally did not learn a single thing.

Lots of iClickers!!! You'll probably be fine without going to class but you would lose that iClicker participation credit. Homework is not heavy and can do on your own pace. Tests are not hard if you actually study and do the practice tests, if not prepare for a D or below.

I had to take these classes as an elective and it is the easiest class / least effort needed. I don't know why people are hating on her, I think she's a super fun woman and if you want an easy pathway 4 elective here it is. She talks about the most random stuff during class, and 90% of the time you can do the homework without being in class.

I rated this professor hilarious because of what a joke this class was. I'm unimaginably dissatisfied with the professor. Eddleton has no idea what she's doing, just riding out tenure and wasting students time/money. Whatever you do, DO NOT TAKE A CLASS OF HERS. Classes are never informative, you won't learn, you'll just hate it.

Do NOT send me grade questions. ANY and ALL grade questions will be treated as violations of Academic Integrity and Student Conduct. I thought this summed up her personality pretty well. Not allowed to question her, and if you do, you fail the class and risk disciplinary action. Not a great way to foster a learning at atmosphere.

Day of the final, comes into our room and goes on a multiple minute long rant about how men are useless and good for nothing. Made me feel great to see that she saw nothing in the dozens of hours I spent on her class. Pretends to be funny and hip but she really just doesn't care. Complains nonstop about "teacher's salary" she makes as a professor.
It is so bad. I want to give you a zero. But that's not possible. So I give you, a one.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She answers questions well but you basically have to teach yourself the material before class to understand.

Eddleton isn't your best choice when it comes to 1035 professors. She doesn't really lecture all that well and you definitely can't rely on her teachings to pass. You gotta sit down and read the book lone wolf style. Take another professor, but you'll still survive chem with Eddleton if you have a decent work ethic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Eddleton is an enjoyable person to talk to outside of class, except NOT as a professor. She is hard to follow and sometimes it seems like she wants us to fail.

I love this woman so much, she always blasts music before class. her style of teaching is engaging and she makes it easy to ask questions even in a 200+ person lecture. That said, it is still chemistry either work hard & study or you will get weeded out. She also drops your lowest test grade

Do notttt take this class! I have never hated a professor more. She does 3 iclicker questions in class and constantly screams about how all of us are bound to fail. It is definitely not worth your time-- listen to all of the other reviews and choose a different professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Yeah I got a D in this class, VT chem almost weeded me out. But overall she was an average teacher, honestly I dont really have a good opinion since I just dont like chemistry in general . Also hopefully if shes reading this itll make her day when I say she has good music taste.

Worst professor ever my lifeeeee. If u fail the tests, prepare to take a W for the class because your entire grade will depend on those tests. In lectures, she does 3 iclickers then does two problems for the entire class and calls it a day. If I had the ability to go back in time, I would stop myself from picking this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Allows you to ask questions in class and makes sure that you understand the material.

She's a bit of a nut but she's a nice lady. Her handwriting isn't the best but she does her best to explain problems in lectures. Also has some funny lines every now and then. Not a bad prof just sometimes a little overwhelming and nutty.

If you value your time do not take this class. She has to be one of the most useless and disrespectful professors Ive come across. Failed an assignment for following the rubric because she didnt like the layout. Would give her a 0 if possible

If you are looking for an easy and interesting pathway class chem in context is what I would recommend. Eddleton is nice and gives interesting lectures that arent super math heavy so non stem majors with understand the course. All tests are writing assignments that she graded easily.

If you believe you are not a chemistry person you can still take this course and do very well. Professor Eddleton is a very understanding professor and has made the course doable for all different majors. She gives plenty of opportunities to succeed and also has very entertaining lectures. Lecture is not required necessarily, but go, they are great

Students are expected to do textbook reading and homework outside of class and come to the lecture period ready to ask questions and work practice problems. Dr. Eddleton puts in a lot of time and effort to make sure she is available to students who have questions about the content and she generally explains the content well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Eddleton is... Fine. She is pretty funny, gives fairly decent lectures, but she doesn't teach. She simply reviews textbook material that you would have gone over for homework the night before. If you hate the usual lecture learning, this is the class for you, otherwise, take someone else.

Eddleton is a classic case of college chem professors. If you read the material before arriving at the lectures, they easier to understand. If you have her be ready to read and do homework. She tries to make chem fun, but will not hand you an A without work on your part. As long as you acknowledge that you will have to work hard you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor did not once put up notes once notes during the entire semester. All we ever did was 3 iClicker questions per lecture. She always got off topic talking about random things that did not pertain to class. She would not be accesible outsite of lecture hours. I highly recommend dropping her class or finding a different Chem 1035 teacher.

IF YOUR PROFESSOR SAYS EDDLETON, DO WHATEVER IT TAKES TO SWITCH. She does not show notes in the class, literally never once did she display information. Other 1035 instructors prepared notes for their sections daily. SHE DOESNT EVEN HAVE OFFICE HOURS If you decide to stick with her, get ready for emails every night telling you ur gonna fail! :)

All this teacher does it iClicker questions. You wont learn anything at all in her class, and she is extremely unhelpful. No notes are taken in class, questions are answered in confusing ways, and she in genuinely rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is probably one of the hardest classes I had taken during my freshman year, and it wasn't good. All she does is iClicker questions, both that and the homework doesn't influence the final grade that much overall. If you want to well in that class, better be great at test-taking

All you do in class is IClicker questions. Eddleton doesn't go over notes or anything, so you are forced to read each chapter of the textbook out of class, or your grade will suffer. I would recommend choosing any other professor for CHEM 1035, as it is a demanding class.

LOVED HER. she's very tough on her students but that ended up motivating me to work hard and do well in the class. highly recommend going to all of her review sessions (she has one every week). she's super willing to help you out if you ask which is awesome. sometimes gets distracted in class but honestly it keeps it entertaining in my opinion.

If you are looking to knock out a CLE and want an easy A, I highly recommend Dr. Eddleton's Chemistry in Context class. I found her quite fun and easy-going. Your grade is made up of in class assignments and quizzes, homework responses, and in class tests (she gives you a lot of answers). As long as you show up and do your work, you will be fine.

You could tell that she really tried to be a good teacher however often the notes that she gave us to fill out would leave many sections blank leaving out crucial information that was left to the student to find on their own. One positive is that she gives you the answers for the iclicker before closing them so you should get 100% on that grade.

Eddleton herself was amazing. CHEM1035 is the most hated class I have ever taken after 3 years of college. The class sucks. TONS of innane, fill in the blank online work that barely connects to the test material. But Eddleton was super available, gave so many resources for help, tried really hard to get everyone to pass. Funny, passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Eddleton was kind of rude to my class. She would put us down a lot and didn't make it easy to access her outside of class. She doesn't have office hours, but she has a help session. She doesn't follow notes often, and mostly just goes through examples that are hard to understand sometimes. Chem is hard, and I wish I chose a different professor.
Had a blast in her class. She really cares about what she's teaching. It's a REALLY good idea to show up to lecture. Speaks with enthusiasm and passion; knows how to explain to the layman.

Very passionate about teaching. Loves to teach chem and IS AWARE THAT THIS IS AN ELECTIVE. She knows that it should NOT be a hard class and that WE DO HAVE LIVES AND OTHER CLASSES TO WORRY ABOUT.  Tophat ($) Pearson ($) Canvas and her PPT slides 5 tests. NO FINAL. OPEN BOOK/EVERYTHING. You get points for doing homework on Pearson/Tophat

Personally, Eddleton's teaching method DID NOT work for me. She goes off on tangents and skips about from one chapter to the next & back. It drives me insane. My notes looked like hell. Had to withdraw because i earned C- and needed at least C. mind you I studied my butt off only to receive awful grades on each exam. No extra credit. No curves.

She's really excited about the subject, so lectures will be filled with her energetically explaining the concepts and occasional demos where things will be blown up. Tests can be tough, but if you think you understand the concepts, you'll be fine. Recitation really helps and she offers a crazy amount of resources, including weekly help sessions.

She's really into what she teaches. She tries to show interesting demonstrations which can be pretty funny; she usually has the whole lecture hall giggling. The subject material is hard but she gives you all of the resources you need to pass the class.
Refused to teach a section of material because she didnt know the material
If you need a science elective TAKE HER. I failed 3 out of our 5 exams and still got a B based on homework and other assignments. If try at all, you're guaranteed a B. Very good prof
Ridiculously easy course if you need your science elective filled.

Great Teacher and very easy class.  You can pass the class without even taking any tests.  A lot of online work- some do weekly, and other assignments due by the end of the semester.  I would recommend this to anyone who needs to fulfill a science credit.  Eddleton is always willing to help and is very fun.

The class is pretty straight forward, she has powerpoints online and she lectures from them. She adds to the lectures so its good to come to class, she also takes attendance and its part of your grade. HW is an online book, its easy. Tests easy if you read and come to class you have 4, you drop 1. She does cool experiments and stuff too; explosions
Do the homework and you'll do well. If you're doing well you can be done by Thanksgiving. BE CAREFUL not to miss submitting homework. She drops a lot of grades.
great class to take care of your science requirement.  go to office hours and you're practically guaranteed an A on every homework.  Study homeworks for exams.
very interesting and understanding. also very funny at times. the powerpoints are great because you can add extra notes to what has already been written.

Uses power point in lectures so print out before class. Doesn't use the book religiously but do look through before tests. Homework is super easy. If you go to office hours you'll do well and get all the answers to the homework. She loves it when you ask questions!
GREAT PROFESSOR!!!

She was wonderful! i enjoyed her class so much and as long as you keep up in class and take a few notes here and there you're fine. her tests aren't bad and she tells you everything you need to study for them. She makes chemistry fun!

Oh my goodness. This woman is remarkable! She is down to Earth and has awesome knowledge of chemistry. Anyone who does not enjoy Mrs. Eddeton's class should see someone about possible psychological damage. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

awesome teacher! very helpful, just go to office hours and she will answer any questions. grading method is really easy to get a good grade. final is not cumulative and she drops a test grade... good class very enjoyable
Very easy course and she's a really nice lady. She really cares about her students and knows almost everyone's name by the end of the semester.
awesome teacher i defintly recommend her. very helpful especially if u go to office hours

I am awful at science, but I thoroughly enjoyed her class. She is very easy to talk to and is very helpful. Homeworks are tricky but she offers alot of help. Her grading is very fair, and she is very upfront about what she wants and how her tests will be.  Her class is pretty entertaining!
I love her!!
she does a lot of fun demonstrations in class
She is so much fun.  I enjoy her classes.  Some homeworks I find a little tricky, and for me atleast, it is not a free A, but I have learned a lot.   No regrets.

she's awesome. gives review for homework so you have some idea whats on the tests. gives tests more often than some teachers so you dont have to remember as much for one test. makes class fun and easy
she made class soo exciting and fun to go to.. tests are not hard if you review the notes and go to class.. she is very helpful and just a great person to learn from
Cant say enough about mrs eddleton.  really cares about her students, makes the class fun and easy, definately take this class if you need a core science.
definately take this class if you need science credits. mrs eddleton is a great teacher. many opportunities to do well in the class.
She is an awesome teacher.  Go to her office hours, she will answer any and all questions, gives a lot of opportunities to get a good grade in her class.
Great teacher, really makes the class enjoyable.  Great taste in music.
She is a great teacher. She really seems to care about the students and is willing to help anytime.  I didn't like chem in high school but she made it a relatively fun class.
She is great overall. She gives good, clear homeworks, which she drop 5 of the 15 grades, and she's willing to help anytime.
She's an awesome teacher with great demonstrations in class to keep you're attention.

One of the best professors and classes I've taken. Her class is very hard not gonna lie. I have no clue how I have an A. It's a LOT of work. The debate project took a lifetime and her tests are insanely hard. But I gained so much from this class and Dr. Jamison is truly such an amazing teacher. I was excited to go to her class no joke. So fun acc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: These reviews are lying. She is very sarcastic and over all snarky with students. She is also a tough grader, and the class is boring as a whole. Don't take if you can take something else. You will not get an A.

Not a good teacher.  She just talks in class and it's never clear what we're supposed to be learning.  The tests are based on the readings, but the questions still feel random even if you read them.  The group project is way too much work for a pathway class.  I would NOT take this as a pathway, Eli takes it way too seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Reading hw are assigned only a day or two before, the entire semester is a group project, get graded on attendance and participation matters. Didn't know the class was about superheroes the entire semester. Kind of a hard grader. She is very nice and wants everyone to learn and have fun.

Very nice, always smiling. Readings usually due before class, but never too much (and she doesn't check if you've actually done the readings). Content isn't difficult, just requires some application. Class is based around a semester long group project, so pick a good group. You'll have to meet outside of class, but it's not a hard project.

Professor Jamison was a fantastic teacher and individual. She tries her absolute best to create connections with every student in her class and gives really well-made assignments. She is passionate about what she teaches and makes every class engaging and beneficial for all parties. Would recommend to anyone!
Great professor. The class was fun and she made the content very enjoyable.

She was very sweet and understanding if you talked with her, especially during office hours. You could tell she loves teaching. Only downside with this class is it is a pathway (global bus) and I had exponentially more work than my other classes. Huge group projects that in my opinion seemed senior level. Attendance is also mandatory.

Professor Jamison is by far my favorite professor at Tech. She made it exciting to go to her class and she really cares for her students. I plan on taking her again for my senior year just because. Attendance is mandatory and speaking depends on your grade. Her class wasn't hard at all, TAKE HER if you can. She truly is the best!!!

Professor Jamison is one of my favorite professors at Virginia Tech. She is very passionate about the course and provides a room of no judgment. She makes attendance and speaking up in class mandatory to facilitate discussion. She has weekly quizzes which are not hard but her exams are difficult if you have not read the readings. 10/10 recommend.

I loved Eli so much. She was a great professor teaching wise and just as a person. The class was group project heavy and it was easy as long as you made any effort, and have a relationship with her and it help you a lot.

It wasn't an option, but I had Eli for her Global MGT class, and it was such a great experience. There's a good amount of work that you have to do for the class, but it's manageable, and she is an incredibly understanding professor if you miss something. Just take your time on the quizzes, carefully read the rubrics, and you will ace this class!

Dr. Jamison is one of the best professors at Virginia Tech. Even though she challenges us to think, it isn't difficult. Her exams aren't too difficult if you study. I look forward to her class, which is the first time I have said that in college.

Quizzes every week were a pain. They did make you read the book though. Tests were almost too damn easy you did the same project 4 times with same group on different companies. Cpap, tca are pretty much same thing. Good group and divide and conquer are best strategy. She has no control over the classroom people constantly talk over her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Jamison is the BEST! She gives amazing feedback and genuinely wants you to do well in her class. I highly recommend taking anything she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Love this professor. She is so friendly and actually wants you to succeed. A bit of a hard grader but that's my only critique. I'm taking another one of her classes since she's such a good teacher.

Dr. Lin was a good professor. However, he talks in a very monotone voice making it difficult to stay engaged during lectures. Also, he has an accent that was difficult for me to understand especially because he is very quiet.

Dr. Lin is not the best professor, but he is by no means bad. Out of the professor pool for PHYS2305, he is easily the best option. His lectures are engaging with useful demos, and he loves to make jokes. 25% of your grade is the lab and recitation section, so don't worry too much about exams. You will have to teach yourself some content, though.

He is for sure passionate about physics, but it's hard to understand the material. He expects people to know what he is talking about when in reality very few do. The exams feel like nothing we learned in class or on the homework/ given study materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: These lecutres made it so hard to come to class it was so boring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice professor, just boring. Not even his fault; the class just drags. He tries to keep it interesting by doing demonstrations in class. Easy to get in touch with, answers emails fast, even late at night. Super test-heavy, but the pre-quiz can save you. Having a good formula sheet is key. Lab is a drag, super long, mostly just busy work though.
Very boring professor and does not prepare the students well for the tests. This is the only difference between the different profs, the syllabus is the same.

Professor Lin gives fantastic lectures as he explains everything clearly and tries his best to show how formula comes. He gives extra credit except the optional quizzes. Exams are really easy and similar to pre quiz and practice problems. His clickers questions are in line with the material he just said, so listen carefully and they'll be easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: lectures are boring but he does his best to keep the class engaged 2306 is jus buns tho
Good professor who did many in-class examples and demonstrations. However, it can be a little hard to follow his work on the board sometimes.
Really nice and tries as best as he can to help students understand material. Does lots of demos in class. Personally didn't like 2306 but he made it a lot easier. Def recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very kind professor who gives a lot of extra credit and curves the tests as well. Lectures can be a bit boring, but he occasionally does live demonstrations of the concepts we discuss, which can be interesting. Would definitely recommend for physics.

He definitely seems like a good professor but I just suck at physics. He would crack some funny and unexpected jokes during his lectures so definitely pay attention for those. Overall a good professor but like I said I just suck at physics.
Really nice and kind professor. I got 100 in the exam, and another 5 extra credits because of the curve for the whole class.

I think his lectures were mediocre and hard to pay attention to but a really nice guy and the class is not hard to get a good grade in. As long as you have okay test scores and don't f up lab you're set for an A or B. All tests are CTE so no advantage of any class, iclickers are so easy its basically extra credit (there is also actual extra credit.

solid professor, lectures are pretty boring as he just works through problems on the boards with the occasional iClicker question. he's not the best at going in depth for things so you'll probably have to study quite a bit. overall good prof. hard subject

Very helpful, funny, and a caring teacher. His lectures are thoughtful and well-prepared, with a lot of practice problems. The last 2 tests can be a little trickier, but the curve is so high that everyone generally does pretty well. He is extremely nice and has nothing bad to say about him.

His lectures are really good but can be hard to keep up with when solving a long problem, but it's my fault for not studying the material before hand (which you are supposed to do by doing the weekly reading). His demos are legendary. The things I don't like about the class aren't related to him (recitation and lab).

Be prepared to put in a lot of work between recitation, lab, reading quizzes, and homework. Exams are curved based on pre-quizzes. He's very sweet and if you pay attention in lecture, this class will be a breeze. Definitely the best option for foundations 1 (from what I've heard about other teachers)

Professor Lin is very sweet and friendly. I'm not the greatest at physics but his lectures made it easy to understand, and he is very approachable. I can tell he genuinely wants the best for his students. This course is hard but he does his best to help out his students.
The nicest guy you will ever meet, but he is not great at teaching. This makes his course very hard, but I still like him.

Dr. Lin is honestly just a silly guy, and I would feel bad saying anything bad about him. I genuinely just really dislike electromagnetism physics, so i didnt pay much attention during class, only for the iclickers. as long as you know what to put on your equation sheet, youre set. he curves tests very generously, so i wouldnt worry.
Uses clicker question every class. Is very understandable and nice. To the people complaining about the big tests, that isn't his control that's the physics' department heads. I would take him again.
Great guy!

Professor Lin was pretty good overall. Very nice professor and responds to any questions/emails pretty quickly. Lectures were sometimes a little hard to follow. The weight of the labs and homework make up for the two exams. IClicker grades were also used.
His accent is tough to understand at first, but he knows what he's talking about. Occasionally overexplains things, but overall he's a solid teacher who cares about what he does.

Fei is a great professor, while a little boring at times, he gets his point across and is a really nice guy. His accent is tough at first but honestly I never really misunderstood him. If you have any prior physics knowledge from high school, you will most likely pass, since I zoned out during a lot of the lectures and did fine.

Dr. Lin is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are easy to follow and he explains concepts really well. He does many experiments and demonstrations in class as well. Dr. Lin is the GOAT!!
10/10 Physics 2 professor. Phy Did a stellar job explaining physics c

Fei Lin is a W. The nicest and funniest professor you will ever encounter at Virginia Tech. Sometimes goes too quickly in lectures but is super helpful and available in office hours and before/ after class. He will be invited to my wedding.

PHYS2305 is difficult if it's your first time seeing physics. Lin is a very understanding professor, his lectures prepare you well so don't skip (iClicker too). There are only 2 exams but your grade is comprised of so many different categories (lab + studio) an A is extremely manageable. Exams are "curved" with pre-quizzes.

Tough accent, very hard to understand. Lecture heavy, and the lectures get boring quickly. Attendance is graded through IClicker quizzes. Only two tests in the class, both are INCREDIBLY material heavy (like 50 topics each). 
Lecture attendance is not mandatory, but recommended. Class grade depends on tests + lab grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lin is one of the nicest professors and he is very accessible outside of class as long as you communicate with him. I find physics to be difficult in general, but he genuinely wants you to succeed. Gives iClickers often throughout class, so attend regularly. Lectures can be boring, but his powerpoints are helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lin's lectures prepare you for what is on the tests. He is also very very kind with IClicker questions and will help guide the class to the right answer. Overall he's a nice guy and he wants everyone to succeed. As far as physics professors go at VT, he's pretty good.

He's a nice guy and his lectures aren't THAT bad. iClicker was 12% of your grade so going to class was important. There was also an extra credit quiz system in place to help curve your midterms and final exam. Overall the course is just hard and you have to put in a lot of work if you want to finish with a high grade no matter the professor.

Went over lecture material pretty well, but didn't know that all his students were not physics geniuses. Gave easy iClicker questions, and 1 10 question HW assigned per week. 2 midterms and a final, each 20 questions really took a toll on your grade. If you didn't study or understand problems too well, it wouldn't end well. Sometimes curve exams.

Love the man! His lectures are very easy to follow along with as he posts lecture slides far in advance. He is very detailed with showing his work and he goes through the step by strip process clearly! Definitely deserves more than 3/5

I had a decent amount of knowledge in physics coming into this class, which helped a ton, and I see a lot of people saying the same thing, but I think thats just how physics is at tech. The lecture, problem solving and lab are disjointed and dont line up, and tests have a huge weight on your grade. Physics at tech is overall bad, its not just Lin.
Overcomplicated the material and kind of just worked through practice problems instead of actually teaching. Main thing I learned from this class is that the physics program here is disorganized

As much as I want to like Dr. Lin, he is a horrible lecturer. Smart guy, but forgets that we're just dumb college students. Two tests that weigh a quarter of your grade takes a nice toll on you. Lot of your grade will depend on your studio and lab grade. Invest in some Monsters to chug before classes.

Prof Lin is a super nice guy and I want to like him so bad, but he is just such a bad lecturer. I took a lot of physics in high school, so I basically just coasted, but his explanations honestly hurt more than they help. He overcomplicates a lot of problems, and I would recommend another professor if possible. Good at responding to emails, though.
He's a very smart guy and knows a lot about physics, and I think that's what makes him a horrible professor. He lectures like "you should just know this it's common sense" but it really isn't.
Definitely knows what he is talking about, but seems to forget that his students don't. He is hard to understand as well. I would recommend another professor if you don't feel like getting a tutor.

You've seen it before, physics at Tech sucks. Fei Lin wasn't outstandingly amazing, but I don't know if there are any other better professors. His handwriting is neat on the board and he goes through relevant practice problems. He wants his students to do well!

Fei Lin in my opinion is one of the best physics professors you can find at VT. He makes the subject interesting and does his best to explain all concepts. His explanations make sense and the notes he provides in class are more than enough to score well in the exams.

I am not a fan physics in general, and I really dislike it. Dr. Lin didn't make it super engaging but he did try to! I was often bored and could barely focus. Dr. Lin was as good as he could be for the course, but because the course is garbage, its impossible to teach it in a good way, in my opinion.

Took PHYS 2305 with him online for Spring 21. Everything he went over in lecture was useful for exams. I strictly studied just lectures and the slides, there was nothing on exams that he did not teach in lecture. Physics @VT is challenging by nature, but he will guide you in the right direction by going through many practice problems in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He goes over practice problems but you do need to study outside of class if physics is something that is hard for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is really a friendly person. There is a lot of thinking in his class some of them were challenging, but overall it helps you to understand physics much better. His exam is always similar to his practice exam, thus, as long as you do the practice you can get an easy A on the exam.

If you have never taken physics before avoid this man at all costs. He is probably the worst teacher I have ever had because he doesn't explain anything. It may be easier if you have taken physics before but I hadn't and he taught me absolutely nothing.

He's a nice guy but the worst teacher I have ever had. He is hard to understand and does not explain the material for crap. If you have taken physics in highschool, more than just a semester, then you may be fine. If you only have taken Physics once before, you will be taking the tests in this class blind. In other words hes a terrible teacher.

Take Stuart as a last resort! He is very unprepared for classes and creates assignments last second. I was weary if his rating was fair but I can now confidently say it is. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS! Very extensive homework and he has very little care about his students. He expects the TA's to answer your questions and is not accessible for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Almost the whole class was McGraw Hill. Large assignments were given with short notice and the professor made random course changes, including switching to hybrid. Most of the grade was based on three exams. I would either not take this professor or heavily study the McGraw Hill chapters and practice exams
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM, he doesn't teach just tells you to do smartbooks, any time you need help he tells you talk to the TA's who know even less than us. He refuses to have exceptions for anything, one time he posted 3 assignments after the due date and said there would be no late credit because in the real world thangs happen and we all got 0's

I took Feigenbaum this semester, and it is easily the roughest intro course at the whole school. He goes through slides once a week, yells at students for the same thing every class, and is irritable and unhappy. Tests are averaged in the 50's for a reason, and he doesn't curve. He also randomly made the class hybrid. DO NOT TAKE

Genuinely just reads off the slides for every lecture, and wonders why we all fail the tests. The tests are pretty difficult, you can study for four days and still fail. He also does not curve anything, despite the low grades and the extra credit he assigns is intense work. Homework assignments take forever and aren't worth anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor expects you to teach yourself the topics before class, and then proceeds to spend the entirety of class just reading off of PowerPoints, while then complaining about poor attendance. He also blindsided everyone by announcing the class would be a hybrid instead of only in-person, when the class was only listed as in-person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Read off slides once a week then expected us to teach ourselves the rest. Then blames the students for the lower test averages, and the lack of participation. Not to mention all work is worth a total of 3% of your grade and the rest is exams. Expect to get yelled at every class for things that are a result of his teaching.

Not a good professor. He professes that his class is "run like a business" so he can hand down any professor duties to his TA's. His exams are 80% McGraw Hill questions and he spends actual class rambling about nothing. IF THERE IS AN OPTION FOR A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR FOR HTM 2314, TAKE THE OTHER PROFESSOR!!!!!!!!!

Attendance is semi-mandatory (some chapter tests have codes), but if it doesn't, don't show up. Just work through the weekly assignments and don't go to class, he can get confusing. He won't accept late work or make-ups under any circumstances; he doesn't care if you get the dean to write a note, "It comes down to whatever I say, and I'll say no."
Definitely a bit of a challenging course, but if you do the readings you shouldn't have any issues. Exams are straightforward
He's disorganised and the homework assignments that take 1-2 hours are worth like 10% while the exams are like 70% of your grade. Easy class and textbook's 130 bucks but would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I passed with an A bc I did everything myself. He doesn't provide helpful study resources and everything is on McGraw Hill.

He was great! I could listen to his stories all day and not get bored! If you can make it to class he doesn't get upset but wants you there. I feel like i learned some cool things in his class especially because I'm not in the major.

Class was very disorganized. Problems occurred almost every week with assignments. Exams were harder than the homework. There was extra credit opportunities, but he used the extra credit as an excuse to not take accountability for messing up grades, or assignments. I would not recommend but I would not avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stuart is a stud but should not have a job as a professor. He thinks his class structure of “running it like a business” is genius while it is merely an excuse for him to be lazy and delegate to his “managers” (TA's). Cannot say that I have learned a single thing in one of his lectures being that he teaches for 10 minutes of the 85 minute class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please please please try to avoid taking this professor. I managed to scrape by with an A- but only because I did every single extra credit opportunity. I don't even know how else to describe it other than he literally wants you to fail. He switches around due dates for fun with no warning and lectures you if you miss them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is the most incompetent professor I have ever had; every class is spent working through the mistakes he's made throughout the week, he randomly assigns and changes due dates, most of the learning is done through Smart books that are way too long. This isn't a hard class, but I would strongly recommend a different professor.

His "lectures" were 100% useless, just a random reiteration of textbook info. Stuart was consistently rude when anyone asked a question.  He sometimes assigned tests two hours before we had to take them, with no warning. He even assigned a test before the readings for that chapter were due once, so no one knew the material. DON'T TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are the exact questions on the quizzes and tests, so that's the best thing to study. His lectures were kind of pointless to go to, as they didn't pertain to the assignments. The group project was okay, but very random, not too hard, but annoying to get your group together. This class is alright if you know what to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS, but if you do wind up taking his course just spam the chapter practice quizzes and tests because they are literally the test questions.

If you just so happen to be one of the lucky individuals who get to take his class, drop out while you can. Up until him, I have never hated one of my professors as much as I do him. He might as well be Mr. McGraw Hill himself. He is very passionate about the subject but by no means is he a good professor and he is very outdated.

Easily the worst professor I've had a Tech. Lectures are just him rambling and it seems like he just likes to rant about our age group while claiming he's trying to help out. Everything about the way he runs his class is horrible, avoid if you can.

If you're not religious, pick a religion and pray. He is awful, assigns meaningless work, and rude to students. The class was based on Mcgraw Hill and his lectures were so unhelpful. Avoid at all costs.

This guy is so bad, I've never felt the need to make an account to write a review about someone until now. Crazy amounts of work are given each week, they aren't hard but barely count toward your grade, which is 70% tests. He changes grades randomly like 5 times and when emailing to him he complained why we wanted our points back. Avoid if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goes off track in lecture to claim "this is what a real college course is like" to justify poor teaching practices. Ignore good reviews, they are simply regurgitating what he says because they don't know the difference between an authority figure and a professor. Real college courses have real instruction, real engagement, and real structure.

He is not a good professor and doesn't care for this age group, although he claims he does. He admits that he cares about our education, but he manipulates your grades to get you to email him and complains that you emailed him.

Very sweet and passionate teacher who clearly knows his stuff. Assigns more work than others, BUT it's super helpful for the exams, which are very similar to the homework. Class only meets once a week, with an optional second session for questions.
Sets clear expectation and if you do the assignments they are just like the exams. It says you meet 2 times a week but it's really only 1 which is nice.

Stuart is the reason I do not look before crossing the street. The class is fully ran through McGraw Hill, besides the 3 exams that are nitpicked from the most specific details from the chapter. Half the time he has assignments listed wrong, and the class is extremely disorganized. Attendance is mandatory but he just summarized the textbook.
He's very disorganized and doesn't really know or understand how to use technology.

Had him the the Fall of 2022, he's a lowlight. He seems very lazy and unprofessional in his teaching style. Give out way too much homework and give us limited time to work on exams. Definitely one of the worst professors at Pamplin.

The only professor at Tech I could say I had a problem with. Incredibly rude in emails and when asked for help. TAs take care of most things, and they barely know what is going on. In class he reads off the slideshows and doesn't expand on topics at all. I would absolutely not take this class especially since it's supposed to be easy.

This professor is embarrassingly terrible. I wish he would just quit or be fired. He doesn't teach anything and he is so terribly boring. He's so old and asks questions about current events when he bothers to show up to class. Which is like never. He has a house in Florida he needs to just retire and go to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is absolutely awful, he never responds to your emails, as well as not knowing or being on time when it comes to putting in grades. When responding to emails he responds angry and always the most difficult ways around things. He is a very confusing professor as he may say something but he will change everything he said the next day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Some lectures can be boring but it is not difficult to succeed if you try in the class. He will give out extra credit and is very open to asking questions after class. The tests are similar to the textbook and homeworks so definitely study with that material. The work is also manageable.

Stuart is 20 years past his prime. He spends more time talking about the class structure than he does actually teaching the content. He might as well change his last name to "McGraw Hill" because that's the entire class. What happened to teachers actually teaching instead of just handing us a McGraw Hill packet yo?

The material isn't hard, but the international business class is VERY test-heavy (almost 70% of the grade is on tests). Every week, there is a reading assignment, and it's usually around an hour long. There are a lot of grades, but it doesn't matter if you fail the tests. If you don't do well on the tests, your grade won't be recoverable.
