reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Feigenbaum is the worst professor I've had. The workload is absolutely unreasonable. The material is easy, but he overcomplicates it. His teaching method is disorganized and confusing, alternating between in-person and online and will cancel class without notice. He's rude and dismissive with no respect or care for students. Don't do it.

There was weekly homework assignments that were just reading the chapter and answering anywhere from 50-120 questions correctly. Other than that the class is super easy. Study the McGraw quizzes for the tests, many of the questions will be the same. I stopped going to class because his lectures were just the textbook chapter from the homework.

This class only requires attendance once a week and you will have a discussion group. You have a chapter a week and in class assignment. The final is not cumulative and there are up to 5 full points of extra credit offered. As long as you understand in college you have to do work you will do well. He rounds final grades too(89.7=90)interesting clas
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, the reviews dont do him justice. it's a true college class and a lot of people complain because they can't handle the work. I definely learned a lot in his class.

He's not a really good professor. He reads off slides and the homework is not bad, but it barely barely raises your grade. Your grade is pretty dependent on the exams which are lockdown + camera. In-class quiz. The exams aren't easy. I also looked at his LinkedIn and he used to work for playboy which made me feel weird as a woman.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Feigenbaum was not as bad as the reviews state. He gives a good chunk of homework but its manageable and was not hard by any means. The main portion of your grade are exams. There are three exams but no final. The BEST way to prep for exams is practice the homework tests/quizzes. Most or even all of the exam questions come from there.

I enjoyed having him as my professor. If you talk to him after class, he will sometimes offer to look at your test to see if there are any "ambiguous" questions he can give points for. Do the readings and QUIZZES and tests many times to study. It is daunting at first, but it is just fine as long as you put time and effort in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Feigenbaum is undoubtedly knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter, but students should be prepared for a heavy workload. The online course is packed with assignments that can feel overwhelming at times. There's a significant amount of busy work, which often detracts from the learning experience rather than enhancing it.

Stuart is a wonderful professor with a wealth of knowledge in the industry. He may be a little old-fashioned, but he encourages real-life application like no other professor I've had. Yes, the Connect assignments are tedious, but they're not difficult and if you study his exams are not hard. Great prof if you really enjoy learning!

This professor is low-key lazy in terms of organizing this class. So many assignments due each week and heavily proctored exams. Its a shame cause this class content is compelling. Just wish he would do more.

Stuart is basically never present, except for his zoom lectures. Don't expect to hear back from him if you write an email to him. The class is all over the place and the grading can be inconsistent. He will sometimes curve exams if grades look bleak, but he insists he doesn't believe in curves. He tells us to get over a bad grade, he's ridiculous.

He is completely incapable of being a professor. Doesn't teach at all and never responds to emails. His TA's are also useless and just as in the dark of whats going on. This class feels like a failed science experiment.
Just wish that Professor Feigenbaum would use class time to expand on what's in the textbooks...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's terrible. We are halfway through the semester and he still seems unsure about the setup of the class. He barely teaches anything and spends most of his time complaining about class participation.  He says that our 50-question quiz should be finished in 15 minutes. The only teacher at Virginia tech that I can say I really dislike.

Avoid if possible. He makes an online intro class a total pain. Its a shame because the content is very interesting. I just wish he tough the material instead of piling a bunch of homework for us to complete in a small window.

Stuart genuinely wants all of his students to succeed!! Just pay attention and do the practice tests and quizzes repeatedly when studying and you will be fine trust. The people who wrote bad reviews literally don't know what they are talking about.

This class just plain sucked. Stewart was disorganized and very unhelpful when it came to asking questions. He's very unreliable, as he will never answer emails and will randomly adjust grading scales without informing the class. That alone made this class unbelievably stressful, even though the subject matter was very interesting.
Not an enjoyable class, period. Wish he actually tough something and gave us more time to complete exams.

Super straightforward and easy to get an A. There's a smartbook, HW, quiz and test for every chapter which seems like a lot, just start early not 2 hours before it's due. For the exams, practice the tests and quizzes repeatedly and you can get a high B or A. He tells you exactly what to do to pass and wants all his students to do well.
Great professor, while the class may move a little slowly, he is very helpful and forgiving if you meet with him. He you join the zoom and turn your camera on you are good to go.
He made this class more nail bitingly stressful than it needed to be. Like come on, its an intro class, should be an easy A.

The way he structures this class is horrendous. He unintentionally makes the class a lot more difficult than it needs to be. Plus you have to attend his stupid single zoom session every week otherwise he'll deduct your overall grade. The class feels entirely disorganized and truly aggravating after a couple weeks. Class is interesting though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself is not super difficult, but the way he structures the class is ridiculous. Gives unnecessary large amounts of homework that doesn't really affect your grade, but it DOES help you for the exams. All I can say if if your taking this class with Stewart, make a study group and stay diligent.

He said attendance isn't required at the beginning of the semester then it turns out that at the end it is worth 5%. His lectures are very useless. I loved the content but when I joined the class it was super boring. Uses a $125  textbook that insanely adds big amount of work you do every week compared to other professors who teach the same course.

Asynchronous class where he and the TA did absolutely nothing. Everything is done on the online textbook and the powerpoints are literally just pages from the textbook. Expect to teach yourself everything then take an exam with ridiculously random questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Test #1 results: low = 44, Q1 = 68, median = 78, Q3 = 88, high = 100. No curves. 3 tests in total, each 22% of our grade.

Our class is "flipped classroom" which means we have to do the homework before he teaches the material (aka reiterating our textbook), so it's basically self-taught. Only reason ppl show up is because attendance is graded.

Don't bother going to the zoom calls. There's 1 discussion you need to do with 3-8 other students. I didn't even prep for it and got 100. The homework is just busywork. Very tedious. Due dates are at noon, and not midnight. This screwed me over a few times. Do the "Quiz" homework as many times as you can; it's the best way to prep for the tests.

The lectures were once a week. The class was max 30 min each week because he claimed he couldn't teach the class because "nobody did work." More than half of that was talking poorly about the people who don't show up to class. There were 4 extremely long assignments per week. Completely self taught class and tests weighted 72% of the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As an async teacher, he was entirely absent. When I emailed about the potential to retake a quiz he gave a long (sorta harsh) lecture about why he doesn't believe in retakes/extra credit and basically said, to study harder next time. Didn't provide any extra value to the class, it was just the textbook and quizzes, he did no teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every week there are 4 assignments due for a chapter on the day of class, sometimes 2 (totaling 8 assignments in one week). He offers no extra credit, made it clear he doesn't think it is needed. The exams are worth 72% of your grade and he offers no curve because he's "never had to". No exam prep material. Don't take this class or you'll use a W.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Feigenbaum is my favorite professor at Tech. He has a tough personality and can be very blunt or brutally honest. However, if you do the work and attend his lectures (which alway go under the given time), you will succeed in his class. He gives grades for participation and discussion so come prepared. He cares about his students!!!

Everything is done on McGraw Hill Connect. There is Smartbook(1-2 hours) HW(20-40 mins), practice quiz(10mins/optional), and a weekly test(15min) If you wait until last minute you wont get it done. He gives multiple chapters due once a week. I wish I took a regular class and not this dumb hybrid. Take him and this class if everything is filled up.

**Taken spring 2019** I've heard this class got harder. When I took it, he took attendance @ beginning and then you could leave, but I stayed to enjoy the lectures. He is so knowledgable about HTM and cares about your success. Would love to take another one of his classes. I used Chegg for the HWs.

Tests were way more difficult than they needed to be. This class used to be easy a few semesters ago but he has made it so much harder now. Stay away from this professor if you can. He is very disorganized and not very helpful. Calls out on people in class and forces you to answer. Very boring class and the professor definitely did not help at all.

This class was one of the most disorganized classes I have ever taken. The professor barely knew how to work the software he chose for our class and was constantly changing due dates and homework settings to the point that if you were not checking it every day you would miss assignments. Tests were incredibly hard and not at all based on lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Being a hybrid class, you only have to go one a week (he counts attendance as a grade) and then do a weekly quiz. The 4 exams are made up completely of quiz questions and you can take the quizzes as many times as you want. Seems like a nice guy but can be kind of condescending or rude at times. My easiest class freshman year.
This guy is great!  He knows so much and makes it fun to learn.  It's a must take.
A great professor. Class isn’t very hard, and you'll actually learn a lot of very valuable skills. Just don’t miss class! Missing those quizzes will hurt you greatly.
Great guy, hard class.

His teaching style: 3 objectives are, learn about service, have fun, & get a good grade. He trys to make his classes fun & interactive, he wants you to come and just hear his anecdotes about service, he knows you'll learn without having to really try- which as it turns out is an effective method
such an awesome professor. the class is an easy A if you just go to class and he makes it fun. i actually learned without trying
Prof. Feigenbaum is so helpful he takes time out of his own schedule to help out his students, and he will also be very understanding....not to mention he makes class fun!!

dude, save your grade and mental health, 50% of the class failed the first two midterms, and he has the audacity to get mad at us for doing poor. Actually save yourself, DO NOT take this professor please.

Go to the lectures, write everything down on autopilot because muscle memory is key here and he goes through it quickly. If you write ahead, spend that time figuring out the material and marking things you don't know for later. Spend little time and effort on homework, which is high effort for diminishing returns and low grades. Don't trust him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Rabby for Linear Algebra 1. This was the most difficult class of my life. With that being said, considering how hard it is he did a good at adjusting homework difficulty and lecture content based off the students need. Classes are incredibly fast paced but the tests were extremely fair, mostly based off homework and lectures.

Canvas has no purpose, and he recommended 4 separate textbooks lol. His lectures are 95% definitions which are represented as 15% of the test, and the 85% of the test is that 5% of lecture where he actually does examples. My friend who stayed in the class said by the end, 2/3 the class had dropped/withdrew. Grading takes 3+ weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hardest class i've ever taken in my life even harder than orgo ngl. After i took his class, im no longer afraid of jaywalking. I pray to the god even though im atheist for people who'll be suffer in his class and for him to reconsider his career.

Dr. Rabby's lectures were practically useless. He moves at the speed of light and does not post his lecture notes. Also gave impromptu quizzes in class to track attendance. Homework assignments were practically impossible and took at least 15 hours to do. He does curve exams a lot, which is his only redeeming quality.
Lectures are hard to follow, prepare to spend 10+ hours per week outside of class to self-study or to read the textbook.

Fazle is a character. Hardest class I've taken at vt but I learned so much. He was super inconsistent and kind of inaccessible but he does care about us. Lectures are confusing but helpful you have to lock in though. Forces you to put in a lot of effort but I really did get a lot out of it. Interesting and funny guy. Absolutely grotesque homeworks.

Really nice professor and graded fairly. In-class FRQ quizzes were difficult and the homeworks took a while, but there were a lot of ways to get extra points. Lectures are fast and a lot of writing, but helpful for the tests and quizzes. Office hours were also really helpful to understand the material.

Would definitely take Dr. Rabby again - he really pushes and inspires you to deeply understand math and cares a lot about his students. The hw and mcq/frq quizzes are very challenging, however will only count for a small percentage of your grade, and the tests are extremely fair. Go to office hours - super helpful for hw and general understanding.

I highly recommend taking orofessor tabby for any class. He is a hard teacher but that is a good thing. He cares about students and tried to push them further than they think they can go. You will not only learn more math in his classes than others, but grow as a person/academic.

Very theory-heavy lectures that require relearning the material. Insanely hard written homeworks. He will drop more grades than the syllabus says, and he wants everyone to pass his class. The 2204 concepts aren't too bad, so his tests aren't that bad either. Know how to sketch 3D regions. He also likes to reuse lecture practice problems on exams

He's a good but hard teacher. Working with 3 others, his written homework took us at least 5hrs. He talks about math theory most of the time. He takes into consideration input from the class. He writes A LOT, so be prepared to take notes quickly. He was very generous in grading. He gave extra credit for showing up early to tests.

Hes a goodguy but my god his lectures were terrible. He was so unorganized and literally said he didn't want to be here. bro? On top of that hes a very lecture heavy professor and also graded for attendance. His hw were absolutely disgusting. He said himself that his class was hard and bro he was right. Save yourself now don't make your life hard.

This topic is extremely powerful and allows you to push calculus very far. Dr. Rabby's class is more difficult than other professor's because he tries to push and inspire his students. He changed the way I see math. If you see the importance of a deep understanding of math, take his class.

Very tough class but was worth it. You will spend 15+ hours a week doing homework and the class is very difficult and proof heavy. However, he regularly holds office hours and is always willing to help his students. His lectures are very speedy but he thoroughly covers the content. Also a funny guy. Will drop homework and quiz grades at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gave an unbelievable amount of homework. I had to dedicate at least 18 hours a week to just homework. This does not account for time spent studying. Quizzes were given during class and they were not easy. Good person, but absolutely horrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Be prepared to spend 15+ hours a week on his class. He gives at least one homework a week, occasionally 2 a week. His tests are 75% doing problems and 25% proofs. He is extremely proof-heavy on homework and shows very few examples of computing the problem in class. Make sure you have the availability to go to his office hours every day. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Rabby is an amazing teacher for MATH 2114. His lectures are interesting and informative. His homework and quizzes are very challenging but they prepare you very well for the tests. If you show up to every class on time and ready to learn you will struggle but you will learn linear algebra on a deep level. His office hours are amazing as well.

Very hard class because Dr. Rabby really cares about his students learning. Take good notes in the lectures! The homework and quizes are hard but prepare you well for the test which are very similar to quizes. He will drop lowest homeworks at the end of the semester so don't sweat your grade too much. Prepares you well for the final.

One of the best classes I've taken yet at VT. Fazle Rabby is an amazing math professor, and he has really good lectures. He puts a lot of time and work into teaching his students. This class is difficult, but if you get through it you learn a lot and are prepared for future classes. Definitely recommend if you want to understand linear algebra.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The first lecture was honestly very overwhelming. But, Dr. Rabby holds office hours every day for 2+ hours. And the office hours are essential because he wants everyone to fully grasp the material and do well in his class. He cares about every one of his students and will help you any second he can.

His class is probably the hardest you can get. Regularly assigns 5-10 hour homework. Sure, he teaches the content with more depth than other profs. Unless you're a math major, the amount of time you sink into his class isn't worth it once you're onto the next class, since you won't be expected to know everything he teaches you.

Lectures were quick paced. Understanding what he was teaching was hard while trying to take notes. The homeworks took time, he constantly pushed them back by a few days because people asked for extra time.

Dr. Rabby is the best math teacher Ive had at VT. His class does have a lot of proofs which you might find annoying if you're not a math major but I think they really help solidify your understanding of the subject matter. He's also one of the most respectful and understanding professors I've had.

Dr. Rabby's class will seem extremely difficult at first, but he has office hours every single day during the week for 2 hours and will help you with anything that you are struggling with. And, if you are willing to stick it out he gives you a ton of opportunity to drop grades and get extra credit. He's the best!

This was an insanely hard class. Although I pulled an A, it was more work than all my other classes combined. You MUST attend every class or you will miss material. He intentionally makes the beginning of the class a nightmare to make people drop. That being said, he will teach you linear algebra and he will teach it well.

Rabby's class is NOT an easy A or an easy class. He spent the first half of the semester purposefully scaring his students and half the class dropped by late drop. He lectures via almost exclusively theory and his homework is mostly proofs. You will not pass his class if you skip and he gives out more work than any other linear instructor.

His class is extremely hard but the key is to participate in class and go to office hours. His class is great if you are really interested in learning A LOT of theory and proofs, but if you want an easy A, go with another professor.
If you are a woman, he will pick on you, starting from the first day of class.

This is definitely one of the best professors I have had at Virginia Tech. Dr. Rabby puts an incredible amount of effort into his classes and truly cares for his students success. His office hours are really really good and you should try to go to all of them if you want an A. Overall, amazing guy but a very very VERY hard class with lots of work.

Very engaging and well thought out course. One of the only good math instructors at Tech. Would recommend if you enjoy math and the theory behind it, but if you don't care and only want to get things over with, maybe don't take him as a teacher. Overall, great experience and super helpful... he is also very funny so that also carries thru the class

Good lecturer and accessible outside of class time if you need any help. Does have hard HWs but he does this so students have a better foundation for the final. If you put the effort into the class and attend office hours, you should do good. He also allows you to retake quizzes after the mid-point of the semester, which should help your grade.

If you are taking linear with professor rabby, be prepared for a miserable semester. Mandatory classes, long homeworks (5-10+ hours per week), not accessible outside of class since every student will be at his office hours, and complicated, strictly graded tests. When I left the class, everyone I knew was failing.

I really wanted to like Professor Rabby. He seemed like he likes his students, but he doesn't. The homeworks, quizzes, and tests were graded to a criteria I didn't understand, and it was stuff I've never seen before. He also said he wanted students to drop and struggle so they could learn how to study. It took 10 hours every week of my time.

Assigns very difficult homework assignments and quizzes, yet they are on concepts he did not teach in class. He is very disorganized. I am three weeks into his class and we are very behind other classes. Goes fast through lectures. Lets you know last minute about pop quizzes at very inconvenient times (fridays on lockdown browser) outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I genuinely do not understand how so many people like this guy. Maybe he's good for 1225 or 1226, but he was horrendous for 2114. He speaks and writes so fast and never really goes into any detail, so all I could do was try to play catch up. 2 weekly quizzes at very inconvenient times (weekends), and his homework is NOTHING like lecture, so hard.

Not gonna lie his class is hard and many students dropped at the beginning due to difficult weekly quizzes. However, it is clear the Rabby cares so much about his students  he holds office hours very often and will drop lowest quiz grades/let you retake quizzes at the end of the semester. One of the best teachers despite the difficult course!

I took Rabby for Linear Algebra. Class at first was difficult, however, he really cares about his students and that we actually learn the material. He will force you to learn it. Overall my favorite math professor and a really good guy. I recommend taking any of his sections for math.

I'll be honest, this class was hard. The homework and the quizzes, especially the MC ones, were very challenging. You will most likely fail every one. But he lets you retake them at the end, drops a lot of grades, and the tests are very similar to the quizzes and you will be well prepared for the exam. Highly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Rabby in his first semester teaching 2204. He had a MC quiz on thursday and FR quiz on friday for almost every week, and not gonna lie they are hard; however, he dropped many of them and let us retake all MC quiz. Hard HW. Easyish exams. Rabby is a really great and caring Math prof, he had office hours almost every day. He made me love calc.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He does give a lot of work, but its not busywork and he is available to give great feedback and to help. He cares a lot about your grade and his students, and his teaching style is very thorough and he makes the content easy to understand. He's intimidating at first but a really great guy once you know him. Very flexible and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rabby was a great guy he cares for your grade if you put in the work and attend office hours. He praises you if you are a good student and if you read the textbook, that being said tho you actually have to read and do the homework if you want to do well in the class. Also beware of twice a week quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is hard, if you dont try. You will need to make sure you attend class and do the work. It may seem a lot but if you stick it through and try, you will probably be good. He is a funny guy that gives inspirational quotes from time to time. He is easy on the eyes and his outfit is iconic. He is a professor that you want. (^o^)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof. Rabby has easily become one of my favorite professors, he wants you to succeed, but to do so you must put in the effort. It may seem overwhelming the amount of homework and quizzes he gives, but its not in-place to hurt your grades at all. Go to review sessions and take COPIOUS amounts of notes because the material covered WILL come up again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I cannot speak higher of Rabby. He is very nice and loves to help out if you have questions. He seems scary at first, but really cares and is a good teacher. His class is challenging, with weekly quizzes and difficult HW, but he ends up dropping about half of the quizzes and written assignments at the end of the semester if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Rabby is a very good calc teacher, he does give a TON of challenging homework that other profs didn't have. There are alot of quizzes also, but he basically drops 50% of them which helps alot. He is the self-proclaimed hardest calc teacher at VT but he is nice, a good teacher overall, and really wants everyone to pass.

Dr. Rabby is a very good calc teacher, he does give a ton of challenging homework though, and lots of extra quizzes people with other profs dont have to do. At the end of the semester he basically drops everything though to make it even. He is the self-proclaimed hardest calc teacher at VT but he is very funny and nice and a good teacher overall.

His class is hard but it will prepare you for harder math courses, he wants students to succeed and will drop and/or give reattempts on many of the quizzes and homeworks at the end of the semester. Put in genuine effort and work and you'll be rewarded for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Rabby is tough, but he will drop half the quizzes and homework if you put in honest effort. His recitations were helpful because the problems presented would help you on the homework's and tests. Sometimes the test problems would be straight from the homework. Gives out about 10 quizzes but his review sessions are very helpful after.

Makes the class way harder than necessary. Complains about being too busy to put in the bare minimum effort. Recitation is not helpful and does not empathize with students. I had to spend 10x more time and do 10x more work than a student in the same class taught by someone else. Truly made first semester terrible and actively advise against this.

Truly helps you understand Calculus thoroughly. Hard quizzes and homework, but they help you learn critical concepts and get very high grades on tests. Most of the questions he writes seem complicated at first, but they are quite easily done if you analyze the problem and comprehend the concepts.
Tough homework and quizzes, but half of them get dropped so your grade doesn't suffer and it helped me do really well on the tests. Great guy. Go to class
Gives really hard homework which I hated at first but really helped me do well on exams. Really nice guy go to his review sessions
He is awesome

I tried my best to reach for help and succeed, I felt like she really didn't really care about my grades or anything. She did easy examples in class and she put the hardest in the test. Take her if you want to have the worst semester ever and if you want to teach yourself the whole differential equations class.

Must attend the lectures to know how to do homework because if you do 1 step different, it is wrong (doesn't post solved notes). Tough grader (no feedback on test). Random in-class quizzes so mandatory attendance.

Honestly an easy class and lectures were all you needed to understand the material. She told you what to study if you attended lecture and the one time I did study, I got a decent grade. Doesn't round grades tho sadly.
She is somewhat of a good prof if you can get past the accent but it was extremely hard for me to learn, had to teach myself the whole semester

Exams were harder than the homework, and the material was dense. We spent a full week and homework on one topic that did not appear on the exam. During an exam week I had a family emergency; she couldn't help because it would be unfair to other students, which felt unfair. I retook the course at nova and earned an A. Accent is strong.

She posted completed notes on Canvas and gave us printed notes that we could fill out in class, which were very helpful. Lectures were ok, and she would sometimes give extra credit for attending class and doing work. The tests were difficult, but if you can do the homework they shouldn't be too bad.

Class sucked dude main thing was her tests are hard as hell. Shes the type to give you a study guide and come the test everything is completely different. Its not impossible to do well in her class but the homework is heavy and you cant get by by just studying you have to fully understand the material
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Compared to calc 2 and calc 3, this class is very manageable. She posts completed notes on canvas which are very useful. Homework is not that bad. Sometimes she would have in-class assignments which were kind of annoying. But tests were always something done in class and the notes make everything easy to learn.
You can barely understand her explanations sometimes, learned more from youtube than the actual class

A good professor, she does her best to ensure that every student pays attention in her class. She gives extra credit in some sessions to those who are present. I used to learn every topic on my own, but I believe that if I paid attention to her sessions, I would have achieved a better grade.

My goat. Her lectures and explanations are insanely helpful and thorough. Having taken this a 2nd time, she makes calc easy. You will never feel lost in a lecture if you attend regularly and ask questions, since she explains steps that you might've forgotten, from algebra to calc 1. Her homeworks are helpful and tests extremely reasonable.

If you are taking her for diff eq and are used to the vt math program, she's an okay choice. Lecture heavy, and a pretty abnormal homework load. She makes consistent mistakes during the lectures, so be ready to learn the material on your own, but she is very kind, and has more office hours than any other prof.

Overall Professor Elsrrawi was a very kind, respecting professor. She provides very organized notes and posts all annotated notes after every lecture. Unless English isn't your first language, it's really not that hard to understand her accent. The exams and homework are all very straight forward, so if you put in moderate effort you'll be fine.

Honestly she did a pretty decent job. She always gave out printed notes so we didn't have to write everything down. There were some simple mistakes she would do, but was thankful for them to be pointed out. Compared to my friends who had different diff eq professors, she was pretty good.
Tough make up deadlines, was in the hospital for a week and the make up deadlines were tough especially given the circumstances. Very punctual on deadlines try to stay ahead.
Was in the hospital for a week and I was given some tough makeup deadlines. She's pretty punctual on timelyness.

IDK how Virginia Tech thinks they can get away with math professors like Dr. Elsrrawi. Very fast, difficult accent, doesn't fully understand english, when a question is eventually asked due to her lack of teaching abilities she is very short, almost angry in answering the question. Office hours are no different. Find a different prof or take online

Her accent is hard to understand, and her lectures are not easy to follow. Many reviews say attendance is not mandatory but she will randomly decide to give in class assignment, and you will get a zero if you are absent. Tests were super hard and no review days. Don't recommend taking this class unless you want to teach yourself calculus.
Can't understand her, hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
a lot of people speak bad about her, but i found that her lectures were very informative. she starts talking about material and stuff before the class time, so make sure to show up early. 
people also say she has an accent, but it's not hard to understand at all. her office ours were also very helpful

Dr. Elsrrawi is better than the reviews you'll see here. Yes she can be hard to understand, but if you're paying attention, she is actually easy to understand. Just complete ALL of the WebAssigns, home works, and get help when you need it. If you do that, you'll be fine. She really cares about her students, and will be more than happy to help you.
You will have to teach yourself everything. The only positive is that she posts everything online which cannot be said for all professors, but that's about where the positives end.

Very sweet and cares about her students and wants us to succeed. Lectures were hard to pay attention to because it took so much energy to figure out what she was trying to say. Always willing to answer questions but her answers weren't helpful; didn't feel like she ever understood what people were asking. Not a bad grader but I had to teach myself.

I feel like the hate this professor gets is unwarranted. I completely understand that she has an accent that is particularly hard to hack but that's just something you have to deal. As long as you show up to class and actually try, you will succeed. I strongly recommend attending her office hours and asking questions frequently. She moves quickly.

This professor...I can't put into words how much this class almost ruined my first semester of college. She is nice, I'll give her that, but she's the worst teacher I've ever had in my life. Nothing on the practice tests are on the actual tests. If you can help it PLEASE TAKE THIS CLASS OVER THE SUMMER. The math department is awful. God bless.

Dr.Elsrrawi was a great professor, she was always there to help and was always very nice. She has an accent but I understood everything she said just fine. There was a lot of homework but it was just busy work so it was never hard. Attending class and going to office hours was very helpful.

How do I sum up my experience with Fariha in 350 words... right, I can't. I toughed this semester out so that whoever sees this can understand my pain. I had to go to every office hour, help session, and I got a tutor for this class, thanks to her. Basically, if you get her for 1225 I'm gonna be honest with you, just find another professor.

This class moves very quickly, and there are a ton of small assignments to do every. She is a fairly tough grader, which makes getting an A in her class difficult. That being said, she clearly wants her students to succeed and is willing to help them do so. Her teaching of the material is good.
Not a good lecturer, but she is nice and cares about you doing well

A very thick accent makes complex material even more difficult to understand. *Do not rely on the practice test for the test* She is very strict about notation and even if you do it correctly but not her way, you can get points deducted. Do not expect to end class on time.

Professor Elsrrawi will start lecturing the moment class starts (sometimes a few minutes before), and won't stop until 3-5 minutes after class ends. She goes super fast and doesn't explain things well. She also has "group work" which is HW that you do in a group except no one talks to each other. If you want to pass, find another professor.

Big weed-out class as a freshman. Accent was hard to understand, she went too quick. Posted class notes, but wasn't too helpful. Dumb 5 question Canvas quizzes with 3 tests and 1 final. MATH 1226 sucks in general, had a better time with MATH 2204. Doesn't curve or show grades on Canvas, not a great first semester math experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She has such a thick accent, you can barely understand. She also teaches very fast and its just not good. I watched Dr. V calculus 2 videos, because she has very similar notes as to this class in 2022, and I also watched professor leonard. 

Just not good stuff
Her accent made learning math nearly impossible. On top of that, she isn't particularly good at teaching math. She goes too fast.
Not a good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elsrrawi is impossible to understand because of her accent. I have already struggled in math for years, but I have never struggled more than with her. She starts talking before class starts so you basically have to arrive early every day, and it is not uncommon for her to teach up to 5 minutes past when class is supposed to end.
Impossible to understand and frequently gets things wrong or explains things in ways that complicate it even more

Math department at VT is bad all around, my greatest issue with Professor Elsrrawi was her accent. I mean, it's really, really bad. Seriously, if her accent weren't so thick I would've had a better time. I ended up going to Professor Leonard on YouTube to learn. She's very kind and supportive, but I couldn't get past the language barrier. 2/10.

Everyone I knew in this class struggled with me. The course covers the same as the other 1225 courses but the instruction was very hard to follow. There were also lots of random "group work" assignments towards the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I've had Charlie for multiple classes at Tech. He loves his students and really enjoys what he does. All of his classes are structured around completing your own linguistics research, and you can go as deep into your research as you want. If you've ever been curious about language, take this class !!!
Classes run long sometimes but I find his lectures to be enjoyable. Course was not that difficult, quizzes are all online, including the final.

I really enjoyed Charlie's class and became a Language Sciences minor because of it. No late policy on work. All tests and quizzes were online, and many assignments were open-note. The lectures are very long and fast-paced, but he also posts the slides from each class on the Canvas page. Overall, very passionate about the subject and very kind.

Although I did end up withdrawing, Professor Farrington was very good. He's very laid back and chill with the students. One thing for sure though, be sure to show up to class! Even though attendance is not mandatory *on paper*, he does give out writing prompts and since you aren't graded on much, it could help boost your grade a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Charlie is a super chill professor. Attendance is technically not mandatory but he would give out random short writing prompts, and if you're not there, you get a 0. Discussion-based class but was very interesting material. He is passionate about what he teaches. Midterm and final were a little hard in my opinion.
His lectures are kind of long and sometimes boring. But he is very informed on the subject and clearly very interested himself. The class conversations are definitely the best part of the class.

Good professor. Definitely a lecture-heavy class. Go to class, it makes the tests worlds easier I wouldn't say he's a boring teacher, as he really knows his stuff, but he doesn't go out of his way to make things exciting. I found the subject matters interesting though it was obvious my peers did not, not a lot of participation in lectures

Super nice guy, accessible via office hours and email. Lectures were so, so boring. Assignments could use a little organization, but weren't bad. More engaging lectures and more of an incentive to attend class would work wonders.

The lectures are extremely long and boring. The assignments were not too difficult, but you have to pay attention in class to pass. I never read anything from the textbook and still ended with a B, so you'll probably be fine if you don't like to do assigned reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He talks very fast and the lectures are very long, but the actual grading, homework, and tests are very easy as long as you pay attention in class.

As a person, prof. farrington is super awesome, but as a teacher, not so much. During class, he gives lectures of about 40-50 slides, which he just absolutely blows through. He does a bad job at highlighting what's important and what's not, and when taking the quizzes, I was beyond confused. Wouldn't recommend for ENGL 1514.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Generally, each class had an assigned reading that we would discuss. Very few assignments, just some open-note quizzes and a final paper on any topic, and participation credit at the end of the year. Very friendly and helpful in class, held office hours, and was understanding if you missed a deadline/needed help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Charlie is an amazing professor. His class is definitely difficult, it requires a lot of reading but he provides all of the readings for the semester. The final paper is tough but if you start on it early its no problem. Charlie is just a super fun professor and you'll definitely enjoy his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took BIT 4624 with Professor Flora. You can tell that he truly cares about all his students. I haven't had to go to him too much for hw help but when I did, he was very helpful and understanding. Definitely recommend taking him, not just for this class but for any class he's teaching.

THE BEST BIT CLASS I'VE TAKEN SO FAR. Professor Flora explains the matter clearly to you, and the tests are a piece of cake in comparison to the exam. If you know the HW=Good grade—great teacher, accessible out of class, and understanding. Highly recommend him for 2406
Professor Flora takes his role seriously. If you attend class consistently, actively listen to the lectures and guest speakers, and engage with the material, you will be well positioned to earn an A.
Michael Flora is one cool guy and his lectures are NOT boring. Two thumbs up for this guy!!!!
Professor takes his one credit hour class very seriously. Assignments are not difficult, but lectures are very very boring.

Professor Flora was a great professor! The class was pretty straightforward, and his lectures were pretty easy to follow. The exams were definitely 10x easier than any of the homework, but the homework was still helpful. In class exercises served as a sort of attendance grade. if you put even an hour or two to study before your exams ur chill

He took his one credit class mandatory class more seriously than it deserves. Assignments would be due within 48 hours of them being posted and they rarely matched what the lecture was about. The lectures were boring; nobody wants to hear middle aged men talk about getting a job over and over again. Ultimately not difficult but definitely annoying.

Professor Flora is passionate about the topics in the class. He obviously cares about his students and helped me out in the beginning of the semester. The class is just lectures. There is a group project, but it is straightforward. Readings help with exams. Took this class as my BIT elective and don't regret it at all.

He's is very good at teaching and extremely knowledgeable about almost every topic you can think of. Also a really great person to go for advice or help. His class assignments, quizzes, and exams are all very different and really meant to solidify the knowledge. He also gave us tons of extra credits for participating and coming to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's nice and cares a lot about the material he teaches. It's a easy class that I spent around 20 - 30 minutes a week on. The only thing that might catch you off-guard are the exams which sometimes test on the outside reading. There's a group project which is not hard at all. Overall, its a pretty easy class, just read the articles he sends
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had for BIT 4604. Great professor. Very understanding and caring, while always accessible for feedback outside of class.

This was for an LLC - it wasn't too important. However, this class is 1 credit and he took attendance more seriously than any classes, including OChem. It was an 8am in Goodwin but we couldn't miss class even once. All professors give some amount of understanding towards the fact that life happens - sometimes you sleep in or are sick. Not Flora.
Only had him for a LLC class, but he was nice and gave easy and intriguing assignments.

Professor Flora is a really nice professor, but wasn't really prepared while teaching the subject. Exams were in person on a lock down browsers. They were also nothing like the homework/in class materials. The averages for exams were around Cs & Ds so he had to curve them so people could actually pass the class. Overall it wasn't great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is an ideal professor for college students. Doesn't really stress on attendance or participation, he has clear slides to read from which are more than enough for the exam. His material is well-researched and quite in-depth to get a good understanding. I have had him for 2 semesters. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a very easy class to do. There will be occasional attendance quizzes, but nothing that expects much out of you. There's a very clear grading criteria that I doubt people would fail unless they chose to put the class on a backburner. In regard to the professor, chilled dude and very accessible outside class if you have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class itself isn't hard if you just practice the exam reviews. Ferris however is not a great professor. She would get all of the answers wrong in front of us and it just seemed like she didn't know what she was doing. If you know you struggle with accounting then I would try to take a different professor.

Ferris is a good professor, a lot of people don't like her just because the class is not easy (especially for non-accounting majors). She is straightforward and direct with her responses, which I personally like. If you review content before class, you should be fine.  I liked her teaching style and would take again.

She is not as bad as the reviews say. As long as you come to class, pay attention, and try your best, it will work out. She is very nice if you put in the effort to try to succeed. Her assignments can be difficult, but it would be difficult regardless of the professor.

I genuinely don't understand the Prof. Ferris hate. She is a fair grader and rewards participation and effort, and is always happy to help students with questions. I can see how some people could feel that she can be passive aggressive, but I truly think it comes from how passionate she is about the topics she teaches. (I promise I'm not her lol)

I had Professor Ferris for both 2504 and 2116. As long as you're on top of assignments and lock in with studying then you'll be alright. She's very fast-paced and loves to call on people at random. If you fall behind when she speeds through labs and in-class examples, best to look on Canvas or ask a friend… she'd lowkey be so rude to people.

She would always cold call on people in class and would give attitude if you didn't know the answer or were struggling. Just generally went through topics quickly and wasn't very helpful. I recommend taking the course with Eric Allen Martin if you can as he created the course and I've only heard good things about him

She isn't terrible; I expected a lot worse based on these ratings. As long as you do the work and turn everything in on time (and follow all instructions) it shouldn't be hard to get an A. The tests were annoying to prepare for but there was only two and no final. It's just one of those classes you have to get through. Also a few group projects...

Homework wasn't even hard; it was just so time consuming. McGraw hill accounting wise is the worst website I have ever used. Ferris wasn't rude but very passive-aggressive. She also would fly through the PowerPoints too. Practice exams are almost verbatim the actual exam. I recommend teaching yourself for the class or taking with another professor.

Prepare to teach yourself if you want to pass the class. Unorganized and sometimes didn't even know how to complete the problems herself. Sent out the practice problems for the final exam 2 days before the exam and apologized because she thought she sent it out last week and didn't post the answer key till less than 12 hours before our final exam.

Very passive-aggressive and unprofessional; seems like she cares more about grading harshly and making students feel miserable than enjoying this class. Emails she would send regarding grading issues, she was dismissive. Would also not allow students to leave the classroom, even though attendance is not mandatory. STAY AWAY AT ALL COSTS.

To be fair, it's not all her fault because the class is run by a different prof. Overall, the only way to succeed in this class is to teach yourself and spend hours prepping for exams. Homework helps boost your grade. But tests are the majority of the grade, and they are difficult. Actual accounting majors ik were struggling to pass this class.
If you have ever seen Harry Potter and know Dolores Umbridge, Porf Ferris is basically her.

Professor Ferris is easily the worst professor I have ever had. Not just because of her boring lectures that related little to the work we actually did in the class, but because of her attitude towards her students. She was extremely rude and unprofessional in the classroom and would even openly shame and complain about students.

I have had Professor Ferris twice and she has been an okay teacher. There are clear deadlines and assignments which is nice but she just isn't an effective lecturer for me, but to be fair my class was at 8 am.

This professor is extremely rude, harsh and overall someone you should avoid. She acts like answering questions and helping students is a burden to her and grades projects very harshly with little feedback. She is also just unnecessarily rude to students. Please do not take her for any class, find any other professor and you will be better off.

One of the most frustrating classes I've taken—not because of the material, but because of how Prof. Ferris teaches it. She's passive-aggressive, brings students down when they ask questions, and offers little prep for a massive final project that's graded harshly. Strongly recommend choosing another professor.

Professor Ferris was one of the worst Professors I have ever had. I never once used Rate My Professor to complain about a professor, but I felt the need to do so with her. She waited until the day before the major group project was due to go over it in detail, which wasn't very helpful. We were given a template and no instruction for this project.

I liked Prof. Ferris' class a lot. She grades strictly, but in a fair and rational way. Just pay attention and do your work and you will be fine. Attendance is mandatory. Tests are proctored and closed book, but she hosts a review session the class before (with extra credit opportunities) and they are exactly what was taught in class.

Professor Ferris was never prepared for class. Her lectures were incredibly boring, and homework sometimes wasn't relevant to the exams. Last year, she accidentally sent out the accounting exam to all the students in that class and other sections.

Professor Ferris would get problems wrong in class and not know the answer. She also would give students attitude and wasn't the best at answering questions. ACIS 2116 is mainly a class you learn through homeworks and the book anyway so that's how I was able to get an A-. She also was never prepared for class.

Obscene amount of group project work with no guidance. I spent probably 40+ hours on my part alone.  Project took up majority of the grade which she graded extremely hard. Lectures didn't seem to correlate to the class and I feel like I learned nothing. She was also passive aggressive. Don't take this professor if you wanna learn something.

Passive aggressive/condescending. Was having technical issues when accessing our textbook- she sent me a rude email and she personally reached out to my advisor about how much time in advance I had to complete the homework. Graded difficult. Learned nothing from class except her bragging about her job at EY. Hard group project with 0 instruction

Her lectures were random and boring. We would have random quizzes and the average on some of them (especially the ones with excel) was probably a 50%. The group project was hard because she gave not a lot of class time to do them and not much help in group meetings. Her grading of them at the end of semester was super harsh. Passive aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Final project graded extremely harsh, all while not providing much help or any context until the last day of class. Accidentally missed a couple things on our excel for the project and she took off over half the points, despite doing the other 99% well - dropped my grade from an A to a B. Learned more from ChatGPT and class Bootcamps than her.

Felt like she was teaching a forensic accounting class - the only contextual info she provided was about forensic accounting which was unrelated. Was able to keep up with the in-class material, but could tell a lot of the class didn't and she didn't provide much help. Final project was graded very harsh and she provided little to no justification.

Avoid if you can. She is incredibly condescending, terrible at giving instructions, acted like we were professionals rather than students. Gave no direction on the project and rants about how hard her job was compared to it. I learned nothing from her; she goes too fast and does not really teach. The project was actually horrible.

She was extremely passive aggressive and provided virtually 0 structure for the final project, which is the majority of your grade. She moves entirely too fast on in class assignments and expects a level of proficiency in excel that is unreasonable. Do not take her class if possible.

The worst. Attendance is mandatory. A semester long group project with 0 direction & 0 time in class. Makes you get PowerBI, which is not accessible to those with a MAC (not on syllabus). Moved so fast in class, and was often passive aggressive to students who asked valid questions. HARSH grader, waits until last minute to grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't think a single in-class assignment had an average above a 60. She just does things and acts like the students already know how to do them. Very little explanation about anything and good luck if you're able to do well on the semester project because she tells you just about nothing about it. Whatever you do, DO NOT take her class.

Although she tends to move quickly in class, most of the assignments are relatively easy. Her course lacks structure, but if you work with her, you can still earn a good grade. This is probably the first class at VT where I've actually learned something in Excel.

Professor Ferris was a good professor. She went over all of the problems in class and the class was not too hard as long as you go and pay attention to the lectures. The accounting class was directed by a different professor so Professor Ferris did not have a lot of room in deciding our homework and tests. Overall she was a good teacher.
Barely teaches in class and when she does, she is extremely fast. Very passive agressive too.

Your entire course grade is practically(not in actuality)determined by a semester long project that she gives both 0 instruction on as well as next to 0 class time to work on with your group. Instead lectures are filled with nonsense time wasting rants about her glory days at EY. I would run and not look back if you got her from course request.

A teacher told me to my face that women shouldn't be allowed in stem, and I have still never had a teacher as terrible as Ferris. I couldn't tell you one thing I learned in her lectures because even in the rare event it's relevant, she goes too fast and explains nothing. She's rude and passive aggressive when giving feedback. Do not take her class.

Dude, I think he's one of the only professors that I think is so lit. I like history and lectures so this class is definitely that. Exams are based on his lecture and slides, and they aren't trying to trip you up. He gives back points if there are questions that a majority of the class got wrong. I ve never heard of that before. So lit, take him

Very nice and caring professor! Everything he tested you on was on the lecture slides in class (attendance not mandatory tho), however some lectures felt like pure word vomit with paragraphs on each slide, still not a bad teacher, but sometimes less is more for lecture slides

Professor Fleenor is an outstanding teacher. The class is composed of 4 exams worth 25% of your grade. This seems rather intimidating but the slides that he posts are very helpful in studying for his exams. If you have the opportunity to take his class, I would highly recommend doing so because it really isn't too difficult if you pay attention.

Although the class is solely based on the 4 exams you take, everything is based upon the material on the slides he posts on Canvas. Lectures are not mandatory, but he covers the content very clearly and has a funny personality. Wants the best for his students grade-wise and in life!
Fleenor is a great guy who is very easygoing. The class is graded exclusively on 4 exams, but they are relatively easy. I absolutely recommend taking it with Professor Fleenor.

If you take Fleenor your grade is only based on 4 exams throughout the semester. He is a super nice guy and if you follow along with the lectures you will do good on exams. All slides are posted on canvas after to study. If you study the slides you'll be fine on exams. He also drops questions and adds points back if most of the class got it wrong.

This class really sparked my interest in law. He's a great professor who cares about your learning. It is a lecture heavy class but he makes most of them interesting. Attendance is not mandatory but going to classes will definitely help as he uses real life examples to explain and the textbook is very expensive. Class is graded only by 4 tests.
Very nice guy. The only grades are 4 exams, but the questions are all directly related to the lectures. If you take notes and study them you should do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Judge Fleenor is awesome.  Despite his somewhat challenging exams which are the only assignments he gives, he was able to turn what usually is one of the most negatively perceived classes (business law) into a fun, interactive discussion about these legal concepts. He's got a great sense of humor and exposes us to real-life examples of all topics.
Judge Fleenor is a great professor, your grade for 3054 is based entirely on 4 exams throughout the semester and no final. Go to lecture and ask questions and you should do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best professor I've had! Grades are based on 4 tests, and if you attend class and pay attention, you'll do great. His passion for law makes lectures engaging and even sparked my interest in the subject. He truly cares about his students. If you're choosing a BLAW professor, he's your guy. Trust.

Best professor I've had at VT. He gives real life examples, and explains complex subjects so well. I learned SO much in this class. Very lenient, treats you as an adult. Exams were very fair. Come to class, pay attention, and you will do just fine. He seems like an overall great guy in addition to being a good teacher. 100% recommend him for buslaw

Very respectful, smart professor. Class is made up of four exams. While attendance is not required, it's easier to go to class and listen instead of trying to learn through the powerpoints. He will review the slides in class and simplify it so just do that. Also, the examples on the PP are very important. The application is what's on the exam.

This was his first semester teaching. Tests made up 100% of your grade (4 tests, 25 each). However, they're significantly easier than other teachers' and he curves generously. One question was "which of these is not one of the 3 branches of gov". You do need to study a little. Read textbook if you want to be engaged. No homework. Plus extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although a "tougher" grader, Gibbs is a very professional instructor and has an incredible understanding of the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This guy is the GOAT, I hate english and yet I enjoyed this guys class. His research project for ENGL 1106 allows a lot of persoal choice in the topic and I was passionate about working on my own project in his class.

The class is portfolio-based grading, so whatever you turn in is used to give you a letter grade. Even when I fell behind, I was still able to submit old assignments and come back from an estimated B-C to an A. He responds to emails on time and gives good feedback on how to improve on everything you turn in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Was fair and gave us plenty of opportunities to step up and improve our writing capabilities.

Prof. Gibbs never gave a specific rubric for what he was expecting in his essays, which allowed for creativity. He was not a harsh grader, but he rarely gave 100s. Overall, your grade is almost entirely made up of 5 critical essays written and attendance, with a few assignments that are easy As. I love Prof. Gibbs. I would recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every week, you have several short stories to read (2-3 total hours) and you'll do a reading quiz and group discussion over them. The workload is super light as long as you don't read all the stories at the end of the week. The reading quizzes are a little thoughtful, but you get 2 attempts. The group discussion is just a post and a reply
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Gibbs is an amazing English professor. He genuinely cares for his students and tries to know everyone as an individual. There are quite a few papers to write but the grading is very relaxed since he focuses on improvement rather than the quality of that individual paper. He provides very good feedback so you can easily see what to improve on

Gibbs made this class enjoyable. Attendance is the biggest thing. Showing up to class makes Gibbs an easier grader. The grading scale is a little funny but show up, engage, turn in the work, and trying to show improvement will earn you an easy A. Great class and teacher
Mr Gibbs is a great teacher and I recommend everyone take him.

English is a subject where difficulty is based on your professors discretion. Professor Gibbs had papers due virtually every class all with thorough thought and reading associated. In addition he had harder research assignments due frequently throughout the semester. Hes a great guy personally, but Id find a different professor expeditiously.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Overall a great professor and willing to help you. Gave excellent feedback throughout the course and graded pretty easily.

Dr Gibbs provides great feedback on classwork and is somewhat flexible grading-wise. He holds one-on-one conferences to discuss writing and goals. Be prepared to do lots of reflecting on your writing. Course uses a portfolio grading system which is flexible and is mostly effort-based. My writing skills and confidence vastly improved in this course.

I usually don't like english, but Gibbs made english awesome. I was able to read what I wanted and write a term paper on the subject of my choice. It made my semester actually very interesting. He was also great to talk to and enjoyed having conversations with him out of class. He was super helpful and if you put in effort you get a good grade.

Gibbs was such a great professor! I enjoyed his class so much. He always reads your writings and gives amazing feedback. Compared to other teachers, he does give more assignments so be prepared to write (it is a writing class). If you are looking to become a better writer and learn different styles TAKE THIS CLASS. One of my favorite classes!!!

Best guy to take your requires English with. Hilarious and just such a character. The class felt like I was back in high school, all of in the class became friends. Much better gen ed experience than I was expecting! Also, a lot of freedom with the big paper, so I got to do something I actually cared about.

Jared Gibbs is probably the best Eng1106 professor. He is one of the nicest people to ever teach. He wants his students to enjoy what they are writing and will work with you the entire course to ensure that you show improvement in your writing. If you are taking Eng1106 try and get into one of his classes.

This dude is awesome. If you show up, participate, and show effort, youll get an A. He's easy to talk to, super helpful, and really nice. He also wants you to do want you want to do/are interested in, not just work on boring stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you do your work outside of class with effort, you'll get an A. Very nice, knowledgeable guy.

Mr. Gibbs was a great teacher and really helped me develop my writing skills even as a Biology major. If the papers were turned in on time and the writing challenges were written, the class was an easy A. Definitely recommend getting to know him and asking him for feedback and notes!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Mr. Gibbs made english for a science-major as pain free as possible. There was quite a lot of small assignments each week building up to the big research paper at the end. Gave so much feedback on your writing and how to improve. Class discussion was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The Gibbster was a good teacher. Kind of monotonous class (we just discussed the homework we had done the night before for THE WHOLE CLASS), but he was a pretty lenient professor when it comes to grading, and a very personable guy. I would recommend him to anyone.

Dr. Gannon was an awesome professor. He cares very deeply about students' and their learning. The way he runs his class makes you truly learn and not be stressed about the course. 30% of your grade is simply coming into class and doing the work with him, 40% is step by step labs, the other 30% is based on tests that you get 2 attempts on!

In class quizzes, so attendance is mandatory, but they're super easy and he goes over them and lets you retake. Tests are pretty easy and straightforward. He is super engaging and always makes class fun and interesting. For someone who knew next to nothing about the course material going into the class, he makes it easy to learn.
Awesome professor, highly recommend.
JP is the GOAT.

He makes it easy to succeed. There are locked quizzes every class so you have to go to class but he gives answers and tests are open-note the second attempt. Labs are simple, and he provides helpful videos. With lots of grades and chances to do well, it's easy to stay on track and pass the class.

This is one of those nice breather classes. Although attendance is required, the class is very easy and slow paced. He gives you two attempts for tests, the second one being open notes. Very little homework ever.
JP was an absolutely fantastic professor. He is engaging with his students, and if I could take him again, I would. His class is easy as long as you show up, and he's always willing to help you out.

Professor Gannon was my favorite teacher first semester of college. His course had some homework to understand the material but it was never overwhelming and the group project at the end of the course was structured well. Always there to help and was forgiving if you had to miss class.
Great professor. Very funny, made the lectures interesting. Would definitely take him again for any of his classes.

Dr Gannon was a very good professor and although in class no one thought he was funny I personally did. His lecture slides are interesting and the labs you do in class are straightforward. If you have trouble with them the TAs are also very good. Exams aren't bad as they're 2 attempts with one being open book, open everything. Great professor!

I am currently in this class (Spring 2022), & loving it! He is super relaxed about due dates & attendance (he records all lectures and posts them on Canvas, just give him a heads up you will miss). During his lectures, he codes along with us in R. All resources/textbooks are free. He has a GroupMe for the class so we can message everyone for help!

JP is really a wonderful professor! hes very nice and respects students, you can tell he wants us to succeed. he gives a lot of good feedback on projects and paces stuff such as coding slower so it is easier for students to pick up. hes very understanding and pretty goofy too. this class is pretty easy if you show up to it!

I took this class online in 2020. My main issue was the final being replaced with a group project. Other than that, this class was easy and interesting. The professor was very caring and waived his late work penalty. He gave extra credit once or twice. Not tough, would take again.

Honestly, my favorite professor. Patient with assignments, explains material well, and interesting lectures. Just make it to most of the classes and keep track of deadlines. Office hours are super helpful if youre struggling.
One of the Best professors I've had. Very student-centered, flexible to help with anything, and makes class enjoyable. All assignments are done through Canvas making the class very straightforward.

If you can avoid taking this class with her I would. She was almost always late to class and is incredibly unorganized. She used AI for everything, and I learned nothing in this class. We literally never had class because she was always cancelling it super last minute. Overall, just super unorganized.

This class wouldn't have been so bad if she didn't wait until the literal last day of classes to start grading. It's impossible to adjust to feedback when you receive none. Almost all assignments are group work which was frustrating. Super harsh grading despite being incredibly disorganized all semester.

DO NOT TAKE IF YOU CAN AVOID HER. Would go weeks without posting assignments with no communication as to why, then post 3 assignments at once and made them due in 4 days. Majority of your grade depends on a semester long online group project. Didn't give feedback on assignments and wouldn't let you see your grade. Insanely disorganized and a mess.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is very disorganized. A majority of the final grade is a group project that she did not grade any parts of until the day final grades were due. This meant we were not able to receive any feedback to improve throughout the semester. She also graded very harshly despite no feedback and minimal guidance. Overall,grades felt very unfair.

The best way to describe working with this prof is "painful". She was absolutely terrible. I don't know what happened to her between now and 2019 when the other reviews were posted, but OMG it was so bad. So disorganized, , mediocre instructions, and almost every assignment is group work which is AWFUL online, especially with a prof who wont help.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is by far the most disorganized professor I have had. She had to cut down assignments on her syllabus significantly because she couldn't get the assignments posted, and when she did, they were lengthy, and had a very short timeframe for completion. Her feedback was surface level at best. I would not recommend taking a class with her.

I have no clue how this prof has a 5/5 rating. She is the most disorganized professor I have had in my life. I will admit that she gives good feedback when she grades assignments and is helpful when she responds but don't count on her responding to your emails. If you value consistency and regularly scheduled work, I'd advise taking another prof.

As long as you do the readings and show up to class, this class is an easy A. She's super funny and her lectures are entertaining with lots of videos to keep it interesting! The tests are pretty easy as long as you study the powerpoints!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Grafsky is the greatest professor I have ever had! I loved her lectures, and she's a real/genuine person. Take notes during her lectures and read the material on REVEL. She does not take attendance, but has random in-class assignments. You are allowed to miss 3, or it will start to lower your grade. Study her notes really well and pay attention!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. Keeps it decently easy. Must do online homework for a decent grade. Homework is easy and do at the beginning of every class but it's so easy it's easy to forget about.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There is so much extra credit for this class that you should get an A. If you listen to the lectures you shouldn't have to use the textbook to study, just your notes. Her lectures are very conversational and she's relatable to the topics because she is a young mom.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very nice guy and clearly cares about his students, unfortunately I can't understand anything he says. Exams were insanely hard with not enough time to take them. Doesn't post your final grade until after classes end so I had no idea what I had in the class all semester. If you can avoid it, do not take macro with this professor.

Dr. Gebremariam is a great person and a bad professor. He clearly wants his students to succeed but does absolutely nothing in class to supplement that. None of the posted powerpoints are annotated, lectures are confusing, and quizzes are trivia questions. Don't expect to learn anything from this class by just showing up, you're on your own.

If you value your education in the slightest, avoid this professor at all costs. Lecture heavy with iclickers (which is fine) but the language barrier is truly INCOMPREHENSIBLE.
