The fact that he is the Econ major specific instructor is a disgrace to the Department of Economics. You are completely on your own if you take his class, good luck.
He is the goat.
Very inspirational and wants students to succeed.

Gebre was an amazing professor. I had the opportunity to talk to him one on one, and he is one of the kindest, most inspirational people I have ever had the pleasure of talking to. The class was very manageable; my only gripe was that iclicker is used. I literally made an account just to write about how great he is.

Truly such a caring and kind soul. He always started off the class reminding us that life was beautiful and made it very clear that he wanted us to succeed and put in the effort to do so. iClicker's every class unless it was down and homework and quizzes weren't anything too difficult, also you're able to skip ~5-6 classes worth of iclicker

He has an accent, but you will be able to understand him. I had him early in the morning as a first class, and he was always so bright and cheerful. I loved getting to know him better, and he was always ready to help however he could. Every week you have 2 homework's and a quiz but very manageable.
Really sweet guy, and tells you iclicker answers so as long as you go to class you should be fine. Homework and exams are online.

One of the best professors! He is so happy to be teaching and always grateful to be there. He uses iClicker so attendance is mandatory. This course was very lecture heavy but if you actually listen he presents the material in a fun and easy way. He drops grades at the end of the semester.
the class is easy but his teaching was confusing sometimes.

Very goated, if you see him than take him because it's the easiest A of your life. He's very friendly and truly inspirational, be sure to go to class as he is very positive and extremely cheerful. Never a dull lecture even though he has an accent he's very good at teaching. He uses iClicker so attendance is sort of mandatory, plus exams are online.

Gebre cares a lot about his students and his grading scheme shows that. He drops the lowest two homeworks, midterm exam, curves the final, and gives bonus points if you show up to class.Very kind although he goes on tangents a lot, which shows he is passionate about what he teaches
So so kind and cares so much about his students. The class is easier if you pay attention but the homework and canvas quizzes set you up well for the course. He is the kindest ever.

ECON 2006 with Dr. Gebre wasn't too bad. He has a thick accent, which could make it hard to understand. However, he is very passionate about macro and wants students to succeed. The slides were informative. He provided plenty of study material to prepare for the exams, which are online. Attend class as i-Clicker is used. Overall, a good experience!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gebre is kind and inspirational. However, his lectures were based on information copied and pasted from the textbook, and he would often go on tangents. I was able to learn better by reading the textbook. All quizzes and exams are online and can be taken at home. Nonetheless, his class isn't difficult. Just put in effort, and you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Anyone who rates Dr Gebre anything less than 5 must have never gone to his class once. He is amazing!! So kind and funny, and he genuinely wants his students to do well. Tests are easy and basically straight from the notes, which he posts to Canvas for anyone who needs. iClicker attendance questions but he gives you the answers to each one.

Gebremariam was such a kind and inspirational man, however he wasn't a very good professor. He is hard to understand and often would go on tangents. I was able to teach myself the material. The attendance is tracked by Iclicker and he has built it so you can miss a few classes. All the exams are on locked down browser and you can take them at home.

He's a very nice man who is passionate about teaching and genuinely cares about his students. There is iClicker attendance, but the class isn't difficult. I didn't find his accent hard to understand, but lecture slides are posted on canvas regardless. HW is straightforward and exams are take-home. If you do the work you'll most likely do well.

Attend class; he uses iclicker, and you get bonus points for attendance. His accent can be challenging to understand, which made it hard to focus even though I was sitting at the front. Despite the language barrier, he is a passionate teacher with a positive attitude who cares about his students.

Gebre has a thick accent but after going to class a couple times it gets much easier to understand. He cares deeply about the well-being of his students and you can tell he is very passionate about teaching. The class isn't very hard and as long as you turn in your assignments should be able to get an A or B. Would definitely recommend.

Gebremariam is genuinely a nice and funny professor who is quick to respond to emails and is very understanding. The only difficulty I experienced is he has a thick accent, but the slides he uses are very "to-the-point" and easy to write notes on besides graph slides. Tests are online and homework takes only an hour and a half to do. Easy class!

Professor G is such a nice and caring professor. Even though there is a little bit of a language barrier he still makes the class understandable. There are only 3 homework assignments a week. There are also 3 midterms and one final that are all online and at home exams. Overall he is a very good professor that makes the class an easy A.
Hard to understand his accent but his notes are super detailed so its easier to follow
Professor Gebramariam was one of my best professors and made crunching through the material of macronomics a lot more understandable. He's very forgiving and overall one of the best at VT.
Dr. Gebre is a super cool guy and a very passionate professor. He is almost always available for office hours. Tests are hard so study for those. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

Dr Gebre is a very nice teacher and obviously cares a lot about his students, but he is not the best at actually teaching. He seems to go on tangents and the language barrier is hard to understand.
2.5% bonus points if you show up to class, drops your lowest test, curved the final exam. 
Overall, its an easy enough class if you use the textbook.

Very flexible with assignments and midterms, allowed students to come to different lecture times that fit better with their schedule. A little bit of a language barrier, but overall a very interesting guy.

He is a very kind and caring man, although during lecture you don't learn much. He isn't the best at teaching, but he is so sweet and has so much passion for what he is teaching. During class, there are iClickers. If you stay on top of your work, the class isn't too difficult. Many of the answers can be found online.

Great person but I never learned anything in this class. Most of the answers for the class can be found online. He does have a tough accent to understand but he's incredibly peppy and cares for the education of his students.
He is an awesome person and wants you to do well. Stay on top of your work and you will get a good grade.

Professor G is nice, but he is very bad at teaching in my opinion. He doesn't really teach, he kind of just talks to you, and he goes on a lot of tangents during class. He is obviously very excited about what he teaches but the way he teaches econ is just not helpful to students. Nobody even takes notes in class because there's nothing to write :/

He's an accomplished man, but not a great teacher, largely due to the obvious language barrier. Its very difficult to understand him, and it gets to a point where no-one shows up because they realize they could teach the material themselves. If you have him, I recommend you switch, otherwise buckle up.

Gebre's class is structured with lectures, Canvas quizzes, homework assignments on each chapter, and exams taken on lockdown browser. A good grade in this class is very possible if you stay on top of your work! He also gives extra credit added to your final based on attendance.

One of the most motivational and passionate profs you'll find at Tech.

Everyone says he's hard to understand and at first, it seemed like it but if you just go to class, pay attention, take notes, and listen it's not that hard. Dr. G is actually such a genuinely nice guy and is very excited and happy with what he does. Also, he provides nearly everything on Canvas so you can always go back to the PowerPoint slides.

He is a great man, but it is hard to understand. Yet if you go to class and take notes its not super difficult. Plus he's really accommodating and gives extra credit. He is open to move assignment and test dates for your own convenience. But if you don't put the effort, your unfortunately going to suffer.

Gebre genuinely cares for his students. People will tell you that he is difficult to understand, but literally by week two I could understand everything with no problem, just give it a chance. He gets so excited when people show up to class (bc honestly very few do), so just show up and give this sweet old man 50 minutes of your day.
Great professor and the well-being of his students is his number one priority.

Professor Gebremariam is passionate about what he teaches. He cares about student's success if you talk to him. Tests are online with lockdown browser but gives good flexibility to students and drops the lowest midterm test. The class isn't difficult but not the easiest.

ECON 2006 is naturally a boring class. Prof Gebremariam is a very passionate teacher and seems to really enjoy teaching. He drops one of the three tests and drops serval homework assignments. Exams are difficult but with the drop and homework boosting your grade, you should be able to get a B in this class

He's a nice guy and all, but he is almost impossible to understand, although i had him during COVID so the mask definitely didn't help. ECON 2006 I thought was much harder than 2005. If you have a hard time understanding people with accents try to take someone else
He has a very inspiring story and overall is a great professor. He offers a zoom option if you don't want to attend class and exams were online.

One of the nicest and most accessible teachers I have ever had. As someone who struggled greatly in ECON 2005, Gebre's thorough lectures helped me succeed in 2006. He gives a decent amount of work, but it is all relevant to the class and given to help you do better. He also has a very inspiring story and cares for all of his students.

Somewhat hard to understand the first but after the first class or two, it's not that hard to decipher. He always shows up happy and very energetic to teach, a real gem of a person. Seems to absolutely love his job and loves to teach. Class isn't too difficult, just PowerPoint lectures during class with weekly quizzes online. I think he is awesome.

Took this class online this semester; prof sends weekly emails with updates about the class and reminders for homework. Fast responses and he let me make up a quiz I missed! Econ is hard but he provides many video lectures explaining the concepts. Study and youll get a good grade.

In my opinion, Im half thru online course. Do not take unless you have to. The video lectures are so long and ambiguous. It seems like I go one step forward and two steps back. The textbook is useless and vague. He tries to explain the concepts but just makes the water murkier. The lecture videos could be cut in half but he goes on tangents a lot.

Gebre was very difficult to understand, but he cares very deeply for his students. Go to class to get the iClicker points because these are a huge part of your grade. Also do the online HWs. Read and take notes on the textbook to learn. I played Wordscapes every class and did fine (:
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: People say they can't understand him but honestly, a few classes in you clearly know what he's saying. Go to class for IClicker Points because they influence your final grade curve. He talks a lot in detail about stuff which isn't on the exam tho. To do well, read chapters and take notes on them. Do and know Exam review questions. Love him, great
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You'll have a tough time understanding him. Lectures are confusing and sometimes too deep. Be prepared to read from the textbook a lot, you'll need it because lectures don't help. Try to do decent on your exams, but at the end he creates a "grading scheme" that curves everyone's grade up several percentage points. Difficult class, but easy A/B
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As a person: amazing As a professor: awful. He's very unhelpful and does not even cover material relevant to the exams in class. He uses his own graphs and examples which isnt helpful. His "practice" exams are excessive, confusing, and nothing like the exam. If you have the option to take with a different professor or elsewhere -- DO IT.

Gebre is a great guy with an amazing story, but not a great professor. Tests are extremely difficult and not like the lectures at all, you should read and study the textbook to get the best picture. The practice tests are awful and totally different than the exams. His accent is very difficult to understand and you will be lost if you don't focus.

His accent is nearly impossible to understand at times. He follows his own curriculum and schedule outside of the other professors in his department so if you wanted to study with your friend from another section you're out of luck. He doesn't allow taking notes on laptop and speeds through his lectures not giving enough time to take notes by hand
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a super nice teacher and always willing to help! Don't be afraid to take his class! If your a decent student and study for the exams you'll be fine
If you plan on coming to class (which is required by iclicker) and being bored out of your mind for 50 3 times a week because you can't understand a single word he says, then this class is for you!!

Terrible teacher. Can't understand a word that comes out his mouth, constantly flips between clustered powerpoints and illegible handwritten notes, and what he talks about in class is rarely if ever covered on exams. He does some curving but its not enough
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult to understand. Nice guy, a big push over. Tests are difficult but he does curve and drop the lowest midterm. Class is very boring however.

He is a very nice man! Totally will help out his students in MANY ways. Yes, his tests aren't easy..meaning you DO have to study. His accent is VERY thick so I didn't understand a word he said. Also, used iclicker for attendance but thats only 5% of the grade. He drops lowest midterm, final wasn't cumu, and curves overall grades.

Whoever says they recommend this guy are ridiculous. Yes, you have to study, as with any other class, but in order to succeed its sometimes nice to be taught rather than having to go to pointless, incomprehensible lectures, and having to teach yourself. He knows his stuff, just a terrible professor. Don't take him. you'll hate it.

he's got a foreign accent, difficult to understand--BUT he's extremely helpful, and passionate about what he does. final isn't cumulative (we had the choice to decide... lol), he drops lowest 3 HW assignments, drops lowest midterm, and curves a LOT. very helpful, i recommend him. his accent is annoying is all.

It's not that the class is hard, it's that he is a terrible professor. If you can avoid his class, do it. If not, good luck. You cannot understand him. The only thing you can understand is "of course, no?" which he says every other word. Also he is disrespectful when trying to meet with him in person. Good luck if you get stuck with him!

People who call this course difficult obviously simply failed to study.  I have been to two classes over the entire semester, I look at the practice problems the morning of the exam and I have a 95 average.  Prof. G is incredibly nice and helpful and the exams are exactly like the practice questions he gives us.

Gebre is a very intelligent and nice person but he is a horrible teacher. He goes over material in depth in class that is not covered on the exams. He has an EXTREMELY thick accent and I could not understand ANYTHING that he said. His lectures are straight from the book but the exams are ridiculously hard. I DO NOT suggest taking his class!

this class is so hard. you cant understand what he's saying most of the time. but you have to go to class cause of ICLICKER. tests are impossible, but he does a pretty good amount of curving, so its not too too horrible

he's a very nice guy with good intentions! just he talks veryyy fast and has a strong accent. but he's always happy and seems more than willing to help. he also takes all student input into consideration. our class wanted hw to count for more and tests for less, so he changed it. he also lowered the number of questions on the test when we asked!
you cant understand a word he says but go to class because he takes attendance.

Lectures can be very dry and boring, and TAs will absolutely mince your quizzes down to the exact language the professor uses, even if it is logically similar. Slides could be better, otherwise decent at material applicability.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For Morality and Justice, we had 13 quizzes and 8 counted towards our final grade. All the quiz answers were covered in the lectures, and then we had a mandatory resuscitation on Fridays. Lectures were sometimes dense, but they were interesting.

Professor Novack is knowledgable and makes good examples/analogies for some of the concepts from class. Only quiz days and recitation days are required, but skipping other lectures will be detrimental to your grade. There is a lot of material to read, especially in the last unit, so seriously focus on reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are quizzes every monday but if you study you should be fine. Your great is mostly quizzes and the final exam. The TAs are really nice, the teacher is fine. I haven't had a bad experience but some had. The class is not difficult if you apply yourself. Lots of reading. I would recommend it if you need a pathway 2 if you enjoy philosophy.

Avoid this professor. He can be pretty rude and unwilling to help. He shows a lot of YouTube videos and expects you to learn from them. If he even catches you on your phone it's 5% off your overall grade and that goes for even if it accidentally rings. He dumps you to the TA once a week, and she was honestly clueless. Everything is on paper.

I would avoid taking this professor at all costs. He doesn't care about his students and he is not willing to help you out. The class consists of quizzes and exams that are all in person and on paper. They are pretty hard and his slides are terrible.

Expectations are clear, if you follow them you will succeed! Novack is helpful and very nice. 

The TAs are historically awful, like genuinely the worst experience of this class. My TA routinely had no idea what was going on and would often make my understanding of a concept worse. 

*I took this class spring 2024
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professional Sleep-inducer, fails to teach key philosophical concepts. Teaching and slides are miserable and hard to follow; not a naturally good speaker. Choose somebody else, plenty of other good Phil teachers

Dr Novack is a great teacher for a hard subject. Logic is challenging, but if you take the homework seriously, attend all the lectures, and go to study hours you will be able to genuinely learn the patterns. That being said, if you miss a class you will have to work hard to catch up as the lessons and rules build off of each other. Awesome teacher!
Great but challenging

Took this class as a pathways course, not even major required, hands-down, my hardest class. Once the middle of the semester hits, it gets undoubtably hard. If given the opportunity to take this class and Greg again, I would not. Overall, just not a very helpful professor and made things very difficult. Worst decision ever taking this class UGH.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While many of these reviews are negative, I personally really liked taking Logic with Prof Novack. This course is very difficult, but if you go to class, do the homework (which can be redone for full credit), and ask questions, you can succeed. Attending class is necessary. You are given all the resources to succeed in the course if you use them!

I took Professor Novack for Modern logic and its development. I do not know if it is the class, or the teacher, but this class sucked. lectures were not engaging, and did not help with homework. The subject itself is very hard, and the teacher cannot explain it well, plus he is a tough grader and if you screw up one thing he takes points off. 2/10.

The perfect professor for 3505 - intelligently designed notes and very clear lectures. Studying the book ahead is a must. You earn the grade you get, but he offers extra credit and allows collaboration on take-home exams (of which there are 2). Hilarious and very accessible outside of class.

He takes 2.5% off total course grade for discussion section absences and 5% off for using/hearing devices during lecture. Can be rude. Course is very difficult in general and I had to watch a lot of youtube videos from other profs to understand. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Novack lowk is a chiller (and dilfy tbh), but I was just so utterly confused by the material. Attending lectures and reading didn't help. If you are planning on taking this to get out of a mathy class (that was me), honestly just take the math class. If you are a philo major/minor, you'll prob love it tho.

Honestly the best professor I've had so far. He comes off as strict but he is really funny at times and is incredible at teaching. The poor ratings are likely from people who skipped Wednesday classes which are the most lecture heavy and not mandatory attendance. The class is difficult but quizzes and the final exam are not graded harshly.

Some units were fine and others were really hard. The professor often goes off topic and it can be hard to follow along sometimes, so you just have to pay attention at all times. This professor is by far the worst professor, especially for a pathways class. He does not care what so ever for his students and his policies are ridiculous. reviews.comment: Relatively engaging lectures but more importantly he gets to the point and explains it well. If you go to class and actually make an effort to learn you will be able to pick it up. reviews.comment: recitations ARE mandatory, and you can only miss 3; no excuses(even excused absences), but they're just with the TA, so they aren't too bad. one unit is super confusing, but everything else is fairly easy to grasp if you're paying attention. nice guy, I find him hilarious, but it's definitely in a goofy/dad way.

Novack is not your typical professor. Where most classes rely on memorization, he ensures that you're able to solve concepts logically. His brain works at a million miles a minute, and sometimes he goes off on tangents, but that's part of the fun. Pay attention, take notes, and understand, don't just memorize. Great, down to earth guy. Loved it.

no device policy, friday recitations are definitely required and you can only miss a total of 3 no matter the reason, dry humor, easy but helpful hw, tentative grades are NOT available. class super depends on whether or not you like the TA

I love Philosophy and took 1504 as an elective. I hated it. He makes a 1000 level class difficult for no reason. He takes no time to actually teach or explain anything- if someone gets it everyone does in his eyes. He thinks he is a GOD because he knows more than a bunch of 20 something y/o students. Pretentious narcissist in a sweater-vest. Avoid.

Philosophy in general is hard, but Professor Novack made it as easy as possible. Professor has a good sense of humor. The readings aren't easy but he goes over them in class. reviews.comment: He was a great professor, but be prepared for quizzes once a week and NEVER have your device out in that class. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor with great lectures, the material is hard and can be rough at times but he does a good job of making the class interesting. He can be awkward but once you get used to it he is awesome.

When a course is this fast-paced & difficult, there is so little a professor can do but be very open to helping you as long as you're dedicated to this class. And, he is. He's a good professor/ not 'warm' though & wish he had more Q&A time and explained things less vaguely! That's the issue I found from him; but, again, so much one can do.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is no joke, it is extremely difficult but I think Professor Novack was amazing. He will make time for any student at any time and he genuinely wants to help. He is very organized and explains everything in great detail. He is honestly one of the best teachers I have ever had, and I am so glad I was able to take this course with him.

Professor Novack was a fairly solid professor. He never recorded his lectures so if you didn't go then you had no idea what happened in class. If he heard or saw any technology in your hand (phone, laptop, etc.) he would take off 5% of your grade. Definitely be prepared to read a lot of material and learn about topics that don't always make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Novack is definitely intelligent, but pretty socially strange. He teaches logic with "his foot on the gas" which means as fast as the smartest person in your class. If you struggle with logic that is NOT good for you. He will tell you to come to office hours, but he is quite akward and makes you feel bad for taking up his time.

Novack is the Goat. TBH I do not know why he received bad reviews on these platforms. The material is not easy to understand, but he works to make it as easy as he can for everyone to comprehend. Hard class, Good professor

Was extremely rude from the get go. I had to miss the third class due to having the flu and he had absolutely no sympathy and refused to give me the SSD notes that I am entitled to for that day. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Kogan is a great guy. He does a great job at explaining the in-class assignments and even posts videos to watch to catch up on. The exams are a little difficult, however, the review sessions help out a solid amount, and if you are in class, you should be fine. There was one group project that wasn't very difficult at all. 10/10 recommend.

Only 2 homework assignments per week which were very easy. The exams were pretty hard and would ask very specific questions about his lectures. I like how we would do excel case studies during class. Overall pretty good, but not the best.
I did not like this class structure. Thought there was lots of busy work and long assignments for barely any points. Also, the exams were pretty difficult given the course content.

Not really great at explaining things and randomly threw in a group project out of nowhere in order to “up grades” after an exam instead of just curving or changing the grade percentages, but for every homework there's an accompanying video which basically explains the whole thing.

Prof Kogan was the best prof I've had at VT. He's accessible outside of class and really wants his students to succeed. He's super knowledgeable, and an A in his class is doable as long as you put in the work.

Great professor overall. You can tell he wants his students to succeed. He is very enthusiastic about teaching which makes lectures engaging. Very approachable if you have any questions and consistently has extra study/make-up sessions. An "A" is very easy achievable with Prof. Kogan.

Super kind and caring Prof! Lectures are a little quick but GO. He walks you through pretty much all of the assignments. Exams are mid but there's only two. Really cares about the content and students.

Professor Kogan is awesome. He's passionate, caring, and knowledgeable from his industry experience. Classes are hands on, the homework is light, and the exams are mostly based on the HW. Exam review sessions are offered  as well where he emphasizes what topics to focus on. There are two group projects which take some time but he grades leniently.

Great guy and super passionate about the subject. Easy class to do well in if you put in effort. Test are not bad, but we all would get B's. Project is cool, if your group is bad it is not hard to do on your own and he is understanding of those things. Wants you to do well. super easy B, need more effort to get to that A, but not unreasonable.

Professor Kogan was one of my favorite professors at VT. His enthusiasm for ACIS is amazing, and it made coming to the lecture a lot easier. The class consists of exams, in-class assignments, and 2 group project presentations. He definitely wants students to succeed; he even has exam reviews and offers extra credit. I would take his class again.

Great overall professor. He is obviously very enthusiastic about the subject, as well as teaching it to his students. His lectures are engaging, and his assignments are helpful for the material. He even held weekly homework workshops in order to go over the homework BEFORE IT WAS DUE. This guy really cares about the success of his students.
Content can be difficult, but Prof Kogan is really helpful. He is also extremely caring and wants all his students to succeed. As long as you go to class and put in effort, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor!! He really cares about his students. All you need to do is come to class.

I am not great at accounting and this class set you up for success. He provides many resources for you to thrive, so you can choose how much you put into the class. The homework is not time consuming and he has weekly meetings to review the chapter each week. If you attend the review session you get extra points on your test!
The class is very structured and if you use all the resources available you will do well but it will take a very long time.
Overall good prof, lectures are kinda boring but helpful for the exam.

Currently in this class online. Lectures and assignments are pretty simple, the issue is that there's just a LOT of them. Probably 1.5 hours of pre-recorded lectures, 5 lecture quizzes, and 5 homework quizzes separated into 3-4 sections each. In total that's an average of about 20 separate assignments per week, so it's really easy to get burnt out.

Very kind teacher. It is his first semester teaching this course so things have been a little chaotic. He was extremely forgiving/beyond helpful in trying to raise my classes grade up. Tests were online with lockdown+web cam.  He added in a group project half way through the semester, I dont know if he will keep that around. Tophat for attendance

He genuinely cares for his students. I've had him before for an online class and I have him now, and he just wants the best for everyone. If you are struggling, he will help to make sure you get on the path to success. He is so kind and caring, and also passionate about what he teaches. This is a difficult course, but worth it if taken with him.

Long, usually boring lectures but homework and quizzes have unlimited attempts. Tests are pretty comparable to quizzes/ homeworks and can get extra credit on all of them. Definitely take notes, go to office hours, and practice before tests. Good grade is very achievable, but requires effort.

A good great is easy if you study. He gives up to 4 extra credit points (test are /30) if you go to his office hours for 30 minutes. The lecture videos can be long/boring but actively listen and take notes on them and you will be fine. There is a lot of hw due each week. I spent 3-4 hours weekly. Very helpful and answers fast. Test based on review.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Async class with good video lectures (not him), weekly modules with hw and lecture quizzes - unlimited attempts on both. Exams were at home, difficult and often included review questions. Definitely would take notes and review lecture quizzes (some were on tests). Getting an A is possible! Just need to really put in effort and make sense of it.

Class is entirely self taught. Assigned a lot of homework and exams were pretty difficult so make sure you actually try to understand the homework and study for exams in advance and you'll probably do fine. He offers A LOT of extra credit which honestly saved my grade. Not hard to get an A or B if you put in some effort.

Never met this professor outside of test days, but I know he never readily responds to emails so beware! Class wasn't bad; just didn't put in much effort. Don't do stuff the night before its due and don't start studying day of the test and you'll be fine! Lectures he posts (for asynchronous class) are not his, but the lady is still good.

Currently in tears writing this, and it will be you next if you take him for your class. My mental health is in severe pain. Please save yourself.

I actually really enjoyed this class. He has a sarcastic sense of humor, which made the class more engaging for me, but it might not come across that way to some. Very poorly taught, I only went to lecture for attendance. If you want to get an A in this class, you'll have to self-study. 100% take with another professor if possible. He's passive aggressive and his class was the reason some people drop out of the CMDA major.

reviews.comment: Heath is such an amazing guy. If you put the effort in and ask questions you can tell he cares about his students and wants to help. He is very knowledgeable about the subject. reviews.comment: Meh. Barely taught anything. He didn't teach a single thing. I learned everything from google, chatGPT, and the online readings. I did not gain a single piece of information from this man. The professor is the most unhelpful professor I have encountered at Virginia Tech in my 2 years here. He is the least accommodating professor, no matter what problem you have, a deadline is a deadline and will not be moved or allowed a later submission. Technical issues do not exist in his world.

Professor Hillman is a blatantly rude person who does not respect his students. The class is taught through a textbook, with no real lectures. He also does not provide any help when asked. reviews.comment: Very easy class if you attend lectures and do the homework instead of chat gpt. lectures can get boring but attendance isn't mandatory. the quizzes/tests are very easy, they're all like 6-10 questions and look very similar to homework questions.

CS1014 is a good intro class to computer science. Dr. Hillman and his TAs are always open to explain problems you don't understand. My TA was also very accessible outside of class. If you pay attention in class, it's a pretty straightforward class. The two final projects have sort of complex rubrics but your TA will help you if you ask.

Lectures were boring and pretty pointless, but he posts the notes on Canvas so that's nice. The class isn't that bad except for the last project, but he isn't very helpful if you go to him for assistance, he seemed to judge me when I asked questions. Not the worst but meh.

Not helpful at all. When you go to him with questions, he just acts like everything is obvious and that you should just understand it. Lectures are pretty much pointless. Most of the projects were pretty average except for the last one which was 10x harder than anything we had to know for our quizzes or what was in our textbooks. Quizzes not bad.

I though the in-class demonstrations were good and well layed out. In my opinion to do well without cheating, you have to go to class and do the reading. He is a good and fair grader and if you do the work you will be fine.

Honestly, unless you have a background in python or can read textbooks very well, goodluck. Lectures are useless, TA's are shared across all the sections and they're also students so it can get a little overwhelming for them. The last project average was around a 56/100, while the others were 70-80/100. Professor himself just yaps about anything.

The lectures for this class are pretty much useless. I had to learn everything through the textbook/practice assignments. The projects were awful and were way harder than anything we covered in class or in the textbook. For someone with no prior coding experience this class was hard. He is also a weird guy in general.

he's a really good professor but in my experience everytime you ask a question he kinda brushes it off or responds in a really passive aggressive way which averted me from asking him for any help. the TA's i've worked with honestly don't really know what they're doing themselves and they aren't there until a half hour after and it wastes time

This class was pretty easy, but it was important to stay on top of the projects. Because 1114 is a weedout course, the workload is somewhat intense, with projects being due every week. Professor Hillman is really funny and it provides an interesting time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class if you already have exposure to Java or even programming in general. I think the way Hillman responds to questions can be taken as condescending, but a lot of the questions he is asked were pretty self explanatory or already explained, at least during lecture. Overall great professor, would take again.

This class is overall very difficult for someone who is just starting out in the programming world. Do not wait till the last minute to do programs, ask for help early and you'll survive. Wait till the deadline and you won't. CS1114 doesn't cover anything heavy so make sure you're understanding these concepts properly.
Heath was an amazing professor. He will help out if you have any problems. Lectures are boring but go to him after class or during office hours to get more help. ASK FOR HELP ABOUT THE PROGRAMS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: "Helpful Heath" is a good professor, and does his best at teaching one of the most terribly designed courses ever. He does a good job during lectures, but because of the large class sizes, is almost impossible to actually get help from. The homework is well worded and it is very clear what you are supposed to do to succeed.

Overall, I would not recommend taking Heath if you are a BIT major trying to fill in your coding class w/ CS1114

This class is intense. There is a lot to just know and do to be successful. Thankfully I come from a coding background and was able to adapt to using Java however I know people who were extremely close to failing. Take PYTHON instead
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

I feel he can be kind of demeaning though if you're confused about something "obvious," he'll seem pretty frustrated with you, which makes him less approachable. The key to doing well in this class is TA office hours.

Prof Hillman was not very welcoming when I would go and ask him questions and I feel like he talked down to me also. I didn't feel comfortable asking him questions or going to the TAs and asking them for help either. He doesn't teach very well and mostly has access to only the TAs. Easy class to grasp just not a supportive environment.

No idea why he has such a high rating. This man gave me the creeps, especially as a woman. Not only was he super rude and condescending every time a question was asked, he couldn't teach very well and had a habit to ramble. Grading is also tough and nitpicky. Definitely designed as a weed-out. 

Prepare to rely on TA's. Don't be in a room alone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Has great lectures. CS 1114 is a very large class, so it is hard to get help from him. But, there are LOTS of TAs that can help during tutoring hours. Hard class, but he teaches well. The only thing I didn't like about his class was that he took a lot of questions during class, so we sometimes didn't cover all the material in lectures.

Mr. Hillman is great! Office hour lines are long, but he will honestly do the code for you. His lectures aren't the greatest, but he is super resourceful and stays after to help. The quizzes are difficult and require some extra work. The programs aren't bad, just don't overthink. I had a 96 prior to the final but bombed it so I ended with a B+

From one who has never done CS class and little code exp. His lectures are copying his code. Then do projects beyond lectures - extreme difficult unless A) you wait hours in line bc limited office hours + amount of people or B) spend hours at the TAs. Nitpicky autograder. Tests are extremely difficult. If experienced, you're fine,if not, good luck.

Professor Hillman is pretty funny. The class is mostly taught through the Canvas course, and his lectures served only to supplement that. He is very laid back. He will answer any question you have for him regarding the material and will help fix bugs in your code if you are stuck.

Dr.Hillman is truly an amazing person. This class was made much easier because of his guidance. He has a very fun personality and is nice to be around. I currently have a 95% in the class just waiting for the final grade to be released. The class is a hard intro class but Dr.Hillman cares about his students and will do all that he can to help.

He is super sweet and always answers questions. There may be some attendance in class, but he always posts it the night before. Recitation attendance is required, but easy. He posts test reviews that are nearly identical to the tests, so it's easy to cram. He cares about what he teaches and his students performance. If you want an A, take him.
Best math professor I have had. The practice tests are similar to his tests. Attendance mandatory when there is online class activities.
Best professor ive had at VT thus far, super easy to study, tests are exactly like practice tests so study those and you will be great. Excellent teacher and makes lectures easy to follow.
If you take him and you put in the effort to study for exams and homework and actually learn the content, it's a guaranteed A. He's mostly available for help so just go to office hours.

One of the best statistics professors I've had. His exam review sessions are a must — very clear, well-organized, and they help you see how all the course topics connect. His assignments are practical and closely tied to real-world applications, which made me truly understand and apply the material. Highly recommend taking his class.
He is a very kind professor who really wants you to succeed. He has good lectures and his test are very accurate to what is taught in class. Would recommend him 100%
He is truly the best. He cares about his students and is very kind with grading. Group project at end and 3 exams but it's a chill class
The nicest, most encouraging professor. He also makes all the material clear and his tests are very fair. Would love to have him again in a future stats class.

He is super kind and understanding. He is flexible with extensions. I took his summer class, and he provides videos to watch and take notes on, and then there is a quiz and homework every week, due at 11:59 on Sundays. There is extra credit provided every week as well, but not mandatory.
Fantastic. Made the course material easy and had me entertained the whole time. I ended up completing homework for other classes during his lectures because of how quickly things clicked with Hamdy.

He's very friendly and patient. Lectures can be a little tough to stay awake for, and he can yap a lot, but he almost always lightens the mood when he starts teaching. I hope to have him again for higher level stat.
The greatest professor ever. His lectures are super organized and he is always available if you need help. Super nice and easy to talk to. Truly the best professor ever.

I LOVE professor hamdy. He made the class so enjoyable and useful. The test are almost exactly like the practice tests he gives and there is always extra credit on the tests. The final isn't cumulative. Homeworks are given once a week and only take an hour or less.

great professor. He definitely cares about all of his students and wants them to do well in his class. He offered a lot of extra credit (even on all the exams). Homework load is not heavy and homework is graded leniently. Exams are pretty easy. Would definitely take him again. He does a great job of answering questions.

Hamdy was a very enthusiastic and caring professor. He gave lots of extra credit and made the homework and exams very easy. He always answers questions about the material, homework, et cetera directly and often just gives you the answer if asked. He was very accessible outside of lectures and was always willing to help. Absolutely would take again!

Hamdy is one of the best professors at Virginia Tech. He consistently maintains a positive attitude during lectures, ensuring that everyone enjoys his class. He is responsive to emails, and if you can't attend his office hours, he accommodates your schedule. Overall, Hamdy is an exceptional professor who cares about his students.

Post lecture slides online. The lectures are nice, he's a great teacher and can explain topics in ways you can understand. Also awards extra credit if you participate in class. Workload was fair and manageable, and if you had questions, he responds to emails pretty fast. Overall, an amazing teacher, highly recommend taking him if you can.
Very nice to his students, always prepared with notes and examples, fair homework's, responds quickly to emails and is available outside his office hours. Wish he was teaching 3006.
He is such a great Professor!! He cares about his students and is the sweetest. His exams are easy, and he sets you up for success. Definitely take his class!!
Best professor ever! He's so nice and really cares about his students. Learned so much in this class and he gave extra credit!!
Very dedicated towards students' success and learning. Light grader, just attend lectures and make a galient effort. Also, it helps to attend office hours and annotate the slides during the lecture.

Amazing professor, certainly my favorite in the department of stats. I have taken all of the classes he has offered and would happily take them again if I had to. Loves teaching & cares about his students. Lovely man. 10/10

Hamdy was an amazing professor! I took his online biological statistics class over the summer and it was great! His lectures explain material very well and he always responded within a day of me emailing him a question. If I ever needed to take another stats class it would be with him! Take him! Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: absolute GOAT of statistics department

Hamdy is one of the best professors you will ever have. He wants you to pass. He is super easy going to talk to, you should ask him lots of questions. He made almost all of our tests open note. Only con is that his lectures are hard to follow. Besides that, I am grateful that I had him.

He is a great professor. He actually cares and wants everyone to pass so he does a lot of extra credit. If you go to class you will have a good time because after a chapter is over he does kahoots for extra credit and on every test there is a bonus point question. It is only two tests and the final, if you do the practice tests then it will be easy
Hamdy is one of the best professors I have had at tech. He is very kind, understanding, and knowledgeable. Definitely take him if you are able to, his class is an easy A.

He is the best professor here at tech. He makes his students laugh and feel cared for and is always happy to help you if you need it at any time. He offers many extra credit opportunities and loves to see his students succeed. Hamdy is the sweetest professor and loves his job so much and it shows. 1000/10

Hamdy is the best, absolute angel. Definitely take him if you're trying to decide who to take for stats. His homework and study guides are always a little bit harder than the test which is nice. He never makes you do excessive amounts of math just because and he always tries to make your life easier. I have never seen him without a huge smile.

Best professor I have had at Tech. He genuinely wants you to succeed and understand what is happening in the class. Very simple assignments and exams. If you absolutely need it, he had no issues allowing extensions on assignments. Very kind man and I highly suggest him.

I took him as a freshmen for bio stats and even though it was a junior level class, it was easy. He teaches so well and has a great sense of humor. He is always willing to help you on anything and there are a lot of chances for extra credit.

Very caring professor who tries to make sure you can succeed, offers frequent office hours and will quickly answer emails. Course is made up of homework, quizzes, exams, and bonuses which can be helpful at the end. Best professor for bio stats and made the material easy to understand.

Hamdy is amazing! Easily one of the easiest math classes I've taken while still learning something. He provides opportunities for extra credit and he gives out practice problems for tests which makes them easier. He really cares about his student's success and is also funny. Highly recommend him if you're planning to take stat.

If you're between choosing a professor for STAT 2004 take Hamdy! He is easily one of the sweetest professors ever, funny, and he cares for his students. Attendance is not mandatory but it is essential to do well, he gives out extra credit frequently. Workload is not bad to keep up with.

If you need to take stats, TAKE HAMDY!!! He is literally the sweetest and nicest professor. I took him for both STAT2004 and STAT3615, and I don't regret taking him. His class is not hard at all either, and he is available to help with homework or if you have questions. Literally one of the best professors I have had here at VT.

Professor Hamdy is honestly the BEST professor for bio stats, he deserves the whole world!! He makes the class fun and has a great sense of humor. He genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. If you ever need to take this class for a pathways credit, TAKE THIS CLASS. PLEASE. You won't regret it.

He is awesome. If you have the chance to have Hamdy as a professor then absolutely take it. Best professor at Virginia Tech. He explains everything so well and he is super nice and down to earth. He loves to see his students do well, which is rare.

Super nice guy who truly cares about the subject he is teaching- unfortunately his teaching style just didn't work for me, and I really struggled to pay attention or care. That being said, the class if very easy if you learn the material, and if you do the practice test you will get an A on the test.

Professor Hamdy is the BEST professor for Statistics. Easy A because he gives you SO much extra credit. Always available to help during office hours & if you have questions on the test, it's easy to go up to him to clarify questions. Go to most the classes bc thats when he gives you extra credit. Online HW is very easy & he gives 2x to get it right

Dr. Hamdy is an amazing professor. He cares about all his students and genuinely wants them all to succeed. He gives lots of chances for extra credit if you show that you are willing to learn. He knows what he's teaching and he able to explain things very well. If he taught a more advance class, I would DEFINITELY take it.
Hamdy is truly an awesome professor. Even if you don't do well on the tests, there are other assignments that will bring your grade up.
Hamdy is a cool guy. Good teacher. Hes pretty funny. His class is pretty easy but definitely go to class and take notes. He really cares about his students and wants them to pass.
Best professor I've had so far at VT. Really cares about his students getting a good grade. Super funny and down to earth. Really easy, as long as you pay attention in class you'll be fine

TAKE HAMDY for Statistics. He is an amazing professor and does EVERYTHING he cans to ensure you get the grade you want. He literally gives tons of extra credit out and sometimes the extra credit would be silly like answer a question right in class. The material is not that tough just do his study guides for his test.

If you pay attention and learn the formulas you will get an A in this class. He gives partial credit for work on his exams which are multiple choice. Make sure you always do the homework and go to the recitations and you will be good to go. He is a great professor and is so caring and wants his students to succeed.
He is the best teacher I have ever had at VT!! Thanks professor Hamdy Fayez Mahmoud!!

If you need to take ENGL 1106 take it with professor Isaac, he makes the class very easy and gives great feedback. Is super flexible with 95% of deadlines and is grading contract makes it super easy to do well. Cannot recommend him enough!

Prof. Isaac was very chill and super flexible. I was dreading taking english and he made it seem so easy and light that it made me enjoyed it. He is very compassionate with missing classes and overall has a welcoming and positive tone for the class. He also gives you a lot of positive feedback on your work which was nice. Definitely reccommend.

Professor Isaac consistently shows support and understanding to his students. He gives good feedback, offers a LOT of extra credits, and communication with him is easy. Also he is an absolute chill grader, you can literally get 100 in this class.

Bad reviews are generally trump supporters coping with their lack of comprehension skills lol. Easy A and yes the course is generally preachy about environmental and sustainability issues, but if that's considered "radically liberal" idk what to tell you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: super passionate and educated guy. the bad reviews are from pressed trump supporters lol
It is his own textbook, and all of his opinions.

This class is such a waste but is an easy pathway. The whole class is just Greg making you pay a ton for the textbook he wrote about his own personal opinions without actually learning anything. The quizzes are pretty easy and the discussion posts cover any points you might lose. Easy A that was a complete waste of my time.

Honestly, this class is really easy BUT the grade distribution is slightly unclear in the syllabus at the beginning of the year. This means you can only get an A in the class if you get 100. The questions on the quizzes are weird because an answer could technically be right, but if the info wasn't directly stated in the reading, it's incorrect.

This is the most liberal textbook I have ever read in my life and there is no attempt to hide it. Not my vibe but if you're into being preached at about topics that have literally nothing to do with a design course go for it. He basically spends every chapter complaining about the failures of society.

Textbook written by professor. Some interesting aspects of course but gets very repetitive after a while. All grades except final project are 5 question quizzes with unnecessarily complicated responses. I would always read the chapters assigned and would rarely get all questions correct. The short quizzes also led to one mistake giving you an 80.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy class as long as you're consistent and doing the weekly work but even if you don't do well on the quizzes there is extra credit for each assignment. Just a lot of reading.

He is a very interesting man that has very strong opinions. I was unsure of him at first, but I began to see his vision as time went on. He wants you to respectfully argue with him. You are almost guaranteed an A in his class, and in exchange he expects you to care. Not a hypocrite when it comes to lifestyle choice. Rides his bike in 5 degrees lol

I tried really hard to like this class but it was just so political that I couldn't enjoy any of the material. The content is all based on his opinion and you really don't learn anything about general design. I expected to be learning about building instead I had to read about how we need to restructure the government in America

The course is very easy but does require careful reading and thinking. I do not recommend taking this course if you do not care about the content and want to breeze through the course without much effort.

Tew is knowledgeable and teaches well. My only complaint is regardless of if you thoroughly read or not, his quizzes ARE sometimes opinion based or worded in biased manner. I'm not saying it's political as some do- people are quick to make that claim. I believe if you LIKE the topic then you'll do good. You have to know how he words things.

This review is all for his classes. It's easy. Just read and do the work and you're fine with an A by the end of the semester. Its an interesting read from him. Those who think he's pushing a political agenda are kinda "behind" and have a cyclops mentality for not being aware of how infrastructure in America is historically. Just sayin'

Professor Tew created one of the easiest GPA booster classes at VT. Read the article, which takes only 20 minutes, and the quiz will be easy—the discussion after takes no more than 10 minutes. If you need to fulfill a pathway 6 class, then this is for you. He has crazy ideals, but who cares! Easy A, amirite?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class is super easy. You waste money on a textbook because you need it to do the quizzes. The textbook isn't a real textbook, it's more so Tew's thoughts on how everyone should not have cars and should live with 20 roommates and you shouldn't have kids or use plastic basically. Super unrealistic political agenda but you have to try to not get an A.

Easy A class, dont slack off. Do the dissuasion posts and you'll get an A. More political than I thought it was going to be. If you think its an art class where you talk about color theory etc. youre wrong. Its about how civil design effects the environment, basically.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is really easy as long as you skim the textbook chapters. Two quizzes a week and optional discussion posts for extra credit. Very easy gpa booster so long as you actually do the work, which is not much.

This class (Design appreciation) is an easy A, but a stupid class. You spend way too much money on a Textbook the professor wrote, just for it to be based solely on his opinion. Nothing in the textbook is applicable, it is simply the professor pushing his political ideology on you.

As long as you actually read the chapters you should be good for this class since all the answers on the short quizzes are found directly in the textbook or linked sources. The class should only take at max two hours per week. Just be willing to consider different view points and take some time to think about your stance on the topics.

this class is a painful joke. the ony reason I ended with a B+ is because I didn't do the discussions so definitely do those. otherwise his quizzes are stupid and even reading the textbook chapters thoroughly won't even help you. pmo

Assigns weekly readings from the textbook and quizzes to go along with them. Quizzes are okay to comprehend and always remember to watch through the linked videos for specific details. Participate in the discussions for points back as they're easy to get, and set a reminder to complete them on time! Material is more conversational than textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a horrible course. The entire textbook are full of his various political opinions and if you do not agree, you get the quiz questions wrong. The only reason I passed was due to the discussion boards & not reading the $100 textbook. If you read the textbook, you would get questions wrong because you'd disagree with his views.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Easy 6a Pathway and very hard to fail. Just do the biweekly chapter readings (discussions = extra credit), and you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Greg Tew is extremely liberal, which is fine but reading through his textbook and discussions are brutal. The class is honestly a joke, and you can get an A without even opening canvas. Don't waste your time, or do if you need a GPA boost.

This whole class is a joke. The extremely overpriced textbook is just a lengthy lecture on his personal (very extremist) opinions with little fact behind them. The quiz questions sometimes aren't even answered in the text. It's ultimately it is a waste of your time and money. All he does is criticize others for driving cars and eating fast food.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class only takes about 30-45 minutes a week and it is actually interesting. He gives extra credit if you participate in discussions.
Design appreciation was so easy just do the weekly quizzes and discussions, answers straight from the book you just need to get 8/10 on every quiz for an A. Easy 6a pathway.
The textbook is very easy to read and flows like a normal lecture would. The quizzes are very easy if you do the readings which are pretty light. There's many extra credit opportunities as well.
Unless you actually die halfway through the semester you will get an A in this course. Weekly assignments that are easy, you can miss like 3 or 4 and still get a 100%.

This class is super easy there are no tests. If you don't get an A, it's probably just because you didn't do the assignments. Even if you don't get a 10/10 on every quiz, he drops a lot of them and the discussion posts help bring your grade up. Really easy class, especially for a pathway.

Greg is a solid professor. He cares a lot and will give good feedback.

BUT, he is very left leaning and states many of his opinions as fact. That is fairly off-putting.

Really easy A if you skim the textbook and do all the discussions. You can be done a few weeks before the semester ends. But the textbook is ridiculously overpriced for what it is (just Professor Tew's opinions on different topics, some of which are hard to take seriously). But overall, good class to take for Pathway 6.

Easiest class ever but all Greg Tew does is make you pay his bills by forcing students to buy his overpriced textbook and spend their semester reading a written lecture on how everyone else should spend less money. I think he has some very idealist and radical opinions but it makes for very interesting discussion forsure.

Design Appreciation was one of (if not the) easiest class I have taken at VT so far. While the textbook was VERY overpriced (in my opinion), the class itself was still very easy and manageable if you just read the chapters online (which aren't that hard/time consuming) and did the discussions to earn bonus points. Overall, very easy class.
Overall, this class was really easy. Make sure to do the chapters on time and DO THE DISCUSSIONS! Textbook is a little expensive, but otherwise it's a good class.

He must have hit his head really hard at some point (probably while getting out of his car, which is why he hates on cars), as his textbook is overpriced and makes absolutely no sense. He just spends the entirety of it yapping about his senseless opinions. Sadly, no one is going to care that you walked through the ditches to school every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Design appreciation was probably the easiest class I have taken. As long as you skim the textbook chapters, you should be able to get an A in the class easily. While the discussion posts may seem annoying, just do them; they will help you get an A in the end. The professor is very passionate about his work and you can tell from the textbook.

Great course. Textbook is fun and easy to read and if you are worried about cost, the text is much cheaper than the Auto Safety course for Pathways 6. The format is super clear with reminders and announcements to stay on track. I wasn't expecting much, but the class was actually really interesting. I'm taking Tew's other class in the fall.

This class is an easy A, but the content is subjective and not very insightful. The textbooks are overpriced, and it feels like the instructor is trying to profit from them. I recommend BMES 3004 (Helmet Design) instead, which is also online, more engaging, and easier. Overall, a pretty boring class.
Easy pathway - write the discussion posts and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I genuinely laugh at everyone that gets less than an A in this course. This guy also isn't much of a professor since he just sends canvas announcements out and farms money off everyone looking for a GPA boost. Its ironic because his book is all about cutting back on waste and consuming less, yet this class is a waste of everyones time and money.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Textbook sooo expensive, but its not that bad.

This class is essentially a grade booster and it is very easy to get a good grade. There are two weekly quizzes and readings that only have 5 questions. Each chapter also has an optional discussion post, if you respond to the discussion and post a reply to another student I believe you have the chance to gain 27 extra points at the end of semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His classes are not worth your time. All of the textbook chapters are based mostly on his own opinion, so theres no academic value. Its so clearly biased that it pmo. Its not a hard class by any means but hes so insufferable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A if you do all the assignments and discussions. I did not and still got a B+. The quizzes aren't on quizlet anymore and they don't show you what's right and wrong so beware. I got a lot of 8/10s on the 5 question quizzes which gave me a lower score.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is so easy getting an A is so lightwork. Easiest pathway and a gpa booster for minimal effort.

You have only one day to read the chapter and take the quiz for full credit so that was kind of annoying. And some of the quizzes have trick questions and wording matters, so always read the quiz questions and answer choices before the chapter. Overall, it's definitely a good class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The textbook was a little expensive, considering that he himself wrote it. Other than that, I loved this class. Taking it in my first semester in college was a good idea. Very easy workload, and the discussions had me really think. I'm kinda aspirational like him, so I enjoyed it. But it was also easy to not pay attention and still get good grades!

Didn't like the class one bit. Thought it was going to be design appreciation but it was quite the opposite. I have no idea why I learned about robots in an architecture class. It was so incredibly hard to reach him if I needed help with something which was a bummer. If you had to choose this class over a different one, don't chose this one.
Super easy class. It's not SUPER exciting, but just do the assignments and discussions and it's an easy A.
Easiest pathway. Impossible not to get an A. Professor is the man.
Gregs the man

This class is extremely easy. It's a guaranteed 95% (A) or higher—I would be impressed if someone failed, because you would have to deliberately try to fail. However, this professor is scummy for locking the course behind a $90 paywall for his trash textbook and opinions. Easy GPA boost, but don't expect to gain anything of value.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Design Appreciation is my favorite class. 10/10. Sure, some of his ideas are pretty far out there but he explains that design is about imagination. The US and world have serious problems and Tew has some interesting thoughts on how to fix them. I love the textbook. It is fun and easy to read and I found myself looking forward to each new chapter.

prof knows that ppl share answers to the textbook, so he makes the questions very weirdly worded and like everyone else is saying, quizzes are based off of his opinions. Textbook has so much yap and overall terrible online class.  quizzes every Monday/Thurs. optional discussions for extra points, 0.5 pt for posting, 0.5 pt for responding to a post.

I've never learned more interesting stuff in a class. Some people complain the whole class is just his opinion, but he backs everything up with data and he is simply pointing out the need for everyone to work together for sustainable living. The discussions are really interesting and the bonus points essentially guarantee an A in the class.

Design Appreciation is amazing. I'm a junior and it is by far the most interesting and relevent Pathways class I have taken. I've never had a class that tied together so many aspects of life into one coherent story. I'm finished with my Pathways but I plan to take Tew's other class, Life in the Built Environment just to take another class from him!

Greg has one of the simplest jobs and he still failed. Listen, if you have spent more than 10 grand a semester to go to VT, do not pick this class, as in my opinion its worth about 5$ and a poor handshake. TOPICS DISCUSSED: junk food, slavery, health insurance, society, literally anything that could somehow be connected to design of anything.

Very simple and understandable set-up for readings, quizzes, and discussion posts. Textbook is opinion-based but brings light to prevalent issues in our built environment. Not difficult to read and do discussion posts.

Easiest A you'll ever get—basically paying $100 for no effort. The real issue is the professor's writing: aggressively one-sided, almost extremist left, treating opinions as facts and ranting far outside his expertise or the course scope. I'm not political, but even I found his writing very hard to read. It's very narrow sighted.
Class was easy but high-key the quizzes were a lot easier when you stopped thinking critically and just tried to find perfect 1-to-1 matches in the textbook. Do the discussions and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Super political, wants you to believe that only his views are correct. Quizzes just test you on his opinions.

Although I don't agree with a lot of Greg's views in his book, it's refreshing to read something that makes you look at things through a different point of view. Honestly, his book has opened my eyes to a lot of new things. Sure, it's just his opinions, but he stays true to the intent of the class: how everything is a design problem. Quizzes are EZ

This guy just assumes his opinions (far Left) are accurate. There are many unproven facts that he passes as 100% true which can be extremely misleading. Plus, he is charging $100 dollars for this. Sure, take the easy A, but just be cautious with what you take away when you read in this textbook.
No comment.

I've taken Design Appreciation and Life in the Built Environment. Loved both classes. The textbooks are super interesting and easy to read. The quizzes are not hard (as some people say) and Tew offers a bunch of bonus points to guarantee an A in the class. I'm planning to take his new class Architecture and Culture in the fall.

Expensive, but interesting textbook. A lot of students claim that it's just opinions passed off as facts, but nowhere does he force any student to hold any beliefs, and he has discussion boards specifically for students to have open conversations and disagree. If you can spend two hours a week reading, then this will be an easy credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Easy course, mainly just annoying due to quizzes with each chapter that are extremely confusing and don't expect to consistently get 10/10 on them. The textbook is written by him, so he earns a commission off of each one sold, and is very clearly just political. This class has nothing to do with design, it's just climate change and car hating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Life in the Built Environment is fascinating. I've been to Europe 3 times, and I always wondered why the US is so different, in a bad way, compared to Europe. This class and Design Appreciation have opened my eyes about the problems we have with sprawl and driving, so I plan to live in walkable neighborhoods when I graduate. Thank you Greg!!

Love, love, love this class. I expected a boring Pathways but I'm a junior and this class has quickly become one of my top 5 classes. There's so much real world info in the class and the textbook is amazing. Never thought I'd say that! I'm planning to take his other classes before I graduate.

Without fail, every quiz there will be horribly worded questions. Do your best to turn your brain off while reading because the text book (which costs$90 and he wrote himself) is full of opinions that he likes to pass off as facts. easy A but probably not worth the sanity and hair loss this class will cause if you actually do all the reading.

make question so confusing. gives like 4 options, a b c d and then to make you confused add two additional answer choice of 2 or more choices from the 4. terrible as you only have 5 questions

I respect the guy; scamming college students and forcing them to buy his $90 insane textbook is quite the hustle. A textbook where he teaches his opinions and tries to present said opinions as fact. Easy enough class, though.
my glorious greg tuah

The content is very subjective to some people, as the textbook is created by him, but my rating is just based on trying to get a free A for credit as well as having some fun. 5 if its a filler class, a 4 for a class if you take it seriously. Besides that, he's very forgiving with the course policy. Do the extra credit

This class is an easy A, just take 30 mins to do the weekly readings and quizzes. Do the discussions, they are graded on participation and are extra credit, they make a huge difference. Some people don't like the content of the textbook, but I don't mind because of how easy this was. I will say this isn't really a design course.

Quizzes are tricky because they are formatted as select all that apply yet graded as multiple choice, aka no room for partial credit. With that being said, you could do well if you read the chapters. My quiz avg was ~80% (4/5), and I got a 100.45% in the class because of the extra credit. Topics are opinionated, so not for everyone, but an easy A.

reviews.comment: ITDS1114 is a straightforward class, but you'll need to put in the effort. The quizzes can be tricky, so reading the textbook closely is key. Utilize unstuckstudy and other study tools to ace this course.
Easy A class

DESIGN APPERATION IS NOT A DESIGN CLASS. It is a class where he can rant about his random political opinions and the way that he connects them to design are a stretch to say the least. However, it was a super easy class. One quote that I think sums up his is "kidney stones hurt worse than childbirth, I asked three women."

Professor Tew offers insightful opinions in Design Appreciation, and the topics covered are genuinely very interesting. The two weekly quizzes are quite convoluted, you can't just skim the article, you must read the entire page to do well on them. This isn't too much of an issue, however, because the content genuinely is quite fascinating.

Extremely easy class. Just do your work and don't skip quizzes. You can get one point of extra credit every time you take a quiz with discussion boards. it was alright, pretty boring

Greg is an amazing professor and this class was amazing as well. He opened my eyes to so many things in the US. How to notice problems, figure out what is causing them, and brainstorm solutions. reviews.comment: Easily the most interesting class I have ever taken, and the most knowledgeable professor I have ever had in their field. The chapters were really short and interesting, and I had never felt so engaged reading them. The discussion questions were also very engaging. I missed two quizzes and bombed a few as well, still ending the course with >100%

His class is super easy. All assignments are super quick too. It's all textbook based + it's online. It's his own textbook though, and he's very preachy & self-righteous in his writing, constantly talking abt how great he is, so it's very annoying reading his textbook.

The workload isn't bad, its just reading and a quiz twice a weekThe material of this class was very opinion heavy (he wrote the textbook), and the bi-weekly quizzes are kinda chaotic.
