reviews.comment: Easy. Straightforward
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm in Life in the Built Environment after taking Design Appreciation last year. Love both classes. Easy but also interesting. I'm taking his new class Architecture and Culture in the spring. The flexibility of his online classes make my schedule of work and classes much easier to manage. Win win!

I'm in Life in the Built Environment after taking Design Appreciation as a freshman. Most Pathways classes are boring, but these classes are awesome. I see the world differently now, and thanks to Greg's classes I am better prepared to make adult decisions in my life after college. Everyone should be required to take this class. 10/10.

I'm a senior and this is my favorite class in 4 years. I'd heard the class was interesting, and even though I didn't agree with everything, even when I didn't agree, the class made me think about stuff more than any class I've ever taken. I'm taking Life in the Built Environment spring semester. I've heard it's even better.

Design Appreciation was amazing. I'm taking Life in the Built Environment now. Both classes really make you think and take about an hour twice a week. It's hard to accept some of the things discussed in the textbooks, but the professor's point of view is always backed up with facts. Both classes focus on climate change, and the facts are scary.

This is a class put bug in my brain. I see everything differently now. I never paid much attention to design before taking both of his classes, but I now see how the design of everything influences our economy, equality/inequality, and my quality of life. I hope that some day, the US will wise up, and make the changes discussed in this class. 10/10

He basically just pushes his own beliefs and opinions onto you repeatedly for a whole semester. The class might be worth taking because it is easy, just prepare for your brain to be decaying by the end of it.

Class was super interesting and not hard. Was surprised to read the negative comments here. But then again, a lot of students are too lazy to read the syllabus or do the very reasonable amount of work needed to earn an A in the class. Will definately take his other online class.
Nobody below the IQ of 690 take his class because if you ask him to repeat anything you don't understand he will not and then ask you to not contact him again

This was an easy class but he wasn't a good teacher. He puts no effort into the class. He also decided it was too much work for him to post on canvas to tell his students when there is a quiz. Basically everybody at VT takes his class and it only takes about 30 minutes twice a week. The quizzes are pretty easy if you read the textbook instead of guessing. He gives bonus points for the online discussions, so participate and you will make an A. There are 1000+ students in his classes every semester so expect a few negative reviews.10/10!

Awesome teacher/classes. I took both Design Appreciation & Life in the Built Environment. Both are life changing for anyone that has an open mind for learning. My experience in this class was awful. Not only could I not see my grade until after withdraw forms had closed, but the professor is also extremely rude. Tew knows that this class is often taken by people solely for an easy A or credit. Design Appreciation is tough. Sometimes the quizzes were easy, but other times the quizzes could be pretty rough.

This is probably the best pathways course to take, it is basically a guarantied A if you do all the quizzes which are just twice a week.
Great professor, he charges $75 for everyone to have a textbook that he wrote. His views are made known, so it's hard to stay unbiased.

This class is very engaging and really makes you do good critical thinking. Greg is super nice and a great professor- all of the chapters were very well written and brought up great points. Quizzes are pretty easy, and I highly recommend doing the discussions every week. (This is a good class if you're looking to improve writing skills too.)
Easiest A you could ever get. It takes at most an hour of work per week and no exams.  Does require a textbook written by the professor that costs $70+, but I would still say it's worth it.

ITDS 1114 was by far the easiest class I've taken at Tech. As long as you do your work and don't forget about the class, you will easily pass with an A. Easiest class at Tech, with 30 minutes of homework a week plus an optional discussion post. The textbook is pretty interesting to read, but it is mostly just his opinions on different issues.

I took this class for a pathway and I am glad I did. This class took about 40 minutes to an hour each week. There are discussion boards at the end of each chapter which are extra credit. Very easy and engaging.

Over 4000 students have to take this class every year and he is charging them $70 for his book. It is obvious why he is teaching this class ($280,000 a year) which is about three times his regular salary!!!!
Good at setting expectations and has a easy class
literally the easiest A at VT. do all your work before its due which takes at most 45mins twice a week and you will have a 100%.

The hardest thing about this class is remembering to do the quizzes. I'd recommend doing to the extra credit discussions just incase.
Very passionate professor and love what he was teaching us. Always was engaging in discussion post even thought it was fully online. Recommend taking both of his classes.

I have taken both if his pathways classes and they are probably the easiest classes at virginia tech. I find the way he sets up his classes very easy to follow. Two chapters a week and each has a quiz and a discussion board if you do a certain amount you get EC. This class will really open your mind to a lot of new ideas. 100% recommend taking it.
Super, super easy class. Just read the book and answer the questions. The discussion board responses give bonus points at the end of the semester based on how many you do.

This is a very easy class, you read about two chapters a week, and there are quizzes at the end of each chapter, which is only 5 questions. Material hard to get through without getting mad. Professor was very much 'my way or the highway' line of thinking.

The ITDS 1114 class itself is very easy, just wake up and do basic reading comprehension. One of the best/easiest pathway classes you can take. If you're worried about the quizzes, just participate in the discussions every week, and you're almost guaranteed an A.

reviews.comment: This class was both extremely easy and inspirational. Professor Tew wrote the chapters you read, which keep you engaged, and you find yourself seeing the class material outside in the real world. I learned a lot about the American infrastructure/environment. Would definitely recommend this course and take his other class if I could.
Took this in Fall 2022. Also another easy class, and structured very similar to Design Appreciation.

Took this class in Spring 2022. Very easy class, grades are primarily from completing quizzes and doing discussions for extra points that covers missed questions. Enlightening class in which you get to see how people respond to different things in discussions.

Easiest Pathways 6a course and class you'll take at VT. Very opinionated class, but learned a lot of different opinions and topics about our world. 2 five question quizzes per week, DO THEM. reviews.comment: Super easy class, but he's very very opinionated.

Overall, tis class was super easy, so easy to get an A. Mainly is just two 5 question quizzes and a discussion post for each one every week. Doing the discussions can sometimes get pretty political, but I found it pretty easy to stay neutral and just get the extra points.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: LOVED THIS CLASS. It's a very easy A, while you're still learning interesting material. The course work is easy and he gives his students a lot of extra credit opportunities. My advice is to do ALL the discussion posts, it'll be for your benefit.

reviews.comment: So this class was incredibly easy. I barely put in an hour a week and got a perfect 100. But, his class is just hearing his same strong leftists view over and over. You don't learn anything but it fulfills a pathway.

You are given quizzes once or twice a week. Hes sometimes the death of me but if you keep up the quizzes and do the discussion post then its an easy A class. This class is a grade booster just have to stay on top of it.

reviews.comment: If you actually want to learn something you should take a different class. However, if you only care about getting an A there are very few other classes that will be less work than this one.
Easiest A at VT. Also very interesting class and material, if you arent politically biased youll gain alot of very insightful info throughout the course on pressing issues like climate change.
Just do the quizzes and you'll be fine. The class is an easy A if you don't forget about it. Professor Tew seems like a chill guy.

If you stay on top of the assignments, it is super easy. And participate in the discussion posts! That is the most important thing! It will save you from stress if you mess up on a quiz. Overall, the class is easy and as long as you put in minimal effort, you should pass.

the goat, bi-weekly quizzes with lots of extra credit available

Gregory Tew is a great teacher and his class is very interesting and not hard at all as long as you remember to actually do the little work there is. Just don't consistently forget to do the reading quizzes like 5 times in a row like I did.

reviews.comment: Definitely take his class. Its 26 5 question quizzes and he drops the lowest three, and he gives optional discussion questions for extra credit.
