Dr. Tew's class, Design Appreciation, was very interesting. The textbook he provides, which he also wrote, is clear and concise. His grading criteria is almost all participation. Do the work, you'll have no problem passing. While his ideas are very interesting, I'm not sure he gives enough explanation of competing theories or opinions.
Great course to take as Pathway 6a or 6d and very interesting content that can be relevant later in your life! Recommend it as an easier course if you take it alongside some harder courses.

Super easy class. You read a short chapter that's not difficult and take a 5 question quiz twice a week. The answers are in the short reading online. He also drops your 3 lowest quizzes and will give extra credit if you do some discussion questions. Its easy for the pathway 6 credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He teaches a very easy but interesting class focusing on the influence design has played and impacts our current lives. Although I never met him, he provided much input into our discussions. The class is structured with 2 quizzes a week that are usually easy as long as you read your textbook. He also gives extra credit in discussions.

Professor Tew was very active in discussions. He was clearly passionate and loved hearing students' opinions. He had plenty of extra credit opportunities, his textbook was very well written and interesting, and his quizzes were fairly straightforward.

Relatively easy, and Greg is a cool guy. Do the biweekly quizzes and the extra credit discussion boards. I will say that the "extra credit" aspect is not super true, as the margin for success by the quizzes alone is very thin. Also, you'll need to do at least 14 discussions to get any extra credit points, so don't wait until the end.
Easiest Class I've ever taken. He's political and doesn't really respect your opinion if you disagree with him so just suck it up and act like a leftist in the discussion.

Design appreciation is fully textbook quizzes and optional online discussions. It's two weekly 5 question quizzes each with one simple discussion question. Doing all the quizzes and discussions will get you an A. It was the easiest class I have taken and took me a max of 30 minutes to complete each week. Would reccommend.

Easiest A you'll ever get in your life. Two 5 question quizzes and two discussion boards per week. Total time per week at most 1.5 hours. Gotta get his textbook which is written in a weird way but not hard to follow, also make sure to post on the discussion boards since that will essentially secure a passing grade. Want an A? Take this class.
He is understanding and very easy going

This class is an easy A if you put in the work for it, and the readings and quizzes don't take longer than 40 minutes. You do have to buy his textbook in order to be in the class because that is where the quizzes are taken. He writes the textbook through his point of view, but I think it is very eye-opening, and that everyone should take this class

Easiest class at Virginia Tech. He assigns two reading chapters per week, each with a 5 question reading quiz and an optional Canvas discussion post for extra credit. The only way to do poorly in this class is to simply not put in the effort.

This class is based on Professor Tew's textbook, which provides interesting and thought-provoking inquiry into very relevant topics that affect us all. Those who complain about his opinions seem to miss the point: critical thinking. If he disagrees with a discussion post of yours, he'll respond. 10/10 class, and a very easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Not a very hard class, assigned 2 chapters weekly with 5 question quizzes at end. Discussion post are optional for more points, but very opinionated.

This guys ego is higher than ive ever seen before. he makes you buy his textbook where every fact is his opinion about political and social issues. I have never seen anything like this before and it disgusts me. I have no idea how this guy still has a job
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy class but the class is based around a textbook made of his opinions. I thought it was interesting but it was a class to make you think about topics, not so much to learn about new ones. Overall was a good class and great way to boost your GPA.

The class is very easy with just 2 chapters a week, 5 question quizzes, and a discussion post for bonus points. Read the book and watch the videos and you should do fine along with doing discussion posts for extra credit. He is very opinionated and does challenge your views but it does change your view on design. Great professor and easy class.

Professor Tew is terrible. He is very unforgiving and not understanding of any issues that come up, even legitimate health issues. Even if you're sick and have a university excused absence, getting make-ups is a huge challenge and are limited and he doesn't reopen quizzes or discussions. He is rude and cold - definitely not taking him again.

Gregory Tew's Design Appreciation class is one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Grades for the class comprise of only quizzes and if you complete the Discussion Questions then you get an easy A. My only issue with the class is that Mr. Tew is extremely opinionated. He is an extreme environmentalist who lets everyone know his opinion.

Professor Tew uses a quiz based reading grading system. 5 questions, 25 chapters. He also drops some of your grades at the end of the semester. If you do the work and participate in the discussions, you will have an easy A.

This is the easiest class you could possibly take. You have 2 assignments a week that shouldn't take you more than 30 min each. Super easy to get an A. Interesting content too. Take this class if you are looking for an easy class to add to your schedule.
Best pathways class at tech hands down. I loved the textbook and hearing his ideas, even if I did not always agree. Changed my world view about our built environment.
Great and insightful class. You have to read the textbook and participate in the optional discussions, but otherwise the class is an easy A.

Design Appreciation was a great choice. It's super easy. You have to read the textbook bc that's what the whole course is based off of. There are optional discussions to participate in, however if you don't, it'd be hard to get an A in. He does state his opinion a lot, but he gives you the opportunity to say what you believe and talk to peers.
Great professor I really enjoyed this class

Very easy and not bad at all. You read a short chapter and take a short quiz on the material and do a discussion post once (maybe twice a week). I took this asynchronously and there were no class meetings. He was very nice and opinionated (I agreed with all of his opinions and beliefs but some did not). Overall, great simple class and a great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes are 5 questions on the reading from the online textbook. Do the discussion board posts for extra credit. Read the syllabus, takes 8min and super helpful. Very easy class to get a good grade. Set reminders on your phone to remember when things are due. Just participate, it's literally not that hard.

This whole class is just reading a chapter, and taking the quiz that follows, but you can use the chapter to take this quiz so it's super easy, but he is very opinionated, so go in with and open mind!

prof is nice but very political. you may not agree with a lot of his view points. theres a few pages of reading (twice a week) and two quizzes each week. pretty easy and lots of opportunities for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awesome guy! Thought the class would be about art stuff, but it was about the design of the world and how we can improve our lives. Very interesting points and topics covered. Makes you think. Only 26 quizzes. No final, no tests. Lots of bonus points.

This is a pretty interesting class and it's incredibly easy. Just read the textbook and do the discussion posts -- it's time consuming but not very difficult. Beware, Greg is very opinionated and can get a bit annoying at times, but he offers up good information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I can tell this man cares about his job but this entire class was sort of Greg just encouraging us to live the most minimal lifestyles and be very liberal. I am a heavy moderate, so if you're like me, you probably won't be interested in this class but it's super easy. He gives a lot of feedback to discussion posts which is nice though.

Your entire grade is a quiz at the end of every chapter. That's it. Just read the textbook or use Ctrl+F to find the answers to the quiz questions. But, Greg is VERY opinionated. Be prepared to talk about climate change and biking in every chapter. Also, there are many opportunities for extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really good professor, gives extra credit opps and has easy lectures and quizzes.
I took his class online and it was easy and interesting. It requires maybe three hours of work a week and he encourages feedback and discussion

If you go to class and take the quiz after each lecture, you will get at least a B. There are 25 quizzes, 6 question multiple choice, that make up your grade. If you write your thoughts about each lecture in his notebook or do some discussion posts you will get significant extra credit. Lectures got repetitive, but easy if you need a gen ed.

Gregory Tew is a very opinionated man. All of his lectures are centered around his opinions and a few internet articles he found online. THIS CLASS IS NOT ABOUT DESIGN AT ALL. The majority of the class is focused on caring for the environment and changing our infrastructure to be more bike friendly. You've been warned.
This professor says some interesting things, however, none of it has anything to do with design. This professor teaches design appreciation as more of a history course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: ITDS1114 ended up being completely different from what I expected, but I loved it. Greg put together such interesting lectures that really made me think about the issues he presented and I felt like I took away so much from this class. I continue to research and discuss ideas presented in this class in other classes and everyday life.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Greg is an amazing teacher and is tough. You will get great feedback and a teacher who really cares about how you are and where you are in progress. If you get him for studio you won't regret it he pushes you to be the best and rise above to the top. He will give you his STRONG opinion on EVERYTHING! lol but he's great nonetheless I loved it.

You must go to class everyday and CANNOT be late whatsoever (even being one minute late will not be tolerated). He expects much peer critiquing and communication among the class. Talks a lot during the in class critique... Lots of work has to be done outside of class (so lots of studio time if you want an A).

I highly recommend this class. The material and the professor is interesting. there is no final, the only grades are having 6 comments in your sketchbook at the end of the semester and taking a 10 question online quiz after every class.  There is a lot of extra credit points you can receive to get an A, too.

Professor Tew's Design Appreciation class was excellent, highly recommend! His lectures are very well put together and relevant to society, and his topics are interesting. Go to class, do the homework and any extra credit, and make sure to write plenty of thoughts in the sketchbook. Great class

This was the Design Appreciation class, it was very well taught.  The final was optional, if you collected 'trading cards' passed out every class you wouldn't have to take the final. No text, but often would require reading an article for weekly quizzes.  Quizzes consisted of about 10 rather simple questions, only on 1 did I receive below a 80%.
great teacher

Easiest class I've ever taken. Just two "major" projects that took very little time to complete. The only thing that matters in the projects is functionality, not looks. Would take again any day. Great professor.

This professor was absolutely amazing. They obviously care for the subject, and the work is so incredibly easy. There are daily assignments, which make up most of your grade, but it's just 1 question that requires a 2-sentence-long answer. Then there are two big projects which are fairly easy, and you don't even have to present to the class.
Super understanding about grades, the class is designed for you to pass and do well.
Very supportive and understanding professor. The course is project based and overall just an easy introduction to college English.
Very caring professor who loves teaching. Never a dull moment in class, always exciting.

Great professor! Gives good feedback, and the assignments and course load are more than reasonable. Professor Johnson is very nice, but make sure to attend class and to start working on assignments well before the deadline, as they might take more time than you think.

Ms. Johnson is a great English professor, and I could say she is one my favorite professors on campus. There is no homework in the class besides the papers you have to submit, but she makes it so that you get those papers in on time, and she gives you a lot of time to get them finished. Couldn't ask for a better professor who cares about students.
A lot of freedom and space for improvement and reflection. Amazing professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson is a wonderful human being and you can really tell she cares so much about you improving your writing rather than the grade, as evident in the fact that she lets you redo any assignment until you have the grade (and the skills) you need. That is a lot of extra work for a teacher.

Ms. Johnson is one of the best teachers I've ever had. I'm not a fan of English classes, but she teaches her classes in a way that I enjoy and understand. She really cares about her students and truly shows that she teaches because she loves it.

Ms. Johnson is a great professor and person. She makes it very clear that she gets paid to grade, but she is there to teach, and she loves her job. Because of the small class size, you get to know your classmates. She fosters a discussion-based environment. Go to class, put some effort into your assignments, and you'll be fine.

Good person and teacher, pretty cool, grades well and gives feedback on papers, no ridiculously hard assignments, not textbook heavy (she gave us access to the few textbook articles we needed), we mainly talked about short passages in class and gave a few short presentations along with a few papers (not bad at all). Definitely take her 1105 class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Mrs. Johnson is an amazing professor. I had her for First-Year Writing and I actually liked going to class. The class itself had 20 students and it seemed more like a discussion than a lecture. There were 3 papers, an online project, and a final presentation, all were easy. If you put in any amount of effort you will do well.
Probably my favorite professor I've had at Tech. Gives great lectures with interesting content, and wants students to do well in his class.

Great professor, really interesting class too, he made everything super relevant to current events. Lots of reading for homework and specific quizzes in class randomly everyone did bad but so did I and I still ended up with an A. Exams are based on the lectures and slides, but just pay attention and participate in class and if you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Adjerid is the GOAT

Professor Adjerid made lectures very entertaining and fun to attend. Classes are mandatory as there are random pop quizzes on reading hw assignments. Pop quiz and exam material asked about specific details on readings/lectures. There is a group project as well that you present to the class on zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great professor! But the group project really was confusing, especially when the TA spent the whole class teaching us how to install the dependencies of R and eventually failed. I learned basically nothing from that project, and it feels like we spent too much time coordinating because a group of 12 is really inefficient.

Probably my favorite professor I had during my BIT cyber degree program at Virginia Tech! Makes class fun and actually gets you to think deeply about cybersecurity topics. My one gripe is the group project's instructions weren't very clear, but they did not grade it harshly at all so it didn't end up being a big issue.

Easy class if you put in work. Bi-weekly open-note reading quizzes. Mid-term and final (non-cumulative) not that bad. To study memorize slides(esp. bullet points) and exam review class material. Group project super easy. Doesn't take attendance but says he knows who comes and graded end of year. Lectures are pretty interesting. Doesn't respond emai
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Entertaining professor, makes lectures more fun. Expect final and midterm, essay, a few easy labs, pretty easy class presentation, and group project that isn't that bad if you get a good group. Group project should take you max 15 hours. Best way to study is to memorize the slides and pay attention to the exam reviews. Class not bad if studious

While Dr. Quinlan is nice and responds to emails in a timely manner, I almost always left class more confused than I was before. Honestly, I think attending the lectures negatively impacted my grade in this class and I should have just taken the class online because I learned how to do everything completely through the ALEKS homework.

Theyre very nice. Does overcomplicate things quite a bit. Some of their explanations are questionable and tend to make things more confusing than needed. Sometimes jumps to definitions that they havnt explained yet. Probably wouldnt take them for Calc 1. Very nice person though and open to giving extra help.

Fine if you can teach yourself half of the material. Make sure to go to office hours for an easy A. You can retake quizzes for up to 100% every time + they make it very easy to get 100s on anything that's not an exam. For exams, make sure you know + teach yourself a lot of the material. A lot of the times the professor overcomplicates the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I felt like she was teaching the class like everybody in there had taken it before. It felt like review but for me I had no precalculus experience and got left behind a lot. If you're taking this class as a retake and you have math experience, you'll be fine but if you're just starting precalculus, make sure you give her 100% of your attention.
Terrible teacher you would have better luck getting taught by a 4th grader.

I got a A on calculus in high school but didn't get high enough on the Alex to get into calc so I did this class which should have been easy but this professor cannot teach and was the worse grader ever unless you did everthing perfectly exsacly how they would do it your not getting full credit I once got the question right but got 0.5/5 on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Considerate, kind professor, CANNOT teach. Class time felt unhelpful because they didn't explain the math—just threw problems on the board. If you're great at teaching yourself math, this prof is fine. Fair grading and retakes. Lots of short quizzes and heavy ALEKS homework. Chill person, but bad at teaching.

This might be hands down the worse math teacher I have ever had the only thing they taught me was that they have a cat named Mingus other then that I taught myself every part of the class. There is physically no point in even going to class because you won't learn anything. If you get stuck with this professor please switch.

Spring of 2025 was their first time teaching 2534. 1 homework per week. 3 tests for the semester and I would say they were all graded fairly. The lectures were average; there is a good chunk of time during lectures to ask questions. 

I only got an -A because I did poorly on the 2nd test but that is on me for not doing well.
Solid professor. Tough grader. First test was simple next two are much harder. Go to all classes.

I got a low grade in the class, but that was completely on me. They do their best to give you partial credit back on written homework and exams. Very understanding and takes the time to explain concepts. Never graded anything harshly.

They are very nice but they CANNOT teach. Test 1 is super easy but after that it just goes downhill very fast, they take off so many points for every test. Practice tests were written by students and were not helpful at all.

Dr. Quinlan is nice, and that is about where the positives end. They take points off very easily on everything from homework to tests, and your grade will be greatly impacted by this very quickly. I rarely got questions fully right, they would always find something wrong with what I did, take a point off of every question, and an A became a B

Absolutely wonderful to work with and very prompt to respond to emails, and always willing to work with you to help you succeed. They had energetic lectures even in the morning hours, and it was always a fun part of my day to be there. Very good at explaining material, and made sure you knew what was on the tests. They made note-taking VERY easy.
Absolutely awful, never again

prof quinlan was honestly a really good teacher. this was their first time teaching calc II and i think they were able to explain concepts very well in class that helped a lot with homework. homework is usually 4 webassigns due once a week, very solid prof for a difficult class like calc II !
Solid professor, reasonable and understanding.

Prof Quinlan was a good professor for 1214. The ALEKS modules that you have to do every week were a lot more work than was needed for the class, but did make the tests easier. Tests were usually fairly short, with a mix of multiple choice and FRQs, but tests are made by the department, not Prof Quinlan

what others were saying is true. the group project is at the end of the semester and she grades so hard making your grade all of the sudden drop. very boring class and hard to understand her lectures.

Her lectures were so boring it made it hard for me to want to go to this class. A lot of what you do in class requires a single spaces page of reflection afterwards. Not to mention she's a tough grader. If you don't like group projects, I would not take this class. She assigned a group project with 4 submissions and a 30 minute presentation.

The lectures are not interactive and feel boring at times, but it is nice because I got a lot of work done in class. There are 6 quizzes that are pretty tough and a long group assignment that is done over the course of the semester, but no exams. She is a harder grader for the paper, but if you follow her exact comments then you should be ok.

Dr. Ju's lectures are very boring and reads from slides for 1.5+ hours. Additionally, her grading on one of the most important assignments (35% of grade) is very harsh and unreasonable. Overall one of the most boring classes I have EVER taken. Do not take this class.
He is definitely one of the best professors at VT and definitely cares about his students. Would definitely recommend.

My last semester at Tech, and this is my first ever C, and it's a C-. I think that's pretty telling. A 2000-level rhetoric class should not be this difficult. Kyupers is unsettling and extremely political too. He even did the Nazi salute 2 times on the first day of class. Grades = weekly reading quizzes and 3 tests. That's it. Don't take his class.

He's honestly a really nice guy, the exams are extremely difficult and you will have a quiz before class once a week (which are based off of a LONG reading he'll give you) Ive spent hours studying for his exams and have failed both. He reads his lectures off of a note sheet and does not post his slides nor his notes, he speaks fast.

the only grades are quizzes and exams (exams being worth 60% of your grade). This is just kinda dumb imo. the tests are extremely difficult and the quizzes are pretty hard even though they are open note. He needs to consider a few other assignments to balance things out for bad test takers (they deserve to pass too). He is also very set in his ways
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kuypers is nice, but he is set in his ways. He is very conservative politically and would pop off about mainstream news media being "unfair" towards conservative political figures. The final project is in a group, and he grades it very harshly. Overall, not the worst I could have had, but not great either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While his classes are a little tough he sets you up for success. His lectures are fun to listen to and he is clearly extremely knowledgable about what he teaches. He is easy to access outside of class and cares about his students. The bad reviews for him are not justified at all (at least in my experience) Attendance is required.

Kuypers media and politics class is extremely hard especially if you're a bad test taker. There is 4 assignments 2 tests, a paper, and presentation with a group. The tests come from the lecture and readings, if you don't study good luck. If this class isn't required take a different one or different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the harshest grader I've ever had as a professor.  Extremely inflexible with assignments and will give you a zero for turning in something even in extenuating circumstances.  Literally quoted the syllabus at me when I asked for an extension for a very serious reason.  Comm 1014 is supposed to be easy but he made it unnecessarily hard.
Bro this guy blows, trust me take Buddy he the boy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr Kuypers can be a bit frustrating due to his sometimes vague explanation of the assignments but I understand why he does it. Really nice guy and really does care about the course. I hate public speaking but if I had to take it again it would be with him
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Zero instruction given, yet still expects you to meet his very specific guidelines. No rubrics or written instructions given for any speech. His canvas page is just the syllabus, nothing else. There is no way to know what he is expecting, so leads to a lot of frustration.

Maybe the worst teacher Ive ever had in my life. He doesnt give any rubric and expects you to meet his standards anyway. Hes a somewhat a nice person but then again didnt remember my name in an 18 person class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Nice guy and very caring. Makes you work hard, but then well deserved. Good looking for an older guy, which makes it more enjoyable to come to class
Loves this stuff and it shows.

Obviously knows what he is talking about and tries to help those that are willing and wanting. If you want to learn something new and try to challenge yourself, take a class. As long as you try.. with as much effort as you deem necessary.. you will get an A. Great guy, pretty funny, easy to come to class hung over and still learn a lot.

The class is a bit tough, but as long as you come to class, the tests come straight from the notes (nearly verbatim). Kuypers is clear and very helpful, though I'm sure his sarcastic sense of humor doesn't sit well with some people. Honestly one of the best classes I've taken in Comm so far.

This is one of those classes where you have to make sure you do not miss any days. Kuypers is very nice, but often vague on assignment instructions. There is A LOT of outside reading, but as long as you skim a few of them you'll be fine because they aren't really on the test. (All you need for that is notes) Overall, this class is tough but helpful

Lectures are full of heavy and often ambiguous material which he meanders through, leaving you to scratch your head about what to write down. Out of class reading often requires you to wade through multiple page essays on abstract and somewhat useless theories from ivy league professors. Tests are a cumulation of tricky syntax and complex subjects

I'm a CS major so I figured I would get a cle credit out of the way. Now I'm minoring in Comm. you do have to go to class and you do need to study but studying for me consisted of telling my friends what I had learned because it was actually useful! The test were in essay format which can be good or bad depending on how much you know.

TERRIBLE, even at the graduate level. I'm an excellent, grade-A student who is hard-working and doesn't mind a tough class. This wasn't only impossibly tough, it was incomprehensible and ridiculous. Kuypers was VERY VERY rude and arrogant.
Material is very thick for an undergrad class. His lectures are very vague and hard to follow. His tests are made to confuse.
Hard to understand. Material is uninteresting and there is no attempt to change that. He is arrogant and if you do not agree with what he believes then you are in trouble.

SAVE UR SELF from waking up w cold sweats at night abt calculus and TAKE this class ONLINE. Prof is a nice person. However, lectures were confusing and ta's/ prof left me more confused when asking questions. Hw and hw quizzes don't help with material for exams. I get physically ill in a 50ft radius of the building. Had to teach myself entire course

Genuinely the worst math teacher I have ever had. She does not teach material, instead explains why something works, but never actually going over the how. I have not learned anything from her, having to teach myself the material. And asking her questions just leaves you more confused. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.
She is very thorough when explaining problems. The homework and quizzes have several attempts and the tests are very short and just like any practice material.

A lot of assignments. if you do good on the assignments though you have enough of a cushion to pass the class. Her grading is very stressful she takes long and isn't transparent with you final grade number amount in the class. she just posts ur current grade letter.

Overall a great professor. She cares about her students and will take as much time as you need If you have a question. She likes when people participate. She is funny and has a very engaging personality. Lot of homework but it is helpful if you decide to skip class. All quizzes are online. Tests are difficult but if you study you'll be fine.

There's a lot of homework, but it sets you up really well for the tests.  She is very willing to help you and does not judge based on what level of understanding you are on, and she understands we are students going through things. The only "bad" thing I have to say is that she canceled her office hours frequently, but she did reschedule.

Amazing instructor, just a general ray of sunshine to be around and to be taught by. She was very insightful and helpful, and encouraging with students, making sure we all felt comfortable with the material and content. She also was open to feedback and our criticism. I truly believe she had the best interest of us (the students).

Amazing lecturer. Really good at describing content. A LOT of homework compared to other classes. Very strict when grading written homework, even if you got it correct. But there is extra credit, she's very forgiving if you talk to her. Just make sure you know how to do the homework.

She is awesome! :) She offers extra credit as your first assignment, two ways to grade your final grades (she takes the higher grade), super sweet and funny, lots of homework, attendance not mandatory but dont skip- you won't pass, go to math tutoring and study past homework to pass tests.
Awesome professor.

As someone who has always struggled with math, I can say with full confidence that Dr Thompson is the best professor I've ever had. She's amazing at explaining everything and is super approachable and easy to get in touch with. Definitely go to her office hours as you'll get lots of one on one attention. She answers all questions and is so nice

Amazing math professor. She does a super great job of explaining things in-depth and giving clear examples. None of the precalc concepts are particularly challenging but she's super easy to get in touch with if you need help. The class is very test heavy and there is a lot of homework but its honestly super great preparation for the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very kind and easy to understand lectures. I found the class rather difficult but she holds lots of helpful office hours. There is one written homework, one online homework, a module, and a quiz due every week. Best way to study for test is to review the online homework and quizzes until you feel confident. If you study hard, you should be fine.

Yes, there are a good number of assignments each week, but she provides multiple resources for students outside of class and is super caring. If you habitually attend her office hours, she will make sure to get to know you and your learning style. Overall, I enjoyed her.

I loved this class! She explained everything in a very easy to understand way, helping me to understand concepts that I didn't in high school math. There is a weekly module, homework, and quiz, but no week took me more than about 2-4 hours combined. The exam question pool is the same as homework and quiz questions, so they were easy to study for!
Learned a lot in this class. Definitely not an easy one. Highly recommend it.

Jessica Thompson is an extremely nice professor and I definitely would reccomend her to anyone wanting to take PreCalc. The class is hard at first and the work load takes a little while to get used to but if you space it out throughout the week it is not too bad. If you go to office hours and pay attention in class she is great! P.S. I suck at math

I loved her. She is great at explaining concepts clearly and making sure that students understand them. I went to her because there was a mistake with my grade and she was really understanding and changed it immediately. She is great at getting the ideas across and also teaching certain concepts in multiple ways to cater to many learning types.
She was a very nice teacher who actually cares what she was talking about and was very helpful. The material was hard and a lot of homework but if I was better at math I would give a 5/5

She breaks down the math questions to understand it better, but the material is sometimes a little difficult. She hols lots of office hours and is a nice teacher. She is open to suggestions if questions don't feel fair. There is homework, module, and a quiz through ALEKS due basically every week.

Mrs.Thompson was great! Really clear lectures and was very insistent on group work. The homework policy is kind of wack but honestly, she was a really nice person so can't hold it against her. Has sooo many office hours available and loves to talk to her students. Please give her a try she's amazing!
She grades very strictly. Even if you turn in your homework late, she still gives you a zero and fails you. She doesn't curve the grades.

Math emporium is a mistake unless you are ready to teach yourself hard concepts with limited resources. Dedicate lots of time every week to teaching this to yourself, do practice problems over and over, GO TO TUTORING, and if you can, work ahead. At home quiz once a week, for two weeks, followed by a test over those lessons, and repeat.

First of all, you are in the math emporium which is the first mistake. Second, she doesn't teach you instead has it where you have to read the math empourium textbook so it's a teach yourself kind of class or go to the math tutors there who have zero clue what to do. You HAVE to go to the math emporium to take your quizzes and test.

this class isn't hard if you spend a few hours a week on the practice problems. however, thompson was no help. she never responded to emails and cancelled office hours pretty much every week. the only time i saw her was during her "orientation" and she was kinda rude. textbook was confusing and unclear. try to form a study group if you can.

Never saw her once. don't even know what she looks like. I don't know if it's her choice though, it was an emporium class that I ended up withdrawing from because I couldn't do it. The online textbook is horrible and unclear, and you have to resort to tutors that work at the emporium. avoid the emporium at all costs.

I never once saw my professor throughout the entire semester. Her one job is to hold office hours and she cancels almost every week. Math classes should never be self taught much less with absolutely no guidance from any type of professor. She gave us an orientation video then sent us on our way and I never saw her again. Terrible.

Dr. Jones is a great guy with awesome lectures. He may come off as a bit entitled at times, but he honestly is just holding his students to a higher level of accountability than most. His classes are hard, but guys these are weed out classes, come on. He is significantly better than most teachers in these classes. Love his math explanations.
rude acts like he's better than everyone and grades like he wants to give you a bad grade. Grading feedback is minimal and is belligerent to student feedback
he's scary
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Enjoyed professor Jones' class. When questions were asked, he made sure that whoever asked it understood his answer. Great teacher, and conversational outside of class. Genuinely cared about his students and learned everyone's name. Good guy.
The worst professor I've ever had in my entire life. Does not care abt his students, super rude, will not help you. I genuinely stopped looking both ways when crossing the street to his class.
Poor teacher

Honestly, not that bad of a guy, just very strict on the Honor Code. You cannot cheat 1524, and you do have to put in the work; however, it can be done. Heavy on reading and homework. If you have to take 1524, take it over the summer and go to all of your TA's Office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mr. Jones does not care about the students at all. He is not understanding and does not try to help you succeed in his class. I would avoid his classes at all cost.

This guy does not care about his students, especially if you're a male. Extremely difficult to make up missed work, as he will not take any excuse for absence on important days. Also not very helpful when asked questions, hostile environment.
HECK NAHHH DONT TAKE HIM HES SO MEAN
Lectures were useless considering he sped through them. He was rude to me when I asked him to fix my grade that he messed up. He's just an overall strict person and unnecessarily rude.

He's actually a mean, strict, terrible teacher, every time I walked to class I wish I got hit by a car so I wouldn't have to go. I emailed him multiple times about HIM MESSING UP MY GRADING and he was so rude to me and honestly I'd rather drop out of college than take him again, but other than that great class!

He's a stern one! Not a bad guy but I found the lectures to be a waste of time.

Idk if any 1524 Prof is any good, but, my advice would be:

Take course -> Skip Lecture -> Pay VT Math Tutor ~$20 for his videos -> Breeze through the class.

VT Math Tutor is the best, trust me lol

I can also help if needed :) @jutu on insta

If you are not good at math, do not take this course. I went to most lectures, most recitations, and I still struggled with this course. It is very fast paced and you pretty much have to teach yourself or get a tutor. He also shows no compassion for missing assignments/exams for situations that are completely out of your control.

If you're not religious, pick a religion and start praying. The lectures were extremely important to understand the material, but the lectures were so fast-paced and would only provide one explanation and expect you to understand the concept. All of the work is online and takes quite some time, but exams are only a few questions and in person.
He give you the basic information during lectures but not everything. I thought it was easier and I did better on exams when I just taught it myself.

PJ is a good person, but this class has so much homework and no exam prep. He will not help you during class and his office hours are for 10 minutes outside lecture hall. He doesn't care if you have family matters he will give you a 0 no matter what if you miss an exam, or HW. I only took pre calc and this class was extremely difficult, use tutors.

He was flexible to schedule for office hours, but inside of office hours when he responds to your questions by saying "idk is that how you do it" or "is that correct" in a condescending way is not a great way to support your students. Inside of class he literally says that he does not care about you as an individual and you have to figure it out.
If you go to office hours and put in a good amount of effort, then you can get a good grade. Jones explains things well and is relatively chill. Just don't expect extension for any reason.

Despite the negative reviews, PJ is a really good professor and if you have never taken calculus before I definitely recommend taking his section. He posts an outline in Canvas for each unit so all you have to do is copy down the work for the problems making it much easier to pay attention to the slides. Overall very kind and caring professor!

Jones is a great professor! He is extremely prepared and provides you with all the resources you will need to be successful in the class. There are a lot of homework assignments and sometimes they can be difficult however the test questions are much simpler. Overall great professor and really cares about the well being of his students!

If you've never taken calculus, this is not the professor for you. Too fast during lectures while showcasing a power point (PowerPoint is NOT posted on Canvas). My laptop wouldn't download the mandatory software and his response was that I'd need to work some things out, and solve the problem. Not expecting a handhold, but be a little nicer please.

I ended with a 99% only because I had taken AP calc in HS and did well on the AP exam. PJ is horrible at lecturing and is uncaring. He made fun of questions which people feel horrible. He also doesn't teach, he just presses next on the clicker and the answer shows up. I had to tutor my friend who took his class because he was so bad at teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Honestly a very straightforward professor. Great at teaching the course as well. If you can just simply pay attention and study you will excel in this class. Homework's and practice tests are far harder than the actual exams. There is a lot of homework but other then that the class is not hard and the professor is great.

Professor Jones is actually a very nice person. He has very strict grading rules (does not accept late work or give extensions) but he makes that very clear from the first day of class. There is a fair bit of homework but it is not very difficult and you have plenty of time to complete the homework after he covers the materials. Very test heavy!

Really great professor. Definitely tough and sticks to his guns, you will not be getting an extension on anything. That being said the class is overall pretty easy. Plenty of resources are provided to make sure you do well on exams. Good amount of homework but it's quick and easy based on the chapters that were just taught

Taking calc in HS is important to be successful in Professor Jones' class. He works at a fast pace and if you don't have background knowledge of the topic you may struggle. Tests are not very hard and if you pay attention in class, he hints heavily what questions will be on it. No extensions or extra credit will ever be given.

Not mean, just really straightforward. Gives extra credit for going to recitation sessions. Class is fast paced. A lot of people think he's mean because of his policies (no makeups or extensions), but with 200+ students he really doesn't have a choice. Just put in effort and you can pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just straight up terrible, can never ask for feedback. get ready for a long semester.
worst math teacher I have ever had, does not care about any students. Is extremely rude about feedback and emails. Can't believer he still works at tech.

the class itself isn't hard if you understand basic calculus. he isn't very nice or understanding to say the least and if you have a question he thinks is dumb he'll make it known. sometimes his powerpoints have the wrong answer  and makes easy concepts confusing for no reason
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have to get a tutor to pass then he isn't a good teacher, period. I've attended every single class but there's literally no point. He is not good at lecturing. I should've switched professors like everyone else. I wouldn't say he was mean, but he doesn't care if you pass or not. He only laughed at someone's question one time.

I'm surprised at the poor reviews. It's true he doesn't excuse mistakes or extensions. But he's not mean, just straightforward. He gives exam motivation, says our grades don't define us, etc. I've NEVER been good at math, but it's not that hard if you do your work, notes, and practice. He's literally fine, but maybe I'm just used to bad teachers.
Just terrible. shouldn't be even teaching.
So much could be done better with Paul jones and the business calc course. Also not very understanding or lenient toward simple misunderstandings. Not the best professor for business calc.
Take this class through math emporium. Professor Jones is not understanding nor lenient, his tests are very challenging as well.
Paul Jones was a terrible professor who does not care about his students. If you have to take this class take it with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He knew the material very well. His lectures moved very quickly so if you don't understand, you feel behind after one class. I had to use the McBride tutoring lab to actually learn the material. If you go to office hours he will explain things. He's a nice guy and I ended up getting to know him outside of class. A good man.
Doesnt care about students, not flexible at all.
He teaches through lectures and goes too fast sometimes but will stop and answer questions. He is not very empathetic but he will help you if you ask politely.

1524 is easy as long as you try. I skipped most of the lectures and got a B plus. As long as you go to office hours and don't ask stupid questions, you will not be laughed at like others here said. Also, don't email him; ask questions in person for a better response. Overall, he is a decent teacher. Definitely not as bad as people here say.
Horrible teacher, multiple mistakes, lacks good explanation
terrible professor, not understanding at all, and tests are very difficult. His lectures do not help at all so you are basically teaching yourself.

Professor Jones did not teach. He would present slideshows with pre-worked out problems and there were usually errors in these slideshows. He didn't provide feedback on our work. I am GOOD at math and knew most of the material before this class, but his "teaching" made me confused. About half the class dropped or withdrew.

Mr. Jones is an awful professor. He doesn't write out his notes while he shows problems. He has them all typed out on slides that are usually wrong. His slides skip over important steps. He's not very helpful when you ask questions either because he tells you "You should already know this." and says he can't help you with anything further.

Professor Jones presents all topics in an organized manner. If you attend all of the lectures this class is easy to follow along with. He thoroughly explains each topic and takes questions after doing examples.

Professor Jones was a good teacher who taught information that was relevant to all exams. There were times when his PowerPoints contained mistakes but they were not detrimental to my learning. Overall a good teacher.
If you attend the lectures and pay attention, you'll pass the class.
does not teach.

Attendance isn't mandatory, there's 3 tests/exams (12 ish questions each) which are 45% of your grade. Weekly written homework is 15% and so is the weekly online homework, chapter quizzes (taken at home) are 5%, and the final exam is 20% (20 ish questions.) Calculus is calculus but it's not terribly hard, TA's and professor aren't much help.
Go to class, go to office hours, be honest. Even if being honest means admitting something is your fault.
Not only is he a not good teach but he is not a great human either. He laughs at students when they get answers wrong and o
moves to fast

Paul Jones is actually terrible. My peers and I agree that not only are his teaching methods subpar, he also doesn't like helping students. He openly admitted to not reading student emails if they were "too long" and we have seen him laugh at students when they ask him a question instead of answering it. Please do not sign up with him.

Mr. Jones is the best math teacher I've had my whole life. He's patient in class and answers questions kindly. Whenever I've struggled with a concept he has easily shown me different methods to solve the problem. You can also regain credit on written assignments if you review with him during office hours! He genuinely cares about his students 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An easy A if you pay attention in class. He has quizzes in class which are graded but very easy. Gives the best feedback to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great Calc I professor with high expectations for his students. I felt prepared for all of the exams and he always gave feedback on assignments/exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was actually such a good teacher, his lectures were amazing. He gave you everything you needed to succeed. Before every test you also get a few practice tests and great reviews. My friends always came to me for help because I could always answer their questions and all I did was pay attention in class and do the homework.

I would say he is one of the best teachers at Virginia tech. He understands his students and is there when you need. If he knows his test is on a day that a lot of other exams are on, he will move it. He is an amazing teacher and makes everything easy to understand. I would recommend taking him for any accounting class you can.

Prof. Shortt is everyone's GOAT. I took 3115 over the summer which was kind of intense, but he went out of his way to set up extra office hours at odd times to work with my busy schedule. I had lots of questions, but he never made me feel bad for asking them, and explains everything so clearly.

Professor Shortt is the best accounting professor I've ever had. He makes the material clear and understandable and is very transparent about what will be on exams. The cheat sheet policy was a huge help. If you can take his class, do it—you won't regret it.
Very clear in explaining. It'll be your go-to professor for accounting courses!

I took ACIS 3115 with Professor Shortt (no option to rate him under that), which was the best decision I have ever made. Great guy, awesome teacher. He is the only reason why I did not struggle in a "weed-out" class. If you do not take him, I do not know what you are thinking.
Hard class, but Mr. Shortt is the goat and makes it doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3115 - actually an evil class tbh, so difficult, but prof shortt is the best prof i've had so far at tech! cares so much and WANTS you to succeed. will def be taking another class with him!

I enjoyed taking his class. He is funny and gives you the information as plain and simple as possible! There is a group project, but it was real light and made sure that it wouldn't stress anyone out. One of my favorite professors here at Virginia Tech for sure!

Best teacher at Virginia Tech. I don't understand why anyone would rate him below 5 stars. He's so caring and compassionate and never puts too much pressure on the student. Class content is not bad at all, mostly just memorizing some slides. He basically tells you what's gonna be on the exams. This is my second time taking him (first was ACIS3504)
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Shortt is a good professor who teaches well and is understanding and caring. Attendance is taken every class, tests are proctored and during class time. ACIS 3504 was easy, mostly vocab and concepts.

Prof. Shortt is AMAZING. He is very passionate about what he is teaching and always made the lectures interesting. Accounting is not easy but he made the class doable by providing many practice problems and being accessible outside of class.
Top 3 professor I have ever had. He cares so much and cracks jokes during his lectures to keep them somewhat interesting. Accounting is not fun, but he makes it better.

Professor Shortt is OUTSTANDING !!! Best professor I've by far ever had and not only is he an amazing teacher but an amazing person. He goes out of his way to provide you with more than enough resources for the exams and even goes over them in class. He also provides homework help videos and is also so kind and patient about helping his students.

Professor Shortt is such a great professor and nice guy! His lecture slides really helped me prepare for exams. Accounting is hard for me so it is necessary for me to have the right study tools. The practice exams he posts prepare you more than enough for the exams. I would 100% recommend taking his class.
Best professor at Virginia Tech. Actually cares about the content and students and tries really hard to make it a meaningful class.
Best Professor I've ever had

Take his class! Hands down the best professor I've had at VT, and after retaking this class his flexibility and direction made all the difference. If you get the Quickbooks done asap, attend or watch his lecture recordings, and speak with him about any issues in the class and you will 100% pass. 10/10!

10/10. He gives amazing lectures, knows the information by heart, gives really good real life examples or alternative helpful ways to think of concepts, and he is overall the kindest person. Test were only on 4 chapters each, and he dedicates a day to review in class with jeopardy and other material.

Professor Shortt is the nicest teacher you will ever have. He really does care to help you learn and succeed. He leaves every chapter with its notes and a video for each module of him explaining and the in class problems as well (they are pretty short videos). Highly recommend taking him for any of the ACIS classes.

I'd gatekeep the professor and his classes but he deserves to be rated as the best instructor at Tech. His classes are extremely helpful and interesting, and he's willing to help with anything you need. Some exams are a little bit harder than the others but aren't impossible, and in most cases you'll easily be able to get over a B+ on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Shortt is one of the most caring instructors in Pamplin. His class is useful, relevant, and engaging. However, seeing as the material feels quite easy, he tends to grade more harshly than necessary. He thinks a B is a grade to be ecstatic over. He gave amazing feedback on my project, but I still got an 85. Very difficult to get an A

The absolute best accounting professor I've had at VT. He is super caring and loves his job. Class has three exams(not cumulative) and connect homework. Group project is really interesting and will take you max 15-20 hours. Not a bad class at all and you get to learn technologies that are used in present day. 11/10

One of the best professors I've ever had. He really cares about his students, and if you listen (show up to class!!) and take okay notes you'll have no trouble. He really listens to his students, so if he's going too fast or something he has no problem going over a concept again.
He is so so sweet! Very willing to work with students and genuinely just wants students to understand the material. My favorite class this semester

Professor Shortt is a really great guy. The class requires you to put in a lot of work but it isn't crazy hard. Exams are almost just like in-class problems. There's homework due every week that takes 1-2 hours. Exams are mostly free response which helps your grade a lot. There are videos of the lectures and the in-class problems on canvas.

Because 3504 is a fairly easy class, its hard to make the lectures interesting, but he is really good at keeping it as engaging as possible. He cares about the students and genuinely wants everyone to do well, so he doesn't give trick questions on his tests. If you pay attention in class and do a little studying, you'll probably be fine

It is safe to say that Dr. Wilson "sees the matrix" -- he has a very clear understanding of the content he is teaching, and how it connects to bigger picture concepts. His weekly quizzes are slightly difficult at first, but overall very helpful in preparing for the tests. In office hours, you work through the problems and he'll help as you go.

Professor Wilson was one of my favorite professors. His lectures are interactive in the way that doesn't feel pressurizing but also makes you pay attention and really learn the material. This was probably my easiest class because of how well he teaches it. I was  looking at other classes he teaches just so I could take him again!
Great Professor! Highly recommend, the lectures make sure you understand the material. One of my fav profs I've had.

his tests are almost exactly like the notes he provides, and gives soooo much extra credit. such a kind guy and was always willing to help. especially grateful for this considering the class is 6 credits. would 110% take a class with him again.
His lectures are saturated with content that is not too difficult, and the exams come out relatively easily.

Dr. Wilson is an excellent professor in the CMDA department! His lectures are very good and I learned a lot in his course. His office hours are great and he really wants to help you learn the material and understand what is going on. The class covers some interesting topics and he makes the course relevant to current advancements in the tech world.

he is absolutely such an amazing professor. he really cares about his students and is always willing to help. I recommend taking advantage of his office hours because it's more beneficial and he'll always ensure you understand what's going on in his classes, especially this one. I couldn't have asked for a better professor.

Lectures are pretty fast-paced, but he's always willing to slow down. This is an award-winning professor, students only have good things to say about him. I've taken three of his classes. You want him as your professor!!

Attendance is not taken but there are classwork assignments almost every class. His lectures can be boring, but the homework assignments are super similar to the lectures, and his tests are similar to the classwork and homework. He is very accessible outside of class and always wants to help, don't be afraid to ask him for anything.

Dr. Wilson is very laid back and personable in class. He makes sure to get to know people's names and that they're doing alright in the class. The content of his lectures are very interesting as well, and he explains them with easy to understand analogies. The homework in this class is difficult at times but usually comes from what we did in class.
The class itself is kinda difficult, but manageable. Wilson is a very good instructor, and sets up his class in a way that makes it pretty easy to learn.

Dr. Wilson teaches the differential equations part of this class. The material is pretty easy to follow and it's not too difficult to follow. There are in-class assignments (which are easy cause you do them after lecture), HWs, and 2 tests in the class. Not an overly diffcult class and the tests are modeled after the HWs which was great.

Absolutely fantastic professor!! Have taken him three times and want to take more classes from him. He moves pretty quickly during class but often asks if it makes sense and if he needs to slow down. Very reachable over email and very helpful in office hours. Show up to class, take notes, reach out if you need help and you'll be fine.

Best instructor I've had at tech by far. Hes a really fun proffesor and lectures in a manner that is easy to follow and understand. Tests aren't too bad and solely based on notes and homework. There is quite a bit of homework but it's just based on the examples from notes.

Great professor, teaches the multi section of CMDA2005 pretty well and the HWs are similar to what you do in class. There's sometimes a small assignment you do at the end of that class which will be used as a grade (which boosts your grade as long as you make an effort into it) and also sometimes has a few of the exact problems from the HW
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Willing to work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor for the Calc 3 section of the class: laid back and chill professor. I would have gotten an A if the Calc section was its own class. It is not super hard: there is HW almost every week, start on them asap. The tests will be doable and not a surprise if you do the homework. He is a very lenient when grading the test.

Dr. Wilson is an excellent professor. He is in charge of the math section of the course. He will make the lectures clear as crystal for given assignments. For exams, he prepares extra practice sets and will be there for any questions. Just go to his office hours, it'll make it worth the grade you strive for.

Not a bad lecturer, but don't think is a reasonable professor. Been sick that I cannot attend classes and do assignments, and asked for accommodation, but got rejected and got a penalty for being sick. Unreasonably tough on grades. Too much work. Please take an alternative option if you have one.

Great option for linear algebra! Explains topics very clearly, accessible for office hours, and willing to help students. Tests can be tough with some conceptual questions, but you will really understand the material with Dr. Wilson.

Jason is the coolest dude, he's pretty nice about turning in a homework assignment in late if you ask before hand (Just make sure you do the homeworks!). The proofs in the class are not something you need to study a lot. Tests are mainly covered based on homeworks so study those the most. Pay attention if you go to class because it goes fast.

Professor Wilson is responsible for the math of the CMDA 2005 Class. He does a great job of teaching the material at a fair pace and frequently interacts back and forth with the class while going through problems to make sure you understand them. He is very approachable personality. Tests are straightforward and easy if you study. Great teacher.
he's the best

For someone who didn't graduate on time I don't understand why she grades super harsh. 1015 she is fine and then in 1016 it's like she just forgets how she graded the previous semester. Speeches and Essay always average in 60's or 70's. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR.

Insane amount of work for a freshman communications class. No one in the class in a communications major and is taking the class because they have to. Super passive aggressive, harsh grader and genuinely takes COMM 1016 too seriously.

She is a very tough professor to rate I feel cause in 1015 she is good but 1016 she gets so much harder and grades very harshly. She is kind but is definitely a very tough professor and probably the hardest for communication skills.

Please do not take this professor. You will have to do three times the amount of work that other students have to do in the same class. The amount of homework that she requires is more than almost any class you can take your freshman year. Take a different professor. She is also very passive aggressive, and makes the class ask questions.

Katie is a good professor but compared to other professors she has a lot more assignments and readings. There is media of the week, which is really easy and general participation in the class is required to get a good grade. Lots of extra credit opportunities so take advantage of those. Overall, I would take her class again and would recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Katie was pretty strict on grading and would call out on students who weren't paying attention or on their phone. Very passive aggressive. Any assignment involving APA format, she will find a way to still take points off. The good reviews are from COMM1015, but for 1016 it is another story. This class was the bane of my existence.

She was fine, but was just pretty passive aggressive. We had useful speeches that were great preparation for COMM classes you will have in the future, but she wasn't my favorite teach I have had. If I could choose again, I would take a chance on a different teacher.

Take any other teacher for this class. She made it way way too hard and it turned out to be my most time consuming class out of all of them and it should've been my easiest one. She acts like it's a senior level course when it should be an intro course and I heard all of the other comm teachers grade much much easier.This class kept me up at night.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very tough grader, harder requirements for assignments compared to other professors teaching the same class, would not take again.
Just don't, trust. She will move heaven and earth to make your life miserable. Doesn't excuse assignments or give extensions. JUST NO
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Moving on, like I said, she is fine in COMM1015 but remember that you have to have the same prof in COMM1016, and it seems like she forgets that this is a pathway class for freshmen. For participation if you fall asleep in class once, that goes into you participation grace for the week. you can try to explain but she jsut doesn't care bro.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: [[[ First, if you are coming to Virginia Tech, do NOT choose KATIE THOMAS. you may see that there are some 5-star reviews on this page, but that is from COMM15, which you take in the fall. something that they don't tell students at first is that you are forced to have the same professor in the spring class. I'll explain more in another comment ]]]
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I would recommend any other professor for this course. The grading scale and expectations were never consistent. The average on almost all speeches were in the 60s or 70s. There was minimal mutual respect to her students. The days she was nice, she was really nice, but the other 70 percent of the time she was extremely passive aggressive. Good luck

You can tell how you'll be treated the moment you walk in. She takes her anger out on everyone and is extremely rude. She acts like this class is the most important, yet I've learned nothing because of her attitude. She replies to emails fast, but they're passive-aggressive and unhelpful. Other professors are much kinder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She was nice, 40% of the time. She is a super tough grader on speeches and papers and is not always so clear when explaining assignments. She makes assignments much more difficult than they have to be. In 1016, you'll have the longest project ever and have a speech almost every week. Just painful.

Throughout the semester, she was an uptight grader, an unavailable teacher, and just rude to her students. It's impossible to ask her a question without being made to feel like an idiot. Whether she gives an actual answer or not, she never fails to be condescending and to make a student feel bad for asking. Choose a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I feel strongly that this teacher makes this class much harder than it needs to be. She doesn't respect her students or allow any grace. She also has a confusing grading system, so many assignments are graded differently. Would not recommend taking this course because other professors teach the same information without setting you up for failure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Katie is a good professor but she has very high standards when it comes to grading papers and speeches. She is helpful when you email her and edits your papers occasionally. There are other professors for this same class who I have heard are much more relaxed about the same assignments with much less work.

Absolutely awful professor. I chose her because she had good reviews on this website, but those were proved wrong very quickly. She teaches a pathway class like it is an aerospace engineering class and it the toughest grade I have had in my entire life. She is 50/50 in her moods: 50% nice and calm and 50% the devil.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Too many unnecessary headaches with this professor. A decent amount of work, attendance is not only mandatory but you will automatically be failed if you miss ~5 classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Katie is so sweet and understanding. You get 3 free unexcused absences and she excuses most other absences as long as you email her and is also super willing to give extensions when necessary. Most assignments are pretty simple and she gives good advice and information for bigger assignments like essays and public speaking assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Katie was amazing. One of the only teachers at Tech where I apply almost all of what I learned to my future work. Quizzes are open book so just participate in the lectures. Easy group work too. She made what should've been a difficult class way easier. Take her class.
By far the best Comm Skills professor. Take Katie's class.

Katie was an incredible professor!! For ANYONE taking Comm Skills there is no one else I would recommend but her. She allows you to submit papers to her ahead of their due date to be edited and is very easy to get in contact with outside of class. Study for quizzes/tests because some of them are tricky!
Great professor, I watch some guy eat 8 swiss rolls
Great guy! Super enthusiastic and energetic. He is readily willing to explain material and provide additional assistance.
you can tell he loves econ, makes the class so much more fun

As long as your go to class and take notes you will do well in his class. He's a super funny dude who's very passionate about economics. His tests are fairly easy as long as you pay proper attention in his class and review your notes a few times.

The class is about very basic economic topics. If you come to class you will do well on the tests. You're really only graded on the tests and then some homework assignments. He's a very engaging professor to listen to.

reviews.comment: good, wish he posted the lectures online but thats my only compliant. funny guy

Kurt is a great teacher; his lectures are engaging and fun. As long as you study the basics of economics, you should be able to pass this class with ease. Not math-heavy, but requires a basic understanding. Would take this class and professor again, 10/10.

He is sometimes not prepared for class, and he doesn't use slides or any sort of presentation, but he cares a lot about students and is funny and engaging. Even though attendance is not graded he says random stuff in class that will be a question on the test.
Kurt Stephenson the Nicaraguan now living in Villecheneve, France is a known child abuser

Kurt is super awesome, and very passionate about what he teaches. His class is only hard if you don't show up to lectures and he does a really good job at engaging the class in difficult topics. I would highly recommend taking a course with him.

He's a really nice guy and is passionate with his students. I didn't like his teaching style, there were no lecture slides which made it hard to study for exams. The exams were difficult but you were allowed to bring a notecard so fill it up. Overall he's good but his teaching style isn't for everyone.

It's a relatively easy class, with the exception being the tests. His tests can be a lot but he'll allow you to bring in a notecard with whatever you want written on it. This class is easy to forget which was my downfall so make sure you keep up with his lectures. Biggest issue is he doesn't have lecture slides so be sure to pay attention in class.

His teaching style did not work for me at all. He just lectures and the notes provided are not very useful. His handwriting is barely legible. I spent a lot of my time teaching myself the material. His test are hard even if you study a lot. They were all application based. I highly recommend doing the practice problems he provides.

Great guy who care about his subject- but his teaching style absolutely did not work for me. He'd spend the whole class talking about one example among other things and I struggled to pay attention. The problem sets help a lot, and I ended up just teaching myself the material through that and the online textbook. Tests aren't easy, but reasonable

He's awesome! I was mad to have to take an econ class for my major but after a lecture or two I was really glad to be there. He's animated and passionate about what he's teaching, also exceptionally good at getting the class to participate. Tests were challenging but not too bad, just go to the review sessions. Homework is a grade booster.
Kurt tried to be excited about teaching his class; however, I thought that he was unorganized. This made it difficult for me to learn, and I definitely think there are better econ professors.

Professor Stephenson is great. Just come to lecture and pay attention and you'll be fine. Hes really good at using examples and making sure you really understand what he is talking about. Hes really funny and has great stories. I highly recommend his class.
Very fun and interesting. Makes the class enjoyable and applicable to life.

Kurt tries to learn everyone's names, uses great examples (snack cakes!), includes in-class activities, asks the class for opinions, explains the material really well and will teach you a lot. He's hilarious. I was afraid that this class would be boring, but I loved it!
Great teacher! Uses helpful examples that apply to the real world. Makes the topics easy to understand. Tests are not that hard.
Really cool class.  Projects were real life situations and interesting.
By far the best professor I had my first semester at VT. Hes hilarious and keeps the material interesting. I highly recommend coming to class. I really did enjoy his lectures and learned A LOT.

Fantastic teacher; the material's not difficult as long as you show up for class. Tests aren't too bad, basically know how to do stuff on the problem sets well and you're all set. Dr. Kurt's a lot of fun; really gets along with the students.
No Comments
He is so funny and goes crazy in class to make a point! He is a great teacher!
Awesome teacher.... enthusiastic and really cares about the students.  Highly recommended.

Professor DiSalvo is a great professor. This class is additive, so you can only gain points on attempting assignments. All assignments are open notes, and previous lectures are available. This is important for the application part of the class. She's very funny, and is always serving
