reviews.comment: Lauren is a great professor. You have to come to her classes, but her assignments are very doable as long as you take notes in class and pay attention. She is super sweet and will help you with whatever you need. I took her classes for my pathways and I'd recommend!

She was amazing and very passionate about the subject. You could tell she really cared about her student's success and provided us with a lot of resources to succeed in the class. She has a great grading system and always gave very good feedback on our assignments, and was very encouraging. She was also very sweet and fun to talk to.

Lauren is not a good communicator and has a very limited understanding of modern technology. The course structure is poorly developed, disorganized, and counter-intuitive. You will need to supplement the course materials using resources outside of the class. Genuinely, save yourself the headache and choose another instructor if possible.
Easy to understand and succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It is easy to succeed in this class, there are many grades and opportunities to raise your grade. Paper and participation heavy. She is strict with attendance and late assignments. She also has nice outfits.

Lauren is one of the best professors I have had here at Tech. She is so kind and provides super interesting lectures with attention to detail and a genuine joy for her subjects with clear grading criteria and a choice in assignments. I had her for both Greek Art and Art and Archeology of Death. You should take a class with her if you can!

Professor DiSalvo is an amazing professor, easily in my top 3 so far at VT. She has a unique grading system which allows you to do assignments that you want to, rather than being forced to. She is incredibly kind and understanding and genuinely wants you to succeed. She's easy to approach and will give wonderful advice and help on any assignments.

I took Roman Art and Architecture with Professor DiSalvo. She has a weird grading system where there is a total of 150 points and you can get up to 100 for an 100%. It is very flexible but you need to be responsible and plan ahead what you need to complete when, or you may fall behind. Very fun class for people who like the classics.
Super nice and friendly, has a very extended knowledge of the subject. Great course to take for pathways.
This class was very easy and simple. All assignments are on canvas and due on Sunday every week. Powerpoints and voice lectures are great.
Really enjoyed the class and the lectures were super easy to follow along.

Prof. Neser sets up this course to be extremely easy. The lectures are clear and simple to understand. All of the assignments are quick and straight to the point. I would recommend taking any of her courses, especially for gen. eds.
Laura was so awesome! She is so sweet, her lectures are super easy to understand, and the material is very clear! Homework is due every week on Top Hat, but it is not super time-consuming.

Dr Neser is the best. She is so engaging, and there are so many funny easter eggs in her slides. I would talk to her after class now and then and she is so friendly and kind. She also brings in rocks to class sometimes or does demonstrations to keep the class even more engaging. On top of all of this, the class is not very homework heavy at all.

Dr. Neser's GEOS 1004 class was very easy, and she still finds ways to engage the class! For example, during our chapter on minerals and rock formations, she brought in minerals and different types of rocks for students to observe at the end of class. All quizzes and exams are online and open-note. If you need to take a Gen Ed, take her class!
Very easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Nesser is a very nice person and she is very passionate about what she teaches. I took this class because I needed a pathway and it was very easy. There are in-class tophat questions, so you should go. The tests are open note/internet, so they are easy. I was surprised by how much I liked this class and I highly recommend it.

Dr. Neser sets up this course to be very easy. Everything is opened notes! She provides great lectures and other detailed resources to help you get a guaranteed A. You do have to purchase FlatWorld for some of the homework assignments. I recommend her for any geoscience courses!

The online version of GEOS 1004 was incredibly easy. Each "lecture" is a powerpoint with voiceovers from Dr. Neser, and they were usually very well written and explained
The assignments are usually quick and easy
Tests and quizzes are open resource
the discussion boards are graded by AI that tells you how to make your score better

Overall this course was an easy A. As long as you completed all of the weekly small assignments on time and completed the three exams, there is no reason why you shouldn't pass this class. Dr. Neser was also very nice and provided detailed notes and lectures on all the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have never met her becuase I took GEOS 1004 online asynchronous. However, the voiceovers over the powerpoints were very effective. They explained the content in detail but allow you to go through the lecture at your own pace. Overall, I would definitely reccomend Dr. Neser for GEOS 1004.
I took her for both of my science classes. She is well organized and very understanding. I highly recommend her classes if your not a huge fan of science but still want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class for a pathway and it was super easy! I didn't like having to pay to access tophat (it was ~$50 for the semester), but it was an easy course. Everything is open notes and open internet so it's easy to make an A

Dr. Neser is amazing. She is very understanding & is generous with grades. Easiest class with open notes, book,&internet for all tests & quizzes. Everything is done on TopHat, but the textbook is free & is helpful with the tests. In person is probably better but I did asynchronous & got an A+, so if you need an easy pathway to fill take this.

Dr.Neser is an amazing professor. She ensures that students understand the information and she's willing to accomodate as well. Everything in the class in open-note and open internet (including tests and quizzes). All the homeworks are in TopHat but the textbook is completely free to use. I'd take this class all over again if I could.

Everything was open note and she walked you through step by step on half the homeworks. Textbook is definitely helpful when taking quizzes in tests. Does require a little intuitive thinking skills when trying to decipher the textbook into the quiz and test questions. Tests are weighted the least. Overall great professor who knows what she's doing!
Super easy science pathway. There are weekly open-note quizzes with powerpoints to accompany. There is also a packback every week which is fairly easy.

Had her both in-person and online for 1004/1024 respectively and she is amazing! Super kind, very clear curriculum and easy short homework weekly. Test and quizzes are open-note and open-internet; paying attention to lectures and/or doing online discussions will help you ace this class. Cannot recommend her enough.

The class was beyond easy. We used tophat for this class and just had homework due every week but it was very little. Everything is open note/ internet and we used tophat, she will sometimes take questions from past exams/ quizzes. Just don't forget to do her weekly work. But it's not much work and such an easy A. She is also super sweet/ caring.

Her class was super easy. You do need this thing called Pack back we used this semester and all you do every week is sometimes answer a discussion post of hers but every week we had to make an original question and respond to like 3 classmates and sometimes quizzes. Quizzes and exams are open notes/ internet just don't forget to do the weekly work.

She's so nice!!!!  she is so flexible with rescheduling exams if u ever need to and also gives many extra credit opportunities.  shes great at simplifying and relating the concepts to real world examples

Dr. Neser was the best professor I've ever had. She's extremely gracious and kind, truly cares about each of her students and their wellbeing, and provides endless chances to meet past deadlines AND extra credit. Her lectures are clear and it's obvious she knows what she's talking about. There's more I could say but I'm out of room. PLEASE TAKE HER

I took GEOS1004 last semester and decided to take this class because I enjoyed the structure of the class! It is similar to Design Appreciation, being heavily graded on discussions (with the occasional homework & quiz). I would recommend this class for anyone who's not too into the subject matter, but if you are, I would recommend GEOS1004 instead.

I wouldn't call it an easy A due to the amount of time spent on the discussions and assignments each week, but I really liked the class! Her PowerPoints basically summed up the textbook so I didn't raelly have to read the book to still do good. She always emailed me if I didn't finish my work by the day it was due which I really appreciated!

I took this class asynchronously so I cannot attest to her as a person but as an instructor she was great! It would be extremely difficult to receive a bad grade in this course. Recommended if you need to fulfill a pathways 4 requirement. Wouldn't recommend to anyone who is passionate about the subject matter of this class.

Professor is caring and well-respected. Don't half-bake your answers while doing assignments, as they are only one attempt (which cannot be undone). Take your time, so long you submit before deadlines. Quizzes and exams are open-notes, open-book, open-internet. No Lockdown Browser. Uses Top Hat (where most stuff takes place). Discussions are fun!

Dr. Neser was a great teacher, I took her class virtually and it was great. She provided lectures with her personal voiceovers and it was rather helpful. I didn't like the TopHat textbook, but that was outside of her control. It was still a great class.

GEOS 1004 is an easy A. All you need to do for this class are weekly discussion posts or individual exercises with occasional quizzes and exams. Dr. Neser is an amazing professor, and she makes it clear how much she enjoys geoscience in her lectures. I'd recommend taking this class online since the workload is very manageable.

Laura is a super caring professor that will absolutely make accomodations for you if you need them! The integration of Top Hat within the course is a little difficult to navigate and also the individual assignments were slightly hard to complete, but other than that she is a great professor!

Ngl I took Dr. Neser's class for the second time as a pathway and she is by far the best teacher I have had at this school. She wants students to interact in her classes while learning and she also is very caring. She is super understanding and gives extra credit at the end of the semester that can clutch up for your grade. Highly recommend her.

Professor Neser was a really good professor! Her class was interesting and easy. It takes about 1-3 hours a week to complete the week's work, including the reading. To top it all off, it's open book and open notes! :D

Super easy class! Take note of deadlines since this is based on your entire grade. Ms. Neser always responded quickly to my emails and answered any questions I had. I am not a fan of science, but I learned a few interesting things in this course. Would definitely recommend this class.
Dr, Neser's class is an easy A. She cares about her students grades. She allows all exams to be open note open internet open everything. I really liked her and this course
The only things graded are the 3 online exams and weekly discussion posts. Couldn't be easier to get an A. I didn't read any power points and aced everything.

Easiest class Ive ever taken. No lectures. Textbook not needed (I didnt buy it). Tests open note open google. No group projects. Less then 2 hours a week of work including watching PowerPoint. Discussion post every other week cake. Take this class for easy A.

Very nice Professor but this was definitely a harder pathways class than I was expecting. The homework assignments are only one attempt, so they act like a quiz. Definitely can not wing these assignments and exams. Lectures are good but take absolutely forever to take notes on because they're online with added spoken media.
I had Dr. Neser for GEOS1024. It was a pathways, and all the quizzes and tests so far have bene open note. She's very nice and will definitely help you if you reach out.

Do not take this instructor. She thinks her class is the only class in the world and expects you to treat this entry level class like a 4000 level class. She gives busy work that doesnt matter and has 0 weight on your grade and it doesn't contribute to learning.
She is an amazing professor and very respectful. Would recommend.

Girl, we know its you leaving these reviews. Your class is so boring and you talk way too much. This class could be done in a day online if she didn't insist so much busy work. Showed up everyday, got an A+, and hated your class. She is the classic 1000 level professor who acts like their class should be the most important thing in your life.

I honestly don't understand the low ratings. It seems like some of the students who rated her poorly may not have been attending class regularly you really need to show up to do well on the assignments. There are both in-class activities and larger assignments completed outside of class. She's a great teacher.

Don't take. Well, as long as you don't talk about anything remotely relevant to anything, and pick a topic she likes, and agree with her opinion. Missing class will get you an F (3 missed-down a letter, 6 an  F). If you take COMM 1015 you will be required to take 1016 with her in the spring, and its just as bad.

Consider this your warning.

I don't quite understand the low ratings. It seems likely that some students who rated her poorly may not have attended class regularly, which is important for doing well on the assignments. There are both in-class activities and larger assignments outside of class.

I don't really understand the poor ratings here. I have a feeling the people who gave her bad ratings are ones who didn't go to class - you definitely need to go to class in order to do well on the assignments. There are in-class assignments but also bigger out-of-class assignments. She is a wonderful teacher; I think some people are just petty.
Took her for Media Writing, super caring and sweet but lectures can be kind of dead and useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class a lot. Participation and attendance is absolutely mandatory but for good reason. You will do a lot of small on the spot group projects but they are not bad and they prepare you for the latter portion of the class. Tough grader for writing assignments but once you find what she is looking for you are golden.

The First Assignment: "Write Whatever Comes to Mind." Just an open-ended request. So I wrote a deeply philosophical piece on how socks mysteriously disappear in the laundry. The feedback? "Interesting. But not really what I had in mind." What did she have in mind? I assume it was a 700-page manifesto on the metaphysical nature of paperclips.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Picture this: an elderly woman wearing a cardigan that looked like it had been inherited from a cat-hoarding grandmother, holding a cup "coffee," but smelled suspiciously like regret. She didn't greet us with a smile or even make eye contact. She stared at the whiteboard for a solid minute, trying to remember what a "sentence" was.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: I once saw her break out a bag of frozen peas during a class to demonstrate how "writing should be like the perfect vegetable—firm, yet flexible." You had to be there to truly appreciate the metaphor, but I think we all walked away with a deeper understanding of the writer's craft… and a slight fear of frozen vegetables.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her feedback is… peculiar, yet profound. On one assignment, I received a comment that simply said, "This feels like a giraffe trying to solve a Rubik's cube." Later, I realized she was complimenting my creativity and suggesting my structure was, in fact, a bit too lofty. I haven't been the same writer since.

What I appreciate most is that she creates an environment where it's okay to stumble and learn from mistakes. Her emphasis on excellence may be demanding, but it's clear she believes in each student's ability to succeed—this belief is motivating, and it pushes you to keep improving.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's not only an excellent teacher but also incredibly supportive and approachable. She's always ready to offer helpful feedback, whether I'm struggling with a concept or just need advice on how to improve my writing. Her kindness and patience make the learning process enjoyable, and she creates a positive, welcoming environment in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She doesn't grade every assignment; she picks and chooses and usually grades the ones you don't do. We had 2 speeches in the start of the year that she just didn't grade. She is horrible at checking email. The only way to get in touch with her is to talk to her during class but even then sometimes she ignores you. Take another professor

If you have to take comm 1015 with LP, comm 1016 does get better. Not as much of a harsh grader. Still says stuff like "your grade can depend on how tired I am." If you're reading this, take. another. professor. you will have her for a whole school year if you do 1015 with LP
Too harsh with grading
Don't let other reviews fool you she's a pretty good professor. Her class just has a lot of "busy work" and group projects, but as long as you show up, do your work and participate, you'll be fine.

LP is extremely nice. Super harsh grader when it comes to essays. No criticism involved just straight will tell you how it is. There is a lot of writing work assigned and beware of the group projects. Overall I did have fun in her class and our class her favorite. You must go to class for credit. She is very understanding in situations but explain

i had LP for a couple of months as she covered for one of my teachers that was on leave. she is very nice and understanding with her students and tries her best to show some enthusiasm while teaching. she explained all of our assignments thoroughly and i found her feedback for my writing helpful. i thought she was a good professor and i liked her.
Easy class but huge amount of normally useless busy work. It's required for most so you ought to just get it over with but be ready to have to grind out busy assignments.

Mrs Purcell is nice enough. In class shes fine but she gives the rudest and harshest feedback on writing Ive ever had from an instructor. At times not even constructive just condescending. Also the pure amount of assignments is just obnoxious as most of them serve no real purpose, just more work for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Christian Lucero is an excellent professor with a clear, structured teaching style that makes complex material approachable. His lectures are well organized and focused on building real understanding, not just memorization. He explains concepts in a way that connects theory to application, making it easier to follow and retain.

He is a really bad professor. His lectures are tedious and he doesn't even go over them throughly. The tests feel like they are made to fail you yet he calls them "easy". He tries to be funny but his jokes make me fall asleep. As a statistics professor, he kills any interest I had in the subject. Take the other CMDA 2006 section if possible.

He's an interesting guy. Teaches content quite well mostly, but sometimes is out of touch with the class, whether he's calling a massive HW assignment easy or making slightly surprising comments. Not a fan of how the tests are structured, 100% multiple choice with no partial credit given. He does offer a nice amount of extra credit though overall

Not great. Lectures are boring, projects were compressed at the end of the semmester, and not that many assignments in the class so small mistakes were made bigger. He does offer a big extra credit assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Would not recommend at all.
5's are only coming from people who talk to him a lot outside of class.
Extremely hard to work with. Much more focused on his senior classes (which he constantly degrades in class). Constantly felt (myself and peers) that he thought himself above the curriculum
Dr. Lucero was alright. 4654 covers advanced concepts, but it wasn't hard because the concepts weren't covered thoroughly. Overall, the information is interesting, but the class is just uninspiring.

Dr. Lucero gives good lectures, but his assignments often got tedious to do. For many of them, you can either choose or are randomly assigned a partner. The assignments didn't give me much insight into how the theoretical concepts tie into the data analysis; it mostly felt like busy work. Try not to skip class, and be prepared to code a lot in R.
Challenging but rewarding. Will help you in office hours.

I have had him for three separate classes. At the 4000 level, he spends way too much talking about basic fundamental concepts. His lectures are mostly confusing with irrelevant and repetitive information. They are also riddled with countless mistakes. Overall, not a great lecturer nor an educator.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for 2005, 2006, and 4654. Lectures are hard to get into, and his pacing muddles key takeaways with smaller details. Lecture slides are sloppy in their information, flow, and format. He's good at optimizing though because students have max stress and min learning (way too much work for amount of learning). I speak for myself and many peers.
I found Professor Lucero's lectures to be less engaging than expected, with limited opportunities for interaction or clarification, which made the learning experience challenging.

I had him for 2006 and for 3654. Both classes he posted lecture notes online if you need to read them over again when doing homework. I would say if you engage in class then you will get a lot more out of it. Gave bunch of hints about tests in class, but did not have study guides due to how tests where formatted just ask questions week of.

Professor who looks out for his students. Be meticulous on the homework and actually understand what you're doing; the material builds on itself. Lectures are very, very fast and often I left class feeling like I didn't process everything. But definitely come to class! Try not to cram for exams.

Good when it comes to resources for exams, content covered is made very clear. If you struggle with the course going to class will help in both your understanding of the content and tons of hints are dropped on what the exams and homework will be like. However, lectures can be very impassionate, whiny and boring if you aren't struggling
the best
