reviews.comment: The professor knows the material and he knows what he is doing. He goes over the material well and is usually is available when you go to his office hours or if you email him. He posts a lot of great resources on his canvas page. The class can be difficult if you don't stay on top of your things. But if you put in the work, you will do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor. He knows his stuff. He also posts video lectures that are really helpful. Don't skip class, because there is ALOT of material. So go to every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: GEOG 3104 Dr. Juran is one of the best professors I have had! He is excited and passionate about his teachings. There are 6 pop-quizzes throughout the semester, but they are 2 true false questions worth 1 point. The tests are worth much more than the other assignments, but there are only 2 tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed prof. Juran for GEOG 2004. His tests were fair and the curriculum was overall interesting and could be applied to many subjects
Mr. Juran was a decent prof, the content of the class was familiar to me since I already to APES, but even if its completely new to someone it really isn't that bad.

I studied with Luke on a study abroad trip in New Zealand. For the course, he was not giving most of the lectures, but graded essays very fairly and felt like a friend outside of scheduled sessions. He is very fun to be around. I will not forget my great time with Dr. Juran.
he was amazing.
I actually had her for Engineering Economy. Lots of in class activities but they are barely weighted anything. Attendance isn't mandatory

Really cares for her students. Does have graded in class exercises that make up an attendance grade of around 7% of the grading scale. Bi-Weekly in class quizzes that you can make a formula sheet for, and can submit corrections for points back. Bi-weekly HWs were helpful. Lectures were recorded and uploaded on canvas.

Dr. Savage is great! She has a bunch of small quizzes instead of tests which I much preferred. She would fairly often cancel class and would sometimes replace it with a zoom meeting. Everything was on Top Hat, which I liked. The class is pretty simple excel stuff. Overall, very easy class and nice professor.

Made the class so much harder than it needs to be. Extremely harsh grader, doesn't explain well why you get certain things wrong well. NEVER responds to emails and if so, does it so late you don't care at that point. I honestly bumped because I was excited for this class but towards the end, everyone was over her harsh grading and constant workload

Very sweet professor who was great for this intro class. Lots of good information presented clearly about the subject. Lectures were interactive and all questions were answered. If she didn't have an answer she'd email the student later. Grading seemed easy but took a bit to get back grades.
He is very rude and did not teach very well. Take anyone else.

Didn't explain concepts well, and instead jumped straight into solving practice problems. Typically got said problems wrong and either searched up the right answer or just moved on. He never showed up to class with a plan, and he always seemed very tired and exhausted while teaching. Also, he never wears shoes.
He is not a very good professor. Not very good at teaching and it comes off very confusing. Would recommend anyone else.

Told us that for extra credit, we could discuss our first exam with him after it went poorly for the class. (Average was about a 60; I received an above-average grade) He told me in front of two other students that I had no clue how to study and that I had a problem in the class that he didn't believe was able to be solved. Never got extra credit.

Matt Park should not be a teacher. Throughout the semester he taught us on vague concepts and example problems that most of the time were wrong. We had to check his math almost every time he did a problem because of his chance to error. Also the grades he put in Canvas were wrong and he didn't tell anyone and screwed over half of the class.
Professor told me to kill myself

His lectures never feel planned, his work is never clear. He introduces new topics with a handful of practice problems he puts onto the board, never really explaining them to begin with. He's usually exhausted in class and it shows in his hand-wavey explanations and poor clarifications. His grading is fair but his feedback is useless.

I dropped this class after the second session. By day two there was already a quiz, and instead of teaching, the instructor just wrote a concept on the board and told us to figure it out. I learned more from short videos, and several others also dropped. The course is entirely test-driven.

He is an ok guy, just isn't a great teacher. The only way to learn was through study groups and outside work. Going to class was a waste of time. He had such a hard time introducing concepts and often would go through problems just for a student to point out his mistakes. I would switch classes, or drop it and take it online or next semester.
Honestly a pretty entertaining guy if you get to know him. Wasn't an awful professor by far, you'll honestly be fine if you just do the hw and study on your own time.

I took his class last semester for calc 1. As long as you know the very foundational concepts of what you will learn in this class, that's all you need to know and you will be fine. He did a fair job in teaching, and amount of practice problems and examples provided throughout the course really helped me.

He sometimes doesn't explain core concepts in a stable enough way so Organic Chemistry Tutor and Paul's Online Notes will be your best friend. He's pretty chill in class & does encourage other students to study with each other to improve for test grades. The tests he makes are reasonable except for Sequences and Series which was horrendous 😭

On my way to pamplin every time I went through the construction site on my way to his class I wish the trucks ran me over. I took calc 1 last semester with him and it was an experience I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy. You'd have to study everything on your own, people barely showed up to his lectures.

He taught the MATH1225 syllabus really well and efficiently. He did get ahead of other classes but this gave us more time to practice for tests. He also gives really good homework questions that are very relevant for tests and the necessary practice that can help you score well. The practice problems he gives in class are also very exam-oriented.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Did a solid job teaching compared to other instructors I heard about for math1225. Would explain the important topics well and give a good amount of practice problems for tests and in class.

There is a good amount of homework, but the practice is necessary for any math course. He covers the material in a timely manner and we always had time for review before a test. We had a couple other math 1225 subs, and it was clear that he was a better teacher. This class is going to be hard with any teacher but his teaching definitely helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The amount of work in this class was absurd, he was incredibly in-compassionate and the tests and homework did not reflect what we did in class. If we did bad on a test (often) he would shame us in front of class. After talking with students in other classes I found that he was not properly following the curriculum and missing essential lessons.

You will learn literally nothing in the lectures. Doesn't cover the basics of calc and forces you straight into complex problems. You will be forced to learn all of the material yourself outside of class. Had a sub one time for 2 days and it was the best 2 days of my life, the teacher had an actual structure. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH MATT PARK.

Lots of homework
Grades strictly w/o explaining errors or allowing revisions
Doesn't follow the course's content, leaving gaps in material covered
Tests heavily impact grades
Lacks respect for students, openly belittling them
Ignores questions
Leaves students behind
Doesn't simplify topics, expecting constant understanding
Relied on YouTube videos
lol

Professor McCrea was an easy professor, but will fail you for random things. His classes are fine, but participation matters and he will only call on select students, leaving others with no chance to earn points. Would recommend if you are a student athlete or male, as these students he seems to like, but other than that, would not recommend.

Good personality teacher. The grading criteria would be hard to understand, but not hard to perform well. Video & attendance mandatory. Handful of companies visit to talk. Could be randomly called on. Assigned one group for many projects through the semester, so may impact how the class goes for you.
Professor McCrea cares about his students, and keeps the material interesting and relevant!

Took him for Professional Sales. Enjoyed some parts of his class and having guest speakers. Overall fun class to take and learn about Sales. He is a great guy, just a little unorganized. Still recommend him though

Everyone I know who has actually interacted with this guy ( which is probably less than 5% of students as he doesn't participate in any of the actual labs...) has never had a good experience. Zero empathy or sympathy for students, and his grading system is unfair. Whether your lab section is Monday or Thursday, everyones lab is due Friday. Bad guy.

The lab itself is not hard, and the content is a great way to conceptualize the lecture's general topics. There's one no-questions-asked makeup for a lab that you don't have to provide proof for. Dr. Merritt doesn't appear in labs, but is timely with email responses. Overall, a meh class that you have to power through, no way around it.

bro, not even gonna lie, he just makes all the pre-lab quizzes basically impossible. They have been even harder than usual. The nice part is that they are built on your last attempt, and you get three. The bad part is that you can't even see your grade once you complete it. you have no idea what you need to change or how well you did on a problem

All class sections have the same due dates, the friday after your lab. Meaning if you have the lab on thursday, you only have one day to do your lab report, while people with a monday lab have 5 days to work on it.
Never in class, your success depends on which TA you get.

A lot of these reviews say that he never shows up, which is true unless you are a physics major. If you are, he will be at every lab. Super great guy and genuinely cares about his students. Homework heavy but it is mostly completion, so read the rubrics. He also doesn't assign lab reports, you just submit your lab notebook!

Did not have a good experience communicating with this professor.
The lab itself is quite easy, and I liked the GTA for my lab. Your experience in this lab is largely dictated by your GTA.
The first two or three labs are quite brutal in terms of meeting the time the lab is over, but after that, it's smooth sailing.
Very bad person, needs his doctorate stripped as he never shows up to class and doesn't do anything.

Class depends on your TA. My TA was a tough grader and provided zero help when something went wrong during the lab, some other people had TA's that just gave out free 100s. Dr. Merrit is an enigma and you will NEVER seen him. Labs are sometimes tedious but otherwise it was really easy, you can always get the whole lab done during lab time.

Never saw him once. The class is so easy that it genuinely is not helpful for learning physics in my opinion. Some of the questions in the lab manual are really strange too. As someone who knew physics decently well going into it, this was a waste of time.

The TA's are great and typically very helpful, however, the coordinator actively tries to make his job easier by making his student's lives harder. He does not accept anything late, nor does he allow makeups if your submission gets corrupted by technology. He does not even enter the classroom, I had his labs for both 1 and 2 and I never saw him.
uhhhhhhh....? I'm pretty this guy doesn't exist. The lab was super light though, nothing near as bad as chem lab... so I guess take him if you can? (you'll never see him once)
I have no complaints about Mr. Merritts's lab curriculum; he was very patient and kind to me when I needed help with assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I've never actually seen this guy so I'm not sure if he exists. Labs will depend on your TA, but in general they're not very difficult (especially after chem lab). You'll be in groups of 3 and are given lab directions concerning a certain physics topic. More often than not you'll finish before the class period ends. Just don't miss any labs!

I took Dr. Merritt's PHY2305LAB. The labs are fully ran by TAs so I've never seen him. I wish he can conduct some of the lab office hours because the TAs are often not sure how to do some of the Mathematica homework themselves. Be ready for those Mathematica homeworks (coding and stats). They're usually pretty hard and require a lot of reading.

Manager of PHYS 2305 labs, and he's pretty accessible outside of class especially if any problems arise. PHYS 2305 lab isn't difficult just do your work during the lab and make sure to read the grading rubric for every assignment. Your TA grades your work, but he posted everything you need to know on Canvas and page was easy to navigate.

It depends on TA like every other lab. My TA was amazing, explained things very well and wanted to help. He also graded super easily and was nice. I know other TAs are different but I think they still grade somewhat easily.
Lab is dependent on TA. All you need to know is GO TO EVERY LAB. If you miss one without a good excuse, you'll get a 0 which will tank your grade when there is only 10 labs.

PHYS 2305 lab depends on TA. Go to labs and work well with group, you'll be fine. Refer to rubric before submitting labs and post-lab questions. Attend every single lab and try not to miss any since making up labs suck. If you don't have a good reason for missing a lab, you'll get a 0 and it won't get dropped. Show effort and lab shouldn't be hard.

Lab really depends on your TA, mine was nice and graded very leniently so it's honestly an easy A. Instructions can be confusing though. Dr Merritt, I've never seen in person but he responded to my emails in a timely manner. I missed lab for a stupid reason and he allowed me to retake. I think you just gotta own up and be honest, and ask genuinely.

Never saw him during the semester, and my TA was terrible. Lab instructions are hard to understand and hardly give any background info to help. Luckily, the grading was not harsh. No exams, just weekly lab assignments and one paper at the end. You're assigned a lab partner each week, but most of them never show up or are difficult to work with.

Physics lab itself is a fairly easy class, but set multiple reminders to submit your assignments on time. Even in an extenuating circumstance, he will not award you ANY points for a late submission. One 0 will automatically give you a B+ at best, and he knows that. He's the kind of prof I would never want to be like, he has been rude every time.

I would like to preface this review by saying that this professor failed to respond to emails in a timely matter when first being force added into the course. Additionally, he has 0% of human decency in his body and genuinely believes that being cold hearted and intentionally creating more challenges for students makes him a better professor.

If ratemyprofessor allowed you to put a rating below 1, I would have given this instructor a -100000. This instructor truly does not care about anyone but himself. He does not care what anyones circumstances are. I was unfairly given two zeroes because of him and given a C+ in the course despite deserving an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: High A average on the labs and forgot to turn one in. Grade dropped 10% because he wouldn't even give me partial credit for a lab I had scanned and timestamped before the due date. Nobody should have to lose so many points for such an understandable human mistake. Remember to always turn in your labs on time.....
If you are going through anything he wont understand or compromise to help you succeed in the class

Travis loves answering emails from his students so he is always there to help out. He is younger which makes his lectures more relatable and allows him to better understand his students (both in humor and our courseload). His lectures were always entertaining for such a difficult subject.

Merrit has been one of my favorite professors at Tech. He is always so enthusiastic about what he teaches and definitely teaches it well. His office hours were always really helpful, so definitely go to them if you know Physics is your weak spot. Tests might get a small curve and the final is usually curved. Really wish he taught PHYS 2306.

Merritt is the best physics professor you can get at VT. His lectures are engaging but honestly i might just be paying attention because he looks like ryan gosling. Merritt is relatable and "hip." You will look at him and wonder "this mans really has a doctorate?" If you suck at physics you will have to put in work, Merritt cant work miracles.

Travis is a real gem. He's very helpful in lectures and during office hours. He's young and exuberant (which is hard to find at Tech) and curves all the tests. He gives multiple clicker questions per lecture and always holds us until the time class is over. He's always collected, prepared, and not too bad on the eyes, either.

Merritt is a great professor. I really didn't think that physics was for me as I got a low C in AP Physics C. However, taking this class the subject seems so much more straightforward. He's pretty thorough in class and makes an effort to engage students. There are usually curves on the tests and even without them, it's easy to get a B or higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Merritt is a great choice. The lectures are as interesting as physics lectures can be, and he's funny and attractive, too. Tests are challenging, but he provides practice exams that are pretty similar to the real thing. I personally found the subject itself to be difficult, but with the grading distribution it isn't hard to do alright in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: SUPER attractive.  Lectures are light on math even though tests arent
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Merritt is an amazing professor. If you get the chance to take him, do it. He explains things really well if you ask questions and go to his office hours. Really cool guy. Looks like a Jay Crew model every day too. 3
Straightforward lecturer and a good teacher. He rambles a bit though.

I have never had to come on here to leave a review, but after this class I felt the need to so that you don't have to suffer through this course like I did. I am an A student and a hard worker, and this class tanked my gpa. Throughout the course my grade dropped with every assignment. She was rude in her feedback and a difficult grader. Don't take.

Rubrics are so vague and difficult to understand what she's looking for. Don't take any of her classes if you have even a little understanding of art or prior knowledge of the history, otherwise she will accuse you of cheating. Spends more time reporting people for cheating than actually giving good feedback

You have to watch 3 to 5 hours of video content every week. After you do that you then have to answer a discussion board that makes up maybe 5 minutes of content from the videos, so good luck trying to remember where that was. Then you have a quiz for that week, which if you haven't perfectly memorized all the material you will not do good on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There is barely a rubric for her discussion posts. She is an extremely tough grader, it feels like she's trying to trick you with these questions.  I was given an example paragraph for a discussion post because she didn't like my response, but it was near identical to my analysis on the art pieces. Your GPA will go down in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: My experience in this class led me to being accused "outside content" in a discussion. Which doesn't make sense. I understand not wanting students to cheat, but I have a background in art history knowledge, and sometimes I like to bring up relevant information I've learned from past classes. Am I not supposed to share things I've learned at Vtech?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Be prepared to take A LOT of notes and expect those notes to NOT help you in the slightest. The way that she writes these questions can really confuse you, making you wonder if she talked about that subject in the video lecture. Her lectures can be really dull, and the time limits for quizzes are strict and frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She shows no interest in abstract reasoning or evidence of learning—only verbatim regurgitation. She implied I cheated by using “outside sources” (prior knowledge as an art major) and said I was lucky not to be reported. She doesn't use rubrics-grading is subjective. Feedback is vague, lectures dull. Take good notes and use her exact words on tests

She grades way too harsh and doesn't give any helpful feedback. Watching the lectures fully doesn't even prepare you for the test, not to mention the lectures take too much time and have no real impact.

Honestly one of the worst professors I've had at this school. She's a harsh grader despite this class being an elective. Incredibly monotone during her lectures and the content is horribly boring(which is completely her fault because she presents it so poorly). I wouldn't recommend her classes to anyone.

Content was easy to understand, but she's tough (I pulled my grade out of my ass). The class was well-structured and easy to follow, but you need detailed notes and must use her exact terms (you will lose points if not, and sometimes not know why). I love art, and I did very well, but if it's not your thing, I wouldn't recommend taking it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is an extremely tough grader, no matter how much effort you put in, do not expect a good grade. Her quiz questions are meant to trick you, and her feed back is extremely unhelpful. I was told to use more terms from lecture? and her examples of words to use where not even from the lecture. Each unit has over 3hr of lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A little difficult. Took her asynchronous class for Chinese and Japanese art, I really liked the class but missed an exam which caused my grade to drop. The class structure was easy and good for a routine. As for the professor, somewhat difficult to reach or communicate with outside of class. Would take again but stay on top of deadlines.

I am an engineering student taking this class for a pathway requirement and it is the hardest pathway I have ever taken for no reason. The professor grades super hard just because, if you do not meet her exact criteria you get points taken off even if the content is accurate. She does not try to work with students at all, do not take her classes.
Ungodly amount of lecture videos for quizzes on the most random things. Nitpicky about word usage on essays and will give you 0s on exam essay portions. Too harsh of a grader for a pathways class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is not someone that is very reliable as a professor that wants to help her students, so don't count on participation points. It's like if you're not a novelist, she will deduct points for not masterfully articulating keywords and examples from the 3, sometimes 4-hour lectures that she doesn't use to specify what you need to know for exams.

have to watch several hours worth of lectures just to take a quiz with questions that don't seem to have been covered. put into discussion groups despite and limited to a small pool to pull from, despite what she might say, and you get a zero if she or the TA thinks you covered something someone else did.

overall, just don't
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: just f no

she requires you to talk in class and if you don't talk you aren't gonna pass. Thats honestly where my grade went down so much mainly because I just didn't speak up. Also she honestly is a tough paper grader. I've had a lot of professors praise my writing but to her it's bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Each week included a lot of lectures, and while the professor herself is really interesting, it's a lot to listen to and take notes on. The quizzes and tests are an easy A as long as you listened to all the videos but the discussion boards are all applied learning.

Taken as a CLE this class was tougher and professor just grades pretty harshly. I am an engineering major student and if you do not have a good art background, it will just be like a foreign language.

Taken online winter class for my major.  Its not difficult to understand the material, but she's excruciatingly harsh about grading. If I didn't have to take this class, I wouldn't. Nope. Never. Not everyone is an art history buff and she refuses to be lenient on those with troubles. Also rambles and uses a lot of useless info in hours long lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Good teacher and lectures. Cares about the student but she defiantly makes you work for it. DO NOT SKIP CLASS. A lot of material is covered in the 1 hour 15 min class. She is a chairman of the Art History board thing so her recommendation letter is to die for.
Not helpful at all and doesn't really care how you do on her exams. It's supposed to be a CLE not a 4000 level class.

Just an unbelievably unreasonable teacher. It's like she doesn't realize most of the kids in her class are not art history majors. Depth and amount of material covered is too much and she puts very little emphasis on which points she actually expects you to know. I would never take her, she will try to ruin your GPA.

Dr. Moseley-Christian is by far the best professor I had at Virginia Tech.  Her enthusiasm for 17th century-dutch art is very contagious.  Course consisted of: 2 exams, 25% each, a research paper, 20%, quizzes 20%, and Participation, 10%.  She has helped me write my papers better than my English professors.  She expects a lot, but it's worth it!

Dr. Moseley Christian has been one my best professors at VT and favorite out of the art history ones.  While her class is difficult, especially if you know nothing about the material, she helps you until you get it.  3 exams 20% each, 2 short papers 10% each, quizzes 15% and 5% participation.  I liked her so much, I'm taking her again in the fall!
One of the best Art History professors I have ever had. She is amazing and makes the material relevant to all majors. She is the highlight of my week and well worth taking.

I've had her for a few classes, and shes truly a great professor.  She is so willing to help students and really makes the material interesting because she is so excited about it.  She inspired me to switch from a minor in Art History to major, and is very involved in the field, notifying students of scholarships and internships.  A++++

Overall, the class isn't a hard class with tests making up 70% of your grade. He tells you everything that's on the test right before so it's just all memorization. He's a nice guy and makes lectures engaging. Although, the McGraw Hill is mandatory for the class and it's 100+ bucks. Waste of money
Lectures every day, but really if you do the assignments you get a 100% on them. Decent amount of homework but nothing too bad.
Great professor and very accommodating - tests are a little hard though as it's a lot of memorization.

Nadav was a good professor and as long as you put your fair part into the class he will take care of you too. He gives so many good resources its just a matter of using them and you will be just fine in his class.

my goat. my king. he's really engaging so the lectures don't feel boring all the time. mcgraw hill homework was annoying and time consuming, but 70% of your grade is exams and he covers literally everything you need to know in the exam review recording. responds fast to emails. pay attention to attendance quizzes.

First off, I took his MKTG 4754 class, BEWARE!!! If you do not have time outside of class to go to his office and get feedback once every week, THIS CLASS IS NOT FOR YOU!! Nadav comes off as approachable and understanding when it comes to the class/grading, but he is not. Do not be fooled. Groupwork heavy, he will GRILL u in the final presentation!

he was a cool guy with actually great experience. exams are 70% of your grade but he gave great review on canvas before each one which was basically identical to the test. exams are in person so as long as you study your fine. he only lectures for about 20 minutes and then you do in class activities each class. i'd recommend him over the others.

Really nice professor who cares about students. Lectures can be a bit boring but the class is easy overall. Best advice is to show up to lectures and listen to the exam review audio file a few times before the exams. Do that and you'll be fine.

Great professor. He posts EXACTLY what will be on the test in his review video (roughly 10-15 min of content posted a week before the exam). Transcribe the audio to text, while listening to the audio file and you'll at a minimum get a 90 on the test. One down side is that you have to show up every class due to his lectures quizzes/discussions.

DO NOT LISTEN to the other reviews! Nadav is a super nice guy who has a great attitude every lecture. His lectures are easy to follow, he gives lots of tips on what to remember. Nadav is very knowledgeable in entrepreneurship and is here at Virginia Tech to help his students succeed. His tests are fair, plenty of time! Very good guy, he cares!

Nice guy, don't think he knows how to teach. Basically would rap his lectures in 20 minutes time, then spend the rest of class making us talking about a podcast/case study/article that I personally did not find helpful for understanding the content. This class was harder than my coding classes. Avoid at all costs.

Professor made us purchase access to McGraw Hill for $150 and then told us the weekly homework and textbook reading wouldn't be on exams after the first. Asked for feedback but didn't implement it. If he says “the riches are in the niches” or “keep it simple stupid” study it like the bible. Content isn't hard but you need to be able to recall.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Talks insanely fast, does not post notes, exams are hard if he doesn't give a review, not flexible at all

Great Professor who's willing adjust based on feedbacks from students.He structured his class where students can learn better through the short lecture (best to record) and a lot of discussions with other students for engagement. First two exams were definitely a curve ball like others have mentioned below, but he adjusted where it got a lot easier

The first two exams were unnecessarily difficult for the class and material of this level, but he adjusted for the last two exams. He helped by giving review videos since the exams were fully based on his lecture slides, which had zero words on them. He's a great guy and cares a lot about his students. Watch out for a quiz at the end of every class

Semester started off bad bc I had to learn a new way to take notes and study for this class. 1st exam was horrible,mean of 68. Became an 80 by the end. He heard our critiques and changed but you have to be willing to adjust to do well. Download notes and do them on the slides. Class is mandatory, he is fast. Write down anything he says is important

Nadav just began his first year at VT, I think there was a learning curve for him coming into tech. His lectures are not really related to the book and all the connect homework you have. He does a post-lecture quiz that is fill in the blank after every class so attendance is mandatory. His tests are somewhat difficult and lengthy.

Prof. himself is nice, chill, & knows what he is teaching. The structure of his class is easy w/ assignments, but exams are more complicated than they should be & really affect your grade. Feedback provided by us might change his layout, but I was able to get by this class by studying notes, so take good ones! Daily quizzes, McGraw, & discussions.

He talks too fast, doesn't give curves or extra credit, doesn't take feedback, and although he says he wants to succeed, he does not take action. His exams are hard because they are mostly fill-in-the-blank, and formats are changed for every exam. I didn't think it would be hard, but I was wrong.

It was his first semester, and he was a kind professor. While he adjusted test formats, he cared about students learning to be better managers. He was fair, sometimes regraded fill-in-the-blank questions, and went over tests with you. The class wasn't too hard; you just need to study.

This was his first semester at VT and you could clearly tell. Would ask for feedback after each exam but would never actually listen to it. Believes in 20 minute lectures so speaks very fast, making it very hard to take notes. Tests are lecture focused so don't rely on the slides AT ALL. This class shouldn't have been as hard as it was. No curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is his 1st sem at VT and we were clearly in his guinea pig class. The professor changed the format for each exam making it completely unfair. He lectures in 20 minutes out of a 75 minute class and does not slow down when requested. His exams are strictly based off lecture content that isn't written down. Best advice is to record the lecture.

You can tell he loves what he teaches. However, he goes on tangents each class about how he has interacted with whatever topic we are learning, which can make it hard to stay focused. Because these tangents plus the lecture take up so much time, I have had to stay after class many times to finish the end of class activity.
Dr. Mike loves his students and incorporates ways to advance your career into his lecture. Also lots of cute dog pictures!

When my dad died, he shrugged and said, "It happens, my dad died too." He would not let me make up the in-class assignments I missed while attending my Father's funeral in Texas, despite my filling out the Absence Verification Form with the Dean of Students, providing proof of travel and showing him my Dad's obituary. Not very kind at all.
Amazing professor! everything you need for tests, he gives you. Easiest class ive taken at tech because of professor mike. Best class ever!
Activities were hard but the TA was helpful.
Wants everyone to succeed and makes class interesting!

Funny, sometimes talks for a while. Make sure to do the notes beforehand and watch the videos and/or look at the slides. I highly suggest watching his review sessions and going over the on paper test review before each exam!

Bio department sets up a flipped classroom, and because of this I feel like he somewhat rushes lectures because he expects us to understand already what we watched. Definitely go to office and TA hours because it'll clear up the confusion of what you might not get in class. Incredibly funny guy nonetheless and his lectures are very engaging.

Great teacher, definitely loves what he does and provides a lot of information to set you up for success on exams. Attending review sessions and doing the practice exams is what helped me do so well in this class.
very fast pace!!!!!

Professor Mike definitely knew what he was talking about. His exams were all application-based, so you had to understand the material to do well in his class. He provided recorded review seesions. Sometimes he spoke about irrelevant subjects, making the lectures run longer, preventing the assignment from being completed on time.

Still a good teacher who tries to make the class fun sometimes. The tests can have some bs questions, but otherwise, studying from the iclickers, homeworks, and other activities should get you a passing grade.

Dr. Mike was very clear about how to study for exams and do well in the class. I studied using the review iclickers and class iclickers in addition to Anki from the lecture slides. Overall, a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easily one of, if not my least favorite professors at tech.  Bio is not my favorite nor best subject but I have never had such a bad experience.  Everyone's learning and teaching styles are different but if you are neurodivergent, I would strongly suggest opting for a different professor.

Easy A if you review iclickers and watch lecture outlines. His lectures/notes are not helpful. He is very passionate/knowledgeable about biology, but lectures are way too long, full of information that is not tested on and he often goes on rants about himself. Also, he is condescending when students ask questions he thinks we should know already.

He was an alright professor, but was rude during office hours and was NOT helpful for any struggling students. You know how sometimes professors are so far removed from learning the material that they forget what it's like to be a student? That's this guy. He understands biology, but is not fit to teach a freshman course. Take Lipscomb instead!
He plays My Singing Monsters 10/10

He's a great guy, he is very passionate about biology and the environment. His tests are not bad as long as you review clickers, it's an easy A. He does take a long time in lectures, and it will get a little boring, but that's not bad.
horrible class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a horrible lecturer. He goes on his own tangents that don't pertain to the subject. You can tell he likes what he teaches, but these tangents add so much to time to the class which is 1 hour and 15 minutes. In addition to the lectures, there's an in-class activity that is a waste of time. Tests aren't awful, but there's so much information.

A goofy professor with tons of resources you can use to study and practice with. Tests were pretty fair, although sometimes some of the questions weren't really what we learned. Cracked many awkward, but funny jokes and has an amazing soundtrack to his class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Mike's BIO1105 class is challenging but rewarding. The format of pre-class videos, in-class activities, and exam reviews helps you succeed. unstuckstudy was a great study tool alongside the textbook. Overall, an engaging and worthwhile course.

Hands down, the best biology prof at VT. He's very caring and his lectures match up to the test. He makes studying for the test clear, concise, and easy. He is available out of class and is a clear communicator. It is very iClicker heavy, so you must stay focused in class. But, it did help me stay engaged in class, and I did well overall.
Honestly one of the best bio professor here. He never makes tests unnecessarily hard like some others. Very passionate about what he teaches.

Cares a lot about the students who are doing well. Tends to come up to you in the middle of a lecture and embarrasses you if you aren't doing so hot. Majority of my class isn't doing well due to his egoistic tendencies.
Explains content well and very clear about what is on exams. Cares about the course and students

Dr.Mike really is the best. I took him for Bio 1105 and 1106 and have no complaints. He is interesting to listen to in class because clearly cares and he doesn't just read the slides. If you put in the work by going to class, taking notes on lectures, and using the review material posted you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had him for Bio 1105 and he could be passive aggressive at times, but as long as you are respectful it is fine. Once you get how the class works it becomes easier (lecture video before class, class, hw). He gives very helpful zoom exam reviews. I switched into Dr. Mikes class for Bio 1106 too because I liked him more than the other I had.

He gives a lot of review material which is awesome. Gives you a bit of feedback. Activity at the end of every lecture is helpful. Lectures are actually pretty interesting. Can sound a bit egotistical and often gives more information than necessary.

He offers time slots to go over your test but I signed up for one and he quickly went though saying "Oh that was in your notes" or something like that, never really explaining each question. Lots of group work & independent thinking, rather than teaching. Felt like I was teaching myself the class.
Dr. Mike is the BEST, super funny guy and makes the best out of a hard class like BIOl 1105. He's very realistic and makes clear expectations. Wants to see students succeed.

I LOVED having Dr. Mike. He is very engaging, funny, and interactive during lectures. If you're looking into a career in the biological sciences, I recommend taking his class and meeting with him frequently. He loves to interact with students and will set them up with jobs and internships ;)

homework is watching/taking notes on a few videos and doing a quiz. Decent lecturer and is clear, but often sounds condescending and arrogant. Attendance is in forms of iclicker questions throughout class, so technically not required but counts towards your grade.

Dr. Mike is an amazing lecturer! He's good at conveying information and passionate about what he teaches. However, this is my second semester taking Dr. Mike and I can definitely say he caught such an attitude compared to when I took him for BIOL1105. He's more on the condescending side for this class but he was such a caring professor for 1105.

I was excited to take Biol 1106 with Dr. Mike because of how great his reviews were. I struggled with the first test, or two but he always encouraged coming to him for help so I did so. He doesn't seem like he really wants to help students when he meets with them. My overall feeling about him are conflicted he is usually pretty condescending.

The class is easy if you just show up to class, read the slides, and follow the review guide. You can't mess up the grading guidelines--doing the iClicker questions for attendance, the in-class activity, the ten question homework, and taking the tests are all you need to do for a good grade. He does an amazing job at explaining hard concepts. Love.

Some reviews are salty lol, he is a solid prof. He does answer very quickly in review sessions, I would not call that rude tho. I highly recommend him! iClickers, additional notes, and the exam review guide is enough to get you over a 70 on the tests for sure

He is an alright professor, his need to narcissistically mention his accolades is a bit unnecessary at times. He is a good lecturer but frankly an unkind and rude person when you ask a question as if you're wasting his time with confusing information HE FEELS you should know, but maybe don't fully understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: definitely the best bio professor at tech, he gives good supplementary study material such as study guides, quizlets, review sessions and  and practice tests. he's clearly passionate and his lectures are rarely dull. a bit unapproachable at times and i always felt dumb asking his questions lol but other than that solid prof.

Dr Mike is a great teacher. He is passionate about the material, and goes the extra mile to make lectures fun. Compared to other bio profs, Dr. M emphasizes the need to put in work writing notes, staying on top of materials, and creating guides. He is a big note guy and will even meet with you to help with your study habits. TW: The tests are hard!

Dr. Mike is a great professor. His lectures are engaging and you can tell he really cares about the material. There is a lot of note-taking before class with the textbook and video lectures. His iClicker questions, activities, and test review sessions are great in preparing you for the exams.

Dr. Mike is an amazing teacher! He is passionate about biology and wants to see his students succeed. He was an amazing lecturer and he really is an amazing person. Attendance isn't mandatory but he does have iClickers and group activities that will be counted against you if you do not come to class. Overall, amazing teacher and taking him for1106!
You can tell he really cares about you and the lecture give lots of helpful information
very good, would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Read your textbook before class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Be ready to take a lot of notes. He provides "additional notes" which he lectures on. You also have a quiz after every class (like every other bio class) but the additional notes he posts have the answers. Very good at lecturing and enjoys it. He really cares about his students as well. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you want to pass go to class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is amazing. If you are looking for a bio professor that challenges you but does not torture you with work and hard tests he is the one for you. He is clearly passionate about biology and he even shares his personal experiences. Bottom line, he has been the best teacher so far for me at tech.

The professor is caring and he is helpful if you reach out to him outside of class. But the tests are very difficult, especially if you are not a good test taker. Other than the tests, the class is not too difficult. But I would not choose to take the class again because of how difficult the tests are.

His test are somewhat difficult mostly because the wording on some of the questions is different than what he taught in class. If you review the Iclikers and go to the review session you can get a good grade on the test without having to really study.

Dr. Mike is one of the best freshman biology professors here at Tech. He is always very engaging with the class and you can tell he loves what he teaches. He holds review sessions which I have found to be ESSENTIAL to the tests, and the review guides help to reinforce what you know and clarify what you don't so you can review the pre-lecture videos
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Mike is my favorite professor. I found it extremely important to watch the lecture videos outside of class and to take notes because it made learning material easier. Pay attention to what he says in class because normally that is what shows up on tests. I found the work load manageable and the tests straightforward for the most part.

out of all the bio professors, mike is probably one of the better ones. however, you still need to put in a decent amount of effort to get the grade that you want in his class. his review guides and practice tests were pretty helpful and he did have a few review sessions. lectures were confusing and you had to do most of the learning before class

Personally was not a fan of Dr. Mike's teaching style. Love the content and he was excited and passionate about it. My high school biology class saved me because there was a lot of reading and videos to watch outside of class. The lectures just reinforce the content, not necessary teaching. The tests were not to difficult.

Mike was nice to work with. After tests you can sign up for meetings to go over the exam and the in class iclicker questions are not graded, which was nice. There are graded group worksheets and homework quiz's due after each class. Lectures felt long and were, at times, confusing. Textbooks were said to be necessary, but I hardly ever used mine.

Professor Rosenzweig is literally the BEST biology teacher at Virginia Tech. He makes class intersting, while also efficiently teaching the material in an easy to understand manner. I loved biology before him, and now I love it even more.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Mike is by far one of the best teachers Ive ever had. He gives you so many notes and resources to help you pass. As long as you put in the effort and show up to class, you will easily receive a good grade. Also, if youre struggling with anything, you can meet with him and he will help in the best way he can. Even if its just to talk :)

Dr. Mike was a great professor. His clear intention wasnt to try and trick you, but rather to make you think and expand on ideas. He provides everything you need to be successful, but you have to put the time into studying to get a decent grade on one of his tests (which make up most of your grade). Review homework, activities, and iClickers.

As long as you pay attention and take notes on everything he says + go over iClickers, you should be set for the exams. You can honestly ignore the textbook as it's just confusing compared to Dr. Mike's succinct teaching style. I remember Exam 2 being pretty tough for everyone so make sure to not slack off on that one!

Dr. Mike gives his students a lot of resources to do well, and if youre willing to put the time and effort into using those resources you will likely do well. i wish i had taken advantage of the resources he provided more
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, he is hilarious, welcoming, full of stories, and is very inspiring and motivating to all of his students in my experience.
He is an amazing professor and takes bland material and uses small video clips and comparisons to make the information all the more interesting. Highly recommend having him as your professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Mike is the best professor you could get for 1105&1106. I had a different professor for 1105 and chose Dr. Mike for 1106, my gpa had an immediate change. His lectures are interesting and hes always available for any questions. His review sessions are extremely helpful and reflect almost exactly as the exam. He made me enjoy bio so much more!

Dr. Mike is one of the best professors I've had so far as a Freshman. He makes a hard and very detailed subject matter fun and easier to learn. His lectures are very helpful and he always dives deeper into the information he wants you to know for the test or that you may just not understand, SO GO TO CLASS. He's funny & makes it a priority to help!

Dr. Mike is the best BIOL1105/1106 professor at Virginia Tech. He breaks down the material better than any other professor. Attendance is MANDATORY as there are iClicker questions & graded group activities at the end of each class. Reviewing before & after class is the best way to study & attend his test review sessions. He gives test questions!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Mike is easily my favorite professor from my freshman year.  I had him for both BIOL 1105-1106 and he never failed me, even when I almost failed him. The material is tough, but thats not his fault because he give you more than enough material to work with and practice from to get a good grade. Participate, do pre-class quizzes, & activities!!

This class was very difficult in my opinion, but if you do the work, a good grade it possible. He has lots of office hours and cares about his students doing well. There are videos/quizzes before each class period that take a long time to complete if you want to actually learn from them and do well. Tests are 70% of the grade; final is cumulative.

I had come to his class as a scared, naive freshman with loads of anxiety, having never taken an AP science class. I left a confident, well-organized and time managed freshman looking forward to the future. If you go to all outside reviews offered by Dr. Mike and show him the effort you put into his class, you will do fine! do revisions!

I took Dr. Mike for BIOL 1105 and 1106 and overall hes a wonderful professor! The flipped classroom, although a new style of teaching for me, ended up working out after I learned how to properly study. He really helps you study if you go to his office hours after the exams. GO TO HIS REVIEW SESSIONS they help! I didnt use the book at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Truly a great professor that loves his field and cares about his students. Provides a number of resources for class and provides study guides that follow the test exactly, but you still have to work super hard to get the grades that you want. I 110% recommend him for Bio 1105 & 1106!

Dr. Mike is the best professor I've had so far. I had someone else for BIOL 1105 and struggled. Dr. Mike goes very in depth in comparison to other professors, but you learn a lot more and it helps you to put the whole concept together. I went from barely getting 70s on my exams in 1105 to getting 90s in Dr. Mike's class. Go to his office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Mike is a great professor, who genuinely cares about his students. The class is set to active learning, so you do the readings/ take notes outside of class, then most of class time is spent doing activities with a small lecture beforehand. Overall great and funny guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Doesnt spend time talking unnecessary lecture topics. Can be difficult to work with sometimes. Assignments can be long and cause class to run 20+ minutes over time. Do not schedule a class immediately after when his class is supposed to get out, you wont get there on time. Overall an engaging and knowledgeable instructor, clear with expectations.
Hes a good teacher and doesnt ever spend time on what you need to know. However, I occasionally find him to be a bit stu
Lots of reading.

Dr. Mike does a good job at taking difficult Biology concepts and making them easy to understand for students. He is caring and his review sessions practically spell out the test questions. He is willing to meet outside of class and it feels like he really WANTS you to do well.

Had a horrible bio teacher for 1105 and could never get above a C on a test. Took one test in his class and got an A! I actually feel like him learning during lecture instead of having to teach myself. He's not necessarily "easy" just a really great teacher!

Dr. Mike is great! Taking 1106 with him next semester. Takes a while to get used to his teaching style and not the biggest fan of breaking into groups. Attend his review session for exams, they really help

I love Doctor Mike! He is amazing! I am in his 1105 class and I am signed up to be in his 1106 class. I took AP Biology in high school and I did not do near as well as I am doing in bio right now. He is a great professor. 10/10 a total gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is a really nice guy and I love how he has a t-shirt that correlates to the lecture. His class is tough though and I would not recommend ever skipping it.

Dr. Mikes class was pretty good his tests were really difficult but at the review sessions he said what to focus on. His in class assignments were a pain in the ass sometimes but reinforced the material so helped in the long run. Overall it was a pretty easy and enjoyable class.

Dr. Mike is the best teacher I've ever had at Tech. I currently have an A in the class and i'm going to apply to be a TA. His teaching is relevant and concise, and his review sessions pretty much tell you everything you need to know for the tests.

I really enjoyed having Dr. Mike as a professor but struggled a little with the class. His tests apply what you've learned from his lectures to real life and so you really need to know the material before taking a test. Make sure you focus on the activities, powerpoints and iClicker questions in lecture because they will show up on the test!

Dr. Mike is very clear about what you need to know. His review sessions are very helpful as are the outlines he sends. It's a flipped classroom so there aren't lectures anymore, but he reviews in the beginning of each class and that's what you need to know. He can be rude at times, but if you speak up  in class and go to him, he can be okay.

Dr. Mike is the best teacher I've had at Tech so far. He clearly outlines what you need to know for tests and his review sessions are extra credit and super helpful so it's an easy boost to your grade. Go to class and study a lot for tests and you'll be golden.

He makes himself widely available to answer questions and hosts review sessions before exams. On the down side, his exams are fairly difficult. They are worded strangely and will cause much self doubt even if you feel confident in your knowledge of the content. One of the more difficult professors for this class.

You will not find a more caring professor than Dr. Mike. He makes himself available almost all the time. So many office hours as well as online office hours and weekly help sessions. The class is definitely not easy but I found the tests doable as long as I did the online study guides thoroughly and went to the test review sessions.

Although Dr. Mike's lectures are kind of boring rushed, he's pretty clear on what the class has to know. He posts study guides before each exam and tells you exactly what you need to know. Lectures cover main points on the  test. If you need more information then he will tell you to look in the book or watch videos. Review sessions are helpful!

He's really boring, put me to sleep a lot. I really only went to class for the random attendance quizzes. His powerpoints are very scattered. He words his exams really weird...but I was able to get a 75 & up on all of them by reading the book.

Dr. Mike is OK, I guess. His tests are easier than Simmons, and homework is a big % of grade, but the concept maps are very vague and take way longer to do than they should. Also, he teaches almost nothing in class compared to Simmons, forcing you to read the book a lot when studying. He's also pretty arrogant, and his review sessions are WORTHLESS

Dr.Mike is a good guy that cares about his students. That being said, his class is challenging because his lectures have very little to do with his test material. I had to rely solely on the textbook to complete the homework and study for his extremely hard tests. If you don't mind reading the book, you can sleep or Facebook through every class.

Mike is a really cool guy. His lectures are really just supplements to the book. I ebayed, facebooked, and stumbled through the somewhat monotonous lectures, and showed up solely because attendance is a minor portion of the grade. Read the book, study it before tests, and this class is a no-brainer.

Bio 1106 is great! We watch lots of cool videos and class is really interesting, don't let his monotone voice scare you off! Tests are average difficulty; go to class, take good notes, and go to review sessions and you'll do fine. Review sessions with the TA are VERY helpful. Simmons for 1105, but Dr. Mike all the way for 1106!
turn. back. now.
switch out while you can, his tests are impossible. i put solid 12 hours of studying into them and still got 50 percents

Dr. Mike's class was a very, very difficult class.  It took me all semester to figure out how to study properly to get a good grade on the test.  In the end though, this class helped me learn new ways of studying and more about bio.  Also, friendliness (meeting/ talking with the professor) does help in terms of curving.  Study his notes more than t

Get out of this class while you still can. Dr. Mike is an extremely nice person, but his teaching style is a recipe for failure. No matter how much you study, you will not be prepared for his tests and you will fail. They are 100% applied questions. Averages are 56% on tests. This class is not only disappointing, but a GPA killer.
If you haven't taken AP bio, then this class is really hard. I didn't like his teaching style at all.
this dude sucks... soo boring, I just woke up from a nap and now i'm leaving this review for him
Interesting teaching style. Spends most of class talking about the pictures in the book and showing related video clips. Tests aren't as easy as other bio teachers.
I didn't like his teaching style...also very boring.  He likes to tie everything together, so test questions can be really confusing.
Awesome
Worst professor ever. He is beyond boring and the class is almost unbearable. Don't take his class unless you don't have any other choice.

GO TO CLASS. and if you can, bring your laptop, write down everything he says because he talks fast and most of the stuff is not in the book. he will give a lot of figures to look at in the book but then will give his personal comments about it, so make sure you write all that down and you will get an A!

Going to class is optional, but I highly suggest going. He helps with examples, and explains everything.  If you know the material he teaches, and how to apply it, then you will do very well in his class.
MONOTONE!! So hard to pay attention in his lectures!!
I hate biology, but that's not the only reason this class bored me to death. Home boy is smart, I just wish he's get out of '95 and stop using an overhead projector.
No Comments

His class is so easy!! I took AP biology and have not attended one class! I only show up for the exams. I got an A on the first exam, a B on the second exam, and a C on the third exam. The genetics section is hard, id recommend going to class before the third exam.
I love Dr. Mike he's great!!!His class is definitely worth your attention!

wow, really quite boring teacher...but could really be a victim of the GLCDB(everyone falls asleep at least once in that room).  Rote memorization is his enemy, so everything he teaches needs to be incorporated into a big picture.  His first three tests were pretty easy but the final is brutal, I have never been so frustrated in my life,way to hard

His tests are not very hard I found his classes boring but still went to all of them and did fine, attend his review sessions before the tests they help and do the questions he gives you on the concept reviews because they are usually on the test and similar to one on the test.

A good teacher. He writes his own notes and test reviews. Tests are easy if you study. This was one of my more interesting lecture classes. He uses online notes, overhead pictures, and some video clips.

Dr. Mike is great; GO TO REVIEW SESSIONS they help a lot. This class is the first 3cred. course I've had an A in. Tests are fairly easy; do the concept reviews he gives to you, and "study" like he tells you to. I learned a lot from this class, which is much more than I can say about chem.
Does have an anger problem but the tests are easy (common sense) and he tried to get everyone interested by bringing in stuff and showing pictures etc.
Semester exams were easy, but I totally bombed the final.  Usually don't have to go to class.  Boring teacher, almost fell asleep many times.  Monotone.  Goes off on tangents.  Boring.

Looks down on students more than any other prof I've seen here. Don't listen to him when he says the mock final will be your final - ours had NONE of the same questions. Cuts out A LOT of important information for the sake of voicing his own opinions. Easy grade, but not worth dealing with this guy.

HUGE ego problem. very short temper. class average on tests is usually a 77. goes on tangents alot. talks about how the good and responsible students don't miss the class before spring break or before easter. very available to receive help from though. pompous but you can deal with it. better than some other bio profs.
Totally gets you involved
Best large lecture class I've had.  He brings lots of stuff to class to help us learn and will meet you any time that works for both your schedules

this guy has a huge ego problem! he comes off as being haughty and is not the most entertaining on top of that. he only as certain times that he does study sessions and if u cant make it to them, then u are not a good, dedicated student. he goes off on tangents and is very short tempered.
Very boring class, but the tests are very easy. He has a very monotone voice that will make you fall asleep faster than Lunesta. Other than that, he knows his stuff and conveys it well.
He has a very sedative effect on me in class, comes off being kind of weird, but is all in all a good teacher. I took AP Bio last year and hardly studied at all and averaged a B+ on the tests.
Great teacher, makes biology interesting and easier to learn
Takes time out to help students out. Tests are pretty easy as long as you study. His class is really boring, it's hard to stay awake.

His class is extremely boring. He has a monotone voice that just lulls you to sleep. His tests are pretty easy. When he's mad, he's scary. He got mad at the last lecture before the final exam.. and made the final exam really hard.
Excellent teacher. Attend review sessions offered! They help a lot!
He also took care of the cool museum at Tech, but its sad because it just got closed down... :(
No Comments
Dr Z gets a bad reputation from harder coding classes like 3444. BIT 3554 with him is unbelievably easy, only 1 lecture per week and 1 quiz per week. Takes like 20 minutes per week to get an A.
She is a very caring professor and easily one of the best at Virginia Tech!

I think people give Dr. Z a bad rep.  He's to the point and treats the class professionally.  Yes it's school but it's a very good preparation for careers.  Only 1 30-question quiz a week, a final, and a short essay on some YT vids are the only grades.  Treats it like he's the CEO of a company.  It's awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Z started off the class with very hostile energy and kept it going throughout the course. His feedback was very minimal and the tone in which he gave it was rude and unprofessional. Extra credit is great though. He expects his students to dedicate all their time to the course so if you have a busy schedule I don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is genuinely rude. He says no emergency warrants an extension and constantly posts passive aggressive announcements about how students procrastinate his projects. Class has 3 assignments and 2 are long coding projects. He tried to say my code was written by AI when it wasn't and almost failed me. Will not help with code either.

Dr Z's was one of the most rigorous classes I have taken. His projects were difficult/required lot of time into your projects. I wasn't even sure Id pass until the last day. If looking for easy professor, don't choose him. If looking to truly learn material and become a more disciplined student consider him but be prepared for sleepless nights.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the rudest professor I have ever had. Talks down on you if you have a simple question. Please for you own good do not take him if you want to have an enjoyable semester. I do not know how Virginia Tech has not fired him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attempts to bring politics into the class. He told us we 100% have to do the homework even hospitalized (YES, HOSPITALIZED). The only good thing about this class was that the extra credit papers he had changed my grade by almost 15%. Avoid otherwise and if possible, take over winter.
Very rude to his students and when you try to ask him a question, he just insults you and doesn't answer his question. Very unprofessional. Course wasn't too bad if you are on top of things.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class with Dr.Z is very easy. There is one 30-question quiz a week and then a 100-question final. He has absolutely zero respect for any of his students and will constantly talk down to you. He makes a big deal about how hard his classes are and then proceeds to give the laziest course I have seen from a professor in my time here.

You'll get a good grade if you read the textbook but his attitude was off putting. I think that while he can be "different" and confusing at times, he's truly a good professor and wants his students to learn. Take this class!
