I strongly recommend not taking this professor if you want to gain something out of this class. I truly don't understand why this man is a professor, especially at a good school like VT. He graded one of my essays then changed the grade later on.

He is a horrendous example of what a VT Professor should be. He is unclear, disrespectful, lazy, and outright unfair. He makes conflicting guidelines for assignments, and if he answers your emails at all it will not clarify any of the questions you have asked. In his own words he has said it is not the professors job to teach, what?

Hands down the worst teacher I have had in my 18 years of being in school, and that is saying something. Biko gives 4 papers for the semester---yeah---that's it and he does not put any effort into his job. Here is an excerpt from an email, "I am not teaching you anything" That's all you really need to know. He is a pathetic excuse for a prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is an awful and unclear professor with no intent to further educate his students. He is lazy and continues to disregard emails by giving 0 instruction. He gives out only 4 papers being 25% of your grade each, uses other professors' syllabuses to conduct his classes. NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS.

Awful. If you think you have handle awful professors, this one is a different breed. I believe he does not speak English clearly, making his communication skills awful. HIS INSTRUCTION ARE UNCLEAR. He constantly changes his syllabus and requirements between different emails. He is awful - worse than awful. He SHOULD NOT be a professor or teacher.

I am going to be completely honest, if you are considering taking a class with him... do not take it. This is not an attack on him as an individual because I do not know him outside the classroom. But his instructions are unclear, he does not respond well to emails/ not responsive at all, and overall his method of teaching is VERY lazy.

Non-accommodating during a pandemic. 4 grades, all 25% of the grade. Not clear at what he wants at all on his paper. Heard he was world-renown but I was unimpressed. Uses other professor's YouTube videos to teach his class. Made us read uninteresting textbook. Would not recommend and will do anything to never take a class taught by him ever again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gives no clear instruction, assigns only paper with no explanation and no material. Just very lazy.
I took professor Agee's class during Spring 2022 for BPHYS. Very enjoyable class, I would highly recommend participating and attending class.

The entire class was focused on the group project. We met once a week and he would help answer any questions. very fair grader, roughly 90% of the class will end with an A. If you put in any bit of effort you will be fine.
Phil is a great professor. He really understands MEP systems and cares whether you learn about it or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is not particularly hard, but he does not have a very concise method of assigning textbook reading, and his grading is extremely difficult. He will take off points for things that are correct, but are not how he wants them to be. This is difficult because he rarely describes his exact expectations.

He wants to see effort from his students. Respect, class engagement, & attendance were expected; performance in class may have influenced grades for assignments (off-task  docked 'final grade' points). Assignments lacked in-depth rubrics, but had basic guidelines; leaving them very open-ended (a good thing).

Horrible teacher. Barely understands the material himself and has horrible grading techniques, not providing clear descriptions of assignments or rubrics. When asked a simple question, fails to answer.

While the class material itself is somewhat unbearable, Ashish makes it difficult by making his expectations very vague. There are no rubrics or clear expectations/requirements for the assignments but nit-picks for detail. He isn't much help even when directly asking him questions, he often leaves you more confused than when you started.

This guy should not be a teacher. He doesn't know the material, cant explain himself, and speaks English poorly. If you have to take this class, be prepared to email him constantly with questions about the assignments, as he does a bad job explaining the criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Ashish is very friendly but by no means should be teaching engineering to freshman, as he is a grad student himself. He does a poor job explaining what must be done on each assignment making the class harder than it should be.
Wouldn't recommend taking this online

First thing I'm going to say is I had to take this course online, which is really bad for me because I'm not good at math and I don't do well with online courses. Dianne did NOT help with my case at all. She never responds to emails and on our zoom meetings at 8am she would just do questions and rush through it. Don't try asking questions she snaps
explanations are so hard to understand, found myself getting confused about content that I had already known how to do.

The only "annoying" thing about the course is requiring homework submissions to be both annotated and submitted via PDF, this isn't super easy for all students to do. Other than that, the Prof. was very accessible via email and for office hours. She had help videos up for all the topics.
Talk to your professor. Agud really cares for her students and her course is online but she still cares for everyone
Dawg take her if you want to fail giving 0s on syllabus quiz is insane

Not the best at explaining the material, I found myself skipping the lecture videos halfway through the course because I would get so lost. This class was pretty easy overall, it's homework heavy with 4-5 assignments a week, but it's doable. She also drops a couple homework grades if you for some reason can't finish your work sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had Ms. Agud back in Spring 2011 and she was one of the better teachers I had. Lots of homework and it was randomly graded for accuracy. She was a tough grader at times. Long tests. I recall her mentioning she usually puts one or two tough questions on her tests and/or quizzes to "separate the A's from the B's" but I always thought they were fair.

As an async. course teacher, her course is okay. The only annoying part is she requires "written hw" which she wants printed and annotated, or written down completely and solved. The hw must be scanned and submitted as a single pdf file, thus requiring a printer and adobe acrobat. There is also a paid software, so overall the class is expensive.

I did Math1025 hybrid, and she's really organized with posting the lecture videos and reminding students of deadlines. As for explaining the content, she's okay at that, could be better. Some stuff I have to figure out myself, but overall she's good. However, not only is there a lot of hw, its time consuming too. Double whammy, beware.

She cares about helping students and offers A TON of office hours. The workload is not bad, and the tests are similar to homework on Pearson, but the tests are short. Also, the online lectures were not detailed enough so I had to self study and repeat the homework a lot.

While the work itself was not difficult, Diane was. My grade was more of a reflection of my poor work ethic, but I will say she was very unnecessarily cold and harsh. I also absolutely do not recommend taking this course online if given the option.

Her lectures are fine she cares about the students but basically allergic to responding to emails. Exams are exactly like the alexs quizzes and hws study those are ur fine. Make a point to keep up with it and dont rush thru it.
I hate math and the class really wasn't too bad. Just study on ALEKS and you'll do good. Very straightforward and offers zoom lectures.
She takes off random points on written homework for absolutely no reason, but her lectures are good.
Does not respond to emails

Self manage your time. Lectures are about 45 minutes to an hour long. Tests are exactly like the quizzes in Aleks. She is stingey about written HW so do those exactly how she does them in lecture videos. You usually have modules due on sunday, Aleks homework and written homeowrk due on Tuesday's, quiz wednesdays, and 4 tests on a thursday.

Horrible course and even worse professor. Hope you don't have an exam for another class overlapping hers because she'll say, "sucks for you." Has resources to help but if you don't have any background in calc then good luck. Course work is completely online but exams are in person. -30/10 do not recommend.

I took this class online for Math 1025 and wish I had taken this class in person. The math emporium is the worst you have to take a bus over there to take any test or exams. I wouldn't have passed this class without signing up for the VT math tutor on YouTube. Please don't take this class unless you have to for your major. It ruined my GPA.

took this course online. the resources provided are horrible and the textbook is one of the worst resources ive ever had to use. the examples are completely different in comparison to the questions asked and it provides little to no guidance for each quiz. the course was described as hyrbid but it was in fact not hybrid. would not recommend.

Empo classes aren't the worst tbh. There's no need to read the textbook pages they have, just pay for VT math tutor and do practice problems until you're comfortable with the material. One quiz a week and a test every 2 weeks. Just manage your time well and it'll be a breeze.

Honestly this class wasn't hard solely because of the teacher. But the Math Emporium. It's off campus so you either have to take the bus or your car. And the online textbook for math emporium is terrible, it has little information and the examples are completely different from what your quiz questions will be.

took points off for ridiculous things
grades hw based on correctness
rude

The professor offered many help opportunities but the main issue with the course is the emporium set-up. Just use VT math tutor and do plenty of practice problems before tests and quizzes and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had to withdraw from this class, but only because the Math Emporium setup is so difficult for me, not because of Diane. I didn't interact with her much as it was an online class, but she held regular help sessions and responded very quickly to e-mails. Again, seeing as the class was online, there wasn't much about her that stuck out to me.
If you're taking a beginner math course, take it at a community college man.

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had

reviews.comment: To put it simply, Diane A Gud professor.

reviews.comment: I never understood math until taking a class with Professor Agud. My only complaint is the amount of work that she assigns but she's usually very understanding if for some reason you need to turn in an assignment late.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: She was very clear and would always ask before she moved on. Group take-home quizzes are a thing so try to be in it with some friends or someone really smart. She is sarcastic and pretty funny. Not your typical robotic calculus professor. Overall, better than most.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very good teacher. She is harder than some, but if you do the homework problems you should be fine

Fantastic professor, probably my favorite at tech. I was lucky enough to have her for two semesters in a row (for 1206 and 2224). She explains material very clearly, has great lecture notes, and is always willing to help. Tests make up ~80% of your grade, but hard test problems usually come from the homework.
Semi-decent lecturing.  Feisty.  Always asks if there are any questions, then doesn't look around to see if there are questions and just keeps teaching.

My least favorite teacher I've ever had here.  Very rude.  She demands mutual respect but accused the whole class of cheating lots of times.  Makes students feel stupid for asking questions.  She makes everyone feel really inferior

She's an AWESOME teacher!CONS: attendance every class,goes thru material kinda fast. PROS:Is clear, asks if we have any questions and answers ALL of them,very understanding, and always available for help. Take her!!!

I had a hard time taking Prof Agud's class at 8am.  Though I had taken Calc II in high school, and recieved AP credit, I decided I should take it again as a refresher and an easy A.  However, the tests at the Empo suck. The questions were not based on the notes at all.  I got an 80.5 test average which counts for 72% of your grade, but got a B

she's very helpful if you take the time to goto her office and ask for help. its kinda hard to grasp the concepts in class because she speeds through the lesson material. however she makes herself available to students to receive help.
She's real good. explains the stuff well and is friendly and nice. has note print outs which are helpful
No Comments
So far, she's my favorite math teacher!

Prof Agud is always really helpful. She does explain things pretty well. And she gives you her notes to print out so you don't have to spend your time copying.  If you need help GO TO OFFICE HOURS, she is always very great with explaining stuff to you - and will help you on quizzes if you ask!
No Comments
Not very  helpful to the students. Tough grader. Doesn't help much with the project either.  Pace of the class is  fast. Intimidating. Avoid if you can.
Not a very good person as an academic advisor. Very manipulative. Exploits his students. If you're an international student, avoid at all costs. His classes are easy.
is chill teacher just the other day brought us cake for the fun of it and dont care wat u do as long  as u get it done
is a chill teacher as long as you do something he dosent  usually care
Prof. Agah is the best professor of VT.

Dr. Adams was one of the sweetest professors that I have had at Virginia Tech. She shows a lot of care and respect for her students and wants everyone to succeed. She also offers so much extra credit so it's very easy to do well in her class.

Dr. Adams was very nice and caring. She was very understanding and shes passionate about the course. The class itself wasn't very interesting but she really does try to make it interesting so students still pay attention. No textbooks, ngl don't remember reading in that class, and tests aren't the worst, just look thru anything given to you.

I took Psych-1004, and it was online. Super easy. Videos were provided that you had to watch and take notes on, and she provided texts too that were sometimes long. Overall, the class was really easy to understand. Exams were all application-based based so learn vocabulary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams is absolutely amazing. I took her research methods class in the fall and am now in her Psych of Personality class because I really like the way she lectures. Her exams are all fairly straightforward, her lectures are interesting, and if she feels like the class needs it she provides extra credit opportunities. Def take her if you can! :)
Not a hard class, there are in class attendance activities on certain days. Also, the tests are not bad as long as you study what is on the study guide

it you just go to class you'll nearly ace the class. homeworks are simple if you paid attention in lecture and she gives out study guides for all the exams... if you use them, exams are relatively easy.

Dr. Adams includes pop-culture references and videos often in her lectures to make them more engaging. Class discussions are frequent, including both class-wide discussions and in small groups. One day a week is dedicated entirely to discussion. Attendance is mandatory to get the participation points (which make up a huge portion of your grade).

DO NOT take Sandu as your 4104 teacher. Watching paint dry would be more productive than his lectures at teaching you this material. He reads off slides, doesn't explain anything in great detail, and has not ONCE solved a word problem (the kinds of problems on tests and homeworks) in class. All he does is lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. I have never gone to this website to rate a professor until last semester of my senior year taking 4104 with Sandu. Uses stolen slides from Princeton, which he reads in monotone; he doesn't even understand the course's material. That should say enough. Doesn't have office hours; doesn't respond to email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had at VT. He speaks very quietly and brings no energy to class. He could also be sarcastic when students asked for clarification. Very few resources outside the textbook. If you came in even a min. late, he would make you wait outside for 10 min. so all the late students could enter at the same time.

Pros:
Professor is very knowledgeable. Explains at a low pace.

Cons:
Can't hear / understand his accent to certain level.
The assignments are extremely hard with a very short deadlines.
Too many assignments.
The lectures are not recorded, so if you miss one, you can't do homeworks.

I took Discrete with Mr. A, and he was chill. He gives extra credit on homeworks, and the tests aren't too bad. Very proof heavy class, which I personally hate (proofs suck). Make sure to read a lot of the textbook, which is free and updated by him.

He was a good professor and offered some extra credit on homework assignments. His lectures were engaging, and attendance wasn't mandatory, though I would recommend going to avoid falling behind. I would recommend reviewing the notes and homeworks to study for the test. Overall, I thought he was great and I enjoyed the class.
He is a great professor to be with assuming you know the course before or you're really good in calculus. But his lectures involved very less examples so tests were really tough.

Mr. A is a great person but not a great teacher. Lectures consisted of him running through PDFs and left students very confused. He just talks through notes in a way I'm sure he understands but not so much for the students. He's very flexible with grading and deadlines but I found the class difficult due to the lack of actual teaching in lectures.
he is nice, but strict and tests make up 80% of the class so beware of that.
nice dude, tests are 80% of your grade and there are only 4. Great lecturer, very knowledgeable and clearly interested in the subject matter. Not the easiest class but that is not any fault of his.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Adjerid was a great teacher. He taught linear algebra like they should (wrote down all the theorems and explained them). Tests were very fair if you studied. Participate in the class and he will like you. He is a very knowledgeable person in the field of linear algebra.

this professor made the class miserable . it was difficult to understand where he was going with his words and what he was trying to say. he would often contradict himself, and say things that are wrong. he would never let you finish your question and would answer something completely different
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a pretty good professor and you could tell he was really into linear algebra and was really passionate. His lectures consisted of him writing notes and examples on his iPad which were clear most of the time. He really does love questions. Sometimes his lectures got a little confusing and some terminology I feel he could have explained more.

Slimane is a good professor for Intro to Linear Algebra. He is a fairly good humored Elderly Algerian man who knows a lot about his area of expertise and always thoroughly explains the material. He loves questions, and although he is a tough grader, he definitely makes sure that everyone understands why they got marked off and how to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Moves quickly through slides, making it hard to follow.  Introduces formulas without clear explanation.  As a result, it's difficult to grasp the concepts, and many students stopped attending. Tests are fair and resources help, but his teaching style feels vague.  Overall not the worst, but far from the best.  I enjoyed deforms but hate this class.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures suck, he runs through notes really fast and doesn't really show you how to solve problems just talks briefly about the concepts. That being said, there is good extra credit and the tests are not super difficult. If you anticipate skipping class often might be a good teacher because the worst part of his class was definitely the lecture

Good prof, kinda hard class. Buy the extra credit, its worth it. Go to lectures bc he hints the exam questions. Exam questions come from the practice exam and in class problems. Homework was just busy work.

His lectures are not helpful at all because he doesn't actually solve problems. He just shows them on the screen and says he'll post the slides so you can look at it later. He does give a lot of extra credit on tests which helps your grade a lot. You can tell he cares about people understanding he just doesn't really know how to teach.

I had him for deforms (ESM 2204) which is not listed as an option at the time of this review. 
Good: Caring. Pretest activity will significantly boost your score, and the content on it is often VERY similar to exams. Wants students to succeed.
Not great: His penmanship and lecture style gave little motivation to attend, but again nice guy.

He was fine, 7/10. He was accessible outside of class which was nice and on a personal level he would bring his little son to class which was really cool to see. HOWEVER, homework was graded hard which was frustrating. He also would not post homework answers or make practice tests which sucked. Exams ended up being easy so study and you'll be fine.

Goes through lots of example problems, usually will take a problem straight off the slides or practice test for the test, which helps. However, he's not the best at explaining the concepts behind the math, which can make following the lectures difficult. Does provide extra credit/curve for all tests, which is helpful.

Gives substantial extra credit but doesn't waterfall which makes test grades feel like luck as small mistakes at the beginning can lead to -20 points. Somewhat boring lectures and can be hard to understand at first. On the other hand, he was accessible, provided valuable info and examples, and cared about student success, just ask him questions!

Practice tests are very similar to what is on the actual exams however I feel like he's a pretty tough grader for them, does try and help students during exams but can be misleading. Accent and handwriting can also make this difficult to understand during lecture

Dr. Aidi's lectures were somewhat hard to follow at times, but that's his only real downside. He's accessible outside of class, the homework isn't bad, the tests are similar to the practice tests and gives extra credit on each test. He runs through examples during class which can help but doesn't explain the concepts extremely well.

Aidi is quite boring during lecture and will run through practice problems without really explaining the concepts behind solving them. Gives tons of extra credit and is very clear about what content to expect on exams. Helpful during office hours. Overall very unique guy - he always seems like he's about to burst out laughing for some reason.

Aidi was very boring. I took his class from 5-6:15 and he wanted to leave just as much, if not more, than all of us. He just goes through the slides and you have to zoom along with him. Sometimes hard to understand his accent and handwriting. He grades pretty fairly on tests and gives extra credit for all of them.
Tough grader but curves in the end. Most tests are like his practice tests. In class he does go fast.

He did lots of examples in class, but he didn't explain the concepts. He solved problems in silence and asked if there were questions. He moves fast and doesn't care if the class understands. The tests aren't curved and is harder than the homework. The people who did well in his class, are the quick learners or who already understand the concepts.

Very cool guy. Always has this smirk on his face that's pretty funny. He gave me a deep understanding in Statics and is a good visual teacher. He also explains how the things we learn are going to affect us in deforms

Nice guy but seemed to explain everything in the most difficult possible way. He goes so fast and has high expectations. Very hard to learn from. My other friends in other statics classes learned way more than I did. I'd try to find another professor, but if you're stuck he won't make your life suck.
Professor Murphy was a decent teacher but I will say that her class in basically inaccessible outside of the classroom. If you miss a class their isn't any easy way to see what you missed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you like to write or just need a pathway, definitely take her for creative writing. Only a portfolio and weekly Friday assignments. If you hate public speaking, wouldn't recommend because you do have to read out your writing or participate in discussions in class.

Dr. Murphy is fantastic and cares about students. If you take this class, make sure you at least care about the subject somewhat. As long as you put forth effort and show some passion, you'll have no trouble at all in this class. Everything is discussion-based, so it's a very comforting environment to be in. I'm minoring in Creative Writing now!

Prof. Murphy is an amazing professor and person. She's super caring, but she does get very frustrated if you don't participate in class. Come to class, give your peers clear feedback, do enough of the reading to answer a question or two in class and you'll be chillin. She doesn't make you write to a certain word count for your papers which I loved!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Murphy is great; as long as you try, you will do well. However, attendance and participation are mandatory.

She literally bases her "participation" grade off of the last 2 weeks. Showed up and spoke up in class all semester but missed a couple classes in the last couple of weeks (burnout and finals) and got a 60/100 which brought my grade down to a B+. Really annoying.
She helped me change my grade when it came down to the final week. She's really nice and understanding

She really wanted to get to know her students and provided us a lot of content that was helpful for the class. She was funny and was reasonable something came up and could offer extensions. If you come to class and participate, you will do good and pass this class.

Aileen is awesome! This class is great for writers & non-writers alike. Whether you're passionate about creative writing or just doing Pathways she works with you and sets you up for success. She really pushes you to find your own voice and make writing work for YOU. If you put in the work and actually show some effort it should be an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is such a caring professor! She truly wants you to do well in class. I've turned things in late and still got an A. Almost every Friday you have to write 250 words about whatever she gives but it's super easy. We had to write a poem, a second poem, a nonfiction short read, fiction, or whatever else quick read. Just get your work done.

I had Dr. Murphy for my Community Writing class and she was spectacular throughout the entire class. I was sick constantly through the semester that I took this class, and she allowed me to remediate assignments I had missed resulting from this. She is very helpful in refining our lesson plans and conducts class in a very organized, meaningful way.

Aileen is probably the coolest prof you'll have this semester. She's super chill and really just wants to see you succeed and use your own unique voice. Had her for creative writing and was the only writer in the class (everyone else was there for pathways) and she managed to individualize the experience for all of us, helped me work on my passion!

I had professor Murphy for my intro to creative writing class online in a synchronous format. She is extremely caring and overall just a great teacher. As long as you turn in the weekly assignments and write your pieces for class on time for the workshops, you will receive an A.

Absolutely loved Mrs. Murphy, and I hope to have her again. I took her Intro to Creative Writing Class, and she made me want to minor in Creative Writing (which I now plan on doing). She is kind, caring, respectful, and genuinely cares about the well-being of her students. If you do the work, participate, and show up for class, you'll get an A.
Definitely the best english teacher I have ever had. She is so awesome!

Great professor!  She is very helpful and interested in your writing and how to improve it.  Peer workshop, good discussion. Just participate and you'll do fine. Great class; great professor!  Wish I could take it again!
Be prepared to work hard and be challenged. Not easy, but worth it. Extremely approachable for help, but she is a stickler for details. I learned a lot, but really worked hard for the grade.
I would not take prof akoma as my instructor at all, stay away if you can.

I definitely think Professor Akoma is a stickler when it comes to work. Shes very meticulous about grading and making sure assignments are submitted on Thursday; yet doesnt submit weekly grades until almost 2 weeks later. This is an online course, and Ive never had a professor be so picky with everything. Id avoid it if possible or get another prof

Professor Akoma tries to overcompensate for the fact that it is an online class by making really strict regulations/requirements about everything.  Overall a really annoying class. I would have dropped it if I hadn't already expended too much energy on the forum postings.

For an online course, there is little room for flexablity. In this I mean you are required to do 3 postings online a week to an online blog. Each response is read and critiqued by her. You must post once on thurs once on fri or sat & once by sun. Dont take this particular class unless you have to. STAY AWAY!

I took the bookbinding section, and it was one of the most fun classes I've taken! Amelia is truly one of the kindest people I've ever met! I had some heavy family stuff going on throughout the semester, and she could not have been more understanding or flexible. As a non-art major/minor, I HIGHLY recommend taking an art class while you're here!

She clearly has a passion for art and does her best to cultivate that same passion in her students. Her handmade books class was way more enjoyable than I had expected, and her creativity and love for art are infectious.

She is an awesome art teacher. She takes care to make sure every student understands the material and goes out of her way to help students who need inspiration. She is very sweet and her class is always enjoyable!

Such a genuinely kindhearted person who truly cares about her students! There are lots of projects but she is very understanding and often gives extensions. Amelia has a passion for art that is inspiring and infectious. She is a great teacher and really opened my eyes and gave a lot of great feedback.

Had for 3D art and design. Very sweet teacher, but doesn't seem to get the material across as I believe she hopes to. I found lectures dragging on. I also felt like she was upset and could not demonstrate her actual feelings (slightly passive aggressive). Made us do things I felt were irrelevant, such as leaving class and unimportant projects.
Sweetest and most caring professor I know. Very understanding if you have to miss classes. I 10/10 recommend if you get her!! I had her for drawing for non-majors and she was amazing

An absolute sweetheart and a joy to have had as a teacher. Ms. Salisbury cares so much about her students and is very accepting and easy to talk to. Makes PowerPoints for all material, no quizzes or tests, and her love for the subject is infectious. Gives good feedback and fun projects, just remember to put in the work.

I loved this class! I am trying to take it again. Amelia is the best! She just wants you to put in effort and try to improve. I love painting so much more after taking this class. I took it with my friend who is an amazing painter and we got the same grade. You don't need any experience. Easy A. So relaxing. Best class I've taken in college
Amanda is kind and genuinely cares about her students. She makes this class very approachable, and if you follow her instructions and work with her you will get a good grade.

she's cool but the content of the course is extremely overbearing when overlapping with my other classes. it took far too much time out of my schedule for me to get any kind of enjoyment from it. i didn't find the material interesting at all, and most of the time i was just stressed about getting it done because it felt like there was way too much

I took Amanda's ENGL 1106 course in the Spring of 2025 as an engineering student just fulfilling a general education requirement, but I can say that she was incredible. She was super caring and understanding that most people in the course were out of major. She preffered we call her Amanda and there was a clear mutual respect between everyone.
