reviews.comment:
good
very very very very good

Amazing professor, best case scenario for ENGL 1106. Gives new meaning to "you can get an A if you try," Gives personalization to how you're graded, but doesn't make things unbearable. Engaging classes, and she makes you interested in learning. Not much else to say but shes definitely the best englihs teacher I've ever had.

Amanda is a kind and a respectful professor. Although her "grading contract" requires you to do three extra credit options to get an A, she was extra patient when I came to her office hours regarding questions about my research paper, even though she went over the concerns in class.

Amanda is a very professional and caring professor. She is often lenient if you communicate beforehand with her and show that you are really going through something. The only thing I dislike is grading contract for projects. Because if you do the minimum requirements you will get an 86%, so if you want more, you have to do extra to boost your grade

Professor However, do not think that's a bad thing.  These activities add up to making your projects easier.  Her grading contracts are clear.  You can decide on what grade you are looking for from this class and then follow the path to complete the extra items to earn that grade.  One of the best English teachers I have ever had.

Amanda is amazing. It's very easy to reach her via office hours or email, and she is willing to work with you if you need extensions, etc. Her grading criteria is the clearest I've ever experienced from a professor, making it so easy to know what grade to expect, and know what I could do to bring my grade up if needed.

Such an amazing professor! She gives extra credit opportunities to get a higher grade on your papers and projects and that helped so much and I ended off the class with a 100. Marzolf is so sweet and understanding, and she cancels class the day before a break or extends deadlines if needed or if you ask her.
She was very understanding and flexible. Although attendance is mandatory, the course load is not heavy. She also makes it very easy for you to get an A in the class.

She is a great professor and is more than willing to work with you throughout the course, so that you can get the grade you want. The class was also not to difficult, and the in class activities helped to guide you through the major projects throughout the course.

Professor Marzolf is amazing! She doesn't expect all that much of you, her class is easy because she explains everything so well and is helpful outside of class as well. She is super responsive to emails and gives very clear feedback on drafts of papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Amacher is a very kind professor. The class is interesting and relevant, but the material is difficult and you are only graded on "quizzes" (basically mini tests). Gives out a healthy amount of extra credit just for coming to class consistently, so it pays to show up.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: extra credit when attendance is low. A is an 85 or higher. hes funny. and its not apart of tests or hw but in lectures he ties in examples from other econ classes to make you realize how everything plays out in the bigger picture and how all different types of economics work out(none of that is tested) highly recommend as an econ elective.

the material can be difficult at times but is generally manageable. he is amazing at teaching, which really helps. the curve really is killer and will boost your grade by up to 20 points if you do the extra credit quiz and just show up to class - it's worth it anyway bc he's hilarious. lectures were applicable to real life and very interesting.
Great guy and will help in office hours. Don't be too intimidated though he's a good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's an awesome professor - his lectures are really funny, but the course content and tests and stuff are really tough. He's more than willing to help you until you understand what he's talking about. He's incredibly knowledgeable about his subject, and I'm very glad I ended up in his class.

Amacher was an entertaining professor.  He told the same stories all the time, but did a decent job of engaging us.  Though it was a high level econ class, he had a killer curve that added up to 15 grade points to your final grade, just for coming to class.
Engaging lectures with demonstrations. Very available outside of class, especially during office hours. Exams are no joke and a large proportion of your grade, so you will need to study.

Morris was very condescending, laughed at tests turned in while others were still taking the exam & tested/quizzed on material she briefly mentioned in class. I only missed one class, read the textbook pre/post lecture & would study a week for her exams and still score D's. She tricks you instead of testing to see if you understand the material.

Morris is very intelligent, but expects too much of her students. She is condescending and egotistical, which is clearly shown in lecture, which makes her very,VERY unapproachable. She knows the material well, but is not able to convey it clearly, which makes class TOUGH. That said, she gives quite a bit of extra credit, which was much appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She did a awful job explaining material that was going to be on the test. A lot of times she would omit to explain something that was on the quiz or test so the TA had to quickly explain it before the quiz. Definitely go to all the recitations if you want to learn how to do the material for the test.

The lectures were online, and we did the homework/problem sets in class. Dr. Morris is one of the best chemistry faculty I have ever had at VT and she sets herself apart by diligently answering any students questions, or changing their frame of mind on a topic.

Go to class/review sessions. HW every week. Quizzes each Friday other than test weeks. Usually a quiz in recitation during test week. Tests are very hard but given around 4 hrs to take them. Usually takes test questions from examples in book/end of chapter problems. The class is difficult. She drops a test and 4 quizzes.
Really good history professor. Is a lot of reading though. Honestly just get some audio books so you can listen to the books while youre working on other stuff. Really caring, great lectures.

I am currently taking a Vietnam War class with Prof. Demmer. She is AMAZING. She cares so deeply for her students and is so understanding and fair. Not only that, her lectures are probably the most interesting I've had in college. I look forward to going to her classes.

Professor Demmer is great. I had her for recent American history and she did an amazing job teaching every day. The only homework is reading and the reading quizzes and those are usually on primary or secondary sources. There were two papers and they were long but manageable. She did a great job teaching every class and making it interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Demmer is very passionate about the classes she teaches. There are lectures every class, that students should take notes on. The lectures are informative and helpful. She cares about all of her students and offers many office hours. The workload is not bad, and if you take good notes this class should be an easy A.

Very strict and unprofessional professor. He claims that he cares about you as students, but actions speak louder than words. He doesn't grade fairly, no error carried forward. The final is 45% of your grade, 5% homework. Extremely messy notes. Doesn't post lecture slides or recordings. He brags about people dropping his class.

TL;DR: Don't take Nain unless absolutely necessary. 
He's friendly and claims he is harsh because of "tough love", but the way he does it is unnecessary. Mandatory lectures. No notes posted in Canvas. Extremely tough exams that are too long for 50 minutes. No formula sheet. No curve. Final grade is 50% midterms (5 total), 45% final. Good luck!

Every trait you can possibly think of that could make an inconvenient professor, Nain does it. Weekend lecture, empty canvas, no office hours, at some point just stopped making slides for notes. Definitely dependent on how you learn and how much effort you are willing to put in, but if you can get a different prof, save yourself a lot of trouble.
Great lectures. Managed to make thermodynamics an interesting subject. Did not allow formula sheets on tests. I was initially very intimidated but I ended up doing ok and I learned a lot in the end

I had a horrible time in Prof Nain's class. every time your absent he takes away 5% of your finial grade. also the final was 45% of the grade and didn't let you use a cheat sheet. Tests were 15-20 question in a 50 minute slot (Hard Themo problems that take 5-10 minutes each). Overall this professor enjoyed embarrassing his students and was mean

Hes a tough professor no doubt.But unlike many vt profs he makes an effort to teach and help you learn the material. 95% of your grade is tests so get a study group asap.Dont skimp office hours, the TAs are geniuses.His grading style doesnt work for college but he will ingrain the knowledge in your  head.I appreciate his class AFTER having taken it
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midterms were 50% of the grade, the final was 45%. No curve. Nice enough person and the lectures were helpful, but this did not offset the difficult tests and final making up most of the grade with a refusal to curve or provide ways to remedy grades. He failed a lot of people that probably should not have failed. Take Nain to nuke your in major GPA

Lazy teacher, very unwilling to help. Disappeared multiple times during the semester, once for 2 straight weeks to go to Japan. To "make up" for the 2 weeks he would be gone, he held two 5-hour lectures on back-to-back Saturdays (which he refused to record). Tests were made and administered by TAs. Had 2 exams in the same week.

Lectures were fairly comprehensible, but tests were unreasonably difficult, with the final being 45% of the grade as well. Also encourages cheating by allowing computers for tables instead of printing them out on the tests.
Overly hard and believed in memorization, claimed his laziness was really him just weeding us out.

Lectures are awesome and very engaging and I learned so much from them. Nain goes over concepts multiple times and does a ton of practice problems in class. If you study hard and work all the extra practice problems that he gives, you will be okay, but exams are difficult and don't expect a curve.

It's true, Dr. Nain is an extremely hard professor. But because he held his students to a higher standard, we ended up learning really well. The final is 45% of the grade, which is kind of offset by what a cool professor he is. Office hours are amazing. Very fun to be in class, despite the tedious subject. Take him if you want to learn thermo well.

Dr. Nain teaches a really hard class but is an amazing lecturer. He cares about his students and can seem hard at times but he is overall pretty solid. Be prepared to have no equation sheet and the final is worth 45%.

This professor definitely doesn't know how to teach online. He sends a link to school email for every zoom class. He does not record lectures. He does not post notes. He does not post practice tests. He does go 15 min over class time every lecture. Test are far too long to complete. Final worth 45% of grade. Do not take Nain unless you like pain!!!
The kindest lady, 4 exams lowest dropped !

Professor Chekili is incredibly nice and understanding. She is a great teacher and although the classes are only lectures, the tests are really easy. There are 4 exams and she will drop your lowest exam score. There are also a couple in-class activities that are very easy and overall, the class was great.

She only has four tests and the lowest test grade gets dropped. Her questions on the test can get a bit confusing at times but if you ask her to clarify she will do so. The lectures and slides are all online and easily accessible and it's clear what's going to be on the test thanks to her study guides. She's really nice!

This was Professor Chekili's first semester officially teaching I believe, and she's off to a good start. It's pretty much all graded on attendance and 4 tests, and she drops the lowest test grade. A few really small homework assignments and extra credit opportunities are sprinkled in as well. She's very kind and helps out if needed.

She seemed like she was pretty new based off her teaching style but her exams were super similar to the slides. Slides are posted and there are only 4 exams and the lowest one is dropped. She randomly takes attendance on days where there's discussions in class but I wouldn't worry too much about it. No outside of class work and overall clear stuff.

Shes a great professor. All work can be completed based off her lectures, can be very time consuming but if you are able to do well on them you will be fine for the actual exams. Labs can take somewhat long but aren't very hard if you have a good group.

A lot of people say this course is difficult, but it's really not. Before exams, go over the assignments and understand the process of the questions and you'll be just fine. The professor is super kind to always willing to help or give extensions if you need, you just need to ask.

Tests and homework aren't that bad. She talks to students like middle schoolers and wastes a lot of time in class by wanting us to almost guess what is on the slides before she shows us. She makes the class more confusing than it needs to be. Just zone out in class and then go over the slides later and it makes way more sense.

Homeworks really aren't that hard, just do them ahead of time so you can get help from her or a TA. Labs can be painfully long if you don't have a good group. Also do your field notebook before it's due so you can get help if needed. Understand how to use equipment for the field exam. Redo homework and extra practice to prep for midterm and final.

It's still organic chemistry, but she explains everything really well. I like that she explains background behind things we learn, that while we don't need to the exam it gives us context on what the point of learning the thing is. Speaking of, she is very clear about what will and will not be on the exam which I really appreciate.

She is the best! Go to her office hours the minute you feel behind, ask for help on the homework, and use the grading method to your benefit. She grades very lenient, so ask for help and understand the homework to do well on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Santos is the best! She took a difficult subject and turned it into a very interesting, easy-to-process class. She is very passionate about Pchem and it shows in her lectures. Most of the grade is exams, but she tends to take questions from homeworks and lectures to put into exams. 10/10 recommend taking her classes!

Professor Santos is a fantastic teacher. If your goal is to understand the material, she does a fantastic job of explaining things from the ground up. However, her grading system is quite harsh(one hw drop, little to no curve on exams.) If you're looking to take organic in preparation for the MCAT, Dr. Santos is probably your best bet,
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had her for Ochem 2, Overall great professor, Explained things well, exams were always fair (everything could be found on slides for exams and hw). Also very easy to reach and genuinely cares about her students. Overall 10/10 would recommend

This is my second time taking OChem 2, and I have enjoyed her class sooo much more. She teaches and explains things really clearly and has realistic and balanced exams based on the material.  Super kind and really engaging in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Truly the best professor I've ever had, she said she wants to make ochem a less daunting class and she did just that. The homework matches the test and its only a few problems/week. She provides ppts and annotating them was the only studying I needed to do because she explained everything so well. I did so poorly in gen chem and this was sm easier.

THE BEST OCHEM/CHEM PROFESSOR EVER! First day she said her goal was to make ochem less scary and she did just that. Test are just like HW always willing to work with you tons of office hours. I cannot recommend her enough she made a 5 pm class enjoyable. I never thought I would love Ochem but it was my favorite class this semester.

Absolute queen! She is very accessible outside of class and wants her students to succeed. She is new at Tech, so there are not many things to practice with until she can make them but has many TAs. Overall lovely and has a great way of explaining things.
Test heavy but the tests weren't too bad. Mostly exactly what we did in class. He would post online notes of everything so it made the class pretty easy.

This professor is amazing and truly cares about his students. Lectures can be long, but he works hard to help everyone understand the material. Homework can be time-consuming but really helps you grasp the material. The review packet is VERY helpful for test preparation. Attend class and do the work, and you'll do well.

His attitude was unprofessional at times, and disrespectful, making personal comments even during an exam. Every student can have their moments outside of the class that can impact their grades and attendance, but I don't think anyone deserves to be treated like that. I was very disappointed. It affected my confidence and motivation to participate.

Had him for 2214 (diff eq). One of the best math professors at VT. You can tell he really cares about his students, always encourages students to stay engaged and participate. Prints out notes, and tests are similar to homework/notes. Inspires students with advice. Talks about how he "appreciates our presence." Don't watch a movie my dear students.
Good afternoon my dear students. Top 3 differential equations professor and he's not number 2 or 3. The GOAT.
Poor teacher. Expects students to know the concept immediately after teaching it without explanation. Laughs when students ask questions.

Had him for diff eq (2214). Best math professor I've had at VT. He prints out and distributes notes, HWs, and test reviews for you. The HWs can be long but they genuinely help. Tests are very fair and are similar to HWs and reviews. He can be condescending at times but not on purpose. Definitely cares about his students and wants them to do well.

(for differential EQTS not 1225) He prints out annotated notes for the whole class, and the written homework is graded pretty leniently. The online math homework is a pain, but the course is otherwise very straightforward. One downside is he can get very frustrated when people don't participate in class, but other than that he's a solid teacher.

Best 1225 prof at VT. Super nice and caring and always willing to help and loves when you ask questions. Accent and handwriting are hard to understand at first but will quickly understand them. Best way to get an A is to go over notes after every class and go to his office hours. He always wants to help and wants his students to do well.

His exams are WAY HARDER than the examples given in lectures and homework, He never discusses the type of questions that are going to be on midterms. You have NO IDEA on how to prepare for them. 

Also, he has a pretty strong accent, which was even worse since I took an online class of his and the sound quality was bad.

His lectures were too the point, but hard to follow at times. I personally found the questions and format on the midterms confusing but with some studying I was able to do better. While I would not want to take his class again, I could have worked harder in the beginning of the semester.
dont choose him
terrible and couldn't do final because he barely taught anything on it I do not recommend and it was all on zoom and his notes were too hard to read

Stopped bothering to attend lectures after week 5. Lectures were proof based in a non proof class which made understanding concepts impossible. Expect to teach yourself from the textbook which is fortunately really good. Grades also take forever, one homework assignment took over 2 months to get a grade.

Drop if able, get ready to lock in if not

Was not very good at teaching the material and would take a long time to grade anything whether that was the homework or the tests. He mainly taught the material in proofs making basic definitions hard to understand and sometimes introduced irrelevant information.

Was not good at teaching. Only explained new topics with proofs. Accent is really difficult to understand. Very unclear and last minute with communication. Waited until two days before the final exam to respond to my emails about when and where the final exam was.

Very difficult to understand with his heavy accent, especially over zoom. Generous curve but burns through subjects quickly. Do the homeworks and make sure you understand them, there are only 9 of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable, willing to help students and answer questions. Does not return homework promptly and is sometimes difficult to understand under his accent.
recommended
highly recommended
No Comments

Lectures are slightly on the boring side, but content (CMDA 3605, wasn't listed as an option) is straightforward and easy to understand. Very nice and helpful, obviously wants to see students succeed. Homework is somewhat tedious, but it and exams are fairly graded. Projects are essentially just large homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very passionate, helpful with material, and a joy to learn from, but the course was extremely heavy (spent approx 15 hours on homework, 5 hours studying a week). A quiz or test every week with pretty tough grading, but overall grades feel deserved on effort. Would highly recommend as a professor, but not recommend this course

she gave amazing lectures, explained and answered questions very well. we had written assignments once a week in homework groups. webassign was OPTIONAL. I didn't even buy the textbook. tests had a mix of conceptual and solving questions. be careful bc sometimes she wants a sort of proof-style answer. offered 2% grade boost if 95% does spot surveys
Genuinely cares about the students understanding, extremely nice and approachable. Explained things clearly and precisely. Not had for math 2204 but 2214, linear algebra.
She taught the class in a very easy-to-understand way. Was super kind. Can't ask for a better professor.

Great teacher, tough class. I struggled in the class which wasn't due to her, but the concepts and how the course was laid out. This course is test-heavy - 4 tests (3 exams and the final), each 20% of your grade. Very friendly and caring as she wants her students to succeed. After the final, I had a 72.2% in the class and she bumped it up to 73%.

She is a very nice and caring professor that is accessible outside of class during office hours and will help to understand concepts.  The class for me was extremely hard to grasp despite a well performance in the previous calc classes, but that is not going to change with any other professor.

Math 2405H and 2406H are difficult for someone with no background in Calc 3, LA, or Diff Eq, but she did a great job going through concepts and their applications. Weekly homework took about 10 hours but was more difficult than lengthy. She is always willing to help outside of class if you talk to her in advance. Fun application projects too!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Professor Rodriguez for both MATH 1225 and MATH 1226. My advice is to always go to office hours. It will help a ton and she is always willing to help. Before tests, she held review sessions. Make sure to go to these! They are a great way to prepare. She is a fair grader and her tests can be tough if you don't do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Andre Jones cares about his students and will always help if you ask. He is very knowledgeable on topics and he gives good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Jones was a great professor! I had him for ENGL 1105 and his class was very easy! The good thing is he's a chill grader and as long as you put in effort into the essays you should be able to get a B at the lowest.  Because of Professor Jones, I now actually enjoy English and have been able to embellish my creativity within my writing.
Great teacher, with a flexible grading criteria.

Dr. Dre is an amazing teacher!! He gives great feedback and accepts late work anytime. There are 4 big grading projects and the rest are discussion posts. Very easy to get an A, as long as you do your work. I sometimes missed his class, which is OKAY because he doesn't care for attendnace as long as you get work done.
I loved his class was very fun and got very informative feedback!!!

Professor Jones is the GOAT!!! He's super chill and fun to vibe with. Also, he always adds extra office hours so that people in his class understands what the project is about. Overall, I definitely recommend him as an English professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing. would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Andre is an extremely lenient and understanding professor, who is easily accessible. If you were to turn in assignments late, or not be as participating in class, he was still interactive and gave good feedback in assignments. Attendance is not mandatory, although there are daily activities. He is someone I would recommended to many.
He is the absolute goat. Super chill, funny, and is not too strict of a grader. Allows lots of extra time for assignments to be turned in without losing credit for late submissions.

Prof. Jones was an amazing professor. He was very caring, everything was relaxed, and he's very understanding and nice. His essays are challenging but there are only a few of them, and he's a lenient grader and gives outstanding feedback. Overall would recommend him for anyone, especially freshman and/or those who aren't strong at writing.

Great guy! Haven't attended any classes except the first and last two. All my work was late still he gave full credit for it. He is literally the best prof there. His classes r fun and he tries his best to give us a good grade and indulge the class. Save urself and drop any other prof for him. Take his class even if it's an 8am

Professor Jones was amazing and very understanding throughout the semester. Gives great feedback and asks meaningful questions in class. Honestly, a pretty simple class if you put in the effort and do the assignments each week.
He is absolutely one of the best professors you could have. His class isn't mandatory, but going really isn't bad. He's a funny guy who just wants everyone to get a good grade.
Great professor, great man, would take again.
Great dude! Genuinely cares about his students and their growth/success. Constantly available whenever you need help or just want someone to look over your work. Highly recommend.

Dr Jones was probably one of my favorite teachers I've ever had. He's a chill guy who isn't too tough on grading (as long as you get your work done) and is very understanding. He made English, a subject I'm not good at nor do I like, something I could look forward to with the discussions we'd have in class. I 1000% recommend him.

Professor Jones is super laid back but also goes over the material well. There are only a few major writing assignments, and they are not graded hard. If you go to class, put in a little effort on your writing, and turn things in on time, you will get a guaranteed A. He is also a good person to chat with before class and is a really cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great professor

I loved Andre, he is a very easy grader and very understanding towards students. The course itself is writing heavy more so than reading, but he is flexible on deadlines. He clearly explains what he is looking for in terms of assignments. I can't wait to have him again next semester!
he's awesome sauce

Prof. Jones is a very caring and honest professor. Going to his lectures was never a chore, though very often the lectures were canceled this semester (I think that was a this-semester-only kind of deal though). All assignments are discussion posts, which take up to 15 minutes (easy), or writing projects (3 total). Overall, easy & I'd recommend!

I loved this professor. He was very clear on assignments and provided any clarification needed. He is very sweet and understanding. He will accept late work for full points and if you put effort into your assignments, he will give you a 100. I recommend this course with this professor. Best English class I have ever taken.
Best English Professor I've ever had. Genuine guy who wants to see you succeed.
Mr. Jones Jr. has been my favorite professor by far while attending University. He is very respectful to all of his students and gives amazing feedback on papers.

he was definitely the most laid back professor i've had and he cared and respected his students a lot more than the average teacher would. his teaching environment was comfortable and he always gave helpful feedback on any questions i had. there were few big projects that were a little stressful, but not too bad.

He is a great teacher and person, you can tell he cares for each of his students and wants us to succeed. He lectures well and he is an easy grader. There were a good couple writings, but those are part of the curriculum. Once again, he's an easy grader so don't worry too much about it. Would recommend!

Great teacher and even better person. Cares for each of his students and he grades easy. There is a decent amount of writing but once again he grades easy so nothing to fret over. Very kind and well spoken guy, would recommend.

Very understanding and caring for students, gives good feedback on assignments, if you do the work assigned its an easy A, has good discussions in class, cancels class a lot but gives opportunities to reach out and discuss assignments
He is not a harsh grader and is very understanding but made me feel very discouraged early on in the research project.

I was generally really unhappy with the professor. The assignments were incredibly unclear and when I would reach out for clarification, he wouldn't respond even with follow up emails. If you do the discussions and complete the assignments you'll get a good grade but I was really unhappy with the lack of professionalism.

My main gripe is how unclear the assignments were. The description of what students were supposes to do was super unhelpful when trying to work, and the rubrics were extremely generic and provided no further insight. Class average on most papers was around a 50% simply because the students had no idea what he was asking for even with his feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jones was an extremely easy grader. Basically, if you genuinely put in effort and abided by the grading guidelines, you got a 100. He assigned readings but there was nothing graded based off them. There's lots of discussion posts, but they're an easy 100 so long as you answer and respond on time. He accepts late work for full points.

He's so great, I love Andre. I'm taking his class again for 1106, he's very fun and light-hearted and really chill. He treats you like his equals and friends, rather than just his students. Could not recommend him enough, he's the best english professor/teacher I've ever had

I had him last year and he was one of the best teachers I've ever had. He's super nice and cares a lot about his students. There is a textbook but you don't need to get it. There are four projects but they're pretty easy and if you're ever having trouble, he'll make sure to guide and support you!

One of my favorite professors! Easy class, just prepare to write a lot of papers, and talk to your peers. Was very understanding if you could not make it to class, as long as you stayed on top of your work. Made the classroom atmosphere comfortable by engaging with students with casual conversation. Overall was there to help you succeed!
He's the best English professor I have ever had. He cares about you and helps you with your papers. He treats you like equals.

An amazing professor. Shows lots of respect towards students and is very understanding. If you need more time for an assignment then he will gladly give you the time you need. He gives good feedback on all assignments and gives multiple chances. As long as you do what is assigned and listen to his feedback, you will definitely do well in the class.

This class was my easiest freshman class. Attendance wasn't mandatory at all, I attended less than 10 classes all semester. He is super understanding about anything, whether its not showing up to class simply bc you needed sleep or if it is late work. As long as you do the 4 main essays & listen to his feedback it's an EASY A. Also super funny guy
He is very nice and doesn't care about anything really. Just do the essays and the work but coming to class isn't always that important

He really wanted to make us think and use our skills rather than memorize for tests. Andre was a great guy and loved to help one-on-ones and was very open to helping students in need. He tries his best to engage the class and make it enjoyable while learning
He such a great guy. Assignments were not too time consuming and he is always willing to work with you. His class was such a joy and Andre is the man!

The most understanding and flexible professor I have ever had. He is a super nice guy who gives clear and helpful deadlines, but will accept late work as well. He cares about your well-being, so if you submit everything and work will him you will easily get an A in the class.
Not sure what the dislike for this professor is. Very nice and approachable.
He's a great guy and professor

Class is not engaging at all. Does not answer a lot questions so we can figure it out ourselves, and somehow expects everyone to understand concepts. TA also just refers your questions back to professor.

this guy the GOAT, the class is bit time consuming but honestly he makes it class feel like a comedy stand up with how awesome he teaches. LOOK, if you like Creative Writing, like to write in a creative way then definitely take it but just know you'll work on assignments for about a 1 or 2 hours a week. BUT CANT RECOMMEND HIM ENOUGH

Mr. Hobin you're the goat. I never liked English classes in the past so this class being my favorite was a pleasant surprise. He made English fun and you can easily tell he loves his job. He is so funny and he connects with his class rather than just lecturing. He isn't the easiest of graders, just pay attention and don't use ChatGPT.
Mr Hobin is great. I really enjoyed this class and never left without a good laugh. He has very clear grading criteria and the class is easy if you put the work in. 100% would take again

Excellent professor overall. Attendance is mandatory (10 skips and you fail). You write a personal narrative, a rhetorical essay, and a persuasive essay, as well as participate in several in-class discussions. The professor is funny, provides good feedback, and provides peer-review time in class for essays. Very fair grader. Take him if possible.

Professor Hobin is a great teacher and gives solid feedback on your work. I took the winter course and that consisted of a weekly written assignment based on a few short readings, 3 poems, a short story and a reflective essay. The workload is really manageable if you are looking to take this course over summer or winter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Love this teacher forever. I personally have never liked English and was more of a math and science type of person, but having him made me actually think I kind of liked English. He is the most real person ever and his style of teaching will engage you in all the lessons he does. He cares about each of his students.

Great professor, The class is based on two major projects a short story and a few poems. Make sure you go to class or you will lose grade point but he is an amazing guy who has no filter and will make you laugh as well as help you get you interested in writing even if you don't like it he finds a way. Overall it was a great class and 100% do again.
Mr. Hobin is a phenomenal professor who really cares about the students well being. He is extremely intelligent in his field and gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is the goat. You don't need to worry when you're in his class. Gigachad

I took Hobin's intro to creative writing in Spring 2024. One of my favorite courses by far. Class consists of reading and discussing various poems + short stories, and applying knowledge from the discussion and feedback from class into your own writing. He gives great feedback & is super approachable and understanding. Same deal for his ENGL 3315.

He's easily the best professor I've ever had! He pushes everyone to do their best and is extremely supportive. H has a great sense of humor and you never truly know what to expect from his class which makes every day so fun. Even though attendance is mandatory, it truly doesn't feel like it because you just want to go to his class anyway!

Professor Hobin was the best English teacher that I have ever had. He gave amazing lectures that kept all students interested and he assigned easy and clear assignments. He is a wonderful teacher and I am glad I had him.

Hobin was a phenomenal professor and honestly, he felt more like your friend than a teacher. He made sure to memorize people's names and give fantastic feedback on your writing. My only gripe with the class is the 14-page short story that you have to finish by the end of the semester, but if you can manage your time you'll be amazing. A must-take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mr. Hobin is a phenomenal professor! He is hilarious and uses his humor to grab the attention of students. His feedback for essays is great, and he gives extensions if you go to the writing center. He is very easy to reach outside of class and really wants to make sure you do well in his class.

SUCH an amazing teacher. I loved this course so much. Participation does matter and is graded but it is super easy to chime in and he leads the conversations well. Funniest guy ever and easy class. Just 2 big assignments all year which are writing poems and a short story. Definitely recommend this class.

I took ENGL2744 with him in Spring 2023 and I miss it a lot. It is one of my favorite classes I've ever taken and Professor Hobin is one of the best professors I've ever had. He was funny, inspiring, relatable, thoughtful, and so enthusiastic, it was infectious.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mr. Hobin is by far the best English professor I have ever had. I have always despised English but he made it fun. Super funny, friendly, and it showed that he cared about his students and that he wanted them to improve. Attendance is mandatory. If I could I would take him for every English class for the rest of college. He is truly amazing :)

There aren't enough good things to say about him. I have never created a "rate" before, but I'm doing one for him because he is JUST THAT GOOD. People talk about professors that change your direction for the better; for me that's him. I now minor in CW and even after 2 sems, he still says hi and remembers my name when we see each other at Kroger.

Most phenomenal English teacher I've ever had. He is downright hilarious and you can tell he love his job and was born to be a teacher. He cares so much about his students on an individual level and he instills so much confidence in you it's not even funny. Took him for ENG 2744 and wished he taught more classes. An absolute must take.

Like everyone else said, he keeps the lectures energetic and engaging. Very laid back and likes to get to know his students and also wants you to succeed. Attendance is mandatory!!! You get one unexcused absence before it starts impacting your grade. Also participation is very important (and required)

One of my favorite professors. He genuinely cares about his students, and you can tell he really enjoys what he does. Puts a lot of effort into his lectures and makes sure you stay engaged which is super helpful. There is a grade for participation at the end of the semester but he gives a bunch of opportunities to improve. Would def recommend!
BEST ENGLISH PROFESSOR. It is the first English class I have taken where students were actually engaged and enjoyed going to class. He is so entertaining - must take ENGL 1105 and 1106 with him.
Great professor. Gives great writing feedback and engaging lectures. Definitely a gem if you want a fun professor for the required English credits
great
Great teaching style

Great guy, keeps lectures entertaining most of the time, and he openly admits mistakes he makes on exam questions whenever they pop up, which is rare. Great professor, I had him for 1035 and 1036 and wouldn't have it any other way. He made the content manageable and understandable. Love when he goes on tirades against alkaline water.

Dr Wagner is a really good chem professor, he makes concepts very easy to understand and has fun demonstrations; It may partly be that chem 1035 is just an easy course but with him I was able to get an 100 on every exam including the final except one (Beware test 3). I like the way he teaches and he calls out the BS with Aleks as well.

great professor, does not have a monotoned voice making it easy to stay awake during lectures and makes class easy to comprehend with a clear voice. Very understanding, for example I missed my final and he worked with me to make sure i completed it another time. Explains topics in a easy way to understand, overall wonderful professor.

Didn't really explain stuff well, would go off on random tangents, overexplained simple things while also brushing over complicated topics. but as long as you self study and can do well on the tests you should be fine as they are 75% of the grade and the homeworks and iClickers are free
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wagner spent as much time teaching as he did cursing out the registrar. Even if you didn't take AP Chem you'll be fine. Homeworks and iClickers are easy 100s and the course gallery is underrated. Go to office hours literally no one goes
Very honest with students doesnt sugar things. Lectures are alright nothing special most learning came from the ALEKS stuff. Attendance is only mandatory cause of iClickers.
not very helpful lectures but you have to go for the iClicker which he does every day. Lots of ALEKS homework but it helps you learn for the test

Dr. Wagner is a great professor for 1035. Test/final are weighted 75% of the grade so it's important to study ahead if you struggle in test. Wagner is a great professor for people who have been exposed to chemistry prior as his lectures are pretty fast but he's super accommodating to people who haven't been exposed to chem. HIGHLY RECCOMEND

Took CHEM 1035 as a second year because I switched majors and had to fulfill a graduation requirement. I was grateful to have Wagner as my professor. He made CHEM 1035 far more manageable than the stereotypes surrounding the course. I'm not downplaying the difficulty. It is a hard course, but his teaching made the course feel more approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Lectures were amazing! The class is hard and rigorous. Do your ALEKS and get your I-Clicker points, and it's almost impossible that you fail.

Chem 1035 was light if you are a good test taker. Formula sheet on test lets u answer 90% of questions. Wagner is a good teacher but I didn't even pay attention once in class and just study the day before and bang out 90's on tests and only got 1 question wrong on the final. Lots of help resources available so its not bad at all.

Wagner is a kind professor. I have taken chem before and was familiar with most of the content, but he explained all of in in a way that made in click and interlink. Lots of Aleks homework, but thats departmental.

He is a good teacher, and is actually engaging with the class. Always super nice, you can tell that when he is "strict," its really just to not coddle the students. iClickers were never actually hard, he always gave the answer before closing the window.

Dr. Wagner was an engaging professor. Gen chemistry is difficult. I would recommend going to his office hours and review sessions before tests, and even consider getting outside of class tutoring. Stay engaged in his lectures and do the homework and you will be fine.
Super nice guy, the class can get hard sometimes but it was just the content. Not too bad overall though.

Wagner cares deeply about chemistry. Since the classes are so large you are not getting 1 on 1, but his office hours are typically empty. The only assignments we have are daily short quizzes online, in class attendance questions (he gives you the answer), and the tests. People complain about the tests, but if you lock in it'll be fine.
Very good professor. Tests are easy, with small daily assignments.
Professor Wagner is a fine professor, but he tends to go off topic during lectures. The course material is not very difficult, but the exams tend to be harder than the study resources provided.
Very funny guy. Hes nice and caring and makes lecture interesting. Chem is all the same for any teacher you get but I'd choose him again bc hes hilarious.
Chill guy, you dont really have to pay attention to the lectures because the ALEKS modules are a lot more helpful. The lectures are better for conceptual stuff. Just a lot of tests
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He literally yaps so much and so little of it is actually important. Everyone around me is either on their phone or asleep. He also spends the majority of the class talking over things that are either common sense or that we have to memorize anyway. Then for the last 5 minutes he likes to speed run the material we actually need to know
Gave great lectures. The homework often reflected what was on the lectures. He is forgiving with his grading and due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chem is tough, but Wagner was pretty good. He's probably better than the other profs except for Dr. Arachchige. His lectures are pretty good, and he'll give you a couple good tips that most of the other professors won't give you. downside is lectures are long and a little boring

He was so boring and a little unbearable to listen to, read directly off the slides the whole time and was always wheezing. That being said, we got through content in good time and the iclickers are a free grade bc he tells you the answer. Def not hard pass and get a decent grade in if you can stand to listen to his lectures.

Goes through the material so slowly that he has to skim thru content the day before the test. There are definitely better chem professors out there. Uses clickers occasionally. Lectures are not engaging and feel like a waste of time. You will learn most content thru aleks instead. Tests are department wide. Use studios to get extra practice.

I think he was a good professor, but he taught a lot slower than the other professors but in my opinion he went more into depth and explained things very well. The aleks is frustrating at times but they do help a lot. The tests are department wide and there were a few that were not taught in class or briefly mentioned. Uses iClicker.

Run. Wagner truly doesn't explain anything in class and just reads off his slides. I think bots are rating him because I have never met a person who liked him. He tries to be relatable by using foul language and how he was also a crazy college kid... how about you act professional as you literally have a Phd. You will learn this course yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wagner is the best Gen Chem 1035 professor in my opinion, he is super kind and willing to help and answer any question. The class itself is hard, but Dr. Wagner helped me so much. He writes on slides in class, so if you are a visual/auditory learner, it's great. The slideshow he does in class really helps with studying.
Great professor. Gen. chem is a hard class and the tests are the same for all the professors but wagner tells you exactly what you need to know for each test. Best professor for chem in my opinion.

Very intelligent guy, very clear he has a passion for Chemistry as a subject. I struggled a lot with health issues through the semester, and he was very accommodating and helped me get an A in the course even through tough times. You'll need to study on your own time for this course, practice makes perfect. That will be true of any professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible do not take him. I had to use a withdrawl, goes off on random tangents and randomly curse. Always behind other classes because he takes breaks mid class. Goes over new material day of the test. I would do the practice tests and go to review sessions but the practice test was nothing like the real test. Get Dr. Arachagie if you can TRUST.

Truly just a chill guy. His lectures weren't the most engaging, but they explained almost every tested topic in a shockingly efficient and digestible manner. Impressive. ALEKS homework can at times be a bit of a pain, but that's more of a class issue than a prof issue. Certainly one of the better chem instructors I've been taught by.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are not engaging so you might fall asleep for an hour and half. He is not a bad professor, but not a good one either. He would go off on tangents and teach new material the day of the test. Sometimes the test doesn't line up with what I was learning. He's a chill guy.
He is really chill and would help you out whenever you need help.

Great lectures! He did go off a bunch but I always enjoyed it. When it came to concepts in the primers (hw for next lecture) ALL doubts I had were solved. The tests themselves were tricky but doable through practice tests and heavy review of notes/assignments. Homework is a lot but very helpful (like 1-2 hours per assignment and 3-5 per week).

I only took standard chemistry in high school and had no higher level chemistry background coming into this class. Despite this, the resources provided by Wagner and the Chem 1035 team were more than enough to succeed in the class. DO THE PRACTICE TESTS. Go to review sessions, do the aleks homework and youll be good. Wagner is your best bet.

Professor Wagner was alright, he would go off on tangents during class at times and was a pretty boring professor overall. Almost all of the material is learned on your own outside of class anyways though. Chem 1035 is a hard course, but the professors provide resources in order to help with studying which I heavily recommend using.

This class was the reason i cried daily. as someone did not take chem in high school this was unbelievably hard. for the homework i knew what i was doing and then for test i was failing. i withdrew and i'm taking during winter semester and it's equally as terrible. class is fine though if you know chem somewhat and he's very nice.

This class is assignment and exam heavy regardless of the professor you have. Professor Wagner is a great teacher. He explains the content in an extremely digestible manner and always was on time when posting review material. The only issue is that his lectures get very boring and it can be hard to pay attention. It can be very easy to fall behind.
Excellent professor. He is great at teaching all material, realizes if he makes a mistake, and goes over it again. The class itself involves a lot of work on ALEKS.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He really cares for his students, I enjoyed attending his class for sure.

If you aren't going into this class with a strong foundation in chemistry, Dr. Wagner isn't the professor for you. While he was nice, his lectures were not helpful, as he spent the whole time going on unrelated tangents. He will be teaching new material the day of the exams. If chemistry is not your strong suit, I highly recommend a tutor.

I can't lie, ALEKS taught me 1035, not Wagner. He is a yapper which is fine until we are finishing chapters the day of or before being tested on them, meanwhile other classes are numerous lectures ahead. If I had put in more effort I could've done better, the 1035 profs really do prepare you well for the exams. He cares about his students' success.

This class was the most difficult class i've ever taken. I studied for about two hours everyday and three hours a day for weeks leading up to the tests and would still do horribly on the tests. He does not explain any problems that he solves in class, he just writes them out, expecting people to understand why he's solving them the way he does.

Wagner is very funny so I'll give him his points there. His lectures though aren't very engaging. He's definitely a good prof if you enjoy chemistry. He gives extensions on certain homeworks which is nice. Attendance isnt mandatory but you will have to do iClickers, so be sure you show up often if you don't want it to largely impact your grade.

He is very sweet, cares a lot about his students, everything you need is in the slides, if you pay attention in class you'll be totally fine but you can also not pay attention and be fine. ALEKs taught be everything, he was very nice and wanted to help everyone, not amazing at explaining things though. He made things as easy as possible I think.

Wagner was a funny and chill guy- super down to earth. He does all his lectures based on the slides and goes fast on somethings but really slow on others. If you already know or have taken chemistry and done well, it is not too bad. Subject teaching order is a little odd. If you do the aleks assignments, you get free points which help boost grades.

Dr. Wagner is a super caring and respected professor. He is very good at lecturing, and knows how to clearly explain difficult to hack topics. He even uses unconventional methods sometimes that he find easier, and for me personally, worked really well. He is fun and is around if you need help. Would definitely recommend.
Cares a lot about chemistry, and is a very caring professor. The test are hard, but they prepare you well for them. Best professor for the class.
Wagner is the type of professor that makes you fall in love with chemistry

You can tell he cares so much about his students. He gave so much support and opportunities to make up for it being such a large class size, I didn't feel like a number at all! He was so respectful and I appreciated how he didn't call random people out during lectures. his lectures made a lot of sense and he was very confident in the material.

Best chemistry professor ive ever had. If i could take him again, i would. Chem is a difficult course, for sure, but retaking with him made life so much easier. He was understanding and explained the course VERY well. If you had to pick a professor for chemsitry, i highly recommend taking it with him! #wagnerfan

He demands hard work, but is really kind! I had a TON of health issues this semester and he accommodated me every single time, was so kind and compassionate and really went out of his way to help me out.

Difficult class, lectures boring but informative, test-heavy course. If you want to do well, you NEED to take advantage of TA's, tutors, and office hours. All my friends did better than average because we found chem tutors at Gilbert. Prepare for tests a week early, go to reviews, do practice tests. Hard class but if you put in the work you pass.

he talks a LOT at the beginning of class, and then proceeds to go past our class time. However, I found him really good at explaining concepts in class. Tests are rough, but that's just kind of the structure of all chem 1035, i would say he is one of the best ones you can have for the class.

Wagner is probably the best professor you can take for 1035. With that being said though, I was not a fan of the class. The lectures aren't engaging at all so I would easily lose focus. It was nice that he went slide by slide and shared all of his notes. The tests are pretty difficult and curving really isn't a thing so studying is a must.

Dr Wagner is definitely one of the better chem professors at VT, but sadly I still felt I was lost most of the time. Wagner is very heavy on lecturing and does not make class very engaging. Chem 1035 is a weed out class and a waste of money. Example being the average on a test across all classes (almost 1,000 students) was a 53%.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Solid, but not amazing. Boring lectures. But gives you easy points and is super caring, respectful and considerate.

Dr. Wagner is awesome, probably the best 1035 prof other than Wall. He (very obviously) cares about his students a lot and he's very straight with you. He will help you as much as he can, if you seek it out. Study and pay attention... and try to get Wagner as your professor!

Talks for the first 15 to 20 minutes of the class about unimportant things, then complains that he does not have enough time later. Class test averages are abysmal, refuses to curve. Creates the tests, then has to apologies later for making them too difficult. Expect to have to learn everything on your own, as he is always being in class.

He takes notes on slides while lecturing that he then uploads to Canvas. This makes it so you can just listen at times and not worry about missing something. They are a great study tool to go over as well. At times he can go slow when you don't want him to and fast when you want him to go slow, but overall it was a good class.

Dr. Wagner posts a lot of material online and gives iclicker answers in class so that's basically a free +10 points in your final grade if you attend class. I wouldn't say that the class is super engaging, but chem is chem.

Dr. Wagner is definitely one of the better CHEM 1035 professors. His recorded lectures and slides were helpful. He did a relatively nice job explaining material, when he was there. If you have the choice between him or Dr. Eddleton (our sub for a few classes), pick him or you are in for a long semester. The department tests were pretty bad.

he was very easy to understand in lecture and genuinely cared about his students. makes sure that his TAs hold student hours enough so that students can attend. as long as you study enough for the tests, this class is a breeze.

The chem teachers do review sessions the week before the test and he was the most helpful when it came to these sessions. He explained things straight forward and gave plenty of examples on how to do certain problems. Although the lectures seem boring they are a good review after you learn the work from the online homework with multiple attempts.
Dr. Wagner did a great job of explaining the content and supported it with demos. However, lectures sometimes felt a bit monotone which could make it hard to focus.

I've always struggled with Chemistry so I decided to do the Summer session with Alec Wagner. He is one of the BEST professors I've ever had. He gave extra credit to us because he understood it was a hard course. I really recommend taking him because he is such a caring professor :)

Wagner was a fantastic professor. His lectures were great and he explained things in a way that was easy to understand. He was also very nice and funny. The only negative is that we would often only finish test material the day before the test which was slightly annoying but if you look ahead you will be fine.

Dr. Wagner is one of the best professor's I've had. His lectures are very helpful and he takes time to make sure everyone understands the material. The homework is tedious, but they really set you up for the exams. If you put a lot of time into this class and attend his review sessions you will be fine.

Dr. Wagner is amazing. He was always ready to help and most of the time for iclickers he would just give you the answers. Studio can kinda suck sometimes because of TA but the quizzes are great practice for tests, and do the worksheets for studio and ask questions on them. This class can be hard so get help when you feel you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Wagner's class because he is very well-versed in the subjects he is teaching but I felt like some of his lectures weren't helpful for the tests that were given. I Would recommend him to other students but this is a very challenging course.
Good professor and easy to understand as well as lecture slides and other course material. clicker questions were good too, but you still miss some and he drops ur 5 lowest

alec is a legend. he keeps it real and teaches you what you need to know. if you actually do the homeworks and studio worksheets/quizzes yourself, you will be fine. the class is a breeze when you keep up with the material. for the tests, redo the connect assignments and do the practice test. this class is not that hard if you put in some work.

Weed out class, but with Wagner, your effort determines your grade. He is super funny and if you pay attention in lectures, you will be fine. Before each test, do the worksheets then the practice test. THE PRACTICE TESTS ARE BASICALLY THE SAME AS THE ACTUAL TESTS!! Still do the worksheets though. Final exam is wayyy easier for some reason.

Dr. Wagner is not a horrible teacher, but there could be areas of improvement. Be ready for every class to be lecture style, and do not be surprised if the class falls behind schedule. Test prep isn't his favorite, so be prepared to go over all material on your own.
Was a good teacher, read the textbook and pay attention during class and youll be fine. smash
I took CHEM 1035 and 1036 with Professor Wagner. He's very nice and he has clear expectations for the class. His lectures are straight-forward and I learned a lot in his class.

Dr. Wagner is a fantastic choice for Chem 1035. Homework was somewhat heavy but it was never very hard - just a few reading assessments and practice problems each week. The tests are the biggest impact on your grade, but as long as you do the practice test before each test you'll do fine. As long as you put effort into this class you should pass.

Dr. Wagner set clear expectations for us as students. This was very helpful, and the syllabus made it easy to keep track of all our assignments. For me, at least, the lectures were easy to follow (sometimes unengaging), covered what would be on the test, and answered questions. He is a fine choice for Chem 1035, just don't ask him for extra credit.

Wagner's lectures were clear enough and its easy to ask him questions (try sitting closer to the front). Definitely go to his office hours even if it is just to do your homework. Beware of the iClicker. He does a question every class and participation in this class is worth ALOT. Don't cheat on the homework and do the readings, it will pay off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's pretty good. Not outstanding, he has some flaws - like his office hours kind of sucked because there were a lot of students there - but I would just go to my TA's and they were much better. The material also is not hard at all, just do the readings before class as listed in the syllabus and you will be fine!

Dr. Wagner is one of the best professors for gen chem. He will make you laugh sometimes when he's not being serious and scary about the upcoming test. As long as you go to class every day and do the reading/homeworks, the class is super easy.

Dr Wagner is amazing! He not only gave us the slides ahead of time & allowed us to annotate them(very effective way to learn, for me at least), his class is well organized & reinforces the material really well. My advice would be to carve out at least half an hour each day to do review, practice problems, etc. Very caring professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Wagner is a wonderful professor and a respectful guy. This course in general is homework heavy just because general chemistry is a standardized class. His lectures can get boring, but he is great at explaining things and will answer any questions.

Take the difficulty of Wagner with a grain of salt. The entire chemistry department is standardized so all teachers will grade with the same intensity on tests. Wagner was a fantastic teacher and did a great job of explaining every thing in class. You need to attend this class and take notes to understand the material. Would absolutely take again.

He's fine. He's a really good guy and treats you really respectfully, but his teaching is just not great. He goes through lectures really quickly bc he wastes the first fifteen minutes of every class rambling about nothing important. However, if you need help outside of class he is very helpful and will get you help

He wasn't the worst teacher, but I always would forget the stuff he taught us. He would always rush notes which didn't help yet he was still behind, teaching us content the day before the test. He was a little harsh but realistic. Was boring and never theoretically explained stuff. My friends and I struggled on HW because he didn't teach it 6/10

Dr. Wagner is a really nice guy and is pretty chill during lectures and will treat you like adults. His lectures were just him going through the notes and fillings things out, plus a lot of practice problems. He explains things pretty well, but you still have to study for the tests since they are a bit tough and worth a huge percent of your grade.
Pretty good guy, just read textbook and listen to him and you will be fine.

Wagner is a great guy but in the 50 minute lecture that we have, he spends 15 announcing random stuff or answering students' questions before starting the lecture (should be done at the end of class). This leaves our class behind and needing to learn material the day before an exam, which is 15% of our grade (there are four in a semester).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great at answering questions

This is the worst professor I have ever had. He is lazy, and doesn't go out of his way whatsoever to help you out in any way. He teaches awfully, however makes attendance mandatory, so pretty much class is a waste of your time, but you still have to go. He makes the tests difficult for no reason. Goodbye.

Wagner really seemed quite apathetic when teaching, especially towards the subject matter. He would be like "ugh this is really annoying to explain and for you to learn, but you got to know it", however he would never go out of his way to throughly explain something.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wagner doesn't necessarily make his lectures interesting, but he goes over all of the content well. If you pay attention during the lectures, do the homework and study for tests, you will do fine in his class.

He is extremely inflexible; the class is pretty normal, but tests can seem impossible. He is extremely rude to you if you ask any kind or study questions. He's terrible about reading emails too. If you ever ask for extra credit he will threaten "Honor Code violate" you.

CHEM 1036 will not be hard if you actually put time and effort into it. Dr. Wagner is a very nice Professor, He hosted lots of office hours and create lots of change for you to ask questions. His lectures are a bit slow and feel sleepy sometimes. The studio quizzes hurt your grade, not blaming him but blaming the Chem department!. PUT TIME TO STUDY
Lectures were so slow and boring, bad at responding to emails, and lowkey kinda rude. If he didn't do iclickers, I would never go to class. He posts lecture videos and practice tests.

I had Dr. Wagner for Chem1035 and am taking him again for 1036. He does a great job thoroughly going through examples and will always stop to ask if we are understanding. He also posts the lectures after each chapter online which really helped me, also is just a really nice guy
