reviews.comment: Teaches on the slower side and wasn't for me. I've had occasions where I had to teach myself material because we did not have enough class time before a test.

Wagner is honestly not bad. When he is actually teaching the material, he explains it well, but the problem is that he gets distracted and veers off so easily that we would often be significantly behind other blocks. He will spend 10 mins at the beginning of class talking about how we are behind. A decent choice for 1035, but get Wall if you can.

This is a pretty easy class and only reason I did not get a better grade was the fact that the exam times always happened right after a Calc1225 exam. The material is easy to pick up from class and if you actually do homework and study a passing grade is no problem. Large lectures are hard but Wagner made sure we knew about different resources.

Dr. Wagner is a very helpful teacher, as he'll spend a lot of time pointing out common mistakes made on tests and how to avoid them. He's always happy to answer questions and responds to emails in a timely manner. Great choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Let us take the tests a second time with a group for 30% and individual attempts are 70% of final test grade. This method helped me retain a lot of info. The tests were pretty hard but so are all chem tests. Really good at explaining info.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Wagner was great. He answered his emails promptly and gave good lectures. When I got Covid and missed classes for two weeks and Test 4, he got me up to speed with virtual lectures and allowed me to take the test at a later date. There is a lot of homework but, if you are confused the office hours are really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Tests are hard, and attendance is through iclickers ( 5 of each are dropped so its not bad) but they help to boost grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wagner is a great chem professor. He respects his students and is there to help you. His class isn't technically mandatory, but he has an iclicker grade worth 8% of your final grade with questions done randomly in classes, so attendance matters. I had him for both semesters of gen chem and I have appreciated the structure of his course.

Dr. Wagner is a nice guy, he clearly cares for his students and wants them to do well. Lots of homework but it helps bump up your grade from tests and whatnot. Took attendance through iclicker, weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Out of all of the chem professors at VT, I think Wagner is definitely the way to go. Really helpful when it comes to needing help outside of class. Doesn't just read straight off of a slide show during lectures. Really nice guy
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Wagner was a nice guy! He respected students and made sure his explanations were clear. Take notes on his in class examples!!!! As long as you do a lot of practice problems and nail the concepts you should be good! Prof Wagner gives good updates and responds to emails quickly.

Dr. Wagner is a fantastic choice for chemistry at Tech. Class was not mandatory since it was online, but I highly recommend attending them to watch him to practice problems if that is the case in later semesters. Also, this is a class where a lot of studying is needed outside of class. I recommend doing at least a little chemistry every day to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He explains as simple and straight to the point as possible. He cares about his students and understand when topics are dragging/difficult. Unlike my original chem 1035 proff, he doesnt speak excessively about everything. His lectures are amazing but exams are difficult. Studying and hw a LOT. skip class u rlly wont pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The chemistry department as a whole really sucks and does not care about the students mental health. However, Dr Wagner really does try his best to help out his students. He is quick to respond to emails and gives us plenty of advice to help us any way he can.

Chem was listed as synchronous, but all the lectures were pre recorded and watched outside of class. He had weekly help sessions that just went over homework problems. The chem dept sucks- curves would 've saved my grade. He was very kind and caring and answered emails fast though. His colleagues wrote the tests which doesn't help. Great guy tho
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class was all pre recorded videos and the help sessions are not helpful. In the long run this made it so much more difficult to learn the actual material. Had a really tough experience with this class and the tests are basically your whole grade therefore if you do poorly on 1 exam, your chances of ending with an A are little to none.

Despite the class being listed synchronous, all the lectures were pre recorded and had to be watched outside of class. The weekly sessions he had were mostly useless and they did not help much with actual content. Prof was bad but the chem dept at tech is the bigger problem. The dept policies of no curves was damaging especially with Covid.

Overall, Alec is a very good professor and he presented the material very well. I did not put as much effort into the class as I should have, which is why I got a C+. The exams are just very difficult and fast-paced, and even though he offered plenty of extra credit during this COVID semester, it was a super hard class. Study hard if you take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! The lectures are made very well everything is explained clearly, and he is always willing to help students with any problems.

Took chem 1035 first semester and had to withdrawal.. took it in the spring with Dr. Wagner and he made it so easy to understand and described things so well. Really cares about his students and their success in the class. favorite professor ever

Dr. Wagner is a great teacher and want's his students to exceed. He gives very helpful feedback during office hours and explains confusing topics clearly. The test's are difficult though, and you need to do many practice problems. His lectures aren't boring most of the time and does some entertaining demonstrations. Highly recommended

Alec Wagner is an extremely good chemistry teacher. He makes the material very clear and easy to understand and gives students many opportunities to get their grade up. He really wants you to do well and if you reach out to him for help he will make sure you understand what you are struggling with!
He's a new professor but really cares about students. Make sure to go to review sessions before tests.

I personally loved Dr. Wagner. I had Patricia Amateis (who was said to be the best) firs semester, and I failed this class. Took it again with him second semester and got an A. I went from getting 53s on tests first semester to gettings 90s. Uses the same powerpoint as Amateis but goes through it at a slower pace. Also super accesiblw if need be.

I really enjoyed Wagner. I had to take CHEM 1035 twice but I had him my 2ns semester and I went from geting 53 on the first chem test first semester to getting a 90.3 on my 1st test with Wagner. Contrary to most people, i liked him better than Amateis (had her first semester). He used the same notes as her but went through them slower.
He's a great professor.

At any other school he would be one of the best chem professors but the way the classes are set up at Tech every teacher that isn't Dr. Amateis ends up basically just reading her notes off to the class. He's a younger teacher so sometimes his answers are a bit roundabout, but he really cares about the class.
He clearly cares about his students when they need help.

Dr. Wagner is a very good chemistry 1035 teacher. I found his class to be very easy, however, my high school chemistry teacher was very hard and prepared me for this class well. Therefore, individual experiences may vary. Dr. Wagner is very accessible outside of class with office hours most days. He is willing to help with any conflicts with tests.

She's really sweet but kind of a tough grader, really nit picky. Kind of scared for the rest of the semester, but she's open to meet. She's a bit hard to understand, but I would definitely take her again.
I took this class in Spring of '24, Dr. Saad was absolutely amazing. Always open to meet, always open to help, and she genuinely cared if the students learned the material

Professor Saad does a very good job explaining all concepts and helping to understand coding in R Studio, which is used on homework assignments and your final project. This class is very technical/statistics based, but if you ask for help, she is very patient and will make sure you understand the content.

I hate math but Prof Saad made this class bearable. You need to come to class, pay attention, try, and KEEP UP. If you stay on track, you're golden. Prof Saad is super sweet and always so helpful. Lots of grading opportunities so your grade does not fully rely on exams (even though you can pass if you keep up) (ps, you don't need the textbook)

She is very caring and willing to go the extra mile to explain content to people. The class itself is one of the more difficult/technical in the PSCI department, but she made it so much easier than the professors my peers had. She grades generously and gives detailed feedback if anything is incorrect - would recommend to anyone!
She genuinely cares about students. She was really easy to get in touch with and is extremely helpful. She explains everything in a way that makes sense and is clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There is a total of nine homework assignments, a final research project (tied to the homework), and two exams being the midterm and final. Syllabus says that you need a textbook, but not really. She will do what she can to help you inside/outside of class. She made a hard class seem easy. It is a little bit of coding and statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is good for a new prof. Some of his lectures were not so engaging and I found the course easy, so I was tempted to skip a few classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He has a tendency to give everyone similar grades instead of focusing on merit. The content of his class needs to be made more relevant. Nice guy but honestly found other profs much better.
Amazing professor, one of the best I have had at virginia tech. Grading is fair and class structure is well thought out. For his first semester at VT, he did an excellent job!
Sarmah is an awesome professor, helps anyone who needs it, clear and concise lectures, tests were exactly like he tells you it's like, and is a nice and funny guy too. thats why hes the goat

Best professor I've had so far in Chemical Engineering. Super passionate about teaching and genuinely wants every student to succeed. If you have the option to take a class with him, definitely do it!
The best professor in chemical engineering. Cares deeply about how well his students do, goes over what will be on the test, and an all around great guy. If you see this guy for a class, take it!

Lectures doubled as lullabies #snoozefest. Kurdila manages to take what's already a difficult course and make it nearly unintelligible. Lectures jump all over the place and don't effectively teach anything. Worth noting that the practice exams were very similar to the actual exams, which was nice. However, be ready to teach yourself Controls.

I had this class at 8AM so I did not go, but the homework was easy, and the tests were not difficult (same questions as the homework/in-class examples). He made the final optional this semester because "there were so many assignments already," and he seems to care about students. OneNote is hard to read, but it has all the info you need to succeed.
Kurdila's class was a blast! I never felt more undeserving of a grade in my life.

I'm not actually sure what Kurdila is doing with my grade. He has released the final and said that HE doesn't know what our grade is. If you can, take this class with anyone else but Kurdila. The final exam is much harder than anything I've ever seen. It's like cooking a pizza and just throwing EVERYTHING at the plate and hoping it works.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kurdila is actually a very good professor, not sure why he gets a bad rep. The material is really not very challenging in concept, but very easy to make simple mistakes. He grades mercifully with points for the correct method. Onenote notebook is almost a transcript of what happens in class, with good examples and plenty of side notes.

Truly the worst professor I have had at Tech. Ridiculously hard class and his lectures make no sense. After the first exam nearly half the class stops showing up and maybe 10 of the people there manage to attention. He lectures by writing notes on a blank OneNote page and his notes are illegible. Good luck learning anything from this guy.
Good guy, but does not deliver information clearly. The content is difficult enough as it is. The most I've ever struggled with a class in my life. Avoid taking him for this class

Take any other prof if you can. He is confused most of the time, teaches very niche things and isnt helpful at all. You pretty much teach yourself and have to guess. He can't do half of it either and the class isnt well organzied at all. Overall an awful experience I learned nothing.

This is easily the worst class I have ever had the displeasure of taking. Dr. K is a good guy and knows the material very well, but the delivery of information is so inconceivably confusing and out-of-scope that it's almost impossible for an undergraduate to get any sort of education from this class without formal tutoring. Avoid at all costs.

Genuinely one of the OKAYEST professors I have had at Virginia Tech! He is somewhat prepared for lectures and provides decent info. The tests were also pretty fair, and if he says something is going to be on them, then it might be on there. You might be rewarded for going to lectures but idk. He's bar for bar the most mid of the mid professor ever

Genuinely one of the WORST professors I have had at Virginia Tech! He is never prepared for lectures and provides useless info. The tests were not fair, if he says something is going to be on there, then it won't be on there (Vise Versa). He also makes sure that you are not rewarded for going to lectures. There is nothing positive to say about him.

He is exceptionally scatterbrained. Uses OneNote; notes are illegible though. Does not frame anything you're learning. Teaches it like it's a signals class. You are just memorizing things to survive. Personally feel like I learned nothing and am just memorizing useless symbolic equations that mean nothing to me. Loses students' exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very confusing and often forgets what class period he is teaching or is in. Often just talks about subject too deep or very vague as he often thinks the students are "experts" at the subject. Notes are confusing as he jumps from the present lecture to previous lectures to write in them. Recommend taking  another professor if possible.

reviews.comment: How he is allowed to be a professor boggles me. He is teaching either info that is not relevant or graduate level methods for Vibrations, which is confusing to every student. Even by attending class I am more confused, we just derive equations that make no sense. I compare with friends in other Vibes classes and it looks like a whole other subject.
This is a vibrations/control systems class for Mechanical Engineering but he teaches it more like signals and systems in Electrical Engineering. Very difficult class, try to get someone else.

Rambling, unprepared, confusing. His lectures suck and rely on slides ripped from another professor. He clearly doesn't so much as review material before class as he constantly gets confused during explanations and takes far too long to convey a bare minimum of information on each topic he lectures on.
He’s at Tech to do research so do not expect good teaching.
GOAT

Do not take him. VT should be ashamed to call him a professor, much less the one that oversees all the vibrations classes. Fire him and put Roger Chang in charge. reviews.comment: I like Dr K as a person, but not as a professor. He's funny and a reasonable guy, but he's disorganized and doesn't explain things clearly.
