He's very helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great guy, really tries to help out and although the class can be tough, he does his best to show examples and go through homeworks. The only problem, is that he knows the material too well and gets excited so he tends to skip steps that he considers trivial. However, if you stop him and ask, he will explain.
Hot. Funny. Best class eva!

Dr. K is a great person. He will agree with me that he is totally scatter-brained. He really wants you to understand the material. System Dynamics is a hard class but he will make you get a good grade if you work for it. The tests are tough. He likes to get coffee on saturdays and talk about matlab and class. He is a really funny guy.
Convex Analysis & Robust Control.  Be prepared to not understand anything but still probably do well, since his tests are just definitions.  Way too theoretical.

The professor provides absolutely no assistance and does not even provide lectures for the class. If you don't enjoy learning by only reading from a textbook and taking exams with very specific questions that are almost impossible, it may be a good idea to avoid this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was rude even when I asked for help, and our course was only 3 tests and a paper. She only posted notes from the publisher, had no office hours, and asked very specific questions from the textbook that were nearly impossible to answer, even if you read the text.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was the best prof. I had for online classes, very short and simple powerpoints that were only open for the day but you can save them and keep them as notes. Assignments are a weekly (like 3 paragraph) essay about a short-er movie and was a very simple, straightforward class.

Her class was probably one of my favorites ever--she's so nice and interesting. Sitting in her lecture is like having an in-depth conversation, because she almost stream-of-consciousnesses her discussions, which can make it hard to take notes but is really interesting. There is a lot of reading, but as long as you talk to her, she's super helpful.
Very easy and by far the nicest professor i have had
Demands a lot of work.

I agree with the comment about forgeting about talking to her about when her test questions don't match the book.  She held something against me the entire class to.  I thought I did amazing on the final project but ended up not doing so well.  Her class is too much work and definitely not worth it.
I took history of madern Latin america- and her class is interesting- alot of writing and reading but its not too bad.

She sped through the lecture or gave so much information we were weeks behind which then didn't align with the lab. Her grading was rediculious and clearly she picked favorites. No one got 100 on the final and for her “quizzes” you have to know 22+ diagrams. This class made me want to switch majors the same way a bad coach makes an athlete quit.

Very lecture heavy, and the slides are what you will go off of for the entire class. Group-project oriented, but none of them are particularly difficult. Very caring and understanding teacher who appreciates about her students' opinions. Not too difficult if you can follow along with slides content.

Dr. Shah does have a very lecture heavy class so be ready for that.  Her quizzes are difficult but exams are multiple choice.  She is accessible outside of class and encourages and helps students to succeed even after they leave her class.

Shah is very knowledgeable about the content that she is teaching and loves to teach it. As long as you study and understand everything that is on the slides you will be fine. She loves to reference slides images so make sure you pay attention to those. Also be warned quizzes are harder than her exams be prepared to know more content.

Dr. Shah is awesome, super caring, and usually explains stuff pretty well. There were only a couple exams and they had an enormous amount of info on each one, like the most info I've ever had on one test ever. But! The tests are fairly easy, and the quizzes are fairly hard. In a really hard/info heavy class, she def didn't make it worse.

This class contains a lot of information, a lot we did not get to. Dr. Shah is very caring and is very passionate about neuroscience and teaching. She was very interactive in class and is very accessible outside of class. She has a few group projects but nothing too hard. Her tests were fair and the quizzes are slightly harder. She's lovely:)

I think Dr. Shah is an amazing prof. It's a STEM major = not going to be a cakewalk, you have to put the work in outside of class. She's very accessible, and if you take the time to talk to her, you realize how much she REALLY cares about her students succeeding in the world of science and their careers. Get to know her, she's an amazing person.

I feel as though this professor does not understand how to teach an introductory level class. I was extremely overwhelmed all semester with the amount of material (over 200 slides per exam) and the lack of buffer assignments to help with quizzes, tests, and high stakes assignments. It was extremely difficult to follow her lectures as well(monotone)

If you are not on her good side, you may as well be toast in this class. She is very curt and gives a lot of attitude to her students in the most normal of conversations. She does not give test study guides which is tough for a class as content heavy as NEURO 2026. Feedback on assignments done by TAs.If you can take this class with anyone else: DO.
She is very lecture heavy, memorizing the powerpoints is all you need to do for the tests. The assignments are graded pretty hard and play a big part in your grade.

in-class lectures are confusing and required textbook reading to comprehend. often exams would recall information mentioned in textbook and not lectures, or the smallest detail from a class lecture slide. lectures are repetitive and mundane. i would not have survived the class without reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a good professor, but sometimes her lecturing is just reading off slides. The class isn't hard if you pay attention. She gives the textbook for free and there are random in class assignments. The homeworks weren't bad and she drops the worst exam. Im taking her for NEUR 2026 as well

Boring. As a Neuroscience major, I wanted to get excited about these things, but the way she teaches them sent me right to sleep. Just memorize the slides and you'll be fine. Stopped showing up about a quarter of the semester through and my grade never suffered.

Dr. Shah's class is difficult, but it is not as crazy as some of these other reviews make it out to be. You have to remember it is a neuroscience course, and a lot of the subjects and concepts take a lot of time to fully grasp. Dr. Shah is very kind, knowledgeable and accessible outside of class, if you put in the time, you'll do well in the class.

Very lecture-heavy and does not go into detail about topics but expects you to know the details. Textbook is not required but alot of the homework questions are found there instead of the notes. TAs grade very strictly and provide little to no explanations. Easy to fall asleep in class, she does not make an effort to make the class engaging at all.

Shah wasn't a great teacher. Her content is very lecture heavy; with long slide shows and several notes under. The tests were fairly short but hard. The average on her test is 72-74. Her test questions are incredibly detailed even though she doesn't go in-depth in class. The homework is graded by the TAs and very harshly.

Shah is a nice professor but she just isn't the best at her job. Reads of slides a lo and relies on them while asking very specific questions on the test, not explaining things fully then testing on them with assignments quizzes or tests, she isn't bad by any measure but theres a lot she could do to improve her teaching

NEUR 2026-Professor Shah is very accessible outside of class and records all her lectures. The content can be a little difficult at times, but that's the reality of taking a neuroscience class. The exams are very doable, everything on them is mentioned in lecture. She drops your lowest exam, which is nice. The homework is graded harshly though.

Dr. Shah did not explain the content well and only read off of her slides in class. Then, on the tests, she expected us to know every tiny detail from the slides. I felt as though the questions on the tests were too hard and not helpful for learning about the subject. This semester I have her again and it is the same way. Not enough teaching!

Pretty good with lectures, though there was some concepts that the textbook explained better and more concisely. The exams are detailed orientated but all covered in the slides and lectures. She provides pdfs to the textbook as well! Lectures are engaging with the polls and videos. Harsh grader for the written HW tho
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It felt like the entire semester she was trying to figure out how to teach. The tests were very detail-oriented so it always felt like you had to know everything she said to a tee though she didn't give much material to study off of. She also went off her syllabus calendar which was very confusing for me since that's what I rely mostly on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is content heavy, but it's not too difficult. Professor Shah is extremely accessible if you have questions, and she records all her lectures which I found very helpful. She drops your lowest test and there is no final. As long as you attend lectures, the class is very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Shah. She is extremely understanding and easy to work with. The class its self is a bit hard but as long as you put the work in to understand and take notes you'll do fine. I also don't believe she is the reason its hard. its hard because its neuroscience.

His class is super easy. People should not be complaining this much. His exams were also so easy I finished them in 20 mins. You do work on 1 big group project for the entire semester so pick your group wisely!

The way he "teaches" the course makes me wonder if the course is needed. Actual class is a joke and the only thing I have learned is the existence of perplexity AI. Project heavy not extremely(3 months) late feedback. Syllabus schedule never followed and always under "revision" Lectures are more him talking to himself with long stretches of silence
Although the lectures are more slow moving he is a nice guy and if you do the work and study you will get good grades. Professor is understanding and wants people to learn.

soooooo boring and such a hard grader. after submitting a group project his reasoning was ridiculous which prompted us to speak to him privately where he simply reiterated what he wrote in the first place. just do not.
The online class was something I looked forward to - not something I can say for most online classes. Arthur is super nice and genuinely cares about you.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: His test wasn't hard if you read the textbook and go to class

He rounded our class participation grade at the end of the semester. Attending his class was like getting a root canal. I was an HR major going into his class but switched afterwards because just the thought of HR made my skin crawl

avoid this class like the plague. the man needs to take a basic teaching and public speaking class because he has the worst approach to classroom instruction I've ever seen. His participation grading was purely subjective, and his general answer for how to study better for a test was to ask someone who did better than you.HewasNever willing to help

Just don't. Course is hard, especially if you don't have prior knowledge of computer science. Professor puts students down for getting questions wrong and treats them with no respect. If you want to feel like you are in high school again, with teachers looking over your shoulder, take this class!
Unhelpful. Smug while also incorrect, needlessly interrupts the actual professor during lecture, sadly the only TA available for lab section of 220. avoid if you are able to.
He is arrogant and does not help the students very much. He grades way too hard on students and penalizes students for the smallest mistakes by taking off a lot of points. Avoid him if you can.

Extremely unhelpful individual and terrible instructor. Grades harsh for no reason even if you follow the rubric exactly and will always somehow manage to take points off for some vague unexpected reason. Avoid him at all costs. Makes the class harder and your life harder than it has to be.

One of the TA for 2114. Extremely unhelpful and do not recommend his services at all. He doesn't give a single useful piece of advice is overall arrogant and not understanding. Do not recommend receiving help from him. There are much better TAs willing to help and guide you.
He is very rude and doesn't explain content properly. His explanations are very condescending. I would avoid him if possible.

Basak has pretty good lectures/demos and has extra videos to help students on some of the projects. The midterm/final are not difficult to study for at all and the projects aren't too bad either (I thought the 1st was the hardest to understand). Highly recommend taking him if he does teach it in the summer (online) again

he's in the stone age cause doesn't know how emails work(seriously don't expect a reply ever). doesn't put up the syllabus for the test until the very last minute.  teaches from the textbook. teaches in a weird order with context to other differential equations teachers.

I had Arun Biswas for 1225 and he is a great teacher. He seriously knows what he is talking about and is very knowledgeable. He should honestly be the course coordinator as the current one is not as great. Calc 1 was hard for me but it was very easy to go to his office hours and schedule zoom one on one sessions to manage my way through.

My Math 1225 experience was very pleasant. I was extremely nervous as I have never taken Calculus and jumping into 1225 was daunting. Arun is extremely intelligent and helpful, his explanations are detailed and they make sense. He goes a little fast sometimes so pay attention. The words that come out his mouth usually are on the test! Funny too.

Dr Biswas is the goat. He is a funny guy and made math interesting. He didn't give much homework and gave very clear tests. His practice tests were basically the real tests, of course the concepts slightly modified/ the numbers changed. Very easy to succeed and do well in his class. He is a must take!
Great teacher, if you go to class you will do well. The practice exams were just like the real tests. Final will replace lowest test grade.

Amazing professor, you can tell he really loves what he does. Very enthusiastic about helping you to succeed and has material that prepares you very much for the exams. I aced test 1 and 2 (final being test 3) with minimal studying other than the home works he provides. Probably the best thing is the completely solved problem sets that he provides.

dr. biswas is such an understanding and silly guy! he has a strong passion for the material and you can tell, but he describes everything in a very easy way. he never gives you a curve ball on exams, but uses the wide library of practice problems he gives you instead. great guy really, one of the best for diffeq

Without a doubt the best math professor I've had at VT so far. If you pay even a small amount of attention in class you will pass. Gives an insane amount of optional practice problems to practice with and I feel if you understand just those you will pass. Very funny man and overall makes his lectures interesting to go to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Differential Equations is always going to be a difficult class. But Dr. Biswas will make it as clear as he can. His homeworks are understandable if you pay attention in class. He really roots for you. I also love his humor and passion for math. He at least tries to spread his appreciation for diff eq, and I really respect that.

Biswas isn't perfect, but as math professors at VT go, he's one of the better ones. Lectures are just him writing on a chalkboard for 50 minutes, but that's not a problem if you pay attention. He does have a bit of an accent but it's not too distracting. He does curve tests, and he has great stories. Office hours are super helpful with him too.

You will spend most lectures desperately trying to keep pace with his writing pace. Material was often unclear, and questions were met with an irritated attitude. Like others have mentioned, he just copies his typed notes straight to the chalkboard. His Canvas page is pretty empty, missing many of the things that other professors included.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Biswas is definitely the best math professor I've had so far. He's a really nice and entertaining guy that tells you funny stories during the lectures. Some people don't like his teaching style of basically copying the lecture notes, but he asks questions and explains things well. Also, most importantly, **he curves exams**. Hard class, though

Biswas is the only math professor I've had at Tech who wasn't awful. His lectures were informative and the textbook that he wrote is very helpful. His tests can be difficult but are never unfair they look very similar to homework questions. He gives generous partial credit on tests and was very flexible when I had a couldn't make it into a test
Professor is great. just the class itself is hard

He is really stingy with his partial credit on exams. He never really knows what is going on with the pathways quizzes and his course layout is really confusing for no reason. His lecture notes are numbered, but he consciously makes them not line up with the textbook. The textbook is not great but you will need it if you want to understand anything

Dr. Biswas is one of the few math professors who is really passionate about his subject. He's taught Diffeq at other universities and he really strives for his students to learn. For example, if you're shaky in Linear Algebra (trust me, you'll need it for Diffeq), then he will individually work with you until you understand the concept.

Dr. Biswas might be one of the best professor you can get for Diff Eq. He assigns 3 - 5 problems per week as an assignment and cares about you doing well. Tests are easy even if that worth 25% each. His lecture will be always copying things down, and that's the only thing that makes me a little uncomfortable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I think this program is really well put together, especially if you're new to data analytics. The projects teach you a lot and are honestly the best part. Events make it easy to meet people and make friends. Dr. Ara is supportive and genuinely cares. Attendance matters, and if you care about projects, you'll do well.

This course was part of a data analytics program. Dr. Ara is a great professor and explains everything in a way that's easy to understand. The projects help a lot with understanding the material. Just show up to class and events, participation really matters to her.

I found Dr. Ara to be very knowledgeable and genuinely caring. She respects her students and encourages class participation. She listens to our opinions and used student surveys to improve the course. The project was a major part of the class, and I learned a lot. I would definitely recommend this course.

Please do yourself a favor. Do not join Impact, do not take this class. It was a thorough waste of time and brainpower. You likely won't learn anything and on top of that, Dr. Ara is one of the worst teachers I've ever been made to deal with and she highly overestimates how much work should be done for a one credit class.
Horrible class, and horrible instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just terrible!
Awful!
Professor Shahbazian explains the course material very clearly and answers all questions well.
Great Professor. He was the most understanding professor I have ever had in Econ courses at VT.
He is a great economics professor who explains content well and wants everyone in his class to succeed
He's awesome. The best professor I've had at Virginia Tech.
Professor Shahbazian does a great job of making a relatively abstract course easy to understand.
Great instructor. He presents course content effectively and his teaching method for each lecture is consistent.
His class is by far the best economics class I have taken in terms of instructor content and communication at VT.

Dr. Shahbazian posts the lecture notes prior to each class, giving me a clear idea of what will be covered. He explains the material in a straightforward, easy-to-understand manner. Also, he always answers questions efficiently and responds to emails quickly. That, along with practice exams, helped me out a lot. Best Econ prof I've had at VT!

The instructor was very well prepared and followed the course schedule which was very effective for me. Because he adhered to the schedule, it was easy to prepare and review the topics before class. Overall he fostered a very educational and engaging class.

His class was awesome and I enjoyed the course material. I think his method of teaching was very compatible with me. He asked if there were any questions in the class and ensured we understood the content. I really appreciated the practice exams and study material he provided and he is very prompt in his emails.

The class was a very insightful entry to intermediate microeconomics. I enjoyed the lecture notes format and never found myself too confused. The only challenging aspect was the tests, which were difficult and sometimes contained very specific questions. However, the instructor clearly cares about his students' success.

An amazing professor. He did an outstanding job being a reliable and understanding instructor on this course for his students. He is one of the most straightforward, helpful, and communicative professors I've ever had.

Mr.Shahbazian is by far one of my favorite teachers at Tech. He teaches in a very straight-forward manner so if you put effort into learning the material, you'll get an A. It's obvious he wants his students to do well. ECON 3104 is a weed out course, so I was very lucky to get him as a teacher. He has an accent but he's very easy to understand.

If you need to take Microeconomic Theory, take it with Arin Shahbazian. He is very understanding and grades all assignments fairly. He also offers extra credit for one of the midterms and the final exam. If you can do the homework and in class examples, you will be fine for the tests! He is a good teacher and wants everyone to do well in the class!

Lectures are mostly about history/news, by week 2 the room is half full but attendance is extra credit. Tests are easy and you basically just have to memorize the homeworks and then some definitions for an 100. I slacked and didnt review the homeworks once and got the class low lol, a 60%. If you like reading textbooks this is the class for you.
His tests are fairly easy and he offers a lot of extra credit. His lectures are a bit dry but if you do the textbook reading beforehand it makes a lot more sense than if you don't.

Lectures are fairly informative but very dry. If you were good about reading the textbook I think they'd be more helpful. Homeworks aren't too difficult if you follow the material, and he is happy to help in office hours. Tests are fairly easy. If you're motivated, it's not hard to do well in the class. If you're not motivated, it will be rough.

I hope his in person classes are better than his zoom classes. He runs through power point slides at 10x speed however, most of it is copied straight from the text book. On zoom his computer microphone very frequently cuts out, we have complained to him and his TA but he has an 'oh well' approach to it and can't be bothered to fix it.

Mediocre teacher who interrupts class. His facile rants on philosophy of science and religion are less sophisticated than those of a freshman. He struggles with phil concepts and terminology, should take an intro course to better educate himself. Speaks on politics + phil topics with undeserved confidence, somewhat embarrassing to be honest.
The course was very inspiring to me as a musician. Very good lecturer too.
Straightforward class. Gives easy homework, Tests are alright. Gives too much extra credit. Could be exempted from final exam if test average is above 90.
Classes are just a repeat of the text. If you do the reading and take good notes, attending class is hardly necessary.
Awesome teacher.  Interesting material. Easy A.  Definitely recommend!
Go to class to get participation/ clicker points. Do extra credit, and study the lectures.

Nahum Arav is an excellent professor; he is very enthusiastic about astronomy. This class is an easy and interesting A. If you don't get an A in this class, you're doing something wrong. He drops your lowest test grade and he offers plenty of extra credit opportunities. He won't hesitate to ask students to be  quiet while he's lecturing.
BORING!! DO extra credit and you will be fine
Class isn't all too interesting...a medium amount of effort to require a respectable grade. Fair teacher overall.
Great professor, very interesting class. I recommend it to everyone.

Great class. He loves his subject and is serious about what he teaches but as long as you show respect and listen you will be fine. He has a funny sense of humor but doesnt allow for a lot of chatter in his class because it is so large. Just pay attention what he teaches is interesting and worth learning.

Arav is a professor who is in high demand so the class most people take of his (astronomy) is a science requirement class but once you go past that in your interest you can get so much use out of this man. Observational astrophysics being his cup of tea.. if you have an interest this man is one to get to know and its easy to do so too. great prof.

I found his class boring. Arav has a thick  accent, making him hard to understand. His powerpoints spit out the textbook, meaning you learn nothing new in class. He has in class clicker quizzes which keep you from not going. He often expresses his personal views on topics like global warming and doesn't provide other views. I'd avoid his class.

I found it very hard to pay attention in class. He goes off on the most random tangents about Obama, astrology, finance...Anyways, I did not like his class. His tests, although you get one side of one sheet of handwritten notes (not open notes like someone said) Are still difficult. The final is cumulative and he gives no review
He is a very nice and goofy guy, he provides many ways to bring you grade up. Overall a very enjoyable class.
He was really into doing iClickers based on the readings everyday so go to class. Open note tests really helped, and he repeats 80% of the questions from old tests so use Koofers.
His nationality is ambiguous, the mystery is killing me
his tests were a little hard because of all the material. class was not that interesting but not my major so i didnt care. good teacher and very helpful. gives lots of extra credit
Great Guy. Really cares about his students. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Big iClicker fan
Go to the office hours

Great guy, great class, if you know anything about astronomy this class is easy.  Attendence is taken with iClickers in class but is not worth much.  I get As on the tests and HWs so I never go.  TAKE THE LAB it is awesome and a VERY EASY A+ (all work is done in class)

This class is definitely an easy A if you do the reading and take notes on it. It's not "required", but it is if you want an A. I stopped doing the reading, and I scraped a B by luck. Furthermore, when you do the homework ("MasteringAstronomy"), actually spend time on it--don't just guess the answers! it doesn't take long to google answers. lol.
Open note tests- the hardest part is the homework. Reading quizzes every day- go to class. he likes brown nosers. don't be one.
Unreasonable beyond belief
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Reed is extremely passionate about American Literary History, making her lectures engaging. But, because of her passion, there is a lot of reading to do each week. Dr. Reed mostly picks entertaining works, though. Basic open note midterm and final but requires two 5-page essays throughout the semester and grades those harshly, so be careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her lectures are very engaging. Be prepared for a few hours of reading every week. Two essays, but you decide when to do them. Midterm and final are easy if you take notes.

Dr. Reed is an expert in American Literature and this makes her lectures enthralling--the class is far from dull. There's an insane amount of reading, so be prepared for that. Otherwise, the class is pretty straightforward. 2 papers on flexible topics and a midterm and a final, which are open-note and not tricky. She's also very kind and helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed her lectures, she is a very kind and understanding professor. However, be prepared to read a lot. The papers are a little difficult but there aren't too many of them. The midterm and final were super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a very sweet professor, but be prepared for a loooot of reading. The website that grades your analysis for these readings is easy to get through, but be prepared to have to write more than you feel is necessary to get full credit. The essays, imo, were kind of difficult in comparison to British Literature. Very easy midterm/final though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 3204: Man....... If pointing at illegible notes (that are often incorrect) from 5-10 years ago on the projector whilst constantly losing your train of thought every 5 seconds was an olympic sport, this guy would rival Michael Phelps for the greatest American olympian. He stares at you like you have three heads if you ask a question.
Great office hours and great professor to choose for macroeconomic theory
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Course relies heavily on lectures, but the delivery is hard to follow. The frequent use of filler words makes it difficult to stay engaged. Course material isn't shown in a way that's easy to understand, with no effort to adapt teaching methods for student learning. It might be time to consider a more student-focused approach—or maybe, retirement.

This was for econ 4303. He needs to retire. Homework is due at 4PM. He just talks to you and assumes you understand the material at first time he says it for lectures and they are not easy to follow along. Makes you buy his own book and it's not much better than what you get from the lectures. One of the worst professors I have had.
Tests are easy and he grades pretty leniently. but please study your STATA commands or else you won't pass this class.
The class is very lecture heavy, with each lecture being very hard to follow.

Dr. Ball made sure to explain everything thoroughly, and posted lecture slides and homework answers to help you study for exams. The homework was kind of difficult, but it was similar to the problems done in class.

He is a cool guy who always seems to want to help you do better, and his slides that he always posts on Canvas are amazingly helpful. however he is also a very tough grader and a bad planner (he combined our third exam with our final exam due the day after a lab and a day before a major project because of one snow day!)

Professor Ball is a terrific professor in his field. You can clearly see that Professor Ball loves what he does and, most importantly, cares about his students' success in this field in the future. I had no prior knowledge of electrical concepts or techniques, and Professor Ball did a great job teaching and making me pass!

Dr Ball's lectures are can be fast. The in class problems sorta help sometimes, but get ready for a lot of self teaching outside of class. He connects a lot of what we learn in class to real world applications, which is nice. The exam review slides are also great since that's where the multiple choice questions on the exams comes from.

Took circuits and devices with him over the summer and that was probably the best class that I have ever taken - he made complex topics make sense and helped fill in gaps in our knowledge that we had from previous classes.

I'm in ECE 2024 right now and it's difficult but nothing that I can't fix by paying attention in class. It was the same for 1004. You just have to pay attention in class and look over the homeworks before each test and you'll do fine.

I am someone who has a hard time learning in heavy lecture classes, and his teaching style did not help at all with me, and I ended up dropping the class. I wouldn't say he's the worst; he is a good guy, just not someone I can easily learn from.
Amazing dude, really passionate in teaching and the thing he teaches, easy 5/5
His lectures are clear and concise, often relating material to real-world examples. He even showed us an IG reel during class, haha. If you can, definitely enroll in his section for 2024.

Solid professor for ECE 2024. 2214 with Ball was fair. Ball is good at connecting the lecture material to industry/real-life. Ball is open to questions and accessible. Ball as a person is cool; it's evident by how many students leave good reviews. 

2214 (Ball) : 4 unit exams, ~10 homeworks (fair size), 3 labs, ~15 mini quizzes

Spectacular professor with great lectures, in part because of his private sector experience. Always willing to answer questions (clearly) and completes useful example problems during class. Makes expectations very clear and genuinely cares about his students. Lectures match what appear on the tests. Definitely take Dr. Ball if possible!

Excellent professor with great lectures. Dr. Ball breaks down complex concepts to make them easy to understand and is always willing to answer questions. He also does example problems so that you have an idea on what to do on the homework and tests. The tests are reasonable, and Dr. Ball prepares you for them. Definitely take Dr. Ball if possible!

Professor Ball was the single best teacher I had freshman year. He is very respectful and his lectures are extremely helpful. His grading is very fair and will always respectfully answer questions. This class is somewhat difficult however, it is very fair and you always feel like you deserve the grade you receive.
Spectacular lectures, really cares about us doing well not just in the class, but in the future. Relates things to the real world. Showed us instagram reels one time, amazing.

I've had Dr. Ball for three classes (1004, 2024, 2214) and he is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had (not just for ECE). His lectures make a lot more sense than other sections and his averages are always higher. He relates everything to real world applications which makes everything more interesting, and he's a really great person.

Ball was quite good at explaining the topics for the course. While attendance is not mandatory, I doubt you'll do well if you miss lectures. Tests are easier than the homework, and his homework and quizzes are very helpful for test preparation, as well as his practice tests. Make sure to keep up with homework and lectures.

It is very important to attend class because he provides answers to quizzes during lectures. The homework is challenging, but if you understand how to solve all the problems, it will set you up VERY WELL for the test. Attending the lectures make understanding the content significantly easier.

I was hesitant to switch into his 8am classes but it was so worth it! He's great at explaining new concepts and how it can be applied to what you already know, as well as application in the real world. He's very approachable and knowledgeable.
I enjoyed his class a lot, he explains things well and is very knowledgeable. I would definitely recommend trying to go to every class since the lectures are very important.

If you haven't taken a physics/circuits related class before, you need to go above and beyond to put effort into this class. His office hours are very helpful if you're trying to learn and understand the material better. Also, DO NOT SKIP OR MISS lectures under any circumstances, and if you do, meet with him to try and understand the material.

Ball was a pretty good professor. He oftentimes shares quiz answers during class and on test review days he will give out information that is often useful on exams so attendance is definitely beneficial. Sometimes he wasn't the best at explaining certain topics but with enough practice it was doable. He was very nice and always accessible to help.

A lot of weight is put into tests/exams in his class. If you go over the slideshows after class again and skim/take notes of the textbook you'll do really well on the tests (advice I did not heed). Although attendance isn't taken, I would highly recommend not skipping, you're definitely going to suffer on the tests for it if you do.

Dr.Ball is an excellent teacher who makes a genuine effort to remember students by name. He's approachable and is always willing to help. The class itself isn't too difficult, but his tests carry 15% more weight than Professor Dunning.

While 1004 can be a tough course, he explained most topics quite well, and whatever I didn't understand I could easily look up as there are so many great resources. Overall, the tests weren't too hard, and while some lectures can be boring they are usually pretty interesting.

Ball really knows his stuff and is an amazing lecturer. The lectures sometimes dragged, but he teaches the material so well and applies it to the real world. Genuinely get him for any class you can, because it all feels useful and meaningful with him.
Great professor. Get him for any class you can.

Dr. Ball is one of the best professors in the ECE department, hands down. I've had him for both 1004 and 2024, and both times I've come out with an appreciation of how well he lectures. On top of that, he's just a good person and genuinely cares about his students. Take him whenever you can; I promise you won't regret it!
Such a great prof. I want to take as many classes with Dr. ball as I can. He knows almost every student by name and has great stories and anecdotes to relate to class. Overall great.
He's great, but he gets really passive aggressive over piazza. He would be a 5/5 if someone would take away his keyboard.

Dr. Ball is an excellent professor. He cares students and made several extensions to assignments and curves on tests to not screw over everyone tackling Tech's ECE gauntlet. His lectures often go over time, but he emphasizes what's important to know for the future, and gives us tips for interviews and opportunities that other professors don't.

Great professor, the slides are very informative, and grading policies are generous. You are almost guaranteed a B on a homework as long as you tried every problem (even if the solution is incorrect) and submit it on time. He is very generous with extensions, too.

He's a professor that knows his stuff, but goes kind of fast at times. As somebody with no prior knowledge, it was hard to keep up. Attendance won't directly change your grade, the classes with low attendance had significantly lower test averages than the other classes (he will call out classes with low attendance). DO THE HW, IT WILL SAVE YOU!

He's a chill guy. Lectures were fun even if they were hard to understand. He's also really good at making everything practical which helps a lot with understanding. Easily one of the best professors I've ever had.

Amazing professor for ECE 1004. Relates the concepts in class to his time in industry a lot and that really helped put things in perspective and think about practicality. In-class problems are really helpful to give a preview to the homework and exam problems. Was accessible for questions out of scope of the class and was really accessible.

Dr. Ball is a great teacher, gave good lectures, and always responded fast to emails. He was not in charge of ece2024, but the class (which is already hard) was extremely disorganized and poorly set up. Errors on all assignments, lecture notes, and answer keys. Go to office hours, really helpful and cares for you. Does his best with what's given.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ball is a great ECE prof. He knows a lot about analog & power electronics and is great at connecting theoretical concepts to what actually happens in industry or with his audio projects. The class itself is tough because it moves through topics at mach speed and the assignments/labs seem unorganized, though this has nothing to do with Dr. Ball.

Dr. Ball is the best professor for this course, I had lectures by Cooper and Dunning when Dr. Ball was out (with Covid-19, and receiving an award). This course is challenging, no question, but that is part of ECE. Don't listen to the 1/5 ratings, Dr. Ball will try to make sure you understand the material. Note: Office hours never hurt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: LOVED prof Ball! If you need a teacher that actually explains these concepts he's the one to pick! Beware of his random pop quizzes that he gives after class that is due the day of. He messed up our notifications so we didn't know they were due and it really affects your grade. So if you skip class, make sure you're checking canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I definitely would have failed if I hadn't had him as my professor for this class. His office hours were very helpful and you can definitely tell that he cares a lot about his students.

I think a lot of the lower ratings had a really hard time understanding the topics in ECE. He know his stuff but it was a really hard class to begin with and complicated topics. Sometimes he talks above what the students understand but, again, its hard material. Always available after class, seriously good guy and teacher, highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor and great lecturer. Very smart, sometimes expects more than students can handle. Relates material to real life, knows everything there is to know about circuits. Friendly and helpful. A class you will have to work hard in but a fantastic professor nonetheless. Difficult course work but he's very easy to talk to about it.

Overall Dr. Ball had pretty good lectures and I liked that he had a class of review before each exam. However, some of his explanations were not ideal for someone who has no background in the subject. Sometimes it really felt like he did not want us to ask questions either. If you want a good grade, be prepared to work hard for it.

Dr. Ball clearly cares about the subject matter that he teaches, but can sometimes come off as a bit condescending to questions and those who might be struggling a bit. He is a tough grader but will grant extensions on deadlines if you ask in advance. He's not as bad as some of the 1/5's say but he's also not as good as the 5/5's either. 2.5/5
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Ball makes the subject so interesting and teaches well. His online lectures this year were as intriguing as they could be and I found myself enjoying the classwork, labs and subject in general. He made the concepts clear, but studying is still necessary for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed his lectures and his way of teaching. He wasnt just teaching ECE concepts, but also how they are related to the real world and fundamentals of engineering, while making it very interesting. I dont understand the the harsh comments that are recently made by others. Also, as a CPE major, I never felt excluded. 100% recommended.

Dr. Ball performed pretty well given the online format this semester. He made a point of making solid connections to real world issues and concepts and gave good examples of where different circuits, IC's, and skills were put to use in student led projects around campus. However, he is disrespectful at times and his quizzes are often unclear.
I say attendance is nonmandatory because his lectures are so bad it would be better to just not attend.
Get ready to speed run an engineering exam, 22 questions and 1 hour to do it. Avoid this guy at all costs, worst professor I've ever had.
I expect more from a Virginia Tech Professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures make no sense that also come with quizzes that don't match them. Everything I learned from this class has been my own time. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Brilliant teacher that knows his stuff without sounding pretentious. Always gives off a warm, yet serious vibe that makes you listen during lectures. He's great during office hours and may be willing to talk about topics relating to the class without getting too off track. He wants you to be aware of the big picture.

Very charming and cares for his students. He's very passionate about all things ECE especially audio amplifiers and sound equipment. Wish I had made more time to just talk about the field of ECE with him because he is a very down to Earth character. He will be very repetitive on important topics so pay attention to that.

Take him for every class you possibly can. Dr. Ball is everything you could want in a professor: he knows his subject, has tons of really open office hours, is incredibly friendly both in-person and through Piazza, and gives plenty of practice and examples. The only sucky part about this class was the lack of proper feedback on assignments.
Obviously cares about his student's success. Decent lecturer, and he knows what he's talking about. Very professional.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ball is good, he has lots of experience in the ECE field. The course is very easy ONLY IF you have learned electricity and magnetism in physics. Computer logic things like flip-flop is a little bit confusing. Labs are a little bit hard, but they are fun. It's fun to shock others by telling them "I have learned XXXX in my freshman year!".
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Ball is a really good professor who is very knowledgeable in his subject area, and is willing to answer questions during class. He performs very good examples in class, but if you are confused he will take time to help in office hours. Overall, a really good professor who explains difficult material in a way that students can understand.

Dr. Ball is the best professor I have had at Virginia Tech so far. He has a clear grading criteria, gives extra credit and fair questions on his tests, cares about his students, good examples during lecture, and is just a great guy. He assigns about 10 homework problems a week, sometimes more. Has detailed lecture slides, wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Taylor is the sweetest! She clearly respects her students and wants them to succeed beyond her class. She gives great feedback on deliverables and is always willing to discuss ideas or concerns. There are a lot of writing assignments, and the turn around time for large projects can be short, but they were definitely manageable.
this teacher is amazing

Dr. Taylor is so great, and is very understanding and caring. This class is group-project based the whole semester, and she interacts thoroughly with each group. She is also quite easy to reach outside of class. I really enjoyed her lectures and thought they were interesting and inspiring. This class is pretty easy as long as you put the work in.

Professor Beleny is just all over the place. She seems to honestly not have a ton of knowledge on what she's teaching which made the material hard to follow through the semester. You'll also have 500 assignments due, all are group projects, and they're graded seemingly at random with no feedback. Please don't take her, she's just incompetent.

This was for MGT 3304, The work can be alot sometimes but its really simple, however its easy to get a terrible grade on the exams if you don't put in the effort. There is also two short essays/projects that are worth a decent part of your grade but if you actually try its a very easy class.

MGT 3304 has a couple of assignments every week, short quizzes, and 2 exams with lockdown browser and a camera. Overall, the class is not super hard, and shouldn't take more than a 30 minutes to an hour each week.

Professor Beleny is kind but very unorganized. Tests are on a lockdown browser with a camera and are extremely difficult. Lecture material doesn't help much with homework or quizzes. Expect around six homework assignments weekly. The class feels like busy work, and she rarely responds to emails, making it hard to get help or clarification.
Easy class. She can be rude. As a person. Not a deal breaker though. Just rude. With an easy class.

MGT 3304: Super easy online class. Assignments were on real-world, useful material with lots of extra credit. Fair grader and abt 3 assignments a week which I genuinely enjoyed doing. Most assignments are abt 250 word group discussions. If you enjoy work like that (I sure do!) then I highly recommend this class!!!

She's very nice. Definitely attend lectures, pay attention and ATTEND LECTURES, read canvas assignments in their entirety, and there's no reason you shouldn't do well. People that complain usually are the ones who don't pay attention or listen to instructions.
Beleny spreads her pages so wide even the principal can see. likes to offer up cookies

Overall easy, but exams were horrible. Always had breakout rooms during class. Exams were lockdown browser and very difficult, so specific and was often about stuff she barely talked about in class. 70 question. Horrible. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities but they are extremely time consuming. Major group project at the end, very easy.

I took her class online. It wasn't too bad. We did breakout rooms but she tried to make it a good environment and something that students enjoyed. I would take her again. She knew the material she was teaching and the course material had lots of variation. Some assignments were fun. Group project in an online class isn't fun.

Class is easy as long as you keep up with the assignments and group projects. Make sure your group is on top of things as it can get hectic when no one has done anything near the submission date. Beleny can be extremely passive-aggressive in her emails and attendance is honestly not required.

Honestly, the class wasn't hard, but DO YOUR WORK. The only reason I got the grade I received is because I was up to date with my work. Attendance is not necessarily required, but what she talks about in class is on the quizzes. The TA did not help at all, but it helps to know people who have taken this class before.

Professor Beleny means well but her class is chaotic. You can tell Beleny knows a lot but her thoughts are not clear. None of the students know what is going on. Her assignments are pointless projects. There are a ton of projects with the same group for the whole semester! She assumes we know what is going on with NO instructions or rubric.
x
Lots of group projects. Free textbook. Good TA. Overall, I liked the class
Awful with responding to emails, class is boring and completely online. Not engaging at all and she was extremely passive aggressive about turning on cameras.

Professor Beleny is one of the WORST examples of a slacking principles professor I have ever had. She makes it very clear that she does not wish to be in a 1000 level course, and will be extremely rude to any emails or requests. Very unwilling to work with students and does not bother to update the years old canvas. Many assignments have wrong info

Her lectures are hit or miss sometimes with their structure, but she rewards participation with EC. Homework wasn't that difficult. Quizzes and tests can be especially difficult because of how specific they are, go to office hours and study. She is much better with technology this semester, so I wouldn't worry about earlier reviews saying that.

Took this in Spring 2022. No textbooks because it's provided. You might be asked to buy software that are tied to group projects later on though. Webcams is mandatory and it's your typical presentation-style teaching. Responds to emails quickly, beware of pop quizzes, and a bit messy in preparing assignments, but will correct if mistakes are made.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Beleny is always prepared, brings personal experiences and engages a lot with the class. This class is tough, but you really get what you put in. Talk to the teacher if you have any issues, she will absolutely help. Get to know the professor, do the readings, take notes, and you'll get that A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: When the time I took her classes, she was really kind and replying all my emails on time. She might put some assignments on the wrong date but she will fix it as soon as you let her know or she found out. Honestly, the class wasn't too hard, at least the time I took it, it wasn't.

This class was terrible. The professor was nice, but NEVER responded to emails. Luckily TAs were amazing. The tests were wicked hard and some quizzes were too. The group project is very easy and thankfully that was weighted far more than the tests. Lectures need participation and cameras on. Lots of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Tests/final make up 15% of your total grade, this class is one of the easiest As ever and teaches alot of important lessons on IB. Would highly recommend if you want to learn more about IB and get a GPA boost! I studied maybe 1 total hour for every test we had combined and finished with a 97 so i'd like to think I can SayAnA IsAchievableForAnyone.

Goes on tangents, never prepared, assigns an ungodly amount of work that she never goes over but expects you to know for quizzes and exams. You'll spend 98% of this class reading and doing assignments that she picks THE MOST SPECIFIC CRITERIA TO TEST YOU ON. I want a refund.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She has never been prepared for online class. Ever. It is incredibly hard to stay engaged in her class, and deadlines and due dates are unclear. Do not take her class.

She really only taught from the book, everything that was taught could have been found in the textbook almost word for word. Not sure how knowledgeable she is on the subject, but she tried to make it engaging for the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have had, hopeless

I dont know what happened to her teaching style based on recent reviews but she was great during the Spring 2021 semester. I found this class incredibly easy as long as you got the assignments done. There were a couple group projects so make sure you get those done early.
HORRIBLE. IS NEVER PREPARED. EVER. ASSIGNMENTS ARE OVERLY SPECIFIC AND SHE IS INCREDIBLY VAUGE. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The most unprepared teacher I have had at Tech. Every class something is going wrong and wastes a lot of the class time. Goes over a broad range of material, but asks extremely specific questions on assignments. Asks students if there is anything she can do, but then never does it if someone suggests something.
DO NOT TAKE HER. She's always confused and non of her assignments teach you anything. Save yourself the time.

Professor Beleny is a poor teacher who is rigid aloof and doesn't convey the material very well. Perhaps we can blame distance learning for her deficits but I doubt she would be better in person. Grade F.

She's very unorganized and the lectures make no sense whatsoever. This class is all over the place & everyone was confused all semester. Midterm and Final are hard and the "study guides" she gives do not cover any material on the exams. Grades tough for no reason and pre-readings for class are irrelevant. Avoid her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class & lectures were disorganized. I wouldn't know what we were doing in group projects/what was expected & we didn't get any review or study guide for the final because we all did so poorly on the midterm that she was not going to help us again. Not too hard to get an A but still a hard class. She also wouldn't respond to a lot of my emails.

actually one of the worst professors I've ever had. She's very disorganized and her exams are a joke. About half of the questions are weirdly specific and pretty much impossible to answer. A good portion of the semester is spent working on a group country project that I found to be a waste of time--I didn't really learn anything.

Her classes are very disorganized with much of the class time being wasted by her technical difficulties. She will also take off points from straightforward assignments for seemingly no reason at all. Her exams are also difficult, with her exam study guides excluding many of the topics that show up on the actual exams. Would not recommend taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is all over the place and always seems to have technical difficulties, as the class taught online. Additionally, her weekly quizzes are extremely difficult due to some questions being way too specific, even if you read the material. There are only 2 exams, but they were super difficult and many did poorly. Would not recommend Take someone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very disorganized and not good at explaining things

Alot of group work, her class is all over the place, most of the time she has no idea what's going on. Very vague when explaining heavy graded work and uses other professor's lectures. This may be because its her first year here but it's just hectic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very boring in lecture, all he does is read off of the slides. The tests were all online and open note for me, so the class wasn't hard. However, he doesn't answer questions very well nor does he really seem to care about his students. I was interested in MSE before taking his class, but that interest has disappeared thanks to him.
I just want to let all future students know that after Fall 2024 tests will be on paper and attendance will be graded.
Lecture was very dull and your grade is based mainly on homework. Test aren't too difficult if you pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework is the majority of the grade. The tests are online, directly based on homework, and you get one week to complete them from the start date. Lectures are boring but this is an easy class to get an A in.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I know this class so much. Compared to the other science courses offered, astro is so easy and so much less work.

Ashall is the best professor ive had so far at tech. His class was not attendance mandatory, but his lectures were very funny and interesting. He also gives extra credit for showing up to lectures which helps a lot. It is kinda impossible to fail this class.

Very chill, clearly passionate about what he does. There's weekly homework due on Fridays but he gives you 10 attempts on each question and has help if you're still struggling. He doesn't take attendance but you should go to class for the extra-credit surveys at the end; they boost your grade a LOT. No quizzes or tests, just a final worth 30%.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very easy Intro to Astronomy. You only have a weekly Mastering Astronomy homework to do and a final exam. Dr. Ashall is a very nice person and he is also very resourceful and accomplished in the field of Astronomy. As long as you pay attention in class, you should get an easy A.

Extremely easy first-year astronomy class. Homework was 70% of your grade and the final was 30%. You always had chances for extra credit. 1-3 hours of homework a week it was all online. As long as you go to the class there will be no quizzes or tests. He was overall a funny guy as well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She goes through the proofs for known shortcuts thoroughly and also warns to not assume the conditions are the same in every problem. She clears up misconceptions and hints at exam problems. While tedious, the many problems this class gives between problem sets, homework, in-class examples, and in lab work, reinforces the physics principles well.

Dr. Ashkar is a good professor. She offers many extra credit opportunities and explains concepts well. However, her course is fast-paced, so it might be challenging if you've not studied much of the content before. She also gets furious at the end if you leave class early or talk too much while she lectures. Overall, she is a pretty good professor.

Professor Ashkar was fantastic. Her lectures were clear and concise. Just showing up gets you all the clicker points. If you ever went to office hours she was very helpful. Everything that was wrong about the class, poorly written homework questions and a terribly revised lab is stuff that is the same in all the physics classes.

Professor was amazing. She has the highest percentage of As in her department (she told us on the first day of lecture and you can check institutional data). Anyone who complains probably didn't pay attention in class, she TELLS you what type of questions will be on the exam. Not hard to do well as long as you do the homework and extra credit.

She's a good teacher and many things in her class are easy credit, but she can be rude in her lectures. Gets frustrated when students try to leave before she is done and makes rude comments about it relating to grades. Also, she's not forgiving if you have an issue out of your control and doesn't give second chances. Hw is harder than tests

Physics is hard to teach newer students, and Dr. Ashkar does a somewhat decent job explaining it. She gets pretty sidetracked when teaching material, so understanding the material can be challenging. She is flexible with office hours and will happily help you with material you don't understand (only during office hours though).

This professor is very kind and always answers questions very thoroughly during lectures. Her office hours are extremely helpful, and she is willing to spend as much time as possible to explain any concept. Some of the complaints in other posts are with the course load, but the department decides the assignments required and not the professor.

She's nice if you talk to her during office hours, but the class a weed out course. However, her section tends to be among the highest in test/quiz scores. She works through problems, but there's a lot of material. Sometimes she laughs violently if you get a question wrong and will get angry if everyone tries to leave early.

This Professor is a very kind person, if you go to office hours and talk to her she will try her most to make sure you are not left behind. The concepts are hard but if you are good at math then she is a good professor.
Impatient and rude in lecture, often gets mad at students when they don't know the answer to a question. Other than that, decent teacher and definitely knows her stuff

Pretty difficult to pay attention to in lecture, there are rarely any demonstrations, which I feel is needed to break the long lecture up. Homework is extremely difficult, and she is kind of rude. However, the structure of the class is organized and easy to follow along with.
Lots of homework, tests worth most of the grade. Terrible lecturer and teacher,
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of reviews here are negative, but they're also old. They don't match my experience with Dr. Ashkar at all - she is a great professor who is responsive outside of class and always friendly. Lectures are cohesive and posted. She even started throwing candy to students who correctly answered questions.
Not a cohesive teacher, lectures are not structured well

Not all smart people are good teachers. She forgets sometimes that we don't know a lot when taking her course. She is rude and not a respectful person. I love constructive criticism, but her version of criticism borders on insulting and making you feel small/worthless. Must be how she was taught. I know she treats her grad students the same way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm sure you've read the other reviews of this professor, but it's just as they've said. She seems to not understand basic cordial professor-student communication. The class itself is awful but that's because of how it is standardized at VT. She simply made it all the more worse.

Spent more time on YouTube than her lectures. She isn't very good at explaining concepts and is the first teacher I've ever seen get mad at someone for asking a question. She seems to have a power trip kind of deal going on where she sees all her students as inferior because she knows a lot about physics. Not very personable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Note, I took this class during the coronavirus pandemic. She teaches as if you already have taken physics in high school and expects students to instantly understand. She is not a pleasant person to interact with if you need help. There's a reason why the class average is around 10 points lower than every other section of PHYS2305

Does not accept any fault of her own on teaching despite our class average consistently being 5 to 10 points below other sections of the class. The class allows you some room for error but in order to succeed in the class you must have some background in physics. Is also not pleasant to talk to regarding questions

She's a very direct teacher and tells you in class key concepts that will be useful on exams. Online homework is harder than the exams will ever be. Her iClicker questions are difficult and trick questions, but overall her teaching was pretty straight forward and she was always willing to answer questions.

Ashkar is alot like a high school teacher. What I mean by that is she gets mad if youre talking to much in class and she will call you out and she likes to pull "we still have two minutes." There is alot of extra credit but beware the practice tests are nothing like the real tests. The curves are also nice and a lot of grade forgiveness.

The way she explains stuff in her lectures threw me off so much that the first 2 tests I got a 70 (w/o the curve). Shes not very kind, but you don't have to pay attention to pass-you probably have a better chance of passing actually. There is so much EC, curves on every test, and the final exam redemption policy from the department its easy to pass

She is flat out rude and yelled at the entire lecture for not being smart enough to answer her clicker questions with both speed and accuracy. On the note of her clicker questions, they are IMPOSSIBLE I think I got 100% three days all semester and there were many more days where I didn't get a single question right. She does not teach to the tests
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Ashkar's good at explaining the material, but she spends a fair bit of time in the beginning going over proofs for things that are usually self-explanatory. The iClicker questions are misleading but they're not worth too much. The amount of time she spends on a topic in class varies, so reading the book is helpful but not too necessary.

The clicker questions are designed to throw you off and she misleads the class into getting the clicker questions wrong. The only reason why I stayed alive in her class was because I had taken AP physics 1 & 2 in high school. Also at the start of the semester everyone in her class had signed up for O'Donnell, but the school changed the professor.

Awesome class and really straightforward. Whats on the lectures is whats on the test but applying it to scenarios discussed in class. No final, just a written min of 1 page report on researchers presentations from class. I have nothing bad to say about the class or the teacher himself. Would recommend.

I liked this class! I like ecology, and it's clear that Dr. Gray does as well. His lectures felt relevant to the real world, and there were no surprises on the tests. His policies were fair, so I was surprised to hear some complain about them. Just sit down and study, you'll do great!
literally the best professor i've ever had. he cares so much about his students success and gives so many point opportunities and what he teaches is EXACTLY what is on the test. TAKE HIS CLASS

Dr. Gray is a great professor! He truly cares about his students and offers a lot of opportunities for you to succeed. His test are straight forward and his lectures are interesting. If you simply show up and do the work you will do well in this course and also learn a lot about ecology. If you have the chance to take this class, do it!

Great professor. If you did well in BIOL 1106 this class will be a breeze. Makes topics easy to understand, so you'll still have the knowledge in your head by every exam. Gives back credit if like 50% of the class gets a test answer wrong, so at least a 6 point curve is a given. Easy 5 EC points per test if you skim through the papers. No final
his test are extremely difficult and his study guides correlate to nothing he shows on the exams if possible find another professor for ecology
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very good teacher and is insightful

Completely asynchronous, recording podcasts is the only grade and they are due every other Sunday. They are reflection-based off the cumulative minor. As long as you complete the directions and answer every question, you'll get a 100.

Wonderful person, horrible class. WAY too much work for a pathways course. At least 7 hours of work weekly on top of the major essays and projects. MUST attend class, if you have TWO unexcused absences you WILL drop a letter grade (insane). All about leadership and taking a stand, so, as a student leader. DONT. DO. IT.

reviews.comment: Seems like a really nice guy who is very passionate and invested in leadership, but LDRS 1414 was ridiculously work heavy for a pathways elective. reviews.comment: Seems like a really nice, genuine guy who is very passionate and invested in leadership, but LDRS 1414 was ridiculously work heavy for a pathways elective.
