reviews.comment: Dr. Council is a very nice professor who wants his students to learn. He is not a tough grader and mostly looks at if you are reflective and actually trying. There is one assignment a week, usually a discussion board, but there are a few larger assignments like essays/presentations. Highly recommend the asynchronous version of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Super caring, you can tell he really wants his students to succeed. Used a "de-centered" grading criteria where every assignment was weighted the same so that there was a focus on learning rather than on grades, which I loved. Just participate in discussions and complete assignments and you'll do well!
He is kind and truly wants you to succeed.

I took Dr. Council (LDRS 1015) leadership course and I liked it. It was a lot of work and material but if you manage your time properly you should be fine.. Fairwarning, there was a major writing assignment due every other week and sometimes every week. But at the end of the course you will have good exposure to leadership and its concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Has trouble with racial differences. Bad to discuss only his view. Negative attitude to all unless you only agree with his beliefs about blacks.
Such an amazing professor! He is extremely nice and helpful.

His class is interesting, but do NOT take it thinking it will be easy.  To get an A, you will have to go to every class, take notes, and read every article, because he tests on EVERYTHING.  Don't expect to do well unless you are a really good student.

The man is a genius! It is kinda hard keeping up. He's available for help if he sees that you are doing what is in your power to do well. You 'll need to read the articles he talks about, come to class & read the text. Do that your fine. If you're a slacker(irregularly come to class, dont read or pay attention) & expect to do well you'll be screwed
terrible

Great Prof. Great lecture style. Clear and concise. Learned a lot. Too many people here complaining because he actually makes you READ the material and STUDY! How terrible! Just go to class, take good notes and read the book- you'll do fine.
He rambles on and on about nothing, it never makes sense.
He's great! Huge knowledge base but he doesn't let people slide. One of the few instructors around that still expects people to earn their grades

Beware. If you miss one class, he will not help you. His lectures are are great if you over look the fact that he has no consistent thought pattern. He rambles on and on. Average day of notes is 5 pages. He once said a total amount of 5 sentences on a study and there was 3 questions on the test on it.
The material is easy to understand, but you have to really focus on it and learn it all to get an A. If you put it enough work you can get an A.

Lectures were extremely boring and painful to go to.  You have to read to get an A and you have to attend lectures and take good notes.  Tests were multiple choice and short answer, and they were hard.  I wouldn't recommend this professor.
if you do the reading, you'll get an A easily. social psych is pretty easy... just understand the underlying concepts and the tests are easy.
No Comments

Professor Price is one of the best professors I have had the privilege of learning from. The class is not easy, but she makes understanding the law and legal jargon digestible. Exams are hard, but she is super fair. Her class requires your full attention, but her clear and caring teaching style helps make the class so much better.

Prof. Price was the most organized, intelligent, & well-spoken professor I've had at VT. Everything she said made sense, and every question was answered precisely. She made sure we participated w/o making it laborious. She had such reasonable grading & exams. She even talked with me about post-college plans. I haven't learned this much in a while.

Quizzes are hard, but they prepare you for the tests, which are easier. Exam reviews and quiz bank questions are very helpful for studying. The professor takes attendance in every class. You can use one cheat sheet for the exams, and the final exam is not cumulative. By far the best professor I've ever had, she makes a hard course enjoyable.

Professor Price is by far my favorite professor at VT. I recommend taking her if you want to pass the course. She does make students put in effort to receive a good grade, but it's for a good reason. She wants you to learn this material, not just "remember" it. She provides test reviews, USE THEM. They help A LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Quizzes are extremely hard, and the tests require lots of studying, but if you pay attention, you can do well. Very interesting class where you learn a lot and doing well on the tests feels extremely rewarding. Very diligent with grading and wants every student to succeed.

Professor Price was the best professor I've had at Tech. The class is challenging, as there is a lot of material to learn and memorize, but it is exciting, and the professor does a great job teaching it. DO NOT miss classes, as a good portion of your grade is based on class attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you're the kind of person that likes to skip class you should NOT take Price. She uses an on-point system, so you have a few classes where you absolutely have to participate. Her tests were completely aligned with the in-class slideshows and quiz questions so really as long as you care enough to put in effort you'll be fine. She's great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Price is an awesome professor. She knows her content and is clearly passionate about it as well. Her lectures move fast, but she is considerate of the students and goes very in-depth into the content. Weekend quizzes kind of suck and tests can be rough. However, they were made much easier because of how great she is. Take her if you can

I loved this class. The material was very interesting and Price is a great professor. There is a lot of reading so be ready. Attendance is mandatory, you only get two absences before a grade penalty. There are weekly quizzes but if you take notes and do the reading you'll do well. The exam questions are super similar to quizzes. I would take again.

Professor Price is one of the best professors i have had at Virginia Tech. She genuinely cares about her students and her lectures are very interesting and intellectually stimulating. There are readings before every class and when you are "on point" you have to participate. Its not really that bad as long as you try your best.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lots of reading when you are "on point" but learned a lot in the class. Participation matters and if you just show up to class and do minimal on the homeworks, then you are going to do very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Price is probably one of my favorite professors at VT. Yes her BLaw class is hard and requires a lot of time outside to study and comprehend, but she makes the class fun and enjoyable for each student. If you come to class, ask questions and go to her office hours, you will pass the class.

Professor Price cares a lot about her students and provides plenty of extra resources for us learn from if we don't quite understand a topic. Price does the best she can to convey all the information she teaches in a way that clicks with students and never leaves us wondering what topics will be covered on the exams. Overall great professor.

Professor Price conveys law in a very clear and concise way. The lectures contain a lot of material, but she makes it easy. She uses an on point system which basically requires you to have notes before class to use for participation twice a semester for a grade. Aside from the class, Prof Price is a kind and understanding woman, highly recommend.

Prof Price honestly makes BLaw super enjoyable. She keeps lectures simple and easy to understand, while also incorporating real-life examples into lectures. I do think the course is hard because there's a lot to interpret and understand. Her on-point system was certainly something to keep in mind, if you're not prepared it's awkward.

Don't listen to those who say Professor Price isn't the best teacher for this class. I'm glad I didn't let those reviews discourage me from choosing a passionate, driven, and superb professor like Ms. Price. As long as you do what is needed, you should be fine. Her class has been a pleasure, I look forward to having her again in the near future.

I had never been interested in law until I took her class. Really great lectures, largely discussion based. Take her class if you wanna actually learn something.
Getting an A will be relatively harder than in other courses in Pamplin, a lot of reading and slides, and the exam questions simply require you to truly understand the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Do NOT take her. She makes this class way harder than it needs to be. She gives out a quiz every weekend rather than during the week. Her exams are way harder than they need to be.

Had her for cyberlaw FIN 4014, and she's one of my favorite professors I've had at VT! I didn't expect the class to be interesting at all, but the conversations she facilitated in class were all very interesting real-life scenarios. Also, its obvious that she really cares about your grades! Very compassionate and understanding.
Talks all class an gave us 2 day warning for the midterm

She was absolutely AMAZING! Always available to help and very accessible. Explains every topic in detail and applies it to real world which makes the hardest topics seem the easiest. Cannot recommend her enough. One of the best professors I've had.
Price has great lectures, but they always take the whole time. Her on point system helped me a lot personally, and having a cheat sheet on the exams was clutch.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You can tell that Prf. Price is really passionate about her lectures and class. Definitely be prepared to read and study though. She makes her class more difficult than other professors with on point and open ended questions on exams. I'm literally scared to miss one class because I take at least 7 pages of fast notes each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her class lectures are very thorough and she as a teacher is super knowledgeable about the subject. However, you gotta prepare for the on-point system she has in place because she can either ask a broad/general question or asks for a specific example of something. Compared to other profs her tests have short answers where others don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Price is so nice and the subject is kind of boring at times but she does a good job of making things interesting. She's very understanding and accomadating as well. She gives a cheat sheet on the exams and while they're still difficult, they're not terrible
Professor Price is amazing! Her class is difficult and there is a lot of material, but she makes her class so interesting. She is by far one of the best professors at Virginia Tech!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Atkins has little scrutiny against the way she teaches the course. While she clearly knows what she is talking about, her lectures and notes are often too abstract or, conversely, too simplistic. She makes the class far more arduous than it has to be, and does not cover topics very well. A lot of self-study is required.

He was probably the best professor I have ever had. Absolutely worth the class.

the nicest teacher, you can tell she really is interested in what she teaches. super understanding. tests are very similar to study guide and she uses class time to review!

awesome professor, really brings the material to life. her tests are straight from the lectures so you don't need to read as long as you go to class. definitely my favorite professor, hands down. it's worth getting up at 8am for and an easy a.
Very helpful. Clear, easy to understand. Entertaining.

Dr. Bell was the best teacher I've had at Tech so far!  She is very organized and you will do great if you go to all her lectures.  Very sweet lady, tests are easy if you pay attention.  Makes class very interesting!
Nice guy but his lectures were hard to follow. Self teaching concepts was common throughout the semester. Never released the final test grade.

Exams are worth 85 of your grade and consist of very few questions. Exams are much harder than the homework. Go to all lectures and make sure you do all the practice problems and more that are listed in the syllabus. Doing bad on one exam will make it impossible to come back from. His lectures are hard to follow so you might have to self teach.

Teaches Diff‑Eq (MATH 2214) but admits he's “learning with us”. Doesn't speak very loud, Projects onto the chalkboard and writes over it, making the work very hard to see. Teaches from the online textbook with minimal additional explanation and fails to address questions clearly.

Sweet prof who wants you to learn, homework is manageable and harder than tests, so you feel prepared. Calc 3 is just hard, so it comes off badly on the professor, but he was willing to help when asked and would crack jokes sometimes.

Super nice guy and he teaches in depth. Go to his office hours it helps and he will review tests with you. Assigns homework that is on the test after the test so make sure you cover everything thats going to be on the test because the homework helps a ton.

Very sweet professor who cares. He thoroughly explained topics and was more than willing to re-explain difficult concepts. Pretty easy to know what was going to be on the exams. He gave generous partial credit on midterms and graded in reasonable time. Only thing I didn't love was that I never saw or got my grade for the final exam.

He is a sweet professor, can get to the point fast, and has an obvious presentation. There is not a lot of mandatory HW, but there is HW and practice problems in the syllabus,s which are helpful to keep on top of.

His lectures are definitely a struggle to keep full attention, but he is very sweet and explains things thoroughly. His slides and the practice problems he goes over in class are directly from the textbook, so that is really your only resource in the class. He also rarely assigns homework, so very little practice unless you do it on your own.

Diamond in the rough. Puts the rest of the math department to shame. Remember all the times you're just waiting for your math/sci/eng professor to get to the point and give you the actual formula and a practice problem to cement it in? That's what this man does. He's polite, low-stress, his lecturing flows like a calm stream that makes multi fine.

The professor is a nice person who I think is caring overall. The course is not too difficult with fair grading, but requires a good amount of self study. However it is very unorganized. The professor is not really responsive to emails and often forgets things.

Bad at explaining things. His handwriting was hard to read, he also gave about 2 example problems the whole semester. And yet expected you to do problems for homework and on tests for no partial credit. Although he did curve the class a letter grade at the very end, it was annoying not knowing how our grade would turn out.

This spring lab focuses on a team-based senior design project. Teams meet regularly with assigned TA and faculty advisor. There are also three meetings with the professor. Teams post weekly updates on Canvas and submit a final AIAA standard paper. There are no exams, and it's not too hard to earn an A with a solid project and consistent effort.

For it being Professor Davoudi's first time teaching Fluid Dynamics at Virginia Tech, he did his best to cover the material. He was constantly reassuring, inspirational, and caring about our success not just in the classroom but in life as well. He excelled at providing an engaging learning experience, often connecting theory to real life examples.

He is bad at: responding to emails, setting clear deadlines, controlling emotions, etc. Overall, be on his good side or you will know that you are not on that side. He is very unclear on the grading and deadlines. This is very important for project based classes, he does not send rubrics or deadlines dates until it is tooo late. Best of luck, GG

Dr. Davoudi is nice, but this lab was disorganized. After two labs, the schedule lacked structure. The 3rd lab, a foam glider project, felt like arts and crafts and pointless to report on. The 4th lab, satellite navigation, was scrapped. Graded on 3 lab reports and a senior design experiment with occasional meetings. Easy lab but poorly executed.

Prof Davoudi is a great guy,  but the structuring of this class was awful. The lectures consisted of him purely reading off of the slides and giving general equations. Never did ANY example problems and did NOT post his lecture notes. Constant issues with HW assignments. The tests were all in person and many of us felt grossly underprepared.

Dr. Davoudi is highly intelligent, and knows his material, but is apt to go on tangents and doesn't teach clearly. Most of my learning came from the textbook and other sources. He was also regularly late to classes, and asked us to stay late to make up for it. He's a great guy, but just be prepared to do the grunt work of learning on your own time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy and great class. I would say though if you're looking for class to take to just get credits and need it to be super easy this might not be the one. Theres just a lot of homework and projects, there all easy to do it just takes time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: BEST PROFESSOR! I would take his class every semester if I could. I didn't get into his ENGL 1106 and I am currently so upset. Such an approachable teacher and always makes you feel good. Can't forget that he's hilarious.

Kind man, easy grader. I look forward to his class and his performances. He says correct spelling is oppressive if that doesn't sum up the English class. You can submit late and it can be informal. Genuinely a great class

There is a decent amount of homework and reading, but it's very easy. Hee grades are based on completion, and if you do your work, you will get an A. He is entertaining and very understandable. Would definitely take again. Cancels class often, like every other week.

Dr. B was very chill and easygoing, often acting as a guide for the direction of my research project. Although there are a lot of assignments, they build on the project you are working on, making the final project easy to do if you have completed the previous assignments. You have to make a prototype to help teach your topic, but it is fun.
Although there is a lot of homework and things to do on your own, very cheerful, very easy grader too. Would definitely recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 100% Top notch!
Hes very cool

best english professor at vt!! he's so nice and its almost impossible to get anything below a 95 in his class. a lot of the work done for homework is just busy work but it does help with the projects.

Dr. Bennington makes the first year writing class more fun and engaging than other professors. For 1106, you had to make a board game with a group which was pretty fun. Also, if you are having problems with anything, he will help you out. Lectures are boring and there are several small assignments but overall, he is a great professor.

Professor Bennington has made my first semester of college amazing. He is caring and truly just wants to see his students succeed. There is a lot of homework, but if you at least try your best on the assignment, you will most likely get full credit. He does not lock his assignments after the due date and is very lenient. Best professor I have had!

There's a LOT of homework assigned but it's honestly easy busy work. Dr. B is also an easy grader, and he's super lenient with due dates & deadlines. As long as you do your work, you'll probably get an A. His lectures are actually interesting--and this is coming from somebody who HATES writing/english classes.

There is A LOT of pointless homework, but he is an easy grader so it's an easy A. He never really understood the assignments that he had assigned us. Attendance is not mandatory most of my class never went. Tough group project where you build a functioning board game from scratch which was cool but tedious. Would take for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy A but worst professor I've ever had. When I say I could not physically sit through a lecture without crawling in my skin I mean it. He has a 20 minute long intro video on himself that he makes you watch on the first day and karate performances he does by himself dedicated to his mom. Cringed to hard I don't think Ill ever be the same again

Juan Berrios is very enthusiastic & cheerful. Lectures are not "technically" mandatory, but 10% of your grade is based on random attendance grades. The course content is somewhat difficult, as are the tests, but getting a good grade in the class is not difficult. I found the lectures a to be long, and at times scattered.
lots of assignments but they are easy, only 2 exams.

Professor Berrios is a very good and enthusiastic professor in my opinion. His lectures weren't quite 'mandatory' but he did grade based on random attendance check-ins. The listening exams were fairly difficult, but as long as you pay attention you will do fine. The final written assignment was also not difficult. The class was enjoyable overall.

Took this online, so I don't know much about the professor (he looks fun though). The class didn't have much work, and as long as you completed your assignments, you will get an A. Tests weren't too bad either, and you will get to listen to some weird stuff halfway through the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He is really enthusiastic, but for me the class is kind of a drag. He moves very slow in the content and attendance is graded. The inquisitives are pretty annoying, but easy. The class itself was just too slow paced for me, but I am a musician to begin with. At the end of the day I like Professor Berrios though.

Very enthusiastic about the subject material and presents his lectures in a way that make them interesting. If you aren't into music this class will bore you, but at least you will be entertained. The class grading scheme is designed to get you to pass if you put in the work but expect to put a few hours in each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The content of this class is honestly terrible, but Professor Berrios is very passionate about the subject, making it easy to follow along. He is very funny and radiates such great vibes. As long as you do the Homework Assignements and go to the review sessions on zoom, you will pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just a very low effort teacher. I don't know how she got hired, but whatever. If you want a good grade, you really can't rely on the teacher. The lectures harp on points that I think are not that important and don't touch on what really matters and what's on the test.

Her class isnt all that bad, most of the homework assignments and quizzes are the exact same. For example the homework assignments questions would be on the quiz and then also on the midterm. She is a slide reader, but easy class to pass if you put in the work yourself.

i'd rather watch paint dry than go to this class. only like three graded assignments a month and in-class tests/quizzes that are hard and given with little time to complete. She just reads off the slides too and everything is posted in canvas. take this class at community college unless you want to suffer.

reviews.comment: Don't rly need to buy the textbook bc she just has everything on the slides. Heavy slide reader. Watch Youtube videos instead bc she's bad at explaining and makes it more complicated than it is. Few things to be graded on (1 quiz and 1 hmwk mcq per module, + exams) so if you bomb anything it hurts your grade. Ok person but bad teacher.
Incredible professor with great analysis on South Asia and West Asia. Situates history in structural systems. Caring and accommodating. Flexible and replies to emails quickly.
THE BEST LONG LIVE KADRI
