He's great, Very easy to follow

Good teacher but was sometimes boring and zoomed through lectures. He provides test practice that is similar to the actual tests and will gladly help if you ask him for assistance. He always did seem rushed while going through his lectures and went by very fast to get to the next slide.
A nice guy, tests are worth a lot but not hard, and lectures are pretty good. You won't need to work hard to get a good grade.

Although I have taken gen chem twice before, Professor Bowen managed to teach me new things. Any major problems with 1035 like large lectures, connect homework, and iClickers are out of his control.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Although CHEM 1035 is difficult, attending class was important because Dr. Bowen gave good lectures that explained the content in a less confusing way than the textbook. He works through graded iClicker questions before closing them and records and posts his lectures. The practice tests and worksheets prep you well for tests.

A great guy and very approachable. Always open for questions even during lectures and makes sure everyone feels comfortable in class. Very easy course overall but you have to go for the iClicker points
Great professor. Lectures were interesting, and he prepared everyone for the tests well. He gave good feedback in class when working on problems. Would easily take again.
Provides worked out tests which are very helpful for review, and takes a lot of questions during class. i-clickers are grades but answers are often provided before they close.

I really struggled in this course. Professor Bowen tried his best, but his teaching methods didnt help me to learn. This class is a huge weed out class, so get ready to spend days studying and still fail the tests. Its overall a really difficult course and I feel as though Professor Bowen didnt help a lot with my understanding of material.

Prof. reviewed a lot, sometimes too much and lectures became boring. Often reviewed too much, which then caused us to have to rush on the new material. Responded to emails in a timely manner, and had many opportunities for office hours. There is a lot of homework and class is lecture heavy, but it is that way for the whole chemistry department.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: tests are all multiple choice. there are lots of homework assignments half of which are completion.

Lectures are important, you don't really need to ever read the textbook if you go to them. Attendance is taken with iClickers questions. If you have a decent grasp of Chem, this class will be extremely easy. Bowen is a nice guy, cares about students and takes plenty of time to explain difficult concepts.

Attendance isn't mandatory but will assign graded classwork out of the blue. Very tough grader that will take half your points for small mistakes, refuses to offer any revisions/late work to certain students but will happily give to other students in front of the whole class. Hate his lectures when he flexes what he's done in his "interesting" life

Certainly an odd professor, but it is a good and easy course to take. Always spoke down to his students and got a little too personal sometimes. Felt unprofessional. His grading feels arbitrary at times, too.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor always finds a way to take a ton of points off essays which is unclear why. You think you did a good job on an essay and then you end up with an F. He tells you that your speech is too long when you hand in but then when you present it he fails you because it's too short. You can't win with this guy. He is awful.

This dude grades prerequisite classes like this class will make or break your life. If you want to focus all of your time and energy on a class you are only taking because you have too, take this class. No matter what you do He will find something to pick out and drop 30 points off your essay for it.

He's a pretty chill professor who doesn't assign a ton of work, it is pretty easy to stay on top of all the assignments. The only meh part of this class is his grading. He is a pretty hard grader, but it was fine for me since he offered revisions for 2 of the big assignments and an extra credit oppurtunity at the end of the semester.

He is pretty chill and doesn't assign much work accept for essays.  The essays are not that difficult or long but the grading is not super clear.  You may write what you think is a good essay but he will find some way that it does not line up with the prompt.  There are revisions however, which is good to have.

This professor if probably the best professor i've had. Dr. Brown has very engaging lectures where he intergrates interesting topics such as the parinormal, Horror, and of course the Strange Animal Of The Day at the end of each. I really enjoy his humor, passion, and how knowlegable he is on every topic he covers. In all I love his class.

Very writing heavy class that I found easy as a PSCI major. If you are in class and pay attention that is enough to do well on all of the tests. The essays we had to write were long and felt a bit like overkill but overall were not very difficult. I would def recommend for a pathways or PSCI elective.

reviews.comment: Not a CS major, but I found the class interesting and did learn more about all kinds of security. There's a simulation at the end of class that is interesting but does get tiring toward the end of it. Also enjoyed the in class activities that we did
Dr. Brantly is knowledgeable, strict and very politically opinionated.

I took Professor Brantly for Foundations of Contemporary Security enviornments. For every module you have to write a reflective essay, which can get annoying but are easy once you understand the assignment and what she wants to see. The last 5 classes are a simulation, which is amazingly fun, but you must do the readings to succeed in this. 8/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: There is a simulation for the final project, which is a lot of fun, especially if you get on the red team. Dr.Brantly helps students throughout the class, and is great to talk to for information about technology and security! You can tell she knows what she is talking about!
Dr. Brantly tries to make this class interesting by having an in-class discussion activity at the end of every class. She cares about your input and wants to see you do well.
Cool class with lots of interesting material. Caring and thoughtful professor.

I love this Cyber Security class. The slides are neatly designed and very helpful to take notes down for future paper. During lecture, there are a lot of interesting group discussion. I think paying attention in class is the best to write her papers.
Not the worst professor of all time but the class was extremely boring. She didn't even attempt to make the class fun, just stood at front and lectured reading off the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a good professor however the class has a LOT of work. The group work during class could get frustrating and she gives hw every lecture day. She also has a pre-lecture reading that you have to read to do well on the iclickers. Her test are also pretty hard. She knows her materials and is a good person however this class can be overwhelming.
Inconsistent and unhelpful with her study guides, doesnt match the tests. Feels like she is talking down to you during her lectures, which are not very helpful.

reviews.comment: Very unhelpful class, does not feel like a respected relationship. Would not take again.

Get ready to teach yourself things that she tells you to learn that end up not being on the exam. No help if you miss a class even once. Genuinely made me hate my favorite subject. I would give a 0 if I could

Dr. Bretz is super nice, and is eager to ensure her students have everything they need to succeed. The recorded lectures could be a beast, but the notes from them and the in-class notes were always representative of what was on the tests. However, give yourself plenty of time to study for the tests, as there is a lot of info included on each. =)

Challenging class because I didn't take AP Bio in high school, but by attending class, doing the homework, and reviewing, I was able to get a good grade. Bretz was very kind and good at lecturing, which made the class feel less daunting. She also curves the tests most of the time. Liked her so much i'm taking 1026 with her at 8 am.

Bretz was a great professor. Taking AP Bio in high school is an advantage, but lectures, class participation, asking questions, and referencing the optional textbook offset that if you didn't. Class time involves significant group work and TA guidance so TAKE ADVANTAGE. Alex K is great if you get her!

She was very nice and tried her best to make the class good for us. She'd curve our tests and drop our lowest grades. I felt like sometimes her study guides didn't align with the test and sometimes that something on our test was only mentioned once. However, she was really sweet and her final brought my grade from a C to a B!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Bretz is a amazing and super sweet. Very pre-class learning heavy, and not everything is covered in the class lectures. So, be prepared to know the material before every class. Very accessible and open for office hours and has a great way of explaining. Tests are pretty straight forward to material/iClickers.
There are better teachers to take for Bio at Tech

I really enjoyed taking Bio with Dr. Bretz! She is a genuine person, talks in-depth on materials in slides, and explains the missed i-clicker questions well. She is definitely the best Biology teacher I have had. Also, do the study guides and attend office hrs/schedule meetings with her if you can!

Bio is a hard class in general, but if you're willing to put in the work, she is amazing. I went to her after a couple of bad exams, and she walked me through every question and explained why the answer I chose was wrong.

Gives little to NO extra credit on tests -- with the exception of 2 points once, because her child interrupted the exam. It did not feel like a respected teacher-to-student relationship. Not very helpful with her mini lectures, and the best part of class was the group actives (that the TA's curate). Would not recommend and would not take again.

BIOL 2804 but theres no option for it here. Lecture material didn't match exams. If you miss a class youre basically screwed. Inconsistent and unhelpful study guides. Passive aggressive and exams are 50% of your grade. Dont know how she was for 1105, but she doesnt curve in this class. Feel like I learned nothing even after studying a lot

reviews.comment: best prof for bio 1, she also curves tests so the mean is around a 75
imo best professor for intro bios, very good at breaking down topics and explaining things, easy to talk to if needed, and genuinely cares about her students despite the large class sizes.

Great teacher overall. Patient and helpful during office hours. She will review tests with you. Tests are very straightforward, and she often curves them. Watch video lectures before class because class time will build on those. TAs who grade the group activities can be unpredictable. I enjoyed her classes a lot.

she's a pretty good teacher. she sometimes seems to be confused herself about some content during the lectures. homework is easy, and the activities are easy. she curves the tests which is really nice, and offers few points for extra credit on the final exam. the tests honestly aren't too bad, if you know the content you can apply it on the test

Dr. Bretz was great! Although you watch the main lectures outside of class, her mini lectures were helpful. She was very easy to contact if you run into any problems. She curves her exams which I don't think many other biology professors do. Definitely do try to study at least a little bit for the exams.

Dr. Bretz is a great professor. Her mini lectures in class were helpful and there was a lot of practice material available. Also, she curves her tests unlike a lot of Biol1105 professors which is great. Biol1105 covers a lot of material so doing well in the class requires a lot of studying.

Really enjoyed her class and would have definitely took her again for BIOL1106. Does mini lectures at the beginning of each class but most of your learning will come from videos you have to watch outside of class. Most of the class is doing group activity. She curved every test we took including the final but her tests aren't hard in general.

Very reasonable teacher, starts class with slides about the homework then we end class with a group activity. Lots of on your own work but she was very helpful and always gave us helpful hints or tips and tricks as well as a lot of study resources.

Professor Bretz is very fair and always curves the tests. She takes attendance but sometimes gives extra credit if there is low attendance or if you fill out evaluations. There's a lot of notes and homework to do prior to class, but it's manageable. She seems to genuinely care about her students and want them to succeed.

Prof. Bretz was nice, but she would make her own tests without the other professors which sometimes made collaborative studying harder. Very lecture heavy, and she loves to see participation. Watch the videos before the lecture, they help a ton.

Probably the best bio professor you can get. Her exams are not that tough and she provides MANY study tools to help you with the exam. Sometimes she'll skip the iclickers or give extra points on the iclickers. She curves every exam and is VERY helpful when you ask questions. Study the lecture vids, hws, and class lecture slides and you'll do fine!

Video lectures and studying for the tests can be a beast and really time-consuming but if you ask Dr. Bretz for some help, she's super accommodating. The real kicker is getting a good  TA which is really just a matter of chance, but I would say as long as you study, use your TAs, ask Dr.Bretz for help when you need it, and you'll do great!

Bad, disorganized. Blames it all on an injury, expects grace, but gives no grace to others. Seems like she feels morally superior. Tangents, unrelated to class material but connected to her life in weird ways, which often makes students uncomfortable. Very weird professor...and not the good weird.
She is not good at all
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

AT-TIT-TUDE.
Not nearly as funny or cool as she thinks she is. Insane superiority complex. Overemphasizes basic grammar that we (should have) learned in grade school. I dreaded every minute of class.

reviews.comment: This woman should not be even employed by the vt college of civil enigneering much less teaching a class on legal issues within civil engineering.
evil man. avoid at all costs
Tough quiz for every class, which requires you attend all the time. No computer or phone use, literally none. NO ROUND GRADES AT ALL EVEN BEING ACTIVE, EVEN ONLY LESS THEN 0.5 FOR NEXT LEVLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Buengel is an overall nice professor but his Management Consulting is the complete opposite.    The class very seriously and provides very harsh feedback and requires students to be present at every weekly lecture. His grading is very harsh as he rarely gives students above a 90 in any assignment. There are better professors than him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Buengel is a very fun professor but he has quizzes at the beginning of class on the assigned reading, 2 exams, no HW, 1 individual presentation, and 1 group debate project. Outside of all that, his lectures are interesting and he really cares about your learning. He will also occasionally bring his dog in for class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very serious, do not recommend. Makes things harder than they need to be.

Don't get me wrong, he's a nice guy. However, he's not a good teacher. He's a harsh grader, and the major projects count big towards your overall grade. Tests can tend to be ambiguous, and the study guides are not helpful at all. Basically tells you to study everything, and there's a lot of content covered. Can tend to get off track in lectures.

Fun class with lots of thoughtful discussions. Prof. Buengel is kind and funny. His grading can be harsh, but as long as you work hard on the main graded assignments (individual presentation, team debate and corresponding paper, and 2 tests) you will be fine! There is a quiz every class on the chapter but they are 5 questions and weighted lightly

Very tough grader, will take off points for wild reasons. Should be an easy class but take Jameson instead. Very controlling of the class and makes it so you have to go way above and beyond to get an "A". Will say you have a quiz but then not have it just so you will go to class. He was very intense.

Best professor I have had at VT without a doubt. Dirk is a fantastic lecturer and although he is a bit of a harsh grader, he makes it feel rewarding to get a good grade. He gives excellent feedback on all assignments as well and you can tell he cares about the assignments because his feedback/analysis can be literally pages long. 10/10

Extremely high expectations for the little amount of teaching he does. Did a poor job expressing feedback and getting on the same page as groups. Everyone I spoke with worked very hard and did not feel the grade reflected it. Rarely gave higher than a 90 on any assignment, moser averages were 85, but low was only 80. So do less work and get the B.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Monotone lecture style with “Clear Eyes” energy. Expectations can feel unclear at times, so ask for specifics early. Lots of writing and APA formatting. If you prefer structured rubrics and consistent directions, this course may be frustrating.
Doesn't teach, unresponsive, doesn't hold office hours, material and homework was not applicable.

Does not teach. There is a presumption that you know the material, the terminology and concepts before you take the class apparently. He shows demonstrations of how to do things without explaining actual concepts or meaning so you have no idea why you do the things you do. Worst class of the 11 I had to take in the MIT program at tech.

Very good teacher, by far my highest grade in any math class at Virginia Tech. He goes at a very manageable pace as long as your paying attention. But honestly had no problem paying attention, really enjoyed this class.
He's a more difficult professor but you'll definitely learn the content necessary; he's a very good teacher, very nice as well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His teaching methods are very clear and concise. As long as you do the homework problems assigned, you'll do jut fine on quizzes and exams.

Easily the best mathematics professor I have ever had. Had to withdraw from DiffEQ before to save my GPA. The first math professor at VT that I have had who actually had exams that looked like the homework he assigned. If you do the homework and actually try, you will pass this class. He is very easy to understand and works through problems slowly.

I took MATH 2214 with him, Intro to Diff.Eq. He is super passionate about what he is teaching, and he knows his martial really well. He's exams and HWs are a little hard, but if you show up to every single class, you will be fine. He cares a lot!

Prof. Burleson was an awesome math teacher, especially considering the negative things heard about other math professors. Was consistent, timely, kept lectures engaging, and was easy to understand when explaining topics. 

This was his first semester teaching 2204 (multivariable calc), did a good job. 
quizzes at the start of every class,
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Burleson was kind and helpful during office hours. I would recommend taking this online with Burleson rather than in person. This class is difficult (especially for non-mathematics students) and takes a very large amount of time. Nevertheless, if you put in the work (and read the textbook, trust me) you will receive a decent grade.

His daily in class quizzes can get tricky, but the point is to make you a better student. He also gives plenty of opportunity to improve quiz score by going above and beyond with the material. His lectures are to the point, and get you all the information you will need, and he is great at answering questions. Mr. Burleson is an absolute must take.

Although I did withdraw from this class this spring, Professor Burleson was a great teacher. Make sure you show up to all classes as he gives quizzes nearly everyday. Very difficult class, but if you are prepared and put enough time in, you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: OpMeds is a very difficult class, but Professor Burleson's office hours made it much more bearable. He's redesigning the class starting Fall 2023 so I don't know exactly how the structure will be, but definitely go to his office hours for the homework because it's very difficult to do alone. The exams take me at least 10 hours, but it's manageable
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Burleson is a great lecturer and helped during office hours. Videos are actually made by a TA but they're useful to have a better understanding on material. Homeworks and tests were difficult, but definitely doable if you look at online lecture notes and videos as well as the textbook. Wished he would be better at responding to emails though.

Dude was the GOAT for me in 1225. I am severely math dyslexic which as you can imagine made 1225 a little bit of a challenge but Burleson never made me feel stupid for asking extremely basic questions in class and would go back over material if there were questions. Always willing to explain things multiple times in office hours. King
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. B is such a goated teacher. He gives quizzes everyday with a 5 minute time limit, which may seem bad at first but it helps with quick thinking. He is so smart always willing to answer questions and his lectures are so informative. He is also such a chill and laxed man to talk with. Definitely would have him as my professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Burleson is a great teacher. He makes materials easy and clear to understand. He is available for help outside of class and he always answer the students' question. Very nice teacher. The daily 5 minute quizzes are actually quite helpful. It only account for very little of the total grade. Just a bonus, I love his silky smooth voice

He is very easy to understand and presents the material in a clear way. He also enjoys being asked questions. My only complaint is that there are quizzes in the first 5 minutes of EVERY class and are worth 10 points each, SO DON'T SKIP! That being said, most test questions are pulled directly from the quizzes so they are a good resource
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took his class for Calc 2, I have to say I enjoyed his class quite a lot. I found his explanations of concepts quite good if sometimes a bit technical (not that I mind that though it may be harder for some). His office hours are really useful, definitely use them. Overall, really enjoyed his class and can recommend.

I took Calc 2 during my fall 2022 semester and I have to say Mr. Burleson is a pretty good professor. He responds to emails quickly and grades usually quick. He is amazing at teaching theoretical matter and is very helpful during office hours. Based on past comments on RMP, I think he has definitely changed and gotten better. Would recommend 7-8/10
John is an amazing teacher; his lessons are very clear and precise, and he knows how to answer just about any question you have. Homework wasn't excessive and it was always pretty doable.

He's a really nice guy and good at explaining concepts and examples in class. His homework assignments are hard but he does give you extra chances to resubmit them for full credit back if you get a bad grade on it. Is always willing to help during office hours and is very organized on his canvas page with completed notes from class.

Worst teacher I have ever had! If you are struggling and reach out to him through email he doesn't answer. I went a whole semester without an email back from him.His office hours are mid day and seems annoyed when asked questions. He flies through topics and expects all students to understand. multiple Homeworks due in one night with test next day

Mr.Burleson's class was fairly difficult. He is a very conceptual teacher as he likes to look into most of the theoretical aspects of Calculus. You need to show up to lectures and need to do some extra work. The test I would say were the most difficult. However, I could tell I was learning more in his class compared to students in other classes.

I took his class last semester for calculus one. Personally, I felt like his teaching style made it nearly impossible to pass the class. He grades super hard. Due to people skipping classes he made the entire class take in-class quizzes which went on your homework grade. His teaching style was never slowed down to match his student's needs.

I liked Burly a lot more for 1225, but was still good for1226. This semester he didn't respond to emails and had horrible office hours only on zoom. He is a very smart guy who explains material well but definitely can be cocky and condescending when he won't admit to being wrong. His tests are way easier than most professors so I do recommend him.

He's good in lecture but horrible for everything else. He claims to be available but during his zoom office hours he doesn't walk you through a problem, he just gives vague instructions. He also doesn't respond to emails like he claims. Sent 3 with no response. He's a young guy and very cocky and won't admit when he's wrong. Can be condescending.

He is a super nice guy and a great lecturer. His tests are much harder than other prof and he grades pretty harshly, so keep that in mind. He is a younger guy who is clearly very smart but sometimes he can come off as condescending, especially when test scores are low. Bad at keeping up with grades and responding to emails.

JT is a great professor if you're taking Calc 1. His test averages were consistently 8-10% higher than the university averages, he's good at lecturing topics that are on the exams. That being said, you probably won't pass the class if you don't study. It's not necessary to purchase the physical textbook, but you have to have the virtual textbook.

reviews.comment: This class was challenging, but Burleson tried his best to teach us the material. He always tried to connect us to the material but if you do not out in the work outside of class this class would have been impossible.

reviews.comment: Mr. Burleson is one of the best professors that I've ever had, he has excellent review sessions for this hard weed out class. He is very helpful at office hours, cares about what he is teaching, and is interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the most passionate math teachers Ive had over my years of education. Hes a young guy who is very talented with calculus and math in general, and he cares so much about making sure his students understand the subjects as best as he can. He sets up review sessions and practice tests as well before each test which are extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He was a very nice professor, but he was terrible at keeping up with grades, and literally, the whole class would talk about how they bombed the test cause it is the hardest weed out class. If you have no experience with calculus do not take his class you will end up dropping out.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: We met in person once a week. The tests were partially free response made individually by each professor. My friends with other professors had much easier free response portions that were graded easier as well. I felt he graded unfairly being that the course was taught by recorded videos from other teachers. Find the easiest teacher and take them.
Really great professor, really cares about what he's teaching and it shows. Really good feedback on all projects and papers

Prof B is an amazing professor; he is genuinely interested in the material. It was one of my only classes I enjoyed going to every week. It is a lot of reading and there are group assignments throughout the semester but nothing crazy. Participation is a HUGE part of your grade so always try to engage in the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Burkette is a passionate and engaging lecturer. If you participate at least two or three times in the discussion for the day and put in the effort to skim the readings and do your part during the group projects, you'll see great success. Additionally, he provides extensive help during office hours, so I highly recommend visiting him then.

Bizarre experience,

I loved every class, motivated professor, with academic knowledge and real life experience, 

Trouble arose when I got near maximum grade at all written assignments, in route for a easy A, all was left was the participation grade, in which I participated diligently, he gave me a grade so low it dropped me to a B! no idea why!!!

Took him for PSCI 3734 and loved him. He singled me out to praise a discussion post one day and we got to talking and now he is just as invested as me in my hunt for an internship. Checks in every class for an update. Amazing lectures. He was born for this. A must take professor! Flexible deadlines and cool projects. One of the best professors.

I took this over the summer so it was structured differently, but definitely do the readings and just keep up with the class. You will get a good grade if you just take a position and support it, you don't actually have to believe in what you are arguing.

Professor Burkette is a fantastic professor! He's so passionate about what he's teaching and gets so excited when students take an interest in what he's talking about. The course is quite difficult for a 1000 level course and requires a lot of reading, but as long as Mr. Burkette can tell you're putting in the work you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: His Global Ethics course has a lot of reading and discussion. He does a great job of breaking down big arguments into simple ideas, is a little lenient with attendance, and keeps things fun. Grade: 15% 3 presentations, 25% 3 short ppr, 30% final paper (6-8 pages, double spaced), 30% participation. No tests. Put in the effort, and you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Bugh seems nice but is a poor professor. He assigns 100-200 pages of repetitive reading weekly from multiple books. He rarely uses Canvas, only for occasional announcements. Lectures are passionate but 90% tangents, and relevant material isn't on exams. Grades harshly on the only 3 assignments: midterm, group project, and final.

reviews.comment: Very passionate about the subject but lectures can be lengthy (still informational). Lots and lots of reading for every class and attendance is mandatory, or else you won't understand the slides. Exams are hard but if you do the work, you'll get a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bugh is an amazing lecturer. For this class, tests are short answer questions and will require specific detail. There is also a decent amount of reading. I think this class is doable if you go into it knowing what he asks of you. He also offers extra credit, this saved my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Bugh is pleasant and he's not rude or difficult. However, he assigns an outrageous amount of reading (upwards of 150 pages a class) and his lectures are boring and not particularly informative. The class moves through history so quickly it's impossible to learn or prepare for exams, which are incredibly difficult even if you're studious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He gets offended when you don't know specifics. If you don't read, YOU WILL FAIL. He looks for specific words and if you don't have them, you will get VERY little credit for his quizzes. 2 quizzes, 1 midterm, and 1 project. Provides some extra credit but not much. Doesn't put grades into Canvas. If you want to take this class as a pathways, don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Bugh makes the class very entertaining with a lot of lectures as well as four required texts. The reading is necessary for the quizzes and exams which there are two of each and a project with another person in the class making a presentation and writing a paper. The class is very interesting and the professor is very knowledgable.

Attendance is mandatory and keeping up with the readings is mandatory. His lectures are very dull and unclear. He often tends to ramble and go into deep detail of info that you will not be tested on. In addition, there will be material in the book he will not discuss, but you will be tested on. Which the readings are very rigorous.

Dr. Bugh is a great Professor, and I feel like he is the only professor I've had who has pushed me to earn every point of the grade I earned.  Usually giving 75% gets me a 90 or better, in his class you are "the master of your fate" as he puts it.  He has been around so long he knows how much effort you put in and your grade directly reflects it

Not a bad guy, but his lectures are pretty unclear at times. Spends more time talking about pictures he has of columns and walls than relating the reading to the class. Tests are really hard and I don't think he gives out many A's, so don't expect an easy A, or B for that matter. And if he doesn't tell you before your exam, memorize the dates.

He is a good guy and grades fair.  There is a ton of reading and you will fall behind if you don't keep up with it.  He doesn't use blackboard and gets off topic in lectures.  Never late coming and he always keeps you until the last second.  He is pretty cool though and is willing to help you if you fall behind.  Tests are HARD!!! Seriously!!!

Follows somewhat with the text books, if you miss a lecture then you fall behind. Lectures are pretty clear, lots and lots of reading. Stay on top of the reading and you'll be fine, if you don't then your "doomed".
He is very nice and a nice grader. Tests were difficult to study for

Dr. Tsang is an outstanding professor who is very passionate about economics. The homework was challenging, but if you understood it, you did well on the tests. There is a group project as well that was a fun way to end the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His homeworks are abstract and difficult to solve and requires you to really think, but he is available and willing to help you with it. The tests are easy compared to the HWs if you understand how to do the HWs. Overall, fairly easy-moderate class

This professor is great, he talks about extremely interesting topic regarding classical economics. The books read in this class are extremely interesting and Professor Byron is great. I would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Tsang teaches the material and grades based on applications, some of which you may never have seen before. It's a highly challenging course, but you do learn to think independently about the material. Prereqs 100% necessary. He curves a lot, so succeeding is possible, but homework/exams are very difficult and time-consuming.

He talks really fast, so might be hard to understand. he also curves a lot. I got a 16.5/30 on my first exam and asked him if he thought I'd pass, and he said yes. He's a cool guy, kinda seems nervous when he's teaching. I personally learned more from the textbook than with him (Macroeconomics, by Olivier Blanchard), but he was helpful regardless
Dr. Howdy is awesome! This is class is really easy (it's a one credit hour course), and all of the grading is dependent on who your HUG leader is.

All around great class, it was a big lecture with almost 200 students in it but he tried his best to make it seem more intimate and personal. Made difficult concepts easy to grasp, just show up to class and you'll know everything you need to.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class BECAUSE of Buddy. At first I didn't really understand the lectures, but once I started looking at the presentations afterwards and taking the class seriously, I picked up quick. Just listen and take notes, and you're good. Pop quizzes are there but they're not hard.
Buddy is the GOAT, only bad thing I can think of is that there were some boring lectures, but they were never lectures given by him so lowkey he just picked boring people.

As a person, he's very nice and brings a positive attitude to each class. The class is all lectures which is either a hit or a miss for some people, and for me it was a miss. Not that it was a bad class, I just thought it was pretty average. Frequent pop quizzes so attendance is important. PARTICIPATE!! you'll get extra points on quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Buddy was amazing! the class itself is a lot of words and remembering, but the exams aren't hard and if you listen in class and show up you'll be fine! pop quizzes every week or 2 worth 20% of your grade.

Yes, he is a personable guy. But this course is way too hard for an intro. No homework, classwork, projects, or groupwork; the entire class is graded on exams and quizzes. If you don't pass one exam, the best you're looking at is a C. He says "attendance is optional," but if you miss anything, it's a 0. My advice: go to every class and study a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy class, especially if you study before each test. Graded only on tests, quizzes, and pop quizzes. He is very caring, dropping your lowest pop-quiz score and giving plenty of extra credit for doing school events. He is a funny and caring professor and if you just look over the material before each test you'll be fine.
this class was WAY too hard for being intro to comm, he wants to make it a weed out class and the exams are 1000% more difficult than they need to be, would not recommend
Exams are pretty chill. He's personable and wants to help students. Does pop quizzes that you can only do in class so as long as you show up you'll be fine, kinda his way of doing attendance i guess.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Howdy is very funny and informative. He is open to any criticism and really tries to help students in any way he can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Love Dr. Howell. I think some of his teaching styles are a bit flawed but he is 100% willing to accommodate his students in any way he can (something that Kuypers would never even think of). His exams are tough, so you will have to come to class, listen, and study a good amount. Overall I like him as a person more than a professor but he's great

Buddy is a great professor. Wants students to succeed, gives extra credit for meeting with him. Make sure to go to class and take notes. Tests can be phrased weirdly, but if you go to review sessions you're almost guaranteed to get an A. Does give pop quizzes, but in classes prior he tells you when they are. Very nice and easy to talk to. Love him!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Buddy is a great professor. You will be fine in this class if you pay attention and take notes. His tests can be weirdly phrased, but if you attend his review sessions you are almost guaranteed to get an A. He is extremely sweet and accessible outside class, and wants students to succeed. He gives extra credit for meeting with him. Love him
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love him he is precious
Very energetic guy, even for a 5pm lecture. He's very laid back I wouln't worry about going to him in case you have any problems in his class or with deadlines.
Overall a really chill professor and you don't really need to buy the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: He is very caring and personable to his students and overall is very nice. The class itself is fine, if you take good notes and look over them before exams you will come out okay. Go to class, there are a lot of 5-question pop quizzes that are easy but weigh a lot. The first unit sucks if you hate philosophy, but the rest of the class is fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Buddy is the best professor I've had at VT. He's very passionate about what he teaches, and makes it entertaining. His tests can be tough, but he offers a review session before each one and goes over previous quiz questions (which may be repeated). Often it hints at what will be on the exam. Make sure you attend!

my 3rd time having buddy as a professor. he's nice, you can tell he's passionate about the material, and he made an effort to learn our names. class is super lecture heavy and sometimes he goes on tangents (esp about his personal life). the class is only graded on the quizzes and exams so make sure to go to class and have really good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Howell is the only professor I've decided to leave a review for this semester. 100% recommend him. The class I took was extremely easy. His tests are very very fair, and he also curves. If you attend his classes, you'll ace all your exams + the pop quizzes (which are based on his lectures). He made the most of what a communication class would be.

This class really is not difficult if you come to class. He does 10 pop quizzes throughout the semester and a lot of times he will give you heads up about them and even give the answers since thats his only source of attendance. There are 3 quizzes (open notes, taken at home) and 3 exams (taken in class). Studying will save you in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Buddy is one of the best professors in the school of comm.  Content isn't difficult, but TAKE NOTES. Grade is composed of a couple exams, quizzes and pop quizzes. Attendance not mandatory but you never know when there's gonna be a pop quiz (sometimes he gives you the answers in class.) If you study and put in a bit of effort you'll be fine.

Personally, Buddy was my favorite professor I've had at VT so far. He truly cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He keeps lectures interesting by relating concepts to personal stories. Although, his tests are pretty difficult and require tons of studying. I would definitely take one of Buddy's classes again!

Buddy is nice, but sometimes his lecture examples can be a little controversial, and he has snuck his opinion in before. Besides that, tests are somewhat difficult because they try to trick you. Just pay close attention to the wording of the question and take good notes in class, not just what's on the screen. He has review sessions, though.

Buddy is such a baddie I love him so much. There is no attendance, but pop quizzes (which he usually gives the answer to). His exams can be challenging, so study in advance. He also wants you to come up and ask for help during these exam. Talk in his class, because he frequently gives out extra credit to the first person that raises their hand.

Buddy is so kind and truly cares about his students. His tests can be difficult but he gives study guides and does exam review sessions before each exam. His lectures were engaging and he made us laugh. 5 quizzes (to prep you for each exam) and 5 "pop quizzes" (he hints at when each will be). He truly cares about the info he's teaching. Great guy!

Dr. Howell is my favorite professor that I have had at Virginia Tech. I have had him for COMM 1014, COMM 2064 and now CMST 3064. He is very inclusive and made me feel very comfortable to talk to him and talk in class. The class is exam heavy however, if you attend class, actively listen, take notes and go to the review sessions the exams are easy.

Had him for the comm first semester experience, and he is not for everyone. Very outgoing but will call you out in front of a room full of 200 students. He picked on me often saying things like, "You can smile every now and then" and other snarky remarks. I was not a fan of his extroverted personality as an introvert.

Great guy overall, he is genuinely interested and very knowledgeable in the field.  Pop and reading quizzes are pretty easy as long as you show up and tests take effort but are not too bad.  He cares about his students and will do his best to help you pass.
He's just a great person. It's easier to pass the class, you would need to try extremely hard to fail.

There are 5 pop quizzes and 5 reading quizzes designed to monitor attendance, they are somehow predictable since the class population increases on those days. Please don't take this course if you aren't planning on attending at least 95% of the classes, leave that spot for someone who is willing to attend.

This is my second time taking a class with buddy and it's similar to intro to comm. It was mostly lectures with a few documentaries. There's four tests and four quizzes and that's all the assignments that are given. Definitely recommended studying for everything since tests are taken in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class isn't really that hard but the exams are. You can't just wing the exams. Buddy is a great guy and is always willing to help, but you actually have to go to him if you want to do well in the class. If you go to his office hours and take the exams seriously, you'll be fine.

Buddys a great guy, however, I would never take this class again. I had friends with other professors who finished with As while doing so much less work than me. Buddy takes forever to grade so you're never really sure what your grade is, and he also grades his essays super hard. If you get above an 80 on an essay, consider yourself Steven King.
Buddy's a good guy, one of my favorite teachers, however he is really flakey, he cancels class a lot, he takes forever to grade, and never responds to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Buddy is a super nice person just the lectures are boring and you have to attend class to get good notes and pop quizzes. Towards the end of the semester the quizzes were only on Thursdays so do what you will with that. Tests are extremely hard though so study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell he is a nice guy, but his class is oddly difficult. His class is not interesting whatsoever, and he always goes off on tangents that are hard to follow. You are graded on like 6 assignments so you have to do super well on those.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Buddy cares about his Hokies more than any professor in the world. He wants everyone to succeed. That being said, the tests are difficult -- so STUDY!!

Buddy has been one of my favorite teachers and I have taken many of his classes. He is kind and truly cares about his students. COMM 1014 is definitely a challenging course, but it is interesting and Buddy makes it fun! Take good notes and study hard for the exams. He is available to meet outside of class so don't be afraid to ask for help. :)
Buddy is the comm goat. just go to class and youll be alright. if you dont you will literally fail. take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher, truly cares about his students and his content. If you pay attention in class you will be fine. He is very ready to work with you if you are struggling, and will help you improve. Grades are just tests and pop/quizzes, no assignments, so do good on all of them or else its hard to make up for it. Show up to class for xtra credit!
Buddy is a great professor, he makes this class so fun and you can really tell he cares.

Buddy Howell is the most caring Professor you will meet. In a class of 200, he WILL get to know your name if you want to talk to him. He obviously loves what he does but loves the students even more. Material can be tough. Intro to Comm (1014) goes into ancient rhetoric people and theories. Pay attention. Go to class and study sessions before tests

Dr. Howdy is THE best professor that I have ever had. His lectures are a lot to take in, but if you genuinely listen in class and take detailed notes, the class is a breeze. He makes himself extremely accessible (Will literally text you back at any hour) because he SERIOUSLY cares about his students. Take a course with him, you will not regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Howdy as he likes to be called is the best prof I have ever had. He is extremely caring about his students and truly wants them to succeed. The class is extremely easy as long as you go to class and take the notes. Do the study guide and youll get an A on the exam. Need more profs on campus like him
Part of the exam tests you on the material, but a bigger portion depends on your critical reading skills. You need to pay close attention in class to succeed

This class is graded by 3 tests, 3 quizzes, so kind of nerve wracking. However, he's very helpful - offers study guides for tests/quizzes, office hours are helpful, and is very understanding with rescheduling exams/quizzes (if you tell him beforehand). He's a good instructor (if a bit ramble-y), & I think this class would be better if not an 8 AM.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Buddy is very kind & respectful. Class was an 8AM but he would cancel often which was nice. No assignments just lectures every class, quizzes, and exams. Also pop quizzes. Tests are somewhat difficult but he has review sessions beforehand to help.

buddy was a great professor who showed enthusiasm for the course and care for his students. the class is an easy A: u do 2-3 essays/letters and write a reflection paragraph every class. if u miss a class you can't make up the assignment which will hurt ur grade. he has hug leaders who grade all the assignments but also hunt u down if u miss class:(
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Buddy Howell is the reason I didn't drop out freshman year. I LOVE this man.

By far my favorite professor this semester! I could tell Dr. Howell is passionate about the subject of communications and because of that he does an excellent job explaining the concepts we are tested on. Also, GO TO THE REVIEW SESSIONS BEFORE EXAMS! Those review sessions saved my test grades. He's funny, cares about his students, 12/10

Dr. Howell was a great professor. He was kind and he makes an effort to get to know his students, even in a large classroom. Be ready to take notes as he doesn't post his slides. His exams are difficult but he gives review sessions and review sheets for each graded assignment. He really wants you to succeed.

Great professor and made a seemingly boring class interesting. Your grade is based on 3 tests and 3 quizzes but they are fairly straightforward if you take notes during class. You don't have to read the book but it does help. Gets a little preachy at times but overall a really funny and interesting guy.

Super funny! For Spring 2021 semester, he posted YouTube videos that had to be watched and were used for quizzes and tests (which, be aware, are the only graded assignments in his class). He made the videos super fun and they could be watched on your own time. Even gave his phone number if any problems came up. Very caring!

One of the best VT has to offer. Buddy Howell is hilarious, charismatic, and caring. His energy keeps lectures interesting. He provides study guides and exam reviews that are super helpful. He makes an effort to learn students' name and connect with them. You're lucky if you land a spot in his class.
I loved Professor Howell! This class was so informative and a lot of fun. He is super big on the VT community and it really shows. Take his class!!!!

I loved Intro to Comm. with Dr. Howell. I struggled with the class at first but he was always around to look over exams and offer feedback. By the end of the semester I was getting A's on my assignments. Dr. Howell definitely makes you work hard for your grade but he makes the class interesting and worthwhile. Don't skip! He doesn't post lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Howell is one of my favorite professors at VT. He cares about all of his students and takes the time to try to learn names even in a super large lecture. You don't need the textbook for this class. Go to review sessions and you'll do well.

Great professor and easy class, but you have to study if you want an A. Go to class so you don't miss pop quizzes; he's a really cool guy and actually cares for his students. would recommend this class.

Buddys' COMM 1004 was a super easy class. If you do your homework its an A+. However, his second semester class 1016 is one you have to work hard. The test are harder than you think. He provides a lot of help for the student. He truly cares. He tries to engage in his lecture. Get to know him and you'll have a good class.

Buddy is so kind. He really does care about his students, even though his classes are large, he makes it feel like a smaller class. Highly recommend taking his class, he will do everything in his power to help his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Buddy Howell is a fantastic professor. He's hilarious and truly cares about his students and wants them to be successful. I missed a few classes and got the notes from others and still did well. The beginning of the course is a little tough, but gets much easier as it goes on. I wish I could take him again!

This class only met once a week and is only worth one credit, so it reflects in the work load. You show up, listen to people speak and explain opportunities in the Comm department. Second half of semester you have to write a paragraph reflection on the speakers, but over all a free 1/120 of the graduation process.
Very entertaining lectures and not too much work as long as you pay attention and show up.
He's awesome!

Easy class to take, very informative, easy for an extra credit hour. Mostly have panels to inform you about what you can do to prepare for college. Minimal work really only one paper with a few minor assignments that take 10 minutes. Best to go to class to write assignments

GREAT teacher! He makes the class fun to go to. His test are some what "hard" but he goes over everything in the notes. I didn't really need the textbook to pass his class. Just take good notes and you'll be fine.

Really nice professor! Did not take attendance but will give extra credit sometimes for classes before breaks. Tests are somewhat challenging, just make sure you are in class that's really where the information comes from.
Dr.Howell is one of the best professors at VT. The tests are not easy, but Howell will tell you all the stuff you need to know to be ready. Fun class!

Dr. Howell is hands down the BEST professor I have had here at Virginia Tech. He was amazingly interesting, and it was obvious he truly cared about the wellbeing of every single student. He made an effort to memorize each and every person's name, which shows his personableness. His tests are somewhat difficult, but not impossible. LOVE Dr. Howell!

HOWDY! Dr. Howell tries his hardest to interest students in the material. Not only are the notes and study-guides key to your success in the course, you have to listen! The things he says during class are sometimes word for word on the exams. Take this class if you are not afraid of a little hard work

He is an amazing teacher that loves what he is teaching and is very knowledgeable.  I had his Rhetorical Traditions class and I really enjoyed it.  His tests cover a lot of information but he takes many steps toward making sure you do well like study guides and review sessions before tests.  Great teacher

Had Dr. Howell for Comm and Rhetoric - such a good prof. The best teacher I've had in all my years of school..so beyond helpful and genuinely cares that his students learn. exams are really not as difficult as people say, as long as you do go to class and use his study guides..they literally say everything that's on the test/quiz. Such a good prof

Professor Howell is a very friendly, helpful, and outgoing professor. He goes out of his way to help students prepare themselves for quizzes and test. However, the quizzes and test are very difficult. At least 2-3 days of studying are needed to do well.

Extremely thorough testing. be prepared to slog through the review. Not so good at keeping the material interesting- I lost focus about five minutes in. Maybe I took the wrong course? He did not seem all that great to me.

I had Dr. Howell for Intro to Communication. The best thing about Howell as a college professor is his helpfulness. He's happy to answer emails regarding any questions you have, and he's always open during testing if you want clarification on a question. Also, he makes study guides for quizzes and tests with material that may show up. Good guy.

He is a great guy and really knows his stuff, but his exams are so hard and will take a good 2-3 days of studying to even attempt to accomplish a B. Thank god he gives out other grades or this would be a next to impossible class
Howdy! Subject matter a bit tiring, but Howell does his best to keep you in it. Good prof, won't regret taking him.
great teacher but the test are very hard, at least a  few days of studying are needed
Easy, fun, as long as you sit there and take notes when he emphasizes things you will be fine.

Dr. Howell is a great professor. He will say at the beginning of the semester," This class will change the rest of your life." He puts a fresh perspective in your head as you survey rhetoric throughout the past. You will learn what rhetoric actually is and its role in our daily lives. Overall: the class is enjoyable and not too hard.

I love, love, love Dr. Byers. She made classes so fun, and it is obvious she truly enjoys what she is teaching. At every chance, she tried to make class engaging. I never felt nervous to share my opinions with her or to ask for help. She is so kind and patient.

Dr. Byers was very helpful, but her class was primarily lecture and went very fast through slides as we were struggling to keep up. She didn't put a single grade in until after mid-terms and it wasn't even my midterm paper. Otherwise, she tried to make her class fun and lightweight. I liked Dr. Byers, but not the class she taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lyla was literally the best professor I've ever had. I'm so sad I won't ever have the opportunity to take her again. She was constantly willing to help, literally hilarious, down to earth, and so passionate about what she was teaching. She made WGS 2224 so enjoyable. It doesn't matter what course it is, take Lyla whatever chance you get.

This class is honestly a lot for an elective. I took it thinking that it would be fun, but it's not. We have to do about 3 in-person podcast sessions, we have 2 exams that are, for some reason, weighted very heavily for an elective class; we have 2 group presentations, so many in-person and out-of-class assignments with no explanation from class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very passionate about her field and laid back as well, kept class very interesting.

Loved Prof. Kogan. Her class is easy, there is a good amount of writing assignments (but you basically just get to yap about yourself). This class focuses on your mental health which is something that isn't often focused on, which was cool. She wants you to actively participate, but won't cold call, she made us want to participate on our own.
She is very kind and her class is simple. She just wants you to be present and give feedback in class, not be on your phone or computer. The class is fun and you get to do a lot of group work.

I would recommend anyone to take your full time given on the test even if you feel like you don't need it, he really likes people who take their time answering test questions and will reward it, as well as showing you've paid attention to his feedback on assignments. You can tell he wants everyone to do well and really learn to material.

This class isn't too bad if the lockdown browser isn't using cameras. however, because the tests are online does not mean they're easy - there is a tight time limit, so you still need to really thoroughly know the material. overall, this class isn't as difficult as it's made out to be.
So rude. Winter course is so bad. It's like he wants to see us fail. my GPA is a 3.9 and I'm hoping I can just pass the class at this point.

Do not take this class, absolutely not worth the stress, especially in the winter. Content is interesting, but he makes it way more difficult to pass the class than necessary. He is very vague and cryptic in answering questions you have. Right now, I am just hoping I can pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Just super rude

Lectures were good and very knowledgeable. The test questions basically come straight out of the slides, so I would take notes during lecture. Dr. Myers is straightforward and reasonable with his expectations, and lets you use AI on assignments if you want. I enjoyed the class and found it quite easy—there aren't many assignments.

Myers' Law class is lecture-heavy. You must purchase and read the textbooks to perform well. Not a class you can slack off in, but the material is really interesting, and he explains everything well. I recommend taking it over the summer so you do not have other classes to worry about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is super chill. To fulfill your attendance requirement for the semester, you have to attend 10 classes. Outside of that, it is optional. Every class is a big lecture, but he has a nice voice, so it's not too boring. The homework is basically a guaranteed 100, and all of the exams are online on your own time with a 24-hour window.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: easiest class ever, very esay a. do whatever in class, you don't need to take notes

Professor Myers is a good teacher. Sets very clear expectations for the class. All of the tests are pulled straight from the power points so take notes. Textbook is not worth purchasing because its all on the slides. Recommend taking notes before class because he presents and talks fast. He usually only lectures for an hour too. Interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't buy the textbook for this class!! Is lectures are pulled straight from the textbook and half of the stuff is verbatim from the text. It's also an incredibly boring class (but pretty easy if you give like over 50% effort).
Super easy class. One of those classes where you can do work for other courses in it and not fall behind. All exams, assignments and essays are online only. Myers is a chill dude
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has a reputation for being extremely tough and the class you're most likely to fail, but I would not accredit that reputation to Dr. Myers. While the material of the class is tough and is a lot to learn, his teaching is very effective and he often helps his students by telling them specifically what to focus on studying for the exams.

I liked the setup of this class. Pretty much only made up of lectures, 2 tests, and discussion boards. Attendance counts for a grade but he doesn't usually keep the class longer than an hour and cancels often. Dr. Myers is a really good lecturer it's not hard to stay engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: comm law ... hardest class i've ever taken. felt like law school. difficult class but you get used to it. the powerpoints are insanely long and everything he covers isn't even on the exams, focus on the study guides. there's quizzes, responses, and exams. he's pretty strict but i mean he's just doing his job, i got used to his teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Idk about these others ratings DONT LISTEN IF UR TAKING MEDIA AND SOCIETY!!! he is a very easy grader and the lectures are great and easy to follow. Plus he often ends class early or cancels. He is also a very great teacher overall and makes things easy to understand

This professor's course was definitely one of the hardest classes I've had to take. However, he's fair and gives you all the information you need to succeed. In my opinion, the #1 thing to watch out for is information overload. Make sure you look at the study guides before tests, as it goes over the most important info. Class is tough but helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was so hard, and he made it very difficult. He graded very harshly and gave little to no feedback. He gave short time on tests which would cause my grade to drop low. Very hard class and not a nice teacher that cares whether you pass or fail.
Very nice and laid back, some of the assignments take forever so I would recommend not waiting till the day of to do them but other than that this class was very easy

I really loved Professor Cousins! She is such a fun and passionate person, though her class can get a little heavy at times. The assignments can take awhile, but are fairly easy and honestly enjoyable. 4 major group projects throughout the semester (photo, video, website, and one more). I would take her again; she loves her students.

She's very nice and always finds a way to keep class interesting and engaging. I will warn that sometimes she won't really talk about upcoming assignments/mini projects due in Canvas, so make sure you check often. Besides that, she's a pretty easy grader as long as you put in effort, and the class is definitely worth taking.

Love love love. I took her Visual Media class COMM 2034. This class was so fun and engaging. NOT boring lectures and tests. It's all fun little projects and designing things. Carrie is so kind, relatable, and fun. My only advice is to follow directions and pick good group members!

Professor Cousins is great! She is kind and caring and wants her students to succeed! I was not looking forward to this class because I'm not artistically inclined but she made it very enjoyable and interesting! She doesn't really explain assignments at all so if you're confused, ask her questions. Offers good extra credit and cancels class often.
DON'T TAKE HER CLASSES

reviews.comment: Her class genuinely made slusher feel like a safe and comforting environment.

reviews.comment: This class will waste your time. Lectures are not helpful, you basically end up being required to teach yourself based off a few readings.  However, she is a great resource out of class and easy to get a hold of, so if you already know java pretty well, this class could be ok with this teacher.
Cannot teach coding at all, have to learn a lot on your own and definitely makes the class very difficult for no reason. Quizzes almost every week, hard to learn
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took in spring.  She seems not prepared & often couldn't finish lecture notes. I always felt anxious about my grade after lectures. In one lecture, she got stuck on a C compile error, later a segmentation fault, tried deepseek for minutes, which is not helpful, and only fixed after a student pointed it out. Spending time on lecture notes may help.

Couldn't really understand her lectures, but she makes it up with her accessibility outside of class. She responds to emails really quickly and tries to help if possible. I stopped going to her lectures after a couple days, but I didn't feel like I missed out on much. Reading the lecture notes, and doing the HWs and projects helps with the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although her lectures weren't that good, you could tell she was trying. Stopped going to her lecture after a couple days. You really don't need the lectures if you just do HW and read the lecture notes before the test. The test is hard harder than cs 2114, but there is a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Classes are just lecture, very boring. Stopped going a couple weeks in. Not a good lecturer. Gets stuck. Good thing is she posts the notes on canvas. And you can see the other professor's notes, as well as the old(good) notes. HW/Projects are free 100s if u put in the work. Tests kinda difficult, need a deep understanding of C. Good curve though.

Definitely doesn't understand C when lecturing but she is pretty good with assembly towards the end. One lecture she ended 10 minutes early because she couldn't fix her code and gave it as an exercise for us. As long as you start early on the projects you will do well.

Nice but unable to answer many questions on content.
Skipping classes is extremely common.
Easy classwork, hard projects
Difficult exams - study guides are useless.
Super nice but has no idea what she's talking about. It's workable having her for 2104 especially with good TAs but I couldn't imagine how bad she'd be for 2505 or any other real class

Lectures were pretty useless, get ready to learn everything yourself day before exams. Homework and classwork is absurdly easy, exams absurdly difficult. Exams are all very niche content they barely cover in class.

She lacks basic understanding of what she attempts to teach in lectures. I had a class where students sat in silence for up to 10 minutes as she tried to figure out why the program she was teaching couldn't run properly. Students tried to help her figure out the issue and sometimes succeeded. Waste of time to go to class. Learning online is better.

She is not a teacher you want, although 2104 is a ridiculous class to begin with. She isn't very elaborate in what she teaches or is she informative. A lot of the times she lacks in understanding of the questions you might have and isn't thorough in teaching.

Does not seem like she knows the class material at all. Just reads off of pre written notes and doesn't even understand what she is talking about. I can't even attend class because it's a waste of my time, material is hard to learn on my own but the class is no help at all.
She's not the best teacher, but is really sweet. During lectures there are times when she seems confused and most of my class had to learn Python outside of class. The final is mostly memorization.

I learned nothing during her lectures. Somehow she manages to sound confused while teaching and can barely answer questions. The TA's really pulled through for learning and helping with assignments. For assignments there are weekly homework assignments and then classwork due throughout the week. Attendance can be apart of your grade if you want.

She is not capable of teaching. when she starts teaching a new subject she looks confused, and when someone asks a question she does not know the answer and tells you to refer to UTA. She responds to emails pretty fast but does not help you. she might have a degree in CS but that doesn't mean she can teach. passing information is not teaching.

Dr.Cao is so sweet! The class dives into lots of different topics: Python, cryptography, networking, etc. None of the assignments were difficult. No late credit. There is a decent amount of group work. The class covers alot of content, so there is going to be alot of memorization for the midterm/final. Attendance lowers weightage of the tests.

Most of the time people would only show up to class for attendance credit and to work on classwork assignments since that material is posted ahead of time. Also, Cao couldn't communicate the concepts of this class very clearly and overall isn't a great lecturer.

the professor was nice but wasn't involved with the class, she would just give us lectures and that would be it. the TAs however were so helpful, graded everything, & talked to us more than the professor did. for me this class was HARD and the only way i got an A was because of my cohort. u have to do lots of difficult coding, quizzes, & projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy-A course if you have a solid group of friends in the class. The TAs are super helpful and the projects are not bad at all. Homework and reading quizzes are due at the beginning of every class but if you semi-pay attention theyre super easy to complete. Really sweet professor too.
Took her for geomatics, very easy, very boring lectures but she is nice and reasonable.
Homeworks/quizzes were easy, but tests were fairly difficult to know all the content
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fairly easy class but labs count for a lot of the points. Apart from lab and the tests a very easy class overall if you pay attention.
Linear algebra is weird at first but her lecture notes are very usful.

Kind of confusing lectures, but made sure students were prepared for tests and gave very good study guides. If you use the guide and can teach yourself you can do very well on the tests. There were weekly quizzes, she assigns homework about once every two weeks, and tests were relatively easy compared to other teachers' tests.

She understands the material but struggles to relay it. She has misgraded assignments, demeaned students, and limited opportunity for success. Each test was worth 20 points; each point worth 5% of the grade.
If you are taking her class, you are better off taking the class asynchronously with the amount of outside work you are going to need to do
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures never made sense and I had to reteach myself everything outside of class. A lot of material to cover, weekly quizzes. She is one of the toughest graders I have had. Hours of studying with multiple failing grades. She belittled a lot of our math abilities in front of the whole class.

To be fair, I did skip several classes and didn't focus too much during lectures, so I struggled. DiffEq is difficult, so attend every lecture and make sure you understand the material! That being said, she does write really tiny on a chalkboard which can be messy and hard to read. The VT emporium is a great resource for studying and practicing.

She was great for DifEQ. I never felt unprepared during a test, which is more than can be said for a few of my friends. She provided a template for notes, I just took my own because I prefer that, but having the option is nice. She does have a soft voice and a small accent. Don't skip class, DifEQ is tough. One of the best in the department though.
Professor Menegay was really nice. She goes over examples during class and the study guides really help for tests. The class itself is tricky so things can get confusing pretty fast.
If you don't have a good understanding of the topics prior to class you will struggle severely

She is a very respectful and sweet professor who cares about your success. She will meet with you outside of class and will always try to make sure that she meets with her students. Of course the class itself sucks, but as a professor she tries to make everything easier for the students. Honestly a great difEq professor. 10/10 recommend taking w hr

reviews.comment: Speeds through lectures and most of the content I learned I had to review extensively/self taught. Okay but not the best. I'm not a math person but after self teaching it's okay. Homework takes forever though that was a bit tough.

if you're not religious, pick a religion and pray.

reviews.comment: Prof Caruso is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is approachable and his office hours are very helpful.
