Take 2534 with a different professor his way of teaching is harder to understand. His class is boring and he doesn't post notes or a study guide unlike other teachers.

The class wasn't too bad, the lectures were good, and if you read the textbook along with the lectures, you were fine. Homework could be pretty difficult but he had a lot of office hours so getting help was easy and he was very helpful. In general, the HW was very helpful at forcing you to build an understanding. Would take this class again

Great professor, his lectures were fantastic. If you just do the homework without googling it you learn more than enough for the tests every time. He is very conceptual though, which I like but many don't. No clue why he is so lowly rated.

I enjoyed his lectures, and he was very helpful in office hours. However, he doesn't really post any material online so you have to go to class. His tests were usually a toss up because they often included some type of proof, so it was difficult to prepare for. He's very sassy, but it's in a fun way. He made an effort to get to know his students.

Taking MATH 2114 with this guy is basically an automatic -10% to your grade. The class is already hard, and he makes it worse. Teaching is okay, but assignments and exams are insane and nothing like other professors. No notes, no study guides, no bonuses. Exams are way harder than intro level. Take it with anyone else. RUN FOR YOUR LIFE!!!!

Great professor. His lectures were well put together, and I found that the homework he assigned adequately prepared me for tests without too much extra studying. Seems like a nice guy outside of the academic space which definitely showed in class throughout the semester. Would take again

He's a pretty sassy guy but he's not as bad as the reviews make him out to be. The one con about his class is you're cooked if you miss a day since he does in person notes. He's pretty helpful in office hours tho and is nice with partial credit on tests.

Dr. C is a great professor! Don't listen to the haters. The subject matter is really hard and if you don't show up to class you are obviously going to struggle immensely. However, if you actually go to class his lectures are super helpful and he answers all questions fully in class. I had him for linear as well and it was the same deal.
Hard class, professor made it even harder. Office hours were mostly unhelpful.
Pay attention in his classes and practice your math, if you don't practice then you can't blame the professor. He does his job and now you do yours!

Good lecturer, is very open to questions and is glad to answer them. Lectures are not boring either. Written HWs only once a week due Wednesdays. Tests so far have been quite harder in difficulty compared to lectures and homework material. Written HWs aren't awful/too difficult. Prepare yourself for the tests and also no formula sheet either.

As others have said, the tests will make you question whether you really understand linear algebra. He isn't terrible, however, the conceptual and theory-heavy approach didn't stick for me. If you struggle to visualize mathematical concepts, I wouldn't recommend him.  If you took Discrete and did well, you will be fine in his class.

Lectures are all on chalkbaord and aren't posted. If you go to class the notes are solid, but he doesn't provide any other resources for review. Written homeworks are pretty impossible, and no feedback is given on what was wrong and why unless you go to office hours. Tests were tough but not impossible. Spencer def better than tim smits.

Teaches on chalkboard so go to class. HW is challenging go to office hours to understand better. Highly conceptual tests and HW rather than computational. Go to office hours. Does some review for the CTE final. Go to office hours. Nice guy and is good at answering questions. go to office hours if you want to do good and ask questions about the HW

Honestly, linear algebra is not that bad of a course. However, the way this man grades will actually make you question reality. His policies are so strong for someone who takes so long to grade. I would definitely try to switch out of this class if you have this man. He just makes the concepts and work so much harder than it needs to be.

This professor encumbered my calculus ability and forced me to teach myself. The homework had questions Einstein couldn't solve. The test questions will have you questioning if all of that studying was worth it... (you still know nothing). Half of the kids dropped or took W's and if you have Spencer, you should prepare to do the same.

Spencer taught me Calc I. I use this phrase loosely. This was the worst experience in a class I've had. He talked at you going over problems extremely quickly, with no explanations as to what he was doing or why. Skipped many steps. Calculus is not a hard topic but with him, do fear. Would not work left to right, no workflow. Impossible to follow.

Great teacher for Math 2114. His lectures were very easy to follow and intuitive. He's also pretty chill unless you write in pen on the tests - just use pencil. Overall a great teacher, I would definitely take him again. He's also very helpful at office hours if you need extra help.
His teaching style is very difficult to follow and his tests are very theoretical. Overall its a struggle to learn with in the class and avoid taking it at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Have to say that I know a decent amount of people struggled in his class. Tests were mostly theoretical, not computational linear algebra.

Guy is totally awesome. His lectures are great, and if you don't go to them, you're scamming yourself out of some cool stuff. His office hours, though, are really what helped me get through the class.

I had an okay experience, but whenever I was at office hours, he seemed kind of rude and condescending to other students (I was there frequently). His tests are 80% and he is a harsh grader. He does partial credit, but it definitely isn't generous. I think he is really knowledgeable on the subject, just not well experienced as a professor
Had him for Linear Algebra 2114, he was really good at explaining and he gave a LOT of extra credit on the tests, which makes it easy to get a 100%. Not lenient with deadlines at all though.

Had him for MATH2114 not 1226. Lectures are chalkboard so if you miss class you have to ask a friend. Tests are similar to the written assignments so those are important. If you want a good grade you have to show up to office hours honestly, you have to make the effort. Tough tests because you really need to understand concepts more than anything.
Tests are way more difficult than whats standard for the course, can be very condescending at office hours. Overall unaccommodating. You will have a far better time with other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst calc 2 professor. Couldn't explain anything and was so condescending. The subject matter isn't difficult, but he makes it convoluted. He expects you to be able to solve problems before explaining them. Other professors give their students notes but he teaches by writing random problems down and solving them. Also rude at office hours.

Spencer is one of the best professors I have had. This being said, the class moves very fast. He makes the tests harder but he prepares you well for them. Go to office hours and study, and you should do fine.

Very difficult class. The tests are much harder compared to other Calc 2 professors at VT. Office hours aren't helpful at all, and the lectures move very quickly, so you need to pay close attention. There was a very heavy emphasis on series, and we went very in-depth on difficult concepts. There is written and online homework each week.
best professor ever.

He cares more about showing that he knows how to do problems than actually teaching them (and frequently didn't actually know how to do what he was going over). He told me several times that I'm complicating things for myself and I should think about it in a different way but never specified what that way was or provided help in any meaningful way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was the worst math teacher I have ever had. He was condescending when asked for help and did not really seem to care about teaching the material. The lectures seemed like a race to get through as much material as possible and he skipped a lot of steps in the practice problems. There was also very little feedback on the homeworks.

Spencer was close to no help at all at office hours. During lectures he speedran through the whole curriculum like it was a videogame. He never gives any feedback on written hw assignments, which he pulls from directly for his exams, so you're basically screwed if you're not a math genius. He is the prime example of what a professor should not be

Spencer is an absolute super genius. With this, he is the worst possible teacher I could have ever imagined. He does steps in his head while teaching you things, giving you no insight into what he just did. He prides himself on how bad his kids do and how tough his tests are compared to the rest of the departments.Skip class and read your textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Spencer isn't bad at explaining things, he's very helpful when you go to office hours. The problem is that he makes sure to give his students tests that are WAY harder than the rest of the Calc 2 classes. He also speedruns his lectures like he is trying to get the world record for the fastest class 2 lecture. We were ahead the whole semester.
Professor Smith is a small person teaching a big topic.
She was very nice and passionate about what she was teaching.
She is super caring and very engaging

Dr. Smith was amazing. She made an effort to know the students and relay the information in an understanding way. I don't think her teaching strategy would work for everyone, but if it works for you, you'll thrive. Super sweet!

Dr. Smith is THE best professor I've had here at Virginia Tech. She doesn't let you use technology, but it really helped me do well! She tries really hard to get to know you and cares about her students. It is clear that she know the material and she's very enthusiastic! It's definitely not an easy A but if you go to class and read you'll be fine!

Fantastic teacher.  She tries really hard to get to know you, especially if you go in for office hours.  She treats you with respect, and does a lot of research to see what the best teaching methods are (hence no technology allowed in class).  She's very sweet and enthusiastic about what she's teaching.

This is not a hard class, and if you're interested in the material, it can be entertaining. Attendance is a really good idea and reading the book before the exams is too. Study guides for exams are really broad but if you understand the concepts completely, then the they are really straightforward (and she even drops your lowest test grade).
not a fan. treats her students like children and tests a really hard for a 1000 level class. she also does not have detailed notes. i would not recommend it if you dont have to take it

The notes are not detailed at all so you have to fill out the study guide with the book. Not allowed to use computers in class. Tests are hard for a 100 level class. She makes the GA's sit in class with students to make sure you aren't using your cell phone. Treats you like 5 year olds. But you can tell she really cares about the material
Very excited about what she teaches. The class was surprisingly entertaining!
Just ok... does not come across all that friendly sometimes and was rude to a few students.

She is really nice. There is in class activities that will boost your grade so try to go to most classes but it won't affect your grade too much if you miss. I recommend this class. It's easy and the teacher is really nice. You have to write one paper but I am horrible at papers and I got an A.
Dr. Smith is great. She is harsh on slackers, but it can be pretty entertaining.
consistently late, consistently unpleasant

She is not at all a good teacher. If you end up getting her I recommend switching immediately. Her lectures are very confusing and her notes do not help. If you do get stuck with her, go to her office hours because she's much better one on one than in a lecture setting.

She is just a terrible teacher in general. If you are an audible learner than she is perfect because all she does for me is speak gibberish and never puts anything important or comprehensible on the board. In the tragic event of you having her, go to other teachers lectures and only show up to her classes for the in class exams.

I can see her frustration when she enters class, kind of like huffing and puffing... NOT ATTRACTIVE. Also, she doesn't understand that we are not chemists!!! She thinks we understand what she is talking about but NO, we don't... She shouldn't talk down to her students during lecture. No one appreciates it. She also gets frustrated super quickly.

I learned more in my highschool AP chem class! She is a terrible teacher which is why her test averages are the worst of all the chemistry Proffesors. I dont go to her class anymore because it is easier to just read the text book.

Dr. Cribbs has a really hard class. I got a wake up call after i received my first exam grade, so I worked a lot harder and went to office hours and weekly problem sessions and improved greatly. Just go to her when you need help- make sure you understand everything even if you got it correct on connect- and then you'll be fine on her tests.
Very difficult lectures and tests
She fails to understand that we are not all chemistry majors she also gets frustrated too easily.
awesome teacher, very hot!

Dr. Cribbs is the most helpful professor I have had at Virginia Tech. She's not easy, but her review sessions and office hours are great, and she is really good in a small group. Many people struggled in her class, because there were hardly any people at her review sessions. She does an awesome job at helping students understand chemistry.

its not that she is a bad teacher but she does not know how to put a test together. I knew all the information but her tests were absolutely incomprehensible. I know at least 1/2 the class withdrew! i don't know why they would ever hire her again

The one good thing about her is that she was available a lot. She had office hours almost every day. however, her tests were hard and the lectures weren't that helpful. The problem is that she has her PhD in ORGANIC chemistry from Stanford and has worked in a lab and everything; she's a professional, so she shouldn't teach FRESHMAN chemistry

This ain't high school. Cribbs is a good teacher, but you have to do the work to get a good grade. She has high expectations, and forces you to live up to them. If you do the work, her class is immensely satisfying. She is not the greatest lecturer (it's only her second year), but she is super smart and can answer/clarify any questions you have.

her class is pointless. going to lecture doesn't help and neither do her notes or powerpoints. her tests never coincide with the connect homework. try to switch out of her class. you'll regret it if you don't.
New teacher did not help me much and made class confusing. There were many kids i knew that dropped out or withdrew, while a lot of others just failed

The entire the class is group project based, so either you love it or hate it. He is an amazing teacher and really gets to understand the students. When talking to him he honestly feels more like a friend rather than a teacher. He has years of experience in the field and is great at giving out of class examples to what we are learning.
Dr. Czuba is the best. I have never met a professor like him before. He genuinely cares about undergrads and is awesome about getting them connected with his research. He is also just very cool.
He knows his area of expertise and explains it so that you can easily understand too. I always thought his lectures were interesting and loved when he would lead the labs.

Professor Dao's class was largely based on proofs and memorization of materials rather than true understanding of the concepts. She would move too quickly through most sections, and for the more difficult proofs, you were left to fend for yourself and do them at home. The homeworks were worth very little leaving no room for mistakes on tests
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are proof based and more memorization rather than conceptually. Not a very good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dao is one of the few teachers in the math department who truly cares about her students and it shows. She is always willing to help and is reasonable with grades and expectations.
She was very hard to follow, covered a lot of unnecessary topics, and graded so harshly. She would take points off for the smallest things.

Dr Dao is a good teacher but sometimes hard to understand due to ESL. There's little leniency and very little extra credit. I remember criteria for HW was 0 points if all of the work shown was “not relevant”. I got 0 points for many questions, despite showing lots of pertinent work. She was unwilling to reason and didn't offer partial credit.

Hard to understand and not a great teacher. Tests and homework were graded harshly. She knows what she is talking about, but does not do a great job explaining or giving students a solid understanding. You have to dedicate a lot of time to teaching yourself to succeed.

Definitely one of the better calculus professors at VT (a notoriously bad program), I'd recommend her! She's very accessible in and outside of class, and is always willing to help. Tough homework grader for sure, but it prepares you for the test grading, which is also incredibly meticulous and strict.

Her teaching was great and she breaks down concepts well. Her grading was harsh on HW, but on exams she was fair and I was able to justify points back on multiple occasions. I've seen her explain concepts as dumb as 1/4=.25 without judging the student. She is great at taking feedback and admitting mistakes. If you try you will easily pass her class

There was some extra credit, but the class was hard to follow. She was difficult to understand, and the structure of the class was really bad. It was basically AB Calculus made harder for no reason. Tests and homework were really harshly graded. Even if my answers were correct, I'd lost points at times.

The professor was great and understood the students as well. She was very harsh with grading hw assignments but there were plenty of extra credit assignments to make up. I have never heard anyone in my class criticize her and is always ready to answer your queries no matter how dumb they are. She is also ready to admit her mistakes unlike most.

Dr. Dao's office hours were very helpful. She takes the time to work 1 on 1 with her students when approached for help. She gives lots of extra credit written homework assignments and offers corrections on written homework for partial credit. This class is hard being a weed out class at VT, but her teaching made the content easier.
Nice lady, I took her class and did a study abroad with her. She grades tough on somethings and not on others. If your respectful towards her, she is to you too

Tough grader, will not give out 100s even if you follow the rubric word for word. She uses index cards for attendance in a class full of 200+ students, which is my biggest pet peeve. Super helpful career based class. She will make you go to the career fair, which can be a bit annoying. Expect to hear pessimism abt going to vet school every class.

Dr. Wood takes forever to grade all assignments and constantly docks points off even when your assignment followed the posted rubrics. If you want to go to vet school, don't mention that to her. She will condescend everyone who wants to be pre-vet.

In my opinion, people are dramatic about Dr. Wood. Yes, she grades tough and there's a lot of work for a seminar class, but everything you do is useful and stuff you would need to do anyway (resume, elevator pitch, etc.). I was intimidated to take her class because of the reviews but she really isn't that bad and clearly cares about your success.

Dr. Wood taught the class for half of the semester because our other professor left. Dr. Wood helped a lot with understanding different concepts and lab days. Overall, the class was a lot of work for a one-credit lab, but the midterm and final were graded fairly, and overall, if you study and attend the labs, you should be able to get an A.

I'll admit, the negative reviews about her are true, but I wouldn't say she's all bad. Some of her guest speaker lectures were interesting, and she gives okay feedback on assignments, that is when you finally get them at the end of the semester. She does grade harshly, and the only reason why I have an A is because I did some of the EC assignments.
Expect not to get a 100% on everything. She will give you broad expectations for her instructions on an assignment and then grade it harshly.

dr woods takes FOREVER to grade everything. The feedback she does give sucks and just overall unhelpful. Also very discouraging, if you want to go to vet school don't talk to her she made me feel like I couldn't and don't try to contact her outside of class because she has "hundreds" of emails to go through and just not enough time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be ready not to get a 100% on anything. She even says she doesn't go by the rubric because they are wrong. If you have to leave class early she asks the class a question to know who is still there and she does this every time she sees someone get up and leave. Some of the information in the course is good to know.

Probably the worst teacher I've ever had. Be prepared for the most boring class of your life. Even if you follow the rubrics exactly, it's super hard to get full credit for each assignment. Very unforgiving and expects wayyy to much effort for a FYE class.

Really discouraging and dismissive to anyone trying to go to vet school. Takes until the end of the semester to grade anything, and all assignments are just busy work for an unnecessary class. She makes you attend a career fair, even though any companies there related to APSC majors are geared toward the production/business emphasis.

Dr Wood grades stuff too harshly, even for some of the most simplest things. Kinda boring class. Doesn't provide good feedback on what you did wrong. Not the worst professor I've had, but not the best either.

Dr. Wood is a sweet woman who is there to realistically help you plan your future. However, she does tend to babble on a bit. She takes off points if the simplest things are off in assignments like the title. The class kind of feels like a waste of time but attendance is unfortunately mandatory and a big part of your grade.

Cindy Wood is easily one of the most difficult professors I've had in my two years here. Her grading style is unique to put it in nicer terms. She will state broad expectations in the instructions of the assignment but grade it on completely different criteria. Also, you will have to wait until the end of the semester just to see your grades.

Dr. Wood was kinda rude on several occasions. I really got the vibe she doesn't care for students dreams. makes you feel dumb for asking questions. Grades things months after the due date, doesn't take late work either. The lab is only 1 credit but makes you work like a 3 credit course.

Dr. Wood is the worst professor I have ever had. Her tests are unfair & are designed for students to fail. The 1 credit lab class should be a 3 credit w the amount of work she expects us to do. The lab is supposed to be fun but she makes it miserable. She never answers emails even if it's important (I emailed abt the final and didnt get a response)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you have a passion and love for animals, GOOD LUCK. Im officially traumatized. Oh and dont go to the carcass lab, youre welcome.

WILL grade your assignments 2+ months later and expect you to re-do them 2 weeks before finals. Also very unclear grading criteria, ex: I got permission to turn in an assignment as it was in a different format, it was then given a zero because of that format. Will not respond to your emails (told us within the first half she was 2+ weeks behind).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rude and crushes any aspiration to go to veterinary school. She is one of the main reasons I changed majors. If you have any technical difficulty that prevents you from turning in work she will give you a zero and say" should have contacted 4help" hw assigned is pointless and hair pulling stressful to figure out on your own. TAs do not care about u
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE DR. WOOD! Very difficult to deal with, mandatory attendance, no flexibility, no willingness or care. I had an issue uploading my video recording, I emailed it to her to not be penalized. She emailed me back with "I do not accept assignments outside of the canvas, contact 4Help". Then sent out an announcement outing me out to the class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm not sure if this is the right Dr. Wood because her name is Cynthia not Cindy but oh well, I'm too mad to not leave a review. I had Dr. Wood for APSC FYE. That's right, first year experience. I got a C. How is this possible? Well, because Dr. Wood is so unclear with deadlines, a harsh grader, and didn't grade until the end of the semester.

Very unclear about everything. The class was a disaster and no one knew what was going on. The SLOWEST grader. Nothing graded until the end of the semester so absolutely no clue what my grade was. Never answered my emails. Answered other students emails, but not very kindly.
Makes FYE (a one-credit course) incredibly too complicated. Dredded going every week. Lectures alot, class runs over time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had! Her requirements to turn in assignments changed between every assignment. I had her for FYE which is supposed an easy transition class, but she made it very difficult and didn't help at all. She doesn't answer questions asked during lectures and doesn't care to help students.

Worst professor I have had so far. The assignments are meant to be easy but ends up getting graded extremely harshly for reasons that don't really matter. Lacks information for requirements for assignments. Does not answer questions clearly, and is extremely hard to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The Animal and Poultry Science department shines, except for Dr. Wood. She is easily one of the worst professors I've had throughout my college career, and her teaching style for lab is horrendous. There is little to no review for exams, and quizzes are more difficult than needed.
The lab itself is pretty fun, but the weekly quizzes online are really hard. The midterm is also pretty difficult too.

This class is absurdly hard for a freshman-level class. Lectures are irrelevant and she won't answer any questions you have. Need to know every vocab word as she'll test you on them fill-in-the-blank style. All her tests have trick questions on stupid minor details and there's only 2 exams which doesn't give you much room. HUGE curve at the end.

Reading the textbook is necessary to prepare for the tests. The actual lecture slides aren't that helpful. The tests are unncessarily hard. Review sessions were pointless. Just show up to class on days most people skip to earn extra credit. Curves at the end of the year.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Intro to animal science lab was supposed to be fun--at least I thought. Dr. Wood only cares to tell you about pigs. Pigs this, pigs that, but nothing else. She's always trying to trick you up on your test as well. There is only a midterm and a final. So glad I'm done, I switched from a major to a minor in animal science just because of this lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Dr. Wood is a really sweet lady and the TA's seem like they care about the students and want to help you, but what stumped me in this class were the exams. I studied hard and thought I did okay when I finished but ended up bombing it. The average grade for the class was a D and all she had to say was to study harder. Kind lady but very hard grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her tests and quizzes don't relate well to the material you learned. You'll never know what to study. Her lectures contain a lot of information and it seems as though the important parts are never the things you're tested on. She also teaches lab and nothing ever makes sense. This class was mandatory for my major but I hated it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She is very strict on her grading and changes the requirements of the assignments all the time.

I loved having Dr. Wood for Intro honestly. She is a sweet and intelligent women (the first woman in VT's animal science department btw). She gives quizzes regularly but drops the lowest and gives you assignments you can get 100s on if you go to her for office hours. KNOW YOUR VOCAB. Also, gives lots of bonus and curves tests. If you study her slides and add a little detail while knowing how to apply the concepts, you'll do fine. Tests were not that bad. Got 91s on every test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Respected

reviews.comment: The tests are very tough and specific. They rarely cover things discussed in lecture and she won't give you any hints of what will be on the test. She honestly doesn't seem like she knows a lot about the subject (animal science) either.

Dr. Wood was an engaging lecturer and I understood the material well in class, but she makes the hardest tests.  Her multiple choice will make you question everything you've studied. She says two correct answers in class, and they are both answers on the test and only one is right. Know every vocab on the vocab handout, reading book isn't needed.

Dr. Wood may seem nice, but her grading scale is absurd and her expectations for the class are way too high. I spent at least 3 hours each week studying for the lab quizzes and I almost never got anything higher than a C. If you don't need the class, don't take it.

Super hard lab. Doesn't matter if you have animal experience or not, Dr. Wood will teach you her way of doing things and it's her way or the highway. She seems nice at first but if you make a small mistake during lab she will make you feel like you are an inch tall. The midterm wasn't bad but the written part of the final is super hard.

Very hard lab. She posts lab handouts 3 days before the actual lab and the handouts are usually about 14+ pages long. It's a LOT of information and her quizzes/exams are really hard. Your whole grade depends on how you do on these quizzes and exams.
Great teacher! A little on the goofy side but it keeps it interesting. Its obvious she is passionate about what she teaches. One of my favorite classes all week!

She's really understanding and takes time to respond to you diligently. I felt that the exams and quizzes had some hard questions and grading sometimes seemed unfair. If you pay attention 100% and take notes, you should be okay.

Don't get me wrong, shes a wonderful lady. Shes really nice and willing to help. However the quizzes are way too hard and irrelevant, and the midterm was too challenging. It has made me want to change my major from animal science to biology. This may show you whether this is the right major for you. Not as much science as i would have liked.

She has one way of teaching and to her, that's the right way. If you are good at learning from that style of teaching, you will be fine, but if you're not, good luck. By this style of teaching, she pretty much restricts her students to one way of learning, so be prepared to look a lot of things up on your own.
pointless class.
A Professor that really cares about your success and will help you with ANY problem!
She's so much fun -- I totally recommend any and all of her classes.
She is a nice person but her exams are absolutely horrendous. Ridiculously hard. Thought you studied well? Guess again.
Sometimes I feel a little all over the place, and then I attend this class and realize there are worse cases out there.

I took this class online, so it was a little different. She gave us extra credit on all 5 exams just by completing a kahoot. Homework was hard but doable, and discussions were fine. The cheat sheet for exams helped me a lot. I'm not sure if I would've done well without the sheet. I'd recommend introducing yourself to her to make a connection.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think she makes the exams unreasonably hard, and she knows they're hard because they're all open note/open book/ open resource. She puts stuff on the quizzes and exams that we didn't even talk about. She does extra credit kahoots for exam review.

She talks at at a PhD level and has absolutely no idea how to simplify information and make it understandable. I went to every class and paid attention the entire time, and still had no idea what was going on. Slides are extremely confusing and lack information. Tests are open notes but the questions are so specific that it doesn't do much.

Do not freak out about your grade in this class. If you do all the participation and bonuses she gives, you will end with at least a C or B in the class - even if you bomb the tests. Show her your point of view and she will likely give you those points back if you thought you were right when you answered it.

If you want to be confused take this class. Her lectures are all over the place and when you finally organize everything she tests you on material that you haven't learned. Hope you love research papers and genetics because she will test you on those as well. The one good thing she does is if everyone fails the test she will curve it.

It's unfortunate that she sucks so much because this class is required for HNFE. She is a bad teacher and her textbook is not well written and confusing. I went to class everyday and still didn't learn very much. In my opinion they should replace her
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Definitely a work intensive class, but I am surprised by the amount of negative reviews I see here. Professor Deane is super caring and a really understanding professor. He is happy to answer any questions and when I needed to shift time to take an exam he was incredibly willing to work with me on that. Start your group projects early though.

A 20 hour project plus quizzes and exams almost every week is a whole lot but that's pretty much the entire class. His quizzes and exams are open note which helps. He's nice but he has a lot of weird policies with how he grades things and counts absences. Pray you get a good group and company to work with otherwise your grade will suffer.

Difficulty is definitely a range but I spent 40 hours on a min 20 hour project. #1 tip is once you find a nonprofit your team wants to work with, confirm with the prof ASAP. Don't get stuck with a new org that will work you to the bone. Deane expects you to read the textbook, watch lectures, take exams, and keep your project managers happy. Sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took fall semester- seemed like an easy class until presentation days. He approved our projects early on but then decided to give a 1-2 page critique acting confused why we chose our topic + solution. He *loves* guest lectures from Deloitte, and will test on their "fun facts". Requires attendance at an 8AM class and gets pissy if you're late.

He was incredibly strict on grading and did not give any credit at all for late work. He also was not helpful in aiding our group with out project or telling us what he wanted out of the final project until it was much too late.

had him for comp modeling and decision analysis (I think that's the name).  He was ok, and wanted to help, but I got nothing from the classes.  I really wish I would've skipped them all b/c I had to read all the slides over anyway.
Great class, great professor!

Loved Dr. Poets, basically no homework except a couple take-home quizzes, an essay and group project that were all pretty easy. Attendance was not mandatory, I didn't mind that lectures were boring because she was very kind and always willing to help if we had questions, you can tell she's very knowledgeable and passionate about this subject.

If you like talking with other students in class, you will like this class, as its mostly lectures with either the professor or a group giving a presentation with much "discussion" time. If you dont like talking in class the lectures given by the professor are good, but the frequent group presentations by other groups can be pretty boring.

I took intro to World Politics with Professor Poets. The lectures were lackluster and boring and rarley cited the readings. We had in class reading quizes which were harder than they needed to be and very subjective. Also be prepared as prof. Poets is very proggressive and will not hide it. Exam were easy if you know what you were doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best professors at VT. It's obvious that she cares about her students and the material in class. Her lectures are incredibly interesting and attendance and participation is not a problem because you will WANT to go to her lectures. Assignments require work but aren't a problem. Great class and professor!

Professor Dennis was a great professor. He was kind, and really cared about his students, and will absolutely help you out when you ask. The caveat to this is that his lessons are very long and very lecture-y. He puts everything he is going to say on his canvas page, and then reads the canvas page word for word, which ends up being very boring.

He does over explain a lot of the assignments, but as someone who had no experience with 3D modeling prior to this class, it ended up being useful when I would forget things. The projects are lengthy, but also very fun. He is also very willing to help if you need it.

Having Dustin Dennis as my professor was genuinly such a different expierience. Attendece is mandatory and the projects are soemtimes very limiting. His overall attitude was not bad but a lot of the time the directions were jsut over explained and it felt really exhausting to be in that class for so long. I tend to find myself really bored.

He was a great professor and always seemed very prepared! It's a long studio class and he lectures most of the time, but his demos/instructions are really helpful, especially in the 3D modeling portion of the class, and he always made sure no one was left behind. He really cares about his students and is even willing to help outside of class.

Loved how everything you needed to do was straightforward and completely laid out for EVERY single assignment. Also has this amazing late grading policy where you lose 15 points for late work after the deadline and have a week to get it turned in, so if you're willing to take a hit for a couple assignments thats okay

Dustin is incredibly kind and is always willing to help you out if you're stuck on a particular segment + makes sure that you understand it. His projects are very clear-cut and understandable with what he expects from you. He's very chill and understanding. Might be a bit slow-paced if you're the kind of person who likes to jump ahead.

Super kind and caring. Drops the lowest test score, open-note homework quizzes that match the exam content well. Professor Milly's study guides also correspond well to what's on her exams. She has a very cheerful spirit, and it is clear that she cares about her students as well as being passionate about teaching.

This class started out promising. I was excited for another class discussing international politics but was overwhelmed by the sheer amount of unclear/convoluted assignment descriptions (e.g. 5 page doc describing a 5-6 page paper). I recommend PSCI majors pick something else for their 3XXX elective.

Dr. Milly, as shown by other reviews, is obsessed with Japan, hence why she teaches an entire class for it. She is passionate about the subject, and while I do admit she can get somewhat boring during lectures, but the material can be interesting if you make it. Not a hard grader at all and gives good feedback!

The tests are difficult unless you complete the daily readings. The daily readings are dense and lengthy. The lectures are boring. She is very dedicated to helping the class understand the material though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is so boring. Oh my goodness. Be prepared to stay up all night studying for an exam and then see questions on the exam that weren't in her lectures, notes, or study guides. Also recommend sitting in the front to try to stop you from falling asleep. She has a weird sense of humor and is just so dry. SO BORING!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a very nice lady and but extremely boring. It would be helpful if she made more useful study guides or held more helpful review sessions. At least give the students more to work with; if it's difficult to keep students engaged in class try and make the lecture notes easier to comprehend. Regardless, your gonna need more than hard work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: The most boring professor I have had in my 12 years of education, it's extremely difficult to stay remotely engaged. I honestly couldn't tell you about the curriculum bc I was probably asleep. Papers are hardly worth any of your grade and are very time consuming despite this. I would say you definitely need to read the book.

Nice lady, fair grader, attendance is taken every day, exams are fairly easy if you are good at studying/make time to read the assigned reading before the exam date. I got a 82 on my first exam and a 90 on my most recent one. Test average is a solid C.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: OKAY first off, she is LITERALLY the most boring person I have ever encountered. For some reason she is OBSESSED with Japan. Her powerpoints make no sense and her tests have multiple right answers. Basically if you don't do the readings, ya done for. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I loved politics and she somehow made the topic excruciatingly boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I didn't like Politics before I came to this class, now I really don't like Politics.  Thanks Deborah, you made politic more boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: No way to pass the exams without doing the daily readings. Has a variety of graded assignments: quizzes, short papers, exams, and an essay. She is really nice but she is boring. I've fell asleep and/or had to fight to not fall asleep multiple times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Milly is a very nice lady and she is so helpful. Has lots of assignments and your tests are only like 35% of your grade. Bless her heart, but she is so boring! I had to fight to stay awake.  She is very fair and often gives away test questions in lecture before the test. Reading is very helpful to understanding the lectures. She loves Japan.
do no take her class. she makes no sense and her tests have mulitple right answers for each question. the book is very boring as well.
Class is very boring. Tests are fairly difficult and studies guides don't help at all
This women is boring...avoid at all costs!!!!
No Comments
Great professor and great econ elective!

Professor Debass was very insightful in his teaching and is very passionate about each topic he brings up. Although the class can be so long, he still tries to make it as engaging as possible. Be ready to talk in class. The assignments are straight forward and easy to write.
Gets mad if you are late but shows up late frequently, which is quite ironic. Does not respond to emails. However, his class isn't hard.

Dr. Debass is a fantastic professor who really connects with his class. Main criteria to succeed in his courses is to always attend the zoom, camera on, and ready to participate in the discussion. No exams or finals just a discussion based courses, a few reflections, and final group project. Would recommend to any student looking for Econ electives
Great Teacher and the class was really fun. Definitely Recommend you to take.

Though limited by its online format, Professor Debass was one of the best professors I had during my time at VT. He clearly is passionate about what he is teaching and has a wealth of experience and knowledge to offer, take advantage!
Very knowledgeable professor, really enjoyed his class! He has so many connections and brought in awesome guest speakers.

I loved having Dr. Komal K. Dhillon as my professor. She is extremely knowledgeable in course material and  is very fair in what she assigns and how she grades. Every exam is open note and online, plus she lays out what will be on each through her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A little harsh on attendance, but she offers lots of extra credit. Super kind and passionate about her class.

Ms. Dhillon is passionate about the things she teaches, but your experience in her course will largely depend on the participation of others. If other students (or you) are disinterested in discussions, I would avoid her courses. If you are confident in your opinion and not shy, though, she is wonderful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Dhillon is an incredible professor and an even more amazing person. Her compassion for her students does not go unnoticed and it's a privilege to be one of her students. Her class, while still having challenges, is passable if you put in some effort and ask questions, and just make it aware that you're there to learn. She is truly the best.

I am a Dr. Dhillon fan first, human second. She does not play when it comes to things like critical thinking and seeing an outside perspective. I thoroughly enjoyed her lectures because it wasn't just a show-up, read from slides, and leave... Had her for PSVP 2044 and senior capstone! She is very engaging as long as you put forth an effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I didn't really enjoy this class... it felt like we learned enough material for maybe a 2-3 week chunk of the class and the rest was just movies and group presentations. easy a but i didn't really enjoy it.

Does not review before quizzes or tests and that makes up most of your grade. Her slides are difficult to refer to because most of the time there's just questions on the slides with no answer. Does not have sympathy for students. Wouldn't take her class again.
She is a phenomenal professor and person. I would 100% take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She's relaxed, she respects your opinion, and gives great topics and insight into African American culture. Also, one of the nicest professors to talk to during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was the worst teacher I have ever had at tech. Only talked about her opinions and I learned everything on my own. No lectures, no slides, just assigned mass amounts of reading and then discussed her opinion on them the entire class. Her grading was ridiculous, she gave no information on what should be included in projects and papers.

Disorganized, and does not teach. Mondays were for group presentations on textbook chapters and Wednesdays we did not meet as a class. Refers you to a WikiHow page if you have questions on assignments, or references textbook, only provides vague feedback and instruction and grades harsh if you dont do it right. Extremely rude Do not take her class

So Dr. Dhillon I guess is new. She teaches Gender& Women's studies (at Hollins University). Her classes are disorganized and pushes her own opinion onto to the class instead of encouraging the students to develop their own. She is a bit anal with certain things and that gets annoying. Doesn't connect well with her students. Class is not interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice professor. There's one writing assignment and one group project. The quizzes are 5 questions and based off of the lectures. She does assign readings but they're going to be throughly explained in the lecture. The exams are online and based off of the textbook; that's the only time you'll need the book.

Professor Dhillon is a wonderful professor. Her lectures are interesting and informative. She is easy to talk to and offers lots of opportunities for extra credit. To be successful, I would suggest doing the readings and paying attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: take this class

To say this class was trash will be putting it likely. The teacher, who I call teacher because she doesn't deserve to be called professor, barely knew what she was talking about. But oh did she talk class, felt like someone was melting my brain. If I could give anything lower than zero, I would've.

Not sure why people hate on him so much. It's very easy to get an A if you just do the the work. He's understanding if you email him with questions or need to turn something in late. His first impression isn't super warm, but he's not a bad guy. People complain about lab reports, but it's a chem lab, what do you expect?

Yall hate on Dr. Deck for no reason. While yes, he seems a bit intimidating at first, he's actually a really nice guy and wants all his students to succeed. In addition, he grades very leniantly and tells you exactly what you did wrong.

Dr. Deck is a very nice guy and loves to crack some dad jokes, however he does not know how to teach Chem 1036. It is very hard to understand his lectures and I found myself getting lost most of the time. I was only able to get an A- in the class because of his lecture videos (which helped more than his actual lectures), class studios, and practice

take ANY other professor. in regards to lectures, hw, and exams, it is standardized among all the 1036 classes. however, his iclickers based off accuracy rather than telling you the correct answer unlike how the other chem 1036 professors do. you will be at a disadvantage bc of this. other professors are better at explaining the content as well.

I was originally set to be in Bowens chem class (highly recommend), then force added over to Deck. He's a super sweet guy but he can't teach 1036. I learned everything from studio and from my friends in Bowen. I would suggest switching over to a different teacher
Dear god. Never again
This guy blows doesnt teach whats on the tests.

Dr Deck makes it clear that he wants his students to do well, and seems like a nice guy, but for the love of god he cannot teach 1036 topics. Random tangents take up most of the lecture time, making going to them feel useless, but genuinely the only way to boost your grade because of iClickers. Switch professors before you end up teaching yourself.

Paul Deck is such a sweet guy, and you can tell he loves the content. I think this was his first year teaching 1036 and you could tell. . .. He loves the content but he's not very good at teaching it, which was unfortunately seen in the majority of the class. If you get him, you have to teach virtually everything to yourself or get a friend.
Professor Deck genuinely wishes to see you succeed, but he is a little intimidating. He gives concise feedback on all lab reports. If you show up to lab without PPE, don't bother entering.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He genuinely cant teach to save his life. I study so much and my grade is horrid. He takes so long and rants about things that aren't on the test so we never finish the content on time. He writes like a little kid so you cant even read his hand writing. If you get this man change professors. Just take chem online it's not one worth it.

Professor Deck seems like a nice guy, but he just doesn't come off as a good teacher. He's not super great at explaining the concepts and he talks about random things in class that just confuse people more. I ended up teaching myself everything for this class, so coming to class felt useless except for the IClickers.

we were all switched into his class last minute and he does not usually teach this course. He genuinely says so much in his lectures but nothing at all- if that makes sense. You have to teach yourself everything by doing the home works and having a tutor. He gets so conceptual and talks about organic chemistry every class

Dr. Deck is the worst professor I have ever had. He told us that he hasn't taught this course since 2003 and it's quite obvious. He spends half the class talking about nonsense and when he finally teaches, he does it wrong. If you take his class be ready to teach yourself everything and have a tutor on standby. Or at least have another W left.

He yaps about the most random things ever. He also talks so slow it will put you to sleep not to mention he doesn't actually finish some of the chapters before the tests. Overall he should stay as an advisor and not teach.

I was put in Dr. Deck's class last minute and I have never struggled so much in a chem course. He is a very nice guy but I (any many others in my class) just simply struggle to understand his lectures. He rambles and just does not explain concepts well. I did well in 1035 with another prof and I understand chem usually and other profs are better.

I quite enjoyed Dr. Deck's first year chemistry lab. He is a genuine and honest man, which is to say he did not pull punches when grading or correcting in the lab. I found this helpful, and sometimes a little over the top, can definitely understand why as chem majors he wants to get this in our heads as early as possible. Very understanding too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The only issue with him is that, in the work you turn in, he will point out the most random things that may seem small to you but major to him. You can lose a point for writing .76 instead of 0.76. But other than that, his prelab assignments are very similar to the labs. Just pay attention. Could you do the work and don't skip labs?
It was the worst one-credit class I have ever taken. It was too much work. My Calculus 2 class is easier than my first-year chemistry lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Deck is nice; however, the class is so awful that it made me want to switch from a chemistry major to a business major. I took AP Chemistry in high school, and this class made me feel like I could not comprehend anything. There is so much homework and lab report assignments for this class, which is one credit. I cry because of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Grades seemingly at random, you could do a whole few pages of a worksheet and he would give a less than 50% with only one comment about something specific.

Dr. Deck was incredibly understanding as long as you communicate with him beforehand. Attendance is mandatory and he does not like when students are late, so be punctual. Overall, he was a great professor who truly wants his students to learn from his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr Deck is a very good gen chem lab prof. The way he structured the class taught us basic lab techniques we will need and provided us with kind of a foundation for writing lab reports. He was very accessible in office hours and it was very easy to get good grades as long as you asked him questions about things you were unsure about.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Deck was very specific in how he wanted everything. This class was very challenging at times for just being one credit but as long as you go to your TA for help and use his rubrics you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Deck is an amazing professor who clearly does not get enough credit on this website. I had him for the 1065 gen chem lab for majors course and he was simply incredible. I could write so much more summating how great the course and professor was, but there simply aren't enough characters allowed on this review. Needless to say I got a 97.4%
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Everyone gives Deck a hard time, but he was a really good professor and was so willing to help you- if you showed you were trying and put in effort. He was easy to talk to and wanted to make sure you succeed. Responds quickly and is easy to talk to. He will help you if you put in effort in yourself first.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Deck is strict and very particulate as a lab teacher, but he will give you all the hints and help possible if you just approach him. His sense of humor is great in lab, if he sees the enthusiasm and passion to learn and think throughly with the assignments he assigns then he will be on your good side.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Deck was a very straightforward and sometimes mean professor. He gave very clear and helpful feedback on assignments, but didn't come off as the nicest at times. He wasn't very approachable, but I appreciated how clear and organized he was, which helped me get the grade I got in his class. If you can get over his attitude, you'll love Deck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I didn't personal enjoy his way of teaching but he was a nice professor at the end of the course. there is a ton of homework and i advise to work on it before hand and dont wait. also if you wanna pass go to office hours he would literally go over every problem with you. but worst chem class so far. he takes point off your final grade if your LATE.
Great teacher, his lectures are engaging. Test do encompass everything, including things briefly talked about.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is not a difficult course with the correct teaching. Deck did an amazing job at making videos for us to watch before a lab so we understood what was happening, but provided little to no help. Deck is also a very strict grader which is a plus if you're looking to fail. I suggest trying to find a new chem lab professor if possible.

HALF of the class is failing. Class average on most tests is a D and he does not care or curve. Tests are nothing like what you study for. Worst class that I have taken at a VT. This is coming for someone who got an A in chem 1035.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Deck is a really touch grader and most people do really poorly on the first couple of assignments, but he's good about answering questions and explaining things. reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you enjoy teaching yourself and getting arrogant responses when asking a simple question, then take his class.

He's a tyrant in a way because he's very demanding, making lots of students consider his class as a disaster. However, I understand his love in chemistry. His strictness are just from his sacred belief in chemistry lab. If you exert yourself in the lab report, he will serve you well and express his joy. Otherwise, all of you are losers in his eyes.

Professor Deck was an awesome lab teacher. I took 1065 lab which is a freshman chem majors lab. He was very, very helpful, and I love that he uses piazza and answers any questions you have. As long as you respect him, he will help you in any way possible. The post lab reports were difficult but like I said, he helps in any way he can. Awesome guy!!

Dr. Deck is extremely knowledgeable in the field of chemistry and it amazes me how much he knows. Lab reports can be tough but using Piazza as a resource for questions is very helpful. He explains all of the labs before you do them so that there isn't a misunderstanding and will answer questions in the lab if needed

I went to office hours to talk to Paul Deck because I was failing the class and he basically told me wow that sucks there is no way I can help you. I now am withdrawing and will have to take the class again next semester putting me behind. He is so boring during lecture and talks about the most random stuff. If you want to be successful drop him

Great lab professor! He was well prepared and very clear with what should happen. He is always willing to help, and if you tell him you're struggling he will set up an appointment. You can even ask him about lecture and he will explain things really well!

He's predominantly a grad student teacher, so he's going to be tough. Read the book, do the homework/practice questions and you're going to pass.  He's also one of the few undergrad chem professors who goes out of his way to help students. That being said, don't take his classes unless you have to.
he makes class much harder than it needs to be. Switch out, the other professor's tests are much easier to deal with.

His freshman chem class is just ridiculous. His teaching is awful, he's boring, I literally can not stay awake during his class when I try to. His tests are just annoying, too. I'd switch out if I were you.

He was absolutely HORRIBLE. None of his lectures helped you to understand the material. Yes the class is hard regardless of the teacher, but he makes it that much worse. He doesnt't do extra credit, nor does he drop low grades, or curve. DO NOT TAKE HIS CHEM CLASS!
Honestly, switch out. The way he talks is incredibly annoying, and his tests suck. If you don't have much prior knowledge of chemistry from high school, he doesn't help.
Worst professor and worst class ever! Difficult to take notes and the tests are ridiculously hard.
Very boring teacher. Made the class harder then it needed to be
One of the hardest classes I've had to take! His help sessions for exams are not very helpful and the exams are very difficult as well. Switch out as soon as possible!

This was by far my worst class first semester of freshman year. Drop him if you can. I was .3 from a C and he would not round up. His lectures are boring and his tests are hard. He is not helpful at all, even if you go and ask for help.

The lectures for this class were pretty boring. However, he posts the powerpoints ahead of time so all you have to do is fill in blanks. He wasn't always the most helpful guy, but if you study for his tests using old tests he posts, you should do be able to pull off a B.

Not a good professor! His class is so hard. I put in a lot of effort and he didn't seem to care.  If you get him and your not very good at chem...GET OUT! switch.  I had a tutor, studied, stressed, went to office hours...not much help.  His tests are crazy

This class was really difficult. Take it with someone else if you can!! I did the homework, went to the study sessions, and really studied for every test and none of it seemed to help. The class averages on tests were usually in the 60's, and he seemed fine with that. he will not curve.

He is so boring! So hard! It is hard to get help because he has so many people come to his office hours, so no individualized attention. He is a horrible teacher! I had to drop his class and take it with another teacher.

MANY professors give tests just before break, REGARDLESS of game days, so that we aren't overloaded with info during the last two weeks of class.  Deck is a pretty good professor, you just have to PAY ATTENTION and DO YOUR HOMEWORK.  The material is difficult, and it's taught at 8am-put in some effort!  He's a great prof!

Takes too long on some simpler concepts, and speeds through some of the harder concepts, but with a ton of work you can do pretty well, you have to put in almost 2hrs a night. Not too bad, but if you fall asleep easily bring lots of caffine or try and take a different professor.

I HATE HIM!  DROP HIS CLASS IMMEDIATELY! He does not care about teaching, he is only there for research. made us take a test BEFORE BREAK and AFTER thursday night game! practice tests are not real, real tests are 1005 harder. DOESNT DO ANY CURVE. STAY AWAY!!!!
NO good

DO NOT TAKE CHEM 1035 WITH DECK!!! i went to his office hours to discuss my grade after the first test and he told me that if i didnt get a good grade on the next exam to drop the class and take it in the spring!!! plus he cursed!! not very professional and professors should help u in some ways, not put you down!dont take chem with him!

Easiest gen chem teacher there is.  His tests are extremely easy, yet the class average is still low.  I have seen the tests for the other professors and they are much more in depth and challenging than Deck's.  He is very cocky but overall a decent professor.

Extremely easy! Never opened my book. Paid attention to his teachings because the test ?s are exactly like his examples. Do the assigned chem skill builders, attend class, take the "koofers" he makes available. Guaranteed A for anyone who does these

I don't agree with the latter reviews. Deck dumbs Chem down so much just for the kids who don't understand.  If you go to lectures and pay attention to his examples,(which now he uses a tablet to display work) the class is extremely easy.There is no way he can show examples over and over in a 50 min lect.Use your book or CSB if you don't understand

Hardest teacher i have ever had, asked other chem majors and they told me to get out of his class and to tell everyone to get out of it because it was so hard. dont take his class, he just reads off the board and does not help at all.

Hmmmm...everyone says he's really hard....but I ended up with a 96 in the class...and that's only because I got a 92 on the Final...the rest were 100s....he's not too bad....he's really cocky...and the slides HELP if you actually look at them once in a while..I didn't open the book once...everything was on the slides.

Extremely boring (many times I've fallen asleep)and unhelpful.. Reads directly off slides. He's focused on just wanting to finish the lectures rather than helping students. His tests are very hard. Take Durrill or Amateis!!!

Listen, is she skilled at marketing? sure. Does she like her job? sure. Is she a good teacher? no. classes are a joke and are hard to follow for the PowerPoints, rude to her ta and guests she has. Exams are hard to study for because you have no idea what she will put on them.

She forces her students to add her on all social media so she can plug her own professional interests into the class and gain more social media interactions. Really big class, super boring lectures, not a lot of homework but the online chapter homework is just annoying and time consuming. The class is not hard its just time consuming and I did not enjoy it. She does online polls so you have to attend class. I found this really annoying because the lectures are pretty useless.

I took Wertalik's online marketing class over wintermester. There were 2 multiple choice exams. We covered 1 chapter per day. I watched her video lectures and took notes, then did the corresponding HW. About 1-2 hours of work per day. Her lectures were 20 min each and were interesting.

Easy A if you do all the homework, SONA labs, and do well on exams that you don't have to study much for. Unfortunately she does polls for attendance otherwise I would not show up. Definitely not my favorite class or professor but it's alright for a class that everyone has to take.

reviews.comment: She randomly talks about irrelevant material that's not going to be on the exam. Attendance is mandatory because she has random attendance polls at the end and if you're not there you get deducted 2 points. I personally can't stand her and the way she has the class structured. Points are randomly given and taken. TAKE THE ONLINE CLASS!!!!!
I never missed one of her classes. I found her to be smart, funny, honest and inspiring. Not to mention one of the sexiest profs on campus.

I always looked forward to attending Prof Wertalik's Marketing Communications class.  She had first hand experience and knowledge in the marketing field and came to class prepared with real world examples. She genuinely cares about her student?s future and is always willing to help.  Not only will you learn, you'll have fun doing it!
Awesome professor that knows how to bring the real world into the classroom! She actually lives what she teaches and is great at bending it to attract student interest...great class!
Seems to really know what he is talking about and it very smart. I only had him for my lab time but he was just very rude when you would ask him a question.

One of the best professors I've had at VT. Lectures are laid out in a very methodical way, and all information provided is relevant. Clearly knows his stuff, and is easy to approach if you don't understand something. Homework and labs take a decent amount of time each week. Attendance isn't recorded, but I don't know how you'd pass without going.

Dr. Dove was a solid teacher overall. His lectures are pretty boring but very informative as he does really know his stuff. Homework and lab reports are given often take a while so be prepared to have a good amount of work outside of the classroom. Notes are posted online but going to classes in person makes the class a lot easier.
cool guy
Makes lectures very interesting, grades won't be an issue if you do the work. Theres lot of opportunity for extra creditr.

Dr. Ellis is absolutely amazing. He loves what he does and speaks with a sense of fun and passion. None of the work is hard but some of the formulas can be challenging. I would take his class again in a heartbeat.

Ellis is a great teacher for earth's climate. Lectures were pretty accessible. Tests weren't bad since you could have whatever you wanted on the review sheet. Sometimes he'd take questions straight from the slides.

Dr. Ellis is a sweetie but the class is somewhat difficult. 4 exams (20% each), 7 assignments (20%.) Short weekly quizzes that only count as extra credit. No textbook, all lecture but he posts the slides on Canvas. Allowed a 'cheat sheet' for every exam that's one sheet of paper front & back. He let our class take the final exam at home.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ellis is a patient man who helps his students do their very best. His lecture notes may be difficult to understand at times but he elaborates on each slide.
