I had him for Intro to Earth's Climate, and it was a very straight forward class. He offers extra credit for attending lectures and give plenty of review material for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The most helpful and respectable professor I have had in college. He is always willing to help out students! During exams, he allows a 3x5 index card which helps a lot. Definitely recommend taking any of his classes.

Ellis was a great professor for Dynamic Meteorology. The material is not easy, but he makes it comprehensible during lectures. He is very helpful during office hours. The tests are not too bad as he allows a 3x5 notecard.
I love this dude he was the best. Such a chill guy and honestly made me want to be more creative.
ENGL 3764 - Dragon was good. Provided solid feedback and didn't grade harshly. I found myself excited to work on some of the assignments in this class despite having a low interest in writing.

Super encouraging prof and his feedback on writing is really nice to hear, especially if you aren't the best writer. He will make you feel like you just ate even if it sucked. And he is pretty nice to look at, so that's a plus!

Perfect professor for introduction to creative writing. You can tell he's passionate, well-read, and down-to-earth. Much of this class is the weekly readings; fairly short yet intellectually eye-opening to the potential in creative writing (even for a STEM major). If you're able to, take a class with him! Easy A and very rewarding.

Initially, I wasn't looking forward to taking English, as it wasn't directly related to my major. However, Mr. Dragon made the class both entertaining and inspiring, which helped me grow as a writer, despite being a STEM major. If you attend class, engage in discussions, and follow the rubric, you'll be on the right track towards earning an A.
Really great professor. I am not the best writer, but as long as you do the work and try your best you will do good.
Great professor, easily my favorite one of this semester. If you can choose him, he gives really good feedback and always wants to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Choose him! Choose him! Choose him!
Very understanding. Great teacher. Going to class is VERY important.

he's super nice and definitely cares about his students. attendance is important but he's pretty lenient if you just let him know. great feedback and simple assignments with plenty of time to get them done.

He is a very laid-back guy who was a pleasure to have as a teacher. If you show up to class and do the homework (which isn't hard at all), you'll get an automatic A. In terms of grading, he is looking to see if you put effort into the paper rather than having absolutely perfect grammar and structure. I'd take his class again if I had the chance.

If you need to take an English class your first semester, absolutely see if Nathan is an option. I've heard stories about horrible professors for First Year Writing, so I definitely got lucky getting Nathan. He was a super easy grader, and as long as you show up and do the work it should be an automatic A. Super nice guy.

He was a very nice teacher and made sure to help everyone if they needed anything. Very straight forward but can get pretty repetitive. Attendance is mandatory and helps with engagement/participation which he appreciates. Grades pretty easily if you do the assignment. I recommend taking if you need to take ENGL 1105/1106.

Nathan Dragon is a great teacher and he tries to teach the material well. I think he does a good job even though the material is slightly boring and repetitive. He grades pretty lenient, and showing up to class surely doesn't hurt. I would definitely recommend taking his class for ENGL 1105/1106

Professor MacKinlay gives great digestible lectures, reasonable amounts of homework, and will help you pass if you show up to class and talk with him. I was able to make up a ton of work and pass after stumbling in the first half of the class. If you can take his class, do it future LSU students!

Might be one of the best professors in the finance department. The way he was able to break down concepts and explain complex financial topics was incredible. Cares about his students and their success a ton!

Hard class but he's outstanding professor. Class is very involved with a lot of information thrown at you. As long as you go to class and practice you will do well. He's always willing to help if your struggling and is very approachable.
Great professor. Best of all time. the GOAT! 100% recommend. Hard class but he makes it easier.
Great professor, best option for the class.

Please take Professor MacKinlay, after taking Hart and having to drop analytics I did really well in Mackinlay's class. He is very helpful and includes almost everything you will see on the exams in assignments, Kritik assignments, and quizzes. I would recommend him for anyone who needs to take 3134.

Hands down one of the best professors I've had. Great lectures and truly wants all of his students to do well. No surprises on any exams or assignments, he's very transparent on everything. Lenient grader compared to other analytics professors. Overall just a great guy and makes a tough class not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This guy is the man, super good lectures, easy grader and an overall really good guy.

Do yourself a favor and make sure you get him for analytics. The class has a bad reputation for a good reason, its a hard course thats very math heavy. Andrew is not like the other analytics professors since he actually teaches the material and is very fair with his grading. But once again, don't go in expecting an easy A, its still analytics.

This man is an angel. He makes the class actually enjoyable with his lectures. Still, the class is a beast and you have to work diligently to get a good grade and/or pass. MacKinlay will "curve" grades at the end of the semester, which just shows how he wants us to succeed and of course not retake the class. Highly recommend!!

If you're taking analytics, I highly recommend this professor. He explains things very clearly and gives a lot of extra leeway in his grading. He works with Bradley Paye, so no wonder he's decent compared to the other analytics professors.
Such a nice professor, and teaches the material really well. Highly recommend.

Best teacher I have ever had at VT. Make sure to go to all the classes and appreciate what you have in MacKinlay. He's the only good analytics teacher at VT and I wish I could've had him for every finance class.

Even though I finished the class with a C, he's still one of the best professors I've ever had here at VT. He's very knowledgeable, but this subject is difficult to teach. His curve at the end of the semester is very generous and truly shows how personable he is to his students!
My favorite teacher by far. He really loves what he teaches and he wants every student to do well. Great person and even better teacher. Not a hard teacher but definitely a hard class.
Great professor, wants you to do well. Difficult class though.

She's one of the kindest and understanding people at tech that I've met.

Dr. Driscoll is an excellent and engaging lecturer. She presents the class concepts in a very clear way, and is very responsive to student needs. Would absolutely recommend! 

If you are a CMDA student taking this class, don't stick to R. Take the time to learn JMP, it makes the class way easier.

I took this class Fall 2020 (during COVID). It was already online before COVID, so she had it down pat. She is amazing! Her lecturing is clear and easy to follow. The homework isn't hard. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

Homework easy too.

Very kind professor. Grade based on weekly quizzes, and quizzes based on the lectures. For the highest grade I recommend meeting with him or TA if you're confused. Go to TA office hours for the quiz, I found the class is easiest when doing that. Easy A if you take advantage of teacher and Ta help. 7% extra credit and 2 quizzes dropped.

This class was not the easiest I have taken. Each week we have a quiz that is very hard to understand with his wording, I had to meet with the TA for guidance. His lectures can be interesting some days and others not so much. He does give 7 percentage points added on to your final grade that really benefit you in the long run for simple tasks.

His lectures were very boring, and the class was based on 12 weekly quizzes, which were quite difficult. You only get one attempt on the quiz and have an hour to complete it. I would not recommend taking his class if you struggle with biology.

Very boring lectures so I stopped coming to class. I would only go for the exam reviews. He gives lots of extra credit for easy things. The extra credit bumped my final grade up 7 points. He only responds to emails that he wants to respond to which is annoying. He seems like a funny guy & he is very sarcastic in a funny way.

All lectures and recorded and posted. Grading consists of 5 online take-home open note quizzes (1 is dropped) and 4 hws. Quizzes are HARD but the class itself is very conceptual in general. Dr. Draghi cares about his students, accessible outside of class and passionate about what he's teaching. My advice is do the extra credit, (grade went up 7%).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A lot of my classmates didn't enjoy this class, but I absolutely loved it. It's not much memorization, and mostly conceptual understanding. I can tell he's a nice guy, but he sucks at teaching. He goes off on tangents with no main points. His style sucks. His tests are so hard and he's ignorant to our strggle

I would consider Dr. Draghi a very good professor because he really makes you think about the concepts instead of just solely memorizing. The class was not easy, but I felt like I learned a lot after taking this class.

He seems like a nice enough guy, but really he doesn't care when the majority of the class is confused and he made the exams more difficult than they should have been. reviews.comment: Probably the easiest and most interesting class at VT. Highly recommended.

reviews.comment: Super easy class, only two open note quizzes per week plus the occasional lab. Just set a reminder for yourself so that you don't forget to do the quizzes and you'll be fine. =)
Online course and a very easy GPA boost (plus the material is actually interesting).

This class was great! The textbook was a fun and easy read. The final "essay" and test are short and also easy. There's an extra credit opportunity at the end, but it's basically impossible to not get a 100 in this class from the assignments. A great option for a Pathways 6 that isn't creative writing, drawing, or design.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The course is run on an online textbook that opens up 2 chapters every week. The quizzes are incredibly easy and the course is basically an easy A so long as you don't forget to do the quizzes. Automobile Safety is ran the same way as Concussion Perspectives. Definitely take this course.
Legendary.

easiest class of all time (got a B bc I forgot to do the chapters), would always recommend it for a pathways course. the entire course consists of 26 chapters, 35 questions final exam,  and a final essay (a couple of paragraphs). 2 chapters due a week, each chapter is a small read with a 5-question quiz about the chapter at the end.
amazing and passionate professor! definitely recommend taking his class!!
This is the easiest class I have ever taken in my life.

Concussion Perspectives was interesting and not difficult at all. Every week there's two online quizzes to take based off of the chapters, and there is extra credit provided towards the end of the semester.

Concussion perspectives was an incredibly easy and interesting course. It is completely asynchronous and you only have to read 2 relatively short chapters and complete 2 quizzes each week which was very easy and quick. So long as you consistently do the work the course is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This class is really easy and honestly really interesting. There is a lot of different things you can learn from it and he gives feedback on the labs to help you with your writing.

I absolute loved this class- it's a very easy pathway and the content was super interesting! Duma is great at going into detailed explanations on the topics, and as long as you pay attention to the end-of-chapter quizzes every week, the final cumulative quiz is pretty easy. Highly recommend!
If I had to describe his classes as a sauce, I'd say they're awesome sauce.
Amazing. If you need an easy pathway, just take this one. It's interesting too.

I really liked this class, it was very easy and I didn't need to go to the class to do any of the assignments. There are two online open note quizzes each week and the final is open note too. Dr. Duma was really kind, had engaging lectures, and was helpful.

ugh i loved this class. just two quizzes a week (some mini assignments here and there) and the lectures have all the answers. the content was really interesting and the website used was very engaging and easy to navigate. it just sucks u have to pay so much for the program. i'm taking the new helmet designs course next sem too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class is super cool and has an awesome online textbook. Apparently he is also making a new class with a similar textbook that counts for a 3 and 7 pathway.

Took the class in person this past spring and it was super nice. Quizzes were straightforward since Dr. Duma marks what exactly is tested from each class. Tons of extra credit too and interesting lectures. Had a friend who took the class asynchronously in the fall and he also really liked it. Similar experience with quizzes and extra credit.

Take this class if you need an easy A or to fulfill a pathway!!! Can't recommend this class enough. Course is organized well so you know what will be tested and don't need to waste your time studying random stuff. Course material is also interesting if you like the content. Take the class!!

I had Dr. Duma for concussion perspectives and absolutely loved it! I was talking to him after class and he told me about a new class he's creating for spring 2024. It's called helmet design (BMES 3004) and counts for pathways 3&7 and an engineering technical elective. I saw the textbook, and it looks fun and very similar to BMES 2004!
This class was absolutely flippin fantastic. This man carries the virginia tech curriculum on his back. I highly recommend.

This has been one of my favorite classes I've taken at VT. The material is really interesting, and Dr. Duma has cool stories incorporated into each lecture. Definitely take this class before you graduate!
My favorite class at Virginia Tech! He covers a great deal of material, but you know what to study and the exams are not hard. Also, there are many options for extra credit.
Professor Duma has an abundance of knowledge and his class shows it. This class really is a hidden gem at Virginia Tech.
Best Pathways 1 and 4 class, I recommend students take this fun and interesting class. Lots of funny jokes worked into each lecture.
The best Pathways class I have ever taken. You will LOVE the class, great teacher, and the concussion material is fascinating.
Excellent professor, great class, learned so much about concussions and science. I recommend this class to everyone. So much of the research actually took place at Virginia Tech.
Amazing professor and class. Everyone should take this class. Extra credit really helps.

Easiest class you will take at Virginia Tech. Attendance is not mandatory but the subject matter is interesting which makes class enjoyable! Everything on the exams is clearly marked and there is so much extra credit, it's hard not to get an A in this class. Highly recommend for a pathway!

Really good class and has interesting topics. Dr. Duma is a great guy and loves what he teaches. Take this class, and if you do the extra credit and pay attention class you will get an A. What a great class!!
Literally anything you'll be tested on is clearly indicated on presentation slides. Incredibly easy A, I have shown up 4 times and got an A with ease.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this asynchronously in Fall 2022. He does this in-person in Spring, and online in Fall from what I remember. Everything about this class is amazing for someone who loves to work ahead! Exams are ACTUALLY based on what he provides in the slides (you'll see an indicator as to what slides he will likely test you on).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super understanding professor, and information is very clearly marked when needed to know for exams. Tons of opportunities for extra credit.
This was a very easy class. I currently have a 106 because there's a lot of extra credit. He puts checkmarks next to the information you need to know. The material is also interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was asynchronous, but everything was clearly communicated. Powerpoints outline what is important for exams. Lots of extra credit. Professor was nice and understanding.

One of my favorite courses! He makes the material very interesting and easy to understand. The workload was very light and he lets you do it at your own pace. Offers multiple extra credit assignments and highlights the information on the power points that might be on the exam.

Professor Duma's class was so enjoyable for me. His lectures were intriguing, and he provides clear expectations of what is to be known for the exams. The subject matter was also very interesting, and he presents it in an excellent way. The online class (fall semesters) is at your own pace, so it is really nice to be able to do it on my own time.
Great professor- made it easy for you to get a good grade and the lectures are clear and include interesting material!
This is an absolutely amazing professor. I had him for Concussion Perspectives and it really was an easy A. He is very generous with extra credit and will sometimes give out candy :)
Pretty good

His office hours are incredibly helpful and he is always willing to help out students, whether about class material or future plans with ECE! Can definitely be challenging, but making a study group is always helpful. Great professor and I wish he offered higher level classes as well.
Ridiculously hard class that needs to be more reliant on lectures.

Dunning is super funny, relatable, and nice person. Cares a lot about his work and the students. 1004 was definitely a challenging class, but very reasonable. Lots of practice problems/exams posted.  Dunning was a big reason I enjoyed my first semester in ECE and decided to stick with it.
Mr. Dunning is one of the best teachers out there. He's always willing to help if you go to office hours, is very accessible, and his homework prepares you well for the tests.

Absolutely, take advantage of office hours. He wants to see you succeed and will help with any problems you may have, but it helps if he knows your face. Also, take advantage of TA hours; plenty of people go and work together to help each other understand complex topics. Office hours can easily turn a 2-hour homework struggle into a 1-hour ordeal.
Goated prof. Hilarious and a great teacher. Content may be difficult for first time learners but can be managed if you try a bit. Gives out extra credit opportunities like candy too.

One of the gems of the electrical engineering department here at Tech. Absolutely take Dunning's section if you can, he is a great lecturer and he is readily available outside of class. Take advantage of his office hours and above all, go to class.

Very good teacher, one of my favorites so far. Attendance is not mandatory but he encourages it through lecture quizzes (they aren't hard). The HW are challenging and difficult but the best source of prep. Go to class, do the HW, and search gary tuttle for practice problems and you'll do fine. Book reinforces lectures. Find a group for the labs.

Professor Dunning was amazing, he was very kind to students and did his best to help everyone. As long as you study, tests are fair and the review sessions are very helpful. Just don't wait last minute to do the labs and homework's.
Very good professor, but lectures are jam packed and fast paced. Lots of long homeworks and labs. TAs are good for office hours and are moderate graders.

Dr. Dunning made my first semester at VT very enjoyable. He is a very entertaining lecturer and he clearly cares about his students. I would've definitely had a higher score if I listened to his advice about how to study for the exams. I wasn't sure about ECE at VT at first, but taking this class with Dr. Dunning has encouraged me to keep going.

Dr. Dunning is one of the best ECE teachers I have every had. While the class is quite hard, if you show up and listen to his lectures, you will be okay. 
The biggest thing is showing up and going to class. Yes he posts the slides on canvas, but there is so much he says in class that is not on the slides.
Amazing prof. Do everything in your power to get a spot in his section.
Take him for intro, he's easily the best professor for it
Great professor, loved his class taught everything well, and gave great feedback.

Posts notes/Example problems. Has TA hours every week day from 10AM-7pm. Gives practice exams, goes over what will be expected on the test. Posts Keys. Has extra credit opportunities. Responds to emails fast, very flexible with when you take tests. Has dropped whole assignments just because. Extremely likeable, engaging lectures. Scott is awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dunning is very knowledgeable about what he teaches and provided excellent feedback. The lectures aren't amazing at explaining the topic, prepare to do some self teaching but once you understand the topic, Dunning will help you understand everything even better.

He's patient and always willing to answer questions; he also shows problems and narrates each step in the beginner class. His tests are similar to Prof. Ball's so the curriculum is well-structured throughout the department. He also does similar problems to what would be on tests and less from the more advanced homework, so that's much appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing prof i wish i could have him for every class.

Dr. Dunning was a really great professor to have for ECE1004. He explained things well, was always easy to understand, and clearly cares about his students. I highly recommend taking any course with him.

Dr Dunning is a pretty good professor. He explains the concepts very well and very clearly. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities through hikes and as well as dressing up for Halloween. Overall a good professor and grades quite nicely as well.

Prof. Dunning is approachable and always willing to help with homework, labs, or exams. His lectures are engaging and essential—missing them can set you back. He creates a fun learning environment, even offering extra credit for dressing up on Halloween. The TA's aren't that helpful though apart from one or two, so always go to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dunning is great. He clearly cares about the subject and his students and he does a great job conveying the information. If you miss class a lot you can get the information from the book and doing the practice problems. Graded by a lot of things but weekly homework is weighted pretty heavily. 4 exams, cumulative final, and post-lecture quizzes.
He is a pretty easy grader for the test and his class was generally acceptable. However, he does assign homework that takes hours to complete. Go to office hours!!!

Professor Dunning is a great teacher. Even though there is a textbook for the class, I never had to open it as long as I paid attention in class, and there was no information on the tests that came from outside of anything he talked about in class. He is funny, charismatic, and you can tell he loves his job.

Scott gives it to you straight, you put in the work you'll do well. He prepares you well and gives the resources you need to succeed in 1004, just put the time in. Clearly knows what he's talking about the knows how to teach.

Is really knowledgeable about each of the topics and is always clear when lecturing and working through practice problems in class. Homework can sometimes be a challenge however the tests are not bad if you study. He will post past tests so those will be your best friend in passing.
Very funny as he does not take his job that seriously. Very fun class with frequent real life examples. Teaching slides are shared with students. Amazing teacher.

Dr. Dunning is, hands down, the best professor in the ECE dept. He has a VERY strong understanding of the content and, even better, knows how to teach it to his students in a non-confusing way. He is flexible with office hours and will happily help you with content you don't understand. He is hilarious and has such a bright personality. 10/10

As someone who already knew basic programming, this class was a cakewalk with Dr. Dunning. This class teaches the very very basics of programming, though it may be challenging if you have never programmed before. Dr. Dunning is a really cool guy, and I would take him again for any class.
Great teacher, generous grader.
Dr. Dunning is a very kind and respectable individual. He makes the class engaging and introduces an exciting aspect in his lectures. He is very helpful and all his students seem to love him.
He's a good guy. With all of the awful Professors at Virginia Tech, It is refreshing to have one that cares about his students and genuinely enjoys to teach. Can't go wrong with this guy
He's a great person but sometimes is not the best at teaching to the knowledge that students have on the content.

ECE 1004 is a decently challenging course, and Dr. Dunning made it very accessible. He's a great person that gives helpful analogies and feedback, and wants his students to succeed. It's difficult teaching a large foundational class like this, and I feel like he did a very good job. Ball is also a great choice but Dunning is slightly better.

Had him for S23. Great professor, accessible outside of class. Lectures were interesting and I felt I used just about everything I was taught. There are extra credit hikes they count toward lecture quizes. Attendance is graded for a small percentage of your grade and random attendance quizes are taken four or five times throughout the semester.

I loved Professor Dunning! Even though the class is difficult, he honestly makes up for it. Favorite professor I've had. He genuinely cares for his students and is easy to make a connection. He hosts tons of socials and helpful office hours. Just prepare to study.

If you're picking your classes, definitely choose him- even if it *is* an 8am class.
he has good jokes and lectures were easy and made sense. office hours are super helpful and his office is cool.

The class is really tough and covers a lot of content, if you fall behind it will really hurt you. Dr. Dunning is really helpful though, grading wise he's pretty forgiving, and he's very willing to help if you mess up or are lost.

Dunning is the goat of professors. He is a great guy, actually cares about you, and teaches well. He takes his classes (and the ECE department) on hikes for extra credit and gives out snacks etc. Take him for whatever you can. He makes the class easy and simple, is funny, and great to talk to. Best professor I've ever had.
This guy is awesome. Made C++ less intimidating, felt like learning how to fish with your chill grandpa. Get him for any class you can!
Amazing teacher but hard content. A great choice for anyone that has the option to take a class with him!

He is a great professor that really cares about his students. He organized hikes for us outside of class and was always accessible during office hours. The class is tough and be prepared to fail the first exam (my class average was a 45). If you read the textbook and ask questions you can definitely end the class with a strong grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Dunning was the best professor I had this semester. He is patient with questions asked during class and cares that students understand the materials. His lectures are engaging and humorous. Does an excellent job telling us why we're learning concepts and where we'll see them in the future. The tests are difficult, but the same across sections.

Take him if you can. Pay whatever amount of money to have someone switch sections. Great teacher that cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. Provides plenty of resources, both in and out of class.
His lectures and homeworks were valuable.

Had him for thermo in fall 25'. he was an amazing professor. he cares a lot about students' learning. his exams are not too difficult. if you do the homeworks to the best of your ability, show up to lectures, and go to office hours if needed, you will go far in this class. his lectures are easy to understand and shows pics of his dog each day

Very engaging lectures and gave great feedback on all assignments and tests. He's great at breaking down difficult topics and showing us how they work in the real world. Great Fluid Dynamic professor!
This is for ME3414 Fluid Dynamics. DUBIK IS THE GOAT!!!! IN DUBIK WE TRUST!!!! MAY THE FORCE BE WITH DUBIK!!!!

I heard there was a lot of competition for Professor Dubik's current job in the ME department, and they absolutely picked the right guy! Great professor who truly cares about his students and wants them them to succeed

Dr. Dubik clearly cares about his students and is passionate about the subject. When going to his office hours, he was very helpful. His homework is a little challenging, nothing extreme. Dr. Dubik's exams are also fair game and are similar to his homework and practice exam.

Fav proffesor at tech, got me through fluids and thermodynamics. He makes the classes super interesting and breaks down the concept. Taught an entire topic in office hours, super super helpful. Grades fairly.

I've been here for four years and Justin Dubik is the best professor I have ever had BY FAR. He's right out of his PHD so he gets students. He was a fair grader, gave good lectures, and brought in materials to show real life concepts. He also extended a deadline for me when I had to miss class when my brother was hospitalized. GIVE HIM A RAISE!!!!!

Justin is such a great professor. He writes out the notes and explains all the concepts very well. He responds to questions very well and loves to give help. His quizzes and tests are very reasonable and much easier than the homework. He also only uses metric units on his problems which is SO nice. 10/10 would recommend for thermodynamics.
Great teacher and great guy. Thoroughly go through slideshows and homework assignments and you'll be fine.

What can I say, this guy is great at teaching thermo. Made me enthusiastic to learn it again considering I already took it at community college. Great at explaining concepts, outlines his notes neatly, gives quizzes to help students retain information for tests, and is pretty understanding.

Dr. Dubik is a wonderful! Super caring and really strives to make sure students feel welcome in the class and doesn't make you feel stupid for asking question lol. He's incredibly personable and down to earth, really good vibes all around !! He's able to break down concepts really well and made this class one of the ones I understand the most.
Really good at explaining difficult topics. Also incredibly responsive to students' comments/questions.
Something is wrong about this person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The guy wants you to solve things while you are stressed out. The person was literally looking at me for so long while taking the exam and I couldn't focus. Barely cared about students during COVID when some were infected.

He was honestly one of my favorite professors as he knows the material really well, but because of that he is not afraid to call you out if you make a mistake or wrong assumption in class. I started going to his office hours and that helped me a lot because he is really good at explaining the material in office hours.
A really cool guy that tries to make the lectures engaging. Sometimes, though, he will glaze over something important. Be prepared to grind. Thermo is hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice professor, easy class

Class was extremely easy--probably spent 15 total hours on the class and got an A. Incredibly forgiving with grades, late assignments, etc. Lectures and class readings are incredibly boring, but very easy to fudge so can't complain. Don't take Prof Dunlap if you want to learn something, do take if you want to knock out some easy credits.

You can tell he cares about his students - he puts a lot of effort into making assignments simple for everyone. Class is mostly centered around a case study you present with a partner which takes a bit of time, but besides that it's just discussion posts and in-class participation.
Very chill, engaging, and entertaining professor. Very willing to go out of his way to help students outside of office hours. Coursework is fine as long as you can write and attend class.

The course consisted of reading quizzes, pack-back essays, discussions, and a case study presentation. His lectures were entertaining, and the case study presentations from each group made the course interesting.

Mr. Dunlap was seriously awesome! one of the best professors I've had. He's super chill, engaging in lectures, and knows his stuff. Plus, his personality is top-notch and his character is just awesome. If you ever run into any trouble or just need some help, reaching out to him is a breeze, and he's always there with warm vibes ready to assist.

Very fun professor that is clearly passionate about his class. Loves discussing ethical and legal situations. Had him for the Zoom class so there wasn't too much student participation, but it was still one of my most enjoyable classes because you could see how much he loved teaching this class :-)

Dr. Dunlap is fun, he's very enthusiastic about the case studies which is amusing. The coursework is super easy, so the class is really chill. Attendance is mandatory, but 95% of the classes are just students presenting their case studies (you only have to do 1). You can just treat it as a study hall and do other work.

I took his class over winter, there was a discussion every class, 12 pack pack discussions, 5 essays (750 word - 1000 words), 10 reading quizzes (most of the answers are on quizlet), 1 case study (proposal + presentation + report). Basically the class is very easy, he is an easy grader and chill prof. As long you did everything you are good.

Weekly quizzes and simulation, as well as a major project that we do through out the semester. Online textbook that is mandatory for weekly assignments, ~100 dollars. Great professor, clearly knows her stuff. I enjoyed this class and would definitely take it again.
Professor Duncan was a great professor for social media analytics. She made the semester-long project relevant to this career field and had reasonable deadlines. Would take again.

Prof. Duncan is a great professor who is funny and cares about her students. Her class is engaging and has assignments that actually apply to future jobs. There are graded reflections throughout the semester instead of attendance, simulations, and weekly open note quizzes. There are no exams, just projects. Overall, she is awesome!

professor duncan was nice, engaging, & made an effort to learn our names too. the class was interative & adhered to what college students would like. she drops a lot of assignments which i really appreciated. the class moves fast and there's a lot of stuff to do. had to pay a lot for the textbook/program and there's a huge semester long project.

Dr. Duncan is good at what she teaches. There are assignments at the end every week, you have to do them. Attendance isn't mandatory but it is easy to fall behind. She drops multiple assignments, one quiz, and one exam. She is also super accessible outside of class. There are 3 group projects due but she gives lots of time to work on them.

I can see why other students would like him, but personally, he wasn't my favorite. If you like any kind of structure in your assignments, do not take his classes. Usually prompts are very vague and it's up to you to figure out the rest. He is a very tough critic, and if he think your project is bad, he WILL tell you in front of the class.

Absolutely loved Les. Was in art 1604. Super amazing at teaching and learned so much about so many different things. He cares about students and wants us to succeed. Has soft deadlines so honestly you can turn stuff in whenever, but it is obviously better to get stuff in as soon as possible. Lenient until you disrespect him. Definitely recommend!

ART1604-4D, not a very rigid professor, so a little unorganized, but I lowkey mess with that. Every deadline is a soft deadline, so if you procrastinate easy maybe not the best choice. I learned A LOT from this course and going to class was actually something I looked forward too bc of that.

Les is hilarious and extremely fun; he clearly cares a lot about his students and wants the best for everyone. Highly recommend having him in-person. He uses Discord to communicate with the students really quickly and his assignments can get a little confusing criteria-wise but he really pushes you to think outside the box.
He's nice and easy to talk to, the weekly lab quizzes are tough though. The labs itself are easy.

Dr. McDaniel is an incredibly nice guy. Curriculum wise - it is a lot of information for a 1 credit lab. Weekly quizzes were free response and harder than the practical exams, and were worth a good amount. Make sure to definitely read the lab manual before lab for the quizzes

Dr. McDaniel is a really nice guy, though you won't interact with him often in this lab which is pretty normal. This semester was especially hard for reasons that were somewhat not in his control. Each lab, there's a really difficult short quiz on a huge amount of info. As long as you study hard from the jump, you'll get a better grade than me

McDaniel is a nice guy but the new curriculum is tough. There are 5 question quizzes each week and two noncumulative exams. Participation is 10% of the grade (crazy for a lab). He is willing to help in class if he shows up/stays around long enough. You don't get quizzes/feedback back. Overall it was a tough class and a mediocre but nice prof.

One of the worst professors at tech. I went to office hours- he did not show up, and I waited for 35 minutes. I emailed him over 2 months ago twice- still no response. Weekly quizzes, weekly lab reports, a midterm, and a final (all in person) with no drops. Seems like a nice guy, but he is a terrible professor.

Great professor. Very empathetic towards students and has grading policies that both help your grade and help you understand the content. Gave clear, thorough lectures and was available for office hours. Easily the best math professor at VT.
Mr. Park was amazing, his lectures were so easy to understand and made me feel like I was finally getting calculus after struggling in high school.

Mr. Park is great. He lets us resubmit our homework for full points. Him and his wife are the nicest people ever. They made us chex mix and cookies for doing well on tests. He's an amazing teacher and takes tons of questions. If you find a mistake on the test, he will go through it and possibly regrade it. I wish he could teach all math classes.

Genuinely the best math teacher I have ever had
-Presented information clearly
-Legible, color-coded, organized notes
-Lenient as possible with grading
-Gave specific feedback
-Resubmissions
-Last minute extra credit
-Made class enjoyable
-Lays out and reviews all learned test material class before test
-Honestly wanted to help however possible
Professor Park is the best math teacher that I have ever taken. He is a brand new professor but teaches the course like he's been doing it for years. Build your schedule around his class

Mr. Park is a super fun and caring teacher, he doesn't hesitate to help students on whatever they need, is super lenient when it comes to making points back up on HW, is approachable and teaches actively. 10/10 would recommend!

The class was pretty easy, just watch the lecture vids before the quizzes and you should be fine. Did not buy the textbook, I just used the free version from the syllabus. Class only took 2-4 hours a week for me, so not bad. I would take this class again, content was interesting.

Very easy class. Tests are with lockdown browser (without a camera/mic) even tho the class is entirely online, which makes no sense. There are 2 video discussion assignments which are easy. There are “rapid responses” which can be 5 to 2 mins long with ten questions which is annoying and stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class itself was easy, the online quizzes were tricky but the book had every answer. You will get used to looking up words quickly in the back of the book. She is horrible when it comes to grading the pronunciation tests; one wrong stress on a syllable gets the whole word incorrect even though people pronounce terms differently in the field.

I'm not sure why everyone is hating on him. Maybe instead of hating they should do their work instead of being lazy. This is not a class you can coast in. However if you do the work, show up to class, and study, he is very helpful and will do his best to help you succeed.
His class is very boring, but is very knowlegable. Just study the power-points and go to office hours an you'll be fine.

The material in this class was difficult but Easterwood is a good professor. Attendance isn't mandatory but going to class will make the exams a lot easier. The practice problems provided were really similar to the questions on the exam. Lectures were boring but if you go and take notes you'll be successful. He is also very helpful in office hours.

This is the second time I have taken this class and Dr. Easterwood was a much better professor. He's a tough teacher but will make you learn the material. This class will be difficult regardless of who you take it with, but his class will be your best chance of getting a decent grade
He is such a harsh professor for a very challenging class. A lethal combination. Easterwood is not the best at explaining stuff and grade pretty tough as well. Avoid, avoid, avoid!
He makes this class impossible. Avoid if possible.

I really enjoyed Easterwood this semester. Lectures are boring, but if you just take notes and listen to what he says, the exams are quite easy. The practice problems and projects he provides are almost identical to what he puts on the tests, and he is extremely transparent about what's on them. Funny guy, don't let his dry humor offend you!

Overall this was better than I expected coming in. Classes are basically PowerPoint lectures which can be tricky, but he's good in office hours about clearing things up. He makes it clear what will be asked on tests which is very helpful. Make sure sure to start group projects early. I would definitely recommend him,
take literally any other professor for this class. Hardest class i've ever taken by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty tough class, supposedly one of the hardest finance classes at tech. Its basically doing basic financial problems like TVM, amortization, and bond and stock valuation. He makes you work for a good grade but hes a good professor, definitely knows his stuff. Go to office hours if you need help and show that you are working hard to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Easterwood is the type of professor that just reads off of power-points and expects you to learn the info. Boring dude and boring class. The tests are VERY hard. The grading is about 85-95% tests. I would avoid taking this class with Easterwood. I don't like leaving bad reviews, but I have never felt so unsatisfied and disappointed in a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: the hardest teacher!

Don't let Easterwood scare you on the first day of class, He's a pretty cool guy and he's fun to play with and make jokes with in class.  You'll find he has a the funny type of dry humor.  He tests are straight forward, but you'll find his instructions for the homeworks suck! So just go to his office hours or the TAs.  Overall positive experience

One of if not the best professors I've ever had at VT. I took this class as a senior after having taken no history since HS. He gave great lectures and made them very class-driven by having us ask questions about what we wanted to discuss. I learned a ton. Workload isn't too crazy either. Would 100% recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Cherry was by far the BEST history professor that I have had at Virginia Tech. I took his class online and it was very easy to manage. A weekly quiz based on the readings that was open note/open book. Easy class, easy readings, great professor 10/10!
Prof. Cherry is awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cherry is a great teacher. His History of Virginia course is taught by having the students read an assigned chapter from the text book and then ask him questions at class time, afterwards he goes in depth on the readings and draws upon his personal experiences and family stories to further enrich the chapters we just read.

Mr. Cherry is a decent prof. He teaches at a public school 1.5 Hours away and maybe showed up on time once, all other times expect a 10-15 minute wait. He also ran class late A LOT. This class was easy for a history major but if you're not a history major it might be hard, 50 pages a week and 600 word response, with a 3000 research paper at the end
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was a pretty lowkey class. We read out of the textbook A LOT. Expect about 50 pages of reading each week. Each week we also had to submit 600 word reading responses, and we had a 2,500 word research project due at the end of the semester. Cherry is extremely caring, helpful, and respectful to students. He doesn't always end his class on time.

I loved Prof Easterwood ! She sets you up for success as long as you put in the work. I actually failed this class once before and ended up with an A this semester. As long as you don't miss class and do the my finance lab questions after each class you'll be fine. She also gives you a cheat sheet on the exams which is a huge help.
yes her class was difficult and lectures arent the most helpful but she offers a lot of extra credit and does genuinly care about your success in the class. Just show up and youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doesn't have a long teaching experience. The grading is balanced on three exams. If you take her don't waste your money on purchasing the my lab she didn't really use it and it has so many questions that she doesn't even go over in the lecture nor the test. personality a little obnoxious I hate the smirk when she says this or that will be tough

She was very nice and cares for her students, but her grading scale is solely based on tests and her lectures are incredibly boring. No attempt to make it the least bit interesting. You would be well off not coming to class and just looking at the slides, but the only other grades beside tests is attendance so you are forced to sit through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took MUS 1104, overall is pretty easy since all of the answers are on quizlet anyways. There are some written assignments that are a complete waste of time, like the class. The e-Text website is so slow and uselessly expensive. This professor will never answer your emails, and does not give any sort of feedback. He doesn't even teach at all.

Wally is a pretty nice guy. He is the horn professor but also teaches music theory, which is what I've had the past two semesters. Many lectures are reading out of the book, but he tends to explain it well and if anyone has questions, he is happy to answer. You can tell he wants his students to succeed (especially his horn students haha)

Wally is a really chill dude. He is also french horn professor, but I had him for music theory. For the higher theory course track (20##s), a knowledge of how to read sheet music is necessary and prior theory experience really helps. While he assigns HW every week (typically 7-10 worksheets), they are really easy and can even be done in class.

While he was somewhat accessible outside of class, his advice was far from stellar. His feedback was vague and often left you with more questions than answers. The second exam was unusually difficult and was not reflective of the practice exam or homework; it felt as if it was done on purpose in response to the good performance on the first exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Valeyev is tough to judge. He makes p-chem hard, but it's no matter who teaches it. Often, the only tips he had for us was "study more". Honestly, he's right. We probably DID need to study more to fully understand. But if you're taking it with anything else mildly difficult (CHEM and ChemE's always are) you just don't have time.

I think he could be great for 3616. He is obsessed with trying to get us to take statistical mechanics and teaches far more on that subject than p chem. Since this is a prerequisite for stat mech I'm not sure why, except that this seems to be his favorite subject and so regardless of topic matter he will teach that.

Valeyev is a horrible professor. PChem is incredibly challenging and he doesn't explain anything. There are 3 tests (not including the final) but 1 is dropped which means you have 2 tests that will make/break your grade. The tests are ridiculously hard. There is a HW assignment every week and he grades VERY harshly. He has almost no office hours.

Dr. Valeev is excellent. He really does genuinely care about his students & is more than willing to help you. His courses are tough, but that is only because of the subject matter. The only people who do poorly are the ones that don't take full advantage of his help. I wish all of my professors cared half as much about their students as he does.
No Comments
No Comments
Left with gf

Professor Gabor, or Edward (ed-a-ward), epitomized the quintessential erudite. His unparalleled dedication to his students was matched only by his profound commitment to the advancement of their intellectual pursuits. Indeed, his legacy endures in the countless minds he has shaped with his unwavering devotion and pedagogical finesse.

One of the best professors out there. Has extreme knowledge in his area of expertise. Very relatable to the students in his class and puts the time in to help them succeed. Gives great real-world examples of probable social scenarios that the material would be applicable in. Encourages class interaction in order to enhance the lecture atmosphere.
Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ed Weathers is my favorite professor so far at Virginia Tech. Too bad he retired! If you can get him teaching again part-time, I highly recommend it.

I LOVED this class.  It was by far my favorite class to attend this semester.  Mr. Weathers is so entertaining and he really knows what he's talking about.  The assignments aren't hard and very useful.  If you get a chance to talk this class, DO IT!  You won't regret it.

Was by far my favorite teacher this year.  There is a lot of writing which sucked but the quizzes were easy and the class lectures were interesting.  If you can get into his class I encourage you to do so
A lot of writing, but you learn a lot.  Does require time on your part.  An excellent teacher who grades fairly.  Makes classes interesting.

It's literally impossible to get an "A" in this class.  A "B" is hard to come by, and IF he likes your style of writing, you may be in luck.  If you get this guy, DROP IT NOW.  You won't regret it when you hear your friends complain about his class.

Ed Weathers is challenging in that he assigns a lot of work, but he is very fair at the same time. He has a lot of experience from the professional world, so you'll learn many practical skills from him. Best teacher I've had at VT so far.
Content was really interesting to learn about! The readings were dense, and the class felt more like a 3000-level course in terms of depth and rigor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Go to the lectures, take notes ,you will be fine

Though he was helpful and reliable throughout the semester, he wasn't for the final. He was very nit-picky and concerned about sources that came directly from the textbook, and seemed to be grading on a completely different scale compared to the other assignments. Not sympathetic or willing to negotiate after giving the entire class bad grades.

Intro class was awesome and pretty straightforward. I will say read the syllabus before deciding to take this class or not. Very finicky about citations and if you're not a history major this might be troubling. grading for the final tanked me so I'm confused why this was advertised as an intro class, but to each their own!

not the 2005 level class but a 1000-level history class (no option).. final had an average of 70% .. for a 1000level class that is ridiculous and displays an inability to teach or provide clear guidance. If you're looking for a fairly relaxed intro class to a historical subject, this professor is not it. bro grades like it's a 4000 level class

Dr. Polanco is an excellent professor who genuinely cares about his students' success. Growth is key in his class—one mistake won't hurt much, but lack of improvement can. He offers great feedback and actively supports students with the lengthy class paper.

Difficult class for sure but he works so hard to make it manageable for his students. He's easily accessible and is a great resource for the paper you work on throughout the class. I guarantee if I had any other professor for this class I would have done terribly. Seriously can't overstate how helpful he is with the material. He's also funny af
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Large paper required for the class, with the paper being THE main focus. However, great professor who cares about students. He understands the difficulty of the class and is willing to help by any means. Also funny jokes.

The greatest professor I have had yet. He gives fantastic feedback on papers and really pushes you to succeed. It is a heavy reading class with mostly discussions instead of lectures. His final paper is long but he gives several checkpoints throughout the year to keep you on track.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Polanco has been the best professor I had. The class was very hard, lots of reading and advancing your skills. However, he wants everyone to succeed and is very patient so if you're willing to learn a lot and work for it, you will not regret taking this class. He made me a better historian.

I'm currently in Dr. Weisband's Nations and Nationalities class, it's one of the most interesting classes I've ever taken. He's incredibly passionate and kind and I know I will miss this class when it's over. The subject itself is slightly challenging but if you take the time to think it through it's fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I actually really enjoyed Dr. Weisband despite him basically making up his own language. His lectures are dramatic and strangely engaging in a way that preps you for grad school. It's easy to learn his terms and how they connect while also gaining insight into a subject in a way you never have before.

He's a great professor, really passionate about what he teaches.The slides can be a bit hard to follow during class, so I recommend taking pictures or notes as he goes. For exams, focus on learning the definitions and key concepts from those slides. The class might feel a little tough at first, but the professor is actually very kind.

He walked up to each student and got in their personal space (without permission) by pointing at them, touching them, and putting his face super close to theirs on the first day of class. Very, very odd, but he's old, so I'm sure he means well. I just started the course, but just beware that even if you don't make eye contact, he will find you.

Professor Weisband desperately wants to convey his passion about the material to his students. However, no one can ever understand what he is talking about or the information he is trying to impart during his lectures. He uses very complicated language to explain simple concepts. No homework, keyword analyses and final exam are graded heavily.

This class was not extremely difficult, however, I ended with a lower grade than I would have liked. The pop quizzes are difficult, and it can be difficult to study because there are no clear definitions of words. The lectures are so boring, I would bring homework every day. The prof is kind though, and the TAs are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
He is a wonderful lecturer and intellectual. His concepts are super interesting, just really hard to follow at times since his terminology is a bit dated. Make sure to ask him questions for clarification.

He does not take questions during his lectures though, which is a letdown. However, he is really influential and has a lot of prior experience.

Dr Weisband is a weed out class for people serious about Political Science and international Relations.  A real old school lecturer, and someone who truly brings passion back to a beige academic experience of canvas slides and  quizlet cheating. The skills learned here are crucial for higher education. Prepare to actually learn and be challenged.

This call was absolutely unbearable due to Professor Weisband's rants. This class is not lectures it is him yelling about the most random things for about an hour and 15 minutes, he turns a very easy concept that the average person could understand in about 2 sentences into the most confusing thing you have ever heard.

This class wasn't too bad as long as you showed up, took notes, and did readings. Try to do as well as possible on the scheduled quizzes and the pop quizzes, as they were mostly easy and would fluff up your grade. His lectures took a while to get used to but were mostly interesting, if a little repetitive. Essays were standard analytical papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not to be rude, but I could not stand this man. He sure was passionate for what he taught, but he didn't lecture, he preached. It was almost comical, he made it miserable. He spoke in a manner as if he was attempting to overcomplicate everything rather than make it clearer. Didn't like him at all, but hey, maybe you'll love him.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weisband rambles the entire time and insults students. Sometimes it comes across joking, other times it comes across as being rude. Very opinionated. Bangs his fist a lot and yells. He just says random stuff and uses big words to appear like he's saying something. Honestly he comes across as being a legitimately senile old man that needs to retire.

Weisband does not require attendance but has pop quizzes, and he does not post his slideshows on canvas either so if you miss a class prepare to go to his TAs office hours. You have to buy HIS book and nothing he says in his lectures has anything to do with what is on the slideshow so you have no idea what to write for notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: what is bro waffling about

Professor Weisband is difficulty a character. His powerpoints are all over the place and his lecture style can be disorganized at times. I strongly recommend taking notes about his presentations and also what he says. Also, make sure to stay on top of the readings as there are pop quizzes and quotes from the book are expected in essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. He teaches in literal riddles, you can take all the notes you want but they do not help. He has a quiz every week, but the majority of your grade is three essays. He offers no feedback whatsoever, it feels like he pulls grades out of a hat. The TA does not know much more, but he is the only one who can operate a computer!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is plain bad at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weisband has an insane amount of passion and energy towards this subject. Lecturing style is fun thought the concepts are tricky to understand. He really does want you to understand the material and participating in the class will help a lot. Course is weighted heavily on 3 essays but if you can write a good analytical paper you will be fine.

He cares about his student even if he's yelling half the time about the most random things.  The lectures are set up so weirdly and I would rewrite them to make them more comprehendible in my notes. There were random pop quizzes that drop your grade exponentially because the only things graded are 3 written papers and pop quizzes for attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is knowledgeable in the subjects taught in class, but he is bad at teaching it. The lectures aren't shared but expected to be known and blown through during class so just take pics. He rants every class for at least 20 min and then everything is rushed to the point that you feel lost. Don't take if you can't attend every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weisband goated. TA's weird asl. This class is considered hard to understand because he tries to get you to understand concepts that are complicated. MAKE SURE YOU TAKE NOTES AND PREPAIRED FOR THE QUIZES EVERY WENESDAY. You have a pretty much guaranteed A if you do well on these. Quote the book for the essays too.
He does not keep track of attendance, but his classes are very heavily based on lectures. His grading is skewed based on the midterm and final . He has weekly quizzes that you need a code for.

This class was absolutely terrible. He used words that made no sense and just yelled about the middle east the whole time. We never used the textbook and he makes everyone get it because he wrote it. There are only 3 papers and they are graded very weird by the TAs. I would avoid this class at all costs because of how awful and boring it is
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super passionate about the subject + very interesting lecture topics, but the class structure itself is weirdly difficult and the TAs are harsh graders. I didn't buy the textbook at all, but if I did it again I would cause they want you to quote the book in your essays. 3 essays make up the entire class grade.

loved this class - a lot of reading but its all straightforward - graded on three papers - take notes bc he won't share slides - really cares about students - def one of the smartest people you'll ever meet - lectures r engaging & he's super passionate - makes up his own words sometimes which can be annoying - a bit repetitive
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Weisband is thorough and clearly knowledgeable. His lectures are great, but often repetitive, slow, and hard to understand. He also only graded my class based off of three papers, one of which was worth 50% of my grade. If you can understand it, you learn a lot in this class, but you also have to work hard on the few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wesiband is clearly very intelligent But his online course wasn't well prepared, the audio was rough, the professor also doesn't provide feedback on test grading, resulting to a generalized commentary for all class, it's really tough understanding what you are doing wrong and right, doesn't share class recording, which only makes studying difficult

Weisband seems well liked by past students, and he seems like a nice guy. But so far this year, my intelligence has gown down. His lectures are repetitive, futile, and confusing. He makes up words and he overcomplicates every sentence. He doesn't know how to make a powerpoint AT ALL. It's frustrating. I think I'd teach the class better.

He's extremely passionate and caring, however his class is a complete waste of time. His class (due to COVID-19) only had 3 grades, and the final grade is 60% of the entire course. All grades were essay based, so grading is based on opinion of the grader. The content is interesting but he presents it in rambling lectures. 10/10 would not take again

He is a very passionate and smart man, and truly wants his students to succeed. His lectures can be boring but he also like to joke around in the middle of them. There are only 4 essays for the entire course and he grades them hard but if you use your resources and get help, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best education professionals I've had the pleasure of taking a class with. He truly cares for the well being of his students and is passionate about the curriculum, making the class extremely interesting. I would highly recommend him to any student interested in PoliSci or International Studies.

Weisband is insane but a good professor. He'll lecture at you the entire class and usually go off on tangents about unrelated things. Sometimes he'll redo entire lectures because he doesn't remember if he's done them yet.

Had Dr. Weisband first semester freshman year. His lectures are not just about reciting information to students, they are very conceptual and you have to be able to think for yourself to do well. The essays were challenging but we had pop quizzes that helped your grade if you went to class. The material was incredibly interesting and relevant.

In the first classes of having Professor Weisband, he wasn't my favorite. After being with him in class for over two months now, he's probably one of the best professors I have had. This man is so UNBELIEVABLY smart. You will learn so much important information in this class. It's hard to get used to his teaching style, but once you do he's amazing
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Weisband is passionate and his lectures are not dull. His main goal is to get his students to comprehend large-scale concepts. As long as you take good notes in this class and from the readings and participate in recitation, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Weisband has really, really good intentions. He often times gets wrapped up in passion and it's easy to get confused and lost in his lectures.I think he makes up his own vocabulary words sometimes, which can be annoying. However, he wrote the text book for the class. If you focus on the readings, and ask your TA questions, you'll be fine.

He is very passionate about this class. He only uses essays and not exams which was helpful for me.  There was a lot of reading and a weekly journal, as long as you stay on top of the work, it is an easy class.

Weisband is very passionate about his class and subject. You'll understand if you hear his lectures. He will definitely keep you awake if you sit near the front. Attendance is not required, but needed if you want an A. Also, go to recitations and make sure you walk away with a very clear understanding. Class reads a lot of books, so start early.

He is by far the best professor I've had at Tech. His lectures are extremely interesting and force you to question almost everything you understand about the role of the self in the cultural development of the modern world. To get a good grade in his class, make sure to attend the recitations and know your TA well, because they grade your papers.

So much passion and knowledge in his lectures! However, he tends to go on tangents and the relationships between the points he makes aren't always clear. Concepts are extremely abstract. To do well, make sure to attend the mandatory recitations, as the TAs frame everything in a pretty comprehensible way. I enjoyed attending lectures.
His lectures are not the most clear in the world but he defiantly has a passion for teaching. Plus, his enthusiasm will defiantly wake you up in class!

Dr. Weisband is absolutely crazy, but I LOVED it!  He has so much passion for the world and people.  The class was sort of difficult because everything is abstract or theoretical, but it was very interesting.  The lectures are hard to understand, but recitation usually clears everything up.  The TA's and Weisband are very helpful!

I really appreciate the guy?s passion and his overall care for students. I remember I hadn?t said a word to him all year and he came up to me randomly after class one day and introduced himself. I would say his lectures went over my head; he?s way too smart for anyone to understand him. I would take him for the experience but he?s not a ?must take?

N&N: best class I have taken so far at Tech. Weisband made class interesting from day one, and I have yet wanted to skip a class. He is a genius- the lectures are sometimes hard to follow because they"re so abstract, but you can always go to his office during his hours for help...recitation helps to clear up anything. Changed my outlook on the worl

I usually do not rate my professors, but Dr. Weisband is SO AWESOME I HAD to rate him. lol, seriously he is one of two favorite professors I've had at Tech so far, I'm a junior. Please take his class, you won't regret it...He is funny, entertaining, explains things very well, is very well organized...no tests, just 2 papers.

Dr. Weisband is perhaps the craziest teacher I have ever had in my life. He's really a genius, but I like to compare learning economics from him to learning physics from Einstein. I often rely on my TA to translate what he has lectured about each week. But that being said, he does "love his hokies".
Great teacher! Very energetic! Really makes you want to learn what he is talking about.

Weisband is a genius, that's all you need to know.  Yes, he does go on tangents but they are interesting and helpful especially if IS/PSCI is your field.  He really cares about his students and is more than happy to explain anything to you during office hours (his office is a must see - lots of interesting things from all over the world!).

he rambles a lot and goes off on tangents  every day but it's interesting if you're awake enough to follow his logic...no exams just 3 major papers which are graded by your TA so just hope you get lucky

This class was really hard to understand at the lectures. The only way I survived was through the recitation, although my TA graded the papers way harder than any of the others so that was still difficult. Don't take this class unless you have to.

A little hard to understand at times..goes off on random rants and by the time he got to the point he was trying to make he had already lost my attention. You read a lot in this class but there's no finals, just three major essays.. it's not too bad, the recitations really helped.

This class, however complicated, confusing, and complex it seems throughout its experience is a MUST for anyone who appreciates psci or IS. Weisband, scary enough, knows what he's talking about! An exciting lecture, combined with a man who truely cares about his subject and his student makes for an unforgettable class. Its painful, but its worth it

this guy loves his job and his students, but if you dont like abstract classes it's not for you. at the beginning of the semester i paniced about the class since im a bio major but now towards the close of the semester i find it to be my most interesting class. as long as you read, do you journals, and show up for class you should do ok,

This class turned out very different from what i thought it would be.It was much more focused on sociology than politics, but Weisband had a way of relating everything that made the class quite interesting.Yes, it's true about his made-up words and such, but with the help of a GTA who uses their own language instead of his,the material is profound

Wow...this guy was something else....yes some of the lectures were kinda interesting, yes he was...original...yes he knew the topic very well...but he has this knack for using the biggest words in the dictionary, and making up terms....the readings were horribly boring and i coudln't understand half of them...honestly...i wouldn't recommend

Nations and Nationalities and Global Political Economy were the two most useful political science courses I took.  Weisband is very into the material and wants the student to be too.  The GTAs were very helpful, its a reading/writing heaving class, but if you pay attention its interesting.

His teaching style is very spontaneous and engaging...some of what he says may be confusing at first, but it all makes sense in the end. His energy in the room and eagerness for his work makes him a very enjoyable professor.

Dr. K is very nice and tries, but he was not a good professor. No one in the class really understood the content, and he responded negatively to ubiquitous constructive criticism. His assignments, especially the group projects were dull and vague. Your grade largely depends on the efforts of the others in your group. He bends into a "z" often
I took jazz history with Dr. Knoeckel for a pathway, and it was an insanely easy A. I stopped showing up to the class a month in and still ended with a 100, just make sure you do the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for music theory.  He's a great professor and makes the classes fun.  The biggest tip to being good at music theory is to practice, go to class, and ask questions.  If you are struggling with a topic, you can always ask him questions via email or during his office hours, and he'll put in the effort to help.  Overall, highly recommend him!

Lots of people say music1104 is easy class but this will be my 1st B at VT bc I underestimated this class. The quizzes r hard. You have to actually listen to the music for them, which makes it impossible to look up and therefore NOT easy. Final asked to answer things from the text BUT THERES SO MANY QUIZZES TO LOOK THROUGH AND THE WEBSITE SUCKS
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, made russian very easy and fun, couldn't recommend more
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super fun class would take again great teacher

Dr. Bob is a very easy teacher as long as you show up to class (what could you possibly learn about Russian language if you didn't show up to class?). He is very willing to assist anyone who has any questions or any problems. He makes things as easy as they can be and takes the time to do so.
dude is awesome. i didnt have to take russian second semester, but i did just because i liked his class. i could have been playing guitar hero, but i went to class

When questioning whether or not to continue russian, efird made it easy....he's a wonderful professor who works with his students and makes the class interesting. you'll always walk out of class with a new corny joke.
Efird is the best!! Odd-ish sense of humor, but fun to talk to.  Never, EVER, say you don't like Dostoyevsky :)
Efird is just awesome. Very kind man! Always willing to help. Wrote a terrific letter of recommendation!!! If you ever think about taking a russian class, he is definately the way to go!!!!!
Good teacher who gives you a great deal of help, is hilarious, and makes learning Russian interesting.  He also makes a good person to talk to about episodes of "The Simpsons."

Lindsay's class was my favorite english class yet, and i don't like english! We wrote a lot in class and she knows a lot about composition and research. take her if u want to work hard but learn a bunch.
love her! Ms. E was my favorite teacher this semester. A lot of work but she grades fair. Also she is helpful outside of class and really cares about class

Ms. E was actually my favorite teacher this semester. It was nice to have a writing class instead of my science and engineering ones. She is WAY smart and is clear about what she wants from students. People who didn't like her prob didn't work hard. She does expect a lot but she's really helpful too
Her class has no structure. It feels like she comes up with the class lesson like the day before.

I did the bare minimum and did fine in the class. DON'T BUY THE TEXTBOOK I NEVER OPENED IT OR NEEDED IT. Assignments and quizzes alternate every week, so every other week there is a quiz on two modules worth of material. All quizzes and the final exam are lockdown browser but with no webcam. Professor seems nice enough and easy to reach.
