Assignments are boring and he tries to cram way too much information into one semester course at a 1000 level

Professor Eick was a really good and caring professor. He gave good feedback on all of our written assignments and we had all the material we needed for our tests. Overall if you have to take ENSC 1015 take it with Professor Eick.

Dr. Eick is a super kind and respectful professor. But for an introductory class, his quizzes are downright impossible and extremely specific. You will not pass this class if you don't get a little outside help if you know what I mean. You will maybe get 1 or 2 questions from the actual lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course was taught flipped classroom, so coming to class didn't matter unless you had some questions on the problem set, which he would help you answer. However, his explanations were always confusing and it felt like he looked down on students if they didn't understand something. Reading the textbook helped on exams and problem sets.

Grade is based on weekly quizzes. Lectures don't matter for your grade. Quiz is based on textbook but has too many overly specific questions, so don't expect to pass unless you use quizlet. Teacher seems nice and is available during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: born to research, forced to teach
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is hybrid, but in class lectures were usually cut short, so we didn't go over much of the chapter in class. To me, this wasn't very helpful with understanding the chapter. Reading the chapter is your best bet for doing well on the quizzes, but I feel as though the quizzes have quite a few overly specific questions from the textbook.
He's really nice and very lenient on grading. Very easy to talk to and makes class interesting.

Professor Eick is passionate about the environment and is respected within his department. The class is an online hybrid where you show up once a week for a lecture and discussion. This was a difficult course but an A is very doable if you put in the time and effort. You will learn a lot of interesting things!

I took both 1015 and 1016 with Professor Eick and I would take them again if I could. He is understanding and caring. Reading the textbook goes along with the in class discussions so if you read, you'll be fine. Makes lectures interesting and captivating.
Everything he covers in class can be studied from the book. Frequently shows videos in class and does his best to make it as interesting as possible.

It's obvious that Dr. Eick really cares about the material he is teaching. Extremely fair grader, awesome personality.EXTREMELY KNOWLEDGEABLE of a large range of material. One of the best professors I have ever had.

He is a great professor! You can tell that he is passionate about what he does and truly cares about the subject and his students. Environmental science was pretty easy; multiple choice tests, one of which is dropped.
He talks incredibly fast, but is more than willing to explain as many times as needed until you understand.
Eick is my hero.

OK, I'm a hetero male, and even *I* think Eick is sexy!  A triathelete, his brain is as intimidating as his stature.  The man could be a geologist, biologist, chemist or engineer as easily as he could be a soil scientist.  He is nothing short of a god.
He's one of the best professors I've ever had.
matt - i love you so much. can i have your baby?

Joe is a chill dude. Clearly passionate about what he teaches. Classes can be boring but he makes it interesting (you'll have to discover it yourself lol). Overall, I would def take a class with Joe again

Dr. Eifert provided an interesting class and was super respectful to all his students. Found the class to be a very easy A with few assignments and minimal prep for exams. Very lenient grader as well. Appreciated his kindness. Learned somewhat less than most other courses, but was definitely introduced to some new avenues of thought!

Very easy A so I'd recommend the class, but be prepared to fall asleep during lecture. He is clearly passionate about the subject but he rambles on about irrelevant information. This class could clearly be taught significantly more concisely, a lot of the lectures feel like a waste of time.
Attendence was checked but we only had to go to about 75% for full credit. Tests were online, open book. Really liked the final project.
Do the study guide, even though you don't receive credit for it the tests follow the guide verbatim. And you can use the guides on the test.

Not the easiest class I took but not the hardest either.  Tests online, open book, open notes.  Must be able to apply concepts.  We did poorly on one test and she gave us a retake that could add 28 pts to our grade.  Very Nice Prof! Gives credit for trying.  I would recommend her.
No Comments

Show up to class—he doesn't post the notes! He is super boring and sounds very uninterested in the topic he's presenting. The only time he is passionate is when he's doing a promo for his books that are completely unrelated to class (he mentioned his sleep book so so so many times. Please get the hint that we do not care!).

Interesting class with the only grades being two exams and reading notes (2 full pages). Show up consistently because lectures are long and he doesn't put them on Canvas. He's very understanding and cares for you as a student. The workload isn't bad at all, you're assigned a book & notes like every two weeks or so and then you just have the exams.

Ekirch is an extremely kind professor who strives to make his classroom engaging and welcoming. He doesn't post his lectures anywhere so it's crucial you pay attention the entire class and take notes as 40% of your exams is the vocab portion. Do the reading notes, STUDY for exams, and try not to miss class and you should be good!

Prof. Ekirch is one of the nicest guys you'll ever meet. He actually cares about his students, and wants us all to succeed. His lectures tended to drone on when he got off topic, but he is extremely dedicated to his work. In HIST2004 you'll have to write a 15-20 page paper on a topic of your choosing, he doesn't require much else.

The American Revolution with Professor Ekirch is the most enjoyable college class I've had by far. Ekirch is so nice and there's not a ton of work so it's not stressful. He may venture off-topic with stories but theyre always funny. Obviously, if you don't like history this won't be a good class for you, but if you do, I can't recommend it more.

Took for Methods.  Do the readings, turn in notes, study for his 2 vocab tests, and get started on your paper early.  The paper required for Methods is 15-20 pages, so don't put it off.  He's helpful with your paper if you bring questions to him.  Cannot place enough emphasis on not procrastinating with your paper.

I took his American Revolution class, and I have to say I actually looked forward going to his 8am lectures. He really captures the story of the American Revolution. Class attendance is defiantly mandatory, and I highly recommend reading the assigned books. Overall, probably one of the best classes I have taken at VT.

He is a great teacher. Most of his classes are in lecture format and he goes over a small number of major points then expounds upon them. They're very interesting. often comes into class late and talks about sports unitl set up. Readings are often the enitre books but the notes are one page front and back. Enjoyed both 3004 and 3014

Hist 2004 is a writing intensive class required for History majors. Prof Ekirch is a really nice guy, but the subject wasn't terribly interesting. The class wasn't very difficult, but it was really boring.

going to class is mandatory.  there is no textbook but only books you have to read and take at least a page of notes on.  the tests are terms and then essay.  the teacher is a nice guy but the lectures aren't always interesting.  there is a lot of video watching.  take the class if you like colonial american history.
As long as you pay attention and take notes you'll do swell.
Great class, would definitely recommend for anyone in PolySci or humanities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is so into teaching the class. She really ejoys teaching world politics and she is so knowledgable about it. She formats the class to be like a discussion, it doesn't feel like she's lecturing, it feels like she's just helping you to understand the subject. I learned so much, and was given so much to think about. Definitely take her class!

I absolutely loved Professor Gosink's class. You can tell that Professor Gosink genuinely cares about her students. I loved how she incorporates political theory into her lessons, I think it gave me a nuanced perspective on world politics. She doesn't really lecture, we had discussions which was just so much better.

Overall, an awesome professor. You can really tell that she's knowledgeable about anything thrown at her, despite it not being the main topic of discussion within the class. Classes are very interesting and discussion-based, which I found to be engaging and prevented the class from getting boring. She assigns three books, all easy reads.

Overall a 10/10 Teacher, someone who actually loves & cares for her students while being passionate teaching her class. A fun and easy class that will have you learning something new, even if you fell asleep in her class. Even if you wanted to talk to her after class about anything, she will stay and talk to you, not as a teacher, but as a friend.

Dr. Emori is a caring and kind professor who genuinely wants his students to succeed and do well. He is always accessible outside of class through his office hours and via scheduling appointments. He was very understanding with asking for extensions and for extra support throughout the class.

I cannot recommend Dr. Emori enough! I am a physics major (now a physics and nano dual major) and his class was honestly my favorite. Straightforward homework that doesn't take much time to complete. Weekly quizzes, but he tells you what will be on them so they're no big deal. Fun in class demonstrations/experiments and easy to understand content.

Dr. Emori is such a caring and kind professor. His lectures are thorough, but make sure you have a method of taking notes that isn't electronic for his class as he does not allow electronics. He genuinely cares about his students and is very easy to talk to about extensions and sickness.

I've had him for nano 1015 and now the new nano 2984 class. I would say I'd 100% take any class he offers or teaches. Does have weekly quizzes and attendance, but if you show up and pay attention (which is easy because he's a great prof.) then you'll do fine! Cares about his students and was always very cooperative with sickness and traveling.
Dr. Emori is one of the best. Take any of his courses if you ever get the chance. He has a way of making even small things interesting.
Cool

Great guy, he's kinda awkard but good teacher. Homework is really easy and tests are almost a copy of previous homework. Tells you what will be on the test and how much each topic is worth. Allows a full sheet of paper for cheat sheet on tests. Can tell he's passionate about his work and the topic.

A nice guy who cares about his students and is willing to help you out. NANO 1015 was a breeze - DO THE EXTRA CREDIT IT'S WORTH SO MUCH. Overall, not a super special professor but definitely solid and I wouldn't mind taking his class again.

Dr. Emori is overall just a great person and professor. The lectures are very clear, the homework is very easy, and the quizzes were very straightforward. Just attend class and you'll have a fun time learning about nanoscience.

This has been my favorite professor so far; he is so enthusiastic about the criteria, and he just makes it all interesting. I am most definitely looking forward to possibly having him for PHYS 2306. I would absolutely recommend taking a class with him because he just makes the class better.

Great for nano. Had quiz drops and no tests. Homework was a little hard, but the quizzes were exactly like the homework so once you got the homework down, you're good to go. Had extra credits on each quiz and they were based on things said in the lectures not written down so listen extra carefully to the lectures if you want extra credit.

He gave all the information needed in his power point and he made it clear what was going to be on quizzes and what wasn't. He gave 5 quizzes no tests or final and allowed a 1 page cheat sheet on quizzes. Lectures where always infesting especially when he was talking about something he was passionate about.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Emori is a relatively new professor and that is probably why he doesn't have many reviews but he is by far one of the best professors I have had so far. He made physics really easy to understand for me and he is really helpful if you ever need help with any topic. I would definitely recommend taking him as a professor for PHYS 2306!

she was repeatedly rude to me over the course of the semester. i attended office hours, i scheduled meetings with her in her personal office, and whenever i would ask questions because i didn't understand she took personal offense in that i seemed to be insulting her somehow? her lectures were often not useful, most learning was done via textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gentry was AMAZING!!! She is clearly so passionate about what she teaches and she is great at taking difficult orgo concepts and breaking them down in ways students can understand. She assigns lots of homework but it's all extremely helpful. Wish I could have her for another class.

A fantastic teacher who cares about students. I wish Orgo wasn't soooooo difficult because I would have enjoyed the class more. I wish she taught organic two because her lectures were so clear and concise.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gentry was an amazing professor. Her course is extremely organized, with every assignment being posted in Canvas at the start of the semester. She was very caring about her students and even provided an extra credit opportunity after harder tests. She also responds to emails within minutes.

Dr. Gentry is amazing. Orgo is insanely difficult; however, she attempts to make it as easy as possible for us. I struggled so much in the class, but she provided very lovely, clean, detailed notes. This subject did not click for me: was not because of her. I wish I understood this subject because I loved her as a teacher. Wish she taught Orgo 2.

Dr. Gentry is a fantastic professor. I am enrolled in her class; however, she makes me seem heard and respected. Orgo has been VERY difficult and makes me want to cry; however, Dr Gentry has provided me with resources to do well and not give up. There is a lot of homework; however, it preps you. Practice exams are similar to the actual test.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just show up to the lectures and try hard because organic chemistry can be very difficult at the start. It will become easier once you get the hang of it. She also has frequent office hours and recitations if you need help. She will miss your emails.

Dr. Gentry is truly the best! She provides great practice exams for each exam that are really similar to the actual tests. She also curved each exam so that the average was around a 73 which was really helpful. She draws clearly on the board, color codes what she is doing, and explains things really clearly. If you can, TAKE ORGO WITH HER!!

She is a great teacher who is very knowledge in her subject. She is a very graceful grader and she presents the material where you can walk out of the course with great knowledge of organic chemistry. Had a great time
Such an amazing professor! Practice tests exactly like the tests and gave extra credit/curved tests. Held helpful review sessions and her lectures made the content very clear.

She was very unresponsive to emails while reaching out. When I could get into contact with her, she was great and very useful. When I could not, I struggled because the directions she provided were difficult to follow.

Dr. Waldman is sweet and passionate about her specialty, comics. She's flexible and adjusted the class as it went to find the best way to teach the topic. She isn't great at communicating outside of class and posted many of the assignments very late or not at all. Even so, she's a solid professor and comics is a cool topic for Contemporary Fiction.

Waldman is fine and things are very straightforward on her Canvas page. She does not respond to many emails, but I generally figure out the answers myself. Her reading quizzes are very specific, but the comic discussions make up for them. Generally I found that writing a lot and very specific gives full points. Lots of comics to read!
Very unorganized. Regularly late to class. There were multiple quizzes that most of the class failed because the questions weren't clear. Unclear about assignment deadlines and criteria.

One of the best professors I've had at VT! She is very skilled at guiding group discussions, and cares a lot about each of her students. I was worried about analyzing poetry, but she never made anyone feel like their interpretation was wrong or incorrect. It's clear that she's educated and passionate about her course material!

Front-loaded homework and seems intimidating at first, but really is easy if you keep up and put some effort in. Wikle is very sweet and gives you lots of useful stories about her life, and this class teaches you to sit down and listen. Very generous on extra credit and very down to earth.

Professor Wikle is a decent person but not a good professor. For a 1 credit class there is a lot to do and her lectures were very off topic at times. She mainly had her TA's do most of her grading and work and her assignments had very confusing directions. Also the final is 100 questions, 70 of them are from a Kahoot and the rest are random. Avoid

I finished the class with a 90.00, helped by extra credit. She's not the best though. The lectures often felt unfocused, and I had to learn much of the material on my own. The final exam was rushed, with 100 questions in 50 minutes. This course may work for independent learners but honestly would recommend a different professor

Wikle starts off w/ scare tactics to weed out those that lack effort. Lectures are personal stories that relate to the material. All tests/assignments are super easy but you must read the book. Course is heavily front loaded, but by the midpoint it's all about showing up to class. Tons of extra credit. If you fail then it's 1000% your fault.

For a 1-credit class, this was way too hard and way too much work. Most days were just slides plus side stories, and we only did one Kahoot. The final was 100 Qs in 40 min, rushed and js memorization, with no study guidance. She was often late and came off arrogant, with little passion for teaching. There are better ways to help students learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wikle does a great job of introducing you to different career paths within finance. She is a laid-back teacher, but TA's are strict graders. Attendance is mandatory, final is about 100 questions as well. Lots of work at the beginning, but it lightens up. NO PHONES IN CLASS!!! you will be marked off. Class is P/F next semester.

I heavily disliked this teacher and her "teaching" style. Each time she was "lecturing", there was nothing learned except for side tangents. The work was excessive, with assignments not even being inputted until the day after they were due. Finally, there was a final that was 100 questions, all for a one-credit class, and was only 40 minutes long.

Professor Wikle has a very odd style of teaching. About 90% of the tested material is learned exclusively through the textbook and never mentioned by her unless you explicitly ask. The lectures seem like a waste of time, but do not skip class if you can avoid it because she only explains extra credit assignments in person. Overall I would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, but does not really teach. She goes on about random life events and tries to tie it to the course. There is a required textbook, with 17 chapters. There is the textbook assignments, 4 exams plus cumulative final, stages interview, and development packet. This class is an easy A but you must put work into it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Wikle is easily one of my favorite professors. Her lectures and the stories she adds to them are amazing and she genuinely wants every student to succeed. You have to go to a certain number of events to pass class, but they actually help you network and build skills, both interpersonal and technical. The work is simple. It's hard to fail.

Easy class, don't sweat it. I can't tell if it's her or the class, but an hour a week of her rambling is not the end of the world, just a bit annoying that it's required. Also, you are required to go to a bunch of events, so take this class before you join any other clubs. Also, they are a total waste of time disguised as "networking" so have fun!

For a 1 credit careers class, she takes it way too seriously. Many assignments are harshly graded and you need 40 event points to pass the class. Although she does care about her students and helps finance students succeed and connect with alumni- you need to be really into finance to enjoy the class with how much work it is

If you are taking any business careers class they usually come with a mandatory event attendance system, but they aren't all created equal. She created new opportunities to go to events until the second week before classes ended. ACIS 1104 only had events available until the 3rd week of classes. Assignments are clear, lots of events, good attitude.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wikle is a gem. The value of the class is in her lectures where she gives relevant, practical experiences. Taking this class helped me grow as a person: Mrs. Wikle is in incredibly inspirational and knowledgeable person. Class: Online textbook module must be purchased, 1 comprehensive project, and you'll have to do a presentation.

Professor Wikle is great! She may come off as blunt or rude, but she is here to help you. The actual material in the course is really easy. She does make you do a bunch of events for points towards your grade, but they will help you! Only thing is that attendance is mandatory, and you need to come to class to get a good score on the final exam.

Show up to class and read the textbook and you are set. Her lectures are very story based but if you go and listen you will do really well. No phones allowed but you will honestly be entertained by her if you pay attention.

Best professor I've ever had at VT. She doesn't teach during lectures fr but attendance is mandatory. Show up, listen, and just engaged and you'll pass. The work is extremely easy especially if you've taken a personal finance course before. She really cares about her students and is accessible outside of class. Extra credit is great and easy!

Professor Wikle is by far the most outstanding professor I have ever encountered. She is truly passionate about the material she is teaching and cares more about her students than anything else. As someone who contemplated dropping her class initially, staying was my best decision. Although challenging at points, I suggest this class to everyone.

I love Wikle. She is an amazing teacher and great person who cares about her students. She always wants the best for her kids and gives a lot of important life lessons. Does not teach content in class but attendance is mandatory. Lots of extra credit but multiple chapters of reading due every week. Not a hard class if u do the work and show up

Mrs. Wikle truly cares about her students and their success in life. When a family issue impacted my ability to keep up with classwork, she didn't just mark me down for missed assignments. Instead, she helped me during her office hours. Her dedication to students extends beyond the classroom. Every Finance major should take her class if they can.

She is an exceptional educator who genuinely cares about her students. She goes above and beyond to accommodate those with disabilities, ensuring everyone has the support they need. Her approachability outside of class fosters an open environment where students feel comfortable seeking help. Her dedication to their success is truly inspiring!
Very rude and disrespectful to students with disabilities. Loves to give a "that's not how it works in the real world" speech to people with learning disabilities.
Easy class, helps you get into networking and extremely helpful.

Ms. Wikle is an amazing professor. Her lectures are genuinely hard to not pay attention to because of her witty sense of humor and funny personal stories that make you want to listen. Some people say her tests are hard, but if you study/pay attention during class there are no surprises. She is also very helpful and easy to reach via email.

Ms. Wikle's class is unorthodox, but I loved every second of it. If you go to class, do the homework, and put in an effort, she will do the same for you. Make friends and build a community in the class -- that makes it infinitely more fun.
Tests are REALLY hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As a Freshman, I had no idea what to expect when signing up for this class.  However, I am positive I will never find another professor like Mrs. Wikle.  She tells the best stories that connect to class, and there was never a dull moment.  I actually looked forward to attending her lectures.  Great teacher, and great class to take.  I recommend it.

Amazing professor! I love listening to the stories she shares to tie them back into the content we learned. Tests can feel difficult, but she provides formula sheets that are so helpful for someone who is forgettable like me. She's very strict about the Honor Code, so don't even try. Textbook is a lot, but going to class helps digest information.

One of the best classes and teachers I've ever had at Tech. Very wise professor who shares her amazing life experiences and teaches. You will learn valuable life skills and tricks and enjoy going to class. Will miss this class.

I adore this woman. I was lucky enough to be in her investments/fin. literacy class. While I knew some basic concepts she taught (time value of money, etc.) she really stressed some things that I know will be beneficial in the future. She doesn't know it but she's a 2nd mom to me; I've taken so many steps to better myself knowing she'd be proud.

Ms.Wikle is a character. Her teaching style is telling stories about her life. I have learned more in her class than all my other classes combined. She is passionate, funny, and a piece of work. Go to class and be ready to listen. It'll make sense later even if it seems bizarre at the time. Take advantage of all opportunities in her class.

She cares about her students inside and outside the classroom more than any other professor I've had. The class is really easy and you only need to spend an hour a week on the assignments. She expects you to participate and wants the class to be conversational with questions. If you don't engage she plays boring lecture videos.

She keeps it real. She doesn't sugarcoat things. Genuinely cares about her students. Study for her tests though. If you need help with something, she will help you. Her classes are pretty awesome. There not normal I'll tell you that and she brings in food sometimes. Awesome class and professor.

Wikle is an intelligent, well spoken, and determined individual who teaches a captive audience how to free themselves from a system that is largely rigged against their financial success. Insightful and informative, a wondrous person. Take this class, it could save you from terrible decisions.

I switched into this pathway from a stats class and it was the best decision ever. She is the most genuine professor Ive had. She brings an energy to the room that makes you want to listen and she has very helpful real world advice. Definitely makes finance fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ms. Wikle is my favorite professor at VT and she showed throughout the semester that she really cares about her students. Her lectures are always relevant to real-world situations and I felt that I got something out of each class I went to. As long as you keep up with the readings, this class is a no-brainer.

I absolutely loved Ms. Wikle. She teaches in a way that really catches the students' attention and in a way that makes you want to learn. She's super caring about her students and knows what she's talking about. She does have a lot of homework and projects, but they're not hard as long as you stay on top of it. Highly recommend.

Ms Wikle is a teacher unlike any other I've had. Her lectures were enjoyable to go to, she cared enough about her students to where she would often hold late night calls with them, including me, and she genuinely cares about our education of personal finance. Her class requires dedication but the info is actually useful. Would take this class again

Ms. Wikle was one of my favorite professors I've had at VT! She is a great teacher, very helpful and relatable and spends most classes telling (sometimes) relevant financial stories about her own life. HW and tests are easy as long as you read. One of the few classes I always enjoyed going to
Prof. Wikle is my absolute favorite professor I've had at VT. She is funny and makes going to class enjoyable. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is included in part of the participation grade.

Professor Wikle is one of my favorites. I only had her for a one credit class but she made it enjoyable, fun, and interactive. We occasionally met on zoom and she would always ask us about our weekend, etc. Her lectures were organized into powerpoints which I personally like and the final was all multiple choice.

Tests and the majority of hw are straight out of the textbook. Class was pretty easy if you can read the text and spit it back out. This woman seems super intimidating and harsh at first but youll come to see that shes actually a big softy who'd do anything to help a student out. Gave great finance and life advice.

One of the biggest gripes I have with Emilia is how much this class feels like Highschool english. While she has several generous extension policies she doesn't accept latework at all, she requires full attendance and doesn't let you leave until class time is officially done, and she's overall just kind of uppity. Not the worst but annoying.

Class was cancelled a few times throughout the semester, but overall, Emilia was a solid instructor for ENGL 1106, made the grading criteria clear, and was accessible for help outside of class if you needed it. Also make sure to use the built in extensions she gives you in the syllabus, because she does not accept late work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She might be the worst instructor you may ever take in college. Not only does she not allow late work, but you must also show up to every single class. She was late a total of 9 times throughout the semester.  She canceled class 8 times throughout the semester. She expects so much when she is lazy, does not try, and truly seems not to care at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Mrs. Satterwhite for Appalachian Studies and had a pretty good time taking her class. She is very passionate about what she teaches which makes Appalachia more interesting to learn about. You spend a lot of time doing group activities which helped stimulate my attention during class.
I felt that I could not freely express my opinion on some topics without fear of grade retaliation for not agreeing with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Satterwhite's class. The class was essentially composed of completing 3 essays evaluating topics read outside of class and discussed in-class. Satterwhite promoted interesting discussions and debates on popular culture topics. Great class if you have space in your schedule!

The class is bored very boring and if the subject doesn't really interest you then it seems pointless. There are readings assigned every night but it is not necessary to read them because you review every class. However, it is an easy B and if you are a good writer, then it is an easy A.
Very good Professor. She is knowledgeable, helpful, and friendly. Dr. Satterwhite sincerely likes for students to do well in her class and produce meaningful thoughts and ideas.
Great Class Discussions, Very Enjoyable

Great professor who taught an extremely interesting class. Definitely my favorite. Homework assignments weren't too hard but definitely time-consuming. Midterms were open note and final was in-person all exams can be taken with a cheat sheet with formulas and diagrams. Also pre-exam in-class quizzes focused on conceptual and some quick math.
Brilliant guy, great lectures.  Homework was a bit lengthy, but multiple attempts were nice.  Midterms were open-book which was nice.  Final wasn't open-book, but was curved

Lectures are heavy but are posted as recoding online as well.  Homework isn't too bad, but some might take you a while to do.  Multiple attempts on HW with highest score kept makes it less stressful which is nice.  Professor is chill, 10/10 recommend
Absolutely awesome guy, offered extra credit when we did terrible on the tests

APSC 4464: Seems like she cares but is a bit rude and doesnt accommodate well. Purposely removes parts of her lectures, only shows them in class even tho attendance isn't mandatory. Let us know with only 2 days notice that labs would be off campus?? Uses up entire class time for no reason (this class is taught by multiple profs and none did this).

Dr. Feuerbacher failed to answer any of my emails the entire semester, even when they were urgent. She also did not do much during class and did not provide a lot of feedback. Very nice but not very helpful

Had her for shelter dog training with Dr. Gunter and they were both amazing! Feuerbacher is a literal absolute angle. She is always willing to help you with training techniques and will always give great feedback. The class itself is pretty simple and there will always be extra credit assignments available. She is phenomenal at teaching.

Her slides are super basic so you MUST go to class to actually know what's going on. Notes can be 45+ mins of non-stop writing and half the material won't even be on the exams. Takes forever to grade, post material, etc. I thought it'd be an easy-A class, but effort is actually needed. Explains material well in-person but class is boring.

Reinforces content with readings, case studies, and graphs. Office hours extremely helpful for preparing for the final. Buying textbook not necessary but helps for quizzes who's questions often show up on exams. Attendance optional but MOST content is in the lectures. best professor I've had at Virginia Tech :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures have lots of information, however 80% of the test questions are taken from the homework quizzes. Many students (including myself) found major issues with her attitude. She is incredibly disrespectful and rude toward students and makes students scared to ask questions. Easy A class if you prepare for the tests but don't expect her help.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very kind professor, tests were very fair and based on either the homework or notes in class. make sure to have a friend in case you miss class for the notes. final was basically pulled from the homework practice quizzes. overall an interesting class and if you put in a bit of effort you should get an easy A

good enough teacher, classes were lecture/note heavy, but the class was not difficult. if you want the notes, she doesn't post them, so you need to go to class. enough assignments to have good grade if not a strong test taker.  on the other hand, she was a very passive aggressive person, she would come to class with attitude towards students.

Dr Hotchkiss really cares about her students. class/homework counts for a good amount of the grade, its refreshing not to have exams count for almost all of it. study notes and key terms and you will do well on the exams! she is very busy aside from teaching but willing to make appointments and holds student hours.

Only accessible course content is left handed-written notes that are sloppy and hard to follow in class. Professor is knowledgeable of ecology; however, does not present information in a meaningful or organized manner. Attendance mandatory if you want the notes.

The most boring class ever. I skipped it a lot and I was a bit graded on not showing up. I recommend a junior to take his class to have a friend with me. The person dropped the class the after few days.

Professor Kiran is one of the more challenging professors I have had. The tests are worth 80%, and the homework is worth 20%. The tests can be difficult, and partial credit is rarely given. He told me my test grades were "below average," which is unprofessional and rude. He did boost my grade at the end because I showed up to office hours a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A little slow-paced, but clear lectures and very doable tests. Can be a tough grader but fairly open to giving points back if you can show your reasoning. Can always improve your grade if you do better in later tests, even if you bombed a test.

10-question tests that are formatted in a way that sets you up for failure. Make 2 tiny mistakes? There goes your A for the class. Want partial credit? Welp, he doesn't believe in that. Oh, and if you get all questions right it won't guarantee a 100% bc if he doesn't like how you came to your answer you could get half credit (yes Im being serious).

Dude is a BEAST - absolutely on top of the material, and a great lecturer and great guy. Learned everything I ever wanted to know about sensor fusion+estimation and filtering...I would say that even a CS graduate student would find lots of value in this class, too. Grades were for self-selected project (personal or group), and homework. Very good!!
Dudes one of the nicest teachers I have met. If you fail this class, drop engineering as a whole. He is a nice grader and posts everything on canvas.

Dr. Komendera gave good lectures and included all details needed to fully understand the concepts. Homeworks and exams weren't too bad. Pretty lenient grading on exams as well. Also posts lecture notes and records videos with homework hints. Would definitely recommend taking his class.

She's fine? I don't really have much to complain about but nothing super good to say. Format same as 1025, HW and quiz T and R, participation assignment due Friday that you don't HAVE to be in class for but can be if you want to ask questions on it. Sometimes felt like she was going soo slow and sometimes felt like she was going too fast.

She is very nice and genuinely connects with her students. Calculus is an interesting topic to learn, and she explains it very clearly. I understand why people are down, but don't expect to get a high grade in a class that requires work. I'd say Erika is the best calc teacher.

This class was slight. She was very thorough and made sure everyone knew the content. Always answered every question thoroughly and was kind and respectful with every explanation. Amazing professor and easy class if you show up. If someone thinks this class was hard it's because they probably skipped class.

Calc 2 isn't an easy class to begin with but I found it much easier than Calc 1–Erika is such a caring professor and goes through things clearly the first time when teaching them. As long as you pay attention during lectures and understand what you're doing when you're doing it you'll be fine! Definitely attend office hours if you need them.

Had erika for 1025 and 1026, which was much harder than 1025. Be prepared to do most of your learning outside of class, since she rushes through new concepts and expects you to keep up. The notes are also hard to understand if you arent in class so go to class on M and W to hear. The homework is nothing like the tests and tests are graded harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She was a good professor I just preferred Peter in terms of how they handled the course. The quizzes every week were more severe for her class which I did not prefer as they are called participation but are graded by accuracy for her class versus graded on PARTICIPATION for Peters class. She was cool though.
Tests are stuffed with arbitrary trick questions.

The tests were 100 times harder than the homework, quizzes, and practice tests combined. She also did have a bit of an attitude when answering questions but she was a good professor compared to others.

Often rude when answering questions. I never went to her office hours so keep that in mind, but the tests were basically all of the hardest questions that could come from whatever lesson we learned. Didn't really explain she just worked through problems very fast and expected us to follow along.

lost my car keys on test day once. sent an email and she had no problems letting me retake the next day. she is caring. 1026 is a bit harder than 1025. spent quite a bit of time at the tutors but id still recommend her, shes nice and respectful. good at answering questions
I did not enjoy her lectures much, but when I would take the tests, they did not align with the material learned at ALL. I then retook 1025 at the emporium and did MUCH better.
Worked so hard just to fail because of her egregious grading policy.
How am I supposed to study for tests with homework if the homework is not the same as the test?
If you ask her a simple question, whether on email or in person, she gives some major attitude.

Some of the problems on the tests were not from homework or practice tests, so that is lazy on her part for not preparing us. She also has horrible office hours. Doesn't respond to emails. Take whatever she says with a grain of salt. The laziness here is appalling; if she took the time to care her students would do better.

Great for a math class. Gives a decent amount of homework but you get infinite tries. Class isn't mandatory but I recommend you should go Monday and Wednesday, for the learning aspect. Fridays are simply class participation which you don't need to be there for. As long as you attend review classes and do the homework you should do good on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor made class interesting because she was so funny. She was very straight to the point and made sure to explain everything, even the "easy algebra" and she made sure that we had all the materials that we needed.

I would highly suggest taking her for calc 1025! She is so kind and funny! I will say how well you do in this course is very dependant on your attendance. She offers practice on fridays and will tell you exactly what you should be studying for the tests and has practice tests. Homework is annoying but standard across all 1025 sections I think.

I was never that horrible at math in high school and just needed the credit to complete a pathway and ended up having to withdraw. She moves extremely fast and while she will answer questions, they are never explained well or clearly at all. The tests are open answer and there's no curve. Don't take her class if you want to pass a simple calc class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher! Really helped me understand math, and she's very down to Earth. Doesn't really answer emails unless you ask her, but overall great teacher. As long as you show up and do the homework you'll be fine. Tests are very straight forward.

Overall, Erica Rappold is a good professor for 1025. Her lectures were helpful and it was obvious what you needed to learn before the test. The homework can be lengthy at times but that helps prepare you for the test so it isn't too bad. She's also very willing to answer questions and clear up anything that you don't understand if you ask.
She is very good at explaining course material and clear about what will be on exams. Her reviews are very helpful and it is so nice she goes over practice exams. She is also so nice and very funny

I took Calc 1&2 with Professor Rappold and would take every single class with her again. She was the most caring and understanding professor I have ever experienced. It is calculus so obviously the content will not be easy but she provides so many resources and clear problem solving, as long as you put your mind to it you can do well in the class.

The way the tests are set up with open-ended math answers can make it easy to do badly on a test. Her test reviews are very helpful either. For the final, she only posted a few questions and didn't show the work for a lot just marked the correct answer. She also posts some stuff at the last minute that would help for studying.

Calculus is not easy, but Professor Rappold makes it digestible. She is VERY clear about what's going to be on tests and she's transparent about how to do well on them. I've never had a problem focusing in class (I have ADHD) and she wasn't afraid to make jokes, which was relieving! Undoubtedly one of the most helpful professors I've had to date.

Ms. Rappold is extremely kind and always willing to help out. The course dynamics and math department have moved away from the Emporium, and I have heard that things are better now, but when I took the course, I was largely guided through the Emporium, which was incredibly challenging. Despite this, Erika had great lectures and was very patient.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I could never get a hold of Erika. It took her two weeks to respond to my email. She did not even know my name. She is not fair to students who attend class and is not accessible. If you struggle in math or need some TLC in the subject, do not take her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Erika was great! She joked around a lot which helped to keep my focus. She answered all questions clearly and would give extra examples if needed. As long as you pay attention and do the homework you should be fine for the tests.

She assigns all of the hw a little last minute and expects you to get it all done. The quizzes are only a few questions, on months worth of material so make sure you know every but of info. Make sure you show up and take good notes, it is possible to do well in her class.

If you take this professor in person, beware. Her tests are mostly fill-in-the-blank, which is terribly hard. I struggled a lot because if I made 1 wrong mistake, it was held against me. I feel as if she is a nice professor, but I strongly recommend taking her online. On one of the tests, the average was a 9/18... insane (NO CURVE EITHER)

math empo is terrible but erika is great! knows the material well and is good at explaining. she isn't in charge of test material, so that's not really on her. super funny and very real. cares about you. also will always say bless you when someone sneezes.

Definitely go to class! Her lectures are so helpful and she goes over how to do each problem. Print or be able to write on your laptop/iPad of her blank notes she provides as it contains the problem but not the work of how to do the problems. Last half of class can be challenging with integrals. Straight forward but caring!
I have been absolutely miserable in dealing with the Math Empo but Dr Rappold is awesome. She makes this course bearable

Erika is funny and explains the content really well. A textbook was associated with the class but I never even bought it and passed the class with an A. Beware that the tests are weighted very heavily. Exams are considered difficult but if you put in the work and focus on understanding the material you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall good teacher, you will learn the material well. However, she will grade your test based off her feelings and not whether you got the problems right. Her "multiple choice" questions are not actually multiple choice, since she will take off points if your work had any errors even though you got it right. She grades work, not correctness.
Phenomenal professor for Differential Equations. Very understanding, and the tests were fair and not overly challenging. For one of the hardest math classes engineers take, she did a wonderful job.

Rappold is a must for Multi! She uploads note outlines before class so that you don't have to take as many notes. Her tests are fair and kinda predictable. As long as you do the practice problems from the book, you will be ok. She does a great job of teaching this course and presents the material in a way that's easy to understand.

Erika's differential equations class was one of the more reasonable math classes I've taken at VT. Her tests were fair and pretty much tested students on whether or not they knew the material. Go to class since she doesn't post lecture notes online. Only con is that her printable lecture notes are handwritten. Overall, clear and concise for diff EQ

Very good professor, very nice, but makes her tests way harder than any other prof in the department. My class and her other section had test averages in the low 70s, while a lot of other sections taught by other profs would have high 80, low 90 test averages... So be prepared for more rigorous tests.
Very good teacher. She a very good at explaining hard concepts and she prepares you well for the common time final. If is very nice and easy to talk to.
Awesome teacher, no complaints

Dr. Eska is one of the sweetest professors I've had at tech. I'm an engineering student and took this class for fun simply because I was interested in linguistics and she did not disappoint. I genuinely looked forward to her class each morning (even though it was at 8am), and if I had the room in my schedule, I would take another one of her classes
Literally the sweetest lady ever, always looked forward to going to her class.

Dr. Eska is awesome! She is always happy to help you with stuff and has a good sense of humor.

In general there is not a lot of work, mainly just three tests I think. Textbook is like $70.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not enough good things to say about Dr. Eska. She made the linguistics lectures fun and the tests totally reflected what was taught in class. There are only 2 midterms and 1 final so make sure to maximize the test grades as those add up to 85% of your grade. Don't forget to complete the 3 mini 5% assignments (I forgot 1 and it wasn't ideal).

Professor Eska enjoys the subject matter a lot, so the class actually ended up being very enjoyable. She doesn't post a lot of online announcements, so you'll definitely need to show up to class or email her if you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's definitely passionate about the subject and is good at teaching. Come to class ready to learn and read the textbook chapters she assigns and you'll pass. She's very approachable inside and outside class, so don't hesitate to ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She makes the lecture material fun and interesting even when it may be boring in and of itself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prepares you for tests, however none of the lecture material is posted on canvas so if you miss the class you wont be able to get the info. The course work is also pretty dull but she manages to make it interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She was always willing to go over material with me when I needed help. She's very passionate about linguistics and she shows it. I always felt prepared for her tests.

Absolutely great teacher. She's got a quirky side, and the material discussed in class isn't enthralling, but if you pay attention and put in the work, she'll notice. She also does a fantastic job of preparing you for the tests, which can be tricky.

She's very consistent. She makes sure you know exactly what is on her tests and she prepares you for them very well. They are difficult, but the fact that you are not in the dark as to what to study for makes them a lot more bearable. She does a great job teaching overall.
Tries very hard to help every student understand the material, even though it can be kind of confusing.  Tests are easy if you go to class and pay attention.
She's very nice and very helpful, but the information itself is a little boring.  She is a hard grader for papers, but her tests are a little easier.  For a required class, it wasn't too bad.
Excellent professor, however participation matters if you want to succeed in the class.

This professor is very kind and teaches her lectures in ways that help students to both practice the language and understand the curriculum. Some say she is a hard grader, but I wouldn't say so (although she isn't the easiest grader either). Her classes are small which she uses to form relationships with her students and provide great feedback.

Professor Bauer is very understanding and cares about her students. There are lots of assignments due daily as with any foreign language class. Buying/renting textbooks/workbook is essential and be prepared to do some reading. Attendance is mandatory as with any small group upper level language class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pretty good prof. Just show up and do the work. The class is simple basic.

Lazy, careless, and uninterested is how you would describe Mrs Amy Simpson.

She treats her students like children and doesn't understand she is there to teach a group that is not fluent in the skills/class that she is teaching.

Does not appear to have the heart to teach, is only there as "another job " 

Does not have much patience to explain stuff without giving you the "are you serious look." More worried about other stuff than focusing on her job as a professor and the future she is teaching. 

Worst class, worst professor ever.

While nice enough, Mrs. Simpson is a very lousy professor. Every single assignment was explained poorly and she'd be extremely judgemental if asked for clarification. The most annoying part of this class was the semester long group project she assigned. Make sure you group with people you like and make sure to plan way ahead of her deadlines.

Incredibly nice and a great teacher. Most classes are lectures followed by the daily quiz on the reading and lecture. If you stay up to date with the online readings and focus in class the daily quizzes are very easy. There are group projects that seem like a lot of work but if you put the effort in and stay on top of it they won't be an issue.

This class all business majors take and have the same assignments she is one of the best professors of the 15. She is so nice and enjoys teaching the class. She brought the class donuts and candy and had super fun extra credit test reviews. Daily quizzes that are easy to get 100%s if you read the textbook and take notes.

Daily reading quizzes and tons of group work. If you don't get a good group, good luck. Assignments are easy but super vague instructions so you have to ask exactly what she is looking for. Class not that bad just one big project that requires a ton of work.
Treats intro students to the same standard as grad students. Makes things harder than they should be.
Knows his material.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Hard course, but Esker made it fun. Took it 3.5 yrs ago. He allowed the students to eat and drink during the evening test sessions. Knows his material well. Test grades averaged around 50-60, but he curves (stated in syllabus- READ), so that 75+ is an A, and so on. If you know your calculus and diff Eq you're golden. Very sarcastic sense of humor.
horrible
ok
Hard Class but he really wants his students to work hard and understand the material.  If you work hard you will get an A in the class.
HARD!!!  Ridiculous amount of homework each week.  Expects you to know stuff that he should be teaching you.
No Comments

I studied with Dr Sheinberg at the University of Edinburgh and can honestly say she is one of the very best tutors I've ever had. Tough, of course, but only because she cares that students work hard to get their grades. For me a great clarity of thinking and helped me understand HOW to think, not just what.

She was an ok teacher just hard to understand. It's an easy class for those who play or know how to read music. If you don't know how it's hard to keep up. I dropped it after a few weeks. She moves very fast.

it is not an easy A. you have to learn the material and understand for the final exam although it is open notes. 2 easy hw grades and 1 final. no hw. sit in the front row because it is hard to hear/understand her from the back. if you dont take notes you will have to learn it on your own before the final so take good notes

I never attended class except for a few days because I know a lot about theory as it is, but she is an amazing teacher. All her lectures flow perfectly. Also, there's only three exams that are all open notes. So that's cool.

Dr. Sheinberg makes Symphonic Lit. and her other classes challenging and interesting, just as upper-level music major classes should be.  I learned a great deal from her, and enjoyed taking several other courses under her direction.   Attendance is not mandatory, but if you miss the daily quizzes and informative lectures your grade is in trouble!

This class was freshman theory for music majors.  Although she obviously knew the material, we had MAJOR communication issues with her.  Music majors have to take this class, but the more you talk to her, the more understanding she is. If you explain why you did something differently than her, she'll usually give you credit.  And read the textbook.

I wasn't a student of Dr. Sheinberg's at VT, but at Edinburgh Uni. She's certainly a tough cookie, but undoubtedly one of the very finest teachers I have ever had, and extremely caring of her students. I've been lucky enough to study with some of the best teachers in my field, and can confidently say that Dr. Sheinberg is one of the best.

the class isn't hard, but putting up with Dr. Sheinberg is. doesn't have a lot of respect for students and a lot of things she says/asks are hard to understand. it's an easy A, but you'll have to put up with a lot to get it.
it was torture.

She started off as a horrible teacher, she would just write blank problems on the board without explanation or the answers.  Now she teaches a little bit, but I still don't understand everything because she isn't clear or very helpful.  I would definitely take Berg if you can get in his class

If you want to learn organic chemistry all by yourself, then by all means take Etzkorn's class. If you would like some instruction on this troublesome topic, then take pick a different professor. Etzkorn's lectures are useless because she won't completely teach anything...you'll have to learn most of it on your own.

I wouldn't call her a professor because she refuses to teach anything of use in class. She never finishes examples or answers questions fully because she thinks that students should just read the book to get the answers. Don't bother going to class its a total waste of time and you'll wind up more confused. Just read the book and cram for exams.

She really is a terrible professor. She tried to give in-class quizzes as punishment when no one volunteered to do work out problems before class. She does a bad job at explaining the material, and will hardly answer questions in class-- The textbook was more helpful than she was. She has mood swings and gives off bad vibes. Don't do it!

Etzkorn is awful.  She's awkward, unapproachable, and shouldn't have ever been hired to teach a class.  She doesn't like to answer questions, and if she does she makes you feel dumb.  She makes mistakes, which are usually corrected by students during every class. She makes the material hard to understand and gets irritated when people don't get it.

If you have to take "Identification of organic compounds" with her, just grit your teeth and rely on the curve to do well.  She doesn't teach very long on how to actually interpret spectra... only theory behind the experments.
No Comments

Very helpful professor. She makes sure to clarify everything and is very clear on how she will grade assignments (follows rubric perfectly). This is a group project based class and quite a bit of written assignments but if you pay attention and stay on top of your work, it's an easy A. Great class and I learned a lot.

She is really nice to others. Gives good extensions if asked. Lots of reports and useless papers to write. Project based with a team. But if you put in the work it is an easy A. Sometimes it is hard to understand what she says, but she really tries her best to speak well. I had minimal issues with that. TA was cool too.
The entire class was group work so just hope you get some good group members assigned to you. Lots of papers but overall our TA and the prof made it pretty easy to get an A
Great teacher, would recommend.

Most of the class work is group work, so pray that you get good group members. The work is mostly busy work and will not help you as an engineer. At the end of the day though, the grading seems to be honest, and putting in a decent amount of effort will get you an A. Never had a problem with her English either.

Eunsil Lee is from South Korea. Because of this, many people complain that she has broken English, however, she is often able to push through that easily and carry along her ideas clearly. At the beginning of the year we are broken into teams. So long as you actually put in the effort (2-3 hours a week outside of class), you will do well in here.

Very nice person, but as a teacher, she is very hard to understand at times (very broken English), very disorganized, provides basically no feedback, and I was left constantly confused in her class as what exactly we were hoping to accomplish. Also, tends to ramble on about nothing in lectures, and gives walls of text for most assignments

Material seems like common sense so when she repeats herself its tiresome so lecture can become very long and boring. Very good at fair grading and timeliness. There is a good amount of work outside class, but she gives you time during lecture to work. Sometimes she struggles to understand what you are actually asking but tries her best to help.

She is very nice however sometimes I find it a little hard to understand what she wants. A lot of the times she would talk about an assignment and tell you things to do that are either completely different from what the assignment sheet said or not even on it, also sometimes expects things that she didn't even mention for us to do.

She is a great researcher, but not the best professor. She is very critical of your work if it is not the way she would do things, which is the most frustrating because as a design major, everyone does things very differently. She can be difficult to understand sometimes, which she obviously cannot help. She is different depending on the class.

Very nice but her classes seem very juvenile. She is a great researcher, but isn't very inspiring as a professor. If you ask for help, she will go above and beyond to help you. She is funny and down to earth but she can be a little hard to understand sometimes. She is very aware of that and tries to work around it!

Eugene is amazing. He relates to students, and he works really hard to make sure you feel comfortable and confident. Not only is he the smartest professor ever, he is able to make complex topics topics like physics seem attainable to people who do not know anything about it. He makes some hilarious jokes/comments. Take him. He will help u succeed.

Very cool guy overall, pretty down to earth and easy to get along with. Gave me an extension for any assignment I needed more time for, met with me personally to go thru questions and excused my lab absences this summer so I could go to the beach. A+++ professor, even though physics kind of sucks in itself!
EXTREMELY helpful during physics common office hours. Is really enthusiastic about what he's teaching and it shows. Knows what hes doing and is really a great teacher! Really recommend!!!

Attendance quizzes on concepts each class, 2 homework assignments per week, loves to help students, TONS of extra credit opportunities. Does curve to an extent.  Tests are 1/2 concepts.  Very flexible professor.  Very energetic.  Demos in class.  No powerpoint presentations!

Eugene was a very helpful teacher. He was extremely fair in grading his exams. He understood which questions were too difficult for the students and would grade accordingly. This class requires a lot of studying and time in doing homework--but it would require a lot of hard work regardless of professor. Wish I could have had him for PHYS 2206.
He was very helpful if you went to office hours and really nice.Good class overall.

Eugene's teaching was pretty unorganized, as he just derived formula after formula and tells us to know them all, but come test time we never used them.  Tests are not extremely difficult but do require studying.  He gives homework every class, and also takes random attendance quizzes so you have to show up to class.  Ok professor, but not great.
Make sure you go to class. Homework isn't that bad. Watch out for the pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Hands down best Calc1225 professor out there. She is extremely efficient and goes at a fast pace but very welcoming of questions. She loves to give extra credit and will basically do whatever you need to pass the class... trust me. She is also EXTREMELY friendly and truly a good person. Exams are consistent with examples from class.

She is the nicest and most personable professor I ever had. She has your back if the math department is trying to pull a fast one on the students and helps you out in every way possible. Can be a tad bit hard to understand sometimes but her massive enthusiasm makes up for it.  Take her if you can

Prof Chang is the best Math Teacher I think I've had ever. She's very helpful and although she can be hard to understand, if you tell her you are lost on something she will keep going over it in different ways until you get it. She's really sweet so all you have to do is ask for help and you're good for the whole semester. DO THE HOMEWORK

Great teacher. I definitely recommend her! It's an easy class, so don't expect to be "challenged". However, if you're like me and just need this class for economics (or whatever your major is), Prof. Chang is the one to go to!

AWESOME professor. I was kind of scared when I saw the name, thought it would be another prof teaching me that I should be teaching english. But no, this prof is probably my favorite I've had. Gives alot of extra credit and really cares for the students. If you ever get the chance to get her DO IT!!!

She was a great math teacher. She gives a variety of examples per topic to help you understand. She gave tons of extra credit toward the homework and quizzes. She does great reviews for the test. She would use the last 3 classes before the test to review, and hold extra reviews if needed. Some other students found her hard to understand.

It's a HARD class but you'll learn a lot.  Just keep up with problem sets and practice tests and go to his office when you have questions.  Things are so much clearer one on one because he'll break it down for you.  Prepare to have a heart attack when you see your test grades but know that they are curved ridiculously well.

His tests are tough but put in the effort to understand how to do the practice sets he gives out and you'll get at least a B. The practice sets also help out A LOT for his quizzes because sometimes he repeats, etc. Go to his office hours! Don't be intimidated.

BEWARE!!  Constantly mumbles to chalkboard, is not clear with a teaching plan, does not use a mic, problem sets are useless for his tests, and his tests are ungodly tough.  He rounds up test grades, but out of necessity so the whole class doesn't fail.  He's the only Bchem prof so you have to take him, but just be ready for it.
One of my favorites.  Great guy and awesome teacher.

Dr.Gregory is AWESOME!!! His tests are really tough, but he's a great professor. If you have any questions, he's very helpful. He gives quizzes each week to give extra points, and curves a LOT at the end. EXPECT to work hard-you will earn your grade in his class (he reminds me of Santa Claus).

His quizzes and exams were always very hard; usually, they contained information he mentioned once while you were standing around a bunch of animals, so you had to really listen as hard as you could. Most of us did badly on them, but he was a gentle grader. He's a great professor, though, and fun to talk to. He wants to see you do well.
He is an exceptionally difficult grader. He will base large portions of tests and quizzes on small details he hardly mentions and then proceeds to accuse you of not paying attention or studying.

I don't recommend him. Simply exams after exams, only two HW's to help our failing grades, and we end up trying everything we can as students trying to build our grades up. I've also heard from my fellow peers who have attended his open hours that he comes off as judgmental and rude when asking a simple question. Not helpful at all. DON'T TAKE HIM!

Amazing professor, highly recommend! Offered so much help outside of lectures especially around exam season. He clearly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He often asks students what we're passionate about and then incorporates that as an example to explain things in lecture. Overall he's an awesome professor with engaging lectures

Jeff is a really nice guy and makes the content as understandable as possible. He really wants his students to succeed and puts lots of effort in outside of class to make sure that happens. When I took calc 1 in high school the material made no sense to me, but when I took it this time around Jeff explained it a way that actually made sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor!

Likely the best math teacher I've ever had so far. Breaks things down and in a simple and effective manner without being excessive or boring either. Cares about student success and makes sure the entire class is able to keep up, even by arranging study sessions on his weekends during test weeks. Absolutely pick this teacher.
He is the goat

Prof. Evans is great. Certainly, the best math professor I have had. Very nice guy, open to office hours, very transparent about what he expects from his students. Tests are tough and there are a lot of homework assignments, but Prof. Evans prepares students well and is willing to negotiate due dates and test dates. (Took 1226).

Amazing professor. Good lectures, good practice packets, fair, etc.

My shitty grade is because I should never have gotten this far in maths. 

The only reason why I even passed this course was because of Evans. ha see what i did there

anyway yeah take this guy
My king Jeff

TAKE JEFF! He was the best professor for such a difficult class. Extremely helpful, always kind and made my day better always. He has the BEST test taking tips that I still use today. He has super helpful study guides. You will succeed if you take notes and do practice problems. Jeff is the best. enough said

What a legend! Probably one of the best professors at all of Virginia Tech. He makes this very rigorous course a cakewalk. He is extremely helpful, extremely kind, patient, thoughtful, genuine and so much more. I pray to have him again! 
MATH 1225 is very hard and is standardized across all classes, but he makes it 1000x more enjoyable!
Thanks Jeff
Absolute legend, one of the best math instructors I have ever had.
HE IS THE GOAT IF U CAN TAKE IT JUST TAKE IT MAKE TIME FOR HIM

One of the best professors I have ever had. Chill guy who really loves his material and his students and just has this amazing energy that he brings to every lecture. 1225/1226 are annoying classes but he is probably one of the best options to take. Attendance is not mandatory but since Calc 1/2 is full of material I would suggest going anyways.

Best 1225 professor; good at making you think about what's actually happening. Very kind and accessible; he will certainly take the time to help you individually. Pay attention and get to know him, he's simply a great guy!

By far the best professor I have ever had at tech. Evans genuinely cares so much about his students, not just grade-wise, but also mentally. His lectures are detailed and easy to follow, where you won't fall asleep. I would recommend his class to everyone, as people fought to be in it.

Jeff is an amazing instructor, he wants all of his students to succeed. My advice: be active in class and make sure he knows your name and face, this will go a long way with any professor, especially Jeff. Don't be afraid of emialling to ask for help in addition to going to office hours and test reviews. Do whatever you need to to take his classes!

Jeff is godsend when it comes to taking 1225. He always checks in on his students during lectures to make sure everyone is on the same page. He really cares about the success of all of his students, so do not be afraid to reach out for help. If you have him for 1225, you are one lucky person!
Really hard class but he consistently checks in during lectures to make sure everyone understands what's going on.

Evans was one of the best teachers I've had in my life.

Hard material, but will do everything he can to make the class understand it, answering any questions you have. Will gauge the class's understanding by asking "How are we feeling?"

Genuinely cares that all students learn. Go to office hours if you can.
(Beware, he is allergic to emails.)

His lectures are engaging, which makes learning content interesting. He really cares about how students are doing both in the classroom and outside of it and he's extremely clear about what you need to learn to be successful. He also encourages participation from all students and doesn't leave people behind even if they have no calculus background.

I had him for 1226, a relatively difficult class that I was a little worried about, and he made it a great experience. He makes lectures personal, he always says "nice to see you", which is really nice. He goes above and beyond, he offered like 10 hours of his personal time for final exam review sessions, and he makes sure the class is doing good.

Let's just be honest, 1225 sucks, but Jeff is the best professor to have for this class. He makes it easy to understand and is super easygoing (ex: "how do we feel?"). Not only that, he is super nice and always says "glad to see you". Combine his lectures with Professor Leonard on YT plus do practice problems and you'll be fine.

Jeff was my first math class at VT and it was calc 1 (1225). He cares more than any other teacher about his students, and if you want to do well, he will give you a path to do so.

He makes class personal, rather than just another lecture.

Prof. Evans deeply cares about student success, offering support during office hours, through quick email responses, or post-class discussions. His impact led me to drop other classes for Calc 2. He's not just a teacher but a mentor, guitarist, guide, and advocate, making him one of the best, or the best professors in the math department.

I took STAT 1004 with her (didn't give an option for that course) but found her to be very clear on what she expects. I found this very helpful. Just do the work (easy) and pay attention in class to guest speakers and her lectures and you will find this class enjoyable! She gives very clear feedback, and I found her class to be very interesting!
There is a weekly quiz and assignment based on material from textbook and slides. Nice professor, the videos were helpful.

Very straight forward teacher. Everything is outlined in her syllabus and she is strict about deadlines for assignments but also very accessible outside of class. If you study for the tests and make sure to complete every aspect of an assignment you will be just fine. Final is a research project that you present instead of an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was online and it was pretty easy. There was an assignment and quiz due every week and the lecture videos were so insanely helpful. The tests are open notes and there is a textbook, but I only used it if I was confused on a topic, so it isn't necessary.

Not a hard class but her lecture videos are not helpful at all in my opinion. Basically she quickly *speaks* a hour worth of information in 10 minutes with slides that typically only contain images, not even the content. I had to use the transcript for reference. Quizzes have vague questions and the labs are graded by strict TAs.
Jane is a good teacher. She does not deviate from what she has posted in the syllabus, meaning she doesn't make any exceptions for late work or family emergencies. Outside of that, she's fine.
