Since this course was taught asynchronously, the course was pretty much self-taught-based, which made the course pretty challenging. This class required many hours of studying since I had to teach myself most of the content. If possible try to take this course in person to avoid confusion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I thought the lectures were super easy to follow, and I liked how she gave examples of problems that were on the assignments. If you watch the videos, you'll do well on all the assignments. As someone who hates math and is not good at it, I would 100% take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was an online course, so I didn't interact with professor Robertson often. Every week there was a quiz and assignment due, and typically there were videos and resources to help, but I struggled with doing it "correctly" even though I followed the instructions to a tee.
She's horrible I had a family emergency, and she said, "Sorry but I never take late assignments", like it was under my control.

Prof valued attendance on zoom. She asks questions to people, but only to gauge whether people understand the lecture. She had a research project instead of a final which I thought was very different and I actually developed what I learned in the class. Very nice and very fair class.

I would not recommend taking this class online, though that's nothing to Professor Robertson Evia's fault. This class was incredibly difficult in terms of the material and took lots of effort and completely focused hours of time each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: In the beginning it seems like this class will be kind of a waste and all the guidelines feel stupid, but by the end you will have learned so much. He's a tough grader, but you just need to spend a lot of time revising, and as soon (or even before) the assignment is explained in class begin.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson is very straightforward with his guidelines and will send out Canvas announcements with detailed descriptions of everything he is looking for. He's easily accessible outside of class which makes it easy to get any clarification if you need it. Make sure you know your AP style guidelines and you'll be fine in his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very strict about grading but also lists out what is expected and what will be deducted if you do not follow. His feedback is very useful. All around he is genuinely funny and well spoken

A super tough grader and will knock off 15 points for using a comma in the wrong place, but he's super clear about his instructions so you know what you're getting into. I've heard he's better than the other prof who teaches this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Everett is a very passionate person about real estate. He can go on and on about the material and what you should do in many different aspects of your young professional lives. The class is not hard; however, the class is very repetitive, and you will find that you are going over a lot of the same material for weeks on end.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Everett is great! The class is very interesting and the grading is based off of 5 exams with the lowest grade dropped. His lectures are great & he really helps you understand the material. The most important part of the class is the textbook. Learn the material in the textbook & you'll be A okay!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I really liked this class. I thought it was an easy A class, as long as you read the textbook and go to class. Professor Everett posts powerpoints, you take notes before class, and then he lectures from the PowerPoint in class. Your grade is based on 4 tests and an exam (optional), and your lowest grade is dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lectures full class period each day. 4 exams and a final with a few extra credit assignments and that's all your grades. Makes his exam questions tricky. powerpoint he posts/uses has very base level info (doesn't really help you on exams)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: REAL 2004 is an amazing class that goes fast and is insightful. This class is based on 4 exams through the semester and a final. Out of the 5, the lowest one was dropped. He gives an opportunity for extra credit after each exam, so he wants you to succeed and actually learn the material. Reading the textbook and taking good notes is crucial.
He has great lectures and are easy to understand. Great professor at VT.
He is gone which is the most impactful thing Professor Sullivan has done at Virginia Tech! Rude professor, did not like to lecture. Hopefully is not hired elsewhere.

Horrible professor. Shows no care or concern for any students and often grades harshly. Shouldnt be teaching at any level. Personally targeted me in recitation classes and gets mad anytime a problem is done incorrectly. Take this class with anyone else, except Everett Sullivan.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: pretty rough teacher. He doesn't give a lot of homework, but the homework given takes a lot of time. I recommend getting a buddy and doing hw together.

Amazing professor that really ignited my interest in mathematics. I personally loved the way that he would explain topics and give a reason as to why the topic is important. He always gave good feedback and encouraged participation and questions during class as well as outside of class.

Does not express any kind of care or concern for students. When in office hours, I would ask a question, to which he would respond: "go look it up in the textbook" Does not lecture well at all and gets mad whenever a student gets a problem wrong. Has a very high drop out rate.

He is so mean. I had him for online class and we had to meet on a zoom once a week. If you didnt answer his confusing question right, he would respond very rude and his responses were never helpful. The homeworks are beyond difficult and he never reviews them until the week of the test if you ask. HES AWFUL
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Sullivan is a very harsh grader and will find anything to take points off of. He also responds to emails with one sentence in very little detail. He was okay with a failing test average among his classes.

Everett is a good guy. I'd say a stereotypical mathematician. Says "precisely!" to correct answers and is definitely not the most social guy. He is also pretty strict about format in homework and tests. However, he teaches material pretty well and can give decent help in office hours. I had him 2019 before online, so that can change a lot of stuff.

Math 1225 online is the most difficult thing I have ever done. The lecture videos are extremely long and often take way more than the time they are supposed to. Professor Sullivan did not help much with the class, and when asked for help, responded with "it is somewhere in the textbook". 0/10 do not recommend Math 1225 at Virginia Tech.

Greatest Math teacher I have ever had. Without him, I would not have passed Math 1225 at Virginia Tech. Caring, respectful, funny, and overall a great and genuine person. If you can, go ahead and take this professor over any other in the math department.
Jeff Evans is probably the best teacher I have. He makes a difficult class manageable and does a great job preparing the class for tests. I would change my schedule to get him for Calc 2.
Amazing guy, I don't know what the other dude who rated him poorly is saying. He does talk about his personal life a lot but he is a great teacher, especially for an introductory math course.

I had Jeffery Evans for my MATH 1225 class. He is a nice guy and got to know many of his students, but I learned nothing in his class. He made it difficult to learn in his class because he would just go on random rants about his personal life. Additionally there was a time where a student had asked him a question in class where he just said no to.

Jeff Evans is a great professor who for his first semester teaching at Virginia Tech had done an amazing job making his lectures interesting. He is always happy to help when asked and would schedule his office hours based on feedback from his classes to ensure he can be available to students when needed. Highly recommend 
attending his class.

Prof. Evans is a G, offering support during office hours, through quick email responses, or post-class discussions. His guidance made me find my passion. This impact led me to drop other classes for his Calc 2 class. He's not just a teacher but a mentor, guitarist, guide, and advocate, making him one of the best professors in the math department.
Best professor ever, I would rearrange my whole schedule to be with this guy again. Does everything in his power to ensure that his students succeed in both his class and future classes.

He is super chill, funny, and nice. Explains the content in a very simple way which is great when reviewing the notes. It's super important to watch the lecture videos or read the textbook before class because of the activity/homework due each class day. The tests contain a lot of material, so make sure to study well and understand application too.
Amazing professor! super funny and cares about his students. If you put in the work you will get the grade you want.

Dr. Evans was an amazing professor, he was easy to learn from & very interactive with lectures. The only assignments were small quizzes after class & an activity with groups during class. The course, in general, isn't terrible if you're good at bio, just be prepared to study hard. His tests were a bit difficult with the way it was worded.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do your stuff on time and you will pass. All the stuff is really easy and there is only like 4 assignments so you have to do them.
Not at all hard. Do the bare minimum and you'll literally pass.

Dr. Evans is definitely one of the best professors here at Tech. He wants everyone to succeed in the biology field, and is there for any questions you might have. The course is designed to give you information to help you, and it did. It's not a boring class, and he's hilarious which is nice. Not many people like him to be honest. would have again!
The class that I had Jack for was a very, very easy class, but he made it very enjoyable! He's super funny and the course material was extremely helpful in navigating my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He was a very good professor that assisted students when needed and he made the class very enjoyable! I would definitely have him again as a professor again. Make sure you study for the tests though.
jeff is the goat

Had him for 1225 and he was a great prof. Might be difficult if you've never taken calc before but the tests were reasonable and he has review sessions before each one. Really funny professor and makes an effort to connect with students on a personal level.
Jeff is the GOAT. If you have him you're one lucky cookie. Get ready to do the most fun math of your life.
So amazing. Always provided notes for us and held review sessions. Very inclusive and understanding of every students' needs. Really strived to be kind to every single student and know everyone.

While Math 3214 was definitely not my favorite math class at VT, Prof Palsson was a great teacher. He is enthusiastic, intelligent, very knowledgeable, and lectures well. He also gives good feedback on tests/homework, as well as good partial credit. However, beware that his syllabus was very test heavy: 90% of the grade was tests when I took it

This man is the best math professor ever his lectures are amazing and there isn't much homework. He is very easy to reach for questions and genuinely cares about everyone understanding the course material. If you can take a class taught by him do it.

Professor Palsson is the best math professor I've had at VT. He's super knowledgeable and gives great lectures, and also is such a kind person. He took the time to memorize all of our names via Canvas and really likes to get to know his students. Be sure to ask questions because he answers them to the best of his ability. Take his class if you can!
There is a sign in sheet and there are quizzes on the readings before you talk about them in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am not a mean person, but when you have a native German and a native Turkish men teaching the class, it gets very mundane and very boring fast. Professor Wendt does not allow any technology in class, requiring pencil and paper. Attendance is mandatory and points taken if you skip. Pop-quizes are expected, will not give you dates and no make-ups.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Inability to show interest in teaching. Entire class is recycled from the reading you do the night before

I took the PPE gateway course with Professor Wendt. I greatly enjoyed this course, but it required a lot of reading and engaging with said readings on a deep level before each in class quiz. Luckily, the lectures were good and had exactly what you would need to study for exams. 
overall a good proffesser and very interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was awful. I hated every minute of it. Went to office hours once because I was struggling and was told "well it's pretty straight forward..." Know that this is coming from a student who raises their hand every day in class, did the readings, went to office hours and made study groups. Take this class with ANYONE ELSE but Wendt.

I know that philosophy can be hard to teach in an engaging way, but lectures were very boring. We had extensive readings before each class. His lecture PPTs were almost copy and pasted from the readings. I did not learn much from this class and stressed a lot about papers and the final. Only reading responses and essay grades. Ask ?'s!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy who wants you to understand and succeed. Weekly homework and a few exams, but if you show up and pay attention to the lecutres you will do fine. He does not check his email often though.

Really good professor and a nice guy in general. You can tell he is really knowledgeable and wants his students to succeed. He is good at answering questions and will help you if you need it. If you get a chance to speak to him he is a good connection to have.

Dr. Jazizadeh is a great professor and his class is very straight forward. He walks you through everything you need to know in class and will give extensions when necessary. He is very down to earth and does not use trick questions. You learn a lot in his class with applications in every area of civil engineering.

You get a weekly homework assignment that is super easy at the beginning of the semester and by the end is entirely impossible. He is difficult to reach but extremely helpful when you do, and the lectures are easy to follow while the homework is material never covered (he sends out messages saying this). Tests are just like the homework (hard).

Mr. Jazizadeh is the best professor I've had in Civil Engineering at VT. He is very kind and responsible. The sentence that Mr. Jazizadeh impressed me the most was "My rules are no tough questions. If you feel like it's really hard, you are very likely going in the wrong direction." You can learn a lot in his class and get an "A" relatively easily.

Pouya is really friendly and makes class feel comfortable. Even if we make mistakes, he explains everything clearly and calmly. He is approachable, but also serious about teaching. He enjoys working with circuits and is always open to questions. I could even ask him questions outside office hours, and he would still answer.
Pouya always responded to our emails promptly and provided constructive feedback on all our reports. His feedback was valuable in our process.
He was a pleasure to be in class with and highly entertaining.
He's available outside regular office hours, and he's really good at debugging problems and explaining the debugging process in a clear, easy-to-follow way.
You can ask everything from Pouya

Pouya is among VTs top instructors, a really helpful and kind lecturer
He stays and answers questions without hesitating or being condescending, and he replies to questions outside of class. He made an effort to assist without going straight to the point; he tried to teach debugging thinking. He had broad knowledge base that could answer any query.

From someone who never did, please start the projects before they're due. The grading platform is too finicky to be messing with it an hour before it's due, and the late penalty can hurt. As a professor, he answers questions well, nice guy who wants you to learn, and he's very accommodating if you reach out. Free test retakes are incredible.
Class is great. The professor is great. Don't lose stupid points by doing the project late or not showing up and you will get an A. This guy was retakes for tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was a very sweet guy with great lectures that went into detail about the content. The class is "flipped learning" style which surprisingly helped a lot.

By far the best professor I've had at VT. Projects can be time consuming but as long as you start early you'll be fine. There are quizzes during most classes for attendance, which is 5% of your grade. It's a easy A as long as you keep up with the material and assignments.

Best 3114 professor by far. 3114 takes a lot of time regardless, but Prof. Farghally is a good lecturer and gives alot of leeway. Projects are the main bulk of the class, so (1) start early, (2) get a great partner, (3) go to office hours the moment you get stuck, and (4) take advantage of the 10% bonus given by turning in early.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good class, and good professor. Used to teaching larger classes and sometimes doesn't pay much individual attention.
Great prof, go to his office hours if you need help.
He's the best. no other words

Farghally was very helpful to me and definitely knows what he is talking about. The greatest quality about him was the fact that he was accessible outside of class, and was always willing to help a student thoroughly, no matter the magnitude of question. I would definitely get a head start on the projects, and make sure to attend his lectures!

Dr.Farghally was a great professor. His lectures were well explained and he posted the annotated slides afterwards. There were daily in-class quizzes on the slides taught that day ( 2 - 5 questions). He was very reasonable. Granted extensions on projects. Had 2 exams, midterm and final (wasn't cumulative). They were very straightforward.
Professor Farghally is kind, smart, and organized. There is a lot of work if you don't already have a background in CS but with him as your professor it will be as painless as it can be.
Had him a couple semesters ago. If you can't interpret an Egyptian accent, you may struggle. His explanations are decent, and he's approachable.

I came into this class with very poor past experiences with coding, and left with a love for Java. Farghally is a really nice dude, and is clearly knowledgeable about the subject. He teaches right out of the online textbook, and unlike most classes the textbook is actually worth the investment. I honestly had a lot of fun with this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly, I was unsure after going to the first class and reading the reviews. But as far as math professors go, he's pretty decent at condensing the material in his lecture notes and examples. If you prefer the blackboard and chalk lecture, he's more old-school. I usually did all the Webwork sections covered as practice before unit tests !

Quiet guy, and the accent was difficult to understand at first, but overall a good dude and solid teacher. His lectures can be slightly boring but concisely cover necessary information with plenty of examples, and his homework does a good job preparing you for exams. If you're locked in and reach out, he's a great resource to have in a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I wouldn't listen to the harsh reviews to closely. I think if you succeed in a math class that does many practice problems as opposed to just lecturing about theory or something then he's your guy. 3 midterms that are fair, are 60% of your grade. Homework is 20% and the final is 20%. He has a bit of an accent which might explain the poor lecturing.
Worst proffesor. DO NOT TAKE HIM. often gets examples wrong and creates more confusion. i learned more from youtube than attending lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor I have ever met. I have vehement hate towards this guy. No, hate is too light of a word. This dude can't teach, like, at ALL. You're better off going on YouTube. However, his tests are so UNIMAGINABLY difficult to where even if you DO go over every example and every textbook problem, you're screwed. Hope he gets fired

Dr. Yan is the GOAT for diff eq's. He does not grade harshly and is very nice during office hours. He is not the best at teaching and can be a little hard to understand his lectures, but he is more than happy to answer any questions. Unlike most the math dept, he won't find pleasure in belittling the students in the classroom. Adjusted grade scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She has been my favorite professor during my undergrad. She is so intelligent, and her lectures feel like she is telling a story if you follow along. There are readings that you have every week, and the final exam touches on those readings. Attendance isnt required, but some classes have in-class participation. She is kind and cares!
Could not recommend her more!! Take her classes!
The lectures were so inspiring! Come to class ready to discuss
This class was amazing with a more amazing professor!
amazing and engaging lectures. cares about her students

We had 3 professors in this class, and I always dreaded it when I saw on the syllabus that it was her days to lecture. All she does is read the words off powerpoint and talk slower to make it sound more meaningful. I wish she would talk a little more (and pause less between sentences) to keep us more interested in class. But, she is knowledgable
Her lectures were just SOOOOOOOOOOOO boring. The cadets could never stay awake and most people just tune her out.
Best Professor in the Political Science Department

I've had this Faulkner for 4 classes and she's a great professor! She engages the class with stimulating discussions. She also provides really thorough study guides for the exams, even though all the exams are essay format.

Extremely easy to understand and follow. She expects a lot out of her students but if you work hard you will do well. I recommend anyone who is a political science major at tech to experience one of her courses.

No absence is ever excused, whether it's sports, real medical issues, interviews; nothing.  Group projects tend to consist of about 10 people-too large and difficult to meaningfully work with everyone.
Dont take him

You need initiative if you choose professor Soomro. Only 1-2 easy questions per week for written hw, no practice exam, no review session. He seems to be too careful at the beginning, hoping to get everything in detail, which makes him left behind 2-3 lectures than other teachers. He has to do the last chapter very hurrying. Do book problems to help

Dr Soomro is the GOAT. I withdrew the class because I bombed the first test and couldn't come back, but that was on me not him. He's super useful when you need help on stuff and really goes in depth with content in class. He is a lil slow with lectures but I appreciated it since it helped me understand the content better than if he flew through it

This is the first math teacher I had where I could genuinely understand math. He's a bit slow in lectures which can bite you in the ass but he is the professor I've had that has actually answered questions I had instead of being super vague about it. He was a little nitpicky on grading tests but overall great guy.

His teaching isn't terrible, just really slow, which made us fall behind and told us to watch videos outside class to keep up. Homework is not helpful with only 1–3 problems. Tests are easier than other teachers' but he deducts a lot of points for small mistakes.

He teaches painfully slow and does not review during the class. The material was not super difficult, just memorizing different processes. He gives about 6 practice problems a week, which is just not enough to learn the entirety of the material. Overall not terribly difficult, but takes a lot of effort outside of class to learn the material.
Amazing professor! She is super nice and caring for her students. Homework assignments are not too difficult and gives plenty of time for essays.
Easiest grader and very caring teacher. In class discussions are very interesting and thought provoking.

This class is not necessarily difficult, but as a chemistry major, I did not need it to be. She asks very thought-provoking questions and genuinely makes me love writing essays and engaging in class. I look forward to this class so much, and am taking 1106 next year with this professor.
Literally made an account just to say that she was amazing and was very considerate. She is a wonderful professor and I learned a lot from her class and discussions.
Very kind and cares about each student.
Great teacher

She is a super lenient (students are allowed to miss some of the assignments) and kind professor, as long as you are willing to finish her homework in time (80% are extremely easy, like posting some short comments of reading reflection, the last 20% are about essays stuff) and have a positive attitude towards her class, you'll get an A.
Extremely kind

I loved Fehr! At the beginning of the semester we did a lot of in-class discussions and they were really interesting. You could skip class but there are assignments that can only be submitted in class. She gives lots of drops for assignments which comes in handy. If you keep up with the assignments and put in a bit of effort, you will be fine.
Only one big main paper along with small other writing assignments that help you with your paper. The rest of the grading is just small homework assignments and group projects in class.

Laura is a fine grader. There is a lot of busy work but nothing too strenuous outside of class. There is really only one assignment and that is a research paper. In this class, you will write about 6 different drafts all graded on completion, before submitting your final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's nice, and it is very easy to get a good grade in her class. Very left-leaning and it definitely shows up in her classes. Lots of work, but as long as you do it, it's a super easy A.
Super understanding when it comes to extensions. High workload but not a strict grader so as long as you do the work, you should be fine. Really enjoyed her class.

Her class was very laid back. Even though she did get political and I didn't necessarily agree with her, there was still respect. She didn't grade too tough and was always responsive. There are a couple of annoying assignments but they are worth it if you want to get a good grade.
Unprofessional, extremely political, misspells words often despite being a literal writing teacher

Cares about her students. She gives you so much time for assignments and is very flexible. She drops some grades and overall is very easy. She gives great feedback and is just awesome. We barley use the textbook we had to buy.
Approachable. (3) Papers are not that hard and she will help you if you are suck. Just ask for help.
"I gotta stop smoking the cheap stuff" - Dr. John Ferris

The first few lectures of the semester were a little rough, but Professor Ferris gradually became a favorite. It is no secret that research is his primary focus, but give him a chance and ask many questions during lecture. His style is meant to be interactive. If you ask for a more in depth explanation or Matlab demo he will usually oblige.

I actually learned something when taking ME 4544. If you have a basic understanding of how a car works then you should easily get a B. 2 of the exams had a take home part that was challenging, but doable. How he assigns final grades is awesome, I didn't take the final. To get a B in the class, you only had to get 80 out of the 140 available points.

He's at Tech to do research and not teach. He is not a great teacher and stops before completing explanations. Everyone who has the other professor is doing well but not with him. He said there would be partial credit on the test but there was almost none.
Nice guy, generous grading scale. Reasonable and teaches well. His gpa average is almost always over 3.0, which cannot be said for some of the other ME 3524 instructors.

Automotive Engineering, ME4544. Great teacher overall. He explains everything clearly. The first few lessons (about slip angles) are the hardest -> don't drop the class, it's super interesting and easy after that. Only graded on hw & tests, tests are easier than hw. There is little feedback on hw. 4.5/5. Take this class, it's really cool.
Great Professor, homeworks are good and exams are fair

For AOE 3154, Dr. Fitzgerald had by far the most helpful lecture slides out of any class I've taken so far. He comes to class well prepared, and teaches with passion. You have homework roughly once a week, which code will be your best friend on. There are two take-home midterms, where you can use code as well. TLDR: great course and great teacher!

This is my second semester of research with Dr. Fitzgerald. He's a great and understanding guy who wants you to enjoy your work. He will give great feedback and can help you if you ask! Also teaches AOE 3154 and taught a few lectures when Dr. England was absent, he explains topics very well beyond the slides and answers student's questions well.

Professor Fisher is very organized and the class is very structured. One quiz weekly plus one project. Long chapters to read and very long lecture videos to watch before class. More time spent on prep work than actual assignments. Overall very kind and reaches out often. Grading and deadlines are very strict but often have ample time to complete.

Dr. Fisher is so nice. Always sends reminders throughout the week about what's due. She opens assignments at the start of the week and it's due on Thursday it forces students to get their work done before the weekend. If she posts assignments late then she gives you an extra day. You have 4 days to do ur work. I would 100% take her again.

If you want an easy A, then go ahead and take this course. However, Dr. Fisher discusses many things in her video lectures that she is uneducated on. Many of the examples she uses for class are heavily opinionated and incorrect, which can be discovered through a simple Google search. I encourage others to be very conscious of how she frames things.

i had this professor online so there isn't much to say but she was nice and emailed us with reminders every week - which were very helpful. the class is pretty easy - each week you read the textbook chapter, watch her lecture, read articles, and then take a short quiz. my fav class i had this year because it was easy and the info was interesting.

He was very intelligent. Speaks in a fairly monotone voice, but if you can manage to pay attention the entire time then the content of the lecture is interesting. Readings are a bit difficult, but he explains them well. Going to class is very important because tests are based on what he says in lecture. Smart guy. I would recommend him.

The lectures were pretty boring, but they help with understanding the material from the book. There is a lot of reading but it's pretty pointless because he'll explain it the next day. Two tests and two papers that the TAs scale enormously. A B+ wasn't hard to get.

lectures were all about him. his belief, his opinion and such. not at all what i had in mind. essays were graded to tough on the fact that if we didnt agree with im we were wrong. dont recommend taking

I was unsure of philosophy when I signed up. But I found it really interesting, and really enjoyed listening to Fitzpatrick. He is very intelligent, and the tests aren't too bad. You have two papers which can be challenging. A is definitely possible.

Fitzpatrick is a nice guy.  I'm a science major, so philosophy was not my thing.  This class involves a lot of reading, and you must come to class with an open mind prepared to listen for details.  He has no tolerance for laptops, or people leaving class early.  He will call you out on this.  Class can be enjoyable, but it is not an easy A.
fitzpatrick is an awesome guy - very very smart and can be extremely funny. i loved going to class and just listening to him ramble on about philosophy, it was really interesting.

This just goes to show how easy of a major Philosophy is.  Took this class as a non-technical elective (CS major) and breezed through it.  Essays can be written the night before without any trouble, and the material is very easy to understand.  The prof is personable and makes the material easy to understand. Class is optional, even for an A.

Fitzpatrick is a genius! His knowledge in the subject is extensive, classes are very interesting if you like Philosophy. The readings are pretty boring but the recitations help you learn the material. His tests are straightforward if you've come to class. Go to class, the recitations, and talk to your TA before your papers and youll be good.

He definitely knows his stuff, but I found his tone extremely boring and found myself zoning out a lot. If u try REALLY hard, u will pass the class. He does help u if u go to his office hours. Also get started on your papers/studying for exams EARLY.

This guy might be the smartest person you'll ever meet. I had look up vocab words every class period. If there's a complex issue that needs to be made distinct, he can do it so that a retarded turtle could understand. That's how smart he is. Other than that he's generally an awesome person partially because he loves his wife and son.
He's a decent teacher, but tends to be a bit boring at times. The workload isn't all that hard. If you try, you should get a B.
A thorough introduction to Ethical Theory. Fitzpatrick knows his stuff!
No Comments

my senior capstone class. huge semester-long event project with classmates. she was a good professor. straightforward, clear with assignment criteria, and checked in on our group often. a little too blunt sometimes and she wasn't very encouraging when it came to my group's event. i learned a lot through the class but i'm glad its over.

While I enjoyed the material itself very much, the professor was the worst communicator that I have ever had. The only assignment that she graded herself was the final project. The TAs grade everything except the final so their feedback throughout the semester did not help in the end since it seems she doesn't communicate with them either.

The work load was very manageable and exams were taken at home on canvas. Only con was that she takes weeks to grade assignments. Make sure you read the assignment rubrics as it has stuff not stated in the assignment that are required. Overall Fitch is a very understanding and caring professor

Professor Fitch made Event Management simple and fun while also being extremely simple to learn from. If you miss a class, she has activities to do to make sure you gain credit for the day(s) you missed. She understand that life gets in the way and is very easy going. Take her class!

I LOVE prof Fitch. She really cares about her students and is the first prof. I ever had that changed due dates and asked students opinions if assignments could get done in time. There is a group project that is semester long so chose wisely. Attendance isn't mandatory but helps and she's funny so its not terrible.

Pretty cool class, the whole semester is assignments that lead up to and help with the big final project. There's only 3 quizzes but they're super straightforward from the notes and no tests or finals. Super interesting class if you're interested in event planning. Prof Fitch is just very difficult to reach outside of class, so get your TAs email!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I personally didnt enjoy this class, but it was easy. Professor Fitch was very nice and personable. The whole class is centered around a group project and many assignments that build up to the big project. Quizzes come straight from the slideshows. Take this class if you need an easy A.

For this class I planned a wedding and loved it. Your graded on an assignment each week that works up to the final project which is just a combination of all the previous ones and you get to work in groups

Big project is planning an event. If you actually want to be an event planner in life (or anything in hospitality), the project was pertinent and useful. If you don't, it's a lot of work all for nothing. Online quizzes are easy if you pay attention and weekly discussions aren't hard. She takes attendance.

I enjoyed her lectures, however she was really bad at grading things in a timely matter. There are 6 main assignments, a few quizzes, and one group project. The group project kind of sprung up at the end, but we ended up doing good on it. As long as you pay attention in class the quizzes are relatively easy. No exams or final, just a final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Candace is an amazing professor when it comes to lectures. She is straight to the point and even very funny, making material relatable to students. However, she is not good at giving feedback and comments on graded work (her TA grades the assignments) and she is very hard to get ahold of outside of class. YOU NEED TO GO TO CLASS TO PASS!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Over the course of the class, there are 6 major assignments, 6 quizzes, and one semester-long group project. The group project takes more work than you initially anticipate, but otherwise not TOO hard a class.

Fitch is the type of professor you want for an elective class (like I was taking this class as). She is really nice and straight to the point. There are a lot of assignments and discussion boards but they do not take long to do. In my class we has no exams, only 50 point quizzes. Attendance is super important for your grade but good class overall.

Professor Fitch is really nice, and I went into office hours once and she was really nice. Attendance matters! Watch Canvas because she didn't really post periodically. I thought it was a really interesting class. I used it as a pathway and I'm a Pamplin student and I thought it overlapped with lots of other material I was learning.

Fitch is one of the best professors at VT! If you need this class for HTM or just credit it's the easiest thing you will ever do. She is hilarious, engaging, passionate about her field, and is a great resource for future jobs. Quizzes are on Canvas weekly (open note), attendance is a majority of the points and a weekly discussion on canvas. TAKE IT

Prof Fitch made having a class at 5 pm fun. The only assessments were Canvas quizzes that were done at home (so you could use notes). The final exam was a paper that you could choose any topic to write about. Go to class and try to participate, but if you can't go, just let her know and she will give you 4/5 for participation.

Fitch was one of my favorite professors. She is funny, keeps her lectures interesting and interactive. You have to show up to class, but quizzes and assignments are fairly easy. A lot of guest speakers, no textbook. You do have to read a book for a series of assignments but I personally didn't read it and got a 100% on all of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She takes literally a month to respond to emails, even though she states that she responds within 24 hours. Her TA grades everything (tough grader) and her quizzes are vague. Pay attention to the lectures (not her lecturing either) and take really good notes. The class was interesting but she was never the one to provide any kind of feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Everything she discussed was made clear by her. She cares more about the students rather than just their grades

Fitch is an amazing professor. She clearly lays out what you will be doing in class and her powerpoints are great. She does do an attendance/participation grade for pretty much every class so just show up and its easy points. Quizzes are online and you can do them on your own time. She has a lot of guest speakers and I enjoyed that a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I've only been here one semester but I love Professor Fitch! She is very helpful not only for the class but also gave me great career advice. She really knows a lot about HTM and has worked in pretty much every area of hospitality so she is perfect to teach intro to HTM. The class isn't hard if you work hard you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was definitely intimidating on day 1 but it ended up being very manageable. Participation is a huge part of the grade and you have to speak up, not just be present. It is a capstone course but wasn't super difficult. There were a lot of group projects so make sure you pick a good group. Need to read the textbook to do well on exams.

Who am I to soil the 5/5. Florian is a super passionate professor. Even though this is a capstone class, it really is not as serious as he makes it out to be. That syllabus is scary, but it's because it details the rest of the course + instructions. Participation is EXTREMELY important, go to class, talk. He's blunt, but don't be butthurt haha.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Florian is one of the best professors I have taken this year. The class itself is by no means an "Easy A," but he is very caring and gives insightful feedback. Come to class and participate (showing up alone is not enough), read the case studies thoroughly, and work hard on your group projects. His teaching style makes it well worth it.

Dr. Zach is an awesome professor. He's super personable and engages with the students a lot, which means he really values participation. This is not a skippable class, as he weighs attendance super heavy. But if you show up, ask a few questions, and pick a good group for projects, you're set for the semester.

Once again, Flanagan is the man-again. Second class with him, and I can guarantee that you will have a good understanding of the subject if you have him. His teaching format is very effective, and he makes everything clear. Tests are hard, but practice problems help. Very generous with partial credit!

Great professor, had him for linear algebra (math 2114). Tests are very straight forward if you do all the homework and the review materials he provides. Make sure to study up on your theory for this class, he likes to ask true/false questions where you will need to provide backup and/or proofs.

Dr. Flanagan was a really good professor, but my only complaint is that he has a very monotoned voice, and I could not pay attention. He provides a lot of resources for tests and assignments, and he explains everything really well.

Flanangan was a great professor for this class. The homework setup was made to be clear and easy to perform on which can help your grade well. His exams were fair in terms of difficulty and the practice tests have a similar concept to what will be on the actual exam (its not always 1-to-1). I may have sucked at this subject, but he's great.

He uses guided notes that are actually really helpful, I recommend printing or downloading them--I tried just writing things down as he went, since there's a lot of blank space allotted so it feels like a lot of paper and I was struggling to keep up. Easy homework, easy pop quizzes, easy class, very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fair grader. The best. Everytime something goes wrong, I always remember the wise flanner phase "Looks like the dish/washer method won't help me out of this one..." I would definitely take him; you will do well if you pay attention and ask him for help.

Best teacher you can have for Calc 2. Gives packets of notes that you can easily follow. If you complete the homeworks and written homeworks, you can easily take the tests as they are very similar questions. You can easily ask him questions after class and he is very good about answering emails. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He uses fill in the blank notes which are very helpful imo. His Canvas page is always very organized and he posts filled in notes and practice tests before exams. Other people have mentioned the number of WebAssigns, which I agree is a lot but necessary for the course. Calc 2 is hard, but Dr. Flanagan makes it easier.

HIGHLY recommend Kyle. He is super nice and his lectures are easy to follow and concise. He grades very fairly, and it is not difficult to get an A on tests as long as you do the practice problems in the textbook. Only thing I didn't like was the daily WebAssigns. But still they help you prepare and are harder than the tests anyways.

Had him for MATH 1226, such a fantastic professor. The lectures were easy to follow and quite helpful with fill-in notes and phases to ask questions. Very willing to help during office hours. Gives partial credit generously on exams. There's lots of webassigns but I'd say it's manageable overall.

Flanagan was a great professor for MATH 1226. His lectures were paced very well and he shows that he wants his students to do well. Attendance is not mandatory, but it helps to go he posts notes before the tests and prepares you well for the final.

Dr. Flanagan is kind and helpful. I had him for MATH 1226. He's very patient and always giving plenty of examples and willing to stay back after class to answer questions. If you don't understand the notes, my advice is to ask questions, go to his office hours, do the homework, and you'll succeed. The math lab in McBryde is a great resource too.

I had him last semester for MATH2114 (Linear Algebra) and he is the best math professor I've had! He's extremely caring, gives great feedback, and explains concepts thoroughly. He uses fill-in-the-blank notes which are very helpful! His homework assignments and tests are reasonable, and he grades fairly.

A Really great professor! I took them for MATH 1226. Everything you need is in the notes, and their tests are SUPER fair. They're not the kind of professor to set you up for failure. As long as you understand the lecture notes, this class can be manageable. Plus, he is a extremely fair grader and always give partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a great teacher who makes sure everyone understands the material required, and there are no surprises on the tests. If you go to class and do the homework, you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Did great on the tests, low pressure

Flanagan is an amazing professor. He explained everything clearly in class and took the time to answer questions during class and within office hours. All his test and assignment questions are very reasonable and include content clearly went over in class. If you are confused, go to office hours! He is always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He can be a little monotone when speaking for a while, but speaks clearly and delivers a lot of good information in lecture. He gave good feedback when taking points off on graded assignments which I think really helped me improve and do well. He was always willing to answer questions and make sure you had were confident in your understanding.

Very good instructor who clearly cares that his students learn the material well. You will have no trouble passing his class if you show up to lectures and ask questions. Easily one of the best math teachers I've ever had.

Flanagan is one of the best instructors I've had in mathematics. He is very personable, and is willing and able to help each student individually. He did a very good job introducing concepts in a way that is understandable for everyone, and answers questions completely.
Kyle Flanagan has been a great teacher for a difficult class. He takes the time in class to answer everyones questions and makes sure everyone understand the material. Highly recommend!

Kyle was the best. He was a very nice person, taught the material very well and clearly and would always answer questions before anything else. Although he wasn't so lenient on the written assignments, he gave good feedback and was one of my favorite professors I've had

This guy is one of the best in the math department. He wants each student to succeed and makes sure to answer any questions. Not only is he an excellent instructor, but he also is a cool guy! If you see a spot available for a class with Kyle, take it immediately!

He was a grad student teaching Calculus when I took his class, and honestly a great teacher. May seem monotonous at first but if you pay attention, he's very clear in his lectures and grading and tests etc. Gives great feedback on tests and assignments. Overall great teacher and you should be fine if you pay attention and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The first test will be brutal, just accept that. He includes a lot of "for life, not the test" info in his lectures so be prepared to filter through that to get to the actual material. His method of teaching can be confusing, the tutors will be your best friends. However, he is very clear about what will be on the tests, and has good office hours.

He's definitely a bit intimidating at first, but it's because he holds his students to a high standard.
Be prepared for him to grill you with questions! You end up learning so much from him in the end though, since he's so dedicated to teaching --- I don't think I would have been prepared so well for higher-level courses without learning from him.

I'm currently taking ISC 1106 with Professor Schubot, and he's an amazing professor! He masters walking the fine line between grading fairly without trying to beat our GPAs into the ground. His PowerPoint presentations may be a bit difficult to follow when studying, but he excels at explaining the content in class!
He may judge you for being stupid, but he'll still help you. He lets the TA grade everything, so your grades may depend on your TA.
He is so funny! Wants us to genuinely understand the material and will spend extra time if he needs to to teach us sections we don't understand. Respects us and wants us to master biology.

Dr. Schubot was my ISC professor this past semester and I really enjoyed his lectures. Although he does make you work for the good grade, he is willing to help you get there in any way he can. I definitely recommend attending his office hours as he does a great job of breaking down difficult concepts into simpler terms.

Very helpful professor.  In the molec bio class he gets a guest speaker almost every 3 lectures to give us an idea of the research going on on campus.  So it is a good class to take if you're looking to get a better idea of your research interests. The tests are half multiple choice and half written.  He does curve.  He has a cool German accent.

Genuinely cares about his students learning the material and does a good job at somehow bringing giving Molecular Biology "personality."  Don't be afraid to ask questions before, during, or after class, sometimes he just doesn't have the time to go into long explanations during class, but he's great at clearing things up!
Great professor, the class is hard but there are ample extra credit opportunities.

Professor Flintsch was not ready to teach at all. Didn't understand how to use Canvas. Uploaded assignments late and still expected them to be turned in on the same due date. Never responded to emails. Consistently traveling with no regard to the semester, would cancel classes, put them on Zoom. Never gave feedback. worst professor there is.
Great Teacher
Best professor i've had in a long time
Best professor i've had in a long time

The lectures for this course were very interesting and engaging.
However, the grading system could use some work.
The exams are very difficult and long. It would be nice to have more extra credit opportunities to help with the grade. Class supports naturally talented ones. Hard work did not help me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher and a really nice/caring guy. He wants you to succeed and will help you if you go to him. In general, it is a difficult class and exams are hard but the more you go to office hours and get help, the better you will do.
Very clear at teaching. Would recommend, but can make the fluid lab difficult than other sections.

No grades homework, only chapter quizzes and exams. Definitely the better option than Scardina if you're trying to get a decent grade. Still a difficult class, but at least you have a chance with this prof.

Homework is optional so the class grade is essentially composed of exam grades. 4 exams (lowest dropped) + final exam. The homework is great practice for the exams and the recitation sessions are exremely useful. If you study these, you should do fine on the exams. This prof also makes the class fun and is far less terrifying than Scardina.

I didn't really like the class, his way of teaching is rather old school and exams are on scantrons. Idk, if I studied I coulda gotten an A+, but it just wasn't very interesting to me and the tastings werent my favorite either but that could be different for you.

he's really nice and passionate about the subject. i learned so much. the work is all pretty easy just make sure you study for exams bc the info can get pretty detailed. be mindful that there are 3 wine tasting nights--most of the classes are normal lectures!
Passionate professor. Only once per week and homework is reasonable. Would recommend

i had this professor online so there isn't much to say but they were nice and i found their weekly email reminders very helpful. the class itself is pretty easy with powerpoints to read, weekly discussions, quizzes, and a few assignments here and there. nothing too difficult, i'd recommend!

MGT 3074. Lisa is very sweet and clearly cares about the students. Her classes drag on a bit and will always go until she's fully out of time. Every week there is a required 500 word discussion question post with a 200 word response. My groups paper ended up being 26 pages for the first half and about 20 for the second so get ready to write.

Dr. Lisa was great. She explained everything very well, and I never felt ambushed by the questions on any of the quizzes or exams. If you show up to class and read all of the required sections in the online textbook, you should have no trouble getting a good grade.
Theres a few pop quizzes. If you aren't good at timed test/quizzes you won't do your best.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The best professor at tech! She is super caring and her lectures are actually interesting. Her reviews before tests are awesome as she basically tells you everything on the test. Totally would take her class again.

One of the easiest classes I've taken. She's so kind and breaks up her lectures with discussions and you can tell she wants to hear from students about the topic. Show up to class, especially before an exam and she will tell you exactly what will be on the tests, got easy 100s

Dr. Foriest is by far my favorite professor I have ever had. The class involves a bunch of discussion, but she is more than willing to adjust. She is well educated and able to provide different insights into criminal justice that no every professor is able to have. She also does not require a lot of homework. Would definitely take her again.
He's a good teacher but VERY HARSH GRADER. ALSO THE TESTS ARE VERY HARD.
He is good overall. Just prepare well for test 2.

Prepares you well for the final exam and has harder tests than the average professor. He rounds up grades at the end though due to him grading tougher. Cares about every student although he really appreciates and gets to know the students who care as much about his class as he does. Go to office hours. Thank me later.

Show up to his lectures. I can't stress this enough. I had perfect attendance at his 8am and it was a relatively easy A. However, this class is in general, hard to get an A in. His test averages are lower than other professors, but he makes up for it in the rounding of the final grade. Also, he prepares you well for the final CTE exam.

Professor Fowler is simply the most engaging professor I have ever had at Virginia Tech. Each lecture genuinely feels like a story, and you almost feel like you are discovering linear algebra on your own rather than being taught it. He is extremely funny and approachable, but with that being said this is still a challenging class.

I had Professor Fowler for a short time (dropped class only because my workload was too high). He was a very good professor in the time I had him and was funny and nice. He did grade difficultly but also offered extra credit if he made a mistake (seems like he made mistakes on purpose haha). Highly recommend

Professor Fowler has been my favorite math professor so far at VT. Show up to class every day and you will do well. He wants you to succeed and will learn everyone's names (who show up). He will give out some extra credit if you come to class regularly and submit the assigned practice problems.

was such an engaging professor for a relatively boring topic. the last two tests were really hard in my opinion, but thats more just reflective of the class. he was very accessible for office hours and never made me feel bad if i had to ask a quick question about homework. genuinely a really nice guy

Amazing professor, used humor and socialability to engage his students into the material he's teaching. Material was quite difficult, and I definitely could've gotten a better grade. Homework is really important, and your grade is essentially 3 tests and your homework average. A bit of a picky grader, but could be reasonable. Overall goated prof

Professor Fowler is a wonderful professor. His lectures are very well done and makes linear algebra easy to understand. Go to office hours and you will do well in this class! His teaching is beyond effective and he is overall just a good person.

Very chill and funny man. Made coming to class enjoyable. Taught well. Kind of a picky grader, which he admits cuz he deeply cares about the material. Test 1 pretty good, test 2 hard, the final was just a test 3 (pretty chill). Posts practice exams with key. Review classes. Enjoyed his class. Hopefully he teaches combinatorics.

Great. Saved my grade from the nightmare which was Jonathan Hughes. Hughes was so bad at his job, and had to be taken out of teaching mid way through the semester. Half way through the course I had no clue how to do anything, but I left the class feeling curious to learn more.

Fowler is fantastic. If you are in his class, you will do just fine.
Entertaining prof. Him and his TA were pretty strict graders. Overall, I learnt far more the textbook than I did from class.

I didn't get an amazing grade and I love this guy. I feel that should explain everything. Cool dude. Liked the lectures, eager to explain everything and makes attendance worth it. Material is hard, plan to take this as your only math class in a semester (don't repeat my mistake). Office hours are great. Doesn't make you feel dumb for asking.
Made the classes fun to go to and engaging. He also was able to dumb down the terms and processes so it was understandable.

Had discrete with him and I'm so sad im not taking another math class with him, it's giving me like depression. But anyways LOVEEE garrett he's relatable, HELLA FUNNY and bro actually teaches stand up comedy in math. He makes the hardest things sound simple. Like genuinely one of the greatest human I've ever met. Seriously gotta love a bald baddie!

Took discrete with him, best professor I've ever had AND I actually learned the material. I'm taking Linear Algebra now and I'm having no problem dealing with the logic element of that class thanks to Fowler.

Had 8am linear and he made me still want to go to class! He puts things as simple as he can so that it makes sense and works closely with students during class and at office hours to make sure they understand. Jokes with the students and makes sure everyone is comfortable.

Very chill professor for Linear Algebra. Prepared very well for tests with both assignments that mirrored the test format and practice exams. Textbook is "required", but only for homework assignments and not required reading.

EXTREMELY chill guy. Best math lecturer I've ever witnessed. Makes hard things so simple and understandable. Homeworks and tests are not too hard. He is young and connects with students easily. He knows that school isn't the most important thing and his policies and general nature reflect that, but he's also the best lecturer I've ever had. goat🐐

This is the kind of professor that makes you not want to miss a single lecture. He is passionate and knowledgeable on the subject while also explaining each concept thoroughly. Graded by 3 exams worth 25% each and 25% worth of weekly homework. Totally manageable workload and exams are a fair expectation of what you should know. Chill and funny dude
Great professor, super easy class, nothing to worry about if you get Garrett 🙏

As all the other reviews say, Garrett is one of the best math teachers you can get. He really cares about his students and wants you to learn and succeed. His tests and homeworks are pretty hard though, and supposedly his discrete class is much tougher than other sections (because he actually wants you to learn) so take that into consideration.

I got a really bad score on my first test, went to his office hours, and I felt like he cared more about helping me succeed on my next two tests than any other prof I've had. He's a funny guy, and treats students as his equal. He teaches hard math, but is very open if you need help, and makes math feel fun again.
Great teacher. Discrete Mathematics is a hard subject (to me) but there's no way I would've passed without this guy.

Best professor especially given the amount of content we cover. Typical week includes around 2 open note quizzes and 1 homework assignment. Everything except the 3 tests are open notes and he will help you in office hours with questions/look over homework before turning it in. Easy if you do your work and pay attention to lectures
Just take him bro.
By far the best math Professor I've had.
Lover of Math, Hater of Physics
Never wrote a review for anyone in my life. He made me write one. That's how great this professor is.

He's such a fun person to spend class time with but he still gets easily through all the content in an in-depth and understandable way. His personality is definitely very distinct and some people could certainly not enjoy it as much, but I think most people in my class enjoyed the energy he brought to class

*2114 Garrett is probably the best teacher I've had for all of my 14 years of school. Super smart passionate guy, super laid back. I was not looking forward to linear algebra at all, but he has sparked my interest in it by a lot. HW can be a little tough but the revise and resubmit is so clutch. Best VT math teacher.

*math 2204 
i cannot even begin to explain how amazing garrett is in just 350 characters, but i'll start by acknowledging the passion and dedication he has to math and the success of his students. captivating lectures that make you engaged purely by garrett being garrett. homeworks can be challenging but in a good way. 1000/10

Fowler has a soft spot for students which makes him a heck of a good instructor. He's lively in class and heavily encourages questions since the material takes a while to click. Do take advantage of homework corrections though, since the few graded materials makes it pretty tough to recover from a bad HW grade. HW is usually tougher than the tests.
great guy
Gave extra credit for attendance when tests came around. Will bake cookies if class does well on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As all the others 5 star reviews suggest, Virginia Tech students are lucky to have Garrett teach here. He is a cool guy and a superb lecturer. Garrett is an amazing instructor, and does his best to make sure you can succeed and get an A. I only got a B because I was being lazy. There is a lot of homework, but for good reason.

Garrett is an amazing professor. I wouldn't say he's a tough professor, calculus is just hard :( Attending class is important because of the extra credit and lectures, but he never took attendance and there's supplementary videos on canvas anyway. Genuinely one of the best professors I've had-He's hilarious and his homeworks are actually fun.
Dude is honestly the best professor for 1225. Highly recommend to go to his office hours early and often and you should be fine in this class.

Assigns very hard homework but the very hard homework makes the class difficult but the tests not so bad since you are very prepared for them. He has many office hours outside of class which allows easy access to help when you need it, as well as the fact that he uses a chat app, if you need to reach him over a break or when he isn't on campus.

Had him for Calc 1, 2, 3 & would take him for more classes. While difficult, he teaches very well and it pays off in the end. He's funny, understanding, and passionate to teach. His HW's are difficult, but he gives you every opportunity for help. His review sessions are so helpful. Even if you don't have him, he's always willing to help.
I had Garrett for two semesters (calc 1 and 2). Would take the classes over again (tenfold). Even if you don't get into his class, go say hi to him at his office hours.
Garret is really a phenomenal teacher. Such a cool guy and great at explaining things. Calc is hard though and the math department at vt is unforgiving.

Garrett Fowler is one of the best professors I have ever had. His homeworks are quite difficult, however, if you work together with other people and go to his homework reviews/office hours you should be fine. I had him for calc 2 and our tests were untimed and easier than the homeworks. He is the single best thing about the math department at VT.

If you're reading this review because you just ended up with Garrett as an incoming freshman, congratulations, you got the best professor possible for this class. He actually cares about students grades and will stand up for your grade if the department grades in a way he thinks is too harsh. He also makes himself very available to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While attendance isn't mandatory, it is very difficult to do well if you don't attend them
So far for my college career this has been by far my best teacher, every day he comes into the classroom with a good attitude and is always ready to help his students.

Fowler is amazing. Definitely saved me from dying in calc 1 and I have him again in calc 2. He is caring, his lectures are entertaining. I wouldn't recommend if you want a "professional lecturer" who talks in monotone. Homework help sessions/office hours were amazing. In his calc 2 currently he has no time limit on tests, and I love it.

Garrett is absolutely the best professor at Virginia Tech. The math department is saved by him and him only. The lectures are enjoyable, and while the homework is hard, it really makes you understand the concepts and do well on the tests and exams. GARRETT IS THE BEST.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Garrett is the best. He really cares about his students. He was able to keep me awake during my 8am with him. He does give rather difficult homework, but he is always willing to give help. The homework is usually harder than the test, so I always felt very prepared going into the tests. One of the best teachers I've had in all my education.

Though Calc 1 is overall a very challenging course, Garrett really makes it enjoyable and his lectures, extra help sessions, and office hours are all really useful. He is understanding when it comes to turning things in late and helps students when he can.
Best professor I ever had, would have failed if I had another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor in the math department by far. Charismatic, Caring, Informative, and HONEST about the work load, tests, your grade, exc.

reviews.comment: Great Professor. VT math sucks but he probably sucks the least for Calc 1. Pretty fun and entertaining guy and is really understanding when it comes to late work/other circumstances. Easily accessible outside of class and supportive. The class is still hard but do really well on webassigns and homework to carry your grade and you should pass.

reviews.comment: Hard intro to Calculus on-campus freshmen year, but he made it bearable and I loved every second in his classroom
Best math teacher I've ever had BY FAR. If you can get into his class you're set. Hilarious guy and phenomenal teacher.

Garrett is one of the best math teachers I've ever had. He explains concepts with patience and clear direction, adding in fun comments and making the class enjoyable in general. Some of my friends who had different professors struggled greatly until they started going to his reviews, and he soon became a fan favorite among Calc 1 students.

His lectures may seem chaotic at times but, 2021 was his first year teaching. Outside of class, if you ever need reinforcement about the concepts or have questions he is typically available. He has flexible officer hours throughout the entire week. As someone who failed the first test with a 56, going to his office hours helped to achieve a B.

Lectures are non-comprehensive of exam content. Only passed the exams because I throughly read the textbook - it's seriously the only way. The textbook is cheap and accessible. He has moments of being funny but, talks in circles, and is very disrespectful. I wouldn't ever take his course again.

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor May's class. It was very group-work and test-heavy, but I felt it was manageable. While he gave harsh feedback during presentations, it's necessary for future marketers and advertisers to experience pushback.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. May has closed note, on paper exams. They're not super hard, and he gives you free points back on every one. His class has a lot of projects and presentations, and 3 case studies that you just have to talk once in class to get credit for. He is a little boring unless he mentions his personal life, and always debates back if you say anything.

The class is horribly structured.Has numerous assignments you need to simultaneously work on which wouldn't be as bad if he actually took the time to clearly go over what he wants you to do.Exams are hard. He belittles students whenever they answer a question in class. Genuinely never had a worse professor. I almost feel like he tries to be awful.

Prof. May isn't a bad person, but the class is awful. The lectures are some of the most boring things you will ever sit through and are riddled with charts that don't make sense. Exams are borderline impossible to prepare for so actually buy the textbook (it's your only hope.) Wouldn't even consider taking the class again.
I have no problems with Professor May, but I do wish class was structured differently than just lectures. This material could include so much class/group discussion or even activities.

Boring lectures with bad slides. Exams are on scantron and are hard to prepare for. You have 3 exams including a final, 25 page final paper, and 2 presentations that he grades hard. Also have a few case studies that he doesn't remind the class of so you have to look at the syllabus to see when they are. Do not take him there are better professors

The TA's for this course were ridiculously harsh graders. They were very picky and just over the top. The professor was not vert good and not great to learn from. The course wasnt hard at all, just not fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Frost is a fine professor, but her TA's are the issue. I received an 85 on a post class reflection form for “not having depth” and oftentimes the TA's do not even grade based on professor Frost's rubrics. Would avoid this class if not required.

She's not AWFUL, its her TAs. She gives opportunities for grades but she's a trough professor. For 1000 level class the work load is insane. Her TAs will give you horrible grades that are straight chat gpt and the whole class notices it. Honestly this class would have been so much more enjoyable if the TAs were even in the class and were helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Frost is a great professor/person. She is very passionate about the topics she teaches, BUT can lecture for a long time, and it can be boring. Her GTA is a brutal grader. reviews.comment: Tough grader with little explanation as to the grading scale, TA is not very helpful, group projects and writing assignments are tedious. Take with a different teacher if you can.

reviews.comment: Dr Frost is very nice, but the GTA's grade ruthlessly, and she assigns A TON of reading, 40+ pages per class. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes I've ever taken. TA's are so picky that you would think this is a graduate school level class. Dr. Frost doesn't grade anything.

reviews.comment: I understand why people could think she is a tough grader because her class is pretty hard. reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you absolutely need to and if you do need to I can only pray for you. Her grading is ruthless and the readings are long and confusing. reviews.comment: Do not take this class. It is by far the worst class I have ever taken at Virginia Tech. The grading is incredibly harsh (especially for such a low-level class), but with very limited feedback, and it is near impossible to get any help or support. I regret not dropping this class.

This is the worst class I have ever taken. I have never had a teacher grade so harsh yet so densely on papers. You have a strict word limit and the TAs grade like this is Harvard Law. It is ridiculous. The teacher will not do much to help you and if you ask for her to help on papers she will be beyond. Don't take this class. Worst decision ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: This has a 1 because 0 wasn't an option. Difficult teacher, nit-picky Ta's, useless readings, unnecessary pop quizzes. I'm glad I never have to take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pop quizzes for the incredibly long assigned readings are basically to encourage attendance but destroy your grade, papers graded intense, and lectures feel repetitive. I did learn some from this class and enjoyed the the professor and material but the readings and grading ruined this class. Glad it's a one and done requirement for my major. 6/10.
