reviews.comment: Dr. Frost is so kind and passionate about her job- However, the grading is  ridiculously nitpicky and harsh. I'm a fairly good writer in most classes but was graded poorly in this class. The TA's do not help much
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: In my opinion, Professor Frost is great.  She explains things well and is willing to work with you, just ask. TAs are nitpicky but she'll let you appeal a grade if you want. Just show up to class and pay attention.  Quizzes are super easy, discussion posts are simple, grading criteria for final paper and exams is reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was a good professor. assigned a lot of reading which was hard to keep up but you can still get a good grade in the class if you don't read. attendance mandatory but gave us two absences free. 2 majors papers and reading quizzes throughout

Started out good, but attendance is apart of your grade, and only 2 get dropped. Grade is made up of two exams (each 25%) and an essay (another 25%). The other 25% is made up of quizzes, discussion post, and attendance. Classes are long and kind of boring/repetitive if you read the textbook. There's ALOT of information she covers.

I like Dr. Frost, but she's a tough grader. Class started off great but then quickly got annoying. Her TA for the semester had no mercy and nitpicked every essay I turned in. The lectures are super boring and she would drag it out to LITERALLY the last seconds of class. Textbook was not easily accessible and it was annoying to have to use it.

Honestly this class is monotone. It's long, drawn out and boring. You need the text book, but not for daily reading. More for papers and what not. She covers everything in the textbook in her PowerPoint. There is a lot of writing for this class, 3 discussion posts, one major paper, and writing sections in each exam. Frost is nice though

Took this in Spring 2022. She was very accessible outside of class and is genuine in helping her students. Grades were very test-heavy, as you can excel as much you want with formatives, but don't do well on 2 of the 3-4 exams, you're not going to make it. I find the class overwhelming but is good for people who are diligent and hard-working.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: BEST online async class I've ever taken. Set up very well and helps you actually learn the information in a way that makes you legitimately comfortable with it. Dr. Fox is very accessible, caring, and gracious with deadlines, and she has a great sense of humor. Tests were difficult and weighed heavily on your overall grade, but also open-note.

Dr. Fox knows what she is talking about it. You're not allowed to use your laptop for notes, so prepare to take notes by hand or on a tablet. The content itself isn't difficult to understand if you read the textbook and do the practice. However, the class is test heavy so put in the effort of studying for the grade you want, exams are open note.

the resources she provided to study for the exams had little to no relation to the actual tests.  Why would you give your students a "final exam review" canvas quiz if the test isn't structured in any way like the practice, and the topics are different.  

It's like I had to be an economics guru to get an A in this god forsaken class.
Tests aren't really like the reviews and the teaching is not good. Not good to learn from.
Dr. Fox always wants to help her students; has a great ability of getting students what they need to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Fox is a great professor and you can tell she is really passionate about economics. However, the class exams are hard so you really have to work for the grade. She does curve for the exams which helps a lot with your grades. Go to her office hours! She is really nice and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fox has good intentions, but her class is just physically impossible. I took this class online making it 100x harder to pass. You have tons of homework each week and she makes the exams basically impossible. They cover things that you've never seen in your life because they were not taught in class. Take this course with a different prof.

Professor Fox is okay. I don't really recommend, though, because I don't think I learned a lot in her class. Her tests were very hard because it covered things she didn't go over in class. She's a nice teacher, but I don't think her lectures were very helpful, and I feel like I didn't learn well in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her exams are extremely challenging, so you really need to study for them. There's usually a good curve on them. She is a really smart lady and knows her stuff, but makes the class kind of difficult. If you take her, make sure you're ready for challenging exams. She'll replace your lowest exam with your final if you do better on the final.
Do not take her class. She is extremely hard for no reason and her lectures and notes do not help on the test. Take any other professor for Econ 2006 and you will get an A.

Dr. Fox is a great professor who is definitely well educated in her field. I would highly suggest her to anyone that is an econ major or is interested in econ. However, if you are just taking this class because you need to, I would suggest getting another professor. Her tests are incredibly difficult without any curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fox is has amazing and helpful lectures. I would recommend her for Econ 2006 however, her tests are difficult and you have to work for it. I enjoyed how she runs her class. She knows what she is talking about.

I think the bad reviews are unwarranted. The material can be challenging, but she'll literally bend over backwards to help you. Frequently, she'd schedule study sessions way after hours. The issue is, typically only a few people would show up. If you use your resources, you'll be fine. I found the people who didn't were most likely to complain.

Signed up due to it being a synchronous class, but it was immediately made asynchronous. Unfortunately, learning purely through an online textbook and sporadic videos made it difficult to grasp the material. She was good at communicating due dates, but was harder to reach for specifics. The class should not have been as tough as it was made.
Drop this class. Impossible exams with rare and minimal curves. Exams overly challenging for no reason pick a different prof.

This was the hardest class I have taken in my life for no reason. I don't know how she is in person because this class was online but I am not gonna pick her again. Her lectures and textbook have none of the material covered on the exams so you can't prep for it. Good luck if you get her
Class is a lot of work especially if its not your major and you just need it to fulfill the requirement. Better off with another teacher. Tests are not easy and you have to answer free response.

Dr. Fox is probably your best bet for Econ 2006. She is very knowledgeable in the subject and knows what she's talking about, she gives you multiple attemps on homework so it's almost impossible to get below a 90 on it, and she often extends deadlines for your convenience. Her last two exams are kind of difficult but if you study you'll be fine.

Fox was a great professor, especially for the class being in the Fall 2020 (all online). Her class is somewhat difficult, but if you put in the effort it's easy to get an A. She makes the lectures pretty interesting. She's one of the professors I wish I had the ability to have face-to-face because you could tell she was really knowledgeable in Econ
She's a decent choice for Econ 2006. Tests are a little hard due to the free response part, but she made things during COVID really easy to understand.

Her lectures were hard to follow. She drew things on her iPad that were pretty hard to seem lots of jagged lines. The concepts were much more complex than I was expecting from a macro class. She's a very knowledgeable and nice professor who wants to help, but her class seemed unnecessarily difficult. Still the best choice for 2006 at VT.

I had a really good experience in her class. She gives great lectures that actually explain the content that is on the exams. The homework comes from the online textbook, but every exam topic is actually covered in class and she will explain further if you ask. Lots of easy ways to rack up extra points and she will slightly curve exams if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher. She is really unorganized on her slides and would write everywhere on it, which makes it confusing. Also whatever she writes, you better write fast because then shell go to the next slide. As a college student, we had to pay so much for the program she wants us to use and another app. Her last 2 exams are also ridiculously hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is an interesting professor, but the material got very hard for me at the end of the class. I would recommend her though, as she knows what she is talking about. She treats the class like an AP course, with the exams having a "FRQ" section. She was an AP Econ exam grader, so it makes sense. She is a good choice if you have to take this class.

Open note quizzes and exams (quiz almost every class so keep up with the reading and go to class even though it is not mandatory). There is a large, semester-long team pop-up business project, but it seems a lot more daunting than it really is. Professor Freemal is super nice and is always willing to help and provide support.

She is super nice and an amazing person. The material is super easy but for some reason the quizzes and tests were always very hard despite being open notes. Attendance is not mandatory but she gives pop quizzes 2-3 times per week. She is super nice and means well but for some reason makes the quizzes and exams way too challenging.

reviews.comment: no attendance but quizzes about each chapter of textbook once a week minimum. exams are easy but worded weird for every question. couple of group projects but textbook is free. she be reading straight off the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor! There are pop quizzes so you do need to keep up with the readings. All exams are open note. There is a group project that lasts most the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I think she is good
Semester long group project takes a lot of time

Professor Friedel is knowledgeable and it's an interesting class. Grading on assignments is not harsh, but the midterm and final are very difficult, although weighted low. Lots and lots of reading and lecture heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Friedel is so knowledgable and nice! Very reading heavy and while attendance isn't mandatory, she does random pop quizzes often so its better to just go. She also is not a harsh grader but the exams (midterm and final) are hard. Though, they aren't weighted very heavy so if you do well on quizzes and other assignments, you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved professor Friedel! Her tests were hard, but they're weighted low so even if you don't do well, you can still get a good grade in the class. She'll also throw out 'unfair' questions if you make a good enough argument! Lots of reading outside of class, and attendance isn't mandatory, but you definitely should go. Would love to have her again!

Professor Friedel is a very kind professor who legitimately cared about my performance and learning in class. Her class is very content heavy and she expects participation and reading to be done outside of class to supplement her lectures. 

Her tests are hard, but weighted lightly. Do ALL the readings and participate in class and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is very straight forward and not too test heavy. Overall supplemental assignments are graded very lightly and can keep you at an A even if you average a C on tests. Attendance is not mandatory but she does allow you to retake quizzes you did poorly on if you show up and gives extra credit which really helps.

Professor Friedel is a great professor and you will do well in the class if you read the assigned readings, show up for class and study hard. She genuinely wants her students to do well and you will if you try. Had her for Environmental Law and taking her Ag Law class in the spring!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: awful do not take her class. She reads off her slides, tests us in things she did not bring up. She arbitrarily gave out 40% of her midterm exam to those who failed it, but did not give any extra credit to those who did not fail. Class is a waste of time, has nothing to do with law. I would call this class "history of the EPA" not "Environment Law"
She talks a lot so get ready to try and listen. Doesn't really give good explanations of questions before an exam.

Great professor, I look forward to taking her again next semester. A lot of textbook reading but the reading is interesting. Her tests are also hard, but feel fair. Definitely makes you work for it but it is offset by very interesting subject and engaging class. She is also new and still learning so I am sure she will become an even better prof.

Always comes to class with great energy. He always asks students if they understand the content he is discussing before he moves on to the next topic. If the class doesn't understand, he happily dissects the content to clear up confusion among students even if the discussion takes multiple classes. He has a very professional comportment

Professor Ding is a great teacher who understands college students. His lectures are monotone, but if you watch the videos provided beforehand and participate in class the next day, you will succeed in this class. He provides study guides that are very helpful. Participation matters.

This class was a breath of fresh air following the nightmare of ACIS 2504 with Ferris. The lectures are easy to follow, there is minimal homework, and he gives study guides that include everything that will be on the exam. The only textbook required is for the QuickBooks assignments, there are 5 and they take about 60-90 minutes. Very easy class!

Professor Ding will work with you if you have any problems. Just ask him for help, and he will try his best to help you. Lectures we're a little hard, but there are videos. He gives test review packets, that really help when studying for his tests.

Prof Ding was amazing. He did a really good job at explaining concepts, even though the class isn't easy at all. He was also very generous to students if they needed extra help, resubmissions, etc. He wanted to give you as many opportunies as possible to succeed. If you come to class and put the work in, you will get a good grade.

He is one of the most knowledgeable people, and does a great job of explaining the why behind a lot of questions. He applies this class to real world scenarios which shows his caring nature for students. Come to each class and give him 100% of your attention and you will pass. Has the highest test scores of any 2116 professor for a reason.

He is a poor graduate teaching assistant. He doesn't do a good job of teaching the ideas on the course. He regularly makes mistakes while teaching us and doesn't correct them. He frequently does problems in class, gets them wrong and then can't figure out why he got it wrong.

Good teacher, goes over quiz review right before every quiz. As long as you attend almost every, if not every class, and you put in the time outside of class she expects of you, then you will probably be alright. Most difficult part of this course was probably the projects, make sure you know your group and also make sure to start early.

She's a very nice person but she her class is pretty dense compared to other 2406 classes. What caught me off guard was the amount of work I had to put in outside of class. This class is not hard but is very tedious and the weekly quizzes will cook your grade.

This class is relatively difficult, 2 midterms, 2 group projects, and tons of content. But this professor is so kind and a great teacher. if you don't understand a lecture, you can learn it with the videos on canvas. ChatGPT (currently) does not understand the group project questions, so don't crutch on that. Any other prof, and i would've had a B.
She is way harder than the other BIT teachers. 2 hard projects and most teachers have none or 1 easy one. Tests are in person and the others are online and can do whenever.

Felt like high-school. I guess if you are a freshman or sophomore you'd be used to it but her class felt like I was in gradeschool all over again, where it was clear that grades don't matter and neither does learning. It's very basic but the steps are very repetitive and they become annoying to the point where I stopped caring.

Not a nice professor that doesn't gaf about you or your grade. She gives quizzes worth almost as much as exams every Tuesday and you have to learn material outside of class on Wednesdays. She's difficult to work with and tells you to contact disabilities if you're struggling in her course.

Attend lecture for extra credit, but isnt necessary since she posts all lectures online. Quizzes are alright as long as you attend lecture and quiz review on tuesdays. textbook isnt req. but if you struggle youll need it for practice problems. HW is easy, group projects are tedious. some lecture videos and notes have to be taken on your own time

she does not gaf about you, she gives INSANE projects- you will put in 40+ hours for one, and one is right before exam week. Quiz every week and the kahoots before the quizzes do not help and the material doesnt relate. you have to watch hours of videos BEFORE the lecture to understand the lecture. she is nice but not helpful and very test heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Group project sucked but Professor Fraticelli is extremely helpful and caring. She is pretty easy to reach and will help you if you get stuck. She prerecords videos for all topics on canva and also provides lab exercises to help.

Dr. Fraticelli cares about every student she has. She answers emails at any time of day and is here to help everyone. She does not try to trick you and gives lectures that are the same as the tests and quizzes. The format is consistent ever week, she is a great person!

Quizzes every Tuesday, but the review was very similar to the quizzes. We had lectures on Thursday and online lecture videos to watch over the weekend. The videos were long but, the pacing held me accountable to complete my work. She is by far the best prof. I've had at VT. 10/10 recommend

Dr. Fraticelli is a great professor, very nice, and wants you to succeed. Class is structured so that Tuesday is just review, followed by a quiz. I found this very helpful. Thursday is lecture, she really helps you understand the material, and you have to watch videos over the weekend. If you don't like work outside of class, this isn't for you.

I've taken 3 classes with her between undergrad and graduate level- there is no better professor to teach BIT at VT, IMO. She's prepared and organized with provided fill-in-the-blank / follow along notes (so you aren't trying to rush through writing absolutely everything), always reachable via email, and writes her own exams exactly like the notes

Great prof. Quizzes every Tuesday but the whole class period was quiz review first. You do have to watch about 45 min to an hours worth of lectures over the weekend but it isn't that bad. You also get extra credit points for going to the Thursday lectures which help on the exams. Exam are just like the quizzes. 10/10 recommend.
Great lecturer and wants you to succeed, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: While Dr. Fraticelli was a very nice person, her class was a complete disaster. The lectures were disorganized and confusing, and the fact that she made us watch them at home was ridiculous. There was no busy work, but the class felt unorganized and lacked structure. Unfortunately, her grading was also inconsistent and often unfair.

Fraticelli is the best professor ive had at VT. super kind and caring but also has a very organized course schedule. you gotta stay on top of the lectures and actually watch the videos outside of class. she is amazing and slays

I thought this was easier than 2405. Dr. Fraticelli is very quirky, fun, kind, and cares about the success of her students. Accessible outside of class, clear expectations, good lectures. Quizzes and tests are not too hard if you do the Labs, lectures, and Kahoots, time constraint is the hardest part. 2 group projects that are somewhat challenging.

I do not agree with any of positive reviews about her. I took her class last semester and it was awful. Only her kahoot questions were useful BUT WOULD SHOW US THE DAY OF THE QUIZ. Take Bowden or Simundza instead...I heard from other students that they actually cared about their students and learned the course.

Dr. Fraticelli is the best BIT 2406 professor you can take. Her class consists of Thursday lectures and a kahoot review/quiz on Tuesdays. If you show up to the Thursday lectures and do the kahoots the class will be very easy. There are two group projects with your choice of group members and she will help you alot during office hours.

class met 2 days a week. on one day she would do in class lecture and teaching, then on the second day of the week all of class would be spent doing a kahoot review and then the last 15 minutes are spent doing the actual in class quiz. to make up for the loss of day she would assign video lectures for you to watch before the quiz.

Dr. Fraticelli's class is taught through one in-person lecture a week, and then another ~1.5 hours of weekly asynch lectures. You can get by on 95% of the class by just attending class on Tuesday for the Kahoot! review sessions. Dr. Fraticelli cares significantly about her students mental health and is genuine when she says she is there to help.

Prof Fraticelli is absolutely amazing. She genuinely wants the best for her students whether it be academically or mentally. The kahoots are super super helpful before quizzes, but I would recommended watching her live lectures for extra help.
Easily the best teacher anyone could have for this class. She is very clear with everything and structures her class in a way for you to suceed.
She is the best!! There's quizzes every tuesday but the kahoot is SUPER helpful. The group projects weren't my favorite but other than that, the class wasn't bad at all!

This professor is amazing. Truly one of the best I have had a Virginia Tech. I struggled in 2405, but this class was wayyy easier for me. She does a great job of simplifying things. We have weekly quizzes (tuesdays) but she does a Kahoot review before all of them which is almost identical to the quiz. Take her class if you can.

Dr.Fraticelli is by far my favorite professor at VT. Don't buy the textbook it is unnecessary unless you really benefit from the HW problems, I didn't do any of the HW problems as they're not very similar to the style of quiz and test questions. Do the review questions thoroughly, and review your quiz before tests and you'll do fine.

tbh u don't need to come to class or buy the textbook. Even doing the ungraded hw is not necessary. She gives a review kahoot before the weekly Tuesday quiz and it's like exactly what's on the quiz. Sometimes i felt like even watching all the vids wasn't worth, just the kahoot during class. Weekly quizzes, 2 midterms, and final. Easy B+ take her
absolute best professor i've had here at vt. genuinely cares about each and every one of her students and is very easy to get in contact with. would totally take her class again!

This is not a tough class. There are weekly quizzes in this class and these questions are repeated on tests. Weekly Kahoot sessions really help. If you look over your quizzes before tests you'll be fine.

Dr Fraticelli is hands down the best professor I've had. She is super straightforward and makes note packets for every unit for you to follow. Made it super easy to learn. Reviews before every quiz too. Take her if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher absolutely cares about her job and the students.

Dr. Fraticelli is excellent! She obviously cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I took this class over the summer, so the pace was a lot faster than other classes, but it was still a breeze. Her lectures are thorough and the tests are built right off of them, so take good notes and you'll do just fine!

Dr. Fraticelli is my absolute favorite professor I have ever had. She clearly teaches exactly what she wants you to know for the quizzes and tests. There are quizzes for each chapter which really helped when preparing for the exams. If you put in the work and go to the lectures (or watch them later) then you will do really well in her class.
i barely attended class but i did read his lecture material and the textbook and was able to take quizzes and tests without any issues

He ignored student needs to force me to wait 35 minutes and 48 minutes for office hours then said he had no time to talk to me and walked off. He drags his kid to work, forcing uncomfortable situations he judges you against for his kid royalty treatment, unprofessional unethical lame. Avoid. & his wife Angela Scarpa blamed me for her taking things
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not listen to slandering comments about Dr. Friedman. His class is really tough, but it is a high level class and if you work for it you will be rewarded. He is extremely smart and well-read, and is not arrogant at all. Definitely don't be afraid to go to his office hours for extra-help, and he will give opportunities for extra credit points!
I think that failure to consistently show respect toward how persons of color have to work minute by minute 10X harder, longer displayed unworthwhile fluctuating effort and unproductive.
He showed more concern about his feelings and wants than teaching or students. He got emotional twice.

If you study for his tests, he is not that difficult grading-wise.  If you go to his office hours, he is more than happy to discuss any issues you have.  He even makes suggestions for papers.  He is a well respected man in the field and really knows a lot about the topics, but still makes it straight forward and easy to figure out.

Are you people nuts? Easily the most all-around well read member of the faculty and more than willing to share his knowledge with people that are willing to listen. There is no arrogance about him... Considering the depth and breadth of his knowledge, I would say he's humble. Probably not a favorite among folks who expect to be given a good grade.
Easy to understand, tests are difficult and challenging.  Studying will get you through with a B.

I didn't do well in his biopsych class, but that was all my fault. I also had him for psychophysiology. I actually really tried in that class and made an A. Although he is arrogant, difficult and strange to deal with, if you try hard in his class, you will learn a lot.
Very unhelpful, arrogant, and brings problems from home into the classroom.  Unfair, stubborn, and just an all-around ****.  I passed his class, but he was a VERY unlikeable person!

Relatively easy class with lots of quizzes and discussion posts. He does not give out A's on discussion posts very often, mostly A-'s. He gives feedback on personal discussion posts and will also make an announcement of overall feedback of the class. There is a big writing assignment at the end of the semester, but it is not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Loved this class with Prof Fuller. The structure of the class makes it easy to stay on track and the course material is actually interesting so that helps. He gives sincere feedback on writing assignments and is overall a great guy.

I took Global Ethics with Fuller asynchronously and would definitely recommend the class. Your grade is made up of 2 papers and weekly readings/discussions. You do not have to devote a lot of time to the course, just be thoughtful/reflective. He also posts all of the content at the beginning of the semester so you can work ahead if you'd like.

Fuller was a very nice professor. The class mainly consisted of discussion posts, quizzes, and papers. However, one flaw is that there isn't a clear rubric for the discussion posts which can make it slightly difficult to understand what he wants. Despite this, he would give feedback and help students individually if they reached out to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Decent professor, but I felt disconnected from the lectures sometimes. Course is heavily based on PowerPoint lectures given in class. Attendance is not mandatory for lecture sections, but IS mandatory for discussion sections. There's some reading outside of class involved as well and do prepare yourselves for the writing assignments (essays)!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is seriously one of the best professors I've had. The classroom ambiance is friendly, but you must participate and at least express some understanding of the assigned reading. The material is very interesting and useful.  Attendance is mandatory but you also receive credit for it, so it is a win because you get points simply by showing up.

Prof Fuller really tries to make the information as interesting and relatable as possible. He posts all of the readings on the canvas page, so there's no need to buy anything. There are a few papers, and attendance at the Friday discussions is mandatory, but overall a very easy class with a great professor

Don't buy the books because he will provide links to 99% of the reading material anyway. You'll read assigned material before every class and then in class he will lecture on the topic and discuss as a group. Cares about his students and tries his hardest to make course interesting and relevant. Must read. Must go to class. Must participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took this a couple years back. Professor made exams fair and class was chill.

I took this class for granted. Tests were easy and fair (rare to come by at VT). Lectures were a little redundant and boring at times but at least he adds in comedic relief. If you take bio 1105 or1106 TAKE FREDDY! I took Rosenweig (big mistake). If you're wondering why I got a C, I had a high B in the class then messed up and bombed the final.

Dr. Fredericksen was one of the nicest professors I had my freshman year. I had him for BIO 1105 and 1106 and would take his class again in a heartbeat. Study quiz, practice test, and lecture material and you'll do great on the exams. He's understanding if you are sick with Hokie Plague, and responds to emails super quick. Love his shirts!!!

Really nice and helpful guy, tries to lighten up class material or connect it to interesting real-world scenarios when he can. I felt like all the assignments given were really well-based off the material but still pushed me to apply the information differently. Easy to do well if you use the resources he provides.

Fredericksen is a super sweet dorky guy but he really needs to speak up during lectures. He has a microphone but doesn't really use it and has a sort of monotone voice that made me fall asleep sometimes. His class is fairly easy as long as u study the material and do the study guides/practice tests.

Definitely choose this professor over others for intro to bio. The majority of the final grade came from tests, but the questions were almost directly from the practice exams provided, so if you studied them, you will do fine. The final was a bit hard. You have to show up to class because attendance is counted and there were group assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall, he was a good professor. His lectures could be a little boring, but he made little dad jokes and had some fun pictures in his slides. He posts two practice tests for each test, which are basically the tests so make sure to do those. He's really lenient when it comes to missing class and easy to access outside of class.

Very fun and understanding professor, however; attendance is mandatory and he does so with clickers. Tests are 70% of your final grade and it is a lot of material in tests. If you attend all the classes and study the practice exams and clicker questions (he recycles them on tests) you should definitely be able to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was very fun in class - super nice guy. Although the lectures can be boring, it is an intro to biology class. Definitely go to class but you are guaranteed to pass the test (and class) if you take the practice test!

Do the homework quizzes, ACTUALLY try to get clicker questions correct (yes, they're graded), and do the review sheets... you'll be just fine. The review sheets are quite literally almost identical to the tests. Would definitely recommend choosing over other bio profs, as I have heard the tests are more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is AMAZING! Such a wonderful guy and really knows his stuff! Tests were not easy but if you pay attention and take good notes you will be fine.

His lectures might be boring but I promise you will be happy to choose him over the other bio professors. Exams are easy/doable and he's just a cool, chill guy. Very easygoing and understanding. Tests are weighted heavily so your grade relies on them, and lucky for you he goes easy on you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fredericksen is a super cool dude. He makes lots of dad jokes in class and incorporates lots of funny pictures into his lectures. The set up of his class is the same as all the other BIOL 1105 professors at VT, but his tests are heavily based on the practice exam and the iClickers done during class, so make sure to write those down!

Overall, yes I would 100% choose prof Fredrickson over the rest of the Biology Profs. I will say, yes, he is kind of monotone in his lectures but honestly he's just a really chill guy. He really made the class feel low-key and he makes funny dad jokes. His exams were not hard at all because he just recycled clicker and quiz questions! Choose him!!!

Prof Todd is very nice, approachable, and funny at times. But his lectures are pretty dry, I have to fight to stay awake sometimes. Compared to other professors teaching the same class, he goes less in depth, and his tests are easier. So if you're looking for easy, choose him. But if you're looking for stimulating, choose another professor.
One of my favorite professors ever at Tech! He was very nice and the exams and homework assignments were very easy. Very helpful and truly wants what's best for all his students.

Really nice guy no doubt. Teaching wise, he was very monotoned & seemed to mainly just read off the PowerPoints. Intro bio has a lot of confusing material & he didn't always explain it very well. I will say though, the tests were mainly questions from clicker questions, quizzes, & practice tests that he gave out. That made the class much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's truly a lovely person, however as a professor, he could be better. He is very monotone during his lectures and seems to get confused easily about what he's talking about. I taught myself all the material and although his exams were fairly easy, he did not do a good job in teaching the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fredericksen is a super cool guy and fun professor. Made class easy and straightforward, but kinda boring lectures. Overall, if you study, go to office hours, and pay attention, then the class is Easy A or B.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is the easiest professor for BIOL 1105/1106. Took AP bio my senior year of high school so I did not study for his class. It is possible to get an A but intro bio at tech is difficult because of the lecture style. He will round your grade up and he is very nice if you are having problems. His test questions come from old Canvas quizzes/Iclickers.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Funny guy but lectures were incredibly boring & unhelpful to me. Very monotoned & he seemed to be bored by what he was teaching. The class material itself was very hard & he didn't do a great job in explaining it either, BUT the test questions were mostly all on canvas quizzes & clicker questions we had already done, so they were fairly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zhou was very kind and knowledgeable. She's set on her rules though so be on time, don't forget materials, and don't ask for freebies. Genuinely just show up, watch the videos, do work, try in lab and you'll be fine. She's super funny and explains material well. I had a very positive experience speaking with her one on one also! :)

Zhou Fu is the GOAT. Sweetest professor I've ever had. A lot of reviews on here for her Neuro lab class are complaining about the difficulty, but honestly it was not bad compared to other neuro classes. The lab was super fun and interesting. The lab procedures and directions were sometimes convoluted but Dr Fu was always willing to help.

It was a lot of work and reading for a 1 credit class, so be prepared to put in the work. She's so sweet and funny, but the lab itself has difficult quizzes and the final was a total curveball, it dropped so many's grade. But, labs itself are doable, just the quizzes and exams (which make most of the grade), are somewhat difficult.

I love Dr. Fu, but, this lab was too difficult for only a 1 credit lab. Pre-lab modules are often time-consuming and questions can be confusing (language barrier). Study for the in-lab quizzes, since your grade will rely heavily on them. Midterm and Final were ridiculous and tanked my grade. Mostly a TA-led lab and very little assistance was given.

Dr Fu made this lab way too hard for 1 credit as someone who got an A in neuro lecture. She seems sweet at first but isn't helpful at all and told us before the final not to email asking to round our grade because that's not how life works and life isn't fair. She is unclear (language barrier) and tested on things we had never learned/done in lab

she seems super sweet and caring in the beginning of the year, but her midterm and final were IMPOSSIBLE. everyone i knew failed. the final brought my grade down TWO LETTER GRADES. she also does nothing to help you in the lab so that sucks. and you have to study for the in class quizzes because they were harder than i thought they would be

Such a sweet human, she just doesn't allow for ANY wiggle room if you are struggling. She told me that there was no way I could succeed in her class mid-way through the semester and I had to learn through failure. I know she told other students the same thing.

Dr.Fu is amazing. She cares and is so so sweet. I loved this lab. Make sure you turn in everything on time. The class is heavily participation based so show up to every lab and you should be good to go. The class is run by the Tas but she is there if you ever need help.

*in this class you will be handling live cockroaches, crickets, and worms*

Dr. Fu was amazing! Complete online pre/post labs ASAP and review a little bit before in-class quizzes and you'll do fine. Labs were very helpful with understanding lecture material, so make sure you attend.

Homeworks were reasonable overall, though some were a bit difficult. The exams were difficult but solvable, and open-note. Having some experience in python/matlab/mathematica will make a lot of the homeworks and tests easier.

Lectures are hard to follow and monotonous. However, very clear notes and she does a few examples which helps a little. Lots of homework that was a tossup whether it was covered in class. Two AWFUL midterms harder than anything covered in class. The average raw for one of them was a 20. The project was time-consuming but preferable to a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fu provided clear lecture materials, that made homeworks a breeze. Homeworks are 40% of the grade, and we had 2-3 a week, but each was only 3-4 questions. Coding these will be helpful, as it can be recycled on 2 take home exams, which closely follow homework and lecture examples. There was no final, only a short FEM project!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Fu is a great professor who lectures material well and she's very nice. Definitely go to class even though it's not mandatory she may give extra credit. HWs were on Canvas only a few questions some took longer than others. Exams were timed on Canvas but very similar to HWs and class problems. No final exam, a short Abaqus project at the end!

This class was mainly just the textbook and then lectures were summaries of what you read. You NEED to read and do the homework in order to pass this class. Professor Galer was pretty helpful if you had questions and has real work experience in the accounting field, so he does relate everything to real world examples
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I personally liked Galer's cost class! The material is dry but he does his best to explain it in a way that simplifies it and makes it understandable. He drops quizzes, and allows cheat sheets sometimes. He is a very lenient professor, and will throw out questions if a majority performed poorly. I feel like I learned the material well.

Absolutely one of the worst. Sucks at teaching and does the bare minimum explaining things. only way to get a good grade in this class is to study on your own and read the book other. Take a different section if offered with a different professor. I was forced to take it with him because they only offered two sections and both were with him.

Maybe I'm being unfair by saying I wouldn't take him again, but I don't know if I'd consider him my professor in the first place. The lecture videos he posted were not of him, and I ended up emailing his TA's whenever I was having trouble. He seems to care about his students, but not the subject. His monotone voice made it tough for me to listen
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is structured well in theory, but he does not follow the schedule. My class was behind the entire semester. Requires reading a textbook chapter every week and taking an online quiz, which are not too difficult. However, the tests are awful. They include statistics and very specific details not discussed in class. Does curve tests though

boring class. he doesn't teach 50% of the material that is on his tests because they "come from the readings" aka read the ENTIRE book.  I think if he tests us on it he should at least go over it a little.  if you hate reading and are bad at it, do not take this class. its about 100pages of textbook reading per test and about 140 slides

The lectures are very boring and the tests are very tricky with specific questions. He requires writing assignments in and out of class. Attend class because a lot of the lecture material is on the tests. His PowerPoint slides are not helpful at all if you miss a class.
Extremely easy and extremely boring. Attendance is not recorded and uses power points. His tests can be very tricky, though. I expected an easy A and received a B.

3116- protect this man at all costs. super straightforward about whats gonna be on exams, so much easier than 3115 in my opinion. super caring, will get on zoom w u right away if you email him that ur stuck and he is available. love him so much

ACIS3116-Amazing guy! tests are exactly like the practice exam, he goes over the material multiple times in class. He loves his students and teaching, will get on zoom in the evening with you if you want. If you had lowry for 3115 you can relax here!
Gatzke is so nice and engaging with his students. The class can be tough though, so you should try to attend class even though attendance is optional.
Gatzke is a great Professor. ACIS 3116 is challenging but he tells you exactly what will be on the exam and he wants you succeed. Gatzke or Professor Shortt are great for ACIS 3116.

Gatzke was the most caring professor I have had at Virginia Tech. He would go out to his way to hold zoom lectures after work to help you out. He also would go through the tests before hand and let you know what material was on the test and make a power point review. Do hw in pieces it's very similar to test. Don't wait until last minute! Great Guy

Professor Gatzke is a nice person. He knows the content and is willing to help students. The homework is time consuming but not hard if you read the textbook and attend the lectures; work on it throughout the week as it's due on Fridays. The exams will be harder if you cheat/don't put effort into reading the textbook or doing the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the most caring professors I have ever had. His class is hard, but he is more than willing to help students and will make time for them. His class is very lecture-heavy and would often talk the entire hour and a half, but bring coffee or chew some gum to stay focused. He really tries to get to know his students, so don't be afraid to chat.

He really cares about his students and wants them to do well. The lectures were optional, but you either need to watch his videos or go to class. He will help you with homework and responds in a timely manner. The tests were a little bit difficult for me, but I never did terribly. The homework's sometimes took awhile, but that's the class not him.

One of my favorite math professors here. His classes are lecture-heavy, but he explains concepts clearly and welcomes questions. Good test grades are achievable with effort and exams include a few multiple-choice and mostly free-response. The reviews before exams help a lot. Written HW is graded strictly. Extra credit (lot of work) but helps.
He didn't respond to emails, and was hard to work with. He could explain things in class decent enough, I needed to use the lesson videos to learn the material cause he went fast

Class is very test heavy but the teaching is great. Go to class and ask questions and you'll be fine. Don't be afraid to go to office hours and actually do the homework, its super helpful. Definitely a hard course but Professor Garcia is great and he offers extra credit.

Nilton is a good teacher but not generous. Eighty percent of your grade is based on tough exams with no curve and no option to replace your lowest exam with the final. Feedback is minimal, usually just “how.” A strong test taker might be fine, but averages are often below passing.

Overall, he is a good teacher; you will leave his lectures feeling like you have learned something. However, the course material is 99% memorization of patterns, so it is very simple. When comparing his tests to tests of other teachers in the MATH 1226 area of teaching it is blatantly clear he tests harder and more complex. Difficult testing 100%.
Chill teacher, homework is graded harshly but otherwise he is good.

He is the best teacher/math professor I have had. You always learn something in his lectures and he moves quickly but will always slow down if you need him to. Always wants to help in office hours, would highly recommend.

Dr. Garcia was the best math professor I've had at VT. He is super helpful and kind in class. Go to his office hours, MATH 1226 is a hard course here at VT and they are super helpful for getting help on homework or other material related to class. Do the extra credit he assigns since they are super helpful to your grade in the class.
I had him for two semesters and was by far the best professor for Math 1225 and 1226 at VT.

One of the best math professors at VT, Dr. Garcia, is one of the few good ones. You'll leave his lectures feeling like you've learned something. His office hours are helpful, so go to them. When it comes to exams, he makes them as simple as he can. If you review his lecture slides and do the homework, you'll do well.Participate in class,it'll help.
Dr. Simonds is the best! He truly cares about his students and their success. Participate, ask questions and reach out for advice.

Relaxed but engaging class meeting twice weekly on Zoom or in person, with required attendance and participation. He taught like a med school professor using real clinical scenarios. A former neurosurgeon and published author, he brought in guest neurosurgeons and designed a low-burnout, discussion-focused course

Amazing professor/class, lectures on what the students want to hear and things that matter. It's easy to stay captivated by his lectures, no matter what he is talking about. Participation matters, but it's engaging topics and the assignments are relatively simple.

Dr. Simonds has been one of my favorite professors at Virginia Tech. He breaks down these wildly complex topics well and makes them entertaining. He is HILARIOUS and always has interesting lectures. His grading is fair, and he genuinely cares about student success.

Dr. Seidel's lectures generally consist of him reading derivations off a slideshow and occasionally making a witty remark. He's an intelligent prof, but lectures feel incredibly pointless. You learn from the homework. If you don't have a group, the homework is torturous, taking 5-20 hours a week. It's a weed out class. Grit your teeth and bear it.

Dr. Seidel is kind and understanding. The homeworks were hard and kinda sucked but they were doable if you put in the time. The only thing I didnt like were the lecture slides. They had a ton of info on them and there was nothing to take notes about bc it was all written in the slides already. This made it hard to learn and keep up with lectures.

HAVE A GROUP OF FRIENDS. MatLab is your bff. Make code to solve hw so you don't have to redo the calculations when you inevitably get it wrong. Hw can be upwards of 44 questions (#6, beware). Takes atleast 10 hours (assigned once a week). Start days in advance & send code in between each other to make it easier for you all. Tests are open note yay.

He's a good guy but his lectures basically consist of reading over 40 slides of densely packed algebra and nothing more. The HWs can be done easily with matlab and chat but if u want to do good on the (open note) exams i recommend spending the time to really understand the material and do the homework yourself. also all his lectures are recorded

Intro to aero really should be two semesters, but we must make do with what we have. Seidel made some incredible slides for the course, which were incredibly helpful for exams, but his lectures were pretty bland and just restated what was on the slides. Although attendance isn't necessarily graded, go to class (and office hours, I wish I went more)

I took Dr. Seidels AOE 2104 course in Fall 2025. He is well respected and is always willing to help students at office hours. Some of his lectures do get long and kinda boring, clearly a weed out class. exams are not incredibly difficult but the homework assignments due take a long time, he recommends using Mathematica to solve. Overall great prof.

AOE 4324. Hardest class I've taken here. So much Mathematica its actually crazy how much this guy loves Mathematica. Homeworks take hours and hours but he is very helpful during office hours. Lectures are very boring and there are quizzes due after each one. Exams are half copied from these lecture quizzes and half mathematica. Don't procrastinate.

Dr. Seidel taught 2104 in the fall. The 8am lecture was tough but he made it worth it. His lectures are well-structured and easy to follow, even though the subject matter is a bit difficult. He gave lots of partial credit for work, so my grade was always much much better than the raw score. If you put in work, you'll get a lot out of this class.

Honestly he was alright. The class is a struggle because the hw takes so much time every week and the lectures are kinda boring. He just reads off slides and it doesn't add anything. You NEED the slides to do the homework though. Definitely work in groups and start as soon as its assigned. Go to the TA office hours! Work hard and you got it!

Dr. Seidel is an good professor for an 8 AM class. Intro to AOE is challenging but manageable. Homework is tough and requires Matlab or Mathmatica, but Gary and the TAs are very helpful during office hours. Tests are somewhat similar to the homework so you need a good formula sheet and they are curved. Overall, the class is tough but not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great guy who is genuinely interested in what he teaches which makes lectures more engaging. Most kids stop showing up to lectures and those are the ones who fall behind. The 8am lecture sucks but it's worth it and go to all of his office hours because he'll answer all your questions and help with homework. All exams are exactly like the homeworks

Seidel's class was incredibly difficult, easily being harder than the three credit hours it's worth. His lectures are impossible to follow, assignments are graded very harshly, the tests are impossible to finish in the time given, and the class overall just made life more difficult for no good reason. Overall, it was a weed out course.

Gary is an absolute king. He offers tons of extra credit, keeps the highest score of your homework with unlimited attempts, and posts all his notes and videos of each lecture online. He is the best, treat him well and he will do the same to you, God bless this man.

Great guy who gives great lectures and ensures his students fully understand the material. Slides can be pretty dense though but very informative. Homeworks and exams require Mathematica make sure to get good at it fast to do well in this class. Gives lecture quizzes too but they aren't too bad. Take advantage of exam corrections and extra credit.

This man is a genius and tells the best dad jokes. He teaches very tough subjects and expects a high amount from his students. His slides may be dense, but I don't think I could find another professor that could explain the subject as well as he does.
Peak lectures, homework was easy and if you needed help, he was readily available.
Galitz is a great professor but for an extremely hard class.

Dr. Galitz is exactly the guy you want as an engineering professor.  His lectures are incredible, he answers questions thoroughly and gives plenty of real-life examples.  He cares greatly about the profession and his students and wants to see them succeed.  Midterms are difficult but curved well.

Very nice man. Infuriatingly bad teacher. I learned about 25% of the course from him. Loves tangents. Loves curves. Loves extra credit. If you're planning on skipping every class, he's your go-to. I went to almost every class and it was a waste of my time. 

My grade raised from a C to an A- from the final and extra credit.

You will either love or hate him. Does not work many example problems in class, and spends most of class going on rants and tangents, so be prepared to put in work outside of class. Curves every test, so your grade will be fine. I personally just didn't really care for his teaching style or his attitude.

100% would take his class again. HW took a long time but thats just bc the questions take a bit, not bc its a lot. He's a really kind prof. and you can tell he cares abt his students. Tests aren't too bad if you study and he curves heavy. He also helps w/ hw if you ask and responds quickly to emails. Plus his lectures aren't too boring for STEM.
Simple lectures and not to much homework (max two assignments a week). His test are hard, but he curves really well so it's totally fine. He's a really nice professor and explains the topics clearly.

First off you have to understand Statics is a hard course, anyone who had a bad review for Galitz just did not care enough to put effort into the class. Tests are heavily curved but there is a fair amount of homework. Has great lectures and is enthusiastic about what he's teaching. He does care about your grade but also that you learn the material.

Really amazing professor that wants to see you succeed inside and outside of the classroom. He talks through most lectures so you probably won't be taking too many notes. Try to understand the textbook homework as those concepts are translated to tests. Galitz gives you so many opportunities to make up your grade and learn from your mistakes.

Past reviews were misleading. His tests are different from homework and his curves are good but not enough for the difficulty of the exams. Studying for his tests is hard because you never know what to expect. He curves and gives extra credit but it was still a struggle to pass. In lectures, he talks about concepts instead of going over problems

He was a really great statics professor this year. He was always very understanding of students stress and made his lectures fun. The tests are hard but there's a big curve with every test. The class is very concept based and he doesn't work on very many example questions but he takes feedback very well and is helpful when you reach out.

You would have to try to fail Professor Galitz's class. His homework can be difficult, depending on the subject, but rarely is it overwhelming. His tests are very easy to score well on, as you can get 120/100 even before the curve, in which he curves the entire class to a median of 85/100. Take good notes, as you are allowed a cheat sheet on exams.
He was able to make 9am statics fun and engaging.  I didn't think that was possible. Highly recommend

Galitz is one of the most caring professors I have met. He deeply cares about a student's education and wants you to be successful. The course content can be difficult at times but he has safety nets for all the students so you don't have to worry about your grade. Attendance is not mandatory but you should definitely go anyways to learn.

He's definitely not the best lecturer I've had but he may be the most caring professor. He is genuinely passionate about try to teach students and works constantly to improve his teaching methods/materials. His exams are hard but they have large curves, expect to do poorly on the first one but don't freak out. Overall, solid professor.

Professor Galitz is very passionate about Deforms and he is always finding ways in improving his lectures. He is a very kind and generous man when it comes to test curves. He gives out massive test curves but his tests are very hard. Additionally, he also gives out extra credit opportunities. Not a lot of homeworks. Overall, a very good professor.

Dr. Galitz is easily the best professor I've had at my time at Tech so far. His eyes light up when talking about the material and he will happily answer any questions you have. He genuinely cares about teaching and he treats the class like he would his children, which includes disciplining them when necessary. Also gives out generous curves.
Galitz isn't the very best lecturer, I wish he would do more example problems in class, but his tests are very difficult with HUGE curves, so it is easy to succeed in his classes.

Nice guy and clearly passionate about the material. I wish there was less theory and discussion and more quantitative examples and math emphasis, but he did make an effort to make lectures entertaining which was appreciated. Generous curves and pretty quick homework assignments usually. Tests were definitely the hardest part but, again, big curves

His class is tough and test averages are usually low, but he explains what will be on each test clearly. He is a fair grader and what sets him apart is he grades on a curve that doesn't tank your GPA and actually reflects how you learned the material overall and compared to others in the class. Highly recommend him for statics

Professor Galitz cares about the success of his students. It is very possible to get a good grade in this class if you keep brushing over concepts you learn. If you are confused about something, put the effort and go to office hours. He is always ready to help and has office hours everyday!

Very down-to-earth professor that makes what could've easily been a boring and difficult topic into something intriguing. Tests are difficult but he will give you a chance to correct mistakes later on. Would recommend.

His teaching style isn't for everyone. He goes very deep into concepts, which I think confuses a lot of students, but if you go to class and ask him questions when you're confused, you will have a very good understanding of the subject. He genuinely wants you to do well, and offers good help during his office hours. Also, interesting guy to talk to

The only reason this guy is rated highly is because his curves are so generous he passes almost everyone in his class. He is not good at explaining the material and you will not leave his class with a good understanding of statics. If you don't need statics for future classes he's a good choice otherwise take it with another professor.

The tests are consistently hard. Thankfully the tests are all curved based on the results of the class, which can lead to a generous curve. Galitz is one of the best teachers I've ever met. He often cracks corny jokes in class and in-office hours will help you in a way to specifically make you understand. Once his student, always his student.

He curves each test so that the median is 85% - your grade will be fine. He tries to be motivational but just goes on tangents all the time and never fully works out problems so if you want to really learn statics/deforms take Chang or Davison. Hes not the worst and asks for feeback but he thinks he's better than he is so he doesn't really listen.

He's a horrible lecturer, doesn't work out problems, and just makes everything hard to explain. I had to teach a lot of the class to myself and the only reason anyone passes is because of his huge curves.

Many say that his exams are way too hard which is understandable but he curves majorly to make up for it. I got a 44 on the first exam for Statics and got curved to a 77 and after that I studied so much more and got at least a B+ on the rest of his exams including the final. Just study and put forth the effort he asks for and you will be just fine.

Everyone hypes this man up so much because of this curve but fails to mention that his class is entirely conceptual. He does not teach concepts well. The homeworks are long and time consuming. The exams are stupid and difficult. This man is the reason I am not passing the class, stop praising him.

Galitz  �� If someone is complaining about the difficulty of this guys class they dont care enough to try. I got a 73 on test one and got curved to a 100. I wont sugar coat it. If you fail this class with this guy as your prof. Youre stupid. His tests are hard, but curves are appropriate.

Great guy and professor, really passionate about teaching and you learning. Powerpoint lectures were boring due to covid, but still solid teaching, plus an in person review weekly that was great. ests are seriously over complicated, but get curved heavily to make up for it. I had a 68% become a 100%, so no complaints, they're just a good challenge

If you really want to learn and stress less about grades, take Galitz. One of the most respectful and understanding professors I have ever seen. He genuinely cares about every single one of his students and wants you to learn.

The Wiley hws are due at 6pm!! Watch out this is super annoying. I basically taught myself the class through the Wiley hw. He teaches well but different from what I'm used to. He adjusts test grades to balance the grade distributions which is nice. I learned some useful skills needed for deforms, etc.

I had him for Statics, and I've got to say, he doesn't work out enough example problems as he should. I found myself needing to teach myself a lot of this class. He has lots of very generous extra credit opportunities throughout the course and curves tests a lot. The class average was an A-, and I ended with a 101% in the class. He is very likeable

I had Dr. Galitz for Statics and he was a great professor and great guy overall. He knows statics very well and explains everything very well. His tests aren't as terrible as people say they are. Massive curves took my 3 tests from 82 to 106, 76 to 103, and 90 to 108. Lots of extra credit. Most ppl had A's in the class. I ended class with a 105.2%

Probably the hardest class I have taken, at least in terms of the tests. Deforms is somewhat straightforward but his tests are absolutely brutal. In the end, I really appreciate what he did for me. I felt like I know the material in more than just a 'here's a problem, just plug in the numbers.' He pushes you and makes you better because of it.

Dr. Galitz is very smart, brings to the table years of experience, and he makes you think outside the textbook, which is good for engineering training. I had a very hard time learning with his method of teaching. The material isn't even that hard, but I have to teach myself out of the book because he does not do enough examples in class.

test averages were 50's in a course where other instructors had an average GPA of 3.97.

run
Good guy, very smart. Just an alright professor. Lectures were a bit scattered, but if you got the basic idea, you could probably learn the rest on your own. Homeworks/tests were straight forward.

In my time at Virginia Tech I can confidently say this is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He clearly knows what he's talking about, but he has no idea how to convey it. Lectures consist of scribbling on a chalk board, mumbling, and posts no notes. Why the department has him still teaching, let alone a 4000 class is beyond me.

George Terrell is knowledgeable in Statistics, but he can not teach. His notes are scattered, and his homework does not relate to the test. He is rude and unapproachable. I don't know why the VT Stat Department has him teach 4000-level classes that people need to graduate because until he posts the final grades you don't know if you passed.

Avoid this professor at all costs. For certain statistics classes, he is unfortunately your only option and in that case good luck. Terrell is the most unforgiving and unprepared professor I have ever had. His lectures are all over the place and very rarely cohesively teaches a topic. The mathematics involved are not difficult, but he is.

Only professor for this class at VT, very little feedback, upon doing poorly on a test and asking what resources were available to fill in the gaps or get a better grade was told "haha, well you'll do more homework and exams". 
Lectures go on in a monotonousness fashion, will start or state things with seemingly no connection or follow up.

Was an organizational nightmare and some of the worst teaching I have ever had in college and then some. Avoid him like the plague if you can, but he is the only professor so f's for you gpa. Curves a ton though.

I've never taken a statistics class but feel pretty comfortable with mathematics. I took this class just for fun and it definitely was challenging but he does a very good job explaining concepts. However, he is not good at explaining questions to you and will just say "think about this...". Just make sure you go to every single class! I Fun class.

reviews.comment: This professor wants nothing to do with you. I asked for a tutor, and he said no. I asked for a Zoom session (we had to take this online due to Corona), he said no. The only way to ask questions was via email. He might have thought he was trying to answer the questions. I could tell he wanted us to learn by struggling. I just needed extra help.

Grade: CC Seems to know what he is talking about but doesn't teach well. He goes over a simple example each class which is nothing compared to the homework and exams. Final was worth 49% of my grade after going online which seemed a bit much considering lectures were recorded and not good quality. Not very accessible outside class. Avoid if you can

reviews.comment: This professor is not good at teaching what he expects you to know on the tests. I would take a different professor for STAT 4714, except VT doesn't give you any options so good luck.
The worst professor I had at Virginia Tech. Don't take him!
Terrible at explaining the material.
OH MY GOSH THIS CLASS WAS IMPOSSIBLE.
His exams were really hard.
I think she took 20 years off of my life

She knows and acknowledged that ECE students would not have learned python in any classes up to this point but fills homeworks and a final project worth 25% of the grade with python programming that she also refuses to teach anything about in lectures. Also lecture slides are very disorganized and filled with more memes than actual information.

Professor Gerdes has good lectures, and projects that teach you a lot about DSA. That said, with the grader dropping often the same day a project was due, and overall lack of communication I find it difficult to give her above a 2. 

Grading was tough, no tests in the grader are provided. Sometimes EC.

Take Ha/Shin for less stress with the course.

I will be the only non 1 you see Gerdes having, and I do not recommend her. However, I really enjoyed the class and felt like I enjoyed a lot (I am insane). Projects are insanely difficult but you will learn a LOT if you stick it through. Just be prepared for this class to take up all of your time for the entire semester, take Ha for less stress.
Everyone in the class tried to get her fired. Avoid at all costs
Currently having the worst experience in ECE since I've been here.
Bad professor, avoid at all cost. Cant teach, releases homework late and full of errors. Does not seem to enjoy teaching or working with students at all.

She constantly released projects with unfinished starter code or code that had errors. She expected all students to test all cases thoroughly, but she constantly missed cases and the project specifications were almost always incomplete. This is the first professor I had to write a review for because this class is truly awful.

For ECE 3564:
Showed her lack of care all semester.
When 75min exam started >15min late said to "calm down" and "should only take us an hour." 
Got on students for being "irresponsible" but consistently released HWs and projects late. Didn't submit grades at deadline, don't even know my grade in the class.

Avoid if you can: lazy and doesn't care.
Awful,avoid at any cost

To his credit, Gerdes does give generous extra credits if you participate in his in-class quizzes. I heard he wasn't bad before, but in fall 2021, only 2 of his projects did not have mistakes in the starter code, and his autograder was so broken for one project that he delayed it for a week, and hours of work was wasted as the project was modified.

I'm a little shocked at these ratings -- Dr. Chandler was one of the best professors I ever had at VT and pushed me to be a better writer. She's passionate and wants people to participate and be fully engaged in class. She has a great sense of humor and fosters a good environment. If you work hard, you'll do fine.

Don't be deterred by the poor ratings. Dr. Chandler is amazing and her lectures are super engaging. No, she won't just hand out As, but if you do the reading and learn to apply the concepts, you'll do well. Any syllabus changes were for students' benefit, like making an essay optional. I learned a lot in this class and felt supported throughout.

Gives great lectures but extremely harsh grader when it comes to essays

reviews.comment: She has great lectures and her tests are fine if you study. However, she changed the weight of assignments on the last day of semester without notice which dropped my grade from a B+ to B-. I found that quite a disgusting thing to do without telling students or updating her syllabus. She never discussed the change with students

I honestly really did like her. We had many projects in this class, but these are the same projects everyone had, regardless of the teacher. I am someone who procrastinates a lot, so it was nice that her due dates were strict because you ended up doing and submitting parts of the project before the big due date.
I don't think her class is hard, and also she is nice, but she gives lots of homework every after every single class, with a tight due date, usually it's due on the day she assigned the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a tough grader and doesn't really take any excuses as to why something might be late. I also found the class quite boring and just felt like I was doing busy work the whole time. Overall, I much preferred my 1105 teacher.

The way the class is structured is so dumb. Tons of busy work that isn't graded but is mandatory to complete. Otherwise she won't read/grade your papers or presentations. She grades easy, but only if you put in effort and submit your assignments on-time.

Class is pretty easy, but the way she teaches the class is horrendous. She gives tons of busy work that isn't actually graded, but you need to do it if you want your projects to get graded. However she is a easy grader and gives extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In high school, I sucked at English but in her class, I finished with over 100%. Follow all instructions, listen to her feedback, and do all extra credit. I did minimal work but followed the rubric so I got full marks. If you need assistance she is willing to help.
Good experience
so unorganized and structured awfully
Most unorganized class I have ever taken

Gives out tons of homework that isn't graded, but is needed in order for her to read your essays. The class is dumb and is pointless. Take it over the summer if you can, and try not to get her because the way she structures class is random and disorganized.

Hard to understand, doesn't give any partial credit on exams even if you do the whole problem right and make a typo on the exam. The lectures are useless, he just reads the slides and doesn't explain anything. He forgets to post assignments until the day before they are due. He doesn't know how to use canvas and he is unintelligible.
