reviews.comment: Ghorai is probably one of the worst professors I've had in my academic career. ME 3024 is an awful class no matter who the professor is but Ghorai somehow made it worse. Lectures were incomprehensible due to his thick accent. When he was teaching it seemed like he was seeing the slides for the first time and just completely winging the class.

Lectures are useless. Reads directly from a PowerPoint slide he did not create. Hard to understand. No partial credit on exams. Easiest class content-wise of junior year first semester but the most unreasonable in terms of workload and Ghorai Prasenjit does not make anything easier.

Professor Ghorai is one of the worst professors Ive encountered at Tech. He is barely intelligible and his accent makes him extremely hard to understand. The class is just an excessive amount of busywork and there is no partial credit on exams. The material taught in the class is useless and a large part of the grade is poorly outlined group work.
She is super nice and gives partial credit when grading tests. She doesn't give practice tests so do the homework. Always posts lecture notes post class. I would recommend her to anyone.

Lectures were ok. But she was very caring and took extra time to explain something if someone didn't understand it. She let's us know what (roughly) to expect on tests which was helpful. Definitely recommend taking her!
Great professor. Lots of bad math professors at VT and she is not one of them. Calc 2 was a hard class that many people fail but she makes the class much easier. Great teacher would pick her again.

I had her last semester and she was amazing. From what I've heard the math department is not really good at VT, so if you have her it is a Christmas miracle! Even though the course is difficult she wants her students to succeed and helps those who take the time to show up to class

Professor Seebohm was a diamond in the rough, given VT's math department. Her lectures were very similar to the test content, and she would slow down to answer questions or clarify. I took her for MATH 2204, my first math class at VT, and I could not have asked for better. You will spend a lot of time studying, but it'll be worth it.

she's super chill and approachable. imo the class + tests get progressively easier, and the final (especially FRQ which is written by her) was a lot easier than i expected. she genuinely wants you to do well in this class.  only thing i didnt like was that the written assignments were in-class, they're kinda stressful, but you get 3 drops.
Good lectures even though they are optional. Not very much homework but optional textbook problems for practice

Maybe the best math professor I've had at VT. Brilliant and easy to understand lectures, no unnecessary work, fair test grading, accessible, kind, and clearly experienced at teaching math. Made calc 3 a breeze, would highly recommend.

Took her calc 3 class fall 2025, she was a great prof and really knew how to present information in lectures. she would always stop to ensure we all understood. her examples were great and she kept the class very engaging. 10/10 recommend

Took MATH 2204 (Calc 3). Good lectures that are example based. Takes time to answer questions and is invested in making sure students understand what's going on. HW is Webassign but not too many questions. Tests are only slightly harder than in class examples. Would recommend.

One thing I loved about Professor Seebohm's class was the fact her lecture notes were always posted online. I utilized this opportunity to pay every bit of attention in class and re-read the notes after. Great opportunity and this is clearly a professor who knows how to teach Calc 2 in a very digestible way!
Great professor, knows how to teach the subject really well and a nice person too. Tests weren't too hard as long as you studied.

She made Calc 2 digestible and easy to understand. It is still a lot of material you have to learn, but she is a great professor and very understandable. I would love to take another class with her if I had the chance.

As someone who isn't stellar at math, Gina Seebohm was a fantastic professor. She is very clear and easy to follow. I will say she does move fast in lectures, but calc 2 is so much material to get through that I get it. If you get Gina you're in good hands!

Professor Seebohm is an incredible teacher who instructs an incredibly difficult class, and she very clearly cares about her work. She will spend additional time on topics she deems difficult, the written assignments she assigns are clearly built to teach you more in-depth about the material, and class time never feels wasted.
Highly recommend

Gina Seebohm is one of the best, if not the best, Calc 2 professors at Virginia Tech. She genuinely wants you to learn and will help in any way possible. As long as you review her homework assignments and notes, you'll be fine.
The Calc 2 GOAT. Review the written assignments and textbook problems and you're golden.

Gina was a great professor considering 1226 is a difficult class. Her test prepared us well for the common time final while being very similar to our in-class (group) graded assignments and homework assignments. Several hours a week is need for homeworks and preparing but it is a very manageable workload.

Class is difficult just by nature of being Math 1226, but she does a great job of making the material digestible and preparing you for the tests and the final. The in-class written assignments are very similar to tests and she posts all of her annotated lecture slides. Definitely one of if not the best professor to get for Calc II at VT.

She's an okay professor/teacher.

Tests are pretty similar to in-class quizzes and homework. She does curve if average is low. 

She is great compared to everyone else. Please try to take her!

Probably one of the better math professors. Lectures were a little fast and hard to follow sometimes, but if you were to ask a specific question, she would answer in detail. The class grade was ~50% tests, so if you bomb one, it can really lower your grade. But, If you pay attention everyday and do well on assignments, you will do well with her.

Best calc 2 professor you can get, hands down. While her teaching might be confusing hard to understand, she is by far the nicest calc 2 professor and she grades generously.  If you have a hard time understanding concepts in class, just watch prof leonard at home.

Gina Seebohm's jersey must be retired in the rafters. She was absolutely without a doubt my favorite professor and my most supportive and engaging professor. The course was slightly challenging but definitely on the easier end of the VT Calc 2 spectrum. She truly wanted to see everyone succeed and the class and environment was designed to do so.

This is a teacher who is transparent and wants you to succeed and will give a generous amount of information about upcoming tests and what to expect on the final. You can come to her freely about any concerns about her grade.

It was her first semester at tech when I took the class. Still she gave great, easy to follow lectures. She's very good at answering questions. I'm sure now that she knows the structure of the class better lectures will be even better. Common time exams so no comment there.

Gina was extremely helpful especially after I got sick during the semester. She helped me find extra points to get my grade up. wants her students to exceed but does not create the exams. Group written assignments during class help get grades up. Great teacher, extremely straightforward, with no accent or bad writing, and would take her class again

Gina is genuinely an outstanding professor, she explains the material very well and is probably one of the best picks for a first-year math teacher. Also is super helpful in office hours and actually cares about her students. I have nothing bad to say about her, take if you can.

Wasn't always clear when explaining new things to us. Multiple times she would mess up a problem and end up having to redo it in whole. Sometimes we would only get through 2-3 problems in the whole class period.

Very knowledgeable. Promotes life lessons and inspiration that you can take with you for use in your life. Very intriguing course where I feel I actually learned useful things.
Although his lectures were entertaining from time to time, his tests were comprised of material that had many extremely close answers, making it very difficult to score a high grade.

The definition of incompetence and delusion. Geller only ever presented in the form of political cartoons and believed that would be enough. He frequently got political in class and would wine and cry about everything. VT is making the right choice by forcing him out and I'm so thankful no student will ever have to take a class of his again.

This class goes from a great professor to an awful one. He stands up there talking about his boomer comics and his weird green bracelets and gives no way for students to study. What kind of teacher puts "Dr.Geller says..." as questions on a final. I really hope he puts this on his board at the beginning of the year so i can warn you all to get out

Bro uses reverse reverse psychology on students, plays VICTIM CARD, forgets to finish sentences. Ur basically signing up for a yap session that's not even considered psych. THE FINAL EXAM WAS HIS ASKING QUESTIONS ABOUT HIMSELF. Bro said he'd curve and forgot about that also

The lectures are terribly boring. About 1/4 of the class would actually show up. He tried to explain everything using cartoons, but with no notes, no study guides, and no application, his definitions of the terms using cartoons were useless. Terrible switch from Dr. Hoffman.

He is just the worst teacher I have ever had, and he is completely full of himself. He is out of touch and almost all of his lectures are a waste of time. Furthermore, he also provides lecture takeaways that are misleading to questions on the test, as if he is trying to make students fail.

He taught a lot with cartoons which he says are memorable but really aren't. Definitely has good spirit and intentions, but he didn't give review sheets. Class not mandatory, but only things he goes over in class will be on the tests, so its good to go anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was super nice and funny, however his teaching style is a bit more old-fashioned. He doesn't make test guides which is something I struggled with personally.

He was funny and definitely knew a lot about the subject. His notes just list all the things you need to know, which is mostly just definitions for applications of psych, and includes a lot of images. He does practice questions at the end of lectures. Test was pretty hard in comparison to Hoffman. Make sure to do extra credit
Brings up random unrelated things in class. has taught for over 5 decades and somehow hasn't learned a thing. delusionally believes he is funny and a good person

Has great energy and is funny, lectures can get a bit confusing because there its not straight forward but shows examples, rely on the textbook to read before lectures and to study to understand the content that will be in class, gives good take away questions and key terms at the end of each lecture which is very similar to what is on the test

His teaching style was not for me. His powerpoints were confusing, with A LOT of cartoons, there aren't really any true notes. Does not give study guides. Tests were on application, so studying terms & cartoons won't do any good. He also gets extremely offended if you leave class to use the bathroom. All I can say is goodluck & do the extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very lecture-heavy, but the lectures can be a bit confusing. Class is only graded by testa with some extra credit. Very nice and caring professor, but the material could be a bit more clear. Overall, good professor. I just wish the slides and notes were clearer and had fewer visuals.

Most boring class I have every taken. He used his own cartoons as a way to explain psychology but doesn't have many true written notes. We had hoffman for the first part and he was amazing and then having geller was a terrible switch. He claims he is going to retire and I hope home boy is cause he reminds me of my grandpa who just yaps.

Dr. Geller is extremely nice and knowledgable. I found his exams to be rather difficult. Memorizing terms won't do you much good, as his exams are on application. Sometimes his questions on exams are a bit confusing. Definitely read the textbook chapter before coming to class to get most of it. He's a great teacher, but not for everyone.

Course was graded on exams only, and the exams were mildly difficult, but should be easy if you show up to lectures and know the material. It is possible to not show up to lectures and still pass, but you have to read and study a lot to make up for it.

Gellers tests aren't hard, but you have to rely on reading the textbook and go to class. All he does is show cartoons and promote his ted talk, books, and AC4P brand. He sometimes explains the terms you need for the test, but he mainly goes on tangents and has gotten political in class before. Pay attention to takeaways and practice questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Geller is a very nice man, but his teaching style was just not my way of learning. Lots of cartoons in his powerpoints and sample test questions in slides were pretty much the actual test. This section of the class is more opinionated and if you don't think like him, figure out how because his opinions are typically the correct answer.

Dr.Geller was extremely caring and professional.He uses cartoons and key takeaways as the main parts of the lecture but included practice questions that he gives the answers to and chooses some to use on the test. Some people hate the way he teaches but if you listen to what he is explaining then you will fully understand the concepts.

Geller is super engaging but he's not always clear. As someone who took AP psych, I don't find it difficult, but I can see how his teaching style could make the material confusing for someone who doesn't already know it. My advice is to read the chapters before classes and tests so that the wording doesn't feel as confusing and you should be fine.

Professor Geller is an interesting character. He has good intentions for his students but his teaching style wasn't exactly for me. His lectures/powerpoints weren't information-heavy and instead he used cartoons and pictures. Not much you can really take notes on and most of my learning was just doing the textbook readings so make sure you read it

Geller's teaching style wasn't for me. He speeds through lectures because he doesn't want us to take notes (just listen). The way he explains some topics is pretty confusing. He also incorporates some political opinions into his lectures which isn't great. Overall the class was fine. I did like all the comics he used.

Lectures are irrelevant cartoons and motivational speeches. The ONLY way to get good notes is the textbook. Tests are hard, different for every person. I studied for 11 days for 2+ hours a day and got a 30%. Waste of time and $ and ruined any interest I had in Psychology. If you're not a psych major don't waste your time using this as a pathway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Geller is a terrible professor when you have had Professor Hoffman for the first semester. Geller's lectures are AWFUL, the cartoons are so stupid and it doesn't help at all when needing to study. I wish I didn't have him as a professor.

He only gets a 4 cuz I'm comparing him to the legend Dr. Hoffman. He doesn't give study guides before exams so going to lectures is more important. His slides aren't as easy to follow and if he's reading this, please dont put red text on an orange background im begging you!!!

Professor Geller is the type of teacher that should be in a smaller class. I like his style of teaching because he treats class more like a conversation instead of a lecture, but I just don't think it works well in a massive lecture like intro psych. Also sometimes all the cartoons he shows can get a bit annoying, but other than that he was fine.

I had heard a lot of negative things about him before taking this class, but I thought he was great. So funny and inspirational. Definitely take his advice about reading the textbook and studying the key terms and takeaways because it makes all the difference. You have to meet him halfway when it comes to effort which I find very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr.Geller is a love em or hate em professor. I enjoyed his style of lecture but if you are a person who needs to take notes and have detailed slides, he's not the teacher for you

I took this class for a pathway. I did not perform well on tests which caused me to struggle however, making flashcards and going to test review sessions help a lot. He does practice questions and takeaways on slides but reading the textbook before class is better for understanding the lecture. Just do well on tests and complete the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Geller was a decent teacher. His in-class slides were all cartoons and not very helpful. Class is graded off of four exams, no homework or other assignments. Extra credit is available and easy to receive. Participation was not mandatory but there were practice questions at the end of the lecture that always appeared on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you couldn't tell from the reviews, you will either love or hate him. This has a unique style which I liked but I could see how others would struggle with

Dr. Geller is great to listen too and hes very passionate but he has the worst notes I have ever seen. His slides are full of political cartoons that are supposed to explain the concepts but are really ineffective. If you don't go to his class you will be so confused just looking at the slides.

Professor Geller's lectures are interesting, and he provides takeaways of what you should have gotten out of them along with sample questions. He was very empathetic. Extra credit is available, no homework.

Imagine having someone teach Geller what will be on the exam, then he teaches it to you from that.  It is obvious he knows the material but refuses to give it straight.  I do not care about his stories and want to pass the class.  He is a motivational speaker, not a teacher.
great professor

He says every class that everything on the tests will come from his lectures. What he doesn't tell you is that the terms and things he gives in class are kinda insufficient and he just throws a lot of psych words around, so do the readings before class and it will make more sense. His powerpoints are a bit barren aside from random comic strips.
He is a GREAT professor and the exam was slight. You just need to come to every class. None of the exam is from the textbook, all from lectures.

Geller is not a professor. He is a motivational speaker who tries to teach psychology. He is very cocky and goes off topic all the time. There are no words on his slides so it is really hard to go back and study for the exams which are your only grades in the class. His slides consist of cartoons. Study the textbook and do the learning curves!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very tough class, with heavy memorization (basically the whole textbook pus extra stuff from the lectures) The tests had weird content that seemed not spread out across all the information he asked you to memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For a long time, I respected Geller as a teacher because I thought he was very inspirational. After spending more time with him in other classes I realize he is not so much of a teacher as he is a motivational speaker. His ego gets in the way of the connection with his students. If you're not his favorite from day 1 don't bother, he won't help you.

Geller is a great professor. His class is hard. If he doesn't cover the material in class, it won't be on the exam. However, his tests are 99% application questions. You need to understand the concepts covered. GO TO CLASS. He gives you sample questions similar to the exams at the end of the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Geller would be a great professor if we didn't have exams. His slides were mainly cartoons so it was difficult to get any content down. His classes were interesting but it was hard to study for exams without good notes from class.
Your grade is all based on the exams. Professor is not accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: not a fan of geller's teaching style. i found it difficult to study for his tests because his slideshows were just cartoons. he sounded more like a motivational speaker than a professor to me. tests were a little difficult.

LOVE dr. geller! super awesome professor. i had dr. hoffman for the first half of this course, and i will admit that the transition from hoffman to geller was difficult because they have completely different teaching styles. as long as you attend geller's lectures, you'll be fine. textbook is not needed for his section of the course
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The only grades are the exams and he re-used all of his online lectures from Spring 2020 which was very unhelpful. He didn't seem accessible, and the TA's seemed in control of this class.

Dr. Geller is so well-spoken, it's really nice listening to him speak. He makes his lectures interesting and includes practice questions at the end of them, so they're really helpful. Just study and use your resources. The textbook is useless in my opinion, you'll do fine without it, don't waste your money on it. Also, offers a lot of extra credit!
His lectures are very entertaining and easy to listen to. I highly recommend taking a class from him.

When I say inspirational, I don't mean this in a good way. He tried to talk as if he had made a discovery for what makes people happy. Super political during his lectures and just kept sharing that you need to keep your head up, which a lot of students buy into. Basically is convincing yourself that you're fine when life is hard. Total BS material

I had Geller in Psych 101. For the first half I had Hoffman, and I had an A+ in the class with ease until Geller. His lectures are dull and incredibly difficult to take notes on. I'm a visual learner, but his slides are ONLY COMICS that he drew himself. Some lectures are 100+ slides long, and I studied for days only to get an 80 on the final.

I took this class with Geller online due to COVID-19. He clearly outlines 95+% of testable material. Test questions (50 mult chc) are exclusively on psych stuff. He's not political, but he does talk about actively caring, the environment, interdependency, etc. a LOT. I took tons of notes, studied, and the lowest test grade I got was a 96.

He is very passionate and cares a lot about what he does, which I respect. He seemed like a good guy but he could be hard to follow sometimes due to his rambling. The class is difficult mostly because the only grades are 4 exams so you really have to know the stuff. People say he's political, but he wasn't really - just factual and straightforward.

This guy hypes up his class as very easy with giving out the key terms and practice questions, but its all a hoax. His tests have 3-4 questions that are not in readings and debatable at best as legitimate test questions. Very liberal and promotes his ted talk for no reason. His robust teaching style is failing the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did pretty good with the professor in the first half of this class. I couldn't understand Geller though. He's awful, self-absorbed, and his lectures are all cartoons. I don't know how people do well. He's impossible to follow in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Towards the end I stopped liking this class. Dr Geller is very liberal and pushes his pro-environment ideas on us, passing it off as curriculum. He talks about himself all the time and is constantly is promoting his books/accomplishments to us. He is unprofessional by how often he gets political... Probably some good life lessons but hes annoying

Seems as though he teaches for the opportunity to promote his own book and his organization. Tries to push the his political views. Is a very seemingly ignorant person and thinks everything he does is the best. His lectures don't get you anywhere, it's just a motivational speech. Gets offended by grades for a test he didnt teach for to begin with.

Dr. Geller is a professor that makes you just want to show up because every lecture you get a little life lesson too. A lot of the concepts are easy to grasp. A good storyteller, not a serious lecturer. If you want to get more out of class than just definitions and concepts, he's the guy. Tests aren't hard if you go to lectures!

Scott Geller spends the entire class promoting his ted talk and book. He also helped write the textbook, so you would think that would help you prepare for the exams but it doesn't. He writes questions about how certain psychologists (like Freud) would act if they went to therapy. How is anyone supposed to know this? Don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You have to buy a textbook for his class that he helped write, after the year you cannot sell the textbook back to the school because he just makes a new one. He teaches with comics as if everyone in the class is in elementary school. He says he "does not like to get political" but does it pretty much every class. Just seemed like a weird dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Geller would be better as a motivational speaker. He's a nice guy but a very poor teacher. He doesn't spend much time teaching because he spends almost all of his lectures trying to get students to "actively care for people." This is not helpful, as the tests are based on psychological concepts.
Scott Geller wrote part of the textbook for the class 1004. I bought it, and tried to sell it back and the school wouldn't give me anything for it.
Political in his later lectures, far to many tangents and awful grade averages compared to the professor before him.
He never made eye contact and I felt vilified as a person of color in his self labelling white supremacism

I did not like Dr. Geller's teaching style. He only uses overhead projectors, which is very weird in college, and he has all of these comics that he shows which are pretty pointless. He emphasizes reading the book (which he helped write) before class, as long as you read the chapter before the exam you will be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not a big fan of geller. Perhaps very knowledgable but has a very big ego. Teaches to a handful of catchphrases he made up. Annoying overall. Still a nice guy though.

Geller is AWESOME! loved going to his class and getting to hear him speak. He is an inspirational, thoughtful man. He cares about his field and LOVES teaching it. He gives key terms for his tests and they're all to know from the chapter. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy! But his method of teaching is outdated; nevertheless, he is an above average-good teacher.
Terrible teacher seems like he is knowledgeable but he can focus long enough to convey what he has to say and just likes to talk about himself.

He's very old fashioned. He takes pride in being the age that he is. His presentations are hard to understand sometimes, as he only uses pictures to describe vocabulary. Thankfully, he posts "Key Terms," which is everything you need to know for his exams. He's kind of funny too, sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing, thought-provoking professor with very engaging lectures. What I like about him is that he goes over in lectures what will be on the tests (he makes it very clear what you need to study). Aside from this, he is just a super nice and upbeat guy and makes the subject interesting whether or not you are majoring in psychology

Scott Geller is a good guy. He focuses well on motivating and making his students happy. Each class is about 50 minutes long and 30 minutes of his lecture isnt even about psychology. He just gives us random motivation and tells us about his damn kids or something. He never teaches psychology. Might as well skip class and read out of the book.
Open policy was for appearance

Dr. Geller is phenomenal! He's really inspiring and is able to apply the lesson with cartoons which may seem odd but are really helpful because you can remember them while taking the exam. I highly recommend this professor.
One of my favorite professors of all time! Loved all of his lectures!
Doesn't actually teach anything, just shows cartoons and tells stories. Great guy, but more of a motivational speaker than a professor. Just study the "key terms" he gives you and you'll get an A.

He uses a lot of pictures which are helpful and funny and make the class a little more interesting. He is very energetic which keeps you awake and has a lot of good stories. His test questions are scenarios so know how to put the vocab words into real life.

I really disliked Dr. Geller's teaching style. Compared to Dr. Hoffman, I didn't really learn much and had a hard time grasping the concepts. He spent most of his time showing cartoons and behaving like a motivational speaker. I tried my best to study hard for his final and was left stumped.
One of the best classes I've ever been in! Not only does he tell you what will be on the test but he talks about everything for the test in a way you can relate and understand the material.
He has a great enthusiasm that makes his class more interesting and fun. As long as you listen to his lectures and study, you will pass this class.

Geller just showed comics, banged on his drums, and gave keywords.  He would put his "actively caring" views on every single lecture he could.  While his class was semi-interesting and he was sometimes funny I would like him to change his teaching style a bit but would recommend him. If you look over the textbook youll be fine
Great teacher.

Dr. Geller is awesome.  He does the second half of Intro. Psych, and is definately different than Dr. Hoffman, but not in a bad way.  He has a good teaching style that keeps you involved in the class, and you will do a lot of laughing.  I recommend Dr. Geller.
Gellar is hilarious .. i loved the class .. lectures consist of comic strips that him and his buddies drew lol .. you never know what your in for in Gellar's class
Amazing professor.  He made lectures interesting and relevant, even though his poems dragged on a bit.

I Hate this guy! Coming to class was completely useless.  The one positive thing was that I didnt go to class and just read the book and looked at the key words he posted.  He makes these dumb jokes and is just a real loser.  If you read the book , youll do fine on the test though.
He's really interesting and keeps ur attention which is unusual for such a big lecture. Also, he teaches things in a way that make you remember them.
Great Teacher

all of the stuff on his tests comes from the book. half of his questions come from the online practice tests. the only reason why i went to class was because he's so funny, otherwise, he doesn't talk about anything you don't already read in the book & the book is much clearer.
He was a great teacher and I loved all of his little comic strips and stories!
I Loved all his stories, and the little cartoons he puts up. It made what could otherwise have been another boring lecture into something I might actually wake up to go to ocassionally.
No Comments

As has been mentioned, classes are more like motivational lectures, but Geller's dynamic speaking style and humor keeps your attention. More importantly, he is very helpful and a very good listener...not a bad looking guy, either. Great way to break into Psych!
found him a little boring and condecending, but not a bad teacher.  tests are on lectures.  his part of the class was a little too easy and lacked substance.  very personable and helpful

i loved this teacher!! He deff made the class interesting. There were only like 3 tests and they were somewhat difficult but not too bad. I didn't study a whole lot and got a B with all the extra credit
Awesome lectures

Outstanding teacher! Although tests are not tooo easy Geller makes coming to class a treat. As compared to other lecture teachers Geller is passionate about the subject and often tells comedic stories relating to the subject matter. YOU WANT GELLER AS A TEACHER! you won't regret it :)

I later got to know him by doing research for CABS (& respect him a lot) but I thought he could have been more effective. The intro psyc class at Tech is FAR TOO easy and insulting to psyc majors (no wonder ppl think we're idiots). I would've liked more substance.

If you don't like having a motivational speech 2 or 3 times a week, this guy will get on your nerves. I fall into this catigory. But he is entertaining and does love his subject. So he's a good professor to have.
One of the only classes i can say i have looked forward to. Gellar was always entertaining and made the subject very relevant.

Gellar is awesome !  He was like a motivational speaker more than he was a teacher.  His class isn't an easy A, but it is very interesting.  He has done so much research and is able to relate what he is talking about to something in real life so you can understand it.  There is no cumlative exam!

He was a really nice guy and enthusiastic. Not too hard. most of the test questions came from the lecture. there was a lot of extra credit offered as well which helped. i liked him and enjoyed going to class overall( :

Been like 7 years since I took the class, but he was always really into what he talked about, and yeah, he does split time with another cooler prof (Harrison) -- as I remember he had the tendency to just kind of ramble on a tangent pretty often.

Dr. Gellar is like a motivation speaker.  I loved going to his class.  He teaches the later part of the class. It is split between him and Dr. Harrison.  The class isn't too hard if you come and use the study guide.  Be sure to do the extra credit - experiements they are kinda fun!
No Comments
i thought he was very interesting to listen to and pay attention to in lecture

The guy was always pretty wired and taught the class with another professor (I forget his name).  This guy got his rep, I think, in Industrial/Organizational Psych.  He was fairly entertaining, but sometimes seemed to get a little too into talking.
No Comments
No Comments

Nicolin is truly an amazing professor! She is so passionate, gives a ton of extra credit, and all of her assignments are pretty manageable. Class is only mandatory when she tells you there is group work, otherwise you just go to fill in notes. Honestly, if you put in moderate effort, you should do well in this class.

actually the sweetest human alive and she wants you to succeed. so much EC, where I had above 100% the whole semester, and could get a 35% on the final and keep my A. if you answer the question you get full points, so the only way to not get an A is to not show up for the labs and/or do the discussions. best class and prof ive ever had at VT

She is the best professor at Virginia Tech. She is so caring and wants you to succeed. If you show up to class and pay attention, the exams are super manageable, and she includes extra credit in them (I got over 100% on both of the midterms).

My favorite professor at VT! She doesn't take attendance, but she has random participation assignments that are part of your grade. Her exams are tough, but fair. She has tons of office hours, and supplements the test with other assignments to boost your grade. She's incredibly sweet, and she really knows what she's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She has been one of my favorite professors and I highly recommend taking her HNFE 2014 class. Homework is very light, and her lectures are engaging and full of information. She is very passionate about nutrition and is very responsive to student questions and emails.

Best, most understanding, caring and empathetic professor I've ever had. Really passionate about what she does. Her lectures are so fun because she is so excited. If I could take all my classes with her I would. Only class in my life I have ever been excited to attend.

She is the sweetest professor I've ever had. she's always so happy and excited to share her knowledge. the workload might look like a lot at first but she gives you more than enough resources to get a good grade.

Professor Grieco was one of the best professors I've had at Tech. She genuinely cares about what she's teaching and wants you to understand it. I had her 9am class and she always made my days start in the best way possible. She made it fun to come to class. Absolutely recommend taking any of her courses. Just go to class and you'll be fine.
Professor Grieco is extremely nice, loves her students and wants them to do well. Course material is fairly easy if you pay attention and study. Offers TONS of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor ever. I still use her as a reference, and I've been out of school for 2 years. She is the most amazing woman and professor. I took two of her classes, and they were by far two of my favorites.

Nicolin is my favorite professor at VT. She clearly wants you to learn and succeed and gives plenty of opportunities to do so. She has a great attitude and is just a happy person overall. Take her class, you'll love her and the information she teaches as well.

Great professor, very effective teacher and tests are hard but if you study you'll do well. She really did deepen my knowledge of nutrition and gave me a new perspective on food, I definitely plan to take more classes from her in the future. I'm a junior and she's probably the best professor I've taken at tech- recommend her to everyone
She is super nice, would definitely take again
10000% the best professor at Tech - so caring and loves all of her students. Take every class you can with her.

Nicolin is the best professor ive had at VT. she genuinely cares about her students and is super passionate about what shes teaching. Offers extra credit on almost every assignment and provides quality feedback. Theres only 3 tests with a manageable amount of material, the final is not cumulative. Definitely take one of her classes!!

By far the nicest professor i have had so far. Always answers emails accordingly and always willing to help you. She's very passionate about the class and it shows through her lectures. There are only 2 exams and then some in class participation things, but overall the class is very enjoyable.

I'll keep this short because Nicolin is by far one of the best professors I've ever had. She is genuinely invested in each student and everything she teaches and I hope and pray I get to take another class with her before I graduate! If you get the opportunity, take a course taught by her! You wont regret it!

Dr. Grieco is one of my favorite profs at Virginia Tech. I took her class last year for NALS and again for Science of Food Prep Lab. Dr. Grieco will go the extra mile for any of her students. Lectures are entertaining and she's easy to contact. A lot of professors "talk the talk" when it comes to nutrition, but Dr. Grieco truly walks the walk.

Great professor, cares about her students and makes her classes fun. Offers extra credit (a lot) and sometimes she can be a little too passionate about what she's lecturing on, and often doesn't make it through all the slides (although she always posts what she doesn't go over). One of my favorites at tech!

Best professor at VT. She cares about her students! Go to her office hours, even just to chat. She's very kind and helpful. Her lectures are amazing, although a bit boring at times, but she's so animated about what she's teaching, you won't notice being bored. Tests are easy if you study the note guides she provides. TONS of extra credit is offered

Take research methods with anyone else. He's nice enough, but his lectures are unhelpful and he doesn't teach, just reads off the slides. Office hours are off campus and he doesn't really help. The average on our first exam was failing and he changed nothing and no curve. This a teach yourself course, but even then none of his materials help.

He is a good guy, but he is also a horrible professor. He reads straight from the slides; he is boring and has a rude vibe. I had to teach myself everything for the class and only went to exams after the first week after realizing that no one learned through his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful. Hated every class. Do not take Research Methods with him. His office is off campus so you won't find him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Gibbs is very smart, but to be honest it came across as conceding and rude. He expects you to know the curriculum before you enter the class, and hardly answers questions. It doesn't matter if you read the textbook or not, don't expect to know the class. It's very heavy on Math and Statistics, of which most Polisci Students are not strong in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily the best of the capstone course teachers

His lectures are pointless as he just reads straight from the slide. I had to teach myself to understand the course but if you're not good with excel good luck. Was failing most of the year (D+ to C-) but somehow did well on the last few assignments to get a C+ (was like .2 away from a b-) there's no extra credit and he doesn't curve or round.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dan Gibbs is a great professor. It is clear that he has a deep knowledge and enjoyment of the material. He is lenient on grading and makes sure that you know the material you are going to be tested on. He is really nice and my experiences at his office hours were very helpful.

reviews.comment: I recommend taking Dan for the Capstone course. Whoever wrote those six negative reviews was definitely the same person who had some uniquely bad experience. NEVER TAKE DAN GIBBS FOR RESEARCH METHODS. DO NOT. This course is not supposed to be about coding but Mr Gibbs has decided he doesn't care and has made the entire course about a coding language that you will probably never use in your entire life. He regularly assigns massive problem sets that take 10s of hours to complete. DO NOT TAKE HIS COURSE.

reviews.comment: Do not take Research Methods with this professor. He stands at the front of the classroom while reading off the slides and does not teach the content to the class. The quizzes are hit or miss and the only way to keep your grade up is through writing assignments.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture consists of him just reading off of dense and wordy slides, does not reference the textbook in class, and quizzes are not on what is covered in lecture. He also makes rude comments under his breath about the class if people aren't asking or answering questions.

Lectures are just him reading off of extremely dense and wordy slides. Quizzes did not cover what was learned in the lecture, and came from a textbook we never used in class. Professor Gibbs also frequently makes snarky comments under his breath about the class, making a classroom environment that is hostile and makes students feel unwelcome.

Lectures are only him reading off the many slides. He makes snarky comments if students don't answer his questions. Except the 1st time someone decided to ask a question in this class they got yelled at, so you could understand why no one wants to speak up. The snarky comments are disrespectful to us and unprofessional coming from a professor.

I had Professor Gilbert for one of my classes and will be taking her class again next semester. She is strict about turning things in on time and can be a strict grader but as long as you turn in your assignments on time, can follow a rubric, and can listen to peer reviews you won't have any trouble. She is easy to pay attention to which helps too.

Professor Gilbert is the best professor I have ever had. She is so kind and always open to help with anything you need help with. The class is very easy if you just get the work done and you get to pick your topic for the papers you write so it is pretty easy to be interested in what you are doing. If you have the option to take her course TAKE IT
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gilbert is super sweet and understanding. She is a fair but strict grader. However, she makes expectations clear and offers examples for almost everything. There are no tests or exams. You will complete a research paper/project that will make up the majority of your grade. Attendance is mandatory, but she is understanding of absences.
Ms. Gilbert is a fair grader and as long as you participate and put in effort to her assignments you will get a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Gilbert was a great professor. She cares about nurturing her students as people. She is not a lenient grader, but a fair one. She gives ample opportunity for revision prior to submission. She is pretty stern about not accepting late work and offers great feedback on assignments.

I am taking ENGL 3764 with her. I find her quite lackluster as a professor. She grades the assignments way too harshly compared to many of the other professors I've heard about. Avoid her at all costs.

Took this class to fulfill pathway requirement, and went into it expecting to be super bored as I really don't like English. However, Professor Gilbert was able to make this class enjoyable, always had some interesting stories to tell.

Workload was very manageable, a discussion post and research benchmark every week (usually).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gilbert is amazing!!! You can tell she really cares about her students. Just go to class, even if attendance isn't mandatory. Her lectures are very interesting and clear, and she always points out what will be on the exams. Make it a habit to study your notes before the next class to prepare for pop quizzes and understand the material.

One of my favorite professors at Virginia Tech. You can tell she cares about her students and is passionate about what she teaches. I took her Cognitive Neuroscience class and would definitely take another class with her if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved this class.  Very lecture heavy but super interesting.  Tests are diagram/saq but the class before always gave a very good idea of what was gonna be on the exam.  Attendance isn't mandatory but she does have random pop quizzes; you can usually predict which day they will be on.  She's one of the sweetest most positive humans.

I had Gilbert for Neur 3084. Her lectures were fascinating. The pop quizzes were too much. The exams were similar to Dr. Cline's exams: diagrams & short answer. She offers extra credit questions on tests/quizzes but it was difficult to actually get them right. Overall she is knowledgeable and a good teacher; I didn't like the layout of her course.
Pretty good pilot ngl. Got me my private pilots license.

took gilbert for anatomy and physiology she is very kind and attendance isn't mandatory but is basically required if you want to pass the class.  She grades kindly and most exams/studying include memorizing diagrams(these can be very detailed) she gives a good amount of extra credit and the class is very lecture-heavy. take notes and voice record!

Dr. Gilbert is amazing! The class material is tough but she does a great job of teaching and of putting it into an easy concept to learn. Attendance is not mandatory but it is essential to do well in the class, she often gives specifics on what is expected on the exam. She really wants her students to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Gilbert is the BEST professor I have ever had. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

You have to go to class to do well with her and put in the effort to get an A. She really cares about her students and is always available for extra help.

I loved Dr. Gilbert's class for anatomy and physiology. Her tests (in person) were heavily diagramed based, but she went over the diagrams needed in detail during class. reviews.comment: He doesn't give answers. He'll look at you weird and ask if you read the textbook. He doesn't curve and grades hard. The final isn't a test, it's a presentation. You have to write a tough abstract. He might say it's good in person or email, but still give you half credit. I'd get a better grade with the same effort from any other professor.

He cares a lot about his students. He works with you no matter what level you are on. Definitely use office hours. I personally would not have passed without office hours since my brain is not a Combo brain. He cares more about whether you can think rather than getting the final answer correct. 
Highly recommend as a professor for any class.

He is the GOAT. Hard class but does a lot to explain things well and help you. Best math teacher I've had at Virginia Tech easily. Tests are the majority of your grade but he'll round your grade up in the end if he notices that you come to class and put in effort.

Hannah is one of the most brilliant lecturers I've ever had. She encourages honest, raw, and intellectual (while respectably vernacular) discussion in a way I've never seen in undergraduate. She's a fair grader and I highly, highly recommend her class.

Hannah is one of the most incredible professors I've ever had! It's hard to explain but her class is pretty unorthodox in a lot of remarkable ways. I would take this class again in a heartbeat. She's not only great at breaking down complex ideas and readings, but she also an amazing human being who genuinely cares about the people she's teaching.

Get ready to learn everything by yourself. You have a readiness assurance test(RAT) every single class. The quiz is based on a 7-12 page study guide that the professor provides. she's nice and smart but rumors about the class are true. ineffective teacher, requires insane amount of work, presents topics in confusing order and test questions confuse the class. she doesn't change class structure despite years of complaints. everyone should get a badge for making it through this class. equally frustrating as my year in ochem.

terri isn't that bad, she offers a lot of extra credit. she is super boring but tbh this class is gonna be hard no matter where u take it so it could be worse. if u look up quizlets from previous years and do all the dsms you'll be fine. the TAs also do reviews every test. this semester is WAY better than anatomy 1 tho

Terri is nice, but not a good teacher. Lectures are hard to follow, exams often have errors, and the course layout is confusing.TAs lacked knowledge and review sessions were useless. tests are not structured the way they should be. she takes anatomy and physiology, and then twists it into her own hieroglyphics for nobody to understand. she has a super power to take whatever understanding you may have of anatomy seem like little fun facts on the tests. have a blast!!!!!!

This class is very material heavy, but I think it is good preparation for med school. It is all lot of reading the textbook and teaching yourself since the class is so dense.
