reviews.comment: Hope you like paying tuition to this lady and teaching yourself. Her attempt at lectures sucked and YouTube was a way better source. She is your only choice, I pray for your sanity. You will need some SSRIs for this class, she drains all the remaining serotonin from the last 2 brain cells. Kiss your GPA goodbye, kiss your dreams goodbye.

People are dramatic about this class. Anatomy is a hard class and theres a lot of information to cover. people like to jump to blame the professor when they dont do well. This class takes a lot of work but I genuinely learned a lot. Im not an insanely smart person and I did well and had time for my other classes and still had plenty free time.

Where do I even begin, Terri Gillian is the bane of my existence. For an entire year, this woman terrorized me. Aside from lecture, the entire content is lousy online labs, then APR (some interactive anatomy thing). Literally you will have to go through these structures day in and day out. Prepare yourself to memorise everything by yourself.

I am not even joking when I tell you this class was the start of my depression. The woman who teaches this course is absolutely useless. If you must take this class, I highly HIGHLY suggest you take it somewhere else. In all my years, I have never seen a class so poorly structured, and a professor so unprepared and unqualified to teach it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I cannot stress enough how difficult this class was. Studying for the tests are nearly impossible bc there is so much material! PLEASE take this class somewhere else if you value your mental stability. I took anatomy in high school and got an A, however I had a C in this class consistently. I ended up dropping the course bc it was so stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I know that this is a hard class, but I have NEVER dedicated so much time and effort to a single class. Tests count for a lot but they are impossible to study for. You do homework/quizzes nonstop and the study guides are extremely long. The amount of info you have to memorize is near impossible and you have no guidance. New prof/format needed ASAPP
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's a nice person and has good intentions, but she should not be teaching this class-- or, at the very least, she needs to make *significant* changes. Tests are a huge portion of your grade and the tests are closed note/extremely difficult even after dozens of hours of hard work. This class crushes pre-med/PA/etc. dreams, and it SHOULDN'T.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is definitely the worst class I have ever taken since being in college. The amount of information is insane and sometimes seems to be impossible when taken with other important classes. Unless this is the only class you take the entire semester, good luck to your GPA and mine as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I know this is a difficult course, and she reminded the students. But you cannot and should not devote all your time to a single course. She responded to the email in a timely manner, but it was helpless. This is a compulsory course for majors, but most students do not learn anything. Only VT's math class is as bad as this one. What a pity!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Yes, the subject is hard but she is by far the absolute worst professor I've ever had at VT. I would rather suffer through 10 years straight of losing to UVA in football than take this class again. I hope you like keeping your head shoved in a textbook 24/7 and learning that way cause that's your only hope in this class. Avoid this class if online
The class average for each of the tests should not be in the 60's. Her exams are impossible and she cannot teach well online.

Quite possibly the most useless professor I have ever come to know. Offered no feedback and ruined this entire semester and possibly the Virginia Tech experience for me. She was no help outside of class and I had to withdraw from lab because she wouldn't offer me any solutions. Also had a hard time focusing on other classes. RIP my GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is a review for the summer ONLINE sessions for anatomy at VT. I took it because i thought it would be too hard to take while also taking Ochem. I am unsure if my decision was worth it though as it is a VERY vigorous course with power-points of 100+ slides everyday. Instead of enjoying my summer, I spend at least 5+ hours a day working on lab.

In my observations of this professor I found her to be engaging, extremely knowledgeable, animated, genuine, amazingly bright, overwhelmingly experienced, kind, considerate, and willing to do whatever is necessary to ensure the general, understanding, comprehension, and retained application of the class material. No other professor even comes close

Get ready. You are about to receive 1000+ years of information in 1 semester.  I sincerely hope you have no other classes.  Terri is slow to answer questions and gives you next to no time to complete quizzes.  Part 1 was mild but part 2 was absolutely insane. Good luck, if you can find an alternative DO SO!

So her class may be boring but her tests are not hard if you put time into studying. Everything on the tests comes EXACTLY from the power points. Study the lectures like she says to and you will have an A.
She's really sweet.

Although her tests were very difficult, there was so much information  that we had to cover in just one semester, we would be crazy to expect anything less than difficult.  Anatomy and physiology is not an easy subject, but she is an extremely helpful professor if you ask her to be.  Use the book, her slides, the extra credit, and you'll do fine.

Terrible teacher. All she does is read off slides, her tests are difficult, and you often find yourself ill-prepared for all of her tests. Then when you go to her office hours you find about 3-6 mistakes she has made on the test. She is an awful teacher who has been under review for 4 years now, they just can't find anyone to replace her.

Despite what other's say...Gillian's class is really interesting. Yeah, her tests are really hard but if you study her material, the book and do the extra credit there is no way you should do poorly. Attendance is mandatory bc of the graded Iclicker quizzes each class.
She was an awful professor. She was always late, and read straight off her slides but still made attendance mandatory. She was also not very helpful.

She is a pretty good teacher. Many disagree, but she gives iClicker and online quizzes which count a little more than a test and are an easy way to boost your grade if you are a responsible student and attend class. The 5 Tests cover a lot of material and are mostly from her lecture (some from the book). She also gives extra credit opportunities.
No Comments

Pay attention, take notes, download the powerpoints, and attend class for clicker points to help your grade.  Tests are pretty cut and dry but contain a lot of material, so reading is required.  This professor requires you be a fully responsible student.  Do so, and you'll learn a lot.
DOESNT EXPLAIN ANYTHING, DO NOT TAKE HER AS A PROFESSOR!

Signed up for this as a pathway class not knowing what to expect and left with a great understand of the course material. He is really passionate about the material and makes class very interesting despite teaching a seemingly boring topic. Attendance isn't mandatory but assignments and quizzes come straight out of the notes. Very few assignments.

He is so enthusiastic in the way he teaches. If you dont attend the lectures, then you will not know what is going on for the big projects and exams. Regardless, the lectures are really interesting and the way he explains makes it so much better. Really really sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Actually STS 3705. Professor Goodrum is incredibly passionate during his lectures. Even if there's relatively few people in class, he'll bring the same energy as if the classroom was packed. He gets excited about any questions asked and certain lectures that he'll build up to. He provides good feedback on papers and the HW is comparatively light.

My favorite professor I had this semester! This is a very back-to-basics class with just him and a whiteboard. The class discussions are always interesting and the class flew by each time. If you love any kind of science or humanities you will love this course. Assignments are a few short essays and a final exam. Best class I've taken so far.

Let me tell you. He is a harsh grader, but as long as you show up in the class and take notes, you'll get B+ at least. He is the best professor I have ever had in tech. This is the first class that I never got bored during the class.

This is a great class, but to fulfill pathways 3 I would not recommend it. You have to be interested in this topic. He also does not have a canvas page so you have to rely on going to class and/or classmate notes. There are four assignments total, which are a bit heavy.

Great lecturer and very interesting guy. He is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches. What I will say is that he grades pretty much based off of vibes of what you wrote. There is no rubric to any of the four assignments that make up the final grade. Even knowing I would get a B for a pathway, I'd do it again though.

Professor Goodrum was amazing. It was a lecture based class, but as long as you show up and take good notes the class isn't too bad. He knows what he is talking about and is very passionate about it. He is always willing to answer any questions you have after or during class.

This class was super fun and interesting. He is very into the material he teaches and is always ready to answer questions. The board vocab is important and attending class is as well. Overall a great pathway.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Consistently passionate about his material. Had the patience to answer the many questions we had; often went overtime to consider all queries. I'm grateful that professors like him are willing to stay and invigorate students' interests further. A great inspiration due to his thirst for knowledge and self improvement. Whole class respected him!

Came into this class not knowing what to expect but the material was very interesting as a science major and he made it very fun to listen to. DO NOT take this class if you are someone who skips a lot. He doesn't have Canvas and doesn't have slides or anything. You have to go to lecture and take good notes to do well, but if you do, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I went in with little interest, but it was the most interesting class I had all semester. You need to show up to lecture to do well on his 3 written assignments, but he makes them worth listening to. He's a very interesting story teller and obviously passionate about the subject. Very accommodating and helpful if needed.
great

Most interesting class I have ever taken! The professor is very passionate and excited about all the topics. Best AREA 2 to take! A few papers but follow the guidelines and you will get a high grade. 2 books to read, only need to read few chapters of one of them. ALWAYS right the vocab on the board down!!! Have to go to class to do well!

Fun class. I enjoyed going to class, but I wish I had taken another elective. Even though Dr. Goodrum is a very good professor he grades HARD. I did great in the class assignments (nothing below a B+) but even though I knew the material on the essay final I ended up with a B-.

I took this class as a requirement but ended up loving it! Professor Goodrum is one of the few decent teachers at Tech. He really makes class interesting and as long as you go to class and listen you will do fine on his essays. Recommend his classes to anyone!
Very interesting subject matter and not hard to get an A if you are decently skilled at writing. Professor Goodrum clearly has a high level of expertise in the field of study.

Take his classes if you genuinely are interested in the subjects, you will learn a lot! The class is by no mean easy and he is a tough grader but there is a curve. Be prepared to take quick notes as his handwriting is almost illegible but if you stay on top of things you will learn a lot and get a strong grade to go with it. Loved this class!!!

Professor Goedert is a really kind person who teaches the material in a clear and thought provoking manner. His assignments were time consuming but simple to understand. He is a hard grader but curves heavily. Do the readings and participate in class and your grade will benefit. One of the best professors I've had within the poli-sci department.

*PSCI 2074 Good guy and super smart. Had to buy 4 books for the class. The final was an exam plus a 10 min presentation and 10 page research paper which I think was too heavy of a final for a 2000 level course. Interesting lectures if you enjoy content. Stay on top of readings (which there are many) makes the class a lot easier/more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're interested in American politics, take any of his classes. Extremely smart and I learned a lot

Learned so much from this class. He explains complex topics very well to people who don't understand it. Super good professor who has already published his own book. Any PSCI student should take all of his classes.  However, he does assign a lot of textbooks, but nowadays they're all free online so that isn't even a problem anymore I guess.

Many who say that Dr. Goedert is too hard just don't work hard. His classes aren't a piece of cake, but if you understand the material and take good notes you will get an A. Btw, for those PSCI students who aspire to be law students, Dr. Goedert touches on many different law-related areas as well. Never learned more from someone than him!!!

As with all his classes, this one in particular is super interesting and he actually teaches work from established/famous political scientists. He dives into the history of America's parties and relates it to today's parties as well. If you actually want to LEARN something during your time here you should take Dr. Goedert. I learned so much.

Honestly probably my favorite class and prof I've had at tech. Material is genuinely interesting and he presents it in an engaging way that makes you want to go to class. Not a lot of assignments which is a pro and a con cause he is a tough grader, but does give great feedback on how to improve and curves. Would highly recommend taking his classes.

Overall, even though the lectures could feel a little long, Professor Goedert's class wasn't bad at all. just be sure to turn up to class, do some of the reading, and write good notes. All of the tests were open note, the only real difficult assignment was the final paper. However, as long as you give yourself time and put in effort you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is a 1xxx level course but it taught as a 4xxx level. Professor Goedert already expects students to know substantial vocabulary and slightly above average about the United States government. The class is out of 200 point and research paper (50) weighs more than the final, which is just two essays (30). There were four quizzes (25 or 20).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a fun personality and decently chill. There are readings and he shows a lot of respect for his students. Can sometimes be a little dull but definitely a better professor than most. Participate a lot and you will do well.

Dr. Montero is kind, and really approachable. He really likes his students to be involved in class discussions, and you need to do the readings before class. However, he's a super easy grader and just wants to know you understand the themes being discussed. He doesn't respond to his emails, so make sure to approach him in-person if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Montero is very passionate about the course material. He expects you to do the readings and expects participation in the class. There are a lot of group discussions. The material can be difficult to read through, expect to take time out of class to comprehend the material. This course has a quiz about every other week but not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Yee is a very good professor and it is clear how much he cares about our learning of the material. He is always willing to help in and out of lectures. I appreciated having him as the professor for this course and truly believe he was one of the best professors to teach the course. He is much kinder and more caring than nonmajors claim.
the whole class average was in the sixties

Yee is very clear that he is accessible outside class. He kind of goes on tangents in lecture and it is never really clear what to take notes on, or what will be on the exam. Do the practice tests. He is helpful in office hours. And he holds review sessions. He really does want everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: this man is deteriorating do NOT take his class. class avg grade was a 60 something i stg

It is clear that Dr. Yee is very passionate about chemistry, but I do not like him as a professor. Although it was his first time teaching CHEM-1036, he made errors within the exams and lectures (ie class slides) which made it unnecessarily difficult. The tests were not similar to practice material and his teaching style was not straight forward.

Dr. Yee is a fine lecturer and a nice guy outside of class but he is not meant to teach gen chem. His tests were completely diff from practice questions he would put out so this semester 2/4 tests had an average grade of like 55-60%. Pretty much everything else was relatively fine except the tests, find another prof if at all possible.

I felt like the people in this class were test subjects since it was the teacher's first year teaching the course. He belittled his students. He didn't use his own material but still made his own tests. He would say he filled in the notes and posted them, but the notes were incomplete. There were multiple mistakes on the tests, which wasted time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i had to drop because i would get a C if not. is almost impossible to get a B/A with him. felt hopeless going into every exam after studying 30 hours just for the exam

i had yee as my chem lab professor. he was passionate, and wanted us to have fun, but always came off as in a bad mood. he had us write our own procedures for a couple labs, which took forever. but then would come over during lab and ask us why we were doing it a certain way when there was a better way. it never really made since to me.

Spare yourself and just take gen chem 2 at New River Community. Yee used another professors notes the whole semester but then made his own tests, so they often didn't even line up. There's lengthy homework's due almost every day during the week and they're also nothing like his lectures. just don't take chem with him.

He used other professor's notes and would post them, claiming they were filled in, but they weren't. His tests had spelling mistakes, words repeated twice, and one test question didn't even have a correct answer. He would say the averages were higher than they actually were and has still not released grades even though the semester ended last week.

Worst gen chem professor ever, he had to apply a curve to the entire class final grade just to make the average a C.  Not clear when teaching, teaches general chemistry like we should already know it.  I probably spent 20+ hours studying for the final just to scrape by.

Yee is a nice guy, very passionate about chemistry but his class is pretty dang hard. With lots of effort, this class can be manageable, but I had to fight for my life to get a B-. I wish he would've used his own class slides and material, instead of using the previous professor's, because his exams were very different and much more difficult.

He seems like a nice man, but he is not a good teacher. I had a 95 average on quizzes and 100 on all homework's. My test average was around a 60. The exams never seemed to match up with our quizzes or practice exams. I spent hours and hours studying for the exams only to fail. Wouldn't recommend taking this class with him.

The ONLY time I've ever heard of the CHEM department curving an entire class's final grade. His tests were so beyond unfair, it took us all complaining about it for them to do something. His tests are impossible to pass unless you have a friend who can teach you. Learned most stuff from studio. His iclicker pts are half for correctness. Goodluck.

Gordon Yee is super smart but he thinks everyone else is on that level. He can be funny, but most times is condescending when you ask him questions 1 on 1. He writes his own tests which most times there's errors on it. He uses other professors' studio quizzes, wrkshts, practice tests, and slides. It's almost impossible to get an A with Yee. gg.

Nice guy but horrible teacher. The class average was an F for most exams. Lecture heavy with lots of outside assignments that take a long time to complete. His exams were very difficult and he often had to give points back for mistakes on questions. If you have the option of another teacher, please CHOOSE SOMEONE ELSE.

This class was a nightmare. If you're seeing this save your gpa and take it with another professor. The material itself wasn't that bad but every test violated me to say the least. Averages have been F's across all 4 tests.

He is sweet and smart but I will have nightmares from this class. He doesn't know how to teach gen chem, makes mistakes in class, doesn't fully explain things bc he thinks its obvious. I go to every class, record the lecture, went to office hours, have a 98 avg on my studio quizzes, but have a 60 avg on tests bc they're so bad DO NOT TAKE HIM

He knows what he's talking about, but assumes everyone knows what he does and belittles students when they ask questions and makes them feel dumb. His lectures are long and he makes a lot of mistakes in lecture and homework assignments, which makes things hard to follow. Test averages are fail-65 on avg. Had Candace for chem 1 and did way better

Awful experience in gen chem 1036. Test never matched up with material taught or practice material given and most answers on the practice test were wrong. Very carless and uninterested in the success of students, as the class average was constantly below a 50%.

So so so bad, never take this professor for gen chem.  Unhelpful, unclear, constantly made mistakes.  Last time I checked the overall class average was a 68. It was so bad, I want to give you a zero, but that's not possible, so I give you a one.

Worst professor ever, tests are nothing like the lectures or practice tests, I got 100s on all the studio quizzes but had a C average on exams.  Constant mistakes in spelling/wording of material, he made mistakes in solving problems in lecture and had to backtrack at least once per class.  Condescending when people don't understand the topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible Chemistry professor. Took this class for non CHEM majors. He doesn't care about anyone that isn't a chemistry major. Would frequently get questions wrong solving them on the board. I spent an average of 15 hours per week on this class to complete and understand the assignments, only to get around 45% on the tests. :thumbs down:
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seemed nice but isn't a good teacher. All of the test score averages have been 50's. Did not seem like he wanted to take accountability when students brought up testing concerns in class. Said he'd curve the class so the average student would make a C+ but wouldn't be honest about what the grade of the average student was. Had to drop anyway.
He was nice but this course felt like a slow motion really dramatic plane crash.

Was the worst professor I've ever had. Has no interest in seeing his students succeed. Had to literally talk to head of the chem department about him. Teaches with another professor's slides but makes his own tests so they don't correlate at all. Do not take this class

Tests were just brutal the practice tests he gave us were made by other professors and would often have content we didn't cover in class. When it was brought up he said in real life you won't have a practice test. He is a good guy just not a good professor.

Great for other chem probably, but not for General Chemistry. The tests were all application based and made absolutely NO sense. Had to drop many test questions and often made mistakes in lecture. This was horrible.

He was a good professor and his lectures were okay but his tests were brutal. All application based and 95% of students wouldn't be able to finish the test in the given time. Studied for 3 weeks for his exam and still couldn't pass them.

Gordon's lectures are ok, but his tests are nothing like the HW's, Studio worksheets/quizzes, and practice tests. The average for the past 3 tests was in the 50's. Expect 90% of the questions on tests to be curveballs because you will NOT see similar ones on the practice tests. He acknowledged continued to make the tests nothing like practice ones.
dont take this class. drop while you still can. tests are nothing like the lectures or the practice tests!!!!!! the average on every test has been a FAIL. boo
Drop the class if this is your professor.
Absolutely do not take this class! He does not know how to teach or prepare you for the test. His test averages have been around 50-60.

Despite what others may say about Dr. Yee, I had a rather good experience in Chem 2424 with him. I felt that he truly cared about our success. The lectures were definitely important to attend as some test questions were derived from things he said in lectures. However, the course was fairly difficult as each test consisted of a lot of content.
Does not care if a student fails or passes. His lectures are boring and he does not respect his students. Literally the worst. Do not take his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. Yee is so chill and a very interesting human. I feel that taking easier courses with him is likely more enjoyable but I took Chem 1066 with him and it was insane. Expect spending many many hours in the lab if you do not perfectly understand the concepts, and even if you do, sometimes he will throw in something that you havent even been taught!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: There were times that I was confused on the homework and he met up with me around 10pm on zoom. He definitely "tries" to help his students. However, be aware that his will belittle you and make you feel as you are dumb. He also will blame students for the average tests being a 50 and try to bring up the highest grade to make us feel bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gordon is one of the most caring professors I've ever had! I unfortunately had to withdraw from his class due to personal reasons, but he is extremely accessible outside of class for help, review sessions, or just to chat! He seems to really enjoy interacting with his students and makes class interesting and interactive. Be sure to do the iClicker!

Most caring professor Ive ever had. He will meet with you over zoom anytime of the day to go over concepts/questions because he truly wants his students to do good. I would take advantage of this!!! Uses iClicker for attendance. Lots of homework, but thats just chem1035 in general.  Brings his dog, Grace, to campus for students to play with her.

Taught both through zoom and online, depended one what the covid cases were in the area (in person when low) for person reasons. Handwriting is very hard to read but he will elaborate on any question you have, will answer your email within the hour, and will do office hours any time you need it. Brought his dog in for students to see her sometimes.

Dr. Yee is always willing to help if you have questions basically whenever. You can literally email him at 7 PM, and he will respond and set up a zoom meeting the same night. I didn't really like meeting with him one on one though because he makes you feel kinda dumb if you don't understand it. It is almost less awkward to ask during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer and is very engaging. However, outside of class, he talks down to students and belittles them when they don't understand concepts. He is arrogant, rude, and should not be teaching a class if he is going to make fun of students questions during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Explains it so well and really cares what his students think. He gives easy in-class quizzes that are exactly from the HW, so it really helps your grade. His tests are hard but he gives you a lot of worksheets and last years test to improve. He moves pretty quickly, but has really good demonstrations and is funny, so its worth taking his class!

Dr. Yee was amazing. He knew what he was talking about and made sure that we did too. He stops to ask for questions a lot, and he really cares about our grades. He will meet with you for questions all the time and holds lots of review sessions. He made funny jokes and told funny stories. I understand and enjoy chemistry a lot more because of him.
great, great professor. really wants you to succeed. go bug him for help. he's glad to give it you.

Demonstrations in class really help students grasp the concepts. Provides numerous resources for students to use in order to succeed on the exams. Responds to emails and answers questions that you have so that you really understand. Hilarious during lecture, but when you're one-on-one he's more serious and intent about you understanding the concept
Cool. HE REPLIED TO MY EMAIL.
got to work hard and go to class, it is a hard class but great professor

Dr. Yee is such a good professor. He really wants the students to succeed but doesn't make it an easy course. He is always offering help and practice problem sessions. Go to them! Go to the review sessions! Go to office hours! He will break everything down if you don't understand. He wants his students to learn. Very helpful.
AWESOME!

Dr. Yee is not very sociable and is sometimes disorganized, but is a good teacher. He speaks clearly, moves at a comfortable pace, and allows us to work out practice problems in class. As a perk on the side, he is fairly amusing.
No Comments

Dr. Yee has a great sense of humor and loves fire.  His class is challenging to most who take it, but he curves to make up for it.  The majority who take it are Biochem/Chem majors or honors students.  I would reccomend him highly.
nice guy, very thorough.  enjoys teaching and tries to get the class involved.  helps if asked
interesting experiments in class but moves very quickly, test only have a few very hard problems on them, usually hes the only choice for majors but if youre not don't take him

He usually teaches the majors/honors section of general chemistry. A lot of people have to take general chem for their major even if they're not chem majors. This section is probably the most interesting one of all, but it is somewhat more difficult.

Dr K is the GOAT! The class is fairly "easy", but if you really want to learn a lot and go deep, you definitely can!! The people who are confused about assignment instructions didn't attend lectures and didn't read the instructions. You never know what Dr. K is going to talk about, which makes things interesting and engaging. He's also very kind!

This was the very first class I took for my grad program and after this one, I registered for every other class taught by this professor. Yes, he does changes things on the fly from time to time, but all the projects are very interesting and relevant. He is lenient on due dates and a soft grader. Very welcoming no stress learning environment.
Avoid this professor

This class was one of the most stressful courses I have ever taken. There is no structure whatsoever. He changes assignment requirements after you have already started on a project. Be prepared to not get feedback or grades for over a month even for a discussion board post. Avoid this professor and wait till a term Professor Oliva teaches it!
His projects and classes are interesting. Take him if you can tolerate disorganization. This class is more like go with the flow kind of class.
He's unprepared. We did not know how many assignments we were going to get or how much % each assignment was going to weigh.

Does not offer office hours on the basis of "we are on piazza every day" but his answers to questions on piazza are way too brief (I got a 5 word answer today to a major question) and often aren't ultimately helpful. Piazza is great for quick questions, but not when you have confusion on a bigger topic.

I would highly recommend taking Dr. K. I have him in my first semester of grad school & was very worried by the title of the course as I know from my undergrad, software engineering classes are typically very hard. However, he makes this class very understandable and super lenient. Does not grade tough, very interactive on Piazza & takes late work.

Professor does not explain material well. Provides feedback but it is useless if you are trying to learn. It would be very useful to someone who already knew the material but then why take the class. Many speak well of him but I found him to be an empty suit professor. Takes forever to get grades back so you never really know where you stand

Very good professor. Knows the content he is teaching and is helpful for things you don't understand. I will say though if you're a student who needs a lot of handholding, he's probably not the best professor for that. Practice exams are really similar to the actual exams, and all the problems he goes over in class are very relevant to the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are just slow, he'll take forever to go over simple things all of us should already know like taking a cross product but glazes over the methods behind figuring out how to approach and set up problems.

Good lectures, actually understood the material. Go to class since he boosts grades based on attendance rate at the end of the course. Practice he uploads for tests is pretty accurate to the actual exam so understand how to do those problems and the ones in the lecture slides.

Exams are very difficult; he ALWAYS throws curveballs on exams. Class averages for the majority of the exams were well into failing, and no curve was applied. Lectures were not helpful, as he just steps through content like everyone knows what is going on.

Even somepeople said he did not teach well in statics, but my feeling is that he is not as bad as some comments below. He teaches decient way. His exam is really similar to the practice tests. He was a little bit shy in his office hour in beginning, but later it's fine. He gives good helps on homework after calss and in office hour.

Great professor hard class. Statics is going to be challenging for most people and at least gragg doesn't cater to unicorns who never need study and has a lot of good material for test prep. Homework is straightforward but lengthy and lectures are concise and structured. If you can get him for statics you're better off than most form the start.

Did the Deforms in France program with him and it was phenomenal.  Class was very straight forward and conducive to my summer internship and the abroad portion of the program was a blast.  Gragg is a genuinely caring and understanding professor and is very flexible when needed.  10/10

Took statics online with Dr. Gragg. His lecture videos are from COVID I believe, so some info (like the platform we were using) were outdated. His lectures were straightforward and easy to understand, 10/10. Went to office hours a couple times and he felt a little scary, not mean - probably just an introvert. Would take his class online again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took Deforms with Dr. Gragg. Homeworks are very similar to tests. Adjusted grading scale is super helpful to your grade. Overall decent professor.

Incredibly nice grading scale where a 60% is passing (C-). All tests are identical to the practice test more or less. Lectures can be word heavy but the examples are very helpful and are exactly what you see on every test. Fair amount of homework but it is very helpful for tests as well.

Dr. Gragg provided a very beneficial adjusted grading scale to where its easier to get a better grade with a lower overall grade number, however, he is a tough grader when it comes to tests. He had alright lectures, but I feel like with how accelerated this course was, the lectures were not appropriate for a course that is less than 3 weeks long.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He has a great grading system that is shifted down instead of your grade being curved compared to other people.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gragg was great! His notes were super organized and easy to follow which was super helpful throughout the semester. He uses a curved grading scale which is certainly a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gragg is very knowledgable and helps his students by lowering the grade thresholds. I believe an 86 is an A-. There is lots of homework and you will need to go to class to have a good understanding of the subject. His lectures are a bit boring but still helpful. He gives four midterm exams and the final is very hard but he doesn't write it.

One of the better statics teachers. Attendance can be used for a grade boost as he has a code to log attendance after class. 60% overall is a C-. Lots of homework but no stress to finish it because it's all due at the end of the semester. Study the homework and take notes on the last example before every exam and you will do well.

If you do not have a basic understanding or keep up with the pace of the course lectures and homework, you'll find yourself lost pretty easily. He explains in his lectures well, but the little work he shows is spread out on different slides, barely shown to be related to the problem, and too fast to simply watch and listen to. Write and work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A lot of the reviews on here are pretty old and certainly don't properly reflect his current class. Dr. Gragg is a nice and understanding guy who wants all of his students to succeed. The lectures are straightforward and if you pay attention you will be well prepared for the exams. He is also a very nice grader and awards lots of partial credit.

Class is not mandatory, but it will get you "extra credit". Homeworks are not due until the last day of classes but DO NOT GET BEHIND. He traches straight from a powerpoint and for me that was not the most helpful thing. When helping with homeworks he could never really help me because I really think he didn't understand himself. TAKE DR.CHANG

Had him for statics and highly recommend. He does give a lot of HW but it's all due the day of the exam instead of 1 or 2 due per week. Exams aren't that bad, questions are easier than the hardest homework problems. He doesn't curve but uses a shifted grading scale so 90 is an A. Also rounds grade up for attendance up to 1 point so 85.2 to 86.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Gragg is a decent teacher. His lectures are ok, but can get boring if you're in a 2 day section. The entire grading scale is adjusted so a 60 is a C-, and the partial credit lets you get points for questions you have no idea how to approach. There's a lot of hw, but it prepares you decently well for the exams.

I took his esm 2104 class asynchronous, it was the best online course set up ive seen. Very organized, very easy to follow. There were many lectures, but they were all very helpful and efficient. He taught the material very well and explained things as easy as possible. The homeworks are pretty hard, as are the tests. The course content is hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Teach nothing

At first, I thought Gragg would be a really good professor because he extends homeworks upon request and will boost your grade based on your attendance. However, when we went into course material he moved super fast and goes through example problems so fast you cant understand them. His tests are also very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gragg is an incredible teacher who has hit the perfect balance between theory and practical in his teachings and power point presentations. Tips: Attend class (he rounds grade up based on attendance), Redo notes problems(similar to test questions), don't be afraid to ask questions, and he doesn't curve but uses shifted grading scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I've never been a fan of statics. I dropped it last semester at tech but this semester I had Gragg. He is one of the best professors at tech. I didn't use my resources enough but he had endless. He made statics super easy and not scary. He knows what college kids are like. get gragg if you can he is seriously awesome

I had Gragg for Statics also, and I can say he's much better with dynamics; he enjoys the material more, and that translates to class. HW is heavy but done on Wiley plus, and he has lots of office hours where he is happy to help you understand a concept. Won't curve grades but adjusts the grading scale instead.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: All in all he isn't too bad. Tests are very straightforward; if you can do all of the engineering they're an easy 100, no tricks. With that said, the book is terrible at explaining statics, and he can run quickly through topics, though he can explain things in detail at office hours. The HW sucks and there is a lot of it, but same for all sections
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This is my first and only review of a teacher and I just finished my sophomore year. He made it clear there was no "bumping" of grades at the end of the teamster unless you attended all the classes which I did and yet he did not bump my grade from an A- to an A which would have given me straight As. So yes I am salty. Also reads right from textbook

To this day I'm not sure he even gets what he's teaching. A couple friends have taken homework problem's he has assigned to his office hours and he can't even get them. Inconsistent with points on tests, incredibly harsh, and makes A LOT of errors. Will begrudgingly give some back if you go to his office hours but you need to fight for them.

I actually really liked him as a professor. He lets you extend homework assignments and exams if you need to. I think he teaches fairly well to, he does sample problems in class. He is really understanding and responds to emails fairly quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: picks the hardest version of each problem for the test. Picks the question that has as many exception to the rule and deviates the most from examples in class. You can really know the material and still do poorly on exams. Partial credit is worth nothing to him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to switch to a different teacher, you should! He lectures directly from the book and isn't helpful (if you can find him) in office hours.

Pay attention and do much more work out of class or you will not pass. He copies the lecture out of the book and refused to go over Wrench Moments because 'he doesn't like them'. If you can get Chang or anyone else do that and save yourself a repeat or a GPA drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, just very new to teaching. He doesn't teach; he copies the lecture out of the textbook and copies the solution onto the board. His exams are confusing and time consuming, and aren't good preparation for Hendrick's final.

He uses his own textbook to teach, which is fine if it wasn't written in a way that's hard to find information. Plus side, exams and quizzes are open-note, even for past practice tests he gives. Even reuses some questions from past works, so it helps a lot. His office hours are helpful, even available to meet online!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great statistics professor. He explains concepts clearly, gives helpful examples, and is always willing to answer questions. His class feels organized, fair, and supportive. I learned a lot and would definitely recommend him

he pretty much lectures exclusively from his textbook that he wrote himself, which is okay but that pretty much defeats the purpose of coming to class excluding review days. his exams and quizzes were all open everything except the internet, the practice exams he goes over in class are very similar to the midterms given out. also seems mean to me
all you do is read the textbook. if you don't read the textbook you'll fail. he doesn't teach either because "its all in the book." he is a nice guy though and helpful if you go to his office hours.
Great teacher wants to see you get a good grade

Professor Cheng is great. He cares a lot about making sure we understand the material and is simply a great guy. However, the course does require you to buy and use a specific financial calculator and will not allow any other type or brand of calculator to be used in exams. Otherwise, the course was very easy and worth taking.

Very sweet professor, gives extra credit for many things, including attendance. He is very sweet and made this class bearable and engaging. If you have the option to take this class with Dr. Cheng, don't pass the opportunity up!

This class is so easy. He takes extra credit attendance often, and attendance is optional except for exams. Be sure to get the right calculator because you'll use it the entire course. He does have a bit of an accent, but all of the lectures are posted to Canvas as slides. Overall, he's a great and understanding professor!

I took this class as a 5F pw and it was an easy A. Minimal studying and tons of extra credit (while still learning important life info). He is just so so kind and wants to make sure that his students aren't stressed out! He even let us use 2 pieces of paper front and back as a "cheat sheet" for the second and third exam! 100% recommend for a pw 5F!

Cannot say enough good things about professor Cheng!!!! He is so kind, so sweet, and truly just wants everyone to get an A in his class. You don't really neeeed to buy the textbook but it helps for chapter quizzes (which are all on quizlet). He gives extra credit for literally going to class. Probably the nicest guy you'll ever meet

great professor, he really cares about his students and explains the math very well. always open to questions. i didn't use the textbook once so i don't recommend buying it. he does random participation extra credit which was really sweet, and he allows cheat sheets during exams.

do not bother buying the textbook, i went to every class before the first exam and did amazing without studying then the other 2 we could bring a cheat sheet and I never went to class again after the first exam and still ended with almost an 100 amazing teacher who truly cares about helping and getting good grades

Dr. Cheng is awesome! If you need an easy pathways class take this with him. He really enjoys teaching and will explain it to you until you understand. Random extra credit for attendance but not mandatory. He says you need textbook but i haven't used it. Also, 2/3 exams are online.

He's super awesome. Explain topics clearly and answers any questions willingly. Gives out tons of extra credit for just showing up to class, and for 2/3 of the exams he let us bring in a double-sided full paper of notes. Would 100% recommend it!

Prof. Cheng was lovely! His lectures were clear and digestible to a non-math-savvy person such as myself. He's a funny guy who always has a smile on his face. Never seen the guy frustrated at a student. The quizzes and tests are real thinkers, so prepare for light studying. Though 2/3 of the tests he let us use a note sheet!

Great class. He gives out a lot of extra credit for attendance. The tests were a little tricky, but he let us make a "cheat-sheet" for formulas and other information we wanted to have during the test which was nice! Just make sure you take notes and actually pay attention in class, as the topics get more complex as the class progresses.

Dr. Cheng is a lovely professor, and very knowledgable in the field. Everything you need to know for tests is taught in class, and he gives plenty of in-class practice/help for the math, which isn't too hard. Showing up to class is worth it, as he gives extra credit for attendance. And the final isn't cumulative. Great class for math pathways.

Great professor. Class wasn't too hard, just make sure you go to the lectures and take notes. He gives out extra credit for attendance frequently, so if you come to class it can really help your grade! I didn't really use the textbook at all, most of the information (if not all) came straight from the lectures.

Professor Cheng was such a sweet professor, and you can tell he cared for those in his class. The class itself wasn't hard, you just have to pay attention and retain the information being given. He says you will need a textbook, but I never opened the book at all. Attendance was never mandatory, but he would randomly give extra credit for coming.

This class was fairly easy but as the year went on, concepts got more complex. Overall, if you go to most of the lectures and do some studying before the exam (make sure to attend the in-class review session), you'll do fine. Classes were lectures with practice problems. Very low-key class. I found the textbook for free online.

Dr. Gray was my favourite proffessor this semester. There is a lot of assignments to cover, but working on them actually taught me stuff. He makes lectures very enjoyable. If you have the ability to choose proffessors, make sure to search for his classes.
Super nice guy, made the incredibly boring course worth attending. Both UTA and GTA (Jacob kawada and Anika) are very cool and pretty charitable.

Dr. Gray was a great professor, and I wish I could've taken him for 1216. The class is pretty easy as long as you do your work and follow the rubrics. My TA's were also very helpful , so that was a plus. Only bad thing about this class was group work, my group was terrible but it's obviously different for everyone. Overall, good prof, easy class.
Lot's of work but thats every 1215 class, he makes this boring class pretty entertaining and funny.
Very good and funny

if you got dr. gray you won the lottery when it comes to engineering professors. he is the absolute funniest, most down to earth guy i know. if he doesn't know how to answer your question, he will just say that and point you towards a resource that can help. this is a pretty basic and boring course, but he makes it super entertaining.

Fortunate enough to have Dr. Gray for both 1215 and 1216, saw a man with a mustache, thought he had to be cool.. and he was. Gave a great foundation for what it means to be a Hokie Engineer. Caring and great interactions w/ students through daily surveys and walking around class. While the curriculum can be cumbersome, Gray made the class great.

Very funny professor who is accessible out of class as well. Had him for 1215 and 1216 and personally loved the way his class was run. Always interacting with students through daily surveys and walking around class checking in. While both classes were kinda boring and easy, Dr. Gray made classes as fun as they could get. Loved the shark facts too.
100% should take this professor's class.

Dull class, but Dr. Gray does a good job of giving you time to work with your team in class on your project. Most of the assignments can be done within 30 minutes. Gives funny shark facts every class and has an awesome mustache.

Dr. David Gray is one of the best professors at Virginia Tech. He will set you up for a lot of engineering related activities outside of his classes and provides a lot of support for both in class assignments and personal projects. Plus, his mustache is beyond peak.

Great professor; makes what is otherwise a tedious class entertaining and engaging. You are assigned a group for the entire semester, but he provides peer evaluations throughout the semester. The work can be a lot at times if you wait until the due date, and TA grading can be inconsistent and nitpicky, but nothing too bad. (Also, great facial hair)

Super fun professor. The entire premise of 1215 seems to be busy work, but I don't think that's his fault. All of the assignments lacked clear instructions which made things difficult, but if you started work early and went to his office hours for help you would be totally fine. He wants his students to succeed. TAs graded harsh, again, not on him.

Dr Gray is an amazing professor! His lectures are clear and fun. One of the fun classes I remember is drawing the steps to make a toast, which highlights the importance of logic flow and so to introduce us to coding. Besides, Dr Gray also helped my team to solve conflict, which made teamwork more harmonious.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Gray is currently my favorite professor so far entering into Virginia Tech. I think he's a fun dude with a good sense of humor and takes things pretty easy. The class itself isn't that hard, but there were a lot of team assignments that were somewhat tedious and a good amount of writing. Glorious mustache and loved talking about platypeople.
Amazing teacher that cares about making sure his students succeed in their careers. Pretty easy class as long as you do your work.

He is a great professor; he loves to use data to improve his teaching techniques. He is also hilarious and makes class fun. During the first 5 minutes of every class, he does a slideshow of collective funny things from the class before.

He has been the best professor/teacher I have ever had. If you can get him for your Enge section it is a must do. He was so good I even based my schedule for my next semester to be around the only 2 sections of the course he was teaching.
Immaculate Mustache. Really good dude.

Although I did struggle with the coding aspect of this course (which isnt too much) I enjoyed sitting in class for the hour and 15 since Dr. Gray made it interesting. Sometimes the lectures seem pointless but when it gets to something important like MATLAB or group project directions/explanations he makes it interesting. Nice mustache too.
Cool dude with the best mustache. He makes the class interesting even though the subject matter is not.
Gray is an amazing teacher, but your group really makes or breaks this class

Probably the greatest professor at Virginia Tech. He is hilarious, has amazing facial hair, and genuinely cares. He makes his own curriculum for the class, so you will be doing different things than your friends with different instructors, but you learn the same thing, and it's so much easier. He loves facts about animals, specifically platypi.

Dr. Gray is an amazing professor, highly recommend taking his class. His lectures are very informative and pretty entertaining too. He has Platypus facts, and they are pretty humorous and a good way to start each class.
Class is easy and Dr. Gray is very laid back. There is group work, but not a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really cool guy with a glorious mustache. Had him in Spring 2021 so everything was online, but he really cares about his students and worked to make the class fun and interesting. Every semester or so he has sent an email to my class checking in on us ever since. Highly recommend taking the class with him if you have the opportunity.

Dr. Gray did a great job of preparing students for a college education in engineering. The concepts and methods he taught are used to this day. The group project can be hit or miss depending on your teammates but I continue to work with them to this day. He has a lot of undergrad research opportunities so ask him for that! Go Porcupines!
super nice guy, really funny, just a lot of busy work

He is so much fun but the lessons he give are still invaluable. The introductory ENGE courses seem ultimately less important than more specific content-focused classes but Gray still found a way to make this course remarkable in both the fun we had and the things we learned.
He was an extremely fun teacher and made the class interesting. We learned about porcupines each day and then got into so engineering projects.
Super funny guy, engaging lectures.  A lot of the assignments were tedious and the TA's graded a bit harsh for what the level of material.

Dr. Gray is great at keeping lectures engaging and interactive. He's a friendly and funny person who genuinely cares about the success of his students. Very responsive in email, and super helpful in office hours- will address any questions in great detail.

A very great professor. Assignments are individual at the beginning of the semester and these are very easy but very time-consuming and dense. Later in the year, most of the assignments are for your group project. There is a lot of freedom in these group projects. Gray overall is just a very considerate and funny professor- makes class enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gray is a great, caring instructor who is very adaptive to the needs of students. He listens to student feedback constantly, and adjusts assignment expectations and due dates whenever needed. I would definitely take him again. There is a considerable amount of homework, but if you start it early, you should be fine.

ENGE 1414***    Genuinely the best professor I have ever had. Dr. Gray is extremely smart and is very good at teaching. He masterfully navigates a long list of monotonous course learning objectives and manages to make class fun and funny constantly. He teaches course content and life skills, prioritizing mental health.
He was a great professor and like really liked him as a person but I took ENGE 1414 with him and the class was a pain. I felt like there was a lot of busy work.
big w
Dr. Gray has an amazing mustache and a great style of teaching for a design-based course like ENGE 1414. Porcupines and engineering go very well.

Dr. Gray himself was pretty awesome. He was a great professor in what wasn't a great class. ENGE 1216 requires you to be in a group for the entire semester, so if you end up in a bad group (which I was in), then youll be working long hours annoyed at your group members for not putting in some effort.

Dr. Gray is super easy going and funny. He starts and ends every class pretty lightly. We got into interesting engineering concepts that felt more practical than lots of what we learned in other classes. Definitely my most engaging class in online school. He's also great to talk to if you're on the fence about your major or engineering at all.

He is a super fun teacher and actually keeps students engaged through zoom. His class might be very slightly harder than with other profs, but it's definitely worth it. I asked him advice on applying for research he gave me a bunch, put in a good word with the professor for me, offered to read my application, and gave really helpful suggestions.

I LOVE DR GRAY. Seriously, take his class. I had it online and he does a pretty good job of keeping it entertaining. He is super caring and encourages people to come to office hours and chat about how they're doing and he gave me great advice about choosing a major. He is also a bro and has a super rad mustache.
He is personable and laid-back, while also caring about the well-being of students. Super easy to reach outside of class, and very nice when doing so.

Dr. Gray is super sarcastic and funny. He cares about his students and appreciates you for putting in effort. We had a lot of group work and a big group project so be sure to do your part in that. Overall, he's a fantastic guy!
Great teacher. Getting used to the material as he is new but is outstanding to learn from. Gives great personal experience lessons that everyone should learn.
Tests not too hard, read notes and attend office hours. Very chill and understanding
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gugercin works mostly in CMDA so tries to relate linear to coding, even by making MatLab homework's. He changed the common linear syllabus to take off easy webassigns and make them extra credit, but then added the leftover weighting to his harsh/theoretical exams. The exams may look like 4-5 FRQ questions but they all come with parts a, b, c, d.

Serkan is an excellent professor. Not only is he a world-renowned researcher, he is passionate about teaching and goes to great lengths to make sure his students succeed. His homeworks and exams can be challenging, but for the right reasons; they are fair and make sure the student knows the material. I genuinely loved CMDA3605 and CMDA3606.

Serkan is a great guy and very passionate about his classes. However, his class is far from easy. He gives weekly homework of about 5 -6 questions but it take around 5 ish hours for each homework. You can do with one buddy if wanted. The test are similar to homework which is nice but they certainly require so many hours of study just to average a B
Professor Gugercin is great! I'm not the best at math so I still struggled in the class, but he was super accommodating and is clearly passionate about the subject.

Professor Gugercin is a great professor. He is very engaging and expresses his enjoyment for the subject matter in class. He's got a good sense of humor and is very approachable outside of class. His homeworks were interesting and expanded on the lectures, but a downside is that they often involved MATLAB.

Professor Gugercin is great. Use his office hours because he is very patient and guides you the correct answer. It's better you print class notes before hand so you don't have to write a bunch of notes during class. He has a sense of humor and light up the classroom atmosphere.

He really cared about the class understanding the material. You need to be specific about what you are confused about if you go to office hours. He printed out lecture notes. He would do examples in class. Weekly homeworks were more theoretical. Three exams, weekly homeworks, and either a final exam or a term project make up your grade.

I would take this class even if it had nothing to do with my major. Professor Gupta is one of the most incredible professors I have had at VT and I wish I could take more of his courses. He is so passionate and keep students engaged, which is hard to come across. His love for teaching is palpable and motivates you to want to do well. 10/10

Engaging with Professor Gupta is something that comes easy as long as you sit there and listen. By no means is this class easy, but the way it was taught made me want to succeed and learn. It was my favorite class I've taken at tech and I hate economics.

Dr. Gupta was an excellent professor for this class. The only caveat is that you need to pay attention in class. You can easily miss something if you don't soak it in or write it down. Dr. Gupta would always ask mid-lecture if we understood what he just went over and would always ask us to ask questions. Don't be the person who sits on your phone.

Professor Anubhab is genuinely one of the best professors I've had at VT. The course was intellectually inspirational taught in a way that was clear and motivating. I liked how he connected development theory to real-world policy and evidence—papers, data, and practical examples—not just slides. He is also a generous grader.
Probably one of the best professors at Tech. He wants the students to succeed and gives a lot of grace.
I will take the course again!

Has weekly quizzes that are based on the lecture. You are expected to work with your dog 4 times a week, but it can be very hard to sign up for an open session due to the high amount of people in all class sections. Most of the time sessions are all booked and you cant get it excused. Projects can be tedious and slightly difficult.

This class had a lot of potential but failed to reach it. Dr. Gunter cares a lot  about her students, and is clearly knowledgeable. This class was more work than the credits, and was very disorganized. The professors were in over their heads and lacked details and plans

Dr. Gunter is the sweetest and most understanding professor ever! She always provides feedback on how to do a training technique to help you succeed. Outside of class you are expected to work with your dog 5 times a week for 30 minutes. She truly cares about her students and will not hesitate to make adjustments to help you succeed. Best woman ever

I really liked my time with GQ. I felt like nothing he asked us to do was unreasonable in terms of assignments and tests. He's one of the kindest professors in the department, you just have to show you care and he is more than willing to help!
The class was definitely tough but over he was the best teacher that I could of asked for!

First time teaching the course (thats why he gets 2 instead of 1). Early in the semester he had no idea what he was doing. Pop quizzes every week (which are hard). He does not understand how to use canvas. While, I feel did learn something in his class, It would have definitely better without his irrelevant tangents during class.

Pop Quizzes every other class, 
Hard 15 minutes window to download pdf annotate and submit pdf of work
Doesn't teach from the textbook but need to buy it anyway for online assignments
Not very approachable outside of office hours
VT has no prerequisites listed, this is not how it is taught
Need to have calculus knowledge and physics knowledge
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid, his tests are very hard.

He was a good professor in terms of prepping us for exams and giving homework help when we asked. Going to class was valuable because of his hints. The material itself was kinda difficult but without him the class would've struggled a lot more. He cared about our well-being and genuinely wanted to make sure we had all the resources to do well.

Tests are always way too difficult but then graded generously, making going to class pointless. Not clear at all what you need to know. The first test is graded harshly to scare people but a the lowest test is dropped.

Good luck understanding anything he does in lecture. He loves to ramble and then transition to "material" except there is no structure to his class. No way to follow what he is going through or even know what to expect in the next class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: FR 3114 not 3106. Dr. Guèye is super passionate and knowledgable on francophone studies. It's a literature class, so you'd better enjoy reading. But the any class is super good when the professor is obviously really into what they're teaching about. Just read and use your brain enough to have original thoughts on your homeworks.

reviews.comment: DO NOT GO ON THE STUDY ABROAD WITH HIM TO SENEGAL. THIS WAS THE WORST DECISION OF MY LIFE. IT WAS COMPLETELY MISERABLE AND YOU LEARN ABSOLUTELY NOTHING. IT IS TOO EXPENSIVE FOR THE AMOUNT OF ENJOYMENT YOU WILL GET--WHICH IS NONE.

Definitely the best teacher I have had at this school. He was always so positive, helpful, and pleasant. In class we had conversations in French rather than written assignments which really helped learn the language. Over all a great funny guy.

He's super easy and a very fun professor! He's from Senegal so his English is sometimes a little difficult to understand, but you're there to learn French anyway. Definitely take him. If you do the workbook, the tests come directly from it and he also pretty much gives you all the questions/answers on the review sheet  right before the exam!
awesome french prof. fun class. very easy tests right from the workbook!!

this class was really easy, you just need to show up and do the work. im not great with foreign lang but i still got an A. hes a cool prof, sometimes hard to understand but he def knows his french cuz its his first language!
She is probably one of my favorite professors this semester. The class was very manageable and pretty easy if it's something you're genuinely interested in.

reviews.comment: I had her for intro to creative writing, and while her class was not difficult, I just would not take it again. As long as you do the assignments on time and completely, you will get an A. But her attendance it really random and her reading checks are terrifying. Also kind of intense for a pathway course.

reviews.comment: Professor Voros is a difficult grader an really makes you work for it, shes not very specific on the rubric. If you get on her bad side life will be much more difficult, show up to class as she randomly takes attendance. Lots of readings, and the assignments are pointless the class could be just the final paper.

reviews.comment: 25 writing assignments on canvas from poems to short stories. Had 8 in class workshops to read, edit, and reflect 1-3 paragraphs on over 30 pages summed of classmates work (Ie. 13,15,8 page papers in one due date). Attendance is randomly taken. Reading assignments the first 3/4 get called on if you aren't participating to make sure you did read.
Gyorgi was the best professor I've ever had. Be prepared to read and participate in class but otherwise this class is a breeze. Genuinely enjoyable lectures with great personality.

I would actually rather watch paint dry than take this class. Her attendance policy is based off of random days she chooses, so you never know when to go and not go. For the classes I did go to she showed up late more than half the time. An annoying amount of work for a mandatory entry level course. Literally take any other professor besides her!
Very friendly professor. You have to write a few essays, but she will do anything she can to help you get a good grade.  Just do your essays, and you'll be fine.

Gyorgyi is a pleasant woman who helps stimulate pretty decent classroom discussion.  Honors Freshman English with her wasn't too bad, homework assignments were usually simple.  This class requires only 3 essays for the whole semester, not bad.

Voros is very nice and approachable for help with the 3 papers you have to write.  Sometimes it is unclear what the papers are supposed to be about but you can rewrite the first 2 for a better grade. Interesting class dicussions, highly environmental. She doesn't mind hearing views different from her own, so you don't have to worry about any bias.
Amazing Professor. Hard Class.

Professor Hammer describes himself as "not a milk and cookies professor," and that is exactly what you want. He teaches clearly and really tries to understand you if you have a question.  The homework can be hard, but when paired with the optional textbook practice problems, it prepares you for his fair tests. He also likes to engage with the class

Great teacher, well-prepared and clear lectures. Only has the textbook as a supplemental resource and for extra practice. Tests are fair, and if you understand the homework and in-class examples you'll be fine. Makes a genuine effort to understand your questions and if you ask for help he'll really try to answer in a way that makes sense to you.

Incredible teacher. The best math teacher I have ever had. Expects you to attend every class but is amazing at lectures. Explains the subject in a humorous, clear, and simple way. All hail Dr. Hammer (Combo Spring 2025 btw)

Great class and professor. The class was only graded based on weekly homework and exams. Going to lecture is important to stay on track in this class. He did not post notes for this class, although he did for Discrete Math. You can find the textbook online for free if you look hard enough, and its not always needed for the homework but is sometimes
I highly recommend Prof. Hammer for combinatorics. He covers the material thoroughly and provides good, focused lectures.

Amazing lecturer, attending class was always helpful and relevant to the assignments. Homework included 2-3 problems each week (with homeworks having a small grade buffer) and somewhat difficult exams. Partial credit was lenient.

He is a good professor, I would definitely take again. My favorite quality is interesting lectures, as I have a short attention span, he always jokes or interacts with the class to keep retention high. He also is great at answering questions, in the sense that he will never embarrass you or not make effort to understand what you are saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Combo is hard class but Hammer is great. He said he won't posts notes anymore online so you have to go to class. There are 2/3 problems per week for the HW and he offers bonus points on those. He ended up curving the class grade at the end too.

Steve Hamer was okay for taking Discrete. If you don't attend his lectures, you will probably be lost on the daily HW he assigns. The subjects being taught towards the end made no sense. He doesn't post HW answers to see what you got wrong. I have heard from other students that have taken discrete and that Newman Malik is really and is easier.

He talks with his students a lot about all kinds of off-topic things, which make lectures really enjoyable. He knows a lot about this subject and it really good at teaching/giving feedback to students that need it. Strongly recommend for Combinatorics.

Kind of a boomer but is entertaining and so its easy to stay awake during his lectures. Pay attention during lectures & take notes because the textbook is incomprehensible vs. him. Also if enough people attend, he posts the notes online.
Tests are pretty easy if you study, HW is once a week so minimal.
Textbook is online for free, just google it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Combinatorics is a pretty difficult class, but Hammer makes it easier. His notes are easy to read and follow along and he makes a lot of subtle jokes. He only assigns 3 HW problems per week (1 for each lecture), but they do require a bit of thought. That being said, start the HW early, but if you're stuck don't hesitate to go to his office hours

Hammer is a great professor and is extremely helpful during office hours. He doesn't post any notes and the material is extremely confusing to learn if you don't attend class. Do your homework asap after every lecture and take your time understanding the material, it'll help you in the long run. Also, his final is non-cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Hammer teaches the topics in-depth and with great detail. But, he does make you work for your grade. You need to attend lectures and do the homework. However, using these with office hours should get you good test scores (3 tests > 25% each  75% of course grade)! Overall, take if you want to actually learn the material, not for an easy A...

reviews.comment: Absolute Goat

reviews.comment: First exam was really hard, second exam was really easy but the information he told us to study in an email was misleading so I didn't study the correct information and did poorly. Final was challenging but doable as long as you studied. An ok professor but I think he needs to do better at telling us what is on the exams.

basically your whole grade is based off of class attendance, so you have to go. Simutext is dumb and takes up so much of your time, and he actually grades it so it's not for a completion grade. I did pretty bad on the tests and the TAs are kinda hard graders sometimes. A lot of boring topics and slides are hard to study.

Very easy professor until the final exam. Lets students grade their own quizzes so basically its always a guaranteed 100. Midterm exam is difficult but its not a big deal cause his class has a lot of other easy things that bring up your grade. Final was a take home due to snow. Even with open notes it was insanely difficult, average was 72!

His teaching style is very good in a sense even if you didn't read the book or missed out on something you can catch up. The material is clearly outlined in class and attendance matters. Great class and great professor.

reviews.comment: Super easy class! All you have to do is write a blog, a discussion post, and take a quiz every week which are all super easy. Quizzes are open note and 2 attempts. Blog and discussion posts are easy 100s.
His lectures are boring, but have you ever attended an English lecture that wasn't? He is VERY lenient with deadlines. He is also funny. I would 100% take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things
