Professor Moore is hilarious. I do struggle on his exams but that is because I don't study that much for them. He means well and is very engaging. I'm taking him for Ethology next semester because of how much I like him. He's like a chill dad and I'm totally here for it lol. I 100% recommend him to anyone.
Really chill, understanding professor. Sets up plenty of opportunities to study, and open to questions.

Great professor and liked his lectures. Took his Ethology class (biol 4474). Has 6 quizzes and a final project. Easy going but tests were 25 questions mc/true or false and very specific questions. You def need to read the whole question and understand what he wants. Loved the class but did badly on the tests. He curves at the end so that's nice.

Dr. Moore is a great teacher for 1034. He knows what hes talking about. The class is definitely not a weed out class, and he gives a lot of leeway for grading. 9 quizzes and a final is what youre graded on. The powerpoints are whats gonna be on the quiz, so study those.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures were interesting and he genuinely cares a lot about the material, but there was so much material on every exam and I never knew what to study. Started out strong in this class but it went downhill from there. I got a lower grade in this class than I did with Bump in Organic Chem. Definitely wouldn't recommend it.

I was very interested in the subject so I found this class engaging, However, this class was by no means easy. Each of the regular exams were difficult and the final was basically impossible. Only take this class if you plan on going to every lecture and taking detailed notes and you're willing to spend hours each week reviewing the material.

This was a great class!  I was not very interested when I signed up but ended up loving it. He does not require the book for the class but he still lists readings, I did the readings and went to class and got A's on every test. He gets pretty detailed, and learning the physiology so well actually helped me rock the bio section on the mcat.
Overall he is a pretty good teacher.  His classes are pretty fun to go to, but his tests are ridiculously hard! The lectures do not prepare you for the tests at all.
Tests are really hard, have about 5-9 options for each multiple choice and it's designed so that being able to eliminate some options does not help. Attendance is taken using iClickers.
I wish he could pronounce "equator" correctly

By far the weirdest class I took. His lectures are so boring and we had two small papers and that was it. No homework, nothing. It was the easiest class I've ever taken. It seems like it's gonna be hard but it isn't. Cool dude though, it's a shame his class isn't more structured because it could be interesting but just is not

Professor Luciak is one of my favorite professors at VT! I've taken both of his classes and thoroughly enjoyed both of them. His lectures are a bit monotonous at times but it's clear he's very interested in the subject matter and cares if his students are grasping the information.

reviews.comment: Great guy!

You will not learn much. His tests are more about his personal family history and opinions than the class material. His final exam was about the role of gender in South American revolutionary movements for a class about comparing government structures. By far the strangest most irrelevant class I've ever taken.

His lectures can be a bit dry, especially if you don't do the reading. He is a lenient grader and is a very funny guy. He tells stories and has a lot of personal experience in what he teaches, but it can be very boring. His powerpoints online are also very vague, so pay attention and do the reading, although, I got a great grade without doing so

reviews.comment: He focuses the grades solely on exams. Once he realized our class was failing too much, he offered two extra credit assignments to help out. His accent is difficult to understand sometimes and you really need to go to him directly for help on his study guides. They tend to focus on broad concepts and dont help for the test.

reviews.comment: I attest that this is the worst Prof I had at Tech. She was condescending when students that she didnt like asked questions. The final project is heavily weighted and she provides no rubric. She gave every group a C besides one group that she gave us a F with no feedback. She Promised 2 Drop a HW in syllabus,secretly updated syllabus, and denied it

She is the hardest Enge 1216 professor at Tech. She takes forever to grade anything, and she gives very minimum feedback to why she took points off. She expects nothing less than perfection on every assignment, and will tear your group apart with ridiculous questions during the final presentation.
Slightly condescending and takes forever to grade. She also grades based on guidelines that she doesn't give us. So its pretty much a lose-lose situation

Professor St. Omer is a good professor. She gives a lot of assignments, but most of them are pretty straightforward. She has very high expectations for group projects, but the class itself is not very hard. She let us do a few group projects in the Frith lab which was fun. She is a solid choice if you are looking for an engineering professor.

reviews.comment: 80% of assignments remained ungraded until AFTER the class was over. I did not know what my final grade was until then. Avoid this professor.

reviews.comment: doesn't care about the students at all. wouldnt let me retake a test that I had a wifi error in. didnt take my mental illness under consideration and gave late penalty for everyone. very cold heartless doesnt teach material well WANTS YOU TO FAIL if you want to become depressed then take her class, she is a horrible person, doesnt give feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I have to say from this class I learned nothing but it drags my Gpa. The painful part of this class is she released the grades months after we submitted. Also I was confused about why I lost points but I would never know the reason. She is a nice person in general but I am disappointed with her class.

Decent person, she can be a nice person.  Doesnt change the fact that we didnt know any of our grades until weeks after they were submitted.  She didnt even meet the university deadline to submit final grades.  TONS of writing, very stressful class, and she provided little to no feedback to help us.  Id avoid at all costs

Like, she's not good. She doesn't grade quickly at all. The last day of classes came, and I was still waiting for something from October. She talks about how "the course is flawed" but really she is the flawed one. Overall, a condescending and kinda mean professor that you should only take to avoid an 8 am.

reviews.comment: She is literally the antichrist in female form! Avoid her at all costs and your GPA will thank me! I took her for ENGE 1216 and she never fully outlined what she expected from us, especially on group assignments. Arguing for points back on assignments only makes it worse and it takes her an eternity to grade anyway! Not worth the effort!

Tough grader is an understatement. Her grading is better described as trying to fly with a pair of wings strapped to your arms . You can flap as hard as you want but you won't go up much. The best theory as to why she is such a hard greater is that her "time in industry" is over and all she has to show for it is a sensor that nobody decided to use.

Lectures are poor. She doesn't explain anything, she gives zero guidelines for assignments, and grades them so incredibly tough and specific. Oh, and she takes forever to grade the assignments too. There were assignments given in September that we didn't get back till the end of the semester. Please, please, please do not take her class.

She is a terrible teacher who gives no explanations. She grades incredibly strictly after giving little to no guidelines for assignments. I dreaded going to class. I would not recommend her to anyone, please avoid.

I cannot express how terrible of a professor she is. She takes months to grade any thing and when she finally gives out grades they are a million times lower than any other professor gives for the same class. She is terrible at answering questions and I did not learn anything from her. Avoid having her as a professor at all costs.

Overall she's great great Professor who's passionate about the subject and is willing to help her students. She may come off a bit rude sometimes but personally idc, i think it's just the way she talks, not her personality. But she truly wants students to succeed, willing to make adjustments to class, and accomodate students when something comes up

This class requires a pre req and its important to remember the info from it. Shes very knowledgeable and passionate about the material. Exams are weighted relatively low. Shes alright at explaining things but as long as you pay attention and study well, you'll be fine. Exam questions are very similar to the slide material despite what others said

reviews.comment: This class is extremely rushed. In addition, her tests are really hard despite being open note. That being said, she is very knowledgeable and does want you to succeed. She's open to feedback, and has pushed back assignments for us. She gives many examples, emphasizes what to study in exam reviews, etc. I just think the material is hard to learn.

Professor Ionescu is horrible at teaching content. Her lectures consist of her reading off the slides and then saying it is self-explanatory. She also mentions you need to already know content that was not taught in previous courses. The reviews & slides cover 15% of the content on the exam and she does not curve.Not all experts make good teachers!

Overall good professor, polite, helpful during office hours, can rush through content at times. Exams are open note, open internet but you have to average around a question per minute. Online Comptia assignments make up most of your grade. Has strict late work policy. If you submit all assignments and prepare for the exams, its an easy A.

reviews.comment: very incompetent professor that does not seem to understand his students and talks about family issues during lecture.

reviews.comment: lectures are scattered and hard to follow, rambles about personal matter unrelated to the class.

Professor Iorio is the best professor I have had. His course is set up in a very unique way but if you put effort in the beginning of the year you will more than likely not even have to take the final to receive an A.

Dr. Iorio is a great professor who definitely cares about his students and makes the class very manageable. The class is taken over the summer with no lectures and no hard deadlines. The assignments take some time but are mostly very easy. Make sure to stay on top of your work and use the soft deadlines as the work could definitely pile up.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this professor. Grading is extremely strict, emails are not answered promptly, and assignments take a long time to be graded with little time to fix mistakes. Despite consistent effort, grades did not reflect work put in. This was my lowest grade despite stronger performance in harder major courses.

We had weekly assignments with discussion boards and he gave us full creative freedom to do what we wanted. He was a very easy grader, and he was also always accessible outside of class when I wanted to meet with him for additional help. The class was completely virtual though, so you don't have to meet with him. I 100% recommend him! Loved him!

Super caring professor, he recognizes we have lives outside of his class! Four exams using lockdown with webcam. You get put in groups at the beginning of the year where you work on 3-4 big assignments with them. Sometimes there are pop quizzes in class. He tries to make research interesting!

Jason Malone is respectable and not a bad teacher, but I found the lectures boring and slides underwhelming. They didn't prepare me well for the exams, which were long and hard to study for. Attendance is a big part of the grade. I'd take another professor or online if possible.

This guy is bad, his slides are basically pointless it goes over terms of the subject which correlates noting to the exam. Exams are basically the only grades in the class. Also very inconsiderate when it's exam day and doesn't know how to be quiet.
4014 - The slides were not helpful so make sure you listen and take notes in class, everything is based of the cases that he talks about so just know what the outcomes are and youll be fine

His lectures slides aren't that great and it's often vague. But his textbook is insanely long and it takes like 4 hours if you want to take notes and read the chapter at the same time for one chapter. He's nice and funny and gives a generous amount of extra credit so the class is hard but doable. Messed up on the 1st exam so it tanked my grade.

Show up to class and you will do well, read the textbook if you are struggling. I never bought the textbook but I also never missed a class. There is no homework besides studying for exams, he wants his students to succeed and offers tons of extra credit during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AWSOME GUY. One of those teachers you can tell actually cares about his students. I woke up late for one of the exams and he still let me take it in his next class. bro actually cares! It is a difficult lecture class, you have to read the slides and textbook to do well, but thats college tbh so just go to class and pay attention and you do well!
Great professor, class is test heavy though.
I would recommend taking him, he is super laid back and fun.

Malone is a great professor. He paces the lectures directly to questions any student had. He offers but doesn't require you to buy a textbook. I didn't buy the textbook and did well. I suggest if you don't buy a textbook to attend as many lectures as possible. The grade is based on only tests and quizzes and the slides are not all inclusive.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's an engaging professor, but if you care deeply about your GPA, then I'd recommend taking this course with someone else. Malone's lectures were good verbally, but his slides were not very good (this makes studying somewhat difficult). To that point, you NEED to read the textbook if you want to ensure you do well.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!!!!! Seriously if you get the opportunity to take Malone, I promise you won't regret it. He is literally the funniest and sweetest professor I have ever had. His lectures are hilarious but also very informational. The only homework in this class is to come up with a joke. I would take Malone a million times over if I could!

Malone is a really nice guy, but he has 2 exams and 13 quizzes (3 are dropped). He also requires students to purchase a textbook that he wrote ($100+). Unfortunately, the lecture slides are mostly unhelpful. Exams are conducted in class using a lockdown browser. If attendance is low or if he finishes his lecture early, he will give extra credit.

Loved this class, but it is hard. Your grade is made up of your 3 exams and quizzes. I thought lectures were super interesting and he was a great professor. If you show up to class there are chances for extra credit (2-4 points max). Also after exams if a lot of people get certain questions wrong he'll give back points, so overall not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Malone is a really fun guy with informative and engaging lectures. The lectures and textbook have all you need to know for the quizzes and test (those are the only assignments). I got a low grade because I barely went to class or read the textbook. If you do both, the exams are straightforward and class is a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Respectful and engaging in class. Slides are general but he explains them well in person. 3 exams each worth 25% and 10 chapter quizzes with your 3 lowest scores replaced with 100s. Exams were 40 mc, 10 T/F, mostly application based; they're difficult but he reviews specific topics the class before. Overall not a bad experience!

Very fun class. Each class was interesting and attention grabbing, but the tests were very hard to study for. Most information was directly from the lectures. 10 quizzes and 3 get dropped. Tests weighted heavily. Extra credit quizzes are offered throughout the semester, but you have to be in class to get the code. All of the tests are application.

Professor Malone is a phenomenal professor. I highly recommend him for your professor next year. His tests are difficult, but he gives plenty of opportunities for extra credit and drops 3 of your 10 quizzes with perfect grades! Plenty of room for error and he knows his stuff!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Malone is one of my favorite professors I've had while at tech. He's really knowledgeable in the field and makes classes fun and sometimes just hilarious. His tests are very difficult and require a ton of studying, and since the class is mostly weighted on tests, you need to do well on them.

Extremely personable in class and passionate on this topic, overall a class to look forward to. However I think that the curriculum needs adjustment, the PowerPoints were pretty basic and short, with difficult exams and extremely difficult quizzes. This is an into to law course it should be graded like one.

Professor Malone is super funny and makes the class interesting and relatable for students. The textbook is optional but can be useful on the 5 question weekly quizzes he gives based on that week's lectures. The class was something to look forward to, and exams were not that bad if you studied and were curved. Overall, fun class.

Amazing professor. His lectures are very entertaining. Weekly quizzes are difficult but if you read the chapters assigned, you will do way better. Exams are hard but if you memorize the slides, you should be in good shape. Loved this class and learned so many interesting things, it will come in handy later down the road.

Professor Malone is the best! I took Business Law before him with another teacher and failed. I took his class and had no trouble doing well at all. He is so funny in his lectures and comes up with funny examples to really help you understand the material. Definitely take his class.

I LOVE THIS PROF! So like no I didn't excel int his class, material is hard but his lectures are HILARIOUS and he's a really great person to teach this course. Makes it really entertaining and can't tell you how many times I kinda died laughing- good thing we on zoom right now. Anyway 100% recommend. 2 lectures 1 quiz every Friday. 4 exams
Outstanding professor! His lectures are clear and intersting. He sets high expectations (show up to class!) Did I mention he is hot? ...really, really hot!
HOT PROFESSOR!!!!!!!!!! 3 tests make up your whole grade. Go to class.
Business Law was my favorite class ever!
Awesome professor!

I had Malone for Fin 3055 and 4004. I found he was interesting and able to break down difficult material for better understanding. VERY helpful, definitely a professor worth getting to know! He isn't the easiest, but you will leave the course having learned something useful.
Very interesting lectures!

Professor Malone is by far one of my favorite professors. While most girls rave about his looks, I found his knowledge and insight of the law to be what made me want to come to class.  He has a dry sense of humor, however is extremely helpful outside of class and will make time for you if you need it.  An overall great guy.

Bar none, one of the most fun classes I have ever taken in the business program. He uses hilarious hypothetical situations to break down the b.law concepts. I strongly recommend, plus one glance at his good looking self makes you NEVER want to miss class.

Great in class at explaining things and making classes interesting. And extremely good looking! But hard test that take a lot comprehensive skill, fall 09 was his first time teach b-law though so might be better next time though.

Dr. Jelesko Is a very passionate teacher. I found his lectures engaging. This course is test-heavy, with 7 exams, but they are very easy. He does tend to yap a alot; be prepared for a 20-slide PowerPoint to take an hour and 15 minutes to get through, which makes the class drag on. I think he read his reviews and fixed the course, he was great!

Class wasn't super hard, but there's quiz after every lecture (4-6 points each) and he requires full Lockdown browser + camera. Overall pretty strict and was not a fan of his lectures cause he yaps so much.

In class, we learned some cool topics, but attendance is mandatory and graded. There's a quiz after every lecture, and tests every two weeks, which require a lockdown browser with a camera. The questions are tough, and we don't know our grades throughout the course, making it a bit stressful.

Every day, I drive to class without a seatbelt in the hopes I crash and die so I won't have to attend his lectures. He's a decent teacher, but his unwillingness to work with us and constant unnecessary provisions (like making us do every single assignment in lockdown browser and then taking away our access to the answers) are awful. LOOK OUT!

My John was not sufficiently Jelesko'd by the communication skills of this professor. He teaches very well, has interactive lessons, and knows a lot about biology, however, he is cold-hearted and not very forgiving. He also has an air of arrogance and competitiveness that sometimes makes lectures unenjoyable. Overall, 2/5.

Her teaching style is very open-ended. I would recommend her to anyone if you want to push yourself in the field of History. I've had her 3 times, and I feel like I have grown into a better individual.

Professor Taylor was a very sarcastic teacher. She was aggressive when it came to teaching and did not really give good feedback. She was condescending and honestly made me hate going to class. She honestly made me feel very stupid. Without the discussions or quizzes, I could've failed.

Dr. Taylor was honestly amazing. She was good at explaining the subject clearly. I took Native American History, and she seemed very passionate about the subject, and was determined to make it from a Native perspective, rather than from a white one. There were quite a few essays and reading, but the material was interesting and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--So many papers--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Taylor. She made my least favorite subject so fun that I wanted to take more of her classes even though I'm bad at history. Made class fun and engaging. Had several "pop" quizzes- she almost always tells you, and had to read 2 novels that were pretty interesting and easy reads. Some essays but your class writes the prompt!

I absolutely loved her as a person. She cares so much about her students and tries to tailor the class for them. We decided as a class all of the prompts for papers and a lot of the test questions. She really cares and wants you to pass!

His lectures are very informational, but you can only actually gather maybe 1/3 of what he goes over since he goes so fast and just skims through. They aren't his notes. He also uses a chalkboard which half the class can't see. Tests are extremely hard even when studying for 10+ hours. No curves. Good guy, not a good professor by any means.
Willing to go above and beyond for every student. The best!

A professor that is willing to go above and beyond to ensure the students will be successful in their careers. If you are in Financial Planning, he should be your go to resource for all things jobs, internships, and mentorship, as he is so passionate about helping you find where you will grow and the best place for you. Just care and study well.
My very favorite professor ever! He goes above and beyond to not only help you learn the material, but help you in your career.

Great Professor who really cares about his students when you show up. If you go to lectures and participate in class you will get a good grade. If you want to be a financial planner this is the professor you need to make a connection with.

So, so much unnecessary busy work. She is really nice and easy to talk to though. The work isn't necessarily hard, but I would not consider the amount reasonable. There can be up to 2-4 assignments due a week.

So much busy work, expect to do 2-4 assignments a week. She is a nice professor and easy to talk to, really cares about her students but if you are looking for a PSCI class with less assignments, this is NOT it. Some of the work feels redundant or unnecessary, not an easy class you can just coast through.

Good professor. Sometimes brought donuts to class. Was a pretty boring, busy work class but professor Hanratty was a good professor for this class. She is witty and generally decently laid back and makes the course more relatable.

One of the best professors at Pamplin! She makes complex material very easy to understand. The classes are always concise, clear, and informative. I've learned many analytical skills that I'm sure will be useful in my future job. I wish she taught more analytics courses.

Super cool and easy to talk to. Not the easiest to reach outside of class though. The class is very structured and clear. Projects can be tough, but she gave really helpful feedback, and our group worked well together, so we did fine.

Dr. Liu created an open and supportive learning environment. She always paused to explain things clearly and never judged anyone for having trouble understanding.The class moved fast at times, but the content was engaging, and she gave really helpful feedback. I liked the AI practice at the end. I really enjoyed and learned a lot from this class.

Professor Liu is amazing! She's extremely approachable and inspiring and goes out of her way to help us understand the material. Always clear and concise in class. She proves how smart she is by making complex concepts easy to grasp. Homework reinforced learning, and the final project let us apply it all. Couldn't ask for a better professor.

First 2 HWs are extremely easy. You could probably complete them solely with the knowledge from 2405/2406. The final exam is AWFUL, not a lot of direction other then "Look at this prior students work and try to replicate it". Still a good professor who will teach you how to get better at EXCEL, but could definitely explain the final project better.

Liu was a pleasure to have as a professor! Even if she was quick during lectures, she made sure to answer questions and go back if people needed help. If you don't go to class, you'll have a hard time keeping up. There is an opt in final exam, but if you do fine on hw you don't need to. She gives ample time in class to work on the final project.

She speaks very clearly and teaches at a good pace. Your grade consists of 3 HW assignments, a midterm, and a few in class submissions. The only problem is that you have to attend class to understand the material because the powerpoints are very surface level and she dos not record lectures.

Professor Liu genuinely cares about this subject and her students--one time she purchased the entire class starbucks--she's awesome. Very fast-paced, but she encourages questions and collaboration. Only wish is that she held more OH's.

Get ready to play catch up. She moves insanely quick, if you lose yourself for more than a second you may easily get lost. Attendance may not be taken every class, but you definitely want to go as every lecture is built on top of one another. She stays after class to answer questions but her patience seems very short, I would go to TA's.

This professor was amazing and tried to make the lecture content relatable to more comprehensible concepts. Text is helpful but not necessary. Tests are easy if you study the powerpoint and TONS of extra credit opportunity. Class is not test heavy and the professor is actually amazing and flexible with student accommodations.

His class is difficult, but he drops a test, curves tests, provides extra credit, attendance isn't worth too much, is flexible with rescheduling exams, and is a very knowledgeable and liked professor. Put EVERYTHING on the cheat sheet, and you'll be fine. I got a B because I hate studying and barely went to class, still passed lol.
I just watched the lecture videos and filled out the cheat sheet. He drops an exam as well. Got an A.

Day one: syllabus roulette.
Random font chaos, slides made when he was not on earth.

Tests felt AI-written at 2 a.m.
On two exams: Bloom's Taxonomy??
Keep expectations low.
Unhelpful Canvas page.
How many mole rats must we look at?
Instructions unclear, grades worse.
Structure? We beg for it.
At this point, I'd rather be bullied.
Allows cheat sheets for tests and is all around a good guy. Gives 5 minute breaks during class and makes his lectures interesting. He cares about his students and is easy to reach outside of class.

Great guy but a TERRIBLE lecturer. Half of the content on the exams are not covered in class. You have to read every little detail in the textbook. Even the smallest detail (if it was mentioned in one sentence), its on the exam. Goes over the most basic concepts (like ionic bonds) and then expects you to teach yourself the difficult concepts.

Dr. Tokuhisa is the best professors I've had, surprised his rating so low. He curves exams, records lectures, has participation points, extra credit, non cumulative final, and allows a cheat sheet for every exam. Studied a day in advance. Adds gifs/visuals on slides to help. Cares about students success/well being and answers emails promptly.

He's a great guy, but a terrible test maker, his tests are awfully worded, and there's 5 of them, so no getting away. Not to mention half of the questions are things you cannot find in the lecture notes.

He can tend to stay on certain slides for a while but studying the slides is that main part and toward the beginning using the textbook is helpful (can be downloaded for free online). Taking or already taken microbiology is helpful. You get a notesheet for every test and final isnt cumulative so its not that bad. Do practice tests b/c he repeat q's

Typically explain hard concepts in class and provide reading material to support most important ones and the tests covers comprehension of material. Tests might have been for a different class?

Also - attendance policy is for classes where missing a day of a a major set back, not a weird joke for the prof when he reveals he only counted 5 days.

easily one of the best professors to have for Cell Diff. He cares for his students and wants everyone to succeed. He offers easy points to raise your grade, curves the exams, and lets you have a cheat sheet for every exam. The lectures are confusing to understand because its a lot of info but he records his lectures & 2nd time viewing is easier. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Slide decks are a mess. Lectures are unstructured and tangential. Tests include questions not covered in class.

He allows you to use a cheat sheet during exams that was not helpful because he rarely talks about the things he will test you on and his slides are not informative and organised. Only test 1 was easy, the rest became really difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made us feel so bad whenever we contacted him to the point I stopped reaching out and asking him for help. My best advice is to not depend on his lectures and try to read the textbook.
He made us think attendance and participation mattered for earning points, but at the end of the semester he only counted few which was unfair for those who attended class every day. I contacted

tbh his explanation is not so good so I had to read the textbook a lot and the things he brought on exams were not discussed or talked about in class. He only counted five of our attendance when he literally told us that attendance is mandatory. the whole class was a complete chaos and he posted assignments and quizzes 1-2 days before exams.
One of the hardest classes I've ever taken. His exams are very hard and his slides are not helpful.

He is an incredibly nice person and very respectful, but it seems like everyone, including myself, find this class to be very difficult. The lectures are extremely long and full of information that you must know for the exams (there are five). I study long and hard and find myself not doing nearly as well as in any other classes I have taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is difficult in its own right, but with him be ready to read the textbook and go to all the lectures just to scrap by with a C. his teaching style is horrific and i would just recomend dropping the class or not taking it with him if possible.

Tokuhisa was a fantastic teacher. He genuinely cares about his students and works really hard to make the class interesting for them. He is easily approachable and very helpful when you take the time to go and talk with him.  You have to work hard, but taking a class with him is worth it.
Most caring professor you'll probably ever have. Great person. Only draw back is the class is just kinda a pain in the a** especially if you got harder classes to take care of.

Fantastic professor, if you get the chance you should take her class. She's very patient and cares deeply for her students, it really shows that she wants you to learn, this has been my favorite class so far as it's pretty fun and you'll learn a lot without realizing it. There is a fair amount of reading, but you get used to it.

Amazing professor. Her class is somewhat easy but she really cares about each of her students and makes sure they are participating/learning from the class. She is funny and makes her lectures entertaining and she creates a friendly learning environment. She will make sure you get the grade you deserve and is willing to work with students!
I've really enjoyed having Professor Cana Jimenez, I am a graduate student who has learned a lot in her classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really sweet lady. I don't know Spanish very well but she was so very patient with me :)
Dr. Caña-Jiménez knows everything about Spanish culture and theory. She helped me to become a better writer, in teaching me to focus on key parts of analyzing the works that we covered.

Maria is an amazing teacher - she is a Spanish native, so really teaches you how to speak authentically. If you plan to get an A in this class, you better be prepared to earn it, because she gives significantly more work than other Spanish professors (especially with the mandatory blogs). But you WILL improve your speaking skills one way or another

Mari Carmen is awesome, she is fun and she is very clear about her expectations for the class. Her class is hard, but if you are struggling or something comes up she is very understanding. Class is practically mandatory, but I enjoy class so much. Theres a lot of work though.

Had him for fall 2023, and it was a disaster. Personality-wise, he's alright at best but overall, his teaching style does not work between his constant inconsistencies, the fact he is unable to teach without relying on a packet of notes he loses track of constantly, and nothing posted online. Those wanting to keep their GPA high, find someone else.

Lectures are incredibly hard to follow, he makes several mistakes and doesn't make sure the class understands what happened. He did maybe 10 exam-type problems during lecture throughout the whole semester, he would just derive formulas from theories then move on. Unless you have prior physics knowledge, prepare to teach yourself the entire class.

I learned from Pearson's videos and textbooks ONLY. His lectures are bad. He doesn't reply to emails. He can be a bit rude toward students. Easy class to pass, hard to get an A. Pre-exams allow you to get 2/3 points back on exams, depending on score. Only take if you can teach yourself outside of class, which is time consuming. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but he really struggles in lecture. I find them hard to follow, and sometimes he contradicts himself or gets lost and confused and has to retrace like 5 steps. When he messes up, he also disregards his mistakes and assumes everyone knew what he meant. Also doesn't answer emails consistently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's very forgetful and struggles to do the problems that he's trying to teach us with. Most people in the class seem to be really struggling because of how poorly it is taught, and I have to learn mostly just right off the textbook

Link is a very kind person, but his teaching method is horrible. His lectures are all over the place and hard to follow along. He is not good at explaining his work, and he assumes that everyone understands so he just moves on. The class is extremely difficult, however there are enough grades weighted so you can fail all the exams and still pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Link is a very nice person. He made an effort to get to know the students before class started and was kind. However, his teaching style was extremely flawed. He was not good at explaining things, and his lectures were all over the place. The class was very difficult, but there is enough grades weighted so you can fail the exams and still pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His sense of humor is hit or miss but I loved it, it helped keep lectures engaging. Attendance is mandatory because of the in class iClickler questions. He helps create the problems on the exams, so attending his class helps you learn how to approach the problems effectivley. He does get lost while writing proofs sometimes

Link is a great guy, but his teaching style is hit or miss. He uses the chalkboard for notes and will sometimes get lost in a proof. I found taking notes in class confusing, so if you like taking your notes from the textbook he is a good choice (that's how I passed). Mandatory Iclicker questions in class, and tests are curved, as usual in physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very smart, nice guy, but he can't teach. In the lecture he is always getting confused, and has a great amount of trouble trying to solve the problems on the practice tests.
he's helpful
Homework take a long time to do
You should take this professor; he is very thorough with his teaching.

This class is not difficult for most students as it is an introductory Microsoft Excel course. This course is also very generous with multiple assignment attempts, extra credit, and open-book exams. Professor Sharp is also extremely responsive with emails, which is very impressive considering the number of students in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: not a bad thing to say about this guy! he gives you everything you need so take advantage of that! jarp is amazing and you are blessed to be in his class

Professor Sharp is an amazing professor for ACIS 1504. He cares about his students and provided  a lot of opportunities for help and amazing resources. Each module had about 3 homework sets, with video-guides if we needed help, and exams were OB, ON, lockdown-camera. Extra Credit opportunity at the end of semester helped a lot.

Super easy class, all you need to do each week is watch a few videos that explain and show the homework step-by-step. The exams are online and open note and open textbook with lockdown browser and webcam. You don't even need to study for the exams, just make sure you're familiar with the textbook. Professor Sharp is very kind and helpful!
Very easy class, all the exams are online, and he is very understanding about assignments and homework grades. There are also practice exams and extra credit to help you succeed in the courses.
So easy. He posts videos on how to do each assignment every week, and that is basically all you need to do.

Professor Sharp made this class really easy and the assignments and exams, which are all online, were straightforward. For an asynchronous class, the work load was well expected. He also gave extra credit opportunities towards the end of the semester before the final exam. Would definitely recommend.
Very exam focused and he did give a good amount of extra credit but not being allowed to use any notes on the exam was a horrible experience.

Very easy A if you take notes on the textbook and use the resources he gives you. All exams are open note and textbook, and he gives extra credit opportunities as well as homework help videos. This class was very useful, and I would recommend taking it with him!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has homework help for all the homework and also posts practice tests that are very similar to the test. The class is not bad as long as you put some effort. I will miss him; he is the goat.

The course isn't hard if you're ok with online: read the textbook + the homework help videos are beneficial. Exams are open-note and open-book but review beforehand since they're based on the textbook rather than Excel exercises. Overall, Dr. Sharp is kind and considerate: just send him an email, and he's always willing to accommodate your needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a great guy. Very caring, and he wants everyone to succeed. The class itself is really easy, but be sure to study for the exams, as they're knowledge based and not the hands-on like the homework.

Jason Sharp is a very respectable professor. I took the class virtual, so I rarely saw him, but when I did he was extremely supportive, flexible, and understanding. You'll find that many professors teaching an online oriented course take their role or course too seriously, Professor Sharp is much better than them. He is logical and realistic.
He is one of the best!
Great professor, explains everything. SmartGrader assignments are easy, the exams are open note ************BUT************ can be tricky, so be careful. Most of your grade are the exams.

He's super nice and the content isn't hard. If you need help with the homework, there are videos where he walks you through all the problems. The tests are open note but you definitely still need to know the information. He is also easy to reach and responds to emails quickly.
Fairly easy, informative class. If you spend at least 4-5 hours a week on this class consistently, it shouldn't be very difficult for you
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy class would recommend. Stay on top of everything and use your textbook for the tests all of the answers are in there. You will do good.
I could've done better if I locked in but he helps you so much with the work, giving videos how to do the assignments and a bunch of extra credit opportunities. Honestly a great teacher
Professor Sharp created a very good online course, which was very in-depth and explanatory for even beginners. I would recommend his course and take another if offered.

Just about the easiest class imaginable. While there's a fair amount of homework he provides homework help videos and exams are open book and open note. Just make sure you buy the physical copy of the textbook to use with lockdown browser. My biggest gripe is that his online exams are only available for a single day, but otherwise they're fine.
lots of homework help videos and the tests are all open note and open textbook including the final exam.
I really loved involved Professor Sharp is despite not having an in person class! He has step by step videos for all of the homework & textbook problems. Really makes it hard to fail the class.

Great teacher. All his videos makes sense. u should be able to handle the class without actually reaching out to him if you actually watch his videos and put in the time. If not, that's on you. In his videos, he shows you how to do everything step by step, so if you're failing the class, its a YOU problem.

This class was taught entirely virtually, yet he will still post detailed step-by-step videos to walk you through all the material and the homework. Everything is open-book as well - for the exams, I would recommend making a sheet of page numbers all the terms he says in the exam review videos (watch these videos, and you will do well).
I took the online class and it was fairly easy. Just keep up with the weekly homework. Buy the physical copy textbook as the exams are open HARD copy textbook and notes.

Even though it's an asynchronous class, he sets it up pretty well so you can figure out what you're doing. He posts videos to help with the homework, which I recommend watching on 1.5x speed. Tests are open note and open book, so they're pretty easy. He does a great job at communicating with students!

Super super super easy. Don't even need to read textbook, just follow along with his pre-recorded lectures. Exams are most of your grade but pretty easy. His lectures are super easy to follow and concepts are easy to understand. This class should only take up 2-4hrs/week.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Professor

Professor Sharp was an amazing asynchronous instructor. His homework help videos and extra credit opportunities were really helpful. The exams can be a bit tricky, so it is best to do the prep work and watch / read all of his exam review. I would highly recommend taking this course with him, as all he wants is nothing but student success.

Professor Sharp is amazing. The homework is extremely straightforward and even has videos to help. He helps you review before exams and tests are open book if you buy the paper copy version. I recommend taking this class!
Prof. himself is nice and communicates quickly. HW assignments had videos to help when stuck. However, exams are a bit tedious and can be hard. They were open notes (without internet) at least.
pretty good teacher goood freshman class

This class is completely online. Because the assignments are easy, it's easy to forget you're even taking the class sometimes. Even though the test are open book, make sure you take the time to look over the textbook and study the material. Jason Sharp is knowledgeable about the subject and will respond quickly to your messages if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Sharp is a very kind and very well organized professor. a few homework assignments a week with videos that follow you through each problem step by step, exams are open book(hardcopy only) and open note taken on lockdown.
Super straightforward corse if you put the work in and keep up with the chapters. Professor Sharp has so many resources and help videos available. Test are all open note and book

Clearly puts in effort to help his students better understand the course. There are videos for just about anything relating to the course that he takes the time to make and upload. Weekly homework's are extremely easy if you watch his homework help videos. Tests are exactly like the study guide, are open notes, and are proctored using webcam.
W professor
A very accommodating teacher who will work for your success in his courses.
Took it asynchronous but it was super organized. Exams were Lockdown + Webcam but open note/book. Great intro to Excel which helped in BIT 2405/6 and in ACIS 2504. Would take him again.

Professor Sharp is awesome. He was super good at explaining the hard topics in Excel, especially for a non-finance major. He responds quickly and gives extra help. The workload can be a lot at times but he has videos that literally cover everything, which are great.
