Some weeks have insane amounts of homework due all on one night, which would be fine if I wasn't taking any other classes. She grades harshly (and rudely) on assignments without making expectations clear. Don't take this as an elective.

Took APSC 3134 (Animal Ag & Environment), didn't enjoy the class because of how disorganized it was and how inconsistent everything was with feedback. The TA's grade easier than her. Overall, the assignments are tedious for being an asynchronous class and it feels like you're typing the same thing over and over again about nitrogen and phosphorus
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is clearly passionate about dairy. Knowlton is smart, but too disorganized. Canvas is in disarray, class is canceled/rushed as things happen last minute. That being said, she always bakes and brings treats for her classes, will answer any question you ask about cows in class, and likes students who are curious and willing to participate.
It's obvious she loves teaching, is enthusiastic about the topic. She really enjoys working with students. Can be snarky, but more funny than mean.

I love Dr. Knowlton. She knows her students on a personal level, even outside of the classroom. She's very helpful and readily available. I actually think she's my favorite professor at Tech thus far. Definitely a fair person. Join Judging Team and she'll love you even more.
She's tough but fair. WONDERFUL lady if you get to know her, just DO NOT get on her bad side. She wants all of her students to do well. Really smart lady.

Reading and group work heavy course. Good at what she does, but a very unnecessary course. Over the top workload for what it is. Dr. Carper is very full of herself, so do your best to nod along and be quiet.

Dr. Carper is a very good teaching professor and knows what she's talking about. Grading is VERY harsh. She clearly gives the TAs a different rubric to grade off of because every single point I lost in this class wasn't detailed in the rubric provided. This class should be an easy A, but due to the subjective grading of the TAs, it is not.

Passive aggressive and closed minded. Began the class by explaining how she was an English major and we were Engineers and typecast everyone into hating writing. TAs often graded poorly and communication of project expectations was horrendous and often pretty misleading. Attendance is super mandatory.
so strict and feel bad

She teaches a communications class, but can't communicate what she expects out of each assignment. Will take off points for random things not on the rubric. She doesn't feel human at all, almost robotic.

Very patronizing professor. She doesn't seem to care about her female students, especially when they are being excluded in male-dominated spaces. More focused on being addressed formally than engaging with student concerns in a meaningful way.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a simple class about grammar and putting together a report, the grading is super harsh. Dr. Carper runs the class very strictly even though the TAs do all of the work.

I don't know why Carper has such good reviews. She is a really hard grader and literally will not help you with anything because she makes her TA's do everything. I think she is the only option for 3034 which sucks

Dr. Carper was an amazing professor! Her lectures were very informative. She gave good feedback throughout the semester. Make sure you pull you weight in your group, as your participation is a big part of your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
I really enjoyed Dr. Carper's class, she's a great professor.

This class is all about learning to write standard and professional reports and presentations. Your teammates rating of you account for a large percentage of your grade, so make sure to pull your own weight.

This class was a roller coaster. My group had to claw are way back up to a C to an A. We bombed our first big assignment. This seems to happen a lot in the class, and it definitely teaches you to be perseverant. The class can feel really extra / picky at times, but Carper is super willing to help outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Didn't learn a thing from Professor Juste. He thinks the entire class understands every concept he's teaching at all times. If you get him as a professor, I recommend VT Math Tutor online. I learned everything from him and will finish with a solid grade.
Dude is not a good professor.  Won't respond to your emails, TA's are uncapable, speeds through material people aren't familiar with, can't understand him sometimes, doesn't explain concepts AT ALL.

Good professor. Lots of weekly homework assignments. I had an A in the class all the way to the end until the final i ended with a B+ because he decided to make the final only on content that was covered a week or two prior. Before a test, go through every homework problem because the test is very similar.

ted is an amazing guy and definitely a good teacher in some ways, but he was very behind in the course while the other teachers were wayyy ahead. if you pay attention and go to class then youre good, but it can also be a snooze fest. so if youre a math person you will be fine, otherwise i pray for u

This class is actually quite dreadful, the homework takes FOREVER to do (60+ questions a week) and the mandatory recitations are a huge waste of time. Honestly, I wouldn't even waste your energy going to class, I just taught myself all of the material before the exams anyways. Professor Juste also doesn't respond to any emails.

I took ap calc ab in high school so this class wasn't too difficult. Lots of homework but don't worry because the exams are a lot easier. Make sure to study the lecture notes and written hw before exams. The professor seems pretty nice but I didn't get his teaching style very much. This class is a lot of self study.
One of the best professors at VT.

would not recommend this professor unless you're comfortable self teaching. he's a nice person, but his teaching style didn't work for me. if you took ap calc ab or bc, the material is very similar with only a few new topics. weekly recitation is worth 5% and there is no partial credit. also paid around $70 for the recommended textbook.
Grading is insanely strict. Lectures were boring. Content can be easily learned outside of class, although attendance is not required. Decent at teaching,
Every Business Calc professor at VT is terrible. He's the better one, but still not good. Lots of homework. Weekly recitation classes. Exams make up 65% of your grade. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unless your insanely locked in and actually interested in business calc, don't take this class. He goes very fast and along with his strong accent it's so hard to understand him. He isn't engaging and sounds like a robot. Tests are very difficult, the usual median grade among all students on his tests are below a 65%.
I dreaded going to this class. Recitation was the WORST thing ever, so annoying and literally only worth 1 point. NO PARTIAL CREDIT. The exams are horrible. Literally did not learn anything ngl..

BRUTAL grader, no partial credit, exams are worth 70%. Class is a bit hard, but his heavy accent doesn't help. You would know more if you taught yourself. Would recommend choosing a different professor. He also doesn't answer emails, so you really gotta learn it yourself

Ted isn't a great teacher in my opinion. He doesn't give partial credit on extended response questions especially since some questions piggyback off of the previous question. He does not respond to any messages or emails, so if you want to talk to him, better see him after lectures. Very test heavy, so its harder to recover if you screw up.

I dread coming to this class. The professor has a heavy accent, so I barely understood anything. Every time I see my exam grade, I cry myself to sleep. When I cross the street, I don't look for incoming cars, hoping they could end me right then and there.

good professor. answers all questions. actually makes sense during lecture too. he is a super hard grader though so beware. also quizzes every week. I don't think he curves either. the average for a lot of the quizzes was around a 25%...

Ted is very focused and straight to the point. Overall, if you go to class and do the homework you will be fine, the tests will be easy in comparison to some of the homework problems (which you get unlimited attempts on). If you need this class for credit, Ted is your best bet.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ted was a great teacher. Goes a little fast, but he is very open to questions. Just listen in class and ask questions and there will be no reason not to do good.

Honestly he is better than the other business calc teacher. However, he is difficult to hear in the big lecture room, never responds to emails, and doesn't clearly explain the material. He does typically post his notes at the end of the week so you can teach it to yourself.

I stopped going to this class to get more sleep but all of the lectures notes and homework are posted on Canvas. I do the work for this class on my own time. It's not necessarily hard but everything builds up so you have to make sure you have a good understanding of everything. Exams are very easy (but make sure to double check you answers).

Not a great professor. He is not engaging during lectures, he writes exactly what is in the textbook when explaining problems/formulas with no further explanation. The class is easy, so it's still very easy to get an A. Exams are not difficult.

MATH 1524 at VT is brutal. No curve, no partial credit, no formulas on tests.Tests are worth 60% of your grade. Lectures are just him doing problems with no structure or review. You're forced to teach yourself. Drop/withdrawal rates are so high- a month in I felt like I was being set up to fail. It made me miserable, and I studied a lot for tests.
The weekly quizzes and tests are based on Epp, Hammack, and past homework and classwork. As long as you do those and attend the mock exams you should be good.

Not a great teaching style, just reads off his lecture notes and writes everything on board, not very engaging. I think it's important to go to his lectures though. Class is easy enough, would recommend but I think there's better discrete teachers.

He says he has a textbook but instead he has two which neither are accurate to what quizes and tests are on. A lot of the quiz and test questions are ones that were on any homeworks or classworks which makes it really hard to study for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Notes heavy, notes arent posted online, which is unfortunate. Tests are reasonable if you study enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Juste, if you are reading this. Please, please, please post the answers to the Classwork 5/Mock Final. I am studying for this exam and I want to see how you are solving these questions. The final is in two days and there have been no other resources that have been posted for the final on canvas.

DO NOT TAKE JUSTE. he puts in 0 effort into the class. literally two days from the final and he hasnt given us any review material. also takes forever to grade assignments. doesn't do a good job of covering concepts in class. posts no material in the canvas. worst professor i've had at vt by far
There's a lot of homework and tests, but it's an somewhat easy course if you take advantage of all the available resources.

I personally would advise against taking Ted, he doesn't post notes on Canvas, makes basic algebra mistakes constantly, and only writes notes on a whiteboard.

This class in general isn't particularly difficult so it is manageable, but if you don't show up to class you're out of luck unless you get notes from someone else.
Puts no effort into the class. Barely posts anything on canvas, doesn't provide much resources to help us study for quizzes/exams.

This class was required for my major, so I switched majors. The lectures are so boring and confusing, you're better off teaching yourself. I stopped going to class and learned more from friends and VT math tutor on YouTube. Lots of homework and exams are heavy weighted. Avoid this class, if possible. I have nightmares about it.

Ted Juste was a very nice person, but didn't teach the class well at all. He didn't have a syllabus for the class which made it difficult to refer back to policies and class structure. Not to mention, he frequently made mistakes on the board and students had to correct him. Overall, he wasn't well prepared and his notes were hard to read.

If you took and remember stuff from Precalc and Calculus in Highschool, you'll be fine. Otherwise? You're gonna need to study. I found it impossible to learn from his lectures and thus taught myself the majority of the subjects with notes provided online. The exams are 10-12 questions with no partial credit, so make sure you're ready for them.

Tests are hard. No partial credit, curves, or extra credit. There is lots of homework so make sure to keep up. The lectures are not enough to get an A in the class if you aren't already good at calculus. Need to self teach.

This class was really easy, especially if you took calc in high school. I stopped showing up to class and was still doing well. Though, when I did go, he occasionally made mistakes, usually a couple per lecture while solving problems. Though, he is willing to go through every problem step by step.

Frequently gets his examples wrong, but goes slower on the content compared to the other professors. Only reason I passed is bc of VT Math Tutor on YT and recitation with my TA Jacob who also set up study sessions before exams. 3 exams worth 45% and final 20% so you can fail one exam but you have to do pretty well on the others to make up for it.

Nice guy but lectures are impossible to pay attention to and a little hard to understand. Tests are not too bad if you study. I learned everything on my own and found it easier to learn through friends. I know this class is unavoidable, so I literally changed majors.

Professor Juste is a super nice guy. His lectures are a bit boring, but very easy to follow along. He gives a lot of homework. Tests aren't that hard, as long as you practice. Best business calc professor by far
The tests are 45% of your grade. He doesn't give partial credit to any of the problems and no curve. Very hard to get an A.

I never went to class except for exam days but still ended with a high A but I did take ap calc bc in high school. Tests are just like the webassign homeworks and theres 4 tests. cant really say much about the professor's teaching because I never went to class but he never responds to emails which was annoying.

Attendance not mandatory but if you don't go you wont get notes you need for assignments. A good amount of homework each week and you can get points back on tests if you go to his office hours. Very understanding and forgiving.

He's a boring teacher, simply copies from the textbook onto the board. His classes are just storytime but the story is the textbook. He never responds to any emails, is always making mistakes when explaining concepts, and never has canvas grades up to date.
Professor Juste was a good professor for this class. He very clearly goes over everything that we're learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Never responded to emails ever!!!
He went pretty quickly during his lectures, but he is probably the best professor for business calc. He's really nice during office hours and tries to help.
Went pretty quick through lectures but is overall a pretty nice guy.

do not pick Ted. He is not good at explaining and makes everything more confusing. For our last unit he spent the enitre time reading from the textbook and just writing things down without actually teaching it. He messes up a lot, which is even moreconfusing. The tests themseleves aren't hard at all, you just have to put the effort in to study.

Overall, Ted was a really nice person. However, the class was extremely difficult. He gives out on average 4 online homework assignments a week, with nearly 15 multiple step questions. On top of that he gives out written homework and possibly a quiz. Exams will either make or break your grade regardless of how good your other assignment grades are.

He goes through the material slowly which is very nice. He would have recitation classes once a week for extra help (technically required but you're fine if you don't go). Lowkey his lectures were boring. It's a passible class and Ted seems fine I just didn't really like it.

Professor Juste is a good professor who goes over all the material for 1524 pretty well. Make sure to pay attention during lecture, and if you get confused, seek help ASAP because you will regret not getting help earlier. His office hours are helpful and he can help you understand topics you are struggling with. Study hard and you'll pass.
Lectures are important in math. Always be ready to take note of whats on the board, it'll definitely be useful later.
Ted is a sweet man who is very nice and well-spoken during his lectures. Tests emulate homework so as long as you do those, you should be fine.

I had him Fall 2022. Compared to other teacehrs, he made calculus 2 not be a weedout and seem doable, albeit a bit difficult. Great at going over problems during lectures and answering questions. Very understanding in general and also isn't stingy with partial credit.
I took my friend to his office hours and she was amazed by how great he was. Tests and quizzes aren't too bad. Love this man!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ted was an amazing teacher. He taught concepts very well. He was also a very sweet and nice teacher. If you are able to take him, you should!

Ted is a great professor, he lectures slowly which really helps you to take notes on everything and is very good with questions. The homework he gives, while long is very manageable and does very help in teaching you application and prepares for his tests very well.
Loved this guy. Take his class if you can. He is sweet and caring. Just pay attention. Does not feel like a weed-out class with him. Generous partial credit and grades clearly.

I took Professor Juste for math 2214, differential equations. I thought he was fine. All of his notes were written on the chalkboard with no online supplements. The tests weren't terrible. He was pretty good overall. Top 3 math professor I've had here.
Great calculus professor. Gave informative lectures, answered questions, and was a big help during his office hours. Much better than what I've heard from other calc professors
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good teacher overall. He curved my grade at the end of the semester since I needed 0.3 points to reach the next letter grade. He is very understanding and easy to ask questions to.
One of the hardest weed out classes, hes probably the best teacher for it though since he gives quizzes that boost youre grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is amazing, take him for Proofs. He does a great job explaining
well it looks like his strong suit may be lectures based off of the other reviews. i would love to experience his lectures, but he just posts links to youtube videos someone else made.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Tough grader--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are very interesting he tries to give anecdotes at times to explain math. Before covid he gave out easy quizzes that were a grade boost. I had taken IB math HL in high school so most of the topics were familiar to me, but even then he was great at explaining what he was doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super nice guy. You will learn everything from lectures. 10 minute quiz every friday at the end of class. Homework mostly through webassign, a few written assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved professor Juste. I had to retake calc 1226 because my previous professor was not my style and getting into this class was a blessing. Hes great at lectures, office hours are super helpful, and his weekly quizzes reinforce material and boost your grade. I dont know what I would have done without this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ted Juste is a fine choice for a professor. He is still learning his teaching style, so at points in the subject I personally got lost and had to look in other sources. He isn't too harsh of a grader for homework and written assignments. It was a hard class that I had to work hard to get the grade I got. I'm, by choice, taking his next class.
Super cool and chill. Go to class and turn in your assignments and you will get an A.

Dr. Katz was an amazing professor! Super duper easy class. The only people who failed didn't do the assignments. The lectures were great since they explored the 8 different focuses of civil engineering and you get to hear first-person experiences from people within that field. Overall, great class, even better professor, and I learned a lot!

Katz is amazing! Funny, kind, and a great lecturer. CEE 2804 is very guest speaker-driven driven so he does not lecture much himself. All guest speakers were very engaging and the class does a great job at introducing one to all of the CEE disciplines.

This class is probably the easiest class I have taken in my undergrad. Taking it online is definitely preferred, his lectures that he provided are great! The homework was easy, and tests relate a lot to the material taught in the lectures. Also took him for Intro, amazing professor, great to get to know.
Dr. Katz is very nice and it's clear that he cares about what he teaches. He definitely wants his students to succeed, and the course provided valuable content.
He's a really nice guy, very easy class. He doesn't like cheaters.
Extremely easy, super nice and friendly, hates cheaters, wants us all to succeed and wants to help.
Katz is a great professor. Tried to be funny in lectures although most of the time it is guest speakers in 2804. Class is really easy, just show up and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Transportation can be complicated but he gives you plenty of help with homework and exams that with minimal effort you can easily get a high A in the class.

Katz is a fun and enthusiastic professor. 2804 is a busy work class so don't sweat it. Lectures are long and boring, and the "small group" recitation meetings are massive time wasters so just power through and do the writing assignments early.
Great teacher

Dr. Katz is very passionate about what he teaches and is an amazing resource for all things Civil Engineering. His class is entirely lecture based and exploratory. He brings in interesting speakers so the lectures were interesting and engaging.
Lectures not required. Papers every 1-2 weeks. Easy grading. Overall easy but informative class.

Overall a good professor but has boring lectures. Papers and memos due weekly over the last couple of months. Attendance is taken in class each day and he offers extra credit at the end of the semester which can boost your grade by about 3 points. Easy class if you do not procrastinate.

Tests matched the homework and practice problems very well; always felt well prepared for tests/exams. Lectures are helpful and easy to follow, rarely found myself needing to consult other lectures on the internet. His personality is a little quirky, but I actually liked this and found him to be a pretty funny professor.

Professor Kasebian is an exceptionally peculiar soul. He will often ask questions to the class, knowing full well nobody knows the answer, and smile mischievously when nobody speaks up. He doesn't mind good questions, but will make sure you know if you ask a bad one. Overall, taught good, clear lectures, and gave extremely reasonable exams.

Interesting man. Talks in monotone voice & calls people out in class & says like "you'd think im speaking chinese by her face" and then clarifies 10 mins later "that was a joke". Sit in front to hear & see. lecture is him writing on a paper that's projected. Useful lectures, not posted online. Tests problems align with lecture & hw. Overall good
Very funny prof. with excellent visuals to demonstrate concepts during lectures. Idk how he does it with a chalkboard.
Drop this class. Get a new one. Add drop is your friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but was VERY unclear on a subject I struggled to understand conceptually. Linear is really not that hard so if you self learn (I did not which explains my grade) but I would not recc relying on lectures. I took the class in he fall where he gave me absolutely no partial credit but I heard he got more lenient in the spring  so idk.

Class was heavily weighted by tests and homework graded by TA's who don't give any feedback. There are no online notes or anything to use for review. I found myself looking over incomplete notes and scrambling to be prepared for exams.

He's a chill professor who needs a little getting used to, since, at first, his mumbling is irritating and difficult to get by. However, his visual style of teaching greatly helped me throughout the semester since I'm a heavily visual learner.

Kaveh Kasebian is nice enough, but he doesn't care about teaching. Every time he stepped in front of the class it was obvious that he hated his job. His tests and assignments weren't too difficult and I was able to follow along for the most part in this class, pay close attention because he mumbles. His class is survivable, but painful.

Kaveh is a sharp and witty instructor who relies on his notes heavily during lectures. He's a lenient grader, but his tests can be quite challenging, often with unexpected curveballs. While he explains concepts fairly well, there are no practice tests provided except for the final. You should do fine in his class if you do the homework.

Deadpan, sardonic, and strange man. Lifechanging nonetheless. Very good professor by all accounts. Extremely easy tests if you take good notes and show up to lectures. Dude literally tells you what will be on the exams.

He doesn't have much emotion when he teaches, but you can tell he is a really smart guy that knows what he is talking about. Sit in the front if you can. My strat was to learn a lot of the material on my own before attempting the homework and then use his lectures as review. Tests are easy but if you mess one up you probably wont be getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor, do not take his class. Lectures are useless, he does not even talk in complete sentences?? Also does not hold office hours at all, and the TA's only job is grading homework which they do extremely harshly. The other reviews here are false. I stayed past the drop deadline in hopes he would change, but I had to waste one of my Ws.

If you want to put in the least effort, take kasebian. He doesn't give much homework at all, and his exams are the easiest thing ever. At times i forgot I was even in the course because the homework was so rare and I barely ever had to study for the exams. The exams ask only the most basic of questions, and he's open to new approaches

This is only math class were we've read Shakespeare, and a line from the late poet Dante. He has practically zero online presence, so attendance is pretty much mandatory if you want to succeed. Might not be the best professor, but something about dry humor and math goes well together.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Okay sooooooo (his catchphrase), Kaveh is an interesting character and is a good guy. The main issue with him is his English is not great, so you have to ask a lot of questions to get the most out of lectures. However, he goes over a lot of examples and his HW is similar to tests. Not a bad professor, but his poor English really holds him back.

He is a ghost, a comedian, and a poet at times. His class was quite easy and the tests were as well. Online he is nonexistent. I have yet to find a picture of this man, and trust me I have been looking fervently. One time in class, Kasebian blessed our hears with the story of Odysseus. From then on I have sacrificed a goat to him every night.

Pro:
He gives real world examples

Cons:
He is terrible at basic arithmetic.
He doesn't complete examples or give proper solutions to problems so there is no way of knowing what you did wrong.
He responds to questions with derogatory remarks.
He did not prepare for class.

I've had worse professors I guess...
He is a good professor that can teach pretty well. He grades pretty gracefully and if you understand the material and have a good concept on what to do you will be in good shape
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very good at explaining vector calculus concepts in a easy and clear way, with great writing/drawing on the blackboard. Tests are easy if you go to the lectures and do the homework.

Kaveh is an absolutely amazing professor, probably the best math prof at VT. I had him for Linear and Multi, and as long as you attend lectures, he does a great job of breaking things down. He has a great sense of humor and gives really helpful feedback on homework assignments. Really hoping to have him again in the future.
Professor Kasebian is a very easygoing and funny guy in class. His class can be very easy but also very difficult at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kasabian's a peculiar man. Very quiet, so try to sit at the front of the class. He also tends to ask questions to the class and sit there with a mischievous grin until someone answers or he gives up. I don't know if I would recommend him, but you'll make it out alright if you end up with him.

Professor Kasebian a pretty tough guy. He was condescending towards students when the correct answer wasn't said, and was just overall not approachable for help outside of class. He went super fast when going over the material. Definitely knew his craft, but wasn't good at teaching it. Had to take a different professor who was much better.

Incredible Man. Mysterious Man. Nobody knows anything about him. The math department doesn't have any picture of him on the website. He will crack a half smile when he's fooled someone because he asks some trick questions. Fantastic at explaining calc concepts but a terrible presenter. Sit at the front of the class if you can.

His lectures are clear, and he covers content that will be on the test. Also, the tests are just like the homework, and he makes it obvious what content/problem-types will be on the test and is open to answering questions around this. He answers questions well and is humorous at times. However, it takes energy to get through lectures at times.

He was always very clear in class and I rarely had trouble understanding what he was going over. He was very respectful and helpful to students that actively participated in his class and did well, and was less so towards disrespectful students that would crack jokes at him or not participate. My advice for this class would just be to participate.

Prof. Kasebian showed his indifference toward teaching from the very beginning of class. When class begins, he is in an angsty rush to go through the material. He mocks and denies questions from students. Huge disconnect between exam content and material presented in class. Very hard to reach. No emailing. Same angsty attitude during office hours.
Dr. Kasebian is amazing at explaining concepts and is a very fair grader. If you need extra help he is very accessible outside of class and he really wants everyone to succeed.
Horribly confusing at explaining any concept. Exams are HARD! Have to rigorously teach yourself with material you can find online. Would NOT take again.

I had Kasebian for 2114 and 2204. He's a great professor and it's easy to succeed with a good strategy. Become proficient with every concept on homework as they will give you a good idea as to the exam content. Attend class and pay attention. He does many problems that are important to know for assignments. Study and take the course seriously!

I didn't have the best first impression of him, as he's a quiet guy and didn't seem too engaged with the course for the first few classes but it definitely got better. A lot of learning in class is spent doing practice problems instead of him just writing his notes on the board, which is what I prefer.

This class was the only class I actually went to, but I somehow failed. His lectures weren't terrible and he wasn't necessarily boring; however, he refused to answer questions. He was not at accommodating for make-up assignments and half the time he had no idea what he was talking about. He relied on his notes that were most often than not wrong.

Professor Kasebian does not explain things well and would basically laugh in your face if you tried to ask a question in class. Thus, no one liked him and a quarter of class had to drop the class. I only learned from online videos I found from the year when everything was online. Do yourself a favor and dont take his class!!
If you take this class without friends you will probably fail. Insanely hard because he doesn't teach at all but the tests are not easy by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Doing well in this class means teaching yourself. It's hard to hear his voice from across the classroom, and he has straight up refused to speak up when asked. Rude demeanor. He has rejected questions he thinks are stupid, and will instead tell us that this is material we should already know. Finally, material is presented way too hastily.

Will belittle you in class if you ask questions he deems "dumb", would not recommend this class especially if you aren't already exceptionally good at math or aren't willing to basically teach yourself the course.

The instructional material is pretty terrible. If you dont keep up with a schedule, youll be swamped with dozens of eyewatering videos on a sad sunday night. Kavehs tests dont have many questions or points, if you mess up on one question it can bring your grade down by a letter. Grades fairly and is a cool guy, seemed like online brought him down.

The lectures themselves were not by this professor but we had one weekly session where he went over examples. The class is not too hard but there were not many questions on the tests which can make them hard to ace. Overall he was pretty chill and understanding if you needed an extension on homework.

For online classes, all of the linear algebra classes are using videos made by people who likely are not your professors. The videos were mediocre but Kaveh held classes once a week to review material. Overall he is an easy grader.
Kasebian is the hidden gem of the math department. He is the best.

Dr. Kasebian is a great professor if you're good at math. He doesn't go very in depth during his lectures, but he covers everything well enough. If you don't understand it immediately, you're going to have to teach yourself. He has almost no homework, and the quizzes were take home, open book, open note, and collaborative.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He toned it down to the VT students' level. His exams were not hard at all.

His entire class was just doing a couple easy example problems, and that would be the lesson for a whole section/unit. The webassign problems were much harder than the examples he did in class. However, the tests he makes are not too difficult: just do the homework. Also, the common time final (multiple choice) is so freaking difficult!!!

Kasabian is one of the most helpful professors i've had here. His lectures can be sometimes boring, but they are very informational. He always makes sure that every student gets the opportunity to clear any confusions and makes times outside of class to meet with students who need extra clarification. By far the best Calculus teacher i've ever had.

He's a great professor, very detailed in his lectures and goes over everything very thoroughly, but not in a boring manner. He made learning the information simple and was willing to answer all questions until the student knew it. Would Recommend! He's also funny

Dr. Kennedy is a really kind professor and is very passionate about her work. The lectures definitely tend to drag, but are for the most part interesting. There are lots of choices for homework and you do not need to do every assignment which I liked. Attendance is necessary due to tophat questions done in class. Tests were online and pretty easy.

Although Dr. Kennedy's lectures do get very boring, her stories that relate to the content are mostly interesting. Getting the homework points is very easy as long as you put in some amount of effort. The exams are not nearly as hard as I thought they'd be, plus they're open note, and online. Her and her TA Alex are amazing.

Attendance is mandatory for this class. Dr. Kennedy is passionate and knowledgeable about the topics in this course. Make you you study for the exams even though they are open note because they can be difficult, but she posts the slides after class to review. I recommend taking her class.
The class was super easy and she really cares and wants you to pass. She's a super sweet lady and drops a lot of interesting lore during lectures.
lisa kennedy is the best professor I have had, her and her TA Alex were awesome.

Dr. Kennedy is a lovely professor. The homework is easy as long as you actually care and the classes are easy to understand. The tests could be hard but they are not in person and are open note. Would recommend.

Dr. Kennedy's class is very easy to follow and succeed in. She does TopHat questions as attendance and they count towards your final grade as participation. Usually gives an online quiz a week and a few online tests throughout the semester. Lectures can be boring but it's good to know material especially for CNRE.

Easy class! Dr. Kennedy is nice and makes it easy to understand. Top hat attendance is required. Light homework if you just watch the sinking cities episodes and do a few other assignments. Usually finishes up class a few minutes early. Open note exams

Physical Geo at times was a little boring but you are learning the basics of the field and it was important stuff to know. Participation matters, just show up, or let her know you can't make it, she's super understanding and flexible. She has a lot of funny stories which makes class fun! Point system of pick and choose assignments which was nice!

Professor Kennedy is amazing and really cares about her students. The topics in Physical Geo are straightforward and with her lecture slides (that she does post on canvas) quizzes and exams are easier to understand and score higher.

She does a points system for homework so that your can pick and choose assignments that interest you. She also gives a lot of quizzes that are super easy so it's really hard to get a bad grade in the class. The exam is just quiz questions and things from the lectures. She's really caring and a great professor

Lisa Kennedy is one of the nicest professors i've had at VT. Her lectures can be a bit long but the class itself is pretty easy. Definitely take intro to physical geog!! Not too much work either, interesting content.

Attendance was mandatory and we used TopHat daily. She uses a point system, just make sure to do as much homework as you can in the beginning of the semester and get it out of the way. Tests and quizzes are easy as long as you take notes. She really loves power point presentations.

Dr. Kennedy is a great professor. Her class was very substantive yet not heavy on workload or difficulty. She is very accomplished in her field, and incorporates interesting personal experiences into her lectures. Despite a large class size she went out of her way to give thoughtful feedback. Anyone should be able to get an A if they put in effort.

Uses point system for homework and offers many more points than you need. You can make many of the assignments as interesting as you want them to be. Uses TopHat for attendance and posts lecture slides. Relates lots of content to her own experiences and tries to make class relevant. Make sure to review for exams since the first one can be hard.

Dr. Kennedy truly cares about her students and the content she teaches. This is all very obvious through her exciting lectures, many of which involve her own personal research! She offers an awesome point system that rewards hard workers. I would certainly take a class with her again.

Used Point System. To get an A we needed 320 ptS, she offered 710 pts. 2 tests and must get  50% to consider getting A. No final. Small quizzes in between (not required but if you want pts then take it) You can fail the quizzes and it wont matter bc its point based. Posts PPT lectures after class. I did so much extra work than I needed to.

Very passionate about what she teaches. Have to buy TopHat for participation. Point Based System. To get an A you have to get 340 points, she offered 860 points! Her quizzes are online but very short. 10questions in 8mins so no time to use book/notes. Very easy to get A if you just PAY ATTENTION.

She's a really good lecturer and keeps the class interesting. Attendance isn't mandatory but you can get extra credit for it. A good class but you definitely do have to study a good amount for the exams. Don't skip class.

Good teacher who gives extra credit 4 or 5 times a semester for simply attending class. You have to do well on the 3 test because they are 75% of your grade. But the test material is fairly easy and simplified. Great teacher in my opinion

For a science class, this thing rocks. learn lots about how the world works and some stuff to take home too. Like don't build your house on a floodplain:). Really pretty interesting stuff and she brings it down to everybody's level.
Great class and not hard. Makes the material real by giving lots of real life examples.  Lots and lots of slides keep it interesting.
Very easy class, powerpoint notes make it even easier to pass the test and also make the class more interesting
No Comments
VT should not have her
shes nice but is no go for me

People on here complaining about professor kennedy just don't give any effort in the class. she can be unorganized at times but she is a very knowledgeable and very kind. the class itself isn't bad as long as you show up to class and give a little effort. putting in the bare minimum effort will get you at least a C+. its really not bad at all.

She literally just talks about herself the entire class period and reads off slides that she did not even make herself (she took it from another professor) so she is completely unfamiliar with the content. Her tests are all written and conceptual and she just talks about the market and doesnt teach at all. AVOID HER IF YOU CAN at all costs.

While Kennedy is very knowledgable in her field, she often got really sidetracked talking about politics and the government. We spent over half class time talking about things that were unrelated to exams. The TAs also did all of the work for her. She is very kind and interesting but the class as a whole was hard to sit through at times.

I really enjoyed Asset Valuation and Governance with Professor Kennedy! She starts every class by going over current events in the markets, which helps everyone stay informed on important news. If you participate in class and do the practice problems, you will be prepared for the exams.

I took FIN 4244 with Professor Kennedy and found the class to be very straightforward. Kennedy is very knowledgeable and actively tries to engage students by talking about real-life examples and events happening outside of class. The exams are fair, so as long as you pay attention in class and attend the review sessions, you should do well.

This was one of my favorite classes, it was obvious that prof. Kennedy loves her students. She brings in valuable guest speakers and engages everyone to talk about current events at the beginning of class, building great habits for your future career. My advice would be to prepare for the material before and after every class and youll do great!
She's just ok. Doesn't really teach, she just talks. Has powerpoint slides that she never uses, strict with participation and group projects. Class is not super bad, but can be annoying sometimes.

She peeved me off. Every class was disorganized mess of her talking about current events and personal experiences. She also grades harshly for participation, even if you have perfect attendance. She never goes over exam material, and expects us to know random stuff prior to each class. Don't recommend.

Her class is all over the place. She never goes over PowerPoints related to the exams and just yaps about current events. She's also strict on participation, even if you have perfect attendance. She very nice though and gives extra credit with spot survey.

Classes didn't always pertain to the course material tested on the exams but friendly teacher, always willing to help out students, and the study guides told you exactly what was going to be on the exam. Lots of interesting real world discussions as well.

Idk what all these reviews are talking about. Professor Kennedy gave good lectures and literally gave study guides with everything that was on tests. This was one of the easiest classes I took in Pamplin.
She's super disorganized and is confusing to listen to. She rambles about current events and sometimes comes to class late. Very unprofessional and infuriating.

Kennedy is nice, but she's not an effective teacher. If you don't have background knowledge in corporate finance, good luck. Flipped classroom, absent TAs, and on top of 4 exams and only 3-4 lengthy group HWs, there's a group presentation at the end of the semester. Her background is awesome but she struggles to convey her expertise sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very nice and credible person, but an ineffective professor. Literally doesn't teach and makes her exams super difficult.

Nice lady, questionable professor. She does a flipped classroom, which was awkward silence other than 2 or 3 students participating. She barely lectures exam content and it was mostly discussion of whatever she felt. Not a lot of assignments and test heavy. Unorganized but that may have been due to outside factors. Class isn't very hard though.

She is such a nice person but I think she is taking on too many classes. She seemed pretty focused on her other classes and didn't really do much teaching. This class was not bad because of taking Kenders class at the same time. Most of the classes were cases and current events.

She is a very nice lady. She has no idea how to teach. She stands at the front of the class and asks questions that no one knows the answers to. It took over a month for our test grades to come back. There is just no bright spots about her. She grades slow, does not convey information, and everything on canvas that is helpful is Easterwoods.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: although Professor Kennedy seems very nice, she is not meant to teach. Her classes consist of lectures of her past experiences and she tries to connect that to the lesson but doesn't do it well at all. She assumes her students are all accounting geniuses and acts as if we should know all of the information she is presenting to us.  DO NOT TAKE HER

Don't take her but she's also the only professor for this class. Literally copies everything Professor Kender does. Made the first exam extremely lengthy and hard, no one finished. Taught nothing. No textbook but made you pay close to $5 every other week for cases. Nice person but genuinely not meant for teaching.
The subject was pretty interesting, he had great stories to tie it all together. The tests weren't necessarily that hard, you are mostly graded on attendance.

My Favorite professor! He is entertaining and keeps students engaged. A little hard to reach outside of class, he doesn't respond to emails quickly but catch him after class and he is very helpful. He has a lot of connections and knowledge so make an effort to chat with him!
Hamed is the best!! If you know, you know. But seriously, I had the best time in Field Bio, so if you have the chance to take this class, you definitely should!
Hamed is amazing, he's one of my favorite professors and gives super entertaining lectures. Field Bio is a great class, so if you get the chance to take it, you absolutely should!!
My absolute favorite professor at Virginia Tech.

Dr Hamed is easily one of the best professors in CNRE. Although some of his coursework can be difficult and sometimes requires a lot of studying, he is a genuine person who will care about you. He is incredibly relatable and will treat you like a human being not a robot as a student.
Dr. Hamed is the best professor at VT. He cares about his students and wants them to succeed. The course takes commitment and time out of class to learn the species binomial names.

Dr. Hamed is my favorite professor at this school. His class is engaging and he offers endless opportunities to boost your grade through easy homework assignments and for showing up to class. Nothing is weighted so you can make up for a bad test grade through attendance. He is incredibly kind when it comes to absences and keeps class fun.
He was very nice

Kevin seems like a kind person, but his class has been disappointing. The homework feels like busywork, and the lectures lack structure, making it hard to stay engaged. It's frustrating because the topic is interesting, but the disorganized teaching style takes away from its potential.

He's super relatable and kind, but he is so unorganized it's insane. Some of the due dates were put in incorrectly on multiple occasions and caused a lot of unnecessary confusion. He's great, but he could be more organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Hamed is the man. This class is definitely not an easy A. He makes you work but it's enjoyable and you actually learn cool things that will probably benefit your career.

Kevin is SO awesome. There were a lot of issues with grading in our class due to problems with the TA's, so we got an extra 12 points on our final exam and 4 points on exam 2. He also offers a lot of extra credit and had super enjoyable lectures; he teaches some really great stuff.

Dr. Hamed wants all of his students to succeed. If you show up to class and watch his exam reviews you will make an A no problem. Only issue was organization/grading but I'm pretty sure that was on the TAs. Plus, he will work with you to fix everything and even gave everyone 10 extra points on the final because of prior grading mistakes.

There are only 2 tests and a final in this class. His lectures consist of mainly him speaking and a slideshow, but there are also in class activities with the group you sit with which is how attendance is taken. He does a good job at working with his students if there is conflict with an assignment. He is super nice and cares about his work.

This class was honestly so fun. There is daily participation grades which act as a huge grade boost alongside some homework and 3 tests. There's an online program that cost money which homework assignments go though. Dr. Hamed really loves this subject and wants you to learn, great professor!!
Such a great teacher and a passionate man. Learned SO MUCH this semester !

kevin is the best. super hilarious and wants you to succeed. if you want to take this course as a "whatever class", don't. there's a lot of assignments and he's a pretty tough grader. tests aren't a walk in the park either. my rec, take notes on the lecture slides and pay attention to case studies. do this and you'll be fine.
This man is an icon. So fun to listen to and really cares about his students. He engages with everybody in their groups and is truly awesome. Prepares you greatly for the class.

Dr. Hamed is a funny, personable guy who puts a lot of work into making sure each individual student knows what's going on and wants them to succeed. He is hilarious and a great lecturer, easily the best of the four professors teaching this class. He makes learning super interesting and keeps everyone's attention.

Dr Hamed is the absolute best. Definitely my favorite ever professor. Hes just so easy to talk to. As long as you put in work for his classes you will do just fine. If you are ever confused about anything, email him and he almost always gets back to you within a day
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My roomie and I LOVED Kevin. Simply put, this man is the best. BUT, you need to pay attention. Neither of us did that hot on his exams unless we really dug down and it's so lecture-heavy that that's kinda difficult but take notes and engage with your groupmates and you'll be fine. YAY KEVIN!!
great professor, he's easy to talk to and very fair

I had profressor kern for two classes virtually. He is a great professor, and if you don't join the live zooms just watch the videos he has posted on Canvas. He is a cool guy, and he is very understanding. He also gives a oppurtunity for extra credit at the end of the semester if a certain percentage of students complete the spot survey!

Professor Kern is easily one of the best professors at Virginia Tech. He is super kind and caring of his students and wants you to do well. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you miss a class he has video lectures on canvas so you're not behind. Honestly your set up for success

Attendance isn't mandatory but you will fall behind if you don't attend lectures. Super kind professor and easy to talk to. Tests are definitely harder than quizzes and homework, but open note and you get two attempts.

The only reason I got a B is because I did not study that much. The class was straightforward, only grades are maybe a few quizzes a week and test grades. He is a very kind professor, all exams were open notes/devices just no ai. I passed the class with a B without trying that hard. Heavily recommend him. (he did assign a test on Halloween though)
I was rocking with this prof until he assigned a test on Halloween. You are worse than the Grinch sir. I did all my work for every class to enjoy my weekend and it completely ruined all my plans.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All the homeworks are on Hawkes/ Pearson and once you learn how to do the problems there- no need to go to class. Quizzes and exams were online (lockdown, no camera) with about 5-7 days to do them, you get 3 attempts for the quizzes and 2 attempts for the exams, 1 attempt on the final

I really liked Professor Kern, as I thought he was helpful in teaching the material. However, I absolutely hated the online textbook that they used (Hawkes), as I felt that the questions from there didn't really help that much with the exams in my opinion.

NGL, I didn't like Professor Kern's class. It was monotonous, boring, and not practical when preparing for tests. Having stated that, the class, homework, and practice exam will not prepare you enough for exams. The tests are rigorous. You have two opportunities, so please consider reviewing the first before proceeding with your final attempt.
He is so sweet and all the tests, quizzes, and homeworks are online. The quizzes/tests can be quite different from the homeworks at times though, and this can make it a little harder.

The professor is a nice guy, and the exams aren't too bad since you get two attempts at them. There's usually one homework assignment a week, and it'll take about an hour to do, so the workload isn't bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Long lectures but all homework, quizzes and exams were online where you have a week to do it. You get 3 attempts for the quizzes and 2 attempts for the exams.

Kern is a great guy, and whenever I had questions about the exams, he would come to office hours, help me understand, and even increase some points. However, after doing the HW, and practice test, I can say that these tools don't significantly improve exam performance. The exams are two attempts, so revise your first try before taking the second.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kern is the kindest professor that wants you to do well in the class. The HW is not required but if you can do that then the test will be an absolute breeze, they are very surface level. Kern simplifies everything and is always willing to try different ways to help you understand. Easiest and nicest person to take this class with. No proctor test.

He is an awesome professor and cares about your grade. He has flexible office hours and will go over anything you need. Unfortunately this class is pretty difficult with the tests, & a lot of the practice questions are completely diff than the test. He also gives all of the materials you need to do well on the tests, although it takes lot of time.
Good professor, however, it is not his fault a lot of the stuff that is on the practice problems through the online program arent actually tested in the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a good teacher and will take the time to help if you have questions. Tests are a huge part of your grade so ask questions.

It's almost an online class, with optional in-person. Homework is not bad, but the exams online are horrendous, it's as if the homework doesn't help at all. A few extra credit options, but overall, if you are good at math, you'll be fine. Go to his office hours (points back on exams). If you need extensions, he is relaxed on it.
Professor Kern was so sweet and I loved taking his class. Attendance wasn't mandatory which made it difficult to go sometimes, but his lectures were helpful and in depth of the material.

I had a hard time with the course material. But if you go to office hours after an exam/ quiz, he'll walk you through what you did wrong. He will give points back if he sees you were on the right track. (Keep your scratch paper for this)

Class was very hard, content was not easy to understand, kern did his best during class to try to go through questions and make it make sense to his students, unfortunately like no one went to class by the last week it totalted 10 kids in a 150 person lecture class. even though its not required going to class helps!

Kern is so caring and kind towards his students. material was hard but you can learn everything through Hawkes through the tutor button. Tests were difficult and I felt like I had no idea what I was doing on them despite doing well on certifications and quizzes. I rarely attended class but if I had I probably would've gotten a better grade.
Great guy who makes the subject matter very clear.  Gave tons of extra credit, making it easy to boost your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You NEED to do the textbook and certifications in order to pass the class, but that is for all sections. Professor Kern is a really good professor and really cares about his students. In class he is very responsive, and if you have a question he will stop mid sentence and answer you. He also will do partial points back on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Kern was super nice, and you could tell her enjoyed teaching. He's very willing to go over any particular question or reexplain material. We use an online program, which some enjoy some don't. I personally like it because comes with an "open tutor," and takes you through step by step.

The best prof. I have ever had. He is very kind and understanding, a very down to earth person. He is also great at explaining, lecturing and answering questions. This was one of the only classes where attending an optional class actually was helpful instead of just doing the homework; he makes a hard subject easy to understand.

Make sure to do the quizzes! The HW isn't required but they're harder than the tests so if you know the HW, you're good on exams. I stopped going to class in-person halfway through the sem but made sure to keep up with the material and ended up well. Really nice guy and held class on zoom!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this class summer 2022! Had a surgery while taking the class, and Kern was very understanding. The Hawkes lessons can be tedious but it helped me learn the material. Tests were alright if you knew the material. Put in the work and you'll be good! He may also give out partial credit if you go over past exams with him but don't count on it!

All of your work is done on a platform called Hawkes where you do problems and a quiz every week. I struggled with the course as the exams and quizzes were much harder than what was taught to you on the certifications, and I also had no prior stats background.

Kern is a caring professor and is always willing to help if you just ask him.

The entire class was on an online platform. Going to class did almost nothing for my understanding of the subject. It was entirely based on lessons each week and a quiz for each. The work you do for the chapter and the quiz are completely unrelated. The exams are also not aligned with the chapters or the practice problems. Everything is online.
Professor is understanding and forgivable if you have a genuine reason as to why you are not performing very well in the class. Very helpful and gives feedback quickly.

Professor Kern is fantastic. If he could teach every BIT class I would 1000% have him as my teacher each time. There is a lot of homework, but if you do each problem and understand it you'll do fantastic on each exam. You have to put in the work to get a good grade in this class, but it really does pay off and it wasn't too difficult!

He's a great teacher for a decently hard class. Lectures are very helpful and he communicates due dates well. He also gives a lot of extra credit and curves on exams which helped push me from an A- to an A.

He is pretty much a stereotypical, off the top of your head, average college professor lecturing. He seems pretty professional though and can be quite lenient on grades which is actually super helpful especially because his tests can be hard.

Kern is the best professor for this class. I highly recommend him. There isn't much work for this class. I love Kern this was the second time I had him as a prof. He has quizzes after most classes but they are so easy and grade boosters. His exams are what you should expect, no trick questions.

Kern is 100% the best prof for 2406, the class is way easier than any other prof (I took all the tests & quizzes for my friend in Simundza, they're so much harder). One question quizzes like every other class that are super easy. If you go to class and review the homework there's no reason to not get an A. Also, an A in the class is 90%, not 93%.

***TAKEN DURING COVID19**** This class was online due to COVID, but Professor Kern did a wonderful job of continuing to be engaged as much as he could with students. Although the certifications and quizzes are pretty straight-forward and repetitive, the exams are NOTHING like the certifications, please make sure to review recommended problems!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: From what I've seen of Kern he's a nice guy, and really wants his students to pass. I'd never taken stats before, and didn't attend lecture. Kinda threw myself to the wolves on this one, but I ended up alright. Don't just complete the homework but try to understand it and you'll do just fine.

This class is kind of difficult if you have never taken statistics, but Kern is very helpful in explaining. There is usually a lot of homework, which is time consuming but completion based. His tests and quizzes are significantly harder than the homework assignments, so watch out for that. He offers a few bonus opportunities but don't bank on them.

Professor Kern provides all of the materials you need to pass the class and get a good grade, it just depends on if you are willing to do the work or not. He explains everything very well and provides a lot of examples to help you understand the material. He also is very easy to get in touch with for office hours if you have any questions!

There really isn't that much benefit of going to the lectures since everything is pretty much online. If this is a required course for you I highly recommend Kern. He's such a likable guy. Some tips before you enter this class. The certifications for BIt 2405 are nothing and i repeat nothing like the exams. Make sure to study hard and do your work!

I had him for BIT 2405 this semester and I'm taking him again for 2406! He's a very sweet guy how gives plenty of opportunities for help and extra credit. This class is mostly online and the homework, quizzes, and certifications are easy A's. The tests are much more difficult, but if you do the extra credit/other things you can easily get an A .
I had him for BIT 2405, super easy class, all online, not necessary at all to come to class but if you do you can really learn something. He's a really cool dude!

Kern is a very nice & funny guy but his lectures aren't necessary, so I wouldn't bother going. Certifications and quizzes are not hard to get 100s on as long as you do the practice. The exams are difficult (barely anything like the certifications) but he gives you the opportunity to get points back in office hours. Bumped my 1st exam up by 10%.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing professor for a boring class. The class is mostly online but professor Kern is by far the best professor. He is really nice and funny and puts in alot of effort to make sure you do well. You can ask him questions during review days, office hours, on canvas, etc. He gives extra credit (3%!!!) for doing practice exams. He wants you to do well
This class relies heavily on you teaching yourself. All homework, quizzes, and tests are online and take forever. Terrible lectures and exams are impossible. Have fun!

WARNING: This is entirely an online course. All of the quizzes and tests are completely online and at home, meaning you have no excuse if you don't pass. That being said, Professor Kern, despite being nice and quirky-funny, is not a good lecturer for this class. He needs to slow down and explain concepts. Keep track of the AM test deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: The class wasn't that hard, but for a 1-credit class, I felt like we did a lot more work than we should have. I also wasn't expecting to take a final exam in the course since it was a 1-credit course, but we did. However, it's still not a challenging class as long as you attend the speaker event.

Professor Kender is a great guy and such a great connection to have because he knows just about anyone you want to get in contact with. The class itself is pretty self-explanatory, and there is no reason why you cannot get an A if you just try and attend the guest speaker events.
Great guy, has a lot of experience in the Finance world. If you go to class and speaker events, it's an easy A.
Such a great professor, he has so much expirence, show up to class and listen to what he has to say.
Awesome prof, he cares about the students and their future, will help you when you need and get you prepared for life.

Kender is a great guy who cares for his students. His class was a harder than I anticipated though and he grade pretty harshly on the homework. But he won't fail you as long as you show up and put in effort.
Just pay attention and study and you'll be fine.

The class was very informative on finance careers and he was a funny guy with a lot of real world experience. The main thing I would stress is please go to every class and get as many speaker events you can in the beginning of the semester so you don't need to study for the final.
