She is awesome but read ppt too much. Level 4 course was easier than I thought.

The exams for this class are challenging due to the specifics that are tested on but Prof Kim posts review videos and practice quizzes before every exam. Do all the extra credit you can because it makes a huge difference in your final grade (3 EC is 3 points added to total grade). The lectures are a bit boring but attendance quizzes at every class

Attendance quiz at the end of each class. Your exam scores define your final grades. 3-4 extra credit assignments, so your grades can be better. Gives very concise lecture slides, so you can rely on the slides to study. Kind of heavy accent which could be a problem depending on the person.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor King is an awesome professor. If you attend class, turn in work on time, and put in a little effort on the projects, you'll be fine. He uses in-class exercises to teach specific skills and allows flexibility in projects. If you ask him for specific feedback, he'll take extra time to discuss your work.

While covering a lot of important subject matter in his lectures, Professor Nate King tends to rush through things and overcomplicate them. This makes it difficult to follow the content in his class without seeking outside help. On a personal level, I felt disrespected by Professor King, and I will not be taking his classes in the future.

I love Professor King. I had him for New Media (ART1604) and just recently finished his 2D Animation (ART4504) course. Does talk very fast, and I actually fell asleep during some of his zoom synchronous lectures since it was 'lecture heavy.' Just arrange to speak to him outside of class if you're struggling. Also a lenient grader, and VERY caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor King knows what he's doing in After Effects, but he teaches fast and its easy to get lost in his flow, he needs to slow down sometimes. If you ask him to show something again, he will.

Every test is open note but it does not matter because about 50% of every test does not appear in any lecture or assignment, test are worth 64% of your total grade, slideshows are impossible to understand, if you dont have to take this class dont

exams are basically worth your entire grade. exams are so hard and not really based on his notes he gives out or the lectures. Exams are open note so there's no reason everyone should be failing. wouldn't recommend its so hard and not even a major requirement just a suggestion. don't take unless u have to

Exams vary in terms of difficulty, but they are open note. Reach out if you are struggling before the first exam and reflect on/revise studying once you receive your score. Attend class, take notes, and be engaged!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not take SOC 5034 unless you are a SOC major and it is required. I was not a SOC major and he acted like I should know all the sociological foundations he discussed in the course. There is ZERO indication of what your grade might be during the semester. He even preaches that grades don't matter then randomly assigns them at the end.

A very chill guy, but if you don't have to take the class, don't do it. The tests are hella hard. It's open note, but it will still get you. Attendance is not technically mandatory, u can do the top hats from home, its just an inconvenience.

Such an interesting professor. His lectors were mandatory but amazing to listen to. It is important to pay attention to what he is saying and not what is written on the slides. Do the readings, ask questions if you don't understand something, go to class and listen and you will be fine.

His lectures were interesting and the content is pretty straight forward, but he makes the test questions extremely difficult and super hard to understand. Some of the questions asked aren't even taught in his class lectures. Some questions you can only get from reading the 30+ page research articles. Would not recommend for a pathways course.

This guy is super interesting to listen to. The slides do not help at all, but if you listen and write down what he says... youll be fine. He cares about his students. He uses Tophat which is annoying but he does help you by giving you ten points at the end. However I bombed all the tophats. Just listen and youll be fine.

Easy homework assignments, just some reading and online discussions. The tests are somewhat difficult, but they are online and open note, so if you take good notes and review the posted review, you will get an A. Attendance is graded by top hats, which you need to be in class to see the question.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework was very straightforward. You would have a week to complete 3 items. Reading his notes (the one with pictures) was very helpful to study and revise my notes. Also, if you're not satisfied with the outcome of a test, he may allow you to redo it by writing an essay with a prompt. He is very understanding and is willing to help you pass.

Tests are difficult because most of the questions are based on the weekly articles throughout the course. There is lots of reading and can be hard to keep up. Attendance is technically not mandatory but there are tophats during class which count as a good portion of your grade.

King is a phenomenal lecturer. He is super fun to listen to and makes his topics easy to understand. There is a lot of reading outside of class, and tests are graded kind of heavily. However, they are open note and if you go to class and read you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor requires in person attendance and he uses tophat and whatever ur percentage is based of questions asked gets 10 added to it. So you really can't miss class that much as this counts for 17%. The exams have nothing to do with his class. He is sociologist but his class is based of every other sociologist. His slideshows are worthless.

The concepts of the class are easy to learn, his lectures are a little hard to follow. His slides are photos and little info. It's more important to take notes on what he says, if you take notes only for what's on the slides, it's useless. His tests are open note and open book, but his questions are hard to understand and is just a ton of jargon.

TERRIBLE GRADING. I had no grades in canvas all semester, did not receive any test grades back, received no feedback on assignments.  He talks about weird stuff in class even talked about mass shootings and made us watch videos of them on the anniversary of the VT shootings which I think is very disrespectful. Do not recommend.

Attendance is mandatory for this class as it uses Tophat for in-class questions based on the lectures, it is also 20% of your grade. Lectures are pretty interesting and entertaining but they have little correlation to what is on the tests. Homework is the same every week, with a discussion post, a short 2-6 question quiz, and asking a question.
Go to class and do the Tophats, i got an A on every exam and ended with a B+ because I stopped doing the tophats. Dont be like me lmao

Dr. King is an incredible guy and very passionate about his study, and I found the class to be very interesting. Unfortunately, his tests are SO hard and you will not perform well unless you have thoroughly read his 20+ page required weekly readings and know how he words things (which is very difficult).

He is a very funny guy, and tried to make jokes that the youth could relate to. He was also understanding when I had to switch the time I took an exam. He is easily reachable outside of class. Exams were a little difficult, as they are based on weekly readings that are lengthy and hard to understand, and questions are worded confusingly.

He is a very nice guy, and his lectures are pretty interesting, and he does a good job of trying to keep you engaged. The only issue is that a lot of the exams relate to the weekly readings you have to do which are very confusing and hard to comprehend

LOVED his lectures. They were fun and he is genuinely the only professor that has made me laugh a couple times. He connects the material to the real world and is entertaining. Only issue is the exams. The questions are insane, we get an hour and a half to answer 25 multiple choice questions and i run out of time every exam, they are rough.

Professor King was by far my favorite professor yet. He would often make jokes or even attempt to relate to today's terms. I really enjoyed his class and style of teaching. The downside however is that he doesn't use the Canvas grading system therefore most of us really didn't know what our current grades were for the majority of the year.

My favorite class this semester. Amazing lecturer, he knows his stuff and is very witty and funny at times. Easy weekly homework due on Sunday. Each lesson is written incredibly well in a PDF, so I highly recommend downloading those for your main study source. Tests are simple, open notes and multiple choice. Great lectures, great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hilarious, engaging lectures. Curved tests with the opportunity to make up test grades with homework, online tests.

Mr. King was a good professor. His lectures were very enjoyable. He gets involved. He does have readings he would like for you to read but you don't have to. His tests are also open note, open readings, and open internet. You can use anything but other people. His tests also aren't cumulative including his final exam. Overall, a really great guy.

His lectures r interesting, but class isn't mandatory. One important thing, HIS EXAMS AND HIS LECTURES HAVE A MUNITE CORRELATION. It's super annoying but it's not too bad. Every week you get 3 assignments: a 1 question survey, a 4 question quiz (usually on quizlet), and a discussion board. (and he'll give extra points for your final exam!) 
-PINKIE
Dr. King was very energetic and kept a fun vibe even though the lectures are like 500+ people. He's very helpful during office hours. All exams are multiple choice, and take home. Super great guy.
He's a chill dude and easy to work with. The test questions are sometimes hard to understand. His class is super laid-back and the concepts are fun to talk about.

This class definitely isn't super easy but i really enjoyed it! It you show up to class, learn the material and make sure you get enough homework points, all you really have to worry about is the tests. There's definitely a learning curve to get used to the study strategy but once you do it gets much better. Also USE OFFICE HOURS.

Exams are multiple choice and open notes but worded weird. He tests you on the 20+ page readings due every week instead of his lectures, but you still have to go since TopHat is a large part of the grade. His lectures are interesting and he is a nice and understanding guy but I think he overcomplicates things and I would recommend someone else
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice dude, bad exams. Most of your grade is taken up by TopHat questions (essentially your attendance grade), discussion boards, and his exams. The exams are only on class readings, and the questions are insanely confusing and unnecessarily complicated. The average score was always so low that he'd have to curve the grade for each test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Not too great. The notes he gives are by far some of the worst notes I have ever seen. The exams are open-note but the notes barely help. The exam questions are also phrased in a really weird way. One of the worst classes I've taken. He curves exam grades and is a nice guy...that's why I am giving a 2/5 instead of a 1/5. Take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor King is an amazing professor, his lectures are interesting and engaging. The readings are important because they are on tests and quizzes.

Neal King is the best professor at Virginia Tech. I highly enjoyed his class and recommend it. Extremely down to earth and funny guy. His test are open note and we love a good tophat question from neal. Ritual AF

His lectures are long but I have had much worse. He will ask the class plenty of questions to help involve everyone and that is helpful. He clearly states in the beginning that if you just study the lectures then you will fail the class, so read the material he assigns. The tests are hard to understand but they are open notes. They're still hard.
There was so much reading each week and the tests are only based on the readings. His lectures were fine but the tests have nothing to do with the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible. He lectures all class about sociology and I take notes all class but when it comes to the test nothing he lectured about was on the actual exam. NOTHING. Everything that's on the test is in the long and confusing reading. Questions on the test are also worded very poorly and hard to understand which makes the tests that much harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Neal for WGS 1824 for wintermester. Even though, the class was asynchronous, he is easily accessible outside as well to answer any questions. The work had a lot of reading for a 3 week term but was very managable. Overall, solid professor.

Professor King gives really great lectures. They always grab your attention and he can be funny. His lectures aren't what the tests are on, so definitely make sure you do the reading he assigns. For tests, he allows anything paper and ink. No textbook either, he posts free ones online to use. You can even print those out for the tests if you wanted

Great professor, he makes his lectures interesting, as long as you do the reading, go to class, you should pass. The tests are open text, so if you print the readings you can use them from the text. His exams are always going to be from the readings he gives you. He also uses top hat and gives other opportunities for points through the brief hws
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was asynchronous and consisted of four main tests with at least 30 pages of reading a week. However, this class was the easiest college class I've taken thus far. The tests are open note and the material is not overly difficult. If you actually read the assignments you will find Professor quite up to date and humorous.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was fine. I only met Prof. King once over Zoom (since my class was online asynchronous) and he was willing to help explain the concepts of the week's lesson. He assigns many articles each week. I never read them, but I probably would have done better if I had. This class seems super difficult at first, but you will get the hang of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was asynchronous and may have been better in person, but this was easily the worst class I've taken so far. There were at least 20 pages of reading due each week, along with weekly quizzes that were 2-4 questions, poorly worded, and didn't make up for the amount of reading that was assigned. Don't take this class unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class with Prof. King this year & ofc everything was online. It was an absolute nightmare. He just gives you a pdf with links to articles & then you take a 2 question quiz on the whole thing. I've not learned one thing from him directly. The exams are hard, & I thought it was just for me, but I've asked others & they feel the same.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was ok. There's a lot of reading and it is kind of a do at your own pace class. I have never talked to the professor before as my class was online asynchronous. Your grade is pretty much based off of four exams and a percentage of the homework quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Kings class and found myself always excited to go. Hes funny and makes lectures interesting. Make sure to print out everything you can for his tests because they are most of your grade but he does curve and is willing to help in anyway he can.

You just have a bunch of readings to do every class. Tests are open note and come straight from readings but are only 20 questions and theres rarely a curve. Cool guy though and an interesting class. Theres four tests and some online quizzes and questions for the weekends. Make sure you do the work to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was so difficult in the beginning, but once you get used to it, it gets so much better. His lectures are SO interesting and make sure you take good notes because it will probably show up on the final! Read the readings even if they're long and boring. He's also very generous so don't be scared to go to office hours, he'll help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor King makes this class more difficult than it should be. The tests are very difficult and his language/wording is hard to understand. Don't bother reading the readings he gives for each lecture- it will be a waste of time. Pay attention during class and use his study guides for tests. Take your own notes- his outlines are too confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very interesting class, his notes outlines are a little weird but once you get used to it you're fine. Honestly just go to class and try to think of real world examples for the concepts. Print out the readings for the exams and you'll get an A on all of them. He's a funny guy and gives you lots of opportunities to get points.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was one of the most difficult classes at first, then I realized most of the test answers are common sense. I got a 65&75 first exams(reading articles), then an 85 and 90 on the next two exams without. Do not put too much pressure on yourself to read the articles because if you just pay attention in class you can get the majority of info there
The readings he gives are very heavy and in depth
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: There's also something you guys should know about Dr. King - he is very kind and respectful if you meet him for office hours. He will hear you out! I was struggling with the tests so I asked him if I could write essays instead - he said yes. I got an A in the class! He's very intelligent, and understands if you are struggling in his course!

Professor King's lectures are incredible. He is so interesting and gives you the cold hard truth on a lot of tough topics. He's morbid, but I think it's funny. As for the class, the tests are very tough. You really need to pay attention in class and take good notes.

This class was hard. I expected a D, but then ended up with a B-. Print out the entire articles, especially if you do not read them. He'll ask word for word questions from the middle of the article. He is a fun and witty professor. He'll ask you before the first test what you want him to do, ask him for a study guide. He'll give you it.

Hard because you have long articles that you have to find a line in to get answer for test. Only exams and you get HW points for asking a question you submit online after class. Can get 3 extra credit points. Have to look over articles throughly to help on test. Open notes so just come prepared.

King is an awesome guy but is very smart and makes sure that is known. I feel like I need a dictionary just to understand what he's talking about. That being said, all of the tests in this class are open note but the questions are paragraph length. I suggest reading all of the assigned articles.

He is amazing! His notes could be a little hard to understand, but if you attend class every day, you'd understand him just fine. He hilarious, teaches well, tells you exactly what's on the test, very helpful and promises that if you visit his office hours, you will not fail. The class teaches you a lot about the world and changes your perception
do not take this class with him.
Worst teacher in the world. Condiscends to everyone and is soooo boring.

I took Social Theory with King and was immediately intimidated.  I went to office hours for help and he is very willing to help.  I learned more in this class than any other class at Virginia Tech.  Great Professor!

Dr. King is one of the best professors I've had in college. His lectures are extremely interesting and he really knows how to engage the students in the material. His tests are quite wordy and he uses quite an expansive vocabulary, so its not the easiest class in the world. Nevertheless, if you have a change to take him, I definitely recommend it!

So much reading and he tests on those. Everything is open book and open notes, but he makes the tests really hard. Attendance is kind of mandatory because he does clicker questions for points during lectures. Grades are scaled.

Dr. King assigns a LOT of reading, but it is never overwhelming. If you stay on top of your stuff from the beginning, you won't have any problems with his class. He is very helpful with papers, which will be most of your grade. His lectures are usually interesting and held my attention. If you go to class and ask questions you'll do well.
This guy expects you to have your stuff together.  He expects you to think, express your ideas, write (and write well)and be open-minded.  One of the best profs I ever had in college!
great teacher.  really teaches you how to think

This guy won't hold your hand. He expects you to know how to think, take notes and prioritize. I think he's a very good teacher who is intelligent,interesting and always prepared. Also, very easy on the eye. I love the long hair.

I thought his class was easy. Tests are open-book. You can bring whatever notes and readings you want to the tests. There's a lot of reading material.. I didn't read a lot of the readings and did well. (Sometimes I read the readings during the test) Oh, and he should cut his long, red hair.
King is very intelligent, but even more boring. He writes test questions that really don't reflect on the readings. If you take this class, don't bother studying because it won't help you.

Very boring subject taught by an equally boring professor. If you do not like to read, then I definitely wouldn't take his class. Readings are extremely long and often times it is difficult to stay focused during them. Tests are confusing and unclear, which results in a lot of low grades.
No Comments

Kim is by far the funniest woman I've taken a class with, which kept me concentrated on the lecture. The only negative thing I can say about her is that she sometimes ran past the allotted class time. The textbook is mandatory since tests are through it and are synced with Canvas.

Professor Kim is the sweetest lady! She sets up her class to be very easy but still makes it super fun and interesting! There was a weekly quiz that went along with the chapter readings, and there were two open-note exams throughout the semester. Overall, an easy A as long as you show up to the lectures and complete the assignments!

Dr. Kim is the sweetest person I have ever met. She puts in so much effort to learn everyones name and interests. She is so passionate about this field, and she is HILARIOUS which keeps class so entertaining. She isn't a harsh grader and her assignments/lectures aren't bad at all. I definitely recommend this class!

Dr. Kim so sweet and truly cares for her students and her field. Her humor kept me engaged during her lectures. The class is really straight forward, she never took attendance and there are assigned chapters each week and a reading quiz. Exams are open note, but are strictly timed. There is also an paper which wasn't terrible.
It was so interesting and very easy class. Minimal work outside of class.

If you are taking HD 1004, make sure you get Dr. Kim. As a CS major who took this for a Pathways requirement, I can say for certain that this was one of my favorite classes this semester. She was incredibly kind, her lectures were so funny, and she really cared about getting the material across to you.
Grades mostly quizzes from the online textbook. Open notes for quizzes and exams. Takes attendance.

Dr. Kim is very funny and knows how to lecture in a way that makes them engaging for her students. Her class is heavily based on the textbook and her lectures, which is what she bases her tests on. I took this class for a pathways course and I would recommend it to anyone whether their major is HD or they need it to fulfill a gen ed.

Dr. Kim is the most adorable professor you will ever have. She is so funny and enthusiastic and she truly made me laugh every class. She is definitely very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches and is so willing to help you. Definitely take her class, it will make your entire week.

Dr. Kim is honestly one of the sweetest people here at VT. Even though everything was online, she was always smiling and passionate about Human Development. The class itself was easy if you read the textbook but her lectures are also fun to attend. Id advise anyone to take this class, even if you arent involved with Human Development.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Kim is honestly my favorite prof ever. She cares so much about her student and her job. Her lectures are interesting and she likes to joke around. Uses PowerPoints. Phenomenal. Not too hard of a grader, tests are easy enough if you come to class and pay attention. Projects are really easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim is so cute!! She loves what she does and what she talks about which is what makes her lectures so memorable. I am an HD major and she has inspired me so much. She makes a lot of jokes at herself and tells funny stories about her life as well as gives good examples of the material.
My favorite class. Kim is so funny, caring and is very passionate about what she teaches. Every single lecture was very interesting and important!

Ok so I am going to be straight with you all. Most people who are taking this class are looking to major in HD. They probably took HD in high school and thats where all the "easy classA" comes from. If you are taking this class to fulfill an area, THINK AGAIN! Other HD classes are a lot easier but she teaches in a way where you need to be familiar

She's awesome! She is so friendly and excited every class. She has an accent, but i was still able to understand her well. She makes fun of herself for it too. Her tests aren't that hard, she allows the class before the test to be a review and it gives a good amount of help.
This class was fairly easy. Print out her notes, and fill in the blanks. The only down fall is that she takes attendance, and her asian accent can be difficult to understand at times.
she is SO NICE! one of my favorite professors.

Great teacher! She is so cute and always so excited to teach and come to class. I always looked forward to going to her lecture, and tests are not that bad. The workload is not a lot either. Best techer I have had here!
SUPER AMAZING! SUPER KIND! SUPER HELPFUL! TAKE THIS CLASS!

Extremely nice lady, always smiling and if you listen closely she says some hilarious stuff. Class is so much work and it's often hard to understand her when she is lecturing. Tests are hard, and you have to write a research paper with horrible instructions. She loves her students, just doesn't understand how hard she is.
interesting class. She is the sweetest teacher I have ever had and she can be funny at times. Class is really boring sometimes though, but over all not that bad.
The teacher is not bad. She is so nice, but the class was hard, even it is an introduction. The tests are so hard and you have to write papers for the class. Too much work, I would say...
a very interesting class, shes a good teacher but her tests are very hard. her paper was confusing and hard to write but overall the class wasnt bad.
wonderful person and a great professor.
Very knowledgeable and conveys info well

I took Ancient Greek Phil with Professor Klagge. He is an amazing lecturer and really knows his stuff. If you pay attention and take notes during the lecture the readings become clear. The tests draw from the readings which the lectures go over in great detail. Be aware the readings are hard and you must read to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Depends on what TA you get, but his lectures are awesome. They're basically a review of the reading material, I find that reading before the lectures, then hearing them clears up so much. They're to the point, and are informative. My TA was great, as long as you get on their good side, they'll help you and go easy on you. Go to recitations too.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Unhappy to see students when they are in office hours as well as giving rude answers when asked questions. Not enough assignments in class and the assignments we do have are worth astronomical amounts of points. TA was better than the professor

Klagge is a very nice guy and extremely flexible when it comes to extensions of papers and exams. However, powerpoint slides are extremely vague and hard to study off of, the exams are horrible because there's always one question worth 70 points, and he doesn't grade anything; the TA does. The TA grades super harshly and is not helpful at all.

I do not recommend taking this professor. He makes what should be a fun and introductory course to philosophy painful, dull, and unnecessarily hard. His exams are the worst; one out of left-field question can be worth up to 20-30% of your entire exam score. He does not have clear grading criteria. He allows his TA to grade on their own agenda.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His unclear grading style is frustrating. You will be graded only on two exams and two papers. His lectures are O.K., but studying for the exams are difficult with his style of powerpoint slides. He tends to ramble alot. He is BIG on participation credit but his lectures can be so unengaging that it can be hard to want to raise your hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Klagge isn't a bad professor and its clear he loves philosophy. I wouldn't say he's great but he's definitely not bad. It is clear he cares about his students. The main issue we had with him was how little communication he had with our TA. They had opposite grading scales/ teach styles made it confusing on how to judge what to and what not to study

Klagge is a decent lecturer and knows some basic intro philosophy well. If you are a grad student though, he will waste your time with pointless meetings. He gives unclear grading guidelines which could easily be typed up on his own time. He speaks down to people, but also expects to be shown respect... I would not recommend working with him

Overall, I liked Professor Klagge. I took PHIL 1204 and as long as you come to class, pay attention, take notes, and participate in your discussion group, you'll be fine (even if you aren't always able to do the reading). However, the real key to doing well is to show your TA you're putting in effort and they'll let that reflect in your grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really liked this class and Prof. Klagge -- the material can be boring but he makes his lectures enjoyable. You need to be at his lectures, he posts the powerpoints but they don't really give all the info. TA's grade everything, so your grade is sort of dependent on them but it's overall an easy class if you know the material
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good in class lectures--always starts with music and plays some funny videos! A lot of reading, and there isn't a Sparknotes summary on a lot of them so get ready to read. TA's vary--one is very good, other two are ehh. Be ready to participate in discussion or else you won't do well in that part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easy A if you do the work. TA's grade fairly and hold office hours to ensure your A. IF you spend a microcosm of time getting help, you get a free GPA boost.
Kooky old professor, he's quite fun. You've gotta go to his classes, though, to get any of the things that'll show up on the tests. Papers have to be very sound and well thought out. Don't try to BS!
He plays good vidoe clips during class and starts each class off with music
No Comments
Should be an easy class. However, TA's grade very very hard.

All lectures, but not with Powerpoints, he does practice problems on a chalkboard. Participation isn't mandatory, but you're screwed if you don't go because there is few resources he posts online. Take good, extensive notes because that's all you have to go off of for exams. Do the homework. TVM exam (first exam) can make or break your grade.

Klock gives good lectures but he thinks that when most people fail his exams it is because students aren't passionate enough. Realistically, the tests are asking students to solve problems that we aren't ready for.

Great professor. Yes he is one of the harder finance professors at VT, but that is because he teaches the most. Of all the professors I have had, he challenges the class the most and as a result gives you the greatest knowledge and benefit. A lot of people complain that he is too hard, but I think he just prepares you the most.

Professor Klock is the most interesting teacher. Some of his lectures like how to calculate personal housing loan and retirement money are very impressive and beneficial. Overall, he is worth taking if you truly are passionate about finance.The weekly quizz is timed and the 2 exams are arranged in the evening like 7 to 8:30 pm.

Derek is a bad professor and and even worse human being. He spent the semester ridiculing the class, telling us how much smarter he was than everyone else and how we all "suck at math." At least ten minutes of each class was spent degrading us and telling us how stupid we are.  This professor has some serious insecurity issues. Angry, abusive

Klock comes off as a very hard teacher but really REALLY cares about his students and you learning. You need to take notes in the lectures and pay attention because tests are hard. He makes you earn your grade but you will learn. Good excel projects that you work on with teams and some quizzes. Overall hard class and content, but great guy.

Klock is a great teacher! He cares about you as an individual and will go out of his way to help you. However, his class was the hardest class I?ve ever taken. You pour your heart and soul into this class and you still might not get the C you need. Kids literally have nervous breakdowns during his tests, you gotta convince yourself you can make it!

Great professor!  You will learn a lot from Derek Klock.  Tests are difficult but not impossible.  GO TO CLASS!!!  If you don't, you will be doomed to fail.   Don't be too thin skinned or easily "offended".  If so, take Dr. Cliff....  Would easily take another class from Klock.

Klock is an interesting professor. He comes off as harsh and difficult but he is willing to help with anything in office hours. The key is to stay up with homework and always come to class. not bad but an interesting guy
He is a great professor to have, makes class interesting, a lot better than Cliff for FIN 3134.

Klaus has a significant accent and is iffy on interpersonal skills, but he has great respect for his students. He treats us like equals and not kids. He realizes he doesn't know everything, accepts student input, and even encourages students to go online for homework help.  His office door is always open, although he's not great at one-on-one help.
Absolutely useless.  Couldn't understand a damn thing he was saying and I spent most of the semester clueless. I would not recommend taking his class.
very smart guys but cannot teach at all. strong physics background so every example on the board is about physics. don't recommend him at all.

Klaus is my man. He is a quantum physicist who, as the name implies, really knows his stuff. He is funny, nice, and was helpful when I went to his office hours. The negative side is that his research seems to engage him far more than class. The bright side, he isn't going to grade you hard

This guy knows math, he's just bad at keeping you awake.  My problem was I always fell asleep in class or just stared at the wall from boredom.  Teaches you a lot of useless theory.  Helpful during office hours.

Klaus is awesome! Knows his stuff! Teaches you theory in depth, but then would rather you perform simple applications on HW, quizzes, & Exams! Always willing to help during office hours, and welcomes all questions during lecture! He's the man!
good professor with clear mind and decent manner
This man IS math
A mathematical physicist. Knows his stuff cold.
From Switzerland. A little dry, but he knows his stuff.

Dr. Elgert is a very knowledgeable professor, however if you  go to his office hours for help he wont really answer any of your questions, but rather ask different ones that can make you even more confused. Show up to every class because his notes on scholar aren't very confusing and using the book isn't really helpful, the test are also very hard.
I learned more in Immunology than all my other Biology classes combined. Lot of work, but worth it.

Dr. Elgert obviously puts a lot of effort into teaching his material.  Lectures are great but very fast paced, tests are extremely hard, but he'll go out of his way to help you however possible (if you ask for it).  Read the book and attend all classes if you want that A!
Great class, hard professor.  If you survive the lecture, definitely take the lab!
Very hard, you have to know all the material including the detials, but worth it.
No Comments
great prof. knows his stuff...but a pretty difficult course
Great professor.  Tough class.
This was the worst teacher at VT!  Very uncaring and boring.

Class was Knowledge and Reality.  Does a great job of taking the obscure and hard to understand readings of Socrates, Plato etc. and putting them into realistic and modern context.  Only needed to skim the readings and really pay attention to his interpretations in class to do well with papers and tests.  Take his class he is funny

Class was in existentialism. Very bright guy. Knows what he is talking about. Great presence in classroom. No longer teaches at Tech, which is a complete shame because Tech certainly could have used a strong analytical mind like his to shake the heavily continental mindset which is, unfortunately, traditional of Tech students. What a total loss.

Klipfel is a really good professor. He's hilarious and keeps the material interesting. He has this New York image that is very sarcastic but he's really cool. The material is not easy to read on your own but he presents it so that you can understand it. I highly recommend the class.

Condescending and cynical, and it's fking hilarious. He says stuff that sounds really "WTF" out of context. He's really chill and funny. Grading policy is ok. We were supposed to have a paper due every week, but we've only done 4 out of 15... I suggest you do the reading, at least skim. He likes other outgoing people. Cusses a lot. Has a facebook.
I enjoyed this class and this professor is fantastic.

One of the best professors I've had at VT! Very understanding and flexible if you communicate what's going on. Group project heavy and you often work with your group in class, but class is super engaging and goes by fast. 2 exams with extremely helpful study guides! He is truly rooting for your success and is a huge resource!
Great professor, couldn't recommend more.

Prof. Slagel makes students feel individually valued and cared for. Attendance is mandatory, accounting for ~25% of your grade, which can get annoying as classes can feel repetitive. Slagel seldom lectured, and if he did lectures are somewhat engaging and interesting.
amazing proffesor

Professor Slagel was an AMAZING professor and teacher. He taught our class so many real-world examples of textbook content and connected his real-world experiences to the class itself. He was a very approachable person and was very kind to all. Recommended for sure.
Great guy. Very down to earth, clearly cares about his students. His half of the classes for Innovate were the best.

While I didn't enjoy 1064 very much, Professor Slagel was a bright point in the class. Professor Slagel clearly cares a lot about students' wellbeing. I appreciated his gratitude sessions at the start of the classes he lectured.
One of the best proffesors I've ever had, Definitely someone to look up to, always reminding us to be greatful and have a good mindset.

Professor Slagel is awesome! As the co-teacher of my Innovate class, he was very involved and wanted students to succeed. He went out of his way to set-up networking opportunities with students and industry professionals outside of class time. He is interesting to listen to and will often let class out early. Great guy, would 100% recommend!
Pretty chill and relaxed teacher, isn't too formal or heavy on lecture or content. Homework was easy and class was straightforward. A lot of extra credit opportunities too.
Best teacher i've had so far at VT.

One of my favorite professors I've had at Virginia Tech! Super down to earth guy and he is very flexible with assignment due dates. No exams just quizzes. Super easy class and I would recommend even if you aren't a business major. (Class is Foundations of Entrepreneurship)

She's a very caring professor who genuinely seems interested in what she's teaching, but the classes are just lectures are so boring and heavy and student presentations take forever making class feel super long. The course has a VERY high volume of assignments and 90% of the grades weren't in until the week before the semester ends even with a TA.

Dr Choi was a reason I added additional HD classes to my schedule. While her classes can be rough at times with so much information, she is clear and her lectures are helpful.  Her grading is clear and extra credit is offered.  It is important to stay on top of the readings.  Attendance is taken and part of your grade.  open book/notes exams online
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She taught a lot from the textbook, but you needed to attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course/Grading Guidelines are extremely clear-cut from the beginning. Every class is the exact same: a lecture using Tophat (and yes, you have to buy it) with group presentations occurring about halfway through the semester. Two semester long projects (essays), which can really be finished in about an hour. Only tests are final/midterm, both easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures pretty quickly and is well aware of the material, every class is basically the same. One group presentation that lasts the whole year but takes like 5 minutes to complete. Tests are open note and easy and two projects are very easy as well. Attendance on tophat so can't skip everyday. Easy class to pass overall.

all the material she lectured in class was very accessible online and pretty much everything you need is in the online textbook. you do need the textbook bc homework is the quizzes that are in the textbook but their pretty simple and the due dates are weekly so you can do it on your own time. there's a group project and two papers but they're easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class itself wasn't hard at all, the professor just talks extremely fast, so it makes it hard to keep up when she's lecturing. She bases her attendance off of TopHat, and a textbook is mandatory to complete the REVEL quizzes that she assigns.

She was a good intro to HD professor. She had a lot of simple notes and the concepts were very clear and easy to understand. She did often move extremely quickly through the notes so I sometimes had to play catch up. She uses tophat for attendance purposes which is fine, though you must subscribe to for like 40$ I think.

This class was definitely an easy A, but if you don't like sitting down in class and taking notes every single second and just reading for homework, then this class might not be for you. The material was very interesting and the professor gave great feedback on assignments, but as the semester goes on you'll find it hard to make it to that class.

The class contained an overwhelming amount of notes. The class itself was easy in terms of grading. I just did not like the style of the class because I did not stop writing for the entire hour and fifteen minutes. It is an easy grade though.

I took this class asynchronously. Essentially, we had to read the textbook, take a quiz, and do a writing assignment every week. The instructions for every assignment was always very clear, and the content was interesting. There were no tests, just a midterm/final (open book) which carry most of the weight for your final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was okay. There's a lot of activities/graded work, so you have the chance to bring your grade up. Lots of in-class quizzes that are based from the textbook very specifically, so you definitely have to read. Grading criteria was not always clear, and she didn't allot enough time at the end of class for in-class activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I dropped the class because of her attitude; she is so rude and judgmental. She brought up someone's work in class just to degrade them, not actually give feedback. She insulted me personally for not agreeing with her. I felt bad for the other prof who she steamrolled the whole time, and the other students who were forced to stay for credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Out of a class of 7, 4 students dropped the class simply because of her attitude. She comes off as incredibly rude and judgmental--in discussion, she nitpicks rather than attempting to genuinely understand students and adds unprofessional asides. Her feedback is incredibly unbecoming of a prof. Her catchphrase should be "my way or the Autobahn."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not let the poor reviews scare you. She can be harsh but, if you come to class and read the texts it's not difficult.

I was so scared for this class after reading the reviews but genuinely Dr. Koch is one of the nicest people! Very clear and reasonable with her expectations and I think a big reason she isn't liked is just because she isn't scared to bring up controversial issues when they're applicable to the content and won't let you get away with sitting quietly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The way she communicated with her students was rude and unprofessional. She mocked students for turning in something the wrong way or making a simple mistake, and often made fun of these students to the rest of the class. Her general demeanor was unfriendly, and she did not make students feel comfortable speaking up or simply being in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ill be completely honest. She is a tough professor. I saw these reviews before I took the class and I was very nervous. Im not a good student at all, but I realized that she really is a great professor. She does care about her students, if you try your best and speak your opinion with credibility then she will love you. (Tip- she loves contrarians)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I did all I could to be successful and failed. I tried to get help from the professor, got a tutor, which I have never had to do. I had classmates peer-review my assignments when I started really worrying and they all said my work was perfect. Professor gave me 0's  on exams and basically called me dumb in her feedback. Would never take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: These other reviews are stupid dramatic. She would rather have good discussion than you take notes throughout class. If you're friendly with her then she is more than open to changing the class structure. For example, she let us decide between writing a research paper or answering essay questions for the final. Y'all can chill.

Dr. Koch's class should be taken with great caution. Her lectures don't help with the midterm or the final. She is hostile to any opinion that doesn't agree with hers, and her feedback on papers is useless as you cannot read her handwriting. I would rather go back to Afghanistan and fight the Taliban again than retake her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bettina used Prezi in class and refused to put her slides on Canvas to study later (I asked her for access to them and she told me to pay closer attention in class). She also was not a good teacher, and rarely made lecture interesting. Her tests were so hard, to the point where she gave up on anyone getting over a C- so she made the final an essay
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: I would recommend avoiding her as a professor. She did make the option to attend class in person and on zoom which was nice. She was generally disrespectful in her feedback on assignments and in class, which discouraged people from answering questions. Felt kinda bad for the TA who she called the wrong name for the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is very sweet however it is very difficult to understand her due to her thick accent. I know that's not her fault but it makes understanding the slides and lectures very difficult. But she's funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She talks down to students and does doesn't present the material in a helpful manner at all. She has lectures that have little to nothing to do with what you are tested on, and she expects you to get the rest of your information from the textbook, where she pulls most of her test questions from. Won't not answer questions or get off her high horse.

Dr. Knapp is a very sweet woman and is clearly crazy about what she's teaching. She also gives wonderful feedback on papers and is very thorough with it. My sole gripe has been confusion over rubric requirements, as well as sometimes distracted and meandering lectures. Still - she knows what she's talking about!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Lit & the Law. Professor Knapp is nice and gives good feedback on your work. The works you read are interesting but class itself is boring, which is why it was hard for me to show up all the time. She gives a lot of feedback on papers which is good and you can tell she cares about her students. Not a hard class at all
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Knapp is honestly great! She is eccentric but she's super nice. I took Literature and Cinema with her and there was a TON of reading (a full novel every week). In the place of tests we had to write papers so be ready for a lot of papers. But she's an easy grader and even papers I didn't feel confident on I'd get full credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Literature and law ENGL 3684, easiest class I've taken. She's weird and rambles on for 50 minutes about nothing. As long as you do one of the readings so you can answer the stupid easy 5 questions every month you'll be fine. Two 1500 word papers, one exam, a few 5 question completion grade homeworks, no attendance, ridiculously easy

Her class was pretty easy. New short fiction reading due before every class (sometimes two classes if longer) and every week you answer a few prompts on one of the stories you read. Exams are also questions on all readings you've done up until that point. Very caring, eccentric, and gives good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Knapp is extremely kind and she has adjusted well to online classes. There is a solid amount of reading required but that's expected for a 4000 level English class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. Very vague and weird. Quizzes are only 10 questions, not good. Forget contacting her outside of class, as she will give you the runaround back to the syllabus. Crams in so many books and short stories into one semester, many of which are long and boring. I took this as my fun class and I immensely regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've had this professor for four different classes and she is amazing. She's smart, nice and actually cares about how you are doing. She is open to creative stuff in her projects and is a fair grader as long as you do the reading. I recommend her classes to everyone, they are fun. She is dedicated and knows everything about what she teaches.

Professor Knapp is a nice, but strange professor, offering makeup exams and review sessions. However, the amount of reading you have to do for "short stories" is incredible. For a class that I went to maybe once a week , the outside work took up more of my time than other classes. The classes are incredibly boring and attendance rates are low.

"Coach" Knapp is...weird. She is helpful and very enthusiastic, but there's something just weird about her. She is an understanding and insightful professor, but I am avoiding her other classes that I might consider taking if another professor taught them. I wouldn't deter anyone from taking her course, just be prepared for her awkwardness.

Going to class would be pointless if there were not random reading quizzes, since her lectures only focus on the plots of the short stories.  This is a bit frustrating as an English major.  Otherwise, she's a bit batty, but that makes her interesting.  Though it's too bad her class wasn't as interesting as she appears.  However, it is an easy A.

Coach Knapp is insightful and intelligent. I took her class to fulfill area 2 and thought I could get an easy A.  Wrong.  I read ALL the stories, and only missed 2-3 classes, and the classes I did miss I got the notes from someone else.  My avg on the quizzes was 100 but the exams were extremely vague and difficult.  I would avoid her at all costs.
Very interesting lectures, genuinely don't need to study because of how interesting the class is. You do have to write a decent amount for the discussions but besides that he's a great professor.
He is the best! Super easy class but you should go to class because that is like one of the only grades you receive is in class assignments.

This class does have its fair share of reading but don't stress yourself out over the writing too much, it doesn't have to be that great. The exams are fairly easy if you take detailed notes during lectures. Be sure to show up for review days!!! Sit near someone you'll be comfortable talking to every class, that tends to be part of the activities.

Uses a physical attendance sheet or tophat for attendance but I missed about 5 classes and was perfectly fine. Does random ARQ's at the end of class. Very writing heavy but pretty easy readings from one interesting book and lots of interesting movies. I spent probably an hour writing for this class a week.

Dr. K is truly a gem Virginia Tech should be grateful to have! I have taken him three times and am always blown away by his ability to connect with his students and give voice to socially and culturally overlooked and undervalued populations.

There are ARQ's for attendance, and there is a group project, but it was really easy and we did all of the work in class. There are a lot of homework assignments, including recording yourself practicing the Mind-Body practices.
Overall, the class was easy and he lets you turn in late work, you just have to email the TA.

I would 100% say take his course if you're an HD major. It is easy and interesting, despite it being an 8am. Make sure you show up to class because sometimes he give in class assignments that you can only complete if you are in class. His exams are easy an open note as well. There is a textbook, but as long as you attend lectures, you don't need it
An amazing professor. I am taking more classes with him in the future and highly recommend if you want a professor who truly cares about their students.

Dr. K was such a great professor. You can tell he's very passionate about what he talks about. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but he did have occasional in class assignments. The exams are open book, open note. Come to class and you'll get an A.

This class was super easy, and attendance wasn't mandatory, but he did In-Class assignments that would affect your grade. He recommends a textbook, but I never used it and still passed the class with a decent grade. The class can be a bit boring at times, but it's an easy class and I would definitely take it again.

Very nice and interesting professor. Is passionate about what he teaches and makes it interesting. Grade is mostly quizzes- which are open notes and textbook heavy. Service project is also huge part of grade. Attendance checks randomly- can hurt your grade.
The class is easy and pretty interesting, I also had Dr. K for 2335 and in both classes he was extremely passionate about what he was teaching.

Dr. K is the greatest professor at this school. He has great notes and is so passionate when he's lecturing the class. He is very compassionate and gives his students a lot of empathy if there are extenuating circumstances. Extremely approachable and just an overall very kind dude. I want to take every single class he offers.

I've never had a teacher who cares so much about his students. He truly is amazing and has some very influential lectures throughout the semester. Assignments are pretty easy and so are the meditation practices. Only 2 tests for the semester that are relatively easy. This class is super fun and engaging even though I had to wake up for the 8am.

Assignments were easy and exams are open-book and open-note. The class has a service-learning project that you have to commit to (16-20hrs total in the semester, 2 hrs a week), so it is a commitment. Unless you have to take this class for your major, I wouldn't take it. The subjects mentioned in lectures were important but really common sense.

Dr. K's capstone section is project based and team oriented. While the material can be a little difficult at times, his assignments are easy to understand and graded fairly! He really cares about his students and is always very encouraging. Would definitely recommending taking any of the courses he teaches!

Dr. K loves his students so much and wants to see you succeed. There are readings each week, but they aren't required or really necessary to do well in the class. He offers several extra credit opportunities and will give you an A on everything if you put in some effort!

Two open note tests that are based around the readings and lectures. Recommend reading the text for the tests. 8am lecture sucks but he has in class activities that'll hurt your grade if you don't show. There is a service learning component as part of the class, but hours from my job covered that! He tries to make it engaging /interesting!
I took this class online, and it was an easy A as long as you do all of the readings. Everything was open note. He answered emails very quickly to clear anything you were confused on up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor! You can tell he truly cares about the human service field. You will have to do service learning at a site on your own time (up to 16 hours). Be prepared to add that into you weekly schedule. Quizlet is your friend :) GO TO CLASS! I know it's early, but there is an in-class assignment almost every day. Notes are great for those.

Dr. Komelski is one of my favorite professors. He's extremely caring for his students & is always happy to answer questions. He's really passionate about the subject so his lectures are interesting & fun. He randomly gives small writing assignments at the end of class. There are only 2 (easy, open note) tests (midterm & final). There's 1 easy essay
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: He is one of my favorite professors. He cares a lot about his students and loves answering questions. He plays videos a lot and his class has been an easy A.

Professor Komelski is super passionate about the subject, so it's really enjoyable to hear his lectures. Also, he's caring about his students and always wants to help his students no matter what. It's nice to have a professor who cares so much about his students. The material itself is kind of dry but his class makes it all worth it!

He is a great teacher. He cares a lot about human development and the success of his students. I recommend him as a professor and I recommend human development as a class if you like psychology and children.

Class is very easy. Notes taken straight from book. Exams are open book, online, timed, but more than enough time is given. Professor is very helpful and often extends due dates to accommodate students. Two papers, four exams, and several in class assignments that are given randomly, but allowed to drop two. You want this professor, trust me!

Very easy and enjoyable class. Professor is laid back, interesting, and really just loves teaching. Exams are online, only 20 questions, with generous time limits. In class assignments are given unannounced, but allowed to drop two of the assignment grades. Class notes are taken straight from book, so just highlight book rather than writing.

This is the easiest class you could ever take, it might as well be online!  You have 1 page (double spaced) papers due by Saturday at midnight and 20 question open note quizzes every other week (these are online too).  The only time you have to go to class is when he has assignments, but he tells you about these ahead of time.
Incredibly stringent, if I had the choice I wouldn't take any course with her again

Very unclear about what she wants for each assignment.  A lot of time is spent interpreting what she wants us to do, which can be very frustrating. This might be intentional to teach us about problem solving or something like that but it seems like she is just inarticulate and vague.
Overall, she is a good professor who explains material fairly well.  I think it is simply the way introductory engineering class are run such that the homework assignments are graded so stringently.
super helpful, great one on one. Is willing to work with you at any level. She is good and leading you to the answer without giving it away, which really helped me learn the material.

Where do I start, if your idea of a good teacher is someone who throws together long boring power points, acts like she is above teaching a freshman engineering course and is picky (which is an understatement) about grades then shes for you. Even her TA's complain about her behind her back. And who gave her a hot rating? You sir have low standards.
She is the most boring person I have ever met.She always assume students to know what she knows. thats not KOOOOOOL at all.
She is very unclear about asignments and projects.  She is a very picky grader.  If you have a question she responds but only in the form of a question.  take york if you can
She is fair and always willing to help, however she is a hard and picky grader.

If you dont dot your i correctly, Tamara will knock off points. She's not cool. She's a nice lady, but waaaay too by the book. She works incredibly hard for the class, and you can tell that she loves all her students, but she'll take off points where you might have had a different opinion.
Shes a nice lady but everything has to be done exactly her way, she is very unflexible, i disliked this class.
I like her, it's okay as far as these ENGE classes go.

Took this class for a pathway, was way more work than I expected. Lots of reading required to get a good grade. She is very passionate about the subject, however there are far easier courses if you are just after the pathway credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very passionate and knowledgeable about the course. Make sure to attend class since attendance is very important to the final grade but the lectures are very interesting so it's easy to pay attention. Most of the grade is made up of tests so the lectures and readings are important to pay attention to. Also very easy to contact and understanding.

We didn't get any extra credit opportunities for Summer 2024; however, she still drops lowest quiz grade, and the final exam is mostly an essay if you prefer essays over tough multiple choice assessments (aka: her quizzes). Her 10 question quizzes were painfully hard, but I pulled a solid A in this tough class by doing the discussion board posts.

The online class for Survey of Western History Art was too difficult for an introductory art course. Prepare to be watching 2 1/2 hour slow videos on YouTube of Professor Knoblauch speaking and then taking a quiz every week and a test every 3 weeks as your only grades. Extra credit is offered but not much.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Solid professor. You'll learn a lot in this class and as long as you pay attention and take notes during lectures, you should do fine. Sometimes lectures could get a little dull but otherwise this class is a good Pathways option

I enjoyed this class and the way she taught - it's your standard history class. It's easy to fall asleep in her classes. I gave her a low-ish rating because her tests determine your grade, and they're a lot of things to remember and keep up with. She's a nice person, but she made her class more difficult than it needed to be.

Dr. Knoblauch is very insightful and clearly knows her stuff. The tests are not super difficult as long as you show up to her lectures and take good notes. She does provide extra credit opportunities where you write a one-page paper, but can be graded a bit harshly. Overall, it's a great class if you're into art history. Highly recommend taking.

This class wasn't bad. Prof. Knoblauch takes attendance thru tophat & knows the material well. If you take notes during her lectures you'll learn the info. This was a month long study abroad course in Greece-everyone loved it! AMK is one of the best professors at Tech. She really cares about students and likes to get to know them personally.  She knows the subject matter like the back of her hand so it's really interesting. Take a class from AMK, you'll learn a lot. Also fun to invite to weddings.

shes amazing, she made me want to go into art history

No Comments
Reminds me of a female Indiana Jones in some ways...She knows her stuff...excelent teacher!

So attendance wasn't mandatory unless it was the day before fall break and thanksgiving break (when students want to go home early). Her teaching in Diseases was amazing. It has some difficult concepts, but for the most part there is a  moment where everything makes sense. Overall, I would recommend you take at least one course with her!

This class was great super informative and I really enjoyed her lecture style. She allows exam wrappers which are very helpful. Overall if you study its a great class and the professor knows what shes talking about. However BE prepared for the the the final. I could not stand her, the one time I tried to approach her about something after class she responded so rudely I was never motivated to ask her a question ever again. reviews.comment: Dr. P is awesome, compared to other professors in the same field/department, her class was much easier while still learning the same amount of content. Neuro will always be hard to get at first, but as long as you really listen in lecture and study, you'll be perfectly fine.

I really enjoyed the content of her classes. I took 3 of her classes. I retrospectively regret taking so many classes with her as she chooses clear favorites. If you are not one of her favorites try to get exposed to other faculty that are more reliable to assist your personal journey.

I have had Dr. Phillips for multiple courses and she is great every time. She is very clear on her expectations and cares about learning beyond memorization. Neuroscience and society is a very interesting course as well since it's applying neuroscience to topics like law, mental health, etc.

You get extra credit for attending class, exam corrections in which you can get back 50% of points lost, the biology/neuro class you will ever take in college. Just go to class and pay attention to lecture.

Professor Phillips is brilliant and the course is interesting and engaging. This is definitely my favorite neuroscience course I've taken. Take this class!

Dr. Phillips is amazing!! she really wants her students to succeed as well as get to know her students. She has time where you can go to her office and just get to know her. Exams are cumulative but she tells you what to review from past units for the exam. Attendance is not necessarily mandatory but she gives extra credit for attendance. Love her!

Extremely smart and knows the material very well. She really does a good job of trying to help you understand what's happening in the lecture and is very personable. Very likable and lectures can be a bit boring but she does a good job of keeping you engaged.

Dr. Phillips is awesome. She's an amazing professor and you can tell she is extremely intelligent and cares that everyone can gain something out of her class. There is a good amount of writing, but nothing awful. One of my favorite classes and professors and I recommend this class to anyone who can get it.

Definitely the most interesting class I have ever taken. Dr. Phillips covered so many interesting topics involving neuroscience that were easy to understand for non-majors. Lectures were not posted so you have to go to class but assignments were easy. I recommend this class to EVERYONE!!!
