I would say he's nice... but every class lecture I dreaded going to. One homework due a week, sometimes the in class examples match but most of the times I was on my own. Talks fast the entire block and no interactiveness to stay engaged. He gives no materials for review for exams and only has one office hour at 9am for questions/no TAs.
This guy is not at all a good teacher. He makes errors and does not explain anything well. He has little to no knowledge of how to use any technology. Not sure how he still has a job here.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No slides, nothing posted on Canvas, doesn't answer emails. Doesn't know what the homework we're doing is about. Reuses other study guides from the internet. He does the bare minimum he has to do to be considered a professor. You basically have to learn physics yourself in this class. In my opinion, it's not actually that hard if you teach yourself
If you want to genuinely learn physics don't take his class, can genuinely say in my 4 years at VT he was the worst professor I've had to date

-Doesn't reply to emails 
 -Cancels most of his office hours
 -refuses to do a problem fully with the algebra, if asked he'll say algebra is a prerequisite instead of explaining 
- doesn't understand the homework software, nor does he care to learn
-forgot to schedule us for a final, replaced it with a 3rd exam which we got 1 weeks warning

awful.

The only resources that this guy gives for exams is a flashdrive uploaded on canvas from 2005. Half of the answers don't even look right. No slides, just freestyles everything on paper in class. Nice and funny guy, but he is burnt out of academia 100% though.
cool guy, not great at explaining things, few resources and little to no office hours, great curves on tests so you will probably get a good grade but you won't learn much

Take anyone but him. Lectures are incredibly difficult to follow and difficult to understand. The exams are nothing like his lectures, pretty similar to the homework. No room to write in the lecture halls, and during the final we literally didn't have a surface to write on. Only nice thing is the homework is 30% of the grade and incredibly easy.
NO

Kriton was a very funny teacher, however, the material is pretty hard. He gives you one sheet of paper to write anything you want on there for each test, which is very helpful. If you study and write the formulas down, you can do well. He does curve a lot on each test, however, many students take advantage of how chill he is and ruin the curve.

I did not enjoy his teaching style. While it seemed like he explained everything clearly, when it came time for examples, he goes through with no real numbers and ends up making the homework confusing. Had to resort to learning a lot of it on my own for homework and exams. He curves exams so.

If you have questions, you better ask them in class, because he will not answer your emails, even if the email reads "IMPORTANT READ". He will tell you to email him too, just don't. He will always grade on a curve. He fails to make a coherent sentence. Try and take another professor for your GPA. The homework rarely show up on the exam.

Oh K. Granted this class is just for physics majors, but it's pretty easy. K just goes through the lectures, is very good at answering questions, and is a bit clueless as to what's going on administratively. Exams are easy, we got an optional final, and he likes to have a good time. He cares and tries to make his lectures captivating

K is a funny smart man, but his teaching style is a little off. He just comes in and starts writing stuff down. He does do some homework problem examples, and is willing to answer any questions, though, so he wasn't that bad. If you have a question, though, ASK IN CLASS, his office hours are not great.

He is kind of funny but cannot teach. He shows up with a pencil and paper then just goes on. The lectures barely help on homeworks and the tests are not really like the homework or lectures. He does not really like explaining further and doesn't like contact outside of class. Sadly I have to take him again because he is the only professor for 2206.

Kriton is a funny guy. Unfortunately, that sums up his good qualities. Lecture and homework materials don't translate to the tests as the tests are somehow different. It's not hard to pass bc of the MASSIVE curve on the exams, but it's tough to get an A and understand the material. It's unfortunate bc he is the only professor for algebra physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are not good. When asking him a question, he is helpful but takes a long time to answer your question. He should answer questions more directly and explain the material more practically. However, he is a friendly professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice person, but not a good teacher. I did better on the second exam when I only went to one of the lectures than I did on the first exam when I went to every lecture. Get ready to teach it to yourself. The only things that saved my grade were the formula/cheat sheet you're allowed during exams & the homework being 30% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The curve is rly big because everyone fails everything. It sucks because he's literally one of the only options. His teaching style is very unique and you either love it or hate it. I hate it. Good luck

Taught myself all the material. He doesn't cover material clearly because he doesn't understand it himself. When anyone asks a question, he rambles but never actually answers it. The cheat sheet you're allowed to have on the test is the only thing that saved me... and the 25% curve he has to put on tests to make it look like he's a good teacher.

So confused. Absolutely nothing on canvas to help you with, except practice exams. Cannot comprehend anything in class so I did not go at all. Studied a lot for the 1st exam and then I did not study for the 2nd (except formulas) and then got the same grade for both... do the homework and that'll probably save you.

The lectures are extremely hard to follow. The material discussed in class is not the same as the tests. The grades are so low on the tests that he has to apply 70% curves in order to keep the average looking decent for the university. Absolutely do not take unless it is necessary.

Papavasiliou is not a bad guy, he's funny and makes jokes during his lectures. However, he is not a good teacher. His lectures make no sense and his homework does not look like the tests at all. I got C's on all of his tests, and the only reason I got a B- in his class was that homework is worth 30% of your grade. Do the homework and you'll pass.
bad experience all around. lectures left me more confused than I was. Take this class with literally anyone else.

He was rude and arrogant towards students with questions. He has no interest in whether you succeed or not. There is no feedback throughout the year, the grading seems arbitrary and he does not release answers so you can never see what you got wrong to improve. He demands that you not email him so he's basically unapproachable and unreachable.

Very consistent homework in this class on Wiley plus. Lectures are so boring & hard to follow. He gives example problems in class but refuses to use actual values & work out the problem to completion because this isnt an algebra class This makes it very hard to understand. Get to bring a notes sheet to exams but unhelpful if you dont understand

Kriton does not teach effectively at all. Has been corrected SEVERAL times in class by someone I am close with. No clarity in lecture and then refuses to use examples with numbers. Be prepared to teach yourself, and even then hope the stuff you studied lines up on the test, and that he adds a huge curve like he usually does.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is the most unhelpful class I have ever taken. Kriton's teaching does nothing. The homework, his lectures, and the actual test don't line up. Only things I remember are choose a coordinate system and draw a free body diagram. Spent a class talking about an experiment involving shooting a monkey. Don't know how that's physics related.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I could write a 10 page essay on why you shouldn't take "Cretin". His lectures are repetitive and lack detail, he doesn't even know what is going to be on his tests since he doesn't write them, rarely uses actual numbers in his examples, his practice tests do not reflect test material, and is as unhelpful in office hours as he is through email.

Worst teacher I have ever had. Students give him feedback on what they think would be helpful in the course and he tells the students theyre wrong. He barely looks at his emails. I had a question about one of my grades and he told me I was wrong and then stopped responding to my email even though the grade WAS wrong. Least considerate teacher ever

Kriton is literally the worst teacher I have ever had. The lectures are very confusing, and they don't line up with the exams. He doesn't make his own test or homework, so you will have no idea what kind of questions will be on the exams. He doesn't have a TA and there are at least 300 students, so you need to get help somewhere else.

I am usually an A student. If I don't understand class material it is because of my own doing. However, in this class, I am constantly confused. Kriton loves physics, but is the worst at teaching it. He is not considerate, and does not care about your grade. 70% of your grade is from tests. I understood his lectures, and then his tests were so hard
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to take a different physics professor for an intro course, do it. He's not a good professor for ppl that haven't seen physics before. There are only 2 exams and 1 final. He curves intensely, but the hw doesn't match the exam. I learned better by skipping his classes and reading the textbook/khan academy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful teacher. I'm sure he's a nice guy but oh my god. He literally did lectures on a piece of paper with a camera pointing at it. I cannot stress how little I learned in this class. I literally don't know anything about physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: INever gotten a B before I took this class. He is a nice guy, but does not prepare you well enough for the exams. Any other professor would be better if you want a good grade without having to teach yourself everything.

He only goes by Kriton i don't even know his last name. This man is stuck in 2008 and so is his course material, he lectures by writing in pen on printer paper and is incredibly scatterbrained. The exams have little to do with any textbook material so study hard but probably won't help much. exams are curved but still frustrating. i hate this class

He is comical at times and insists that he does not want to test us. However, his lectures are all over the place and hard to follow. He does not use numbers in examples in class which is not helpful. Homework can be found online, but the tests do not reflect homework. You are allowed to have one sheet of notes for test and he curves tests.
Kriton is better than most of the other physics professors, so he is honestly your best choice even though he still isn't the best.

Homework and final is 30% of the grade and test make the rest. Which is fine, however, the class was not good. about halfway through the semester I started studying on my own because his lectures didn't make any sense. They were all over the place. He also didn't use any technology so he wrote on a dirty chalkboard with about 150+ students.

Homeworks are online (answers can be found on Chegg), and most of his exam problems came from the homework problems. Lets you have a front/back formula sheet for the exams, which are multiple choice. Dresses like a 90s dad, and lectures didn't have many interactive elements. Gives iClicker questions that are worth 1 point each on your overall grade
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Teaching is not his calling.But he is willing to help.Homework is 30% of grade but he will do them in class if you ask.Extra credit is added at the end as PERCENTAGE points!!(up to 5%).The material is very hard,but he curves every test.Also,he replaces your lowest test score with your highest, which is awesome.
SOO helpful! The material can be very hard,but Kriton is so nice and willing to help that it makes physics manageable. Definitely recommend him- couldn't have asked for a better phys teacher.

He's such a good professor! I took physics in high school and hated it bc my teacher was horrible. Kriton is a great professor and he really wants to help. the online hw isnt too bad, but the exams are only like 15 question so if you get one wrong it def effects your grade

I don't really like physics, but Kriton made it manageable.  The online homework was harder than his exams were, but he will go over it in class or during office hours if you ask.  I thought the exams were very fair.  Most of the problems were not too involved, and he gave about 5 or 6 extra credit points for the semester, which helps a lot.

I'm someone who hates public speaking. This class was probably the best class you can get to fill the requirement! Attendance mandatory, only about half of the semester though. Prof is nice and passionate. About 5 speeches total, takes practice to do well.

She was a TA for the COMM program, but was great and super nice! She got straight to the point of each speech concept and gave feedback in a genuinely nice way. Class itself was tedious. This is not the type of class to miss attendance! 5 speeches in total, including 1 group speech. Practice is crucial to giving speeches. Department is same for all

This was her first semester teaching as a GTA, but it went fantastic! This class could've been a forgettable, easy A, and while it wasn't difficult to get a good grade if you tried, Kuhl pushes you to legitimately get better at public speaking without being a stickler. Best teacher for this class!
Sweetest professor, offers very inciteful advice due to being a native japanese speaker.

I have seen many people not get good grades in this course since they did not put in much time outside of class. Do Not make that mistake. Also, speaking with one of my friends in mind, please do not try to get the Japanese minor/take classes if you do not find it interesting or are not doing well in the classes.

I got an A but that's because I have been learning Japanese for 4 years already. You have to put in quite a bit of time outside of class to practice, and there is not a lot of speaking practice in class. Kumazawa sensei will answer any question you have though, which is nice. Just make sure you put in a good amount of time outside of class.

Kumazawa Sensei is a good instructor who will answer any questions you have during the lecture. Attendance is graded quite heavily in this class so make sure to come. You have to get the Genki Japanese workbook and textbook (can't really use PDF but I've seen some get away with it before).

Let me start out by saying only take a Japanese Class at VT unless you are 100% sure that you want to take it. Don't take it just because you took it in high school and it was fun there. The scene here is completely different. Only take this if it is a requirement or you are 10000% sure you want the Japanese minor/want to learn.
He has severe issues in organization, effective communication, and can be very temperamental.

I've had Dr. K for a couple classes now. He is a good professor and knows his stuff. His classes are disorganized, however if you attend class and know what is going on, it's an easy A. Be careful as there are a lot of attendance quizzes that involved the topic that day in class. Points will add up if you miss.

I had engineering economy with Dr. K and it was probably the least I have learned from a class since elementary school. If you show up to class you can get an A or A- but it was just a genuine waste of time, he just used excel for everything and failed to explain anything clearly. Its a fairly easy A but if you actually want to learn stay away!

Dr. K is one of the most incompetent professors I've ever taken, both academically and technologically. I walked away having learned nothing from this course. Exams and homework are often nothing like lectures, and his answer is to watch YT videos on it. The midterms are online and usually only 3-4 questions so if you miss one you're cooked. AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i have had this man for like 5 classes now so the course code/grade prob isnt accurate. he's not a great teacher, but if you are nice to him he's pretty understanding. His classes are usually easy A's if you go to class and pay attention, and he usually drops at least one exam or homework depending on class feedback.
MY FAVE

Kwamba gets loaded up on benzos, shticks, and any other pharmaceutical he can get his hands on before class. He then gets in front of the class and tells silly stories about his daughter stealing his BMW and firehouse subs being the best sandwich in town. Kwamba will then fiddle around in some excel sheet and ramble while he comes down. 10/10 class

Literally the worst professor Ive ever had in my four years of college. Doesn't even know what he's teaching, literally needs to be reevaluated because half of the stuff he teaches us is wrong. TERRIBLE professor, avoid him at all costs

Dr. K may be a nice man, but he was very rude to me throughout the semester.  It felt as though he was unprepared for many classes even showing up late or forgetting his materials to do class.  Exams were 2-5 questions, meaning if you get one wrong you fail most of the time. I repeatedly had to teach myself the material outside of class to do well.

Dr. K is down-to-earth but there's no denying that he and the course were incredibly disorganized. His review sessions felt like answer keys for some tests, but on the flip side, your entire grade comes down to arbitrary precision. Due dates were never communicated clearly, but were at least readjusted in the student's favor. Be responsible!
All over the place.

I love Dr K but yeah he definitely isn't a great teacher, very disorganized and doesn't really get the point across. But, he is an awesome guy and I actually enjoy the class despite the academic issues, just be ready to need to figure out how to use excel on your own.

Worst teacher I have had a Virginia Tech. I thought I could deal with the bad teaching but it is impossible to get through a test because of how confusing he makes the class and the expectations. I got an A because we took five tests including the final and dropped 3. He is a really nice guy but an absolutely horrendous teacher.

Really nice and funny guy. I would love to be friends. However, it felt as though he didn't understand the material which is why he couldn't clearly explain it to us. He'd go on tangents a lot and it was impossible to focus because he'd give the valuable information at some random time in between and you were already too zoned out to capture it.

If you just copy down all the excel sheets he puts up in class, then you should be good. There were times when I was frustrated with the class itself but if you just show up to class you should be able to at least get a B at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Much worse than other professors. He barely prepares for class (i.e. he was unable to connect his laptop to AV system for weeks). He rarely teaches a full concept, so students are left clueless and confused. He is then frustrated that students don't understand. The quality of education in this class is unacceptable given the cost of tuition.

Least organized teacher I've ever had. For the first couple weeks of class he didn't have the cables to use the projector, couldn't figure out how to use the microphone, and refused to bring his own markers do we basically just had to guess what he's talking about. The class would be easy if it weren't for him.

Worst professor I have ever had. He is a nice guy but can't teach to save his life. He often gave extensions on assignments which was great except these extensions were given bc no one had a clue how to do any of the HW. He also would promise extra videos that would explain the HW and never post. Easy A but stressful and u won't learn a thing
He is an example of what a Chemistry Proffessor should be
Put in the work and you're chillin. Go to class for iClickers. Sweet guy, but lectures can get somewhat boring.

Kurt is a cool dude I'm ngl. He wasn't really outstanding in the teaching aspect but he just had that respectable uncle vibe about him. Personally, I liked his teaching style of walking you thru practice problems but he is very lecture heavy and they can get really boring. Be there for iClickers, they make a bigger difference than you think!

I enjoyed this class because he genuinely wants you to pass. He allows you to use a sheet of notes on the exams and the third exam was take home open note and the final exam is one sheet with notes both sides. Definitely do the problem sets/practice exams because he tends to reuse the same questions. Molecule project was easiest 5% for grade boost.

I did not find this class to be overwhelming or very difficult because he was very fair about everything. Gave us a cheat sheet for test 2, and test 3 was a take home test. Definitely do the practice problems and come to class, but overall, he does not want you to fail and made that clear. He is always willing to help clear up confusing material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kurt is such a G and needs a higher rating. He really wants you to succeed and gives you every resource to do so. I am so bad at chemistry and orgo is not for the faint of heart but do the homework, practice problems, and worksheets (hint) and you will be prepared. Easy grader for the molecule project.

When it comes to chemistry it really doesn't matter what professor you get - you have to put the time in. Dr. Neidigh will give you every resource you need to succeed. Do all the homework, do the optional worksheets, and go to his lectures(which are very informational), and you will excel. If thats not enough look up Organic Chemistry Tutor on YT.
A lot of independent study is needed since its hard to derive anything from the lectures, but you still have to attend the lectures to do I-Clickers.

Worst professor ever! CHEM 1035 is a weed-out class, so it can be challenging. One of my tests grades was screwed up, I talked to him and emailed him numerous times, said he would fix it.  He told me if I ask him again then I will be reported for an honor code violation.  He clearly doesn't care about teaching and has horrible notes.  Avoid Kurt!
Had to teach myself all material. All lectures were just fill in blanks for definitions and not how to solve problems

Not a terrible experience but definitely not a good one. The class is very lecture heavy and not very engaging. The lectures are very important to attend since that is where you are given all information and the notes he writes are not uploaded. If you don't show up and write down his notes, you won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Teachers solely from lectures, very willing to help but the class is very difficult

My grade dropped four letter grades because of one exam. No matter what you study there's no way to prep for the exams. There's very little that is graded and if you mess up at all you WONT PASS. He also struggles with technology so good luck getting the "HWs" an hour before the due date...
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself is hard and he does not teach at all he just goes over practice problems. The key to doing well in the class is watching the recorded lectures in the media gallery and taking practice tests a week before the test. Overall he is a nice man but his teaching style is mediocre.
Answers emails and is helpful, however he did not hold a single lecture over zoom for the entire semester, which made the class very challenging and frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture videos were pre-recorded and it was him just writing notes with no explanation . All were super long and boring. Zooms were just for i-clicker questions and he took forever to respond to emails. Seems like a great person, but an AWFUL professor online. DO NOT RECOMMEND HIM AT ALL. Having to retake the class because of his teaching.

Tests are 80 percent of your grade. Chem is a weed out class. Kurt's zoom classes were pointless only needed to go for the attendance/i-clicker grade. Lecture videos were very long and hard to watch, ended up studying through reading the textbook and practice problems.

Really bad experience. His Zoom meetings have no content in them whatsoever, just completely revolves around iclicker questions. Outside of class, he isn't accessible AT ALL, and often won't respond to e-mails. Gets sidetracked constantly during zoom meetings by other students and his lecture videos are incredibly subpar. Try to go for Amateis .
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: No doubt knows the material, and if you ask explicitly, he is able to adequately answer your questions. However, he is a bit unprofessional in the meetings, and often gets carried away on tangents when prompted by his students. You can do well if you can study on your own; it's like taking an async class. Do as many test prep problems as you can.

He was a really slow and monotone talker and not great at handling zoom and canvas. I've heard Dr. Eddleton is way better. His online format has a lot of assignments, lecture videos, and zooms where he just answers questions but you have to join the beginning to do I-clickers. You'll be fine in his class, but you should aim for Eddleton.

Classes were 30 min Q&A sessions with an iClicker question, but that didn't really help much. Made some of my closest friends in this class despite it being fully virtual, meaning he creates a very chill and relaxed environment, but this is only a good thing if you're incredibly self-motivated since it was completely video lecture based.

AVOID! Super disorganized. No notice for assignments or tests. Even dropped an assignment on us during Thanksgiving Break. Lecture videos were uninformative snooze fests. Only survived this class because of Kahn Academy and A LOT of studying.

Unless you already know everything about Chemistry, do not choose Kurt as your professor. We rarely had class and when we did, he would just give us a participation question. We had no class notes, lectures, study guides, it was all up to you to learn the material. Kurt's class average was about 15 points lower than other 1035 GEN CHEM professors.
He is genuinely a good teacher. Responds to emails a while later but teaches very well and solves all the doubts.

He really tries to help us succeed but his lectures are veryyyyyyyy long and boring. Went to every class and review session and still ended with a C-. he was understanding but his classes fully put me and everyone around me to sleep.

Honestly the class will be super easy to get an A in if you go to classes and actually go along with his fill in the blank notes. He does practice problems which help a little, but doesn't help on iClickers. For any chem professor you can do well if you study in your room on your own, but if you pay attention in class it'll be easier.

Neidigh was great. Going to class definitely helps, however he is very lecture based. Despite this, he has very open office hours and genuinely wants to help students. Missed a test, and he let me make it up with medical documents. Very caring. Lots of online homework, but it's easy. Do practice tests and ask questions if you don't understand!
He's a good professor and he is pretty good in office hours. Usually takes longer than the other chem teachers to grade tests though.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very nice and has fun demonstrations. Also pretty funny. If you do the practice tests, you will do fine on the test. Genuinely wants students to understand.

He is enthusiastic about teaching and does some fun demonstrations. Lectures can sometimes be boring but it is easy to follow and gives good examples to help wrap your brain around everything. Definitely a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Neidigh is extremely knowledgeable about chemistry. He truly wants his students to succeed and does everything he can to help you do better on the tests. He also loves to blow stuff up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Harrison is one of the few professors that actually care about the student and their success and who they are as a human--- not a student. He is the best professor at Virginia Tech.
Very easy to understand in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This a great class and Kwame is very engaged in the topic. You can see his passion for anthropology. It is also cool that he does anthropological research on the hip hop scene in San Francisco.  He is very lenient with attendance, but I found that I wanted to be at his class almost every day because I was excited about the class.
No Comments
He is a great story teller and makes them relevent to the subject which makes things easier to remember when it comes to exams!
No Comments

Solid professor in an otherwise lacking math department. His lectures are clear, he is always willing to answer questions, and he tells us what will be on the midterms/final. He provides us with ample practice material beforehand. (I screwed up the MCQ on the final and the first midterm haha). Great professor.
Ask questions if you're confused, he is very easy to have a conversation with. Love his cat!
Loved him, very clear classes, no fluff; ended early most of the time. He will help you out in a clear and concise manner if you just ask, and the practice tests are a legit goldmine.

Kyle is a good teacher. 1536 goes into the basics of calculus, so pay attention if you didn't in 1535. He tries to make class not boring, and does pretty well with it, his voice is just somewhat easy to fall asleep to. Good professor, AND HE WILL HELP YOU IF YOU ASK FOR HELP. SO ASK FOR HELP IF YOU NEED IT, he's there for you. 9/10 would take again

Very chill professor and has created his grading policy in a way that allows you to improve your grade even if you bomb a few tests or quizzes. I would recommend writing down the notes from class. The class is based completely on tests and quizzes, and though Kyle covers a lot of the problems in class, practice problems are your friend.

Good teacher. Caring and relatable. A nice guy and he tries his best. At times messes up on problems but everyone is human. Take notes along with him. Do not sit back and watch him do stuff, write it down in a physical notebook it will help you loads. Plus you can use them on your weekly out of class quizzes. Kyle is cool.

I had him got 1535 where the criteria was pretty easy in my opinion but be aware that 1536 takes into account a lot of calculus and the second half of the semester is ALL calculus. The criteria is a lot harder than 1535, and your grade is still only based on quizzes and exams

He is a great professor for 1536, just beware your grade is based on open note quizzes, and then exams are taken at the math emporium. Those are your only grades, but it’s easy to study and he provides helpful office hours.
Very good professor
Hes really fair and cares about you as a student. recitations are a waste of time but mandatory attendance. really cool guy
He really wants you to pass the class and is fair when it comes to obstacles and whatnot. Definitely, the most understanding professor I've had.

He grades very fairly and is wonderful at explaining concepts. However I wish we could have more lectures with him rather than watching another teacher's lecture videos though. I was real disappointed when I couldn't have him again for 1226.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kyle was my saving grace after my first two semesters with the Virginia tech Math department. He gives you the information you need without all the fluff. He didn't do many example problems and you DEFINITELY need to put in some study time for the tests, but the exams were much more fair than I have had in my past two math courses. Very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He doesn't do many examples in class, so you have to take time with the homework but he uses the extra time to explain the concepts better. Really great class atmosphere.
Super laid back guy and a great professor. Really wants you to pass the class and is considerate of student's perspective. Best professor I've had thus far at VT.

He is an extremely chill teacher for a class that is usually not supposed to be chill - multivariable calculus. His notes and lectures were extremely straight forward and correlated exactly with the test material. He spoke slowly and clearly, so it was easy to follow along with his lectures, which is why I went to every lecture and did well.
Great Professor! She is very insightful into the construction industry and very well connected! Show up to her class and you'll be more than fine!
She is very intelligent about the construction world and is very nice. Very easy to understand the material as long as you just pay attention in class.
Project docs is a helpful class and Lally is an easy grader. She's very kind and super helpful. She's willing to help when and if needed. Don't stress this class whatsoever.

Great teacher and very understanding. Very laid back but sticks by her word and the syllabus. Lectures are very straightforward and informational. The class "crash-courses" you through all types of plans and Lally adds on applicable information for the field. Would 100% recommend for Capstone as well.
Good professor.

bro literally woke up on a snow day, canceled our final quiz, and gave everyone 100s. john lewis my goat.

he knows what he's talking about and explains things well. lectures are kind of a snoozefest but he'll start laughing at his own jokes and that'll wake you up. pretty much everything is graded by the TAs, but he's always there if you need him.
Best professor I have had at Virginia Tech. He is very accessible and makes every assignment clear. He also gives you plenty of time for everything.

If you need to take CS1064, then John Lewis is your guy. Amazing professor, gave everyone 100s on the final quiz because of a snow day. Class is honestly not super difficult, spend time outside of class (roughly 1-3 hours) to try and understand the content and you should be good to go. Lectures are long but he goes over everything you need to know.

Dr. Lewis made my Python learning career as enjoyable as possible. I liked the class, and he always kept it entertaining, even at 4:15 pm. He is a great guy who always warns about deadlines and offers numerous opportunities for office hours. Although the readings can get monotonous, it's practically vital to read them to understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Lewis' lectures are very engaging and interesting -- which is not what I expected at all when signing up for an introduction to coding in python class. I really appreciate how much he cares about the topics, and he is very willing to help his students. The best advice I have is do your work, practice the material, and DO NOT cheat.
Nice guy and teaches clearly. If you show up to class and listen you should get an A.

All assignments were established on the syllabus at the end of the year. If you attend his lectures all of the material is explained to you in simple terms and with some jokes. Quizzes and projects aren't overly difficult and weekly homework should be free points.
Dude gave everybody 100 percent because of a snow day and because he didn't feel like coming to class again

Oh boy where do I even start. John "GOAT" Lewis may be the BEST professor at Virginia Tech. If you need a CS elective TAKE CS 1064 without a doubt. Now I'm ngl, I already knew how to program a little bit in Python, but regardless I know plenty of people who came in with no coding experience and did just as well as me. Lots of extra credit.

Thanks
Professor Lewis is very understanding of circumstances and is a fair grader. I believe deep down he truly cares for his students' success.

Professor Lewis was a great professor. I took his Python Programming class and as long as you do the homework and the reading and have a general idea of what is going on you'll be fine. He is very good at explaining how the programming that you focus on that week works and gives lots of examples in class and shows you how to do it.
Absolute legend of a professor the last quiz got canceled because of snow and he just gave everyone a 100 on it he is pretty funny but just coding itself is pretty hard.

He is very understanding, school was cancelled on the day of our final and he gave everyone an 100. If you pay attention in class and try to understand the material it will be really easy, and use the office hours if you need help especially with projects.

Even though lectures aren't mandatory, he goes through the information slowly and makes it much more understandable. There are 3 big projects per semester and 4 major quizzes, but all the work is manageable. He is a very caring professor and gave everyone a 100 on the last quiz because it was a snow day instead of rescheduling it.

Great professor, he was funny. TA's grade everything. As long as you show up its chill. Skip a class and you will be thrown behind quickly. Theres technically a lot of readings but tbh i dont think anyone actually reads everything. You dont really need to do the readings for the quick checks. Only complaint is with web - cat. I HATE the system.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I love him! As someone with no coding experience, he truly makes this class bearable. Lectures are live coding so def go. He explains things very clearly and simply and also makes it entertaining. Can't recommend enough! Easy workload and very straightforward.

I loved taking this class! Professor Lewis was a really nice person and instructor, and while some of the assignments may have been a bit difficult (like the individual projects), if you take the time to do them properly and seek help when you don't understand something, then you will do good in this class.

Lewis is probably the best and only professor that teaches CS 1064. He's funny and answer any questions you have and likes to strike up a conversation with students. Just do the assignments and read the class text and you would be fine.

Dr Lewis was a good professor and explains everything very well. I have no interest in coding (I had to take this class) so the lecture were very boring. It is overall an easy class and you should take Dr Lewis if you can.

Dr. Lewis was very chill, but gave a lot of assignments. That being said, they were all fairly easy besides the programming projects. He assigns them weeks before they are due, so start on them in advance. His lectures were very straightforward, lecturing in Thonny (the programming software) as compared to traditional slides.

I have never coded before and got an A. The way the class is structured is completely idiotic, focusing on Ticketmaster programs and useless Madlibs generators for projects instead of data analytics (what python is good at). John Lewis is a very good lecturer and is a very strong speaker. His demonstrations are very clear and the readings are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. He breaks things down into normal people terms and stops very frequently for questions. As long as you actually do the readings you'll do good in this class.

I would take this class at a community college if possible (unless you are a CS major). As someone with zero coding background, I felt like Lewis expected too much of his students. TAs grade the quizzes (4 in sem.), essays (2 in sem.), and projects (3 in sem.). Their grading can be all over the place (lax or harsh). Lecture is just live coding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Although his lectures are consisted of live coding examples that could be entirely learnt from the online textbook, he's generous for providing relatively easy extra credit for the class along with being helpful during office hours! Quizzes aren't too bad and go to the TAs for the programming projects.

If you don't have any background in Python you likely will struggle, however, this doesn't mean he's a bad prof. You can tell he wants to help you learn, and uses lots of real world examples and makes it fun as to keep students engaged.

he's so great and so patient. this class was easy for me bc i have coded before in a different language, but this class is super accessible even if you're a complete beginner. do the readings at the beginning of each week and you'll be completely fine
Least favorite class taken in college.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lewis is AWESOME! I've taken CS classes before, but his course truly made me feel like I was finally confident in my programming skills. His lectures are live coding demonstrations, so it helps to do the reading/hw beforehand. He is a super knowledgable professor and genuinely cares about his students.
I love john lewis, best atVT
He was an incredible professor. Really loved taking his class and the material to the point that I decided to minor in CS.

His lectures are just live coding examples, and classes will generally be empty after a week or two, although he tries to make them fun.
Very introductory material, so if you already know how to program in another language, you'll be fine as long as you do the reading. 
Projects have very clear rubrics.
Do the extra credit, it's worth a ~1.2% bump.

prof lewis went through lectures and explained things as if we have never coded in our lives before. the textbook readings aligned with what was went over in class which helped a lot, and by finding extra credit 'easter eggs' in the readings it helped my grade a lot !! this man was great

Funny guy, and he's respectful towards students. If you're not a fan of sitting and looking at code, lectures can get a little boring, but I feel like that's the nature of CS lectures. You can get extra credit for finding easter eggs in the textbook. It's just italicized text, and they can be pretty funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My actual class time was at 1:25 but he let me sit in his earlier class. LOVE THIS GUY he's also funny which makes his lectures a little more interesting. Theres not really many allowance for late work but THERES EXTRA CREDIT at the end and its pretty easy to get an A if u do well on the projects and ok on the exams

Class is made up of weekly homework assignments based on reading (first try), weekly coding exercises, 2 simple essays, 4 quizzes, and 3 projects. If you put in the work by coming to class and utilizing the TAs, you will be fine! Love Dr. Lewis he is a king
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Time restrictions on quizzes were a little too short for comfort. But overall chill class. I liked the easter eggs hidden in the website used to teach the class.

He is funny and his lectures are generally pretty good but definitely got boring. The homework every week was manageable and the projects were the thing I spent most of my time on. It is a good amount of work but you should be able to do pretty well if you study and give yourself time for the projects.
Lectures are very helpful although not required. If you go to the lectures, 1064 is an easy class. Dr. Lewis is passionate and is very down to earth and modest. I would highly recommend.

Prof Lewis is a great teacher! Even though the lectures are literally just the textbook, he makes sure to also write examples of the code and explain confusing processes in detail. Make sure to redo the exercises and practice in Thonny for the quizzes. The projects may get confusing, but he details everything he needs in the rubric. TAs help a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! He'll throw small jokes throughout the lecture to keep the class engaged which was fun. The class itself was pretty easy, you work solely through the online textbook that he tells you to buy and there was 4 short quizzes/midterms you have to do. There are also 3 projects throughout the semester but I recommend utilizing the TA's.

Dr. Lewis is a funny professor and the class itself isn't very difficult. If you read the textbook (which is required for assignments), and understand, you don't really need to show up to class. There are also lots of office hours for TA's and you're guaranteed to find someone to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is mostly copying code but its all posted on Canvas. Projects aren't too bad if you start early, and his office hours/the TA's are very helpful. Put in effort for quick checks, they're worth more than you expect (he gives extra credit with them!). I didn't know about python coming in, and i really enjoyed the class.

Extremely beginner-friendly, I came in with 0 knowledge of Python and excelled in the class. Make sure to start on projects early. There is no reason to show up to class if you're able to just read off Rephactor and understand what it's asking you to do. In-class lectures tend to just be reciting off Rephactor pages.
No background in python is necessary. Class is very straightforward. The projects can be a little tricky but there are a ton of TAs to help.

Dr. Lewis is a very nice professor and exceptional at teaching. There is a lot of work for the class, especially for a 1XXX level, but it ensures that you understand what you're doing. Office hours both with Dr. Lewis and the TAs are beneficial, and you get a lot out of the class. Definitely take if you're even considering
He was a good professor and understanding with grades. Notes are important to go over. You get the grade of the work you put into the class. He also provides extra credit and easy 100% grades.

This class made me develop a passion for programming.  Definitely get some background knowledge of Python before you start the class.  The structure of the course was one of the best throughout my college career, and Prof. Lewis is an amazing instructor.  The only problem I had was the strict grading by the TA's on the projects.

During class time Lewis normally just writes code that you copy down. It is hard to learn with little to no notes to look back on. You have to go to office hours as a new python user to consider passing.
Hard to learn, most of the time you just copy what he writes in class.
John Lewis at the start seems to be a caring person, but as a professor he does not meet expectations. The projects were way to hard for just starting to learn python.

Lewis continues to make his course harder year by year for no reason. The projects in his class should not be considered for beginners. Very little mention for what will be on quizzes until 1-2 days prior of the quiz.

Very nice and funny guy. I never went to lectures but went to office hours often. Please don't be dumb and Chegg the projects like a good portion of my classmates did this semester. If you go to TA office hours, they are glad to help you out. I had little/no programming background and did well.

Your average professor that can be respected. He is very loud, so don't worry about not being able to hear him from the far back of the room. Class is very doable, so long you have good time management. Very clear grading criteria that does not turn you a mess like CS1114 does.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took him in Spring 2022. A very nice teacher in-person. He speaks loud and clear, so don't worry about not being able to hear him in the back. Do your assignments and projects EARLY, so if you have any questions, you can attend office hours. Be careful while doing textbook assignments, as you can get penalized if you just mindlessly choose.
If you do the bare minimum, you should be able to pass this class with a B+/A- minimum. He is a nice guy and passionate about what he teaches.  Not a lot of work, just stay on track of things.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If u understand python dont go to the lectures. Easy to understand to code, it took me a month but u have to do the assignment when its posted.

Easy class especially if you have programming experience. Only show up for the first day or if you are about to go over something you want to understand. All the homework is easy, projects aren't hard if you start them early. He rounded my grade from B to A- because I emailed him AND put in the work. If you try to learn, you will pass.

When I went to Professor Lewis's class, he went over the material in a very simple and easily understandable way. He taught Python concepts in a hands-on way by coding as a class. However, if you have a somewhat decent understanding of the basics of programming, you do not need to attend the lectures very often.

Very fun class! He does expect some effort from students to participate in class, so read and pay attention! The projects were super fun and easy to get 100s on. Homework was easy as long as you read the online textbook. Nice guy and very helpful when I had questions about the projects, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: TBH u don't need to come to class, u need to buy his rephracter online hw thing to do the class. All the reading HW is on quizlet expect for the weekly exercise in which u need to do the reading to figure out how to write it or go to Office hours. Every so often he will assign a project and u have to go to office hours to get done, they'll do for u

Class is fine, professor is good. Pretty easy. You can get away with not showing up to a single class if you have some programming experience. The final is only 10% of our grade but is 120 questions which I find kind of ridiculous.

I enjoyed this class. Professor Lewis is very cool. I had no issues, but I had some previous python experience from a high school class. The class is focused on 5 coding projects. As long as you start them early and come to class, you shouldn't have any issues. He often demonstrates aspects of the projects in class. Attend office hours if you need.

Dr. Lewis is very knowledgeable and sprinkles in humor with his presentations. The class focuses heavily on 5 semester coding projects which are quite easy for the most part. There are multiple TAs that essentially give you office hours for most hours on weekdays, and they can be a great help whenever you run into probems on your projects.

He is well informed and gives clear lectures while answering questions. Attendance really helps with understanding the material. His grading system is well balanced between reading checks, projects, a midterm, and a final. It requires some work, attention, and trial and error to do well, but it is a great intro class for a programming language!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Intro to Python at VT is one of the most neglected courses at the school. For a class that should be used to engage people in CS, prof John Lewis is a boring presenter and a tough grader. If you don't code EXACTLY the way he wants you to, you are doing it wrong. Take it from a CS major who has 3 years experience with python, learn it on udemy.
He is a good lecturer, I never needed to see him after class but I know he was available. Does not matter if you miss class, the notes will be posted for you. Overall good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class will be easy if you have any programming knowledge, otherwise it can be challenging. But there are so many TAs, so if you take advantage of the office hours it's do-able. He's a fun guy and creates a positive vibe in the lecture hall. He's good at explaining stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you have some knowledge of how to code, then you'll excel in this class. The lectures would just go over writing some specific code, and since it was a 500+ person lecture, I didn't have to show up all the time. There are some textbook homework problems, but they are pretty easy. Some of the tas' of this class were also helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great CS professor.. he makes sure you understand the material. He was an amazing professor for a 500 person class. There wasnt a lot of homework, but coding projects are something you need to start early.

The overall material taught is fairy simple, however the professor tends to have an attitude when it comes to grading and doesn't tie in the material taught to the real world. He focuses far too much on how the code looks to him rather than the functionality of it. The class itself is simple, but be prepared for some bogus responses.

My only complaint is that he is not good at submitting grades on time. The material is easy if you have previous experience with Python but if not then it's going to be difficult for a beginner. I had decent experience but found myself baffled with some of the project specs. Other than that a solid professor.

Even during COVID he was extremely accessible during office hours and made videos describing the textbook lectures. During office hours he was encouraging and always gave praise and reassurance. He really wants to help you learn and sat with me as I second guessed my code (which with his encouragement was right!)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Yes, it was online because Covid, but he was hardly involved with the class. The material was too hard and I felt on my own if it weren't for a friend of mine to help me. There's not much else to say because there wasn't that much that he did.

By far my favorite professor. He made the information fun and interesting. There is mandatory reading every week, but nothing too much. Attendance is taken at every class and tests can be specific, but overall it was a great class! I would take any course he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was a great professor, very invested in his students and classes. Genuinely cares about the content of the class and answers questions very thoroughly, which is very helpful on group projects where multiple drafts are submitted. I am taking him again for 1216 because of how much I enjoyed the class and his teaching styles.

Dr. Nieto is very nice and caring and really wants his students to succeed. I honestly thought the material was interesting and I enjoyed most of the projects and reports in the class. Even though I did most of the group reports alone with very little help from my teammates, I enjoyed this class and I highly recommend Dr. Nieto.

Dr. Nieto (Andres) is a very kind person. Could not ask for a better human. However, I felt like I learned next to nothing in his class, and the work requires so little explanation, and he tends to overexplain. Many skip class b/c attending class is not that necessary once groups get set up.

It's a first year general engineering course basically. Most of his reviews talk about the material of the class more than Andres. I though the material was extremely boring but that isn't Andres's fault. He is very kind, caring, and fun to talk to. I would recommend him to everyone taking 1215. I'll have him again for 1216 next semester as well.
Class was a little too easy

I'll preface all of this by saying he was a genuinely nice, caring professor. However, the class was overall useless. I felt I was taught common knowledge, and professor Nieto simply read word for word off of the slides. He spent excessive amount of time overexplaining simple subjects. Young children could follow along. Frustrating to attend class.

She is super super harsh when grading. LOTS of reading to do as well. She seriously pulls the tiniest facts from the book to put in the quiz, like the year the author was born and stuff, so need to basically memorize the texts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had a frustrating experience in Professor Leslie Neilan's class. While her passion for literature is evident, her homework assignments are excessive and often feel overwhelming. Each week, we were burdened with mountains of reading and the expectations for analysis were sky-high. To make matters worse, she was an incredibly tough grader.

I think she would be better off to retire to a private island away than to be a professor. To call her one would be an exaggeration as she is super unprofessional and not very clear with what she wants from us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her grading and her feedback, if she gives any is useless. I had several grades where the only feedback was a critique of my interpretation or how I viewed a story. The exams are closed everything and she takes it way too seriously. I enjoyed most of the stories, but the exams were worthless. She also never responded to the final emails I sent.

Terrible grammar and spelling in her emails while docking an entire grade if your grammar is slightly bad. There is no rubric for any assignments, I have no idea how she concludes grades. If she doesn't like your style of writing or conclusion she also docks point. I'm trying to save you guys to not take her class please.

She is an English professor with spelling errors (the irony) and grades quite subjectively to her own opinion (if you do not follow her ideals, she gives you a bad grade). However, if you try, you will do well. The reading in her class isn't that bad, its only like 10-40 pages a day. Overall, not good but not horrible, hence the 2/5 stars.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: (both engl1105 & 1106) i love her! she is a very very very hard grader. if you are not good w citations or english in general, DO NOT TAKE HER! the best thing you can do is meet with her frequently so she will like you and grade u highly. both 1105&1106 i got an A because she rounded up my A-. just talk to her a lot and she will love you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: the course itself is not that hard, but she grades it very harshly. She'll leave you a comment without further explanation. If you miss three things it is automatically a C. Please ensure that your annotations are everything is up to par and follow the rubric, which is in alphabetical order and that she doesn't provide.

She take away any enjoyments from her classes. Her GPA averages are some of the lowest in the department. It's literally impossible to get an A in any of her classes since her grading is pretty much erratic. Nothing is consistent and she has a very thick skull.
You never know how harsh she will grade your work. She always has to right and prove that your wrong.

This is by far one of the worst classes I've taken at this school, it is a intro to science fiction class most students take it because they need it for a pathway she grades so strict for no reason, and you constantly have to get new books for each reading. If you can take another pathway do that

The final exam for this class is just criminal. She grades so harshly for no reason and her feedback is not helpful. She makes an asynchronous class a living hell. Don't take this class with her or you will face the consequences.
Nothing is more cringeworthy than her disorganized canvas with spelling mistakes. Pretty ironic for an English professor who grades harshly for spelling and grammar.
She sucks. Grades harshly for no reason and takes away any enjoyment from the class. Would not take again:(

Leslie grades journals and papers very harshly. The average grade on the journals were like a low B for a 1000 level class? Plus the final exam was so difficult, it costed my A in the class, since every assignment type is worth 25% of your grade. Horrible professor overall, not professional.

I have never written a review on a professor before, but I need to save the youth. This class is supposed to be an easy A, and instead it is my worst grade. The exams are random details from 50 short stories and she graded different depending on the day.
Do not take her class

I have never disliked a teacher so much that it prompted me to write a review. You could have written the best argument for your case in the world, as well as an analysis, but if she disagrees with your opinion, good luck getting an A. I am quite literally begging you guys to not take her class. Learn from my mistake. Please.

The feedback was very unhelpful and completely opinionated. She teaches her class based on her own opinion and docks points if you do not agree with her or you do not state what she is looking for. Not to mention, her rubric is not a rubric, but more of an outline with very vague descriptions. Also, her response time is horrible.

Leslie's online class is infuriating. She grades harshly and is vague with directions. Plus the exams she gives can be challenging if you haven't kept up with the required reading. She also sometimes gives out work over school breaks, which is not permitted by the dean. If you are planning on taking a class with her, elective or not, please don't.

Class is not super difficult as many have claimed. She can be a bit of a picky grader, but that can all be avoided if you simply read what she wants. She unfortunately gives out work during school breaks, which yes is a violation, but isn't really surprising considering the class in asynchronous.
Do not take her class. Everything is graded so harshly and to do good on the quizzes you have to memorize very specific details.

she is absolutely awful.. harsh grader for quite literally no reason. Her feedback is so generic and is not reliable. Her assignments are also very straightforward, but she turns it into something it doesn't need to be and will grade you unfairly (imo). Girl gave me a whole 89% for an intro assignment and praised me in a comment... be so for real.
Harsh grader with vague assignments

For the spring semester (2021-2022), I took the class online. The only major assignment in this class was the research paper. In this class, you are only graded off of very few assignments. By the end, she'll unnecessarily grade harshly. You could be cruising through the class with an A and then she'll change up her grading style to give you a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I decided to take ENGL 1106 online this semester with Professor Neilan. Never again. She is such a harsh grader and her assignment directions are very vague. The modules are not engaging at all and are very boring to read.

I had her for online english 1106 so I never met her in person. The class was really easy, but some of her directions were so confusing. She also grades based off of what she thinks you should have taken away from something in her eyes which was annoying. She once told me that I took things in articles too literally but it should be my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was the worst. Her feedback was always vague and confusing. Her lectures were copy-pasted from the internet. She grades based on what she expected you to do without letting you know that beforehand. The assignment instructions were unclear and would often lead you to email her for clarification (which you still wouldn't get). NEVER AGAIN!

I've got to start this off by saying that I am an exception when it comes to grades. The majority of my class got at best C+. She is by far the most opinionated person I know. She will try to push her beliefs on you and you have to push back. I believe that is the only reason I did well is because I was the only one to stand up for what I believe.

The class itself was relatively straightforward, but to score well you have to memorize a lot of little details. I found it impossible to get a good grade on the quizzes without reading the entire half of the book right beforehand, and even then it was hard to recall things like specific quotes said by characters which were tested on.

I took her online Sci-fi class. You read a novel every two weeks. She also graded based on her opinion of what I should think of the novels, and I got docked points simply because she didn't agree with me and not because I was wrong. She was nice overall, but her exams require you to know exact names of authors and novels and things mentioned once.

Get ready to read everyday since you need to read half a book in a week. However, I did enjoy almost every book we did read. The quizzes were hard since they ask for really specific things. Reading journals weren't the worst but they were definitely annoying. The books are good and the subject is interesting but this isn't an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's a great professor. She is very casual in class and makes the class one you want to come to. She gives very good criticism on papers and guides the student the student in the right direction. She genuinely wants to get to know her students and wants them to pass. She respects her students and breaks the students-teacher barrier. 10/10 teacher.

She's hilarious, and I generally enjoyed her class discussions, but her tests and daily quizzes on that day's reading are too specific. They test you on very specific things from the historical background and the play that you didn't think would be important. Overall, I don't regret the class, but it wasn't as easy as I would've liked it to be.

You'll actually learn in this class, so that's great. However, the quizzes and tests she has are extremely hard. Some questions are far too specific for anybody to remember. Not that hard of a class, but you probably won't get an A.

Great professor! The books and short stories she assigned were all fantastic classics, and she has very interesting class discussions. I recommend reading all material, but it isn't too much. If you read, you will get a good grade. She tells you exactly what will be on the tests, and the best part is: you do not write a single paper all semester!
