I loved my T.A. one semester and didn't the next. This is kind of a class you just have to get through to get the degree because it is kinda difficult.
I've never met Professor Wooram because the class is taught by TAs. Josh Fife was a great TA though. This lab is super low stress, it's very easy to do well.

Taught by TA's, never saw the professor and the labs are relatively easy. There's one paper and one group presentation at the end, otherwise there isn't a lot of outside work for the class. If you have Grace as your TA, she is really nice and gave us extra credit for the presentation and dropped our lowest quiz grade.

Lab is taught by TAs but personally I loved my TA. The labs are fairly easy and simple and I was able to complete any worksheets during the lab time. We wrote one lab report and we were given almost a month to write it. Final was a group presentation. Make sure to partcipate within your group because it will be graded.

I had a TA for this class. I never interacted with the actual professor. My TA never really explained how to do each lab that well so I was always confused. The actual work isn't bad. I just never knew what was going on in the labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: TA: JUSTUS Our final lab report that was a good bit of our grade he gave the class an AVERAGE of 60%. Grades were dropped full letters last minute. He told us he'd curve it as we had never written a lab report before. He instead curved a Forensics presentation (with the professor's permission) that the majority of the class did completely fine on.

You'll never see him, he doesn't teach, the TAs do. If you get Justus as a TA, switch out. He was very unfair in his grading and did not help when students had questions. When I had issues with Justus, I was able to email Professor Lee and he was very helpful and got the situation resolved.

Class is mainly run by TAs, who are very nice and considerate. They lab is interactive and, as someone who likes to move, I love being about to actually participate at this level. The labs are fun and very informational. When I didn't understand something from the BIO 1005, the lab usually cleared that up for me.

Class is run by TA's, so your experience is based on how good they are. As long as you have a good group to work with, the lab is super easy. Quizzes are not hard, just read through the slides the TA gives you and understand the lab procedures.

Only saw him once or twice since the labs are run by a TA, so they'll impact how enjoyable the lab is. Overall, the labs were not very difficult, especially if you get a good group to work with. There's one paper and one group presentation, but neither were super difficult. The paper is pretty time consuming but not bad as long as you start early.

You never see Mr. Wooram. He coordinates all of the labs but he doesn't teach them. Your class will be assigned a TA and their teaching style will have the most impact on how enjoyable your class is. That being said, I think the biology labs are well designed. The class was easy and went well with the lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I only saw him twice, the class is entirely run by the TA. He did run a class once, and let me stay after to finish the lab because I did it wrong. He's nice from what I gathered from that. Overall, the class was average. Wasn't that hard, but the lab reports were tedious. Labs aren't hard, just follow instructions and do your work on time.

The lab is entirely run by a TA, so the quality of the course depends entirely on who your TA is. During my first semester, I interacted with Lee once, this semester, not at all. Every class you complete a lab with your group, and you complete one individual lab report and one group presentation. Fairly straightforward, but try not to miss labs.
You don't see him because the teacher is the TA. Its easy lab worksheets are super easy just follow the manual and do stuff. Most annoying thing is the one written lab report.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class ultimately comes down to your TA. You will likely never interact with Dr. Wooram, as the lab is taught entirely by a TA.

Lab course is taught by a Graduate TA. Online labs use labsters pay attention which days it is due and the TA's grading guidelines. Wooram only lectures is related to the lab report. Yes some of the data makes no sense, so ask your TA for help. My TA gave my group a midterm & a final, it is up to the TA what's on it. Not many tests but TA dependent
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Usually just two labs per week. Quite easy and does not take a long time. The midterm and final vary in difficulty depending on your TA. His lectures for the paper can be a bit slow/ hard to follow but questions are easily answered by the TA. Your grade will mainly rely on who your TA is
You do no interact much with Dr. Wooram. The class is very straight forward and simple if you can follow directions and announcements posted in canvas.

Took this lab asynchronously during COVID. All of the labs were done online through Labster, which is almost like a video game. This class was an easy A as long as you did the work. The class consisted of 1-2 labs every week, one lab report, and a midterm/final made by your TA. The difficulty of the exams depends on the TA.

I had professor Leonetti for 2D art (ART 1204) and she was great! We got out of class early on work days, so don't let the 3 hour class time scare you. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed, and recognizes that not everyone has an art background. Her class pushed me in a really good way.
art1204 was a great class!

I have Leonetti for 4D right now. I learned a lot in this class in photoshop and after effects. The pace is slower but I think it's perfect and gives me time to finish projects early. Not lots of hw. She is really nice.
Art-1204 (2D)- very nice and understanding, easier art class for non-majors, we got out of class essentially an hour early every day - so don't be discouraged by the fact that they are ~3 hrs
Art 1204...I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved this class. Such a nice break from everything else going on senior year!

I really liked how we had a day of practice getting used to new mediums/familiarizing ourselves with inspiration before jumping into projects. I also liked the different critique days utilized- especially the silent auction-style critique. It helped with the social anxiety I experience during critique days while allowing me to give deeper feedback.

She supported and encouraged me to continue to my artistic vision and was great in her understanding of my outside situations. She engaged with the students actively to see if they needed help in regards to something they were working on and also made sure people were enjoying the time spent in the course.

Dr. Lee is by far one of the best BME professors at VT. He is incredibly kind, easy-going, understanding, and passionate. I was fortunate enough to have him as both my professor in BMES 4064 and BMES 3024, and both classes were enjoyable. He is always happy to answer questions not only about class but also about his career and professional life.

What an amazing and kind professor who really cares about his students! 43% of the course was canvas quizzes and a 1-page paper each week on a research article. Extremely easy! His lectures were very insightful and he explained how our topics were used in real life. Super cool class and an even cooler professor!

This class was my favorite class! Prof Lee made the class straightforward & gave extensions if asked! He was kind, engaging, and genuinely wanted us to learn. The only hard part of the class were the papers because they were so long, so make sure to have good time management.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super sweet and genuinely wants to get to know every student. His lab was really fun and you get to learn a lot through hands on stuff. Pretty much graded on your lab reports and a handful of homeworks. Would recommend.

This is a very hard class, and I feel like she makes this class harder than it needs to be. She expects everyone to already know everything and moves very fast. I will say she is very nice; I just don't think her teaching style is suited well for everyone. I withdrew from this class and changed my major away from accounting after this class.

She only reads off the slides, when it comes to example problems, she skips reading the question and jumps straight into solving it, while you're still trying to read and understand what it's asking. Her exam review confused me even more because she doesn't show us a direct way or steps for solving the problems. Her style of teaching is awkward.

Just a very middling experience. She is kind of weird from a sociability stand point (see "probably homeschooled") Smart enough lady though despite often getting her own in class problems wrong which makes it hard to respect her. I would avoid if possible but if you get placed into her class from course request its not the end of the world

There are enough assignments and extra credit to pull through. You will need to take charge if you want to do well. Michelle often would read off of the slides, say her answer or reason, hit next slide and be very wrong (& cant figure out why). She is judgemental, and trys to induce anxiety. You truly have to understand the material for test.

Nice in hindsight, condescending in reality. phd definitely gets to her head, yet she can only read off slides. Also make sure to not call her maam, she'll correct u and make sure u call her doctor.Also not hard to see her saltiness towards her past, avoid while u can. If ur not a student she likes to give special treatment, prepare to feel small.
Does not know the content. Only reads off of the slides. You must read the textbook. Very difficult exams. Not easy to deal with.

This class is VERY difficult. But Professor Lowry is very caring and willing to help her students learn. If you pay attention in class, actually come to class, and study you will do fine. While it is a difficult class she provides you with more than enough tools to succeed.
Prepare to have a professor who reads directly off the slides. I would definitely recommend the other professor for this class

Very reasonable grader and really just cared about if you applied effort. Even if you don't particularly like the subject she made learning and talking about it quite enjoyable. She's a very kind, caring, nice person and a great teacher.

Definitely an easy class but it was difficult being an introvert as class discussions are required and a speech (for some reason?) but overall she was great I just hated doing the speech and class discussions lol

Good professor, felt a little out of place being one of the oldest in the class (I'm a transfer student), but I really enjoyed the subject and the work. Kind of annoying to take this class as an introvert, as she does make us talk in groups a lot of the time. The lectures and readings were interesting; she also ties in a lot of current topics.

Dr. Lo was a wonderful professor and very understanding. If you communicate problems with her early she is willing to accommodate. The way she organized ENGE with a heavier load at the beginning of the semester was a great way to run the class. It is a bit overwhelming at first, but you will appreciate it when it comes to finals time.

JLo the Goat!!!!!!

The course itself was pretty heavy with the workload (being two courses in one), but the stress was dampened by the fact that JLo and her TAs are just straight awesome. Grading was pretty lenient too; as long as you do the bare minimum (satisfying rubrics), you're practically guaranteed a B.

Goated professor and class is super easy. Because it's an accelerated course (1215 and 1216 together) there are a lot of assignments but they are all easy. Group projects have CATME team ratings so make sure to be descriptive when giving feedback to teammates!

Dr. Lo was an incredible professor. I enjoyed coming to the class and working on our group project. The MATLAB and SOLIDWORKS assignments were tedious but there were plenty of office hours to make up for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Lo is an amazing teacher. The class was a breeze. It's mostly just one big group project with smaller projects, but nothing is ever too hard. She's accessible and caring, and is very nice, usually giving out snacks during class. Also, she cancels class often, especially towards the end of the semester.
She's great. Her expectations were very clear. I only went to office hours once, but she was very helpful. This class isn't very difficult, but definitely has a heavier mandatory workload.
I had her for ENGE 1414, and she was great! She is super understanding of different circumstances, really caring, and very sweet. The class itself is pretty easy too. I 100% recommend her.

Very nice and understanding of situations. Forces attendance through assignments that are graded based on attendance. I had her for 1414 and she gave you the grading criteria for every assignment so if you didn't end up with a A, it's your fault for not reading the instructions. 1414 has a lot of assignments but none are actually hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Lo was awesome. I had her for 1414 and would choose her every time. Almost everything is based on a big group project except for a few small individual assignments. My group never had to meet outside class as we got everything done during class. Grading was fair and you got lots of good feedback. You get easy points by showing up to class
I had her for 1414 and this was my favorite class. Second half of semester is spent on a group project, so I guess it depends on your teammates. It was an easy class though.

I loved Professor Lo. She's super chill, attendance isn't mandatory. The assignments can be super easy sometimes, especially if you're in her 1414 class. She also passes out candy sometimes and that's super nice. She isn't hard with late work, shoot her an email and you will 100% get a fast reply and an extension. Overall no complaints.
Jenny is like my college grandma. I love her and will miss her as I go into the cross fire of mechanical engineering.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: the goat, she very sweet and the class is very straight forward but your enjoyment depends entirely on your group assignment

Great professor who cares about her students' success! Had her for ENGE 1414, and most of the class is based on group work, with some individual assignments included throughout, including attendance-based assignments. Grading expectations are clearly outlined for each assignment and meaningful feedback is provided.

Professor Lo is AMAZING!!! I took her class for ENGE 1414, and I love her class so much. I really enjoyed how she structured the class, and her GTAs were lenient but fair graders. As long as you do the work and participate in the group project, you'll have no problem with this class.
This was a chill teacher and a chill class. The homework she usually easy, but there was a SOLIDWORKS every once in a while that could take FOREVER.

She is a great teacher and this course is overall very easy. Lots of group work and typed reports and surveys. A few slide presentations but they are recorded so no pressure. Overall a great class and the professor is very good at giving feedback and helping when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Doesn't hesitate to give personalized feedback. Her lectures directly correlate to what the projects and homework are about and it's helpful for Matlab beginners to get such intensive tutorials in class. She gives clear instructions and also kindly sends Canvas notifications so that students can be reminded in a timely manner of upcoming due dates.
Great professor, looking forward to taking her again this semester!
She really cares about her students. Make sure to participate in group projects!
She is very nice and she does not expect too much from anyone. She's really sweet and nice to talk to and her class is very easy.
She is a really nice professor. She wants to help students, especially during the office hour.
She is a really nice professor. She really wants to help you, especially during the office hour.
Professor Lo is very caring about her students and ensures all requirements for the class are understood.

You are put into groups of 6 at the beginning of the semester that you will stay in the entire time. She explains everything very clearly and makes sure that you know everything that will be due in the near future. I highly recommend attending class. There are assignments that you will only get credit for if you attend class.

Prof Lo is an awesome professor for the engineering foundations course. Although the course content is not always the most interesting, she was constantly there to help us with any problems that arose. From what I've heard from other students she seems like one of the best professors for 1215/1216.

Great professor, if you can take her for ENGE 1216 in the spring you should take her (if you didn't like your 1215 prof, otherwise just stay with who you know, it'll make getting used to the next semester easier)

Jenny is a great professor, one I would believe is the best professor for foundations. She grades easily, is very clear about work, always makes sure students are on top of their work, and is overall very kind. 100% recommend trying to get into her class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Any class you choose is going to be full of group projects, but they're really not that bad. Although the class feels very repetitive, Professor Lo is a caring professor who makes the class bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: jenny is so kind and caring! she never hesitates to help students. she is even willing to meet with students outside of office hours. she provides many office-hour opportunities so you always have access to help. the assignments aren't too hard. also, this is a group-work and project-based class!

Professor Lo is super nice and always responds to emails timely. This class heavily relies on the team you get so they can make or break your experience. Most classes have an in-class graded assignment. Rubrics for assignments are always easy to follow and the grading is very forgiving.

Dr. Lo (aka JLo) is a fantastic professor. She is very enthusiastic during lectures. Usually the TAs take attendance to see who receives credit for the assignments done that day in class. Almost all the work is done in groups, and most assignments are pretty easy to get at least a 90%.  Dr. Lo knows her stuff and is a great teacher and mentor.
I took 1215 and 1216 with Jenny, she is very friendly which is one of the most important aspects of being a professor or a teacher.

Jlo is a great professor, she's funny and you can tell she cares about her students. She only takes attendance on some days and she lets know you beforehand which ones. She also doesn't make groups present in person, you just have to compile a video and submit it. She was so great I made sure I got into one of her 1216 classes as well.

Professor is very nice and goes through the lecture material well. Very helpful and she'll help the best she can. Class is mainly group projects, but some are individual projects like doing SOLIDWORKS designs. Very easy class, work well in your group and show effort. Did a simple online presentation with discussion-based feedback at the end.

JLo is a very kind and encouraging professor! The assignments and grading are straightforward as long as you read the directions and double-check what you need to submit for each assignment. She answers emails pretty quick and gives good feedback. Learning MATLAB may be tricky if you've never coded before. Your group is also very important.

Jenny is very good at keeping students on track during their projects and has developed a format of teaching that works for her class. If you are not familiar with the basics of MATLAB, it may be difficult to follow her examples in class, so I would recommend reading through the powerpoint before going to class, but its not necessary.

ENGE 1215 was a great class! Jenny is a great professor and knows her job well. She gives great feedback and the lectures were meaningful. If you do your work and come to class, you will do completely fine in the class. Defiantly a GPA booster.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Jenny is extremely nice and gives amazing feedback on graded assignments. Grading is super forgiving and it's not hard to make a good grade in this class.

JLo is the reason I am staying an engineering major, she truly cares about her students and wants to see us succeed.  Responds to emails fast and gave me an extension when i had the flu. all of this class is graded on group projects, she makes groups at the beginning of the semester and ur with them the whole time so that can make or break it.
she's baller

Professor Lo was one of the best professors at VT, and she is so caring and paying attention on how students are doing. Any time that you ask her a question she tries her best to help you, even you can schedule times to talk to her that are not in the office hours dates.

There are a lot of group projects and you'll be with the same group for the entire semester. She does give in-class work days (some require attendance, while others are optional). At the end of every project, you'll fill out a form where you can anonymously provide feedback on your other teammates and let her know if someone slacked off

J Lo is a very nice professor but can be hard at grading sometimes.  1215 is a class that is just busy work and that is how the course is designed no matter who you have.  The group you get can make or break the class for you and I got an excellent group.  She is very good at responding to emails and assisting you if you have any questions.

I took her course for both ENGE 1215 and 1216. Her class structure is nice and straightforward. Everything has a clear rubric and she gives good feedback. A good portion of your grade hinges on group projects though, so be careful! This is not unique to her class though, this is for all ENGE 1216 classes. Very kind and quickly responds to emails.

I have come to the conclusion that Enge1215 and Enge1216 are just a month worth of work stretched to 3 months. It is nothing but useless and tedious busywork that has nothing to do with finding the right major for you. Jenny did her best but the class structure is just so horrible. Easy but useless class. Attendance required :(

Jenny was a great professor. She cares about her students, and will help you out if you ask. Most of the class is group work. Attendance is mandatory, there are assignment based on attendance. Overall good glass and is easy to pass.

JLo was the greatest, but GET A GOOD GROUP! This class is mainly group projects. I got an amazing group but this will make or break your grade. JLo is nice enough that if u had gourp issues she would try her best to fix. Show up and turn in work ON TIME and its and easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. Really cares about her students. Easy A as long as you have a decent group and the work gets done
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Lo was so nice and she makes her class easy to pass. You can tell she really cares about you and wants you to do well. She is always willing to help out!
She is very helpful and wants you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: She cares about the students and wants you to pass.
She is so organized
Jlo was a great teacher! Her class was online but she made it interactive and it felt like a regular class. The class is project based which I liked because I felt like I learned a lot.
Never had a problem with Jlo, she is amazing and always willing to help students when there's an issue. The class is made extremely easy as long as you have a good group
The class itself is easy because JLo makes it easy. Its only hard if you get a bad group for projects.

She's the best. Brings halloween candy for halloween and candy canes for Christmas! This class is literally just a grade booster for engineering kids. She is super nice and a very lenient grader. When she is not permitted to cancel class, she just makes it optional!! I am going to miss her!
robot teacher. fair and sticks to rubric. its like taking an online class. literally do ur work to the minimum and as long as it adheres to the rubric, you will pass with flying colors.

Group project was pretty easy even though it took a decent amount of time. Pretty lenient on grading. Have to actually study for the two tests, not too hard though. MatLab was pretty easy. Small group projects were also pretty easy and graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: It might just be the class but she did not really teach the information. It would be beneficial to have your own basic understanding of MATLAB script before taking this class. Offers clear grading criteria and there are a lot of group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: JLo is super nice and helpful and she really cares about her students. ENGE 1215 is a boring and annoying class but she makes it not as horrible
She is such a sweet lady. I had her for workshop, not lecture and she basically helped us through all the assignments making sure that we got them correct.

This lecture was pretty much useless... but it's required for engineers. Thus the lecture was boring. She is very helpful with advising and answers emails promptly. She offers little help with homework. Direction to the book and other materials is normal.
Compared to some of the other things ive heard about other engineering teachers shes a really good teacher. She explained the material well and gave us the feeling she wanted us to succeed.
I dont really see where all the horror stories come from as far as this class goes
Great class; awesome professor. Would recommend.
Great office hours; she was always there whenever I went over and was extremely helpful.
One of the best engineering professors at VT.  Explains things very well, and she wants to see you succeed.

JLo is a really decent prof to have for 1024. She explains everything well and will try to help you out. She's young so she knows whats goin on.... I think she's a little less strict than what the department tries to require - but still really fair. Expect a lot of work tho-but its just like that.

Great guy, cant hate on the class but I didn't find having the students teach the material that beneficial for anyone. Luckily, his canvas is super helpful and you learn most of the stuff for the test by doing the homeworks. Definitely an easy A, just use his canvas, follow rubrics, and put 2-3 days of light review for each test.
Intuitive lectures and examples, but the pacing for the class was kind of slow. He tends to go on tangents and teach things that aren't tested, but overall he is a good teacher.
Great professor. Explains concepts very clearly and gives helpful review material for exams. Definitely would take him again.

He was nice and helpful especially in office hours. I did not love the format of having the students teach the lectures so I did end up teaching myself what was on the study guides through the homework and lecture videos. No final just a project which was very nice. If you are taking this class in person I would recommend taking it with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm reviewing for STAT 3104. Overall really great professor. Has pretty organized notes and good lectures, and answers questions well. Workload is pretty low and tests were easy with extra credit. Grades fairly and getting an A is not too bad.
STAT 3104 - Loda was great. I found myself not studying for exams until the last minute but his example problems made everything clear. 10/10 professor
Just a chill guy. Great professor who cares about his students, explains things extremely well if you go to office hours
Super chill lecture setting, easy course work but tests can be somewhat difficult.

Very fun and respectful professor that clearly cares about how well his students do in the class. None of the assignments or group projects were rigorous or time-consuming. Tests were very easy and exactly like the assignments given or done during class

Easy class if you stay up to date on your assignments, he gives you a grace period to make up missing ones and there aren't that many of them. Content is also fairly easy even if you don't like coding. Groups present Tuesday of every week so you won't really learn anything from that, but attendance counts.

Dr. Loda is a super kind professor, and knowledgeable about the subject. However, he has students teach the lessons at the beginning of each week. I found this extremely unhelpful so I only attended lecture on Thursdays when he would go over material - even with this, I expect a solid A in the course.

Super chill guy and chill class! The first part of the week a group will present slides on a topic, next class he would go over the topic again with in depth examples. Homework is due once a week and if you come to class you get ec. Exams are half mc and half project but I thought they were doable and comparable to examples he does in class!

I'm reviewing for STAT 3104 "Probability and Distributions", which is not listed above. Decent professor, but very condescending when seeking help or clarity after class. The TA was more helpful and respectful. Textbook was very helpful, so was office hours which again with the TA are highly recommended.
Fair professor. Fun class, would take again.

Dr. Loda goes through the material at a good pace and listens to class feedback. If you put the effort in and communicate with him, you'll get a good grade. While attendance wasn't mandatory, it matters to your performance!
Super helpful, very easy to ask him questions and very happy to help you out.

Professor Loda is great at explaining things, although the class is very difficult. You cannot coast in this class, you will have to study especially as the material gets harder. Tests are pretty hard, there's an in-person quiz every week and a few assignments throughout the semester. Would take him again but I would have to try harder to get a B.

Undoubtedly the best professor I have had in my entire undergraduate experience. Very reasonable and efficient in his homework assignments and exams, although exams were on the harder side. Offered extra credit and stressed conceptual understanding while keeping formalisms accessible. Willing to explain as much as a student is interested.

I learned a lot in 3006 and appreciated the real world application of statistics concepts in both lectures and assignments. Professor Loda was very helpful in answering any questions I had and the workload was very reasonable. Assignments had one day grace period. Overall, I would highly recommend taking a stat class with Professor Loda if you can.
I had him spring 2021 for bio stats so during covid, although lectures were online he made it super clear and easy to understand R, which can be hard to do imo

Mr. Loda teaches the stats portion of this class. He's pretty good at teaching the lecture material and giving assignments that reinforce what you learn in class. Nothing is too difficult really, you just have to put effort in the HWs, in-class assignments, and tests. Just show up to class and you'll be fine
He is nice and willing to help, but grades extremely harshly. Directions for exam reports are unclear. The TA grades exam reports and will easily take meaningless points off.
Difficult grader and made things unclear

Loda is a very good professor and nice guy overall, he was willing to work with students who needed help or clarification on assignments. Attendance technically wasn't mandatory, but it does benefit to attend.

Great professor, he teaches the stats section of this class pretty well, but there's nothing too difficult in the stats portion of this class (lot of it is similar to AP Statistics). Sometimes has weekly quizzes to test you on the content taught in the previous week but no HWs, which is nice. Also some opportunities for extra credit in the class

Prof. Loda taught in a very easy to understand way, especially for someone who had previously struggled understanding statistics. His lectures were always intuitive, and he was very personable in his office hours. Each Friday, there was an in-class assignment, which helped me follow along very well, and the homework was based off of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really nice and always available for help. Attendance was not mandatory but if you went to class enough you got extra credit. There was a group project where everyone was given a lesson to teach, which kind of sucked. It was tough to have to teach the class but overall it ended up being fine. He also went over all lessons at the end of each week.

This class requires coding but the professor is always willing to help and answers any questions quickly. he reversed the way it was taught this semester by students getting in groups and teaching a new lesson each class but it helped to learn and he always lectured some with the students.

I loved Professor Loda. He was an amazing professor. However, this semester he changed the structure of our class and made the students teach. I don't think this was an effective way of learning the material considering we are students, not professors. Hopefully he will change it for y'all in the fall.
Overall a great Professor. Your class is literally just paying attention to other students presentations. Show up to the lectures and you will be fine

Justin is a great guy. He posts his video lectures but if you show up to class you get more intel on the quizzes and exams. He's the definition of a dad and is always willing to help students, you just have to ask questions when you're confused, or just to clarify things since this is a code based class. As long as you do his notes you'll be fine!

professor loda is a great guy! this class was pretty easy; justin explains things effectively and i felt like learning to use R is a good tool to have for the future. make sure you show up to class and do the homework. there are only two midterms and a final but they are not difficult and he is always open to answering questions and helping.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor. He was very clear and consistent with grading. He holds office hours every week and is more than willing to help students. His class made me like statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Loda's class is not very test heavy with only two midterms. He is very respectful of students and quickly replies to students emails over grading or content concerns. His prerecorded lectures are easy to comprehend and are enough to fully complete the homework with. Homeworks were due weekly but were fairly simple.

I had her for 1105 and if you can avoid taking her as your teacher please do! she talks in a mono tone the whole entire class. She also likes to get people in trouble so beware! she got multiple kids in trouble for using AI without real proof and would go out of her way to seek ways to get people in trouble which is very odd. shes evi1
Good Professor! A bit of extra effort is involved to study because her tests are detailed, but she's willing to help. She wrote me a good recommendation letter too

she's fine, all you got to do is watch the video and do the homework before class starts. It's honestly not bad, she gives so many opportunity to ask questions (office hours, uta office hours, zoom meetings, after class, etc.) she does use iclicker and have group activity lessons that are graded every class so realistically class is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. lipscomb writes the easiest tests in alllll of 1106, im not kidding when i say that it's a cheat code to have her. If you study by practicing the study guides SHE GIVES YOU, it will be such an easy class to pass. The annoying thing is, yes, you do have to watch the videos on your own. But you do that no matter what 1105 class you take.

Dr. Lipscomb is kind, but the lectures are often unclear and not very helpful. Most of the learning comes from teaching yourself outside of class. If you fall behind, it becomes very difficult to recover. This course requires a lot of independent effort

mid teacher 
taught myself everything 
had to go to class though, which was annoying !!!!!!!
Sweet lady, tests are pretty straight forward but still difficult because it is a lot of information. TA's did a great job. Sometimes she will add a curve.

So miserably mind-numbing. You'd walk into class after pushing through the lesson videos, only to have her read off the slides and introduce pointless group activities where only one person looked at the material ahead of time. Interesting material, but so content-dense it becomes exhausting after a point.
get help right off the bat

Honestly, I have nothing but good things to say about Dr. Lipscomb, her lectures were good, her study guides were fantastic, and her tests were fairly easy. I finished with a 95 in the course and I fully believe it was because I had her as a professor. If you have the opportunity to take Lipscomb I highly recommend

I really loved Dr. Lipscomb, and actually took her for both 1105 and 1106. Her lectures and grading were consistent and I felt I really learned. She also was just very kind and caring, especially in office hours. You'll know what to expect with her, she's the best bio teacher here (I say this as a current bio tutor). She made me love the subject.
This is a challenging class, but if you take it seriously, it's very manageable. Make friends with your TA, and you will be good!

I ended up taking her for 1105 and 1106. I just watched and took notes on the recorded lectures ahead of time. She has in class IClicker questions that are pretty easy as long as you come to class having watched the lectures. I used her study guides, the homework, and the IClickers to study before tests and I did great on all of them.

Dr. Lipscomb was an alright prof, but there was SO MUCH to do before every class, if you don't have a strong foundation in biology, a lot of the topics are going to be confusing. Just make sure you take detailed notes on the videos and give yourself more time to watch them than you think you need.
She is very nice and cares about her students. The course is pretty demanding, but she does a good job of giving you plenty of resources for the test. Tests aren't awful as well
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was really nice and good at explaining concepts. As for the class, there is a lot of outside work (taking notes), and in class there is a quick recap and group assignments. I disliked this setup b/c its a lot to do outside of class and some stuff doesn't get covered in the lecture. For the tests, its REALLY important to study or you'll fail!!!

LOTS of content to go over, most you learn outside of class through videos before the lecture then Lipscomb repeats everything said almost verbatum in the videos. Lectures were very clarifying though. Group activities in each class, but wasn't related to tests. Tests were repeats of HW and in class quizzes. Put in the work and it should be easy.

Very kind, but I don't think I said a single word to her and I didn't miss a single lecture. You get more help and answers from your TAs because the class size is so large. Overall, very nice professor and clear teaching. Tests are all multiple choice and not too difficult if you listen, take notes, and study.
Class is mostly PowerPoints, but they are uploaded online before class. She is very kind and understanding.

Professor Lipscomb is a caring instructor who wants students to understand the content. While the lectures can be dry, her exam reviews, practice tests, and unstuck ai-powered study tools make for effective prep. Attendance is required but manageable.

Overall Professor Lipscomb knew her stuff, but I really struggled with her teaching style. Her lectures were long and boring. The tests weren't horribly difficult, and some were more challenging than others. We had to take notes before class and she pretty much just said what the notes said and didn't clarify many points. She did offer extra credit

As long as you take notes on the prerecorded lectures and do the homework( to understand it), you will be able to do good on the in class participation and that will help your grade. It is comprised of 4 tests including the final where everything is straightforward. I wasn't a fan of the activities because you couldn't really prepare.

Pretty good teacher overall. Her lectures are a bit slow and don't always cover everything needed. She hosts review sessions that are helpful. Pretty test-heavy class for the most part. If you know how to study efficiently, you will be fine. Overall, she is very sweet and understanding. Would take again.
Avoid. Extreme test heavy. Seemed lost during class, and gave incorrect information. Overwhelming, unclear. Worst science teacher ive ever had.
Lectures were just very slow and boring. Test were relatively easy to get As on if you studied enough.

all of the notes are taken out of class by lecture videos and the classes are mandatory even though she's just going over the notes you already took which wasn't very helpful for actually learning the material. she did give two extra credit opportunities which was nice. if you miss a class, you will get a 0% on the activity but there are two drops

Good professor overall. Iclicker questions for participation in class but they are helpful for learning material. Group activities every class. Lectures are kinda boring and you have to watch the pre lecture videos to get the full lesson. Tests aren't that bad. Would recommend.

Be ready to teach yourself this class. Lots of work outside of class to prepare, then in class is used for a lecture, quiz, and activity. Make friends with your TA; they are the ones who grade everything. Tests are more definition-based than application-based.
Dr. Lipscomb has a very effective teaching style. If you pay attention to the lectures, do the homework before class, and go to office hours, you should get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super easy tests lectures are pretty boring but she does a good job on keeping your prepares. Very similar class structure to 1105

Dr. Lipscomb's lecture slideshows lay out everything you need to know for the test. You have to study a lot to earn a good grade on the tests, but the information you need to know is clearly outlined in the lectures. I made quizlets after every lecture and mainly studied those.

bio is just a hard test heavy class but if you do the work, use her study guides and at least pay attention to either the recorded lecture or the in person lecture you will pass. Also use the TA's because you can check you activity answers with them so you're more likely to get A/Bs on them - which i didn't do in 1105.

Inclass she has a curated ppt for big topics-so by taking notes prior (video lectures) you can add any missed pts (take ur time to get the detail in). Attendance isn't mandatory but the clicker questions (used in tests) and activities are graded. 
test-heavy, but the study guide/practice tests/activities/hw helps a lot. A lot of outside studying!

Her lectures were good. You can get a good grade if you take time to read the textbook and study the lecture notes. I didn't study for her class and ended with a B-. She's chill. Mandatory attendance with in-person iClicker questions and classwork codes.

She is a sweet and understanding person, I slept through my final, I would have FAILED the class and I RAN to where the exam was being taken and she heard my entire situation. If you want advice from me it would be to study the clickers because the exams are a little harder than you'd expect and definitely look at her exam review sheets.

Professor Lipscomb honestly gets a bad rap because biology is naturally a difficult course. That being said, you definitely have several opportunities to interact with the material before tests. Getting an A in her class is totally doable so long as you practice flashcards and online Quizlets former students made (This is my best tip for passing!!)

She was kind and wanted us to understand the material. Some topics she could've spent more time explaining. No attendance grade, but iClickers and in class assignments are for a grade so I wouldn't recommend skipping. She curves the tests a bit, and make sure you review iClickers before the tests some questions come right off the ones from class.

The class isn't too bad, the study guides posted before each test give a really good overview of what you should know. It is important that you come to class prepared and take notes on the lecture videos.

Dr. Lipscomb is a very sweet lady, and she makes herself available outside of class. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is in your best interest to attend class for iclickers and activities. I did not personally watch videos or read the textbook because her class reviews were well put together. Lectures tend to be boring.

Very sweet woman. This class is very hard first semester as there is a lot of reading involved and the material is extremely specific but also not applicable to many majors. STAY ON TOP OF THE WORK do the homework and readings and pay attention in class and you'll be fine. Tests are curved our final was curved 6 points. Averages aren't released.

The class is very quick paced and class consists of mostly reading off the lecture slides. She does curve the exams, which is nice, and while attendance doesn't count for a grade there are iclickers and graded activities to do in class. The tests take some questions right from the iclickers and practice quizzes.

There was a textbook for this class, but I only used it once. Mainly for personal use and if you need clarification on topics, so I wouldn't recommend renting or buying one. She is a nice professor. There is an activity at the end of class with a group. DO watch the lecture videos because they help a lot with retaining information.
Uses iclicker in class so while attendance is not mandatory it does benefit your grade. Overall good teacher when it comes to reveiw and is responsive to questions in class and emails.
Class was a little difficult for an elective, but just show up, do the classwork, read the notes, you'll be fine. Professor Lipscomb is very nice and she'll happily answer any questions you have.

Her lectures are basically reading off a powerpoint, but she's very caring and accessible outside of class. She provides exam reviews on Zoom, practice tests, and test review worksheets that are very helpful. The TAs in her class are great as well. You do have to go to class to get an iClicker grade, but she's very understanding.
Lectures are usually spent reading off the powerpoint, however if you do your work and readings outside of class it will make the content much more understandable and enjoyable.

Professor Lipscomb is super sweet. I'm pretty bad at listening in lectures but I succeeded in this class by watching the lecture videos the night before. She is super accommodating and really wants to help you. Take it with her and be prepared to do a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: definitely watch the lecture videos or read the txbk. her lectures are reviews and the iclickers are easy but if you're like me and can't learn from listening to a lecture then you have to work on your own. tests aren't as bad as people say they are, just study adequately (I use outlines) and she even has review sessions.

She has a required textbook but she provides an online pdf version. There is iclickers in this class but you can use the online version. If you take the notes ahead of time and look over the objectives before class you'll be fine. Tests are mostly straight forward and she provides study guides before each one.

Must attend class for iClicker questions. If you watch the video lectures you dont need to read textbook. Know terminology for the lectures and you will be set for exams. Exams are reasonable and slight curve given.

Lipscomb is nice, but you basically do all of the learning outside of the classroom, so the time you are in class feels like a waste. Her tests are unnecessarily in depth and difficult if you don't know the minute specifics of certain random topics. You get two attempts on all homework and tests are barely curved compared to other classes.

She is very helpful and is almost always available if you need to reach her. She genuinely cares about her students and is overall a sweet lady. Her lectures can be a little boring, but she tries her best to make them enjoyable. You also must be ready to spend a lot of time outside of class watching and taking notes on the lecture videos.

Tests were very much applied, which made them more difficult. She did a good job of explaining the materials on the slides, but you had to apply it yourself. Tons of videos and work outside of class. Class time was review of what you did on your own.

Nice lady, and relatively good teaching style. Explains the subject a lot, tho will read off the powerpoint. Very helpful but you HAVE to ask her questions. Tests are hard and she barely curves, but if you work hard you will get a good grade. Save yourself time on readings by searching up the lesson subject on youtube for 5 min videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice lady but not a great teacher. Her class set up is not for me. I don't like that she skims over material in class and requires you to watch multiple pre-recorded lectures outside of class. Her exams are also fairly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 90% of the material is on you to know before the lecture which is a format I dislike. i prefer to be taught (what im paying for) then study for tests not learn everything myself. There is a homework quiz and an in class activity every class and iclickers.(you can drop 2 of each) her lectures are confusing and her slides even more so.very hard tests

Dr. Lipscomb is a caring professor but her class is the hardest I've ever taken. You're expected to learn everything outside of class and spend hours reading textbooks and watching lectures. Attendance is mandatory for i clickers and in-class assignments but ultimately if you don't do good on her extremely hard exams you'll fail the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is a sweet lady, always willing to clarify anything you are confused on. The only con I have is that she mainly reads off the powerpoints and will only clarify a few things. If you put in the work, an A is achievable. She will tell you what's on/ not on the test if you ask (I highly recommend doing so). Study in advance, prepare for iclickers.

Dr. Lipscomb's lectures were fast paced and not well explained. I ended up having to take a W in her fall class and then retaking it during the winter "semester." Her tests are very hard. She is not very flexible when it comes to finding time to meet with her for office hours. If you skip lecture, it is hard to catch up with the material.
Extremely tough professor. Passable class for some but tests are some of the hardest in the department. Daily classwork and homework. Tests are incredibly in-depth.

I had Lipscomb for BIOL1105 and her class was the worst class Ive ever taken. Shes an incredibly caring and sweet woman but my god the exams are brutal. She makes them incredibly in depth to where you pretty much better have every single lecture memorized
posts lecture videos to watch outside of class. does close to nothin during lelctures. tests are extremely hard and we usually had the lowest test averages of any general bio class at tech

The class itself is not hard if you study. review the notes because in class she is no help. textbook is not necessary, lecture video alone is enough. I would only go over my notes the night before a test and didnt do as bad as id expect.

As far as an introductory class goes, Dr. Lipscomb was a decent teacher. Unfortunately, if you do not have an outstanding memory, this class is going to be difficult. Obviously the more you study, the more you remember, but some topics were left unclear and some test topics came up that had never been covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are the hardest thing that she can possible give. The best advice I can give for this class is to review after every single class and to do a lot of studying on your own because normally she really just reads off a powerpoint. When it comes to Iclicker questions you need watch the lesson video before class or it can be pretty difficult.

Professor Lipscomb is what I would describe as someone who you can tell is passionate about what they are teaching but do not exactly know how to teach it. Tests are very hard and a lot of studying is required but you can tell she tries. She does have some zoom study sessions that help out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Lipscomb is really nice, her class is straightforward. you get multiple attempts at homework, she hosts review sessions, and curves some exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The most boring teacher you will ever have. She reads off her powerpoints and if iClickers were not a thing, it would be useless to even show up to her class. Her tests are harder than any other bio teacher. We also have way to many iClicker questions off content she has not gone over.

I am no longer in Dr. Lipscombs class but I cry when I hear she is the one narrating a lecture for my current biology class. She is clearly reading off of notes and does not explain anything. She talks so fast I have to put it in 0.75 speed and even then I have to pause every 30 seconds. Honestly the worst lectures, I am so frustrated taking notes.

She has the most monotone, croaky voice that sounds like nails on a chalkboard. No camera on lockdown, but it doesn't matter because you'll fail anyway
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Lipscomb was a sweet lady but her teaching style is not for me. Lectures consisted of her just reading off the powerpoint and its not enthusiastic so they are somewhat boring and hard to follow along with.

Dr. Lipscomb is a very sweet lady. She clearly cares about each and every one of her students. She also presents the course material clearly so that it's easy to understand as long as you put the work in. She will work with you if you contact her about makeup tests or extensions. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Lipscomb is very nice, but I found her teaching difficult for my learning style. It may just be the way Biology 1105 is structured.

Nice lady, but she just speaks from the powerpoints. She doesnt give any broader view of the information. Also, if you have a question, shell just repeat whats stated in the PowerPoint. We have iClicker questions but she never explains them. Be prepared for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had her for 1105, and she was pretty good. She did a good job explaining complicated material. She is super nice, and accessible outside of class. There are pre-recorded lectures that you take notes on before class, and during class, she does a 45-minute review of the lesson. Then we go into groups to do a free-response assignment.

reviews.comment: She gets a bad rep., but is a pretty solid professor. She's super willing to help, it's just a matter of you reaching out to her. You'll have homework every night of class due, but it's multiple choice and isn't bad. She uses iClicker and you get put into breakout rooms w/ the TA after her short lecture, so you need to go to class.

reviews.comment: Her class is time consuming. She purposely makes everyone's life miserable by giving tests that are worth 70% of your grade and puts things that she doesn't even know. Don't be fooled by the positive comments, as she put them herself. She doesn't even explain what is covered instead she reads what's on the slide and moves on. Bio sucks cuz of her.

reviews.comment: Great professor in BIOL department. Enjoyed her in class lectures. Tests were very dependent on her in class lectures, so make sure you attend and pay attention.

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Lipscomb's class for 1105 too and she was really good. 1106 has more relatable subject matter as you start talking about bigger picture health concepts (really helpful for pre-med students.) She is very thorough and will answer questions in class or office hours. She specifies what material is on tests and what is just extra info. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice lady, but teaches from a powerpoint. Doesn't engage with students while teaching, just hammers information straight from presentation then makes you take a mini-quiz on it. Lectures are long and hard to stay interested in (that's what she said).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very sweet and easy to understand. iClickers quizzes are used in class as well as group activity work for a grade. Outside of class there is A LOT of work because you have to watch the video lectures and take notes. She is very fair but the class is difficult and you have to work hard to pass. She will not bump up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Lipscomb was a great professor. Her class can be hard, especially exams. The second half of the semester is definitely easier than the first. Attending lectures is essential, and helps boost your grade with IClickers. Overall, her class was solid, tests were hard, but her office hours as well as the TA's were very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Her voice can be quite dry and monotone when lecturing, but if you study the lectures and follow her review guide then you should be good to pass. Bio 1106 is based on anatomy/physiology, ecology, and plants so its different material from Bio 1105. Her tests were easy and very straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is hard. There are classwork assignments and iclicker points every class, so attendance is mandatory for the 15% classwork grade. Tests are very hard but with studying you can do well. Her lectures are very very boring, and long. She will NOT round up grades whatsoever. I ended with a 79.9 (no joke) and she wouldn't round it to an 80 for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring lectures, but she is willing to help. The tests are more difficult than other BIOL 1106 classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mary is my HOME GIRL!!! I love her so much!!! She is so nice and funny. I went to her office hours once the first week of school and she remembered my name for the rest of my time in her classes and even after when I see her on campus she still says hi! Loved her class and if you actually take time to learn the material the class is not hard.
If you are like me who was just looking for an easy gen ed class this may not be the class for you. I really struggled with this class and all the homework and the tests were awful.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very nice person but tests don't always reflect the material and it's a difficult course. Difficult to pay attention during class also.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I found Professor Lipscomb so be extremely boring. She has a very monotone voice that makes it nearly impossible to stay awake in class. Her teaching method consists of reading off the PowerPoint and giving frequent quizzes (pretty much every day- a homework quiz before class and an in-class quiz). Tests weren't terrible but require studying.

Every night before class you are assigned a reading and have to complete this with a quiz by midnight. The next day she lectures for about 45 minutes on what you read - her powerpoint slides are straight from the textbook. Classwork everyday for credit and clicker questions. She's VERY dry as a lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is an active-classroom format, basically meaning you teach yourself the material. You watch online lectures and take a timed 8-minute quiz the night before class. She reviews the material for 20 min. during lecture and asks iClicker q's, so take good notes! The TA's are more helpful than she is. One of the TA's held helpful review sessions.

This class is pretty much a self-taught class.  You go through the lecture videos and take notes and a short quiz before coming to class every day and then Professor Lipscomb does a brief overview of the Lesson, which isn't always very helpful.  Every class is the same: short lecture & group classwork.  The classwork is tedious and long.

Her voice is really annoying, yes, but all it is is listening to lectures online before class. Then she goes over it in class for thirty minutes which I never listened to, and then we did a group activity. Take good notes and look at the study guides the TA's make and you'll do fine.

Absolute terrible teacher, the wording of her online quiz questions as well as test questions are meant to trick you. 010 WOULD NOT RECOMMEND.  Tests definitely do not accurately represent what you know in the class. I was very excited to take this class because it's on my favorite subject matter but she ruined it for me 100%.
Hard class, she is very monotone, does not do much to teach you other than reread the power point in class that she put on scholar.

The class wasn't bad. I used the textbook for homework and studying. Her powerpoints have a lot of useful information. The exam was half cumulative and half new material, but the old material was ALMOST identical to the previous tests we had taken. She lets you keep all old tests so use them to study for the final!

Dr. Lipscomb is very nice and teaches well.  She truly wants her students to do well. Tests are HARD though, so study hard. Class is easy and she offers a lot of hw and clicker points to help your grade.

her lectures can get boring but she is so nice and willing to help. if you don't understand something go to her office hours and she will work with you until you understand it. don't waste your time doing the study guides--half of the stuff isnt on the test. homework is so easy. go to class to get iclicker points and take notes for test.

SO BORING. Her lectures are incredibly boring and she has this awful monotone voice that makes you wanna poke yourself in the eye. You have to go to class for attendance points and you need to read the book. Her test are kind of difficult and semi tricky. Shes very nice but I would suggest another teacher.

her tests are very hard so be prepared to study a lot to get a B. shes really nice but her lectures are very boring but you should really attend them because she gives out class participation randomly and Iclicker questions for a grade. I would take it if you NEED it but other than that you may wanna stay away

make sure you read the book- or at least go over the chapter outlines they have online that comes with the textbook- she's nice and helpful, but the class is boring and hard- the amount of terminology you have to memorize in such a short time is unbelievable

Shes extremely fair, all of her tests are scantron and there are no surprises with test content- everything is  pretty straight forward. I never opened my book and got an A. just show up cause she takes attendance and take good notes

She is very nice but her lectures are very boring and it is difficult to pay attention. She doesn't speak very loudly either. Attendance points are given through iclickers, and her powerpoints are online but are not very helpful for studying for the tests. To get a good test grade you have to read the book.
yessss

Her lectures can be extremely boring at times, but most of what she discusses is on the test. you MUST read the book thoroughly to do well on the tests. Attendance is kind of mandatory because she uses iclicker for participation points
Terrible professor, cannot teach, isn't reasonable -- terrible at assigning grades - does not think of student's benefit regardless of situation

Her lectures were mediocre, but she is a really sweet person once you get to talk to her. I sat in the front of her class both semesters and we ended up becoming good friends. She will help you with whatever you need, and she is very straightforward on what is going to be on her test. Just study and you will get an A

She is a very nice lady, but she sticks to her rules! No extra credit or make-ups. Her tests are pretty hard. You will have to devote a lot of study time to her class. The homework and attendence grades help your grade; they are why i passed, so do them.

A pretty easy class. You do need to go to class for attendance and iclicker questions but it won't affect your grade too much if you don't go to everyone. The class isn't very exciting but the tests are do-able. I expect a B in the class.
I am currently in her class as of fall 2008.  It is very boring and she has a weird, annoying voice.  Class attendance is mandatory because she makes students buy iclickers now.

She is so mean. I was in a class of 500 and the majority were getting a C- or worse and she still wouldn't do any extra credit or throw a curve at all! She treated it like we were all biology majors and loved the subject. She is SO boring. Her tests were material from the book, but usually that meant about 80 pages of text to memorize.

She doesn't post her notes so attendance is mandatory.  Her voice is really grating and her tests are harder than they should be for what she covers in class.  I have heard that if you have her for ecology in the summer she's very nice and easy.
I've only been to one class, but I have an A in it. Read the chapters in the book and fill out the study guides, make sure you do the homework and extra credit and you'll be fine.
She is an awesome teacher. She goes into depth about everything and repeats things so you know what is important. If you go to class and do the reveiws you should have a guranteed A

Most of her tests are based off the book so they can get pretty hard, gives extra credits and the homeworks before each test so they help bump up your grade. There are 4 tests and a final which basically make up your grade.

Class was a piece of cake. Way easier than Ap Bio in high school. All the questions on the test come right form the notes she gives in class. You never have to even open the book...well except for the very few hmwk assignments and she DOES give extra credit
the tests are very different from the reviews.

The class is probably the most boring and worthless thing I have ever sat through in my life.  To do well you really just need to teach yourself.  She's a nice lady but between her monotone voice and her complete inability to teach, you really have to do a lot of work outside of class.

I didnt think that this class was all that hard, the notes were prectically fed to you via powerpoint and the tests came sraight from the notes which came from the book for the most part. Not that hard.

Lipscomb is a good teacher, and she's able to easily get her point across if you simply attend class. Reading out of the book and not going to class the WRONG choice. If you just take the hour out of your day to go to class, you NEVER need to read the book. Everything on the tests are straight from her lectures. Don't make yourself work too hard.

I liked Prof. Lipscomb. She was really helpful and nice to me. Her class is kind of boring, but try not to skip the class. Sometimes she gives students small quizzes without saying anything before. Her test is pretty much from the book, so if you read the textbook, you will be fine on the test.

she is kind of boring and her voice is annoying. I never went to class except to take tests and still got a B. she does give you random quizes and inclass assignments though so going to class is kinda important. she gives extra credit and her tests are mainly from the book. Its an easy B class.

She is not a good teacher, but her class is not hard. Going to class doesn't do a whole lot except reinforce what is in the book. If you prepare yourself well for the tests you can get an A in the class.

her class isnt that bad, a lil boring but overall she makes it so that if you miss a class you really dont miss anything. Her tests are based on the book so they're really not that bad, as long as u look at the book.

This is definately not an easy class to take if Biology is not your major! You may think that it will be interesting and an easy A to fulfill your Area 4 Requirement, but it's NOT! It's a lot of information and you HAVE to go to class every day if you want to think about passing. I really struggled with it, and regretted picking it.
Avoid taking her class if at all possible.  BORING teacher, BORING class. Her lectures don't make sense so don't bother going to class. I go to all the classes and still don't do well on the tests.

again, her voice is extremely annoying. it reminds me of a goat. its easy to get a good grade, even if you dont actually go to class. she did, however accuse me of cheating, so ive pretty much lost all respect for her. and she will not make any attempt to connect with you on a personal level, even if you need help.

her voice is incredibly annoying. her posture is terrible, and i can't help but space out everytime im in her class. she is a really nice lady and everything, but i just dont enjoy her class too much.

HER VOICE IS SO ANNOYING!!!! if you have a problem with listening to people that get quite then loud then wobbly then cough dont take this class.  i went to the lectures the first week and haven't been since... still get good grades because of the study guides

Her voice is monotone but if you can get past that you'll be fine. She knows her information very well. Tests are multiple choice from the study guides and Notes in class. She offers bonus quizes sometimes. Shes always willing to meet with you during office hours if you need.

She is a good teacher. Just pay attention to the lecture slides and take notes in class.  Tests come straight from the slides in class. She even gives out study guides with everything you need to know from each chapter. She does good with the material she is given and knows her stuff :)

Although she is boring, her class is EXTREMELY EASY. Whoever said she isn't clear about the material is obviously not talking about the same woman. She gives study guides for EVERY exam, along with extra credit quizzes that can boost your average up to 20 points. EASY GPA BOOSTER, TAKE HER CLASS

ok shes not the greatest. her voice is kind of annoying but she does know what shes talking about. shes very helpful if you go talk to her. her tests can be kind of hard. get an old one from a friend so you have an idea. study the book too and the cd helps some. shes not bad but i wouldnt reccomend

To be fair she does know her info, but yes shes incredibly boring. The tests arent giveaways, they arent that bad either, & she does offer extra credit quizzes (major help!). You may be as well off just reading the book. If you are going to class, make sure you caffeinate first

Man this woman is a horrible teacher-first she's boring boring boring and her test are hard- the first test avgs are low, she'll tell you to not worry because they'll go up-- oh she lies, they actually decreased in both classes that i took- she always sounds like she's gonna cry or nervous-
She is the worst teacher I have ever had in my life.  All I have to say to her is learn how to talk right with out sounding like you are about to cry. All in all Mary Libscome SUCKS AS A TEACHER
yea she is basically BUNNZZZZZIES!
None of the stuff she goes over in class is even on the test so it is basically a waste of time to attend. You are better off reading the book than listening to her ramble on for 3 hours a week.

This guy didn't show up for class for 6 weeks in a row, not even kidding. He didn't tell us our grade for what we had until december 8th (2 days before the last day of classes). it was an easy class, but it was also loads of bs
Very laid back class, just show up sometimes and do the projects and it is an easy A.
Professor Dandridge is such a chill guy, easy and fun class

Class is kind of boring sometimes, but Professor Dandridge is a cool guy and genuinely interested in cinema. Super easy grader and very nice, but awful at responding to emails. If you need something, talk to him in person or go to his office hours. Attendance is technically mandatory, but it doesn't matter a lot.

Prof Dandridge was a cool teacher. I did feel like he missed ALOT of class which was ashamed because his classes were always fun, I felt like we cancelled class more often than we had it. I also felt like his grading was really weird. There were no guidelines or rubrics on how things were graded so it was hard to predict what he wanted to see
This was the easiest class ever, but I learned nothing. We got to watch 1/2 of a lot of movies though!

This was one of the worst organized classes I have ever taken. He doesn't answer emails EVER and his TA would take a few points off of every assignment and the only comment would be "good job" or something along those lines. Although this is a class many people take as a pathway, it's horribly put together so I would avoid it.

I have no complaints about Professor Madsen himself and he clearly cared about our learning as well as making improvements to the course from feedback. However, the course structure/design was painful. Not enough time was given to complete lab reports and the amount of work required was excessive for a 1 credit hour course.
Homework is INTENSE
You have you teach yourself.  But his tests are so ridiculously easy that it's nothing.
No Comments
Be prepared to teach yourself the class.  Doesn't explain anything he writes on the board and disregards questions that are asked in class.

Dr Lucero did not cultivate an environment of respect; it felt like she looked down on students for asking questions. She expected everyone to already understand the topics and moved quickly through the content. Lectures were essentially the textbook copied onto slides, with no demonstrations. I wouldn't take it if you haven't taken AP physics.

She is not as bad of a person/teacher as people say she is, but I will say if you didn't take calc or physics in hs, you NEED to teach it to yourself (i recommend khan academy or organic chem tutor). She is great if you take advantage of office hours/tutoring but she is dealt a rough hand with the content load.

While her lectures may seem confusing, her office hours help clear everything up! She also has at least one extra credit problem on each exam (sometimes two or more), she wants everyone to succeed and as long as you put effort in you're guaranteed a grade you want.

Dr. Lucero is really nice and wants her students to succeed. Her tests aren't awful as long as you do the homework and practice tests. She teaches much better in her office hours and review sessions than in class. There are a lot of places to get help, whether it be from her, her TA, or the tutoring.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really liked ISC as a course, but Dr. Lucero made it difficult to enjoy. Does not explain any content in a way that is easy for anyone to understand, even if they have learnt the topics being taught before. Often wrong when going through a problem, but gets incredibly defensive if anyone mentions it. Doesn't seen to know the topics she is teaching.
She is very nice and helpful but does not explain things well for a first time learner.

She assumes everyone in the class has already taken AP Calculus, so if you didn't, be prepared to completely learn the content on your own. She does give great partial credit and some bonus problems on tests, so it's still possible to do well  ---  but it's going to be difficult.

If you haven't taken Calc 1 and 2 yet you are going to have a terribly difficult time passing because she doesn't go over concepts well at all. I took AP Calc BC in High school and she confused me on topics I already know.

Pretty boring lecture, just goes over slides the entire time. Gives good feedback if you ask questions but you have to participate if you really want to learn. Doesn't give terribly difficult homework or tests and is good at answering questions out of class.

This is a tough class and tough professor graded mostly around three essays. Especially online the lecture could be difficult to engage with and follow.
