That being said, Luther is incredibly caring and will help you. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. It brought my grade from a C- to an A. He will help you immensely. He is very caring.

Don't take his async class. His class is out of only 100 points and he waits to put the last 50% on the day grades are due. You have to read a lot and really dive deep into the readings and write papers explaining your understanding, way too hard for an async class tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Luther is a very good professor and gives very in-depth lectures on a broad range of material that will help you in your later higher-up classes. However, be advised that this is a theory course, not a geopolitical analysis class, and a lot of the theory can be at the graduate-student level. As such, you should be attending every lecture.

Luther is a great instructor. His classes can be quite dense due to the focus and interaction on the theoretical level. Reading the material is the best way to follow along, as the lectures can be beneficial to your final paper. With Luther, what you put in - is what you get.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Luther really cares about his students, and puts the time in to make sure that everyone feels respected in the class. He gives really good feedback on his assignments, and his class has really prepared me for other IR classes ill take in the future. I highly recommend taking his class, just make sure you are ready to read and be challenged!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He's super chill and really cares about his student's ability to understand his material and grades pretty fair. He assigns a lot of reading but goes over it in class if you don't understand it. He's a great professor and would really recommend anyone take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Wonderful prof. Truly cares about her students. Very flexible w exam rescheduling and late assignments. Once you get the hang of her lecture and exam format, her class is very low effort!

I like Bergamasco, but it is hard to succeed in her class. Her lectures are overwhelmingly long, and slides are so packed with information that it's hard to take notes during class time. Tests cover huge amounts of information, and questions are purposefully written to be misleading and punishing. She also accepts no criticism.

Dr. Bergamasco is a really kind prof but not the best teacher. Grades are based on attendance to certain lectures, pre- test practice quizzes, a final group project, an ec opportunity, and primarily tests. If you're good at memorizing you'll do good in this class and if you like your grade on the first three you don't have to take the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've taken a few of her classes and they are very lecture based. Theres a lot of memorization that has to happen to pass her class. The final project is easy and there is extra credit given at the end if you want to do it. She is easy to talk to and will help you if you need it.

Wasn't a bad class, but it can be very boring. Tests are based on materials from slideshows so its all memorization based and relatively easy. You need to study early since you have to memorize 400+ slides per exam. The final project is easy and doesn't take too long to complete. She has a thick accent which can be hard to understand sometimes.
She was hard to understand, and her lecture topics were long and boring. She would give 100+ slide decks and the tests were memorized tidbits from the lecture.

Truly a caring prof. This is the 2nd class I've taken w her and both have been extremely similar. Her lectures are pretty long but if you study them and use her study guide, the exams should be easy (they're memorization based). If you're happy w your grade after the first 3 exams, you can opt out of the 4th. Also gives extra cred on exams!

Took 2164 last sem and really liked Dr. Bergamasco. If you go to class and study the lectures, the tests are very straight forward, as it is pretty much just memorizing the slides. This class had little to no work outside of class besides studying, which I really appreciated. She is super nice and pretty funny in my opinion and I enjoyed the class.

Dr. Bergamasco is very nice, and her accent is pretty thick but easy to understand once you adjust. Her test was a lot more difficult than the first test with Dr. Moore. Any information she lectures will be on the exam, so memorize everything. The lectures are long with a lot of information, so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: APSC 3304:Great lady but her class is overall mid. Exams are made up of abt 8 lectures totaling an av of 480 slides to study PER exam (plus the slides are rlly wordy). The exams themselves are on the easier side, but studying for them takes awhile. She randomly takes attendance which is worth 20% of your grade. Final project wasn't explained well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A as long as you studying her lectures. The lectures are usually word for word on the tests and she also gives some extra credit. There are select days that you have to attend class but only a few and she usually tells you beforehand.

ALS 2504 is very lecture heavy. In class each day, she lectures on a ~40 slide PowerPoint and pretty much just reads off the slides. She crams lots of information on each slide so it is sometimes hard to know what you really need to know. She doesn't offer the best feedback, but she is responsive with emails and is a nice woman overall.
Her class is all slides and for the tests, you have to memorize all of it. There is no learning going on, only memorization.

Overall, this class is very easy. There are two tests and both are worth 25% of your grade. The first exam was good but the second exam was difficult for no reason. Expect to have confusing questions. I mainly just crammed before exams and did fine.

I really enjoyed Dr. Bergamasco, her lectures were fun with some interesting material. Tests are sort of tough with the way they are worded, but if you take your time they're not too bad. Attendance is part of your final grade!

She expects you to memorize a 22 page study guide for one exam, every single exam. It is a lot more extensive for a class like this, unneccessarily difficult. Study guides are useless as they don't help guide you, its basically just every single piece of information you must memorize for one exam.

Dr. Bergamasco is such a sweet & funny lady! ALS2504 is a pretty stress-free class, not homework. Class is lecture heavy, some class periods consisted of easy activities graded for participation. Attendance is part of the final grade. She makes the tests very easy to study for if you follow her study guides.
She is a very sweet lady and is accessible outside of classs and willing to help! Her tests are tricky because of the format but overall easy and great professor.
Professor Bergamasco is one of my favorite professors at Tech.  She is so sweet and works hard to make class fun!
Dr. Bergamasco is a sweetheart. She is a great teacher and always willing to help!

Dr. Bergamasco is a really nice professor. She's always available to help her students. She has an Italian accent, but she's easy to understand. There are 3 exams (all opended questions) and an optional cumulative final. She gives a study guide and it's very easy to receive an A on every exam. There is an easy project that you get to pick as well.

Exams are very fair, she is very responsive to emails and explains things well. Accent can be difficult sometimes but overall awesome professor. Keep in mind you cannot have more than 2 unexcused absences or you will receive a F for that part of your grade. Attendance is taken by an in class assignment that is graded on completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The exams were open notes. She is a very nice professor and makes the class very manageable.

Prof Zhang is a pretty good professor and the class is very manageable. Although the lectures are very boring, the information presented is exactly what will be on tests and homework. Attendance is definitely mandatory as there are daily in-class assignments and having more than 2 unexcused absences results in an F.

Dr. Patcha-Lum teaches you all you need to know about user documentation. Each week there's 1 big assignment and textbook readings (textbooks are free but not a fun read). She gives lots of great feedback for every assignment, which really helps guide you. The final project is a portfolio which will be helpful when seeking technical writing jobs.

Dr. Patcha Lum was easy to reach and allowed me to resubmit a couple of assignments due to links not working. Homework was doable over the week and she graded pretty easily. There were a couple of group projects, but I was able to do those without meeting up with my group in person.

Writing and Digital Media was pretty easy, but had its moments of difficulty. There was a lot of work to be done each week and if you emailed the professor for help, they would just copy and paste the instructions in their response, so I had to use a lot of outside resources to actually do well in the class.

Randomly starting requiring attendance towards the end of the semester when that was never made an expectation nor in the syllabus. Also was unclear with grading expectations at times. Overall professor is chill but class material can be a bit of a drag.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super easy teacher and class. She just put us in groups and we worked on one big project the whole semester. Really easy and there is a whole rubric to follow. She also explains the assignments in depth and always answers your questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Super easy course with virtually no work outside of class. The class is broken up into two separate group projects, both of which we presented before Thanksgiving break. You won't have a final exam/paper. I got away with not doing a whole lot, but I could have devoted more time. Dr. Patton is extremely respectful and a generous grader. Easy 4K PHIL

She's very accessible. A forgiving grader. Two big papers make up most of your grade. Truthfully, you could not show up to a single class and still get an A. The only drawback is that the content is pretty dry.

Lydia is very intelligent and kind. She gives great feedback on papers. Her classes are well designed. She gives students useful extra readings and is happy to meet outside of class. Cross listed classes sometimes are not great for MA students because undergrads don't do the readings often times. Lydia makes the best of it, given the limitations.

Super easy class, but very concept heavy. The class itself can be kind of dry at times, but she is really kind and will always be there to help. Overall, great teacher- I took her again the next semester for another class.

Professor Patton is very chill. Her lectures are pretty good; she usually goes over the assigned readings for that class. Although attendance is not mandatory, her lectures are very useful. You could pass without reading the textbook but attend all the lectures or vice versa. There are 3 papers worth 70% of the grade & short assignments throughout
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Easily one of my favorite professors i've had at tech. He is so caring and really makes an effort to build relationships with his students. My confidence and public speaking skills grew immensely while taking his class and has made me want to pursue sales. He wants to help with anything he can (internships, advice, etc.) Professor Mark is the BEST!
my goat. he gave us dating advice once. he's so silly. responds to emails fast. loves (and is scared of) his wife. super outgoing guy.

Course does not have any exams, which is nice but relies on the midterm and final presentations. They consist of you immersing yourself into the role of a sales rep for a company. They are not difficult, but they require preparation and practice with Professor Mark. He is incredibly kind and lenient, and makes a great effort to his students.

I have never had a professor care so much about their students as much as Mark does. This man genuinely wants us all to succeed in life, and will help you with anything you need (even stuff out of class like internships). The class itself is very easy, and he made me realize that I might have a future in sales. LOVE THIS GUY!!!

Professor Mark is the best professor I've had during my time at VT. He fosters an environment of respect and makes the class conversational. Attendance is taken, and the class involves public speaking. There is no textbook, but you have to purchase software. Professor Mark is caring, kind, supportive, and sympathetic. You won't regret his class!
I have never rated a professor but he deserves a 100/5 stars absolutely amazing guy! Have taken multiple classes with him and honestly he is the GOAT!! Thank you Mark

Mark is one of the best professors you will have at VT. He really cares about teaching and cares about his students. On all projects, he is quick with feedback and the lectures are also relatively engaging. Be prepared to ask questions and take notes. If you don't like public speaking, Mark will make you like it.

Hands down one of the best professors I've had at Virginia Tech! He is so caring and wants to see his students succeed. I looked forward to this class every week. My public speaking skills improved so much thanks to this course. A must take!!

Extremely tough grader, yet has barely graded anything. Assigned 4 final exams yet hasn't finished grading assignments from back in beginning of march. I have no idea how she'll fairly grade the rest of the assignments for the semester with them being so content heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you prefer quick feedback, this class will be frustrating for you. In my experience, grading often took several weeks (on simple assignments) and assignments didn't always include much detailed feedback. I also found expectations unclear and the professor is rather hard to reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: NEVER TAKE A CLASS WITH HER

Would write essay about her bc she's the worst but can't. assigns us work that can be taught in 2 slides. grades homework weeks after they are due. don't try to email her because she takes weeks to reply. tomorrow is the deadline for final grades and she still hasn't graded ten assignments, including my final project and final essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had this professor my Freshman year and she was very kind and genuine and willing to do anything for the students who showed up and tried to get a good grade.

Amazing professor. Attendance wasn't mandatory but his lectures were entertaining and so informative. Super good at answering questions and gauging understanding. Always cancelled Friday classes. Super funny too. Definitely one of my fav professors I've had.

Made accounting interesting. Gave lots of fun stories to go along with the content and generally kept the class engaged. Tests weren't too bad, but you need to study. Homework was long and in connect, but doable. Would recommend taking it with him than anyone else.

Class was very hard, Almond is a great guy although I felt like class didn't really help at all. I know a lot of people who didn't go to class and did well on exams, me personally accounting just didn't click but maybe it will for you.

Professor Almond was so kind and caring to his students. I didn't go to many lectures but I still enjoyed having him as a professor. The class is very easy to learn through the homeworks and he posts the answers to the hws but with different numbers so it wasn't difficult to learn the material.

2115 and accounting in general are difficult, but Professor Almond always makes the class seem easier and is always available by email or office hours. He is by far the best professor I have had at Virginia Tech, and as long as you do the work, you'll do well in the class, and the homework helps you learn the material. Please take him!

He is the nicest guy ever. I know accounting is really hard but he provides many resources on his canvas page for you to suceed on the homeworks and tests. Just go over the mcgraw hill online notes that he puts under his slideshow and you should be good for tests.

Almond is professional and laid back. He gives mutual respect towards students who try and will do everything in his power to make sure his students pass his class. If you are going through a lot he will accommodate. The only reason I got a B+ was because I took 4 finals in one day and his was the last, but he helped me every step of the way.

ACIS 2115 is a difficult class, but Prof. Almond makes it easier to understand. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you are not understanding the homework I would highly recommend going to class because Prof. Almond goes over the homework problems. Definitely try to take him and not the TA.

Such a nice guy, but his teaching style is not up to date. Lectures are slow, and repetitive. Often gets off track and talks about things that aren't related to the coursework. I taught myself everything. And the time spent doing accounting problems never correlates to whats on the exams.

Such a nice guy but I literally taught myself everything. His lectures were often confusing and he would go off on tangents for 5-15 minutes at a time which would leave barely enough time to cover the material in class. The exams were on Scantron which was so difficult since everything else we did in the year was using the online textbook.
Wants you to learn. Professor Almond cares about you learning the subject. As long as you put in the work, he will help you with everything Accounting!

Took Spring 2022. While Lynn's lectures aren't the most entertaining, I highly recommend taking him over a TA. Accounting is hard, and if you put in the work and really try, you should be okay. The HWs were also tedious, so please do them early. He's also a really nice guy if you talk to him outside of class.

The class was hard to understand and included a lot of work outside of class.The lectures were not very helpful and most of the class is self-taught. Everything is basically weighted the same, so it's important to do all of the assignments correctly/on time to buffer the grade for the tests. 3 total tests and 2 assignments per chapter (12 total).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great teacher, if you go to class he answers questions but only a handful of students go to class. Tests are tough but I didnt read the textbook and still have an A.

Oh my this class was awful. There's no extra credit, so if you do bad on an exam good luck on trying to get a curve. TA's are eh and sometimes don't understand the material either. I tried so hard to get a good grade in this class or at least use notes during a test. TAKE AT COMM COLLEGE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lynn is super sweet. TAKE HIM not a TA, makes a HUGE difference. Go to class and read the textbook and you'll be fine. I realized that a little too late in the semester. He cares about his students and will help you, but you have to reach out and ask for help. The TAs are nice, but definitely don't teach as well as Prof. Almond does.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Almond is a really sweet man! I went to his office hours a few time and he was always kind and helpful. I would say reading the textbook is very important. He didn't take attendance, so I'll admit I wasn't in class a lot unless I was struggling with the material. Also, it was a MWF class and he canceled all Friday classes for the whole semester
Go to class, follow along, and read the book. If you do that and go to him for help, you should have no problems getting an A or B
His tests are literally impossible and he doesn't curve them. Good luck.

Lynn is the greatest professor of all time.  He is so sweet, and actually cares for his students.  I am so very glad that I got to meet him and take his class. His tests are fairly hard, but he gives you quiz points that really help.  if you can, TAKE PROFESSOR ALMOND! he will make accounting fun for you :)

The pre and post labs were definitely a lot of work, but not unbearable. You don't really see him very often in lab, but when you do he was always helpful and wanted to get to know his students and joked around with us. His lab guides and rubrics were not always the clearest about instructions though.

i really like the experiments in his labs, but the assignments in the second class eventually became tedious and frustrating. i understand why we do it, but having to take it alongside genchem 2 and organic 2 was a nightmare. i my biggest issue was with the structure of the reports, you could probably half the analysis and still be just fine.

Why is this course so much work? It is a two-credit course, yet I am working more than in some of my four-credit courses. I love the TAs. Although the grading from them may be unclear, I understand it's difficult because the instructions from Neil are bad. Im so over Orgo. The lab is not helpful unless you want an increase in stress and anxiety.

Professor McAlpine is very caring and helps in lab when he shows up. Every assignment has a posted rubric, and it is clear what is needed from you. Lab is low stakes and not graded on technique. Funny guy too.

Felt diminished in his class. Content was straightforward, but every time he spoke to me, he talked as if I were a rebellious teenager getting in trouble. Did not respect me or anyone in the class. Don't know why he's rated so highly.
The class is easy and fun just pay attention to the rubrics when you submit lab reports. He is funny in person when he occasionally shows up to the lab. Passive aggressive emails tho.

i had mcalpine for two semesters of syntech lab. he was so funny and never made us feel bad if we messed up. he just wanted us to learn and have fun. was also an easy grader. easily my favorite class.

Professor McAlpine's lab is run by TAs so you don't see him much but the labs aren't difficult and any reports and prelabs are graded extremely fairly. The rubrics are always straightforward and he gives helpful pointers in all of prelab lecture videos. I would take another class with him.

I didn't interact with McAlpine too much, as the class was run by TAs, but he is very kind and funny. The class was pretty easy and he never made me feel bad if I didn't understand something. He posts helpful lecture videos and is pretty laid back in general. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. McAlpine was by far one of the best professors I have had for a lab, ever. His rubric for each lab report was clear and concise, and always gave great feedback in and out of the lab. Just follow everything in the rubric, and you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is incredibly kind and cares deeply about the material which made the class so much more interesting. We did three labs throughout the semester that were all fun!

Professor McLain was very disorganized with assignments. Grading was inconsistent, and we didn't know our grade the entire semester. The syllabus was never followed; her personal opinions became the focus for the class, not educational material. Attendance was not mandatory, and there were no exams or quizzes, but there were 3 lab assignments.

McLain is a wonderful professor. She is very good at communicating and really cares for every one of her students' needs. I struggled a bit in this class when it came to music theory as I have never played an instrument before. However, if you have played an instrument, this is a relatively easy class. Make sure to participate as it makes an impact

Professor McLain is an excellent communicator and I enjoyed her class despite it being moved to an online modality early in the semester. She is always ready to help students and is very flexible when it comes to assignments or other issues. Most of the points come from textbook assignments and in-class participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor McLain is a very easy-going and approachable professor. Unfortunately, for most of the semester, the class had to be taken online. However, she made the class interesting despite the circumstances. The class is not too hard, as most of the work is easy homework. If you take a class with Prof. McLain, make sure to say hi to her cat, Misha.

Professor McLain is a great professor. She truly cares about the well being of her students and always asks for our input on assignment/project adjustments. There are textbooks readings assigned for every class and questions asked for points throughout the virtual class along with various assignments and group projects/presentations.

Mrs. McAllister was definitely my favorite professor from my first semester. She is super helpful and is always willing to give you an extension if you need it. She is great at teaching and cares for each student. COMM 1015 is not a super hard class. 100% take her class if you can.
Great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ms. McAllister is by far the best professor I have had at Tech. Her lectures are entertaining, the quizzes are helpful, and she provides the best feedback on all major assignments. She is truly a great person and cares about each student individually. If you are taking COMM1015/16, Ms. McAllister is the way to go.

Amazing! She really cares about her students, and she shows that by giving great feedback. I am not the best writer, but I received an A on all five major writing assignments. I 110% recommend selecting her as your COMM 1015/16 instructor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I love this professor! She is awesome, especially when being a freshman. She explains thing so well and is very flexible.

Kacy McAllister is my actual queen. I had her for Comm 1015 & 1016, and I absolutely loved her. She really cares about her students and is willing to give extensions when they are needed. She also does a great job engaging students and you don't feel like you are being talked at. Be prepared to write and give speeches often.
Great teacher, very caring, and will give extensions if needed. Put the student first, but be prepared for public speaking almost every week.

This professor is amazing. She gives good praise to students whenever. Professor McAllister is so enthusiastic whenever she gives a lecture, making it more entertaining. This professor is very inclusive since she wants everyone to participate and have a good time in class.
Great teacher! Learned so many new things and she truly cares about her students.
One of the best teachers Ive ever had. Truly cares for her students and wants them to do good in the class. Had her two-semester and will always give extensions

Ms. McAllister is an excellent teacher; I had her for both COMM1015 and COMM1016. Assignments, papers, projects, and speeches are all clearly laid-out with specific rubrics that tell you exactly what you're striving for. Ms. McAllister is a fair, sometimes generous, grader that gives great feedback. Amazing teacher overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ms. McAllister is one of the best teachers I've had at Tech. She is caring and will give extensions. I've had her for both COMM1015 and COMM1016. The class does have a lot of papers but they aren't hard if you take the time to do them. There are also speeches, more so in 1016 but if you prepare you'll be fine.

Kacy is probably the best professor I have had thus far. She understands mental health so well, and you can really tell she loves her students. However, she does not play with school. Do not wait to write your papers the night before they're due-she'll know. Go to class; the topics in her lectures will come up in the quizzes.
A good teacher that cares about the students. You should get a good grade as long as you do all the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Steele is a very passionate professor, but her teaching style was not very effective. Tests were hard, and when test averages are 50%, thats a problem.

Dr. Steele's class was the only class that I looked forward to this semester. Her lectures are the best that I have ever recieved, and it is very clear that she is knowledgable and enthusiastic. 
Very few assignments, but much studying is neccesary for exams. Routine study will prepare you well.
1 group project worth a large portion of your grade
She is great. Very helpful and cheerful. She made the class fun and I really enjoyed having her.

Easy class, tests are based on the powerpoints. I recommend using quizlet to study. The lectures were fine, she def does care about what she is teaching. She lets you choose the deadline for HW and projects. Gives good feedback for projects-if you follow her feedback she rewards you for it. Final exam pulls questions from previous tests super easy.

Her class was not too difficult. The tests are detail oriented, so make sure to review the slideshows. Very lecture heavy course that uses top hat questions. These are your "attendance" points. There is one group project that isn't hard if you have a competent group. She will let you reschedule tests with valid excuses.
Dr Steele was a good professor, I personally just didnt like her style of teaching and felt that she was too tough of a grader for the group project.

As someone who struggles to pay attention in the average class, Professor Steele captures my interest. She tells jokes and makes expressive hand gestures that keep me focused, and her lectures in general are just great to sit through. 
She always gives us a few extra minutes to review before tests, and she lets classes pick their own HW deadlines!

Dr. Steele is great, she cares about her students and wants you to get a good grade. Also makes the material fun and interesting. Very flexible with teaching structure and deadlines (basically she lets you choose both of these). Her test/exam structure is set up to help not hurt you, definitely take her class !

Dr. Steele is a great professor; she's super knowledgeable and provides information in a clear and concise manner. She asks for feedback often and is very approachable. Would definitely take another class with her.

Walter is genuinely amazing. If you want to take a class to watch movies, this is not that class. If you want to take a class to learn about film, its origins, connections to other forms of media and arts, this is an amazing course, and you will have no regrets. His coursework is not challenging; tests are fine if you study an appropriate amount.

Walter is super smart/knowledgable about film, but his lecture style is a bit all over the place and rambling, but funny too. The class does require a lot of outside reading and watching of content. His tests are hard and writing based, but he does grade on a super generous curve which is nice. Definitely not an easy class, but I did learn alot?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Walter is a great guy (notice how I say guy, not professor). He is very passionate about art, and he wants to make you just as passionate. This class is NOT an easy pathway - you unfortunately can't just shove it to the side and expect to do well. He does grade on a very generous curve however

He is definitely interesting , I would say he is smart but has no concept of how to teach a college class. the tests are hard and all writing. You have to memorize every word he's ever said in order to do good on them. Be prepared to watch naked people in many of his video clips and do not take this class if you are thinking it is an easy pathway.

One of the smartest people ever yet his teaching is absolutely atrocious. Be prepared to memorize 50 essays, their writing styles, 100s of video clips, and his own random tangents just for 4 of those items to show up on the exam. One of the funniest professors to listen to while he is teaching but his exam and exam preparation is awful.
Genius, but can not teach. Test questions feel very unnecessary. Clips he shows in class are interesting, but does not answer emails quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is great!
Good guy, great class.

Dr. McPherson is chill and mostly nice. The content is interesting, but he doesnt help prepare students for the tests, specifically the final. I suggest taking the other professor (Senger). The homework and projects aren't too bad.  However, near the end of the semester, they will cram a lot of projects in.

McPherson is a great guy. Very accessible and helpful, doesn't have the attitude that other CS professors have when you interact with them. It is a difficult course because some of the projects introduce a very high level of complexity to topics not covered much in class. Exams are not too bad though.

I wish I could rate higher - funny professor and great office hours. However, ultimately I do not feel like Professor McPherson went into the depth required to succeed on the exams. The homeworks and the projects are not bad at all, however the exams (especially the final) are very difficult, especially if you have no prior course knowledge.

By far one of the best professors I have ever had. He was very willing to work with me when I was struggling to get some assignments done on time or had technical issues. He does get passive-aggressive about people skipping his class, but he is a nice professor, and I would 10/10 recommend him to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McPherson is a great lecturer who makes the class interesting and worth going to. The class is an insane amount of work for an intro class, as there is usually a reading and lab every week, as well as a quiz and program about every week and a half. If you have any sort of background with Java, this class is very straightforward.
Very good professor who cares about his students and is very accessible outside of class. A lot of work for an intro class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had the other 2505 professor and she was so bad I just used his videos and lecture notes for the entire class. Great Professor
The better professor

The best CS professor I've had, amazing lectures, answers student's questions, instant grading on HW/projects with a program he wrote himself (shows u what u did wrong), lowest grades are dropped, lowest exam is replaced by final exam grade. Overall, a very forgiving professor if you show up to class, even if you don't know C or Assembly.

Best CS professor I've ever had, super good at teaching content, very aware that it might be completely new for some students, and still very personable during all of lectures and whenever I talked to him. He helped me understand and really enjoy the subject

I have never seen a better professor than Professor McPherson. C, Linux, and Assembly are among the courses well taught by one of our department's best computer science professors. He is an excellent teacher who uses an interesting approach and is interested in students' success.

If I could rate 6 stars I would. Prof McPherson knows how to teach C, assembly, and Linux better than anyone I've ever seen. Lectures are fantastic and will teach you everything you need to know about the tech in question (what was college for again...?). He coded his own grader for every assignment so there's no WebCat: enough said.

McPherson is the best CS professor I have had. Going into 2505 I thought I would hate it because of C but he made this class really enjoyable. Anytime I asked for help he was always willing to help me, never made me feel dumb for asking questions. He genuinely cares about your success in the course and if you put the time in you will pass.

His lectures are just him coding / showing code, very little notes other than stray definitions here and there. His homeworks are somewhat easy, while the projects are a little harder and should be started early. Tests are hard, just due to all the little things you have to remember. But, if you go to class and pay attention, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor. Great at teaching the material and has very engaging lectures. Only downside is the exams are quite difficult --- need to memorize syntax and basic usage of a few obscure languages you'll probably never use again. Even with that in mind, though, I think he is a staple at VT and students should always take his class!
Outstanding. I was student and also TA in his class. He is one of the kindest people I have ever seen. I will always takes his course as he knows hot to respect people.

Average. He doesn't use ppt slides and his lectures are him coding and explaining the code (can't reference outside of class). You don't have to go to class as all the assignments can be done without going, but the tests are hard (averages are 70, no curve). Projects and HWs are easy and can all be done within 2 days.
Boring, not engaging, hard.
Rude, disrespectful, egotistical

Mr. McPherson has been my favorite professor so far. I have worked with him outside of the classroom on my professional development. Inside the classroom he gives relatable and engaging lectures. He provides hand-on, applicable notes that can be used for homework and projects. Notes are still applicable in future courses.
Extremely engaging professor, however there were times where he did not understand the material completely himself.

This was his first year teaching cs1114 and he did really well! The course is the same regardless of the professor you have. Procrastinating the programs was the worst mistake I made in this class. Office hours help a lot!

If I could take every one of my CS classes with McPherson, I'd do it, and then do it again.

McPherson is honestly the best CS professor I've had so far. He's very clear in his teaching, cracks good jokes, and is super receptive to helping his students learn.

Professor McPherson always brings so much energy to the class and presents everything very clearly. Every project is fair and if you're stuck he will always offer great help in office hours and respond to emails quickly. Tests are straight forward and if you attend the lectures, even difficult concepts will be easy to understand.
CS 2505 is a hard class but McPherson teaches really well. In class, he's entertaining and engaging, and he's able to help students after class.

This was a difficult class, but Prof. McPherson was always very helpful. His lectures made a lot of sense, and he's very funny in class. His office hours are also really helpful. There are some tough projects in this course and the instructions on the projects aren't always clear, but he often posts videos that help a lot.

McPherson is one of the best professors Ive had at tech and by far the best CS professor Ive had. Lectures are interesting and helpful, and he is always willing to help after class or by email. C is hard but he makes it manageable. Pushed project deadline back since most of the class had a math test. Very reasonable.

The lectures were super easy to follow along. He writes his notes and code live rather than using slides. He makes a lot of jokes when they're least expected and his exams are really easy as long as you studied and paid attention in class. He posts the notes and past exams, which are great studying material

Mr.McPherson was one of the best teachers I have ever had for a CS class at Virginia Tech. He cares about your success and will actually help when you get stuck. He also really values that you make an effort to go and ask him things, especially during office hours. If you feel like you are stuck go into office hours it is a lifesaver!
Really good demos in class that help with the weekly labs. Patient and engaging lecturer; takes time to answer questions. Stays after class to help students- I can tell he cares.
Very approachable/hilarious and simplifies the complex topics that are covered in CS 2505. You can't go wrong with taking classes with McPhearson!
He is amazing. Probably the best professor you can get in the CS department.

If you got McPherson for any programming class, that means you hit the jackpot. He gives VERY detailed instructions so that you can quickly master everything even though you crashed 2514 or 1574. Homework and projects are easy if you pay attention. Office hours are beneficial because McPherson can solve every problem you have on programming in "1s"

Prof. McPherson is great, but not for 1004. His background is in software, so he really doesn't know too much about circuits and it shows. He is, however, an amazing professor for the software portion of the course: his lecture on Matlab being a "tool" was one of the most hilarious things I've ever heard. Take him for 2574 and 3574.

McPherson is a fantastic professor who knows everything you need to know about C and C++ programming. His coding classes are extremely beneficial and a great learning experience, but definitely require time and effort to complete, especially for the large projects. Definitely don't procrastinate on programming labs or projects. Anyways he is great
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This is the first year this class has been offered and my oh my. Its horrible. The class replaces the old 1574 which was an easy A and now 1004 is an easy F. Probably the highest withdraw rate for any class at the university. I would say david is an ok teacher but the material is hard stuff especially for him to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Best teacher at tech, it's an easy A if you pay attention cause he teaches the matieral so well you're almost guaranteed to understand it.
The best teacher you could ever have. Always happy to help. Very energetic and explains stuff well. His projects might take you some time but I really loved coding after taking Prof. McPherson Class
Pretty helpful and very nice

Really great guy, very helpful and accessible. I did not find him to be a particularly easy grader (which is good - this was a grad level course) but he was fair and only tested us on relevant material. You need to do the reading and listen to lectures to keep up. But if you get stuck, he'll bend over backwards to help.

Really great guy. His tests are fairly easy. There was only one project and it was easy. For the final test, he gives you the choice of either averaging the two tests' grades you got and use it for the final grade or you can take the final if you don't like your grade.

Easy class! The average was an A- in our class if that helps you. He was the best of the ECE 1574 professors. If you've programmed before, the lectures are boring, but the labs will be simple; if not, it's still not all that hard. You should do the study guides he gives you, they help for tests. The projects are easy too. No curve, but still good.

Easy class! The average was an A- in our class if that helps you. He was the best of the ECE 1574 professors. If you've programmed before, the lectures are boring, but the labs will be simple; if not, it's still not all that hard. You should do the study guides he gives you, they help for the tests. The projects are easy too. No curve, but still go

A fun teacher to have, quite affable and prone to developing project descriptions up until the day code is due. He has a good sense of humor and it probably models actual programming situations, and he makes concessions if he wasn't clear. Lectures are very easy to understand, but then again he tends to read off the slides.

A great guy all around, truly enjoyed his class. Things tested are taught in class and there isn't any 'BS.' He is very helpful not only inside the classroom but outside as well. Also is generally supportive when it comes to lateness, etc.
Great professor for a tough class.

Thermo is inevitably a lot of work. Fast paced course, weekly online textbook homework, ~biweekly quizzes, 3 exams + final. Meadows would make clear what content would be on each exam/quiz (narrowing it down was especially helpful because of how much is covered). Tests were graded generously and most curved. Not easy, but never felt impossible.

Only showed up to class for exams and quizzes so not sure on his lectures. If you want to do good read the textbook, his exam questions are very hard and he will put things in the exam that you will only know if you read the textbook. When studying do every practice problem that is on his class notebook in canvas.

Very nice guy but his test questions were difficult. He teaches a ton of information that its impossible to follow what matters and what doesn't. He throws stuff on the test he very briefly mentions or never shows examples in class. He does a ton of examples in class but goes through them to fast to follow. has the lowest avg gpa per semester.
Gave a generous curve and taught well. He is excellent.
Very hard tests, too much information crammed into one semester to actually absorb anything
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Meadows is a great professor; he understands the material very well, and knows how to help you understand it. He's only been teaching a few years, but the homework is reasonable (5-6 problems a week) and he grades tests well; if you understand the material, you will pass. If you don't show up though things will be tough, as the books are boring
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor. After his first exam where people really seemed to struggle, he actually collected and read every rec from us, then sent out an email and took time the following class to address all the concerns. Honestly probably not even necessary, since he gave a generous curve, but it's very refreshing to see a professor who really cares.

I would recommend taking another professor for 1105, especially if you are not minoring/majoring in the language. She is hard to follow, disorganized, and gives frequent quizzes and tests the define the majority of your grade. The other professor offers test corrections to boost your grade which you will need to if you're not studying constantly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is one of the best professors I've had at tech. She makes the class interactive and fun. She genuinely wants her students to succeed in Italian. I am going to miss going to her class every week.

If you are taking Italian, I would try and get Professor Coburn. She is incredibly knowledgeable in Italian and has a great teaching style. A lot of small group activities to work on conversation in Italian. She's also just a great person and super understanding. It is nice to know that some professors still care about their students!

I have really enjoyed the classes Ive taken with Melissa Coburn! She definitely knows the Italian language very well. I love how personable she is, and she usually makes really small but funny jokes during lectures. Not too tough of a grader, which is appreciated when learning a language, but she definitely makes sure your knowledge is grounded.

Overall a pretty average professor. She does pre-created notes (problems, diagrams, etc.) in class, and posts the completed versions online. Thing is, if you skip class for whatever reason some parts of the notes will make no sense. Thankfully, she's willing to schedule office hours, and is really helpful and understanding during them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thorough if not very interesting lectures for Calc 3, but really shines in written homework and practice sets matching up with tests. She gives a boatload of examples and problems that are test questions in disguise; a very Do the Work, Get the Grade style class. Grading is strict but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great at responding to emails & feedback. Class is straight forward if you do the optional syllabus problems for extra practice and understanding. Dr. Perera does an amazing job at preparing students for her tests -offers mock exams and great practice materials. She'll follow up with great explanations for relevant questions from previous classes.

GOAT! I got a C+ because I failed the final (it was very random), but she is the best math teacher I have had at tech: has notes online, practice tests, mock exams- and posts solutions for all of these. She explained concepts so well, and went at an extremely reasonable pace. Super reasonable homework load. Tests were just like the practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You must go to her class to get and submit written assignments and she takes attendance. But her lectures are amazing and easy to understand. Her exams are also similar to the practice tests. She was the best math professor in tech.
amazing notes and exams are very similar to practice tests

TAKE DR. PERERA! She explain everything so simply and made it easy to understand. The tests were pretty easy and she posted many practice tests that were very similar to the actual test. Overall the best math teacher I have had a tech and you should 100% take her class

Class notes available out of class if needed. Lectures are clear and she answers any questions that pop up. Accessible in office hours and tests are very fair. Missed a lot of class but the notes were well-organized and well-written and helped me get back on track. Attendance isn't mandatory but def go if possible.

HW every week and Webassign every so often. A little difficult. Definitely not impossible. Attendance mandatory, but not graded. You don't get notes access if you skip too much. Tests are VERY fair. Grading criteria is based more off the process, not the correct answer. She does have a slight accent. I liked her, very willing to answer questions.

Professor Perera was a very good professor. Her exams were just like review and practice tests so no surprises. If you go to office hours and understand her practice test, you will be just fine. Her lecture style is monotone which can make class boring but overall, she is a straightforward professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She definitely knew her stuff, I thought she was very good at explaining majority of topics. There will be LOTS of homework (10+ assignments a week). She requires that you make and meet with a group once a week, which I was happy about honestly. The tests might make or break your grade, I did awful on the sequences one and it destroyed my grade.

She definitely knows her stuff, but the content given on tests is a lot harder than what she teaches. Gives LOTS of hw (~10 per week) and tests are very hard. She gives plenty of test prep materials, but they're so difficult that they don't help much. All her lectures are just going over notes, so lots of examples but they're boring.

Professor Perera is a very focused and determined instructor. She is very efficient and wastes no time, sometimes leaving those who do not understand behind. Her coursework and lectures can be very rigorous at times, and her accent is difficult to understand at first. Overall, she teaches the material well and is helpful at office hours.

Perera is a good but rigorous professor. Go to lectures and do the in-class practice tests. They are very similar to the actual tests, so take them home and go over them. Her lectures are good and she does office hours for help. She does her job in a very boring, robotic manner, if you wish for a likable, understanding professor, she is not that.

Professor Perera is very organized and never wastes a minute of class. All of her lecture notes are projected from her iPad, and posted on Canvas once completed. It's better to just watch and take in the material rather than try to take notes. Her office hours are very helpful for getting through homework if you come with questions!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She gives webassigns, canvas quizzes, and written homeworks (average work). She takes feedback very well and will assign you in groups at the beginning of the semester to work with. She has a light accent but its not a problem. She writes very well and has detailed drawings. She gives mock tests, lots of practice, and accessible office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: if you study hard you'll do fine. go to office hours. if this is your first semester, study HARD for the first test. she uploads all her notes on canvas which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Perera knows the materials every well but I felt she couldn't teach well. Class was basically just her doing example problems for 50 mins. Tests were hard but if you study enough you'll be fine.

Dr. Perera is a great no BS professor and she wants you to succeed. You get multiple attempts for hw problems. Written hw can be tricky & comes with tough grading. Practice tests are basically the real tests with different numbers, so look for patterns in types of questions asked. Don't bargain about late work and 1226 will be very doable with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures are clear and easy to understand. Cares about students; always encourage attending office hours. Her class notes are pretty clear and organized. The extra practice sessions were also helpful. The course is hard; lots of assignments graded for correctness. So you must work hard instead of just memorizing.

Mrs.Perera is the best and the biggest advice to anyone struggling in her class is to go to her office hours. She holds them all the time (even the day of the exam). Her notes are very detailed and classes are well taught but it is a tough course so you do have to put in the work. Also, take advantage of the extra time and practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Perera was very helpful during office hours. She lets you rework the homework to earn the pts lost. She is the most organized professor I have ever seen. Her Canvas and the class notes are very organized and clear. Test review sessions and mock exams were extremely helpful for tests. Offers extra credit and her grading criteria is also clear.

Lessons are confusing and very lecture heavy. She does not help during office hours or when asked questions and instead makes students feel stupid for not understanding. Homework is hard and not always like the notes and graded harshly. Tests are extremely difficult and her class average was always lower then the 1225 whole average.
Ms. Perera gives really really good notes that I now share with all of my friends. They find it very helpful too! Overall, I like her explaining and teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lots of homework assignments counted for accuracy. Very help when asking questions one on one and in class.

DO NOT TAKE HER!  She is so discriminative to the only minority in the classroom full other white students. She is extremely rude if you attend her office hours. Be ready to teach yourself calculus. ALWAYS gives rude/annoyed faces when asked question in class. Lectures is all about topics only few example problems. 100% would NOT recommend!

Good at teaching and tries to engage in the classroom. Pretty useful during office hours as well. Sometimes rushes through content and doesn't give a clear explanation. But overall wants you to succeed. Just do the extra work and go to her office hours if you need help and you should be fine.

I honestly didn't mind her class. I got a C+ in 1225 but now I will probably get an A in Perera's 1226 class. Her accent is annoying to deal with and she really likes you to learn her way specifically which is also annoying. However her written HWs are pretty easy. Tests are very similar to the practice tests and seem easier then other instructors

She has scripted lectures that do not deviate from plans she makes before class. She is not open to answering questions, and gets upset when you ask a question or ask her to elaborate on something she has explained. She will not let you solve problems (correctly) using a method that deviates from what she teaches you. I just memorized her notes.

She was horrible. Barely went over topics and could not elaborate on curriculum. All her test averages were below a C which makes sense when you try to understand what she is teaching. Would avoid her if there is a choice.

I took this class in the fall semester and it ruined my confidence. I’ve always excelled at math with little to no effort but with this course I was working upwards of 10 hours a week at least and still never got higher than a 62 on the exams. Math here will weed you out, take it a community college and spare your mental health
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Perera teaches through lecturing. She'll introduce a concept to you and derive the equation you need. Then a couple practice problems followed sometimes by a group work question. She write really good notes. Her office hours are quite helpful. Her test prep is really good. She looks at everyone's HW and reviews common mistakes before test.

Very difficult to understand. Sometimes when she is lecturing she seems like she doesn't even know what she's talking about. Second guesses a lot. Whenever people ask a lot of questions she seems annoyed. Extremely tedious grader, which is still an understatement in my opinion.

Perera ruined my love for math. Her way of teaching was near useless to me. She did 45-minute lectures followed by 1 or 2 problems (that you wouldn't see on the exam) for 5 minutes each. Do not ever take her class unless you already fully understand the material. Stay safe out there everyone!

Professor Pereras style of teaching was a great help to pass this class with a good grade. Her review sessions helped me a lot, she goes over a lot of questions paying special attention to the common misconceptions that she has seen. Her office hours were also helpful. There were lot of assignments but this is college math so it is quite usual.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have never received below an A in math in my entire life, Ms. Perera is that bad. Her lectures were extremely short and we would just do 2 questions max. She was always so rude and condescending even though she tried to act nice. If you end up in her class get ready to attend a lot of help sessions with the teacher assistant, who is quite good.
Got a good grade because I previously knew the content, but I would not have been able to learn calculus properly if this was my first go at it.

Perera is easily one of the worst professors I have had throughout my entire time in school. Lectures are completely useless, in 50-minute review sessions we go over a max of 2 problems that hardly cover any of the content on the exams. She is highly demeaning and rude when asked questions. If you can drop her course you absolutely should.
if you have the opportunity to take calc 3 with dr robert, DO IT!! he's so knowledgeable and made such a hard class seem so easy. he's my goat!!
Super understanding professor with engaging lectures. Definitely the best math professor I've had at VT so far.

Dr. Robert is a great professor who wants everyone to succeed. Knew everyone's names within a few weeks of class and tried to make office hours accessible for everyone. Generous grader who will absolutely give partial credit on tests which are only free response. Moves homework so you have ample time to complete it after learning it.

Genuinely cares about his students and will respond to emails very quickly. Lectures and organization can be a bit all over the place, but lectures and notes still explain the topics well. Provides practice problems and holds out-of-class review sessions before every exam. Nice to see a math professor that actually wants to see his students succeed

Taught primarily using the chalkboard which is a problem in multi. Not a bad lecturer but wasn't very "commanding" (for lack of a better word) and is easy to block out. Tests also have some unorthodox questions on them that are somewhat different from the practice exam and are harshly graded. However, he is very available outside of class for help.

He clearly cares about how well students know the material. He was always helpful during office hours and held review sessions for all tests. He was always kind and easy to work with as well. He frequently moved homework back if he felt we had not had enough time to complete it and students communicated that.

Mitch Miller is such a strange guy. He talks about board rooms and selling art in corporate environments all the time. I lose points on assignment sometimes and have no idea why because all he gives me is positive feedback. The class is fine, the projects are alright but not my favorite. I took it for a pathways so a lot of his money talk was odd.

Mitch is genuinely the best art teacher I've every had. He's so caring and so kind, and genuinely cares about every one of his students. His projects can be challenging, but he works with every student to complete them no matter their skill level. I would have class with him every year if I could, so definitely get him on your schedule if you can.

Mitch was so nice. Some of the projects were difficult especially if you have no prior drawing experience (I was in principles of drawing), but he gave really helpful feedback and actually helped me learn
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
genuinely a great person, im a very standoffish student and hes the first teacher i felt genuinely cared about me and my learning 

this class is only meant for people who are genuinely motivated to improve and do their best, the workload and grading was the hardest class i took that semester but i learned so much but it was so worth and doable

Professor Miller genuinely changed my college experience. He is one of the most amazing people I have ever met and has inspired me in countless ways. This class is a lot of work, but every bit of the time spent is well worth it. I am so grateful that I could experience this class.
If I could take this class again I would.  He is very understanding and pretty funny.  You have around 8 major projects throughout the semester but he walks you through the process.
He's a great start for people getting into drawing, critiques were always a bit intimidating for me but I don't have that many complaints outside of that
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really cares about his students and willing to accommodate when life happens.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mitch is super knowledgable and really wants to help you succeed at art; he's very caring and his critiques are always helpful and he never puts you down. He can ramble a bit but he's really chill and friendly. Projects can be heavy but if you take time to work on them you'll be alright so long as you can back up your vision. COME TO CLASS!

Dr. Madigan is the best professor I have had in the ISE department, based on his clear teaching style and genuine care for students. Some people don't like the class since you actually have to participate and can't just be on your phone the whole time. I genuinely learned a lot and enjoyed the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: If you show up to class, take notes, and study, you'll be fine. Dr. Madigan made sure to give students everything they needed to fully understand the material. Avoid missing lectures as pop quizzes sometimes occur at the end of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No no no. Do not take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If there was any other option I would take it in a heart beat. He is all lectures, random pop quizzes and 0 accommodation. He picks favorites, tries to intimidate and is not at all nice. Trying to be funny but is rude and grades very harsh. Should another teacher teach this course I'd advise you choose them.

He will not lower standards but he will do everything he can to help you reach that standard and he keeps his word. He will help you whenever you need it. You cannot skip his class because parts of the note will be filled in during class. One of the best professors in ISE and he makes every effort to ensure that you understand the material and why.

Dr. Madigan is literally the best. Try to avoid missing lectures because all of the test and quizzes are based off of the lecture notes. TAs can be hard graders, but if something is really off Dr. Madigan will typically hear out your argument

This dude is so chill. He's a great professor, gives exams that are fair, not too much homework and genuinely cares about your success. He's younger so the class feels more casual and friendly while still productive. Stat for EE is typically tough from what I hear but it's been a breeze with Schwob.

He is a great professor who truly cares about his students. He will take the time to explain things until you understand and encourages students to ask questions. His tests and homework's are fair. I am very fortunate to have had such an amazing professor during my first semester at this school. You would be insane not to take this professor.

Dr. Schwob shows a lot of passion and care for the material he presents to students in the class. I really enjoyed his lectures, and I went to most of them because I found them very useful. The homework assignments were very fair and would directly relate to the material learned in class. Excellent professor overall. Pick him if available.

Dr. Schwob's homeworks were set up clearly, he was very receptive to feedback and wanted to make sure that as many students as possible passed. He understood that he was teaching statistics to ECE students and tried to just impart as many key concepts as possible, not getting bogged down by details that will never be used again.
GOAT fr fr

Overall above average professor. Go to class bc he'll hint at important info to know. His material isn't hard, there can just be a lot of it. His exams are extremely fair (no trick questions, material was clearly on the slides, etc.). He isn't super approachable but you can tell he's serious about his job and wants his students to do well.
Grades on exams and showing up to class. He gives you what you need to know for the exams.

Really nice guy, and a great professor too. He makes it very clear what he wants you to know for tests and that he wants to set his students up for success. Sometimes he goes off on tangents and tells stories, but I didn't mind since his assignments were very fair.

his teaching style claims to be Socratic but is just him talking at you and asking you questions about the case. You learn everything on your own so attending class feels unnecessary but is still graded. He makes tests that are intentionally worded confusingly. Wouldn't recommend.

I love him! I've taken 4 of his classes! He is really great once you get the hang of his teaching style. Homework is a participation grade, but he does cold call, so its definitely beneficial to do the homework. His tests can be tricky in wording, but if you did all the homework and reviewed a little bit, it isn't hard to get at least a 90.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
I graduated in 2017 and still think of Dr. Moore. 

He was the only professor that challenged me.

If you want easy A's and a diploma, avoid him. 

If you want to actually learn something about our country, take every course with him possible.

He often loses patience with students who need extra clarification and cold-calls them without considering their comfort or understanding. Though he means well, his lack of clarity when teaching can cause confusion and stress for students. Exams lack study guides, and the provided review table is too vague to be helpful for his tests.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Attendance is mandatory and his exams are tough but you must keep up with the readings or else you will be entirely lost during discussion based class. I would recommend him infinite times if you want to be challenged and to learn.
Very challenging but doable

Moore is a genuinely okay person. However his teaching and grading style is antiquated, trivial, and condescending. His exams are heavily graded and full of intentionally confusing and misleading wording; he argues this is to challenge students to think critically but it instead causes a huge lack of clarity. I would not recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE Dr. Moore. He assigns a lot of reading, but I found it interesting. In-class participation is a large part of the grade, and he cold calls, but it isn't difficult if you did the readings. He doesn't use computers at all, everything is hard copy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you want to go to law school, the best thing you can do is take Moore's con law classes. It's hard to get a grasp at first, but not hard to get a B or an A if you do the readings. He prepares his students for law school better than any other poli sci profs. If he ever teaches a senior seminar, take it! I loved having a small class with him.

Moore cares about his students, not as scary as he seems. Homework once a class and is completion grade. His tests are super hard-need deep understanding of material. His lectures are so incredibly boring and he teaches at a level that is far above most students and expects you to eventually pick it up. No powerpoint, hard to follow, good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Moore cares about you becoming analytical of cases and court decisions.  He really cares about his students and I think I learned a lot from his class.  However, his test are very hard and are meant to trick you.  This brought my grade down a lot.  I would recommend this class and professor if you are wanting to go to law school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There is no technology allowed in his class. He only wants class discussion. There are no PowerPoints or anything to look at during class. Attendance is required, and homework is due each night. It was extremely hard to focus in his class, he is extremely dry. His tests are also hard.

I'll be honest, this is a difficult class, but if you study and put in the work it can be extremely interesting and rewarding. Professor Moore expects his students to have a deeper understanding of the material than most professors, which is more difficult, but it gives you a much better understanding of the course than pure memorization would.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Moore has some trouble articulating what he's saying and breaking concepts down, but take his class. If you're interested in law at all he's amazing to have as a professor. He has great knowledge of the law and what law school is like. The case briefs are certainly tough in the beginning, but as long as you do it you get credit for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is incredibly dull and difficult to follow. He does not break things down well, and the work load is far too much for a 3000 level course, do not recommend!!

This teacher is dry to listen to and doesn't explain things well.  Every class he requires outlines of the readings, which doubles the homework load, and literally hates electronics, including laptops. He obviously knows his material but talks about it at a level only understood by a few of the students.
Great teacher. The material is complicated and sometimes hard to deal with, but he does a great job at explaining the court cases and such.
No Comments
take her no matter what, best class

Molly was a wonderful professor. She graded by completion but still provided helpful feedback. Her lectures were informative, and she let you pick the topic you researched for the semester. I felt comfortable asking questions in an environment of mutual respect. I would absolutely recommend taking her class.

A very caring person who wants to see you succeed, no matter the circumstances. Attendance is part of your grade, but it is very lax.  However, if you're mostly present, you get easy letter grade boosts at the end of the semester. Her class taught me a lot about exploring my creative writing capabilities without worrying about being judged.

Literally most understanding professor ever. Gives ample amount of time for assignments and also gives grace periods to submit. This class is an easy A as long as you submit all your assignments. She marks assignments as complete/incomplete and gives lot of extra grade boost opportunities. TRUST ME TAKE THIS CLASS! She is super caring too.

Molly is amazing and super sweet. She cares so much for all her students and is super understanding. If you need any help at all, she will help and provide you other resources immediately. Response time to emails and feedback on work is also exceptional. I would recommended her to anyone.
Barley any course work and it's all very easy. Everything is mainly graded for completion, and if you need any help at all, she will help you and provide other resources as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She cares so much about her students and is very understanding about busy schedules or other struggles. She grades on completion and she provides tons of extra credit opportunities. It was honestly the easiest English class I've ever taken and she was so considerate, I would recommend her to anyone.

A lot of extra credit, brings snacks to class. The grading is based on completion. I took both ENGL 1105 & 1106 with her. She is very approachable and gives a lot of freedom to complete the assignments. Highly recommend to take her

Molly is a great professor. Her classes are easy, she gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit. She provides great feedback and is very supportive. She even provides snacks in class. Her grading is mostly based on completion.

I took both ENGL 1105 and 1106 and got a A in her class. I don't like to write personally but her class was extremely easy. Her grading is based on completion. She gives tons of extra credit and opportunity to take two late submissions. She cares about the students a lot. Would 100% take her class again.

She is honestly the most chill instructor ever. I don't like writing at all, but she gives you so much freedom on her projects, and you can always talk with her if you have concerns. She cares about her student A LOT. And brings snacks and pizzas some times. AND THERE ARE A LOT OF EXTRA CREDITS. All easy too. Almost impossible to fail.
Enjoyed all of the assignments. Everything was available for us to do at our own pace and all feedback was thorough and constructive.

Course syllabus DOES NOT match course description. There is no technical aspect to the 'digital media' part of the class unlike other sections of the same course. Get ready for lots of discussion posts and vague assignment sheets.
I had Dr. Mueller for Tech Writing. The course is very manageable and he will drop everything to help you succeed. He is a very nice person also. Highly recommend.
Used my first ever w on him enough said

MGT 3404: DO NOT DO NOT take Musselman for 3404 trust!!! Does not post or record lecture slides, lectures are long and boring, includes random lecture content in tests, exams free response + multiple choice but are too specific, you have to know the textbook word for word to do well. Everyone I know dropped the course and is taking it over summer.
He has immediate quizzes after every class and lectures are extremely boring.

I had him for MGT3404 and it was not good. He gives long, boring lectures and then immediately quizzes you afterwards. Quizzes and exams are mostly fill-in-the-blank and are extremely specific. Exams are a big part of your grade and there's no review for them. The only good thing about this class is there's not a lot of weekly homework.

He is a very nice person and gives good lectures. There are not a lot of homework assignments but the problem sets take a lot of time and directions are not strict, which is good because there is not one correct answer but difficult to start and depict what he is looking for. KNOW HOW TO USE EXCEL (the basics at least).

Ryan assigns large simple assignments that take an extremely long time to complete. This leaves us, students, feeling as if the class is pointless and unnecessarily strict. Overall, he provides an education that is so broad, shallow, and time intensive that students are left despising the subject.
