Took for MGT 3404. The worst professor I've ever had a tech. Doesn't do review sessions before exams, only thing he gives for study resources is a list of terms. Vague lectures on easy concepts but quizzes and exams consist of extremely specific fill in the blank questions. Would rather watch paint dry than listen to his lectures. Avoid.

I have had Ryan for two semesters, and both classes were made unnecessarily difficult by him. He gives long lectures that go through a lot of content very quickly and then tests you on very specific information that didn't seem important in lecture and pulls random facts from the textbook. He is very unclear about what he expects on assignments.
Makes an easy class incredibly difficult, assigns a lot of work, confusing lectures, and confusing assignments. Just not good.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher and very smart

Ryan is not good at taking feedback. His class is a heavy group work project-based class, but he also gives broad and unnecessary notes for which he gives two exams. Nothing he teaches provides real-world value because it is so vague and quickly covered. This class requires lots of outside research and asking questions to decipher what he wants.

Her canvas site is very unorganized and confusing. So much busy work. Tests are really difficult, making it very hard to get an A in this class, when this class should be an easy A. Expect a ton of discussion boards every class meeting. I would not take this class again and I do not recommend it to anyone needing to take this class for credit.

She teaches at MS State now. Really good teacher she just isnt the most organized with her online submissions so make sure you turn things in before the portal closes because she does not except late work.
She's really nice and helpful. I went to her for extra help a couple of times. Class was fun, but I couldn't bring coffee...

Great teacher, very informative lectures and overall a really good experience in the class. Go to office hours if you're confused because they help a lot, and he's very willing to explain things and work through problems. It's clear he wants students to succeed. If you put in effort and ask for help when you need it, you will do well in this class.

Nart is an excellent teacher who is passionate about mathematics, which makes the lectures easy and engaging to follow. It is very easy to ask a question in class and he is always eager to help students who need it. The homework's and tests were challenging, but not unfair, and if you put in the effort you will succeed

Had him for Calc 2 and disliked him due to the first test being GENUINELY impossible (tests got easier), but as the year went on, I built a relationship with Nart through office hours(please go) and the class got better. Overall, the class really just comes down to how much effort you're willing to put in, and if you try, Nart will reward you
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You will have to teach yourself

Nart moves through lessons quickly. Showing up to classes is recommended, as this is where all questions can be answered. Attending office hours is a tremendous help, where you can get excellent one-on-one answers. Homework becomes very easy as he will help and walk you through it. Nart is very passionate about math, and it shows.

Very smart, very nice. Can't teach to save his life. Has very thick Eastern European accent, but what he can control is his handwriting, and that's god awful. If you ask him a question, he'll interpret it how he wants and answer something else. He goes through his lessons very quick and explains things horribly. Says he'll help you but won't do it.
Good professor, did a lot of lecturing, two group projects (choose members wisely), do everything on time, participate a lot.

Good professor, even better person. Course material was actually interesting. Does a great job with lectures. Tests and quizzes are not difficult if you study. Group projects were very time intensive, pick a good group and you will learn a lot. Tough grader on the project but many groups did do poorly Id take her again in a heartbeat.

She is one of my favorite professors. She's available during office hours and replies quickly to emails asking for help with homework. She honestly cares about her students and wants us all to succeed. Her lectures are also really good. If you get the chance to take her do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Rogers is my favorite teacher. She gives clear examples during class, exams are very similar to in class questions. She always responds to emails promptly and is extremely helpful during office hours. She's super kind and encouraging. I would 100% recommend her. If you go to class, do the hw, and read the textbook you'll get an A.

Rogers is great at teaching this class and is super nice. It shows that she genuinely cares about her students and constantly encourages them. Her powerpoints include everything you need to know, leaving you prepared for exams. ACIS 2115 has a rep of being the most dropped business class so I 100% recommend Rogers as your professor.

By far the worst teacher/proffesor I have ever had. Not a single person who took Construction Surveying liked her. She would just read the slides word for word and leave afterward. One of the TA's did most of the teaching, like teaching us how to set up the equipment and do our assignments. Was very rude to students as well.
Over lectures, left the class for an hour then came back

Good overall experience. She does a good job teaching the software used in class and has helpful videos to go along with difficult parts of assignments. Class starts off with lots of work that is difficult and time consuming but gets much easier the second half of the year.

Lectures were great and assignments were interesting for the first 2/3 of this course. In the end it felt like we zoomed too fast through a lot of topics.

Teaching was not his main priority. 5 lectures omitted. Hard to get a hold of. Treated the course more like a capstone. Overall would still tentatively recommend, but just be aware.
He is one of the best professors, He makes the challenges rewarding.
It was a pleasure to take a class with Dr.Ramakrishnan. The class was very interesting, fun and I believe I have learned a ton in a rather short  period of time.
Awesome professor, really explains the concepts well and makes sure you understand them.  Has high expectations, however... don't take him if you're lazy.

Engaging and often kinda funny lectures. Very generous with partial credit on exams. Grades homework and exams quickly with good feedback. Made it clear what to study for each exam (provided practice tests + in class review before each one). Does have weekly classwork (not difficult) and for about half attendance was mandatory. Excellent professor.
good and knowledgeable professor, but she doesn't post lectures on Canvas, so try to go to class as much as possible. Tests weren't too bad, but you will have to study for them to do well on them.

The "bad": doesn't post lectures, doesn't grade all homework problems

The good: tests are genuinely easy if you do the practice test, which are very similar, super forgiving with partial credit on the homework and tests, and the lectures set you up very well to do the homework and the test for the most part. She is literally my favorite math prof.

I had Prof. Chung for discrete, and while it was definitely a class I had to study for, I ended up actually enjoying the class and what we learned (and I don't like math). Prof. Chung was funny and gave good lectures, but you definitely need to go to class. She doesn't tell you when the quizzes are so if you miss class that day you're screwed.
Does not post the notes unless you go to class, so if you miss a class it's very hard to catch up. Also a very tough grader and not very understanding.

Provides extremely detailed notes, and great lectures despite her accent. Hw and test questions were exactly like the ones in the notes. Strict with deadlines and grading, including partial credit, but since the hw and test questions were just like the notes, it was not a huge issue. Very fun and engaging professor that could get the class laughing

Professor Chung was great. Her lecture notes where incredibly helpful and if you studied her tests were genuinely easy. She isn't trying to trick you and every question is almost directly from the homework. Her accent is honestly not that hard to understand either she just forgets prepositions sometimes but if you follow the notes you'll be fine.

Her lectures are very engaging (I had her at 8:00 AM and it was the case even then). Also, before any test, she would always make these comprehensive review sheets in addition to practice problems, which really made it easy to study.

She is an amazing and hilarious professor, and she clearly cared about her students. She explained the concepts well, provided reviews for each test that were very similar to the tests themselves, and didn't assign too much homework. However, she usually doesn't post the notes, so be sure to go to class.
Funny and taught linear algebra well - one homework assignment every week, not too difficult
*3124, but she was good. Went through notes a little too fast but always answered questions. Homework's were fair, tests were easy.

She was nice. At first, she's difficult to understand but she recognizes it and does her best to project her voice. I had it at 8 am so sometimes she would be a little cranky but so was most of the class. I would say if you can get her, try to. She's better than most of the Math Department.
She takes points off on assignments unless you do things exactly her way (which is weird). If you have taken linear algebra before this, go with a different teacher.

Lectures were very well explained, and she made a mini review of each chapter and lecture which was very helpful for the exams. Exams are very similar to practice tests so definitely do those. Gives webassign and written homework but they are actually very helpful in helping you understand the concepts. Office hours are a great resource as well.

Her notes are accessible and easy to understand if you consistently pay attention. She provides great help when you go to her office hours (a lot of times during the week). Tests are very similar to the homework. Provides a lot of practice opportunities. Put in the work and she'll help you. Out of all math teachers I've had at VT, she is the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lenient grader, clear and easy to follow lecturer, but attendance is required since notes aren't posted and there are in-class submissions for a grade.

She's honestly the best math professor I've had so far. She explained things very well during lectures and homeworks were fair, sometimes hard but doable. Her tests are similar to her practice tests so as long as u review u should be good. Her tests were not that bad. She's very understanding and will literally help u with anything if u just ask.
Test and homework are straightforward and reasonable. Her study guides and practice tests are really helpful. If you study you'll be fine.
She's very straightforward, makes the lectures super easy to understand. Very little homework and tests are pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best math professor I had. She was super easy to follow, very clear about her expectations. Good teacher, her class didn't require much effort to understand the material just do homeworks and pay attention in class. She's funny and caring too.
Worst professor ever. Does not care if you took this class in the past or not. Very strict with class attendance. For homework only grades a few problems out of like 10.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are easy to follow but notes are not usually posted. Sometimes does a review day before exams and posts those notes, but not always. Tests are graded fairly, but only contain a few questions, so even one question wrong can hurt your grade. DiffEqs is a tough course but she does a pretty good job, although kind of rushed the last few weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take her on my kids bruh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very difficult to understand in lectures she speaks in broken English.  I had her for discrete and her handwriting was also not very good so it was hard to understand what she was saying or writing. She doesn't post her notes and isn't accommodating at all with grading.
not feeling her

I didn't even realize that linear algebra was considered a weedout (especially if you look at VT institutional data). until someone mentioned it at the end of the semester. She was a phenomenal professor. There was a lot of homework, but it genuinely prepared me for the tests.

Prof Chung makes linear very easy and understandable. Her homework is reasonable and helpful. Her practice exams are very similar to the actual exams. The exams themselves are very straightforward; she doesn't;t try to trick you. Exams are out of 20 points tho, so if you lose some, its hard to get a good grade. Doesn't post notes so go to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She explains things very well and cares about your understanding. The homework and classwork problems are sometimes harder than the exams which makes you feel very prepared once you go to take the exam. One of the better math profs.

Overall I think she's one of the best professors in the math department. Homework assignments were pretty reasonable. Her exams are similar to her practice tests and homework. She does randomly give out a quick 1 or 2 question classwork every now and then and she doesn't post lecture notes so it's important to go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She gives many example problems in lectures, which is good if you find example problems useful. I personally couldn't really pay attention because watching someone do problems is not engaging for me. Great lecture notes, if you have an IPad you will love this prof. Be careful for pop-quizzes. They're easy but you'll miss them if you skip class.

Chung provides note templates so you can just print them or annotate the PDF. She does have an accent, but I didn't find it to be a problem. The notes contain lots of examples so it's easier to understand the material. The "pop quizzes" are open note and open peer. She provides exam review sheets, which were super helpful for the exams
Class was not too difficult and professor goes through a lot of example problems during lectures. Homework prepares you well for both the quizzes and tests.

Her accent isn't THAT bad, at least for me. She indeed does not post lecture notes, but if you're legitimately sick and email her, she will help. The class seems to like her. Energetic lectures and short, easy tests. The homework can be time consuming. Find a friend group to study with and get notes from, if necessary.

I do acknowledge that I did not try as hard as I should have, but here a few cons I have. Doesn't post lecture notes. Goes through lecture fast. Hard to understand with her accent. When providing an answer key for practice problems, she doesn't provide the entire proof. Sometimes quizzes/exams will contain questions in none of her prep material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Chung is an amazing professor. She really understands her course material. She likes when the class asks her a lot of questions. She talks kind of quick, but she will usually post lecture notes on Canvas and also is always available during her office hours. She hints to certain questions that may be on exams. Overall, take her if possible!

She makes it easy to do well in the class if you utilize her lecture notes and homework. Her tests are not unreasonable and reflect the material pretty well, and she makes a point to clarify what you need to know. This is a rarity for the VT mathematics department.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved her style of teaching, doesn't bs a lot and is always straight to the point. she is very kind and knowledgeable as well. However, if you want to get the grade you want you're gonna have to work hard af. We had two psets due every week (classwork and homework) both of which were very doable if you start early.

Chung starts lectures before class and goes after the time limit. The homework is long and hard and due on Fridays. Sometimes, the homework does not match up with the lessons. Maybe she is better in person, but online, I do not recommend.

Chung is a great professor. The course material is definitely difficult to an extent but she is a very thorough teacher and getting an A is far from impossible. Be prepared to takes notes quickly or get them from her when the class ends. She makes sure to go over every topic comprehensively before moving on. The tests are doable if you attend class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Chung is a really engaging math professor. Lectures can move really fast so you have to take good notes, but she teaches very thoroughly. Often she will review content from previous lectures, so there is plenty of opportunity to ask questions if you are confused. No curve on tests or final grade, and demands respect and attention during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: do not take this class if it isn't required. his lectures are written in his own code and do not make sense. test averages are super low and he rarely curves.

Firm but appropriate & fair expectations for honest hard work and learning. Lots of practice in class and for HW. Read the textbook before class. I think he's the best physics teacher (clear voice and engaging). The class is hard, but you are in engineering so… it is manageable if you put in the work. TAKE DR. NELSON. Office hours are great.

Uses I-Clicker so you cant skip class. Lectures are boring but useful and if you pay attention in class dont use chat for all HW and do practice problems, you will do fine. Hes a decent professor and is very practical about his lectures not very theoretical.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. The professors slides are impossible to read because it is all written in his own code. Also the test have nothing to do with the homework or the slides. His quiz averages are in the 60s and he doesn't always curve. Just save yourself the stress.
Do not recommend. This class is very difficult for a pathways course, save yourself the time and skip this course. Professor doesn't teach the class well and the cheat sheets do not help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For a science pathway it should not have been this difficult. Average class exams score are around the 60s. If you want to succeed in this class don't even bother with the slides he presents which are basically written in code with so many symbols and unnecessary abbreviations. You will have to read the chapters in the textbook which are lengthy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His tests are insanely difficult. The cheat sheet doesn't even help much. Nothing connects; the lectures, the iClickers, and the Pearson homework all feel completely separate. Save yourself the time and frustration.

Nelson is alright. There's iclickers so you have to go to class. He does give out a lot of extra credit, so your grades can be boosted. Exams are tough but he allows cheat sheets and he curves the exams. Insanely hard to pay attention to his class. His lecture slides are pretty much just symbols and pictures, so don't depend on his slides to study.

His lectures were extremely hard to pay attention in. No matter how hard you may try to pay attention, you probably won't be able to! Attendance is part of your grade because he does iClicker questions that are graded on accuracy, not participation. Exams were tough, do not recommend.

Bad overall.  Was very behing on lectures, kinda hard to listen to. Spent way too much time going over examples, and overall wasn't an effective learning experience for me. I would personally steer away.

I had this at 8am which could have been part of the issue but this class is so easy to ignore and you can get by the homework without learning. I did not put my full effort into the class but this was hard and I felt like I didn't learn much.

Man this class was hard. Idek what to say. New material is covered in a video we are supposed to watch before every week begins. The actual lectures are kind of just random problems and iClickers. There are 3 exams and the averages were SCARY. Lab, HW and EC quizzes are grade savers. Fr never miss those cause the exams are only 10 questions.

I literally just came here to say that this is a waste of your time. Even if you make the conscious decision to REALLY focus you will inevitably zone out within 3 minutes in his lectures. The class is easy but since attendance is mandatory it just feels like purgatory sitting in a chair trying to make sense of the improv lectures he gives.

Professor Nelson and Virginia Tech's Physics Department create the perfect storm to be a headache for any student in PHYS 2306. Nelson expects you to watch hours of introductory videos to topics outside of class. The Physics Department has no clue how to make exams, and constantly gives questions far more difficult than any previous on exams.

Nelson is decent. He started off really strong and I was honestly surprised with all of the bad reviews, but as the material got harder, the lectures got less helpful, and eventually everyone kinda just stopped caring. Physics 2 sucks and I don't think Nelson made it easier, but he's fine. It's more of a material problem than a teaching problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His lectures are basically reading the slides, but he provides a lot of practice as a resource and his office hours is helpful! He may say some unexpected comments if you disrupt his lecture, so don't get at all offended! Besides that, he's alright.

This professor is a life saver. One day, I was on the toilet in my dorm. The toilet paper roll there was extremely thin. I would only get1-2 sheets of toilet paper when I tried to pull it out of the dispenser. I remembered from one of his lectures that I should pull the roll fast (something to do with friction). I got more toilet paper as a result.

I swear he has to be the most dry person on this planet. Nobody can get through a lecture paying attention the whole time(no, for real, everyone watches netflix...). I taught myself in 45 minutes what took him 18 hours of class time to teach us. Worst of all HE SKIPS STEPS AND GETS MAD WHEN YOU ASK HIM TO SHOW YOU. Super annoying.

Honestly, not the greatest Professor in terms of teaching, but he gives you everything you need to succeed. Cheat sheets, extra credit quizzes, and rounds up your final grade by an entire point. The kids who didn't pass the class have awful work ethics or are just unintelligent. A mid B can be achieved in this class with moderate effort.

Uses iclicker.  Boring and over-complicated lectures.  I think our class average was a 55 on the final, the department ended up having to give us a major curve because of the poor performance.  Pre quizzes and tests were very hard but at least you have a few opportunities for extra credit.  Be prepared to teach yourself just about everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory. iClicker questions every single class so if you miss a few it tanks your grade. A lot of the time the iClicker questions are based on slides that he hasn't taught us yet so it seems unfair at times. He's a fine professor I have no complaints about that. He lets you use a big cheat sheet for tests which is super helpful.
He was lowkey boring but other than that he was aight
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I just have a little complaint about Nelson. He is a helpful and nice professor, but his lectures are kind of boring. I would suggest reading the textbook before lectures. His powerpoints are kind of a headache. He abbreviates everything so much that they make no sense. It makes it impossible for student to review it after class or for tests.

Dr. Nelson was good at teaching, however, his class was boring. PHYS 2324 is pass/fail for everyone and if you have above a 75, you won't have to take the final. To complete the homework you'll have to do a decent amount of book reading as he doesn't cover everything in class, but it's very hard to not pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, everyone complains about the physics department at VT. Nelson wasn't great, but as physics professors go, I think he was very clear. He does lots of example problems in class, and honestly, that's all you need. He wasn't amazing, but if you pay attention to the practice problems he goes over, you should be alright.

I already rated Dr. Nelson for his 1056 course, but this semester he seems to have changed a bit. There is absolutely no math involved in 1056, so I don't know if he'll change his 1055 curriculum for that. He became a bit more energetic this semester which was nice, and his lectures were more interesting. If you need a science credit, take this

You need to read the textbook and take notes on it to do well in this class. His lectures are less helpful than the textbook, but he takes attendance through iClicker. It is kind of a boring class, but it is not the worst for a science credit.
Just boring in lecture. Reading material from chapter 5 for quizzes while still lecturing on chapter 1. Slow paced lectures with high paced homework and material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am a physics major, so my opinion of this class is a lot different than the rest of the reviews. Yes, there is math. But it is so incredibly easy if you simply read the textbook, do the homework, and pay the bare minimum of attention in the class. Dr. Nelson is a grump, however, and didn't even make me excited for astronomy, which is my minor.
Nelson is a good choice for taking modules for classes that are from CC into Virginia Tech. He makes the class low key and it is a pass fail. It is comprised of HW and quizzes that are not too bad.

Required weekly homework that is often estimated to take a couple hours but in my case took much longer. Intro to astronomy was a very math heavy course. Doesn't do well breaking things down for an entry level course. At times he was very disrespectful, makes students feel like an inconvenience for asking questions.

Must read, must go to class, some extra credit offered, cheatsheet allowed for tests. Disrespectful to students, math heavy course, often unclear when lecturing, class avg on exam 1  50%, class avg on exam 2  60%, doesn't explain math portion well, work hard for mediocre grade. 10/10 would NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: dr. nelson doesn't seem to know much about astronomy; he often backtracks when going over material, such as mistaking units frequently (i.e. nanoseconds for lightyears...). this course is math heavy. reading the textbook is a requirement because his lectures teach nothing. over half of the class dropped after the first exam due to an average of 55.
Does not explain math well at all and incorporates it to much into the course. Seems to be good at astronomy but he is terrible at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Nelson was unprepared and unaware of how to do scientific notation. His level of experience is too high for entry level courses which makes it difficult to understand his content. 15 point curve on the midterm because of how terribly the class did... BEWARE

Terrible teacher possibly the worst I've ever seen. First professor I've had that literally yelled at our class to shut the hell up. Furthermore he integrates way too much math into the course. DO NOT take this course if you're looking for an easy class. Don't get me wrong you could get a good grade in that class but it would lots of hard effort
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dude gets so lost in class. Tests are hard and gives terriblest curves. Don't take if you want an easy A for a pathway class like I did
Awful teacher. Terrible at keeping the class engaged and has a terrible attitude. I had to drop the class after 3 weeks because it was so bad

I cant attest to his teaching because my eyes glazed over for most of the zoom calls, but Nelson is the most clear and transparent teacher Ive had. Provides very detailed exam information and lists out each topic thats covered. As long as you understand the pearsons homework, review the exam information page, and pray for a nice TA youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Personally he was one of my best online teachers, he was able to teach me all the content presented very well in an online environment. The only reason I didnt get an A was because of my physics recitation TA who gave me all zeros, not because of him.

One of the better Physics professors, does a great job at explaining the material even when its super difficult. The material in this class is just plain hard, but I think I managed to pass because of his clarity. The exams and quizzes were very close to homework problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I'm good at math, and this is the hardest class I've ever taken. Not sure if I just don't get Physics or what, but this class is hard.

Dr. Nelson is clear and concise in lectures. There have been a few times that he fails to explain a concept, but anything he skips he either addresses during the next lecture or in an example in class. You do need an iClicker for this class, any type works, and there is at least 2 questions per day with it. There are also reading quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was a pretty good professor. He knew what he was talking about, easy to understand, clear examples, thoroughly answered questions, and the problems were similar to test questions. I got As on the midterms and its easy if you go to class and do your homework . If youre looking for an upbeat exciting professor hes not your guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Nelson is a decent professor but is not very enthusiastic about what he is teaching. He often rushes through lectures and doesnt go over key conceptual questions in as much detail. He is however easy to understand and the class offers so much extra credit that an A is attainable with a decent work ethic and critical thinking skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests are extremely difficult: 20 multiple choice questions, no partial credit. Nelson is helpful in emails and responds quickly. However, he does not seem to care when teaching the class. He is there to lecture and does not really care if anyone listens or understands the material. Worst class I have taken thus far (just finished freshman year).
Completely lost the entire session. rude, little help to students. failing test averages.

Astro Lab Fall06. He's awful! Go to ratevtteachers.com and read details about him.Syllabus said 1 lab grade would be dropped but then at the end of the semester decided to reward people with perfect attendance a 0.5% curve.I had a overall final grade of 89.55% and since I missed ONE class (that he told us we could miss) he refused to curve me 0.45%
I had him for physics recitation. He hated giving the quizes as mush as the students hated taking them
had him for my lab teacher in both semesters of astronomy, it was interesting and I enjoyed it
This class is a great choice for an easy A in English 1105. There is barely any homework, and the classes are engaging and fun. Definitely one of the better English professors on campus.

Professor Baker is a really good professor, she really cares about all students and this class overall is not hard as long as you show up to class (your attendance is considered for your grade..) there's really no reason why you shouldn't be getting an A
Amazing. If you get her, TAKE HER! There are so many extra credit opportunities and she is a great professor.

I had a lot of freedom to be creative in this class! Textbook is required but we only used it a couple times. There's homework pretty much every class but it's typically easy and ties back into the big project we're working on. She very willing to give extensions and offers a bunch of extra credit opportunities.

I LOVEE her she's been my favorite teacher so far. Her assignments are easy and this class does require a textbook but I barely used mine during the course. She gives LOTS of extra credit there's really no reason you should fail this course.

Professor Netta Baker is one of my favorite English professors. Her classes are fun, she's super helpful and there are plenty of chances to earn extra credit in class and through assignments. Attendance is mandatory and affects your final grade. Missing assignments can hurt your grade significantly if you haven't done any extra credit work.

I took Ms. Baker for my ENGL1105 class, and she was a great professor. If you have any questions, she'll definitely try her best to help you out. She also gave us donuts on our first day and last day of class, which was really sweet of her.

Very easy and independent class, entirely lecture-based except for a video before every test. Attendance is taken with top hat but can be viewed anywhere. I really appreciate Professor Johnson, as he was a decent lecturer and was dryly funny at times. You need the book just for the online quizzes, but honestly, they were doable without it.

Professor Johnson is a nice guy and is extremely passionate about what he teaches. I don't know why he scored so low because the class was not bad by any means. Each class has a lecture and tiny pop-quizzes, but nothing is kept in the dark as long as you read the whole syllabus. Do the work and quizzes and you'll do just fine. I enjoyed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was surprised to see this professor rated so poorly. The only thing I would say is that this class is not an easy A. This was my first time in an Earth science/geoscience class so that may be why. But if you cover the material daily, take notes, and read or watch videos on the topics, you should be fine. He is a nice and funny guy.

He wasn't my fav prof by any means, but I was sad to see how low he was rated :( He's an older guy, classes are more traditional in terms of academics, but he made lectures fun and has cool slides. If you're looking for an easy A, this is not the class for you. However, don't freak out at the other reviews. He's a nice guy and you'll learn a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really liked the structure of this class. There's very little homework assigned (short textbook quizzes), in-class participation through Tophat questions, and no final (course is split into 3 exams). He does a good job of teaching and you can tell he's passionate about the subject. As long as you actually put in the work, you'll do fine.

This is probably the worst class I've ever taken and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. The professor is nice but it's just lecture after lecture and the most impossible tests. I'm a business major and was just looking for an easy pathway but THIS IS NOT IT. Coming from a student that gets fairly good grades this class sucks.

I swear I have never hated a class more. You can take notes on every PowerPoint slide and still fail the tests. TopHat quizzes every class, and pathways assignments that somehow ALWAYS gave me a plagiarism issue even when I reworded the notes that I took...
AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Nice guy but his class is hard for no reason and tests are on very detailed stuff that you briefly go over in class. All he does in class is goes over the PowerPoint that you already get the only reason you have to be in class is for the four top hats he gives every class.

The worst teacher I've had. He just goes over the notes he already gives you. The only reason to go to class is for 3 top hat questions. Try not to fall asleep in his class. Exams are hard for no reason and make up 67 percent of your grade. Not even a nice guy if you go and ask him for help.

Professor Neil is a nice person, but his test are hard for no reason. You literally do the same thing every class and the powerpoint are not detailed at all. The only thing that will keep you from failing is the pathways and quizzes. If I were you I would not take this class if you want to fail almost every test. Only good side, there's no final.

The other reviews are mostly bogged down prior grading issues. The issue with this class is that you have to cough up money for tophat. Trivial exams if you study lecture notes. You can skip if you do the tophat questions at home, but you have to watch your screen like a hawk as there's no notifications. Textbook is required but it's free online

This was my by far my favorite professor this semester, he ensures his lectures are very engaging and is an overall super funny and nice guy. He takes attendance through TopHat but it can be accessed from anywhere. Not a hard class just make sure you take notes and review some days before exam day. I never scored below a 95 on any of his exams.
He was a overall good guy and taught well! Only problem was that you needed to use the textbooks for the quizzes to answer any of the quiz questions.

Exams are VERY lecture heavy. He uses TopHat (like iclicker) during lectures, they'll keep your grade afloat. Quizzes are easy, based of textbook but usually find answers if you look up the questions. No final, just exam on last 3rd part of class. Pay attention during lectures, basically everything he says- tests are impossible if you don't study.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good teacher, but in the beginning he emphasized needing a textbook for the at home quizzes but it wasn't useful. His tests are really specific so you must study throughly. He also grades real hard on the pathway assignments. Theres a ton of material to learn so please stay on top of his slides.

He's honestly a great guy, I just didn't do well on any of the exams which were extremely lecture-heavy. The information overload demotivated me throughout the semester and I tried BSing my way through the exams which didn't work (obviously). If you do your TopHats and pathways assignments well enough you're going to get a C or above.

Neil Johnson is honestly a great guy and his class is organized in a way I enjoy. Besides the lecture exams, you have a ton of time to get all of your assignments done. Paying for Top Hats (his way of grading attendance) is probably the worst part of this class, but overall, I really enjoyed it

He lectures straight from his slides, it gets VERY boring. He is nice, but boring. Slides are posted on canvas though. Attendance is not mandatory, but he has TopHat questions throughout the lectures that are graded. Tests are hard; definitely need to study for them. I thought using the practice quizzes through the textbook were most helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He can be very boring at times but every once in a while he will use a dad joke during the lecture which will sometimes be funny. He also lets class out up to 30 minutes early and he never teaches the full length of his class. His final exam is not cumulative, instead it is just the last third of the material for the class, which is super nice.

He has iClicker questions, not actually clicker but i forget the program he uses, every class which sucks because the material isn't the most engaging, but he tries to make as enjoyable as possible. The tests aren't that hard and they are curved, so if your looking to fill a pathway this isn't a bad choice

He is very knowledgeable of the material and many personal stories to help relate it to the real world. I found it more beneficial to just listen to his lectures than taking notes, he posts them on canvas anyway. Tests should be studied for, but are not difficult, anything lower than a B is rare for the prepared. Looking forward to minerals lab!

Dr. Johnson had boring lectures, going straight off the slides. But he used anecdotes and mnemonics to help students learn the content. He was accessible during office hours and provided good feedback on grades. He assigned a bit of homework, with textbook readings (which helped a lot on the exams so read them), essays, and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson was great, he's obviously passionate about what he does and enjoys teaching. Gets grades out fast for such a big class, and seems like a cool dude. Makes lectures more interesting with jokes and little stories, but they can get boring sometimes. Just follow directions for the essays and skim the textbook and you'll be good.

Dr. Johnson is a very intelligent man that genuinely loves to teach what he is talking about. However, his test are abnormally hard, even with study an absurd amount, you just never feel prepared. Tophat and the pathway assignments keep you afloat in the class. Overall, a great guy, just maybe not the best teacher.

The class itself is relatively easy but the tests are worded very weird and actually surprisingly difficult. Grade dropped a letter because of the tests. Also VERY lecture heavy. Attendance taken by TopHat questions in class (which you have to pay for... thanks Neil!)
Good guy just has VERY heavy lectures.

The quizzes and pathways essays are what kept me afloat in this class. The exams kicked my butt every time because they're a bit more complex than the questions found on quizzes. The lecture videos themselves were alright. Nothing spectacular.

Professor Johnson is a really nice man, and will offer you feedback if you send him a quick email. However, there are 5 tests that are only 8 in depth questions, so if you don't do well on them it can hurt your grade quickly. He is very understanding though and implements drops and curves, so if you watch the lectures it is not too too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor sent out an email stating our final exam was optional with the exact words how to determine IF you should take the final exam and then feel free to ignore the final exam. Any student with a brain interprets this as an optional exam. He then proceeds to put in 0s for every single student ultimately bringing everyone a letter down

The exams were only 8 questions and were impossibly hard. I did terribly on most of them, but he curves them really generously. He is a really nice guy and is willing to help if you ask him, however, the class is extremely difficult. The exams are not really like the notes (they're application of course) but are very challenging.

Tests were only 8 questions and had terrible, confusing questions that had answers like "all of the above" and "none of the above" at the same time. Super harsh on our Pathways essays. I would not take him again.

Worst teacher I have ever had. His 8 question exams are impossible to study for and the materials he directs you to help none. You shouldnt be able to fail an open textbook exam yet Neil has made that somehow possible. Ive never felt better dropping a class and for reference I am at 3.8 gpa student who puts in the work so dont bother taking it.

Ridiculous professor. His exams are impossible to study for - it has barely anything to do with the notes and is basically a guessing game. Absolutely do not take this professor, save yourself the struggle and pain.

I didn't really try in his class and I got a B+, so it's not hard to get an A-/A. He's very understanding and nice to all of his students and there's barely any work, other than to study for the tests and answer some attendance questions. I enjoyed his class and recommend it for anyone who needs another science course.

Hes a good professor. The tests are hard if you dont study - so be sure to take notes in class. Hes updated since clickers (its TopHat now) but thats the only attendance part. But yes DONT buy the textbook, you wont use it. Many of his test questions have to do with the lectures, which have specific details he wants you t remember. Good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK. Seriously. You won't open it. Don't forget to do the quizzes, they're easy with answers mostly on Quizlet. Pull up the lecture files during lectures cause he goes really fast. Really tough tests, STUDY THE LECTURE NOTES.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The test have nothing to do with what he lectures it is all from the textbook. You have to go for top hat questions that are 4 points a class
Extremely nice guy. I would not enjoy the class at all if I didn't have Dr. Johnson; he makes it so that the class isn't so bad to go to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I did okay on quizzes and top hat but the tests which are most of the grade are specific and impossible to study for. I do not recommend him this should have been an easy and it was actually difficult.

So first of all don't get the book. Second His tests are ridiculous and hard to study for cause it's all based on lectures. If he gave a study guide I would have done well. Didn't help the subject was sooooo boring.

There isn't much homework. There is 1 or 2 quizzes every week based on the chapter and they're really easy, but the tests are very, very hard. The tests are all lecture based and you have to write down everything he says to be able to really study. He's not a very interesting speaker. Very monotone.

Exams are the bulk of the grade. He does not seem to respect students and I felt as though he was talking down to me most of the time. He tests on specifics, not general material. The reading will help but his exams are based on his lectures not the reading.

So. Ill give him this. He drops a ton of your work that you didnt do good on. There is no extra credit. His exams are stupid hard. He curves but its non existent. Send help if u have him. Praying for u.

Very nice guy, corny jokes. Hard class though, you have to go to class to do Tophat questions (which are confusing and tricky) which he puts on the exams word for word. Powerpoints are very basic and do not include information that you need to know for the exam; you have to read the textbook and even then you still don't know all the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Attendance is graded by iClicker questions. The only homework you have are 5 question quizzes, most the answers are online. Exams are easy. They are all the same (multiple choice, matching, and T or F). I do spend a lot of time studying for each exam, but I'm always happy with the outcome of my grade. He's such a sweet guy and cares about your grad
