Not that great of a prof. His lectures are very boring and he makes the test basically impossible. Last semester, the average for both midterms and the final was below a 60%. Take full advantage of the TA's though, they are super helping.

He's not a bad teacher like everybody is saying. He's a boomer so he believes in the whole "i've been teaching for 30 years so I know what I'm doing" type. You should definitely keep up with the workload and take advantage of the TAs or you will fail. You can do the labs early and ever visit a lab, like I did but if you need help PLEASE go. Not bad

Barnette does a fine job in class. If you go to lectures, and are actively involved with trying to learn the material (e.g. talk to TA's and frequent the CS Lounge) then you will pass. People say that he is too harsh, but I had him in both 1114 and 2114 and I believe he is just preparing his students for what life will be like in the industry.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Too many people take this course without prior programming experience when it is "highly recommended" and don't go over concepts and PowerPoint slide before starting assignments and it doesn't help that so many kids share entire methods and CLASSES. But barnette is ok.

There are 5 major projects, the last one is a group project. There are 2 tests and a final, the tests are very difficult. Don't really do much in class. We were consistently a week behind on lectures. He is pretty funny and entertaining though.

He is definitely knowledgeable of programming, but his computer programmer nature makes it hard for him to get points across concisely. The class has weekly assignments, but if you don't do them early and talk to the TAs you won't be able to get them done. He is a nice guy though and will extend deadlines if people are having problems.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dwight is the worst professor I have had so far. He doesn't care about this class and if you don't have a friend who knows the stuff then you wont do well. The labs are easy but the programs take forever and the test are ridiculously hard and unfair. He has ignored some of my emails and unfairly graded some of my assignments without explanation.

Barnette's lectures only seemed to "teach" the people who had been coding for years. To top it off, the way he teaches is very dry. He actually came in and subbed one time for another class and my brain instinctively switched off when I heard his voice.

His teaching style is very unclear. The exams(except for the final) come from the practice exams. He assigns quite a few programs, but there is adequate time to get them done. Go to office hours and he will sit there and help you until you figure it out. He is very nice, but the grading is a little harsh at times.  But hes nice

Honestly a nice person but not a clear lecturer. Class starts with very basic material and then makes a jump out of nowhere into insanely hard material. His notes are not helpful and the class is very dependent on TA's. Labs again start out simple and then jump into very difficult material. Tests

Terrible lecturer, often goes off on annoying tangents that have nothing to do with the course material. If you need help, get ready for a snarky, condescending attitude because he does *not* like helping students. Easily the worst professor I've had at tech.

Very unclear with his instructions, oftentimes over-complicating his word choices (ex: "invoke a name for x-variable"), which makes it even harder to learn a new programming language. His quizzes are frustrating, subjective and his email responses are belittling and rude - like answering emails for an online class is really inconvenient. AVOID!
He is the least qualified teacher at this school. He has absolutely no knowledge of the material about which he teaches and is very disrespectful. My advice is to avoid him at all costs!!!!!!!!

Just finished his Java course this Spring. He taught us how to create our own Facebook server system. He's one of the best profs I've ever had. He definitely knows his stuff. Very down to earth and helpful. I hope to take him again.

I had him for 1704 and a few other classes when I was an undergrad like 10 yrs ago.  I'll put it like this: if you have trouble with Barnette, you need to leave the CS dept and switch majors. He is not a difficult professor, not is his material difficult.  I like the guy quite a bit since I'm from WV and he reminds me of family.
He is very helpful if you are stuck on a program and go to his office hours.  He is very intelligent and explains the material well.

He teaches a VERY difficult class for those who have never programmed before so you do have to practice a lot out of class. The Labs are almost TA dependent  and there's a strange difficulty spike with one of the projects.

His class breakdown is: 75% reading directly from the powerpoint, 20% talking about how computers used to be, and 5% on site programming that doesn't show anything. He's a nice guy, but I stopped going to class and read the notes on my own. It actually improved my grade.
Such a horrible teacher. His notes are extremely short and the test have material that is not covered. absolutely avoid at all costs

This is supposed to be a 1000 level intro programing class, where no prior experience is required. I don't see how it is possible to understand anything in this class without years of programing experience.  The CS department needs to stop letting Barnett teach this class. He has no clue how to teach people who have never programed anything befor

WOW- Avoid at all costs. His tests are absurd, and he purposely attempts to trick you on the test. I mean he actually has the problems set up so that they go around and around in the hopes you will not get the answer. There is no continuity, and he jumps to chapter 9 and 10 in the 3rd week. he is useless, and so is his class

Awful, if you have no experience in programming good luck, im going to end up having to take it again with a different professor. This guy just doesnt care about people who havent programmed before, and all his assignments are impossibly hard and you will spend the entire 2 weeks he gives you doing them. Good luck, avoid if you can.

Definitely not a class for non-majors.  I would have failed if I didn't live with a CS major.  The labs are almost impossible to accomplish in the timeframe, and practically everything he says in class goes over my head entirely.  More than half the class dropped (not exaggerating).  He's a nice enough guy, just a HARD class.

If you have never done programming before, this class is way hard. He teaches at a fast pace and it is hard to keep up. He goes over things that aren't in the book. The labs are also really hard and take a long time to finish.

If you have never done programming before, this class will be way hard. He goes through the material really fast in class and the material covered in class is not in the book. I think spending your time working with the TAs is more beneficial than going to class. Labs are really hard too and take a long time to finish.

He knows how to read from the power point slides he creates.  I can also do that so I guess I can teach the class... You will rely on the TA's if you do not have prior programming experience.  good luck you will need it.

Pretty good lecturer but his handwriting is bad and also breezes by some topics that could be on the exam. Definitely not the friendliest. Often gives some  attitude when asked questions or during office hours, like he has better things to do than help you understand concepts. He just seems very uninterested in his student's success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most of class was copying the notes that he copied off the textbook, but the tests and grading were extremely fair, and unless you skipped class (like half of the class during the second half of the semester) you would be fine.

I took Math 3134 with Professor Malik over the summer and had multiple setbacks during this time, however, you need to make sure you communicate your issues with him, and he will make accommodations based on that. He's very understanding regarding events occurring that are beyond your control. If you attend lectures or watch them, you'll be fine.

His lectures are good but hard to understand and quite useless as the words he says and the things he writes down are copy pasted word for word from the textbook.

I gave him a bad rating since I spent a lot of time grinding all the material in the class. I actually performed the best in the class on exams. However, I still received an A-.
Malik is nice and a good teacher, but the lectures are just 75 minutes of copying what he rights.  He is willing to give good feedback which help.  He is not a bad choice for this class.

Decent lecturer and clearly knew his stuff. Some of the topics we covered in class could have been explained a bit more, but overall put an effort into teaching and wanted us to succeed. Although asking questions during class was scary because he'll spend a good minute in silence contemplating it before answering.

I never thought that someone could be so criminal in the way that they teach a course. Consistent terrible test scores fue to content never being mentioned before being on the exam. Often disregards questions give attitude in office hours. Will avoid for all other courses offered.

I compared experiences with a friend in another class, she had been given organized notes, broken-down concepts, and an overall much easier to understand experience. Professor Malik only writes (quickly) on the blackboard, I found myself trying to copy down everything and understand it later; then he was unhelpful in office hours. You should avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had Malik for Intro to Linear. Did not learn the concepts at all. I was able to regurgitate the math on tests but had no idea what I was doing, this was reflected in my high As on short-answer tests, and WAY below average on the multiple-choice CTE. Lectures were not helpful as he read straight from the textbook. Take another prof if you can.
Difficult homework, difficult tests. Gets all his lecture material from another source that he just reads off of in class.

He's a decent lecturer but his handwriting is a bit messy. He gave a bunch of free points for each midterm and I felt that I honestly deserved 10 points less on each exam. The final was tougher than the two midterms, but he curved everyone's grade at the end and the past two negative reviews were right before he made changes to the grading scale.

I had Malik for Multi, so I felt that Diff Eq with him would be fine also. I was wrong. He was completely different in 2214 and the quality wasnt even close to comparable. The midterms were fairly easy, but final destroyed the whole class. Lost all respect that I had for him.

Every time I went to office hours he acted terribly, and for the final, his average on the final free response was a 45%, which was below the common time average. The final dropped my grade from an A to a B, and that was average for that exam. Dont be fooled by good reviews, avoid at all costs.
Had him for multivar and wanted to get him again for linear. He's really good - I think going to the lectures is really important to do well. He's very fair and will always try to help you.

Awesome. By far the best word to describe this man. His lectures and presentations r by far the best in the math department and he is very understanding. Got a problem? Talk to him after class and this man will basically reteach the whole lesson for you. His test are fair. You put in the work, he'll give you a good grade. 100% recommend Dr. Numann

I took his class Fall 2019, it was my first Calc class ever and I worked really hard to understand the material. But Professor Malik gave great written assignments, feedback, and lectures so it was easy to learn from my mistakes. He prepared us well for every test and I absolutely loved this class.

80% of grade is decided by 4 tests, 20% each, 12% is problem sets and 8% is webassigns. Malik has a lot of office hours and really tries to make sure his students understand the subject well. As long as you understand the subject and can do some basic application of it, you will do well in Math 2204. Definitely go to as many lectures as you can.

Professor Malik is a great teacher. He has a lot of office hours and is always available to help. He truly knows what he is talking about and helps you grasp each concept. Surprisingly his homework is one of the best parts of the class because it helps you progress in each subject. Overall great lecturer and teacher, take his class!

I don't know if its because everything is online that I dislike having Mr. Malik as a professor, but he speaks in such a monotone voice that I legit fall asleep every time he teaches. Not only that but most of the time he explains the stuff that doesn't need explanation and doesn't explain the stuff that do need explanation.

Took his class last semester and all I can say is artificial difficulty. My grade my slightly higher than expected due to my extensive experience with programming but Nowinski will throw random curveballs at you in his mid-terms and the final exam (30% of your grade). Rough class with no programming experience and quite frankly unfair.

this course is rough. Labs/prelabs take immense amount of work and take way more time than a 3 credit class should. Some general tips: 1) get a monday tuesday lab since all lab sections have reports due sunday. 2) make sure data is right before going into weekend. data in this class is prone to error. 3) go on friday to fix missed photos/data. gl
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Way too much to do in the lab reports for this class. Easily spent 12 hours on each lab report which are due every two weeks. Prelabs took about half as long and are due on the weeks in between. Just too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Spent 8 weeks learning matlab just for one test with one question, 4 parts, and no partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His office hours are super important and test are really difficult but he wants to challenge you and see you exceed. Very nice professor and enjoyed his lectures.

Practice problems for exam prep didn't match exam. Exam 2 avg was 34%, 90/200 kids got single digits.  Claimed class was "Bimodal." Final was worse. Three sections got curves of 6%, 17%, 27%. 21-pt grade gap for same performance. Emailed for help, ignored. Dismisses feedback, condescending, blames students. Unfair grading.

This guy... the homeworks take a while but are enjoyable to do. The tests suck, if you take your time coding youre cooked. limited time, difficult to grasp questions. the solutions to tests are usually simple but one mistake will mess you up. The test questions are not the practice test ones nor class problems. Expect something youve never seen.

Go into the class with a working knowledge of programming or it'll be pretty difficult. Lectures and examples are okay but prof isn't great at designing the exams. The practice problems are challenging but reasonable, but the final exam was ghastly. Equations were longer than the silk road. You'll never know what to expect on exams so beware

The lectures and pre-lecture material were helpful. The homework will take a lot of time, but going to office hours helps for understanding (there is a ton of TAs, so opportunities to go any day of the week). The tests were difficult for people who had no prior coding experience, so put in the work EARLY and stay consistent.

He's a nice guy who wants students to succeed. The midterms and final were pretty difficult. His practices tests were significantly easier than the test so don't bank on those as a indicator that you will do well on the test. Just do the HW without AI, go to office hours, and hope for the best he doesn't ask ridiculous questions on the exam.

Dr. N is a decent guy. The mid-sem switch from a take-home project to an in-person coding exam was rough. From Spring 2026 on, it should feel more manageable since in-person exams will be expected from day 1. Do MATLAB Grader + HW with minimal AI so you don't rely on it. Ask ChatGPT to generate hard practice problems, helped me a lot for the final.

The way this class is taught is a disaster. The lectures are very unhelpful and do not provide the necessary tools to complete homework and exams. He had to curve heavily two of the exams due to mistakes in the structure/wording. No partial credit on the exams, which makes tiny errors devastating to your grade. Blames students for mistakes he makes

Yes the tests are hard but he curved them a lot. 50 point curve on the first one and 17 on the second one. Most of the hate comes from him switching the test format from take home to in person due to cheating. If you make a point of understanding the homeworks and in class examples you should be able to at least pull a B. Also hes a real funny guy.

Basically, if you've never coded before (like me), good luck... The exams are made for people with coding experience to succeed (bans the functions beginners would use). Weekly homework takes hours outside of class so good luck balancing that with other courses. Oh, and the final is 2 problems worth 40% of your grade. #thankgoditsover

Honest opinion, Dr. Nowinski is a professor that cares deeply about his students developing great problem solving skills. Sure, the tests are extremely difficult and coding isn't everyone's cup of tea but if you practice what he gave you with honesty you will do good. People whining about his tests  in person are the ones you shouldn't listen to…

While changing format of the tests made sense throughout the semester, grades were distributed caused students to do poorly. He has to come up with a sort of partial credit system because I solved 99% of a longer problem on the final with one small error. Had I not, my F on the final would be a B. How does this represent my ability and knowledge?

Male Amy Schumer humor wise. Lectures useless learning wise, go to learn about tests/project. Made the second test more about dissecting blabber than coding which resulted in an average of 35 (which he blamed the students for). Asks for feedback but if its not the right feedback he ignores it. Final exam is 1/3 of overall grade (no partial credit).

Artificial difficulty is how I would describe this class. Tests are heavy (the final was 32.5%) and graded purely on correctness. Changed course policies and syllabus multiple times over the semester and was generally not receptive to class feedback. Requires a LOT of time outside of class. If I had a choice, I would not take this professor again.

I honestly can't blame him for switching the format of the exams, I certainly don't have a better solution. At least I didn't have to handwrite Java like AP CSA in high school. Class was fine, music was great, homework and recitation were very helpful concept checks, recitation difficulty jumped way too much between MLB and MLA.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nowinski is friendlier than most professors, but he tries to make this class hard. The lectures are honestly pretty useless, but you do need to put in a good amount of work on the homeworks, as they set you up pretty well for the tests. Overprepare for the tests because they can definitely catch you off guard in difficulty.

My favorite professor at VT thus far. He'll help but it's up to you to make the effort to go to office hrs or email. Make use of the extra credit and the practice matlab problems. Ask questions!!! This class is extremely difficult and you will not succeed unless you give your 100%. Don't blame the professor and study hard.

Dr Nowinski is a great guy with great stories and a good taste in music. Although this class was one of the hardest I have taken it did expand my thinking and help me to tackle problems like an engineer. From my experience Nowinski does realize the difficulty of this course, however he gives you the tools you need to get by.

To give my honest opinion, prof N. is honestly not a bad guy and he's got a funny sense of humor. Now the class is extremely hard if you have no prior coding experience, make sure you go to office hours and ask TAs questions, I wish I did this more because I have the final in a few days and I'm probably going to fail the class, so good luck.

Homeworks take about 4-6 hours, but helps us think our way through tough engineering problems. Nowinski is great and supportive outside class but often went off on tangents mid lecture. Utilize office hours and the UTAs/GTAs who are willing to help.

Do NOT listen to these "Quality 1.0 Difficulty 5.0" ratings. Dr. Nowinski gives you all the materials you need to succeed, it just takes practice. This is a class of problem solving, not just inputting a function and getting a result. Many people will talk bad about his class because they approach it with the wrong mindset. Practice makes perfect.
If you've programmed before, you're set. Got a 150 on the exam and it was chill. Funny guy and decent lectures.

He said that exams would be take home but changed his mind mid semester. changed grading of exams. comes up with something new every week. wasted class time by tiktok and youtube "funny" videos (they are lame). Homework makes no sense, even submitting is so annoying(guidelines). failed half the class on exam and made us retake only for curve.

I am currently taking his ME3024 class, Nowinski has been a nasty professor. He asked groups to rate each other's projects as "Least likely to succeed" and "Least visually appealing" publicly during an in-class activity. Additionally he told us for the first exam that there would be partial credit available, only to rescind this after the test.

Does not teach well and leaves little to no feedback. In person coding tests averaged around a 35. His response was that 50 percent of the students "do not have skills yet to be successful". Avoid this professor at all costs. Many students do not pass and are forced to withdraw late.

He is the worst professor Virginia Tech has to offer and is only working for money, he does not care about students. He only teaches in office hours and no one enjoys being around him. Whatever you do, do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: get out while you still can! This class's tests will haunt you

The exams....dont even get me started. Just...dont. Its genuinely something you see out of a "average engineering exam" compilation video and I'm literally NOT even kidding. Lectures aren't similar at all to the test, a lot of artificial difficulty. I HIGHLY recommend if you would want to take this class, you BETTER have some good coding experience
Pulls assignments out of his ahh to punish people for not attending when attendance is "optional"

Dr. Nowinski is a tough but fair professor with good taste in music. Each week typically had one MATLAB assignment (4–6 hours) plus some quizzes. They're all pretty challenging, so I recommend going to UTA/GTA office hours—they helped a lot. I had no prior MATLAB experience but learned a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of homework every week, but grading criteria is pretty lenient, and offers UTA and GTA office hours every day of the week. Take-home exams are time-consuming and difficult, but infinitely better than in-person exams. Gives a lot of extra credit so your grade will be fine. Really tries to engage with his students and make lectures fun.

Dr. N is a decent guy, definitely panders to a niche type(cringey meme enjoyers) of engineering students. Not as funny as he thinks he is. If you get a tough TA goodluck, Nowinski swears by his TA's and will not budge when the TA's make a decision. Your TA can essentially decide your course by how much they help in lab and how tough they grade.

just not my cup of tea. gets easily distracted and is loved by all the kids who haven't matured since middle school. constantly pining for validation from students with memes and unfunny jokes, like if amy schumer was a male college professor. lowkey makes you want to end it with all the homework. hires awful tas with bad grading. good luck.

Enjoyed having Dr. N for 2004, and he was just as good for 4005. Didn't think I would like the labs going into this class, but they are actually pretty fun and help to conceptualize everything I learned in other engineering classes. Dr. N always provides helpful tips and tricks to help the labs go smoothly. Put in the work and you will earn an A.

The class is supposed to be a recap of what you learned in engineering and isn't as bad as 2004. Nowinski is a very nice person and wants to see you succeed. He recognizes effort and will be more inclined to help you if you already have tried something to your best effort. The worst part are the TAs, NOT Nowinski. You either get a good one or not.

He's good for 2004, and a good lecturer. However, he gives out some of the most tedious assignments I've ever seen throughout the ME checksheet, even more so than in 3024, another class known for heavy workload. Be prepared to get hit with periodic bursts of work throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Bro assigned a lab with a 20-slide presentation and 5-min video due on the last day of spring break; meaning we had to spend our break doing many hours of work instead of, you know, taking a break (lowkey against school policy). He chose most annoying method of submitting it (zoom link in the cloud) which was worse than just writing a lab report.

I lived in office hours, but he is truly so helpful even if you ask such a simple question!! Go into office hours with some code or an idea of code. The UTA's are normally very helpful as well! Easily my most time consuming class, but very satisfying when it clicked. Failed the second exam and still ended with an A due to the insane extra credit!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nowinski honestly a super nice guy. The problem is that tests are pass/fail. Had okay test grades in this class, attended office hours, spent an unholy amount of time on hw. The final was one question, and you either got it or you didn't. I didn't. Dropped from a B to a D+. Never know what you're gonna get. Most stressful tests I've ever had.

Mid professor. He gives a ton of extra credit, but you never know his next move. His class isn't that difficult/ hard to understand its just that its very unpredictable. Budget a decent amount of time for this class week-to-week.

Dr. Nowinski is a good professor, I would just be a little careful with ME4005 because of the way the labs are graded. He teaches well, the problem is the grading/expectations. There were some things that were not clearly defined in the beginning that were only brought up later in the semester. Just go to office hours when the semester starts.

He's a good teacher and guy. However, the learning curve was very steep. The homeworks chilled out a bit after the first six weeks but took A LOT of time. My group had to get help with each homework. Lots of office hours. The tests were essentially pass or fail. Our final was one question which was 30% of our overall grade. Lots of extra credit.

1 question worth 30% of my grade. I walked into the final not knowing if I'd have a D or an A. No partial credit on code and tests are extremely stressful. Otherwise I learned how to code well and Nowinski is still a great professor. I just almost had a panic attack on the final deadass no cap. (make nowinski cool again)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: class expects you to remember stuff you learned in your other ME classes. thought you were done with deforms, fluids, vibrations? nope! 2004 and 2054 come back to haunt your dreams too. lab reports make you think too much. nowinski is lowkey nice guy, but if you don't meet his inflated expectations, you cooked
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: While he is a very nice man the tests are completely unfair if you are newer to coding. No partial credit is given whatsoever and if you can't get the first part of the MATLAB grader you might as well walk out because you are unable to bypass to the other portions without going through each one. You might as well cheat because those who did passed.

This guy is truly amazing. Despite having to teach to a lecture hall of 200+ students, he goes out of his way to engage with everyone, either through polling the class or trying to grab our attention using "gen z terms". I've never had a teacher be so caring about student's individual lives, and I honestly hope nothing but the best for him.

Super kind and respectful teacher who really does care about his students. This is essentially a coding class for MATLAB. Theres lots of homework, and exams are very difficult. But again, the professor is super caring, and if you are diligent and seek help (office hours) you'll be fine.

Dr. Nowinski is a great lecturer. His slides are very clear and concise, his coding demos are very helpful, and he highlights the most useful parts of the reading quizzes. However, his exams are much more difficult than what is covered in class and there aren't many ways to study for it nor does he provide many materials to study.

If you are in the corps of cadets or play a major sport here, do not take him, trust. I am saving you a headache. You only do well in this class if you GO to office hours, or if you "please him" with interesting conversations which shouldn't be the case because you sign up for the classes, not the office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class isn't hard if you know the basics of coding. I didn't really pay attention in class and I did all homeworks alone and still did fine. If you need help it's hard to get it from him or the TAs, so knowing people in the class is big. He is really strict about deadlines and extensions but does drop a number of assignments. Nice dude overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nowinski is a teacher of highs and lows. His exams place ridiculous weighting on coding portions, resulting in a guaranteed fail if you do poorly on the coding. His MCQ usually asks derivative or unnecessarily difficult questions. Homework can be tedious, too. However, he's a fun teacher, topics are simple once they click, and he is available often

Dr. Nowinski's lectures are informative and engaging, and he's very knowledgeable on the subject matter. Unfortunately, the class can be a bit time-consuming if you are new to coding. There are many resources available if you are struggling, but for an intro MATLAB class, I found the class to be a bit much. Do any extra credit offered, trust.

He truly cares about you as a person overall. The homework assignments can take a long time. Go into office hours if you get stuck! His office hours are very intuitive and will help you get the best scores possible on assignments. He will go out of his way for you to do well on exams the next time! If you are struggling, ask about getting a tutor!

Great and funny professor who cares about his students. Office hours help with difficult homework and workshops. Definitely takes a little bit to get used to coding if you never had coded before this class like me.

Dr. Nowinski is a great professor. I went into his course with zero coding experience, but managed to end the semester with an A. Can be a tough class and homework and workshops are difficult, but if you attend office hours you will be set as Dr. N is always willing and able to assist you in any way possible.

Professor Nowinski showed a genuine interest in students' progression throughout the course. He listened to constructive feedback. The homework was alright and manageable if you had a homework group. Many extra credit opportunities were available and were not super time consuming.

one of the worst classes I have ever taken. If you aren't a good coder already this class will be a nightmare. I probably spent 80% of my week working on homeworks, workshops, or just trying to even remotely understand the content. I would drop out before I ever had to take this class again.

Prof Nowinksi seems like a nice guy. However, he takes ME 2004 wayyyyyyyy too seriously for a 3-credit introductory level course. You will not stop working on workshops, homeworks, and studying for the next exam. Homework and exam problems are very difficult to understand and extremely time consuming. Constant announcements/notifications. good luck
Hate this class. Made every tests and homeworks very time consuming and hard. Good luck if you need to take this badly structured class.
Dingus
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nowinski was a good person, learned mostly through Jason's youtube videos. Home works were very hard, but if you work hard, you will learn matlab. Very interesting course as it introduces many advanced engineering concepts.

this class is hard if you don't have a strong foot in coding to begin with, but more than doable. have the homeworks made me cry and consider dropping out? yes, genuinely lol, but it was a learning moment and one im grateful to have. Dr. N is caring and dedicates a lot of time to his students. this class just takes effort (gasps!)

Great guy and cares about his students doing well.He introduces some topics that some of us dont know and expects us to be fluent in these concepts already.Matlab/coding literacy and working quickly is a must to do well in his class.Tests cover a lot of content and for slower thinkers your grade will likely take a hit because of it.Good office hrs

Super time consuming. Lectures don't help. Very frustrating if you don't want to reach out for help.
