You will def have to figure out a method of studying that works for you. Long tests, the HW helps. Go to/watch the study sessions. Interesting lectures, always has something cool to pass around. Memorization is required.

Homeworks are super long and due at 8 PM which is inconvenient. Tests every other week which are very memorization based and hard if you aren't good at that. Slides are also messy and don't have all the information that you need for homeworks and exams. On a positive note he's a really nice guy and shows us bones or fossils for the topics covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a sweet old guy but his exams which are the majority of your grade are so hard and they are every other week which gets annoying. His slides are also kinda disorganized so it's hard to take good notes which makes the exams harder. He's the type of professor I love as a person but maybe not as much as a teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved going to this class. It was such a breath of fresh air compared to other STEM classes. Opell is nice, & reminds me of a grandfather, lol. Tests are not that difficult, especially if you utilize the review guide and review videos. He always passes around interesting things pertaining to what is being learned. I'm going to miss this class.
His lectures are amazing and he has the coolest specimens to pass around the class every lecture. However his test are really difficult and the study guide he provides is not the most helpful.
Really awesome guy but his slides are so messy and confusing which makes it really hard to study for his exams. On top of that, the exams are the majority of the grade.

There are basically only tests and homework assignments (one of each per unity). He really puts a lot of effort into teaching and brings in fun trinkets for the class to look at relative to each lecture. Totally recommend this class!!
He is an amazing professor who is very knowledgeable on the topic. He cares about his student's success but you have to put in the work and memorize a good amount of material.

Although the course is difficult, I found the lectures to be engaging, and he uploads the lecture material to Canvas. Dr. Opell brings specimens, such as bones, to every lecture and uses videos to enhance our learning. I was going to switch majors to Microbiology, but I think I'll stay in Biological Sciences and study animal science now!

He's a super nice guy and genuinely passionate about his subject but his lectures are so monotonous and boring, I almost fall asleep every time. His tests are so detailed it's hard to get about an 85 on them. There is nothing else to redeem your grade if you do bad on the tests.

Just be sure to utilize the study guides and know everything on them. Didn't study for first tests and got D's but if you just study the homework, study guides, and memorize anatomy and phylogenies you'll be fine (got 90%+ on the other 6 tests). Most tests have questions dropped aka a slight curve. Go to class if you can, lectures are interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Opel is awesome and very clearly cares about his subject and his students! He provides more study material than any other class I've had and holds review sessions that are so helpful. He has great stories and makes this course "real" by using videos and physical objects to help us understand better. Would definitely take another class with him!
hardcore class
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you put in a little effort then youll be fine! Since the majority of your grade are the tests (6 tests to be exact) I reccomend going to his test reviews and youll be set! Just a lot of memorization. He post all of his slides online and combined with the homework questions you really dont have to attend lecture because you have all the info.

Dr. Opell is the sweetest old man always wearing pretty much the same denim shirt. His lectures are interesting since he shows videos and they are easy to follow because he supplies handouts and lecture basics on canvas. The tests are pretty much the homeworks, so studying for those and your notes makes it easy to get a good grade.

i absolutely loved him. very sweet man and a very easy class. go to class and get the notes because tests are right from the notes. loves what he teaches and is very involved. test scores were high overall, although there are many questions on his tests they are very easy.

One of the best professors I've had at Tech. He makes the material easy to understand, and you watch a lot of videos. The notes are all fill-in-the-blank print outs, and you only get tested on the lecture notes. Tests are detailed though, so study the notes several times. No need to read the textbook.

He is a very nice guy, he sometimes mixes up somethings during lecture, but it's pretty easy to understand what he means.  Go to the review sessions, they help a lot.  If you get him, don't change the class, he's a good teacher.
Great Prof. Easy to understand, doesn't go into too much detail. If you do the HW, the tests are easy. There's one hw for each test, 5 tests including the final.

Professor Fakron was not my first choice going in. Infact, I requested to transfer out of his class, but I got denied. I am really happy I was stuck in his class because he is an amazing guy. He is not going to be the best lecturer, but once you get past his acent he isn't too hard to understand. Lastly, GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS.

Great professor for 1225 if you put in the work as he advises you to. He had review sessions on weekends and will always make sure to give a good understanding of the topics. He makes sure you are graded properly on tests and has a lenient homework/quiz policy. If you have the chance to have him, TAKE HIM. If you put in the work you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Regardless of who you have for 1225, AP calc is basically a prereq. Thats just the curriculum. Osama truly cares about his students. Offers review sessions on Sundays. Test corrections for exams. Accepts late homework. Take home quizzes. No other 1225 will offer you these. Plus, is willing to give points back on exams! Cares that his students learn
Only took Pre-Calc before this class. BAD IDEA!! DO NOT DO IT!!!! Super hard and do not know what is going on. Super sweet guy, you just won't be able to understand him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Difficult to understand at first. I had Mr. Fakron for calc 1 at vt and if I hadn't already taken AP calc AB and BC in high school, I probably would have been lost. He means well but his lessons aren't as helpful as they could be. If you get points marked off on a test, you can argue them back. He'll bump you up from a B- to a B @ the end if needed

I believe I should have the disclaimer that Mr. Fakron is not a great teacher, but he is a great person overall and he is the BEST professor you will receive with entry level engineering Math courses at Virginia Tech. Mr. Fakron is very empathetic and genuinely wants all his students to succeed. If you are struggling, reach out to him.

I would recommend taking him ONLY if you have taken AP Calc AB in high school and did well. He is not the best at explaining new concepts so you need some background info to do well in his class. Aside from this, he is a very nice and genuine guy who wants to see his students succeed. We only had 4 written HW assignments the whole semester.

Love, love, love Dr. Solis! He is such a great teacher. Even though a majority of your grade is tests, he provides in class activities and out of class activities, as well as extra credit, to bump your grade and help you out! Really knows what he is talking about and gives plenty of resources for you to use. Study and do your work & you will pass!!

Professor Solis is the man. This class was at 8am and one of my smaller ones, but he lectured less than 5 times the whole year. He knows his students by name and it is very much an activity based class. There are 7 quizzes (drops lowest), 3 discussion post (drops lowest), 2 exams, an optional final and LOTS of assignments (easy).

Dr. Solis is probably one of the most personable professors I've had. His lectures are very thorough, and he explains things in a sense that make it seem like it affects you, because it does. He gives great lessons when talking about financial planning, and his tests aren't too hard. He does give random class assignments for a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Solis is a very good professor and really wants his students to pass. Go to class, do the assignments and study for the exams and you'll do very well. Go to him if you need help, he's so nice and wants you to succeed. There's also a decent amount of extra credit!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Orr is an abnormally good lecturer. His lectures were all very informative and engaging, and he is also very helpful and easy to talk to in office hours. He is clearly a very nice person who cares a lot about helping his students succeed. Just overall is a really great professor, and I had a great time in his class.

Dr. Orr is the goat. He always explained things very simply, and I always left his office hours with every question answered. He's always willing to help, very down to earth, and has a good sense of humor. He also does examples for nearly every topic during his lectures, which help a lot. Show up to class and go to his office hours when needed.

Probably the best professor I've had at Virginia Tech. He has very nice handwriting and always explains the content clearly. Additionally, he is very fair with grading, and he is always willing to help out at office hours. Definitely take him if you have the chance to.
People sign up for classes because he is listed as the instructor

Took Fish, Fishing, & Conservation with Dr. Orth. I enjoyed going to every class as his lectures were interesting and he is a nice/ generous person. He will talk to any student when help is needed and will always push back or extend assignments if you need. Overall fun class and great professor.
Disorganized, very messy canvas, always jumpy with topics. Study guides and exams had very little in common. Would not recommend

Fantastic instructor, definitely worth taking his class if you are interested in fisheries management or if you just enjoy fishing. Professor Orth is very down to earth and easy to talk to, plus you can tell he really enjoys what he does.

Incredible professor and very kind man who tries his best to help you learn. Show up to class and pay attention solely because he deserves it. His lectures aren't on things you'll be quizzed on, if you don't show up enough, he'll start grading attendance. Group project is difficult, but he's a VERY loose grader. Ours didn't even spin, 100.
Even though this is the class (alongside calc 2) that made me decide I don't want to be an engineer anymore, I really enjoyed the class and it was taught well and stayed interesting.

Good, respectful professor.  This section was off-track from the normal course progression, so he understood that most people in the class were transfers and had already taken plenty of engineering.  The whole class revolves around the wind turbine project.
Very caring and helpful. He always made sure to give extensions on deadlines. He made the already easy class significantly easier.

Dr. Ortega was a joy to work with this semester. 1216 in itself is an easy class if you keep up with the workload. Lectures were light but meaningful; everything we did outside of class was based on the lecture content. The latter half of the semester was group work, so get along with your team. An easy A if you pay attention and participate.

Pretty decent teacher, nice guy and very approachable. Show up to class, get assignments done on time, and you should be relatively chilling for this class. Ask TAs for help too if you need, they're really helpful.

Dr. Ortega is great! I would definitely take his class again. He will know everyone's names by the end of the semester, especially if you participate. Dr. Ortega and his TAs give very useful feedback on assignments and drafts, if you actually do them on time.
Tips for ENGE 1215 success: Take Dr. Ortega, do your work, and be reliable with your team.
Dr. Ortega was great. An easy grader and very understanding. I recommend participating in class so he can learn your name and get to know you a little because I believe it can affect your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really liked Ortega as a professor. The grading was pretty lenient, and content was pretty easy to follow. TAs and Ortega are really helpful and nice, like you can tell that they actually care. I did notice that this class had a couple more assignments than other professors did, but it didnt really bother me.

I highly recommend Dr. Ortega. He is very friendly and would often check in with me when I was early to class—you can tell he actually cares about his students. I appreciated him waiving some of the late penalties when things were busy. 

We also lucked out with good TAs, which isn't surprising because who wouldn't want to TA for this guy!?
Great guy. His TAs were also amazing. His class had both individual assignments and group projects. Not too bad. Waived late penalties on some assignments for a few days for some projects.
Makes classes fun, and cares about his students' success and well-being Assignments were all fairly easy and I never had to stress about anything in this class.

Half of the HW projects are way too hard and half of them are way too easy. You also don't get to pick your group so start praying for a good one. His office hours were no help because he is not at them his teaching assistants ands RAs are. Over all a good class
Very nice dude. Group projects are very fun.

Even though attendance isn't mandatory, it may affect your grade if you make a habit of missing class. Ortega and his TAs are great: super caring and helpful. The majority of the class is team projects, and there can be some weeks with a heavy workload but overall an easy class if you do your work. I am literally taking 1216 with him this semester.

I had him for ENGE 1215 and ENGE 1216. He is honestly an amazing professor that gets the class to engage with him and the work. He is quite flexible and understanding in general. Classwork and its difficulty typically depends on who you get as your teammates, which I think is true for other ENGE 1215/1216 sections.
Good professor. Highly recommend taking engineering with him.

Dr. Ortega is an amazing professor. He cares a lot about his students and his class. 1215 isn't exactly the most exciting class but he makes it worth showing up. Ortega is flexible about assignments if you give him a heads up or if you are sick / have an emergency. Overall a really great professor that cares about students and their success.

He is a very good guy, cares about his students. I have nothing bad to say about this guy, he's also very understanding. Pray that you will get good group members, because some people don't. There are a lot of group projects/activities.

Great guy and passionate about engineering. His lectures can be a bit boring but that's mainly just because it's ENGE1215. Some of his TAs are ridiculously dumb about grading, but everytime I spoke to him about grading he was very understanding. The class is easy as long as you get a good group. It's maybe a month of work spread over a semester.

He is very kind and approachable. Even when he was lecturing on boring subjects, I could feel that he cared for his students and his success. He also grades fairly easily. Just look at the rubric and use the templates for the assignments and it's easy to get at least an A-.

Dr. Ortega was an amazing professor through and through and in each of his lectures you could see true passion and care for the things he teaches. He was kind and always available when questions arose, though procrastinators beware because there are a lot of small easy assignments that can creep up on you without you noticing (hence my B).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: A really easy class unless you're stuck with a bad group. If you have a good group and follow all his instructions, you'll get an A. I had some problems going on outside of class and he was super kind and flexible.
Very laid-back professor. Enjoyed his lectures and he encourages participation, which I love.
A great introduction course for engineering at Virginia Tech.

Professor Ortega is a really great professor. He is calming and really enjoys his job. Explains things clearly. Group work heavy so if your in a bad group this class might seem not as good but it is not the professors fault. Smart and calming man!

Ott gave entertaining lectures. However, the course wasn't what I was expecting. Readings took a long time to get through because they were confusing. The paper (30% of our grade) was graded harshly. You had to put in a ton of effort & go to office hours to get an A in participation. The course was harder than an intro level course should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Ott is a great guy, but he does not make the readings nor class interesting whatsoever. He tries to engage the students in class, but I do not think that "Animal Minds" are that interesting enough. Do not take if you are not a Cog Sci major or interested in the subject at hand. @UVA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took Professor Ott's "Meaning of Life" class at UVA and found him extremely engaging and clever. Lecture mainly consisted of discussion of topics found in the readings, so as long as you kept up in them, it wasn't difficult to follow along. Any confusing part of the text was explained in relatable life examples. Overall, would love to take again!

I'm a fourth year at UVa where Ott has been interning. I took his senior seminar. He is a fantastic professor in terms of sheer brilliance, superhuman focus, and clarity. I was consistently amazed by his level of mastery- any serious Phil student stands to gain a lot from him-people who don't like him are probably uninterested in the subject matter

Walter Ott is an arrogant puffed-up professor too impressed with himself to help students. I love philosophy just not the Walter Ott brand. He's too caught up in contemporary arguments to be taken seriously as a scholar. As a moral realist he has trouble making his case about any philosophical quandry.

Dude Ott is so sweet! I totally knew he was the man when I saw his autographed picture of Jennifer Grey on the desk in his office. It was all personalized and everything, so you know he totally met her. Make sure you have him tell the story about when he brought his farret to class and it got all freaked out and took a huge dump on the radiator

Prof. Ott is like the best prof ev! He has you watch Dirty Dancing and he shows you how to do all the dance moves. Never knew philosophy could be so fun! Let’s you know that you’re his woman and he’s your man. And OMG, his nipples look like they could totally cut glass. Tells great stories about his farret. Doesn't make you do any work at all. Ever

This class was wicked awesome - Professor Ott taught me things about myself that I never dreamed of - about life, loss, and what it is to feel again. OMG and he's so dreamy - he looks like Patrick Swayze only not all 80's like with fringe on his jacket - a manly Swayze, a Swayze's Swayze. Grades too hard and sometimes barks. Total communist.

Dr. Ovink was an amazing professor as you can tell she cares greatly about her students. There was only a midterm and a final, both of which were partner tests with a notecard cheat sheet, but both due to the fact that the tests are solely writing that consist of short answers and essays. However, she sets her students up to succeed.
She's very nice and extremely understanding.  She's also great at explaining concepts, and promoting healthy discussion

Very nice Professor! A lot of readings and weekly quizzes but they were all graded very easy. Easy to understand questions and not difficult. A decent sized final paper (I think 10 pages) but I got a 95 on it. Very caring about her students as well, but make sure you put in the work. Not a class you can coast through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Ovink is my favorite professor by far! Her lectures are engaging and informative, the books she chooses are interesting and not traditional textbooks. Her research for her current project is done, but students had the opportunity to hold focus groups for her project as a final project and it was such a great opportunity! She's super kind, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Really nice professor. Lectures are really long and can get boring. Exams arent bad but expect some essay questions and short answers. As long as you do what is expected its a pretty easy class. Go to class though, she takes attendance.
Gives good feedback

If you are looking for an easy, high-grade, Maziar is not the guy. Tests are more challenging compared to other professors; however, he is a great guy and very flexible with assignments. 2214 is a class where your grade is only dependent on your professor, so I would try to find someone else if you want an easier time.

Everytime someone asked him a question in class, he never actually answered the question. Went to office hours to talk to him about how to improve my test grades and his response was "I don't know, if you can do the homework, you should do good on the tests". Doesn't actually teach anything conceptual in class, only does practice questions
Very good professor, consistent with lectures and tests.  Explains all topics thoroughly and keeps the tests reasonable.  Attendance is not graded but he does take it every class.

He's a nice person, but his teaching style isn't helpful. He doesn't have or post notes, so attendance feels mandatory since you have to write everything down. He teaches in a disorganized way, moving too fast—we had covered half of Chapter 3 two weeks before a test on Chapters 1-2. Great guy, but not a good teacher for 2214.
Very caring professor that explains topics clearly. Will stay to help with topics and will stop and answer questions if you need it.

Lectures very efficiently and explains everything well. All homework was in a textbook that was free. If you have a question you definitely need to speak up because he will often not notice people raising their hands. Everything on the tests will be easier than what we practice in class and easier than some homework problems.

Mazier's class is test-heavy, and he's a tough grader. Homework has no drops, and points are deducted when answers are correct. Tests are like book problems and not what we do in class, but the algebra is basically impossible without a calculator. Be ready to study a lot! I took his class bc of his reviews from calc 2 but do not take him for 2214!

Pretty good teacher. Do need to go to lectures. Good lectures, but hard on partial credit. Got a test question wrong for using 32.2ft/s^2 on a test instead of 32 even though all the steps and math were right, so use the constants he tells you to.

Good at lecturing, but sometimes jumps between topics. Make sure you're engaged the entire time in class. Gives little homework, so make sure you STUDY AND PRACTICE. Three exams determine your entire grade, and the material is tough. Need the discipline to practice on your own so you truly know the material. Don't get behind and take a W like me.
Calc 2 is a difficult course, but Maziar makes it approachable and manageable through really intuitive lectures.

Amazing teacher for Calc 2. Taught material in an explainable way, and made sure to explain derivations for equations which further helped me understand the course material. Would absolutely take his class again.

Great teacher. I ended with a C but it was my first semester and coming out of the class I know I could have done better. A fair teacher-doesn't curve but the tests are very reasonable and he redistributes the weighting of tests to your own individual advantage at the end of the year. I would definitely take him again. A really nice dude.

Professor Maziar is a gem in the math department! Since math professors are chosen 2 weeks before classes start, sometimes you get stuck with a really bad professor, but if you can choose Maziar, do it! Go to class, take notes, ask questions. MATH1226 is difficult but you hardly get lost with the way he teaches.

Maziar is so kind, supportive, and inspirational. Cal2 never gets boring in his lecture. He guides the class through all theories and give real-life examples. Good sense of humor. Tests are to test students' knowledge only on what has been given in book, HW. I've been struggling with Improper integral for months, now no more with Maziar. Good luck!

He explained everything pretty clearly and his lectures were him writing on a chalkboard for 50 minutes. You have to put in the work to do well in the class. The tests were super straightforward and just like practice problems in class but I felt his partial credit was strict. There was a weekly written HW that was only a few problems

one of the best math professors you can get at VT. he doesn't expect you to know everything and is very straight forward. not one of those overbearing professors that expects you write complicated proofs or derivations. would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best math teachers in my educational career. He is extremely patient with questions, gives excellent examples and definitions, and his tests are extremely reasonable. Make sure you attend class and do the homework. I would definitely take the class again! Thank you Dr. Maziar!
Very nice guy and good teacher, calc is hard in general but he does his best to help come to class and pay attention and you should be good
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Maziar is a great professor. He doesn't want you to fail :) I missed up bad in my first test that's why I ended up with this grade in his class. If you want to do well in his class do all the suggested H.W. questions from the textbook (all his test/final questions come from the textbook). His tests are easy just practice the textbook questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: After hearing the horror stories of Calculus 2 at Tech, getting Maziar was a blessing. His classes are mainly just him going over problems from the textbook, but he is very open to all kinds of questions about the material, even the most basic algebra, he will take the time to explain. The exams are similar to the ones done in class, so go to class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Maziar was my first calc professor coming into Virginia Tech, and it has been a blessing to be in his class considering the situation with Virginia Tech's math department. He teaches by giving practice problems instead of showing proofs and other nonsense. The only way to pass the class with an A is to do a lot of practice problems before each test
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I feel so lucky to have taking MATH 1226 with MAZIAR. He is very understanding. I took his class on Zoom but all lectures are pre-recorded, just a mandatory weekly recitation Zoom session to summarize the content. Barely any extra homework, easy tests and accessible for extra help! 100% recommend.

Maziar has been an amazing professor. The material is difficult if you dont go to class, but he works through useful examples skipping nothing, even simple algebra in case you have forgotten. Exams are EASY if you go to class and follow along. He spends more time doing examples then talking through nonsense proofs and theorems. Highly recommend.
Maziar is a great professor. Sometimes he may move fast but he will always be willing to answer any questions. He does a great job preparing you for the tests.

In Calc 1226 he works through examples most of the class (which is what you want!). He may go a little fast during class but you will be fine. WebAssign is the only required homework and is not easy (Chegg helps); will tell you what types of questions will be on the test and final. Haven't found a better calc professor yet.
Demonstrates great knowledge of the concepts covered. Grade is comprised of 3 tests, all online homework assignments, and attendance. He will work with you to earn the grade you desire.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Maziar was my first math professor at Virginia Tech and I could not be happier to have had him. He is a great teacher, who goes through examples all class long and is always willing to answer questions afterward. Over the course of the semester we only had 3 tests that count for 60% , so make sure you study the content he teaches!

Does not give partial credit on tests, and they consist of eight to ten "challenge" type problems, which are extremely hard and nothing like the problems covered in class. All class averages for tests are following: 60.00%, 43.67%, 58.50%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Owusu Brown was very caring & accommodating, as she allows students to take make up exams (when necessary) and was overall a very nice professor who wanted you to learn the material. That being said, I felt the lectures were boring at times, and the homeworks could be intense (up to 40 questions). Overall, nice professor and good class.

Dr. Owusu-Brown was one of my favorite professors during the Fall 2024 semester. She actively engages her students using iClickers and is always ready to provide additional explanations and assist with the iClicker questions. She uses many illustrations when necessary to explain and break down complex economic theories.

Dr. Brown is exceptionally welcoming and genuinely desires to see her students succeed. She allows multiple attempts for homework and exams. While she is flexible, she also understands where to set boundaries. I appreciate how she involves us through relevant class examples.

Dr Owusu-Brown was a very sweet person, however her lessons were very boring and we hardly had any practice during class, and even if we did it was too fast. I also didn't appreciate that she had 0 exam prep, even with an exam the next day she would still cover material for the next exam. Exams were  hard unnecessarily hard and so was the HW.

I had Dr. Owusu-Brown for Economics of Gender, and the workload was very manageable. The only things we needed to do were 4 homework assignments, 6 short essays, and a weekly discussion board. She drops the lowest two discussion boards and the lowest essay. Very chill, easy grader, would reccommend!

Dr. Owusu-Brown. I LOVE THIS WOMAN. She is the most genuine professor I have ever had who is always open to answer questions and accommodate extensions. Her lectures are paced well, clear, and extremely helpful. She gives plenty of resources like slides, textbooks, practice problems, tutors, and office hours. Just show up and you'll pass.

Dr. Owusu-Brown is an excellent professor. Her lectures are engaging and easy to follow. She truly cares about her students and frequently makes adjustments to support their success. The tests are online, straightforward, and she drops the lowest exam grade. Attending class and participating in the iClicker activities will set you up for an easy A.

Amazing professor. Genuinely such as nice person, she really cares about her students and is always available for help if you need. In terms of the class, it's super easy as long as you just show up and participate in the iclicker, you should get an A. She makes class super engaging and tests are all online and not hard at all.

Dr. Patel is super kind and understanding. She works with you through everything if you need it, gives extra credit opportunities, wants you to learn. Her lectures are long but if you find the topic interesting then you're fine. It is very reading heavy but as long as you skim the text you're set.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very quick to respond to any questions or emails and very friendly. The class consisted of just discussion posts, short quizzes, and two exams. Make sure to read all the material she gives and fill out the study guide because I skimmed up until the first exam and paid for it. The material is actually interesting and it's a pretty fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Shaily for a New Testament class this fall, and I thought the class was so fun and interesting. The material was not too overwhelming, and she offered a lot of extra credit opportunities. You can tell she really cares about the subject and about making sure students understand it. I would love to take another class with her:)

This class includes a lot of reading from the textbook but as long as you skim for the basic idea of the lecture and attend class you should be fine. Attendance is mandatory so if you do not attend you will get points off. Dr. Patel always answers any questions you have and offers extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Patel :). She is so understanding and cares a lot about her students. She's very knowledgeable and emphasizes the importance of keeping an open mind. She makes her requirements for assignments very clear and is always happy to answer questions. Make sure to come to class, do the readings/assignments and you should do well.

Dr. Patel is a very opinionated person and will fight with your opinion if it does not line up with hers. She was very biased and it showed in her lectures and assignments. It is a shame because he class could have been really fun and interesting if it wasn't for this. If you like to learn things instead of being told how to think avoid her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Does not care about excused attendance. Pass fail class so it doesn't matter much but she is very hard to communicate with and reach out to.

If you go to every once-a-week class and submit all of the (very easy) assignments, you'll likely do very well in this class. This isn't just a class, it gives you a chance to make many connections so use that wisely. Nice professor, was kind and was easy to reach out to.

Pass/fail 1 credit course so I didn't care about my grade as long as I passed, but professor Pannell would treat this class like it was worth 3 credits with the way she graded attendance and gave a huge amount of assignments out of class. I almost failed due to missing one class but barely passed when I did the group project. Wouldn't recommend.

She is very great career coach I wish that career advisory at VT was like this. I made some solid connections through her and if you're lost and need help. Please reach out to her for career advice and some clarity. Also don't underestimate the out to class events as they include CEOs and directors of great firms.
Great Professor, and amazing for networking

I think that this class was beneficial, as it allowed me to learn more career tips (how to optimize my resume, etc.), in addition to giving you the opportunity to develop connections with the guest speakers that she invites. Honestly, while I may not have like the vibes entirely, as long as you show up and do the work, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class isn't hard, but the class felt empty and useless, the whole thing felt like one big checkmark. All the assignments is annoying busy work. She is nice on the outside but is not a very kind person, she is very passive aggressive to students who ask questions after class. After a certain point she clearly stops putting effort into the class.
It is a 1 credit class that she treats like a 3 credit. Other person was right, very passive aggressive if you miss class.

class is actually rly valuable and all you have to do is show up. Early assignments include creating a resume, cover letter, and attending Business Horizons etc. The rest is guest speakers during class that are from the three BIT fields. The professor is flexible, lets you make up missed sessions, and genuinely cares about student success.
she must not realize that it's a 1 credit course
Had to do more work for this class compared to two other 3 credit classes which was stressful. The content was fine but the syllabus change during the year certainly made things confusing.

Eh Pannell wasn't my favorite. She switched up the syllabus halfway through and made it so you had to go to the speaker meetings if you wanted points. Things were weighted weird and she would often get passive aggressive if people didn't show up. Glad it was a p/f, bc she was all over the place. Assignments at the beginning were actually helpful.

Easy A, but she made this 1 credit course into a 3 credit course by making you watch the other section's class. Basically every class was a speaker event and you get to learn a lot about different BIT careers. She records all of them and there is a zoom option so you don't have to attend in person.

Doesn't get enough credit for being amazing lecturer; if you pay attention in class you will learn. Lots of homework but all very related to what we do in class so if you pay attention it's not hard just somewhat time consuming. I worked hard and he learned my name and recognized my effort but I've heard stories of him being rude and unacomadating.
Do not take is class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good as a professor. I heard he has fully abandoned using Canvas, which if true, is a big minus. He is very energetic and clearly passionate about water resources, and will take the time to learn almost if not everyone's name in the entire class. He will never respond to your emails, go to office hours. The hardest class in civil engineering :(
He makes lectures fun but really heavy grading and work also hard  to communicate(he doesnt answer emails.)
Hard class but an amazing teacher. Gets points across and teaches accurately and very well. Incredible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Scardina is a true professor. He is very enthusiastic about the topics and wants you to learn. You HAVE to learn to pass this class. You NEED to start strong its hard to come back as its ALL cumulative. Its hard for a reason. PAY attention, take notes, actively do hw, seek help and be invested in understanding and learning the class. Great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awfu! Very hard class because the test has nothing to do with his lectures. He seems to enjoy failing 50% of the class.

Probably my first "real" professor at Virginia Tech. He is a true professional which I cannot say about many professors now-a-days. I wish all my engineering classes were taught by people like him as we would actually have competent engineers in the world.

Scardina's classes are tough - I choose to take another one of his classes because I thought he was an excellent teacher though. He's the best proffessors I've had. He teaches extremely well. You'll have to work hard but it's worth it. In other classes you don't understand or retain things that well, but in his class you will.

Scardina makes the class so much harder than it has to be. Content wise its not the worse class, but he is horrible on grading and will take off points for random things. Also better not show up late to the lab because thats an instant 2 zeros on lab reports. You will leave the class understanding everything but still have nothing to show for it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is extremely hard compared to Statics and Deforms here at Virginia Tech. Scardina is a very tough grader and is more than willing to fail you if he sees fit; this past semester, Spring 2021, over 60 people took "W's" across his sections with an average GPA of 2.14 across both his Fluids sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are fairly smooth, but the tests are EXTREMELY hard compared to the homework assigned throughout the semester. He grades the test very hard, and harps on the idea that he only "presents" the material and that we should teach it to ourselves. I got B+ in both statics and deforms, but this class you really have to work for.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ben is a great professor if you want to grow as a designer. He pushes you to rethink how you approach design and always has a relevant precedent for whatever you're working on. His studio is demanding, the workload is heavy and expectations are high, but you'll come out of it a much stronger designer and a more interesting person.

You just need to be better and take this class. Gives some of the best and most interesting lectures compared to other professors. He has such an eye for architecture, art, and design. He will change your entire perception of design in a revolutionary way. He will push you to your limit and then some. He's also very funny.

Highly subjective. Would not give you as good of feedback if he didn't like your piece. Also had too big of an ego to accept when you actually make a good point against his. Made me want to quit architecture. Do not recommend.
Cool people take his class. You should too. Don't expect to sleep or have any free time. Do expect to cry. And to have your view on architecture changed completely & make some insanely cool work.
I would drive without a seatbelt every time there was study in hopes that I wouldn't make it to his clas.

Be ready to work in groups and be ready to work hard. Ben is passionate and pushes you to produce your best work refusing mediocracy. You will fail, fail again, and then some more. However, at the end of what can only be described as a marathon, you will be left with a project and a new perspective that you can truly be proud of.

Ben does not teach objectively. While from an outside point-of view his projects seem cool and abstract, he lacks the patience and knowledge to be a second year professor. If you do take ben, make sure to stand firm in your beliefs and not be easily influenced by ben's opinions.

Of 2nd Yr studios, the hardest are Ben's & Hillary's. Ben will work you to the edge. If you're soft, he will break you. We had 2 people drop each semester, but the ones that stuck with him have made leaps and bounds. He is extremely opinionated, sometimes (often) too much so, but it's good. Goated studio. 10/10. Anyone saying otherwise is capping.

She lectures about instructions for the entirety of class. Tends to be a very tough grader and makes you "exceed expectations" to earn above a low B in the class. Additionally assigns excessive amounts of homework with very minute details that are graded on hard. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The assignments were excessively long. However, she was a nice professor and tried to make the labs enjoyable.
I took Materials with Annie Pearce. The entire class is group work - one lab per week and the rest is pretty much online. She is helpful although you really don't see her that much.
Not challenging enough, especially for your technical and analytically skills. Topics which were interesting were not covered with necessary depth.
No Comments

FIN 3134. Not great. Hard to understand, but he's clearly trying. He basically just goes through notes as if he would be just doing them and not the 40+ students in the class. Would not take again just because he seems just as lost as the students. He also stated, "If I were to take the exam, I would not be able to ace it".

I had Professor Pecora for Finance 3134 and he was a great teacher. He explained things really clearly and gave homework's that helped prepare for exams. Overall a really good teacher that I would take again

This was Prof. Pecora's first ever class and he taught it well. It's difficult regardless of the teacher, but he frequently asked for feedback and made generous adjustments to his grading. Was pretty funny, really encouraging and seemed to care about student's success
Pei is an awesome guy and is very lenient with his test grading because of the partial credit. Is very understanding and will work with you to succeed. 10/10

1226 is a difficult course. Pei is very helpful and I highly recommend attending every single lecture. There are plenty of additional resources available on canvas, such as practice tests and written assignments. Tests are very challenging, but lots of partial credit is given. Office hours are very helpful, and Pei always answer questions in class.

Great professor who clearly cares about student learning. He's approachable and responds to emails quickly. Exams were challenging, but partial credit was generous if you showed work. Attendance wasn't required, but lectures helped a lot. Canvas had plenty of helpful study resources.

Very thoughtful, kind, and knowledgeable. Does his very best to ensure that you understand the course material yet is timely and precise in his in-class explanations. Office hours are very helpful and highly recommended.

Tests are incredibly difficult, but a lot of partial credit is given when he can tell that you attempted a solution. Attendance is not mandatory, but the lectures are great and he gets to know the people that attend every class. Definitely an amazing choice for 1226.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very nice professor, curve a lot
Easiest grader ever. Test are hard but he does provide a lot of help out of class and in class review, but he grades the test really really easy. 100% best teacher to take for calc II.
He gives sooooo many partial credits. You still have to put in the work to study, but if you're stuck, email or go to his office hours, he's super helpful. Super easy grader. Chill guy.
He cares a lot about his students and truly wants everyone to pass. Gives good lectures that move slow enough to not miss anything, and also makes time to answer every question.

The times I went to office hours, I would have multiple questions set up to ask, and after 50 minutes, I'd get no answers and would know about one more student who got 100s in his class from 20 years ago. Otherwise homework often took 3x longer than any other math course I've taken while also giving no useful feedback to learn from my mistakes.
He's a relaxed and approachable professor who explains topics thoroughly and clearly. Lectures are detailed, and while the homework can be challenging, it does a great job preparing you for exams.

Worst math professor I have ever seen. Only care if you solve problems in his way instead of your understanding. I got in trouble because I solved a problem using linear algebra. He even threatened me send me to the honor court. And the assignment is really heavy, only a few questions are graded. I don't know the meaning of the rest problems.

After getting an A- in calculus 2 I felt prepared for multi but OH NO. I mean the guy uses HIS OWN VT website instead of Canvas for written hw. The written hw were typically around 20 long questions, which was top of the WAs. The exams were also very difficult and he only told us to look over our homework to study (which never helped).

If you're not willing to put in the work, avoid PW at all costs. Homeworks usually take around 3-4 hours, and only have a few problems graded. PW is a very tough grader, and is more focused about doing the problems his way than understanding the material. He also doesn't give any review materials for the test.
Worst professor in the math department. Doesn't give any study materials or even try to help kids unless you go to office hours, where he blankly stares at you and makes you do it yourself.

Doesn't care at all if you understand the material, only if you follow the way he teaches. I personally cannot learn the material the way he teaches it, but office hours are for "emergencies only" and have gotten in trouble for using other sources to teach myself. We're not allowed to use YouTube, Khan Academy, or tutors.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The grades were unfair, the lectures were boring, and there was a lot of homework.

He worries less about you knowing the concepts and more about answers being in HIS format. Showing him you understand content won't get you credit, you need to do it his way. **He makes that much harder than actually understanding the material**. He can teach concepts well, but he will not give you a good grade in the class for understanding them.

Hes a chill guy. Lectures are very detailed and he usually explains topics very well. Homeworks are tough but they help you prepare for tests. You can't get by if you just repeat your notes on homeworks and tests, you have to think everything through. If you need help, ASK. He will learn your name and respect you if you care about the class.
Avoid at all costs. The homeworks take ages to finish, then he only grades a few of the problems randomly.  The homework also frequently requires methods that weren't covered in class.

Class: 2204
PW was the most challenging professor i've had so far. Did not use canvas for material and the grading style was a learning curve. Written HW weekly that took 6+ hrs and only 3-4 questions were graded. Tests were hard to prepare for with no practice exams. Given rank bc partial credit is generous and PW "curves" overall grade.

The reason for the 3 rating is that his lectures are easy to follow better than most other teachers of this course. That being said he is a very tough grader and assigns a lot of work while only grading a random few. He takes off points liberally and does not care if you had the correct method if you make a simple mistake youll get almost no points

worst professor I have ever taken. he is genuinely unfair and grades are based on personalities and it's obvious. There were many instances where my friend and I had the same HW solutions and he ended up getting 40% HIGHER than me. it's ridiculous. he should be fired. the people giving 5 stars are either fakes or they smoking smth.
worst professor I've ever had in my life. if you want to fail operational methods, take his class. He smart when knowing the content but he can't teach and is completely unfair. Dont take his class.

At first I thought he was terrible. There was so much homework and he was a tough grader. But as the class went on I realized he presents the material in a clear and consise way and prepares us well for his tests. The tests were fairly written and he gave a lot of resources for if you missed class. His class is work but it pays off in the end.

idk what the guys who gave him a 4 or 5 are smoking. Don't listen to them. He just writes stuff on the board and expects you to follow along and learn from that, doesn't explain anything. I learn better from the textbook than when in his class. Also grades harshly and assigns a lot of hw.
Terrible. Just does all the work and expects you to follow along, doesn't explain anything, if you have his class and you're not a math genius already then drop out.

You'll have to work in 2204 honors. The speed is decent for honors, not sure for nonhonors. Lots of homework. If you put the effort in on homework the tests won't be too bad. He'll meet with you outside of class but he can be cryptic and vague in answers to questions and emails. If you have questions in class, ask them because he won't turn around.

This was my first experience with an honors math class and multivariable calculus and it was not great. If you didn't take multi in high school I do not recommend this class, because the professor moves really fast and skips some material that he thinks you should know. I was made to feel stupid for asking a question, so long story short, I dropped
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Extremely helpful and the first calculus teacher I've had in college that actually knew what he was talking about.  I'm currently in his multivariable class and have a B+ halfway through the sememester. I'd recommend scheduling him if at all possible.

Wapperom is one of the best math pofessors out there. His class was well organized, the grading fair, and kept the material interesting by mentioning its applications. The homeworks were due weekly, and if you ask about a specific problem, he'd give you a clear answer by working the problem step by step. The lowest test was replaced by the final.

Professor Thompson was one of the best professors I have had while at Tech. He teaches the material well, and offers fair grading criteria. Attendance is not required but incentivized as he provides key information for the exams, as well as just making lectures enjoyable with his stories. If you get the chance to take him, do so!

Thompson is a great person, motivator, inspirational, chill, and real. His way of organizing the class is just weird. He makes attendance mandatory by making quizzes need codes that he gives out in class. he also includes non-textbook material on the exams and they usually make up most of the exam. Stingy about asking questions when not in class.

Go to class and take notes. Attendance is not mandatory but it'll be the class you never want to miss. He is clear what will be on exam so tbh if you don't do well it's because you didn't study. Dude is real and doesn't hold back. Funny and entertaining

favorite professor i've had at virginia tech. He cares and is passionate about the topic. the biggest reason why i am adding management as a new major. go to class, even though attendance isn't required. he is such a clear teacher, the exams will seem easy. but the exams arent easy, he just is super clear and his examples/stories always help.

Really enjoyed Professor Thompson's class. A very funny and entertaining professor, who's assignments are simple and not too crazy. Please GO to lecture, he provides key information and some answers for the quizzes and exams! Pay attention, and some test questions are given. He's very willing to support and approach with a smile, so say hi!
Awesome person, one of my favorite professors ever tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Only 4 exams, lowest score is dropped so if you're happy with your grade after first 3 you don't have to take the final! He doesn't round up but he gives so many free points throughout the semester and all the quizzes are easy. He only tests on things he talks about in class, but the classes are short and canceled a lot. Slight class, good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance not taken, but he goes over material that is not in the textbook that will be on exams, so very recommended you go to class. Very clear about what is and isn't going to be on the exam, including exactly which sections to study. Drops the lowest exam score, so I was done with this class before Thanksgiving break.

Really funny and great lecturer. He will force you to talk to people and it's very helpful in the long run. SO glad he was my professor. The tests are very easy as long as you study. He's is passive aggressive, but only if you deserve it. Very understanding if you talk to him or email him. Little homework, pop quizzes during lectures.

I really didn't enjoy his teaching method. All the things that he says contradict themselves. 1st day of classes he told us it's all non-textbook material and it was but than why makes us waste time on assignments and give us exam 4 on it. Also I don't really like his attitude as it's very passive aggressive and shallow.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had.

Professor Thompson made the lectures very fun and interactive while still giving you all of the information you need to succeed in his class. If you show up, pay attention, and take good notes, the class is very easy and will not be stressful come final exam time.

Do the HW during trial period, youll never need the textbook again. In his lectures you need to take notes on his comments, and nontextbook (not given slides) material. If you do that and conceptually understand (not hard stuff) youll do great. Doesn't give you any info you wont be tested on so theres no question of what to study.
Very nice professor and will give you everything you need to know for exams. Attendance isn't mandatory, but most of the test material is based on information learned in lectures. Almost no homework.
He gives you exactly what you need to know for the exams, so if you know that you'll do fine. Really nice and cool professor.

Great professor. I learned alot and the way he teaches is very straight forward. He doesn't take attendance but its a class i never wanted to miss even thought it was a 8am. Best tip is to get notes and announcements from classmates if you miss class. he told us this on the first day of class but i didnt listen.
Great professor! My favorite college class so far

Professor is a fun professor and very engaging. He is my favorite professor i've had at Virginia Tech. I ran into him in the hallway yesterday and he mentioned that he will be teaching MGT 3404 during the Fall 2025 semester. The class isn't hard, but it also is not easy. Take good notes and you will be fine. I love the vibe in his class

Professor Thompson made it very enjoyable with music and personal stories. Make sure to attend class because he only gives "non-textbook material" in class. He is pretty clear about what's on exams but make sure to study notes and read the textbook. I'm not one to read the book but just read the sections he says and it should only be a few pages.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Taking Dr. Thompson's class was a blast, he made every lecture entertaining and has a fun personality that I looked forward to seeing in class every time. He is straightforward about what you need to know for his exams, and gives free points to consolidate extra credit.

Exams are worded trickily so be sure to attend class and read the textbook.

Only good part about this class is that you could be done before Thanksgiving break. He isnt understanding or accessible at all. The test questions can be confusing and half of them are all on the same topic so if you don't know that one topic well, you will get a bad grade. Go to class to get nontextbook material that will be on the test.

lowest test gets dropped; class ends late nov instead of dec 6; super engaging; take good notes; "pop" quizzes are open entire day and pretty easy; last two exams are easier than syllabus says they are; i'm glad he turned down ivy league colleges to come teach here at VT-- great professor

I like the music he plays every class. Tests are relatively easy, as he tells you where you should prioritize your focus in studying. While attendance isn't mandatory, a large portion of notes can only really be gathered in-class.
TAKE IT WITH HIM!!! Show up to class, listen, take notes, do the homework. He really wants us to do well and is really caring! One of the best professors I have had at tech.

Prof. Thompson made this class super fun. I really enjoyed his lectures and if you create a group chat or find people in the class its super easy to get the notes when you miss class. You will need the lecture notes if you miss class since he includes quiz codes, quiz answers, and non-textbook material in his lectures.

Thompson is a great professor. It is clear that he cares about his students and the content he is teaching. His lectures are very fun and engaging. Definitely go to class and pay attention to what he is lecturing on because not all the notes are in the slides. The exams aren't too bad as long as you study your notes from class.

Of the many great professor's I've had, he is my very favorite. He is super clear and direct. He uses humor and interesting stories to make the class a must attend for me, even though he doesn't take attendance. I wouldn't say his class is "easy" however the best advice I can provide is to be sure to get GREAT notes if you miss class.

attendance was not mandatory, but u should go since there is a decent chunk of material that is presented in class that he does not publish onto the canvas notes. Homework's very easy. gave answers to most of the quizzes. 4 exams including the final, but lowest is dropped. basically tells you outright what stuff is going to be on the exams.

He's personable and flexible and really sets the class up to prepare you for the future. I would say attendance is mandatory because there is sometimes quizzes that need a code that he gives out in class. Professor Thompson really wants you to succeed. The last 2 tests are on 2 or 3 sections of the textbook and super easy.

Have had to take a few 8 am classes in my time at school, and this course was the least accessible class. There is no way to recover what you would miss in person. His lectures are entirely different from what he will post online. It turns into a class of attendance, and he has a tendency to talk about himself. A lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome Professor. He is my favorite Professor at Virginia Tech. Lectures are straight to the point and he is really good at letting the class know topics that will be covered in the exam. Hes funny and has a ton of energy. He made an 8am class be fun. Attendance isnt mandatory, but you will need to get good notes if you miss class.

Prof. Thompson is one of the nicest professors I've had but he is also very real with you. He will not cut you any slack but you shouldn't need any because he gives lots of extra credit opportunities. He is very knowledgeable in his field and does a good job at explaining his material.

I wasn't a huge fan of the dude himself, but this class was ridiculously easy. You're graded by three things: four-question quizzes, homework that's impossible to not get a 100 on, and three open-book/note exams. There's one 20-minute lecture a week that's honestly unnecessary to go to, and the class is finished in two months.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Such an amazing professor! Really understanding with students but clearly states where he stands. He makes the class manageable and flexible. Hes hilarious and will laugh at himself sometimes and its the funniest thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This guy is a rockstar. This is a class you want to go to every week and when you skip it you feel bad. He gives spontaneous attendance quizzes but the questions are based on the powerpoint so you can still answer it if you miss one. To get an A, read the textbook for the sections and write notes. Also memorize the ppt. Very easy class if you study

His lectures are not necessary to attend at all. Everyone begins each lab completely lost and clueless but someone eventually figures out what to do and tells everyone else. Labs range from fun to absolutely miserable, tests are pretty easy.
Just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I struggled a bit with the labs which are 60% of the grade. Exams/quizzes are on canvas outside of class. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you go to class he would always work through the questions on a quiz if he assigned one. Just set aside time to get the labs done you will be fine. He's very open to helping students and is accessible.

The course content was genuinely interesting and I learned a lot, but the weekly three-hour labs felt unnecessarily long. Much of the time was taken up by overly drawn-out explanations of simple concepts, which could've been communicated much more efficiently. Also, the instructions were outdated and didn't match current software or workflows.

a lot of people will complain about this guy bc the post-lab homeworks are really really long, but the content isn't that difficult! he's personable and funny, and he's really nice in his office hours he'll explain things in detail

Super nice professor but lectures were bland and labs always ran overtime. Content was not difficult but the class was heavy on homework and take home lab reports so beware of stacking other time consuming classes on top of this.

I loved Radtke's Land and Field class! It was one of my favorite classes this semester! Offers a lot of chances on quizzes and tests are online, labs are long but interesting! He wants you to do well, I text him questions and he always responds! The class is a lot of work but I loved the material and Radtke is great at explaining if you need help!

He is extremely thorough and is very willing to accommodate and help students.The material is quite interesting as well! While labs may seem long, you get the chance to work with peers and get help on anything that may confuse you. I believe that those who don't try to succeed or are not interested in the course material would not enjoy this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The labs are tedious and he over explains a lot, but they also cover important information, especially if you aren't familiar with field skills or gis. They are graded harshly and accuracy matters. He gives the quiz answers in class and the exams are take home. He gives an extra credit lab for up to 60 extra credit points towards your lab grade.

Dr. Radtke is a horrible professor. His lab assignments are too specific and unnecessary. He has us walk all across campus to take redundant measurements for no reason. He could choose 20 trees with a few hundred feet of each other be he instead asks us to walk over three miles for almost every lab. I don't have enough character to explain how bad

the rumors are true it's not fun. definitely only take it if you have to and just suck it up and get through it. his tests are fine but the labs suck. i'd suggest taking it with easier classes so you can put time into this one. overall, he's a nice guy if you ask for help but not super easy to work with.

Dr. Radtke is a very nice guy who obviously loves what he does; however, he is not good at explaining things/teaching and the labs are extremely difficult and lengthy. Supposed to be a 2000 level class but feels more like a 4000.

He's a nice guy but sometimes he's not the best at explaining what you need to know. Rather he gets way into detail about little things but doesn't always convey the big picture. Be prepared to try out a lot of different computer programs and for things in lab to feel like a whirlwind. It's not an easy class. Don't save the labs for last minute

Dr. Radke is very personable. He likes to explain thoroughly the concepts, sometimes a bit too much. However, If you work hard in his classes and pay attention you can attain a decent grade in his class. I recommend actually doing all of the labs instead of swapping answers as some do, it will make understanding easier.

Took him for greek and roman myth, he's really funny and I really enjoyed his class

Take any class but this.

I had no idea what this guy was talking about half the time but there's so much extra credit and the tests are easy so it didn't really matter.

Phillips is a fun and passionate professor. As long as you do the bare minimum and to class and take notes on the lectures and you'll be fine. Exams are curved and there are a ton of extra credit opportunities. Quizzes are online and the lowest is dropped.

Phillips is an amazing professor! The tests are difficult but if you go to class, take notes, and study then you'll get a good grade on them. He gives a lot of chances for extra credit. Don't listen to the other reviews do not take this class.

A lot of work for a pathway class. Heavy lectures topics are boring wouldn't recommend.

he tries to make the course material fun and engaging and is fun to listen to in class. his powerpoints are vague and distracting though and he gives tests via powerpoints. interesting material but A LOT of reading and work for an elective class. quizzes were easy but you HAD to study for tests for hours to get a good grade.

Piilonen does curve the tests and gives extra credit in some recitations.  Overall he is not bad.  Way better than Slawney.  And his tests do not reflect the homework.

Piilonen is awesome! If you have to suffer through physics (or if you, like me, actually like physics) you might as well have a great teacher!
