reviews.comment: The material covered during the class is challenging, however the professor taught the concepts pretty well. Don't expect to get an A (or even B) if you skip class.

George was probably one of if not the best math teacher I've ever had. His lectures do move fast, but he explains the topics in such detail that I did not really feel lost at any point. He is more concerned with his students understanding the concepts and material rather than getting 100% correct answers.

Prepare to fall in love with the Organic Chemistry Tutor because George's lectures move so fast it is almost certain you will need to go back and review the concepts.

Homework assignments were tough - usually testing every edge case and unique set of conditions within each problem. I liked this though because it prepared you well for his tests.

Dr. Sharma was truly one of the most influential and caring instructors I have ever had in this time at Virginia Tech. She truly cared about your understanding of the material and had a true passion for her craft. Don't be afraid to say a few icebreakers out loud. Shes not only an amazing woman but a great teacher. Tests were fair. I recommend!
She is the absolute best

Dr. Sharma was great! Her assignments made you think but weren't overly difficult. Exams were online and reasonable with a mix between conventional tests (some conceptual questions with a few workout problems) and an engine analysis done in person. Overall a great professor who clearly cared about her students and their success. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It often seemed like the problems greatly confused her, and she wasn't sure how to solve them. She frequently made errors in her workings. She posts the lecture notes, but they're difficult to follow if you weren't in class. Despite this, her tests were easier than some of the other 2204 professors. It is very possible to do well in her class.

Honestly her notes weren't amazing but if you go to class and write down the necessary things, you will get through just fine. She outlines well whats going to be on the tests and they aren't very hard either. Also does not assign a lot of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She cares a lot about her students, is very responsive to emails, and can always make time for online office hours if you are struggling. Just by doing the homework and provided extra practice (not a ton) without AI, I did very well. My only issue is she can be hard to understand sometimes and her notes can be all over the place.

She is very sweet and is always willing to help her students. However, during her lectures, it sounded like she was talking to herself most of the time. She didn't explain the concepts well at all and often overcomplicated things, not to mention her notes were almost illegible, all over the place, and basically useless.

Very poor at teaching the class. Hard to follow every lecture, especially when a lot of mistakes are made throughout the lecture. Expect to study a lot outside of class. Content in class is just and extension of Calculus 2.

Overall the class was not the most difficult because, in retrospect, the midterms were somewhat reasonable. HOWEVER, as a professor, he is one of the worst I have had. You will be forced to learn almost entirely from the homework as he cannot teach. Additionally, he does not know how to use Canvas so there are no posted notes if you miss a day.

I'm not even done with the class but I'm just salty reminiscing on my last midterm. Took off 8/10 points bc I forgot to plug in the vector i got back into the original tangent plane formula. Did all of the work and legit just forgot the last step that would take 10 seconds. Since there are so few problems I got a 70 on the test.

A lot of what other people said is true, especially about getting confused in class. He also teaches with a high expectation of prior knowledge and ability to learn quickly, both of which I didn't have so I struggled. However, if you have those things, you will enjoy the class because he will expand your knowledge and even make you laugh a little.
This dude gave the easiest test in the world. Yes he might be bad at lectures but it's so easy to get an A in the class if you just study for final.

This professor prepared us well for the midterms with helpful review sessions. The course required studying, but it was fair and not impossible. The final was challenging, but doing well on the midterms helped the overall grade.
Doesn't know what hes teaching, didn't post syllabus until two weeks before final. Do not take this professor!

To all the people here complaining about Pratt, It honestly make me sad to see. John Pratt has been a delightful professor to take during my first semester of UnderGrad in Math 2204. While yes he can get confused when questions are outside of his class notes, he understands material deeply and expects you to too. Test Heavy and only 7 problems sets

Lecture consists mostly of out-of-context examples without any background information. Be prepared to self-study the course or nag someone in a different section/professor for their notes, or else you'll be completely lost. Homework is typically 20+ questions, but honestly, you learn more from doing the homework than actually attending lecture.

Assigns very long homework (25-30) questions, yet only grades around 4-5 questions. He often stumbles over his words during lecture. Tests are only free-response questions, so no practice on multiple choice for the final. Attend the test review every chance to do well in his class. If you can, drop the class and find a new section.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very nice and helpful if you ask him questions. In class he only teaches by doing examples so when faced with something other than that it can be hard to understand. First two tests are relatively easy but the third test is abnormally hard. Seems confused in class sometimes and cannot always explain why he is writing things.

Teaches by solving problems on the whiteboard; often skips steps and covers the problems with his body while writing - making it hard to follow along. Lots of hw questions - with only a few being graded. First two tests were easy, but the 3rd and the final were much more difficult than anything done in class or hw, killing your overall grade.

Good guy but I can see why he's a bad professor. As someone who already took multi before the class was pretty easy, 30q/1.5 weeks homework was honestly manageable. Answers are all online if you look. Class is just problems on whiteboard. Decent ig. Test review sessions are helpful. Go. Pretty much what is on test. Take someone else if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pratt will show you that your GPA is not in your hands when it comes to college. He just decided to make one of the tests harder than anything he taught or was on the hw, and he did the same thing for the final. Please save yourself and take someone else. You'll think hes ok the first 2 tests, then by the end of the semester you will hate him.

Multi is an easy subject but pratt is a bad teacher. Some tests had things we had never learned and were completely different from the review sessions. The frq section of the Final exam is written by the professor you have, so I strongly recommend anyone other than pratt, he will destroy your gpa and there will be nothing you can do about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Long HW that is useless. Only does examples, nothing conceptual. First 2 tests were easier than the hw then the 3rd test and the final had stuff we hadn't even learned and was harder than anything we had done. The Free response of the final is written by your professor, so get ANYONE but him. I recommend Shixu Meng. Pratt will destroy your gpa.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Told the SSD students the wrong time for the final and we all showed up 2 hours late.  He sucks at communication and technology, save yourself the stress and find a better professor.  Dr. Pratt does NOT adapt to his students at all, I've emailed him several times about different things and have either received no response or a "see me after class".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Worst professor at vt. do not take class you will do terribly even if you understand the material. rambles in class and skips vital example problems, extremely difficult tests.

Pratt told SSD students the incorrect time for the final exam and has forgotten to schedule testing reservations with Werth (resulting in taking an exam in a random office). He is one of the least accommodating I've had. He grades harshly, his tests are rough, and he doesn't explain things clearly during lecture.

His lectures consist solely of examples, which leaves you to teach yourself the material from that. He writes on the chalkboard in very small font and stands in front of it the whole time. He loses his train of thought sometimes because he is quite old, which made lectures hard to follow. Hw can be up to 40 questions. So decide for urself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: JP assigns very hefty homeworks that are just unnecessary given that the vast majority of his students are in engineering and a math course is one of their lowest priorities. He has no technology skills and makes homework assignments convoluted and took forever to set up WebAssign. His lectures are somewhat well organized and tests are pretty easy.

Please retire this man! Cons: Horrible with technology, blackboard only notes, never responds helpfully in an email, no consideration for student time, 30+ HW questions, and difficult to get ahold of outside class.  You want your test/homework back? hope you have time to pester him for it after class.  
Pros: Decently organized notes/review session
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only pros to Pratt is that his notes are neat and easy to follow, his tests are standard, and you could say he cares about his students. However, Pratt is incompetent with technology, assigns 40 written homework problems, all WebAssigns are due at the end of term, responds to emails with "See me after class.", and grades harshly on tests.

While Pratt is a nice and funny guy, he sucks at teaching. I get nothing out of the lectures because all he does is mumble through examples without explaining any of them in detail. It also doesn't help that he is not engaging at all. His homeworks are way too long. At least he tells you what questions will be on the test. Take anyone but him.

He gets a lot of negative reputation because he does ramble a bit sometimes but this guy is genuinely a great professor/person. He goes pretty slowly in class and makes sure to engage everyone by calling on people for answers and stuff. His diagrams which are SUPER important for multi are great and in all despite the HW being heavy he is awesome.

Doesn't post notes. HW is long but gets you more than ready for the tests. Tests are easier than the HW. Funny guy. Holds reviews day before the test which lets you know exactly what kind of questions will be on the test. Easy to access outside of class. Answers questions. He gets a little lost in his own work but its whatever. Easy A.

Super nice guy and cares a lot about what he teaches. The thing is, for me at least, the lectures were super hard to follow so I found myself self teaching outside of class hours. HWs are super tedious and are hard to complete without a good understanding of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor

HW is very long and tedious, but great practice: NEVER had to study because of them. Lectures are great, Pratt goes step-by-step with examples that show you exactly how to logic out problems. Holds optional review before each test and trains you for exactly what's on the exam. Knows his stuff, willing to help, and is a great teacher.

Pratt is a very likeable teacher who spends lots of time explaining the concepts behind each lesson before delving into the math itself. Most of his criticism is based on the homework load, which I did not find to be too bad for a Virginia Tech math course. In my experience he is a great teacher and he goes over all test content during his reviews.

This guy only has a job because his wife is President of the Department. Don't take him. 30+ problems per homework assignment with only a few days to complete it. Lectures are completely useless and his office hours are set up so it's almost impossible for you to meet him. Take anyone else or accept that you will get a bad grade for too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have nothing against Professor Pratt as a person, but I do not learn anything from his lectures. His homework are always around 30 questions and very tedious as he only grades 5/30 problems. Most of the in-class examples don't relate to the topic at all and the ones on the test are always completely different.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pratt's teaching style is very old school where he spends most of the lesson going over examples on the whiteboard. If you follow along and pay attention, you will learn a lot. I think this is a lot better than 80% of professors who use slideshows to teach. Aside from the way he assigns and grades HW, I don't know why so many people dislike him

Dr. Pratt's lecturing method is to do very specific examples, so you don't really learn any concepts. He rarely looks up from the board while lecturing, so good luck if you're confused. His homeworks are very tedious and end up not relating to the tests at all, so they are a huge waste of time. Don't take this guy, go to community college instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Go to his Test reviews. He literally goes through every type of question that you'll see on the exams.

Missing one question on hw results in a 12/20. The classes are a snoozefest and are too proof-heavy. The first few tests are easy, but at end of the year, the FRQs given are impossible to solve and harder than a typical Calculus 3 level. Canvas and Websassign is poorly managed. Great guy, but not the kind of professor that is ideal to learn with.

certified bozo just rambles the whole time. homeworks are waste of time they don't prepare for tests at all. lecture examples are too specific and don't help with general questions of topic. its time to hang em up john.

Very hard to engage in lectures since he doesn't "include" the class often.Rambles on and will either use homework problems as in-class examples or textbook examples that aren't that relevant.I haven't been the best with the homeworks but that has changed because of his class.Great guy and knows his stuff,but doesn't explain it comprehensibly.

The assignments were kind of unorganized and didn't make much sense, but I enjoyed the topics of this class. I think she kind of just throws us into our assignments without much thought. Regardless, they were simple enough. I got through without reading and did just fine. Tests were take-home, but she said she's going to switch to in-person.

Im in SOC 2404 with her. She's very engaging and there's a lot of class discussions. The assignments she gives are not hard and are straight forward. I really recommend taking this class or any classes with her.
Class wasn't too difficult and professor Presson was very understanding and fair. Attendance required with built in free absences.
She's great

she's wonderful and i loved this class. attendance in mandatory but very flexible and reasonable. class structure is very relaxed, mainly lectures and discussions with the people around you. this class is much more fun if you enjoy the people you sit near. at home exams and not many assignments but the ones you do, are interesting and valuable.
Very interesting class
Good experience
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Presson is very passionate about what she teaches. She is very easy to communicate with and approachable. The topics she teaches are intriguing and she presents them in a very understandable way. Attendance is mandatory, but you do get some unexcused absences. I haven't used the textbook that much so just pay attention to her lectures.
Dr. Presson is a wonderful woman! Would absolutely take her class again, Social Inequality is a great class and she makes the material interesting and fun to learn.
Class was easy, only had short weekly quizzes and a few papers. Super sweet professor!
I loved Dr. Pressen and would take her class again in a heartbeat. She says the textbook is required however I never read it and still ended up with an A in her class.

Dr. Presson is a great professor. Attendance is mandatory but of you do show up to class and pay attention then there is no way that you can fail her class. She genuinely cares about her students and what they have to say and definitely teaches clearly.

I have taken 2 of her classes and I loved them! She always kept her lectures interesting by talking about real cases and allowing open discussions about the material. There are weekly discussion posts but she is not a tough grader. There was an end of sem presentation but she was very accommodative to students with fear of public speaking!

Prof. was awesome! She makes lectures interesting and she's super helpful and friendly! She gave trigger warnings before class through emails/canvas if we were talking about a sensitive subject in class and provided opportunities for alternative assignments if the subject hit too close to home.

She was always super sweet and you can tell she really cares for her students' mental health. Her lectures are pretty normal, she'll speak off of points from presentation slides and will allow notes on the slides as well as photos of them. The only thing is that her tests are surprisingly difficult, definitely read the articles she posts on Canvas.

Priya is amazing! She's really great at explaining complex economics concepts in simple, easy-to-understand ways. She's kind and personable. Textbook is a helpful supplement to lectures, but not necessary. Homeworks are easy (20 questions, equally weighted, multiple attempts, due every 1-2 weeks), & if you do the homework you'll do fine on exams.

Knows her stuff and teaches it well. She truly wants her students to succeed and will grade you flexibly if you show you care and want to learn. Attendance is taken once per week, tests are open notes and outside of class.
Great professor, just have to do the myeconlab assignments weekly and score alright on exams. Was easily reachable and understanding if deadlines weren't able to be met.

She is incredibly knowledgeable about economics and clearly cares about her student's success. The course was dependent on Pearson's MyEconLab but the assignments were easy if you reviewed the material at least once. She is easily accessible if you have any questions about the material. I couldn't recommend her enough, she is absolutely amazing!

FALL 2024 She is a great instructor over all , quite accommodating and helpful. The class was well planned and a grade booster for me. Just do the  myeconlabs and even  if one performs marginally well in the exams one can still score well! I would highly recommend reaching out to her with questions and concerns over the course that's what helped me

Prof. Pula is one of the best teachers I've had at VT. He is very intelligent and the work load he assigns is reasonable. His standards are fair, he's reachable, and course requirements are reasonable. Those who don't do well in his classes are either in the wrong major, or just plainly not doing the work.

The class was entirely lecture-based, he reads directly from the textbook/readings assigned for the week. He is typically unable to answer questions and half of the time stumbles about and seems very disorganized. He does not allow for electronic note-taking of any kind. There were three presentations but he quite literally gives everyone a 100 on.

Dr. Pula is one of my absolute fav professors. I took PSCI3166 with him as well and it was also very fun. Admittedly, he thrives more in small classes that aren't pathways and have students who are genuinely interested in the content (like PSCI3166). He's extremely knowledgable and cares about his students, very kind and always willing to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He knows his stuff, he's just very boring, and his class has few if any interactive elements.

This class not only inspired me to change my major, but also transfer out of Virginia Tech. It wasn't super hard, and I never really did the readings or studied a lot, but is it unreasonably boring. It made me forget that education (especially poli sci) is supposed to be enjoyable and engaging and that I was paying money to listen to him.

He was fine, I don't have much to say about him tbh. He's fine but he's a very dull lecturer, he just doesn't have much personality. The class that I had with him wasn't particularly difficult, but I found him quite boring.

He's a great guy, clearly very knowledgeable. He cares a lot about the subject manner, he just presents it in a less interactive way. Perhaps if it was less lecture-based and there were more projects/class activities it would be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: This is the first class I have taken where, when walking into class, I felt physically sick. The stress this class has given me is insane - I definetely would not have been as stressed out as I was if he added more assignments so that I could have more grades to fall back on. He also literally just read from the textbook for each lecture...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the Global Economy course. I was concerned in the beginning because I did not have any background in econ, but Prof. Pula's lectures were extremely helpful. I especially enjoyed the topic of global finance. There readings assigned weekly but they are not hard and if you do them and attend lecture you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He often stays on the same slide with a few lines of basic information for 20+ minutes. Without a Dean of Students letter, you will not be excused. He is also very hard to reach by email. You have to pay to use TopHat for tests. The grading system does not upload to CV so it's hard to check grades. I do not recommend anyone take his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pula is a nice professor and his classes are pretty interesting and not difficult at all. I will say you need to attend class. There are pop quizzes, but if you attend class they're really easy and even if you don't do well on one or two it's not a huge deal because he drops the lowest grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Pula is a great professor and is very passionate about his teaching. I was very thankful he continued having class in-person this whole semester (Fall 20') however it was tough when needing to skip class since he doesn't post notes. He teaches straight from the textbook and does pop quizzes from it so you actually have to read it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Class is difficult, but not as difficult as reviews below would make it seem. Attend class regularly, take the notes for the class. Study those notes for the exams, and you'll do decently. Lectures aren't thrilling, but Pula is a smart man (and very understanding) and the concepts are easy if you just do the bare minimum (attend and take notes).
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pula knows what he's talking about and his CPE and GEGP classes are really easy if you're a good writer. He is very reading heavy, but if you do the readings the papers are a breeze. The only downside is that his lectures are very dry, but I think one reason for this is students in his classes just don't do the readings and don't participate.

reviews.comment: Monotone, unsure, random pop quizzes that basically make up your entire grade and if you miss one of 3 questions- you're done. Hard to learn through lecture with his voice and lack of stability and confidence and lack of information on powerpoints and online, no access outside of class, textbook is very important- almost a better professor than him

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The most monotone and unsure professor I have ever had. You mess up one pop quiz, which is easy to do because there are only three questions and you have two minutes to complete them, and you are screwed. There are almost no chances for more points. He doesn't know what he is talking about and lectures straight from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The only reason you would show up for class is to avoid getting screwed by a pop quiz. There are barely any opportunities for points, besides the exams and the random pop quizzes. You can literally not pay attention in class and read the textbook and be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Wayyyy too much work for what the class should be. Requires you to drive far distances for interviews and community service hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The beginning of the semester was fine but the end is what really made me not like the class. From the beginning, she made it seem like we would have a final GROUP project (paper or poster). We actually had to do individual projects and a group presentation. This class was the most work and it was only an intro class. Dont recommend, tough grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Easy class, sometimes boring though. Do the homework and participate and you will get an A
She is super nice and encouraging. If you email her a draft of your paper, she will gladly edit it and provide helpful feedback to improve your grade.
Very nice and knows what she's teaching very well. She is always willing to help. She encourages drafts of papers that won't be graded, but are used to provide feedback.
She is very nice, yet as an awkward personality. The class is easy and she is very knowledgeable on how to write a good paper. 40% of the grade is just coming to class.
She brought her puppy into class and it always made my class. She is very helpful if you ask questions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I wanted to like her so much, but her grading was really bad. Only two assignments were graded until like 3/4 of the way through the semester, and I still didn't have feedback on a few of my assignments by the final so I never knew where I messed up. She's nice, but it felt impossible to learn from my mistakes and succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I fought tooth and nail for my A. Probably wasted over $500 in tuition from all the classes she canceled, & she cancels 20 mins before classes start. We literally got HW 1 graded on Nov. 11th, 75% thru the semester. She NEVER checks email, COMPLETE HW EARLY BC 1/2 THE TIME SHE'LL NEVER COVER THE MATERIAL SHE'S GRADING ON, AND U NEED TO CLARIFY!!!!
She's cool but she takes forever to grade assignments and sometimes isn't very well prepared. She also cancels class a lot which depending on the person can be good or bad.

Easy class, but lectures were boring. She takes attendance but gives you the answer. Exams are done on your own time and are open note/resource. HW and exams can be tricky since some content isnt mentioned in the textbook or lecture. She takes a while to grade things tho. Purely math based. If you receive an A- you can skip the final.
Super easy class. All assignments are posted early, so you can finish weeks ahead. Exams are online, and it's an easy A if you use your resources.

Very easy class, he posted all the assignments for the semester, so you could get ahead of the class. I was able to finish the class like two weeks before the semester was even over. The exams are also online, so use all your resources, and you will get an easy "A" in the class.

Want a low-key class, that is interesting and you learn about the different types of music between race, country, and history? This class is for YOU. Buying the textbook is the hardest part as it's not cheap, but if you need some ease take this class. Professor Reep is really chill, has straightforward grading too! Make sure you respond to others!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Best professor I will ever have. Never fails to put me in a better mood then when I walked in. Just show up and have a good time!

The coolest band director EVER! Chad is so charming and hilarious, but he also has great music taste and knows the course material in depth. All of his band students love him and I hope everyone reading this gets to experience his energetic and uplifting teaching style. My credentials: 4 years of performing in Chad's band ensembles. Love Chad!

took him my freshman year for sight singing and he was a lot of fun. I just wish he challenged us a bit more because I did not feel prepared for ear training the next semester. I also felt like he tried to be like the cool uncle or teacher that is your friend and it ended up back firing on him as students took advantage of his kindness.

I've had Chad for symphony and campus band and he's the best! Super fun, cares for the bands success, and chooses decent music. Rehearsal is always a good time with him. AND he conducts well. Great guy!
One of my favorite profs to this date. #ILoveChad

I really loved him as a teacher. Super chill, but cares about our success as an ensemble. Appreciated his hard work and the energy he brought to class. I want to have him again as a conductor. If he reads this, I want him to know that he is an undervalued member of VT fine arts, and I hope he gets a raise.
Chad is the goat in MVs.
He was an awesome director for both the MVs and for band classes!

Music Appreciation is an online asynch class - so you'll have to purchase an access code to a class page where you read chapters and take quizzes. There's weekly quizzes, a midterm, final, and weekly discussions in the class. Reep will help you out if you have any questions/problems, just need to email him. Easy class, recommend it for 6A pathway

Chad is an incredible professor for the Marching Virginians, and Symphony Band! He knows how to joke around with the class, but is also able to focus on the music. He forms wonderful connections with his students, and truly cares about all of us.

Campus Band was a little more instrumentally balanced than Symphonic Band and the music is more fun than challenging. Nevertheless, it was really enjoyable and Chad was at his hilarious best as usual. Rehearsals are only Monday evenings with 1 concert

Symphonic Band was a blast. You have rehearsals TTh afternoons with 2 concerts. Chad is a great director and he's really funny and lighthearted. The band does tend to be imbalanced (ex. we had 4 clarinets but like a thousand alto saxes and trumpets), but he does the best he can. The music is the right balance between fun and challenging

One of the most chill, funniest, & caring professors. This class was extremely easy and fun! Assignments can be all over the place, but ultimately prof. is very lenient on deadlines (if you ask) and it is straightforward. He can work on being more organized, but everything eventually gets done. This ended up my favorite class this past semester!

Nice family guy. However, get ready for group work! Got totally screwed with a group that never helped contribute. Professor Waters pretty much just taught from his PowerPoints and personal experiences. Exams were oddly harder than you would think they would be for what he taught during class. GO TO CLASS IN CASE OF POP QUIZZES!

Professor Waters is a nice guy, but his teaching consists of him just reading off of power points on things you would be better off just teaching yourself in the text book it's pretty much just vocab. Makes tests way harder than they need to be. I would recommend taking professor Poff instead if you can.

Professor Waters is very nice and okay at teaching. His lectures consist of material straight from the textbook that you can honestly teach yourself. Attendance is not mandatory, however, he does give random pop quizzes throughout the semester. Get ready for lots of group work. Exams are weirdly hard for a class that should be super easy.

He is a really nice professor and is very personable. He is a good teacher but the material can be a bit harder if you do not pay attention or show up. My class had a group project in person that was key to our grade, do not put this off and ask for help if you need.
NA

Professor Waters is a great person, kind and caring about his students. Textbook is very straightforward and easy to read. Attendance is not mandatory but there are pop quizzes. Tests are open note but still pretty difficult. A lot of group work too. If you have to take MGT 1104, take it with Professor Waters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very lecture-heavy, and if you want to pass the class, you just need to take extremely detailed notes. Tests are open note, but they are also timed.
Don't take it, nearly had to withdraw from this course.

The professor is a really nice person, but the class is seriously the hardest pathways class I have ever taken. If you are thinking of taking this as a pathway for an easy grade, DONT! The material is hard to grasp (for those not that interested in art) and the tests basically rely on small details that you would not actually think to write down.

I took this class as a pathway and heavily encourage you to pick something else. Prof was great dont get me wrong but as a STEM major this was my lowest grade (i was taking ochem at the same time for reference.) Lecture HEAVY and incredibly detailed tests, the class is interesting but not worth the stress to take out of major

If you enjoy watching hours of videos and taking a ton of notes then this if the class for you, BUT if you dont, I HIGHLY ADVISE NOT TAKING THIS CLASS.  Shes a tough grader and the tests are veryyyy detailed.  I like art history but this class did not peak my interest at all. If its not required, I wouldn't waste your time.

if you're trying to take an easy "A" elective class online and think this is the class for you. no no no. if you enjoy art then sure but if you're just trying to get through it. I do not recommend this class one single bit. long long lectures. not easy especially if it's open notes for class. don't waste your time.

Took both 2385/2386; actively pay attention to her PPT video lectures because all the commentary is important/will be on quizzes/tests! Take lots of notes, tests have many fill-in-the-blank/short answer questions. If you have a short attention span this class might be difficult. DON'T procrastinate; do the work + extra credit and you'll be fine.

Spaar was okay as a professor. If you're looking for an easy pathways class this is NOT it. There is quite a bit of work involoved in this class, and the material is more difficult to understand than you would initially think.

I took this course as a pathway which was my mistake and I wouldn't take this class if you are the same. It was virtual and point based, with very long lectures that I had to watch in x2. This class is doable though, and there is extra credit given which was helpful, I honestly just didn't put that much work into the class since it wasn't major.

Be prepared to take a lot of notes on video lectures, as your notes will be helpful for open-notes (but not open-internet) quizzes and exams! While this is an asynchronous course, the professor has a very vibrant personality and you know she's enthusiastic about art history as you go through her video recordings. Extra credit are provided!

most goated math professor at tech. he was the only professor where i wouldnt actually dread going to class. tests are slight and the homeworks are manageable even if theyre long sometimes, but he grades super easy. the final was rough imo but other than that awesome class.
Great professor, one of the ones that really feels like he wants you to pass. Will work with you a lot. Do the practice tests and study guides and you'll be fine.

Honestly great all around just as long as you go to class. He's actually good at explaining and answering questions if you have them as well. From what I've heard from other friends about their professors in calc 3, dr reyes is prolly the best prof in this subject.

Dr. Reyes is super lowkey and approachable, you really feel like you can just talk to him. He's very animated and fun to listen to in his lectures, although he could be unprepared at times. He was very helpful in office hours and through email. The homeworks aren't too much work, but the project and final exam were pretty time consuming.
Awesome professor. Has a clear love for math and makes his lectures exciting and easy to follow and learn. Tests are relatively easy if you do the harder homeworks that proceed them.

Dr Reyes is a very funny professor, he incorporated funny memes to try and make the class more engaged. I had him for 2204 during his inaugural semester teaching as well as spring semester and he actively tried improving how he went about the class. His math lectures are one of the best in the dep and is a very fair grader if you know your stuff.
He made what would have been a difficult class into a manageable one. Cares about his students and knows what he's talking about, would absolutely recommend.

Awesome teacher - respectful of students and his lectures are actually enjoyable. Not too much homework - lengthy but infrequent. Things were graded fairly, and the tests were on material he made sure to review with us. Absolutely recommend!

Dr. Reyes was a very fun professor! His lectures always addressed the types of questions you would be asked on homework and tests. He would sometimes extend the due date for the homework. At office hours, he was very helpful and would lead you to the correct answer. He occasionally gave a few extra credit points! The department final was not fun.

I think he's a great teacher, and he makes learning Discrete more fun. He teaches well, but the course is difficult, and he will often breeze through questions too fast before you can really process what's going on.

Took him for linear algebra. Would not recommend if you are a freshman/sophomore because most of his class revolves around using variables to define things rather than words which can make it somewhat difficult to understand what's happening on an intuitive level

Goes through the notes fairly quickly but stops for any questions. Sometimes goes off on a tangent and tests can be tricky. Tons of webassigns and the crowdmark assignments can help bring your grade up. Sometimes had to learn things on my own, but office hours are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, he's a good teacher. Most of the classes are note-taking, but he does stop and answer questions too. Did a review day the class before a test and gave practice tests. Tests are tricky. He is a little hard to get a hold of outside of class; sometimes wouldn't show up to office hours till later than he said.

he occasionally makes funny jokes in class, is well engaged w/ the class on what hes lecturing on, his homeworks are short, but his exams are a bit tougher. overall a nice person, i do like how he sometimes wore a hawaiian shirt to lecture.

His lectures are very engaging and helpful (make sure to ask questions!). He is also very accessible during office hours, which more people should take advantage of. However, it is def a challenging course and he clearly dabbled in the dark arts when brewing up some of those test questions. Regardless, he's still one of the best Calc II profs imo.
He is the best professor in MATH 1226.

Dr. Rick is one of the best professors I've ever had at VT. He is very knowledgeable, and his lectures are engaging and easy to follow. The class is fast-paced, but he takes time to break problems down and makes them very digestible. Attending every class, asking questions, and going through lecture examples when reviewing for exams helps a lot.

Dr. Rick is the best math professor I've had. He's in charge of the math 1226 program and is very knowledgable about the subject. He helps writes the exams and final so he prepares his students exactly for what's on them. He moves fast, but will always stop to answer questions and break things down. His lectures are engaging and easy to follow.

Shaplin was a great prof to have for an intro, but weed out, math class. He is very clear, cares about the material, and wants to see each student succeed. Not very accessible in-person outside class, but will negotiate office hour times and will email with you. Cengage textbook req for homeworks.

He is an ok teacher. He moves very very fast and the course material is hard. The course is hard so you can't blame him for moving fast but this is just something to be aware of going in. He is very knowledgeable about the material and knows what he is doin.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Rick is a great professor he knew the subject well and though he was fast he would stop and answer questions if you had any.

Dr. Rick Shaplin was an amazing math professor. He's really friendly and will answer whatever questions you have enthusiastically. He for sure just loves math. He's also very open to answering any questions on grading. He'll definitely try to help you succeed. His tests were considered pretty easy compared to the rest of the department as well.

If you've never done calc two before you will probs struggle a bit. Went through material extremely fast and taught in a confusing way. Also graded the homework very harshly so there wasn't a whole lot boosting my grade. At least he did give us an extra credit opportunity at the end. Nice guy, not a great professor. Hardest class I've taken so far.

Great teacher but wow he does not hold back on making tough homeworks and tests. If you've never been exposed to calc 2 this class is ridiculously hard. He speeds through lectures, but is always good at answering questions and slowing down if he needs to. He's extremely smart and entertaining, but yeah make sure you really pay attention.
He is very nice and funny. His lectures were very fast. I had to teach myself a lot of the material or get help. Tests are pretty hard but it is also a hard class. Not bad but could be better.

Nice guy, was always there to answer any questions about lectures or homework. He was quick on lectures sometimes and the tests were pretty difficult. overall, pretty good GTA. Calc 2 is a hard class regardless of the professor but if you put in the time you can pass the class.

He's a cool guy, and nice to work with and is willing to help you outside of class. However, the lectures are slightly flawed, as he goes by very fast and not in depth unless you ask questions. If you didn't take any equivalent classes for Calc 2, please, make sure you get help as soon as you get an unsatisfactory test score!

Rick is a cool guy, he's a great teacher and gives good feedback, although he does go very fast and is difficult to follow if you've never seen calc 2 before. Either way, I recommend since I've heard horror stories about other calc 2 classes. Since he's a GTA he might not teach calc 2 again... but take him if you can.

Nice guy, cares about his students, and tries to grade fairly leniently. The tests are pretty rough, but again, calc 2 is pretty rough in general. There are definitely worse professors out there, and Rick is overall a very solid teacher. He does go pretty fast, but will always stop to answer any questions.

The professor is knowledgeable about the topics in the course. This class requires some drawing skills so be prepared for that and there are also strict due dates since the professor does not take any late work. But overall, if you do your work on time and have open communication then the course will go well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Unless you really like drawing, being creative, and reading LOTS of slides with the history of art, don't take this class. Don't buy the textbook, I literally never used it. I did not read any of the textbook chapters or listen to any of the powerpoints, I just studied for an hour before each quiz and did fine.

She was fine and the class was easy as long as you skimmed the presentations. That said, this is incredibly nitpicky but all of her powerpoints, assignment descriptions, etc... were riddled with spelling errors and incomplete or cut-off sentences. Many of the slides (especially those with instructions) were unreadable. Made the class feel stupid.
just a B word.

It was an okay class. She's a nice person, but the lectures were very boring, and she likes to go on rambles. The workload was fine, and the quizzes/tests were moderately easy as long as you studied for like fifteen minutes beforehand. I will have to say, her outfits always eat.
Really annoying honestly. Makes you do so much work for what I thought would be an easy pathway. Take anything MUS 2115 for pathways 6 with berrios instead.

for a freshman level course it's ridiculous. the class takes itself so seriously for no reason. needed it for a pathway and struggling in it now. and the prof doesn't gaf about ssd students. plus the class is boring? pick a struggle.

I took this class as a pathways requirement. It was relatively easy as long as you just do the homework and study the material for like 10 minutes before tests or quizzes. I'm not particularly interested in design so the lectures weren't that interesting to me but they weren't hard content or anything. Easy enough for a pathways class, I recommend.

A ridiculous amount of work for no reason. It's a 1000 level class but is hard. If you're not interested in art/design, DON'T take this class. The tests and quizzes are in a lockdown browser. The professor is really nice but wouldn't recommend for a pathway. Wouldn't be in this class if it wasn't required for my major. Waste of time in my opinion.

I really loved this professor and class. She has a textbook for the class, but I never read it because all the information is in her lectures that she posts on canvas. The exams and quizzes are online with lockdown browser and webcam but they're easy. There are projects but they don't take that much time to do. She's really kind and funny!!

She is a great person and very nice to talk to as long as you show up and at least seem to pay attention.  Attendance is mandatory, however all assignments for the class are pretty easy and can be done quickly if you just focus for a few minutes or an hour for the projects.
Terrible.

Renee is very sweet and you can tell she cares about the topics she teaches (very well educated in them). Her lectures can get a little long (which can be tiring especially at 9:30 in the morning), but she's fun to listen to and engaging. Do the assignments, put in the effort (and try not to procrastinate) and you'll do great in this class.
assignments will be very long or very short. very heavy lectures, will tend to get off topic and continue to blab nonstop. not my cup of tea
cares very little with ssd students. projects are ridiculously long.

I had her a while ago I don't think she knows how to teach and grade fairly. Truth hurts and her truths can be harsh. I don't think she notices the way other students will. I 100% agree she has favorites and doesn't have the patience and courage to teach students with learning disabilities.

I agree with the comment she doesn't gaf about SSD students. It frustrates me how she knows if a student is struggling she's okay but if you make one mistake she can be harsh. Doesn't know how to teach with students who have learning disabilities. Idk what world she grew up in. She definitely has favorites.

This class is really easy as long as you do the work. Attendance is mandatory which is kinda annoying but her lectures are interesting and she usually lets you out of class super early. She's an easy grader so just do the assignments on time and study her slides for the tests.

Some weeks were a LOT of work, however, it is not very difficult just extremely time-consuming. Assignment directions were not very specific but she is an easy grader. Study her review slides and you will ace the quizzes and exams.

Assignment are long, uninteractive and don't enhance the material you learn throughout the course. Hard deadlines so homework can't be made up. Requires camera for test, if you don't want people to cheat than don't assign test or teach it in-person over the summer. If you want a lot of work to learn nothing, take this professor. :)

since i took this class asynchronously i didn't really interact with professor walsh much but from what i got, she was nice but also blunt. she didn't explain things very thoroughly and didn't really care much for students' mistakes and excuses. this class has SO MANY assignments, quizzes, projects, and exams it was a lot to do every week.

Class was a super easy A and a lot of fun when it came to the projects. Go to the lectures and review them for quizzes and exams for good grades. Super understanding and a lot of fun to converse with during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gave assignments for New Year's Eve and things that you had to work on during new Year even though it wasn't specified you had to. She wasn't really engaged in conversation with me and instead just wanted to be snippy and short with me when I had my zoom call with her. She used Respondus Lockdown WITH the camera. She also cares little for SSD help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Decided to move an exam from being on a Thursday to two days earlier Tuesday without notifying anyone or making canvas announcements or sending out emails and surprised the entire class with an early exam that several people missed with zero recourse. Just rambles about nonsense 24/7

The course content itself is not hard, but he doesn't teach it very well. He reads off of his own notes most of the time, and isn't an engaging teacher. He also adds exams that aren't on the syllabus. Other times, he's outright disrespectful and insults you if you answer his questions wrong. So glad that class is over, all around bad experience.

Econ 3104 is a pretty hard class, professor cothren did not make it any easier. His teaching style is mostly solving questions, which on the surface is very helpful but doesn't allow for students to actually understand the content. A lot of study outside of class is needed to get an okay grade

Cothren's grading system was out of 120 points, with 50 of them being test grades (midterm and final). This class is called Microeconomics with Calculus however he doesnt teach the calculus part even though the homework and tests are entirely calculus-based. His lectures are entirely conceptual and unfortunately aren't helpful. He is funny however.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 2 tests worth 40% each and 4 homeworks worth 5% each. Very harsh grader and the lecture notes posted are hard to follow. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took For Microtheory and Macrotheory. Not a professor you can cruise with. But I will say that you learn A LOT. If you take the time to talk to him outside of class, he is always willing to help you with some of the problems you are having. If you dont do HW and dont read, then you will fail. Fun to talk to about applied econ i.e. sabremetrics
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Truly does not care about his students. Assigns work to be done over breaks and right before football games (like hours before). Not sure if he understands that students have lives outside of his class. Incapable of giving example problems and will only give homework solutions if he feels like it. Do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: With this class, I really am just unsure of what I learned - it didn't seem very applicable in the real world to me. This semester was online, and he relied heavily on his TA and almost never answered concerns directly. All the grades are tests, but a 90 is an A. I never really went to be honest, because I never thought it was helpful.

It's very unfortunate that there isn't a standard for professors especially like Richard Cothren who is tenured. All of his assignments are tests that he uses year after year with absolutely no other assignments. He just shows up to class and sometimes doesn't even know what he is talking about. This man is a shame to the future of our generation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: When I took Macrotheory with him our grades were all tests. I would strongly recommend creating study sheets/ summary of everything of all material on a test. I thought that during office hours he gave back good feedback. Also the question sessions I thought sometimes helped. Also I would strongly recommend printing out notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: While I didn't  get A's with Cothren, he is without a doubt the best economics professor I had at Tech.  He is not interested in handing out grades, but really wants you to learn the material, and will spend time to help you if you let him know.  If you want an Easy A, take Ashley, if you want to learn, take Cothren.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Neither I, nor many of my classmates would agree with many of the complaints below. He has his own humor and you can see it at least a few times every class. At times, he had the whole class laughing. He is very nice, willing to talk at any time the day. Exams are tough in the sense that they properly test your understanding of material.

Follow along with the book, it helps explain everything. The class is comprised of 4 exams including a final each worth 25%. Each exam has about 25-28 questions. He provides alot of sample questions are that helpful. He's really not that bad as the reviews say. If you read the book, you're pretty much set.

Cothren is a nice guy.  A lot of students don't understand his style of humor, but I kind of enjoyed it.  His tests are fair because he gives sample questions ahead of time that are very similar to the test.  Ignore any mentioned negatives about him because he is actually a good professor.

He's honestly a good professor and deserves more respect than he seems to get. Having had him twice, he knows the material and communicates it well, and if you put in the the time to show up to class, follow along with his lectures, and read the text book, you'll do fine. He also gives grades on a super curve--this semester, an 80% is an A.

I liked him alot, he is a cool guy.  Material is boring and some think he is as well, but I liked his style.  Tests are kinda hard but he curves alot and its not really that hard to end up with an A, i got a B but i had 2 exams under 50 percent so... my bad.

Coming out of Intro to Micro I was expecting an easy class and instead was faced with Cothren's densely packed intro to Macro/All Nighters course. In his defense I had a 76 going into the final, stayed up all night studying the night before, got a 94 and ended up with an A. Didn't buy the textbook either
He is the worst person alive.
Makes the class harder than it needs to be.

Terrible teacher. Thinks he's amazing but really he's pretty worthless. He'll put your questions to the TA which isn't very helpful. Boring to listen too. If you're good at ECON it's  a good class to sleep through.
The worst professor I have ever had! Going to his office, listening to lectures, and reading his notes just made me more confused. If I’d not had the textbook, I would’ve failed this class.

Rick Law is respected professor in the department but he has a very "if you're not suffering you're not trying hard enough" mentality. His tests are hard, his labs take twice as long as the class period for it. There's really only one unit where he values class participation, unfortunately. 

Ask questions, even if he seems irritated!

Incredibly knowledgeable and a really good teacher. But structure is HARD class and the labs will take you hours outside of class to complete. Don't procrastinate and go to office hours. Hes a harsh grader and cares a lot about accuracy, so be careful on exams and ALWAYS go to review sessions he basically tells you the exact questions you'll see.

Structure is a tough class and there's no way around it, and it's less of the fault of Dr. Law than it is on the course structure. As for Dr. Law himself, he deeply cares for all of his students even if he may seem intimidating from the outside. Attending his office hours and review sessions will do you a lot of good on labs and tests respectively.

Rick law is one of my FAVORITE geoscience professors to date. He is a fantastic lecturer, but to understand the material you really need to go to class and take notes and TRY at the labs (I mean seek additional help). His tests are very fair and going to his exam reviews are a cheat code to an A. LOVE THIS GUY! He cares so much about his students.

Great, respected Professor in the department. Really knows what he's doing, however his grading is some of the harshest I have ever seen. If you take this course, make sure you make a lot of time for labs and projects, along with studying for the exams.
Great lectures and notes. Captivating info.

The class is difficult, but go to the exam reviews, because he lays out almost exactly what will be on them and makes a passing grade more achievable. Very lab-heavy, and those are the hardest part, but just make sure you ask plenty of questions. Can be rude at times, but he's very good at what he does, so do not get on his bad side.
Lectures are alright but generally do not help with exams too much.

Dr.Law is pretty much the man. If you go to class and actually take notes you can manage the tests very well. Lab is probably the hardest part. Overall, a really awesome professor with a lot of knowledge.
just reads the notes. unnecessary to come to class half of the time.  VERY difficult... change teachers before it's too late!!
i took physical geology and his exams are seriously impossible, UNTIL i found out that he uses all the exact same exams from the years past so find someone who took it the year before and your GOLDEN
Get out now.  For the sake of your GPA!!

Hard Tests but fun class, TA's grade hard so beware leave no mistakes!! Take good notes!! Especially for the newport project! I didn't understand all the concepts but I'm sure that was mostly due to it being my first semester at VT (I was very stressed).
Dr. Law is super boring and is hard to tolerate early in the morning. Do not take this class unless you absolutely have to.

I went to all the classs except one.  There is no textbook required, just read his notes that he posts.  During class he will point out one or two questions that will be on the test.  THe final is 50% of your grade, but 85% of the questions are from the old tests which he lets you keep after the test.  He even gives the answers to the old tests.

This class is very hard! The textbook is not required thus making 100% of the test from notes posted on blackboard and lectures. He goes way too in depth. doesnt round your grade. GET KOOFERS! they arent posted online so find someone who had him before. He hasn't changed like 80% of his questions since like 2000. Be careful though hes tricky!

The class was really boring but, then again, the subject matter is really boring. Prof. Law gives you a 5ish minute break in the middle to break it up. He is extremely friendly and helpful if you go to his office hours. However, his class is pretty difficult. Notes are online. I skipped about half the classes and ended with a C+.

Puts all of his "notes" online.  This is no "rocks for jocks" Geology class; it takes a significant amount of time and energy in order to do well on exams one would think would be rather easy (but they're not).
very boring. tests included information not covered in class.
good instructor and the class isn't too hard, he covers exactly what is on the exams during review sessions...the ta's and lab are another story...

Because the class was an 8am, and usually extremely boring, I rarely went.  However, all the information for the tests came from his lecture notes, which he posted online.  From just studying the notes online, I easily got a B.  He believes that the hour and fifteen minutes of class is too long so he takes a break halfway through, which was nice.

So never take an 8am class to begin with...and Law makes class boring no matter what time of day you take him. He tries his best to keep you awake but the material is so boring, not to mention his exams are hard and his final is 50% of your grade as well as on the stuff for the whole year...DONT TAKE HIM, your die of boredom and a bad grade
Absolutely horrible teacher. Extremely boring and the accent makes it worse. The exam questions have nothing to do with what you go over in class. Don't pick him for an 8am
I think his examples for physical geology are terrible... most of them don't make sense
I wasn't really interested in geology but the class wasn't too bad and prof. Law is very helpful.

The class was about the easiest class I have ever taken.  I went to half of the first lecture, and maybe two other lectures all semester and got an A- (I even slept through the third test because he only counts the best two and the final) He posts all the notes online and from studying those, you should know anything you need.
Dr. Law is quite an amusing brit!  Structural geology is quite an intensive class, but you learn alot!  Watch for how he points at everything with his middle finger, its halarious!

I took this class thinking it would be easy.  I went to all the lectures even though they are posted online and even went in for help, studied my ass off and still didn't do to good on the tests.  Some of the questions he puts are things he doesn't even discuss or briefly goes ove.  Also the final i
I have never been so bored in my life, and my father used to talk about the stock market every night at dinner.

What's good is that the exams are ONLY on what was in the presentations, there's a study guide before every exam, a HW that had practice problems, and his TAs held good review sessions. However, I taught EVERYTHING to myself and had to dedicate a lot of time to perform well. He never actually teaches his content and never finishes teaching a unit.

Professor Seylor seems nice, but his class is really rough. Tests cover a huge amount of information, including little things you can easily miss. There are a few easy group assignments and homework that help, but the tests are so point heavy and numerous that it's hard to do well unless you spend a LOT of time preparing and reviewing.

I had him for both genetics and microbiology, and although he seems like he is a sweet guy, he is a hard professor to have. His lectures are very long and hard to stay focused on. His test questions are very specific and easy to miss in his notes. The only way I did okay on the tests was by reading the textbook and taking notes on my own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's the sweetest man and super passionate about microbio but I think he thinks that we come in knowing more than we do. A lot of the material is very specific, and you're expected to have a deep understanding of everything with little explanation provided from the slides. Paying attention to the lectures and watching the review sessions is key.

Very few assignments so tests are kind of heavy. A lot of extra credit points. Weird grading system but I got a higher grade than I thought I would. Professor is VERY boring. Attendance is definitely not mandatory and not helpful. Can do well on the tests without going to class. You definitely need the textbook to succeed though.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seyler is a decent professor, but Genetics is a tough class. He tries to make lectures engaging and genuinely likes the subject. You need to get the textbook asap and start reading it, it is much more helpful than the lecture slides. Each exam had 5 extra credit points built into it and we got 30 extra credit points for a module.
DO NOT TAKE!!!!!! He curves, but not enough! Tests sucked, trick questions on the test!  Grading scale makes NO sense!!!! Nice guy, good guy but dont take if you like your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is nice but unfortunately he is the worst lecturer and I dread going to class. He rambles on about one slide for what seems like an eternity… I don't think he even knows what he's teaching. I only have a decent grade because I teach myself everything… which is so difficult considering his slides are pictures.

Do not take him he is such a horrible professor, he talks so much and never finishes the chapters on time. He didnt even teach us all the topics this year that he was supposed to. He is so boring and rambles so much making it so hard to understand. His note slideshows also are not good.

Not terrible. Lectures are boring but there's iClicker. So many grade boosters (hw with unlimited attempts, group work, extra credit built into every test + extra credit assignment). And he drops 1 test. Teach yourself most of the material, but if you look at lecture slides, watch TA review vid, + read the study guide then test/class aren't hard.

He seems like a very nice guy, but his teaching style is awful; I stopped attending his lectures halfway through the semester and did fine teaching everything to myself. reviews.comment: I loved this class, and I don't like theater. She is a very enthusiastic teacher, and she's very smart. I usually hate reading, but I didn't mind reading these plays because she explains so much of what's confusing in class. You have to go to a play and a musical but they're entertaining. Overall, not a hard class. I loved it.
Show up to class, read plays (short), and you should pass. Doesn't take much time and great to fill CLE. You do have to go to two plays but usually interesting.
If you read the plays and listen in class, it is an easy A. She offers extra credit at the end of the semester, which is also nice.

Professor is very enthusiastic about theatre, and I'm not, so it was pretty amusing at times. I took this class as a joke class and it really wasn't as easy as everyone made it sound. I got a D on the first exam and realized very quickly that I had to go to class and actually STUDY for the exams. Extra credit is offered at end of semester.

This class is extremely interesting and the teacher is nice.  However you do have to study to get an A, its not as easy as everyone says.  As long as you talk to her if you have any problems and behave in her class she is very understanding

I would recommend this course, she's a great teacher. I found the class to be not AS easy as people said this class to be however. I had to study hard for my A. I found her tests to be tricky sometimes. She does give extra credit at the end of the semester though.

Intro to Theatre is an easy A! As long as you read the plays and go to class you'll do just fine. We often watched movies that went along with the plays. There is some extra credit at the end of the course too. Overall she's a great teacher! I definitely reccomend her class.
EZ
Teaching was great!

Teaches a fine class, but very hard to deal with personally!Missed my 1st exam freshman year due to severe illness. I contacted her, no reply. When I was finally better     I happened to go to class when she was going over answers. She was VERY much not understanding at all, mad with  me because now she would have to make a new exam. Got 100 on fin
Amazing professor and a fun class!

an AMAZING class! Its really fun and she's a great professor who loves what she teaches and makes it really interesting! Classes are actually fun and if you go to class you'll do fine on the test. All you have to do is read the plays and go to the 2 plays and go to class. Easy A and definitely a GREAT CLASS!

Like the others said, read the plays and go to class and you should do fine. I absolutely love Susanna! She is fun and energetic and so enthusiastic about theatre. She is always willing to meet/talk with students too--though you shouldn't need to.

She's a really good professor! the class is easy and she makes it enjoyable. all you really have to do is read over the plays and go to class. i know people who tried to just read the plays and ended up doing bad, but if you go she gives you most the answers, i never got below a 96 on the tests and i didnt even finish reading some of the plays
great professor, chill, layed back professor.  She loves what she is teaching.  Just need to go to class and plays and take notes.  Easy A.  Definitely recommended
You must go to class and take notes.  She gives extra credit opportunities...DO IT!!
an easy a, if you go to class and go to the two required plays.  class is pretty boring, just go over the plays you read, but its worth the a.
this clas was really fun and shes a great prof.you can tell she really loves what shes teaching. just go to class or get notes if you miss and see her plays. easy A overall

This class is easy and fun. You really do just need to show up and listen. The plays are easy reads, the exams aren't cumulative, and she'll show movies. She's an awesome professor, very into her subject. You are required to see 2 plays... but if you don't like plays why are you in this class?
One of the most interesting professors I've had.  All you have to do is go to class everyday and you'll be entertained and do well!
Worst, most immature professor I have ever had.

SATCOM - If you pay even a moderate amount of attention, you will come away with a crystal clear understanding of the material. Knows *exactly* how to teach, and how to explain ideas simply and effectively. Sometimes lectures run a bit dry, but you will learn the material to a T. Grades a bit harsh but fair. Extremely reasonable guy, 100% take him

reviews.comment: The actual course material was excellent. How the class was administered left a lot to be desired. About 1/3 of the points for the course are subjective (really subjective). I lost whole letter grades for not including things on my midterm. When I did include them in the final I lost points FOR including them. The same kinds of things go for HW too
he is an ok teacher, but a bit boring. expected a lot from this course, but he did not go into details of everything covered, its more like an introductory class on radar systems.

I took topics in Russian Lit in English with her. Dr. Rutsala is very passionate about the subject and I learned a lot. However, she is an extremely tough grader (the midterm & final were closed-note and essay-based in a Lit class which is almost unheard of.) You also have to attend every class besides 2. Not an easy class at all
She's great, I really liked her and I'm going to have her again and I'm very excited. She came to Latvia with us over the summer and she's just nice and super helpful. Lovely

Undoubtedly the best Russian teacher I have had and disappointed I will not have her for 2114. Excellent help to those who are willing to rise to her level and incredibly forgiving and patient for those starting out.
Prof. Rutsala is super caring and sympathizes with those just starting out in Russian. Super engaging in class and very responsive through emails and office hours.
Engages the class for maximum communication practice. If you are willing to learn and work hard she will definitely help you succeed.
