reviews.comment: Very easy going and caring. Probably the best prof I've had in the ECE department.
Actually the best professor I have taken at VT, I would 100% recommend. Take the class with him he teaches so well and geniunely enjoys teaching. One of the nicest and understanding professors too.

Amazing ECE professor! He always shows up to class well prepared, knows his stuff, is flexible with extensions, very caring, and provide good study guides for exams. Materials was challenging but is fair for what the classes are. Overall, would totally recommend

Dr. Williams is a great professor. Lectures are clear and engaging and very helpful in learning the material. He is always willing to answer questions and explain something in a different way. He also does well in projecting his voice, so he is easy to hear through the whole room. I highly recommend taking a class with Dr. Williams.

Dr. Williams is a fantastic professor. He is able to answer any question asked without ever being condescending, and does a great job at framing information in a way that is understandable, setting you up to succeed in his class. I never write reviews for professors, but he is the first ECE professor to make me WANT to write one.

Ryan Williams is one of the best professors at Virginia Tech. His lectures are crafted to build a ground-up understanding of the material he covers. During online lectures, he answers questions from chat without breaking a stride and without being condescending, something other professors in the ECE department can struggle with.

This class is standardized, so the difficulty is the same across professors, but he is fantastic. Such a nice guy, and he wants all his students to succeed in his course this semester, too, and I am very excited about it!

Professor Hamilton is a great professor. His lectures are clear, though he can move quickly, but he's kind and always answers questions. Grades rely heavily on exams, so doing well on them is beyond important since assignments don't carry much weight. I had to withdraw after struggling with exams, but if you attend class and keep up, you'll pass.

Professor Hamilton genuinely cares for his students and wants everyone who takes his class to succeed. Attendance is not mandatory, but I recommend going because this class gets difficult if you skip the lectures. Class isn't too bad, but it's definitely a step up from ACIS 2115.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Students asked Questions were asked during class...he would repeat them back to the class and when no one answered him she would move on like nothing happened.

Class was like AP stat with some software and a bit denser. Hybrid format was clutch. Class had weekly participation things that felt like a chore but ultimately didn't take too much time. Exams / quizzes were fair, homeworks were annoying but not bad (just don't let them pile up even though that's what everyone myself included did). Boring class.

Easily the worst class / professor I have taken at tech. Ur expected to complete labs using R studio but he never teaches how to use it. His lectures and notes do not make any sense. The only good thing is u can attend virtual or just not go at all. Do not recommend.

His lectures are boring and hard to follow. He assigns a lot of work but it doesn't help you understand the material. He doesn't teach R effectively but expects you to be able to use it. He isn't helpful if you ask questions. The only good things about this class are the zoom option and flexible deadlines.
very nice guy and makes classes very accessible and flexible. can get a decent grade if you commit. (as someone who is bad at statistics)

Class itself was pretty easy - option of online or in-person, assignments were straightforward, grade distribution was reasonable. Main issue is not only are the lectures very boring, but trying to communicate with the professor is annoying. He consistently will reply to quick emails with one word, making what could've been one email into multiple.

Professor Russell had a 50/50 hybrid class where you chose to be in person or online. The teaching wasn't great but it wasn't bad. There was a Canvas quiz for homework every 2 weeks, 2 attempts and it tells you what you got wrong. Things also weren't due until the test so very lenient. Tests were easy and very straightforward. Easy class
pretty mid, does not really teach the material all the well. He has very easy tests and quizzes tho

He's a chill dude but does not explain well. If you took AP stat-you're fine. The nice thing is that class is super flexible: in person, hybrid, or online. There is quizziz participation though. There is coding in R (which I didn't know) but it get's easier overtime. There is homework practice with no explanation, but tests are easy.

This class was a joke and the professor was so rude. I went to office hours to get help with R studio because I am not good with it and he laughed and said I should know how to use it at my age. Im a Political Science major no I don't need to know how to code but okay! The assignments were useless and I gained absolutely nothing from this course.

Recitation in this class is just unnecessary assignments that you'll need the TA's help for. Don't bother going to class in person, just do the zoom option. All exams are online, and the material is not that difficult, but you'll have to teach yourself all of it.

I had hopes for this class at the beginning of the semester but once I made it two weeks in I realized that I was going to have to teach myself everything. The quizzes and tests aren't bad and the recitation is tedious and there isn't much explaining that happens. It feels like he's trying to teach himself while also trying to teaching the class.

To add on to what everyone else is saying; he does not teach. Lectures are bland and everthing that I have learned this semester has been outside of class. R labs are tedious and he does not teach you haw to even set them up. Overall not a great professor, tests and quizzes were not too hard though

He didn't present the material in an understandable way. He wasn't super willing to answer questions or clarify unclear topics. The quizzes and tests don't offer feedback on performance and there's no way of knowing if you just made a wrong calculation or if you really don't understand a topic. I don't feel like I learned much at all.

Like other reviews, he's a nice guy and I felt bad with how little everyone participated in his class, but he's also so boring and is so bad at making the information understandable. Going to class isn't worth it just do the zoom option. Also, the labs are HELL and make no sense and RStudio is the worst with TA's being no help.

He's nice but he has many issues, including that he fails to make class fun/interactive, only teaches stats his way rather than any other perspectives, and his TA that I had for the "lab" portion of the class was not helpful at all. DO NOT TAKE

He's not the best lecturer but if you go to class and ask questions, the material isn't hard. Everything you need is in the lecture notes, the textbook, or his extra resources (which I found helpful). He's also approachable and encourages questions, and tries to make the lectures interactive. If you put in effort the class is not hard at all.

Tried to give this guy the benefit of the doubt after reading his reviews, but it turns out he's actually terrible. Don't bother showing up to class, just do the zoom option. DO NOT BUY MINITAB! Use quizlet to help for assignments. Don't bother asking him questions cuz he won't answer them. He is not good at teaching.

He seemed nice at the start of the semester and I thought all of the previous reviews were spouting nonsense. But as the semester went along, I understood where they were coming from. He doesn't teach and reads off the same slides he tells you to review before class. Seems skeptical a lot of the time. Not helpful/supportive when you reach out.

He seemed chill at first but was very unavailable, especially about using R. He gives take-home tests but scares students silent with false honors code violations if they have problems with them. 

He's not caring at all, but you can get an A if you listen in class and never need help. Shout out to my TA for another class, who helped me pass his.

His notes make no sense and aren't complete, he jumps all over the place during a lecture, and his handwriting is unreadable. The homework and lectures are math/technology-based, but the tests are only conceptual. I've contacted him multiple times and he is not caring or nice. Overall, it seems like he doesn't put much effort into his job.

The class in itself is not horribly difficult, but the online homework is tedious and he DOES NOT TEACH. I get the impression that the majority of the class cheats which is why the averages are so high. Lectures are a total waste of time and his resources are useless.

I'm gonna be so real with you guys, he is a pretty bad professor but he's nice. He seems very unsure of everything he says and doesn't seem to know how to be concise when he speaks. In that same breath, don't be discouraged if he's your only option--if you know how to use Excel and YouTube when you need help, you'll be fine. No extra credit though.

These other ratings seem excessively harsh compared to the experience I had. The class was fairly enjoyable and not difficult; pretty much everything I needed for the homeworks was in the lecture slides and the tests were fair and very similar to the homeworks. During lectures he was relatively upbeat and engaging. Friendly guy as well.
Class is very easy, lectures are decent
Stat 3407 was pretty boring. It wasn't hard though, so long as you pay attention, you can get an A.

Don't understand why everyone's saying that he's so bad. If you just go to class & listen to understand (don't worry too much on notes), then you should do just fine. He gets a bad rap because its hard to make stats not sound monotone. The online homework's and quizzes are a great practice & if you have any questions, he will answer them next class
One of the worst lecturers, but the class is easy to well in as long as you commit to learning using the homework.

did class through the zoom option all semester. reads off powerpoints, didn't actually learn anything from listening to him read so i stopped zoom and read the textbook/taught myself basically. makes you pay for minitab/learn to use it but can't be used on tests/quizzes; know how to excel. tests/quizzes online through canvas which is a sice..meh :/

I enjoyed taking BioStat (3615) with this professor. Tests and quizzes were I thought straightforward, and a lot simpler than high school AP Stats. No curving on tests, final exam, and quizzes. Gives a lot of homework all at once. His lectures are pretty boring and he doesn't really go over how to do things. If you have the choice don't take him. His lectures are dry and never explains how to do problems by hand. Gives 30 minutes for 30 question tests. Pop quiz once a week. He's unapproachable and often very short. I could not emphasize it enough not to take his class.

His lecture is very boring, it is hard to stay awake during his class. His class is an okay class, but he teaches primarily on Minitab, but expects you to do it by hand. This is the most engaging class I have ever had at Virginia Tech. Ryan organized a cheese tasting to demonstrate principles of food safety and and a field trip. A great professor!
Ryan makes the class funny and engaging. Feedback can be slow but he is available during office hours to explain material and homework assignments.

Dr. Calder is a really engaging teacher and seems to genuinely care about student input. I was nervous about my grade during the semester because the material can be dense at times but the evaluations (tests, project) were pretty reasonable.

The class is very broad so we cover a lot of ground, but Dr. Calder is very knowledgeable and makes it easy to retain key points. He clearly cares a lot about student performance and provides many opportunities in class and in office hours to engage with the material.

Ryan is all over the place when describing theories with extensive and confusing homework assignments. The only positive thing about this course is that the final project is broken up in segments throughout the semester which helps a lot.

Amazing Professor! His sense of humor makes lectures go by so quickly! I've heard that people think his tests are really difficult, but the lowest grade I got on one was a 94%. Each lecture was the perfect length and he made even the boring sections interesting. Also helped that he made each topic easy to follow
Loved his class soc 1024
B-o-r-i-n-g and totally full of himself.
Bad teacher. Cocky, arrogant, self-absorbed, power-hungry, belittling of his students and of others. Blech.
I loved this class. Tests are mostly straight out of the notes, and questions from the articles. Awesome Professor. Attendance isn't required, but you definitely benefit from going.

A good class. The tests aren't too easy but he is a good teacher. If you go to class and read everything you can do well on the tests. A lot of questions talk directly about things that he only talked about it class.

Very funny, keeps you interested in what I think is a boring subject. Must be in class because half the test is from the notes. Good thing is class if fun to go to. Great professor, if you take sociology, definantly look for him.
Really funny and interesting guy. Tests are basically right from the lecture notes, so if you go to class, take notes, and study, an A should be no problem.
His class is a lot of fun, i would def recommend takng it! his tests arnt easy though make sure u read the book! overall hes a great teacher!

Definitely take one of his classes... he'll keep you laughing and interested the whole time.  I actually decided to minor in soc because of him.  If you talk to him after class he's a really interesting and nice guy.

this is intro to soc and he is such an entertaining lecturer. i liked going to class, it was fun! his tests were pretty hard though. you have to read and i did but still didnt get great grades. oh well...good prof!

Dr. Saha is a great guy, and most students love him. I did very well in statics, but I feel I was underprepared for dynamics. This may be more of a problem with the curriculum, but definitely study more than you think you need. The exams in this class will be fine if you are prepared and Dr. Saha will prepare you well.

A great teacher AND human being. Every lecture is a joy to be in, as Dr. Saha cracks jokes while teaching. Homework is generally pretty easy until the end of the semester, and exams are more than fair. Although attendance is not required, I would highly recommend going to every one of his lectures, as he explains material eloquently.

I LOVE DR. SAHA!!!!!!!!!! He is a great teacher and really knows what he is talking about. He is funny and keeps lectures interesting. The class is relatively easy, however, there is only one test and the final, both which are worth 30% of your grade each. He gave us a change to get points back on the midterm so it was not bad.
the goat, makes it extremely easy to do well, access to help every day of the week, very test heavy but makes sure you are prepared, homeworks can be a little tricky, very funny personality

Gives us break halfway through class. Cares about the class & our success. Dr. Saha is one of my favorite professors at VT. His lectures are about as interesting as they can be given that the topic was statics (the worst engineering class ever). Was in his statics class fall 2025, he is an incredibly nice professor and very understanding. If you put in the effort for his class you will do great. He always asked us how our days were and lectures were not boring at all. Hes also super short

Truely a one of one professor. He is such a kind soul and really wants to be a great teacher for the students

Practice problems help a lot
