reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Saluga is one of the best professors at Virginia Tech, in my opinion. She is extremely kind, and she is an amazing lecturer. Her notes are fill-in-the-blank; she clearly color codes everything to make it easier to understand, and she makes the tests for the entire department. She fosters a positive classroom attitude. Her score needs to go up!

ORGO is a hard subject to begin, and majority of grade is from exams, which aren't multiple choice. It's something to practice, and she explains things clearly that it becomes easy to understand while practicing. Super accessible throughout the week and wants her students to succeed, would absolutely take her for a class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 85% of the grade is exams and she grades everything pretty hard, I had to go to office hours for 6 separate regrades. Bottom line is for an A/B: the exams are memorization heavy and you need at least 2 weeks of thorough review for exam 1 and 2, and 3 weeks for exam 3. Use TA's for homework checks. Make flashcards. Memorize homework/reaction sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: literally amazing 10/10. i think she had bad ratings from when she first started but she got so good. i was really scared going into orgo because everyone says its very difficult, and you definitely have to put in the work to learning, but every question on the test is something she has gone over before, and the practice tests prepare you so much.

I had Saluga for Ochem1/2. She is kind, her lectures are interesting, but she does have a problem every semester in which she runs out of time to teach before some exams. It leads to her rushing through a chapter of material. Expect many "Gotcha" questions on the tests. Don't expect curves; test averages have been below 65 without change.
class isn't that bad u jus gotta study she makes things decently easy for u

Dr. Saluga is by far the BEST choice for organic chemistry. This is a hard class and you must put in the work but she's always there to help. Unlike any other professor, she has office hours everyday! Her lectures are super engaging and if you have to miss she records every lecture so you'll never be behind! Can't wait to take her again for orgo 2

Had Saluga for OChem 1 and 2, and enjoyed both classes. Lectures move fast, but I think she has the best notes out of all the chem professors. She doesn't curve exams, but I don't believe any professors do for OChem. The class is a lot of work and problem sets are somewhat difficult, but the TAs help you a lot. Utilize office hours for these.

Dr. Saluga is definitely knowledgeable on Organic Chemistry. O-chem is a hard class and if you just show up to the lectures and pay attention you will be fine. The tests are very similar to the practice ones she provides so make sure you look over those before the test. I never used the textbook and still ended with a B+.

OChem is generally considered a challenging course and this class is quite test heavy. However, as someone who isn't great at test taking, this class is more than feasible. She also listened to feedback from previous years of teaching this class, and as a result, many of the problems in her class from previous years have been remedied.

Probably the worst professor I have had at VT so far. Terrible teaching style as she writes notes in lecture for over an hour and just isn't engaging whatsoever. Also doesn't help when majority of the problem sets were harder than exam questions as she doesn't explain how to solve them during class. Better to teach yourself the class or rely on TAs

Worst professor. Would speed through the content in lectures and never give full explanations when asked questions during class. Test averages very low like in 60s range and would not curve. Literally had to retake the class because with a diff professor. Pls save your self and take Dr.Berg. He is so much better and actually gives practice material
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: At first she seemed like a very caring professor however after the first test she would speed through lectures not explaining. Our 2nd and 3rd test averages were a 65 and 62 and she refused to curve. Her tests often seemed like the course work but 10x harder and she would teach important material right before the test.

Dr. Saluga has some of the best lecture notes I've ever seen, making studying for tests not as stressful. The content is very hard and you will need to put in extra effort, but she makes the class so much less scarier. Exams are not curved, but she gives extra credit opportunities and test corrections sometimes. I got a 99%, 81%, and 63% on tests.

She was a very sweet professor and held many office hours however the averages have been in the 60s on tests and she won't curve them. Our second midterm had an average of around 65 and she gave us test corrections worth 8 points however in order to get them u had to get both problems correct. Our 3rd midterm had a 62 averag, she isn't add points.

I had her for 2535 and 2536 and she was great both times. That being said, make sure you study well in advance. O-chem is hard and your grade depends heavily on your midterm grades. She allows you to replace your lowest exam grade if you do better on the final at the end of the semester. Dr. Saluga does her best to make o-chem simple!

Worst professor I've ever had. No matter how much I studied or prepared, the exams felt designed to make you fail. Office hours were useless—she and the TAs were rude, condescending, and made you feel stupid for asking anything. Completely demoralizing experience. At this point I could take the test with studying and still fail.

Your grade in the course is very dependent on your exams. Homeworks are ten points each and fairly easy if you're paying attention to class and attending lectures. It's not the easiest to earn an A in, but it isn't impossible. She is fairly new to VT, but teaches well and students seem to enjoy her teaching style. Saluga > Berg & Santos

Wonderful professor who cares about chemistry and her students. I'd say she is the best non-majors oChem professor, but that's very subjective. The problem sets given aren't sufficient practice for the tests, so you'll need to do extra studying on your own. The tests/final being worth 85% of your grade sucks, but I don't know if she controls that.

She is a great professor and truly cares about her students. If you attend her office hours she helps so much and will make sure that you understand what is going on. I will be taking her again for orgo 2 because she was such a great professor. You need to put in the work for this class by studying but overall it is an enjoyable course due to her.

She did not explain anything besides lewis structures. It felt like she often sped through content and didn't give us enough time to learn it before the exams. Also no exams are dropped/replaced by the final. I would've failed if I didn't go to Bergs office hours.

Dr. Saluga was a great professor for a difficult class. Attendance is mandatory (and for credit), and her exams are difficult but fair. This semester was her first semester teaching at VT and I'm sure she will improve as a professor moving forward. In ochem, you get out what you put in and she sets you up for success if you study hard.

At first, I really enjoyed Saluga. Later in the semester, however, I really started becoming confused in her lecture and everything felt so rushed. The exams also became extremely difficult and nothing helped with exam prep. We barely got review for the last exam as well and had to learn 10 whole new mechanisms. It definitely was a challenge.

Saluga isn't a great professor. She did a poor job teaching the difficult concepts and the homework and exams were always a lot harder than anything she taught. The TA review sucked - half the time they didn't know how to do the questions on the practice exam. Do the problem sets - they'll tank your grade. Don't take her if you have other options.

Dr. Saluga does NOT post her class notes or recordings because she believes less will come to class (despite taking graded attendance). She will tell you to review the TA folder which should contain TA notes, but are often posted late/right before the midterm and contain errors. DON'T skip. Test-prep is 1 prac. exam, old HWs, superficial TA review.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall it's a tough subject but she's a super nice teacher. She's not that prepared and forgets to post the notes before class. She teaches things differently than the TA's, which sometimes makes it confusing. However, her tests are very fair and she gives bonus points.

She was a pretty good teacher but left me feeling wildly unprepared for exams. the only review sessions were with the TAs and they didn't do things her way, so it got very confusing. She has fill-in-the-blank notes which was nice but the info doesn't match up with homework (homework are a step or two above what we learned or whats in the notes).

Dr. Saluga is very good professor for a very hard class. Exams are weighted heavily and the homework is still difficult to still get a good score, but are open note. Exams were easier than expected, but still difficult... STUDY!!! As tough as the class is, she did a great job and explained concepts very well. I will be taking her again for 2536.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Saluga is a very nice lady, and an enthusiastic ochem professor. Her notes were easy to follow along with and class was enjoyable. All semester I thought she was very fair and reasonable, but come the last week before the final, we essentially learned a new, much more difficult unit we were expected to memorize and know completely by the exam.

does not give good feedback, she is always rushing through lectures and never is on time with the course material like the other ochem professor. gives us sheets of reactions to memorize 2 days before exams. Overall, it's all over the place. she also uses highlighters to take her notes!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Caring professor who wants students to do well. Iclicker questions in class every day are counted for attendance. Overall a good professor for a somewhat difficult class would recommend her.

Dr. Saluga is great as long as you put in the work! She is very available to help students and really does care about your learning. Obviously OChem is a notoriously hard class and so you have to expect to put in the work, but if you put in effort it's manageable and interesting.
Doesn't explain

This was my third attempt at the course, having dropped the other times with different instructors over the course of my MIT program. This was my most difficult course in the program, but Dr. Ransbottom made the material as easy as possible for me to finally understand. Be sure to attend the weekly Zoom sessions - he'll gladly help you on the spot!

Dr. Ransbottom is a very inspirational example of what it means to be a Hokie, because he is one! He is readily available outside of class/lectures if you have any questions, and he explains things to you in an easy to understand way. If you want a great professor who will help guide you through learning complex things, then look no further!
Dr. Ransbottom is an excellent professor, though this class doesn't seem to be the best fit for him.

His lectures were very disorganized and mainly talked about his days in the military. Class material wasn't too difficult to understand, that being said we probably only went through half of what was on the syllabus because of the disorganized structure.

EXTREMELY disorganized and a very poor lecturer. Has struggled with grading every semester. Rambles rather than teaches, and we didn't even touch 1/3 of the syllabus. The majority of his students realize his lectures add nothing of value and skip class.

“A poor reflection on VT ECE” is fitting.

Does not reply to emails. Like ever. Like even to infrastructural ones concerning not being able to attend a test due to validated reasons. Would have been a problem, if the class was not this stupidly easy. Biweekly 1-hour long homeworks, easy projects (you could use AI to generate code for project one), take-home online tests.

One of the most disorganized and incompetent professors ever. DO NOT TAKE we did not learn 1/3 of the syllabus. Yes the class is easy, yes you will get a good grade, but it will be an incredible waste of your time and you won't learn anything. I would rate him 0/5 if I could. Truly one of the scourges of the ECE dept DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME WITH HIM

I'm giving Dr. Ransbottom a 2/5 because he's a really nice guy and he obviously knows his stuff. However, his class was an absolute mess. Deviating from course schedule and going on tangents 5was a regular occurrence, he constantly struggled with grading assignments on time/accurately, and we didn't even cover 1/3 of the syllabus.

Constantly lectures what working in the industry is like despite having worked ZERO days in the industry himself. Feels the need to gatekeep our graduation based on his arbitrary, immature, inconsistent decisions. This man takes what should be our most empowering and rewarding experience and ruins it with his ego. A poor reflection on VT ECE

This man really does not give direct answer when replying to email. I asked a simple questions and he talks about professionalism, leadership and all types of stuff. Dont email him. It seems that he just gets very frustrated everytime people email him.

In senior design Dr. Ransbottom can become overly emotional and not specify what he really wants from you. He can then become very frustrated and not be willing to help. In my opinion, he has poor communication skills, and has a bad attitude when students make mistakes.

Dr. Ransbottom is a great professor in a class he really shouldn't be teaching. That's not to say he doesn't know programming: he's pretty dang good at it, but this class is really too much of a joke in its current state for someone with his energy to be teaching it. Take pity on this dude, be engaged, and he'll love you for it.

I don't even remember what the prof looked like bc I never went to class so, it's not necessary for a good grade. I would get someone's number in the class to help with homeworks bc they arent really in the notes. His tests are exactly the practice exams so do them and just remember the answers.

This class was switched to asynchronous right before classes started. I was skeptical at first but it turned out to be great. Optional once a week lecture if you were having trouble which was rarely necessary. He gave tons of practice tests before each exam that pulled from the same question pool. Not hard at all to do well in his class.
Very nice proffesor. Wants his students to do well. Gives lots of chances for students to do well I just found the content not engaging. Little bit of a sleepy voice.

This professor has an incredibly vast and impressive knowledge of materials science. His powerpoint slides and lectures can be bland at times, but his clarity and anecdotes make up for it. Very easy class if you have any semblance of what type of questions will be on exams.

Great guy, he seems uptight at first, but turned out to be one of my favorite professors at Tech so far. He uses a lot of questions from the practice tests he gives, which is the bomb. There are usually two homework assignments a week based on text book questions. While reading isn't mandatory, I highly recommend it (it's my biggest regret).
Great professor. If you do the homework, study the practice tests, and read the textbook, you don't even need to go to class. I felt like I gained a lot from this class.

Take it if you actually enjoy writing, bc its a lot of it. If you love what you're doing the class is amazing. Easy grader, helpful prof, gives lots of insight and personal stories. Will work with groups sometimes. Had a nonfiction, fiction, and big poetry section. Had a little field trip to look at art. Super fun class.

Scallorns is absolutely awesome.  He is incredibly knowledgeable about all things writing and always has insightful feedback to give.  Its basically impossible to fail the class if you do the writings, which compared to most other 2744 courses I've seen, are not extensive.  He also acknowledges that not everyone loves writing which is underrated.

likable as a person, less so as a professor. he can be pretty funny sometimes and weirdly passive aggressive at others. started giving less and less feedback as the semester went on and it was unclear what separated a "good" paper from an "excellent" one. attendance is mandatory, so just show up to class and do the work and it should be an easy A.

Scallorns has the most harsh attendance I've ever seen. 15% of the grade and walking in at 10:10 gets u and 80% for the day. The difference between an A and a B was legit seconds on the minute. Boring lectures with little direction esp for such a high lvl course.

He is kind but his lectures are very boring. It's not his fault the material is just not very interesting which is typical for a low-level required class. He is accommodating - known to extend due dates and offer rewrites. He works one on one with you for draft revisions and seems to genuinely care. But he would post some hw last minute on canvas.

I adore Professor Scallorns. He genuinely cares about his students and fosters their love of written language. I wrote a few magnificent peices with his guidance and he always gave great feedback. The best way to approach his classes is putting real effort into your writing.
Professor Scallorns is very passionate and gives really good feedback to improve your writing. The class is easy as long as you turn in the work on time.

Likeable guy as a person, but frustrating teacher. Creates assignments on canvas that he won't tell you about only for you to get a "0/10" later on because you didn't know about it. So many little assignments that are easy, but a thorn in your side. You get 3 absences and 3 tardies before he deducts your grade; ridiculous for a college class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed attending professor Scallorns' class. He was very kind and respectful of all his students. He learns everyone's name during the first few classes. There is quite a bit of homework, but it is manageable. He's passionate about what he teaches, which makes class more interesting. Attendance is mandatory, but he allows a couple misses

This is a workshop class! You WILL have to show up and work with others. Many people drop this class, not because it is hard, but because there is a lot of writing (which should be expected?) If you enjoy writing, you will love and ace this class. Prof. Scallorns is kind, witty, and a fair grader. If you put in effort, you will get a good grade.
Professor Scallorns is a thoughtful professor. He tries to learn everyone's names (and succeeded in my class!)

Professor Scallorns seems like a great person. He is passionate about bettering his students and is super nice and witty. Attendance is mandatory and if you miss more than 3 classes your grade will begin to drop. It takes a while for him to respond to emails, so go to him in person with issues you're having.

Prof. Scallorns does give interesting work that covers the class guidelines, however, the standards he had and the expectations of time spent working on the class were far too high for a required first level writing course. If you're not an english major, don't take his class, the effort isn't worth it if you aren't super passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: To give him credit, Scallorns is doing his best, but something just isn't quite clicking in his teaching style (at least for me personally). The structure of the writing exercises was confusing and vague, and we would get little to no feedback on everything but the workshop pieces, which had so much feedback it was hard to tackle all at once.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An extraordinarily intelligent and interesting professor

One of the best professors I have ever had. Professor Scallorns gives great feed back and gives you plenty of time to do work. If you fail and do not get assignments turned in thats on you. You always get opportunities to redo stuff

Scallorns is a super harsh grader, easily handing out 60's for rough drafts when we aren't even given an instruction sheet yet; plus, these grades are usually for around 5-10% of our entire grade. This class is all essays, so get ready to write a lot as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Scallorns was extremely flexible this semester and gave many extensions to the entire class for a number of assignments. His class is not easy like other professors but the course content is very interesting and he is very available for help. He really seems to care a lot about his students and wants what is ultimately best for them.

Pretty great guy, super down to earth. Fairly easy going and willing to be flexible. Most of the classes involve reading something and then having a class discussion on it and as long as people participate it's always smooth. He won't give any tests unless your class doesn't participate in discussions.

I really enjoyed creative writing with Scallorns. In class he's got a (good) witty sense of humor, explains concepts lucidly, and sometimes let us out early. In the future I would be happy to have another class with him. To do well, do the assignments and go to class.

I liked him during class, he's not strict and can actually explain the concept of creative writing pretty well. I hated him out of class. He was self righteous and mean, and wouldn't allow for extenuating circumstances, even when already approved by the dean of students. If you know you'll never have to deal with him during office hours, take him.
Scallorns is great. Smart guy, interesting, very clear. He expects good work, but if you put effort into the drafts and see him out of class youll probably do well on the Final Portfolio.

You'll likely get an A if you contribute in class and do the hw. He's just very disorganized: that hurts scheduling, esp. when you don't know what to read/write for what day--you end up doing more work or don't finish it. He's often unclear, but is considerate and flexible to work with, probably b/c he needs us to be flexible with him.
Hard class but worth taking. Great guy, very cynical but it's hilarious!
He was a great professor.  He was helpful and extremely interested in helping students and his work.  Great class to take, and a great professor to learn from!

Scallorns is great! Very down to earth, makes jokes and easily understandable. Journals are due every week which is just an easy response to an essay. Papers don't get graded until the end of the semester with plenty of time for revisement. We got to watch The Sopranos, The Simpsons and even South Park! Take it!!

Scallorns was awesome.  He's a nice guy in general and a decent teacher.  His class is a portfolio class- you do first drafts of his essays but the final draft is not due till the end of the semester.  Required essays were interesting.  We spent two days watching a documentary on Bob Marley, and then Chappelle's show to prepare for one

What a terrible experience with this professor. Probably the most critical grader I have ever seen. Better be on top of your schedule and follow all his orders and demands or he will refuse to accept any of your work.
Perfect. Literally the best I've ever seen in vt
Great professor

Professor Raines is an amazing instructor for MGT 3604. He truly cares about students, brings real-world analytics knowledge, and is flexible and great to work with. The class is challenging for first time analytics learners, but he makes it manageable. He's my favorite professor—great personality and the best.
Amazing professor, really cares about his students
Great guy.
This dude has the most elite ball knowledge. I couldn't compete with him so I dropped the class.

The best professor I have ever had. I could not recommend his class enough. He made me want to come to class and made learning interesting. He cares and knows each student individually. Tests/quizzes were okay; just make sure to study. Truly truly recommend and wish he could teach all of my classes.
He's a nice professor and the class isn't difficult at all. He grades a little hard but the assignments aren't so difficult that it matters.
Good professor

This class was super easy. Raines is incredibly nice and cares a lot about his students. Exams and all assignments are 100 points, so there are plenty of opportunities to improve your grade easily. Raines is an easy grader, and his assignments/exams are not difficult. Lectures are simple and easy to understand; he mostly just follows the textbook.

Dr. Seiler creates an amazing experience for all students in Dendro class and lab. He is so good at relaying information through stories and personal experiences, which helped me memorize tree biology, tree characteristics, and their Latin names. Take him before he goes on his well deserved retirement, he will absolutely be one of your favorites!
Everything he writes on the board will be on the test so if you take notes you won't be missing anything. Not necessary to buy the textbook. Really enjoyed the class!
Great guy. Not a great teacher.

FREC 2324 Dendrology Lab - Dr. Seiler is very knowledgeable and chooses great TAs however this class is very tough. Does not feel like a 1 credit class because you spend 3hr a week in class and lots of time studying. Use the quiz feature on the online textbook, it helps a lot. Not an easy class but passable if you put in the work and ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Seiler is great and his lecture style is very engaging + interesting. Grades are only 3 exams & 4 quizzes. Exams aren't cumulative, but the tree identification (28 to memorize) are so make sure you study as it isn't an easy A. He gives bonus points if you come to class. Class was a bit tedious at times, especially at 9am to learn about trees.

overall very fair professor, he spends almost the entire class on examples since dynamics isnt very formula heavy, which helps a lot as long as youre paying attention. lots of homework but its probably the reason i did so well in his class, the tests are really straightforward and shouldnt be hard if youre keeping up with work/lectures

Homework was a grind but his lectures prepared you for them, tons of example problems meaning tons of notes. The most prepared I've ever been for a final, Study homework's for midterms they explain everything you need to know
Insane amount of HW. Overall good class though. First 2 tests are easy. test 3/4 are twice as hard.

There is an insane amounts of homework with about 2-3 assignments with up to 15 questions on each. We would often have them due over weekends or right before or after breaks. Midterm difficulty is all over the place with some being easier than the lecture/HW while other being significantly harder. He is friendly and gives good feedback on tests.
Won't tell you what will be on the exam, all the exam averages were 50. Average GPA of the class is 2.24 while other professors have 3.8 avoid this guy at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had the displeasure of having. Assigns absurd amounts of homework for no reason. Lectures are not engaging and he posts no resources on canvas. No notes, no practice problems, no practice tests, absolutely nothing to help yourself learn. If you get assigned him for statics, switch out of his class asap.

Dr. Sevak is an insanely knowledgeable professor. He is very direct and straightforward. He provides a lot of homework, I'd say redo them many times. He makes the final exams that were harder than expected. However, pay attention, go to office hours, ask questions, do the homework, and understand why, or you are going to suffer the consequences.

Took him for both dynamics and mechanical vibrations. I can tell you that his classes are challenging, BUT NOT IMPOSSIBLE. I can confidently say that I have learned a lot and retained the info very well. I think he is a good professor if you're willing to try and put in the effort. I never thought I couldn't pass his classes. Go to office hours!!!!

Enjoyed this class.  Sevak is smart, his lectures are very boring though, didn't go to many of them.  Homeworks were a little intense, but I found his tests to be INCREDIBLY straight forward and thus easy, making my life in this class easier compared to others.  Would recommend his section for an easy A.

Lectures are not very engaging, but Tahmasian is knowledgeable and clearly enjoys dynamics. Homeworks are a bit time-consuming, and the lectures alone were not always enough for me. Even though it's not mandatory, get Bolton's textbook and supplement with that!!!!

Lectures are monotone and nap inducing. He does 2 - 3 example problems over a 75 minute class period, while going at a snail's pace. He assigns multiple large homework assignments every week, including midterm weeks. He does not teach all the material before assigning homework problems and do not count on the online textbook for any help.
Tests are pretty hard, but pretty similar to homework and practice tests. Definitely one of the hardest classes I've ever taken.

Sevak is an amazing teacher, but gives really difficult tests. His lectures are very helpful and he is really good at explaining the content. He gives quite a bit of homework, and his tests are pretty hard. He usually won't curve, and if he does it's so the average reaches around a C. If you really put in the work then it shouldn't be that bad.

Most of the other reviews are still valid. He really does care about his students doing well and will help you in office hours, although he won't just give you the answer. My only gripe is that his voice can get soft at times, so just down a coffee beforehand and you'll be fine. Aside from that, he's a fantastic prof and I'd definitely recommend!

Sevak is a very good teacher. He is fairly soft-spoken but you can tell he enjoys teaching and cares a lot about the class. Test questions were always easier than homework questions. Tests are 5 questions on paper with a 2 hour limit. For homework, Sevak uses WILEY plus, which gives no partial credit, and the questions are needlessly complex.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He gets a bad rap for no reason. Genuinely so sweet. His lectures are a bit boring but super informative - you don't need to study any material outside of his lectures if you pay attention enough. Super helpful office hours, lots of homework but tests are very comparable to the hw so it's worth putting in the effort. LOVE HIM

Dynamics is a very hard class. In class, he just uses the projector to write down notes and do example problems. His homework problems are also time consuming because he uses pictures from the textbook and changes the pictures by using softwares and therefore creating his own questions. Midterms are slightly easier than the homeworks. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Its a hard class you have to put your time into it. GTA office hours better than his. Would take another teacher

I had an excellent experience with Prof. Tahmasian. Most of the exam questions were recycled homework / classwork questions, so if you practice, you'll do well. This class's homework is time-consuming, but if you do not cheat and actually practice, you will do well. A lot of engineers coasted through high school, but it simply does not work here.

I thought his lectures were very informative, but very boring. It's hard to stay focussed the whole time, but extremely benificial if you do. He gives lots of examples in class and gives good partial credit on tests. This course requiers a lot of time for studying & doing homework, so be ready for that. Tests get increasingly more difficult.

Overall difficult class but Sevak teaches it pretty well. The units are clear cut and he provides example problems in class. The homeworks are usually very challenging and will take up a lot of your time. The tests are difficult as well but he gives a lot of partial credit as long as you put in some effort on the problem.

Caring professor who wants his students to pass. Solves problems in class and posts notes after every lecture. Assigns a lot of HW which are harder than exams. Sometimes extends Homework which is nice. Go to office hours he's very helpful! 4 midterms and a final, and he sometimes curves. Drops 2 HWs at the end and his grading scale is different.

Sevak is a chill and friendly guy. He does problems in class that are similar to tests. There are two 8-9 online homework problems on Wiley plus per week. Tests can be confusing, which is normal for any statics class. He curves tests to around 73. He grades pretty fast if he is not busy.

Sevak's teaching style is come to class, do the notes, and spend quite the time on homework. Even though he always says people call him boring who cares!! He prepares us well for the tests, answers questions well in class, helps a lot in office hours and is really nice. Have fun spending hours on wiley plus ;P.

Not the most entertaining, but Sevak is a good guy and a good teacher. He really knows what he's talking about and hes work is precise and easy to follow. He does proofs and practice problems in class and often gives you some of the homework answers for free. He gives fair partial credit for tests and is fast at grading.

Do not expect to understand any of the material. Dynamics is a hard class to teach, all Sevak did was derive formulas and rush through problems on blanks sheets of paper. No format to the lectures, and roundabout ways of answering questions. Test were way harder than homework's and in-class problems and almost always curveball questions.
Statics is a hard class in general, if you're not physics based... good luck. I cry at night, it is quite haunting.

If you take him for dynamics be prepared to learn from the textbook and youtube. He just derives formulas in class expects you to memories them then speeds through a problem so ur stuck just copying to keep up. Impossible to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'm giving Tasmanian the benefit of the doubt because dynamics is very tough course to teach; however, his class did not cut it for me. He teaches by projecting problems and walking through them, but I found this to not be helpful. He assigns a lot of HW, and I found his exams to be a lot harder than the HW and worked through class problems.

When I took this class it was an absolute mess, I got through statics and even deforms with a lot less trouble than Dr. Tahmasian's dynamics class. Our test grades were so bad that the grading had to be changed mid semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Tahmasian is really great. If you dont understand the material, go to his office hours and he will work with you until you get it. Homework is difficult but the tests are always easier than homework so they prepare you well. And he always posts the class notes on canvas

His Majesty, the King. He cares about his students A LOT and wants us to learn well. He "will push homework back" and make the last week super busy (so we should work ahead). Statics is a breeze; deform is a gale. 26+1 HWs, 15%. Missing a HW isn't a big deal, but doing and reviewing HW helps a lot learn the material. Aced the midterms and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You will work in this class. A lot. His accent can also be a bit difficult to get used to and he has FOUR midterms. If anything describes the class in a nutshell, that's it. Thing is, he's actually very caring about his students; he will look at how busy you are during the week and will push homework back if other classes are busy during that week.

He teaches from a document camera: "Professor, the camera's too bright and we can't see what you're writing down, can you please change the brightness?" "No." Most of your learning should come from intuition and knowledge from previous classes, not from actually learning stuff in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sevak is a very good professor in my opinion. At first he may seem a little reserved, and his accent may turn some people off. After having him for a semester I really like him because of his office hours. He will spend the time with you until you figure out a problem. His accent is nothing to be concerned about, and he's a genuinely nice person.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved this professor. Lectures were fun & interactive, & you get to know people. That said it was a hard course for me. There's a lot of material & I felt he moved too quickly through really difficult topics. Quizzes & tests are not bad the study guide he gives out is basically the same. Not hard exactly, but I felt it was really time consuming.

Fantastic Professor, he even gives out Italian cookies sometimes! I have taken him for three Italian classes, and his grading is very clear. He makes quizlets, practice exams, and a review Kahoot before every test. Also, he answers questions clearly and respectfully. I never felt scared to ask a question in class.

Literally the best ever. I love taking Italian with him and I can't wait to continue. Classes are relatively the same and I suggest reviewing every night for a few minutes because there is a lot of material. Never any curveballs, and is always willing to help you out when you are struggling.
I love this man with my whole soul. He's actually so amazing and thoughtful. He's literally my goat I love him

Great professor and such a nice guy! His class is genuinely so enjoyable. I feel like I have learned a lot without it feeling like a lot of work. There is homework 2-3 days a week, but it is not too difficult and usually takes only 20-30 minutes to complete. You have to buy the online textbook in order to do the homework. Great class overall!
Super fun class. Makes learning Italian fun and not hard at all. He's also a super nice guy. def take his class loved it this semester.

He's a great guy overall and also a good teacher. His teaching style feels laid-back; however, you feel like you get things done and learn Italian, not just memorize and regurgitate. Overall, he's a 10/10 teacher. The only downside is that the VHL is a money grab, but it's not that bad. If you want to learn Italian, take his class.

Honestly a great teacher but he did move a too fast sometimes which was frustrating. You can earn 2% for your next quiz by correcting your past one. At the end we had to have a convo with another student for 5 to 7 minutes all in Italian which was super stressful but it's in his office. Graded a little harsh for spelling but not bad if you study.

Dr. Sguerri made the class easy, and didn't only speak in Italian. Textbook was pricy, but you have to get it for assignments. He was understanding if I couldn't make it to class, and was very laid back. Not a tough grader. You can redo quizzes for extra credit on the next.
He makes Italian easy to learn, and doesn't only speak in Italian.

Professor Sguerri is an amazing teacher and shows that he loves teaching. He is always engaged with all students and makes sure that the material for the class is clear. He loves to joke and make everyone feel comfortable. He is 10/10 professor, and I would recommend him to anyone who is interested in pursuing Italian as a language.

An amazing teacher - Good natured, very organized and methodical, building on what you already have learned as he introduces new concepts. Lots of class participation, balanced with written exercises and games.  Class is almost entirely in Italian from Day 1, with enough English thrown in so that you understand what is going on.  A fun class.

I loved Michele's class. He made me want to show up to class. With him, Italian is fun. He's super patient, makes the material understandable, and has our success in mind. It's hard to do well if you don't show up to class because speaking and group work is how you learn a language. Highly recommend Michele.

Michele is the most loved professor I have encountered at Tech. He is funny, kind, helpful, & a great teacher. He provides plenty of materials to help you, including many helpful handouts and worksheets. The text & hmwk are accessible bc they are online. Overall class that makes Italian fun. Takes work but youll get an A if you study & do the hmwk
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Michele's the man! He cares for students and is always accessible. He said he learned his  teaching approach from one of his profs at North Carolina, he even took 4 classes with that guy. Don't know what this "new approach" actually is about, all I can say is Michele rocks, I learned so much in just one semester, I can't wait to take more classes!

Dr. Shewchuk himself only appears on the first day of lab to introduce himself, but he's a nice guy. The lab itself was one of the most fun courses I have ever taken, no doubt. You should use this lab as an opportunity to meet other people in MechE and make friends. Just print the lab manual and show up, and you'll get an A.
Bro is really thicc

4214 Lean manufacturing - I would recommend it. It was a boring at times, but his lectures are very clear & detailed. He explains everything very well and he genuinely cares if his students understand the content or not. Office hours are super helpful. Homework is not too difficult. 6 HW, ~17 lectures, 2 tests. The final is not cumulative.

I never interacted with the professor for this lab. The course is taught by instructors that worked in the field for years. It's a very cool class! The lab manual was written by the professor and it is very informative. Make sure you read the manual before the lab and stay on top of the few reports. Also, talk to the TA if you grade questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: ISE 2214 is very fun and useless class for ME students. Dr. Shewchuk does not care if you are failing the class. The class is 100% hands-on. Try to have fun and make some friends. One of the things I struggled with is turning assignments on time. He will not extend the deadline.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easy A I received. Class was also okay.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is new, but she makes sure to reach out to everyone in class and ensure that no one is left behind. Well prepared with many slides and visual materials. The table talk was really enjoyable. Recommended!
She's nice and helpful. I learned a lot from the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She really cares about her students, and it shows! I would take the class again just because of how easy she made it for us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I'm taking her class this semester, you can see she is trying really hard to make concepts easier for us. No unnecessary assignments, or take home quizzes, she has high expectations from us. But class is pretty chill....
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He doesn't respect our time to prepare meaningful lectures.

The only good thing about this course is its fancy name, which includes "Information Technology"..... but don't except to learn any tech stuff. The class materials are surprisingly obsolete and unhelpful.

I honestly didn't learn anything from this class. This class is not beneficial for your knowledge, nor your skills, nor your career. A lot of busy work (e.g. presentations) was just meaningless. I do regret wasting my time and tuition fees to take this class. It's simply never worth it.
Doesn't give the best background for the course. Makes the students work on projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He's unaccessible. Doesn't hold office hours.
great professor, very fun
his tests were meant to trick you. got Bs and Cs on his tests but an A on the final because he didn't make it. was very rude during office hours. thought he was quirky and relatable

Genuinely cares ab the learning of his students and makes math so much less intimidating than it acc is! Lectures are at slower pace, so it's easy for everyone to follow along--engaging too! Also, idk if ur ND, but u may find his teaching style to be incredibly up ur alley lol! he also makes material/snotes sup accessible if u miss class. He rocks!

Professor Silber was one of my best math teachers as a student. He teaches slowly, asks the class for doubts, and is accessible during office hours. Despite all this, I had to put in much effort and re-learn most materials outside class. Still, I recommend this professor for any math class you must take.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Silber is a great teacher and really cares about his students understanding the material. He has a lot of office hours available and they are really helpful if you are confused. I only took precalc in high school and was worried about the jump from that to business calc but it ended up being totally fine.
Great Professor overall. Does work slowly, but has MAJOR availability for Office Hours, and lends a hand when someone needs it.

While this class may be difficult, Professor Silber is very nice! He also has a lot of office hours so he is very accessible outside of the classroom. In addition, going to the recitations is also hugely beneficial.

Dr. Silber is a nice guy. However, his lectures are boring and can definitely get slow, becoming hard to pay attention to. I often had to re-teach the lessons to myself outside of class. The one good thing is he does offer partial credit on exams which does help your grade. Overall, he is definitely not a bad professor, but not outstanding either.

Silber is a very good professor that goes slow in his lecture and answers all the questions u might have in class. This is his first semester teaching business calc, and he's very good at it, although many people in business calc doesn't respect him when he's a very good teacher and have many office hours to help people. This says sum about people.

Silber was a nice professor. His lectures move pretty slow though and I was often bored because they weren't very engaging either. He clearly cares about his students. Tests are fine as long as you do a little bit of practice. Homeworks typically take the longest regarding assignments for this class. Definitely set aside time to do them.
He's a really sweet dude, gives great dad energy. He takes lessons slow and makes sure everyone is on the same page (which I appreciate). 10/10 math teacher

As far as math teachers go at Tech, he's a really great one. Super understanding and really eager to help you understand the material. Only negative is his tests can be really difficult, but besides that he's a great great person.
He can be too slow sometimes that you get confused.

Mr. Silber is very thorough in his conveyance of the material. He does a great job of explaining concepts and giving examples. If you prefer a slower-paced lecture style, he is the best option for you.

As far as VT math professors go, he's 100% better than average. Lectures can be super slow though, making it hard to stay focused. Takes long pauses in between when he is explaining things. Also pretty friendly with students and reminds me of a HS teacher rather than a professor.

I had him twice and he's great! He goes slow in his lectures which can be annoying sometimes but he makes sure you have at least some sort of understanding of the class. He is super accessible and loves to help his students succeed, if you put in the work that is. He will assign in class work and go around and check in on everyone and help out.

Silber goes through new concepts slowly which made them easy to grasp. He isn't very good at responding to emails but he helps if you go to office hours. He really cares about students' ability to grasp topics and gives a good balance of help & freedom to think it through yourself when you are confused on topics. Overall I would recommend his class

He is very boring and not a great teacher, the class is nothing to look forward to. Asking questions feels like a burden on the class, makes you feel like you are behind, and doesn't give the feedback you need. Overall it is not the end of the world to get him, but do try finding a different class if you have time.
Absolutely a great guy and professor. Failed this class first semester and he always has time to help. Highley reccomend taking him. The GOAT

Mr. Silber is the sweetest most caring professor. Definitely one of my favorite professors ever. His grades consist of ALEKS, Homework, and Tests. He lets the class know that you can submit homework late twice during the semester and receive full credit. Tests are straightforward. He is so helpful during and outside of class. Very nice guy
Awesome Professor! Very helpful about course material and understanding of the online format.
Great guy and cares about his students. He is super helpful in office hours.

One of my favorite professors solely for how much he cares for his students, both their grades and their well-being. He has office hours every day and is extremely helpful, he'll even let you sit in his office and just color if you need a break. He is a lenient grader and occasionally curves tests, but reminds you that your grade doesn't define you
Dr. Sierra is so nice and so caring! If you have to take Spanish take it with her. She's a very fair grader and as long as you participate in class and actually care, you should be fine.

She really cares, and wants you to understand course material. She is creative in class assignments, but her historical lectures can be dry. She can be scattered in her teaching method, which makes class hard to follow at times. She also doesn't give students much time to discuss questions in groups, either. She's an easy grader, though.

I love Dr. Sierra!!! She is such a wonderful person, as well as an excellent professor. If you are confused about something, she is very patient and makes sure you get it. She genuinely cares about students, and her class is a very fun, comfortable environment; she explains grammar concepts well. Her class is always the highlight of my day!
Going to her outside class hours is your best friend. She is always there to help and was always there for me whenever I had issues in class as well as in real life.

The best Spanish professor I had at Virginia Tech. Plays tons of games in class and creates a very comfortable environment for students to get better at spanish. Is very easy to talk to and get feedback on any assignments and really wants all students to improve their spanish. Participation in class is a must but she makes it very easy.

Dr. Sierra is an engaging Spanish teacher who requires extensive class participation and and language immersion. She speaks almost exclusively in Spanish and expects students to do the same. She also assigns more homework than is typical in a Spanish grammar course, all of which is a plus for comprehension. She is also a mega-slammin' blonde.

She is a good professor, but requires a ton of preparation and participation. She is young and enthusiastic so I would expect things to improve as her standards and expectations become more realistic.
Great teacher, gives lots of chances to do well, quizzes about every two weeks or so, and you're allowed to re-take the big ones if you mess up
Gives students second chances on bad homework assignments, a lot of in-class games and PARTICIPATION is a must!  Very nice and helpful!

Simmerman is very laid back and flexible with late work and absences. The lectures are light and simple, and he welcomes questions without judgment. As long as you show up and show effort, combined with the amount of extra credit, this class should be an easy A.
A great and very enthusiastic professor that is engaged during his lessons. Only downside is that he doesn't ever read his emails or answer them.

I like Professor Simmerman very much. He is a very interesting person who cares about students a lot. He is very tolerant of students and always likes students to interact with him. He is also a good listener and you can talk to him about anything you like about Japanese culture.

Simmerman is a great great teacher. Super fun & makes it really easy to pick things up. He knows what he's talking about. Workload is laughably low but that's also just how Japanese is at VT. He also cares so so much abt his students, if you have problems then you can work them out w/ him and he's super reasonable abt it all & wants you to succeed.
Dr Simonetti is the best!! Genuinely cares about his students and is sometimes a bit goofy. Tests are very fair and overall a great prof.
Simonetti is an extremely good teacher. He is a pro at putting the knowledge in his head into the heads of students.
Simonetti is everything you can ask for in a professor and more. The way the class is operated is the perfect introduction to physics and one of the best classes I have ever taken.

A very out-going professor and always happy to help his students. His lectures are fun and exciting. The homework is clearly mapped out and it is the same for every week so they're easy to follow (reading quiz, mastering, problem set). Plenty of office hours done either by himself or the TAs and they're always useful when I'm having trouble.

While Dr. Simonetti doesn't teach PHYS 1155 as it is a lab course taught by TAs. The TAs that he appointed to teach to the class were phenomenal. They were nice, easy to ask questions to, and tried their very best to make sure everyone understood the content. The lab isn't difficult by any means because it's all graded on completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Simonetti has a great class! His lectures are all really good, he encourages communication between peers during class discussions and is enthusiastic. I can definitely recommend his class.

Dr. Simonetti is another gem in the physics department. His PHYS 2305/6 courses are for physics majors only, but he is also a great professor in astronomy classes. He's a very nice, caring, and respectful professor and can chat with you about anything from physics to baseball. Definitely a reason to be a physics major or to take his astronomy class

He is very nice and cares for his students. If you talk with him and keep him updated on how you feel in the class he will do everything to help you. He is very interested in what he teaches which makes class a lot of fun.

One of VT's best instructors, IMO.  Astrophysics isn't easy, but he presents everything in a very clear and comprehensible way and uses lots of diagrams and such.  His homeworks can be tricky, but they will more than prepare you for the tests, which are pretty easy and are often multiple choice.  I always looked forward to Simonetti's class.

This man is brilliant but has a sense of humor that you can't let get to you. If you think like he does he's a funny guy though. Good thing is you most likely do think like him if you have him since he teaches astrophysics and physics seminar.
Good professor-  gives LOTS of information each lecture, but presents it in a clear, understandable way, and it very good at explaining concepts.  And what a cutie!

Simundza was a really great professor! He seems passionate about the content he teaches and wants students to succeed. While this course is test heavy, Professor Simundza guides you through the content and gives you lots of practice problems.

Professor Simundza is a great guy who makes the class as easy as possible for his students. He does a good job teaching concepts and makes sure everyone in class understands the concepts before he moves on. He is a really fair grader and a great professor.

Extremely passionate when teaching and nice! Quiz HW problems he goes over were very helpful for the exams, but attendance isn't mandatory. Exam layout changed after first exam for it's now scantron & paper. This is a very heavy self learning class.

Amazing professor. Simundza really does care about people's grade and he's always very considerate and polite towards his students. He's also humorous imo even though a lot of people are just on their phones. Also, honestly, you don't need to go to class for this course. You could just learn things on the homework system and textbook.

Professor Simundza is very understanding and kind. He cares deeply about statistics and wants all of his students to succeed. He will answer any kind of question and although the class is sometimes fast he is always willing to slow down and re-explain a concept. I am taking one of his classes again next semester and I am looking forward to it.

Professor Simundza is very approachable and understanding. He is very passionate about statistics and  is always happy to answer any kind of question. Although the class is a bit fast at times, he is always happy to slow down and re explain a concept if you need it. I am taking his class again next semester and I am looking forward to it.
He was such a good teacher, if you go to class you'll learn easily. The tests makeup a majority of your grade but are online and he gives so much time. Made the class so easy to get through.

Professor Simundza is so caring and passionate about OSM, makes the material very applicable to the real world. Test heavy class, but open notes/textbook/excel. If you learn how to solve the problems by going to class and taking those notes you'll do just fine!

You could tell he was actually passionate about what he was teaching and always goes the extra mile to make sure students understand the material. Very detailed and descriptive lectures, homework accurately reflects the tests and although the material isnt easy he made it very understandable.

Professor Simundza is truly an amazing dude. Exams are never unreasonable as are the rest of the assignments. If you show up, ask questions, and pay attention to lectures this class is absolutely passable and enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've taken Simundza for multiple classes now he's one of the best in the BIT department, he's helpful and his exams are fairly straightforward.

I had a 60% on the first test, but got a 100% on the next. The grading makes it possible to do well. I attended every office hour and studied the quiz results/went over them with him to prepare for the tests. Often I would struggle with something and he never made me feel bad, he would explain it as many times as I needed. Great guy!

He seems to really understand the material but not how to present it well. Boring lectures every class, but attendance is not mandatory or necessary if you read the slideshows. Homework is long with online certifications and quizzes. Tests are semi-difficult but you have two attempts on all 3 except for the final. Very nice guy overall.

I found his lectures hard to follow. He spoke like he was giving a seminar to a panel of trained professionals rather than college students. I felt like I was expected to already know the things he was teaching. Bad handwriting. He did really seem to care about feedback and probably was pretty good to students who found the content interesting.

If you aren't a good and fast math test taker, this is not the professor for you. His exam questions are long and as someone who is not the fastest equation solver, the time limit made succeeding in this class difficult. I ended up getting by with a B, but I owe that more to lucky guessing on the questions I didn't get to more than anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hes an amazing professor.

Class was ok, has lectures from an online semester posted to the course site which are very good, so you don't really need to go to class.The online homework/testing system "Hawkes" is pretty bad though. The homeworks on there are unnecessarily long, repetitive and annoying. Tests were 65% of the grade. No group work.
I just didn't like this class but Simundza is cool. Lecture after lecture though, gets boring. Attendance isn't mandatory but it helps if you have the attention span lol
You can tell he knows the material, but he does not know how to teach it to the students. His lectures do not help and the certifications take forever to do.
Professor Simundza was great! I had him for both BIT 2405 and 2406. 2406 was much easier and not completely online-based. He gives great lectures, highly reccommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class isn't an easy A.His boring lectures combined with a therapeutic voice WILL put you to sleep if you have trouble following b/w powerpoints. USE THE TEXTBOOK and recommended practice problems. Most quiz/test questions come from those. While I did teach myself this course using the textbook, he did care about his students. do practice tests

A nice, caring professor who is clearly invested in what he teaches. However, the course itself is quite difficult. The certification homework is meant to prepare you for the quiz questions, but the quiz questions tend to be very different than what we actually practice. Go to office hours and ask him for help. You'll probably need it.

Great professor that respects his students. Always answers questions in a helpful way and doesn't treat any question like a dumb question. Tests and quizzes are all online using a lockdown browser. Attendance isn't mandatory, but helpful, and you can learn some of the material just using the online platform used for quizzes.
overall a good teacher but some of the test questions were pretty hard. If you go to class and do all the work you should be fine. Average on tests tend to be low but he allows multiple attempts.
Hes a really nice professor and you can tell he really cares about you and your grade
He is a great professor - he reads explains everything really well and does anything in his power to make sure you understand. Lectures can be boring though.

My favorite professor I've ever had. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. I totally recommend him for any class you can get! I'm kind of surprised I didn't get an A, but your grade is only made up of your two midterms, the final, and your quizzes. 10/10 recommend!!
Simundza makes the class easy. Just pay attention and go with the flow. He gives a lot of questions that are easy free points too, and drops a bunch of quizzes.

Prof. Simundza is easily one of my favorites. He's pretty laid back and is always available to help students who ask questions, and his lectures are pretty thorough. I stopped going to class around mid-semester but can still achieve an A just by watching the online lectures and problem-solving videos.

Prof. Dan is a great professor because he's not boring during lectures. He also offers tons of office hour opportunities during the week for extra help. Definitely would recommend going to these because not a lot of people do and its basically like free tutoring and how I learned the most.

Great guy. He really cares about his students and is very helpful in his office hours. He rides around campus on a bike so you may see him there too. Make sure you study. The material can be confusing, but with enough effort you should be fine.

He cares very deeply about his students and expects students to have questions that he is more than happy to answer. The important thing for his class is to stay on top of the material, if not ahead so that you can ask as many questions as possible. His office hours are very helpful so go to them!!!

I can't say enough about Simundza. He's a fantastic professor, by far the best I've had at Virginia Tech. He really pushes for you to succeed, and genuinely cares about his students. If you have the chance to take him, do it. He remade the entire course because he didn't like the Hawkes system, and it helped so much. Take him.

I had this COVID semester and I never really watched his videos or went to office hours. If you can understand what you learn during certifications and check over his recommended practice problems this class shouldn't be too much of a problem. Gets a good bit harder towards the end though. I like how the class is set up.

I did not enjoy my class with Simundza. I have nothing against him as a person; when I did show up to class I think he was very respectful and a decent lecturer. (The class is basically online, you don't have to go in). But BE WARNED that his quizzes are NOTHING like the online material you learn. He makes the class harder than it needs to be.
Pop quizzes and quizzes everywhere, lowkenuinely gave me ptsd.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Slade is an excellent teacher. He pushes his students to learn and understand topics. if you have no desire to learn, the class will be very difficult. The only con I have is there are some lengthy assignments, and the quizzes are tough. He is a nice guy and wants to see you succeed.

Very chill and professional. Bad reviews are exaggerating: 3 pop quizzes (2 were take-home), probably only 10/115 students dropped, generous grader (accepts "stretch" answers), papers 1 p on average, tests super fair, EC on tests. 2354 already teaches 1/3 of 4115. Super easy final, IMO (median: 81). Hints at possible test questions during lectures!

Took class in 2023, first time he's taught since 2021. As a teacher he's great, as someone who understands his students not amazing but not awful. Pop quizzes happen so study more than the day before an exam, he will tell you to study 2 hours a day the week before I did 3 days and passed fine. Quizlets are a godsend since he has no study material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Harshly graded and rarely ever gave points back even when deserved. Gave consistent papers about 4 pages long with 0.5-inch margins. Admitting to making this the hardest class he has ever taught to "prepare people for the MCAT". Need to study at least 2-3 hours a day just to get a passing grade, let alone a good grade.

Absolutely my favorite professor I have ever had, if you take the time to engage he will give the same energy back. Always open to questions and very straightforward about expectations. This class is hard but if you follow the advice to review often, actually care about the material, and ask questions when you have them you will succeed.

Dr. Slade cares deeply for each of his students. He takes the time to get to know you and will remember your name. His tests and quizzes are fair, everything you are tested or quizzed on are from the lecture slides. This class is difficult, but if you study and go to class, you will do well.

Probably the worst professor I have ever had at Virginia Tech. Holds the risk of pop quizzes over you to scare people, 30% of class dropped out, tests extremely hard with around 40 question short answer. Absolutely crazy class with extremely challenging quizzes and expects you to do further research for some questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Slade is the best professor I have ever had during my time at Tech. He cares deeply about the material he teaches, and for the students in his class. Show up, ask questions, and he might just become a mentor to you.

Best math teacher I've ever had. Really nice guy, cares a lot about his students and how well they do. His lectures are amazing; he explains things well and likes class participation. The CTF for this class is notorious. The average on the final is a 50%. However his classes do better. My class had an average of 79%. Little homework, all textbook.
Hard class, fantastic teacher
Great prof.

He is soo great!!!!!!! I am a sophomore at tech now and I have not had a teacher who cares as much as he did about me being successful in the course (or let alone knowing my name). His office hours are very helpful.
He's good. Really likes math. Makes things interesting. Funny. Once or twice a semester he will have a lecture that just blows your mind.  Office hours are helpful. His class is not easy.
She was a great teacher.  I thought she did a tremendous job and after taking her class I wanted to be a geologist!  The class was fair, the lab was a little challenging, overall a good experience.

She expects you to know more than she teaches, and she assumes that everyone in the class wants to be a geologist one day. We had to do a lot of worksheets that hardly made any sense, and a lot of group work that was a complete waste of time. The tests were really difficult as well. I wish I would've dropped the class when I had the chance.

She assumed that everyone wanted to be a geologist. The lessons were vague and on an introductory level, but the tests expected you to know much more. A lot of her assignments were inane and she was not very helpful when I e-mailed her with questions. I was not impressed. I should have dropped the class and stuck with chemistry.

I took the ONLINE INTRO TO PHYSICAL GEOLOGY course thinking it would be an easy class considering it is online and an INTRODUCTORY level course; however, I could not have been more wrong.  As someone mentioned prior to this comment, she is basically assuming everyone is an aspiring geologist.  The quizzes are pretty much straight off Google

Attendance is mandatory for her. Clicker points are partly your life. You miss one day and your grade will go down more than you think. Lectures are boring. She can be helpful if you go to her office hours. Tests are HARD and you will need to write a lot and study the book. Do not waste your time, pick another teacher.

She treats this class as if every single student is a geology major. 99% of the class is taking this as an easy science class, but she thinks this class is much harder than Chem or Bio. I took Chem 1035 and Biol 1115 and am doing 10x better in Geology. Many unnecessary homework assignments, but the tests are start off of the review sheets.

she's sweet old lady, but man that class sucks. This is not like high school world history, this class is about ancient europe and asia. The tests a super specific with a lot of short answers. If you get a short answer wrong you can usually bs her and get some credit back. If there are other pathways open take them instead.

Incredible. She loves her job and she makes it obvious to students. She's passionate and open to discussion. Make sure you show up so you can get participation points and thats about it. Tests are open notes and online. If you're looking for an elective that's interesting and not too hard, I recommend this class.
Very kind and respectful, but wouldn't know vocal inflection if she fell over it. Lectures are informative but boring. They do prepare you for the tests, but at what cost?
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had her for Conflict and Security in East Asia. Her lectures decently reflect the test material and readings. She is very friendly and well-versed on the material. Tests are online and at-home, and though a bit over-specific at times are not an overwhelming percent of your grade. If you show up to class you can do well without reading the textbook.

Very nice lady who wants everyone in the class to do well. A lot of the homework was reading along with the textbook but wasn't completely necessary because her lectures were straight out of the reading. Tests were open note and open book. Very easy class to get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

easy class, recommend
never prepared, NEVER EVER take

Awesome professor, nice dude. Random attendance quizzes through TopHat once a week. Food Cart project can be debilitating to your grade and sanity if you get stuck with a crappy group: work ahead and try to join people you know if possible. Very few grades but is usually generous with grading: show that you care and you'll get the grade you need.

reviews.comment: Fantastic teacher for foundations of business. has a lot of great real world experience
I loved him! He made class interesting and was always available at office hours. His pop quizzes were a little hard, but you just have to read the Morning Brew.
