reviews.comment: Professor Skripak is by far the best professor I have ever had. Foundations of Business was such a useful class and I definitely learned a lot through him. The thing that sticks out about him the most is his diligence to being fair. He will always clearly tell you what he expects, and when he expects it, there are never any curve balls with him.

Great professor if you do all the reading and show interest in the subject. 3 tests in total, read all textbook chapters right before the test and you should be fine. Free responses are pretty random and one of them on the first test wasn't covered in class (read the book). Attendance will either give u extra credit or deduct points from the test!

Professor Skripak is the man! He does such a fantastic job of keeping the class interactive by having discussion with students! He has worked for so many huge companies, so it's great to have a professor who can give real world examples that he has actually experienced. He's extremely personable, and he clearly teaches strictly because he loves it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Skripak is the best teacher I have had a VT so far. He is great at helping students understand complex business terms and ideas. He makes the class fun and interactive. He really cares about the students and won't move on until you understand. Always available and communicates well. Truly the best professor I have ever had in my life.

-Have to go to class or pts deducted from grade -tests are easy if you know the vocab -don't wait until the last minute for the lemonade project!!! -not always clear about when assignments are due. ALWAYS check scholar -very enjoyable class, well respected professor with a lot of connections and knowledge about the business world, get to know him!
Great teacher, excellent corporate background.  You can tell he has really been out in the business world, not just in academia!

Great class! He makes it really easy and is helpful outside of class as well. He will sit and talk to you about careers or help you with your resume. I hear he is harder in other classes but he is a such a nice guy!

You have 2 big papers to write which are most of the grade. Most of the work can be done outside class, go anyway. I found too much of the work to be pushed to the end of the semester. The reflection journals are about 30 pages each. Easy A IF you clearly put effort into your writing and read each of the 4-5 books. Lots of writing but graded easily
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This is a very demanding class. you have to read 4 novels and write two papers on them, both 25+ pages. Takes up so much of my time, but Skinner is a very nice professor who cares about her students, the class is just a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She evaluates students in her own way. Her daily courses are relaxing. She always arranges group chats in class. It is very hard to get a high score in her course. She really paid much attention on grammar problems in your papers.
watch movies all the time

she is awesome. If you work hard you will surely get a good grade. She gives you a lot of room between assignments. She has these peer review things that help a lot. She also brings candies every class. She is really nice and always apprecitate everyone's opinions. Just need to work hard. I would recommend her.:)

Awsome teacher. Very willing to help you.  She gives you a lot of room in terms of assignments.  Makes the classroom environment tight-nit, which makes it easy to ask questions and voice opinions.  She also brings candy if you have her during lunchtime.  Big plus.
The professor is really nice. My first English class in VT was not that bad. If you work hard, you will end up with good grade from this class.
cool class

He cannot be understood, his accent is way too thick.  My advice is get the homework guide and study how to do the homework and always go to class.  Attendance was extra credit, I never studied, did horrible on tests, always came to class and ended up with an A-, you can get through this...

His Polish accent makes him a bit difficult to understand at first, but he's not nearly as bad as people say.  It's helpful to have some background in physics beforehand, but not necessary as long as you do the homework and the reading.  The tests are always curved and come straight from the homework.  If you just put in the work, you'll do fine.
Can't understand him, doesn't explain thouroughly
horrendus
Horrible.
Not as bad a teacher say he is...  If you know basic physics and just need a review, I wouldn't hesitate signing up for his class.  If you need to be taught physics, do not take his class.
Terrible professor. You can NOT understand a thing he says.

Ok, let me be perfectly clear. I had to take this class as a Poli Sci Major for the Navy. However, even still, I barely passed this guys class because of the fact that he is utterly incompetent. He cannot teach well in class and is very hard to understand because he is very quiet and has a very thick accent. Take anyone but this guy.

He's hard to understand because of his accent. He requires that you go to class which I don't think is right. And his tests are relatively hard, although it may be because physics is just a hard subject. He does attempt to help his students though. He holds help sessions once a week and uses a lot of email communication.
Best techer ever! I wish he tought more classes, what a swell man.

Worst teacher I have EVER had the EXTREME displeasure of having.  Cannot understand a word he says through his thick eastern European accent.  He teaches this introductory level physics class as if he's refreshing a grad students memory rather than teaching someone for the first time.  He is more concerned about his students knowing and following h

This guy may be very knowledgeable in physics but thats not exactly what a teachers job is. A teachers job is to help convey information to students and do it in a clear and understanding method. Slawny does not do this. He races thru material and is very disorganized while teaching.  We as students should not have to go to him every week to learn

He is a very good professor if you put forth effort. See too many are afraid to go to him outside of class but he is very very helpful. Get over the accent and learn to listen better. You go in with a bad attitude you get a bad grade. He is a very good professor so dont fear his class.
As the other comments say, his accent is terrible, english lessons would make quite a difference. He seems to be knowledgable, but he can not communicate it well.

He's very helpful outside of class, but in class his teaching leaves something to be desired.  His grading curve is odd, but takes the class average from failing to a C.  I think he's a great guy and a good teacher, but you have to work with him and ask outside of class as well.

He has a heavy polish accent which makes his teaching very hard to understand.  He moves faster than neccesary in the class, never explaining the material and just does examples in class and demonstrations.  Horrible teacher that needs to consider taking english lessons.

The all time worst teacher award goes to Slawny. Fortunate for me I found another teacher to switch to. I had two classes with him and dropped. The tragedy of life is not that it ends so soon, but that you might end up with Slawny.
If you get him for phys drop the class and take it next semester.
I have never had a worse professor.

Slawny has to grade on a T-curve in order to have any students pass at all. He often assigns homework that is either not yet or never covered in class. Sometimes the information he gives us is conflicting, sometimes it's completely useless and never even shows up on homework. His tests are hard and the homework often impossible. Avoid if possible!

Ok Mr. Green Smiley (from below)...we know that is you Slawny....good old Slawn-dog with the jokes

worst teacher i have ever hard(highschool included) teaching a challenging subject and doing an absolutely awful job at it. I learn more from the one fifty minute class with the TA's then the two hours fourty  minutes i spend with Slawn-dog. Basically, avoid him at all costs

Unfortunately no one is lying (except the green smiley).  This guy was so bad that after the second day I dropped the class.  On the second day, he stopped class and yelled at me for having my feet on the chair in front of me, and then proceeded to make fun of another student.  Try to avoid him at all costs.

i really enjoy physics but slawny is by far the worst teacher i have ever had.  he is lazy, doesn't speak english worth a crap, and makes his tests way to difficult.  the T curve helps a whole lot though
Cant ****ing understand him.

By far, Slawny is the worst teacher I have ever had. If at all possible, get into another professor's class. Here's how I aced the class despite his failure as a professor: 1) Don't bother going to class. Only go if you know there's going to be a quiz. 2) Read the textbook. You'll get much more out of an hour of studying than a week of his useless lectures. 3) Keep up on the homework, it prepares you well for the class. 4) When he turns his back, make funny faces and mock his unitelligible accent.

It's sad to see so many ignorant comments. It's  obvious to me that those who filled out the survey were the kids in school who said "tell me what you are going to ask on the exam" and stolled into class in a pair of flip flops with a bottle of coke and bag of chips. Get a clue.
Simply Awful... I would suggest having everyone in the class pay $100 each to bribe him to go back to Poland.
worst class at tech
If you can skip his class to study the material with a friend then do it. He does have mildly humorous mannerisms and a funny accent, just remember to take a pillow to the lecture hall.
He is retarded.  If you can do anything to not take his class, do it.
Worst professor I have ever had.  He once did a problem on the board for an hour, got to the end, erased it all, apologized and left.
The worst professer I've ever had. 'Nuff said.

don't go to class

WORST TEACHER EVER! Take this class over the summer, or get a 5 on AP phys C to get out of this class. Slawny is by far the worst teacher I have ever had. Going to class is useless. You cant understand the man through his accent. Get the solutions manual and learn the homework problems and you should be ok.

Slawny is horrible. Can't understand anything he says and going to class is a waste. I say get more sleep. Just get the solution's manual to do well on homework and actually go to class when he says there will be a quiz and you'll be fine. Also, the labs are 15% of the grade, so that helps.

If you get this teacher, one word: RUN! This guy is not a bad guy he is just simply a bad teacher, his performance at his job his highly incompetent.  You can barely understands what he says. Chris is by far the most impactful professor Iv'e had. This man is so intelligent, funny and just cares about his students and our learning. I truly could not recommend him enough! Ive taken 4 classes with Chris, 1 of which I didn't receive credit for, I just wanted to learn from him. In my opinion he is the best professor in the PSCI department!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chris is a hilarious and caring professor. He gives great movie recommendations, and leads engaging classes (discussion based). Super easy to speak to and approach about your course work, and he manages to be relatable. He's also *extremely* intelligent, but it does not come off in a pretentious way whatsoever; this class was a delight to take.

Highly recommend taking a class with Chris. Most of his classes run as a socratic seminar. Participation is not mandatory, but encouraged. I am usually not a fan of socratic seminars, but love the way his class is taught. It makes such complex topics easy to understand. I definitely recommend taking at least one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was by far the best course I have taken at Virginia Tech. Attendance is not mandatory but you do yourself an injustice by not attending. Chris is extreme intelligent and makes complex topics into simple terms. My writing has also improved because of his comments. Chris will make you think, I would recommend this class to anyone.

One of the greatest professors I have had the pleasure of learning from at Virginia Tech. You could miss almost every class and still pass, but you would be missing out. He is incredibly passionate about his students and can make even the most difficult readings easy to process. If you have the chance to take a course he is teaching, take it.

Really nice guy, However his classes are heavily based on only lecture content. Textbooks can be hard to find and the test averages are in the 50s-60s. But he is actually very smart, little room for partial credit .

One of the best professors at VT. Way more knowledgeable than any of the PhD professors at the school. Tests are difficult but they are open note and his lecture slides are the most informative I've seen so far.

The best professor at Virginia Tech. He is one of the most knowledgeable professors at the school and one of the most helpful. The class is difficult and the tests are hard but the actual content of the class is very informative. He knows much more about the construction world than any of the PhD professors and actually has real-world experience.

Professor Smith has a ton of industry knowledge and experience that he tries to convey to his class. His tests are very difficult with low averages so homework and other assignments are key to keeping your grade up. Attend every lecture and make yourself known in his class by participating and the class will be very manageable.

Mr. Smith is one of the most knowledgeable professors I have had at Tech. He has a ton of industry knowledge and experience and tries to prepare his students for the industry the best he can. His test are difficult and the averages are very low but if you come to class and get your work done, it is easy to make up for. Attendance is key.

One of the worst professors I have had, test averages were in the 50s, not very accessible outside of class. He read his lectures off of a PowerPoint slide. The tests are much harder than the homework. The material itself was relatively easy he just made it harder than it needed to be. Avoid this guy if you can.

A lot of folks give him a hard time, but he genuinely cares about students. He holds students accountable and to a high standard. If you put forth effort, he will see it and help you as much as he can. He's a phenomenal professor as long as you're willing to work.

Worst professor I've had at Tech. Can be helpful in office hours but is bad in lectures. Just reads off of powerpoint slides and can't convey information well. His tests are hard, just online Canvas quizzes with no partial credit at all. Class averages were failing for both midterms and he didn't curve or accept any feedback. Avoid at all costs.

Terrible, awful, not good things. This class is extremely hard and you are expected to know things not taught in the lectures. The tests are overly complicated and the wording is sometimes horrible. All I have to say is good luck?

Smith is an okay professor. Come to class and do the work and you'll be okay. Tests are pretty difficult, but do your best and you'll pass the class. He is always open to how he can improve and is knowledgeable about the field. Ask questions in class and you will be fine.

The worst professor I have ever had in CEM. The class subjects aren't meant to be hard but he makes them the hardest things possible. Boring lectures, no partial credit, doesn't help during office hours, and takes everything seriously. He takes attendance and participation seriously but it's hard to talk in his class when he is so disrespectful

Arguably one of the worst professor I've ever had to deal with in my entire college career. He takes attendance very seriously but just reads off slides. His homework isn't too hard, just takes a lot of time because he provides useless information to mislead you. His exams are the worst of it, no partial credit, very difficult. Do not pick him.

Attendance and participation go in as a grade at the end of the semester. He also has random in-class assignments. He takes weeks to grade homework and exams but does not post solution keys so you wont know why you lost points unless you go to office hours. Exams are brutal, class average was a 65% and he does not round for any assignment.
Tests are hard without reason, also doesn't know how to read.

HW exponentially increased as the semester went on, all assignments were graded very late, despite strict deadlines. You are not allowed to ask questions within 24 hours of a due date, and he does not seem to want students to succeed. He refused to tell us whether the final was cumulative or not, and would not give any guidance of what to study.

He is very specific when it comes to grammar. Also most lectures are not helpful and irrelevant to the course. I wish I had looked him up before because I dread going to class. He is really harsh on grading. I would not take his class if you were expecting a good grade.

I took both Freshman English and Literature and Ecology with him. He's a great guy with some interesting views--very liberal and laid back! Just do the work, and actually try; he grades on improvement. If you actually take the time to get to know him, he'll be one of the easiest and nicest professors you'll ever have.

He was such an awesome teacher! I learned so much. If you actually pay attention to him, you'll learn so much. It may be difficult if you don't put any effort into improving your writing, but once you do, you'll see great changes. I recommend it.

Very eccentric, interesting guy. I think a lot of people had problems with getting good grades but if you just follow what he tells you to do you will most certainly get an A. He told us to go on a "nature walk" for an hour, just do it, it makes it easier to write about something you actually experienced. Interesting books, very interesting guy.

Grades essays hard and essay topics pretty challenging essays. But he is really nice and talking to him during his office hours will help. You will need to work extra hard to get the good grades on the essays. He's a nice guy and I liked his class a lot.

if you want an A or even a B, dont take his class. unless you are willing to spend 10 hours on each essay. lot of reading and writing. he is an interesting guy but as the semester progresses you cannot help but sleep through his never ending lectures about the world coming to an end or robots taking over us.

He makes you read a lot and write a lot for the journals. I wrote really long journals and i still received a B- on all of them even though I increased each journal entry by 5 pages. He is a very hard grader and gives you the same grade you got on your first essay even if you try to improve and use his suggested techniques. Don't take this class!
Biggest college regret ever, hardest essay grader ever, tried dropping it...but he's an overall interesting guy

Michael is the man! Lit & Eco isn't necessarily easy, but he gives most everyone an A. The readings are always interesting, and he says about ten profound things a class. It's the only class I do work for; I love it; and he's so intelligent.

His political and social views are way out there, but his advice on editing is excellent.  If you follow his methods, you will end up with a really good paper.  He is a hard grader, but since your final grade is based on improvement, it is not too hard to get a B.  I don't know of anyone who got higher than a C on the first paper, however, some who
He introduced himself the first day of class, "My name is Michael Smith. I am a communist and a feminist."

Do not take this class, it ruined English for me. Our units were technology (and how because of it we are the dumbest generation) and robots. He talks all class about nothing. He also has really weird requirements for essays, such as 8 short sentences, dashes, parenthesis, etc. I dread going to this class.

Decent class in terms of reading but every class was awkward discussion with Professor Smith rambling and everyone would just zone out. It was hard to contribute due to this. Maybe if this class was a online class or met less, it would have been more productive.  In short, it opened my mind to many new things but the way it was presented was lame.

never stops talking.  i saw no point in coming to class. Too boring. Three essays and all about technology, which annoyed me.  I heard he was biased with his grading.  He would take attendance randomly.  Also too many rules for essays (colons, dashes and whatnots!)

A devout liberal.  By far the worst prof. that has ever walked the face of the earth.  His grading is biased.  Classes and content are boring.  He -->preaches<-- about the environment, the media, and how it all affects us in a terrible way.  This guy is out of touch with reality.  Don't take this class...You will regret doing so.
boring teacher, grades hard, badddd

He definitely did not teach me ANYTHING about writing. The whole class period he would go on in a rant about the environment, and then at then end of the class, he'd be like, your draft of your essay is due next class, any questions? Do not take this class. It doesn't matter your political views because he does NOT teach.

Yes, he's a bona fide hippie. But how that negatively affects people's opinion of his teaching ability is beyond me.  Most people who post negatively will do so just because they are biased, liberal-hating conservatives. Mr. Smith is the first English teacher to actually teach me something about writing, instead of just raping my papers.
An interesting person

If you hate America and civilization go right ahead.  He is the most liberal person I've ever seen.  All he talks about is how humans are destroying the world and how evil America is.  He also is outspoken on his views of religion (he hates it).  Avoid this hippie.

very veyr liberal, preaches every class and pays so little attention to what you do that by then end of the semester 50% of the class wont show up and hes pretty much wont accept anything unless its his point of view. dont take him under any circumstance
great guy....smart....nice....one of the best teachers ive ever had....lax on due dates.....is not a petty person....never raised his voice once....very calm
n/a

Environmental nut: he’ll try to win you over, but his primary goal is improving your editing skills. I was skeptical, but he really is a great editor.  Didn’t make us do the grammar gym. Grading system is a bit ambiguous, but as long as you improve you’ll get an A or B. Class is entertaining.

I love English & he made me want to never go near the subject again. His Freshman English wasnt English but his own environmental ethics soapbox. He teaches a deplorable, unprofessional writing style. If you have no respect for the english language, take his class. Otherwise keep your distance.

Prof. Smits is a very helpful and supportive professor, especially during office hours where he takes the time to explain concepts clearly. The course is fast-paced, so you cover a lot of material in a short amount of time, which keeps things engaging.

Prof. Smits is a very helpful and supportive professor, especially during office hours where he takes the time to explain concepts clearly. The course is fast paced, so you cover a lot of material in a short amount of time, which keeps things engaging.

Prof. Smits is a great professor during office hours. Since the class in itself is fast paced, there is a lot to cover in a short span which can lead to being left behind. His homework's are difficult, more difficult than the tests.

Timothy is a great person, but his classes are challenging. The first exam can feel difficult, and that's okay. While he is a tough grader, you will come away with a strong understanding of the material often more so than in other classes. I recommend taking advantage of office hours as much as possible. He genuinely wants students to succeed.
His tests had me questioning reality. He does not fully prepare you with his classwork at all.

The subject is not easy to understand but he did a good job explaining everything. The class went fast but he always asks if anyone has questions and will break things down even if they are concepts we already learned.

All the linear algebra students had an average of around 70% on the CTE. His class averaged an 85%. He's definitely the best option for linear algebra at Virginia Tech, but you definitely need to put in the work and lock in during class time. If you truly want to, you can definitely learn a ton from this guy, as he cares a lot about linear algebra.

Timothy is a great person, his classes are really hard though. Your first test will not go well and that is ok (i got a 74 on the first one). While he is a tough grader, you will learn the material better than some other classes will. I suggest going to all lectures as well as going to as many of the office hours. He is there to help you.
His tests are hard (very theory based) and our class averages were usually 60 or less. Don't let that discourage you, he is a good professor and curves grades at the end of the semester.

Professor Smits is a really nice and kind person. His teaching style is very difficult, and his exams are theory heavy, however this forces you to actually gain a deep understanding of the subject. This class doesn't reward memorization.

this review is honest and completely unbiased. He is a fine teacher, but his lectures are difficult to follow. The biggest thing was doing work outside of class and not just aing the homework. if you do the homework and fully understand what your doing on them Youll do fine. very generous curve at the end of sem bc of low exam grades.

Professor Smits is a nice person but as a professor I would choose literally any professor over him, he teaches faster than an average human can comprehend information and he does not curve the grades even though the averages on all the exams are like 50 to 60. Taking his class is like intentionally ruining your GPA, do not take him for any course.

I took him last semester and am only reviewing to be a D1 hater. I 100% believe this man is botting his 5 star reviews because there aint no way anyone thinks he's a good teacher. I'm sure he's a good person, but he just can't teach for his life. Never take him, take literally anybody else.

He fails to explain abstract concepts in a digestible manner, to the point where my friends and I were memorizing variables and processes with no concept of why. Additionally, grading is harsh, with the first two tests having class averages of low 50s. People I know with other professors and the same course have significantly easier exams.

Smits is supportive and communicative and nice, but lectures focus on calculation while unnecessarily hard exams heavily test theory. He tends to skip "elementary" steps when doing problems in a lecture. He always pauses for questions but most people don't know what to ask. Averages on the exams are in the 50s with no curve.

I agree that 80% of our grade being 4 tests is dumb but that is not up to Smits. Overall this is a tough class and he handles it well. His lectures are always helpful and he will answer any question at his office hours (“Is this answer correct?). To be fair, he is new to teaching and acts somewhat prepubescent but he's bound to outgrow that soon.

His class was HORRIBLE. He teaches at 100 mph, teaches the course like an advanced proofs of linear algebra course and does not do well with teaching. His exam averages were low 40s and told me he grades based off "vibes", first withdrawal of my undergrad career. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS WAIT FOR ANOTHER PROFESSOR IT WILL SCREW UP UR GPA!

Poor guy is worried about being let go of again and decided to rattle off 5.0 reviews like clockwork. Let it be known that teaching a class where 2/3 of the class drops (if you don't believe me, just check the grade distribution) does not make him a perfect professor to "learn math the right way", it just makes him very esoteric at best.
He is one of the best teachers at Tech. His teaching is very understanding I don't know why people complain so much.
This guy is literally rating himself
Definitely a hard class but he teaches the lectures very well and does care about his students such as grades on a curve at the end of the semester.
Smits may be tough but he is very great at teaching and good to understand
Hard class but teaches very well
This guy does not teach well, 80% of your grade are tests where the average is below a  60%. You will fail this class based on the teacher. Take it with someone else.

He teaches on a blackboard and has bad handwriting, so it's difficult to understand what he writes. The first test class average was a 58. He is a nice person but not a good teacher. If you want to pass linear algebra and not be overwhelmed with the material don't take it with him. We just took an exam and the avg was a 56 while all other professors' classes had avg 70-80s, if that isn't telling I don't know what is.

This was one of the worst classes I've taken. The professor assigns extremely long and time-consuming homework. Exams were unfair to the point that we thought that he was choosing the hardest questions on purpose. We recently did the test and the class avg was a 56. He still had the courage to say that we did better than his last semester class.

You want a good grade? don't take him. he had terrible averages for every exam. He said that he would curve our grade by how well we did on the final over other professor's classes, which is odd, and we barely got a big curve on the final grades. I don't even go here anymore and I had to come back and leave a review because this prof keeps botting 5 star reviews. He isn't a very bad person, just immature, doesn't teach well, and very, very stubborn.

Timberwolf is a decent person, bad professor
Timberland could really be a decent professor if he just listened to student feedback and would slow down so that we could understand his lectures.

Timtam could be a decent professor if he let go of his ego. He teaches far faster than any student could be able to comprehend, gives ridiculously difficult tests, has homework that is completely irrelevant to the content taught in class, and doesn't listen well to constructive criticism.

reviews.comment: Dearest Mother, the winter chills my bones deeply; supplies dwindle, spirits weaken. Before Heaven calls, let me voice my earnest curse upon Timothy Smits—a man whose cruel mathematics hath sapped my strength and dimmed life's flame. May he endure lectures eternal, colder than this harshest winter's eve.

There once was a professor named Smits,
Whose class we all didn't quit.
With too much faith, we overlooked the drop date
Now Timothy's homework gives me AIDS
Now my grades fall like an endless rain.
His speeds through the content with no remorse like A-Train 

If you're reading this, and have him in your Hokie SPA
Listen closely, and drop his ahh.

At this point he could have basically given us the Cambodian constitution and asked us to explain its impact on the Jamaican rum industry and we would've had more of an idea of what was going on than whatever he put on this test

I can't imagine someone could finish his hell hard test in such a short time.He assume we know everything before like god. I even begin to doubt that if I'm still capable as a math major student after met him.

The review saying that he's the best professor in VT definitely had to be written by him. It says they finished with an A+ but the highest grade in the class is around a C. This guy is so sad he has to write himself positive reviews.

reviews.comment: Horrible. Just horrible. If hes on your schedule, DROP immediately and switch sections.

Honestly, I like the guy's attitude, but damn is he hard to follow. The lectures are very quick, which can be helped with office hours and outside practice, but that's not the main issue. Review below me is cap
the best professor I had in vt.

I don't know much about Mr. Smits personally, but I do know that when students ask questions, he views it as some type of personal challenge, which hurts his big teacher ego. There is a reason that over half the people in the class dropped it today, March 3rd, 2025, because of the drop by date. If you get him, you are better off taking this class online or switching professors IMMEDIATELY, don't get stuck with him after the first week of classes. He seems fine during the first week, but you are screwing yourself over!!!

EXTREMELY difficult class. Assigns quizzes on top of homeworks with 20+ parts, all of which have harsh grading. The exams are humanly impossible to finish in time and have a failing average. He clearly knows linear and is accessible, but the lightning fast pace of lectures is so frustrating. I did very well in calc 2 here but am lost in this class

reviews.comment: This is EASILY the worst professor I have ever had. He teaches a concept a single time and expects the students to answer questions loaded with nuance and theory. Weekly HWs are EXTREMELY difficult/ time consuming, and are next to impossible without outside assistance. Our class average on this last test was a 57. Please never take this professor.

A lot of the reviews here already tell you but yeah he's awful. I don't know what to say. Lectures aren't that great, Hws ESPECIALLY Hws I have no idea how he expects us to solve these problems with the lectures we have. None of them look like something we learned. AND THE TEST. The first test average was 57. Just don't take him.
His class average for his tests was 57. This says something. DON'T TAKE HIM.

Professor gives very difficult exams, highest score in our class for Exam 1 was a 62/100, and the class average was a 54/100. These are ridiculously low numbers, and indicative of the difficulty of Timothy's lectures.

He SPEEDS through the notes as if we are all math majors. He has a little bit of an attitude when you ask him questions, but he answers them. His homeworks are HARD...SUPER HARD. I had to spin the block and write another review because of his horrible this guy teaches

reviews.comment:
Blood with only an A antigen is type A, blood with only the B antigen is called type B, blood that contains both is called type AB, and blood with neither is called type O. At a given blood bank, assume 35% of donors have type A blood, 10% type B, 5% type AB, and 50% are type O.

100% would shoot themselves if they had to take this guy again

I speak 5 languages and still could not comprehend what Dr. Smits was yappin about. Instead of inheriting favorable genes he inherited mathematical autism. His HWs need to be solved in such a convoluted and arcane manner that you feel like you're summoning a biblical demon. I scored a 60 on last year's Putnam and only got an A-. Absolute joke.

I believe he made it harder than he had to. Explained the concepts in a very complicated way. Weekly homeworks took hours and were very difficult. Graded them very harshly. No other 1225 professors had homework that hard. Office hours did help and I recommend watching youtube videos to understand the concepts!

VT's math department is notoriously particular and 1225 is certainly a weed-out class, so I don't entirely blame Smits for the class being difficult. He isn't a terrible teacher, but I found his homeworks to be unnecessarily difficult and unhelpful. His handwriting also wasn't always the best.
I don't like him. That's all I can say

He wants you to fail. If you're doing linear or 1226 next semester then he might be your teacher and you're better off switching. Don't take this guy even if you have only one class slot open for that course. Credits are much better imo

Professor is so good that I'm failing the class. He helped me so much, I'm so thankful for everything. He is honestly the best teacher I've had in my life. I'd rather die than do his class again. He teaches us like I'm god and he wants me to inhale the knowledge he is teaching me. I'm gonna apply for being god next semester so I can understand him

This guy is actually awful. I've never seen a professor worse than him. Never take his class please, I asked him to help me with problems I have in class but he never does. He talks faster than flash running. Never gives extra credit but other professors do. He grades horribly and wants you to fail. Please run from him.

Mr. Smits was a good teacher, but I did struggle in his class. I think that it was mostly because the class is hard in general, but going to his office hours really helped. I would take his class again because I really liked the way he taught. We did a lot of problems on the board and then did problems by ourselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty much here to reinforce what everyone else has already said. Homeworks feel like he's trying to get us to prove new branches of math using concepts that "we should already know", and he's in love with his chalkboard. Smits only teaches from overexplaining concepts on a chalk board which is just not how I learn.

Professor Smits teaches both inefficiently and very quickly, and he often leaves students feeling confused. He responds to questions in a snarky manner and offers little guidance. Without homework, students would be lost. Though intelligent, his harsh grading and dismissive approach make it difficult for freshman-level students to learn.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! If you have to be behind in curriculum to wait and get a different professor I would highly suggest that. INSANE homework, you will not be able to rely on that to bring your grade up. Prof is definitely smart and good at math but extremely questionable teaching skills and ridiculously rigorous grader.

Teaches you like you're going to be a math major (which no one in the class is a math major). He gives the hardest written assignments that are worth 15% of your grade and none of the questions are even remotely close to what's on the test. Overall, not a good teacher. Going to office hours is the only recommendation I have.

HE GIVES THE HARDEST WRITTEN TESTS. EVERYONE ELSE GETS 2-3 EASY QUESTIONS PER WRITTEN ASSIGNMENT AND HE GIVES 6 - 8 QUESTIONS WITH 6 PARTS EACH. ALL HARD QUESTIONS AND HE IS A TOUGH GRADER. DROP THE CLASS IF U WANT TO PASS 1225.

Dr. Soledad is amazing! You can tell she genuinely cares about her students and their success. She is super accessible if for some reason you can't turn in an assignment, and gracious with extra time to do so. As long as you and your team do all of the required work, you should have no problem getting an A. =)

Professor Soledad is very nice! Most of the time we were allowed to leave class early if we were done with work. The class and TAs were chill and as long as you turn in your assignments you should be fine.

Attendance is required, but she is lenient with excuses and gives many excused absences before any sort of grade punishment. Suuuuuuper chill grading and not a ton of work outside of a few projects. Go to class, do the assignments, and get an A super easy.
Very understanding professor, had no problem getting extensions for extenuating circumstances.

Prof. Soledad was a great professor, attendance may be required but she is very flexible giving you up to 13 minutes after the start of class to arrive with no penalty. The only thing I thought was annoying was the amount of work I had to do. It felt like sometimes we did the same assignment multiple times. Overall great professor would take again.
Honestly, she was a great professor. She will work with you to make sure you succeed in her class.

Soledad is a very kind soul who is willing to help you with anything and enjoys making personal bonds with her students.

ENGE 1215 is entirely group project-based, so if you end up with a team that doesn't pull its weight, you will be miserable. I knew some people had that problem.

The TA who graded my work was rather inconsistent, but YMMV.

I loved Mrs. Soledad so much that I am taking her class again next semester. She was incredible helpful when I was struggling with MatLab and was always willing to give me an extension. You can tell she really cares and she gives a templet for every assignment. Compared to my roommates teacher, her class is easy.

I could not ask for a better first semester ENGE-1215 professor than Professor Soledad.  Although the homework was slightly overwhelming at some times, it was usually not too bad.  She (and the TAs) left good feedback for assignments, and if you are assigned a group that you work well with, this class is a breeze.
She is an amazing professor and I would suggest to take her class for 1215! It's a very easy course and she is super accessible outside of class.
Prof. Soledad is probably the best professor ENGE 1215/1216. She's an easy grader and has fun projects.

She if very lenient and understanding when it comes to assignments. If you take this course with her, be sure to participate since there is many group assignments and primarily group base. The coding portion can get a bit difficult to understand, but she and the instructional team are very easy to reach out of class.

Professor Soledad is very caring towards her students. She dedicates extra time and energy to helping those in need. She also makes an effort to get to know her students on a personal level, creating a comfortable relationship. Her class is very easy as long as you participate and do the work.

Pretty easy class as long as you do the work. The professor is very sweet and caring she always starts conversations with students and if you finish your work before class ends, most of the time you will and you can leave early.

Prof Soledad is very caring and energetic in class. 1215 is centered around group projects so a lot depends on the members of the group but she will work out problems when they come up. There are many small assignments around larger group projects but most work is done in class. The work isn't very difficult but can be time consuming.

Sophia is the kindest human ever. If you are taking poetry, this is the teacher to take it with. She creates such a bond with all the students in her class. No hardcore assignments except an essay for the final, but she gives you an A as long as it's done. Such an inspiration and remarkable role model to young writers.

Sophia is an AMAZING professor! She started the semester by saying that everyone will get an A, which is always nice. No homework other than at the end of the semester where you do a final project. She cares so deeply for her students and it really shows. She is very understanding and funny. TAKE HER!!

Sophia is super kind and cares so much about her students. She is super friendly and easy to talk to about any questions or concerns in the course. She also gives really thoughtful feedback on pieces and makes great and creative suggestions for revisions and editing. Best teacher I had all semester, highly recommend!

Sophia is so caring and loves what she teaches. Even if you don't like writing, she makes the class enjoyable for everyone. As long as you write something, you get an A, and her feedback is so sweet and thoughtful. Some reading at the beginning but not much. You have to do one workshop, but it isn't that bad. 10/10 teacher
She has mental problems

She is very passionate about making sure you know the subject and will answer/do any problems you come to her with during OH. I will say that she is aggressively passionate sometimes with making sure you know the material, and that can come off as harsh. Her tests aren't weighed a ton and are heavily based on HWs and in class problems. Fair overall

Definitely the better option for 2206. Clearly cares about the material, lectures are good but boring. Has more assignments in the gradebook, so the exams aren't worth as much of the grade. Provides extra credit for coming to class and completing the practice tests. The exams themselves are also pretty easy compared to Kriton.

Absolutely loved Dr. Soghomonian! She is sooo sweet and respectful. Her tests don't weigh much compared to other classes, and she offers extra credit. Her class is semi-mandatory since she has small pop quizzes throughout the semester, but they don't count for much and are easy. Physics is a hard class, but she makes it not that bad.

This professor is not a good person. Do not take his class if you can. He is really just a bad dude with a bad attitude. He is unhelpful. He is not nice. He is probably the worst professor I have interacted with at Virginia Tech.

He has been very helpful to where the class was set up more of an actual worker, not a student. Was extremely clear during lectures and came prepared to answer any questions. trevor was amazing! he chooses an overall theme for the semester's long research essay but he was willing to work with you to help cater the theme to something you'd enjoy researching for 10 weeks. there are 2 assignments per week but they're easy. he's understanding and is willing to give extensions on larger assignments.

reviews.comment: He is incredibly willing to hear you out on your writing and help you with it. He is also very nice it does not feel like an attack when he is helping and going over your work.

A very lenient grader, and as long as you show effort, you'll be fine in his class. Pretty time-consuming class, but this is classic for any college-level writing course.

reviews.comment: This professor was great. He really made the online writing course accessible, and I never had any issues. He also is pretty lenient - he let me redo a presentation because my pet had just died, which helped a lot. Highly recommend.

Professor Snyders has been amazing to work with over this course. He truly cares for his students and as long as you show up to the class and put in the effort you will get an A. He is very understanding and gives amazing feedback. There is a lot of teamwork and class discussion. I would 100% take this course again.

Professor Snyder is probably the most chill English teacher I've ever had. He gives really good feedback on your assignments. As long as you put in the work you should get an A. Class attendance is mandatory, but you get a few buffer misses. There is reading required but its all from this graphic text book so its a pretty quick read. Great Prof!
Trevor was a great professor but he does grade pretty harshly. Work is easy to do and he doesn’t give a lot of assignments (about 2 a week).

He was an awesome professor! You never had too much work and it was very easy to pass. As long as you do the discussions each week, you'll be fine. He cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He will help you if you ask and was overall one of my favorite professors I have had. We only had a few classes and it was clear what was due when.

This class was horrible. I attended every class and read the chapters twice before every exam (you only get 4). I was forced to withdraw because I was failing so badly. It was the only class I've ever failed. It was horrible for an Intro course.

He made this class to hard for an intro class. I attended every class & read the chapters but still ended with a C in the class. I went to meet with him for office hours we set up & he forgot, so I ended up meeting with the TA. I spent more hours studying this class then my Architecture classes. Snizek needs to take a step back for an intro class.
Pretty straight forward class.  You go, read the book and you will get an A.  There are 4 exams made up of 50 questions, 35 from class and 15 from the text.  You can drop your lowest test grade.

I LOVE THIS GUY! He's really funny and really makes class enjoyable I took this class just for fun and definitely do not regret it! I actually wanted to attend this class, if you go to class read the book and turn in the mail bags you'll do fine, it's fun to!
Do not like this class because of the teacher.  He is so arrogant it is absurd.

Snizek absolutely rocks! He is able to actually keep the attention of the students and make the lectures interesting. But you have to go to class, because most of the test material comes from the lectures.
I loved this class. He was very clear and so funny. Easy extra credit and tests were somewhat hard but if you pay attention in class it's easy. He is somewhat sarcastic but i loved it

This guy has to be one of the best professors on this campus. He is very easy to understand and the man knows what he is talking about. 80% of the questions on the exams come straight from lecture material, so you have to go to class. He even gives easy extra credit.
One of the smartest people you will ever meet.  Tests are hard, but the class is awesome.

I like Bill Snizek. He is a very good lecturer and a pretty funny guy. Tests are not hard when you study and you can drop the final. Some of his lectures favor the left side of the political arena; nobody is perfect :) You will love the mailbag...

Very good teacher...easy to understand.  Yes, his tests are hard...but you get to drop one out of four (meaning if you do well on the first three you don't have to take the final) and can earn a bunch of extra credit by simply turning in a comment or question about the lecture or reading assignment.  Overall, getting an A wasn't that hard.

This man is so self abosorbed. His tests are entirely based on examples that involve himself, and he thinks his work is SO important to the sociological world. He is just obnoxious and I am regretting that I took the class. If you are into that kind of prickish teaching style then go ahead and take his class.
His class is really hard and most of exam comes from the lecture, so you have to actually go to class. Overall he is pretty cool.
No Comments
One of the best professors I had at Virginia Tech.

I HIGHLY recommend Dr. Davison, her lectures, homework, and pre-test practice problems were extremely helpful. Put the effort into going to office hours, she had some everyday and it was always worth going to. There is a lot of homework, but it helped my overall understanding of the class. Tests were graded fairly.

reviews.comment: Pretty standard professor. Fair.

She provided a lot of office hour time and helps you a lot for the homework and exams. I will say the homework is difficult and also there is a lot of homework. BUT, if you know how to do the homework, and also did the practice tests, the exam can be slightly eaiser than the homework. But it is worth to take this class with her.

i never wrote rate my professor before but she deserves this. Thermo is already very difficult topic but she explains it so well and have so good understanding about it. The way she answers questions from the students tells how professional she is in this topic. exams and homeworks are very challening, it is worth taking her class. Take her!!!

Her clear explanations and engaging teaching style made a tough thermodynamics class much clearer. Office hours were super helpful with plenty of time and a welcoming environment to ask questions alongside other students!!! It was still a hard class, with a insane amount of homework, but do it in office hours with other students!!!

Dr. Davison is hands down my favorite professor at VT. Thermo is hard, but she has a ton of resources available to help you. Her office hours are great and she's always accessible by email to answer any questions you have. She is the most caring and overworked prof I've had if any vt admin are reading this please give her a raise she deserves it.

I had her for thermo, extremely nice and friendly but the class is very difficult. Not an exceptional lecturer, but above average. Her office hours are amazing and she is available to answer questions most of the time

She was great for statics. Her lectures are dry but clear and simple and if you pay attention in lecture you will be completely fine. She is nice and cares about her students and grades fairly. She is accessible and answers questions well. She is very consistent and posts all her notes. Homework was time consuming but not hard and helped me learn.
Great professor, has very straight forward and approachable homework assignments and lectures.

Although this class was challenging, Professor Davison's teaching style worked great for the class. She posts lecture outline powerpoints before class, students can download them and work through the problems with her in class. She gives a lot of homework, but the homework is super helpful. To do well you need to go to class and do the homework!!

Dr. Davison has office hours every day of the week for long periods of time. She also emails a lot if for some reason you can't make it to office hours. She posts her lecture notes, which is very helpful. The problems take forever, but that is the case regardless of which prof you take. She offers some extra credit at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is tough but Prof Davison is great! Stay active in lectures + do practice problems and you will be fine. It's a lot of HW (2-3 per week, took me about 4-5 hours per hw) but it keeps you practicing everything you need to know for the exams. Attendance not required but she does random in-class exercises for a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: My fav prof I've had here at VT. Super clear lectures with thorough example problems and was super accessible outside of class through office hours and email. Always took the time to help me understand the *why* behind the solutions I was getting when I came to her for help. I don't care what you have to do to make it happen, but take Dr. Davidson!

I think he's adorable. Cares about the environment, makes the rest of us care, tells jokes, pretty clear explanations. Go to all the lectures, look over your notes, get A's on the exams. Professor Spotila is very interesting. Not only is he passionate about Geology but he also seems to enjoy teaching which makes his classes fun and informative.

Lectures contained a lot of information, but if you took good notes and then reviewed them before a test, you did well. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Patrick, although his lectures can sometimes ramble, is a caring and efficient guy. His projects will prepare you very well for other courses, and teach you actual industry relevant skills. In addition, he's a cool guy to talk to outside of class, and has a lot of stories. I'm usually very critical, but genuinely believe he deserves closer to a 3.5

Many find him annoying, but despite his monotonous voice, he is caring and sweet. Anytime I'm worried about a test or a project, he's reassuring. I tbh didn't learn too much from his lectures, but I'm grateful for the projects. I also appreciate that we did an easy Java project, since it was like a little intro into the next class in my path.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, good professor. Has opt-in attendance that basically just adds 10% to your final grade. The lectures are boring and he gets derailed a lot, but nobody stops you from just not listening to him. He's easy to approach and ask questions, and I always left with a clear answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Patrick's lectures do often meander and don't have a direct point, but if you pay attention and ask questions, which he's more than happy to answer, you should be just fine. You can choose for attendance to not be counted, and his tests are slightly difficult, but projects will weigh your grade up. I don't know much about CS at all and got an A-

If you value your GPA, DO NOT TAKE Sullivan. He does not teach, going to his classes are truly a waste of time, you learn nothing. He had the whole class do a code project in Java, for a Python class. Overall an absolutely terrible professor, Hoenstly calling him a professor is me being extremely nice. Would Not recommend.

The lecture was really unclear and difficult to follow. His explanations lacked depth, making it hard to understand the material. The exams were tough, I failed a test because I didn't know how to study for this class. You'll get a project about every two weeks. DON'T take his class if you have no other choice.

Gets a bad rep for boring lectures, but you are given the choice at the beginning of the semester to have a heavier weight on your final if you choose to not have attendance be graded. Workload wasn't too bad, just difficult projects, but it's realistic projects.

The class is hard with any teacher, but Sullivan gives you a lot of flexibility so that you can get a good grade.  He gave 3 points extra on your final grade (significant) for doing surveys.  He also gives you the option to make participation count.  Which means that tests are only worth 20% of your grade total.  So its very fair, just work hard.

The class is hard, which is a big reason why the rating is only a 3/5.  Sullivan is actually very fair.  The tests are easier than the content we cover in class.  Doing and understanding OpenDSA (The online textbook) and paying attention in class will guarantee a good grade in the class.  Pretty flexible nice dude.  I enjoyed it.

Professor Sullivan is very knowledgeable about 3114 topics and enjoys teaching. The lectures can be dry as is common with complex Computer Science courses. It's not entirely his fault. He doesn't deserve a low rating. An extra 10% on the project is very helpful and he also gave an extra 3% this semester. DO THE PROJECT EARLY! You will be fine

The quality of his lectures is embarrassingly poor. Take this class only if you are prepared to teach yourself based off of a textbook. The grading scheme is forgiving, but the exams are ruthless if you are unprepared, and the projects are time-consuming.

The final exam was difficult, but material that we covered throughout the year was not sufficient to do good on the final exam. He just rambles on during lectures without caring if his students understand what is going on.

His lectures are boring. He is very stingy with grades and it is difficult to convince him to give you even a small bump on HW to higher your letter grade. The instructions on some of the homework assignments are ridiculously vague. The assignments are a roller coaster in the way that most of them aren't difficult, but some of them are WAY harder.

His lectures do not correspond with the test material- the test material is at a much more difficult level than explained in class. Lectures are also not helpful because he likes to ramble. The only reason I got an A minus in this class is because I spent multiple hours a week in office hours asking the TA's for help.

He offers a lot of extra credit for submitting projects early which is nice but his lectures don't really teach you. The exams are kinda unnecessary and difficult but they don't count much if you choose attendance. There is a project almost every like two weeks so that helps your grade but he doesn't help so I recommend going to the TA's.

Pick another professor if possible. Lectures are not helpful, he only talks about what he's passionate about and not really what you need to know, but you should go in case of random attendance checks.
Mr. Sullivan gave decent lectures, but mostly rehashed required textbook readings and projects. Sullivan was very helpful in office hours aiding in concept review and project debugging.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures are dry but go in case there is a random attendance check. Projects make up a majority of the grade so pick a good partner and start early. Bonus points are earned for early submission. The project specs are somewhat confusing so go office hours to get clarification. OpenDSAs are the majority of the readings so study them for the tests

Mr. Sullivan is good, he did mess up Project 1 somewhat for our semester but he did change some things after that and the rest of the course was fine. Goes for any 3114 professor, but be prepared to do the projects with less starter code/help (not like CS 2114). His tests aren't difficult and you can get extra points from submitting projects early

Professor uses webcat grading software with mutation testing implemented which was not explained and everyone didn't know how to use the software so the class averaged a 40  on the project and 35% dropped the class before the due date. Professor then said that we didn't work hard enough and how he won't be changing how the course is organized
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Caring and kind professor. Needs more experience but he is young, so he is still learing. Stayed back many times to help students out. Even sacrificed spring break to help us with project 2. Enjoyed learning from him.

This is a tough class. You have to be willing to put extra effort and start projects early. However, Mr. Sullivan is a great and caring professor. He stayed back a lot of times as the project deadline approached to help the students out. He was personable and wants to become a better teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awful.
Avoid at all costs! Trust me, save yourself.

reviews.comment: Bad, very very bad
You know it's bad when the other 3114 professor is changing her curriculum because Sullivan's project structure is unfair for students and TAs.
This is the most frustrating, unreasonable, mismanaged class I have ever taken.

Never responsive outside of class, piazza and email responses are very slow or otherwise get completely ghosted. Project instructions are a bit confusing. The only positive thing is the 10% extra credit for projects.

Professor Sullivan is a very knowledgeable and very passionate professor when it comes to CS 3114. He gives 10% extra if you turned in the project 2 days early which carried my grade A LOT. Beware of the occasional pop quizzes he gives for attendance.
dude is such a chiller.  midterms are so free also. go to office hours he is super helpful. the final is lowk hard but if u do well enough on the midterms it won't matter

Super nice and understanding. If you do well on the exams you'll be fine, the only hard part of the class was the final because it was a common time but if you do well enough on the midterms then it won't matter what you get on the final.

Summers was a good teacher and wanted you to do well. This class was just really difficult and he sped through many topics that I feel like he could have went a little slower through. Tests are crazy hard so make sure to study well in advance. Go to office hours and he will help you all you need, but good luck on those tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very good teacher who's very easy going and understanding. Had plenty of office hours and was willing to help if needed.
Great guy for 1226, go to office hours and put in the work for an easy B at least...

He gives helpful feedback on all homework, quizzes, and tests, and he is always willing to help his students after class if they need it. Just ask. Make sure you know every section from the previous chapters when it comes time to take a test because he will typically put a little bit of everything on them, so you have to know your stuff. Great guy.
1226 is a rough class but he wants you do to well and if you do the work and ask for help when needed he will do his best to get you through it.

I had and she's super easy. As long as you show up to class and do the papers on time, it's a guaranteed A. The class gets a little dull at times, but I can't complain otherwise. Just turn everything in on time!
Professor Swenson definitely did not prefer an online format, but still was patient and graded students well. Show up, do the work, answer questions, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I highly recommend Professor Swenson. The class is super easy-as long as you do the work you will get an A. The class size made it feel much more personal than huge lecture halls. Professor Swenson is compassionate and will work with you if you are having trouble.
She is an incredibly nice woman who genuinely cares about her students. Show up, do the work, and it's very easy to make a decent grade. She's a little boring at times, but she is easy.

Professor Swenson is highly recommended! She keeps things light, so even if you aren't an English major, the class won't kill you. Easy to understand and reasonable expectations. Plus, she's witty and extremely interesting!

Swenson is one of my favorite professors.  She's interesting and very helpful.  I'm also able to get good grades by taking good notes but not reading any of the material, which is very good, since I have so many classes that require heavy reading.

I thought it was difficult material, but that is ballanced by the fact you can get a grade grade IF you ask for help and take suggestions on how to improve writing. Gives feedback. Seemingly freeflowing structure of discusion but then the information adds up in the notes (hint: take notes!) when u study.

The assignments are interesting and original and Swenson really knows her stuff. She's willing to meander but brilliant on her subject. The books are tough but she is very approachable and will help anyones writing improve as well as their knowledge of the material.

She is defintely goofy (ask to see her Grendel tattoo) but I love her.  Swenson is probably the nicest teacher I have ever had.  She is always wiling to listen to excuses and will do anything to help her students get better grades.

Mrs. Swenson can be goofy at times, but she is a really easy..and i mean EASY teacher...her class is fun but sometimes reminds you of high school where you talk about random stuff that has nothing to do with the topic of the day, but shes really nice and easy to talk to. Makes you feel comfortable in class...id recommend here. easy to get an A

Dr Baniya is great at what she does, and is a very understanding and thoughtful grader. She has a couple of major papers and a bunch of smaller, easier assignments that help you balance out your grade. She allows you to turn in benchmarks of the bigger papers to make sure you're on track. She's an awesome professor. Don't listen to the haters :P

Most of the time she doesn't know what she is talking about. Jumps from topic to topic, expects you to already know the material when we haven't even talked about it yet. 
Shares too much about her personal life and her "mental health" and she is not respectful towards her students. 

If this class was not required, I would have skipped it.

She's an easy grader and generally flexible on assignments but her class is terrible. The service learning aspect is very "white savior", she doesn't follow the schedule (assignments are due on a reading before you even read them), and the lectures are terrible. It's all info we already know and super repetitive. I would drop if it wasn't required

First day of class, he will tell you that you only need to show up two more times: midterm and final. You can easily get an A by studying his review slides for 3 hours the night before each exam. But if you want to learn extra stuff that is way more important than any normal college class would teach you, show up everyday
Really funny and laid back. Also gives you very helpful tips to succeeding in the real world, not just the class.
Great and entertaining professor, cares about our personal plans for the future. The workload was very light and the exams were straightforward as well. Made class entertaining

Charley was one of my favorite professors I have had, I wish I had this class in person. He is so passionate and smart in his area and wants his students not only to succeed in his class but in life too. He is also hilarious.

Class graded by only a few things. Two exams total (each worth 25%). No need to go to class because power points are all posted on Canvas. Swayne is a nice guy and class was super easy but I still got a good understanding of all the material I learned.

McGraw-Hill Connect is required for the course. He goes over one chapter per class. Professor Swayne posts a powerpoint file a week before the exam with everything you need to know. There are two exams, a mid term paper, and several quizzes.

You have to buy the McGraw Hill Connect textbook to be able to access the graded quizzes. He will go over a chapter a class, but post all the PowerPoints on canvas. He posts an exam review guide which has all the information you need to know for the 2 exams in the class. Always willing to help you understand a concept and gives good examples.

Best professor I've taken at Saddleback, by far. He genuinely cares about his students and offers extra credit for a one-on-one meeting with him. Very understanding and flexible about late work. Really challenges you to think critically without any judgement, and gives amazing & thorough feedback. Discussions were always engaging. Very smart person

SADDLEBACK COLLEGE
Very nice teacher really cares about their students. Recommend doing the extra credit since it will now let me finish the class with above 100 percent. Really cares about what you submit and gives personal feedback and even asks you questions. Really felt like I learned something in this class.

Ratemyprof blocked adding him as a prof at Saddleback so this profile will have to do. Prof Szczurek is my favorite. He's very well spoken, intelligent about what he talks about, and genuinely cares about all of his students. He asks sometimes after discussions what we thought about the material and if he should change it. Do the work, get an A.

I loved taking Professor Szczurek's class at Saddleback. He is genuinely the smartest guy you'll ever meet. There was never a time in this class that I felt unsupported; he was always happy to help/discuss assignments and expectations. He was very accommodating and understanding. The information taught isn't easy, but it's a very interesting class!

reviews.comment: I loved taking his class at Saddleback Collage, CA. he was a professor who wants his students to truly understand the subject and its information for our benefit. I took Szczurek's class in summer 2021 after I graduated HS. Quizzes consist of a short essay. Highly suggest rewatching lectures & studying weekly discussions.

Unclear grading standards, and dose not provide rubrics for short essay assignments which are done on a weekly basis. No TA provided for the course, and there is no defined office hour period. Professor refuses to meet students via zoom.

she is just the worst professor I have ever encountered, doesn't care about her students, not helpful, very arbitrary grading system, with no clear set guidelines, so it leaves you as a student very confused and irritated. One of the worst teachers I have ever met. Just reads from the slides and expects too much from her students. I would say if she is your teacher just leave the course would learn more than being in her guidance.

reads off long irrelevant slides, gives technical labs that someone else made with little to no guidance, makes quizzes that are basically memorizing a bunch of questions from a book, assigns a very rough semester project with arbitrary grading standards. She doesnt give clear feedback more of just be creative. We had a HUGE final project that we spent weeks on and she never graded it nor gave us feedback. As far as I know, she is the only one that teaches this class which is tough because knowing how to use Tableau is huge in the business/IT world. Assigns and ungodly amount of weekly work

Dr. James is one of the worst professors I have had at VT. During the pandemic she has not shown up to the one scheduled lecture. The class was online. Two weekly assignments due every week you have to do in class. There's also two weekly homeworks corresponding to the weekly assignments. reviews.comment: Worst teacher I've had at Virginia Tech so far. She requires way too much work and expects way too much from her students. Avoid taking this teacher at all costs. Trust me.

Horrible teacher that doesn't really teach anything but just reads the slides. Disappointing considering this class could have been interesting. Don't take her classes trust me it's a lot of stupid busy work
just rambles on and on. the most boring class I've ever taken. doesn't want to help. holds very limited office hours. just a really bad teacher overall.
if you're only taking this class as a pathway six elective.. dont pick a new one. if its a requirement for you major you'll prob enjoy it which will make it less dreadful.

Not sure why people leave such poor ratings. Prof. Warner is exactly what you should expect for an event planner. She is organized, no-nonsense, and has a method to her teaching. She was a harsh grader for every assignment, making it nearly impossible to get an A in the class and didn't seem to care much about her students. This was the hardest hospitality class I've taken, and didn't have to be.

This teacher was extremely rude to her students. She gives very confusing instructions and will say one thing then get mad when you do exactly that. Crazy hard grader, this class if difficult and hard to keep up with. Big group project at the end that takes months, do not put it off. Keep up to date with your assignments and attendance, use the honor code or you will fail. Her not knowing your name is for the better, stay quiet and productive.

harsh grader and not super understanding

I thought this class would be really fun, but it wasn't. Incredibly disappointed in the class. Professor Warner isn't very friendly and makes her class more important than it is. No test, just quizzes and one big final project. The projects not bad if you work on it a bit each week. Overall, she could make this class a lot more fun than it was.

reviews.comment: Sounds like such a fun pathway but I was wrong. She turns a class that could be so fun and interesting into a dreadful experience. You will have a final project that is most of grade.

You'll have weekly homework assignments and the main focus on the class will be on your group project. Although it's a little bit heavy on the workload, Professor Warner was very resourceful and in my opinion was not harsh with grading. Just be sure to do your assignments and project in a timely manner and you'll be golden.

If you are taking this for a pathway DO NOT, it is an insane amount of work. Attendance is not excused (even if you are sick), if you forget to put the honor code on your assignments she takes 5 points off, you are required 4 hours of event volunteer service AND to attend 2 events (not through VT), and there is a HUGE group project (50 pages long).

i have never been so disappointed in a class. professor warner is not understanding and WILL NOT work with you under any circumstances. she takes 5 points off of assignments if the honor code is not included. her lectures are boring and the group project at the end is an unnecessary amount of work. would not take again.

Prof was awesome, funny and interesting! The class was very enjoyable and all the assignments were useful to the final project at the end of the class.
