Super lecture heavy, and half of the lectures could be done with a simple YouTube video instead of a whole hour and a half of her explaining basic knowledge. Tough grader, its all about what she thinks is good so good luck with that. Most difficult teacher I have ever had in all of my 16 years of education.

This was the hardest class I've taken at Virginia Tech. Compared to the other teacher for this class she is like the wicked witch of the west. The other class had easier assignments, less work and much easier grading criteria. She honestly made me hate myself for 4 months of my life. Avoid at all cost.

Would give a negative score if possible. Worst instructor I've had at any level of education. Subjective grader, singles out students she doesn't like, extremely unknowledgeable, probably the most bored I've ever been in my life is sitting in her class. Don't take any of her classes, what people say on here is not exaggeration.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. She's not nice whatsoever, the harshest grader, and makes you feel like you are the smallest person on earth. She has no empathy for students. She never gives positive/constructive feedback, it's subjective and whatever she feels like that day. DO NOT TAKE HER. I hope she reads these reviews.
Just horrible. Save yourself.

Possibly the worst teacher I have ever had. Lives to give out bad grades. Unfair grader and does not do a good job of communicating to students. Classes are terribly boring, she just reads from the slides.
Awful, Just awful
Not a good lecturer at all, reads straight off the slides and doesn't go in depth. Grades hard but doesn't give much feedback for improvement.

She is as bad as everyone else said times a billion. It's almost as if she tries to give out the worst grade she possibly can and her grading/comments are as subjective as it gets so you don't know how to improve. I don't know how she still has a job but avoid this woman at all costs if you want to graduate on time
Avoid classes with this professor if at all possible. She really is as bad as everyone says she is

Worst experience with any professor I've encountered in my career. She lacks any and all approachability and is completely unreceptive to inquisitions. She is incapable of allocating credit where it is due but is ecstatic when excessively critiquing minor and useless errors. Will give negatives on rubric instead of 0/0. TAKE JARRED. Demoralizing af

Highly recommend you stay away from this professor, she makes the assignments much harder than they need to be. Her grading is very subjective and does not make sense sometimes, if she does not like you then forget about getting a good grade. Every other teacher that teaches 2034 is a better option than her.

When I asked her questions, I would often get, "Google it." as a response...what is the point of the school hiring you if you're just going to tell students to google information that you should be able to give us? She is very condescending when you ask her for help on ANYTHING. She just made me feel dumb, and like I was a failure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I didn't really learn anything in this class. The way she graded felt as if she really didn't care about the students. Her reviews were very subjunctive and I wasn't able to take her critiques and improve my work. After every project, I felt like a failure. Don't ask her for help either; she'll make you feel really dumb and give you a rude glare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not ever take this professor. She grades super harshly and makes attendance mandatory DESPITE her reading directly from the powerpoint slides word for word. Her lectures are a snooze fest and she should never be allowed to teach. If you ask her for help she makes you feel dumb, and if you thought youd do SMA/MJ focused assignments, youd be wrong
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT take Robinson for this class or any class. She is the hardest grader I have ever had in the school of Comm, and does not care about students on a personal or academic level.

Terrible person, yet an even worse teacher. No instruction or teaching, surprised she is still employed. Could care less about students, and is more worried about trying to find wrong than right. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

I took this class over the summer, and she never considered that is harder to perform some of her requirements. She was a very tough grader and never gave good feedback..she would just tell you that you did this wrong and need to work on it. Very rude

I have had her twice and both times were awful. I have never spent so much time outside of class doing work for this class. This class is very time heavy and requires a lot mentally and physically. Yes, that means driving to places and meeting up with people. She doesn't teach and watches us like a hawk during a 2-hour class while we do nothing

Genuinely the worst teacher I've had in my academic career. Does not care about you. You'd think she's teaching neuroscience with how overly-detail oriented every assignment is. You will have to earn every single point in this class. Obviously just collecting a check and does not care about the success or failure of her students.

I'm not entirely sure how she just received a promotion when she reads directly from the PowerPoint slides and considers that to be a lecture. Takes forever to update grades, no study guides for the cumulative final. Doesn't fully explain assignments before deducting points. I'll never take her course again. One of my worst professors ever, BEWARE!

The worst teacher I have had by far. Does not care about her students. Gave a final cumulative exam with no study guide, no help, and no avalibility. Overall a rude professor who really shouldn't be teaching if she treats her kids like this. if you can stay away from her do it. Can't emphasize enough how boring and unhelpful she is. Take diff teach
HORRIBLE

Horrible at explaining concepts and giving feedback. Have never received a single word of encouragement the entire semester. 20 points off for even a minute late in submitting and made me realize I never want to work in the news. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Easily the hardest course I've taken at Tech due to the various heavily weighted homework and reporting assignments. Very strict about deadlines and doesn't give you much to work with in terms of bumping up your grade, unless you do revisions for major assignments within a week of getting your grade. Not considerate with other class workloads.
Strict on due dates, she will deduct 20 points off even if you're 5 minutes late on submitting.

There are four major assignments that she grades you on, but she isn't tough on grading those assignments. There are 2 exams and THEY ARE HARD. The exams are the hardest part of the class but the assignments are worth more points. Only need the textbook to answer the review questions at the end of each chapter; this helps with the exams.

Syrenthia has been the worst professor i have encountered at Virginia Tech. She is unforgiving with due dates despite extenuating circumstances past the students control. She does not answer questions efficiently. In class she relies on the back of the textbook to answer simple grammar questions. Avoid her classes at all cost!

online asynch-all the assignments were doable in any format (and actually interesting). readings are provided through pdfs (don't buy anything). there's EC, but i didnt do any because if you did the easy assignments you get 100. there a mid term/final essays/writing, that take a bit, but he's an lenient grader. 10/10 taking another class of his

Professor Taggart is a great professor. The lectures are entirely asynchronous, and the only consistent thing that is expected of students is to complete homework (which is light and rather enjoyable). He is very considerate and lenient when it comes to tests and homework. Students are given lots of freedom on homework and projects.

Professor Taggart is the best. He's passionate about his job and it shows. I recommend his Arab Culture and Civilization course if you're interested in the topic or if you want a good pathways course. I learned a lot and enjoyed the videos and readings. In most classes I dread doing the assignments but I weirdly looked forward to his assignments.

This class was really interesting and eye-opening. I learned a lot about Arab culture and the Middle East. Class assignments are easy, but they also teach you a lot. Make sure to start the midterm and final projects and exams early! Taggart is a great professor!

Will is a super nice guy. It is more difficult to do badly than get an A, he always offers extensions, and he grades easy as long as you put effort into your work. Attendance is completely optional and will not affect your grade, but his lectures are interesting and he is very passionate about the topics he discusses.
All of Taggart's classes are super easy, you have to try hard not to get an A. Offers extensions, attendance is basically optional, but his classes are interesting and he's a cool guy.

Taggart was super nice and always willing to help if you needed an extension or were confused. He had books he wanted us to read for class but we only read one and there's a free online pdf. Highly recommend, if I can take a class of his again I definitely will.

She's fine but usually had an attitude and expected students to already know everything. Will cold call. Be prepared to do a lot of group work with people you don't know. Attendance is taken with class engagement. She seems like a nice person who cares but she comes off as unapproachable and slightly disorganized.

MGT 4334
Do not take Ethical Leadership with her. She was unbelievably underprepared every day, the canvas page is an absolute trainwreck and is impossible to comprehend. She takes forever to grade anything and don't bother trying to email about anything because she doesn't know what's going on either. Save yourself the trouble and take anyone else

Classes are mandatory with a daily engagement assignment. No syllabus schedule - would sometimes receive random canvas notifications about hw w/o being told about it. The one exam given was take-home online (no final exam). Project/presentation is a huge part of grade, so get in a good group. Very high class average on project grades.

Easily my favorite professor I have had throughout college. I have learned the most from her class because she cares more about you understanding the material rather than just grading us on it. Take this class and as many as you can with Professor Kemp because she is a true gem of Virginia Tech.

Really amazing professor - would definitely take her again! Super caring of her students and wants them to do well, also very easy assignments and easy grader! Just show up and participate in the group projects and you'll be fine

She's a super nice woman. Really easy class, all you really need to do is attend class. No need for the textbook so don't buy. As long as you participate and show up to class you'll easily walk out with an A.

Professor Kemp is amazing! She is a very easy grader and just cares about your knowledge of the course, not the grade. I would absolutely take her for Organizational Behavior. The only thing you really have to do is attend the classes.
Just don't choose her!!! She's such grader. I am here on full ride and because of her class I don't meet the requirements anymore.

She's a good professor, I just felt like the class lacks some organization. She's passionate about the topic, and the drawing assignments are very easy. A lot of the assignment descriptions are just very vague, including the semester-long project. She also doesn't release grades until the end, so you don't know how you're doing in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is very art/drawing heavy. Prof Clements is very passionate about the subject and is very encouraging in all the assignments. Lectures are a bit boring but some are fun. Be prepared to draw alot in this class and have a semester long paper with lots of drawings.

I found the course interesting but lacking in clear direction and feedback. No grades are given besides complete/incomplete and canvas modules are often not uploaded until the night before lecture. I thought the professor was very nice but wish the course had more structure and communication.

Ms. Mercer is one of the best instructors I've had. She is responsible to every student and meticulously graded, commented on, and summarized every assignment, quiz, and test. She provides concise feedback and even personally checks in when a student is absent, offering notes and make-up opportunities.
Amazing professor. As long as you do the homework and study before quizzes/tests you will be all set. You will learn a lot with her!

She went over topics several times, which is helpful in learning a new language. Harsh grader and gives little to no feedback. Attendance is graded and there is homework due every class. Very sweet and always ready for class. Lots of partner work in class.
Professor Thornton was an amazing professor. He was an expert on many philosophical books, and I looked forward to going to class.

Zachary Thorton was truly an amazing professor who I think has the potential to change the philosophy game. While sometimes the lectures could be a little boring, he always was sure to be thorough in his explanations, especially since the readings could be somewhat hard to understand. The TA's were amazing as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is very passionate about what he teaches and makes the material very easy to understand. Not a ton of work to do outside of class, just a few papers which you could receive TA feedback on.

Really really great professor. He's passionate about the material he presents and makes everything easy to understand. I feel like I can apply what he teaches outside of the class. Hope to take a class with him again in the future

Professor Tellez's class should not be a hard at all, but her teaching style isn't effective so you often have to teach yourself. I don't really believe that she cares how her students do because on the first day she told us she is only teaching so she can get her Phd. Lectures are really hard to sit through and not engaging at all.

lectures are incredibly boring. there is a capstone project that she makes due the monday after thanksgiving break and she expects students to meet on zoom with her to go over our projects. she has no respect for students time and doesn't care if her students do well or not. its not a hard class to get through but she is very inconsiderate.

Class can be difficult at times, but Professor Tellez is a good professor. Pretty lenient with grading, that is if you show up to class. She gives out bonus points to boost your grade, but they're all random. Give you a reason to show up to class.

She made class super interesting and was very fair with grading. Doesn't take attendance, but gives extra credit in the form of random bonus points for being in class. If you attend class and take good notes your set.

She's very generous with partial credit on exams and makes it clear to whats going to be on them. She also gives bonus points if you attend class which is also really generous. Class is very interesting and not super difficult if, however, you take the time to study and go to class. Otherwise this class can be a bit of a pain.
She is very passionate to the subject and gives practice exams to better prepare us for the midterms. Content is super interesting and not super difficult as long as you go to class.

She's very fair with her grading, especially with attendance. I like how she allows you to bring a formula sheet for your exams. Her lectures can be difficult to understand at times, but she posts all her notes and lectures online which is nice.

She's a good teacher, its just sometimes hard to understand her. She's one of those professors who does her lectures but you the student need to comprehend the concepts yourself since her explanations can be hit or miss. She is really nice and chill though.

Text-heavy PowerPoint slides are what the lectures consist of making the class difficult to pay attention to as it gives the appearance of the professor being uncomfortable with the topics they're teaching. The final exams weight of 50% is unnecessary for a Senior level course. 7 lengthy assignments throughout the course which only account for 20%.

Changing the syllabus a couple days before the final exam to disallow the inclusion of any info you want on the notes sheet (to just formulas) after allowing anything on the first exam (and in the syllabus) is ridiculous. Advance notice should have been given or made the change in the following semester. Final is 50%, 7 (long) assignments only 20%.

Thweatt's lectures were engaging and informative, but he assigned brutal amounts of work, and the deadlines were extremely strict as well. His office hours were very helpful, so make sure to attend those if you're struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: In my experience, course is unnecessarily difficult, and lectures dont feel like help with the actual projects. Lectures frequently ramble, and questions are answered with questions rather than clear explanations. Announcements often turned into rants, grading was harsh,and deadlines extremely strict. The environment felt consistently discouraging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great professor, will go the extra mile to help you succeed.

Insane amounts of work. Take cooper if you can, she gives you case studies that actually help teach this mind numbingly boring material and prepares you for the solo projects that will come on later. Thweatt is a good guy with good office hours. Lectures are terrible since he posts the slides but not the work he does on the slides.

Great professor bad system. Grading policy for the course is extremely strict, the TA graders suck, and the workload can get out of hand. Thweatt however does his best to help you manage through the terrible class structure, holds great office hours. start assignments early, quadruple check before submitting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Incapable of answering a question quickly. Yaps your ear off with reiteration after reiteration of the same thing over and over, holding your answer on a string out of reach for way too long. Rather unaccommodating when you make any error. Surprise entry quizzes for credit that aren't in the syllabus (which says attendance is ungraded).

Professor Thweatt is not a good professor. He is overly strict to a point where it seems that he does not care for his students success. If you forget to submit a single file on your very first assignment, he will still give you a zero despite all the effort you put into the class and the project, he does not care. Horrible.

Bad professor. Very obtuse instructor and rambles on incoherently instead of giving simple answers to basic questions. Grading system is whack and his TAs are quite bad and Thweatt will scapegoat bad course management onto their incompetence while doing nothing to fix it. Pretty sure he has no real experience in the stuff he teaches.

Thweatt is incredible. I really struggled in this class, but managed to get an A because of all the time he spent helping me. He won't let you leave his office until he's sure he's helped you. He had office hours every day and would often stay 2 - 3 hours late to make sure he had sufficiently helped every student there. Take him if at all possible.

This class is a pain, but I really liked going to this class since Thweatt is a great lecturer. You HAVE to start the projects at a decent time and office hours were so insanely helpful!! He keeps things pretty light and his notes written during class can be extremely helpful. Quizzes are basically homework, but it can get hard randomly.

Nicest prof I've had. I didn't think his lectures were that helpful until you got very close to an LE deadline,   but he makes it up in his office hours and announcements. I've seen him hold office hours that last 6+ hours, making sure every student's questions are answered. Pretty annoying class in general, but take him if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Start le's early! LE G was the hardest by far. He's passionate, but jumps around topics a lot, making it hard to take notes sometimes. Also doesn't post his own notes so pay attention to his tangents to retain information. Quizzes matter more than you realize.

Thweatt is an awesome professor. He is knowledgeable about the subject and explains everything clearly. He is funny and a very engaging lecturer. Professor Thweatt is one of my favorite professors I have had. Homework and projects are time-consuming like in 2544.

Great professor! His lectures do a decent enough job of getting across the material, and if you need extra help his office hours are generally pretty helpful. Be ready to spend lots of time on projects though.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: An extremely eccentric man that is super passionate about teaching and just ECE in general. His lectures will keep you engaged just by his personality alone and will even drop hints while speaking on how to do some of the assignments (hint hint). Would definitely take Thweatt again in a heartbeat.

Professor Thweatt was a cool professor but I thought that for digital systems he did not give us enough connections to be able to do all the assignments. It was a HARD class. All the projects are interconnected so if you do bad on one, you do bad on all of them.

Professor Thweatt is awesome. I can't find any cons of him. (Excepts for time consuming homework and projects, it looks like all 3544 and 2544 students have very time consuming works to do, even if they enrolled in different sessions.)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best lecturer at VT ECE department, he's energetic. Not so much homework but LEs (projects) are heavy and super time-consuming. NEVER WAIT UNTIL THE LAST MINUTE to do those LEs because you would ABSOLUTELY NOT make it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Top notch professor! I had Thweatt for Intro to CPE and DD1 and enjoyed his classes. The projects and homework are crazy time consuming, even if you have digital electronics experience. Go to his office hours he will spent as much time as you want going over anything. The only downside is that he will over explain which sometimes leads to confusion
One of the best teachers in VT ECE department. Very good human beign.

Unbelievably unreasonable. Don't even try to argue for an accommodation for any reason because you won't get one. If you're a beginner/amateur to programming, and you ask if what you've incorrectly coded is supposed to work or not, he'll make you feel stupid for coding it the way you did. Not encouraging at all, just condescending and arrogant
Very challenging but enjoyable class - the class is tough but Jason is very helpful in answering any questions and making it more enjoyable.

He is good guy and will work with you until you understand the material.  You will learn from him, and if you don't, that is you own damn fault.  He is tough though.  You will work in his class.  He is also absolutely unyielding when it comes to class policy.  He makes no exceptions for anyone for any reason unless it is part of the class policy.
He makes the classes too hard...his assignments and tests are unsolvable.he doesn't take into account that students are taking other classes than his course..ok..he is funny but how does that count?

He is a nice guy, I'll give you that much, but he makes everything so much harder then what it has to be. He sends out 3 page email messages that are relevant to nothing and then he'll spend hours explaining why he is the way he is. Like I said nice guy, but a little unstable. I would go for a different instructor if possible.

I adore this professor!  He's enthusiastic and funny...okay, and a little sarcastic at times, but you know it's all in good fun.  What's more, he makes class interesting, and is always willing to explain concepts until everyone understands.  If you can get a class with him, get it!
He's an awesome teacher who explains concepts with good explainations.  He may be a bit boisterous at times, but is really helpful.
He's kinda boisterous but still an awesome teacher cause he emphasizes everything too much.
No Comments

His lectures are on the slower side and the labs were sometimes grueling (5+ hours) but at the end of the day he was a great professor and really wanted to help his students. If you review his notes extensively and have a good lab partner you should be able to easily achieve A-B.

This class has a pretty heavy mandatory workload. He was monotone but extremely clear in his explanations. I believe him to be a better lecturer than some of the other 2305 professors. I did notice his test averages to be lower than others. It's highkey annoying that there is no partial credit offered in 2305 as the majority is multiple choice.

DO NOT TAKE IT FROM 5:30 - 6:45 YOU WILL FALL ASLEEP. Dr. O'Donnell was an alright professor. Perhaps it was the timeframe but he spoke in a very monotone voice for the entire semester and it put me to sleep. He was helpful in office hours though.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Fair grader and. Heavy workload when considering homework, recitation, and labs. Lots of extra credit and grade makeup opportunities. Good lectures, but he dislikes any talking during lectures.
Awesome professor, just try to be respectful in class.

This class was very difficult, but it was as easy as it could be with Professor O'Donnell. He is a very kind and always willing to help. His lectures are great and easy to follow, though slightly hard to be engaged since he only teaches at 8am or 6pm (not his fault). Prequizzes were a major life-saver. Very high work load, but that's just how it is

Prof O'Donnell is one of the most caring professors I've met and truly takes the time to make sure all the students understand the topic/curriculum. Lectures can go a bit slow, and attendance is mandatory. He makes everyone feel open to asking questions.

Great professor. Has destroyed 10 expo marker though taboot "tac". Very kind and explains the concepts very well. His prequizzes will boost your grade on the exams, which the dept. design to be very difficult.

Prof O'Donnell is an amazing professor. He always takes the time to review all the course material provides several examples for each concept, and is always open to answering questions. You will fall asleep if you take the 5:30-6:45 section, so try to take a class earlier in the day.

Professor O'Donnell is a friendly, caring professor with extremely clear-to-follow lectures. I forgot my calculator for one of the exams, and he quickly got me a spare one. The only negative about him is that he has a monotone voice. Had his class at 5:30 and almost fell asleep a couple of times; otherwise, he's a great professor.

Kind professor that tries his best to help students that do not understand the material. Made sure to emphasize the usage of office hours if we ever were struggling with questions. Content-wise the class is a little harder than average, make sure to utilize pre-quizzes well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a genuine, caring person that wants his student's to understand the concepts he is teaching. Also, treat the pre-quizzes as if they were similar to the test and do not forget to take them. They get progressively harder throughout the year, and they determine the curve you get, including on the final. He is also very good during office hours.

Professor O'Donnell has to be one of my favorite professors so far. He's genuinely so nice and cares A LOT about his students. Office hours with him are very helpful and with a subject like Physics I do recommend you utilize them. All I can say about the class itself is study, study, study. And take the pre-quizzes seriously!

Prof. O'Donnell is a genuine professor who cares about his students well being. He's a bit quiet, but a fantastic teacher. He is also very easy to reach outside of class and is incredibly accommodating. He's worth it!

Considering physics was my worst subject in high school and I have an A right now, I'd say Professor O'Donnell's a great professor. His lectures can sometimes run flat, but he tries his best to keep things light in nature. He's really good at explaining difficult concepts and provides many examples. I strongly recommend him if you want to succeed!

Definitely the stereotypical nerdy, slightly awkward physics professor, who can be a bit monotonous at times but tries to keep things light. He would explain things again/in different ways if you didn't understand the problem and did very thorough walkthroughs of practice questions. STUDY FOR THE PREXAMS! Those saved my grade this semester.

Dr. O'Donnell is a very caring and good professor. Although he can be very monotonous, resulting in large swaths of my already small class to skip, he is a very good lecturer and makes sure you know what you're learning. Office hours are incredibly helpful, and they are also beneficial in forming good relationships with him. Please go to class!
Tries to make class more bearable but don't take a 6pm class with him you will sleep. Funny at time and would take again.

O'Donnell's lectures are very clear, and he tries to get 1 on 1 engagement with his students. At office hours he was very engaging and explained a lot of the problems very well. Along with that he provides a good amount of ways to boost your grade. The prequizzes specifically are why I'd recommend him.

I absolutely love Prof. O'Donnell!! He was my favorite teacher, and physics became my favorite course the sem I took it thanks to him! I've taken physics before, so I definitely know it's NOT my favorite subject or a strength but he made it so fun and taught concepts super clearly! He always tried his best to be engaging and is very approachable!

Professor O'Donnell is one of the best Physics Professors I have ever had. I enjoyed his class so much that I am adding a Physics Major. He thoroughly explains every concept and practice problem in class. The class itself is fairly easy, there is a homework assignment due on Friday every week, and there is 2 tests and 1 final.

Prof. O'Donnell is a fantastic physics professor for 2305. Despite typically lecturing a massive group of people, he still puts effort into 1 on 1 interaction, showing up to problem-solving questions and asking how each student is doing. He is knowledgeable and involved in research, so he is always up to date with current developments in physics.

Very caring and takes the time to go over difficult problems during office hours. Moreover, Professor O'Donnell is extremely knowledgeable in this field while also being approachable at the same time. Overall, great professor and you won't regret taking him!

The class wasn't that hard for me because I took physics in high school, so I only went to about 70% of the time. However, Prof. O'Donnell is such a nice guy and really wants everyone to do well. Physics is a hard concept to grasp for most people so as long as you study for exams and go to class most of the time you'll be fine.

Instrumental Analysis lab had a very "considerate" design considering how it is taken alongside the second half of Physical Chemistry lab. The labs and lab reports were very simple and Professor Tissue was always available both in and out of lab to help.

Instrumental Analysis wasn't necessarily difficult per se. However, his lectures were not the best and the final exam was killer. He graded based on 3 tests + the final, 8 HW, 5 attendance check marks for speaking in class, and 'muddy points' where you write what you are most confused about at the end of a module. Not terrible, but could be better.
rude guy

Yes, he is hard, and yes some of the material is a bit boring and hard to follow.  But he's a really great guy, he's a good teacher and even though he pretends that he doesn't care if you pass/fail just that you learn it.... He actually does.  He's  helpful in office hours and even though this was my most hated class, he was my favorite teacher.

there are ways to make up for bad test grades, but the tests are really hard and not like the practice ones he gives you a few days before a test. he drops lowest 2 tests and a few quizzes. just do chemskillbuilder, its a grade and helps the most and ended up with a b- with 2 test scores of 45,55

ok, so he's not funny.. doesn't teach too well... and the test are hard... but he curves em good and drops some quizzes... and makes chem skill builder actually worth something. Not hard to get a B assuming u took high school Chem, but if you've never taken Chem, don't even try with him.
Not a very good teacher at all. His lectures put you to sleep and his exams are HARD.  They are nothing like his lectures or the practice exams he posts. And another thing, his jokes SUCK.
Save yourself now!  You will learn more from the book than you could learn from him in a lifetime. Try to get Amateis.
very boring class. he barely taught anything, you really had to teach yourself. it was an 8 o'clock class so noone went. theres no homework or grade booster so that doesnt help bad test grades.
WOW this guy may have funny/corny jokes but cannot teach what-so-ever.  You fill in the blanks for notes and he does not explain at all
Very helpful and a fun guy

I HATE this class/teacher. He assumes students understand the information and just breezes through the concepts.  The tutoring center has become my second home.  When students ask questions in class, he doesn't do a good job explaining.  I have all A's but a D+/C in his class despite studying every night. I do not recommend him at all.
I hate to say it, as Brian Tissue is a really nice guy, I just don't think that he's cut out for teaching.
This is possibly the worst teacher I have ever had.  He is extremely boring and it is hard to keep your head up and pay attention in between all of his "jokes"
No Comments

Tissue is one of the WORST professors I've had - chem or otherwise!  He is not helpful during office hours, does not respond to emails, gives useless information during class and expects you to know relevant info. on the tests and most of all he is BORING to listen to even though i love chemistry.

If you actually listen, then her class will teach you life long lessons. She has a few quizzes, graded attendance assignments, and a final paper. Best professor ever!
Not prepared for class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is one of the best teachers I've had at tech. She is so nice and smart and wants her students to engage and learn. Take her it you have the option!!!! She has had great experience and is so encouraging about her students doing well in life. So glad I got to take a class with her. I did not take her online I could not click in person class!

Silvia is one of the most caring professors you will have at VT. She truly cares about her students and their well-being. She is easily accessible and will respond quickly. She is always happy to meet outside of class, and as long as you attend her class and pay attention, you will do well. She grades fairly and provides constructive feedback.
Easy class, good professor, online tests and in person and a few papers and presentations. If you show up youll be fine.

A great teacher and a explainer. She is a little condescending to students but you can tell it's not meant to be malicious. Sometimes her Spanish was hard for me to understand– but that may just be a me thing. She grades pretty easy, just do your work and study the material she gives you and you'll do fine

Class was depressingly easy. Prof is very sweet/accommodating + great explainer but unfortunately almost nobody put in the needed work, so she was forced to constantly speak in English and teach to the lowest common denominator (i.e. a bit of a waste for me.) Short online HW 3x week but to genuinely learn you need to go above and beyond practicing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was really nice but if you don't like drawing and are just taking this as an elective - DO NOT TAKE IT. Extremely heavy on the creativity and thought put into projects. Overall, super fun class and he was nice. You can tell he wanted to make it fun for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's nice and knows what he's doing. Make sure not to come to class late; he is really strict about attendance and punctuality—being late will definitely get you deducted a lot of points! Other than that, his projects are pretty straightforward—it's a bit heavy but manageable and he's a pretty chill grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Travis is a wealth of knowledge when it comes to art- you can tell he cares about his students and tries to make class fun and reasonable. Highly reccomend

Drawing Concepts is an easy A if you do the drawings and follow Travis's directions for each drawing assignment. He does not use canvas and uses a blog instead which can be hard to keep track of because he doesn't post the assignment due dates on canvas. You do have to do an artist presentation in his class, and he can be a harsh grader with it.

Webster is an incredibly sweet person - he's really found the balance between making a class generative and productive without making it hard or overloading his students. He's also very understanding. I'd recommend anyone take a class with him.

Best teacher in English at VT. I took his class in Fall 2021, and got an A+ in Mr. Webster's class. He is good at making examples and inspiring you on topics and things to write on paper. Grades were given very generously, even the final draft were based on completion. In short, just take his class.
Dr. Webster is a wonderful professor and his teaching his first-rate. Were I given the chance to, I'd take his class again in a heartbeat.

Dr. Webster is one of the nicest people I have ever met. I had him for 1106. The research for the class is a whole lot of work but it is broken into parts and he gives you feedback on all the parts. He grades on effort and the work you put in, so you end up with an A if you do everything.

The best teacher I have ever had, he's so compassionate and understanding. I had him for 1106 and I think the only way you get anything less than a b is by really just not trying at all. Overall just an amazing class.
His class is very fun and he gives great feedback on rough drafts and before every class makes sure everyone is doing well while always wanting to learn something new.

Travis is a profoundly caring and compassionate human being. He has a great sense of humor, is willing to dive deep in class sessions, and views students and people first. Completely genuine and brilliant. Cant recommend him enough.
He's super chill and made the class not super difficult. If you have the option to take the course over the winter, do it!
Took his class over the winter. Very laid back and personable and grades fairly. Class is fine if your group is solid, otherwise the class will not be good.

Overall not a bad class with Dr. Lewis. He is a pretty chill dude, can be a bit "extra" at times with his examples, but honestly not that bad of a class. No text book is necessary, do have to buy Harvard business casepack. Make sure you do the reading before the exams as most exam questions are apply class topics to reading. Group work in class too
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Lewis is a pretty laid back, down-to-earth guy who clearly cares about the subject and wants to challenge students. The tests can be a little rough, but the bulk of your grade comes from group work. Even if you're not a business-minded person, if you read what you're asked to and really think about the work, you'll do just fine.

Professor Lewis was a practical, funny, and honest teacher. He was always looking to accommodate assignments around the needs of the class. Lectures were to the point and no fluff or unnecessary information was ever a major class focus. This class is full of group work, so if you are stuck with an unproductive group, it could be a drag.

By far the worst professor I have ever had. Lectures are textbook paragraphs copy and pasted to printer paper. Extremely harsh grading structure, i.e., follow her proof format to a T or get points taken off. Horrific office hours experiences. I witnessed her belittle, yell at, and blow up on students for asking basic questions. Dropped the course.

Tough grader when it comes to tests and homework. her notes is only writing she writes whole paragraphs about math. if you ask questions she could disregard your question and say its dumb but does explain pretty well.

Her in class notes are unreadable because of her style of teaching. She writes in paragraph form so that everything is completely clumped together. She goes really fast through the notes, and her handwriting is sloppy so its hard to keep up while interpreting what she wrote. Doesn't explain concepts well, whole class gets confused together.
Unless you enjoy taking notes in paragraph form for the entirety of class, this is a must avoid

Julia pretty much just repeats whatever is said in the textbook. There is honestly no reason to go to class especially since all her lectures are online(the only good thing about her class). The online lectures are the only reason I passed since her in person lectures are often very confusing and her handwriting is awful.

It's true that Julia mostly recites textbook material in her lectures, but that's okay as long as the professor knows what they're talking about, which Julia most certainly does. While she is great at answering questions, her homework assignments are quite difficult and graded scrutinously for an already confusing course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worse teacher ever. Can not function well in the classroom, terrible teacher, she grades extremely hard on written homework assignments. By the end of the year more than half class either dropped out or dint even bother showing up because she was such a bad teacher. Genuinely curious how she ever got a job here but yeah she's so bad.
Horrible... horrible professor. Lectures are extremely sloppy, homework is graded very harshly it almost seems impossible to get right.
Very tough grader and hard to follow in class as lectures are in paragraph form. Very specific with what she wants and gives little to no partial credit. I recommend avoiding her at all costs.
Pretty much just pukes textbooks chapters into the lecture and is pretty bad at class interaction. No review sessions for exams and homework is graded very harshly for some reason
Terrible. Lectures make no sense and in paragraph form. Very sloppy handwriting and does not give reliable resources to learn. Avoid at all costs
No comment

Truman is the worst professor I have had the displeasure of taking at Virginia Tech. Dense lectures mainly consist of regurgitated textbook material and difficult homework that has no worked solutions. I first-hand witnessed her yelling at students during office hours. My friends also taking Discrete got confused by my homework problems. AVOID.

Do the homeworks and do them right; correct them if wrong. Tests are the major portion of grade. For Discrete, I recommend doing the WebAssigns at least a few days in advance to be able to follow the lecture properly. Engage and participate in class. Accessible outside of class and answers questions, but don't be afraid to ask.

She is incredibly smart. That being said, sometimes its to the detriment of her efficacy. I knew my shit leaving that course but the B+ wasnt indicitave of that, she is very particular on wording and phrasing and class is very lecture heavy with notes in paragraph form. I would take her again, but you have to know what you're getting into
Avoid at all cost.

He can be very condescending when responding to your questions. If you don´t understand a topic he can be very rude. Dont get me wrong he knows his stuff but the rambling and going off topic does not contribute a lot positives to the class. It is very discussion based and interactive based
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tsarouhas is highly knowledgeable and passionate, but the course offers few graded assignments, leaving little margin for error. Expect rigorous grading on timed, closed-note quizzes, midterms, and a final paper. If you're okay with an A- or B+, the material is absolutely worth it.

Dr. Tsarouhas is an amazing professor who really cares about the subject he teaches. His lectures are very engaging, however he goes off script from the presentations for pivitol information, so don't skip or you'll miss out on 80% of the material. There are very few grades in the course, so the final paper and exam are very important.

Dr. Tsarouhas is an excellent professor. He's a super smart guy and very intelligent on the subject matter. His course is comprised of purely lectures, but they are informative and interesting. His quizzes and tests can be a bit tough. He can also be a tough grader, so be sure you're writing what he wants. Would absolutely take his class again.

I had him for PSCI 2064 and loved him! The quizzes are based on what he says in lecture so you need to pay attention but he is passionate about everything he teaches. The essays were a bit challenging and he grades hard but if you ask him any questions about it he will guide you in the right direction. He genuinely cares about his students!!

Great guy. Quizzes are based almost entirely lecture content that he says in class, NOT what is on the powerpoints so you actually have to go to class to get notes. Tough grader on papers. Overall nice guy and appreciates when you participate in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Professor! Friendly and lenient with grades. Will take his course again.

(Actually took 3166). Great professor who really knows and enjoys what he's talking about. Willing to discuss subjects outside class material as long as it's relevant to learning more about IR. A lot of reading and writing. Difficult tests but he graded kindly. Lectures are often hard to understand, but he's accessible outside class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I LOVE PROFESSOR TSAROUHAS. He cares so much about his students and its clear he LOVES WHAT HE TEACHES. I loved his class so much I signed up for European Unions in the Spring because he is the teacher. Even online, he was engaging and always wanted his students to flourish. His class was hard, but hes very amenable and gives great feedback! 15/10
He was just an okay professor. Full of himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved having him as a professor, I would take his class again!

I really liked this class and teacher. He's really nice and funny and the class is pretty easy. You don't need to come to class, attendance isn't required but he will notice if you're not there. He's very nice if you're sick and miss class. Lots of group projects, only downside is he is a hard grader and grades things to his own personal standard.

Attendance is not mandatory, but necessary. There will be mini in-class assignments to help boost your grades. Doesn't give the greatest feedback on projects, but is a lenient grader. Although some of his teachings don't align with the textbook, they are effective. As long as you put in the effort, you'll pass and pick up some useful tips.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy but i think he uses the sales skills he does have to make you think he knows what he is talking about when in reality he is pulling thoughts out of his a**. He rips into students presentations for stuff that we haven't been taught yet and keep in mind we had very little time or guidelines for the project. He is also SUPER ARROGANT.

Dr. Turner is a great professor. He sets you up well for an intro sales class, even if you aren't interested in sales like I was. He sets you up for real-world projects and communication skills. There are 3 group projects throughout the year, but they aren't difficult.

Im glad this semester is over. Like what the other review says, this is the most unorganized class here. Dates change on the syllabus just about everyday and nothing is really updated on canvas. If you try to email him about something important he probably wont get back to you. If he does itll probably be extremely passive aggressive.

This has to be the most unorganized class I've taken at VT. Assignments were posted on canvas but with wrong due dates, test scores wouldn't be posted for weeks even though they were graded automatically online. Even if you complete an assignment and turn it in, there's a 90% chance it'll come back as "missing" and have you talk to the TA about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: He just starts doing random examples and then test you on the material he was supposed to teach you about. He makes several mistakes every class and you will never actually complete any problems. His "textbook" is more like he rambled on about random things, and then sold it to student. He tells you if you go to his office, he will lower your grade
He's disorganized, writes small on the board, and can't hear or understands students's questions. But his tests are easy enough and he did give extra credit opprotunity.

Though he is a nice person, he is a a terrible professor. His notes are a complete mess - and, by the way, require constant correction - and he doesn't even let us practice as often as we should. Not only is it hard to hear him at times, he keeps making his notes unreadable. Finally, it's stupid to have only exams determine our grade.

This prof is the best in the department period. I have had many of the good ones, including Arnold. However, Turner takes the cake. He cares, explains extremely clearly, and covers material thoroughly.

He was really interested in making sure that each student was understanding the material. His class isn't too much work out of class, we only had 5 homework assignments all semester. Just go to class and you should easily get a B.

Very friendly. Spends all of class doing problems, but needs near-constant correcting. I sit in the front row, yet cannot see what he is writing due to how small he does it. Can barely hear him, either.

This calculus class was the very first class I took at Tech as a freshmen last year! I was really scared but Turner was a lot like my high school teachers; friendly, available, easy, and funny! Take him for Calc 1205 if you can!

The lectures were lengthy, but the demonstrations were memorable. The homework problems are challenging, but they prepare you for the exams. Definitely go to office hours! Dr. Turner explained complex problems with great clarity, and made physics make sense. He kept pace and finished the content early, so there was time for review.

Dr. Turner was a pretty good professor. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities (definitely make use of them) and for the final added a few unexpected curves, which was nice. He definitely wants you to succeed, but make sure you pay attention during the lectures and do the practice problems.

He definitely isn't the best lecturer, I as well as many of my friends had trouble staying awake during his lectures. While there is very little leniency in half credit given and rounding up grades, Dr. Turner does try his best to help you learn the material. If you can, do go to office hours even if you aren't struggling.

DO THE HW and get good grades on it this will carry your grade in the class. There are many extra credit opportunities, go to class and listen to lectures he explains things in depth. He also communicates very well with canvas as well as emailing him. He also brings his dog to his office hours near the time of the final. Great teacher.

Dr. Turner is an understanding teacher, he wants to help when the Physics department is extremely strict. Do the homeworks and get good grades and that will carry your grade for the semester. Professor turner has great lectures, does examples in depth, and answers questions alot. He's a nice guy but the physics department will make him seem strict.

Insanely tough grader will take off points for the smallest things and with such little assignments it makes it impossible to get anything over an 85. Tells you to be more detailed one time then will say too much detail the next. Criteria is not super clear and will drop points because he skims instead of actually reading reports.

(FOR AC LAB) Great professor and an all around good person. A very well set up class, and felt like I actually learned something applicable to the future. A little heavy workload for a 1 credit, but probably one of my favorite ECE classes so far. Highly recommend!

Very caring and helpful professor. Probably the best choice for IDP although his grading can be harsh (this seems to just be the standard for the course). Definitely a nice person and I had no issues with him at all, just get ready to work a lot on your project. He is understanding and gets that we have a lot of other classes to work on as well.

Dr. Milburn is one of the most caring professors I've had at VT and gives excellent feedback to students on their project. However, this course is a very heavy workload for a 2 credit hour course so use your resources well if you get stuck and do not procrastinate.
Awesome professor for an overall mid class.

Amazing professor!  He cares so much about his students, gives lots of feedback, and is super accessible outside of class.  The class is really challenging with any professor but he is absolutely the best and makes the project as doable as possible.  I would absolutely take this class with him again!
GOAT

Easily the best professor for this course. He provides exceptional feedback on reports and is very hands-on and welcoming during office hours. Since I was in a group by myself, he let me turn in work 2-4 days after it was due for the rest of the class. Would definitely recommend him.

Dr. Milburn is the prof to have for this course. The projects are tough but he is chill and friendly and he also really knows his stuff. You can go to his office hours or schedule times to meet with him. He doesn't just give you the answer but works with you to help figure out what's wrong to make sure that you learn the stuff too. Take him!

Dr. Turner really loves evolutionary biology and tries to share that enthusiasm with the class. However, his voice is so boring and he talks so slowly that it is impossible to follow what he is saying without getting frustrated or falling asleep. He basically just reads off powerpoints so there no real point in attending class. Most dull class ever

Even though his voice is a boring, I find the information very interesting and he makes it very easy to understand if you go the class and pay attention. If you look at his old tests his tests are very similar and easy to understand. He also gives out extra credit which is very helpful. Overall he is very straight forward and helpful.

I had heard really awful things about this professor before taking his evolutionary biology class, but I have to say he proved every one of them wrong. He is extremely helpful outside of class and really cares if his students are understanding the material. Not to mention that he is very sympathetic to the course load from other classes.
very monotone and extremely boring. spent more time daydreaming and doodling then listening to him. hated going to class and only went cause there was 9 people in the class, 15 dropped!

Probably the worst professor I have had at VT so far. I would not recommend him to anyone.  I was forced to withdraw from the class.  Tests are nothing like the lecture notes.  I am a deans list student.  "Class designed for fast learning, high IQ students" (he said that) Disagrees with many things in the textbook so no real point reading it.
Class was horrible, our tests sucked so bad that he had to let us do 15 points extra credit on the final to make him look better. He voice was monotone and he was egotistical and boring.

I feel that he has good intentions, but for me personally, his teaching style just made a tough subject tougher.  He speaks very ... deliberately, turns off the lights and uses pwr-point presentations all class long. Lots of ppl nod off during class.  Just hard for me to really learn the material in this setting. extra-credit offered .

I have to say that while he does have a seemingly monotone voice, he is very meticulous about his word choice and wants to make sure that his students understand every aspect of the class. he speaks slowly in order to speak accurately and avoid any confusion.  he is enthusiastic about his subject and is very accomodating to the students.

Turner talks at a snail pace in this horrible droning voice; sometimes he pauses for so long i could swear he's forgotten what he was talking about. One day some kid's cell phone rang, and when he went to turn it off (and it made a shutting-down noise) he kicked EVERYONE out, and still covered that material on the test. One of the worst bio profs.
Everything he says is monotone.  He shows no excitement for the subject.  I love Genetics, but he almost made me want to hate it.
Best genetics professor ever.  He is very smart and willing to help if you ask.  Hate to miss one of his lectures.
No Comments
No Comments
Dr. Thompson was a great professor, and a really interesting lecturer. She is a harder grader than most, but if you communicate with her and prove you are engaged, you will do just fine.
She has great values and interesting projects, but what she teaches is confusing. She's all over the place, which makes it difficult to participate.

Professor Thompson is a terrible grader. She would take off half points for small mistakes and it wrecked my grade. I was not the only one with this issue. When I confronted her about it, her response was basically just to ‘do better work’ despite ridiculous assignments. There are so many other nicer professors to take- avoid Prof Thompson.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kinda scatter-brained and not great at getting to the point. Very bright woman and super interesting to engage with, but she's not the best at engaging with her students. Yelled at a groupmate for asking a question about a final and doesn't give clear instructions. If you like intensive discussion though she's good!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Thompson is so kind! It's clear that she loves her job and being in the classroom. There were a few parts of the class that felt confusing, but she was really open to feedback and doing her best to make the class as accessible as possible. Definitely a great professor and I enjoyed my time in this class! Just be prepared to be called on.

Kinda feels like he knows that most students take his class to check a box, and responds by grading harshly. He gave me 2 Bs on papers that I (and from his comments, he) felt completely or nearly completely met the assignments' requirements. He gives good feedback *after* he grades, but not before, which makes it difficult to meet his expectations.
This class was a breeze. If you just attend class and do all assignments, you'll pretty much just finish with a 100%. Also Saunders was awesome because his class was focused on horror movies.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Just mechanics of writing but most of it is common sense. Aside from the papers, there isn't any valuable content provided in the lectures by the professor. Class environment was very quiet and unresponsive (9am MWF), but his attempts at getting the class involved (just standing there in silence for 5 minutes) often didn't work.
The main grades in the class are the papers. There are only 3 main papers so it is not that much writing. If you ask for help he will help. Super understanding and laid back professor.

I found all the assignments to be very reasonable and fairly easy to do. His lectures on some things discussed in the textbook all made sense. There did not to seem to be any extra credit and I do not think he accepts late work, but he gives you a lot of time to do assignments (and the assignments are pretty easy - if you are good at writing).
He is very understanding and the work load is very manageable. definitely one of the best professors I've had.

I was one of the only students that would actually show up for his class so he was very nice and willing to help in any way possible. His interest in horror was obvious and made the necessary reading and projects interesting. Would take again 10/10

Saunders is wonderful. I used to really dislike English until he taught me. Seriously cares about his students and gives many opportunities for revising. As long as you do the work and take in his input, you are good. Great as a person and professor.
He tries to frame the class to teach you how to do the final project, some of it helps but most of it feels like busywork. Wasn't that worth it in my opinion.

All around cool guy. He allowed revisions on essays and helped me improve my writing. Super patient After leaving the class, I know more about the lives of animals and want to keep writing in general.

Ms. Tydings is by far the BEST professor I've had at Virginia Tech. She's so cool and relates to the students. She has wit and experience in life and can read each individual so well. When it comes to work she gets serious so you just have to take the class seriously. Don't procrastinate and you will definitely benefit from this course.

Ms. Tydings is extremely fair and helpful. She honestly does care about her students even if it is hard to tell. She responds to e-mails quickly and is always willing to skype if she can't meet in person. Overall a great class and I learned a lot.
Very Helpful if you take the time to meet her during office hours. Different yet effective in teaching the material using real world connections.

Highly unprofessional professor. For a communications class, I find it ironic that she has such a lack of ability to communicate with her students. Never responds to her e-mails and posts assignments last minute (if ever). I don't know how she expects us to do our jobs as students if she can't do hers. Really outrageous and unacceptable.

The class consists of weekly labs, some in-class activities, and a final project. Professor Vance is a great person who respects students. My main issue with him was that he didn't even post the grade for the final project, so I couldn't see what I got for several assignments.

Most interesting professor I've had at VT. Lectures oftentimes incorporate fun and interesting hands on learning approaches that really helps students stay engaged and interested. I've never had a class that I genuinely enjoyed going to except this one. The assignments can be time consuming but imo are pretty interesting also. Great professor.

There's a lab about every other week and a reading quiz. Start the labs ahead of time- you will need help and the best way to reach the teacher is before or after class. Does NOT respond to emails. Didn't grade labs or midterms until the very last minute (the day that grades were due for the semester).

Pros:
Good communicator and lecturer
I learned a lot in this class and it was fun
No textbook
Open book final
Cons:
$70 to access program used in class
Doesn't respond to emails
Doesn't grade assignments until the last second -the midterm hasn't been graded and it is finals week.
Weekly labs
Group midterm - 30% of grade
Final - 30% of grade
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In the Field study, she was clear and made it known exactly what needed to be done and when it was due. If you are in the Human Development Department, you are gonna have to take the field study through her. whatever field study you choose, will decide your grade a couple of short essays and some hour's forms are the only things you have to do.

I put hilarious as a tag because this is what this professor is. She's extremely rude. I asked if I could work as a substitute teacher for my service learning hours of HD 4694 and what it entailed. She got angry because she's unintelligent and didn't get it. She then roasted me and said I wasn't ready or prepared to take the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would recommend staying as far away from this professor as possible. Does not care about well-being of students, completely unreasonable, unhelpful, and rude. If you email her, you might receive a degrading response with no empathy, which is ironic for a human service professional. Tech can do better than this with a highly ranked HD program.

One of the rudest people I have ever been in contact with.  Completely unapproachable in email and in person, and if I didn't have to take her courses I wouldn't.  Has no empathy for anything which is confusing because she's teaching about Human Services and how to deal with people.

I can safely say this is the worst HD teacher at tech. Completely unapproachable, no clear standard of grades, assignments weren't clear on what she was expecting. As a former human service worker, it's surprising to see how little empathy she has for others, considering that's literally part of the job
I havent even had her as a professor yet, but she has been NOTHING but rude to me via email. If I didnt need her field study class to graduate, I wouldnt even bother.

Knowledgable on the course, but horrible professor. She's a tough grader and unapproachable. You can't use your laptop to take notes - all hand written. There are no exams, which felt like a plus but not enough assignments to alter your grade. She is rude in email responses and makes it feel like she doesn't care about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely rude.

I took my field study with her. It was incredibly easy, but she is very rude and not an enjoyable professor to have. I only had to deal with her online and even through emails and Canvas postings she managed to be mean and judgmental. As long as you turn in things on time and get all of your hours you will get an A.

This class was so easy, she read straight off the power points and had open-book quizzes. She is a horrible teacher though, doesn't care at all about the students and always has an attitude. Don't bother asking a question or trying to talk to her in her office hours, she will just be rude. Worst teacher in the HD department by far

This class was probably the easiest class I've taken so far at VT, but with the worst teacher here. She didn't seem to care about any of her students and had an attitude with every thing a student had to say. I would recommend finding another teacher because in my opinion the easy A was not worth the entire semester with this woman.

All of her classes are easy. To get an A you need to attend and finish work. Don't buy the books- they are never used. She is one of those professors that you might not LOVE (boring and abrasive) but she is a good resource to have in the HD department so if its your major I'd suggest taking some time to make sure she knows your name and likes you.

She was not very helpful and sent out rude emails frequently. She doesn't practice what she teachers about helping professions. Don't bother buying the textbooks because they are not used in class. While attendance is not mandatory, she does in class assignments that are a big part of your grade. On the upside, it's an easy A.
Great to work for as an assistant. She'll work with people around cir****stances but doesn't like being taken advantage of. Very experienced with the classes. Great person to learn from.

This is one of the easiest classes I have ever taken at VT, and she is one of the nicest teachers. She brings candy every Friday, and never takes attendance. You have about 5 written assignments due, but they were all so easy and considering this is a writing intensive class you definitely luck out. She's the only professor who teaches the class ri
Very easy class because Mindel makes it easy. Attendance not required but lectures are engaging and helpful. Assignments are as easy as it gets

Professor Mindel was very kind and personable. The only downside to this class was the mandatory attendance, but as long as you don't miss a bunch of classes you are fine. He always made an effort to get to know a little bit about each of the students in his class and seemed to really care. Overall, a great professor and would recommend him.
Really cool professor, makes the class extremely fun and engaging by using real world examples that we can relate too. Take his class, super easy.
Very funny and caring professor. Lectures were very entertaining and informative. I don't know what the last reviewer is talking about, Professor Mindel made this class very fun.

Most boring class I have ever taken, and it was at 4pm which is prime nap hour so it was difficult to stay awake. The material is better suited for an online class if I'm being honest. But if you have the slides and can fill out the study guides completely before exams, you're pretty much guaranteed at least an 85. Nice guy just super boring.
Mandatory attendance is the only con. Funny guy class not too hard
Makes a class everyone dreads enjoyable and informative.

Chill guy. Not outstanding, not evil. He was fine. Lots of homework (Mastering Physics) - no curve when I took the class. He does do pre-quizzes, however, which can boost your test grades. Lots of i-Clicker questions. He immediately disappears after lecture. There are better professors, but he won't destroy your grade.

Honestly, I don't understand the bad reviews about him. In my opinion, he was an awesome professor whose lectures were pretty easy to follow. The only reason the difficulty is so high is because of the exams. However, there are so many other grades that it's still easy to earn above a 90. Also, he really does make a 3-step problem into 10 steps.

He is a very nice guy and does a really good job at answering questions and emails. However, he makes problem way harder than they need to be. I will look at how another teacher worked out the same problem, and it would be three steps instead of ten. Overall, he is a nice guy, but could definitely be a bit confusing.

Made the 2305 lectures very engaging with demos and interesting thought experiments, was all around a great guy and very responsive to questions in email and after class. Only thing is he moves pretty quickly through lectures and sometimes misses questions as they come up.

Lots of demos and questions to help review in class. Pretty good lectures overall but can be quite boring at times. Homework is structured to get you to learn new material before reviewing and practicing in lecture. I liked Prof. Scarola as a lecturer, I just wasn't amazing at the material and could've worked harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Scarola is very knowledgable about physics and clearly knows what he's talking about. However, I didn't find his lectures very engaging. He wasn't always the best at explaining things and it was sometimes hard to follow his process. His jokes were decently funny and the experiements he performed in class were at least interesting.
Very Handsome and Very Smart

The only thing that allowed me to pass this class was all the extra credit. Scarola moves on from different topics too fast. Most of the learning is done outside of class with online homework. The homework is confusing and requires some extra googling to finish. In class we do several iclicker questions that do not make any sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Handsome and smart.

She gives us time to work on outlines with her there for questions and we are allowed to turn in multiple rough drafts to her to keep getting notes. Sometimes there is a quick turnaround for rough draft and speeches but you can choose at the start of the semester which schedule you want so it depends on you. Pretty understanding and wants to help

Ms V made the class environment super comfortable to ask questions and gave lots of feedback. She was clear on the rubric and each speeches requirments so it was easy to get good grades. Really nice and always remembered my name and things she cared a lot about students

She provides directions on what she wants but it isn't always clear and she is picky on speech topics. The professor will give feedback late to where you're on a crunch to complete the work for the speech with her critiques. I liked the material of the class and would take it again with another professor.

This man speaks in corporate buzzwords. Freaky. Generally pointless lectures and very strange explanations of trivial engineering concepts. The semester started of promising but slowly devolved into little more than a slog. Most infuriating was the absolutely glacial pace assignments were graded. He wasn't the absolute worst, but his class was.

Easy class but his lectures were very boring and he would go on a long tangent about things. He was very nice and offered office hours anytime but sometimes he would not answer questions clearly. Rubric would be unclear as well.
You wont learn what you are supposed to in 1414. you wont make a final project and dont need to use a lab. easy class but felt useless
Awesome proff. Had him my first semester of engineering. He really made into to engineering enjoyable
Super kind and understanding professor! Class was fun and engaging. Lectures are easy to understand, and the work is very manageable. One paper due a week.

Best professor I've had at VT. Cares a lot about her students and genuinely wants the best for them. It's a fun and engaging class; make sure you show up because participation matters. Show effort on the assignments, be engaged in class, and you'll have no problem getting a good grade.

Best Professor at VT. It's an easy class to pass and you also learn a lot with her. I would always look forward to going to class cause she made it fun and also we became friends in there. There is a paper due every week not including the when the book report and final presentation are due but, they are easy and pretty much just completion grades.

Vicky is an outstanding teacher. She cares about her students and tries to know everybody personally. By the end of the year she felt more like a family member/friend than professor. I would typically look forward to class and suggest it to anybody.

Professor Dierckx was my favorite professor this semester. You can tell how much she cares about her students, and how understanding she is. There's a paper due for this class roughly every week, but they're only about two pages long. All work and projects in this class are manageable. There's an attendance grade, so attendance matters!!

Vlad was truly one of the best teachers I've had. Although the class was very hard, the manner in which he teaches it makes it so much easier. If you show up to class, you will be set. He is very respectful and understanding. I took his class in Spring 22, but I'm writing this now because I realized how amazing he was.

Vlad wanted his students to succeed, he would hold review sessions before every exam. These sessions were helpful as they often resulted in us working through the same exact problems that would be on the exam. If you can get over an accent you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take his class if you can!!! Although there was weekly quizzes, Vlad held AMAZING reviews before each exam/quiz that were a must if you wanted insight on test question content/hints! He wanted everyone to do well and it really reflected in his teachings. My favorite professor so far! All my friends were jealous he was such a good teacher lol

Such a great professor who taught me that non-fiction can be creative and enjoyable. Grades mostly come from essays (they are super easy, and you can write about whatever you want). You also do weekly canvas posts that are like a small journal entry. There's one project about you that you can have fun with. Super sweet and understanding!

As a beginner writer, Prof. Vollmer made me feel more comfortable than I could've imagined to express my thoughts and emotions in however way I pleased. He was so encouraging when giving critiques for essays and always seemed so excited to read our writing. I wish everyone, no matter their major, took his class. He was like the dad I never had!

This class is fantastic. I absolutely loved it. It's pretty writing-intensive, but it's a creative writing class, so that going without saying. We had daily or weekly writing assignments (two pages on a prompt) and two longer short stories for workshop. This class will definitely help you improve as a writer. And Vollmer is foxy.

Dug this class hard. He's funny, so the class is fun and students actually participate. He cares about students and their writing. Not only does he have interesting writing insights, he uses good reading materials and, as a bonus, tells good stories.

I absolutely LOVED his class! He is really down to earth for an English teacher and never assigned too much work. Definitely recommend him as a professor. He often cuts class early (or cancels), makes funny jokes, and isn't bad to look at either! Wish I could have had him for Engl 1105.
