Prof. Vollmer's creative writing class was awesome--I would definitely recommend taking this class...you'll get an easy A if you just turn in the assignments. He's really funny and the class was a blast.....Vollmer = hot.

I took Dr. Voshell for both Phage Hunters classes and truly enjoyed them. She is extremely kind and will work with you during issues that may arise (attendance and experiments) and never gets frustrated if you are confused, as long as you are trying. I finished with a 99 and 100. Highly recommend!!
Voshell is a very kind woman that enjoys what she teaches. Phage Hunters is a very easy class as long as you participate. I finished this class with an easy 100, and enjoyed every bit of this class.

She is a great instructor and the TAs are amazing too. It is very easy to get an A in the class, you just have to do the notebooks and a few assignments that are very easy. The class is really fun, at the end there is a poster and a presentation but it is not bad at all. She is also super understanding and just a great person in general.

Dr. Voshell is amazing. She is very passionate about the coursework but patient with students and wants them to learn. She isn't a strict grader so the environment is low stress. Highly recommend taking her.

She really cares about the subject and will make sure that you know what is going on. She is a patient answerer of questions and will let you ask any questions (and won't interupt!). She is a flexible person, and was always empathetic to a hard working student.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Voshell is one of my favorite professors here. She is quirky and funny which makes the lectures enjoyable. The first exam is ridiculously hard but all of the other tests are pretty easy. I highly recommend taking Dr. Voshell for any class.
Very very nice. Extremely understanding and caring. One of my favorite instructors.
Creative and passionate, will help you if you ask and he will explain it. Creative freedom, enriching lectures.

clive is a really nice guy who is passionate about architecture. he does tend to yap a lot, but you'll appreciate it later on. he is a very easy grader, so as long as you try, you'll be fine. his accent is also super funs

Clive is a great professor, sometimes over-explains things but they will be useful later on. He gives creative freedom to a degree without being detached from your work, and his feedback is valuable. He is not as intimidating as he looks!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clive was a great professor to have as my first semester in Architecture. He is very thoughtful and kind in his suggestions and respectful of our creative process. He gives enough time to work on all projects.

Clive is an amazing first year professor. While we do have some long lectures, he also gives you plenty of uninterrupted time to work on projects in class which is very helpful. All his assignments are clear and manageable and all projects are continuous which makes finishing them very flexible within the time frame of a semester.

I like Clive; he grew on me throughout the semester. He's nice and gives good (and kind) feedback. He will not hate on anything you make even if it deserves hate. Sometimes he talks for too long though and that does get a bit annoying, but I enjoyed his project and class.

On one hand he talks like a knowledgeable design know-it-all. On the other, he appears to show a lack of real world experience and it comes off as nonsense. He talks so quietly you can't hear him from 3 feet away. He sometimes brings his kids to work, and for hours they look so forlorn and pathetic that you have to feel sorry them.
Nice guy, very helpful if you ask the right questions. I enjoyed his class. Don't be fooled by the "not mandatory" attendance he takes note. In the end, a good first year design professor to have.

Her class has little to do with sociology and is primarily just statistics and definitions of mental health issues. She teaches it fine but it is mostly just lectures and small group discussions. There are like 2 required papers for the whole class and those are the primary part of your grade.
Oh. My. God. This professor legit trauma dumps during her lectures. I understand that this class is Sociology of Mental Health BUT IT'S NOT SUPOSED TO BE ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH

Sociology of mental illness is taught incredibly poorly by this professor. If interested in the class, I highly recommend taking it another semester when a different professor teaches it. This professor is seemingly uneducated in Psychology and offers nothing to learn. The lectures are painful. Total grade comes from three exams and two papers.

very personable, may appear a little cold at first, but once you got to talk to her even in zoom meetings, I find her very friendly and helpful. You would learn a lot from her class, just do the work.

She is really good at explaining things, but you have to ask, so don't be afraid to do so. She is very approachable and willing to help, especially if you visit during office hours.  Students in my class shopped online during class, and then would complain about her, and then ask me for help. So don't be one of those people.
Stacy is a wonderful person and a great instructor.  She answers questions and takes the time to help you if you go to her.  Stacy is cheerful and I enjoyed her class a lot.
I had her for grad-level data analysis a few years ago- she uses PPT, kind of awkward, but SO HELPFUL if you go to her office hours.  I learned a lot.
Absolutely the worst teacher I have ever had, for any subject, at any school. Terrible classroom manner, uses ONLY powerpoint slides to talk about math.

Absolutely the worst instructor, of any kind, in any school, that I have ever had. The entire class is simply her showing hideous PowerPoint slides of information from an old textbook. None of the assignments are completed in a way that utilizes any of the slide information. All you need to do is (on your own!) learn to use SPSS. Terrible!
TERRIBLE teacher. Nasty person.
I took her Data Analysis class and thought she was really helpful. She went out of her way to help the students and make sure everyone understands the concepts and the hands-on ways to apply them!

With all seniors and graduate students, she teaches us like kindergardners. Notes are so long that you wish you had a gun to kill yourself-becuase she will not give them out. She likes to hear herself talk and will not listen you anyones opinion. God be with you if you take her classes!

Vogelaar has such a sleep-inducing voice so make sure to drink caffine before class. He doesn't teach very well and spends most of the class going through derivations rather than practice problems. Tests are very hard so don't study too much. Just go over the extra credit quizzes and the curving should boost you up. Attend for iclickers!

Vogelaar was a nice professor but very boring at times. I did not participate in class or pay attention other than the iClicker questions. However, the class itself is not too difficult, there are many ways to pass by doing decent in Physics Lab and the extra credit quizzes. I didn't pay attention at all and comfortably earned a B.

He's very passionate about electromagnetic topics since that's part of his research expertise. His lectures let you look closely at some experiments. He turned off the lights, let everyone come to the stage, and see or even manipulate the Helmholtz coil. He also hosts amazing review sessions (with free candies lol) before tests and the final.

He teaches really well. Dr. Vogelaar is really excited to explain to us the material, especially when it's about electricity and magnetism, and he is open to any questions about physics. Dr. Vogelaar also gave awesome review sessions before tests, and it definitely helped a lot of students. He even had us come close to see his demonstrations.
Phys2306 is not fun but he does not make it fun either. None of the video lectures help and they dont do a great job explaining a lot of the material.

Vogelaar doesn't seem to put a whole lot of effort into teaching this class. he doesn't prepare lecture slides, just messy photocopied notes. The class is unorganzied and hard to follow. He goes off on tangents a lot. The only thing that makes up for it is a ton of extra credit because almost everyone does poorly in his class.

No matter what teacher you have, this class is going to be difficult. At the beginning of the semester, he did not explain material well and assumed a lot of previous knowlege. This got better over time. He did give some extra credit, curved test grades, and had past tests from which to study. He didn't use scholar which was invonvenient at times

I enjoyed Dr. Vogelaar's class. The Mastering Physics is university required, although it is a pain in the butt. Though his class was difficult, I felt I actually learned the material. His lectures were occasionally cryptic, but he was always willing to clarify in office hours or by e-mail.

does not present the material well at all. his tests are borderline impossible and he assumes familiarity with extremely difficult subjects. class is barely beneficial due to his inability to teach. he is clearly a research professor with little to no teaching ability.

The first few weeks had many students wondering why they attended class, as the material was presented poorly. His notes are terrible: he just has handwritten photocopied diagrams that only have context if you ask about them specifically. He doesn't use scholar. His practice tests are only partially relevant to the real thing.
The recitation quizes will kill you. Master Physics is a pain in the but and takes for ever. His grading sysem is wierd. He only cares about getting through the material
Pretty much, he is simply average.  Class is OK, tests are OK.  The worst thing about the class was him using online homework, MasteringPhysics.com.  Besides that, he's pretty normal.

I like Professor Vogelaar as a person but when someone asks a question in class, he always says "look at my notes" and doesn't explain what he just wrote. He is better than others except Chang but giving us homework right after an exam and over spring break is just horrible. Try to take Chang if you can.
I will take anyone over Slawny, but this guy is not bad at all. I am very happy to have him as a professor.
The course is point based so you do not need to do every assignment to get an A. Attendance is also not mandatory, but highly recommended. There were many "extra credit" opportunities as well.

Doc White is amazing!! He really is passionate about what he teaches, and WANTS you to ask questions he really enjoys talking about finance and is really sweet. The class is VERY simple and I highly recommend it for anyone who needs the pathway 5a because you retain a lot of valuable information afterwards too.
Doc white my is my GOAT
Doc White was a great professor, and the class was not super hard. He cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed.

Yeah this might be the easiest class I have ever taken. Take this class. Attendance optional, final/tests optional, lots of opportunities to get points, nice guy. And this class is actually practical and good information for your life.

One of my favorite professors at VT. Very passionate and energetic in his lectures, and had funny jokes. The work is very easy, and he has online lectures in case you miss class. I would 100% recommend his class, and if I had the option to, I would take another class with him.

Doc White is awesome! You can genuinely tell he loves what he does and wants you to learn so much. Class isn't mandatory- I still got an A as the class is points based, you decide what you want. Would take another class with him anytime!

Doc White sets you up for success. Attendance is not mandatory, class is on zoom and in person, and it's a point based grading system. Even if you never go to class you will get an A in his class as long as you try on the assignments. All of the information is useful for the future and he is happy to teach you whatever you ask.

100% take his class! He is such a great professor and the class is very easy. You will for sure pass if you do the bare minimum. Attendance not required and he offers Zoom too. Just wants his students to succeed and cares about his students a lot!
10000000% recommend best most caring professor at tech

It was an extremely easy class and all of the information was stuff that I will need to know. 

Attendance is not mandatory and he does offer a zoom option, but if there are not many people in class on certain days he will give out extra credit, so it's good to go to class even if it's via Zoom. Definitely recommend taking Doc White's class!
A great professor who will ensure that you'll pass the class!
Do all of the personal finance interviews, and then you will pass with shining colors. Go to class, he gives out extra credit for attendance often.

Doc White is an all around great guy and a great professor. The class itself is very easy, and you could do it all without even showing up to class, but there's definitely things to take away from showing up to class. If you're looking for an easy class, where you can learn genuinely valuable and important things, I would take this class.
Take him if you can. Great personality, very flexible, and always makes sure class is fun. The class is mostly online, so attendance is not as important, but will definitely help.

One of the best professors I've ever had at Tech! He made coming to lectures fun, and encouraged the class to ask lots of questions. Also had it to where you get to pick which assignments you want to do, so you can skip the exams and still get an A in the class. If anyone is taking personal finance, go with Dr. White. He is the man!

Very great professor! He knows how to teach and allows an ordinary person to understand finances. He is among my top three favorite professors at VT. He makes lessons entertaining and teaches some of the most helpful financial information ever. 110/100% would recommend taking any of his courses!
Completely online work but still very involved in his lectures. Teaches what's really important and has real life applications while still being helpful and engaging, totally recommend!
If you breathe you get an A. I did everything from home and finished with like a 104%! He's very funny and likes to be engaging for even a 9AM class which is nice.

Take this class. You basically just have to breathe to pass and the content is actually useful. Doc White is the best and will give you bonus points a lot of the time just for showing up to class. Operates on a point system and most of the work can't count against you.

Loved Doc White! Makes finance fun, and teaches you things for life, not just for the class. Uses a point system, so not all assignments are mandatory and it is a very easy A. Records lectures and all assignments are online, which was very helpful! Highly recommend this class and Doc White!

Doc White is kind, passionate, and knowledgable. Tallied up points instead of percentages, making it easier to earn a good grade. Ensured you learned the most important information simply if you listened to the lectures, and helped answer questions outside of lecture material too. Great TAs as well. 10/10.
Loved taking this class, very useful & Doc relates back to real world scenarios as he wants the best for you! Would highly recommend taking this class it does not disappoint.

Assignments weren't hard but were time consuming. Tests were identical to the assignments! Doc White always threw a freebie question or two in as well. You can pick and choose assignments; just do enough to earn a baseline # of points, and boom, you're done for the semester and have an A. I definitely chose to complete hw/quizzes over exams!!

This professor is easily the most understanding and funny one Ive had so far. Course content directly applies to life. Assignments are easy and Doc White (yes, call him that) is very willing to help out where he can. Practically breathe to pass.

Doc White is amazing. He loves what he teaches and it shows. The class was extremely easy because your grade was based on points. A lot of resources were provided. Classwork and quizzes were due every Sunday but if you miss one it's totally okay because of the point system. Easy A.

I took this class to fulfill a math credit and I'm glad I did. You don't even really have to come to class if you don't want to- he posts lectures online. But if you do, he does offer learning catalytic quizzes during class that add extra credit to your exams. The modules are easy and you can generally find the answers on quizlet. He's a good guy.

Doc White was a great professor. I took Personal Financial Planning as a math requirement, and I would highly recommend. He's super kind, has the best stories, and you can tell he cares so much about his students. Lectures can be boring, and he sometimes puts weird questions on tests/quizzes that I swore we never learned. Overall really great guy.

Best prof I've ever had. Genuinely cares about student success and participation isn't graded and you'll survive if you skip a solid amount of classes. Show up on Monday mornings after party weekends and you'll get extra credit if the class crowd is thin. Really knowledgeable and you'll only get a B if you never show or never try. Awesome guy

Doc White's class is likely the most useful class I've taken and will ever take in college. The material can be very dry (especially if you're not particularly interested in finance like me) but he tries his best to be engaging and can answer almost any question thrown at him. Come to class on days most people skip and you'll rack up extra credit.
Dr. White is an awesome teacher. He tries to entertain as much as he teaches. He pretty much throws extra credit at you. I definitely recommend Dr. White for any class he teaches.
Doc White is one of the best profs i've ever had. Super nice and understanding. Lectures are entertaining (well, about as entertaining as taxes and retirement funds can be). Highly recommend him.
Best professor hands down. You will regret not taking Personal Finance with Dr. White.

Dr. White is really easy going and is straight forward about the material being taught. All tests are online and open note so if you take notes on the lectures, you can pass with no problems. He teaches things everyone should know for life, not just your major. Also, show up because he gives random extra credit for attendance.
Dr White is an extremely intelligent instructor. You will not regret taking his class. He is  a bit fast in his lectures, so pay attention. He is also very casual and like to make his finance fun.
I really did not think "professor's pets" were a thing--let alone that professors would allow that. Professor White proved me very wrong. Guess it's true.

Professor White ABSOLUTELY has favorites and does not hide it. This creates lots of difficulty in the class and his grading shows his favoritism. He is a decent man and good at teaching; however, I worry about some of his ethics.
Doc White is a funny professor. Just participate, speak up in class, be involved in dairy and you'll be fine!
Good overall. To get an A just complete your work on time and youll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best summer class I'll ever take.
Always makes due dates clear far ahead of time, rubrics are exhaustive but informative, and the structure of the class makes everything easy.  Also she's the GOAT.

Dr. Wallwey runs 1414 like a workplace, where she is your boss and you are an employee. I really liked this because it felt like she saw us as people first then students. The class's assignments are not bad, but they sometimes feel like busy work, but Dr. Wallwey is really accommodating and if you bring it up with her, she will try to change it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wallwey was a great professor. ENGE 1414 is a fast-paced class, involving lots of team collaboration, but she did an excellent job teaching the course.
The class is fast-paced and jam-packs quite a few assignments in the course of a semester, but Dr. Wallwey has clear grading rubrics and is a fair professor.

Amazing professor. She clearly cares about her student's success. Also the freedom she gives for group projects is very fun. I looked forward to this class every day, she is a very entertaining professor as well.
Amazing teacher with a great classroom environment.
The absolute GOAT and makes the class a walk in the park.
You CANNOT fail this course as long as you're attending class and actively paying attention. I would absolutely retake this course or any others of hers!

Our first week was filled with fun games. But after doing SOLID WORKS you realize that the scores they give are horrible. I don't understand why they gave us low grades. I thought this class was here to raise my GPA not lower it. Cassie's attitude was terrible, she rarely looked me in the eye when I talked to her about assignments. Disappointed.
Her class isnt too hard if you show up and do the work. A lot of work time in class and a lot of group work as well. If you do the work you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class for 4 credits and I'm so glad I had Cassie as my professor. She is so personable and understanding of student needs and expectations. It's literally impossible to struggle in this class because she gives so much flexibility with assignments. The course itself is groupwork heavy and some outside of class but not excessive.
This prof's class is a free A if you turn in everything on time and just follow the rubric. The rubric aint even hard to follow tbh.
The professor is approachable and easygoing; highly recommended.

She is maybe my favorite professor ever. She is SO chill and cares about her students. She is so understanding; she doesn't care about deadlines or grades she just wants us to learn. Very accessible and eager to help. She tries to make class fun and wants us to get to know her and each other. I very much want to take a class with Cassie again!
Great professor. Take her if you can

Amazing professor, would always take time during class or office hours to explain assignments to make sure you get a 100. While a lot of the work is tedious or doesn't make sense, Dr. Wallwey and her TA's try their best to make sure you get a good grade in the class. As long as you put in some sort of effort and have a solid group, you'll get an A.

Prof Cassie's class was super structured and organized. For every assignment, she set clear expectations and gave a lot of feedback on why points were docked. She gives her students a lot of flexibility regarding extensions and missing classes. She is very enthusiastic, understanding, and kind. I highly recommend her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really nice teacher that cares about her student
Overall great professor and easy class - as long as you do the work you will be good, and she is very generous with extra credit and extensions.

I LOVE this this professor. She makes the class fun and is very forgiving with assignments. She also always has a good attitude. A big part of the class is a group project so there's a lot of independent work towards the end of the semester. Get along with your group because that is who you will be working with for the whole semester.

It was enge 1414 so honestly really class as long as you just do the homework. Professor Wallwey is nice, offers extensions and allows you to redo some assignments. Class itself can be a little bland but it's just general topics. Wallwey was pretty good at keeping the class engaging.
The best to ever do it. Class sometimes is a little boring but its intro to general engineering so its inevitable.

Easy to follow lectures, good at explaining software systems, supportive and responsive with feedback. Very easy to do well in this class if you participate and read the rubrics, which are well-structured and easy to adhere to.
Cassie is the best, we debate the syllabus at the beginning of the semester and she is VERY lenient with late work and absences. She is super caring and sweet, would highly recommend.
Had her for ENGE 1215 and 1216. Great professor, super caring and willing to work with and help students with the course. Would recommend her to anyone taking the intro ENGE courses.

BEST FOUNDATIONS PROF!! As long as you follow the guidelines in assignments and ask for extensions early, she is accommodating and helpful.

Nice, easy to talk to, understanding.

I LOVE her, she was genuinely such a kind person and made class so fun! She's very understanding, and provides extensions when needed. I had to ask for an extension because I was slammed with exams and she provided it because she understood, and she genuinely cares about student success.

Likes to open every class by asking her students 5 good things about the day. Very flexible with both attendance and assignments and overall understands the struggles of being a student. Prioritizes creating an environment with mutual respect.

Dr. Wallwey is the best at her job. Very kind and understanding about everything. She delivers content in a very clear and concise way. Cares a lot about her students and was always understanding with extensions and as long as you had a good reason for it she'd grant it. Very accessible after class and cares about the success of her students.

Cassie was one of my favorite teachers and really reminded me why I wanted to be an engineer in the first place. Early semester has a lot of writing, but last fall break is mostly teamwork. Cassie is really understanding for late work and absences, and she really listens to the classe

Dr. Cassie was awesome! She was super understanding if you ever needed to miss class. Every class she went over assignments that were due for the week. She was very open to feedback, too. She genuinely wanted us to do our best, and gave us in-class time for work. Her MATLAB and SOLIDWORKS lessons were very easy to follow. I highly recommend her!
Very good professor, all assignments had really clear rubrics, templates, and directions no matter how big or small.

Dr. Wallwey is an ideal intro to engineering professor. She is very kind, and understanding. She will give you an extension for virtually any reason. Attendance is mandatory, but if you can't make it (or just don't want to) she will give you an excused absence for anything. I would 100% recommend taking her.

Dr. Wallwey is probably the best professor I had this semester. She had by far the most humanity of any of my professors. She was always willing to give feedback and helped readjust me halfway through the semester when my grades weren't so good. If you are taking engineering, take Dr. Wallwey.

I had Cassie for both 1215 and 1216.

An amazing professor. She keeps the lectures pretty short and allows for in class worktime on group projects & assignments. Multiple opportunities for tutoring help, extra credit, and she has a very simple but nice make-up policy. 

Keep track of what time assignments are due though (5pm on fridays for me)

She genuinely cares so much about her students; she asked us about aspects of the class we didn't like and actually made immediate changes to accommodate complaints we had. She is extremely understanding of external circumstances and very very very lenient with turning in work if you have a reason. I 100% recommend her, and she makes class fun.

Cassie really made her class fun. She went out of her way to think of ideas to keep us interested and provided extra office hours when she gave out tough assignments. Said assignments could be completed by looking at class lecture slides but she still offered extra help. She cares about all her students and wants everyone to succeed.

My favorite professor so far. Students' time and energy is respected. Incredibly kind, engaging and qualified. Great at receiving feedback and often responded in an open discussion with the class. Clearly stated her expectations for her class and assignments. Easily accessible outside of class. Made assignments enjoyable. TAKE THIS CLASS!!

Cassy is the best. She's an extremely kind person and really understands her students as long as they communicate with her. She provides the most comprehensive rubrics I have ever seen and is really good with feedback as well. I'm having her again next semester and have told most of my friends to have her as well.

Prof Wallwey is great. She is very understanding if you have issues outside of class and will help you catch up. She is a sort of tough grader, but will allow you to resubmit many assignments for more points. Enge 1215 in general has very annoying projects and busy, but that is normal to the class, and does not reflect her teaching.
This is by far the best professor/ teacher  I have ever had in my life.

Dr. Wallwey is one of the best professors I have had so far. She is easy to reach outside of class, she gives clear instructions and feedback, and she ensures that everyone gets a fair shot at an A in the class. There are a lot of group projects, but that is for all ENGE 1215 sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really good professor, probably my favorite so far. I really enjoyed her class and you probably will too. She does what she can to help you succeed, and while there is a lot of group work, she does what she can to help you accommodate if issues arise. Attendance is monitored through a google form which is open for like 5 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Wallwey is a great professor. Gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and cares about her students. Had opportunities to redo assignments that I didn't get a good grade on. Very responsive with emails and helps outside of class with any questions on homework or MATLAB challenges.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Wallwey is a great teacher. It's her first year teaching at VT, but she really started off strong in my ENGE 1215 class. She's always enthusiastic about teaching the class and regularly interacts with informative stuff. I never felt tense going into the class because it was fairly laid back, but I still learned a lot. Highly recommend!

Professor Wheeler was a great guy to have during my first semester at VT.  He could explain complex political and socioeconomic topics in a way that I could understand and apply to my writing, and he gave great feedback on the papers.  The final project is a little tough, but I liked it as opposed to a final exam.

He is a really great professor, probably my favorite teacher ever in fact! His lectures are interesting and very informative. It's obvious that he cares about his students and really wants you to learn and understand the material. Only hard assignment is the final paper and presentation, but if you put in the work you'll be perfectly fine
Really enjoyed his lectures, strongly recommend everyone take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher (Grad Student) for a fascinating class! He kicked it old school with a chalkboard and I LOVED IT! Very awesome feedback on all assignments and really really fun activities for in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: i think staring at a brick wall would be more interesting than this class. he just talks into the abyss and highkey rude as hell. he seems to know his stuff but just reads off his computer and can be straight up rude in his feedback. If melatonin didn't exist, this class could easily be a substitute.

Dr. Williamson has amazing consulting experience. I struggled in the other project management class, but improved here. He's flexible, smart, always happy with good vibes, knowledgeable in AI, and excited to teach. Great ideas and advice, always willing to help—excellent prep for consulting careers. Amazing professor! :)

Dr. Williamson really knows his stuff with decades of project management and consulting experience. He's approachable, flexible, nice, and great at answering questions- overall great guy. Assignments can be tricky even with detailed instructions, but he's passionate about teaching and students.
very very hard grader and very confusing instructions. If it wast for my team lead I probably would have a very low grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is never clear about what he wants, on top of that waits till the last minute to grade everything. He waited till mid terms to give any feedback on our past five portions of our project, and he was kind of rude in his feedback. His TA pretty much told my group it was impossible to get an 100% on your project regardless how much work you put in
Wouldn't take his class.

MGT 2614

DO NOT TAKE HIM! The "Consulting Project" that you do in this course is unbelievably pointless and is a monster assignment that is graded super harshly. His lectures are boring and offer no guidance on what he is actually looking for. Never available and overall, just a rude guy. By far the worst professor I have had.

Prof. Williamson is a great teacher and is passionate about Project Management. You learn a lot in this class because he is a good lecturer, but the assignments ensure that the material sticks. There are weekly assignments that are manageable, and you have a class team that you complete deliverables with.
Prof. himself is super chill, nice, & caring. This course was straight forward and group project heavy. Daily kahoots as attendance, take home weekly exams for HW w/ 3 tries, & daily deliverables.

Literally the best Professor I have ever had. He is so sweet, genuine, and funny. He truly cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. Attendance is not mandatory but it is recommended as he gives out credit for participation, but he's super understanding if you're sick or something just communicate with him.

Williamson is the best, very laid back but does a lot of things that actually prove his points and teaches something. I like his philosophies behind the consulting work he has done, and he is a great contact to have as a teacher. I have had 3 different classes with him, and he does a great job making them worthwhile.

Super nice professor and really caring of his students, definitely wants them to do well. Lots of group work and projects but him and his TA give good feedback on the assignments. Really passionate about what he teaches and if you do the work and show up you'll get a good grade.
This my guy.
Professor Williamson is chill & cares about your success in his class.

Attendance is required, and the amount of material feels like a lot for a 2000-level course. Most class sessions are lecture-based. Exams are taken in person with Lockdown Browser, but they're manageable if you put real effort into studying the lecture content. She can be a bit slow with grading, but she clearly knows her subject well.

Widgeon is a sweet person. This class is just boring. Don't expect anything fun. Such boring material, and you need a good group at the beginning of the year to do well. Exams are overly hard with niche subject matter for no reason, so study hard (5 exams in total). Get a good group and make some friends.
Angela is a great professor and cares about students succeeding

Attendance mandatory and material is lowkey a lot for a 2000 level class. But in class is mostly just lectures. Tests are lockdown in person but they're fine if you actually try hard studying the lectures. She's a bit of a slow grader. She knows what she's talking about tho

Widgeon's lectures were boring and not well-explained. Pick a good group for the research project, as it is a full semester ordeal. She grades oddly, and it was easy to tell she put the group paper in AI to grade it. Not really a fan, but the class wasn't horrible.

i dont know what these other reviews are talking ab but i barely ever pulled up to class, like literally so rarely and i still got an easy A. maybe she switched things up since i took this class but i remember it being very easy

i do not like this woman. she is a tough grader and if she doesn't like you you're done. 

would recommend anyone else.

She was ok. Lectures are incredibly boring and her grading is wack. She doesn't give good feedback either. Class is a semester long project so pick a good group. Tests are online and the material is boring/repetitive. She doesn't really teach well and explains things weirdly if you have a question (not in a helpful way). Wouldn't take her again.
She's a nice woman, but behind the scenes she kinda sucks. Deducted points off an assignment and left only this comment "where's the pretty document?" All exams were online and big group project.

Dr. Widgeon was an interesting professor. I felt like her lectures were boring and hard to pay attention to. Additionally, she speaks egregiously slow and it can get frustrating. The largest grade is the research project, which is a group project. While I didn't find her class the most difficult, I definitely wouldn't take her again, if avoidable.

Dr. Widgeon was your average communication professor. Fairly monotone but had personality showing through. It's very apparent that she cares about her students as she made various changes throughout the semester to accommodate everyone's needs. Lots of super boring lectures and attendance is mandatory, but it's not the worst class ever.

Prof Widgeon is very nice but I had to learn a lot of the content by myself instead of relying on the material from class. The course has several 2 minute "presentations" in front of the class and 4 exams. The exam questions are kind of specific and cover 3-4 chapters. Prof Widgeon will let you fix assignments, and attendance isn't always taken.
Prof Widgeon is one of the nicest people on VT's campus, but the class is excruciatingly boring. Lectures are impossible to sit through and the attendance grading is wishy-washy.

All I'll say is that for the final exam last semester, she gave us a 125-question test (with both multiple choice and SAQs) and expected us to complete it in under 125 minutes. She is a good professor but is very impractical with the amount she gives compared to the time required to complete it. However, she taught the information in class well.

Professor Woolly is so passionate about journalism and taught me a lot about visual journalism. Class is mainly project-driven, some group and some individual. A few quizzes throughout the semester. Showing up to class is really important for learning and completing workshops, so don't skip. Big website design project at the end of the year.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Woolly is a straight G. The class was super easy and Woolly kept lecture interesting. I might be biased since I have experience with the adobe platforms we used. You also do not need to buy the textbook. I literally never opened it and got 100% on all the quizzes.
Great, genuinely kind, and well spoken Professor. Class is structured to include a lot of partner projects, but idk if that's woollys fault. Prof is really talented so you'll learn a lot from him
Jared is a great professor. You can't go wrong taking a class with him

I have him for photojournalism and AMR and I love his classes! Cares so much about his students and his classes are never boring. Absolutely hilarious and really cares about what he's teaching. Super easy to get ahold of outside of class and will answer your questions clearly and in-depth. Really cool guy overall!

Jared is by far one of my favorite professors I have had a Tech. He is passionate about what he does and wants you to succeed in his classes. He responds fast to emails and always gives you great help and feedback.

long lectures but learning about all the adobe platforms was great. super easy 5 questions quizzes after each topic. definitely the best visual media prof we have. he would go on little rampants often and not really stay on topic which would get annoying. do not buy the textbook you wont use it. otherwise great guy and good teacher

Professor Woolley is one of the best professors that I have had for Visual Media. He teaches you a variety of different skills that I have found really useful in classes outside of his. He makes his class very interesting and lets students go out on campus to get hands-on experience with cameras. He is very fair with grading too!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Jared is by far one of the best professors I've had at Virginia Tech. He's outgoing, incredibly helpful, and has a hands-on teaching approach. He is accessible to his students, and just all around someone you'd want to learn from. If you pay attention in class, you should have no problem getting an A.

Jared is the best hire Virginia Tech communication has made. He is accessible, nurturing, and truly wants his students to succeed. He can have long lectures but all the information is useful & I have applied as a grad. His assignments are challenging yet attainable. Jared focuses on each student and invests in them to reach their highest potential.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Be prepared for long lectures & finding yourself bored halfway through  long lectures. Learning about how to use the camera &  Adobe programs were helpful. I feel gypped on some of my grades. I thought I deserved an A & I always participated & put in effort. I think he was a bit nitpicky on his grading & not sure if it's bc his 1st sem. teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Worch is amazing! He is very down-to-earth and the course is designed very considerately. Only two midterm exams and no final exam. The final exam is supplemented by two other project-like assignments. I highly recommend taking Josh's courses. He gave a lot of extra credit too.

Dr. Worch made this class feel very laid back, for it being a 4000 level class. It felt as if he was just talking about things he was passionate about, and wanted us to know about- rather than it being his job to tell us. Had good banter with students, lots and lots of extra credit, genuinely hard to get below a C in this course. Amazing guy :)

He's a good professor but its still ochem so you still have to study outside of class. Theres extra credit on the take home problem sets and only grades 2 of the assigned problems. Theres 3 exams and he puts extra credit(5-15 pts) at the end of the exam thats not about ochem instead about his life or any off hand things he talks about in class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class revolves around participation "quizzes" on canvas twice a week, a 2-3 page packet every 3ish weeks, and 3 exams over the whole semester. His lectures are good and he's really funny and easygoing. I'm not amazing at chemistry but I still did well in here.

COMM 2124 - Sweetest professor ever. Make sure you go to class and actually pay attention during lectures or else you won't understand the slides nor will you pass the exam. She really wants her students to succeed which is amazing and something I admire. However, SOOOO many group projects. Can get really frustrating

Loved this class!! You get to work with an actual client. Very heavy on writing, work with a group for truly every assignment. Bit of a tough grader, but never gives unfair grades. Highly, highly, highly recommend taking this professor for this class.

Dr. Woods is a fabulous prof and PR cases is an extremely interesting course! You are graded on attendance, 2 major homework assignments (group case study papers that are easy), a midterm, and a final exam. Her lectures are engaging and she tries to be as interactive as possible. I am taking her again this semester because she was so good last sem!

I don't understand the Dr. Wyatt slander. He is easily one of the best lecturers in the ECE department (although a little snarky) and makes sure you learn the material. 40% of your grade being the final is pretty horrendous though but I've never found his tests to be that unreasonable. He can come off a little cold... but he's great at teaching.
He might not have the best personality but he beats almost all professors in this department in terms of teaching quality.
Look at the GPA database and let the statistics speak for themselves. 12 withdrawals and the lowest GPA average among all sections

He presents the material well, but you have to dedicate lots of time and can't afford to miss any lectures. He's a bit standoffish and struggles to answer students in a respectful way when they ask questions. Also, the tests were completely fair, idk what people are complaining about in other ratings - they're maybe a tad long but no curveballs.

The Dr. Cooper of signals, you either love him or hate him. Way harder than the other sections yet somehow his average gpa is about the same, so I feel like that says something. Not very accessible out of class though. Lanzerotti is about 5x easier but if you take this section it'll boost your already inflated ECE ego so there's that.

Worst professor I've had in ECE. Unapproachable and acts like he doesn't want to be bothered. Doesn't post solutions to practice tests, says they would "defeat the purpose of a practice exam". Exams have curveball questions unrelated to homework/notes/lectures. Only take him if you want to gamble your GPA and sanity. Take Lanzerotti if you can.

He is arguably the worst, most disrespectful instructor I have had. Stay away from his courses if you can. He doesn't give you many resources to properly prepare for exams, won't offer you feedback intended to help you succeed, and gives random, curveball questions on exams. Limited office hours, cancelled recitations, he does not care about you.
Very strict professor. Also takes forever to grade assignments. Avoid him if you want to save your GPA. Only take him if you really want to challenge yourself.

Wyatt is definitely a harder professor than Lanzerotti, however his lectures are much better and his test averages are consistently about 10 points higher. There's a lot of extra work, but his GPAs are still the same or higher than other sections. I learned a lot more than my friends did in Lanzerotti's but it is a much harder time so expect that.

"he has tough grading but good lectures."
Has unclear directions/expectations
Occasionally provides useful insight
provides convoluted, confusing lectures; cannot explain simple concepts because explanations are not self-contained
added grad curriculum to undergrad class then graded harshly on grad information without providing enough background

Most weeks, the homework was so difficult the single TA's office hours were packed. Not approachable at all, if you went to his office hours he acted like he didn't want to be bothered, but he was willing to answer questions during recitations. PHRASE YOUR QUESTION AS A NON-YES/NO. Didn't curve on HW or tests. Get Lanzerotti for an easy time.

His section of Signals and Systems is definitely more challenging, but it is not without reward. He explains concepts, does practice problems, and homework to reinforce lecture material, so you will learn as long as you put in the effort. He is a fair grader, though his test problems can be difficult. Would reccomend!

Not a particularly bad professor. Not very approachable in office hours and can be difficult to communicate with in person or through email. The final was a curveball, questions unlike anything in homeworks or practice tests, still really not sure what is up with that but otherwise was very straight forward for most things.

Took for both 2714 and 3574. One of my favorite professors. Both classes had a heavy workload, but the homework was essential for learning the material. For signals, the provided notes were extremely helpful in understanding the class. Attendance is highly encouraged, and the lectures are clear and helpful.

Solid professor for Signals. A lot of people opted to take Lanzerotti for this course because her work is optional and less difficult, but Wyatt will push you further in this course and he has a very detailed set of notes with multiple exam problems that allow you to self-study the material without having to go to Youtube, unlike other ece classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a good professor but his class is harder than the other sections. I would only recommend taking him if you are very good at academics, otherwise, look for someone else.

I took 2714 with Wyatt. He is very well-versed in the class topics and made very high-quality notes for the class (I used only the notes and didn't even bother looking at the textbook). He does, however, only give out homework/practice test answers in class and not on canvas in an attempt to increase attendance.

If you see this name look for another professor. His hw is unbelievably hard and unfair and  it ways a lot. He isnt very helpful he kind of just expects you to know what he saying and barely helps during office hours . Just look for another professor
Please save yourself and get someone else for data structures... the homeworks are totally unfair and the grading weighting is horrid.

Lectures are fast-paced but relatively clear, emphasizing walkthrough proofs. Notes are done on a chalkboard and aren't posted. Lots of textbook homework due weekly, with two uncurved midterms and a final that are similar to the homework problems. She's pretty good at teaching, but the class itself has a heavy workload.
3 exams, multiple choice is difficult, grading for frq is harsh

Lectures were imo super difficult to follow, she has an accent which makes it even harder to understand. She doesn't post notes and literally tells you to study for exams by looking back at your notes, so if you missed a class good luck. She doesn't post study guides & there are no curves on exams even though the average was like a 40% every time

Everything that is taught is written on a chalk board chaotically. Tests are EXTREMELY difficult and nothing like the practice problems in class. If you want to succeed study the webassigns with ChatGPT explaining how to do each, don't waste time going over class notes. One missed multiple choice question is already a -5 points which is absurd.

Goes very fast in lecture. Does an OK job covering material. Tests are VERY difficult especially MCQ. Each MCQ is worth 5 points so you will get a low score if you get multiple wrong. Free response problems are harder than what she covers in lecture but not as bad as the MCQ section. Her office hours are helpful. Gives no extra credit and no drops

Amazing and super nice. Lectures are helpful and on chalkboard; attendance was not mandatory but she doesn't post notes. Lots and lots of homework; 10-20+ questions from the textbook plus WebAssigns due every Thursday. Very accommodating in and out of class and cares about the progress of students. Has an accent, but is most times understandable.

If you're ready to hate computer science, take Young Cao. For perspective, his CS 3114 in Spring 2025 began with 150 students. 70% of his section dropped prior to the drop date, down to 40 students. There will likely be more to withdraw, aswell. Young Cao turned an advanced data structures class into a theoretical based boxing ring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 3114 is already a pretty infamous course because of its projects and time commitment needed but Dr. Cao pushes the difficulty regardless. His tests are insanely difficult compared to the other sections yet the heavy projects and homework are all the same. He does things that make no sense when it comes to course policy and seems almost sadistic

I wont doubt Cao's dedication for teaching but he can be very confusing and takes a long while to get his points across, making it hard to pay attention to lectures. Tests are so much harder than other professors, so if you value your grade, take with another professor.

By the way, "knowledge results good credits" was written by his bot account.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: knowledge results good credits

whole class just received an email talking about how our answers looked like we "weren't motivated to study". his test average been a F for years and he doesn't think an A should be possible let alone achievable. terrible is a kind way of wording his teaching. what i want to say about him would probably get this review taken down.

Took the first midterm, and it was the hardest test I've taken in my life. I've been an A student my whole life up until entering this joke of a department. When will this guy realize that designing tests so the average is an F is blasphemous? How does he expect students to succeed? CS is hard enough as it is. Don't take him, he's an absolute joke!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Makes his class harder than it needs to be for no reason. His tests are twice as hard as other professors take hamouda if you value your grade
This class was a disaster with Cao. His midterms are at least 250% harder than the other professors. If you value your grade, please take somebody else. You'll be thanking yourself soon, I promise/
Terrible teaching style in lectures. Notes aren't good. Very strict grader. Accent makes him harder to understand at times.

cao is a very nice professor and he really does try his best to be accommodating, but he is objectively not the best professor at teaching. his lectures are not structured well and it is very informal/conversational, so it makes learning a new subject very difficult. one thing to note is his course is more math heavy than a usual CS course.

If you can take the other professor just do that because this is not it. He has one of the hardest tests I've take at Tech, and it is lowkey impossible to even study for it because the questions are extremely specific to the lectures. You will not get the lectures too, not the best lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class itself was awful, so be prepared to read textbook or references from else where other than lectures to understand stuffs. Also, start your projects right at the beginning so that you have enough time to figure it out and fix things. Tests are heavy, but at least try to get one test done perfectly. This'll help boost your grade a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This course is extremely hard with too much mathematics. The professor is tough. His score average has been 55% for years.

Cao's teaching style is awful.  His examples are either oversimplified, overcomplicated, or nonexistant. His accent makes him very difficult to understand during lecture, and his explanations are more confusing than helpful. The class average for the final this semester was a 55%. Grading is unfair and many test questions are deceptive by design.
Just reads off the PPT slides and clearly doesn't have any passion for the subject. I did fine because of a lot of prior knowledge but make sure you pay attention to the textbook
She just reads off the PPT slides and is unenthusiastic with her teaching. Don't take her. Not worth it

Textbook will be very important to use. Lectures are online once a week but the slides are going through material you can read in the textbook on your own. She does small in-class quizzes and attendance is mandatory, but counts for a lot. The exams weren't that bad if you read the textbook and understand vocab terms.
DO NOT TAKE HER CAN NOT TEACH AND JUST HAS NO IDEA WHAT SHE IS DOING AND WHAT BEING A PROFESSOR IS

She seemed nice, but all she did during class was read straight from powerpoints that were available on canvas, and attendance was mandatory. You get unlimited attempts on quizzes, but you have to study for the exams or you won't do well.

Met for zoom for an hour each week just for her to read straight from the textbook and be unresponsive. Test were hard simply because you had no idea what to expect or know what to study. Saving grace was unlimited attempts on quizzes. Class is definitely doable, but will require work outside of class because professor is simply not good.

Doesn't do a very good job of teaching and weekly zooms are always so chaotic because she doesn't know what she's doing. Attend every class, they count! Weekly quizzes are all online and easy with unlimited attempts. Tests were difficult but if you just read the powerpoints and study guide you should be good. Don't bother with the tedious textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor does not teach at all! Anything she says in class is her just reading straight from the textbook. She is not responsive at all and never actually answers your questions. Exams are hard because you have no idea what to study. Only plus to her class is that you have unlimited attempts on weekly quizzes.
I bet she is not a bad person but her ability to teach was so underdeveloped. Never take her if you want to remain sane.

The only reason I did well is because I took AP Stat in high school. This class is pretty much an exact repeat of that content. I could never understand anything he was saying because he has a very thick accent, which isn't his fault but made it very difficult to follow the lectures. Only take this professor if you have a strong foundation in stat

Has a super thick accent that is terribly hard to understand. Only had 10 assignments the whole year including exams. All assignments are take-home on a word document. Only take this class if you took it in high school because you will learn nothing in this class. TAs grade everything leniently. He requires JMP software which is also hard to use.
Me and my roommate dropped it within the first 10 minutes of class. You will not be able to read his scribble writing or understand more than one word he says every few minutes.

He has a very thick accent and speaks very quietly so it is hard to hear him. Has no clear grading criteria on homework and exams. Everything is turned in remotely. He posts all lectures and slides on canvas which is helpful, and most people stopped coming to class. Generally boring, uninspiring, and unhelpful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her class can definitely be tough, but what makes her such a great teacher is she truly wants her students to do well. If you put in the effort and commit to learning the material, you can succeed in her class. She's always super patient while answering questions and genuinely wants to help if you go to her after class or during office hours.

Dr. Li is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. Despite my scheduling conflicts, she met with me outside office hours and provided great support. After failing Test 0, I felt discouraged, but her patience and guidance helped me recover and finish the class with a B-. I'm so grateful for her dedication and encouragement!

I really struggled at first—it was rough. But hitting up her office hours made a huge difference. She always broke things down in a way that actually made sense. Her lectures were tough to keep up with sometimes, but she knew how to point out the important stuff and gave great tips on how to tackle different types of problems.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a very kind professor. Everytime I ask her questions or email to her, she always answer me patiently. I like her style of teaching, it is realy easy to understand. I really learn a lot from her class, and got A in her class. She never put too much homework. And her quizs and exams are really eazy too pass.

Please do not take this class with this teacher. No one understand what she was saying since she did not seem proficient in english. Notes are horrible. I understand that the course itself is hard to learn and teach in the case of this class the teacher makes it much harder. Take any other teacher other than her.

Probably the most difficult instructor I've ever learned from. Took BC Calc in high school and had to teach myself a lot of the content in this class. Assigns homework sometimes 8 times a week and expects us to automatically understand the material. She clearly understands what she's teaching, but most of the time we can't understand her.

The class was hard but not because of her. The way the tests are graded are stupid, but she helped me understand what I needed to do to succeed. Without her help it would have been much harder to figure out what they were looking for on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is difficult to understand. She clearly knows the material, but doesn't communicate it to the students very well. Many people in her class just stopped attending the weekly recitations because they weren't helpful. I started attending a different professor's meetings and review sessions late in the semester. It made a huge difference.
She is so sweet and really values her students' opinions. She assigns essays but they only have to be 400 words it's extremely doable. Just make sure you do the homework and get to class.

Absolutely adored this professor, one of my favorite one's I've ever had at Tech. She truly cared about how her students did and was able to welcome differing opinions on subject matters in a respectful manner amongst the students. She has done more for me as a person and student than I think she realizes.

She takes the time to answer any questions or concerns. She is also very clear and straightforward about her expectations from students., which I really enjoyed as I don't see that in other classes. She is also very personable which makes it much easier for students to approach.

I found the instructor's feedback on essays and in-office hours to be incredibly helpful! I really appreciated the instructor's willingness to work with us during the difficulties of the pandemic. Her lectures were great supplementary pieces to the readings! It made everything come together.

Liberal professor pushing her agenda! Make sure to write how feminism is the most important aspect of security studies and youll do fine. Lots of reading involved and plenty of deviation from the syllabus

She has a ridiculous policy where if a student has a legitimate excuse, like going to the hospital or a funeral, for turning in a paper (worth 30%) the highest grade they can receive is an C+. Extremely slow grader and essay prompts/reqs are confusing at best. Lectures are very disorganized and the ppts and readings are reused. Low quality prof!

Kevin was an amazing professor, really took the time to go through the material during class. Labs are difficult, make sure you take them during the Fall semester. If you take during the winter semester, bundle up!
10/10 He's a great professor, very respectful and gives great lectures. He also prepares you well and provides you with all the material needed for exams.
Just Llike Mrs.White but better

Dr.Young is the best professor I have had at Virginia Tech. Though I found his tests pretty difficult, I liked his lectures and personality. He's very caring and encouraging. I worked super hard and he did not ignore that but really appreciated it.

Easy lectures but long tests that are mostly memorization. Labs count for a lot of this class so that's the most important part really. Overall minimal effort class with not much homework but labs certainly make up for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor, takes the time to try and learn everyone's name.

Kevin's CAD class was a lot of fun and he made it very enjoyable to go to. Be warned that the last half of the semester covers Revit, which is taught by "Tom Powers", not Kevin, who is terrible and made the end of the semester miserable in this class. Be prepared to spend 10+ hours on a single Revit assignment so don't put it off.

Kevin is an amazing professor in the CEE department. He has plenty of real-world experience that he incorporates into his lectures, and takes the time to thoroughly explain content. Very manageable and enjoyable class, easy A with some effort. TAKE IT IN THE FALL! The lab is outdoors and you'll be miserable in the spring semester's winter.

I love his teaching style. First goes over concepts, and then uses them to go over numerical problems. Very clear about what we should expect on exams. Also is ok with students calling him Kevin. Super chill dude.

Fantastic professor with a very fair workload. Teaches clearly and concisely. If you follow along with the lectures, the assignments should be a breeze. There is little opportunity to access information outside of class time so make use of it.
Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had at Tech. His lectures are very straight forward, and he is aways willing to help when it's needed. 11/10 would take again.

Yu is a funny, chill professor for a tough subject. His lectures can be boring since he just reads off the slides, and sometimes I get the vibe that he doesn't know what he's talking about. Start homeworks and lab early, as they are extremely time-consuming.
Reads off slides quite a bit. Kind of a boring lecturer and it was definitely hard to pay attention after awhile.

I LOVE HIM. While he's not the best teacher, the 2024 material is manageable to learn on your own. He's also a generous grader and even offers extra credit. He's not perfect, but the class is enjoyable, and you'll likely earn a strong grade compared to other sections. He's a great person to learn from. You'll definitely gain a lot from the course.

Nice guy, doesn't teach very well, seems like he doesn't know what he's doing most of the time. Refuses to give full credit an ANY assignment even if you put in extra work and effort. You will get an 80% if you do everything on the rubric.

This class is a project-based class where you and one other partner make one of four provided projects. Professor Yu does a decent job steering you in the right direction if you ask questions, but it really is an independent class. He's alright and gives decent advice, but ultimately, you and your partner are in charge of your project.

Descent IDP professor. He's an easy grader. Unfortunately, many IDP professors grades based on the figures/pictures...He gave feedback when necessary, and helped steer my project in the right direction. The TAs for Home Audio this semester were really good too-they gave me the most help. Your experience is kinda a gamble on who your partner is....
Great professor and detailed lecturer. Homework assignments were relevant and helped prepare me for tests.

Very nice guy, didn't really like his lectures. I felt he didn't really teach anything, he would just restate lecture slides. I did well in the course by going to office hours every week and doing HWs and labs there. Very lenient grader, does a lot of error care to make sure you get max amount of points.

Not bad. We had the highest test averages compared to the other professors. Tries to joke but they often fall flat. Pretty lenient grader, but made mistakes on grading and answer keys (mightve been ta issue, not sure) so make sure to double check stuff.

Good professor. Homework was reasonable, and lectures were well thought out. Yu provides a lot of study material, such as review slides and exams from previous years, which helps with studying for exams.  Make sure to take advantage of ULA and GTA office hours, as I found those extremely helpful when completing homework and labs.
He is a cool guy. Lectures can be better but generous grader overall.

Make sure to attend his lectures as this class is lecture heavy. His personal website contains lots of solved practice problems that add to the lectures.  The class material is only as difficult as it is due to the material being covered. He does his best to make it easier. Yu does his best to give back points and extend assignments when he can.

Professor Yu is alright. Nothing special really. If you're taking him for IDP, he doesn't give that many good pointers, and sometimes even points in the wrong direction on accident, causing you to waste time. Overall though, he's a pretty generous grader in my experience so I didn't have too many issues overall. Decent prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yu is a nice professor, but is hard to get help from. He often gave vague answers to questions I had about my project, so I had to strongly advocate for myself if I wanted help. I don't know if this is just Yu, but the way he graded the weekly reports was inconsistent. Although, if asked to meet with a group outside of class, he'd try.

Ignore what previous students have said about this professor. William Yu has completely changed his methodology of teaching. He is a very kind, understanding professor. Because of this, he frequently extends homework deadlines and gives students homework hints because of the overwhelming difficulty of this course. Do not miss lectures, however.

Yu has no pity for his students and believes that his students should be as smart as him but doesn't answer "easy" questions. It is impossible to ask him for help outside of class and would reply to issues about homework or a lab days or sometimes weeks after the assignment was due. His lectures would confuse me more than if I never showed up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was hard. A lot of people ended up dropping from it. Professor Yu was really nice but sometimes I feel like he didn't know how to teach us what we needed to know. He was always willing to help and asked for feedback but the difficulty of the class and the amount of HW and labs made it tough.

He makes us call him "Teach", young guy, more like a class know-it-all than a prof. Sometimes won't help students bc he wants them to figure it out themselves. He does play favorites though, so try to make him like you. He likes hard workers, looks down on you if you do the bare minimum. (prof for Integrated design Project).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: This is first semester (Fall 2019) teaching. Thus, he is not great at understanding what students ask him, reads off slides, does examples without really explaining the thought process, and is strict with grading. He will only allow one SIDE for an equation sheet and announce "no partial credit" on a final with work-out problems worth 15-20 points.

Tough accent at first but super caring and understanding. Class can be a little boring, but he teaches the material very well. If you have any questions he's always excited to answer and really knows his stuff. He's also fairly lenient on grading (especially for the homeworks) and his test averages were consistently higher than average. Great prof!

I can confidently say that Dr. Yue is one of the most reliable, respectful, and likable professors at Virginia Tech. Every single lecture of his was high quality and in office hours he would be more than willing to expand upon topics related to class material and beyond the scope of the class itself. His grading is very fair and reasonable.
Very friendly and understanding. Tests and quizzes are graded very leniently and don't have anything not covered by his lectures.

Very excited about math! This class was async because of COVID but he offered extra "class time" where he reviewed the pre-recorded lectures and focused more on example problems. They were easy to understand and he really enjoyed asking and explaining questions. Hard class but just because of the material, fair grader.

Checking phone on the class? You are in trouble. Missing one step when solving the questions? Youll lose half of the points. Want to use laptop for notes? They are banned. Want to record all notes? Theyll be wiped before you finish. Just trust me, never choose him as your instructor. Youll waste your whole semester.

If you attend class regularly then you might or might not understand what he teaches. He has a heavy Russian accent but it isnt too bad if you listen to him carefully. Apart from that, his grading has no clear logic and he makes up some random excuse as to why he gave you 0/12 for a question. He gives no feedback and pushes questions to officehour
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I have ever had at tech. His lectures were almost all derivations that were useless when trying to do homework. I had to learn 100% of the material on my own in the textbook. He would mess up in the middle of lectures and start over. He didn't give any forms of study guides or practice tests for any of the tests.

Bonnie did not treat this asynchronous class like an asynchronous class. She recorded hours worth of lectures that we had to watch, and on top of that had us read from the textbook. She also had a zoom call at a specific time that was required. Her assignments were often very long, and she often graded writing harshly. I was very annoyed with her.

Dr. Zare is remarkable! I took this as an online course, there is a LOT of reading. Only take this class if you're really really passionate about this kind of stuff because it is very time consuming cs I would find this class taking up LOTS of time compared to my other classes that were also challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bonnie is very passionate about the content in WGS 1824, and she teaches it well. But, if you are expecting to take WGS 1824 as an easy online pathway DONT. I'm an engineering major and I genuinely have more time-consuming work for this pathway than some of my major classes.

Dr.Zare is very passionate and well spoken. If you are looking for a class you will be excited to talk about or will remember after graduating, go for Dr.Zare. She is easy going and caring, and makes it clear that she's looking to help you succeed as long as you show effort. You'll have to care about her class, but you'll end up wanting to anyway.

Horrible!!!!! Does not like to be told he is wrong, even though he is wrong all the time. Will basically call you stupid if you attempt to answer a question. So hard to understand and is awful at explaining things. Never take his class

Honestly Dr Shen was not a great teacher. If I would have wanted to do well in this class I would have had to reteach myself everything outside of class (which I did not). I think it is worth noting that he grades incredibly fair. I stayed through the whole class until the final and he gave me points on tests that I probably did not deserve.

He's kind of a rude person and similar to what other people say he expects you to know everything at all times and questions are a burden for him. The redeeming grace is that the tests weren't that hard so it is possible to hate the class and him and still be able to get a good grade. I think the test average were in the 75-80% range.

Shen is rude & hard to follow. He does not understand the student's perspective. When someone builds up enough courage to ask a question, his typical response is "I don't know what you mean", "I don't understand" or may even laugh at you. Lectures are hard to follow as he talks into the board and mumbles. Exam reviews are barely exam reviews.

Dr. Shen wasn't a great professor and he definitely isn't my first pick but in my opinion he wasn't as bad as many other reviews have said. His exams were filled with problems from the lectures(write them down and study them) and the practice problems he posted before. He can be mean at times but towards the end of the semester he became nicer.

Didn't learn from the lectures. Only thing I will say was that the tests weren't that bad. Definitely would not take again and would not recommend. Hard to understand when he teaches and always says stuff like "this is easy" or "you guys should be able to do this". Whenever someone asks a question he never really answers it.

RUN AWAY NOW! DO NOT TAKE SHEN AT ALL COSTS. He has no lectures and simply expects us to watch YouTube videos outside of class. He gave no lectures whatsoever and only used around 20 minutes of class time to do problems that nobody knew how to do since the YouTube videos taught us nothing. If you value your sanity, don't take this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're reading this and you still have the chance to get out, RUN! Unless you're fine with self-teaching the entire multi-var curriculum, DROP! Lectures will make you question your life choices...Do not be fooled by anyone vouching this instructor, please be smart and find someone else.

Shen is just not a good professor. Our class was a flipped model, and it went as well as you can expect. Nobody learned anything, and we basically had to learn everything from poorly done online videos. When he did try to teach us, his strong accent and low voice made is basically impossible to hear what he was saying.

Do not pick this professor!!

He can be mean with his comments, but I found his lectures and notes to be very useful. It was most helpful when he went over examples of each concept (TAKE NOTE OF THEM AND STUDY THEM!!). His exams had questions that were almost exactly from his lecture notes and assigned homework. Still had to watch vids online to understand some concepts though.

Professor Shen always held a helpful review day and created some review questions that if you studied enough then you could always do well on the exams. In most lectures, he gave enough time for you to write everything down, or if he rushed through then you could ask for him to go back to a specific slide after class. Most HW questions had answers.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Rewrites his notes on the board in paragraphs for lectures. Graded assignments have no useful feedback. Learned more from attending student success center tutoring sessions twice than I did in all of his lectures. Take this at a community college or learn how to teach yourself math because Shen isn't going to teach you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things
